name: Ability_GetAuxRecord
callers: About a dozen battle, learn and UI functions (`sub_1400FA94C`, `sub_1400FBA58`, `sub_1401113B8`, `sub_140153CA0`, `sub_140206F90`, `sub_14022F868`, `sub_14028A474`, `sub_1402A102C`, `sub_1402A1DA0` and others)
purpose: Returns the executable's per-ability auxiliary record and an extra category-specific pointer for an ability id.

behavior.text: the id is masked to 9 bits (0..511); *outAux points at the aux table base 0x140787F80 plus 8 bytes per id.
record layout: u16 classic JP cost, u8 learn percent, u8 flags3, u32 flags4.
ids below 0x170 return category 0 and *outExtra = the per-ability 20-byte record from a lazily initialised table (null for ids above 0x16F).

ids from 0x170 return categories 1..8 with *outExtra pointing into one of six small byte tables: 0x170..0x17D is 1, ..0x189 is 2, ..0x195 is 3, ..0x19D is 4, ..0x1A5 is 5, ..0x1C5 is 6, ..0x1E5 is 7, the rest 8. Categories 3 and 4 use a 2-byte stride.
the learn percent is the chance tested against Rng_Percent(100, v) when an ability is learned.
the 8-byte aux header corresponds to the classic game's per-ability data; flags3 and flags4 bit meanings are not established (?).

notes:
The function's eight id thresholds (0x140275A9F..0x140275B70) and its 9-bit mask (0x140275A7E) are immediates in its body. Its six kind tables are read through virtual bases: kind1 0x140785CA8, kind2 0x140789112, kind3 0x140788F4C, kind4 0x140788F54, kind5 0x1407844EA, kind6 0x140788DDA; three of those virtual bases lie inside the aux table and one inside the gap before kind3. Kind tables by role (V by readers, I by name): 1 Item-command item id, 2 Throw item type, 3 Jump horizontal/vertical, 4 Charge ct/power, 5 Arithmeticks masks, 6 running index of reaction/support/movement ids.

The nxd Ability JP columns are what the game reads for cost; this table keeps the classic values and the learn chance. About ten entries differ from the nxd cost.
open_questions: Bit meanings of flags3 and flags4.

name: Ability_GetJpCost
purpose: Returns the ability's JP cost: the u16 at Ability row +64 (jp_cost_low | jp_cost_high << 8); 0xFFFF when the table or row is missing.

behavior.text: same cached table 39 as AbilityTable_GetRow; returns *(u16 *)(row + 64).
decoded cost is 0..9999, 360 abilities cost > 0 (Cure 50, Curaga 450, Curaja 800).

notes:
Also known as AbilityTable_GetJpCost (earlier sheet name). sub_1402B9AD0 subtracts the cost from the unit's per-job JP (unit + 202 + 2 * jobIndex, u16); sub_1402867BC / sub_14028A474 mark an ability learnable (|0x4000) when the unit's JP is not below the cost.

- Correction: arguments 2..4 are unused (the signature has no job argument); 7 callers.
open_questions: Exact meaning of the 0x4000 / 0x2000 flag words (I: learned / learnable).

name: AbilityAction_BuildWorkingCopy
callees: memmove, sub_1403D325C (registry lookup), sub_1403D3BE4 (row by index), sub_1403D2FD8 (row data pointer)
purpose: Creates the writable ability action table: copies the executable's built-in table of 368 records (20 bytes each) and then overwrites fields from the OverrideAbilityActionData nxd table (id 247). This is how nxd data can change ability range, formula, CT or MP cost without touching the executable.

behavior.text: copies 0x1CC0 bytes (368 records x 20) from the built-in table to the working table in one move.
looks up nxd table 247 (cached in a global after the first lookup) and walks its rows by row index, one row per ability id, up to the table's row count.
a field is overwritten only when the override cell is not negative; a negative cell leaves the built-in value.

record layout of the 20 bytes: +0 Range, +1 effect_area, +2 Vertical, +3..4 first flag list, +5..6 second flag list, +7 Element, +8 Formula, +9 X, +10 Y, +11 inflict_status, +12 CT, +13 mp. The remaining bytes (+14..19) are never written by this function.
the two flag lists are list cells in the nxd row (count at +8 / +16, data offset at +4 / +12); the first two entries of each list become the two bytes.
a live comparison of the built-in table and the working copy showed 47 differing bytes, all in the CT and mp columns, matching the stock override rows.

notes:
The working copy (0x14078B2E0) is filled by a memmove (source lea at 0x1402BAE42); the nxd 247 overrides then apply on top. The copy is built lazily on the first AbilityAction_GetRecord call.

About 40 call sites read records through AbilityAction_GetRecord; the formula, range and cost code all read this working copy.
open_questions: Meaning of the zero bytes at +14..15 and the all-ones bytes at +16..19.

name: AbilityAction_GetRecord
callers: about 40 callers: battle formula, range/area, cost and AI code
purpose: Returns a pointer to the 20-byte action record of an ability, building the working table on first use.

behavior.text: returns null when the ability id is above 0x16F (367); ids from 368 up (the passive abilities) have no action record.
on the first call, runs AbilityAction_BuildWorkingCopy once and sets a done flag.
returns working table + 20 * id.

notes: Field layout of the record is on the AbilityAction_BuildWorkingCopy page.

name: AbilityTable_GetRow
callers: Ability menus and UI code that needs an ability's name, icon or description.
purpose: Returns the Ability NXD row for an ability id, or null when the table or row is missing. The table is loaded lazily and cached.

behavior.text: lazily loads NXD table 39 through `sub_1403D325C` and caches it in `qword_143CDA2D0`; returns null if the table manager or the load fails.
looks up the row by ability id with `sub_1403D3AE8`; returns null when the row is missing.
a negative row key resolves to the static empty row `unk_1406F5ED0`.
otherwise resolves the row with `sub_1403D2FD8`.
table 39 is the Ability table. The old-build accessor is a different function in this build.

notes:
The row layout below is ported from the earlier Ability layout research and has not been revalidated byte by byte against this build.

| `0x04` | icon | int |

| `0x1A` | Padding | short |
| `0x1C` | Comment | string |
| `0x20` | ui_text | int |
| `0x24` | battle_voices | int[] |
| `0x2C` | ui_text_2 | int |

name: Achievement_CounterReached
purpose: Tells whether an achievement's counter has reached its threshold.

behavior.text: row = NxdTable_GetRowById(195, id); true when threshold (+0xC) is non-zero and the UserSituation counter named by counter (+8) is at least threshold.
the counter is read from g_UserSituation +24 + 4 * id, or +104 + 4 * id when bit 0 of +16 is set.

name: Achievement_LookupTelemetryRow
purpose: Looks up an achievement's telemetry row (part read).

behavior.text: looks up the row of the TelemetryAchievement-en table (173, cached at qword_143CDA0B0) by Achievement telemetry_achievement (+4) and reads its +0x1C, string +0x2C, +0x38 and bytes +0x3C / +0x3D.

name: Achievement_RowExists
purpose: Tests that the Achievement row of key 9 exists.

behavior.text: the function reads only the existence of the row (key 9).

name: AchievementOtherJournal_Match
purpose: Match function of the Chronicle-event achievement class (vtable 0x1407031E8).

behavior.text: true for notification type 25 (JournalNotification) whose +8 equals Achievement event_id (+0x14).
that value is Journal event_id (+0x18); for example Journal key 310 ('Seekers of the Stone') has +0x18 = 159.

purpose: Match function of the book-read achievement class (vtable 0x1407032A8).

name: Action_BuildCurrentAction
callers: sub_1403167E4, Ai_SurveyTargets (two sites), sub_14038BC00 (two sites), sub_14038C8F8, sub_14038D1EC, sub_14038D65C
purpose:
Turns one packed four-byte action entry into the game's current-action block at `0x1418716A0`: it resolves the
command, fills the action's range and presentation fields from the ability or item data, and for the item and throw
commands resolves the item id and the ability that represents it.

behavior.text:
the entry is four bytes: a 16-bit packed word, a command byte and a flags byte; the word's low ten bits are
  the action id and the high six bits are the acting unit slot.
it clears the first sixteen bytes of the current-action block, the dword at +0x10 and the dword at +0x20.
it stores the entry's command byte at block +0, the packed id word at +2, and the entry's flags byte at +0x10.

the command's kind comes from the byte table at `0x14067E010`, indexed by the command id; the function
  dispatches on that kind.

kind 1 is the Item command: the item id is the action id minus `0x80`, the item's chemist row is read, and the
  kind1 byte at `0x140785E18` indexed by the action id minus `0x170` (that is, the item id the command offers) is
  stored in block word 3 at +6. The table supplies the stored item id, not a paired ability.

kind 2 is the Throw command: the action id is an item id, the item record is read, and equip-categories `0x20`
  and `0x21` are mapped to the fixed throw abilities `0x17E` and `0x189`; any other category keeps the cached throw
  ability word at `0x1418724B4`.

for Throw the item id is stored at block +6 and the resolved throw ability at +2, so the two fields disagree
  about what the word means until the ability is resolved.
kind 7 stores the action id minus `0x26` in block word 3 (+6).

kind 9 stores the kind3 word at `0x140788F4C`, indexed by twice the id, into block byte 4, and stores 1 when the id
  is zero.
kind 10 (charge) stores the kind4 byte at `0x140788F54` into block byte 1.

the default path (also reached from kinds 1, 2 and 7) copies the aux-flags dword at `0x140787F84` indexed by twice
  the id into block bytes 13..16.

for ids below `0x170` it copies several bytes of the ability's 20-byte action row into the block, the fields the
  targeting and display code reads.

for ids at or above `0x170` the action row is skipped and the defaults stay in the block; item, throw, jump and
  arithmetic abilities have no action row.
a raw id above 1023 cannot reach the function through the packed word, because only ten bits are ever read.

this builds the AI and preview "current action", not the player's request, because every caller found is an AI
  or command-preview function.

notes:
The block layout (byte offsets) is only partly decoded; field roles above are by position.
- V: copies the 4 + 1 status bytes (+1..+5) of the added-effect record selected by r14 into xmmword_1418716A0 +8..+12.
open_questions: - ?: what the dword at block +0x20 holds; the function only clears it.

name: Action_PickTargetEquipment
proto: ? (writes a slot descriptor through a pointer in r8)
purpose:
Chooses which equipment slot a steal or break action aims at, from the target unit's hand and body slots, and reports the
chosen slot and item to the action builder.

behavior.text:
It starts from a stored target record and an action output pointer; the first thing it writes is a slot-type byte of
  0xFE, meaning no slot chosen.

It inspects five hand words at +0x1A, +0x1C, +0x1E, +0x22 and +0x26 and two byte-sized hand slots at +0x20 and
  +0x24.

A word equal to 255 counts as an empty slot for the three +0x1A..+0x1E words; the two +0x22/+0x26 words are compared
  against a bound of 261 instead.

The ability case is a chain of subtractions on the current ability id, which is read from a word global, so the case
  ids are not immediates in this body; each case tests one of the equipment words at +26 through +38 against 255 and
  0x105.

The hand slots compare the levels of the two weapons, read with byte loads, so only the low byte of an id is used in
  that comparison.
The bound register also derives 255 (the bound minus 6) and is rebuilt from it (255 plus 6).

A unit whose status byte hides the equipment (the reaction/steal flags it reads early) short-circuits before any slot
  is chosen.

The two byte hand slots are read as 8-bit item ids and also treat 255 as empty, so an item id above 255 cannot be
  expressed in that part of the record.

The chosen slot type is encoded as a bit: 0x20, 8, 2, 0x40, 0x80 for the word slots and 0x10 / 4 for the two byte
  slots; the chosen id is stored as a word at +4 of the output.

The bit values line up with the five visible equipment slots (right hand, left hand, head, body, accessory) plus the
  two extra target slots, but the exact slot naming is not stated anywhere in the code read.

The bound of 261 and the 255 empty value are the same conventions used by the inventory and the party record, which
  supports reading this as the steal/break target selector.

the case ids are compare immediates on the word at 0x1407B0778 (the ability being resolved): 110..114, 138..141, 160..163 and 361..365; each picks one equipment word (slot types 0x80, 0x40, 0x20, 8 or 2, 4 and 16 for the two byte slots); any other id, or a monster unit (byte +6 mask 0x20), clears the slot byte and returns -1 with no item. The choice is keyed by the ability id: see FormulaHandlersChooseTheirEffectByAbilityId.

it stores the slot mask at +0x1B (R+27: 0xFE first, 0 when nothing is picked) and the item id at R+4; it returns 0 when a piece is picked and -1 otherwise. The slot by ability id: 110, 138, 161, 361 head (mask 0x80, unit word +0x1A); 111, 139, 160, 362 body (0x40, +0x1C); 114, 163, 365 accessory (0x20, +0x1E); 113, 141, 162, 364 the weapon with the higher record byte +2 of the two hand bytes (0x10 right, +0x20; 0x04 left, +0x24, only when its value is higher); 112, 140, 363 the right shield (0x08, +0x22) else the left (0x02, +0x26).
a word of 255 or 0x105 and above counts as empty; a unit with +6 bit 0x20 set returns -1 at once.

notes:
- I: Read from the head and the slot decision ladder; the two byte slots are the only place on the item path where an id is
  read from a byte.
open_questions:
- ?: What writes the byte slots at +0x20 and +0x24, and can they ever hold a value above 255?
- ?: Which abilities the case values stand for (I: steal / break equipment); the case ids are deltas in the subtraction
  chain, not immediates in this body.

name: Action_SetWeaponItem
purpose:
Fills the weapon item id of a battle action from the acting unit's equipped weapon, with 255 standing for empty hands and
zero written for an empty or out-of-range id.

behavior.text: It stores the action record passed in rcx and reads a global action/ability kind before deciding which weapon to use.
The weapon word comes from one of three global words, selected by that kind and by the action's own state byte.
The weapon id is compared with 255; a match means no weapon.
A second path accepts the id only when it is below 261, so an id above the stock range is treated as no weapon.

An empty or rejected id is written as 0 into word 5 of the current-action block at 0x1407B0770 (offset +0xA); an
  accepted id is written as itself.

When the id is accepted it resolves the ability action record through AbilityAction_GetRecord, so the weapon id and
  the action's ability row stay linked.

The 255 test and the 261 bound are the same empty/bound pair used by the other equipment readers; the function is the
  action-side writer of that value.

Whether the action record's weapon field is a plain item id or an index into the ability action table is not settled
  by the code read.

notes:
- V: Its two callers are Battle_ResolveAction (the sheet for 0x1403099B0) and BattleAct_BuildResult, which places it on
  the action build path.

name: ActiveUnit_OverheadMark
callees: sub_1402607C0, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_1400D3150, sub_140028B10, sub_1400FDC48
purpose: Places the overhead mark of the active unit.

behavior.text: reads the CharShape row's height (+0x2C) of the active unit's shape as a float for the mark's height.

notes: Name is ours; only the height read was examined.

name: AdditionalKerning_Lookup
proto: float *AdditionalKerning_Lookup(AdditionalKerning *t, float out[3], unsigned __int16 leftGid, unsigned __int16 rightGid)
purpose: Looks up the (left, right) glyph pair in the .ker table's std::map and returns its extra (x, y) kerning (0 when missing); builds the map first when it is dirty.

behavior.text: when byte t+184 (dirty) is set: sub_1403BA3A4(t) builds the map and the byte is cleared.

out+4 (qword) = 0; out[0] = out[1] = rightGid. Key = rightGid + (leftGid << 16). Walks the red-black tree rooted at t+208: nodes with byte +25 == 0 are real; dword +28 is the key; keys >= wanted go left, others right. When found (not the head and key not larger): out+4 += float at node+36 (x) and out+8 += float at node+40 (y).

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BA2D4). Documented in fonts.md as table B; shipped .ker files are empty so the lookup always misses in retail data.

name: Ai_ActionWorthOnUnit
purpose: Tells the AI whether the action in g_AiCurrentAction is worth trying on unit `slot`: 0 no, 1 yes, 2 yes (a stronger case).

behavior.text: 0 when the unit will still be Jumping (5) when the action resolves; when it will still have Reflect (38) and the action has hint bit +14 0x40 (the self test only), or Atheist (33) and hint bit +14 0x04 (I: reflectable and faith-based actions); when status 31 will last and the action lacks hint bit +11 0x01.

an action that adds statuses (g_AiCurrentAction +13 bit 0x10): for each of the five status bytes, the action's bits (+8..+12) that the unit does not have (+0x61..+0x65) and is not immune to (the 5 bytes at +0x5C) make it worth it (with exceptions per byte: some statuses only when other conditions hold).

an action that removes statuses (cancel mode): the bits the unit has (+0x61..) and that are not innate (the 5 bytes at +0x57) make it worth it; for statuses 24 and up only when Ai_StatusLastsTurns says they will not wear off before the action resolves.

the turns passed to Ai_StatusLastsTurns are g_AiCurrentAction +1 (also compared with the unit's own ticks to its next turn, from KO counter +7, CT +65 and CT gain +64); I: the ticks until the action resolves. A removable timed status whose countdown is below that number is dropped from the cancel test.
in the cancel test, statuses 34, 36 and 37 are also dropped when sub_14038E2AC(unit) is greater than their countdown byte.
the add test (hint bit +13 0x10) has no wear-off check: a status the unit has is never worth adding again, whatever its countdown.
so only the 40 statuses of the five status bytes enter this test.
when the unit is the acting unit and the action id is below 368, an action whose AbilityAction record +4 has bit 0x01 is not worth it (the id gate at 0x14038B3DD).
the random pass of hint bit +13 0x08 steps the game xorshift state (xmmword_1408E5FC8).

notes: Name is ours.
open_questions: ? the case of the action flag bit 0x08 (abilities 118..150 with a random pass).

name: Ai_StatusLastsTurns
proto: int Ai_StatusLastsTurns(int turns, UnitWorkRecord *unit, int status)
purpose: Tells the battle AI whether a unit has a status and will still have it after the given number of its turns.

behavior.text: returns 0 when the status bit is not set in the unit effective set (+97, byte status / 8, bit 0x80 >> (status % 8)).
for status 5 (Jumping) it returns 0 when turns is greater than the unit charge counter (+0x18D).

for a status of 24 or more (the timed statuses) that is not in the innate group a (+87) it returns 0 when turns is greater than the countdown byte (unit + 78 + status, the byte at +102 + (status - 24)); an innate status never expires.
otherwise it returns 1 (statuses below 24 other than Jumping are permanent until removed).

notes: Name is ours. The countdown index assumes the 24..39 window; a status id outside it reads past the 16 countdown bytes.
open_questions: ? the AI decisions that use it (all callers are in the AI range).

name: Ai_SurveyTargets
callees: Action_BuildCurrentAction, Ai_ActionWorthOnUnit, Ai_StatusLastsTurns, Item_GetRecord, sub_140321704, sub_14038E2AC, sub_1403170CC, sub_140320490
purpose: Before planning, goes over every unit and every action in the acting unit's action list and notes what those actions could do to each unit (hurt it, help it), then marks which of its own actions are worth planning with.

behavior.text: for each of the 21 units and each of the 34 entries of its row in g_AiCommandTable (ended by 0xFF) it fills g_AiCurrentAction with Action_BuildCurrentAction and skips actions the unit cannot use (statuses 37 Disable, 33 Atheist, the ability gates, items not held: g_InventoryCounts).

it counts the actions whose flag byte (g_AiCurrentAction +13) has bit 0x02 (they hurt) and bit 0x01 (they help), and from them sets bits 0x01 / 0x02 / 0x04 of the unit's AI byte (byte_141872EDE + 16 x slot).

then for the acting unit's own list it drops some entries when nothing needs them (sub_140320490 with 27, 26, 38, 17) and, for each remaining one, asks Ai_ActionWorthOnUnit whether it is worth trying on the acting unit itself (entry flag bit 0x01).
it keeps the shortest reach of a hurting action and of a helping one (+14 / +15 of the record at qword_1418724D8).

for a command of kind 2 (Throw) it walks ability ids 383..392 (sub_1403170CC for availability), then item ids 0..255 (Item_GetRecord), keeping the item whose record byte +5 matches the throw category; the pick goes to word_1418724B4 / byte_1418724B6.
the slot test at 0x14032003F (v5 != 255) is a battle-unit sentinel, not an item id.

notes: Name is ours.
open_questions: ? the exact meaning of each AI byte bit and of the ratio test (count x 128 / total, threshold 76).

name: Ai_UnitTurnStep
callees: Battle_AITurnPrepare, Ai_SurveyTargets, sub_14031F92C, sub_14031F68C, sub_14031F794, sub_140320920, sub_14031F464, Mem_CopyChecked
purpose: Runs one step of an AI-controlled unit's decision (several frames per turn) and, when it is done, writes the chosen move and action.

behavior.text: a resumable state machine (stage byte byte_14187257C): Battle_AITurnPrepare, then Ai_SurveyTargets, then the move pass sub_14031F92C and sub_14031F68C / sub_14031F794, then the planner sub_140320920; a stage that is not finished returns -1 and is resumed on the next call.
before the first stage it sets g_BattleSimulating (0x14186AF80) to 1 and saves the 32-byte state at xmmword_14186AFA0; when the planner is done it clears the flag and puts the state back.
the result: out +0 = 0 with the target tile (x, y, layer) at +4 / +6 / +8, or 1 with a copied action block, or 2 (no action); the chosen tile is also written to the acting unit +79 / +80 / +81 bit 7.

notes: Name is ours.
open_questions: ? the planner sub_140320920 and its candidate loop (sub_14038BC00, sub_14038C95C) are not read yet.

name: App_LaunchClassic
purpose: Starts the Classic executable and ends this one.

behavior.text: `CreateProcessA` of `<game dir>/FFT_classic.exe <args>` (the arguments from 0x1401E6354, the game directory from `qword_143CD9B90`+48), closes the handles, then sets the quit request (`g_Application`+1520 = 1).

notes: Behavior: QuitRequest. Separately, the game imports `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`, called from another function (0x14002F060), not from this one.

name: App_ProcessMessages
purpose: Drains up to ten Win32 messages per call. Returns 1 while the application should continue, and 0 after a WM_QUIT, storing the quit code in `windowObject+64`.

behavior.text: calls `sub_14002FB14` first; that helper compares the foreground window and clips/releases the mouse cursor.
reads `Time_GetTimestamp` once before the message loop.
loops at most ten times: `PeekMessageW(&msg, NULL, 0, 0, 0)` with no remove; if there is no message, returns 1.
message 18 (WM_QUIT) stores `msg.wParam` at `windowObject+64` and returns 0.
otherwise removes the message with `PeekMessageW(..., PM_REMOVE)`, calls `TranslateMessage` and `DispatchMessageW`.
after each message compares `Time_GetTimestamp` with the starting value; a delta of 300000 (one second in 1/300000-unit ticks) returns 1.
the ten-message cap and the one-second budget prevent the message pump from starving the frame loop.

notes: The return value is used directly as the second condition of Game_Main's loop; 0 means quit.
open_questions: The fields of the window object other than +64 and the exact clip-cursor conditions in sub_14002FB14.

name: App_RunFrame
callees: sub_140014CF4, Time_GetTimestamp, IsDebuggerPresent, Debug_DetectCaptureTools, SteamAPI_RunCallbacks, sub_14006CEF0, sub_140018A2C, sub_14001CA40, sub_14001F9D8, sub_14001D038, sub_14001F2E4, sub_14001DAAC, sub_14001CC30, sub_1400206FC, sub_140087C50, sub_140087ECC, sub_14001B578, sub_140088280, sub_1400914EC, sub_14009B6B8, sub_1400A53D0, sub_1400AD00C, sub_140032A20
purpose: One iteration of the game's application loop: frame pacing, the debug/capture gate, Steam callbacks, the UI/render/audio update chain and the secondary frame-rate wait. `Game_Main` calls it in a loop until the window closes.

behavior.text: when `qword_140C69718` is non-null, calls `sub_140014CF4` first.
calls the vtable slots at `app+1152` (+48) and `app+1176` (+64) before timing the frame.

frame limiter: reads `Time_GetTimestamp`, compares the elapsed value against 1/60 s, calls `SleepEx(10)` when the frame is more than 10 ms early, and loops until the elapsed value reaches 1/60 s. The accepted timestamp is stored in `g_FrameTimestamp` (`qword_143CD9B68`).
increments the frame counter at `app+1184`.

debug/capture gate at `0x14002A342`: `IsDebuggerPresent()` true, or a non-null `qword_140C696A8` with `Debug_DetectCaptureTools()` returning 1, sets `app+1520 = 1` and jumps past the normal update block. `app+1520` is therefore a 'suppress the game update' flag (I).
when `app+24` is non-zero, adds the last frame duration at `app+16`; every 30,000 units it calls `SteamAPI_RunCallbacks` and subtracts 30,000.
when `qword_143CD9B90+2304` is set, calls `sub_14006CEF0` and `sub_140018A2C`, performs an address/foreground check, and signals the event at `qword_143CD9B90+2272`.
when `app+430` differs from `app+945`, calls the vtable slot at `app+1152` (+88), then stores `app+430` into `app+945`.

the update block (target `LABEL_42`) computes the frame delta in milliseconds and drives the UI/render object at `qword_140C69680+8`: `sub_14001CA40`, the object's vtable calls, `sub_14001F9D8`, `sub_14001D038`, `sub_14001F2E4`, the transform copies, `sub_14001DAAC`, `sub_14001CC30`, then a ten-entry subsystem update loop (32-byte stride). It finishes with `sub_1400206FC`, vtable cleanup calls, `sub_140087C50`, `sub_140087ECC`, `sub_14001B578`, `sub_140088280`, `sub_1400914EC`, `sub_14009B6B8`, `sub_1400A53D0`, `sub_1400AD00C` and `sub_140032A20`.
when `app+1192` is non-zero, computes a target interval of `300000 / fps` and spins with `Sleep(0)` until `Time_GetTimestamp` reaches it (a second frame-rate cap).
calls `GetActiveWindow`; when it differs from `app+928`, walks the window list at `app+864` and updates the active-window bookkeeping.
the function returns the loop's continue/stop state to `Game_Main`; the exact final expression was not needed to document the update path.

notes: The 1/60 s target is a floating-point constant in the limiter. `g_FrameTimestamp` is in 1/300000-second units (the same unit returned by Time_GetTimestamp and divided by 300000 in this function to get seconds). The debug/capture gate is the path that makes the game stop updating when an external debugger or a graphics capture layer is present.
open_questions: The exact meaning of `app+1520` beyond 'skip the update', and whether the second frame cap at `app+1192` is a user setting or a mode.

name: AtlasShelf_Alloc
purpose: Shelf (row) allocator for the layer atlas page: places a rectangle plus margin and returns the packed integer rectangle.

behavior.text: shelf state = { x cursor, y row start, row height, page index }; page size = u16 +20 / +22 of targetObj. Empty or inverted input rect returns the input unchanged.
margin m = clamp(min(margin, (pageW - w) / 2), 0..) for x (the division truncates toward zero), and the same for y with (pageH - h) / 2; the padded size is w + 2m by h + 2m.

when x + paddedW + 3 > pageW the shelf moves to the next row (y += rowHeight, x = 0, rowHeight = 0); when y + paddedH + 3 > pageH it opens a new page (page index + 1, cursor = (0, 0), rowHeight = 0; the cursor value is the zero pair qword_143D12018, which the database shows as -1 because it is uninitialised data but which reads 0 at runtime, live 2026-10-30). Each test is a signed int compare; the x test is made first, so a row break and a page break can both happen in one call (then x = 0, y = 0 on the new page).

the content origin is cursor + m; when the original x (origXY[0]) is a multiple of 4 and the packed x is not, the packed x is rounded up to the next multiple of 4 (same for y with origXY[1]); the extra pixels are added to the cursor advance. Output = (x, y, x + w, y + h) of the unpadded content, with no margin (the margin lies outside the returned rectangle); the row height becomes max(rowHeight, paddedH + padY); the x cursor becomes cursor + padX + paddedW. The rounding applies only when the packed value is > 0 and the original coordinate is a multiple of 4 (test on the original int rect x0 / y0, which the callers pass in origXY). V (live 2026-10-30): the whole algorithm reproduces x, y and page of all 63 layers of a running Job Tree frame (5 pages) exactly.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403B6D68). The 4-pixel alignment only applies to coordinates whose original value is a multiple of 4 (then the packed value is a multiple of 4 when it is > 0); every other position gets whatever the cursor gives, so its parity follows the widths of the rectangles placed before it in the row (padded width = w + 2 m, plus the alignment pads), not the parity of the original position. The cursor starts at (0, 0) on every page: the first rectangle of a page with margin 32 and a 4-aligned original x lands at x = 32; with margin 2 and an unaligned x at x = 2. See the behavior LayerAtlasPlacement for the recipe.
open_questions: Why the +3 slack in the fit tests (I: guard against 4-pixel alignment growth). No page-count limit is tested here (the sort key keeps 6 bits of the page index).

name: AudioBus_FindByName
callers: AudioBus_FindMasterOut and the audio set-up code
purpose: Returns the mixer bus number for a bus name, or 0xFFFF when there is none.

behavior.text: when the audio library object exists, has its bus table and a version above 0x1090000, asks the library's own name search.
otherwise compares the name with the first eight entries of AudioBusAndEffectNames (BUS0..BUS7) and returns the matching index; a name equal to the master output name returns 0.
no match returns 0xFFFF.

notes: Name is ours.

name: AudioBus_FindMasterOut
purpose: Returns the bus number of the master output.

behavior.text: looks up the bus named MasterOut with AudioBus_FindByName; when that fails, looks up BUS0.
returns 0xFFFF when neither exists.

notes: Name is ours.

name: AudioDsp_InitCoefficientSets
proto: unsigned long long AudioDsp_InitCoefficientSets(int *config, long long memory)
callers: the audio library DSP creation code (sub_140499C58)
purpose: Initialises the work area of an audio DSP unit and fills its per-channel coefficient pointer slots.

behavior.text: aligns the memory to 16 bytes and clears 0x2208 bytes; lays out one 512-byte buffer per channel (the channel count is config[0]) behind it and two further work blocks.

copies pairs of pointers from the lists of AudioDspCoefficientBlockPointers into the channel slots: with more than eight channels from the sub-lists at the table start and 0xC0 bytes on, otherwise from the sub-lists 0x180 and 0x200 bytes on (the code addresses them as symbol differences, so no 0x180 constant shows in the decompilation; the choice also reads config[4]).
stores a 20-byte block copied from config, then calls a second set-up function (sub_1404A26A4) on the work area and returns its address.

notes: Name is ours. Read partially: the second set-up call and the coefficient meaning are not decoded.

name: BannerWord_Draw
purpose: Builds the gradient quads of one banner word image from its run of sprite cells.

behavior.text: the run is [start, next start) of the banner word range table (0x1406724C0), the cells come from the banner cell table (0x140806A60, 12 bytes each; its address is an image-relative displacement added to the scaled run start, not an absolute operand).
each cell gives four corners from its texture position, size and screen offset; the corner colours come from the banner colour table (0x1408073F4).
with text language 2 the cells are shifted right (one special cell by the narrowest offset of the run, the others by 13).
returns the cell count.

name: BannerWords_FillQuads
purpose: Fills the gradient quads of one banner (a row of word cells) from the legacy banner tables.

behavior.text: start = range table [banner] and count = range table [banner + 1] minus start; the range table (0x1406818F0) and the cell table (0x1408E3950, reached with a RIP-relative address, so it is not an immediate of the body) are copies of the stock banner tables.

for each cell writes the four vertex positions (x from the cell x plus the origin, y, width, height), the texture u / v of the four corners and the four vertex colours taken from the first 16 bytes of the colour table (0x1408E42E4).
for language 2 the cells are shifted by a few pixels (13, or an offset taken from the narrowest cell for one special cell).
returns the number of cells.

notes: Read in full; the same job as the banner word drawer of the battle screens.

name: BarTop_Setup
callees: GUIWidget_FindFirstKind1Component2, UIName_Key, GUINode_FindDescendant, UIName_ReleaseKey, UserSituation_IsMet, sub_1402AC520, sub_1402ABCE4, sub_1402AC8E8
purpose: Sets up the tavern's top menu (rumors, errands): the errand row is open only when situation 3220 holds.

behavior.text: finds the BarTop node of the addon's widget, asks UserSituation_IsMet(3220) and builds the menu with sub_1402AC520 (3 when it holds, else 7, and 23).
when it does not hold it also calls sub_1402ABCE4 on the menu; then selects the first row (sub_1402AC8E8 with text 1840).

notes: Name is ours (was sub_14019F330). I: the 3 / 7 argument and sub_1402ABCE4 lock the errand row ("???" on screen before Chapter 2, owner).

name: Battle_ActorResultLevels
purpose: Applies the acting unit's action result and returns, in four bytes, what the level-up banners need: two result bytes, the new unit level and the new job level.

behavior.text: returns -1 for an empty slot (unit +1 = 0xFF).
clears the two top bytes of qword_1407B07B0, stores the unit index (+444) in dword_14186AFF4 and calls Battle_ApplyActionResult with g_BattleStateGate set to 1 around it.
out[0] = unit +488, out[1] = unit +489; out[2] = the unit level (+41) when byte 6 of qword_1407B07B0 is set, else 0.

out[3] = the level nibble of the unit's job (Job_IdToIndex of the job byte +3; +228 + index / 2, low nibble for an odd index) when byte 7 of qword_1407B07B0 (set by Battle_AwardActorJp when the job level changed) is set, else 0.
the caller passes the unit's label task +462 as `out`, so out[2] is task +464 (read by Battle_ShowUnitLevelUp) and out[3] task +465 (read by Battle_ShowJobLevelUp).

notes: Name is ours.
open_questions: ? the meaning of unit +488 / +489 (an earlier read took them for the two halves of a name id: I).

name: Battle_AddJoinedUnit
purpose: Builds a battle unit record for a party unit that enters the battle (a deployment placement or a mid-battle join) in the first free record of 16..20.

behavior.text: looks for the first record from 16 to 20 whose slot byte (+1) is 0xFF (record +0x1BC is set to the index on the way); when none is free and g_BattleState is 83 it looks in 0..15; otherwise it returns -1 without adding a unit.

for the record found: +1 = the record index, +0x1B5 = 1, UnitWork_BuildFromSaveIndex(record, spawn[0]); then the tile from spawn[1] / spawn[2] and the layer and facing bits of spawn[3] into +0x4F..+0x51.

when Unit_CheckSpawnTile accepts the tile: the shape and palette (Unit_ResolvePreviewShape) into +0x18F / +0x190, the event-unit byte +401 (the marker when it is 1..3, else 120), the look queue count cleared and the look queued (LookQueue_Add), Unit_InitBattleStatusState.
always returns -1 (the caller does not use the value).
five deployment placements took records 16, 17, 18, 19 and 20 in order.

name: Battle_AITurnPrepare
purpose: Fills the per-unit AI table (visibility, HP/MP ratios, flags) and then runs one AI turn.

behavior.text: for all 21 units: `sub_140321740(i)` marks the unit in the AI table at `v1`; units not visible get flag `0x10`.

sets per-unit flags: `v1[1] = 1` for units other than the acting one, `0x20`/`0x40` from `unit[2] & 0x20`,
  `0x01`/`0x02` from HP and MP below half, `0x80` when HP is below 3/4 of max; the low bits of `v1[0]` are cleared
  first.
sets `byte_141872357 |= 1`, `byte_1418716B4 = 1`, `byte_1418716BD = 0` and calls `Battle_AITurnRun`.
returns `-1` when the AI driver aborts (engine state restored), else 0, and clears `byte_141872357` bit 0.

notes: The AI table byte layout (`v1[0..4]`) is a scoring input for `Battle_AITurnRun`; it is rebuilt every AI turn.
open_questions: The meaning of the per-unit bytes `v1[1..4]` used by the scoring code.

name: Battle_AITurnRun
purpose:
Runs one AI trial: applies the candidate action on the preview unit table, lets the turn engine play on (up to 255
steps), scores the outcome and restores the engine state.

behavior.text:
saves `dword_14186B040`, `dword_14186B044` and `dword_1407B0708` before running and restores them on abort
  (`LABEL_53`).
loops `Battle_TurnEngine(0)` up to 255 times (`word_141872594`).
code `0x300` -> `sub_14030A488(slot)` (end-of-turn effects).

code `0x200` -> `sub_14038AB28` validates the pending action; on success it clears `unit[0x61]` bits 1/3,
  `unit[0x1EF]` bits 1/3 and `unit[0x18D] = -1` (the charge resolves); on failure it restores the engine state and
  returns 0.

code `0x100` -> `sub_14038BB68(0, slot)` scores the plan, sets the AI table byte `xmmword_1418724B8+slot = 1`,
  and clears `unit[0x1B8]` so the engine can finish the turn.

the tail of the function scores the simulated outcome (it does not choose; the planner compares the scores): for
  each unit, HP x 128 / max HP, plus `tbl_AiStatusValue[s]` (0x1407B22F0) for each status s of 0..39 the unit has
  (Blindness and Silence scaled by a per-unit AI byte / 4; Confusion, Vampire and Charmed halved under some conditions;
  some statuses counted only under conditions), plus an MP term and 51 for each of 7 words of the unit (+0x1A..) that equals a word the AI stored at qword_141873070 (? their meaning); units of the
  acting side add, the others subtract; the total is kept in the high word of `dword_1418716D0`.
it uses `sub_140279370` (facing/pose) when the chosen action needs one.

notes:
Same engine as the player path; the difference is that the AI never shows the command menu and can run several engine
steps in one frame. `sub_14031F534` prepares the per-unit AI table before this runs.
open_questions: The full scoring formula (it is a large table-driven block) and how the Auto command routes player units here.

name: Battle_ApplyActionResult
purpose:
Applies the pending action result of one unit to that unit: HP/MP damage and healing, stat changes, Brave/Faith
changes, EXP/level changes, status sets/clears and the death check. This is the function that moves live HP.

behavior.text:
`slot` must be 0..20 and `rec[1] != 0xFF`; it sets `qword_14186AF68 = rec` and
  `qword_14186AF70 = rec + 0x1BE` (the result block).
reads `curHP = u16(rec+0x30)`, `maxHP = u16(rec+0x32)`, `curMP = u16(rec+0x34)`, `maxMP = u16(rec+0x36)`.

`newHP = clamp(curHP + i16(result+8) - i16(result+6), 0, maxHP)`, then capped at 999; writes it back to the HP field at
  `0x14030A62F`.

`newMP = clamp(curMP + i16(result+12) - i16(result+10), 0, maxMP)`, capped 999; writes at
  `0x14030A638`.

applies result byte +20 to `+0x3A` Speed (cap 50), +21 to `+0x41` (cap -1 = none), +22 to `+0x38` PA,
  +23 to `+0x39` MA (cap 99), +24 to `+0x2B` Brave (cap 100, sign in bit 7), +25 to `+0x2D` Faith (cap 100).

result +42 is applied to `+0x28` (EXP) as a signed byte (bit 7 = subtract); afterwards `sub_140278AD8` is
  called: at 100 EXP the level byte `+0x29` goes up by one (cap 99) and EXP resets to 0.

result +43 != 0 calls `Battle_AwardActorJp`; result +18 bit 7 = level down, bit 8 = level up (handled
  through `sub_140278C1C`).

result +18 bit 1 = "clear all statuses": clears `+87..91`, `+92..96`, `+97..101`, the countdown area
  `+102..117`, `+495..499`.

`Battle_StatusResolve` + `Status_FilterPendingSets` handle `result+29..33` (sets) and `result+34..38`
  (clears); `+0x1EF..0x1F3` changes are folded into `+0x61..0x65` by `Battle_StatusRefresh`.

when `newHP == 0` and the unit has none of `+97 & 0x60` / `+98 & 1`, it increments `+0x18C`, calls
  `sub_14030C110(2)` and returns -1 when `rec+0x1B4` bit 7 is set (death).
result message ids 440/444/446/450/451/452 select the follow-up (item return, steal, etc.) in the first half.

after the HP/MP write it sets `[rec+0x1F5] = 0xFF` (HP/MP changed flag) and applies the six
  stat/status bytes through `sub_14030C080`; result `[+18]` bit 0x8000 subtracts HP damage from a shield pool (`qword_14186B020`,
  indexed by `(rec[+0x1EE] >> 4) & 3`), bit 0 refills that pool to max HP, bit 3 (0x8) returns an item, bit 0x4000 runs `sub_140271C50`
  (death/stone check); `sub_14030C87C(slot, 0/1)` at `0x14030A518` refreshes status and clears HP on petrify (`+97 & 0x20`).
returns -1 when `rec+0x1B4` is negative (KO/removed target), else 0.
`+0x1B4` bit 7 marks a unit whose 0 HP is final (monster/guest); the exact rule is not decoded.

the after-damage reaction chain is the tail of this function (its helper calls are at 0x14030AB03 and 0x14030AB2C). Unless the formula result's type byte (0x1407B0788) is 7 or sub_14030AF88 answers non-zero, it tests the passive bits of the unit held in g_BattleActingUnit in a fixed order: +0x94 bit 0x80 gives reaction 422, 0x40 gives 423, 0x20 gives 424, 0x02 gives 428; +0x95 bit 0x40 gives 431, 0x20 gives 432, 0x10 gives 433, 0x08 gives 434 (through sub_14030BE68); +0x96 bit 0x40 gives 439 and 0x10 gives 441. The first bit found goes to the Brave-roll helper sub_14030BE18 with that id; only one reaction is chosen.

sub_14030BE18 needs the action block's flag byte +39 bit 7, skips the roll in a simulation, and stores the reaction id at block word +16 and copies the HP result (word +6) to word +40; sub_14030BE68 also needs status byte +0x63 mask 0x01. The executor that runs the chosen reaction is sub_1403095E4 (called from Battle_ResolveAction); see AfterDamageReactionChain and PassiveAbilitiesAreAPerUnitBitMap.

notes:
The other half of the result pipeline is `Battle_ResolveAction` (fills the result block) and
`Battle_StatusApply` (status side). `Battle_ApplyActionResult` must run after both.
open_questions:
What `+0x1B4` bit 7 means exactly, and whether the `+0x1B4` bit 6 "no-target" rule is the guest/ally rule.
- The six `sub_14030C080` destinations (+0x2B, +0x2D, +0x38, +0x39, +0x3A, +0x41) beyond the ones named above, and the owner of the shield pool `qword_14186B020`.

name: Battle_AwardActorJp
purpose: Gives the acting battle unit its JP for the current job and reports whether its job level changed (for the level-up message).

behavior.text: the unit is the battle record in `qword_14186AF68`; its job index comes from Job_IdToIndex(unit +3).
reads the level byte before, calls Unit_AwardJobJp(unit +444, JP from +489, team bits of +494, index), reads the level byte after.
when the nibble of the job differs, sets the top byte of `qword_1407B07B0` to 1 (the 'job level up' flag of the result).

open_questions: I: the JP amount at +489 is computed by the action code before this call (not traced).

name: Battle_AwardUnitJp
callees: sub_1402175F8, SceneVar_Read, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_140278AD8, Job_IdToIndex, Unit_AwardJobJp
purpose: Awards job JP to a battle unit after an action: it validates the unit, resolves its job index and JP amount, applies the award and reports the amount.

behavior.text: the first argument is the unit slot and the second a pointer that receives the awarded JP; it is zeroed at entry.
a unit marker of 0xFF, unit +0x61 bit 0x60 or unit +0x62 bit 0x81 makes it return 0 without an award.
job ids 0xA1 and 0xA4 are excluded before the award (the second is reached as 0xA1+3); there is no further job-specific special case.
the job index comes from Job_IdToIndex and the award goes through Unit_AwardJobJp.
the JP row is resolved through the NXD registry and table lookups, and SceneVar_Read supplies a multiplier.
sub_1402175F8 is called first as a gate and sub_140278AD8 computes a level-derived value.
it returns 1 when JP was awarded and 0 otherwise.
this is the battle end/action award path, because it runs from the battle result notifier and writes the per-job totals.
the exact JP formula; the NXD row fields and the multiplier were not decoded here.

notes: Whole function read (728 bytes). The writers it calls are the job-state writers.

name: Battle_BuildEntryUnits
callers: BattleLoad_StepFresh (battle load state 5, after state 4 set the key from scene variable 50), sub_14030476C
purpose: Builds the battle units of the current battle from its 16 entries: fetches the entry block, lets the battle's OverrideEntryData rows overwrite the entries, then places the units.

behavior.text: entries = Battle_GetEntryBlock(); nothing happens (returns 0) when that is null.
zeroes a 64-byte array (one dword per entry) and an array of 16 row pointers on its stack.
when the dword at 0x1407D453C is not 0: OverrideEntry_LoadBattleEntries(g_BattleEntrySource key dword, entries, dwords, rows), which fills the entry block in place.
then Battle_PlaceEntryUnits(entries, ?, dwords, rows) and sub_1402F3A04(g_BattleEntrySource +8, the entry base pointer); returns 0.

notes: Replaces the older reference sheet sub_14030428C, which named OverrideEntry_LoadBattleEntries as the first call and a language id as its argument; the first call is Battle_GetEntryBlock and the argument is the battle key.
open_questions: ? what sub_1402F3A04 does with the entry base pointer; ? the second argument of Battle_PlaceEntryUnits (rdx is not set here).

name: Battle_BuildRosterTeam
purpose:
Fills the live 21-slot battle unit table (`g_BattleUnitTable`, `0x141853CE0`, stride 512) from a 5-entry spawn
list, one team at a time. This is the function that places units on the two sides.

behavior.text:
`spawnList` holds 5 entries of 8 bytes; byte 0 of each entry is a `g_UnitSaveData` index (0xFF = no unit).
  List bytes 1, 2 and 3 are copied to the record's `+79` (tile X), `+80` (tile Y) and `+81` (facing in bits
  0..3, bits 4..6 kept, bit 7 preserved).

the slot cursor starts at **16** when `a2 == 0` and at **0** when `a2 != 0`; which suggests player-side units at
  16..20 and enemies at 0..4 on the generic sortie path; **contradicted live** for the first battle (player side slots 0..4 and others, enemies 5..9, 12, 13,
  slots 16..20 empty): scripted battles place units through the event tasks. Use the team byte, not the slot.
an empty entry sets `rec[0x1B5] = 0xFF` and `rec[1] = 0xFF`.

`a2 != 0` additionally sets the word at `+4 = 0x1801` and the team/type byte `+0x1EE = 0x18`
  (`0x140270E59`), i.e. team bits 4..5 = 1 (enemy).

when the spawn entry's byte 3 bit 4 is clear, the unit is registered with `sub_1403041A4(x, y, layer,
  facing, shape, palette, 255, rec, 0)` and reset with `sub_140278E0C(rec, 1)`; bit 4 set leaves
  `rec[0x1B5] = 0`.
for `a2 != 0` only, slots 5..15 are cleared (`+0x1B5 = 0`, `+1 = 0xFF`, `+0x1B4 = 0xFF`).
the failing `sub_140271178` test rejects a unit that cannot be built (e.g. an empty/corrupt save slot).

notes:
This is the authoritative statement that the table is the live battle table, not a preview: it writes the same
records the action resolver reads, and it is called from the battle scene task (phase 8), not from a menu.
open_questions: What spawn-list byte 3 bit 4 means (a unit that is placed but not present?), and why player units start at 16.

name: Battle_CommandTask
purpose:
The per-frame player battle command task: advances the turn engine, claims the active unit, and puts up the command
menu (Move / Abilities / Wait / Status) or hands the unit to the AI.

behavior.text:
IDA's name `_isctype_l` is a wrong FLIRT match (the body is battle code, not CRT); it is the only caller of
  `Battle_TurnStep`.
`sub_140202930()` non-zero short-circuits with menu mode `48` (0x30) (`0x140202B3B`).

otherwise it calls `Battle_TurnStep`, copies `qword_141871698` to `qword_14184A9B0`, resets the panel state and
  looks up the current unit node with `sub_1402607C0`; the node's `+8` byte becomes `dword_140C6AD8C`.

reads the unit's BWorkHolder at `BattleControl + 0x88*slot` (`0x140202D44`/`0x140202D4B`) and calls its voice
  controller when `+0x80` is non-zero.

when the engine result was `0x100` and the unit is a player unit, it runs `sub_140202800`, resets the held-key
  state and shows the command menu: `dword_140C6B1CC = 39` (`0x140202DB3`), `dword_140D3A864 = 1`
  (`0x140202DD5`).

the post-command handler `sub_14020AD64` calls the AI entry `sub_14031F130` when the unit has idled for more
  than 30 frames (`*(uint16*)(node+12) > 0x1E`) and `*(node+466) == 0` (`0x14020ADC6`) — the Auto / idle path (I).
`dword_140D3A868` (last engine code) is only written by this path, in `Battle_TurnStep`.

notes: This is the function to watch for "the player is being asked to choose": menu mode 39 plus `dword_140D3A864 = 1`.
open_questions:
What `sub_140202930`'s mode 4 (`dword_141853C08 == 4`) means; the exact Auto toggle that makes a player unit take the
`sub_14031F130` branch.

name: Battle_GetEntryBlock
purpose: The 16 spawn entries (40 bytes each, 640 bytes) of the current battle inside the loaded entry data.

behavior.text: returns null when the key dword of g_BattleEntrySource is 0 or the dword at 0x141856AB4 is not 0.
otherwise the entry base pointer (g_BattleEntrySource +8) + 640 x n, where n is the key minus 512 for keys of 512 or more, else the key reduced below 128 (minus 128, 256 or 384).

notes: I: the entry data is the battle placement data (ENTD in the original game) loaded behind g_BattleEntrySource +8; its file and loader were not traced.

name: Battle_Init
purpose: Allocates and resets the battle singletons when a battle starts: BattleControl, post-battle calculator, a 3008-byte battle object, the map-view camera manager, markers and the command menu.

behavior.text: if `qword_143CD9EF0` (BattleControl) is null, allocates 693712 (0xA95D0) bytes, zeroes it, calls `sub_1401E9B1C` and `sub_1401E9E10`, and stores the pointer at 0x143CD9EF0.
if `qword_143CDA750` is null, allocates 3400 bytes, sets vtable `PostBattleCalc_140713F28`, zeroes 106 4-qword records, stores at 0x143CDA750 and calls `sub_1401F92A8`.

if `qword_143CDA740` is null, allocates 3008 bytes and initializes it with `sub_1401EE21C`; sets `+1172=1`, `+1176=1`, byte `+1892 = byte_140C757AA`, `+1928 = dword_140D40548`, word `+1893=257`, `+1932=90`, then `sub_1401EE518`.

resets `word_1408081E2 = word_140808782 = 170`, `dword_142FEC534 = 1`, `word_142FEF6CC = 0`, `dword_140D4058C/90 = 0`; calls `sub_1401EBB48(qword_143CDA080)` (EnhancedMarkingUtility) and zeroes 0x51E0 bytes at `qword_143CDA388+8`.

fills the turn list with 0xFF (36 bytes at 0x140D40490 in 4-byte steps), calls `sub_1402089FC`, sets `byte_140D40906 = 10`, `dword_1407DC2BC = 1`, sets BattleControl `+693388 = -1`, `+693395 = 0`, zeroes 21 52-byte state records at `+691969`, zeroes 0xA0 bytes at `+693504`, calls `sub_1401EB468`.

clears the 16-bit field at offset 689110 of BattleControl, then **resets the command menu** by calling the menu-windows reset (`sub_140101370`) on the battle menu agent, which is the ninth entry (offset 64) of the UI agent manager's agent vector (`qword_143CD9DA8`, vector at +16).
sets `g_CharaRenderMgr + 13502 = 0`, zeroes `xmmword_140D4057C`, `qword_140D40570`, `dword_140D40578/98/A4`.

notes: This is the best single breakpoint for "a battle just started": it runs once per battle, right before the command menu agent is reset. Field meanings of the camera manager defaults are `?`.

name: Battle_InitScene
callees: sub_1402C60E4, SceneTask_Terminate, sub_1402F7E90, Resource_GetSlotObject, sub_1402C4D1C, sub_1401DB4E4, sub_1401442FC, sub_1402B20C0, sub_140103C50, sub_1402CBCA0, sub_1400EB3AC, sub_1400EB408, sub_140143EA8, UIName_Key, GUINode_FindDescendant, UIName_ReleaseKey, GUINode_StopState, GUINode_PlayStateAtFrame, sub_1400F4BCC, SceneTask_WaitFrame, GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState, sub_1401FA5F0, sub_140226208, sub_140220E5C, sub_1402C83C0, sub_1402C7E2C, GUINode_FindPartByName, sub_1401440FC, sub_140144974, sub_1400FC6D8, Input_TestAction, sub_1400F5B0C, UIAgentCursor_Show, sub_14013F634, sub_1402C8440
purpose: The battle scene initialiser started by event opcode 0x78 mode 7: it builds the battle UI, places the units and their markers, shows the cursor and waits for the battle to end.

behavior.text: the event opcode 0x78 dispatcher starts this body for mode 7, the battle-start mode.
it copies the battle message/left-panel state and initialises the battle scene objects through sub_1402C60E4 and sub_1402C4D1C.
the UI nodes it drives are named Select, ShowSelectButton, HideSelectButton, ShowUnitInfo, Collision00, ButtonSelect01 and ButtonSelect02.
the unit markers and their sprites are created through the CharaRender helpers and the per-unit preview records.
the cursor is shown with UIAgentCursor_Show and the scene waits with SceneTask_WaitFrame.
it polls Input_TestAction for the battle buttons and reads the merged button mask.
the function has one caller, the opcode 0x78 mode dispatcher, and ends with SceneTask_Terminate.
this is the battle init rather than a generic scene, because the node names are the battle select button and the unit info panel and the caller is the battle mode.
what sub_1402C8440 and sub_1402C83C0 build after the units are placed; neither was decoded.

notes: Whole function read (5982 bytes). The node names are string operands; the battle-init role is also the one the battle UI notes give.

name: Battle_IsTileOccupied
proto: int Battle_IsTileOccupied(int x, int y, int layer, int flags)
purpose: Tests a map tile for the targeting cursor: bounds, terrain passability, the unit standing there and the large-monster exception for jobs 94..96.

behavior.text: the arguments are x in ecx, y in edx, layer in r8d and a flag byte in r9b; negative x or y is rejected.
x is bounded by the map width byte at 0x140C6AD6A and y by the height byte at 0x140C6AD6B; a layer above 1 is rejected.
the cell is indexed as x plus y times width plus layer times 0x100 (a shl by 8) and read from the tile block at 0x140D8DCB0 with a stride of eight bytes.
cell byte +6 bits 0 and 1 must be clear for the tile to be usable.
when the flag byte has bit 2, the cell terrain byte +3 must be below 0x20 and its low five bits at most 2.

it walks the 21 unit records with a stride of 0x200 and returns the slot index of a live unit whose x, y and layer match the tile; the flag byte decides which units can match (bits 0x40, 0x01 and 0x10 test three consecutive marker bytes starting at unit +0x61).
for a job 94..96 unit (job byte +3) Unit_HasStatusGroup(unit, 0xA) is consulted, and a unit that has that group is skipped.
the returns are -2 for a rejected tile, -1 when no unit matches, and on a match the slot index, or byte +0x1B4 masked to 0x1F when that byte is 0x80 or above.
the job 94..96 branch is a monster-specific exemption, which is why this function appears in the monster-test census.
what status group 0xA contains; the mask table was not decoded here.

notes: Whole function read (351 bytes). The map dimensions and tile stride come from the cursor-range study; the monster test is in this body.

name: Battle_JoinUnitAndLoad
purpose: The mid-battle join: runs Battle_AddJoinedUnit, then the look loader once per frame until it returns 0.

behavior.text: the loader is CharaPalette_ReloadForShape.

name: Battle_MenuClose
purpose: Closes the command menu for the acting unit.

behavior.text: node = `sub_140260824(dword_140C6AFB8, dword_140C6ADAC, dword_140C6AFBC)`; menuId = `sub_14030DBAC(node->subrecord byte +444)`.
`sub_1401015FC(agent, menuId, -1)` hides the page.
if the command addon (`agent+72`) is present and shown, clears addon byte `+5629` and calls `sub_140155FE8(addon, 0)`.
the page hide path (`sub_140154308`) sets addon `+5624 = -1`, so both "shown" and "page" go to their idle values.

notes: Called when a command is confirmed (the owner's observation: choosing Move hides the menu and the glove). After this, tile selection runs with the command menu closed. `+5629` is an internal latch only; the visible selected row is `addon+1120` (radio menu at +840), and this function's hide path clears it to -1.
open_questions: ? whether a cancel path uses the same function or `sub_1401568EC`.

name: Battle_MenuHidePage
purpose: Hides the page for a menu id (or all six pages when `menuId == -1`).

behavior.text: `menuId == -1`: for each of the six `BattleMenu01..06` nodes, stops all states, plays `Uncheck` on each `RadioButton01..06` at frame -1, then plays `Hide` at `frame`.

otherwise resolves the page with `sub_1401542AC(addon, menuId)`, stops its states, and if the addon is shown (`sub_1400F5828(addon+48, 12, 0, 0)`) calls `sub_140155E04(addon, menuId, -1)`; plays `Hide` at `frame`.

clears `addon+856`, `+1120 = -1` (`0x1401545DD`), `+1124 = -1` (`0x1401545E4`), word `+1128 = 0`, byte `+1130 = 0`, `+1136 = -1` and `+5624 = -1`. The `+1120..+1136` block is the embedded `UIGadgetFFTORadioButtonMenu` at `+840` (its +16 count, +280 selected, +284 hover, +288 flags, +296 page id).

notes: The unconditional `+5624 = -1` is why the page field is the reliable "no page" signal.
open_questions: ? the fields at +856..+1136 (some other menu's state).

name: Battle_MenuOpen
purpose: Opens the command menu for the acting unit.

behavior.text: node = `sub_140260824(dword_140C6AFB8, dword_140C6ADAC, dword_140C6AFBC)` (the unit at the current battle position).
the menu id comes from `sub_14030DBAC` applied to the byte at offset 444 of the unit node's sub-record (preview index -> command/menu id).
`sub_1401015FC(agent, menuId, 0)` shows the menu page; the agent is the ninth entry (offset 64) of the UI agent manager's agent vector (`qword_143CD9DA8`, vector at +16).
if the command addon (`agent+72`) is present and its `+48` node is "shown" (`sub_1400F5828(+48, 12, 0, 0)`), sets addon `+5629 = 1` and calls `sub_140156074(addon, 0)`.

notes: Paired with `Battle_MenuClose` (0x1402100F4). The menu id -> page mapping is in `Battle_MenuPageOfCommand` (0x140154248); the page builder is `Battle_MenuShowPage` (0x140154624). The live selected command row is `addon+1120` (embedded radio menu at +840, field +280); `+5629` is an internal latch and did not match the live menu (Legate). For "command menu up", read the radio menu entry count at `addon+856` (non-zero) and `addon+1120` (>= 0).
open_questions: ? what `dword_140C6AFB8/AC/BC` are (a tile coordinate triple, I); ? `sub_140156074`'s role.

name: Battle_MenuPageOfCommand
proto: unsigned int sub_140154248(UIAddonFFTOBattleCommand *addon, unsigned int menuId)
purpose: Maps a battle command/menu id to one of the six `BattleMenu` page numbers.

behavior.text: `menuId == 54` -> 1; every other value -> 0.

notes: `sub_1401542AC` uses `page-1` to index addon `+96..+136` (the six `BattleMenu0N` nodes), so 0 means "no page". The special ids 46..49 come from `sub_14030DBAC` for units with a negative command-row byte.

name: Battle_MenuShowPage
purpose: Shows one of the six command-menu pages and binds its radio buttons, icon and title.

behavior.text: writes `addon+5624 = pageId` (the page request), hides all six `BattleMenu01..06` nodes (stop states, play `Hide` at frame -1), then resolves the page node with `sub_1401542AC(addon, pageId)`.
for the page, finds parts `RadioButton01..06` (both as direct parts and as descendants) and `Icon`, and plays the `Hide`/`Active` states as appropriate.

clears the embedded `UIGadgetFFTORadioButtonMenu` at +840 when switching pages: entry count `+856 = 0` (`0x140155D2E`), selected `+1120 = -1` (`0x140155D42`), hover `+1124 = -1` (`0x140155D49`), flags `+1128/+1130 = 0`, and stores the applied page id at `+1136` (`0x140155D58`).

reads the acting unit's preview record: `index = SHIWORD(dword_1407DCF98)`; if `index <= 20`, record = `g_BattleUnitTable + 512*index`; it tests bit 8 of record byte +101 to choose the title/flag strings (218 or 3010, dependent on `+160`).

stores the page's title string ids into the page's `TextTitle` (3802 / 2721 at pseudocode lines 217 and 235) and sets the widget ids of `ActionMenu` and `ActionList` into `g_CharaRenderMgr+44504/+44508`.
ends with `sub_140153AD8(addon)` when the page is missing.

notes: The function is 1125 pseudocode lines, mostly repeated node binding. The state a reader needs is the radio-menu reset (`+856` count, `+1120` selected) and the applied page id (`+1136`); the rest is presentation. `+5624` is the request id and did not match the live visible menu.

name: Battle_MoveRange_Build
callers: sub_140203B80 (entering Move), sub_1400D94F8 (the per-frame tile-marking reconcile), sub_14031F92C (AI target range)
purpose: Builds the move range of one unit: sets up the scratch block, seeds the unit's tile with its Move budget, spreads the budget tile by tile and jump by jump, then commits the tiles the unit can stop on. Returns their number.

behavior.text: returns -1 when the slot's unit record is empty (byte +1 is 0xFF).
calls Battle_MoveRangeSetup(slot), then Battle_MoveRange_InitTiles(1).
movement mode 1 (Teleport): writes 1 into budget byte 0 of all 512 range-mark records and skips the spread.

otherwise up to Move passes (scratch byte +6); a pass stops the loop when the 'pending' byte (0x1418827FA) is 0, clears it, then scans layer 0 then layer 1, each by rows (y, then x): for every tile whose flag byte has bit 0x01 it clears the bit, points the scratch at the tile and its mark record, and calls Battle_MoveRange_Expand, then Battle_MoveRange_ExpandJump unless the no-jump byte (scratch byte 0x14188261D) is set; after the first processed tile the direction count goes back to 8.
ends with Battle_MoveRange_Commit, copies the slot to dword_140808DF4, sets dword_1437414A4 = 1 and returns the 16-bit count g_MoveRangeTileCount.

a tile reached later in the scan order than the tile that reached it is processed in the same pass, an earlier one in the next pass; the pass limit equals Move, the longest possible path, so it does not cut a range short (the eight captures give the same result with unlimited passes).

notes: All state is global (the scratch block at 0x141882600, g_MoveTileFlags, g_BattleRangeMarks), so a second build for another unit overwrites it; only the committed tile bits stay.
open_questions: ? Which of the three callers runs when the cursor hovers another unit (the red squares of an enemy's range).

name: Battle_MoveRange_CeilingAbove
proto: uint8 Battle_MoveRange_CeilingAbove(int x, int y, uint8 edgeShift, uint8 above)
purpose: The lowest underside, over both map layers of one column, that lies above a given height on one edge; 127 when there is none.

behavior.text: for layer 0 and layer 1 of (x, y), skipping records with byte +6 bit 0x01: underside = 2 * (height - thickness) + slope * ((corner byte >> edgeShift) & 3), thickness = tile byte +5 low 5 bits; keeps the smallest value above the given height.
this is the bridge rule: a unit under a layer-1 tile needs its body to fit below that tile's underside, and a unit on it has nothing above.

open_questions: ? Not exercised by the captures: both maps have every layer-1 record flagged unusable (byte +6 = 1) and thickness 0.

name: Battle_MoveRange_CheckMount
purpose: For a target tile holding a mountable ally: records in the tile's mark byte 3 the budget with which the unit could get onto the mount.

behavior.text: nothing unless the target headroom is at least exit height + body and the budget left (source budget - extraCost - 1) is non-zero and not below the source's mark byte 3.

scans heights from max(the mount's base, the target's enter height + 2 * depth) up to base + the mount's body: stops when either headroom is below height + body; a height above the exit height needs extraCost 0 and a climb within 2 * Jump; a height at or below needs a drop within 2 * Jump. The first height that passes stores the budget into mark byte 3 when larger.

notes: Battle_MoveRange_Commit lights a tile with mark byte 3 set when the acting unit can ride.
open_questions: ? Not covered by a capture (no chocobo ally).

name: Battle_MoveRange_CheckSource
purpose: Prepares leaving the current tile in one direction: the height of the edge being left, the headroom above it and the budget record to spend from; returns non-zero when the tile cannot be left that way.

behavior.text: ground case (direction index below 4): exit height = height * 2 + slope * ((corner byte >> shift of the edge left) & 3); the same with the opposite edge's shift gives the back height; their difference is stored as the slope along the step.
headroom = Battle_MoveRange_CeilingAbove(x, y, edge shift, exit height).
returns 3 when the difference is 0 or more and the tile's flag has 0x40 (a steep tile can only be left downhill).

when the tile has water (byte +3 >= 0x20) and the stored movement flags (scratch byte 0x14188261C) have bit 7 or bit 6 (one test of both, mask 0xC0), the exit height rises by 2 * depth, minus 2 when bit 6 (0x40) is set.
the budget record is the tile's own mark record; returns 4 when its budget is below 2, else 0.

unit case (index 4 and above): the blocker entry is the tile's mark byte 2. Index below 8: returns 2 unless the tile flag has 0x08, exit height = the entry's top. Index 8 and above: exit height = the entry's base + (index >> 2) - 2, returns 1 when that is below the tile's edge height. Headroom is taken above exit height - 1 and the budget record is mark record 512 + the entry's index.

notes: Heights are in half-steps: a height step is 2, a slope unit is 1 per corner value.
open_questions: ? The unit case is not covered by any capture (it needs a unit with flag 0x08 on its tile, or a mounted start).

name: Battle_MoveRange_CheckStep
purpose: Tests one target of a step or jump (variant bit 0 = map layer, variant >= 2 = onto the unit standing there) and, when the unit can get there with a better budget, stores the budget and flags the tile as frontier.

behavior.text: ground variants need tile flag 0x10 (standable); unit variants need 0x28, take the unit's top as the height, call Battle_MoveRange_CheckMount when the flag has 0x20 and then stop unless it has 0x08.

ground: enter height = height * 2 + slope * corner value of the edge entered; the far edge the same with the other shift; a positive rise far - enter on a tile with flag 0x40 is refused (no walking up a steep tile).

headroom: refused when the lowest underside above the enter height (Battle_MoveRange_CeilingAbove on the target) is below exit height + body, when the source headroom is below enter height + body, or when the target one is below enter height + body. Body = scratch byte 0x14188261B (6 half-steps, 4 as Toad or Chicken, 8 with the float ability, +2 per rider).

ground: the compared level is enter height + 2 * the target's depth. Level <= exit height is a drop of exit - level; a higher level is a climb and is refused when extraCost is not 0 (no jumping upward across a gap).
refused when the drop or climb is above 2 * Jump (scratch byte 0x141882602).

budget left = source budget - terrain cost of the target (g_MoveTerrainCost by tile byte +0 low 6 bits) - extraCost; unit variants use cost 1. Refused when below 1, when below the target's stored budget, or when equal and the path's largest climb (kept in mark byte 4; 0 in Fly mode) is not smaller.
stores budget and climb byte; when the budget is above 1 sets tile flag 0x01 and raises the pending byte.
return codes 1..17 name the refusing test; 0 = stored.

notes: A terrain cost of 0xFF makes the budget negative, which is how forbidden terrain is refused. Captures: height limit exact to the half-step on both sides, water cost 2, extra cost per jumped tile, no upward jump, enemies block (no 0x10 on their tiles), allies passable.
open_questions: ? The depth is added to the target but to the source only with a water ability; not exercised by the captures (their water is depth 1 next to depth 1 or out of reach).

name: Battle_MoveRange_Commit
purpose: Turns the budgets into the lit set: decides for each of the 512 tiles whether the unit can stop there, counts them and writes the result to the tile table (bit 0x20 of tile byte +5) or to the marking table.

behavior.text: first clears flag 0x10 on the tile of every unit with status byte +0x61 bit 0x20 or 0x04 (KO, Jumping): nobody stops there.
for every tile: clears its mark (tile byte +5 bit 0x20 when the battle manager's dword +6536 is 15, else state bit dword +6536 of the manager's marking table through sub_1400D9C44).
the start tile is never lit.
Teleport mode: a tile with flag 0x20 is lit when the unit can ride (scratch byte 0x141882616). Any mode: a tile with mark byte 3 set is lit when the unit can ride.

otherwise all of: slope <= 2 or no flag 0x02; budget byte non-zero; slope <= 3; tile byte +6 bit 7 clear (a sign test); terrain not 28; depth 0, or a deeper tile when scratch byte 0x141882614 is clear and, for depth 3, scratch byte 0x141882612 is clear and, for depth 4 and more, scratch byte 0x141882613 is clear; terrain not 18 unless scratch byte 0x141882625 is set; tile byte +6 bit 0x02 clear; flag 0x10; and when occupied (0x04) flag 0x20 and the unit can ride.
a lit tile increments g_MoveRangeTileCount and gets its mark set the same two ways.
the routine writes no other tile byte: bits 0x40 and 0x80 of byte +5 belong to the target and action code.

notes: Captures: tile byte +5 bit 0x20 of both layers equals this routine's result in all eight; the tiles of KO units are passed but not lit (one capture depends on it).
open_questions: ? Which callers run with the manager dword +6536 other than 15 (then the tile bits keep an older range).

name: Battle_MoveRange_Expand
callees: Battle_MoveRange_OutOfBounds, Battle_MoveRange_CheckSource, Battle_MoveRange_CheckStep, the four direction setters sub_14027BA20 / sub_14027BA34 / sub_14027BA48 / sub_14027BA68 (through a table)
purpose: Spreads the budget from the current frontier tile to its four neighbours.

behavior.text: caches the tile's height * 2, slope (byte +3 low 5 bits) and corner byte (+4) in the scratch.

loops the direction count (8, or 36 from a mounted start): direction = index mod 4 in the order +x, +y, -x, -y (four small setters store the step and two corner shifts: 0 / 2, 6 / 4, 2 / 0, 4 / 6 for the edge left / the edge entered); indices 4 and above set the 'from a unit' byte.

skips the direction when the neighbour is off the map (Battle_MoveRange_OutOfBounds) or Battle_MoveRange_CheckSource returns non-zero; otherwise calls Battle_MoveRange_CheckStep for the four variants 0..3 with extra cost 0.

name: Battle_MoveRange_ExpandJump
callees: Battle_MoveRange_CheckSource, Battle_MoveRange_OutOfBounds, Battle_MoveRange_GapBlocked, Battle_MoveRange_CheckStep, the four direction setters (through a table)
purpose: Spreads the budget from the current frontier tile by horizontal jumps: in each of the four straight lines, over 1 up to Jump / 2 tiles.

behavior.text: same direction loop as Battle_MoveRange_Expand; a direction is tried only when Battle_MoveRange_CheckSource returns 0.

for n = 1 .. horizontal jump (scratch byte 0x141882605): stops when the source budget - n is below 2, when the tile n steps away is off the map, or when Battle_MoveRange_GapBlocked says that column blocks the jump at the height the unit leaves from; then takes the tile n + 1 steps away, stops when it is off the map, and calls Battle_MoveRange_CheckStep for the four variants with extra cost n.
so every tile jumped over must itself be clear, in order; a blocked column ends the whole line.
Battle_MoveRange_Build does not call it when the no-jump byte is set (Fly and Teleport).

notes: Captures: with Jump 3 (horizontal jump 1) the lit sets need this routine in three of eight captures, and a jump of 2 would light too much in two.

name: Battle_MoveRange_GapBlocked
proto: bool Battle_MoveRange_GapBlocked(int columnIndex, uint8 shiftA, uint8 shiftB, uint8 height)
purpose: Whether a column stops a horizontal jump that passes over it at a given height: anything (tile body or enemy) overlapping the band from the height to height + body blocks, and so does a column that is entirely above.

behavior.text: tests four things: the layer-0 tile, the unit on it, the layer-1 tile, the unit on it.

tile: the blocked flag (bit 7, a sign test) blocks only when the tile is also occupied, otherwise it is ignored; else bottom = the lower of its two edge heights along the jump - 2 * thickness, top = the higher edge + 2 * depth.
unit: only an occupied tile without flag 0x08 whose blocker is of the other side counts; it blocks when its base + 3 lies strictly inside the band; else bottom = its base, top = its top.
blocks when bottom or top lies strictly inside (height, height + body), or when the band is inside [bottom, top].
after the four tests, blocks when the lowest bottom seen is above the height.
a gap is a column whose top is at or below the height the unit jumps from; a wall or a higher floor ends the jump line, an enemy standing in the gap too, an ally does not.

notes: Captures: without this test three of eight lit sets are wrong.

name: Battle_MoveRange_InitTiles
purpose: Clears the range marks, gives every tile its movement flag byte (slope, standable, blocked), stamps the other units onto their tiles and seeds the unit's own tile with Move + 1.

behavior.text: for each of 528 mark records: bytes 1 and 2 = 0; with mode bit 0 also byte 0 = 0, byte 3 = 0, byte 4 = 0xFF. The last 16 records belong to the 16 blocker entries.

tile flag byte for each of the 512 tiles: 2 when (tile byte +4 & 5) is 1 or 4, and 0x42 when the slope (byte +3 low 5 bits) is also 3 or more; otherwise 0x40 when the slope is above the unit's Jump (scratch byte 0x141882604), else 0.

bit 0x10 (standable) is added when tile byte +6 has neither bit 0x01 nor 0x02 and: the depth (byte +3 >> 5) is 0; or the no-water byte (scratch byte 0x141882611) is 0 and the depth is below 4; or the no-water byte is 0 and the no-deep byte (scratch byte 0x141882613) is 0.
tile byte +6 bit 0x01 adds flag 0x80; in movement mode 0 (Fly) a tile with byte +6 bit 0x02 whose terrain is not 63 gets 0x10.

unless mode is 3, each blocker entry stamps its tile (x + width * y + 256 * layer): mark byte 2 = the entry's index, flag 0x04 (occupied). An entry of the other side (id bit 0x40) loses 0x10 and 0x20 and gets 0x08 only in movement mode 0. An entry of the own side loses 0x08, gets 0x08 back from bit 7 of the entry's layer byte (the unit's facing-byte bit 6, copied by Battle_MoveRangeSetup) unless the acting unit has that bit, and gets 0x20 unless its id has bit 0x20 (0x20 on the tile = a mount the acting unit may take).
a blocker whose unit record byte +0 is 73 turns its tile into blocked: bits 0x10 and 0x80 of the old flags are dropped and 0x80 is set (the mask is built in a register).

mode 1: the start tile (x + 256 * layer + width * y of the scratch) gets budget Move + 1, climb byte 0, flag 0x01, and the pending byte = Move + 1; the direction count is 8 and the variant count 4. When the start tile has flag 0x20 the direction count is 36 and the mount's own mark record (512 + its index) is seeded too.
with mode bit 0 the tile count g_MoveRangeTileCount is zeroed.

notes: Flag bits of g_MoveTileFlags: 0x01 frontier, 0x02 one-axis slope, 0x04 occupied, 0x08 a unit that can be stepped onto, 0x10 standable, 0x20 mountable ally, 0x40 steep, 0x80 blocked.
open_questions: ? What unit record byte +0 == 73 is. ? What 0x08 on a same-side tile does in the expansion (I: the tile cannot be entered or crossed, the flag an enemy's tile gets in movement mode 0). V: bit 6 of unit byte +81 is the JobTable blocks-allies bit (row +25 bit 7), copied to the blocker's layer byte bit 7 by Battle_MoveRangeSetup.

name: Battle_MoveRange_OutOfBounds
purpose: True when the target coordinates in the scratch (two signed words) are outside the map.

behavior.text: true when x or y is negative, x is not below the width (scratch byte 0x141882618) or y not below the height (scratch byte 0x141882619).

name: Battle_MoveRange_WeatherCost
purpose: The movement cost of the weather-dependent terrains: 1, 2 or 3 from event variable 35 and two bits of dword_140D3A830.

behavior.text: v = SceneVar_Read(35); returns 1 when dword_140D3A830 bit 1 is set or v is below 2.
adds 3 to v when dword_140D3A830 bit 0 is set; then returns 1 for v below 3 or v = 5, 2 for v = 3 or 6, else 3.
