name: Battle_MoveRangeSetup
purpose: Prepares the globals the move-range expansion reads: it copies the acting unit move, jump, stance and status data into the range scratch block and fills the sixteen-entry blocker table.

behavior.text: the argument is a battle unit slot; the unit record is the 0x200-byte entry at 0x141853CE0 plus slot times 0x200 (base by lea, stride by shl 9).
it writes the slot to the range scratch byte and stores the constant 0x10100 and a zero byte beside it before reading the unit.
unit bytes +0x4F, +0x50 and +0x51 are copied to the scratch block.
the move and jump values are read from the unit fields at +0x42 and +0x43, per the move-range study.

the blocker table (g_MoveBlockers, 16 entries of 7 bytes, the write pointer starts at 0x141882682) is filled from the unit table: every unit that is present, has none of status byte +0x61 bits 0x64 (Crystal, KO, Jumping) nor +0x62 bit 0x01 (Chest) and is not the acting unit gets an entry (record MoveBlockerRecord): tile, layer, id with the other-side bit 0x40 and the not-a-mount bit 0x20, body height, base and top height.

a job in the 94..96 range decides mounts, not size: the acting unit's scratch byte +0x15 is 1 when its job is 94..96 and Unit_HasStatusGroup(unit, 10) is false; another unit of such a job with no group-10 status and a zero mount byte gets no bit 0x20 in its id (a mount the acting unit may take).
Unit_HasStatusGroup is called only with group 10; Battle_MoveRange_WeatherCost (sub_14027AD6C) returns the cost 1..3 used for the terrain-cost entries that are 0 in the chosen set.

movement mode, body height, the water bytes and the terrain costs are derived from the unit word at +0x9C (its high byte is +0x9D, read as one word), byte +0x9E and status byte +0x63 as listed on the record MoveRangeScratch; Jump is capped at 7 and Move at 124.
a unit whose mount byte (+0x1B4) has bit 7 and names the acting slot is skipped and adds 2 to the acting unit's body height.
this is the setup half of the move-range builder; the expansion itself is Battle_MoveRange_Build.

notes: Whole function read (1336 bytes). The range scratch globals and the blocker table are the ones the C5 cursor/range study names. Revised 2026-11-09 with the full read: the earlier lines about a large-monster bit and about sub_14027AD6C clearing state were wrong.

name: Battle_PlaceEntryUnits
callees: Unit_BuildFromRecord, Unit_ResolvePreviewShape, sub_140278E0C, sub_140271178, sub_140271844, LookQueue_Add, SceneVar_Read
purpose: Builds battle unit i (g_PreviewUnitTable + 512 x i) from entry i for the 16 entries of a battle, decides who is placed and queues each placed unit's look.

behavior.text: first stores into byte_140D405AB the highest byte +29 of the save records in use (+1 not 0xFF), capped at 99 (Unit_ApplySpawnRecord bases random and relative levels on it).
for i = 0..15: unit +444 = i, unit +504 = dwords[i], g_CurrentSpawnEntry = entry i; an entry whose byte 0 is 0 leaves the unit empty (+1 and +437 = 0xFF).
otherwise +1 = i, +437 = 1 and Unit_BuildFromRecord(unit, entry, 0, 0, rows ? rows[i] : null): the entry's OverrideEntryData row is the fifth argument.

then the shape (Unit_ResolvePreviewShape) goes to +399, the palette to +400, +401 is the entry's byte +32 unless 0xFF (else a counter from 0xFE down), and the entry's bytes +25..+27, +30, +31 give +79..+81, +404 and +406.
team bits +5 & 0xC0 and sub_140271178 / sub_140271844 decide whether the unit is kept; a kept unit is queued with LookQueue_Add (sprite 27 becomes 36 when scene variable 39 is 388 and +444 is 1).

the presence bits (work +5 & 0xC0, from the entry's byte +24; the decompiler shows them as a masked and shifted value, so 0x80 is the top-bit pattern of the pair): 0x00 leaves the unit off the field (+437 = 0, +1 = 0xFF, tile kept) unless the dword at 0x142FF9E2C is 1 and a preview unit with the same marker exists, in which case it is placed; 0x40 lets one random bit choose; 0x80 places it (sub_140271178, sub_140271844 and the placement count cap may still drop it); 0xC0 builds the unit and queues its look but leaves +1 = 0xFF and +437 = 0 and does not count it.
an entry byte +32 other than 0xFF goes to work +401; otherwise +401 comes from a running counter that starts at 0xFE.

notes: So battle slot i is always built from entry i, and its OverrideEntryData row is the same row index i of the battle key. The count of kept units is limited by scene variable 57 (7 + 9 - value).
open_questions: ? the exact placement rules of sub_140271178 and sub_140271844 (not read).

name: Battle_ResolveAction
purpose:
Resolves one action request against one target: selects the formula from the action type / ability, runs
the formula handler and leaves a 40-byte result record for the apply step. This is the only caller of the
`g_FormulaHandlers` table (`0x140682BC8`) besides the F106 re-dispatch.

behavior.text:
copies the 20-byte request from `a1` to the stack (`0x1403099E8`); byte 0 is the actor slot,
  byte 1 the action type, word +2 the ability id.

sets the working pointers: `qword_14186AF78` = live record[actor], `qword_14186AF68` = live
  record[target], `qword_14186AF70` = live record[target] + `0x1BE` (result).

ability id -> `AbilityAction_GetRecord` (`0x140309B95`, `0x140309D41`), copies the 20-byte ability
  action record to `xmmword_1407B0790+4`; formula = record `+8`, element `+7`, inflict `+11`,
  CT `+12`, MP `+13`.
`sub_14030AFEC` (`0x140309E19`) runs the pre-formula reaction/status guards.

calls the handler as `g_FormulaHandlers[formulaId]` at `0x140309F53`; formula 106 is the
  re-dispatch entry.
afterwards `sub_14030A11C` (`0x140309F78`) clamps damage/heal to 999 and clears result flags.
the result record is not applied here; `BattleAct_NoEffectStep` reads it later.

the working pointers are set from the arguments: 0x14186AF78 = the record of the request's actor slot (request byte 0), g_BattleActingUnit (0x14186AF68) = the record of the target slot (the second argument); when the battle-state gate 0x14186AF9C is non-zero, sub_1403095E4 (the reaction executor) runs first and a non-zero answer ends the resolve through Action_SetWeaponItem.

the ability id is the request's word +2 (stored in the formula block's word +8 at 0x1407B0778; the two writes are at 0x140309B6A and 0x140309C42); the 20-byte action row is copied to 0x1407B0794 (the row of the id, or row 0 for an id above 0x16F, a compare with 0x170; the second copy for kinds 0, 3, 6 and 7 happens only for an id below 368, else the default formula 1 is used).

id 358 keeps the inflict index already in the block instead of the action row's byte +11 (test at 0x140309D67), and id 357 skips the clear of the weapon or item word (test at 0x140309D8B); the formula id is action-row byte +8, clamped to 1 when above 0x6A (a compare of formula - 1 with 0x69), and the handler is g_FormulaHandlers[formula]. See FormulaHandlersChooseTheirEffectByAbilityId.
a Charge clamp for command type 10 sits at 0x140309EB8.

notes:
The request at unit `+0x1A0` is built by `sub_140282E38` for queued/charged abilities and by the battle
menu for immediate commands (menu path not traced; C3).

- The exact menu site that writes the request.

name: Battle_ScaleByDifficulty

purpose: Scales the HP and MP damage of a resolved action by the play mode's percentages: the row of the DifficultyLevel table that the configuration names, one percentage for one side of the target and another for the other.

behavior.text: copies the result block's words +6 (HP damage) and +10 (MP damage) to the two outputs; when g_ShopModeGate (the Enhanced edition flag) is 0 it only clamps them to 999.
otherwise it finds the nxd table with registry id 111 (DifficultyLevel; the table pointer is cached at qword_143CDA488) and its row keyed by the configuration byte +196 (g_ConfigData), the play mode.

name: Battle_SnapshotLiveState
purpose: Captures or restores the live save state the battle image carries: the item stores and the unit save records, copied between the live globals and a save work block in the direction the second argument selects.

behavior.text: the first argument is the base of the save work block and the second is the direction: 1 copies work to live, 0 copies live to work.

the largest move is a block of 0x7E90 bytes (54 records of 0x258, so the 0x258 comes from 0x7E90/54 and is not an immediate) between the work base and the live unit save table at 0x1411A7D10; it is done with memmove.
the item stores follow at later work offsets: the inventory counts at 0x1411A7C00, the den stock at 0x1411A7700 and the badge flags at 0x1411A7810, each copied with its own loop.
the unit save records outside the block are copied in a separate loop of 16-byte units with a tail, so the whole 600-byte record shape survives the round trip.
the direction is tested in front of each sub-block, so a single call either captures the whole set or restores it.
the routine is shared by the battle capture and the battle restore paths, which is why it takes a direction instead of having two bodies.

direction 1 is the restore: Battle_RestoreSceneVars calls it with the snapshot buffer (a global of the caller, not addressed in this body) and 1, so a resumed battle's live unit records (g_UnitSaveData) and item stores come from the snapshot; Save_ResumeCheckpoint does not run SaveWork_UnpackToLive for a battle resume (behaviour ResumedBattleRestoresUnitRecordsWithoutUnpack).
this is the live-state half of the battle image; the five memory blocks A..E are copied by the caller around it.
whether the work block is cleared before a capture; this body only moves bytes.

notes: Whole function read (1182 bytes). The 0x7E90 block move and the record loop are visible in the body; the item-store offsets are the live globals the same body addresses.

name: Battle_StatusApply
purpose:
Converts the pending status sets of one unit's action result block into applied status bits, after filtering them
against the unit's innate/immunity sets. Handles the two team-changing statuses.

behavior.text:
the unit record is `rec = g_BattleUnitTable + 512*slot`; the result block is `rec + 0x1BE`, so pending sets
  are `rec+0x1DB..0x1DF` (result +29..33) and pending clears `rec+0x1E0..0x1E4` (result +34..38).

for each of the 40 status bits set in the pending sets: skip it when the unit's `+0x1EF..0x1F3` already has
  it and a 16-byte filter table at `byte_140788DFC` says it is blocked; otherwise copy the corresponding 5-byte
  mask from `aDefghijklmnopq` into the pending clears, run `Status_FilterPendingSets(source)`, clear the effective
  status byte through `Battle_StatusRefresh`, set the bit in `+0x1EF..0x1F3`, call `Unit_SetStatusCountdown`, and
  play the status icon update `BattleUnit_SetStatusVisual(status+1, on/off, slot)`.
status 19 clears `rec[0x2E]`.

statuses 9 and 34 (Charm/Recruit) copy the source unit's team bits: `rec[5]` bits 4..5 are set to the
  source's, and `rec[0x1EE] = (src[5] & 0x30) | (rec[0x1EE] & 0xC7)`; status 9 also zeroes result +16 and
  `rec[0x1EC]`.
after the loop, `rec[0x61..0x65] = rec[0x57..0x5B] | rec[0x1EF..0x1F3]`.
the two `dword_14186AF80` guards suppress the effect while an ability is being previewed.

notes:
The status ids here are 0-based (bit 0 = first status). `Unit_SetStatusCountdown` uses the same id, and for ids
24..39 writes a countdown byte at `rec+102+(id-24)`.
open_questions: The id -> name table for the 40 statuses (not a string in the exe).

name: Battle_StatusRefresh
purpose: Applies the pending status clears of a unit and recomputes the effective 40-bit status set.

behavior.text: `rec = g_BattleUnitTable + 512*slot`.

finally `rec[0x61+i] = rec[0x57+i] | rec[0x1EF+i]` for i = 0..4, i.e. the effective statuses are the
  innate statuses OR the battle-applied statuses.
the status id -> bit mapping is MSB first: bit `0x80 >> (id & 7)` of byte `id >> 3`.

notes:
`Battle_StatusResolve` (`0x14030C87C`) is the wrapper: it saves/restores the pending sets, calls
`Status_FilterPendingSets`, `Battle_StatusRefresh` and `Battle_StatusApply`, then applies the Dead status'
side effects (`+0x30 = 0` when status 2 is set, `+0x18D = 0xFF` when none of statuses 0/2/3 are set).

name: Battle_StatusResolve
proto: int64 Battle_StatusResolve(int slot, unsigned int mode)
callers: Battle_ApplyActionResult (three calls), sub_140271AC0; also started through the scene callback slot by sub_14024138C and EventUnitStatus_SetBit
purpose: Applies the pending status adds and removes of one battle unit: filters them, clears, sets, then settles the effects that depend on the new set.

behavior.text: returns -1 at once when the unit row of slot is empty (row byte +1 equal to 0xFF).

points g_BattleActingUnit at the unit and g_BattleActionBlock at its result block (unit +446), stores the slot in the byte after the first byte of xmmword_1407B0760, and saves both pending sets (block +29 and +34, five bytes each) in locals.
calls Status_FilterPendingSets(mode), Battle_StatusRefresh(slot) and Battle_StatusApply(slot, mode) in that order (Apply filters and refreshes again for each status it applies).

afterwards the effective set (+97): KO (bit 0x20 of byte 0) sets the HP word at +48 to 0; when none of Readying, Jumping and Performing (mask 0x0D of byte 0) is set the charge counter +0x18D becomes 0xFF; one of Confusion, Vampire, Berserk, Chicken or Charmed (bytes 1..2 masks 0x14, 0x0C, byte 4 mask 0x20) clears bit 3 of +5, otherwise +5 takes bit 3 of the side byte +494; unless Charmed, bits 4..5 of +5 are made equal to those of +494.
finally it copies the saved pending sets back into the result block and returns 0.

notes: Name is ours (the sheets of Battle_StatusApply and Battle_StatusRefresh call it the wrapper). It is the one entry that every status change passes through.
open_questions: ? the meaning of the +5 bit 3 (it follows the five statuses above).

name: Battle_TimelineBuildList
purpose: Builds the 40-entry timeline list for the UI and overlays the acting unit's current command preview.

behavior.text:
when the renderer mode `*(int*)(g_CharaRenderMgr + 13420)` is 1 or 2, it updates the scroll words
  (`xmmword_142FD35A0`) from the timeline list at `qword_14184A9B0` and the current unit's index.
calls `TurnList_Build(list, 0, 1)` (`0x14030FFC4` with `a2=0`, `a3=1`) and returns its result in `*count`.

otherwise (renderer mode 0) it builds the forecast and then calls `BTurn_PreviewAction(unit, ..., list, 1)`
  (`sub_14030FE60`) to overwrite the current unit's entry with the action it is about to take (used while the
  command menu is up).
returns whether the scroll word changed.

notes:
`a3 = 1` in `TurnList_Build` means "do not insert the active unit at time 0"; the preview overlay puts it back
with its chosen action.
open_questions: The renderer-mode 1/2 path was only read at the field level.

name: Battle_TimelineRefresh
proto: char __fastcall Battle_TimelineRefresh(int a1, int a2, int a3)
purpose:
Refreshes the Combat Timeline panel: builds the forecast, copies it into `g_TurnList`, and fills the visible rows
(portrait, name, HP/MP, CT) and the scroll position.

behavior.text: bails out to the per-unit tag refresh when the panel is not in timeline mode (`dword_140D4058C != -1`).

calls `Battle_TimelineBuildList` (`0x1402333E8`) with a local 40-entry array; the returned count and the flags
  decide the scroll (`v12` = first visible row, max 31/39).
copies the 40 entries (160 bytes) into `g_TurnList` `0x140D40490` (`0x140215Fxx`, the `qmemcpy` of `v127`).

for the 10 visible rows calls `TurnPanel_SetTag(tag, listIndex, unit, entryByte0, entryByte1)`
  (`sub_140215540`) which paints portrait/name/HP/MP/ability name.

the panel header widgets get `sub_14022AA88` (unit portrait/name), HP/max HP (`+0x30`/`+0x32`), MP/max MP
  (`+0x34`/`+0x36`), and the CT field; the CT shown is 100 when the unit's `+0x1B8` active flag is non-zero,
  otherwise `unit[0x65]` (`sub_1400E4E74`, I for the exact widget).
uses the global UI mode `dword_140C6B1CC` (39/90/91/97) to decide whether the timeline is the active screen.

notes: The timeline is rebuilt from live state on every refresh, not cached. The list it copies is the same format `TurnList_InsertEntry` and `TurnPanel_SetTag` use.
open_questions: The exact meaning of the `dword_140C6B1CC` values 90/91/97 (different timeline layouts or zoom levels).

name: Battle_TurnEngine
purpose:
The battle turn state machine: ticks CT, picks the next unit, starts and finishes turns, and resolves charged actions.
It returns an action code `slot | 0x100/0x200/0x300/0x400` (or `0xFF00` on the loop guard) that the caller interprets.

behavior.text:
`reset != 0` clears `dword_14186B044` (phase), sets `dword_1407B0708 = -1`, clears the four per-team words at
  `0x14186B020`, the per-team arrays at `0x14186AFA0`/`0x14186B000`, per-unit state (`+0x1B8`, `+0x1E8`, `+0x1BA`)
  and `g_BattleSimulating`, then returns `0xE000` (`0x14030F0C0`-`0x14030F103`).

phases are dispatched from `dword_14186B044` at `0x14030F126`: 0 tick, 1 select, 2 pending-action countdown,
  3 pending-action ready, 4 status counters, 5 build finished table, 6 pop finished unit, 9 battle start,
  10 active-unit wait, 13/14/15/17/19 clean-up.

phase 0 (`0x14030F46C`): for every unit with `BTurn_StatusFlags & 1 == 0`,
  `CT = min(CT + speed, 0xFE)` with speed `+0x40`, halved on Slow (`flags & 0x20`) and x1.5 on Haste (`flags & 0x10`).

phase 1 (`0x14030F349`): picks the highest CT `> 99` (ties to the lowest slot), or the unit with dword
  `+0x1F8 & 0x400` (bit 10 of the unit flag word, the OverrideEntryData acts_first column; V: it is only considered once some unit has CT above 99, the unit with the bit then acts first whatever its CT, its CT is first set to the highest CT found and the bit cleared); sets the winner's CT to `CT % 100` (255 -> 0), clears the extra-turn bit, sets `+0x1B8 = 1`,
  `+0x2E = 1`, `+0x1BA = 0`, sets phase 10 and `dword_1407B0708 = slot`, returns `slot | 0x100`.
  A unit with `+0x61 & 4` is skipped with CT forced to 99.

phase 9 (`0x14030F4C8`) is the first turn: highest CT without the 100 threshold (initial CT is 1..99 from
  `Unit_ApplySpawnRecord`), then the same turn-start writes and `slot | 0x100`.

phase 3 returns `slot | 0x200` when a unit's `+0x18D` pending-action timer is 0; phase 6 returns `slot | 0x300`
  for units in the finished table; phase 10 returns `slot | 0x100` while the active unit is not done and finishes it
  when `BTurn_IsUnitDone` is true (`0x14030F776`-`0x14030F7A9`).
the internal loop guard returns `0xFF00` after 1200 steps (compare at `0x14030F7D0`, limit 0x4B0).
phases 13-19 are the clean-up of the action (status application, removal, charge resolution); see C4.

phase 4 (the countdown loop with the tests at 0x14030F273 / 0x14030F27D): for every unit present and not Jumping it decrements the countdown bytes +0x66.. of the statuses 24..38 whose bit is in the applied set and not in innate a (tests at 0x14030F273 / 0x14030F27D on their byte 3, +0x1F2 and +0x5A), queues the removal at 0, and runs Status_FilterPendingSets(0).

phase 19 (0x14030F595): the unit whose turn ended (g_BattleActiveUnit), unless absent, Crystal, KO, Jumping (+0x61 & 0x64), Stone or Chest (+0x62 & 0x81): Battle_ResultReset, then Poison (+0x64 bit 0x80) writes HP damage = max HP >> 3 at block +6 and 0x80 at block +39, else Regen (bit 0x40) writes the heal max HP >> 3 at +8 and 0x40; a non-zero +39 returns `slot | 0x300` (the result is applied), else on to the next phase. Phase 19 sets g_BattleTurnPhase to 15 first; phases 15 (BTurn_QueueTerrainPoison) and 17 (BTurn_QueueInvisibilityEnd) jump to the same `jz` with their own result.

notes:
Called once per frame by the player command path and in a loop by the AI path. It is the only writer of
`dword_14186B044` and `dword_1407B0708`.
Addresses: the conditional jump at 0x14030F634 (phase 15, the Poison / Regen result), the CT byte load at 0x14030F49C (phase 0, the CT gain) and phase 4's filter call (0x14030F29B).
open_questions: The exact per-unit work of phases 13/14/15/17 (it overlaps the action resolution documented by C4); phase 19 is read (Poison / Regen).

name: Battle_TurnStep
purpose: Runs one step of the turn engine on the player path and dispatches the returned action code to the scene/UI.

behavior.text:
calls `Battle_TurnEngine(0)` (`0x1402029E8`) and stores `result & 0xFF00` in `dword_140D3A868`
  (`0x1402029FB`).
returns immediately when the code is `0xFF00` (engine gave up).
looks the unit up with `sub_140260ABC(low byte)` (`0x140202A0E`); a missing unit ends the step.

`0x100` (turn start) -> `ScenePreview_ClaimForUnit(slot)` (`0x140202AD2`), which sets the scene object's
  active words.

`0x300` -> `sub_14030A488(slot)` (end-of-turn effects) at `0x140202A53`; if it returns `-1`, the unit is
  removed (`sub_140283784`, `sub_140268F68`).

`0x400` -> the same end-of-turn call plus `SceneObject_FindBySlot`, `sub_14026801C` and `sub_1401FAF54`
  (scene refresh), at `0x140202AA6`.

the returned unit node's `+8` byte is stored in `dword_140CF873C` and `sub_1402607C0` is used to re-run the
  current-unit lookups.

notes:
This is the player-side adapter between the engine's action codes and the scene; the AI side has its own adapter in
`Battle_AITurnRun`.
open_questions: What distinguishes the `0x400` path from `0x300` (the extra scene calls suggest a join/leave or a scene-unit claim).

name: Battle_UnitStatusFill
callers: the battle scene/AT-bar task (`sub_140215540`, `sub_1402158F4` is called from the turn-order code
purpose:
Fills the battle status panel's view record (and the addon's cached fields) from the live unit table. This is the
best independent reader of the record's stat offsets.

behavior.text:
for slot <= 20 the field pointers are computed from `g_BattleUnitTable + 512*slot`:
  `+0x29` (level), `+0x28` (EXP), `+0x1FC` (name id), `+0x14C`, `+0x66` (status countdowns), `+0x61`
  (effective status byte 0), `+0x41`, `+0x2B` (Brave), `+0x2D` (Faith), `+0x8` (zodiac), `+0x01` (occupied),
  `+0x1F8`, `+0x06` (flags), `+0x1EC`, `+0x1BC` (slot), `+0x32`, `+0x30`, `+0x36`, `+0x34`, `+0x38` (PA). The code adds
  these offsets to the table's own address (for example 0x141853D21 = unit +0x41, 0x141853D41 = unit +0x61), so they do not
  appear as separate immediates.

the setters write these panel fields (panel base +65464, view size 212):
  - `+156` slot, `+160` level (`+0x29`), `+164` EXP (`+0x28`), `+168/+170` HP current/max (`+0x30/+0x32`),
  - `+172/+174` MP current/max (`+0x34/+0x36`), `+176` CT source, `+178` Brave (`+0x2B`), `+180` Faith (`+0x2D`),
  - `+182` zodiac (`u16(+8) >> 12`), `+185` flags bit 2 of `+6`, `+186` team/auto code, `+188` slot,
  - `+196` job-derived value, `+200` u32 at `+0x1F8`.
the "CT" value is `100` unless `unit[0x38] (PA) == 0`, in which case it is `unit[0x41]`.

the HP/MP pair is passed to the addon gauge setters, and the name id plus the `+0x14C` block is resolved by
  `sub_1401E8B7C`.
the team/auto code comes from `+0x1EE & 0x30 == 0x10` -> 1, `!= 0` -> 2, else 0; a `+0x1EC > 10` forces 3.
the status icons read the effective status bytes `+0x61` and the countdown bytes `+0x66`.

the record built at the end is the unit's job record: `BattleUnit_BuildJobRecord(unit +1,
  record)` builds it from the battle unit's job byte (+3) and its level, JP and total JP arrays through JobRecord_FromJobId,
  and `sub_14010141C` hands it to the panel (job name, level, JP); it is not a portrait record.

notes:
The companion `Battle_UnitStatusFillAlt` (`0x140228778`) builds the same panel for the target-info window and
takes CT from `*(i16*)(*(qword*)(turnRecord+0x88))`. Neither path reads a CT field from the unit record, which is
evidence that CT lives in the turn system (C2).
open_questions: The exact meaning of `+0x41` and why it stands in for CT when PA is 0.

name: BattleAct_BuildResult
callees: sub_140281C24, sub_140282754, Battle_ResolveAction, Action_SetWeaponItem, sub_140281A64, sub_14030A410
purpose: Resolves the unit's queued action against its targets and fills the scene object's result record (obj +0x1A8): target list, flags and the effect word +0x14 the presentation is keyed by.

behavior.text: the target scan (sub_140281C24, sub_140282754), then Battle_ResolveAction once per target; result +1 = target count, +2.. = targets.

the effect word +0x14 (obj +0x1BC) = the queued action's ability word (unit +0x1A2, read at 0x14028211B and 0x140282185), or WORD4 of the formula state (a weapon spell, < 256) with +0x17 = 1, or 0 when byte_1407B078C is set.
when xmmword_1407B0790's low byte is set (not negative, no weapon spell) it writes the sentinel 512 with +0x17 = 1 and +0x12 = 1 (0x1402821DD).
rejects actor slots >= 21; resets the actor's own result record at record[actor] +0x1BE (sub_14030A410 at 0x140281D80) and the shared working record xmmword_14186AFC0 (0x140281D9C).

builds a 21-byte target mask: sub_140281A64(actor, out, &count, mask) when dword_14186AF9C is set (a charged or special action), else sub_140281C24(request, mask); a multi-target action (dword_1411A7024 != 0) orders the targets by distance from the actor with sub_140282754.

loops j = 0..20 and calls Battle_ResolveAction(request, j) at 0x140281F0D for each mask byte != 0xFF; the summary holds the actor slot at +0, the target count at +1, the target list at +2, the ability id at +20, result flags at +18 / +24 and the hit count at +26.
returns 1 when nothing was hit, 0 when at least one target was resolved, -1 on bad input.

notes: In game 2026-10-30 an ability of id 512 reached this record as 512: the stock sentinel value. sub_140282754 is the distance sort: it reads the actor's tile (record +0x4F / +0x50) and each candidate's, in ascending Manhattan distance. Earlier sheet name: Battle_ResolveTargets.
open_questions: What sets xmmword_1407B0790's low byte (the sentinel case): I, a reflected or bounced effect. The difference between the dword_14186AF9C path and the normal path (charged or immediate action).

name: BattleAct_NoEffectStep
callees: sub_140204CDC, sub_14030A488, sub_140260ABC, Battle_ApplyActionResult, sub_140283784, sub_140269790, BattleAnim_SelectMotion, sub_14027192C, sub_140268EE0
purpose: Applies the resolved action to every target and starts each target's hit motion: the step that turns the formula results into HP, MP and status changes and visible hits. Runs at once for an action without an effect file, and as battle state 43 after an effect has played.

behavior.text: sets dword_140C6B1CC = 44 (0x140206770), gets the acting scene object (sub_14026079C) and clears its animation word +0x0C.

loops over the target list of the acting object (count +0x1A9, slots +0x1AA): for each slot gets its scene object (sub_140260ABC), calls Battle_ApplyActionResult(slot) at 0x1402067DF and stores the return value on the target object.
on a return of -1 it calls sub_140283784(slot, unit record +0x1A0) (the action request clean-up) and sub_140268F68 (KO and crystal handling).
on the first successful hit it sets the target's +0x1F5 = the actor's slot and adds one to the actor's hit counter at BattleControl + 4 * slot + 0xA94D4 (capped at 9999).
effect word 512: copies the object's bytes +0x1C4..+0x1C6 to each target and calls sub_14027192C (the sentinel case).
word 0 (or a weapon flag case): sub_140269790 (the weapon attack motion); otherwise, when +0x1BF is 0, BattleAnim_SelectMotion.

notes: BattleControl is the singleton at 0x143CD9EF0; the hit counter table starts at +0xA94D4. A delayed copy of the apply loop exists in sub_1402029DC. Earlier sheet name: Battle_ApplyActionResults.
open_questions: Whether the loop applies every target in one pass or one per frame (the call from sub_140210AF0 is a state, so likely one pass).

name: BattleAct_SetupEffect
purpose:
Selects the visual effect for an ability: builds the list of units on screen, reads the ability's charge
byte from `g_AbilityAnim`, combines it with the ability element and calls the effect-number selector.

behavior.text: reads the acting unit's ability id (`a2[14].vt` in the decompile) and its slot (`a2[18]...`).
builds a 0xE4-byte unit/position list from the scene objects (`SceneObject_FindBySlot`).
reads `g_AbilityAnim[abilityId].charge` at `0x1402062CB` (`unk_140672DA0 + 3*id`).
when the ability id is < 368, ORs the ability action record's element (`AbilityAction_GetRecord(id)[7] << 16`) into the effect word (`0x140206300`).
calls `Effect_SelectForAbility(effectWord, abilityId, &list)` at `0x140206317`.
`rdi` holds the scene object from `0x14020611E` to the call at `0x140206317` (no instruction in between writes it; the callees keep it); the effect word is in `edx` at the call.

the resulting effect is the spell/impact visual played by the target hit sequence; the motion is
  chosen separately by `BattleAnim_SelectMotion`.

notes:
`g_AbilityAnim` is `0x140672DA0`, 3 bytes per row (charge, motion, battle text), 454 rows.
The same charge byte is used by `sub_140206C14` to pick a cast motion.
open_questions: - How `Effect_SelectForAbility`'s return value reaches the effect spawner (not traced).

name: BattleAct_Step
callees: BattleAct_BuildResult, sub_140204FF0, sub_14020CABC, ItemSprite_LoadPalettes, Effect_AbilityHasNoEffect, BattleAct_NoEffectStep, BattleAct_SetupEffect
purpose: The scene step that executes the acting object's action: builds the result, sets the effect word and chooses the presentation path.

behavior.text: BattleAct_BuildResult(unit, obj +0x1A8); the effect word +0x142 = the result word +0x1BC.

a word that is 0, 512 (the sentinel), another word than +0x1C2 when that is set, or one Effect_AbilityHasNoEffect accepts goes to BattleAct_NoEffectStep; every other word to BattleAct_SetupEffect (charge byte, element, effect number).
the test `+0x1BC == 512 && +0x1BF == 1 && +0x1BA == 1 && +0x1CC` marks the sentinel case (only the sentinel write sets +0x1BF with 512).

the unit argument of BattleAct_BuildResult is the byte +0x1BC of the battle unit the object points at (+0x148); BattleAct_BuildResult reads the action's ability word at g_BattleUnitTable + that slot * 0x200 + 0x1A2 for the result word, so at BattleAct_SetupEffect that word is still the action's whole ability id.

gets the acting scene object with sub_14026079C; when the action has an effect it sets the battle state dword_140C6B1CC = 43 (0x140206BD3: the effect plays, then state 43 runs BattleAct_NoEffectStep's apply loop); with none it calls BattleAct_NoEffectStep at once (0x140206BE6).
writes the acting unit's animation and state fields and loads the item palettes (ItemSprite_LoadPalettes).
the effect is chosen before the results are applied so the hit or miss can select the impact animation.

notes: An ability word of 512 is taken for the sentinel here (no effect, the weapon motion: a punch in game 2026-10-30). Called on the frame after the command state machine reaches state 47 (sub_14020CFEC). Earlier sheet name: Battle_ExecuteAction.

name: BattleAction_ApplyRequest
purpose: Wrapper that takes a request whose first byte is a unit slot, points at that unit action block, and applies the request; on success in the normal battle state it also refreshes the unit action.

behavior.text: the request first byte is the unit slot; the unit record is the 0x200-byte entry at 0x141853CE0 plus slot times 0x200 (base by lea, stride by shl 9).
the unit action block is at unit +0x1A0 and is passed to sub_140281488 with a third argument of 1.
when the apply returns 1 and the battle state word at 0x14186AF9C is zero, sub_140279370 is called with the unit and a zero argument.
the result of the apply is returned unchanged; the refresh call does not change it.
the routine does not validate the slot before indexing the unit table.
the six callers are the command commit, the AI turn, the preview and the save/restore wrapper, so the request shape is shared by player and AI paths.
the 1 passed to the apply means 'this is a request from the menu', because the AI passes 0 on its own path.
whether a slot outside the 21-entry unit table can reach here; the callers are expected to supply a live slot but this body does not test it.

notes: Whole function read (84 bytes). The call to sub_140281488 is the request-to-unit-block step of the item flow.

name: BattleAction_BuildUnitRequest
proto: int BattleAction_BuildUnitRequest(void *unit, uint8_t command, uint16_t action, int preview)
purpose: Writes a command and action word into a unit action block, optionally marks the ring, and applies the request through the common wrapper.

behavior.text: the unit action block is at unit +0x1A0; the command byte goes to +1 and the action word to +2.
when the preview argument is non-zero it calls BattleRange_MarkRing on the block and rejects a result of -1.
a ring result of 0 or 1 is also rejected, and the function returns -2.
it then reads the acting unit slot from the global current-unit word, takes the unit level byte and checks the action record flags.
the block fields at +0xA, +0xB, +0xC and +0x10 are filled with 5, a global byte, the level-derived word and the action record value.
BattleAction_ApplyRequest is called on the block and its result is returned.
the two callers are the preview refresh and the second action path, both in battle.
the routine builds a request that has not been consumed yet; the consume step lives in the apply wrapper and its callee.
the meaning of the -2 return; the callers treat it as a refusal but the reason is not named.

notes: Whole function read (265 bytes). The field writes and the two calls are the commit step of the item flow.

name: BattleAction_GetRangeInfo
purpose: Chooses how an action acquires its range and area: the item path for the item-like command kinds and the ability record path otherwise, filling the caller flags and returning the range result.

behavior.text: the action command byte is at +1 and is looked up in the command-kind table at 0x14067E010.
the output byte is cleared before any work; it receives the record flags at +3, +4, +5 and +6 when the ability path is taken.
for command kinds 0 and 6 and for an ability id below 0x170, the ability record is fetched through AbilityAction_GetRecord.
command kinds flagged by the mask 0x506, or a combined flags byte with bit 0x20, skip the ability record and go to the item range path.
the item path calls sub_140280170, which reads the weapon record of the item and returns the item range.
the ability path calls BattleRange_ApplyShape and returns its result; -1 means nothing could be marked.
when the record flags have bit 8 and the state word at 0x14186AF80 is zero, sub_1402826B0 is called before returning.
the mask 0x506 covers the command kinds that carry an item or a throw rather than an ability row.
what sub_1402826B0 changes; it is called only on the flagged ability path.

notes: Whole function read (193 bytes). The command table index and the 0x170 test are its two sites of interest.

name: BattleAction_RunScript
purpose:
The driver task for the battle presentation programs: reads the current script id from scene block 1,
starts up to four sub-tasks defined by that script's 64-byte record, waits for them and repeats, then
ends.

behavior.text:
script id = `dword[off_140783088 + 0x800 * currentSlot]` (block 1 offset 0); stores it in
  `dword_140D4094C`.

record = `0x140672210 + (id << 6)`; layout `{void *func[4] at +0, uint32 taskSlot[4] at +32,
  uint32 tag[4] at +48}`.

for each of the four entries with `func != -1` and a free task slot, calls
  `SceneTask_Start(taskSlot[i], func[i])` at `0x140234CF6`; writes `tag[i]` into the task block at
  `+0x98`; marks the entry as started (local state 2).

after starting, waits (`SceneTask_WaitFrame` at `0x140234CE0`) until a started task's tag differs
  or the task ended, then restarts the remaining entries at `0x140234D5F`.
the loop ends when the block's first qword is 255; then `SceneTask_Terminate`.

record 0 is empty (all `func = -1`), records 1..6 are the live programs (see
  `docs/reference/battle-actions.md`).

notes:
The tags let the event script wait for a program kind (`SceneTask_FindTag`), e.g. tag 21 for the action
message task.
open_questions: - What the "wait for a different tag" condition is used for (interrupting a running program).

name: BattleAction_StartScript
proto: void BattleAction_StartScript(int scriptId, int actorSlot, int targetSlot)
purpose:
Starts one of the seven battle presentation programs (the "scene script" table) and records the acting
unit and target for the tasks that program starts.

behavior.text: returns immediately when `word_140D4080C == 1` (a battle/menu lock).
stores `byte_140672134[scriptId]` in `dword_142FEC534`.

when `actorSlot != 0xFF`: stores it in the high half of `dword_1407DCF98` (`+2`) and in
  `word_1407832AA`.
when `targetSlot != 0xFF`: stores it in `word_1407DCFAA` and `word_14078332A`.

if scene slot 2 is free (`[off_140783088 + 0x1090] == 0`), calls
  `SceneTask_Start(2, sub_140234B3C)` at `0x140234B10`.

writes the script id at scene block 1 offset 0 (`[off_140783088 + 0x1000]`), then zeroes block 1
  offsets +8 and +16.
the driver (`sub_140234B3C`) reads that id to select the 64-byte record at `0x140672210`.

notes:
The program table and the seven records are documented in `docs/reference/battle-actions.md`. Script 3
is started by the three action-confirm functions; script 2 by the turn-start state machine.
open_questions: - The meaning of the per-script byte table `byte_140672134` (values 1..8) stored in `dword_142FEC534`.

name: BattleAnim_PickProjectile
purpose: Chooses the projectile of a throw motion by the effect word.

behavior.text: word 148 (Throw Stone): projectile 6 (the stone); 382 or 368..393 (Throw item): 16; else byte_140673678[obj +0x152]; then sub_140310C24.

notes: One of the equality tests on stock ids (the effect word of a stock ability): an id not tested gets the weapon-kind projectile.

name: BattleAnim_SelectMotion
purpose:
Chooses the battle motion (animation id) for an ability: weapon attack, cast/ranged special, or a fixed
motion from the per-ability table, then starts it on the unit.

behavior.text:
reads `g_AbilityAnim[abilityId].motion` at `0x1402699D6` (`unk_140672DA1 + 3*id`); the ability id
  is `[sceneObject+0x142]`.
motion 0 -> BattleAnim_SelectWeaponMotion (weapon motion by weapon animation type; the byte at unit `+0x152` is read inside BattleAnim_SelectWeaponMotion, not here).

motion 1 -> `sub_140266890(obj, [obj+0x150])` then a distance test against the target; adjacent or
  same-tile -> motion 58, otherwise an arcing motion via BattleAnim_StartMotion(76, ...).
other motion values -> `motion + 1`.

the motion numbers of the ability table and the weapon table are pair indices of the classic animation file: animation pointer `2 x motion` is the front view and `2 x motion + 1` the back view. Weapon motions land on animations that draw the attack frames and carry the hit marker (one weapon type's animations carry none); of 57 distinct ability motion values 34 were tested: values from 40 up land on animations that draw action frames, the low ones on single-frame poses, one on an empty pointer. `2 x motion + 2` lands on the next animation of the same group, so the choice of `2 x motion` rests on the high / middle / low ordering of a weapon type's three motions (see BattleAnim_SelectWeaponMotion). The code that turns the +0x10 number into the pointer is not located.

stores the chosen id at `[sceneObject+0x10]` (`0x140269A95`) and calls
  BattleAnim_StartMotion(motion, [sceneObject+0x7C], sceneObject).

the weapon path (BattleAnim_SelectWeaponMotion) picks from `aAbAbAbAbAbAbAb` by weapon type `[unit+0x152]` and
  also calls BattleAnim_StartMotion.

notes:
`g_AbilityAnim` `0x140672DA0`: byte 0 charge type, byte 1 motion, byte 2 battle text. The battle
text byte is consumed by `sub_140210AF0` at `+0x18C`.
open_questions: - Answered: the +1 is added by BattleAnim_StartMotion (the stored animation number is motion + 1); the classic animation pair index is the motion itself (see above).

name: BattleAnim_SelectWeaponMotion
purpose: Chooses the motion of a plain weapon attack from the attacker's weapon animation type and, for some types, from how high the target stands, then starts it.

behavior.text: the weapon animation type is the byte at scene object +0x152; each type has three consecutive motion numbers in the weapon motion table at 0x140673890 (3 bytes a type, 24 types); the middle one is the default when there is no target.
when the sprite byte at +0x0A plus 101 is 3 or less, the motion is 62 whatever the weapon.
for type 12 with a target, a signed angle word (0x1437A5C14, wrapped to -2048..2047) picks the motion: below -682 gives 83, from -682 to 682 gives 84, above 682 gives 85.
types 1 to 9 share one triple (64, 65, 66); type 0 has 61, 62, 63; types 11 and 12 share 83, 84, 85; types 19 to 23 have none (0).

the three numbers of a triple are variants of one attack in the order of the target's height (the type 12 branch above picks the first, second or third by an angle word, and the middle one is the default); types with a single repeated number have one variant.
the path for the other types with a target (it reads a byte at +0x1C0 of the target's record) was not read.

notes: The IDB already carried this name. Read: the table lookup and the type 12 branch; the rest of the target path only in outline.
open_questions: - ? the target-dependent choice for types other than 12.

name: BattleAnim_SetChargeMotion
purpose: Sets the charging motion from the charge byte of g_AbilityAnim (the effect word +0x142).

behavior.text: m = byte_1406735A9[2 * charge]; when m != 0, obj +0x10 = m + 1 (or 10 under a condition of sub_1402696E8 and the unit's +0x1B4 bits).

notes: sub_140206C14 reads the other byte of the pair (byte_1406735A8[2 * charge]) and sets motion 3 when the charge byte is 0.

name: BattleAnim_StartMotion
proto: __int64 BattleAnim_StartMotion(int motion, int16_t direction, int64_t sceneObject)
purpose: Starts a motion on a battle unit's scene object: stores the animation number and the facing value the unit's animation will use.

behavior.text: the animation number stored is `motion + 1`, at scene object +0x10 (16-bit); the direction argument goes to +0x7C (16-bit) and bit 0x20 of the byte at +0x8F is set. This is the "+1" the callers' motion numbers carry.
when the global scene mode word (dword at 0x140782A94) is 457, the store happens at once with no other test.
otherwise, when that word is 292 and an event script is running, the store happens only if the unit's current animation number (+0x12) already equals `motion + 1`; in every other case it happens.
before a store, a non-zero byte at +0x156 is cleared and the animation number at +0x10 is zeroed.
what the mode values 457 and 292 are called.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140268E04). Read in full (a short function).
open_questions: - ? names of the scene mode values; ? which code reads the +0x10 animation number each frame and turns it into the classic animation pointer (not located; see UnitMovementAnimationTables and BattleMotionNumbers).

name: BattleControl_FrameUpdate
callers: sub_140210AF0 (the battle frame routine, one call near its end)
purpose: Per-frame update of the battle control object; its first part sets the fast-forward level in battle straight from the held buttons.

behavior.text: does nothing unless g_ShopModeGate (the enhanced-edition flag) is non-zero.

name: BattleFormation_DrawUnits
purpose: The battle formation draw (called from sub_140213F14): per unit index 0..20 it reads the CharShape row of the scene object's sprite byte for the draw height.

behavior.text: the key is the scene object's byte +0xA (0x14021708E); table 174 (CharShape) through NxdRegistry_Find (cached in `qword_143CD9F38`), entry = NxdTable_GetRowById(table, key); an entry with a negative first qword gives the static default row (`unk_1406F5ED0`), else NxdEntry_GetRow(entry).

other scene object fields read: +0x1E a byte the formation scales by 12; +0x15C bit 2 selects the +0x2F test.

notes: Behavior: CharShapeRowMissingFaultsTheFormation.

name: BattleMsg_BuildArgs
callees: BattleMsg_IdFromDescriptor, ItemTable_GetName, FormatArgs_Push, sub_1400F48E0, sub_1401E8B7C, sub_1402B89F8, sub_14002620C
purpose: Fills the format-argument vector for a message descriptor: selects the message id, then pushes the values that replace the template's <string=lstrN> and <num=...> placeholders.

behavior.text: dispatches on the message id: for class 0 subtype 2 it uses BattleMsg_IdFromDescriptor(desc); for class 1 subtype 27, message ids 3981 and 3905 have their own cases.

the arguments come from the battle message record rec (the object's +8): rec[0] kind, rec[1] actor index into g_BattleUnitTable (512-byte stride, index at most 0x14), rec+12 a name string, rec[4193] (byte offset 0x4184), rec[133] (0x214), rec[134..] (0x218, a 256-byte string area) and rec[263] (0x41C).

for message id 10098 the string argument is ItemTable_GetName(id), with id = rec[1] & 0x7FF when rec[0] == 4 and id = rec[1] (unmasked) when rec[0] == 9; when neither holds, nothing is pushed and the function returns 0.
the item name is copied into a 256-byte stack buffer with a 255-byte cap before it is pushed.
arguments are pushed through FormatArgs_Push; the pushed record carries a type dword at offset 256 (4 for a string argument, 1 for an integer argument).
message ids 10141 and 10145 and above push the actor name and a status or ability value read through sub_1402B89F8.

message 3062 (C_Mes_Id_Sample "<string=lstr0>'s <lowerall=<jobname(lnum1, lnum2)>> job level increased!", the job level-up banner): pushes the unit's name (rec+12), then the unit's job byte (+3 of the g_BattleUnitTable record named by rec[1]; loaded at 0x1400F7C6B) as lnum1, then lnum2 from the flags +6: 0 when the byte is negative (its top bit set), else 1 when bit 0x40 is set, else 2.
the banner read "Ramza's knight job level increased!" for a unit whose job byte was 76 (Knight).
the other message-id cases and what they push were not read.
a 0 return means no argument was pushed, which makes BattleMsg_FillArgs use its stored argument set instead.
the 11-bit mask on the kind-4 id is the item text-id field, not the item store; kind 9 carries the item id without that mask.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1400F79D0). The record layout is known only at the offsets named above. The function is 0x7F9 bytes (about 2 KB) and has one direct caller, BattleMsg_FillArgs (0x1401EC074).
open_questions: What the cases other than 3062, 10098, 10141 and 10145+ push; what rec[4193], rec[133], rec[263] and the rec[134..] range hold; whether every case uses the same 0/1 return convention; whether kind 9 is reserved for the item-use record and kind 4 for another item message.

name: BattleMsg_Dispatch
proto: __int64 __fastcall BattleMsg_Dispatch(int a1, int a2, signed int a3, __int64 a4, int a5, __int64 a6)
callers: 21 direct callers in the battle-message handlers, including sub_1402025E0, sub_140202E0C, sub_140203AB4, sub_14020435C, sub_140204B78, sub_1402059AC, sub_14020A7F0 and sub_140238444
callees: SceneVar_Read, SceneVar_Write, BattleMsg_SetKind6, BattleMsg_SetKind1, Item_GetRecord, Item_CountOwnedAndEquipped, SceneTask_Start, sub_140238360, sub_1401FA5F0, sub_1401FA648, sub_140272538, sub_140236378
purpose: Fills the battle message record from an event: it switches on the message kind, writes the kind and id of the record entries, starts the message scene task and resets the action-list widget state. Case 15 is the item message; case 7 is the action message.

behavior.text: a1 selects the message kind; a3 is a unit index (above 0x14 the unit pointer is null); a6 points at a message argument block whose word +2 is the item or action id.

case 15 (item): `v7` is the item id; `Item_CountOwnedAndEquipped(v7)` is called raw, and when it is 99 or more the item record is read with `Item_GetRecord(v7 & 0x1FF)` (`0x140238E56`) and the record's price word is used for the message.
the same case writes the id into the descriptor at 0x140783210/+4 and increments `g_InventoryCounts[id]` when the count is below 99, so the message itself grants the item.

case 7 (action): the word at a6+2 masked with 0x1FF (`0x140238CE5`) selects the action id; a value in 60..85 writes entry 0 kind 7 with id + 0xB7C4, any other value writes kind 6 with id = masked word + 0x7000. The same masked word is stored in `dword_142FD3590` at `0x140238BE2` for the cast-prompt path (case 5).
`v56 == 255` (`0x140238F92`) is the "no item" test of the action message; it selects text 20634 instead of 20633.
the 0x1FF mask is a nine-bit action/item-id limit; the argument word is a plain u16 and the function never tests bit 14/15.
the function is large body and has 21 direct callers; the item record's word +8 shifted right by two is the price used in the text.
the item and action ids arrive through the same argument word because the battle message record has one id field per entry.
the meaning of a2, a4 and a5 for the cases not re-read; the remaining case mapping.

the 9-bit ability for the battle line is cut and stored in dword 0x142FD3590 at 0x140238BE4 (cases 6 and 9) and read back at 0x140238BFD; the line task (0x140233588) is started and the unit index and the ability go into the message object at 0x140783088 (words at +0x2000 and +0x2008).
the line task forms its text id as a value taken from that message object ORed with 0xA800; dword 0x142FD3590 is also written at 0x1402386D4 in sub_140238444 and written and read in sub_140243A60.
because of the 9-bit cut an ability id above 511 never reaches the line task, so no 0xA800-form line text exists for it (the text table was not checked).
id 60..85 (summons) take the text base 0xB7C4 (47044) in case 7 and every other id the base 0x7000, both after the 9-bit cut (confirmed again 2026-11-10).

notes: - V: read for case 15, case 7's mask and the 0xFF sentinel, and the four mask/cmp sites; the other cases are from the earlier battle-message research and were not re-read this pass.

name: BattleMsg_FillArgs
callers: UIMessageBanner_Show (with qword_143CDA388, the banner's argument vector at a1+152 and the descriptor)
purpose: Fills the format-argument vector for the banner: first asks the message-id-specific builder, and when that pushes nothing, copies the object's up to 40 stored argument entries.

behavior.text: resets outVec (end = begin).
calls BattleMsg_BuildArgs(outVec, obj+8, desc).

when desc is null or that call returns 0, it copies up to 40 stored argument entries instead, 524 bytes apart from obj+12, each with a type dword (1 = int, otherwise a 255-character string), pushed through FormatArgs_Push.
the stored entries are the fallback for messages whose id-specific case pushes nothing.
the 40-entry store is the message manager's saved argument set; the record at obj+8 is the battle message record BattleMsg_BuildArgs reads.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1401EC074). 40 entries of 524 bytes are read from obj+12; one entry becomes one 264-byte FormatArgs_Push record.
open_questions: How the 40 stored entries are written; the exact relation between the record at obj+8 and the entry store at obj+12 (the recorded base addresses overlap; only the copy was read); whether the type dword has values other than 0 and 1.

name: BattleMsg_IdFromDescriptor
callers: BattleMsg_BuildArgs, BattleMsg_TextFromDescriptor, sub_1400FCCFC, BattleMsg_ResolveEntry (five sites in four functions)
purpose: Turns a message descriptor into the row id used by NXD table 172 (C_Mes_Id_Sample-en).

behavior.text: the function returns -1 unless the descriptor's class dword is 0 and its subtype dword is 2.
for class 0 and subtype 2 it returns 1000 * kind + (word & 0x7FF), where kind is the dword at desc+8 and word is the signed 16-bit value at desc+12.
any other class, subtype or kind returns 0xFFFFFFFF.
kind 10 with word 98 gives 10098.
the function makes no calls and has no side effects.
the kind numbers are the battle message kinds, but they do not match the battle message record kinds one for one.
the meaning of kinds 14, 16 to 18 and 22 to 23 in game terms.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1400FCC04). 0xFFFFFFFF is the no-row value. The function is 0xF6 bytes (246) and read in full; five direct call sites across four functions.
open_questions: What the kinds outside the list are (they have no row in this table); whether callers test 0xFFFFFFFF before the lookup; which producer emits each accepted kind.

name: BattleMsg_InitHandlerTable
callers: not enumerated (no xref list was read for this address)

name: BattleMsg_ResolveEntry

kind 5 uses NXD table 41 (0x29), cached in qword_143CDA2E0; kind 6 uses NXD table 39 (0x27, Ability-en), cached in qword_143CDA2D0.

the caller walks all 40 entries and resolves the ones with kind above 1, so the banner sees the text the dispatcher wrote.
what a2 is and what the entry+8 value is read by after kind 8 writes it.

notes:
The name is ours (IDB: sub_1401EBBF4). The function is 0x425 bytes. Offsets are entry-relative; the record starts at object + 8, so entry+4 is object + 0xC. Read for kinds 4, 9, 10 and 11 during the item text research; the other kinds are from the earlier battle-message research. The bytes put the id + 10000 store on the kind-8 path, not kind 6.

- V: 0x1401EBF42 is a label inside this function (a branch target, not an entry; an earlier sheet named it `sub_1401EBF42`). What that path does:
  - V: the descriptor fields (class, subtype, kind, word) are handed to BattleMsg_IdFromDescriptor, which builds the message id.
  - V: the id is then looked up with CMesId_GetText, the table-172 accessor, and its result is what the function returns.
  - V: the only data the body touches is a small read-only table; there is no write to the message object.
  - I: this is the read-side twin of BattleMsg_Dispatch: a caller that holds a descriptor instead of a stored entry can ask for the same text.
  - ?: which callers pass a descriptor; the dispatch path builds entries, and the descriptor holders were not enumerated.
open_questions: What the entry+8 value is read by; what a2 is; the full kind list and the producer of each; which kinds above 23 exist.

name: BattleRange_FlagTargetTiles
purpose: Copies the range marks into the tile table: sets tile byte +5 bit 0x40 on every marked, targetable tile of both layers and returns how many it set.

behavior.text: for each of the 512 tile records and its mark record: when mark byte 0 is 0, or tile byte +6 has bit 0x01, or (tile byte +0 & 0x3F) == 0x3F, it clears tile byte +5 bit 0x40; otherwise it sets the bit and counts it.
tile byte +0 & 0x3F == 0x3F is a tile with no surface (empty layer-1 records); byte +6 bit 0x01 is a tile that cannot be selected.
tile byte +5 bit 0x40 is the yellow (targetable) mark of the target prompt; the live check of 2026-11-05 read the yellow set from mark byte 0, which this bit follows except on the excluded tiles.

name: BattleRange_MarkArcReach
purpose: The bow shape: tiles at Manhattan distance 3 or more whose distance, shortened by a quarter of the height the unit stands above them, is within the weapon range.

behavior.text: H = Unit_GetReachHeight(unit); for every map tile at distance d = |dx| + |dy| >= 3 from the unit's tile and for each layer: t = (b3 & 0x1F) + 2 * (b2 + (b3 >> 5)) as an 8-bit value; mark byte 0 = 1 when d - (H - t) / 4 <= range, with signed division truncated toward zero.
tiles nearer than 3 are not marked by it.
in whole steps every 2 steps of height above the target add one tile of reach and every 2 steps below remove one.

name: BattleRange_MarkArea

the byte at record +6 with bit 0x20 selects a shape that is not a simple radius, because the code switches to the direction builders when it is set.

name: BattleRange_MarkAttack

the ability id is compared with the 0x170 boundary at the gate named battle_ring_range.

whether the return value is a radius, a tile count or a status; the callers use it as a small range value but the unit is not proven.

name: BattleRange_MarkStrikeOrLunge
purpose: The melee shapes: the four adjacent tiles (flag 0x80), or two tiles in the four straight lines (flag 0x40 alone), each kept only inside a height band around the unit's reach height.

behavior.text: reads x = unit +0x4F, y = unit +0x50 and H = Unit_GetReachHeight(unit) (half-steps, 0..255).
weaponFlags bit 7 set: BattleRange_MarkTileInBand on (x-1, y), (x+1, y), (x, y-1), (x, y+1) with the band [H - 6, H + 5].
bit 7 clear: the same four tiles with [H - 8, H + 7], then (x-2, y), (x+2, y), (x, y-2), (x, y+2) with [H - 6, H + 7].
the weapon's range byte is not read: the strike reach is 1 and the lunge reach 2 for every weapon; the tile between the unit and a distance-2 tile is not tested.
in whole height steps the strike band is 3 down to 2.5 up, matching the live check (Brice on a sword: a tile 3 steps higher not lit).

name: BattleRange_MarkTileInBand
proto: void BattleRange_MarkTileInBand(int x, int y, int lo, int hi)
purpose: Sets mark byte 0 = 1 for a map tile, separately in each layer, when that layer's target height is inside [max(lo, 0), hi].

behavior.text: does nothing when x or y is outside the map (0 <= x < width, 0 <= y < height, g_BattleMapSize bytes 0 and 1).
lo below 0 is taken as 0.

for layer 0 and layer 1 (tile record + 0x800 * layer, mark record + 0x500 * layer): target height = (b3 & 0x1F) + 2 * (b2 + (b3 >> 5)) with b2, b3 = tile record bytes +2, +3; mark byte 0 = 1 when lo <= height <= hi.

b2 is the tile height in whole steps, b3 bits 0..4 a slope / half step in half-steps and bits 5..7 the water depth (the height the battle HUD shows agrees, seen live: 'Height' = b2 + half step + depth), so the target height counts half-steps up to the water surface.

name: BattleRange_MarkWeaponReach
callers: BattleRange_MarkAttack, sub_14027F974 (abilities whose record byte +3 has bit 0x20)
purpose: Marks in the range-mark array the tiles one unit's weapon reaches from its tile: picks the weapon, seeds the unit's tile and runs one of three shape routines chosen by the weapon's flag byte.

behavior.text: weapon: the word at unit +0x20 unless unit +0x63 bit 0x02 (Toad) is set, in which case 0; when that word is 0xFF or not below 0x105 (built as 0xFF + 6 in a register at 0x14027F000, so no 0x105 constant appears) it takes the word at unit +0x24 under the same test; when that fails too, item 0. Only this one item sets the shape (a second weapon is ignored).
Item_GetWeaponRecord of the item; when it returns null (not a weapon) Item_GetWeaponRecord(0) (the bare-hands row: range 1, flags 0x88 in the weapon table data, not in this body).
seeds the unit's tile (index x + y * width, x = unit +0x4F, y = unit +0x50, width = byte 0 of g_BattleMapSize): mark byte 0 = range + 1 in layer 0 and layer 1, mark byte 1 = 1 in layer 0.
flags & 0xC0: BattleRange_MarkStrikeOrLunge(unit, flags); else flags & 0x20: BattleRange_SpreadDiamond(range) then BattleRange_ClearWithin2(x, y); else BattleRange_MarkArcReach(unit, range).
last, clears mark byte 0 of every record (both layers) whose tile record byte +6 has bit 0x02.

behavior.basis: (data, the weapon table of the pristine executable)
behavior.text: flags 0x80 is set on bare hands, knives, ninja blades, swords, knight swords, katanas, axes, rods, staves, flails and bags; 0x40 on spears, poles and cloths; 0x20 on guns, crossbows, harps and books; bows have 0x15 and so take the last branch (0x80 here = bit 7 of the flag byte; the values are table data).

notes: The second argument its callers pass is not read. The unit's layer bit (+0x51 bit 7) is not used here: the seed and the shapes mark both layers.
open_questions: ? What tile byte +6 bit 0x02 stands for (a tile no attack may target).

name: BattleRange_SpreadDiamond
purpose: Spreads the seeded marks outward one tile per pass for range passes, so every tile within Manhattan distance range of a seed gets a non-zero mark byte 0; heights are not looked at.

behavior.text: range 0: clears mark byte 1 of every record and returns.

otherwise up to range passes over the layer-0 records (width x height, g_BattleMapSize): each record with byte 1 set clears it and, for its four in-map neighbours whose byte 0 is below its own value v, writes v - 1 into byte 0 of both layers; when v is above 2 it also sets the neighbour's byte 1 so the next pass continues from it.
stops early when a pass sets no byte 1.
with the seed at range + 1 the result is byte 0 = range + 1 - distance for every tile up to distance range: a diamond over the whole map, both layers alike.

notes: Shared with the ability range builders.

name: BattleTask_Slot13Entry

scene slot going 0 -> 13 -> 0 after choosing Wait was the scene-task scheduler's round-robin cursor (`dword_140D40948`) cycling, not a Wait
marker (turn-engine review). The task computes no damage and no turn owner.

behavior.text: calls `sub_140226E44` at `0x140229D28` (scene/UI refresh).

sets `word_1408082D0 = 2`; when `word_142FF3CA8` has bit 15 set, sets it to `0xC00` instead
  (`0x140229D55`).
clears `word_142FF3CA8` and sets `word_142FF3CAC = 1` (`0x140229D42`/`0x140229D4C`).

tail-jumps `sub_140228778(&word_1408081E0, 0, &a4+4, &unk_1407832A0)` at `0x140229D7C`; that
  routine is the battle message/event runner and calls `SceneTask_Terminate` at `0x1402290AE`.
no formula call, no result record write and no turn-owner write in this function.
the next unit is selected by the CT/turn engine (C2); this task only closes the presentation.

unlike record 3. Record 2 is also started by the turn-start state (`sub_140209218` case 2), so the same
task may cover both "wait for command" and "end turn"; live check needed.
