name: BattleUnit_BuildCursorRecord
purpose: Builds the seven-byte cursor record a unit contributes to the targeting display: slot and flags, level, terrain height and the tile the cursor should sit on.

behavior.text: the first argument is the seven-byte output record and the second is the unit slot; the record is cleared first.
a slot above 0x14, a unit marker of 0xFF at +1, unit +0x61 bit 0x40 or unit +0x62 bit 1 make it return with the cleared record.
out +0 is unit +0x4F, out +1 is unit +0x50, and out +2 combines bit 7 of unit +0x51 with bit 7 of the caller flags.
out +3 is the slot, with bit 0x20 set for every job outside the 94..96 monster range.
out +4 is 6 normally and 4 when unit +0x63 bits 1 and 2 are set; out +5 is the tile height from the map cell plus that base.
out +6 adds the same base to the height and is the final cursor height.
the map cell is found through the tile block at 0x140D8DCB0, indexed by the unit tile coordinates and the layer, at a stride of eight bytes.
the cell bytes +2 and +3 carry the terrain height and the low five bits of the move cost used in the adjustment.
the record is a cursor placement request, because the callers are the range, target and panel paths and the last byte is a screen height.
what the 0x20 bit in out +3 tells the caller beyond 'not a large monster'.

notes: Whole function read (492 bytes). The output layout is read from the writes; the semantic names of the height fields come from the cursor-range study.

name: BattleUnit_BuildJobRecord
purpose: Builds the 148-byte job record of battle unit `slot` for the battle panels: its job, levels and JP, through JobRecord_FromJobId.

behavior.text: for slot 0..20 the unit is g_PreviewUnitTable + 512 x slot; the job byte +3 is loaded at 0x1400FCFC9 and becomes the record's job id.

the 12 level bytes (+228), the 46 JP bytes (+240) and the 46 total JP bytes (+286) are copied into its own frame; in the first 20 words of the JP and total JP copies a value of 10000 or more becomes 9999; the source then points at these copies, with the unit's flags +6.
JobRecord_FromJobId(out, source) fills the record (name, level, JP).

notes: The level, JP and total JP copies in this frame cover the stock job entries only; a job index beyond them would address past the copies.

name: BattleUnit_RevealOnField
purpose: Puts a battle unit record that is off the field onto it, without building anything: the record must already exist.

behavior.text: when the record's slot byte (+1) is 0xFF: returns -1 if its on-field byte (+0x1B5) is not 0 (a dropped entry, 0xFF); otherwise sets +1 = the record index and +0x1B5 = 1 and, when the record's +5 has bits 0x30, adds its level (+0x29) to word_14114B0B4 and raises byte_140D405A2 to it when larger (a level sum and a level maximum). When +1 is not 0xFF it does nothing. Returns 0.

its two callers are ScenePreview_ShowEntry (for a parked entry: also queues its look, so a scene unit is built for it) and ScenePreview_ClaimForUnit (for a unit already drawn but not placed). Both are reached from the event interpreter (opcodes 0x44 and 0x45 among others), EventUnitBlock_RunTask, EventSubScript_RunTask, Battle_TurnStep and sub_140269DC4.

no code path found adds a battle record after load and deployment: the writers of the on-field byte are Battle_PlaceEntryUnits, Battle_BuildRosterTeam, Battle_AddJoinedUnit, Battle_RebuildUnitTable, the deployment steps, this function and one event-interpreter case that takes a unit off (slot byte 0xFF).

notes: So every unit a battle can show is one of its entry records (built at load) or a deployed party unit; event scripts reveal and hide them. Behavior: BattleUnitsAreFixedAtLoadAndRevealedLater. Cross-check notes: 0x29 and 0x30 are the `[..+29h]` read and the `test 30h` on +5; 0x44 and 0x45 are opcode numbers of the callers' paths, not constants of this body.

name: BattleUnit_SetStatusVisual
proto: int64 BattleUnit_SetStatusVisual(int statusPlus1, int on, int16 unitIndex)
callers: Battle_StatusApply, Battle_StatusRefresh, Battle_ApplyActionResult, Unit_SetChargeStateBits, Unit_ReloadFromJobRow, sub_140272874
purpose: Sets or clears a status's visual bits on the unit's scene object: the tint / pose word or the sprite-change word.

behavior.text: the first argument is the status id + 1 (Battle_StatusApply, Battle_StatusRefresh, Battle_ApplyActionResult, Unit_SetChargeStateBits and Unit_ReloadFromJobRow pass the bit index + 1 of the status sets at +0x61).

it writes the set / clear masks of the scene object (+0x164 / +0x16C for the word at +0x15C, +0x168 / +0x170 for +0x160) that SceneUnit_ApplyStatusVisuals applies; the mask is tbl_BattleStatusIconFlagMasks[status + 1].

special cases (by status id): 1 Crystal, 15 Chest, 21 Chicken and 22 Toad set bits 1, 8, 2, 4 of +0x160 (the effect sprites); 5, 17 and 19 go to +0x160 with the table mask; 9 and 31 do nothing; 22 also calls sub_1403167E4.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_1401FB064; the old sheet read the argument as the status id indexed + 1 inside: the entry code uses it as the index directly, and every caller adds the 1). The offsets +0x15C / +0x160 are reached through the set / clear mask fields (+0x164..+0x170, written here as dword indexes 89..92) and +0x61 is the status set of the callers, so neither appears as a literal in this body. The table index is not bounds-checked; the IDA item is 42 dwords (to 0x140673678) and the game passes 1..40.

name: BattleVoice_AssignPatterns
purpose: Gives a battle unit's voice controller its pattern, from the unit's job and name key.

behavior.text: the pattern id comes from Unit_GetVoicePatternId(job byte +3, name key +508, ...).

units whose byte +6 has bit 7 or bit 6 also use the shared controllers with patterns 100 or 101 (sub_1401ED240); patterns 102 and 103 are two more shared controllers (BattleControl +693224 and +693304).

notes: Name is ours.

name: BattleVoice_AssignSharedPattern
proto: void BattleVoice_AssignSharedPattern(void *battleControl, int slot, int pattern)
purpose: Sets the pattern of one shared voice controller.

behavior.text: calls BattleVoice_SetPattern for the shared controller (BattleControl +689112 + 136 * slot).

notes: Name is ours.

name: BattleVoice_IsSuppressed
purpose: Decides by sides whether a battle voice line is spoken: 0 speak, or a reason 1..5 to suppress (CharacterBattleVoiceController virtual, slot 5).

behavior.text: runs only when the BattleVoice row's side (+0x20) is non-zero; side 0 never suppresses.

with side_test_on_unit (+0x28) set the test is on one unit, the request's unit (request +12; the speaker itself when 0xFF): the same slot as the speaker returns 3; the same side ((unit +494 xor other +494) & 0x30 == 0) suppresses unless side is 2; the other side suppresses when side is 2.

with +0x28 clear the same side test runs over the request's target list (+24..+32): side 2 is spoken only when every target is on the speaker's side (else 5); otherwise it is spoken only when every target is on the other side (else 4).
the sides are read as bits 0x30 of unit byte +494.

notes: Name is ours. Vtable 0x140713F68.
open_questions: ? what fills request byte +12 (which unit the request names): the request builder was not found.

name: BattleVoice_ResolveLine
purpose: Resolves a BattleVoice line to the cue number to play, with the three replacement rules.

behavior.text: returns the row's cue (+8), or the cue of a replacement row: battle_voice (+0x10) when controller flag bit 0 is set (the speaker's VoicePattern flag), battle_voice_2 (+0x14) when bit 1 is set (patterns 100 / 101), battle_voice_3 (+0x18) when the controller's pattern id (+12) is 63.

notes: Name is ours.

name: BattleVoice_RollAndPlay
callees: NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, GlobalWork_GetFastForwardMode, sub_1401ED12C, sub_1401E8AF4, sub_1401ECF84, sub_14008FC68, sub_14009C034
purpose: Rolls the play chance of a voice line and plays it at once or queues it with its delay.

behavior.text: does nothing while the GlobalWork fast-forward mode (+88) is 1 or 2.
rolls a random number below 100 against the group chance (BattleVoiceGroupRate_Chance) and continues only when the roll is below it.
the cue is the id from BattleVoice_ResolveLine; with a delay (+0x1C) above about 0 it is queued with the delay on the controller's queue, otherwise it plays at once through sub_14009C034.

notes: Name is ours.

name: BattleVoice_SetPattern
purpose: Gives a voice controller its voice pattern: group key, flags and voice bank.

behavior.text: controller +12 = the pattern id; controller +8 bit 0 = the pattern row's flag byte (+0x14); bit 1 set for patterns 100 and 101; controller +16 = the pattern row's group key (+0xC, a BattleVoiceGroupRate key).
controller +24 = the voice bank resource opened from the pattern row's path (+8).

notes: Name is ours.

name: BattleVoice_Speak
purpose: Speaks a line unless the speaker's statuses forbid it (controller virtual, slot 3).

behavior.text: skips when the speaker's status bytes (unit +97..+101 bits) forbid speech; line 21 always passes.
otherwise calls BattleVoice_RollAndPlay.

notes: Name is ours.

name: BattleVoice_SpeakAbilityPhase
purpose: Picks the voice line of an ability from the Ability row's voice list by the request phase and speaks it.

behavior.text: the list is the Ability row's voice offset (+0x24) and count (+0x28); the entry is chosen by the request phase (+8): 3 and 4 give entries 0..1, 5 entry 0, 6 entry 1 or 2 by vtable slot 7, 7 and 8 entry 0 or 1.
a line that BattleVoice_UsesRows2And3 marks replaceable goes through BattleVoice_SpeakSwapped, others are played directly.

notes: Name is ours.

name: BattleVoice_SpeakSwapped
purpose: Speaks a replaceable line, swapped for row 3 or 2 by the request flags.

behavior.text: the line becomes 3 when request byte +65 is set, else 2 when request byte +64 is set, else stays; then it calls virtual slot 5 (BattleVoice_IsSuppressed) and, when not suppressed, slot 3 (BattleVoice_Speak).

notes: Name is ours.

name: BattleVoice_TickQueue
purpose: Counts down the delays of queued voice cues and plays the ones that are due.

behavior.text: subtracts the frame time from each queued (cue, delay) pair and plays a cue whose delay is at or below 0 through sub_14009C034.
called every frame from BattleControl_FrameUpdate.

notes: Name is ours.

name: BattleVoice_UsesRows2And3
purpose: Tells whether a voice line may be swapped for rows 2 or 3.

behavior.text: returns the BattleVoice row's replaceable byte (+0x29) as a truth value.

notes: Name is ours.

name: BattleVoiceGroupRate_Chance
purpose: Returns the play chance in percent of a voice line for the speaker's group.

behavior.text: takes the BattleVoiceGroupRate row of the controller's group key (+16) and the dword at +8 + 4 * k, where k is the line's chance_column (BattleVoice +0xC), when k is below 50; the result is capped at 100.

notes: Name is ours. Only +8 + 4k of the row is ever read.

name: BgmMode_BuildLists
purpose: Builds the two track lists of the music player screen from the BGMMode table.

behavior.text: clears the two lists (screen +840 and +872, 32 bytes apart), then for each BGMMode row appends the row id to the list at screen + 8 + 32 * (tab + 26), that is list 0 or 1 by the row's tab (+8).

notes: Name is ours. Cache qword_143CDA560.

name: BgmMode_DrawRow
callees: GUIComponentList_GetItemComponent, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, UIName_Key, GUINode_FindPartByName, GUITextNode_SetTextExpandedTemp, GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState
purpose: Draws one row of the music player list.

behavior.text: takes the track id from the current list (+824) and reads its BGMMode row; the title is the alternate title (+0xC) when the screen's title-language dword (+896) is 1, else the title (+0x10).

notes: Name is ours.

name: BgmMode_OnTabButton
purpose: Switches the music player's list when a tab button is pressed.

behavior.text: sets the current list index (screen +824) from the pressed tab button (button id - 100) and resizes the list gadget to that list.

notes: Name is ours.

name: BgmMode_PlaySelected
callees: GUIComponentList_GetItemComponent, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_1401C87A4, EventSoundEntry_Append, UIListGadget_RefreshVisible
purpose: Plays the track under the cursor of the music player.

behavior.text: takes the track id from the current list (+824), reads the BGMMode row and passes its sound (+0x14) to EventSoundEntry_Append.

notes: Name is ours.

name: BgmMode_SwitchTab
purpose: Moves the music player between its two lists on the tab input actions.

behavior.text: input actions 43 and 44 move the current list index (screen +824) between 0 and 1 (tab nodes +128 and +136).

notes: Name is ours.

name: BgmMode_ToggleTitleLanguage
purpose: Toggles the alternate track titles of the music player.

behavior.text: only when g_LanguageInfo +8 is 2 or 3 and action 195 is mapped: toggles the screen's title-language dword (+896), plays UI sound 0x12F, shows guide text 21012 or 21013 and refreshes the list.
language 2 is French and 3 German (registry TextLanguageCodes).

notes: Name is ours.

name: BitStream_ReadBits
purpose: MSB-first bit reader over the stream at `qword_143C49BF8`; the bit cursor is `dword_140906AAC`. `byte_142FF3CA7 = 1` resets the cursor to bit 7 of the first byte.

behavior.text: returns 0 if n == 0.
consumed bits advance the global cursor.
pattern 'bit k of a bitfield' = reset, read(k), then read(1) (used by Job_IsLockedForParty).

notes: Global state; not thread-safe.

name: BlendDesc_FromWords
proto: char BlendDesc_FromWords(_DWORD *desc, unsigned char count, unsigned char perTarget, unsigned int *words)
purpose: Unpacks packed render-target blend words into the Direct3D 12 blend description array of a pipeline state.

behavior.text: per target word w: BlendEnable = w & 1, BlendOp = ((w >> 1) & 7) + 1, SrcBlend = ((w >> 4) & 0x1F) + 1, DestBlend = ((w >> 9) & 0x1F) + 1, BlendOpAlpha = ((w >> 14) & 7) + 1, SrcBlendAlpha = ((w >> 17) & 0x1F) + 1, DestBlendAlpha = ((w >> 22) & 0x1F) + 1, RenderTargetWriteMask = (w >> 27) & 0xF; each target record is 40 bytes (10 dwords); the header holds the target count (a2) and independent-blend flag (a3 != 0 selects a per-target count).

notes: The packed words come from the draw state (state+0 for target 0) and from the program entries (+8...); the default UI draw state word0 is 0x79420a11 (ONE / INV_SRC_ALPHA).

name: BonusEntitlement_IsOwned
purpose: Answers whether the bonus entitlement of a SystemBonusEntitlement row is owned.

behavior.text: looks up the row by id, compares its entitlement code (+8) with the application's list and returns the matching node's owned byte (+33).

notes: Name is ours.

name: BonusEntitlements_Setup
callees: NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetEntryByIndex, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_14002620C, sub_140026BD4, memset, sub_140092BA0, sub_140027FEC
purpose: Builds the application's entitlement list from the SystemBonusEntitlement table and collects the bonus content paths of each entitlement.

behavior.text: for every row with a non-empty entitlement code (+8) a 40-byte list node at g_Application +1488 gets the code (bounded copy to node +16) and the row's byte +0x10 at node +34, unless the code is already listed.

the row's dlc_path_group (+0xC) is compared with the group number (+8) of every DLCPathList row (table 335): the table is walked row by row and is not looked up by key. The path strings (+4) of the matching rows are collected and passed to sub_140092BA0.
the platform check later sets node +33 (owned) for the codes it owns.

notes: Name is ours. In the stock data both rows that name a group use group 1, so a lookup by key would give the same row: the code compares groups.

name: Book_ShowGuide
purpose: Opens the guide that explains the reading shelf.

behavior.text: an id out of range calls UIGuide_Show(.., 0, 0); otherwise guide 15005 when the word at 0x1411A756E + 56 * id is above 0 (id below 5), else guide 15004.
the per-book word (5 books, 56-byte stride) is a progress or bookmark value; sub_1401662B0 reads it too.

open_questions: ? what the word at 0x1411A756E + 56 * id holds.

name: BookShelf_Fill
purpose: Fills the five slots of the Reading Materials shelf.

behavior.text: the input is {count; ids[5]; sort values[5]; bookmark bytes at +44}. A selection loop fills each slot with the unused book that has the smallest sort value (Book sort_order).
each slot gets its title (+0x14) and icon (+0x10, GuiImage_SetIconById) and 'ShowBookmark' / 'HideBookmark' from its bookmark byte; it ends with panel +1408 = count and sub_1401672A0.

name: Boot_MovieFrame
callees: Input_TestAction, sub_1400D8DDC, sub_14003ABD0, sub_14008757C, sub_14003E6D0, memmove, sub_14003E7C4, Boot_SetState, sub_1400D8B9C
purpose: Per-frame handler of the boot movie: ends it on the skip rules and copies the decoded frame into three textures.

behavior.text: ends the movie when g_GlobalWork +100 is set; or, with movie flag 0x8 set, when action 81 or 21 fires and the pause manager's state is not 9; or, with flag 0x8 clear, when the controller's result bit 0 is set; or when the player time (+1468) is past +1464.
ending calls Boot_SetState, destroys the MovieControl, sets flag 4 and calls sub_1400D8B9C.
it also copies the decoded frame planes into three textures.

notes: Name is ours.
open_questions: ? action 21 has no UIKeyAssign row in the stock data (action 81 is the confirm key).

name: BTurn_FinishUnit
purpose: Ends one unit's turn: clears the active flag and applies the post-turn CT bonus.

behavior.text: does nothing when the slot is empty (`unit[1] == 0xFF`) or the unit is not active (`unit[0x1B8] == 0`).

`dl = (unit[0x65] & 8) != 0` or (the record at `unit[0x1BC]` exists and its `+0x1B9 & 1` is set).
  Normally `+0x1BC` is the unit's own id (proved by `sub_140260ABC`), so `dl` = "moved".
`r9 = (unit[0x65] & 4) != 0` or `(unit[0x61] & 1) != 0` or `unit[0x1BA] != 0` ("turn given up").

`unit[0x1B8] = 0`; `ct = unit[0x41] + (dl ? 0 : 20) + (r9 ? 0 : 20)`; `unit[0x41] = min(ct, 60)`.
  So the bonus is 0, 20 or 40, capped at 60 (`0x1403106D9`-`0x1403106F8`, clamp immediate `0x3C`).
returns 1.

notes:
This is the only writer of the "active" byte `+0x1B8` besides the turn engine. The CT bonus explains why a unit that
just acted starts the next round at 20-60 CT rather than 0.
open_questions:
Why the developer chose 20/40: the flags `+0x65 & 8/4` and `+0x61 & 1` select the two "penalty" cases; their status
names are not identified.

name: BTurn_IsUnitDone
purpose: Decides whether the active unit has nothing left to do this turn, including the two-unit (partner) case.

behavior.text:
reads `unit[0x1B9] & 3` (move + action bits) through the record named by `unit[0x1BC]` (`0x140310738`);
  for normal units that id is the unit's own (V: `sub_140260ABC` compares `unit[0x1BC]` to the requested slot).

`cl` = `(unit[0x65] & 8) != 0` or that record has `+0x1B9 & 3 == 3`; `al` = the same "both bits" test or
  `unit[0x1BA] != 0`.

returns `cl && (unit[0x1BA] || sub_14030DD1C(unit)) && al` — i.e. both move and action done (or the pair
  equivalent), the turn given up flag, and the terrain/actionable check must all agree.

notes: The function is deliberately conservative: both units of a pair can keep the turn alive.
open_questions: The exact role of `sub_14030DD1C`'s return value (0/1/2) in the partner test.

name: BTurn_MarkActionDone
purpose: Records that a unit has used its action and ends the turn if the move was already used.

behavior.text: an empty slot (`unit[1] == 0xFF`) returns `-1`.
sets bit 1 of `unit[0x1B9]` (`|= 2`).
then calls `BTurn_IsUnitDone`; when true, `BTurn_FinishUnit(slot)` runs.
called from the post-move handler `sub_14020B90C` at `0x14020BBB9` when the unit also used an action.

notes:
Together with `BTurn_MarkMoveDone` this implements the "move + action, then turn ends" rule: the turn ends when
`+0x1B9 & 3 == 3`, when the partner has finished, or when `+0x1BA` is set.

name: BTurn_MarkMoveDone
proto: int __fastcall BTurn_MarkMoveDone(int slot, int moved, int ended)
purpose:
Records that a unit has finished its move (and/or given up its action) and ends the turn when everything required
is done.

behavior.text: an empty slot (`unit[1] == 0xFF`) returns `-1`.
`moved != 0` sets bit 0 of `unit[0x1B9]`.
`ended != 0` sets `unit[0x1BA] = 1`; if `unit[0x1B9]` was exactly 1 it becomes 3 (move done + turn given up).
then `BTurn_IsUnitDone(unit)` decides whether `BTurn_FinishUnit(slot)` runs (CT bonus + clear active flag).
the Wait path calls it with `(slot, 0, 1)`.

notes:
The name reflects the two call patterns: movement completion uses `moved=1`, Wait/end-of-turn uses `moved=0, ended=1`.
`BTurn_MarkActionDone` (`0x1403105B0`) is the sibling that sets bit 1.
open_questions:
Which caller sets `moved=1, ended=1` (the "move and act then end" path) — `sub_14020A7F0`/`sub_140210AF0` call it but
were not traced.

name: BTurn_OnTurnStartStatus
purpose:
Runs the per-turn status roll at the moment a unit is selected (after `CT % 100`): decides whether the turn is
consumed by a status and queues the pending status effects for the action block at `unit + 0x1BE`.

behavior.text: computes one LCG step (`xmmword_1408E5FC8`) for the random rolls.

if `unit[0x61] & 0x30 == 0x20` and `unit[0x63] & 0x20` is set: sets damage = `max HP / 10` (minimum 1),
  effect bytes `+0x1BE+8`, `+34`, `+36 = 32`, and returns 2.

when the unit is not being simulated (`g_BattleSimulating == 0`) and `unit[0x61] & 0x20 == 0`, it applies the
  pending status counters: `unit[0x75]` countdown, `unit[0x61] & 2` -> effect byte 2, `unit[43] < 10` -> poison-like
  flag, and returns 1 when any pending status was set.
when the status is "sleep/stop-like" (`unit[0x61] & 0x10`) and the RNG is odd, returns 2 with a queued effect.

the caller treats a non-zero result with bit 0 set as "consume the turn now" (`Battle_TurnEngine` returns
  `slot | 0x300`); a result of 2 lets the turn start normally with the effect queued.

notes:
The first argument (the CT remainder) is passed but not used in the paths read; the rolls come from the global LCG.
The Reraise test reads the effective status set.
open_questions: The exact status ids behind `unit[0x61] & 0x20` / `& 0x10` and the effect encoding at `+0x1BE` (C1/C4 territory).

name: BTurn_PreviewAction
proto: int BTurn_PreviewAction(UnitWorkRecord *unit, uint8_t *request, void *list, int flag)
purpose: Previews what a unit's pending action does to the turn order: applies the request in simulation mode, builds the timeline and puts the unit back as it was.

behavior.text: saves the unit's 20-byte action block (+0x1A0), the bytes +0x18D, +0x1EF, +0x1B9 and +0x1BA, and the simulate mode (g_BattleSimulating), then sets the simulate mode to 2.
calls BattleAction_ApplyRequest on the request; a result of 1 (or -1 when flag is 1) clears byte +0x18D.
builds the turn list with TurnList_Build in mode 3 and, unless it returned -1, fixes it up with sub_14030E2F0 using the unit's bytes +0x1BC and +0x18D.

restores the simulate mode, the four bytes and the action block; five status bytes are rebuilt as the OR of byte +0x57 + i and byte +0x1EF + i into +0x61 + i (the 0x61 is reached as +0x57 + 10 in a five-step loop) (what these two sources are was not read).

the unit's ability word at +0x1A2 holds the previewed ability only while the simulation runs (the block copy is restored afterwards); the reading rests on the restore of the saved block +0x1A0..+0x1B3, which holds +0x1A2 (the word itself is not named in the body), not on a check of the word.

notes: The name is the IDB's (BTurn_PreviewAction); read 2026-11-10. 355 bytes, read whole. It recomputes +0x61 = +0x57 | +0x1EF after putting +0x1EF back (a five-byte loop from the +0x57 base: +10 and +408 from it).
open_questions: ? what bytes +0x57..+0x5B and +0x1EF..+0x1F3 are (the status OR at the end); what +0x1BC and +0x18D are.

name: BTurn_QueueInvisibilityEnd
purpose: Queues the removal of Invisibility from a unit whose turn has ended, when the other conditions hold.

behavior.text: returns 0 when the unit row is empty, or the unit is Crystal, KO or Jumping (mask 0x64 of +97) or Stone or Chest (mask 0x81 of +98).

otherwise points g_BattleActingUnit and g_BattleActionBlock at the unit and its result block, resets the result block (Battle_ResultReset), and when the turn-ended byte +442 is set, bit 0x10 of the battle-applied byte +497 (Invisibility, id 19) is set and +0x2E is not zero, it sets the pending-remove byte at block +36 to 0x10 and the result flag at block +39 to 8.
returns the result flag at block +39 (0 when nothing was queued).
+0x2E is the byte Battle_StatusApply clears when it applies Invisibility; what it counts is not decoded.

notes: Name is ours.

name: BTurn_QueueTerrainPoison
purpose: Queues Poison for a unit that stands on a harmful terrain tile and passes the filter of the status rules.

behavior.text: returns 0 when the unit row is empty, or the unit is Crystal, KO or Jumping (mask 0x64 of +97), Stone or Chest (mask 0x81 of +98), or its +0x1B4 bit 0x40 is set.
returns 0 when the unit is Float (bit 0x40 of +99); for a unit whose +0x1B4 is negative the Float test is made on the unit named by the low five bits of +0x1B4 instead.

points g_BattleActingUnit and g_BattleActionBlock at the unit and its result block, resets the result block, then reads the terrain flags of the unit tile (tile table at g_BattleTileTable, layer bit 7 of +81, x +79, y +80) through the 64-entry table at 0x14067F750 + 64; returns 0 when its bit 0x80 is clear.

otherwise sets the pending-add byte at block +32 to 0x80 (Poison, id 24), runs Status_FilterPendingSets(0) and returns 0 when the filter leaves nothing; else sets the result flag at block +39 to 8 and returns 1.
bit 0x80 of that table is the poisonous terrain flag (it is the only gate on the tile).

notes: Name is ours. The terrain flag table at 0x14067F750 is reached through an image-base-relative address built in the code, so the address does not appear as an operand.
open_questions: ? which terrain types carry the flag (the table at 0x14067F750 has not been mapped).

name: BTurn_StatusFlags
purpose:
Returns the turn-scheduling flags of one unit work record: whether it can act at all, and whether Haste/Slow modify
its CT increment.

behavior.text:
returns bit 0 (`1`) when the slot is empty (`unit[1] == 0xFF`), when `sub_140278FA8(unit, 3) != 0`, or when
  `unit[0x1B4] & 0x40` is set. The turn engine skips such units in the CT tick and in selection.

returns `6` when `unit[0x61] & 0x20` is set (a "cannot be selected" status; the engine then treats the unit as
  not acting this pass).
`0x10` is returned when `unit[0x64] & 0x08` is set; the engine multiplies speed by 1.5 on it (Haste).
`0x20` is returned when `unit[0x64] & 0x04` is set; the engine halves speed on it (Slow).

an extra `0x0A` is OR-ed in when `unit[0x65] & 0x10` is set. No caller in the paths read tests those bits; their

`sub_140278FA8(unit, 3)` is the same guard used by the event/unit code for "unit is gone".

name: ButtonIcon_Draw
proto: long ButtonIcon_Draw(short group, short x, short y, short pressed, short disabled, char flag)

purpose: Draws one animated button icon: the sprite pieces of an icon group with a press animation.

behavior.text: keeps a press step per icon group (0..6): disabled resets it to 0, pressed sets it to 1, a running step 1..5 advances by one each call, then it falls back to 0.

the piece range of the group is [start[group], start[group + 1]) from the group start list of the current text language; the pieces come from the piece table and the scale pairs from the scale table of the same language (0 uses its own tables with 81 pieces, 1 / 2 / 3 use 80 pieces).

per piece: draw size = |size * scale| >> 12 (a horizontal scale above 4100 adds 2 pixels), source rectangle from the piece, position = icon position + piece offsets, mirror bits from the sign of the scales; the piece is queued with the sprite queue routine.
the step selects the texture page words that show the pressed look (three page values are used).

name: Camera_UpdateMatrices
callers: vtable faith::Graphics::Object::Camera (slot 0x140720AF8), called each frame by the scene update
callees: sub_1400AE0C0, sub_1403BFCD4, sub_1403BFEDC, sub_1403BFFDC, sub_1400AD6E8, sub_1400AF784, sub_1403C2390, sub_1403C0994, tanf, Camera_UpdateSecondaryView
purpose: Per-frame update of a render camera (vftable faith::Graphics::Object::Camera slot at 0x140720AF8): rebuilds its view matrix, projection matrix, view-projection matrix, inverses, and sets a 'changed' flag when anything moved.

behavior.text: cam+16 is the camera's scene node (position / orientation read by sub_1400AE0C0 and sub_1403BFCD4); cam+24 selects the render target slot (renderer qword_143CDA098 + 6584 byte index, then the 4-entry table at +56) whose byte +4652 ('idle') drives the dirty logic: bytes cam+3343 (changed), +3344 (previous idle), +3345 (may-compare), +3339, +3732 (force-dirty request set by sub_1403A2774 from the frame update).

every matrix is stored as 12 floats in 16-float slots (the 4th column is skipped when copying) and compared with the previous value by sub_1403BFEDC, which is true when |a - b| <= 1.1920929e-7 (FLT_EPSILON) for the 12 elements; any difference ORs 1 into cam+3343 (only when cam+3345 is set). The position (cam+32..40) is compared the same way.

fov = cam+3284 (radians), aspect = cam+3288, near = cam+3292, far = cam+3296, ortho size = cam+3300, flags cam+3332 (reverse depth), cam+3333 (orthographic), cam+3346 (finite far). Orthographic: m00 = 2 / (S * aspect), m11 = 2 / S (S = cam+3300), m22 = 1 / (far - near) (negated and m32 = -near / (far - near) when reverse depth), m33 = 1.0. Perspective: m11 = 1 / tan(fov / 2) (tanf), m00 = m11 / aspect, m23 = -1.0, depth terms from far / (far - near) when cam+3346 is set, else the infinite-far form m22 = 0 (or -1 reversed), m32 = -near.

view = the 12-float block at cam+48 filled by sub_1403BFCD4 from a constant 4x3 identity template (dword_140906C60..C98) and the camera node; viewProj at cam+176 = sub_1400AD6E8(view, proj) ; inverse of the view at cam+240 (sub_1403BFFDC); cam+304 / cam+368 hold sub_1403C2390 results (4x4 copies of the view/proj, ?); cam+848 gets a third matrix built from the negated translation of cam+288 (the world-to-camera of the translation part only, I); cam+432 receives sub_1403C0994(cam+112) (the projection's extra form, ?). It finishes by calling Camera_UpdateSecondaryView (sub_1403A5ECC).
the orthographic branch is what the UI layers use; nothing here rounds or snaps a value to pixels, so a UI text quad is placed by the projection exactly as the float matrices give it.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403A5674). Runs once per frame per camera, not per glyph. The flag meanings of +3332 / +3333 / +3346 are inferred from which maths branch they select (reverse depth, orthographic, finite far).
open_questions: ? which camera / which of the 4 render targets the Job Tree uses and its ortho size (S); ? the exact roles of cam+304 / +368 / +432 / +848; ? what sets +3732.

name: Camera_UpdateSecondaryView
purpose: Tail of Camera_UpdateMatrices: builds the second view (the one belonging to the render target object at target+32), its view-projection and inverse, with the same epsilon dirty tracking.

behavior.text: reads the target object (renderer +6584 index, table at +56), takes its node at target+32 (sub_1400AE0C0), negates the three translation floats (v67..69 * -1.0), multiplies it with the camera view cam+48 (sub_1400AF420) and stores the 12 floats at cam+656; compares with the previous copy (sub_1403BFEDC) and ORs the changed flag into cam+3343 when cam+3345 is set.
cam+720 = sub_1400AD6E8(thatView, cam+656, proj cam+112) (view-projection of the second view); cam+784 = sub_1403BFFDC(cam+656) (its inverse), again compared with the previous values.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403A5ECC). Every operation is whole-frame matrix maths, nothing per glyph.
open_questions: ? what the object at target+32 is (a second camera node, perhaps the previous-frame or the shadow view); sub_1400AF420 is read as a 4x3 multiply (I) but was not decompiled.

name: Camera_UploadSceneConstants
callees: sub_1400AE0C0, sub_1400AF420, sub_1400AD6E8, sub_1403BFEDC, sub_1403BFFDC, sub_1403C043C, sub_1403C19A8, sub_1403C1E1C, sub_1403C00F4, sub_1403C0E70, sub_1403C2390, sub_140028B10, sub_14003E120, sub_14003E228, memmove
purpose: Second camera vtable function (0x140720B00): updates the camera-relative origin, the double-buffered matrix history, and writes the 1040-byte scene constant block (matrices current and previous) into a mapped GPU constant buffer.

behavior.text: copies 12 floats from target+848.. (dwords a2[212..226]) to cam+3544 and flags a change (FLT_EPSILON compare, sub_1403BFEDC) when different; the same compare is done for the origin triple at cam+3672 (from *(rdx+288..296)) and the camera node position cam+16 +64..72.

d = nodePos(+64,+68,+72) - cam+3672 (origin offset); the translation columns written to cam+3656.. are d (float subtraction), so rendering is done relative to a re-based origin (keeps float precision).

the byte pair cam+3340 / +3341 / +3342 is a double buffer (current / previous matrix set): when the target is not idle (target+4652 == 0), anything changed, or cam+3733 is set, the index is toggled (3341 = old 3340, 3340 ^= 1, 3342 = new). Matrices are stored in 1040-byte records at cam+1168 + 1040 * index (view, viewProj, projection, their inverses, previous-frame forms, light / shadow direction from cam+80..88 via sub_140028B10 (a vector normalise, I) and the extra 128-byte block from sub_1403C0E70 at +2000).

finally maps the camera's constant buffer (sub_14003E120(*(cam+3248), mode 2) = write-discard map), copies both 1040-byte records (current at +0, previous at +520), appends sub_1403C043C-transposed 4x4s at +2080 / +2144 (cam+3352 and cam+3480 matrices), and unmaps (sub_14003E228).
the transposes (sub_1403C043C) are the row-major to HLSL column-major conversion for the matrices uploaded to the shader.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403A6240). Pure per-frame camera upload; the ~900 line decompile was read for structure and the constants above, the matrix algebra of each 4x4 (which order, which transpose) was not followed element by element.
open_questions: ? the layout of the 1040-byte scene record (which offset is view, projection, jitter); ? whether any jitter / sub-pixel offset is added to the projection (none was seen in these functions); ? the Job Tree camera's origin offset.

name: CardSlot_IsValid
purpose: Tests that a slot of the cache starts with the `SC` magic: returns 0 when valid, -1 otherwise.

behavior.text: in ENHANCED mode (or when `dword_140D405B4 == 0`) the slot is `g_SaveSlotCache + 40164 * slot`; byte 0 must be 83 ('S') and byte 1 must be 67 ('C').
with CLASSIC mode and the card layer on, slot 0 maps to `g_SaveAutoSlot` (0x142E75DF8), whose magic word this function sets to 17235 ('SC') itself; other slots shift down by one.

notes: Written in the 2026-10-29 integration pass from the J7, J8, J9 and W0 research reports; each address was re-checked against the decompile.

name: CharaAnim_ReadStep
proto: char CharaAnim_ReadStep(CharaAnimState *a, float *delay, int *opcode, unsigned char *value)
purpose: Reads one step of an animation from the unit's sequence table: row (animation id, step) -> opcode, value and delay.

behavior.text: the sequence class is byte_140673301[4 * shape] (0..7); each class owns one nxd table (loaded by id 108, 112, 113, 114, 248, 115, 116, 117 in class order) cached in qword_143CD9FE8..; I: these are CharAnimSeq0..7.
the row is found by key = animation id (a+56) and key2 = step (a+60); output: opcode = row dword +8, value = row byte +12, delay = float(row byte +13).
CharAnimSeq0/1 key 2, step 0 -> opcode 1 (show frame), value 2: the pose the tree uses shows frame 2 (CharAnimSeq2 gives 2 for key 2 as well).

notes: The classic SEQ file is zero-based (anim 2 = frame 1); the nxd tables are one-based, so animation id 2 means frame 2.

name: CharaAnim_Step
callers: CharaSlot_SetParams (tail jump), sub_1400D4CB0, itself (recursion on a command that needs a second step)
purpose: Advances the slot's classic SEQ animation by one command and, for a frame command, makes sure its atlas texture is loaded (CharaRender_LoadCheck).

behavior.text: reads the next (opcode, delay, frame) from the sequence data with sub_1400CC6C0; opcode 1 = show a frame (checks the 44-byte frame cache at renderer+47152), 118 = shift the x offset by a signed byte, 144 = restart the sequence, 149.. = small x offset steps (+1/+2/-1/-2) with the flag word set to 0x800000; other opcodes are not decoded.

notes: This renderer (the menus and the job tree) reads its steps from the per-class movement tables through CharaAnim_ReadStep, not from the classic animation file; those tables hold movement animations only (see UnitMovementAnimationTables).

name: CharaColorSkin_Resolve
callers: PreviewUnit_BuildRecord, PreviewUnit_BuildSpriteRecord, Unit_GetSpriteSetId, sub_1400FD0E4, sub_1401009E8, sub_140125F38, sub_1401E3A10, sub_1402AC520
purpose: Resolves a CharCLUT chara_color_skin value to the skin to use.
