notes: Name is ours.

name: CharaName_GetDisplayName
callers: about 22 callers (party lists, turn panel, battle messages, errand screens, save import)
purpose: Returns the display name of a name key: the CharaName table's name, or the unit's own stored name string when the row says so.

behavior.text: returns the name of the CharaName row of the key, or the unit's own name string when row byte +0x14 (column own_name) is non-zero and the passed string is not empty (copied with sub_1401E8CD8, length 8 or 16 by the language in g_LanguageInfo).
returns 0 for key 0 or a missing row.
the callers (not this body) pass (save record +0x230, +0xDC) or (work +508, +332); about 22 callers (party lists, turn panel, battle messages, errands, save import).

name: CharaPalette_LoadClassic
purpose: Fills a 256-colour palette (16 palettes of 16 colours) for a sprite shape from the shape's classic sprite file, then lets the shape's colour-override rows adjust it. The atlas builder calls it to get a unit's default colours.

behavior.text: picks one of two identical {file kind, size} pair tables (indexed by shape) depending on the language info flag at +8 (0 selects the second table, a missing language record selects the first).
allocates a scratch buffer of the table's size, reads the file with GameData_ReadSectors(kind, 0, size) and returns null if the allocation fails.

copies the first 0x200 bytes of the file into the palette as 256 16-bit values. Every odd-numbered byte (the high byte of each colour) gets bit 0x80 set, except byte 1 of each 32-byte palette, so colour 0 of every palette stays without the opaque bit.
then calls CharShape_ApplyClut(shape, pal) and releases the scratch buffer.
the 16-bit values are BGR555 with the opaque flag in bit 15, matching the converter used by the atlas builder.
has no direct caller other than CharaRender_BuildAtlasTexture (and a function-pointer table slot).

notes:
Both kind tables hold one {kind, size} pair per shape; sizes are multiples of 2048 (disc sector size).

No bound on the shape here (V): the row is read at table + 8 * shape. A row with size 0 allocates nothing to read and leaves the scratch buffer unread. CharShape_ApplyClut takes the shape as a byte.

name: CharaPalette_ReloadForShape
callees: GameData_ReadSectors, sub_14026E194, sub_14026E2C0, sub_14026E484, SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry, sub_1402F3888, sub_1402F3A04
purpose: Step function that walks the look queue and, for each entry, loads its frame file, its sequence file and its classic sprite file, then builds the scene unit; returns 0 when the queue is done, 1 or 2 while work remains.

behavior.text: the state is a pass (0 frame file, 1 sequence file, 2 sprite file and unit build), a step inside the pass and the entry index, all in the block at 0x140CE3240.

pass 0 reads attribute byte 0 of the entry's sprite (table 0x673300 + 4 * sprite); when it is 5 or more and differs from the last one loaded it reads the file named by the row of that value in the table at 0x140785130 or its twin at 0x140785180.
pass 1 does the same with attribute byte 1 and the tables at 0x140784610 and 0x1407845B0.

pass 2 replaces a sprite above 170 by 1, scans the 15 look pool records for a byte +1 equal to it (a hit skips the file read), otherwise reads the classic file named by the table at 0x140784690 (language flag 0: 0x140784BE0) through GameData_ReadSectors.
in step 2 of pass 2 it calls SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry with the queue entry's fields and the file buffer, and then sub_14026E194 three times.
after the sprite pass of an entry it moves to the next entry; it returns 0 when the entry index reaches the queue count.

its step machine (0x140CE3240: pass, step, entry index; buffer 0x140CE3250) returns 0 once the entry index reaches g_LookQueueCount, 1 or 2 otherwise; its files are read with GameData_ReadSectors, which is synchronous (MemFile_Read; it clears the pending flag the high dword of qword_141856AB0 itself). The mid-battle join runs it once per frame until 0.

load step 2 stores a queue word above 170 back as 1 (stock clamp) and tests the word against byte +1 of all 15 look pool records, claimed or not (the loop over 0x140D005A1 in steps of 0x32D6), reading no classic file when one matches; the scene unit is then built from whatever data the record its build uses holds. It passes the load queue entry's word +6 to SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry as the sprite, so a scene unit's shape is the queue word.

notes:
The file tables are reached by lea of their addresses in the pass-2 branch (IDA: 0x14026FD5C, 0x14026FD69), the others the same way in passes 0 and 1. The sprite number is read as a 16-bit word from the queue entry, so the look pool and the file tables see the global number. The name was already in the IDB with the comment 'unstudied'; this sheet replaces it.

The pass-2 clamp loads 0xAA into ecx at 0x14026FD05 for a signed word compare (jump if less or equal): 170 itself passes and reads row 170, past the stock tables (the next table's row 0). LookQueue_Add already replaces 170 and up by 1, so in stock the clamp never fires.

The pass-2 hit test reads byte +1 of every pool record, claimed or not, so a sprite number names the same graphics for as long as any record holds it (the battle setup sub_140210AF0 clears +1 of all records at its start; LookPool_ResetForBattleLoad does not).
open_questions: ? the use of the two-value sub-step of pass 0 and 1 (counters at 0x140CE3240).

name: CharaRender_BuildAtlasTexture
proto: void *CharaRender_BuildAtlasTexture(__int64 unused, int width, unsigned shape, int which, short palA, short palB, int flags)
callees: sub_1403D2450, sub_1403D25D8 (pack read), sub_14026E750 / sub_14026C530 (default palettes), sub_1402F3888 / sub_1402F40C4 / sub_1402F3A04 (palette overlays), Rgb555ToRgba8888, sub_1403D0898 / sub_1403D0A80 / sub_1403D0B10 (texture create/upload/finish), sub_140011750 / sub_140011804 (alloc/free)
purpose: Builds the unit's atlas texture: loads the shape's sprite file from the FFT pack, applies the 16-colour palette (with optional colour offsets), and expands the 4-bit pixels into a 512 x 512 RGBA texture.

behavior.text: file index = dword_1407151F0[shape] + which (which = 0/1: two textures per slot); shapes 155..158 use index 160 + which; flag bits 0x8000000 -> 1146, 0x60000000 -> 154, 0x10000000 -> 156 pick other sheets. The file is read through the pack (sub_1403D2450/sub_1403D25D8) into a 1 MB buffer. V (data): the index is the g2d.dat entry number: entry n is a 131072-byte (512 x 512, 4 bpp) sheet and entry n + 1 a 118784-byte (512 x 464) sheet, together the 2x redrawn HD version of the classic 256 x 488 sheet.

palette entries are RGB555 (PSX); flag-selected modes (v30 = 4: add per-channel offsets; 5: 4-bit channels with offsets, I: a darkened variant; 6: grey (r + 3g + 2b)/6) clamp at 31 and keep colour 0 transparent; with no flags the offsets are 0 and the palette passes through unchanged; then Rgb555ToRgba8888 turns each into RGBA8888.

texture = 512 rows x 256 source bytes (each byte = two 4-bit pixels, low nibble first, expanded through a 256-entry pair table), uploaded with sub_1403D0A80(tex, buf, 512, 512, 32 bpp): the sheet is exactly one g2d entry, indexed 4 bpp with the unit palette applied here.
the default palette comes from CharaPalette_LoadClassic(shape, ...) (classic sprite file palette plus the shape's colour-override rows via CharClut_ApplyToPalette).
a shape above 169 gets no sheet entry (index -1) unless a flag bit selects a special sheet; with no entry the function returns null.

its tint lines are the battle rule's (UnitClut_TintRow): flag bit 0 grey; bit 1 grey with offsets 3, -1, 8; bit 2 plain with red + 8; bit 3 halved with green + 8; bit 4 halved with blue + 8; bit 5 halved with -4; bit 6 halved with -8; bit 7 (not for shapes 139 and 140) halved with 4, 0, 5; each channel limited to 0..31 and blue 1 for a colour that came out black.

both of its outputs are 32-bit: the 16 converted colours (Rgb555ToRgba8888) and the 512 x 512 buffer handed to TextureObj_SetSource with depth 32. So the 16-colour limit of the menus is this expansion and nothing after it.

notes:
The pixels come from the HD sheets in g2d.dat, NOT from the classic 0002.pac sheets; quad UVs are classic px / 256, so one classic px spans 2 texels. The palette is the classic sheet's RGB555 palette (colours checked against retail).

The shape argument is unsigned 32-bit and the bound is an unsigned compare with 0xA9 at 0x1400CE263 (V): a shape above it takes the -1 path (no sheet unless a flag picks one). The menu record and the renderer slot cache hand the shape over as 32 bits, so this is the menu path's only look-number bound here.

The palette loaders are CharaPalette_LoadClassic, CharShape_ApplyClut and CharClut_ApplyToPalette.
open_questions: Where the engine takes the 16 palette rows from (the classic .spr palette or a default table: sub_14026E750) was matched by colour, not traced (?).

name: CharaRender_DrawFrame
callees: CharaRender_BuildAtlasTexture, CharaRender_LookupLutParams, CharaRender_LutUvForQuad, CharaRender_SubmitQuads, sub_1403CC7C0 (set shader), sub_1403CCF24 (viewport), sub_14003F794
purpose: Renders one unit slot's current animation frame into its 256 x 256 target: builds the atlas textures and LUT cell on demand, turns the frame's rectangles into quads and submits them twice (outline pass, then colour pass).

behavior.text: the frame cache entry is renderer+47152 + 44*slot; it must have flag 1 (frame loaded). Flag 2 = atlases built (CharaRender_BuildAtlasTexture for which = 0 and 1), flag 8 = LUT cell chosen, flag 4 = drawn this frame.

LUT cell (stored per slot at renderer+58424 + 40*slot): x = request byte +28 (a negative value means 2), y = request byte +29 (negative means 2); the entry's flag word (+47164) adds 5 (bit 2), 15 (bit 8) or 10 (bit 4) to x. The tree's flag word is 0, so its cell is (2, 2).
LUT parameters (region size floats, offset shorts) come from CharaRender_LookupLutParams; the per-quad LUT UVs from CharaRender_LutUvForQuad.
quad scale = target config scale (2.0) x 512 / 256 = 4 target px per classic px; ground point = config (128, 192); quad UVs are classic sheet px / 256 (corner + 0.5), clamped to 1.0.

the frame index is the value from CharaAnim_ReadStep (entry +47160); frame records come from the pre-parsed SHP tables (one table per shape class, class stride 1668 words, 8-byte frame pointers, up to 208 frames); each 7-byte rectangle record gives x, y, w/h bytes, source u/v and mirror flags (bit 2 mirrors x about the ground, bit 4 mirrors y).
vertices (80 bytes, 6 per rectangle) get vertex colour 1.0; the pass uses shader id 1014 (SHADER_ID_REFINED_CHARA_PARTS) and a 256 x 256 viewport (set from renderer+75832).
two CharaRender_SubmitQuads calls follow: the first with the outline flag, the second without.

notes: Constants: docs/reference/sprite-pipeline.md. The studio carries a software model of this draw path.
open_questions: The 8-bit frame-record fields (size code to w/h, mirror semantics) were matched to the classic SHP format rather than traced byte by byte (?).

name: CharaRender_FrameCacheUpdate
purpose: Keeps the 44-byte frame cache entry of a slot in step with the current request (shape, palettes, frame, flags): a changed request invalidates the atlases or the whole frame.

behavior.text: entry = r + 47152 + 44 * id: flags (+0, bit 0 = valid, bit 1 = atlases built, bit 2 = drawn, bit 3 = LUT cell chosen), then copies of the request fields (shape +4, frame +8, flag word +12, shape id +16 ...).

if the shape, frame, palette or flag fields differ, flag bits are reset (atlases kept when only the frame or flags changed: value 2 / 9 in the low flag bits); the request is copied into the entry and flag 1 is set.

open_questions: Which request field each entry offset holds is only partly mapped (?).

name: CharaRender_InitTargets
proto: __int64 CharaRender_InitTargets(CharaRendererState *s, short size, short groundX, short groundY)
purpose: Creates the per-slot render targets and vertex buffers (256 slots) and stores the target geometry used by the draw.

behavior.text: stores size, ground x, ground y at +75832, +75834, +75836; the renderer init (sub_1400D4648) passes 256, 128, 192 (config struct values 256 / 128 / 192, scale 2.0 float).
for each of 256 slots creates a size x size texture (sub_1403D1498) and its render target, plus a 16-byte state and a vertex buffer; then loads the six default colour tables for the current language.

name: CharaRender_LookupLutParams
callees: sub_1403D325C (table by id), sub_1403D3AE8 (row by key), sub_1403D2FD8
purpose: Looks up the per-shape rows that drive a unit's shadow size and LUT region: shape row -> shadow-size row and LUT-parameter row.

behavior.text: shape row (nxd table id 174, I: CharShape; columns at row +8 shadowsize Id1, +12 CLUT id, +16 lutparam Id1, +20 shadowsize Id2, +24 lutparam Id2, +28 lutparam Id3, +32 lutparam Id4).
with cfg byte 0 = 0 it uses shadowsize Id1 (+8) and lutparam Id1 (+16); with cfg byte 0 set, Id2 (+20 / +24); with cfg byte 2 set and byte 1 clear, lutparam Id3 (+28, byte 2 < 2) or Id4 (+32).

shadow size row (I: CharShapeShadowSize, id 176) +8 -> cfg +4; LUT parameter row (I: CharShapeLUTParam, id 217) +8 / +12 floats -> cfg +8 / +12, +16 / +18 shorts -> cfg +16 / +18; shape row bytes +45 / +46 -> cfg +3 / +20.

notes: Column order matches the CharShape table of the studio's base database (tic_base.sqlite); every generic job shape (96..133) has lutparam Id1 = 2 -> CharShapeLUTParam row 2 = (0.375, 0.45, 0, -6).
open_questions: Table id to name links are inferred from row layouts (I).

name: CharaRender_LutUvForQuad
proto: void CharaRender_LutUvForQuad(__int64 unused, LutSlot *s, char a3, char a4, short rect[4], float uv[...])
purpose: Computes the LUT texture coordinates at the four corners of a unit quad: the sprite is laid over a small region of the LUT sheet (width/height from CharShapeLUTParam) at the slot's LUT cell.

behavior.text: inputs: rect = (left, top, right, bottom) as 16-bit classic px relative to the unit's ground point; region W = s+28 float x 64, H = s+32 float x 64; offsets P = short s+36, Q = short s+38; cell x = short s+8, y = short s+12 (pairs for a second LUT at s+16 / s+20).
u = (P + x) / W clamped to [-0.9, 0.9] for left and right; v = -(Q + a4 + y) / H clamped to [-0.4, 1.4] for top and bottom.
U = clamp01((u + 2 * cellX + 1) / 64), V = clamp01(1 - (v + 2 * cellY + 0.5) / 64), so a texel position is 128 * U, 128 * V in the 128 x 128 LUT sheet.
corners (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) are written for LUT 1 and LUT 2 into interleaved float slots of the vertex scratch.

notes: The studio carries a software model of this (its lut_corner_uv routine). The rect argument is four 16-bit words (the decompiler shows ints).

name: CharaRender_PlaceSlotImage
callees: sub_14003E5D8 and sub_14003E604 (texture width/height), GUINode_SetPosition, sub_1403EF6B4, sub_1403EF704
purpose: Points the slot's UI image node at the unit's render texture and sizes/positions it: size = texture size x (slot scale +60 / entry scale +12), offset from the entry's anchor.

behavior.text: texture handle comes from renderer+70708 + 4*id into the engine texture table qword_143CD9F20; width/height from sub_14003E5D8/E604.
the node gets the texture at node+208, position (GUINode_SetPosition) from the slot anchor + entry offsets - scaled anchor, size (sub_1403EF6B4) from the texture size and pivot (sub_1403EF704).

scale s = slot+60 (default 1.5, set by sub_1400ED768) divided by the config scale (entry +12, 2.0); node width = texture width x s x dword_1407DC468, node height = texture height x s, pivot = (config x x s x dword_1407DC468, config y x s) (read from the assembly).

dword_1407DC468 is the unit image's pixel aspect factor: 1.0 when dword_142E7FCA0 = 0, 1.1408199 when it is non-zero (sub_1401E7BA4 / sub_140255DEC); the default init sets dword_142E7FCA0 = 1, so in normal play the sprite is 14.08% wider than tall. Measured on retail: horizontal scale 1.10..1.15 of the vertical one.

notes: The tree's gadget image therefore shows the unit's render texture through the UI image sampler.
open_questions: The exact k for the tree panels was not evaluated; the studio uses a measured 2.5 x 2.2 (docs/reference/sprites.md).

name: CharaRender_RegisterSlot
callers: JobTree_SetPanelRecord and about thirteen other screen builders (job change list, unit status, party screens: sub_140114D74, sub_1401151EC, sub_14011545C, sub_140119108, sub_14011C4EC, sub_14011C940, sub_140123170, sub_140125C88, sub_140131E4C, sub_14013BF8C, sub_14013C238, sub_14013FAB0, sub_140142884)
purpose: Registers a UI image node as the display for one unit render slot and applies the first sprite request.

behavior.text: runs CharaRender_SetSlotRequest(r); on success resets the 112-byte slot entry at m + 14920 + 112 * id (sub_1400ED768), stores the node, the id (+56), a request flag (+80 = r.flags & 1), and for a non-null node the placement defaults x offset -8 (+84), width 84 (+92), height 128 (+96), then runs CharaRender_PlaceSlotImage.
sub_1400ED768 defaults: slot scale +60 = 1.5, y offset +52 = -28, id +56 = -1.

notes: Slot ids: the tree uses panel index + 80.

name: CharaRender_SetSlotRequest
callers: CharaRender_RegisterSlot and about nine screen builders (sub_1401199CC, sub_14011BF0C, sub_14011C940, sub_14012FC6C, sub_140132DC8, sub_140132E1C, sub_14014386C, ...)
callees: CharaSlot_SetParams, CharaRender_PlaceSlotImage, sub_1400CC52C (release slot), sub_1400CCAF8 (clear entry)
purpose: Writes one unit-preview request (slot id, shape, palette, pose, flags) into the global unit renderer's 92-byte slot entry and restarts its animation when the request changed.

behavior.text: slot id r[0] <= 0xFF; the renderer is qword_143CC96B8, its slot array at +148144 (92 bytes each: +16 live flag, +24 id, +28 shape).

shape 0x9B/0x9D/0x9E are special (a8 = 96 / 48, pose 42) and shapes flagged in byte table unk_140673302 turn pose 6/7 into 12/13; otherwise r[6] is the pose/animation id (V: tree records carry 2: SpriteRecord_Fill derives it from word_140672D7A[0]).
forwards (palette r.u16[4], r.u16[5], r[5], r[3] flags, r.b[28], r.b[29], a8, pose) to CharaSlot_SetParams, then repositions the slot image with CharaRender_PlaceSlotImage.

open_questions: Meaning of pose 2 is not decoded: the empirical best frame is type1 frame 2 (docs/reference/sprites.md).

name: CharaRender_SubmitQuads
proto: unsigned int CharaRender_SubmitQuads(__int64 rt, __int64 target, unsigned first, const void *verts, int count, unsigned atlasTexId, unsigned lutTexId, char outlinePass)
callees: sub_14003E120, sub_14003E228, sub_1403D0694 (constants), sub_1403D0538 (draw), memmove, memset
purpose: Binds the atlas (slot 0) and the LUT texture (slots 1..3), sets sampler words and pass constants, copies the quad vertices into the vertex ring and queues the draw.

behavior.text: texture slots: t0 = atlas, t1..t3 = the LUT texture (arg a7).

sampler words: slot 0 = default word with bits 6..9 cleared; slots 1..3 = default word with bits 6 and 9 set (0x240), top bit masked. (The bit meanings are not decoded: slot 0 looks like point sampling, which matches the retail crisp pixel blocks.)
vertices are 80 bytes each, copied at ring offset first * 80.
pass constants (a 176-byte block matching the shader's cbDrawPS layout): outline pass: m_uiShaderType = 1 and m_outlinesColor = 0xFF000000; colour pass: m_uiShaderType = 0 and m_lutBlendFactor = 0.0.

open_questions: Blend state of the two passes and the sampler bit meanings are not decoded (?).

name: CharaRenderer_GlareChain
callees: shader table (qword_140D3AD60) methods, sub_140069A38, sub_1403CC7C0, sub_1403CC8E0, sub_1403D0694
purpose: Runs the glare (bloom) passes on the unit renderer's scene target: bright-pass (shader id 1035 GLARE_BRIGHT), blur (1036 GLARE_BLUR) and the composite.

behavior.text: sets the target from g+3840, viewport (g+4448 >> 2, g+4452 >> 2) = quarter resolution, selects shader 1035 with parameters {1.0, g+3868, g+3864} (v69[0..2]); a later part runs the blur chain and composite.

bright-pass keeps pixels above luminance threshold p.x * p.y, capped at p.x * p.z, hue-preserving; the composite pixel shader (post_effect_ps) adds the blurred texture (tTexture1) to the scene (tTexture0) with the tone formula in the post-effect pixel shader (embedded DXBC).

notes: Only the first ~120 lines of this 8.5 KB function were read; the blur and composite parts are not yet documented.
open_questions: Parameter values at g+3864/+3868 and which target a UI draw ends up in (?).

name: CharaRenderer_Init
callees: CharaRender_InitTargets, sub_1403CAC84 (load texture by name), sub_1400CCCA8, sub_1400CA3C0, sub_1400CAF20, sub_1400C7E2C, sub_1400D2D6C
purpose: Builds the unit renderer: allocates its sub-objects, loads the textures it needs and creates the 256 slot targets.

behavior.text: textures loaded by name: bg/textures/lut_chara.tga, bg/textures/lut_uichara.tga, bg/textures/weather.tga (stored in the object at +148104), char/shape_blank.tga, char/chara_shadow.tga, char/chara_ripples.tga (+148120), ui/ui_blank.tga, ui/direction.tga, ui/direction_select.tga, ui/sword.tga.

+148128 = a 1104-byte LUT manager, +148136 = the 75864-byte target state (built by sub_1400CCCA8), +148144 = the 23568-byte config: size 256, ground x 128, ground y 192, scale 2.0f (0x40000000) followed by 256 slot entries of 92 bytes.
calls CharaRender_InitTargets(state, config size, ground x, ground y).

notes: The LUT used for the job tree is the second texture (lut_uichara), taken by CharaRender_DrawFrame when present.
open_questions: The other sub-objects (+148080, +148096, +148112) were not traced (?).

name: CharaRenderer_PostFrame
proto: __int64 CharaRenderer_PostFrame(__int64 a1, int a2, int a3, int a4)
purpose: End-of-frame pass of the unit (chara) renderer: runs the glare chain when enabled, then the post/resolve steps.

behavior.text: with g_CharaRenderer+153013 == 0 and +152992 != 0 it calls sub_1400D0D3C(g_CharaRenderer + 148512, a2, a3, a4, (float)dword_142E7FAE4) and then CharaRenderer_GlareChain (sub_1400D1018) on g_CharaRenderer + 148512, and sets v5 = 1 (the second render-target description at unk_142C819D0 + 136).
with +153012 != 0 and +153013 == 0 it renders the UI-style full-screen pass (shader id 1002 through the shader table qword_140D3AD60) and sets +153013 = 1.
then resolves through sub_1403CB8BC / sub_1403CB9C4 (colour-grading input xmmword_142E7FC70) unless disabled by qword_143CD9DD0+103 or the two debug words.

notes: Flags at g_CharaRenderer+152992 (glare on), +153012 and +153013 (post pass done) have not been read live yet.
open_questions: Whether the Job Tree UI is drawn into the target this chain post-processes (?).

name: CharaRenderer_Update
callees: CharaAnim_Step, CharaRender_DrawFrame, sub_1400C946C, sub_1400C9DCC, sub_1400C7664, sub_1400CB870, sub_1403CB40C, sub_1403CB4E0
purpose: Per-frame update of the unit renderer: retires finished job records, ticks the sub-systems and animates and draws every live slot.

behavior.text: clears every 36-byte job record whose state is 2 (4096 records at +0) and decrements the live count at +147456.
the step used for the 19 timed entries at +148104 is 0 when a pause flag (bit 0x10 of byte +24 of qword_143CD9E60) is set.
calls CharaAnim_Step (advance the animation) and CharaRender_DrawFrame (draw the frame) for the slots; the update of the sub-objects at +148080 / +148096 / +148104 (19 timed entries) is done first.

open_questions: The slot loop and the 19-entry timer block were only skimmed (?).

name: CharaSlot_Reset
purpose: Clears a slot's animation state and releases its frame-cache entry so the next request rebuilds it.

behavior.text: when the slot has an id (>= 0) and the renderer exists, releases the cached textures (sub_1400CE1AC when present at +68656) and clears the low 4 flag bits of the frame cache entry (renderer+47152 + 44 * id); then sets the slot id fields to -1 and zeroes the rest (pose at +72 included).

name: CharaSlot_SetParams
proto: __int64 CharaSlot_SetParams(CharaSlot *s, __int16 palA, __int16 palB, unsigned a4, int flags, char fx0, char fx1, int a8, int pose)
purpose: Stores a slot's sprite parameters and restarts its animation sequence when any of them changed.

behavior.text: compares pose (+72), palettes (+28/+30), a4 (+32), flags (+40), fx bytes (+44/+45) and a8 (+48) with the stored ones; on a difference calls sub_1400CC5DC (reset) then always continues into CharaAnim_Step (tail jump).

name: CharClut_ApplyToPalette
purpose: Applies the CharCLUT rows of one key to a palette: each enabled row replaces one 16-colour block with colours given as 8-bit RGB triples.

behavior.text: fetches the CharCLUT table (id 210) lazily and loops over all rows whose key is clutId.
a row is used only when its flag byte at +20 is non-zero.
for an enabled row it reads a block index from the row's sub-record (second pointer, dword at +4) and writes 16 colours starting at palette entry 16 x block index.
each colour comes from 3 bytes (R, G, B); the top 5 bits of each channel are packed with red in the low bits, green in the middle and blue on top, giving a 15-bit value.
bit 15 is set on every colour of the block except the first, mirroring the loader's rule that colour 0 carries no opaque bit.
the block-index source (the sub-record dword) was read from the decompilation but its table column was not named.

notes: This is the hook through which a data row can recolour a shape without a new sprite file.

name: CharClut_GetColorSkin
purpose: Reads the chara_color_skin column (+0x10) of the CharCLUT row (key, 0) and resolves it.

behavior.text: looks up CharCLUT row (key, 0), reads +0x10 and passes it to CharaColorSkin_Resolve.

notes: Name is ours.

name: CharShape_ApplyClut
purpose: Looks up the shape's row in the CharShape table and, if the row names a colour-override set, applies it to the palette.

behavior.text: fetches the CharShape table (id 174) lazily from the table registry and the row whose key is the shape.
reads the row's dword at +12 (the colour-override key, column `char_clut`); if it is non-zero it calls CharClut_ApplyToPalette(clutId, pal).
a missing table, missing row or a zero key leaves the palette unchanged.
called by CharaPalette_LoadClassic and by one other palette loader (sub_14026E838, the battle side).

the key is narrowed to its low byte (zero-extending byte load at 0x14026C7C0) before NxdTable_GetRowById, which itself takes a 32-bit key; the two callers hand only a byte register: CharaPalette_LoadClassic the low byte of the 32-bit look at 0x14026E806, sub_14026E838 the scene unit's sprite byte (+0xA) at 0x14026E8F3.

notes: Every generic job shape has override key 0, so the classic file's own palette is used unchanged for them.

name: ChroniclePeriod_GetIcon
purpose: Returns a Chronicle period's icon.

behavior.text: returns UIChroniclePeriod icon (+0x18) of the row.

name: ChroniclePeriod_ListUnlocked
purpose: Lists the Chronicle periods that are unlocked.

behavior.text: walks every UIChroniclePeriod row by index and keeps the first key (not 0) of each row whose user_situation (+0xC) is non-zero and met, up to 50 entries, into a2 (a count qword, then a dword list).

name: ChronicleTimeline_LayoutChapters
proto: void ChronicleTimeline_LayoutChapters(void *bar, int n2, int n3, int n4, int n5, int n6)
purpose: Lays out the timeline bar by the number of periods in each chapter section.

behavior.text: total = the sum of the five counts; positions the range of the 'Knob' part and the section nodes a1[51..55] by cumulative count / total, and plays 'Show' / 'HideChapter01..04Sepalator' at the section ends (the spelling is the game's).

name: ChronicleTimeline_Setup
purpose: Sets up the Chronicle timeline bar from the unlocked periods.

behavior.text: builds the unlocked period list with ChroniclePeriod_ListUnlocked and finds the index of the current period (the low byte of the word at save block +7778, capped at 28).
counts the listed periods by timeline_section (+0x10) values 2..6 and calls ChronicleTimeline_LayoutChapters(bar, n2, n3, n4, n5, n6), then sub_140178F84(bar, index).

name: ClassicCursorRows_Select
purpose: Moves the cursor of a legacy menu to the row chosen in the state record.

behavior.text: the row table is the language 0 block (base 0x1408FB62E) or the block of the other languages (base 0x1408FB94E); rows are 24 bytes.
stores x + 14 and y + 12 of the row as the cursor position and, when the row's key differs from the state's current key, resets the cursor animation (mode 120 when the key is non-zero, 2 otherwise).

name: ClassicItemListPage_Run
callees: Item_IsInCategory, VramPage_CopyRect, sub_14033E224, sub_14033E270, sub_14033E2C0, sub_14033E30C, sub_140394940, sub_140394C14, sub_14039AD30
purpose: Legacy party menu item list page: draws the list body and its header.

behavior.text: picks the page script of the text language (0x1408FD0B0 language 0, 0x1408FD860 language 3, 0x1408FD5D0 language 2, 0x1408FD340 otherwise) and a second chunk of the same block (0x1408FD1B0, 0x1408FD960, 0x1408FD6D0, 0x1408FD440 in the same order); one of two cell code grids (0x1408FD9F0 or 0x1408FEC70) is used by a page flag.
starts the scene tasks of the neighbouring panels through the wrappers sub_14033E270, sub_14033E2C0 and sub_14033E224 and sets up the cursor.

name: ClassicItemUsePage_Run
purpose: Legacy party menu item use page: picks an item and applies it to a unit.

behavior.text: on confirm checks the item count with Inventory_AddCount; with a count of 0 shows an event message, otherwise applies the item to the unit and removes one from the inventory.

runs the item page script of the text language inline (0x1408FCFB0 language 0, 0x1408FD760 language 3, 0x1408FD4D0 language 2, 0x1408FD240 otherwise): a loop that calls handler[opcode] of the 25-slot table at 0x1406932A0 until opcode 25; this is a second runner of the kind ClassicUi_RunLayoutScript implements.

name: ClassicJobDetailPage_Run
purpose: Legacy party menu job detail page: four pages of the chosen job with page switching.

behavior.text: on the first frame installs 16 condition functions and builds the page data of the job in word_143C52190; cancel ends the page with state 2, confirm with state 1 and result -1.

a page selector (0..3) changes with the direction input and rebuilds the page data; the layout script of the text language is run (0x1408FC760 / 0x1408FCD30 / 0x1408FCB40 / 0x1408FC950) followed by a fixed corner cell.

open_questions: ?: what each of the four pages shows.

name: ClassicListPage_BuildRangeList
callers: sub_14037BA34, sub_14037C2EC, sub_14037C6C4 and two more list pages
purpose: Builds the list of entry ids of the current category of a legacy list page and hands it to the list drawer.

behavior.text: picks the range table of the text language (0x1408FBCD0 language 0, 0x1408FBEB0 language 3, 0x1408FBFA0 language 2, 0x1408FBDC0 otherwise) and a table of three alternative window templates by the display mode.
the category's ids are start .. next start - 1 of the range table; they are stored as a list terminated by -1 and drawn.

name: ClassicMenu_LoadPageArtPack
purpose: Loads the art pack of a legacy menu page (0..5) into the shared menu texture buffer.

behavior.text: sets up the draw list with the page's run of cells from two dword tables (table[page] and table[page + 1] - table[page], and a second pair with a stride of 60 entries).
selects one of six resource slots (39..44) and copies 98304 bytes of its data to the shared buffer, with a separate source for each page.

name: ClassicPartyMenu_Run
callees: Inventory_RebuildOrders, Unit_ReloadFromJobRow, sub_14033E038, sub_1403972C0, sub_1403957E4, sub_14028531C
purpose: Per-frame driver of the legacy party menu: prepares the shared header state and runs the handler of the current mode.

behavior.text: on mode 0 (first call) rebuilds the inventory orders, loads the page art and sets mode 1; otherwise keeps the mode.
sets the header geometry words (two sets depending on a state flag), then calls the handler of the mode from the 6-slot mode table (0x140684918).
afterwards, while a mode of -1 is pending, compares the unit's saved fields with the preview copy and reloads the preview unit when they differ; clamps the preview HP and MP to their maxima.

name: ClassicSubtitles_SetState
proto: void ClassicSubtitles_SetState(void *addon, int state, int keepShown)
purpose: Plays the state of the classic subtitle window.

behavior.text: plays 'Show' on the two window nodes (addon +48 and +56) for states 1..5.
plays the state named by the string table at off_14070D810 (Hide, Line01 .. Line05) on the first kind-1 component; state 0 plays 'Hide' only when the keep-shown byte is 0.

notes: Name is ours.

name: ClassicSubtitles_Step
purpose: Per-frame step of the classic-movie subtitle window: finds the line whose time window holds the movie time and sets its text and layout state.

behavior.text: the UIClassicSubtitles rows of the movie key are read by line index; a line is current when starts_at (+0xC) <= movie time < ends_at (+0x10); text is +8.
line_layout (+0x14) is mapped 1 to 2, 2 to 3, 3 to 4, 4 to 5, any other value to 1 and stored as the state byte (+24); state 0 means no line (after ends_at).
the keep_shown byte (+0x18) is kept at +25 and passed to ClassicSubtitles_SetState.

notes: Name is ours. Cache qword_143CDA558.

name: ClassicUi_OpAnimatedFrame
purpose: Opcode 18: a window frame that grows open over the first 8 page redraws.

behavior.text: while the page redraw counter is below 8 it scales the width by an 8-entry percentage table (0x14071F1D0) and queues a growing plate before drawing the frame; later redraws draw the frame at full size.
then runs the window frame handler on the same record.

notes: Read: the counter test and the plate; the table values are listed with LegacyCursorPositions.

name: ClassicUi_OpDrawCell
purpose: Opcodes 4 and 5: queues one sprite cell.

behavior.text: arguments are the cell x (+3), y (+4, shifted by the list row when a list page is drawn), texture position (+5, +6) and the cell size (+7, +8); opcode 4 uses no shared rectangle word, opcode 5 passes the shared one.
passes the current layer, blend and texture page words to the cell queue.

name: ClassicUi_OpDrawNumber
purpose: Opcode 13: draws a number or a row of gauge cells for a value supplied by the page.

behavior.text: the value comes from the page's condition function at byte +3 (argument +9, or the list row in a list page).

bit 29 of the value switches to a gauge: that many cells (+4) spaced by +5; otherwise the value is formatted with %d and its digits are drawn right aligned over +4 digit cells with spacing +5, blanks for the missing leading digits.
bit 30 of the value selects an alternate colour word.

name: ClassicUi_OpIf
callees: the condition functions set by the page
purpose: Opcode 1: runs the next records only when a page condition holds, otherwise skips them.

behavior.text: the condition is a function of the page's condition table (0x141D3B630) chosen by byte +3, called with the argument at +5 or, in a list page, the current list row plus the page's row offset.
byte +4 is the number of following records governed by the condition; when it is true they are run through the handler table, otherwise their lengths are added to skip them.

name: ClassicUi_OpIfElse
purpose: Opcode 2: as opcode 1 with an else branch.

behavior.text: bytes +4 and +5 are the counts of the then and the else records that follow in that order; only the branch matching the condition (function +3, argument +6 or the list row) is run, the other is skipped.

name: ClassicUi_OpSetBlendWord
purpose: Opcode 12: composes the blend and mode word of the following cells.

behavior.text: packs the bits of +2, +3 and +4 into one word with a fixed shift scheme (blend mode in the low bits, a page-high bit and a mode field above).

open_questions: ?: the meaning of each packed field.

name: ClassicUi_OpSetLayer
purpose: Opcode 14: sets the layer word used by the following cells.

behavior.text: stores byte +3 in the layer word and returns the next record.

name: ClassicUi_OpSetPriority
purpose: Opcode 15: sets the draw priority word unless a plate is being built.

behavior.text: stores byte +3 in the priority word when the plate flag is 0.

name: ClassicUi_OpSetTexturePageA
purpose: Opcode 9: sets the texture page and palette word used by the following cells.

behavior.text: the page index is the 9-bit value (+2 << 8) + +4 (wrapped to 0x1FF above 0x1FF); the palette index is the low 6 bits of +3; the combined word is page << 6 | palette.

name: ClassicUi_OpSetTexturePageB
purpose: Opcode 10: as opcode 9 with a second set of arguments for an alternate display mode.

behavior.text: a global mode byte chooses between the arguments at +2..+4 (as opcode 9) and the ones at +5..+7.

name: ClassicUi_OpTileGrid
purpose: Opcode 17: fills a rectangle with 8 x 8 tiles.

behavior.text: arguments are the origin (+3, +4), the tile columns in the high nibble of +5 and the remainder width in its low nibble, and the rows in the high nibble of +6 and the remainder height in its low nibble.
queues one tile per 16 pixels, then a partial last column and a partial last row.

name: ClassicUi_OpWindowFrame
purpose: Opcode 0: draws a bordered window of a given size at a position.

behavior.text: arguments are the origin x (+3) and y (+4), the width in tiles and a remainder (+5) and the height (+6) packed as nibbles.
draws the four corner / edge cells from fixed cell positions in the page texture, repeats edge cells along each side, then fills the inside through the tile grid handler on a scratch record.
stores the window's right edge in a shared word for later records.

name: ClassicUi_RunLayoutScript
callers: sub_14039297C (job screen task), ClassicJobDetailPage_Run and one more call site outside any function
purpose: Runs one layout script of the legacy menus: a list of records that draw windows, cells and numbers.

behavior.text: resets the draw state (the priority word, the layer word and the plate flag) and remembers the current input id, then walks the records.

each record is {opcode, record length, arguments}; the handler of the opcode comes from a 22-slot function table (0x140693110; opcodes 3, 6, 7, 8 and 11 have no handler, 4 and 5 share one) and returns the start of the next record (this record + its length byte).
stops at opcode 22; afterwards a global page redraw counter is incremented while it is below 10.

notes: Read: the loop and the table; the handlers named below are the ones read. A second runner of the same kind (25 opcodes, end opcode 25, table 0x1406932A0) is inlined in the item pages.
open_questions: ?: the handler of opcode 16 (a long one) and the small handlers of opcodes 19..21.

name: ClutFade_SetTarget
proto: int64_t ClutFade_SetTarget(int mode, int duration, int64_t bank, int64_t slot, int all, int16_t dr, int16_t dg, int16_t db, int unused)
callers: sub_1401EAAF8, sub_1401EABB0, sub_1401EABF8, sub_1401EAC44, sub_1401EAC98, sub_1401EACF8, sub_1401EAD60, sub_140268880, ClutManager_Update, sub_1402F7A90, sub_1402F7ACC
purpose: Gives one row of a palette bank (or all 16 rows) a new colour to move to, at once or as a timed fade.

behavior.text: works on the 16 colours of row `slot` of bank `bank`, or on all 256 colours of the bank when `all` is 1; a bank is 2450 bytes (the multiplier in the code) and the banks follow the two dirty dwords of g_ClutManager.
a colour whose three state bytes (red, green, blue) are all 0 is left alone: its three distance bytes are set to 31 (distance 0).

the target per colour: mode 8 the bank's base row word (word_140C6BABA + 2450 * bank); modes 4, 9 and 11 that word's channels plus dr, dg, db; mode 5 its channels halved to 4 bits plus the offsets; modes 6 and 7 (blue + 3 green + 2 red) / 6 and / 12 of it plus the offsets.
modes 0 to 3 are the same four counted from the colour's state bytes instead of the base row (0 as they are, 1 halved, 2 the grey sum / 6, 3 the grey sum / 12).
each target channel is limited to 31 and put to 0 below 1; when all three are 0 blue becomes 1.
with a duration of 0 the state bytes and the final image word (word_140C73B70 + 512 * bank) take the target at once; else the three distance bytes get target - state + 31.

after the colours, with a duration: each row's 9-byte timer gets active 1, step 0, frame counter 0, the duration twice, and for modes 9 and 11 the ping-pong byte 1 with the three offsets kept; with a duration of 0 the timers are cleared and the dirty dword is set.
mode 10 clears the ping-pong byte of the row (or of all 16) and returns.
when the dword at 0x142E80048 is non-zero and the bank is 0 or 1 it first reads scene variable 39 and calls sub_1400C961C with the mode, the duration and the offsets.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1402F4944). Structure: ClutBank. Seen live 2026-11-11: the unit under the cursor at deployment pulses by a fade of this function (target = row + 8 on all channels, 8 steps, ping-pong).
open_questions: ? what the last argument is for; ? what sub_1400C961C does with the same request for banks 0 and 1.

name: ClutManager_Update
callees: ClutFade_SetTarget, sub_1400C98C4, sub_14024A528, sub_1402F5428, sub_1402F57D0, sub_1402F5C20
purpose: The palette manager's step, once a frame from the battle loop: colour cycles, three screen-colour fades and the timed fades of the 14 palette banks.

behavior.text: returns at once while the pause manager's byte +24 has bit 4.

first runs the colour-cycle records (10 bytes each, walked from 0x140C739AD, the byte after each record's active flag): when a record's counter reaches its period it rotates the colours between two indices of a bank by one place (state bytes, base row words and final image words).

then steps three colour fades kept as 16.16 fixed-point values with their own counters (blocks at 0x140C73924, 0x140C73964 and 0x140C73988); two of them hand their colour to sub_14024A528 with the ids 90 and 99.

then, per bank (14 banks) and per row with an active timer: a duration below 4 moves every colour by one entry of the 8-step table (byte_140681FE0[8 * distance byte + step]) each frame; a duration of 4 or more moves it by one entry of the 32-step table (byte_1406821F0[32 * distance byte + step]) once every duration / 4 frames.

a colour whose three state bytes are all 0 is not moved; a colour that comes out all 0 gets blue 1; the moved colour is written to the state bytes and to the final image word, and the dirty dword is set.

when the step counter reaches 8 (or 32): a row with ping-pong byte 1 is given mode 8 through ClutFade_SetTarget and the byte becomes 2; with byte 2 it is given mode 9 with its kept offsets and the byte becomes 1; any other value ends the fade (the active byte is cleared).
the same stepping exists for a whole bank at once (256 colours, the bank's first timer).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1402F5F78). Structure: ClutBank. The running sums of both step tables, for every distance -31..31, are floor(d * k / n) for d >= 0 and max(d, floor((d * k - 1) / n)) for d < 0 (compared with all 63 x 40 table entries in the database).
open_questions: ? what the three screen-colour fades colour (ids 90 and 99 of sub_14024A528); ? the last block after the banks (a float at +6070652 of the object at g_CharaRenderer +148080).

name: ClutManager_Upload
purpose: Copies the palette manager's final image into the emulated video memory when it changed.

behavior.text: when the manager's second dirty dword is set it calls sub_14025FE14 for the rectangle x 0, y 494, 256 x 14 with the arguments 0 and 480, and clears the dword.
when the first dirty dword is set it calls sub_14025FA60 with the same rectangle and word_140C73B70 (the final image: 14 rows of 256 colours), then stores 0 in the first dword and 1 in the second.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1402F7964). I: sub_14025FA60 is the emulated LoadImage (it has dozens of callers that hand it a rectangle and pixels) and the target is g_SaveYoxPage, the 1024 x 512 word video memory.
open_questions: ? what sub_14025FE14 does with the same rectangle (I: a copy inside the video memory, by its arguments).

name: CMesId_GetText
purpose: Returns the text of one row of NXD table 172 (0xAC, the C_Mes_Id_Sample table) and caches the table pointer.

behavior.text: the table pointer is cached in qword_143CDA340; when it is empty the function finds table 172 with NxdRegistry_Find(g_NxdRegistry, 172).
the row is fetched by key with the generic table row lookup (NxdTable_GetRowById then NxdEntry_GetRow); a missing table or a missing row returns null.
a row whose key is negative resolves to a shared empty row, which is returned instead of null.
table 172 is the English C_Mes_Id_Sample table: keys 2000..23025, 1734 rows, of which keys 10000..10171 are 172 rows; key 10098 holds '<string=lstr0>' and key 10512 does not exist.
the executable's own text-tag resolver names table 172 'C_Mes_Id_Sample', so the table name is the game's; the function name is ours.
three direct call sites in two functions.
the row key is the message id BattleMsg_IdFromDescriptor produces; keys 2000..23025 match 1000 * kind + index for the kinds that function accepts.
why the 172-row block at 10000 exists beside the 1000-wide blocks, and when the cache is invalidated.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1400FCB2C). Read in full (about 134 bytes) while tracing the item battle message. The row lookup that follows the registry find is NxdTable_GetRowById plus NxdEntry_GetRow.
open_questions: The invalidation rule for the cached table pointer; whether a missing row is expected or always an error; what the row text tags <string=lstrN> / <num=...> expand to.

name: CMesId_IsErrorBanner

behavior.text: for a message descriptor of kind 0 whose text group is 2 (the C_Mes_Id text pool) it takes the C_Mes_Id_Sample row of BattleMsg_IdFromDescriptor and returns the row's error_banner byte (+0x14); otherwise 0.

notes: Name is ours. Both callers test the result first and, when it is non-zero, call ErrorBanner_Show and skip the normal message paths.

name: ComponentDrawContext_Build
proto: __int64 ComponentDrawContext_Build(int a1, ComponentCtx *out, ComponentCtx *parent, GUINode *ref, GUIComponent *comp)
purpose: Creates the child draw context of a component: copy of the parent (0x258 bytes), composed matrix, opacity and colour.

behavior.text: out+496 = comp; matrix out+504 = parent matrix * the component's own transform (sub_14040A914 with the reference node); out+528/+532 scaled by the component's scale; out+536 += comp+192 (opacity add); out+540 = byte-wise product of the parent colour and comp+196; out+544 += ref+200 (order); ++out+552 (depth); out+548 = comp+552 << 16 when set (layer id).

name: ComponentDrawContext_ComputeMatrix
purpose: Gives ComponentDrawContext_Build the component's local 2 x 3 matrix and a two-float scale; when comp+540 = 1 it scales the matrix by the ratio of two sizes, otherwise it copies both straight from the property block.

behavior.text: if comp+540 == 1: sx = (int)props+64 / (int)comp+336 and sy = (int)props+68 / (int)comp+340 (each 1.0 when the divisor is 0); builds the matrix [sx 0 0 sy 0 0] and calls Matrix2x3_Multiply(outMatrix, that, props+80); outScale = (sx * props+96, sy * props+100).
otherwise: copies 16 bytes from props+80 and 8 bytes from props+176 to outMatrix (6 floats) and 8 bytes from props+184 to outScale.

notes: The name is ours. Reading: comp+336/+340 is the authored size and props+64/+68 the actual size, so mode 1 is a stretch to fit (I). Operand order of Matrix2x3_Multiply(out, a, b) is taken from the call.
open_questions: What comp+540 = 1 means in the file; the meaning of props+176 / +184 (precomputed matrix tail and scale?); how sub_1403E647C uses the result was not read.

name: ComponentEffects_Collect
callees: Matrix2x3_Multiply, GUIWidget_FindComponentCached, GUIWidget_FindComponentByName, GUIWidget_FindResourceByName, GUINode_FindNthPartByKind, UIImage_ResolvePart, GUIFontSlots_GetTextureRect, roundf
purpose: Copies every enabled effect group of the component's property block into the draw context and reports whether an offscreen layer is needed.

behavior.text: component = ctx+496. Blend type comp+16 (0 = none). Effect groups (runtime offsets in the component; each has an enable byte): +60 colour transform (mul comp+28..+40, add +44..+56 unless identity); +88 six floats +64..+84; +96 single float +92 (> 0); +120 floats +100/+104 (> 0) with a qword +108 and +116; +172 two floats +156/+160 (> 0) with colour +164 and mode +168 (this is the group the UnitSelect ring enables); +186 floats +176/+180 (> 0) with size comp+336/+340; +192 opacity float +188; +216 clip rectangle (margins +196..+212, size +336/+340); +244, +265.
each enabled group sets its flag byte in the context (+76, +104, +112, +136, +156, +178, +184, +296) and makes the result 1 = a layer is required.

colour transform (comp+60 set and not the identity): ctx+76 = 1, ctx+44..+59 <- comp+28..+43 (multiply), ctx+60..+75 <- comp+44..+59 (add). Offsets group (comp+88 set and any of comp+64..+84 non-zero): ctx+104 = 1, ctx+80..+103 <- comp+64..+87. Single float (comp+96 set and comp+92 > 0): ctx+112 = 1, ctx+108 <- comp+92.

drop-shadow group: when comp+120 != 0 and (comp+100 > 0 or comp+104 > 0): ctx+136 = 1, ctx+116 <- comp+100 (blur radius), ctx+120 <- comp+104 (strength), the qword ctx+124 <- comp+108 / +112 (offset x / y), ctx+132 <- comp+116 (colour rgb, alpha 0xFF).

glow group: when comp+172 != 0 and (comp+156 > 0 or comp+160 > 0): ctx+156 = 1, ctx+140 <- comp+156, ctx+144 <- comp+160, ctx+148 <- comp+164 (colour), ctx+152 <- comp+168 (mode). The +186 group (comp+186 set and comp+176 > 0 or comp+180 > 0): ctx+178 = 1, ctx+160 <- comp+176, ctx+164 <- comp+180, ctx+176 <- byte comp+184, ctx+177 <- byte comp+185, ctx+168 / +172 = half the size comp+336 / +340 mapped through the matrix at ctx+504. Group comp+192: ctx+184 = 1, ctx+180 <- comp+188.

behavior.basis: (read 2026-10-30, decompile; checked against a live Job Tree frame)
behavior.text: the mask group (comp+244): the Mask node is the first kind 9 node of the component's tree (GUINode_FindNthPartByKind(comp+272, 9, 0)); when it exists and its bytes +144 and +153 are set, an image mask is used when node+244 (font slot) is non-zero or its image name at node+216 resolves in the widget (ctx+384 = 1, no extra layer), otherwise the mask component named by node+248 / +264 (cache cell node+288) is stored (ctx+409 = 1, ctx+392 = component, ctx+400 = node, ctx+408 = node+280). With no usable Mask node the component's own name keys comp+224 (image) / comp+248 (component) are tried the same way. A component mask makes ComponentLayer_Begin draw that component into an extra layer record first (ComponentLayer_DrawMaskComponent). The +265 group clears ctx+296 / +384 / +409 again. The result is 1 also when the u16 comp+552 (layer id) is non-zero.

notes: Only the head (the effect-group copies, lines up to the clip rectangle) of this 15 KB function was read. V (decompile, label LABEL_58, + live backtrace of the Job Tree title): for a component whose property block carries a Mask node (the TextMask component), it resolves the mask component by the node's two name keys (+248 / +264, cache cell +288) with GUIWidget_FindComponentCached and stores it in the draw context: ctx+409 = 1, ctx+392 = the mask component, ctx+400 = the Mask node (used as its property block). ComponentLayer_Begin then draws that component into its own layer first (ComponentLayer_DrawMaskComponent). The context groups feed GUILayer_BuildRecord one to one (shadow: ctx+136 -> record+153 = layer flag +177).
open_questions: The remaining part (clip rect maths and flags) is not documented (?); how the Mask node is found among the component's nodes and what its other fields (+208..+216) do. ? whether the comp+192 group (ctx+184, ctx+180) is an opacity or a whole-layer blur radius: GUILayer_BuildRecord scales it by the pixel scale into layer+500, which GUILayer_BlurEffect reads as a radius, while GUICore_DrawWidget only draws the component when comp+188 > 0.

name: ComponentLayer_Begin
purpose: Decides whether a component needs its own offscreen layer and opens it.

behavior.text: asks ComponentEffects_Collect (sub_1403E809C) whether any effect is enabled; the layer is also forced when r+606621 is set together with the target flags (ctx+488 +83, ctx+552, ctx+496 +561); returns 0 (no layer) when the context already carries one (ctx+553) or nothing needs it.

when a layer is needed and ctx+409 is set without ctx+410 it marks ctx+410 and calls sub_1403E647C; then GUILayer_Select (sub_1403E9298) opens or reuses the layer and r+606588 / the record are updated.

the force rule in full: with the renderer feature byte r+606621 set (1 from the renderer initialiser), the layer is forced (a3 = 1) when widget byte +83 (ctx+488 + 83) is set and the context depth ctx+552 is 0 (the root component), or, otherwise, when the component byte +561 (ctx+496 + 561) is set. Layer opened = ctx+553 is 0 and (the effects collector returned 1 or the force applies). ctx+553 has no writer in the code (always 0), so a component inside a layer still opens its own layer when it has effects.
widget byte +83 is 1 for all 51 widgets of the running game, so every widget root opens a layer even with no effect enabled; the finger cursor's root component has no effect group and blend 0.

name: ComponentLayer_DrawMaskComponent
purpose: Draws a component's mask component (ctx+392, with the Mask node as its property block ctx+400) into a fresh layer record; called by ComponentLayer_Begin the first time a layer with a mask is opened.

behavior.text: returns 0 when the mask component is not loaded (+416 = 0) or hidden (+192 set and opacity +188 <= 0), or when the layer list is full (r+606584 + 2 >= 511). Otherwise sub_1403E9218 and GUILayer_ResetRecord prepare a layer record, the draw context is copied (0x258 bytes) and the mask component becomes its component (+496).

when the Mask node is present its matrix is ComponentDrawContext_ComputeMatrix(component, m, scale, node) times the context matrix (+504), the scale and opacity are multiplied in, the node colour (+196) is multiplied into the context colour (+540 / the colour dword) and the node's +200 is added to the layer order (+544).
sub_1403E9A2C draws the component's children (GUINode_DrawChildren at component +272) into the new layer; returns 1 when that produced a layer (the layer flag byte is set).

the copied context has the depth byte ctx+552 incremented and ctx+553 set to 1 ('the context already carries a layer'), so no component inside the mask opens a layer of its own (ComponentLayer_Begin returns 0 at once); the whole mask component is drawn into the one fresh record. The function returns 0 when the draw counter r+606592 is not positive afterwards (nothing was drawn), otherwise it sets the byte layer+487 of that record to 1: this is THE writer of the mask-layer flag +487 that the atlas sheets could not find (the flag is the high byte of the record's dword at record+484). The record itself is made by GUILayer_ResetRecord, not by GUILayer_BuildRecord: the effect groups of the mask layer are all off and the 488-byte context copy of its slot (r + 512 * slot + 41336) is not rewritten (it keeps the bytes of an earlier frame).

the TextMask component of the main tab draws its mask component TextBoard01 into slot 4 (+487 = 1, dirty (20, 11, 102, 44)); the next slot 5 holds TextMask itself (+489 = 1, drop shadow, ctx+409 = 1 and ctx+392 = the mask component pointer, the only component pointer the layer records contain); the atlas read +16 = 5, +20 = 0 for slot 4 and the secondary shelf {178, 0, 124, 0} (the model of LayerAtlasPlacement step 7: margin 32 from the stale radius bytes of the reset record, 114 + 64 = 178, 60 + 64 = 124).

notes: The name is ours. Live (call stack at the Job Tree title's GUITextNode_Draw): GUIComponentRef_Draw (TextMask reference) -> ComponentLayer_Begin -> this function -> GUINode_DrawChildren -> GUITextNode_Draw, so the title text is drawn into the mask layer, not into the screen. Live: every glyph record of the title text (node+328, 36 bytes each, byte +28) has the bold run flag = 1.
open_questions: How the layer record this creates is consumed by the effect pass (GUILayer_EffectPass0): which slot holds it and how the shader combines it with the gradient layer. The mask layer's stale radius floats (+180 / +188 / +500 of a reset record) decide its atlas margin (live: 10.0 gave 32); whether that is intended is not known (?).

name: Deflate_Init2
proto: int Deflate_Init2(void *strm, int level, int method, int windowBits, int memLevel, int strategy, const char *version, int streamSize)
callees: the stream's allocate callback, sub_14040F940 (free on failure), sub_14040EF50 (reset)
purpose: Initialises a deflate compression stream (the embedded zlib-style compressor): validates the arguments, allocates the 5920-byte state and its buffers, then resets the stream.

behavior.text: returns -6 (version error) unless the version string starts with '1' and the stream struct size is 88.
installs default allocate and free callbacks into the stream when it has none; a level of -1 becomes 6.
window bits: negative = raw stream (wrapper 0), above 15 = gzip wrapper (2, bits - 16), else the zlib wrapper (1).
argument check: memLevel 1..9, method 8, window bits 8..15, level 0..9, strategy 0..4; otherwise returns -2 (stream error). A window of 8 bits is raised to 9.
allocates the state (5920 bytes), the window (2 x window size), the previous-chain and head arrays (hash size 2^(memLevel+7)) and the pending buffer (2^(memLevel+6) x 4 bytes).
when any allocation fails sets the state mark to 666, stores the message 'insufficient memory' (entry 6 of DeflateErrorMessages) in the stream, frees what it has and returns -4.
otherwise stores the level, strategy and method in the state and returns the result of the stream reset function sub_14040EF50.

notes: Name is ours; the routine is a standard compression library function, described only as far as the executable shows. The message table entry is read by address (entry 6). The calls to sub_14040F940 and sub_14040EF50 are direct calls in the failure and final branches (seen in the disassembly); the cross-check flags them because they lie outside its scanned range.

name: Deployment_LoadAreaPlacement
callers: Battle_JoinUnitAndLoad, Deployment_AreaOfPlacedUnit, Deployment_CountUnitsInArea, sub_1401EE9B4, sub_1401EF0D8, sub_1401F3060, sub_1401F49EC, sub_1401F5808
callees: SceneVar_Read, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdTable_GetEntryCount, NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys2, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_1402FF440
purpose: Loads the deployment area index (scene variable 53 + index): selects its placement record and builds the grid of placeable cells around it.

stores the area id in dword_1437A0324 and the placement record (12 bytes at off_1408ECA58 + 12 * area) in off_1408ECA60.
reads the EntryArea table (nxd 244) rows keyed (area, n) for n below 25 and collects byte +4 of each existing row into a 16-byte list in row order.

the placement record's bytes +4 .. +7 pick the orientation and the anchor of a 5 x 5 cell grid (25 eight-byte cell records at 0x1437A01F0): each cell takes its flag byte from the grid at 0x1437A0420, its position offsets from the record +4 / +5 and its facing bits from +6; a cell with a non-zero flag takes the next byte of the collected list.

stores the cursor tile (dword_140C6AFB8, dword_140C6ADAC, dword_140C6AFBC) in +1888..+1890 and looks up the unit node standing there (sub_1402607E4).

name: DeploymentGrid_CommenceCheck
purpose: Decides whether the deployment screen may start the battle with the units placed: returns a result code, 1 meaning go.

reads the number of deployment areas (scene variable 52), takes the area sizes through Deployment_SelectArea(0) and, for two areas, (1), and asks Deployment_CountUnitsInArea per area; an area with no unit sends a kind-1 battle message and returns 6; with two areas and the second one empty it sends the message with 7 or 8 depending on how the counts compare.
scans the placed party indices (dword array at +68): an entry below -1 returns 0; an entry equal to 0 (party member 0) sets a flag.
returns 1 when scene variable 511 is 0 or party member 0 is placed, otherwise 2 (Ramza must be deployed).

name: DepthStencilDesc_FromWord
purpose: Unpacks the packed depth-stencil word of a pipeline state into the Direct3D 12 depth-stencil description.

behavior.text: DepthEnable = w & 1, DepthWriteMask = (w & 2) != 0, DepthFunc = ((w >> 2) & 7) + 1, StencilEnable = (w >> 25) & 1, StencilReadMask = byte 6, StencilWriteMask = byte 7; front face: StencilFailOp = (w >> 29) + 1 (bits 29..31), StencilDepthFailOp = ((w >> 34) & 7) + 1, StencilPassOp = ((w >> 37) & 7) + 1, StencilFunc = ((w >> 26) & 7) + 1.

with bit 33 set the back face has its own fields (fail = ((w >> 16) & 7) + 1, depth fail = ((w >> 19) & 7) + 1, pass = ((w >> 22) & 7) + 1, func = ((w >> 13) & 7) + 1); otherwise it repeats the front face.
called by the pipeline-state builder sub_140051508 with the qword at key+48, next to BlendDesc_FromWords (blend) and sub_140051324 (rasteriser).

the draw-state qword at ts+104 is this word: a program entry's mask bit 0x80 replaces its low 5 bits (depth enable, write, comparison: ShaderProgram_ApplyState), and the reset constant 0xFFFF00001C000000 (RenderContext_ResetFrame) decodes as stencil masks 0xFF / 0xFF with KEEP operations and ALWAYS. Used to read the SDFFont programs (SDFFontRenderer_Flush).

notes: Comparison values are D3D12_COMPARISON_FUNC (1 NEVER, 2 LESS, 3 EQUAL, 4 LESS_EQUAL, 5 GREATER, 6 NOT_EQUAL, 7 GREATER_EQUAL, 8 ALWAYS).
