name: Effect_RunStateMachine
callees: SceneObject_FindBySlot, sub_1400D258C, sub_14024F5A0, sub_1402741E0, sub_14031A840, sub_14031A994, sub_14031D658, sub_140381A54, sub_14038DD00
purpose: Per-frame state machine of one battle effect: waits for the file load, uploads the texture, sets up the effect sections and runs the effect to its end.

behavior.text: the state is dword_1418732C8. State 0 only returns 0. State 1 returns 1 (busy) unless the pause flag (bit 8 at g_PauseManager + 24) or bit 2 of dword_1407B0758 is set. State 2 (same guards) calls sub_14024F5A0 with 0x71 (built as 1 + 0x70 in the code), sets word_142FEF6DC to 1, calls EffectFile_UploadTexture and moves to state 3.

state 3 (same guards) resets the effect heap (a free list starting at the texture section pointer qword_1411A3840 and ending at unk_141982E00) and reads the header dwords of the file at qword_143740220[word_141D330BC]: +0 and +4 (each plus 4) give two block pointers (qword_1411A3850, qword_1411A3858), +8 the main script pointer (qword_141873078), +12 a block (qword_1411A3810), +16 the records of 160 bytes (qword_1411A3848), +20 a block (qword_1411A3830), +24 the sound and timing section (qword_1411A3828), +28 a section with an 8-byte header (qword_1411A3860), +32 an optional section (0 = absent; qword_1411A3808) whose u16 at +10 shifted left by 16 becomes dword_14114B124, the sound cue base.
state 3 then calls sub_1400D258C with the effect number (the NXD parameter rows) and starts the first effect node.

state 4 runs the node list each frame (sub_14031D658, sub_14031A840 per node) and, when the list is empty, restores the renderer values, plays sub_14024F5A0 with 0x72, sets dword_142E801F4 to -1 and returns the state to 0.

state 6 (reached through the default branch, same guards) repeats the heap reset from the saved pointers qword_1411A3838 and qword_1411A3820 and restarts the node list; it then sets the state to 4 plus an inner value.

notes: Name is ours. The header dwords are offsets inside the file (the pointer is the file base plus the dword), so the file does not depend on its own number. Section meanings below +8 are inferred from their readers (sub_14034xxx per-primitive renderers, sound functions EffectScript_OpRunTimeline / sub_14031D010).
open_questions: ? the layout of the blocks at +0, +4, +12, +16, +20 and +28; what drives state 6 and what states above 6 do.

name: Effect_SelectForAbility
proto: int Effect_SelectForAbility(uint32 chargeElement, int effectWord, void *request)
purpose: Picks the effect number for an effect word and starts the effect.

behavior.text: word >= 512: g_EffectNumberPseudo[word - 512] (37 rows, else row 0): the effects of event scripts (EventEffect_Start); word 393: by the weapon's element bits (16, 24, 20 or the current); else g_AbilityEffectNumber[word < 0x1C6 ? word : 0].

the compare with 512 is signed (a signed greater-or-equal jump, at 0x140319B8B), so a negative word (a 16-bit value with its top bit set, 0x8000 and above, is negative as an int) takes the last branch and row 0 of the ability table; the pseudo row bound is a compare of the row counter with an 8-bit immediate (37) followed by a subtract-with-borrow and an AND, so a word 549 or more reads row 0. The row is a 16-bit value: a negative one (bit 15) means no effect. The charge element argument is used as a 16-bit index (the 0xFFFF mask of the charge table read is a 16-bit register move at 0x140319C35, so the constant 0xFFFF is not in the body).

a number >= 0 is stored in word_141D330BC and the effect starts (sub_140310B64 with byte_140682B98[chargeElement & 0xFFFF]); a negative one (-1: none) only runs the special cases of 138..145 and 146 / 406..413; dword_142E801F4 = word.

the stored number is masked with 0x1FF (0x140319C23 / 0x140319C32) after the sign test; the g_AbilityEffectNumber row is loaded into eax at 0x140319BF1 (zero-extended, indexed from rdi = the image base), and a jump then reaches the store at 0x140319C13.

notes: An effect word of 512..548 selects a pseudo effect here; the highest word an event script can pass is 32,767 (the operand is a signed 16-bit word).

name: Effect_TintByNxdScale
purpose: Updates one effect node: copies its position and angle into the node record and sets its colour, scaled by the effect number's table row.

behavior.text: when the game is not paused and the frame flag bit 0 of dword_1407B0758 is set, it writes the node position (three values shifted right by 12) into the node record and, for a node with flag 2, an angle computed with atan2f.
the three colour bytes default to 0x80; a node with flag 0x40 takes them from the 160-byte records at qword_1411A3848.

the colour bytes are multiplied by the float at +8 of the RefinedVFXTexture row of word_141D330BC (1.0 when the effect number is 0 or less or the row is missing) and the result is passed on to EffectSprite_StepAnimation.
the number is loaded sign-extended into edi at 0x1403846FD and tested for 0 or less before the table lookup.

notes: Name is ours. The float is column Unknown8 of table 202; every stock row holds 1.0.

name: EffectAnchor_GetPoint
proto: int EffectAnchor_GetPoint(int withHeight, int index, EffectUnitList *list)
purpose: Gives an effect's caster (index -1) or target (index 0..) position: a unit's scene position or a tile's centre.

behavior.text: index -1 reads the caster entry at list +196, index n the target entry at list + 4 + 12 n; an entry with a non-zero first word is a tile: (28 x + 14, -12 height, 28 z + 14) from the map tile (sub_140249000); otherwise the scene object of its slot (SceneObject_FindBySlot) gives the position.
with withHeight set the tile height adds the half-step bits (byte +3 >> 5), and a unit is not placed below its tile.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_140384240). The list is word_141873080 (the effect unit list).

name: EffectEmitter_Spawn
proto: int64 EffectEmitter_Spawn(int16 ctx, int t, int emitter, EffectParticle *parent)
callers: EffectScript_RunEmitterTracks, EffectScript_OpUpdateParticles (child emitters), sub_14031B964, sub_14031C964 and the sub_14034xxx special renderers
callees: EffectAnchor_GetPoint, SceneObject_FindBySlot, sub_14027471C, sub_140274BC0, sub_140274B34, sub_140387AD4, sub_140249000
purpose: Spawns the particles of one effect emitter at time t: count, position, velocity, mass, forces, life, homing and children from its 196-byte record.

behavior.text: record = section 3 + 196 * emitter; offsets below are the code's (they include the 20-byte section header). A value pair (a, b) is a + curve * (b - a) / 256 with curve c = a byte of section 4 at 4 + 160 (c - 1) + t % 160 (c = 0: a alone).

it spawns only when t % interval (+200 -> +202, curve +35 & 15) is 0, then count particles (+196 -> +198, curve +32 >> 20 & 15); each gets sprite animation +21 of section 1 and frame set +24 (EffectSprite_StepAnimation).

position = anchor (+22 & 0xE00: 0x200 a map tile, 0x400 the caster, 0x600 the target, 0x800 the parent particle, 0xA00 the map centre, 0xC00 a scene unit) + offset (+40 xyz -> +46, curve +28 & 15) + random -s..s per axis (s = +52 xyz -> +58, curve +28 >> 4 & 15).

velocity by +26 & 0x410: 0x10 = toward the emitter point at a speed random in +112..+114 (-> +116 / +118, curve +28 >> 28); otherwise a vector (0, speed, 0) turned by angles +64 xyz (-> +70, curve +28 >> 8) plus a random part within +76 xyz (-> +82, curve +28 >> 12; half the start value without a curve), 4096 = one turn; both are multiplied by 8 into the 12-bit velocity.

homing point +68 = by +22 & 0xE0 (0x60 the caster, 0x80 the target, 0x40 a map position, 0xA0 the map centre, 0 / 0x20 fixed) + (+176 xyz -> +182, curve +32 >> 12); homing strength +82 = random +204..+206 (-> +208 / +210, curve +32 >> 28 & 3); particle curve +77 = +32 >> 30; children: +212 on death, +213 every step (+26 & 3, & 0xC say when).
the caster and target points come from EffectAnchor_GetPoint: a unit's scene position, or a tile as (28 x + 14, -12 height, 28 z + 14).

every stock emitter record decodes by these rules; simulated, Blood Drain (effect 210: 10 emitters over 105 frames; effect 335: 5 emitters over 64 frames) shows droplets at the target and blood carried to the caster.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_1403847D8). The random numbers come from the game xorshift state (xmmword_1408E5FC8).
open_questions: ? the flag modes 0x410 (a camera-relative variant) and 0x1040 in full; ? the curve rate for the spawner (t is the phase time).

name: EffectFile_GetTrackRow
purpose: Returns the two numbers that locate the data file of one battle effect: its file number in the game pack and its size in bytes.

behavior.text: reads one 8-byte row (file number, size) at index effect from one of two 512-row tables in .rdata: dword_1406739C0 when the language flag at g_LanguageInfo + 8 is non-zero (or g_LanguageInfo is null), dword_1406749C0 otherwise.

there is no bound check on the effect index; the tables hold 512 rows each (512 x 8 bytes; the second table starts that far after the first), so an index of 512 or more reads whatever follows the table.

in the table used with the English pack, effect E (E at least 2) names the file called efc_eNNNdat_data in the pack file list (effect 260 = file 1133); rows 0 and 1 both point at file 901; the sizes are the stored size rounded up to 2048. The other table holds file number minus one in every non-empty row and the same sizes.
398 of the 512 rows are filled; a size of 0 marks an empty row (114 rows).
a leaf with no stack frame and no unwind entry: rcx = the effect, rdx and r8 the two out pointers; it writes [rdx] and [r8] and returns.
row 511 is empty in both tables and no stock effect word selects it.

notes: Name is ours.
open_questions: ? which languages use the second table (it has the numbering of a pack whose list is one number lower).

name: EffectFile_ResetBasePointers
purpose: Points every entry of the 512-slot effect base array at the one shared effect buffer.

behavior.text: fills qword_143740220 (512 pointers) with the address unk_1418A2E00 and returns that address.
every effect number therefore resolves to the same buffer; only one effect file is resident at a time.

notes: Name is ours. The array has no room past 512 entries: the next object follows at qword_143740220 + 0x1000.
open_questions: ? when sub_140348658 runs (battle set-up is the likely moment).

name: EffectFile_UploadTexture
purpose: Registers the two palettes and copies the picture stored at the end of the loaded effect file into the 1024 by 512 video page.

behavior.text: the texture section is the file base plus the header dword at +36; the pointer is saved in qword_1411A3840.
the first 512 bytes of that section go to the palette manager as bank 12 and the next 512 as bank 13 (sub_1402F7594 with mode 0).

at section + 1024 a 24-bit byte count and, in the fourth byte, a flag: flag non-zero = 128 halfwords wide, else 64 halfwords wide; the height is count / 256 or count / 128 respectively; the picture data starts at section + 1028.
the rectangle is placed at x = 384, y = 0 of the page and copied by VramPage_CopyRect.
when the current effect number is 71 it then clears one more small rectangle of the page (sub_14025FCDC).
the Potion file (effect 260) ends exactly at section + 1028 + 32768, a picture 64 halfwords by 256 rows.

notes: Name is ours. The picture is 8 bits per pixel against the palettes (I: from the 128 byte row for 64 halfwords).
open_questions: ? the exact rectangle cleared for effect 71.

name: EffectFlash_Start
callers: EffectSequence_Run (slot 4 of the effect sequence handler table (0x140682F30))
purpose: Sequence kind 4 handler: the screen flash effect that tints the view with an element colour.

behavior.text: state 1 reads the effect kind from the entry (word +4) and the element mask (word +6); the kind's parameter word (EffectKindRecords, +2) picks a row of EffectFlashProfiles.
the element mask is matched against ElementMaskOrder (nine masks) and replaced by the position of the first match, which later picks the tint of ElementColours (three bytes per slot).

copies the seven profile words into the live flash state; the high byte of the last word picks a row of EffectBlendWeights, whose seven weights scale the tint (weight * colour >> 8) while the flash runs.
later states animate the flash and write the scaled colours into the sprite colour records.

notes: Name is ours; the function is long (about 470 lines) and only the table reads were decoded.
open_questions: ?: the animation states after the set-up.

name: EffectNxd_AdjustSpriteKind
purpose: Changes an effect sprite's draw kind when the effect row's flag asks for it.

behavior.text: when the effect row's flag byte is set (unknown_1c, read by EffectNxd_HasFlag28), draw kind 20 becomes 21 and 23 becomes 24.

notes: Name is ours.

name: EffectNxd_DepthBiasFloat
purpose: Returns the depth bias float of a DepthBias table row.

behavior.text: reads the DepthBias table row (table 315) of the id and returns its +4 as a float.

notes: Name is ours.

name: EffectNxd_HasFlag24
purpose: Reports whether the RefinedVFXTexture row of an effect has its byte at +24 set.

behavior.text: false for an effect of 0 or less, for a missing table or a missing row; otherwise the byte at row +24 is non-zero.

notes: Name is ours. The column is Unknown18 in the table layout.
open_questions: ? what the flag selects (sub_1400D28E4 uses it to decide whether to call sub_1400D2C74).

name: EffectNxd_HasFlag25
purpose: Reports whether the RefinedVFXTexture row of an effect has its byte at +25 set.

behavior.text: false for an effect of 0 or less, for a missing table or a missing row; otherwise the byte at row +25 is non-zero.

notes: Name is ours. The column is Unknown19 in the table layout.

name: EffectNxd_HasFlag28
purpose: Reports whether the RefinedVFXTexture row of an effect has its byte at +28 set.

behavior.text: false for an effect of 0 or less, for a missing table or a missing row; otherwise the byte at row +28 is non-zero.
sub_1400D2D30 uses it to swap a model type of 20 for 21 and 23 for 24.

notes: Name is ours. The column is Unknown1C in the table layout.

name: EffectNxd_LoadRow
purpose: Reads the Enhanced parameter row of the current effect from the RefinedVFXTexture table (id 202) and applies it to the effect renderer and to the loaded effect data.

behavior.text: stores the effect number at rendererSlot + 88; finds table 202 through NxdRegistry_Find (cached in qword_143CD9F88) and the row whose key equals the effect number; with no table or no row it returns at once and changes nothing else.

from the row it copies two bytes (row +26, +27) into rendererSlot + 92 and + 94, converts the dword at row +12 (the depth bias id) with sub_1400D2D6C into the float at g_CharaRenderer + 147936, and takes the float at row +20 for a scale that sets dword_1407DC4F8 and dword_1407DC6C8.

it then looks up table 317 (RefinedVFXCameraControl, cached in qword_143CD9F80) by the row dword at +16; with no such row it stops. With a row it zeroes or shifts per-slot colour words inside the effect section at qword_1411A3860 (21 entries of 6 bytes at +5394 / +5858 / +5520 / +5984) by the row values.

the stock table has 487 rows, keys 0..486; most rows hold the same values (depth bias id 2, camera id 0, scale -1.0 in +20, flags 0 0 1 255) but the rows vary: the camera control key (+0x10) is 1 on key 452 only, own_texture (+0x18) is 1 on 16 rows, +0x19 on 58, +0x1A is 0 on 10, +0x1B is 127 on one, +0x1C is 1 on 17, and one row has colour scale (+8) 0.5 and +0x14 2.0. The camera table has one row, key 1.

the row columns read: +8 colour scale (Effect_TintByNxdScale multiplies the sprite colour bytes by it, 1.0 without a row), +0xC depth bias id, +0x10 camera control key, +0x14 a float that sets two scaled globals (dword_1407DC4F8 and dword_1407DC6C8), +0x18 own_texture (EffectNxd_HasFlag24), +0x19 (read by EffectNxd_HasFlag25, not in this body; stored per texture page, no reader of the stores found), +0x1A and +0x1B copied to renderer slot +92 and +94, +0x1C (read by EffectNxd_HasFlag28, not in this body; changes sprite draw kinds 20 to 21 and 23 to 24).

RefinedVFXCameraControl row: the words at +8, +10 and +12 (columns offset_x, offset_y, offset_z) are added to the first, second and third word of the 21 entries of the tables at +5518.. and +5982.. of the section qword_1411A3860 points to; the byte at +14 sets two words (+5812, +6276) to -1 instead and nothing else of the row is applied; the bytes at +15, +16 and +17 (columns zero_x, zero_y, zero_z) first zero the first, second and third word of the 21 entries of the tables at +5392.. and +5856..; the bytes at +18 and +19 are not read.

the field it writes at rendererSlot + 88 (g_CharaRenderer + 0x24418 for the effect slot) is written by this function (through rcx + 0x58) and set to -1 at 0x140319FBE (Effect_RunStateMachine) and 0x14031A760 (sub_14031A740); a scan of every instruction for the displacement 0x24418 found no reader (a read through another base register is not excluded: I).

notes: Name is ours. Because a missing row leaves the renderer fields as the previous effect left them, an effect without a row inherits the last values.
open_questions: ? what the two 21-entry word tables of qword_1411A3860 hold (camera points: I); what the two globals scaled from +0x14 size; what renderer slots +92 and +94, draw kinds 20, 21, 23, 24 and the three page flag globals are used for (readers not found).

name: EffectNxd_SelectPageTexture
purpose: Picks the texture slot for an effect sprite on a refined texture page (6, 7 or 8) and records its flag.

behavior.text: for pages 6, 7 and 8 returns the effect's own texture slot (10291 / 10307 / 10323 plus the effect) and stores dword_142E7FEE8 / EC / F0 = 2 * effect + 1426.
stores the unknown_19 flag of the effect row (EffectNxd_HasFlag25) per page in dword_140C6ADA0 / A4 / A8; no reader of those three globals was found.

notes: Name is ours.

name: EffectNxd_SpriteKindA
callers: sub_140348924, sub_14034B9F0, sub_14034CC14, sub_14034DE90 and others
purpose: Chooses an effect sprite's draw kind, then, when the effect has its own texture, its texture slot.

behavior.text: calls EffectNxd_AdjustSpriteKind first, then, when the effect row's own_texture byte is set (EffectNxd_HasFlag24), EffectNxd_SelectPageTexture.

notes: Name is ours.

name: EffectNxd_SpriteKindB
purpose: A second form of EffectNxd_SpriteKindA used by the piece emitter.

behavior.text: same steps as EffectNxd_SpriteKindA: sprite kind adjustment, then, with own_texture set, the page texture selection.

notes: Name is ours.

name: EffectPalette_Step
callers: EffectSequence_Run (slot 18 of the effect sequence handler table (0x140682F30))
purpose: Sequence kind 18 handler: a full screen palette effect that starts from six seed colours.

behavior.text: state 1 clears the effect's sprite records and writes the six 5-bit RGB seed colours of EffectPaletteSeeds, packed into 15-bit colour words, twice into the live palette (12 words).
state 2 steps the palette using words of the entry; the kind's parameter word is read from EffectKindRecords (+2).
the states after the first were not decoded.

notes: Name is ours.

name: EffectParticle_StepPhysics
purpose: Moves every effect particle one step: position by velocity, velocity by gravity, drag and force, force by its change or by homing.

behavior.text: 12-bit fixed point: pos (+20, +24, +28) += vel (+32, +36, +40); vel = (gravity * weight (+18) >> 12) + ((mass (+16) - drag) * vel + force (+44, +48, +52) << 12) / mass.

with no homing strength (+82 = 0) the force grows by its change (+56, +60, +64) each step; with one, v = strength * unit vector to the homing point (+68, +70, +72), and force = v + force + k * (change - v) / 127 with k = the particle curve (+77, read at age +88) - 128, or -128 without a curve.
gravity and drag are the globals EffectScript_OpLoadPhysics fills from section 3.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_140388170).

name: EffectScript_OpCallCallback
purpose: Effect script opcode: runs one effect callback at once.

behavior.text: unless paused or stepping, takes the callback from the effect callback table (0x1406759C0) by the signed word at instruction offset + 2, keeps it in the context (+288) and calls it with the context's word at +2.
always advances the instruction offset by 4 and returns 1.

notes: Name is ours.

name: EffectScript_OpLoadPhysics
purpose: Effect script opcode 0x27: loads the effect's gravity and drag from the header of section 3.

behavior.text: section 3 +4 / +8 = gravity x, y (qword_143C51D70), +12 = gravity z (dword_143C51D78), +16 = drag (dword_143C51D4C); the emitter records follow the 20-byte header, 196 bytes each.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_14031B9DC).

name: EffectScript_OpRunTimeline
callees: EffectScript_RunEmitterTracks, EffectScript_RunColourTracks, SoundCue_Play, sub_14038387C, sub_140381C08, sub_140381F50, sub_1403823F0, sub_140310B64
purpose: Effect script opcode 0x28: runs one step of the effect's timeline (emitter tracks, colour tracks, sound tracks, camera tracks) and counts the frame.

behavior.text: calls EffectScript_RunEmitterTracks and EffectScript_RunColourTracks, then steps three sound tracks of section 7 + 8 (54 bytes apart: +644 durations, +678 sound bytes, +696 count; a byte above 1 plays SoundCue_Play(cue + dword_14114B124 - 1)) and three camera tracks (section 7 +1748 / +1850 / +1952 points, +2054 times).
the frame counter is ctx +44 (incremented when bit 2 of dword_1407B0758 is set); opcode 0x1D loops back until it reaches the u16 at section 7 + 8 + 2, the effect length in frames.

the 2-byte opcodes are read through tbl_EffectScriptHandlers (index & 0x1FF); section 2 of every stock file checked is the same short program: 0x2A reset, 0x27 load physics, then a loop of 0x28 / 0x25 until 0x1D says the length is reached.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_14031C2DC). The opcode numbers (0x1D, 0x25, 0x27, the 0x1FF mask) belong to EffectScript_Run and the handler table, not to this body.
open_questions: ? the camera track records (+1748..+2054) in detail.

name: EffectScript_OpSetCallback
purpose: Effect script opcode: attaches one of the effect callbacks to a live callback slot.

behavior.text: unless the game is paused or stepping, stores the callback pointer chosen by the signed word at instruction offset + 2 (the effect callback table at 0x1406759C0) into slot ((byte at +1) >> 2) & 0x3F of the live callback list.
always advances the instruction offset by 4 and returns 1 (go on with the next opcode).

notes: Name is ours.

name: EffectScript_OpUpdateParticles
purpose: Effect script opcode 0x25: moves every particle of the effect, draws it, runs its child emitters and removes it when its life ends.

behavior.text: EffectParticle_StepPhysics on the particle list (ctx +216), then per particle the draw routine of its kind (+84 >> 12, through the table at 0x140693070: the stock kinds 0..3 all draw with Effect_TintByNxdScale).
a particle whose +86 & 0xC is 4 or 8 spawns its every-step child emitter (+91) at each step; its age (+88) counts 0..159 and wraps.

the life (+74) counts down; -1 means until its sprite animation holds its last frame (node +22 = 0); at the end a particle whose +86 & 3 is 1 or 2 spawns its death child emitter (+90), then it is removed (sub_14038449C).
a particle with a stop radius (+86 >> 4 & 0x30) ends when it comes within that distance of its homing point (+68).

notes: Name is ours (was sub_14031B768). Effect_TintByNxdScale is reached through the draw table at 0x140693070, not as a direct call.

name: EffectScript_Run
callees: the opcode handlers, reached only through the table (two of them are the callback opcodes documented as EffectScript_OpSetCallback and EffectScript_OpCallCallback)
purpose: Runs the opcodes of one effect script until it yields or ends.

behavior.text: the script context of a slot is a 312-byte record (156 words); +6 is the instruction offset and +8 the script base pointer.
loops: opcode = the word at the instruction offset masked with 0x1FF, handler = the 120-slot table (0x1406830F0), called with the context.

a handler result of 0 yields for this frame (the function returns 1), a non-zero result goes on with the next opcode and a result of 2 ends the script (clears the running-script global and returns 0).
when the pause manager flag 8 or the stepping flag 2 is set it restores the saved instruction position afterwards, so a paused script does not advance.

notes: Name is ours. The table has 120 slots although the opcode is masked with 0x1FF.
open_questions: ?: the meaning of the individual opcodes.

name: EffectScript_RunColourTracks
purpose: Runs the colour-fade tracks of the effect timeline: palette fades on the screen, the caster and the targets.

behavior.text: four tracks in section 7 + 8: +806 durations (x 8 frames) with +971 mode bytes and +872.. colour offsets, +1006 / +1171, +1206 / +1371, +1406 / +1670; a mode byte with bit 7 starts a fade (sub_1402F7A90, sub_1402F7C20 per target unit, sub_1402F5C20 / sub_1402F5428 for the screen).

notes: Name is ours (was sub_14031BE2C).
open_questions: ? the exact meaning of each track (screen, caster, target).

name: EffectScript_RunEmitterTracks
purpose: Runs the five emitter tracks of the effect timeline: each track is a list of phases, and the emitter of the running phase is asked to spawn particles.

behavior.text: the tracks are 128 bytes each from section 7 + 8 (qword_1411A3818); phase k (from 1) starts at track word 1 + k and ends at word 2 + k (frames), byte 53 + k is its emitter + 1 (0 = none), word 39 + k & 7 is its mode, word 39 + k is also handed to sub_14031BA38 when the phase starts.
mode 0 calls EffectEmitter_Spawn(ctx, t, emitter, 0) with t = the frames since the phase began; a mode 1..7 calls the ctx callback slot (ctx +224 + 8 (mode - 1)) instead.
the IDA database had this function under a library name (EffectScript_RunEmitterTracks); the body is the effect scheduler.

notes: Name is ours (was __ld12mul_1, a wrong library match).
open_questions: ? what sub_14031BA38 does with the phase word.

name: EffectSequence_Run
purpose: Per frame driver of the effect sequence entries: runs the handler of every active entry and retires finished ones.

behavior.text: runs the effect state machine first, then walks the linked list of active sequence entries (96 bytes each, at most 17 per frame).
the handler comes from the effect sequence handler table (0x140682F30) by the kind byte at +3 of the entry (kinds above 22 end the walk); a non-zero result keeps the entry.
a zero result retires the entry: frees an attached object, unlinks it from the active list and appends it to the free list.
it also sets the stepping flags (1 or 2) from the frame counter against a frame skip count, and returns whether any entry or the state machine still runs.

notes: Name is ours.
open_questions: ?: what frame skip counts 0, 1 and 2 correspond to in play.

name: EffectSound_PickSlotValue
purpose: Picks the value a battle effect's sound slot plays this time, by the slot's mode and its play counter.

behavior.text: the slot is 4 bytes at section 6 (qword_1411A3828) + 8 + 4 slot: mode, v0, v1, v2; the play counter is a byte per slot at dword_1418732CC, incremented on every call.
mode 0 returns v0; 1 v0 / v1 by the counter parity; 2 v0 on the first call, v1 after; 3 v0 on the first call, then v1 / v2 by parity; 4 v0, v1, v2 by counter % 3; another mode returns 0.
EffectScript_OpRunTimeline plays SoundCue_Play(value + dword_14114B124 - 1) when the value is not 0.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_14031BBDC).

name: EffectSprite_EmitPieces
proto: int64 EffectSprite_EmitPieces(EffectSpritePrim *prim, int16 *pos, int64 a3, int64 a4, int64 *list)
purpose: Turns an effect sprite's current frame pieces into textured quads at the sprite's position.

behavior.text: one quad per piece (count = prim byte +3); a piece is 24 bytes: +0 u16 palette row (low 4 bits, bit 0x10 = the second bank: palette id (w & 0xF) + 4 * ((w & 0x10) | 0x1EC0)), +1 bit 0x02 semi-transparent, +2 u16 texture page, +4 u, +5 v, +6 width, +7 height in the texture, +8..+23 four corners as s16 x, y (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right).
the corners are rotated / projected by the camera matrix (sub_1400D372C) around the sprite position.

texture page bits 5-6 = blend (0 average, 1 add, 2 subtract, 3 add a quarter), bits 7-8 = depth (0 = 4 bits, 1 = 8 bits); the stock files use x = 6 (video page x 384), where the file's texture is uploaded.
for effects 467..472 with 4 pieces it widens the pieces by 2 / 4 units (seam fix); Effect_PatchPolygonSeams runs first.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_140380878).

name: EffectSprite_StepAnimation
proto: int64 EffectSprite_StepAnimation(EffectSpriteNode *node, char r, char g, char b)
purpose: Steps one effect sprite's animation script and, on a frame change, points the sprite at the new frame's pieces; then draws it.

behavior.text: when not paused and bit 0 of dword_1407B0758 is set, the hold counter (node +22, s16) drops by 2; at 0 or below the next step of the script (node +24 pointer, node +32 position) is read.

script steps are 3 bytes: frame (0..127), hold (stored at +22), a depth mode (stored at +20); a hold of 0 leaves the position on that step (the frame stays). A first byte of 0x80 or more is a code: 0x81 back to the start, 0x82 then s16 x, s16 y = set the position (+8, +10), 0x83 then s8 dx, dy = move it.

a new frame (node +35 differs) sets +6 bit 0; then the frame set offset is the s16 at section 0 + byte node +34, the frame record at section 0 + the u16 at (that offset + 2 * frame), its piece count at record +2 and its pieces (24 bytes each) from record +4; the sprite primitive (+40) gets one pointer per piece (a new primitive when the count changes).
the depth mode picks the drawing order slot: 1 = depth - 8, 2 = 8, 3 = 382, 4 = 16, 5 = depth - 16, else the projected depth / 4, clamped 0..382; the sprite is drawn by EffectSprite_EmitPieces.

section 0 is the file's header dword [0] + 4 (qword_1411A3850); the script comes from section 1 (qword_1411A3858): EffectEmitter_Spawn sets node +24 to section 1 + the u16 at (2 * emitter byte +21) and node +34 to 2 * emitter byte +24.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_140387B70). The codes 0x81..0x83 are tested in the code as a negative byte and (byte & 0x7F) == 1, 2, 3, so the literal numbers do not appear. Seen from data: every one of the 397 stock effect files decodes by these rules into frames that match its texture sheet.
open_questions: ? the rate of the animator step in seconds (one step per drawn frame at 30 or 60 per second).

name: EffectSprites_Spawn
callers: eight sequence kind handlers (sub_140313E10, sub_140314A74, sub_140314BA4, sub_140314CC8, sub_140314EA4, sub_140314FD4, sub_1403159EC, sub_140316160)
callees: sprite setup routine, free sprite slot allocator
purpose: Creates the sprites of one effect sprite group when the effect is inside the group's frame window.

behavior.text: the record of the group is EffectSpriteSpawnRecords (46 bytes per group); it spawns only while the effect's frame word lies in the window of bytes +2 / +3 and its live count is below byte +4.
creates up to the count at +42 sprites: takes a free sprite slot, sets up the sprite from the record with the sprite setup routine, marks it active (0x80) and increments the live count.
the sprite definition pointer comes from a list indexed by byte +0 of the record.

notes: Name is ours. A second spawner, sub_1403138DC, reads the same records.

name: EntryUnits_CheckLookBudget
proto: bool EntryUnits_CheckLookBudget(int slot, int16_t sprite, int budget)
purpose: Keeps the list of distinct sprite numbers met while the entry units of a battle are placed and answers whether a unit's sprite is past the budget.

behavior.text: slot 255 clears the count (dword_143D1A16C); slot 0 starts the list (word_143D1A170) with the sprite and returns false.
any other slot: finds the sprite in the list, appends it when absent, and returns true when its position is not below the budget.
its only caller, Battle_PlaceEntryUnits, passes the entry index and 9 - scene variable 57 (0 when the variable is above 9), and drops the unit on true.

notes: Behavior: EntryUnitsShareADistinctLookBudget.

name: EquipDetail_BuildCategoryLines
callees: StatusLists_BuildOrder, AbilityTable_GetRow, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, UITable_GetRowByKey, sub_1400FA2C4
purpose: Builds the text of the equipment detail category lines (UIStatusEffectCategory, nxd 56) for the equipment attribute record in the third argument.

behavior.text: walks the category order list built by StatusLists_BuildOrder, gets each category row and switches on the category key.
key 1 (Permanent): starts from the record's status set at +24 (5 bytes) and removes every status whose UIStatusEffect row +8 (column ui_status_effect_category) is not 1.
key 2 lists the ability names of the record's bytes +44 and +45 (AbilityTable_GetRow).
key 3 (Applies): starts from the 5 bytes at +9..+13 and adds the statuses of the set at +24 whose UIStatusEffect row +8 is 3.
keys 8, 10 and 11 use record bytes +32, +31 and +30; key 9 uses +19..+23; key 13 reads two item ids at +36 and +40 through UITable 0x2D and their UIStatusEffect rows (sorted by row word +0x20).
status names are drawn with sub_1400FA2C4 from the UIStatusEffect name string.
while building the ordered status lines it skips a status whose UIStatusEffect byte +0x22 (column hidden_in_equipment_detail) is non-zero.

open_questions: ? the other category keys' record fields.

name: EquipDetail_Refresh
callers: sub_1400ED254, sub_14019A110, sub_1401AEEF0, sub_14022F868 (two sites), sub_1402A54E8, sub_1402E600C (two sites)
purpose:
Refreshes the item detail panel for one selected item: it builds the item's large picture path, then binds the picture and the
item name to the panel's parts.

behavior.text: takes the panel object and a selection record whose first dword is the item id.

returns early when a pointer field of the panel is null, or when a helper called with the panel's own record area rejects the
  selection.
copies a 16-byte block out of the selection record into the panel at +0x2A0.
formats the large item picture path for the selected id into a 260-byte stack buffer.

calls the shared item-cell binder with the same id, that path and show-empty cleared, so the large picture and the name go to
  the panel's icon and text parts.
eight direct call sites.
all eight are UI controllers: item, shop and unit screens, because each one binds the large picture or refreshes a panel.

the panel is the equipment/item detail panel, because its callers are item, shop and unit screens and it binds the large
  picture rather than the small list one.
what the early-out helper validates about the selection record.

notes: - V: the head and the large-path site were read; the rest of the body (1746 bytes) was not.
open_questions: - ?: the exact field at panel +0x2A0 that receives the copied block.

name: EquipDetail_SetHelpText
callees: ItemTable_GetRow, Item_GetRecord, Item_GetWeaponRecord, sub_1402A0E58, GUITextNode_SetTextExpandedTemp, GUINode_ApplyStateAtFrame
purpose: Writes one help line of the equipment detail panel: line 0 = the item's description from Item-en, line 1 = three lines built by sub_1402A0E58, line 2 = weapon notes.

behavior.text: line 0: ItemTable_GetRow(item +0); returns without touching the text when the row is missing, else the string at row +16 (relative to row +4) goes into the line's text node.
line 2 (item +8 != 5): for a record with slot bit 0x80 and a weapon record, UI texts 934, or 923 / 3812 and 924 / 3813 by weapon flag bits, are appended.
an empty line shows UI text 917; 'ShowJobIcon' / 'HideJobIcon' follows line 2.

notes: With no Item-en row the description node keeps the previous item's text (V: the early return; I: that is why item 300 showed the Rod's description).
open_questions: ? what item +8 == 5 means here; the callers pass different item structs (the shop passes its 40-byte entry).

name: EquipScreen_InitVram
purpose: Uploads the palette and strips of the equipment screen to VRAM and resets the equipment lists.

behavior.text: uploads the staging block to a VRAM rectangle at x 256 and the 64 x 4 word palette block (0x1407B4E60) to the rectangle at x 256, y 250.
uploads two more small strips built through sub_14025FC38, then clears an eight-byte state and sets four words to 0xFFFF.
takes a snapshot of the inventory including the equipped items and synchronises the saved order lists of groups 0..4 (sub_14039684C), then zeroes the screen's work block.
the item-order work and the call from the unit equipment screen task (sub_14033E038) show this is the equipment screen's set-up.

notes: IDA carried a wrong library name for this function; the code is the screen set-up above. The four words are set by storing -1 (0xFFFF); the value 0xFFFF does not appear as a literal in the body.
open_questions: ?: what the two small strips are.

name: EquipSprite_BuildPieces
purpose: Builds the sprite piece records of a unit's held item for one animation frame.

behavior.text: at the start it reads the equipment palette row of the item id at unit +336 (Item_GetEquipPalette) and keeps byte +1 of it (0 when the item has none).

for each piece of the frame it writes a piece record whose texture row is 8 * (that byte + the frame piece's row value): the byte is the row of the item's picture in the equipment sheet, in steps of 8 pixels.
returns 256 when the frame number is above 256 or the frame has no data (index -1).
one picture per item, from the stock values of the byte; the stock rows were not re-counted here.

name: Errand_ApplyResult
purpose: Applies a finished errand's result to the save: event flags, gil, loot, JP and the active list.

behavior.text: clears 0x02 (dispatched) of the errand's state nibble (event variable 864 + the slot's errand byte) and sets 0x04 (succeeded) when g_ErrandGrade is 0.
adds the pending gil to variable 44, capped at 99,999,999, and refreshes the displayed gil.
for loot kind 1 or 2 sets the won treasure's variable (801 + index or 848 + index) to 1.

for each party unit it clears the busy byte; if its JP gain is non-negative, the unit exists, its flag bit 0x20 is clear and its job is not 161 or 164, it adds the gain to both the unit's current and total JP of its job (16-bit values at +128 and +174, capped at 9999), recomputes the job level nibble and rebuilds the unlock mask into +47..49 with Unit_BuildJobUnlockMask.
on success stores the date (event variables 46 / 47) as the errand's 9 bits of g_ErrandFinishDay (DateBits_Store9); with a treasure find also the treasure's date (0x1411A71E8 / 0x1411A7260).
writes the errand's delay byte g_ErrandDelay[errand] = 0x60 when g_ErrandGrade is 1, 0x90 when it is 2.
removes the active record by shifting later 9-byte records down and decrementing the active count.
the JP / level index is Job_IdToIndex of the save record's job byte (+2, the record in rsi).

notes: This is where a unit's JP in each job is increased by errands (16-bit arrays at +128 and +174).

name: Errand_BoardInput
callees: Errand_SelectBoardEntry, sub_1402D0458, sub_14019DF88, Errand_Recall, sub_14019DCD4, sub_1402D541C, sub_1401A1D28, Errand_ComputeRewards, sub_14036FCB8, sub_14036CB1C
purpose: The tavern errand board's input step: dispatch a chosen errand, collect a returned one, recall one, or leave.

behavior.text: after a closing message, either picks the board entry under the cursor (Errand_SelectBoardEntry with the entry's 11-bit id from g_ErrandBoardList) or goes back (sub_1402D0458).

reads the board widget's request (sub_14019DF88) and switches on it: 0x0D collects the selected returned errand (finds its active slot by the errand byte, then Errand_ComputeRewards and sub_14036FCB8), 0x18 recalls it (Errand_Recall), 6 calls sub_14036CB1C, others set screen states.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_1402ED540).

name: Errand_BuildActiveList
purpose: Fills the board list with the errands that are away (dispatched and not yet back) for the legacy list window.

behavior.text: for each active slot whose flag byte has no 0x04: the board list entry = errand byte - 0x3000, the word list entry 8 when the slot's flag has 0x02, else 0 (the index is range-checked against 0x80 entries); the slot index goes into the window's row table.
then sets up the list window (sub_140379F3C, sub_140379DF0) with at most 6 visible rows.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_140370F38).

name: Errand_BuildBoard
callers: (the tavern errand screen; not traced here)
callees: Errand_LoadRecord, Errand_BuildBoardEntry, PreviewUnit_BuildRecord, sub_14019DC5C, sub_14019DCD4, sub_1402D541C, sub_1400F6C8C, sub_1401E8B7C
purpose:
Builds the list of errands the tavern board shows: one entry per errand record, marked as available, dispatched or returning,
with the preview of the units on a dispatched errand.

behavior.text: starts a local array of 96 (state, active index) pairs, every state 4 ("not dispatched").

walks the active errand slots (`g_ErrandActive`, 9-byte records, count `byte_140D407B2`): a slot whose errand number
  (record byte 1) is below 0x60 marks that errand state 2 (byte 0 bit 2 clear) or 3 (record byte 4 equal to
  `dword_140D493E8`; I: the errand returns in the current town), with the slot index.

for every errand 0..95 (`cmp 60h` loop end): loads its record (Errand_LoadRecord), then either asks
  Errand_BuildBoardEntry (state 4; a zero answer skips the errand) or builds the unit previews of the dispatched slot (up to
  three units, record bytes 6..8; unit indices below 0x36 read the unit records, others use fixed fallback values).

appends `errand - 0x3000` as a u16 to the board list at `dword_140D498F0` (range check at 0x100 bytes: at most 128
  entries) and reads the errand's 2-byte new-flag pair `byte_1411A7319[2 * errand]` for errands below 0x60 (the live copy of
  the save field ffto_world bar.mouke.menu_new: is_new, is_newarrival).
hands the list to the UI and sets the screen state (sub_14019DCD4, sub_1402D541C, dword_140D49ABC = 9).

notes:
Limits of the errand count: the 96 compares here (0x1402ED103, 0x1402ED347, 0x1402ED43B)
and in sub_14036E5DC (0x14036EA2C, 0x14036EA79), the 96-pair local array, the 128-entry board list, and the per-errand save
fields (world mouke_delay[96], mouke_finishday[108], ffto_world bar.mouke.menu_new[96 x 2], active slots mouke_event[8] with
a u8 errand number).

The board list entry of an errand is
0xD000 + errand (the 11-bit id), and the new-flag read indexes with the errand's low byte.

The errand number in an active slot is a byte, so a save can name at most 256 errands.
open_questions: ? What the 108 entries of mouke_finishday hold beyond the 96 errands.

name: Errand_BuildBoardEntry
purpose: Decides whether an errand that is not dispatched goes on the tavern board and fills its board entry.

behavior.text: sets entry +0x144 to -1, then reads the errand state nibble EventVar_Read(864 + errand): with 0x02 or 0x04 set it returns 0 (dispatched or already completed).
returns 0 when the low 6 bits of the errand delay byte g_ErrandDelay[errand] are not 0 (days left before it is offered again).
returns 0 unless Errand_IsAvailable(errand, dword_140D493E8 + 1) (the town the party is in, plus 1).

fills the entry: +0x13C = bit 0x08 of the nibble, +0x150 / +0x154 = words 6 and 7 of g_ErrandRow (the fewest and most days), three unit slots of 0x68 bytes from +0x60 set to -1, +0x138 = the errand, +0x148 = the first new flag g_ErrandNewFlags[2 * errand] when the errand byte is below 0x60 and not negative (else 0); returns 1.

notes: Named before this sheet. The new-flag read indexes with the low byte of the errand (an id of 0x100 and up would pass the test). The caller has loaded g_ErrandRow for the errand before.
open_questions: ? what bit 0x08 of the nibble means on the board (Errand_Start sets it with 0x02).

name: Errand_ComputeRewards
purpose: Computes JP and gil rewards, the grade and the bonus loot for one active errand when it ends.

behavior.text: loads the record of the active slot's errand and records the slot number; then chooses a featured unit.
the selector word decides it: 1 highest Brave, 2 lowest Brave, 3 highest Faith, 4 lowest Faith; a single unit is featured as is.

calls Errand_ScoreParty, then, unless failure is forced, sets each unit's JP from the JP tier table and its gil from the gil tier table, scaled by the grade (JP 100, 10 or 5 percent; gil 100, 20 or 5 percent), plus the unit's score.
calls Errand_RollBonusLoot, which may add more JP, a bonus gil amount and a treasure.

the days elapsed minus the record's base day count, clamped to 0..9, indexes a day-bonus table that scales JP and gil of every unit by a percentage (about 100 to 120 for JP, 100 to 150 for gil); a negative difference gives no scaling.
the featured unit appears to drive the pose or text shown in the result scene.

notes: The selector value is 4 in all stock records.
open_questions: Whether the selector word or the unread evenly spread word 15 is the intended one.

name: Errand_Finish
purpose: Ends an active errand: totals the gil, queues a result entry and applies the result.

behavior.text: sums the per-unit gil results of the party and adds the bonus gil to form the pending gil total.
appends an entry of kind 17 to the result queue with the active slot recorded in it.
calls Errand_ApplyResult on that entry.
if Errand_TreasureMilestone returns non-zero it continues with `sub_1402D3400`, otherwise with `sub_140370EDC`.

name: Errand_IsAvailable
purpose: Decides whether an errand is offered at a town right now.

behavior.text: loads the errand record; if its town word (16) is non-zero it must equal the given town.
condition bit 0: event variable 111 (story progress) must be at least the record's story threshold (word 21).
condition bit 1: a pair of world values (event variables 46 and 47) is converted and its first value must equal the record's reference word (22).
condition bit 2: event variable 864 + reference (word 22) must have bit 4 set, i.e. the prerequisite errand has been completed with success.
all active conditions must hold; otherwise it returns false.

notes: Bit 2 of the condition flags reuses the reference word as a prerequisite errand number, bit 1 reuses it as a world value.

name: Errand_IsOffered
purpose: Whether an errand is offered at a town now: not dispatched, not completed, no delay left, and available there.

behavior.text: false when EventVar_Read(864 + errand) has 0x02 or 0x04, or when the low 6 bits of g_ErrandDelay[errand] are not 0.
otherwise the answer of Errand_IsAvailable(errand, town + 1).

notes: Name is ours (was sub_1402EE0A4). Whole function read. The callers loop over errands 0..95 (the world map town info, the arrival notices).

name: Errand_LoadRecord
purpose: Copies one 23-byte errand (dispatch) definition out of the executable's errand data block into 23 16-bit words, resolving the two fee fields.

behavior.text: the block starts with an offset table; the first offset locates the array of 23-byte records (96 records, one per errand).
each byte of record `errandIndex` is widened to a 16-bit word in out[0..22].
out[4] and out[5] are then replaced by entries of the 16-bit price table whose offset is the block's second offset (fee components).
the 96 records match the 96 errand flags (event variables 864..959).
used by Errand_IsAvailable, Errand_ComputeRewards, the board builders and several UI and start functions.

over all its callers (the shared record g_ErrandRow and the three functions that load into a buffer of their own: Errand_IsAvailable, sub_1402EDF58, sub_14036E5DC) words 0, 1, 2, 4..12, 16, 17, 19, 21 and 22 are read; words 3, 13, 14, 15, 18 and 20 are read by no function.

notes:
Its three blob operands are at 0x1402CCDC4, 0x1402CCDCB and 0x1402CCDF8; the header offsets it reads are data in the table.

Field meanings by word: 0 category, 1 type, 2 errand number, 4 and 5 fee components, 6 base day count, 9 JP tier, 10 treasure pool, 11 bonus roll, 12 gil tier, 16 town, 17 condition flags, 19 featured-unit selector, 21 story threshold, 22 reference errand.
open_questions: ? what the six unread words (3, 13, 14, 15, 18, 20) were for; word 7 is read (the most days a dispatch may take).

name: Errand_ReactionPose
purpose: Chooses which reaction pose a unit shows in the errand result scene from its Brave, Faith and sex.

behavior.text: Brave and Faith are each classed: below 36 gives class 0, 36..65 gives 1, 66..100 gives 2, above 100 gives 0.
result = basePose + table[3 x faithClass + braveClass] + 3 when the unit is female (bit 7 of the record byte +4 clear).
the table is the reaction matrix in the errand data block; a unit index of 54 or more falls back to a placeholder record.

name: Errand_Recall
callees: sub_1401A1D28, EventVar_Read, EventVar_Write, sub_14019DC5C, Errand_LoadRecord, Errand_BuildBoardEntry, sub_1401A1AE4, sub_1402D541C
purpose: Calls off the dispatched errand selected on the board: its units come back and the errand is offered again.

behavior.text: takes the selected board entry (sub_1401A1D28) and its errand (+0x138); does nothing for a negative one.

finds the active slot whose errand byte equals it, clears the away byte (+0x11E of the g_UnitSaveData record of each of the slot's units below 0x36), moves the later slots down by 9 bytes and lowers g_ErrandActiveCount.

clears bit 0x02 of the errand state nibble (EventVar_Write(864 + errand, value & 0xFFFD)), reloads the record (Errand_LoadRecord), rebuilds the entry with Errand_BuildBoardEntry and hands it to the board widget (sub_1401A1AE4), then sets the screen state (sub_1402D541C).

notes: Name is ours (was sub_1402EE1C8). Whole function read.

name: Errand_RollBonusLoot
purpose: On a successful errand (grade 0) picks a treasure or a random bonus and adds its JP and gil to the result.

behavior.text: does nothing unless the grade is 0; clears the loot kind and the bonus gil first.

treasure pool 1 (loot kind 1) lists the unowned items among event variables 801..831 and picks one uniformly; if all are owned it picks any of the 31. Pool 2 (kind 2) does the same over variables 848..863 (16 entries).
for a treasure the category selects a pair from a table: one tier adds JP to every unit and the other sets the bonus gil.

otherwise, when the bonus-roll word is 1, it rolls 0..99: 60 percent tier 0, 30 percent tier 1, 10 percent tier 2 (loot kind 3), and uses row 3 x (category - 1) + tier of a second pair table in the same way.
the random value comes from the game's shared xorshift generator (15 bits of its output).

notes: The chosen treasure index is stored for Errand_ApplyResult.

name: Errand_ScoreParty
purpose: Scores the 1 to 3 units sent on an errand and sets the party grade (0 best, 2 worst). It works on the active errand's globals and is the 'party matrix' of earlier notes.

behavior.text: if the active record's flag has value 2 it zeroes all per-unit rewards, sets grade 2 and a forced-failure flag, and returns (sub_140371790, the legacy list of dispatches away, sets that flag when a dispatch is called back).

otherwise each unit's score is the sum of five bytes: job fit by errand category (8 rows of 22 columns), job fit by errand type (3 rows), a Brave score and a Faith score (5 values per type, index (stat - 1) / 20) and a level score.

the job column is job - 74 for jobs 74..93, 21 for jobs 94 and above, and 22 for lower ids. Column 22 lies past a row's 22 columns (0..21), so a job below 74 (Ramza's own jobs) reads column 0 of the next category / type row; after the last type row it reads the two pad bytes (0).
nothing random and no day count enters the grade (the days scale only the gil and JP, Errand_ComputeRewards); more units add their scores to the total.

the level score index is 10 x (type - 1) + (level - 1) / 10 into the same base table as the Brave score, so for type 1 it re-reads the Brave values and for types 2 and 3 it runs into the Faith values.
grade from the party total: below 59 gives 2, below 99 gives 1, otherwise 0. Per-unit scores are kept for Errand_ComputeRewards.
a unit index of 54 or more falls back to a placeholder record.
the level-score read is probably unintended; a separate rising 3 x 10 table exists in the data block but no code reads it.

notes: Unit data is the 600-byte save record: job at +2, level at +0x1D, Brave +0x1E, Faith +0x1F.
open_questions: Whether the level-score reading is a porting error.

name: Errand_SelectBoardEntry
purpose: Opens the detail of a board errand: the tavern keeper's line, the record, and the legacy message window.

behavior.text: picks a chance from g_ErrandDelay[errand] (10 with neither of the top two bits, 20 with bit 0x40, 40 for a negative byte) and rolls the random generator: under the chance the keeper says message 47116 with 0xD000 + errand as its argument, else message 0xB879 + errand.
loads the record (Errand_LoadRecord) and opens a message window with message 0x8800 + errand (sub_140379CCC).

notes: Name is ours (was sub_1402ED7E0).
open_questions: ? which banks hold the per-errand messages 0xB879 + id and 0x8800 + id and how many entries they have.

name: Errand_Start
purpose: Starts an errand from the prepared board selection: pays the fee, creates the active record and marks the errand started.

behavior.text: subtracts the fee global from gil (event variable 44) and refreshes the displayed gil.
sets bit 8 (attempted) in event variable 863 + errand number.
appends a 9-byte active record: flag 1, errand index, days elapsed 0, chosen days, town, unit count and the unit ids; the active count is incremented.
each party unit's busy byte in its save record is set to 1.
then sets bit 2 (started) in the errand's event variable and sends the start notification to the achievement system.

notes: Errand flags are event variables 864..959: 2 started, 4 succeeded, 8 attempted. The slot's errand byte is stored as number - 1.

name: Errand_TreasureMilestone
purpose: After a successful errand, reports whether the number of treasures found has reached a milestone.

behavior.text: returns 0 unless the grade is 0 and a treasure was won (loot kind 1 or 2).
counts the owned treasures of the pool (event variables 801..831 for kind 1, 848..863 for kind 2).
compares the count with an 8-entry milestone byte table of that pool and returns index + 1 on a match, else 0.
the non-zero result selects a special notification instead of the normal one.

notes: None.

name: ErrorBanner_Show
purpose: Shows a battle refusal message as the timed red banner.

behavior.text: fills the text node with BattleMsg_TextFromDescriptor and the arguments of BattleMsg_FillArgs.
plays the 'timer' state on the window and the 'Error' state on the second node (+56).
the callers (not this body) also play UI sound cue 106 (sub_1400F4BCC).

notes: Name is ours.

name: EventAngle_Quantize
purpose: Stores a copy of an angle rounded down to a multiple of 4096 in a global, for angles from -16384 to 16383.

behavior.text: the argument is the full dword at +120 of the record at the global pointer off_1407830D8, passed by EventScript_Run before each opcode 0x1F.
when the argument is from -16384 to 16383 inclusive, it sets dword_142FEC53C to the largest multiple of 4096 that is not greater than the argument (buckets -16384, -12288, ..., 12288).
otherwise dword_142FEC53C is left unchanged.
it reads and writes no other memory and returns nothing.

notes: The global is read by no code in this pass; its readers are not traced.

name: EventBlock_ApplyOperands
callers: SceneCallback_Dispatch (mode 1, from the opcode 0x28 case of EventScript_Run) and EventSubScript_RunTask (EventSubScript_RunTask).
callees: EventRef_ResolveSlot, sub_140272D70 (which calls SceneObject_FindBySlot, sub_14027DDB8 and SceneUnit_ReleasePartner)
purpose: The callback installed by opcode 0x28: resolves the unit named by its operands and gives it a 128-byte block, a doubled count and a fixed value, using a block helper.

behavior.text: resolves the id at operand bytes 1 and 2 with EventRef_ResolveSlot, using the low byte of the id as the flag. When the result is 2000 it returns 2000 and does nothing else.
builds a three-word vector: word 0 is operand 3, word 1 is operand 5, word 2 is operand 4 (each a signed byte).
the count is operand 6 plus 256 times operand 7 (unsigned 16-bit).
the scale value is 256 minus 256 times operand 8 (operand 8 shifted left by 8, subtracted from 256).

calls sub_140272D70 with the slot, the vector, the scale value, the slot again and the count. That routine finds the unit node (returns 0 when there is none), calls the block helper sub_14027DDB8 with the scale value, the constant 3, the unit bytes at +136, +137 and +138, the first, third and second vector words, and the constant 1.

when the block helper returns a block, sub_140272D70 copies its 128 bytes into the unit record at +168 through +295, sets the dword at +164 to 0, sets the dword at +68 to twice the count, sets the dword at +72 to 0x2000, calls SceneUnit_ReleasePartner on the node and returns 1.
opcode 0x28 calls this function through SceneCallback_Dispatch mode 1 at the moment the opcode runs, with the address of the instruction's operand 1 as the argument. The opcode does not wait.

notes: The block helper sub_14027DDB8 was not decoded, so what the 128 bytes contain is not stated here.
open_questions: What sub_14027DDB8 computes and what the 128-byte block at unit +168 is used for.

name: EventCamera_MoveTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x1B
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x1B: moves the camera from its current state to six target values over a number of frames.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 7 in `qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`.
reads seven 16-bit values from the instruction's operand bytes (the pointer is in the first field of its task block): six targets and a step count.

the first three targets are compared with the three 16-bit camera angles at `qword_140D408C0`, and the last three with the three-part camera position at `xmmword_140D408C8`; each difference is divided by the step count to give a per-frame increment.

each frame it computes the interpolated angles and position, builds the camera matrices with `sub_14027471C`, `sub_14027483C` and `sub_140274AAC`, writes the results to the camera globals, then waits one frame with SceneTask_WaitFrame.
it stops early when `dword_142E7FB3C` and the high dword of `qword_142FF9E08` are both non-zero, which the interpreter also uses as its skip condition.
on exit it stores the final angles and position back into `qword_140D408C0` and `xmmword_140D408C8`, then ends through SceneTask_Terminate.
the six targets are three rotation angles and a three-part position.

notes: The opcode record for 0x1B (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: Which camera axes the three angles and three position parts are, and the units of the step count.

name: EventChain_Find
purpose: Looks an event number up in a 9-entry table of chained events and records the entry's two bytes.

behavior.text: walks 9 entries of 4 bytes at 0x1406848F0 and compares the event with each entry's first word read as a signed 16-bit value.
on a match it stores byte +3 of the entry in the dword at 0x143807790 and byte +2 in the dword at 0x143807794 and returns byte +2.
on a miss it stores 1 in the dword at 0x143807790 and returns -1.

notes: An event number above 32,767 never matches (the table word is sign-extended, the argument is not). The two globals are addressed rip-relatively; their addresses are computed from the displacements.
open_questions: What the two recorded bytes mean.

name: EventChannel_BindStepTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x6B.
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x6B: releases a keyed object, binds or selects its channel, then runs the same frame loop as opcode 0x6A.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 53 in qword_140D40B38[256 * dword_140D40948].
reads the operand bytes through the task block pointer: byte 0 is the key, byte 1 is a count (0 is replaced by 1), byte 3 selects the mode, and bytes 2 and 4 are left for the step task.
calls sub_1402B20E4(handle), where the handle is the key plus 0x10000, to release the key's current binding first.

when byte 3 is nonzero it calls SoundCue_Play(handle - 1), which binds the mapped key to a free channel from 13 to 19 and returns that channel, or -1 when no channel is free or the mapped value is above 0x2B1.
when byte 3 is zero it calls sub_1402B2098(handle), which sets dword_141856AA8 to the handle and sets channel 12 to the value from sub_1402BA8E8.
then it calls sub_140346648(handle, count), which refreshes the channel for the key; that routine uses only its first argument.
the else branch (sub_1402B20E4 for a zero count) cannot run, because the count is set to 1 when byte 1 is zero.
it then tail-calls EventChannel_StepTask (EventChannel_StepTask) with the same task block, so the same operand bytes drive the frame loop. This body does not wait itself.

notes: The opcode record for 0x6B (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: How the channel bound by SoundCue_Play is used by the drawing code (not read here); whether the unreachable zero-count branch was meant to run.

name: EventChannel_StepTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x6A; also tail-called by EventChannel_BindStepTask (opcode 0x6B).
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x6A: runs a per-frame refresh of a keyed object's channel for a set number of frames, then releases or keeps the key.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 53 in qword_140D40B38[256 * dword_140D40948].
reads its operand bytes through the task block pointer at off_140783088 + (slot << 11): byte 0 is the key, byte 2 is the end flag, and byte 4 is the frame count.
byte 1 feeds a local accumulator (byte 2 minus byte 1) that the decompiled code never reads, and byte 3 is not read.

the key handle is the key plus 0x10000; the lookup value is the handle minus 1, passed through sub_1402BA9C8, which remaps values above 0xA7 through the 7-pair table at dword_140718C50 and returns the value unchanged when there is no match.
for the frame count it loops: SceneTask_WaitFrame, then if dword_141856AA8 (the current key) equals the handle and channel 12 is live (sub_1401D7808), it calls sub_1401D6F2C on channel 12 with 0.0.

in the same pass it searches the 7 bound keys in dword_14375F8C4 (channels 13 to 19, stopping at dword_14375F8E0) for the lookup value; when found and that channel is live, it calls sub_1401D6F2C on that channel with 0.0.
the loop breaks early when the high dword of `qword_142FF9E08` is nonzero and the high dword of `qword_142FF9E00` equals 3, the skip condition the other event tasks test.
after the loop, when byte 2 is nonzero it repeats the channel 12 and bound-channel refresh once and keeps the key bound.
when byte 2 is zero it calls sub_1402B20E4(handle), which releases the key from its channel.
ends through SceneTask_Terminate. It does not call SceneTask_Start and does not wait after the loop.

sub_1401D6F2C (called for each refresh) stores 0.0 in a field of each live object on the channel, stores a register value in another field, sets a flag byte when the object's type word equals 656, and then calls sub_1401D6080.

sub_1401D7808 walks up to five objects of a channel and returns 1 at the first one that is non-null, has a nonzero word at +16, and passes the test in sub_1400991DC or the byte at +36 checks; it returns 0 when none pass.

notes: The opcode record for 0x6A (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What sub_1401D6080 changes on the object; what sub_1400991DC tests; what the field stored from an unnamed register in sub_1401D6F2C holds (the decompiler shows it uninitialised); what the remap table dword_140718C50 represents.

name: EventCharaSprite_SetTable256Entry

callers: EventScript_Run, case 0xCB (call site 0x14023E772). Also sub_1400CEB4C (call site 0x1400CEF81), sub_1400CF2A8 (call site 0x1400CF2FB) and sub_14021EE0C (call site 0x14021EE74).

uses the cached table pointer qword_143CD9F60. When it is zero it gets table 256 from the root qword_143CD9CD0 with sub_1403D325C (root, 256) and caches it.
finds the row with sub_1403D3AE8 (table, entry id, and two arguments that the caller does not set).
when the row is missing, or its first qword is non-negative and its data pointer is null, nothing else happens.
copies four dwords from the row data into the sub-object: data +20 to +3888, data +16 to +3892, data +12 to +3896, and data +8 (zero-extended, 8 bytes) to +3900.

table 256 is PostEffectGlare; the key a map variation passes is its post_effect_glare member (Map variation element +0x14).
when the float is negative, copies the 16 bytes at +3888 to +3856 and to +3872, then calls sub_1400D1CB8 on the sub-object. Otherwise it copies the 16 bytes at +3856 to +3872 only.

The name does not fit what the function loads: table 256 is PostEffectGlare (four floats of a row go to +3888..+3900, the key to +3912). Its callers are the event script command and the map variation applier (MapRenderer_ApplyVariationEffects passes the Map variation element post_effect_glare key).
open_questions: The divisor for the duration (the float register value at the call site was not found in the function). What the four positions from sub_1400D1CB8 are used for, and the meaning of the dwords at data +8 to +20.

name: EventCmd_ActivateSlotParam

when it does not equal byte 11, the word at 0x141862452 is not changed.

name: EventCmd_CountedWait

purpose: Class 9 handler: a counted wait. Each call sets the wait bit and advances a counter; once the counter passes the limit, it sets the continue bit instead.

when bit 4 (0x10) of the status word is set on entry, the limit dword_14186243C is set to argument byte 9 and the counter dword_141862438 is reset to 0.

when the counter is greater than the limit, the handler sets bit 2 (0x4), leaves the counter unchanged and returns it. The wait bit stays set.

name: EventCmd_JumpIfClearB
callers: EventCmd_Run through the class table, class 20
purpose: Class 20: jumps to the byte 10 target when the bit for byte 9 is clear in flag table B (dword_140D4CC28).

behavior.text: argument layout: byte 9 is the bit index; byte 10 is the jump value; byte 11 is not read.

tests bit (byte 9 & 31) of dword_140D4CC28[byte 9 >> 5], as in class 19.

notes: The decompiler shows only the stub; the behavior was read from the disassembly of the shared body. The IDA name is still EventCmd_JumpIfClearB; no rename was made.

behavior.text: class 34 argument layout: the 16-bit target is byte 9 (low) and byte 10 (high). Byte 11 is the jump value and is read only on the equal path.

the result is the candidate byte for the selector: byte 9 for 0, byte 10 for 1, byte 11 for 2.

name: EventCmd_Run
callees: EventVar_Read (3), EventCmd_ServiceRequests, `sub_1402F18CC` and the 54 command handlers
purpose: Runs the 4-byte scripted command loop: it services pending requests, fetches the next 32-bit command into the command register, calls the handler for its command class, and repeats until a command stops or yields.

behavior.text: each pass reads event variables 0x5C, 0x5D and 0x5E and passes them to EventCmd_ServiceRequests, then calls `sub_1402F18CC`.

the command lives in a 128-bit command register at `xmmword_141862440` (with companion words at `xmmword_141862450`, `xmmword_141862460` and `qword_141862470`); byte 8 of the register is the command class and the flags word is at +12.

when flag bit 2 of the command register is set, the whole register block is saved into one of five 56-byte context slots at `unk_1411A7560` (slot number `word_140D8DBA4`, only if below 5), a bit for it is set in the bitset at `dword_1411A7030`, and the slot number is advanced.
the handler is picked from a 54-entry table at 0x140681DE0 (image base + 0x681DE0) indexed by the command class, and is called with the flags word and `qword_143CD9E28` as arguments.
command class 22 with operand 1, 2, 3 or 4 is skipped when `qword_143CD9E28` has a non-zero field at +48 and a field of 1 at +80.
the loop ends when flag bits 0x28 are set; it clears 0x08 and returns true when bit 0x20 is clear.

when flag bit 4 is set it fetches the next command: it clears bit 2 and sets bit 4 of the flags (0x10), takes the script index from the high word of the register and the position from the low word of `xmmword_141862450`, finds the script's start as `dword_140D4CC70[index] >> 2`, loads the 32-bit command at that start plus the position into the register's dword at +8 (class in byte 8, three operand bytes in bytes 9 to 11), and advances the position by one.
so the command stream is an array of 32-bit commands with a table of script start offsets at its head; each command is 4 bytes, unlike the variable-length byte-opcode event scripts.
this is a separate small script language with 54 command classes, probably the world-map or scene script; it is not the byte-opcode battle-event interpreter.

notes: The command classes are 0-53; entries 54 and above in the table are not code. The byte-opcode event interpreter is a different routine and is still unresolved.
open_questions: What each command class does, and which routine interprets the byte-opcode event scripts.

name: EventCmd_SetHold
