name: EventColor_Task
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x1A
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x1A: applies a screen colour change and waits out its duration.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 6 in `qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`; the interpreter and other tasks use this tag to find tasks by kind.
takes a pointer to the instruction's operand bytes from the first field of its task block.
calls `sub_1402F57D0(mode, durationIndex, c1, c2, c3)` with the operand bytes: the first byte is a mode, the second to fourth are three signed colour adjustments, and the fifth is a duration index.
then waits a number of frames read from the 16-bit table `word_140672108` at the duration index (no wait when that entry is 0), and ends through SceneTask_Terminate.
`sub_1402F57D0` is a colour-grading routine with modes 0 to 11; modes 6 and 7 compute a grey from the current colour and mode 10 clears a flag.

notes: The opcode record for 0x1A (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What each of the 12 colour modes does to the screen, and the order of the three colour channels.

name: EventColorPath_Task
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x3E
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x3E: moves three values in a straight line from a start triple to an end triple, two frames per step, passing each step to `sub_1402F4618` with the operand's value byte, then ends.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 12 in `qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`.

reads the value byte at instruction byte 1 (passed to the helper at every step), the start triple from bytes 2 to 4 (unsigned bytes), the end triple from bytes 5 to 7 (unsigned bytes), and the step bound as a 16-bit value from bytes 8 and 9.

for j = 0, 2, 4, ... below the bound it waits two frames, then computes each component as start + j * (end - start) / bound (integer division) and calls `sub_1402F4618` with the value byte and the three components (low 16 bits of each).
when the bound is zero or negative the loop does not run.
after the loop it calls `sub_1402F4618` with the end triple, waits two frames, and ends through SceneTask_Terminate.

`sub_1402F4618` stores the three bytes as a new target triple in `dword_140782984`, computes the change from the previous triple in `dword_140782980` (scaled by 128 or 256), and calls `sub_1402600BC` with a time of 32 times its first argument (the value byte).
the three bytes are probably colour components and the value byte a duration, because the helper writes a three-byte triple and times the change; this is not confirmed by the code read here.

notes: The opcode record for 0x3E (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What `sub_1402600BC` does with its time argument, what the triples in `dword_140782980` and `dword_140782984` represent, and whether the value byte is always a duration.

name: EventControl_ApplyCarry
callees: sub_14021EE0C, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_140260ABC, BattleAnim_StartMotion, sub_140135DC8, EventControl_ShowFastForwardLabel, sub_140270BA4, sub_1401DB4E4
purpose: When an event script starts, restores auto-advance and fast-forward from the previous event if the new event's EventId row allows it.

behavior.text: reads the EventId (NXD 156) row of the current event number (dword_140782A94).
row byte +34 set and EventControl +48 set: auto (+47) = 1, the auto indicator is shown, +48 = 0.
row byte +35 set and EventControl +54 set: armed (+53) = 1, hold timer (+36) = 1.0, level (GlobalWork +88) = 1, the 'Fast-forwarding' label is shown, +54 = 0.

row byte +41 (column no_pause) set: EventControl +57 = 1; that byte (pause_block_b) is the second blocker tested by EventControl_TryOpenPause, so the pause overlay (and with it skipping) cannot open in this event.
when sub_140270BA4(event) is true: bytes +34, +35, +49, +50 and +51 are set to 1 (the last two block the hold and the auto toggle).

before that, a loop over the 21 battle unit records runs unless row byte +42 (column reset_unit_motion) is 0: it runs when the byte is set or the row is missing. Every present unit whose five status bytes at +97..+101 hold none of the statuses Crystal, KO, Undead, Jumping, Stone, Chest and Critical (ids 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 15, 23) gets BattleAnim_StartMotion(2).
with byte +35 a fast-forward that was running at the end of one event continues in the next without a new press and without the one-second ramp, as long as the button stays held.

open_questions: ? Which motion BattleAnim_StartMotion(2) is (what the unit is made to do at the start of the event).

name: EventControl_CarryToNextEvent
purpose: When an event script ends, saves whether auto-advance and fast-forward were on so a chained event can start with them.

behavior.text: copies EventControl +47 (auto) into +48.
sets EventControl +54 to 1 when the mode is 2 and the level is non-zero, else 0.
when sub_140270BA4(current event number) is true it also writes the word +34 = 256, the word +49 = 0 and the byte +51 = 0.

name: EventControl_IsAutoAdvancing
purpose: True when dialogue auto-advance should act this frame: the overlay is in its running state, auto is on and no fast-forward hold is in progress.

behavior.text: false unless state (+8) is 1 and auto (+47) is non-zero.
false when the mode is 2 and the level is non-zero, or when the hold timer +36 is not 0.
otherwise returns the value its callers pass in the third argument register (1 at the call sites read).

notes: EventMessage_Task leaves its wait-for-input loop when the mode is not 0 and the level is non-zero, or when this returns true, or on the confirm / cancel actions.
open_questions: ? How long auto-advance leaves a finished page on screen (the callers' timing was not read).

name: EventControl_PausedTick
callees: sub_1400EB7EC, sub_1400F144C, sub_1400F1510, EventSkip_IsAvailable, Input_TestAction, sub_1401DBBB0, PauseManager_Tick, sub_1400F4BCC, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, EventSkip_IsViewerEvent, sub_1402B1FB4, sub_1402B2004, sub_1402BAAA8, sub_1401D7760, sub_1400F0E98, sub_14013BAD0
purpose: Paused frame of the event overlay: accepts the completed hold as a skip (state 3) or resumes on the pause / back action.

behavior.text: when EventSkip_IsAvailable is true and Input_TestAction(action 0x5D) fires (the hold completed), it resets the overlay, sets +12 = old state, +8 = 3, ticks the PauseManager and calls sub_1400F4BCC(0xBA).

then, for an event number >= 0 (dword_140782A94), reads EventId (NXD 156) row byte +33; when that byte is 0, or EventSkip_IsViewerEvent is true, or the row is missing, it calls sub_1402B1FB4(0) and sub_1402B2004 (the reset of the event's parameter slots and of the event sound entry list; the column is skip_no_reset, and a non-zero value keeps the sounds across a skip).
event numbers 213, 296, 309 and 489 call sub_1402BAAA8 with fixed ids (649/651, 650, 653/647, 662/640).
otherwise, on action 0x5F or 0x1B (and the hold not in progress), sets +8 = 0 and ticks the PauseManager (resume).

open_questions: ? What the fixed ids passed to sub_1402BAAA8 do.

name: EventControl_Reset
callers: sub_14020DC78, sub_14020E174 (when the event tick did not return 1), and sub_1402024A8 right after it allocates the 64-byte EventControl
purpose: Clears the event pause overlay state on frames where no event script tick ran.

behavior.text: closes the overlay (sub_1401DBBB0), zeroes the qwords +8 (state and previous state) and +16, the dword +32, the qword +24 and the qword +36, writes 256 to the dword +44, zeroes the dword +49, the byte +53, the word +55 and the byte +57.
calls sub_1401D6F9C(qword_143CD9DD8, 7, 0).

notes: So EventControl +8 is 0 whenever no event script is ticking.

name: EventControl_RunningTick
callers: EventControl_Update (state 1, when the pause overlay did not open)
callees: GlobalWork_GetFastForwardMode, Input_TestAction, Input_IsActionMapped, Input_IsActionHeld, EventControl_ShowFastForwardLabel, EventControl_UpdateGuide, sub_140135DC8
purpose: The unpaused frame of the event overlay: toggles dialogue auto-advance on action 91 and runs the fast-forward hold (actions 89 / 90) with its press gate and its one-second ramp.

behavior.text: auto-advance part, skipped while the fast-forward level is non-zero in mode 2 or the hold timer (+36) is above 0: 'allowed' = byte +55 is 0 and byte +57 is 0 (or byte +56 when the dword +28 is non-zero), and byte +51 is 0.

when allowed and action 91 was pressed this frame (Input_TestAction with action 0x5B), or when allowed, auto is off and g_EventKeepAutoLatch is 1, or when not allowed and auto is on: auto (+47) is inverted, the qword +16 is cleared and the auto indicator of the dialogue window is shown or hidden (sub_140135DC8).
in the allowed case the latch g_EventKeepAutoLatch becomes 1 when auto is being switched on and the config byte +59 (enableEventKeepAuto) is set, else 0.

fast-forward part, only when GlobalWork_GetFastForwardMode returns 2: pressed = action 89 or 90 pressed this frame (Input_IsActionMapped, the press-edge test), held = action 89 or 90 held (Input_IsActionHeld).
while the float +40 is below 0.75 it only grows by the frame time; once it is 0.75 or more, a press sets the armed byte +53.
while armed, held and byte +50 is 0: the float +36 grows by the frame time, the 'Fast-forwarding' label is shown if it was not (EventControl_ShowFastForwardLabel) and the auto indicator is hidden.
otherwise (not armed, or released, or byte +50 set): the label is hidden if shown (and the auto indicator shown again when auto is on), +36 = 0 and armed = 0.
level written to GlobalWork +88 every frame of this part: 0 while +36 is below 1.0; from 1.0 on, 2 when action 90 is held, else 1.
ends in EventControl_UpdateGuide.
the frame time is the application timer's tick count times its period divided by 300000, the same units the 5-second hint timers use, so 0.75 and 1.0 are seconds.

a button already down when +40 reaches 0.75 never arms: only the press edge does. Releasing and pressing again arms at once, the label appears on that frame, and the speed-up and the automatic page advance begin 1.0 s later.

notes: The floats +36 and +40 are zeroed by EventControl_Reset, which runs on every frame without an event tick; so the 0.75 s count starts when an event script begins to tick. Input_IsActionMapped is an older name: the routine tests the 'pressed this frame' bytes of an action row.
open_questions: ? What sets the bytes +50, +51, +55, +56, +57 and the dword +28 apart from the message / panel tasks already listed on the EventControl record.

name: EventControl_ShowFastForwardLabel
callers: EventControl_RunningTick, EventControl_UpdateGuide, EventControl_Update, EventControl_ApplyCarry, sub_1401DBBB0, sub_1402C53F0
purpose: Shows or hides the fast-forward indicator of the dialogue window and remembers it in EventControl +44.

behavior.text: when the event window addon exists it calls sub_140137FD0(addon, show - 1, loop), which shows or hides the node kept at addon +56 and plays or stops its 'ShowLoop' state.
stores show in the byte at ctl +44.
addon +56 is the node UIAddonFFTOEvent binds as 'TextBoardFF' (the binding site stores that name's node at +56); the label read live as 'Fast-forwarding'.

notes: So EventControl +44 is 'the label is on screen', which starts with the accepted press, one second before the level becomes 1.

name: EventControl_TryOpenPause
callees: Input_TestAction, sub_1400F144C, EventSkip_IsAvailable, sub_1401DBBB0, sub_1400EB65C, sub_1400EB5F4, sub_1401D1E30, PauseManager_Push
purpose: Opens the event pause overlay on the pause action and picks its button hints: with Skip when EventSkip_IsAvailable is true, without it otherwise.

behavior.text: does nothing (returns 0) unless Input_TestAction(action 0x5F) is true and the bytes +49, +52 and +57 of the EventControl are all 0.
sets +12 = old state, +8 = 2 (paused), arms the hold action 0x5D (sub_1400F144C).
calls EventSkip_IsAvailable; button-guide mask -1 when it is true, -3 when false; passes 502 and the mask to sub_1400EB65C.
sets +32 = 1, +24 = 502, clears qword_143CD9DD0 + 88 and pushes pause id 1 (PauseManager_Push).
UIButtonGuide row 502 has entry 0 = Resume (text 2646, action 95) and entry 1 = Skip (text 2634, action 94); mask -3 clears bit 1, i.e. hides the Skip hint.

notes: Opening the overlay changes no skip state: the decision is EventSkip_IsAvailable over globals, which are readable without opening it.

name: EventControl_Update
callers: sub_14020DC78 and sub_14020E174 (both from sub_140210AF0), each when the event tick returned 1; otherwise they call EventControl_Reset
callees: EventControl_TryOpenPause, EventControl_PausedTick, sub_1401DB6C4, sub_1401DBBB0, sub_1401DBD14, sub_140135DC8
purpose: Per-frame state machine of the event pause overlay (state 0 off, 1 running, 2 paused, 3 skip chosen).

behavior.text: runs only when the low dword of g_EventScriptActive (0x142FF9EC0) is non-zero, g_ShopModeGate (0x1407D453C, the enhanced-edition flag) is non-zero and the dword at +92 of the object at qword_143CD9DD0 is 0.
state (+8) 0: resets the overlay, sets +12 = old state and +8 = 1.
state 1: calls EventControl_TryOpenPause; when that returns 0 it calls sub_1401DB6C4 (the unpaused tick).
state 2: calls EventControl_PausedTick.
state 3 has no branch here; EventScript_SkipTick reads it (EventControl +8 == 3 while g_ShopModeGate is set) as the skip request.

open_questions: ? What the dword at qword_143CD9DD0 + 92 is (its writers were not found by direct address).

name: EventControl_UpdateGuide
callees: GlobalWork_GetFastForwardMode, EventControl_ShowFastForwardLabel, sub_140135DC8, sub_1400F12C0, Time_GetTimestamp, sub_1400EB65C, sub_1400EB5F4
purpose: Chooses the button guide shown under an event: 503 while fast-forward is held or running, 504 in auto-advance, otherwise 501 / 506 for five seconds after an input.

behavior.text: guide 503 when the mode is 2 and the level is non-zero, or the hold timer +36 is above 0.
otherwise, when ffRunning was passed (the level was non-zero at the start of the tick): hides the 'Fast-forwarding' label and, with auto on, shows the auto indicator and guide 504.

otherwise guide = the dword +28 when set, 504 when auto is on, else 506 when byte +55 is set and 501 when not; it is shown while an input other than the listed actions (26, 91 when auto is allowed, 89 and 90 in mode 2, 21) arrived in the last 5 seconds.
when the mode is not 2 the guides 501, 504 and 506 are opened with mask -3.

open_questions: ? The texts of guides 501, 503, 504 and 506 (UIButtonGuide rows) were not read.

name: EventCounter_Task
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x41
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x41: runs without returning on its own, adding to the shared 16-bit counter on a repeating frame cycle until the skip test ends it.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 13 in `qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`.

reads four signed bytes from its operand pointer: byte 0 is the amount added to `word_140D408EC` at each addition, byte 1 is the number of frames between those additions, byte 2 is the amount added once per cycle, and byte 3 is the cycle length in frames.

each frame it first checks the skip test (the high dword of `qword_142FF9E08` non-zero and the high dword of `qword_142FF9E00` equal to 3) and ends through SceneTask_Terminate when it fires, before that frame's update.
then it waits one frame with SceneTask_WaitFrame, increments the frames since the last addition and the frames in this cycle.
when the frames since the last addition equal byte 1, it adds byte 0 to `word_140D408EC` and resets the count; this count carries across cycles.
when the frames in the cycle equal byte 3, it adds byte 2 to `word_140D408EC`, and a new cycle starts.
the comparisons use the signed byte values, so a negative byte 1 never matches.

notes: The opcode record for 0x41 (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: Which tasks or the interpreter read `word_140D408EC`, and what a cycle length of 0 does (the cycle loop only ends when its count equals the length, so a zero length is not guarded).

name: EventDataLoad_Poll
callers: MultiStr_Includes at 0x1402737A4 (MultiStr_Includes returns this routine's result as a nonzero test; opcode 0x8A reaches it through SceneCallback_Dispatch mode 1). Also sub_140210AF0 (at 0x140212D50), sub_140318090 (at 0x140318190 and 0x1403182CD), and one data reference at 0x143D39400.
callees: `sub_1402742CC` (language table pair for a track index), GameData_ReadSectors (at 0x1402F40C4; sends kind 17 to EventScript_LoadFile and other kinds through `sub_1402F3D58` or `sub_1403D2358`)
purpose: A state machine that starts a table-selected game data read for the current track index and reports busy until the read and a timed delay have finished; it is the busy test that opcode 0x8A waits on, through MultiStr_Includes.

behavior.text: returns false at once when word_141D330BC (the current track index) is negative.
the state is the byte byte_140D40927. States 0 to 3 are handled below; any other value leaves the result false.

state 0: sets word_143D1A1B0 (a delay counter) to 60 when byte_140D405AA is non-zero, otherwise to 0. Calls `sub_1402742CC` with the track index, which returns two dwords from the per-language table (dword_1406739C0 and dword_1406739C4 when the language flag at g_LanguageInfo + 8 is non-zero, otherwise dword_1406749C0 and dword_1406749C4) into a first value and a second value. If the second value is 0, it sets word_141D330BC to 1 and reads again. When the second value is then non-zero it calls GameData_ReadSectors(first value, 0, second value, &unk_1418A2E00). It then sets the state to 1 and returns busy.
state 1: returns busy while the high dword of qword_141856AB0 is non-zero. When it is zero, it sets the state to 2 and returns busy.

state 2: when word_143D1A1B0 is 0, and byte_140D405AA is non-zero, it writes 3 to the dword at unk_1437A5C48 + 96 times byte_140D405AA. It then sets qword_1411A3828 to v + the dword at v + 24, where v is qword_143740220 indexed by the track index, and sets the state to 3. In either case the result is busy.
state 3: returns busy while the dword at unk_1437A5C48 + 96 times byte_140D405AA is non-zero. It does not change the state.
after the state work, when the function has not returned early, it decrements word_143D1A1B0 by 1 if that value is positive.
the function does not wait by itself. Each call is one poll; the caller repeats it once per frame.
state 3 ends when some other code sets that dword to 0. Nothing in this routine sets the high dword of qword_141856AB0 to non-zero; GameData_ReadSectors sets it to 0 at its end.

notes: MultiStr_Includes (0x1402737A0) is the callback the 0x8A loop sets; it is not this address. It returns the result of this routine as a 0 or 1 value.
open_questions: What clears byte_140D40927 and sets word_141D330BC back, and who sets the high dword of qword_141856AB0 while a read runs. What the dword tables dword_1406739C0, dword_1406739C4 and their language twins hold. What the records at unk_1437A5C48 (stride 96 bytes) represent. What sub_140210AF0 and sub_140318090 do with the result.

name: EventEffect_Start
proto: int64_t EventEffect_Start(unsigned int effectWord, int flag, int64_t unused, char flagByte)
purpose: Starts the effect an event script asked for: builds a small request record, fills its flag bytes and calls Effect_SelectForAbility with the effect word.

behavior.text: builds a request record whose first word is 1, with bytes +3..+231 zeroed; stores the fourth argument at record byte +8 and, when the second argument is nonzero or the effect word is 220, at byte +200.
calls Effect_SelectForAbility(0, effect word, record); the effect word is passed unchanged as an int.
its only code caller is the event effect starter sub_14023A0B4, which reads the word at 0x140D40930 with a sign extension and passes it on (the address is the caller's: this body never touches it).

notes: The two flag arguments come from a byte of the event state and from a word test of the scene.
open_questions: What the request record's other bytes carry.

name: EventEndSlate_ShowTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0xEC
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0xEC: adds the end-slate UI add-on, plays its language-keyed state and its Show state, waits until the state ends or the skip test passes, then removes the add-on.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with 71 (0x47) in `qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`.
when the object at `qword_143CD9FD0` is set, calls `sub_1401DB4E4` on it, sets its word at +34 and its word at +49 to 257, and sets its byte at +51 to 1.
reads `dword_1407D453C` (the enhanced flag) and takes the UI manager at `*(*(qword_143CD9DA8 + 16) + 312)`.

creates a 72-byte object with `sub_140011750`, initializes it with `sub_1401D1970`, sets its vtable to the class `vftable_ffto::Game::UI::UIAddonFFTOEndSlate_14070D448`, sets its dword at +60 to 5 and its byte at +64 to 0, adds it to the manager with `sub_1401D16C4`, and stores it in the manager's field at +64.
calls `sub_1401D1A00(object, 46 - (flag != 0))`, so the argument is 45 when the enhanced flag is set and 46 otherwise.
waits one frame at a time while the manager's virtual function at vtable offset 32 returns 0.

the language key comes from the dword at +8 of `g_LanguageInfo` (1 when that block is absent): 1 gives `En`, 2 gives `Fr`, 3 gives `De`, 4 gives `Cs`, 5 gives `Ct`, 6 gives `Ko`, and 0 or any other value gives `Ja`.

`UIName_Key` builds a key from that name, `GUINode_FindState` looks it up in the GUI node at object+48, the state's byte at +104 is set to 1, and `GUINode_PlayState` plays it. When the second dword of the key is non-zero it calls `sub_1403D8D1C(qword_143CDA2A0, value)`.
the node's byte at +416 is set to 1, and the state keyed Show is then found, set and played the same way.
waits one frame at a time while the node's byte at +416 is non-zero and the skip test is not true (dword +4 of `qword_142FF9E08` zero, or dword +4 of `qword_142FF9E00` not equal to 3).
removes the add-on with `sub_1401D183C(manager, object)` and sets the manager's field at +64 to 0.
when the object at `qword_143CD9FD0` is set, clears its bytes at +49 and +51 and sets its word at +34 to 256, then ends through SceneTask_Terminate.

notes: The opcode record for 0xEC (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What `sub_1401DB4E4`, `sub_1401D1A00` and `sub_1403D8D1C` do, what the manager's slot-32 function reports, what the flags written to the object at `qword_143CD9FD0` control, and what the Show state contains. The opcode record describes the start gate as a global state word, but the start path tests a byte on the handler's stack, which was not traced.

name: EventFlagWait_Task
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x8B.
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x8B: waits frame by frame until the global dword_140CDB824 becomes zero, then ends.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 65 in qword_140D40B38[256 * dword_140D40948].

calls sub_140235804, which sets the function slot qword_140D40940 to sub_1402737B8 and calls it once; for a task that is not slot 0 it zeroes task block fields 12 and 13 and calls through the slot pointer with 0.
sub_1402737B8 sets dword_1418732C8 to 2 when it is 1, and returns the value.
then it loops: waits one frame, sets qword_140D40940 to sub_1402737D0 and calls it the same way; sub_1402737D0 returns dword_140CDB824.
the loop ends when that value is 0. The task then returns the result, and the body ends through SceneTask_Terminate.

on each pass the skip condition (the high dword of `qword_142FF9E08` nonzero and the high dword of `qword_142FF9E00` equal to 3) is checked; when it holds, the loop calls sub_14031A7E0 and returns its result instead.

sub_14031A7E0 clears dword_143C51C6C, dword_143C51C98, dword_143C51CA4 and qword_143C51D30, calls sub_14031A6AC, sub_140381A54 and sub_14031A740, sets word_141D330BC and dword_142E801F4 to -1, and when dword_140C6B1CC is not 52 writes 1281 to a word at qword_143CDA758 + 288.
the global dword_140CDB824 is the value this task waits on, and the opcode record says EventScript_Run sets a flag to 1 before starting it.

notes: The opcode record for 0x8B (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What dword_140CDB824 and dword_1418732C8 are and what writes dword_140CDB824; what sub_14031A6AC, sub_140381A54 and sub_14031A740 do (not read here); the caller sub_140241DF8, which also calls sub_140235804.

name: EventId_TestByte27
purpose: Returns 0 when event variable 39's EventId row byte +0x27 is non-zero, else 0x10002.

behavior.text: reads the EventId row of event variable 39; byte +0x27 non-zero -> 0, else 0x10002.
the only caller, sub_14024C068, stores the result in dword_142FF9CA4 and goes on to EventCmd_UiDispatch.

open_questions: ? what the two result values select (the meaning of EventId +0x27 is not decoded).

name: EventLookSet_Select
purpose: Makes one of the eight generic look sets the active pool for an event's placeholder actors.

behavior.text: copies 32 bytes (eight sprite sheet ids) of the set from the generic look set table (0x1407141E0) into the active pool (0x1437A1348).
an id above 7 fills the pool from a default constant instead.

name: EventMapTitle_DrawSweep
proto: void EventMapTitle_DrawSweep(void *buffer, int value, int unused, int layout)
purpose: Builds four 184-byte map-title draw records for one sweep value into a 736-byte buffer and links them into the draw list; the layout argument (0 or 1) chooses the record variant and the link order.

behavior.text: reads the running task block (slot dword_140D40948). The dword at +0 is the X base and the dword at +8 is the Y base. The 0x91 handler stored operand 1 and operand 2 there, so these are the two operand bytes.
the third argument is not read. The sweep task always passes 100.
the four records are at buffer + 0, + 184, + 368 and + 552. The record index is twice the row (0 or 1) plus the column (0 or 1).

all four records get these fixed fields: dword -1 at +76 and at +80, +84, +88, +92, +96, +100, +104, +108, +112, +116 and +120; word 42 at +10; byte 62 at +15; word 16348 at +22; qword 0 at +60; qword 255 at +68; word 0 at +172; byte 0 at +174; dword 0 at +176; word 39 at +34 for column 1 and 71 for column 0.
row 0 (the first two records) sets the colour bytes to 100 at +12 to +14, +24 to +26, +36 to +38 and +48 to +50.
row 1 with layout 0 sets 100 at +12 to +14 and +36 to +38, and 0 at +24 to +26 and +48 to +50. With layout 1 it is the reverse: 100 at +24 to +26 and +48 to +50, and 0 at +12 to +14 and +36 to +38.

the value and the X and Y bases give the position words (+16, +18, +28, +30, +40, +42, +52, +54) and the value bytes (+20, +32, +44, +56); the glyph word of the language (next line) is added to some of them. Clamps apply for values of 32 and up and 223 and up. The full arithmetic is not restated here.
the glyph word is word_1408EB93E when g_LanguageInfo is non-null and its dword at +8 is zero, and word_1408EBA2E otherwise (including when g_LanguageInfo is null).
when the float at dword_142C81554 is 2.0 or more, the dword at +60 of each of the four records is set to 11111.

linking, layout 0: the list head is the qword that qword_140D40868 points to. The records are pushed in the order record 3, record 2, record 1, record 0, so the list reads head, record 0, record 1, record 2, record 3, then the old list. Layout 1 gives head, record 2, record 3, record 0, record 1, then the old list. Each record's word at +8 is set to word_14114A4E4.
calls nothing else.

notes: The buffer is one of two alternating 736-byte areas at unk_1437A5400. The sweep task passes layout 1 only in its third phase.
open_questions: What reads the draw list at qword_140D40868 and what each record field (+10, +15, +20, +21, +22, +32, +33, +34, +44, +45, +56, +57, +60, +68, +172, +174, +176) means on screen; the exact arithmetic of the position words.

name: EventMapTitle_LoadTexture
callers: EventScript_Run (the 0x91 handler, call at 0x14023DA81, made before SceneTask_Start); sub_14020E578 (call at 0x14020E7E7).
purpose: Loads the map-title texture file chosen by scene variable 51 (maptitle_%03d.tex) into a 10,240-byte buffer, unless the enhanced-build test says it is not needed; the 0x91 handler calls it before starting the sweep task.

behavior.text: reads scene variable 51 with SceneVar_Read and subtracts 1. The result is the index.
the index is kept when it is 119 or less. The comparison is signed, so a scene value of 0 gives an index of -1, which is kept and printed as a negative number. Any larger value gives index 0.

when dword_1407D453C is not zero, the index is stored in DWORD1 of xmmword_142E7FCE0. The load is skipped when that flag is not zero and the float at dword_142C81554 is 2.0 or more. When the flag is zero the load always happens.
allocates a 10,240-byte buffer with sub_1402202C8.
formats the file name fftpack/tex/maptitle/maptitle_%03d.tex with the index into a 260-byte local buffer (through sub_1400D5A50).
allocates a zeroed 32-byte loader object with sub_140010F50 and opens the file name with sub_1403D2004 (the loader is null when the allocation fails).
calls sub_1403D21F0 on the loader. When it returns 1, the loader is released with sub_1403D21C8 and sub_14041FB00 (size 32) and nothing else is done; the 10,240-byte buffer is not freed on this path.

otherwise it copies the file data into the buffer with sub_1403D2358 (source offset 0, length taken from the dword at +64 of the loader's data block, or 0 when there is no block), releases the loader with sub_1403D21C8 and sub_14041FB00, and, when DWORD2 of xmmword_142FF9E24 is not 1, calls sub_14025FA60 twice: once with the string table unk_1408EBA28 when the language dword at +8 of g_LanguageInfo is non-zero or g_LanguageInfo is null (unk_1408EB938 otherwise) and the buffer, and once with qword_1408EBB18 and byte_1408F25D8.
then frees the buffer with sub_1402203AC. This happens on the copy path only.

notes: The routine takes no meaningful arguments; the 0x91 handler calls it with whatever the registers hold.
open_questions: What sub_1403D2004, sub_1403D21F0, sub_14041FB00 and sub_14025FA60 do with the data (only the calls here were read); what xmmword_142E7FCE0 is read for; why the buffer is not freed when the loader reports 1; whether a scene value of 0 (index -1) is reached in practice.

name: EventMapTitle_SweepTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x91.
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x91: runs three sweeps of a 0-to-255 value over frames (up, hold at 255, sweep again with the second layout), one draw and one frame per value, using the operand 3 step, and ends early when the input test is true.

behavior.text: sets the low dword of xmmword_142FF9E14 to 0 on entry.

the step is the dword at +16 of the running task block (operand 3 as stored by the 0x91 handler, sign-extended). A step of 0 is replaced by 1. A negative step is not guarded, so the counters never reach their end values and only the input test ends the task.
each draw alternates between two 736-byte buffers at unk_1437A5400: the first draw uses offset 736, the next uses 0, and so on.

each draw is a call to EventMapTitle_DrawSweep with the buffer, the value, 100 and a layout; then one SceneTask_WaitFrame; then the input test. When the input test is non-zero the task calls SceneTask_Terminate at once and the remaining phases do not run.

the input test is a call to sub_1400FC598 with a mask, 2048, 31 and 0. The mask is the bitwise inverse of a 32-bit value whose low byte is byte +3 of qword_142E942E8, next byte is byte +2 of qword_142E942E8, next byte is byte +3 of qword_142E94348 and high byte is byte +2 of qword_142E94348.
phase 1 (sweep up, layout 0): draws the values 0, step, 2 times step and so on, for every value below 255. That is ceil(255 / step) draws.
phase 2 (hold, layout 0): draws the value 255 with a counter that starts at 0 and rises by the step after each draw; it stops once the counter reaches 110. That is ceil(110 / step) draws.
phase 3 (sweep again, layout 1): draws the values 0, step, and so on, for every value below 255, with layout 1. That is ceil(255 / step) draws.
after phase 3 the task calls SceneTask_Terminate. It does not tag its slot in qword_140D40B38. For a step of 1 the full run is 255 + 110 + 255 = 620 draws.
the on-screen effect of each value is not traced beyond the draw routine.

notes: The opcode record for 0x91 (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What the input test in sub_1400FC598 checks for the flags and the mask (its decompile reads a register the decompiler shows as unassigned in the non-zero a2 path, and it returns 0 early when a state byte equals 2); what the sweep value does on screen.

name: EventMessage_Scripted
callers: `sub_14032D31C`; also started as a task entry from seven sites
callees: EventText_FindMessage, EventText_NextChar, EventTask_WaitFrame, EventVar_Read, EventVar_Write, EventTask_Terminate, `sub_1402DDC44`, `sub_1402DDFE8`, `sub_1402DE204`, `sub_1400FC598`

behavior.text: called from `sub_14032D31C` and referenced as an entry function from seven places in the code.
finds the message with EventText_FindMessage (4 uses) and steps through it with EventText_NextChar (16 uses).

builds and animates the window with `sub_1402DDC44` (writes the window frame's corner rectangles) and `sub_1402DDFE8` (window open and close animation, which waits one frame per step through EventTask_WaitFrame).
resolves the speaker through `sub_1402DE204`, the same unit lookup as `sub_140226A18` that EventMessage_Task uses.
waits for the player with 11 button-group tests and calls EventTask_WaitFrame 13 times; it writes event variables three times and reads one.
ends through EventTask_Terminate.
the two message tasks are the same feature built for the two task tables; this one is driven by event scripts.

the speaker's look index is the same sum as sub_14032AB3C's on the save record of the speaker (marker 0x80: 2 * job - 52, 0x81 (tested by subtracting 0x80, then 1): 2 * job - 51, Mime two less), read against g_PortraitCodeD.

the same 0xFB / 0xFC choice codes as EventMessage_Task (cases in its byte switch): 0xFB records the first option row, 0xFC runs the up / down / confirm loop (actions 0x21, 0x22, 0x1A) and stores the picked index at dword 24 of `g_EventWorkPtr`, event variable 24; the first-table task state it tests is the word at block +0x98 of its block (3 = terminate).

notes:
About 11,000 bytes and 1,900 decompiled lines. The event-opcode interpreter that decides to open a message is still unresolved.

- V (2026-10-29): one of the 15 JobTable bound-readers (an 8-bit compare against 0xAE); of the JobTable row it reads bytes 46 and 47 (shape / palette), through the table pointer. J7 had listed it as reading the skillset byte only; that was wrong.
- V (2026-11-08): the speaker's portrait code comes from its own copy of the portrait code words (0x140681A90, read at 0x1402DB41E) with the index guard at 0x1402DB481 (compare with 0xD3); out of range the code is 0 (the register zeroed at entry). Job 91 forces index 130, job 92 index 131; for marker 0x82 the job row byte 47 goes into bits 10 and 11.
open_questions: Which routine interprets event opcodes and starts this task.

name: EventMessage_Task
callers: None directly; passed to SceneTask_Start by nine routines.
purpose: The dialogue-window task: it shows an event message in a speech window, pages through the text and waits for the player. It is the entry function of tasks started with SceneTask_Start and is by far the largest routine in the event code.

behavior.text: started as a task entry from nine places through SceneTask_Start, including the event interpreter, where opcode 0x10 starts it on a slot chosen from the operand byte at offset 1; it has no direct callers.
resolves who is speaking through `sub_140226A18`, which maps a speaker id to a unit in the preview table (special ids 104 and 105 search the preview table for a unit).
reads the message through EventText_NextChar (15 uses) and builds the window with `sub_1402212B4`, `sub_140331EEC` and `sub_140332330`.
animates the window with the rectangle interpolation `sub_140226664` and the frame routines `sub_1402262C0` and `sub_14025FCDC`.
waits for the player with button-group tests (`sub_1400FC598` with ids 0x1A, 0x1B, 0x20, 0x21, 0x22 and 0x39) and calls SceneTask_WaitFrame 14 times.
the decompilation has about 1,740 lines and no strings; its state lives in a local record and in the task's block in the second task table.
this is the routine the older research called the main event loop; by what it does it is the message-window task, not a general event interpreter.

in its byte switch `0xFB` stores the current line number as the first option row (local, 0xFFFF when unset) and `0xFC` runs the choice loop: each frame it places the glove sprite on the cursor line (sprite records of 584 bytes; the table base 0x142FEF870 is inside sub_14021F850, which this task calls, not in this body), waits one frame, then leaves on task tag 3 or `word_142FEC554`; otherwise it reads UP (action 0x21, mask 0x1000), DOWN (0x22, 0x4000) and confirm (0x1A, 0x20) with Input_TestAction. The cursor starts on the first option row and stays between it and the last line reached.

on confirm it writes `cursor - first option row` to dword 24 of the event variable store (`off_1407830D8`, a pointer whose stored value is 0x140D40060, so the address is reached through the pointer, not as an immediate), event variable 24, sets the confirm sound, hides the glove and continues; a `0xFC` with no `0xFB` before it does nothing.
the choice loop reads no fast-forward or auto-advance state and no cancel action; the ordinary page wait (`0xFE`) is the loop with those tests.

while `word_142FEC554`, `word_141874530`, `word_1437F664C` is set, or `g_EventSkipEnabled` and the skip state (high dword of g_ScreenFade) are both non-zero, every byte read is replaced by 0xFE, so a choice is passed without being shown or answered.
the message id is the dword at block +8 of its task block (kind = bits 11..15 picks the pool through g_TextPoolTable, decoder sub_140226208), the speaker reference the dword at +16.

notes: Named for its observable job. The real event-script interpreter (the code that executes event opcodes) is a separate routine that is still unresolved.
open_questions: Which routine interprets event opcodes, and how the message window picks its position and size.

name: EventMode_DispatchTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x78.
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x78: clears a global and hands the task's mode and argument to the mode dispatcher, which starts one of several helper tasks.

behavior.text: clears the global dword_140D40844 to 0.
tail-calls sub_1402CB9E8 and returns its result. This body does not read the task block itself.
sub_1402CB9E8 reads the first dword of the task block as the mode and the second dword as the argument.

mode 0: starts sub_1402CB054 in a slot from SceneTask_FindFree(16), clears that slot's first qwords, calls sub_1402C5290 with the argument, sets the slot's third qword to 2, calls sub_1402F7F4C to wait for the slot to finish, sets xmmword_142FF9EC8 to 1, and terminates.
mode 1: starts sub_1402C7DAC in a new slot, clears its first qwords, sets the third qword to 0, waits with sub_1402F7F4C, and terminates.

mode 2: starts sub_1402C53F0 in a new slot, clears its first qwords, waits with sub_1402F7F4C, sets dword_1411A7D08 from 1 to 2 when it is 1, and terminates. With bit 8 of dword_1437ADF48 set, mode 2 first reads SceneVar 508 and checks dword_1437EDF50; for values 570 to 577 and 543 to 547 it calls sub_140326180 (with 30 or 42) before the same start.
mode 3 and mode 4 terminate at once with no other work.
mode 5 starts sub_1402C6514 and mode 6 starts sub_1402C72B8, both in the same way as mode 1.
mode 7 calls sub_1402C8818 when qword_142FF9E4C is not 1, then terminates.
argument values of 8 or more first call sub_1402CA3AC with the argument and the tag array; dispatch then continues as above.
every path ends through SceneTask_Terminate; no mode waits on its own before ending except through sub_1402F7F4C.

notes: The opcode record for 0x78 (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What the started bodies (sub_1402CB054, sub_1402C7DAC, sub_1402C53F0, sub_1402C6514, sub_1402C72B8) do; what dword_140D40844 is used for; what bit 8 of dword_1437ADF48 and the values in dword_1437EDF50 represent; what sub_1402CA3AC does.

name: EventMoveTargets_Rewrite
callers: EventScript_Run (opcode 0x1F case, after EventAngle_Quantize) and EventStateTrack_RunTask (EventStateTrack_RunTask).
purpose: Rewrites the operands of the next opcode 0x19 from the vectors of two units and, in mode 0, adds an angle target equal to the current angle plus the shortest turn to a fixed angle table.

behavior.text: reads the first id from operand bytes 1 and 2, the second id from operand bytes 3 and 4, and the mode byte from operand 5.

scans forward from the byte after the instruction, step by step with EventScript_InstructionLength, until it finds opcode byte 0x19. The scan has no bound in the code. The operands of that instruction are the target.
resolves both ids with EventRef_ResolveSlot. When either result is 2000, it writes 0xC0 over the 0x19 opcode byte and does nothing else.

otherwise it calls sub_1402269C0 for each slot. That routine copies three signed 16-bit words from the unit node at +76, +78 and +80 into a three-dword buffer, one buffer per unit. It writes nothing when the node is missing.
the three targets are 16-bit words at the 0x19 operand bytes 0-1 (x), 2-3 (y) and 4-5 (z). Each is twice the sum of the two units' values for that component.
the y component of each unit gets +32 before the sum. When the raw first id is 73 each unit's y gets a further -80; when the raw second id is 65 each unit's y gets a further -32.
the x and z sums use the raw unit values with no adjustment.
mode byte 0 only: the code also writes an angle target at the 0x19 operand bytes 8-9 (the word after the 6 target bytes). Other mode values write only the three position targets.

in mode 0 the current angle is the 12-bit value (dword at +120, masked with 0xFFF) of the record at the global pointer off_1407830D8; the 16-bit word at +120 of that record is the base of the angle target.

for each unit, the three bytes at unit node +136, +137 and +138 form an index: byte 136 plus byte 137 times the byte at byte_140C6AD6A plus 256 times byte 138. That index selects an 8-byte entry of byte_140D8DCB0; the low four bits of byte +7 of the entry (mode 11 of sub_140249088) form a mask. The two units' masks are OR-ed.
the table has four 16-bit angles at unk_140672100 to 140672107. Entry j is skipped when bit j of the OR-ed mask is set.

for each remaining entry it computes the signed difference from the current angle and the shorter circular distance in 4096 units; the entry with the smallest distance wins, with ties going to the lower index. The distance starts at 32768 and the direction at +1; when every entry is skipped the target is the base plus 32768.
the angle target is the base word plus the direction times the distance, written as a 16-bit value. The direction is +1 or -1, and the function returns it in mode 0.
in modes other than 0 the return value is the high byte of the last position target written; how the interpreter uses it was not checked.
the function does not wait, and it does not change the 0x19 opcode byte when both ids resolve.

notes: The second argument is passed as the reference flag to EventRef_ResolveSlot; for the second id the code does not set that register, so it carries the value left by the first call.
open_questions: What byte_140C6AD6A holds; what the four table angles are; what the 0x19 targets mean to the 0x19 handler; why the decompiler shows the second flag as unset.

name: EventMusic_LoadTrack
proto: int64_t EventMusic_LoadTrack(int64_t obj, uint32_t channel, int32_t track)
callers: EventScript_Run, at 0x14023D6D7, in the default branch of the switch that also has the cases 0x7F, 0x80 to 0x83 and 0x85; that branch is reached for opcode 0x84 and the call passes channel 9 and the operand plus 44. Also sub_1402BAB78 (at 0x1402BAC2B). One data reference at 0x143D35B6C.
callees: `sub_1401D964C`, `sub_1401D5F34`, Str_Format, `sub_140011750`, `sub_1401D5E2C` (which calls `sub_1401D5EB0`), `sub_1401D7760` (which calls sub_14009B550 and, for channel 8 only, `sub_1401D9784`)
purpose: Starts background music track number `track` on channel `channel` of the global sound object, which is the body of opcode 0x84 with channel 9: a cache hit is handed to a replay helper, and a miss replaces that channel's resource with a new 56-byte resource for the track.

behavior.text: forms the key `track + 1` (for opcode 0x84, operand + 45) and hashes its four bytes with 64-bit FNV-1a (offset basis 0xCBF29CE484222325, prime 0x100000001B3).

looks the key up in the hash table at `obj + 1432`. The bucket is the hash AND the qword at `obj + 1456`; the chain is walked from the node at bucket +8 by following the qword at node +8 until the bucket's stop pointer. A node holds the key as a dword at +16 and a value as a dword at +20. The table's sentinel is `obj + 1408`; a chain that ends there, or at null, is a miss.
on a hit it calls `sub_1401D964C(obj + 1384, node + 20)` and returns 0. Nothing else in this routine runs on a hit: the channel slot and the entry list are not changed.
on a miss it reads the pointer at `obj + 8 * channel + 480`, which is `obj + 552` for channel 9. When that pointer is not null it releases it with `sub_1401D5F34` and writes 0 to that slot.
formats the text 'sound/music/music_%05u.sab' with the track number into a 260-byte stack buffer using Str_Format. That buffer is not an argument of any later call in this routine.

allocates 56 bytes with `sub_140011750` (heap at qword_140C696D0 + 32, alignment 8) and constructs the resource with `sub_1401D5E2C`. The constructor sets the vtable to GameSoundResource_140713440, zeroes the qwords at +8 and +16, the qword at +24, the dword at +32 and the word at +37, sets the floats at +44 and +48 to -1.0, and calls `sub_1401D5EB0` without any argument visible in this routine.

if the constructor returns a non-null pointer, calls `sub_1401D7760(obj, channel)`. That helper goes over five pointers at `obj + 296 + 8 * channel + 184 * k` for k from 0 to 4 (for channel 9 these are obj+368, obj+552, obj+736, obj+920 and obj+1104). For each non-null pointer it calls `sub_14009B550` on the sound manager qword_143CD9B60 when the entry's +16 handle and the manager are both non-null, and then sets the entry's state byte at +36 to 4.

appends a 24-byte node at the tail of the entry list whose sentinel is `obj + 280` (count at `obj + 288`; the node is allocated through the vtable of the allocator at `obj + 272`). The node's +16 is the new resource. It then stores the resource in the channel slot `obj + 8 * channel + 480`.
returns 0 on every path. A null allocation or a null constructor result leaves the object unchanged.
the new resource is meant to carry the music track. The file name built by Str_Format is not passed to any visible loader, so the file load itself is not proven by this routine (see open_q).

notes: The hash table at obj+1432 is only read here; no code in this routine inserts into it. The Str_Format result has no visible consumer in this routine.
open_questions: Which code inserts into the cache table at obj+1432. Why the track file name built by Str_Format is not passed to a loader here, and what `sub_1401D5EB0` receives as its path, since `sub_1401D5E2C` calls it with no visible arguments. What channel 9 means in the sound object.

name: EventNode_PlayShow
callers: EventScript_Run, case 0xC4 (call site 0x14023E342), and sub_140181914 (call site 0x140181974).
purpose: When a global byte is set, marks a UI node and plays its Show state.

behavior.text: does nothing unless the byte at the global object qword_140C69690 +23 is nonzero.
sets byte +416 of the GUI object at +48 of the node to 1.
builds the key 'Show' with UIName_Key and finds that state with GUINode_FindState on the GUI object at +48.
when the state is found, it sets the state's byte +104 to 1 and calls GUINode_PlayState on it.
when the key's interned id is nonzero, it releases the id with sub_1403D8D1C on qword_143CDA2A0.

open_questions: What the byte at qword_140C69690 +23 is, and what sets it.

name: EventNode_SetFromTable224
proto: uint64_t EventNode_SetFromTable224(uint64_t node, uint32_t key1, uint32_t key2)
callers: EventScript_Run, case 0xC4 (call site 0x14023E339), and sub_140181914 (call site 0x14018196B).
purpose: Finds the table-224 entry for two keys and passes its text offset to the GUI target of a UI node.

behavior.text: uses the cached table pointer qword_143CDA450. When it is zero it gets table 224 from the root qword_143CD9CD0 with sub_1403D325C (root, 224) and caches it.

finds the row with sub_1403D3B5C (table, key1, key2). That routine returns nothing for table mode 0, calls sub_1403D4304 with both keys packed as a pair for mode 1, and calls sub_1403D3D58 with key1 and key2 for the other modes.
when a row is found, its data pointer is the sentinel 0x1406F5ED0 when the row's first qword is negative. Otherwise the data pointer comes from sub_1403D2FD8.
calls sub_1403F113C with two arguments: the object at +56 of the node, and the address inside the row data at the offset stored at data +4, plus 4.
the routine returns the result of sub_1403F113C.

when no row is found, the data pointer stays null and the code still reads the dword at address 4 of it. The decompile shows that path, so a missing row would fault unless the table is always present. This was not checked.

notes: The node is the object at [[qword_143CD9DA8+16]+368]+64 as passed by the 0xC4 handler.
open_questions: Whether the no-row path is reachable, and what sub_1403F113C does with the text offset (it was not read).

name: EventObject_MoveTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x6E; also called directly from EventSubScript_RunTask (a call site at 0x140235CB7).
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x6E: tags itself as a move task and runs the movement worker for the object named in its operands.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 11 in qword_140D40B38[256 * dword_140D40948], which opcode 0x6F tests to wait for moves.
calls EventObject_MoveWorker (EventObject_MoveWorker) with the operand pointer from its task block and the argument 1.
then ends through SceneTask_Terminate. This body reads no operand bytes itself; the worker reads 12 bytes (see EventObject_MoveWorker).
the worker does the frame loop, so the tag stays set for the whole move; this body does not wait by itself.

notes: The opcode record for 0x6E (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What EventSubScript_RunTask does and whether it passes operands in the same 12-byte layout.

name: EventObject_MoveWorker
callers: Called by EventObject_MoveTask (0x140240100) with mode 1; also called from EventUnitMove_Task, whose mode argument is not read in this entry.
purpose: Movement worker for opcode 0x6E: moves a unit record from its current position to three 16-bit targets over a number of frame steps, shaped by a curve mode.

behavior.text: reads 12 operand bytes: bytes 0 and 1 form a 16-bit object id; bytes 2 to 7 are three 16-bit targets (first, second and third axis, little-endian); byte 8 is the curve mode; byte 9 is a curve weight; bytes 10 and 11 form a signed 16-bit divisor.
resolves the id with EventRef_ResolveSlot(id, mode). When that returns 2000 the worker does nothing and returns 2000.
otherwise it stores the resolved slot in the qword at 0x140D40B40 + 2048 * slot (the qword next to the tag) and finds the unit record with SceneObject_FindBySlot.
reads the unit's three 16-bit position words at record offsets 108, 110 and 112 as the start point.

when mode is 1 the step count is replaced: the squared axis differences, each multiplied by 16, are summed, the square root is taken, and the step count becomes that root divided by the divisor (signed integer division; the remainder is unused).
the square root of 16 times the summed squared differences equals 4 times the straight-line distance in raw units, which matches the opcode record.
start and target values are then shifted left by 8 bits (8.8 fixed point), and the step loop runs for step indices 1 to steps minus 1; when the step count is 1 or less the loop does not run.
mode 0: each axis becomes start + (target - start) * t / steps, where t is the step index.
mode 1: the mode 0 term plus (weight / 16) * (target - start) * t * (steps - t) / steps^2.
mode 2: the steps are split at the midpoint (the second part is selected when 2 * t is at least the steps); the code is a two-part curve that uses the weight and a half-count divisor.
mode 3: each axis becomes start + ((2 * weight * d * t / steps) + 2 * d * (16 - weight)) * t / (32 * steps), where d is target minus start.
any other mode leaves the stored step value unchanged.

each step waits one frame (SceneTask_WaitFrame), calls sub_140273908 on the unit, adds the negated previous offset to the unit's position words with sub_140272F04, adds the new offset (value shifted right by 8), keeps the negated new offset for the next step, and calls sub_140273838.
sub_140273838 sets one flag byte in the unit record only when the global dword_140782A94 equals 386.
after the loop it removes the previous offset, adds the target values (shifted right by 8), waits one frame when the step count was 1, and clears the byte at record offset 139.
when the unit record is missing during the steps or at the end, it calls SceneTask_Terminate instead of finishing.
this worker has no skip-condition check of its own.
the three targets are the unit's position words, and the mode and weight shape the path between the start and the targets.

notes: The opcode record for 0x6E (data/opcodes.jsonl) does not set starts_task; its operand list matches the 12 bytes read here.
open_questions: The exact fixed-point form of mode 2; what EventRef_ResolveSlot does for its later branches (ids 100 to 105 and the special id ranges); what sub_140273908 writes; what sub_140262808 returns; the caller at EventUnitMove_Task and its mode value.

name: EventPad_UpdateRepeat
purpose: Updates the held-button auto-repeat state used while the event system runs; only the scheduler slot (task index 16) does the work.

behavior.text: returns immediately unless the current-task index is 16.
latches the current pad word `word_1437EDF80` and the previous one, and stores the current word in the repeat-mask cell `off_1408B9AB8`.

reads five button-group masks through `sub_1400F6C8C` (ids 0x21, 0x22, 0x23, 0x24, 0x2D/0x2E) and, while a held button persists, counts frames in `dword_143791D30`, `dword_143791D34` and `dword_143791D38`.

compares the counters with thresholds from the bytes at 0x1407829FB, 0x1407829FE and 0x1407829FF divided by `dword_14078D578`; when a threshold is reached it writes the repeat mask to the cell at `off_1408B9A48`.
this is the held-button repeat: an initial delay, then a faster repeat for the directional buttons, with a different mask when the button group tested by `sub_1400FC598(.., 128, 0x1D)` is active.

notes: The button ids are not decoded; the threshold bytes are plain data.
open_questions: Name the button groups and the meaning of the 0x1D test.

name: EventPanel_PickRow
callers: EventPanel_ShowTask (tail call at 0x140233E9A). A data reference at 0x143D3E494 was not traced.
callees: `sub_14013B3AC`, `sub_1401DB4E4`, NaptrDnsRecordConvert_1 (name not verified), EventPanel_QueueAndWait, SceneTask_WaitFrame, SceneTask_Terminate
purpose: The second half of the 0x7D task: reads the row number the task stored in its block, picks that row of a language-dependent panel table and runs the branch for the row kind.

behavior.text: reads the signed dword at +0 of the running task block. The 0x7D handler stored the operand byte there, zero-extended, and that value is the row number. It is used without a range check.
calls NaptrDnsRecordConvert_1 with that dword as its only argument and ignores the result. The IDB name of that routine was not checked in this pass.

the table is unk_1407B4720 when the global g_LanguageInfo is null or the dword at +8 of it is not zero; otherwise it is unk_1407B4A30. A row is 14 dwords (56 bytes), so the row starts at table + 56 times the row number.
the first dword of the row is the kind. Kind 0 runs the title-panel branch, kind 1 calls EventPanel_QueueAndWait, and any other kind does nothing.

title-panel branch: takes the object at +88 of the object whose pointer is at +104 of the object at +16 of the global qword_143CD9DA8, calls sub_14013B3AC with that object and the row number, and calls sub_1401DB4E4 on the UI global qword_143CD9FD0.
sets the word at +34 of qword_143CD9FD0 to 257, the word at +49 to 257 and the byte at +51 to 1.
waits one frame per pass with SceneTask_WaitFrame while the byte at +416 of the object at +48 of the object at +88 is not zero.
then sets the word at +49 to 0, the byte at +51 to 0 and the word at +34 to 256.
in every case it then clears the byte at +33 of qword_143CD9FD0 and ends through SceneTask_Terminate.

notes: The table holds rows 0 to 13 in the 784 bytes from unk_1407B4720 to unk_1407B4A30. In both tables rows 0 to 6 have kind 0, row 7 has kind 1 and rows 8 to 12 have kind 2.
open_questions: What sub_14013B3AC does with the row number (it passes it on to two text routines); the meaning of the other dwords of each row; whether NaptrDnsRecordConvert_1 has side effects; what the table holds past row 13, which an operand of 14 or more would read; what the flag at +33 gates in other code.

name: EventPanel_QueueAndWait
callers: EventPanel_PickRow (call at 0x14033D691). Data references at 0x143D3E47C and 0x143D3E488 were not traced.
purpose: The kind-1 branch of EventPanel_PickRow: queues the value 50 in a two-entry queue, waits until the queue is released, then calls the callback sub_1402B1F08 with 1 and changes the global dword_1411A7D08 from 1 to 2.

behavior.text: calls sub_1400ED6EC with an argument the caller never sets (the callee does not read it) and 0, 0. That routine tests a virtual method of the object at +144 of the object whose pointer is at +16 of qword_143CD9DA8; when the test is non-zero and the pointer at +72 of that object is not null, it clears the byte at +168 and calls sub_1400FB3B0 and sub_14014129C (not traced).

sets the callback qword_140D40940 to sub_1402B2004 and calls it with 0. When the running task slot is not 0, the call first clears the qwords at +96 and +104 of block 0 of the task table and then calls through the callback pointer; otherwise it calls sub_1402B2004 directly.
sub_1402B2004 calls sub_1402B1ED0, then sub_1402B1E74 with 1 and with 2, then sub_1401D9784 on qword_143CD9DD8 plus 1384, and returns 0. Only the first call's effect was read.
sets the callback to sub_1402B1DF0 and calls it with 50, using the same slot rule.

sub_1402B1DF0 looks for a free entry among the two qwords at qword_141862400 (free means zero). It stores 50 in the dword at qword_142E7FB0C plus 4 times the entry index, stores a pointer to unk_14185A2E0 in the entry, sets the low dword of qword_1418623C0 to the index plus 1 (the count) and returns that count. When both entries are used it returns 0 and changes nothing.
loop: waits one frame with SceneTask_WaitFrame, sets the callback to sub_1402B1E40 and calls it with the same slot rule; repeats while it returns non-zero.

sub_1402B1E40 returns 0 when the count (low dword of qword_1418623C0) is zero. Otherwise, when the high dword of qword_141856AB0 is zero, it sets the queue entry at count minus 1 to 0, sets the count to 0 and returns 0; otherwise it returns 1.
sets the callback to sub_1402B1F08 and calls SceneCallback_Dispatch with mode 3 and argument 1.
then, if dword_1411A7D08 is 1 it becomes 2; any other value is kept. The routine returns that value.
the queue entries are consumed by sub_1402B1F08, which was only partly read (its first step is sub_1402B1ED0, which resets the step state from a fixed table at xmmword_140723AE0).

notes: The queue globals are qword_141862400 (two entries), qword_1418623C0 (count) and qword_142E7FB0C (values).
open_questions: What the value 50 means to the consumer sub_1402B1F08; what the high dword of qword_141856AB0 is; what sub_1402B1E74, sub_1401D9784 and sub_1400FB3B0 do; what the values 0, 1 and 2 of dword_1411A7D08 mean.

name: EventPanel_ShowTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x7D.
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x7D: takes a turn in the shared sequencer, then shows a panel chosen by its operand from a language-dependent table and waits for that panel's work to finish.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 61 in qword_140D40B38[256 * dword_140D40948].
calls sub_1402334FC(12, ...) to wait for and take the shared sequencer slot 12 before any work.
sets the byte at qword_143CD9FD0 + 33 to 1.
tail-calls sub_14033D5C4, which reads the first dword of its task block (the operand byte that EventScript_Run stored there) and uses it as a row index.

the row table is unk_1407B4720 when the value at g_LanguageInfo + 8 is nonzero (or g_LanguageInfo is null), otherwise unk_1407B4A30; each row is 14 dwords, and the first dword of the row selects the branch.
before the branch it calls NaptrDnsRecordConvert_1 with the same operand value; its result is not used.

branch 0: looks up the title UI nodes by key (strings TitleL and TitleS, and Show) through sub_14013B3AC, runs sub_1401DB4E4 on qword_143CD9FD0, sets its fields (+34 to 257, +49 to 257, +51 to 1), waits frame by frame while a byte in the UI object is nonzero, then clears +49 and +51 and sets +34 to 256.

branch 1: calls sub_14033D4C0, which runs sub_1402B2004, queues the value 50 with sub_1402B1DF0, and waits frame by frame while sub_1402B1E40 reports queued work (a queue entry exists and the high dword of `qword_141856AB0` is nonzero); it then sets the handler to sub_1402B1F08, calls SceneCallback_Dispatch(3, 1), and changes dword_1411A7D08 from 1 to 2.
any other row value does nothing.
at the end it clears the byte at qword_143CD9FD0 + 33 and ends through SceneTask_Terminate.

notes: The opcode record for 0x7D (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What the panel is (the UI nodes and the queued value 50); what NaptrDnsRecordConvert_1 really does (its IDB name may be wrong; not verified here); what the flag byte at qword_143CD9FD0 + 33 gates; the meaning of the table rows and fields.

name: EventPanel_ShowWaitTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0xAB; EventScript_Run starts it only when `dword_1407D453C` is 1
callees: `sub_1401402BC`, `sub_14014D4CC`, `sub_140140078`, `sub_140140160`, a virtual call on the sub-object at owner+160+64 (not named), SceneTask_WaitFrame, SceneTask_Terminate
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0xAB when the enhanced flag is set: shows the UI table row named by its operand on the panel and waits until the panel closes or the skip test passes.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with 73 (0x49) in `qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`.
reads the dword at +0 of its task block into `edi`, the operand value the opcode handler stores there, and uses it as a row id.
the panel owner is `*(qword_143CD9DA8 + 16) + 144`. It calls `sub_1401402BC(owner, 0)`, which plays the GUI state keyed Top on the panel object at owner+160.
when owner+160 is set it calls `sub_14014D4CC(owner+160, id)`, which reads row `id` of UI table 34 and sets the dword at +1904 to the number of non-zero dwords among that row's dwords 2, 3 and 4.
calls `sub_140140078(owner, 0)`, then `sub_140140160(owner)`. If that returns 0 (the panel state's active byte at +416 is clear) the task ends at once.
at the top of each pass, if the dword at +4 of `qword_142FF9E08` is non-zero and the dword at +4 of `qword_142FF9E00` is 3 (the skip test), the task ends at once without the closing call.

otherwise it sets a local dword to -1 and, when owner+160 is set, calls the virtual function at vtable offset 56 of the sub-object at owner+160+64 with a pointer to that local, the dword read through `off_1407DCB48` and the word read through `off_1407DD348`. The output is only compared with -1 and is not kept.
if the local no longer equals -1 the task calls `sub_140140078(owner, -1)` and ends.
otherwise, if the skip test is true it calls `sub_140140078(owner, -1)` and ends; if not, it calls SceneTask_WaitFrame and loops while `sub_140140160(owner)` is non-zero, and ends when it is zero.
ends through SceneTask_Terminate.

notes: The opcode record for 0xAB (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What the virtual function in vtable slot 56 does with its dword and word arguments, what `sub_140140078` does with 0 and -1 on the panel, and what the rows of UI table 34 contain.

name: EventPreviewUnit_StageSlot
purpose: Finds a preview-unit slot for a 16-bit reference, copies its 512-byte record into the staging buffer and sets the staged flag.

behavior.text: the argument is a signed 16-bit value. EventScript_Run builds it from the byte at instruction offset 1 (low) and the byte at offset 2 (high), shifted left by 8 and sign-extended.
the value is given to EventRef_ResolveSlot as its reference. The decompiled call shows no argument, and the argument register is not changed before the call, so this is inferred.

when EventRef_ResolveSlot returns 2000 and dword_140782A94 is 281 and the argument is 25, it scans the 21 slots of g_BattleUnitTable for one whose byte +0 is 25. When one is found, it saves that slot's byte +1, writes the slot index into byte +1, sets dword_142FCF86C to 25, and uses that slot. Otherwise no slot is used.
when the resolver returns a value other than 2000, it calls ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot with that value. The slot is used only if the index is 0 to 20.
when a slot is used, it copies 512 bytes from the slot to the staging buffer unk_142FD1390 (four 128-byte blocks) and sets byte_142FCF85F to 1.
it zeroes a 156-byte scratch record (sub_140103C50), then fills it from the slot with sub_1402CBCA0. The dword just after the scratch record is the value it uses as the result.

result = dword_142FCF86C. When the dword after the scratch record is not -1, that value is the result. The result is written back to dword_142FCF86C. When the saved byte +1 is positive, it is restored to the slot. The function returns the result.
the dword after the scratch record is treated as an output of sub_1402CBCA0, which was not checked in full.

notes: The 2000 special case for argument 25 under state 281 is a temporary change to byte +1 of one slot that is undone before return.
open_questions: What sub_1402CBCA0 writes into the scratch record and its trailing dword, and what consumes the staging buffer (sub_140214404 reads it in EventPreviewUnits_RunFrames).

name: EventPreviewUnits_RunFrames
purpose: Runs the per-frame preview-unit update for opcode 0xC1: it applies flagged preview-unit slots and, when any were flagged, waits while the UI reports busy.

behavior.text: reads no operand. EventScript_Run calls it with four register values (0, 1, a value and 193), and the body does not read them directly. Two of them are passed on to sub_1402B20C0, which takes no arguments in the decompiled form.
does nothing when the low dword of qword_142FF9E4C is nonzero.
when dword_140782A94 is 8 and the high dword of qword_142FF9E08 is nonzero, it waits one frame at a time while the high dword of qword_142FF9E00 is nonzero and not 3, then waits 30 frames.
sets the high dword of qword_142FF9E00 to 2. When the interface object at qword_143CD9FD0 is non-null it sets word +49 to 257 and byte +51 to 1.
when byte_142FCF85F is set and byte_142FD1588 has bit 0x40, it calls sub_140214404 on the staging buffer unk_142FD1390 and clears byte_142FCF85F.
loops over the 21 records of g_BattleUnitTable (512 bytes each). When byte +1 is not 0xFF and byte +504 has bit 0x40, it calls sub_140216C78 with the slot index, then sub_140214404 with the record.

loops over 21 records at unk_141853CE1 (512 bytes each). When byte +0 is not 0xFF and byte +503 has bit 0x20, it calls sub_140216C78 with the index. For the first two such records it stores the index in a dword list at (the pointer at +144 of the object at [qword_143CD9DA8+16]) + 188 + 4 times the count.

if any record was flagged in that second pass, it calls sub_1402B20C0, looks up the key 167 in table 69 with UITable_GetRowByKey and dispatches on that row's type code (the four targets were not read), sets word +34 of the interface object to 257, calls sub_1401DB4E4, calls sub_14013FAB0 with the object at +144 and the flagged count, sets the low dword of qword_142FF9E00 to 1, and waits one frame at a time while sub_14013F71C on that object returns nonzero.
loops over the 21 slots of g_BattleUnitTable again. When byte +1 is not 0xFF and byte +504 is negative (bit 0x80), it calls sub_140214610 (no arguments).
calls sub_140214828 with the last argument values. It returns no value that the routine uses.

clears word +49 and byte +51 of the interface object and sets its word +34 to 256 (on the interface object at qword_143CD9FD0). If the object at +144 holds a non-null pointer at +136, it calls sub_1400EDC68 twice on g_CharaRenderMgr, with the sub-objects at +2440 and +2472 of that pointer.

the bodies of sub_140216C78, sub_140214404, sub_140214610, sub_140214828, sub_14013FAB0 and sub_14013F71C were not read in full. The statements about what they change are from the calls and their use, not from their internals.

notes: The high dword of qword_142FF9E00 is set to 2 here and is not cleared in this routine. The callee sub_14013F71C or the wait loop may clear it elsewhere, which was not checked.
open_questions: Which routine clears the high dword of qword_142FF9E00 after this one returns. What sub_140216C78 and sub_140214404 do to a slot. What the four targets of table 69 row 167 do.

name: EventRef_ResolveSlot
callers: About 64 call sites in 20 routines, the widest-used resolver of the event code: EventScript_Run (32 call sites), EventSubScript_RunTask (8), EventMessage_Task (5), and about 13 others such as sub_140240144, sub_1402404CC, sub_140241BD0 and sub_140242140.
callees: ScenePreview_FindEntry, sub_140272538, ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot (ref 105 only), SceneObject_FindBySlot (ref 105 only), ScenePreview_SlotOfIndex, SceneVar_Read (argument 39)
purpose: Turns a script reference id into the slot number of the object it names. Most event opcodes call it to find their target; it returns 2000 when nothing matches.

behavior.text: `ref` is the reference id, taken as 32 bits. Callers pass a signed 16-bit operand read from the instruction, or a constant such as 2, 23, 52, 62 or 131 to 138. `flag` is stored into a local that is overwritten before any read on every path, so the result does not depend on it; most callers pass 1.

step 1 looks `ref` up with ScenePreview_FindEntry, which compares the low 8 bits. Only when that finds nothing, and `ref` is 162, 163 or 1 to 73, it asks sub_140272538 for the record index of the unit id. If the index is 0 to 20 and byte +401 of that record is 120 to 124, `ref` becomes that byte.
ref 104 scans records 0 to 15 for the first whose byte +5 has bit 0 or bit 1 set, and sets `ref` to that record's byte +401. If none is found it returns 2000.

ref 105 scans slot numbers 0 to 20 for an object (SceneObject_FindBySlot) whose preview index (ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot) names a record with byte +440 non-zero, and sets `ref` to that record's byte +401. If none matches, it looks up refs 1, 2 and 3 in turn and keeps the first with a non-negative status. If none qualifies, or the record it stopped on has bit 0x04 of byte +97 set, it returns 2000.
refs 100 to 103 do not give a slot. They return the 16-bit value at index (ref - 100) of the table `qword_140783038`, and a stored 1000 becomes 2000.
otherwise it calls ScenePreview_FindEntry(ref) for the record and status. A negative status other than -2 returns 2000, unless SceneVar_Read(39) equals 404.

it finds the record's index k (0 to 20) by comparing pointers over the 21 records, using 21 when there is no match, and calls ScenePreview_SlotOfIndex(k). It returns 2000 when that is -1 or when bit 0 of the record's byte +98 is set. Otherwise it returns the slot number, 0 to 255.

notes: Fixed values in the code: 2000 for no match, 1000 in the qword_140783038 table, the ref ranges 1 to 73, 100 to 105, 120 to 124 and 162 to 163. In EventScript_Run the first call reads the reference as a signed 16-bit operand at instruction offset 1.
open_questions: What record bytes +5, +98, +401 and +440 mean; why refs 100 to 105 exist and what the scans behind 104 and 105 select; what SceneVar_Read(39) equal to 404 means. Step 7 reads byte +98 with no null test: if no record matched but ScenePreview_SlotOfIndex(21) finds an object, the read would go through a null pointer. Not confirmed whether that can happen.

name: EventScene_QueueHelpText
callees: memcpy, sub_1400FBB40, sub_1401D78C0, sub_1401E37D4, sub_1400F71E8, Unit_GetSpriteSetId, sub_1402C3570, sub_14021E7FC, EventTask_Start, EventTask_Terminate, sub_14041FAE0
purpose: Prepares a unit preview scene task: it builds the preview sprite record for the selected party unit, queues the shared help-text id as render command 12 and starts the event task.

behavior.text: the selected party slot is the signed word at 0x141811428; the unit pointer is g_PartyUnits[slot] and its job word is at +0x126.
Unit_GetSpriteSetId is called on that job and the result feeds PreviewUnit_BuildSpriteRecord.
the help slot at 0x1418736B4 is sign-extended and written to the render command block at 0x14078D5D8 + 0x800, with command 0x12 and a zero word after it.
the command block is then handed to sub_1402BA698, the render queue.
EventTask_Start creates the scene task and EventTask_Terminate ends it when the preview cannot be built.
the render command uses the S3 text slot.
the function has no direct caller; the event scene state machine reaches it by a stored pointer.
this is the help-panel preview task, because the queued command is the shared help text id rather than a dialogue line.
what sub_1402C3570 creates before the task starts; it is not tied to a named object here.

notes: Whole function read (697 bytes). The missing direct caller is a fact; the dispatch route is inferred.

name: EventScript_FindInstruction
proto: uint32_t EventScript_FindInstruction(int offset, int opcode, int altOpcode, int argByte)
purpose: Scans the loaded event script for an instruction with a given opcode (or an alternative opcode) whose first operand byte has a given value.

behavior.text: for any opcode other than 0xD5 it walks instruction by instruction from `offset` until the end opcode 0xDB; a match is an instruction whose opcode equals `opcode`, or equals `altOpcode` when that is not -1, and whose first operand byte equals `argByte`.
a match returns the match's offset plus 2.
when the end opcode is reached with no match it calls `sub_1402F7EC8` and returns 0.
opcode 0xD5 takes a different path: it walks the instructions from the start of the script up to `offset` and returns a position derived from the last one passed.
opcode 0xD5 is a jump-target style opcode and is searched by position, not by argument.

notes: Used to resolve jump and label targets inside the loaded script.
open_questions: The exact return value of the 0xD5 path.

name: EventScript_FindOpcode
purpose: Scans the loaded event script from a byte offset for the next instruction with a given opcode and returns its offset.

behavior.text: starts at `offset` in the event buffer pointed to by `qword_140D40A90` and steps instruction by instruction with EventScript_InstructionLength.
returns the offset of the first instruction whose opcode equals the requested one.
the end opcode 0xDB (219) is checked first: reaching it returns 0, so searching for 0xDB itself always returns 0.
used by the event preparation routine `sub_14023A868`, for example to find every 0x92 instruction before the event starts.

notes: A zero return means not found, which cannot be confused with a real match because instruction offsets that follow a scan start are greater than zero.

name: EventScript_InstructionLength
purpose: Returns the length in bytes of the event script instruction at a pointer: one opcode byte plus its operand bytes.

behavior.text: opcode 0xE6 is variable length: the byte after it is the operand length, so the instruction is that value plus 2 bytes.
every other opcode uses a 256-entry operand-length byte table at 0x140680F00 (image base + 0x680F00) indexed by the opcode: length = table[opcode] + 1.
when the enhanced-edition flag `dword_1407D453C` is 1 three opcodes are longer than the table says: 0x10 (DisplayMessage) by 3 bytes, 0x51 (ChangeDialog) by 2 and 0xEB by 4.
the table holds the original (classic) lengths, for example 14 for opcode 0x10, 5 for 0x51 and 0 for the end opcode 0xDB; the enhanced differences are applied in code.
about 9 callers, all of which walk or scan the script buffer.

notes: Any tool that edits event scripts needs exactly this length rule to step from one instruction to the next.
open_questions: The meaning of the enhanced-only opcodes; this routine gives their length only.

name: EventScript_IsSkipStop
purpose: Decides whether a given opcode counts as a stopping point when the interpreter skips forward through a script.

behavior.text: returns true for a fixed set of opcodes and false for all others.
opcodes 0x19, 0x58, 0x59, 0x7F and 0xD0 count only while the current event number `dword_140782A94` is 213, and opcode 0x3D only while it is 2.

opcode 0x78 counts only when `dword_142FF9EBC` is non-zero; opcode 0x76 counts only when that is non-zero and `word_142FEC554` is zero. When either counts it sets `*flagOut` to 1 and clears a field, and 0x76 also sets `word_142FEC528` to 32.
opcode 0xE5 counts only when `*flagOut` is non-zero, and then clears it.
called twice from EventScript_Run, in loops that step forward with EventScript_InstructionLength until this returns true.
the true opcodes are the ones that must still run, or be noticed, while the player skips a cutscene.

notes: Named for its use in the skip loops; the opcode set itself is a decision table in the code.
open_questions: Confirm the skip behavior against a running skip, and name the state words.

name: EventScript_LoadCurrent
callees: SceneTask_WaitFrame, SceneVar_Read, EventScript_LoadIntoBuffer, `sub_140242588`, the NXD helpers
purpose: Loads the event the game is currently on, if it is not already loaded.

behavior.text: waits frames until `sub_140242588` returns 0 for each of the scene task slots 4 to 14, so no earlier task is still using the buffer.
reads event variable 39 with SceneVar_Read; this is the current event number.
if it equals the last loaded event number `dword_140782A94` it returns 0 and does nothing else.
