otherwise it consults row 156 of the NXD table list (through the table helpers `sub_1403D325C`, `sub_1403D3AE8` and `sub_1403D2FD8`) and an eight-entry list to set a flag in `qword_142FF9E4C`, sets a byte in the record at `qword_143CD9FD0 + 52`, calls EventScript_LoadIntoBuffer with the event number, stores it in `dword_140782A94` and returns 1.
variable 39 holds the story event number that decides which script plays.

notes: Together with EventScript_LoadIntoBuffer and EventScript_LoadFile this is the whole path from the current event number to bytes in memory.
open_questions: What NXD table row 156 supplies and what the eight-entry list selects.

name: EventScript_LoadFile
callees: `sub_1402F420C` (number formatting), `sub_14002620C` and `sub_140026288` (string copy and append), the file helpers `sub_1403D2004`, `sub_1403D21F0`, `sub_1403D2358` and `sub_1403D21C8`
purpose: Loads one event script file from the game's script folder into a caller buffer.

behavior.text: builds the file name `<root>/script/enhanced/event<NNN>.e`, or `script/classic/event<NNN>.e` when `dword_1407D453C` is 0, where NNN is the sector index divided by 5, or by 3 when the language-info field at +8 is 0, printed with `%03u`.
the root is the game data path in `byte_142C81598`.
opens the file; on failure it returns 1 without touching the buffer.
on success it writes the file size plus 4 into the first four bytes of the buffer, then reads the whole file to `buffer + 4`, and closes the file; it returns 0.
the divisor 5 versus 3 reflects the enhanced and classic layouts, in which one event spans 5 or 3 original disc sectors.

notes: This is how event scripts reach memory.
open_questions: Where the loaded buffer is parsed into the event interpreter.

name: EventScript_LoadIntoBuffer
purpose: Loads an event script into the shared 10,240-byte event buffer and substitutes a variant for a few special events.

behavior.text: loops, waiting a frame each time (SceneTask_WaitFrame), until GameData_ReadSectors(17, eventNumber * 5 or * 3, 10240, buffer) succeeds; the buffer is `unk_140D3CD50` and the script itself starts at `unk_140D3CD54`, after the 4-byte size prefix.

when `xmmword_1437A62B0` is non-zero and the event number is one of 0x19B, 0x19D, 0x19F, 0x1A1, 0x1A3, 0x1A5, 0x1A7 or 0x1A9 (411 to 425, odd), it picks a slot 0 to 7 and replaces the tail of the loaded script with that slot's stored variant, then rewrites the size prefix.
when no variant was applied and the enhanced flag `dword_1407D453C` is 1, it calls `sub_1401DAE20(qword_143CD9DB8, eventNumber)`.

finally, unless the size prefix already holds the marker 0xF2F2F2F2, it stores a pointer to the end of the script (buffer plus the size prefix) in `qword_140D40990[0]` and overwrites the size prefix with 0xF2F2F2F2.
the eight variant events are the scripts that carry per-run changes, such as player-chosen content.

notes: After this call the interpreter and the scan helpers read the script through the pointer `qword_140D40A90`.
open_questions: What the stored variants are and who writes them.

name: EventScript_ReadDword
callers: 46 call sites in 2 routines: EventScript_Run (42) and sub_1401DEC14 (4).
purpose: Reads a 4-byte little-endian operand from script memory. EventScript_Run uses it for most of its operands.

behavior.text: reads four bytes from the given address in order and combines them: byte n is shifted left by 8 times n and OR-ed into the result, so the first byte is the lowest.
returns the result as an unsigned 32-bit value, zero-extended to 64 bits.
the code is a four-iteration loop with no branches and no global access. The enhanced-edition flag `dword_1407D453C` is not read here; the disassembly has no reference to that address.
EventScript_Run passes addresses of the form script base (`qword_140D40A90`) + instruction offset + k, with k of 1, 2, 3, 5, 9 or 13 in the calls read.

notes: I: any difference between the editions in operand size is handled by the callers, not by this function.
open_questions: Where dword_1407D453C is read, and whether it changes operand sizes in EventScript_Run or in the callers of this function.

name: EventScript_Run
callees: SceneTask_Start, SceneTask_WaitFrame, EventScript_InstructionLength, EventScript_FindOpcode, EventScript_FindInstruction, EventScript_IsSkipStop, SceneVar_Read, SceneVar_Write, SceneVar_Alu, SceneTask_Terminate and many opcode helpers
purpose: The event interpreter: it walks the loaded event script one instruction at a time and carries out each opcode. It is the biggest function in the event code, with about 19,000 bytes and 3,700 decompiled lines.

behavior.text: reads the script through the pointer `qword_140D40A90`, with the program counter in a local; each step loads the opcode byte at the counter and the operand bytes at +1 to +4 into locals.
dispatches on the opcode through 13 binary-search `switch` blocks; about 170 distinct opcode values are handled in this function.
advances the counter with EventScript_InstructionLength after each instruction.
the end opcode 0xDB stops the script; it is also forced when `word_141874530` is set and none of the scene tasks 2 to 15 is running.
before the main loop it scans the script with EventScript_FindOpcode for 0x92 instructions and, for units whose flags allow it, starts the task `sub_14024189C` for each.

starts 21 task bodies through SceneTask_Start, waits with SceneTask_WaitFrame 74 times, reads variables with SceneVar_Read (15 times) and writes them with SceneVar_Write (14 times), and calls SceneVar_Alu directly for the variable opcodes.
uses EventScript_IsSkipStop (twice) to find the next instruction that matters when it skips forward.
opcodes that take time (waits, walks, messages, camera moves) are handled by starting a task and waiting for it, while simple opcodes run inline.

at the start of an event it tests byte +36 (skip_once) of the EventId row of the event variable; when that is 0 it reads the OverrideEntryData row for g_BattleEntrySource and tests bytes +0x93, +0x94 and +0x95 (guest_join_panel, withdrawal_panel, betrayal_panel). I: a non-zero byte there acts like the EventId byte: g_EventSkipOnce is set to 1 (the event may be skipped only once); otherwise it is cleared (see the behaviour EntryRowMarksEventSkipOnce).
the objective camera tour sub_1401EA2F0 is called from this function.
opcode 0x43 (scene set-up) is the default arm of the switch for opcodes 0x2D to 0x44; its behavior, by mode:
opcode 0x43, the section is the default arm of the switch for opcodes 0x2D to 0x44 that has no case of its own; no case for 0x43 exists in the switches around it, so opcode 0x43 reaches this arm.
opcode 0x43, the mode is the byte at +1 of the instruction. The section does nothing else with the operand bytes at +2 and +3.
opcode 0x43, waits four frames with SceneTask_WaitFrame before any branch.
opcode 0x43, reads scene variable 508 with SceneVar_Read. When it is zero, the mode 1 and mode 6 branches run. When it is non-zero, those two are skipped and every other branch below still runs.

opcode 0x43, mode 1 (variable 508 zero): when scene variable 39 is below 78, it calls `sub_1402842CC`, reads one byte from the record at qword_143CD9DE0 (offset 171 when bit 0 of the byte at offset 16 is set, otherwise offset 91), calls `sub_140227458` with that byte and ends the section at once. When variable 39 is 78 or more, it calls `sub_140227458` with 0 and continues with the later branches.

opcode 0x43, mode 6 (variable 508 zero): for each slot from 2 to 14 it writes 0 to the qword at offset 0 and 0 to the qword at offset 8 of its block in the task table `off_140783088`, writes 1 to the qword at offset 16, writes 3 to the tag qword qword_140D40B38 of that slot, and calls `sub_1402F7F4C` for the slot, which waits until the runnable qword at block offset 144 is zero.

opcode 0x43, mode 6 then reads scene variable 39 (300 sets dword_142FEC514 to 1, otherwise variable 100 is written 1), writes variable 81 as 1, clears the high dword of qword_142FF9E08, calls EventSequencer_TakeTurn(14, ...)`, sets dword_140D40850 to 5 and waits until it is zero, sets the low dword of qword_142FF9E00 to 1, writes variable 100 as 0 and clears dword_142FEC514.
opcode 0x43, mode 6 then repeats the same slot reset for slots 2 to 14. The repeat loop leaves the mode operand at 15, so the mode 15 branch below also runs for a mode 6 instruction.
opcode 0x43, modes 2 and 7 write 365 to scene variable 84 with SceneVar_Write.

opcode 0x43, mode 3 loops over 21 units: for each unit whose flag byte at unk_141853CE5 (stride 512) has bits 0x30 clear, it adds 10 to the byte at unk_141853D0B with the same stride, capped at 100. The loop bound is 21, so the branch for index 21 and above is not reached.

opcode 0x43, mode 4 loops over slots 0 to 20: for each slot where SceneObject_FindBySlot returns a unit, it reads ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot; when that is not -1 and ScenePreview_FindEntry on the record byte at unk_141853E71 (stride 512) gives a status other than -2 and the byte at offset 494 has bits 0x30 set, it calls SceneUnit_ResetAndQueue4(slot, 2, -31, -31, 0). Afterwards it waits 120 frames.
opcode 0x43, mode 5 sets dword_142FF8280 to 1. Mode 8 sets dword_14185670C to 0.
opcode 0x43, modes 9 and 10 write scene variable 83 as 1 and as 0.
opcode 0x43, mode 11 reads word_142FEC530: a value of 1 is changed to 2 first. If the value is then 0, the section ends at once; otherwise it waits until word_142FEC530 is 0.
opcode 0x43, mode 12 sets word_140D40900 to 0, word_140D4091C to 19 and word_140D408FC to 0, then calls `sub_140234990(19, 0)`.

opcode 0x43, mode 13 copies byte 141854B2F to byte 141854D2F and byte 141854B30 to byte 141854D30. It sets the high bit of byte 141854D31 from byte 141854B31 and keeps its low seven bits. It calls ScenePreview_ShowEntry(8, 1), waits until word_140D407D0 is zero, then waits two more frames.

opcode 0x43, mode 14 loops over slots 0 to 20 with SceneObject_FindBySlot. For each unit it found, it replaces the mode with ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot of that slot, so after the loop the mode is the value from the last unit found (-1, 0 to 20), or stays 14 when no unit was found. The branch then reads the bytes at 141853D2F and 141853D30 (stride 512) and calls SceneUnit_SetFlag156 for the units that match.

opcode 0x43, mode 17 copies byte 141853F2F to byte 141854B2F and byte 141853F30 to byte 141854B30. It sets byte 141854B31 from byte 141853F31, except bits 4 to 6, which keep their old values. It calls ScenePreview_ShowEntry(7, 1), waits until word_140D407D0 is zero, then waits two more frames.

opcode 0x43, mode 15 uses slot 3 and the byte at 141853F31; mode 16 uses slot 4 and the byte at 141854131. Each calls ScenePreview_SlotOfIndex with its slot number. When the result is not -1 it writes the words at 142FEF860, 142FEF862 and 142FEF864, writes the seven-byte record at unk_142FEC580 plus seven times the result (byte 0 = four times the low nibble of the source byte, bytes 4 and 6 = 0), calls `sub_140272F3C(result)` and calls `sub_14021F538(result, four times the low nibble)`.

opcode 0x43, in modes 15 and 16 the value written to word 142FEF860 is read through a pointer that the decompile does not assign on these paths, and the value written to word 142FEF864 is read from an address that is not set on these paths.

opcode 0x43, mode 18 calls EventRef_ResolveSlot(62, flag); when the result is 2000 the section ends. Otherwise it replaces the mode with ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot of the slot, calls `sub_140241080(slot, 0)`, sets qword_140D40940 to EventUnitStatus_RefreshNode, and then: when dword_140D40948 is not zero, it writes 0 to the qwords at offsets 96 and 104 of `off_140783088` and calls qword_140D40940 with the slot; otherwise it calls EventUnitStatus_RefreshNode with the slot.

opcode 0x43, mode 19 calls `sub_1402B20C0`, sets a local flag that the 0xE3 transition body reads later, and when dword_143807794 equals 2 it sets the low dword of qword_142FF9E00 to 1. When dword_143807794 is not 2, the section ends there.

opcode 0x43, mode 255 calls SceneVar_Alu(190, 48, 0, ...), sets word_140D40910 to 1 and waits until it is zero, calls SceneVar_Alu(176, 48, 2, ...), sets word_140D40910 to 1, clears qword_14114A0F6, dword_14114A0FE and word_14114A102, waits until word_140D40910 is zero, and calls `sub_1402694E4` for each entry of the list that starts at qword_140D3A410.
opcode 0x43, any other mode value, including 0 and 20 to 254, has no branch and only waits the four frames.
opcode 0x43, after any branch the section ends at the common exit, which moves the script position past the current instruction (the same exit as the other opcodes that finish without a jump).
opcode 0x43, the mode 1, mode 6, mode 11 and mode 18 branches can end the section early, which skips the branches after them.

notes: Opcode semantics are spread through the function; per-opcode sheets would document the individual cases. The loaded script layout and lengths are described on EventScript_InstructionLength and EventScript_LoadIntoBuffer.
open_questions: The behavior of each opcode case.

name: EventScript_SkipTick
callers: The event script runner's per-frame tick
purpose: The event fast-forward tick: while the skip action is held it raises the skip state that makes the event text advance.

behavior.text: it writes 1 into the high dword of g_ScreenFade (the skip state) at 0x140239D33; it is the only writer of that value in the image.
the write is gated on the skip action (action 0x1F) being masked in, or the event UI node being in state 3, and on four further flags.
it reads and writes scene variables and tests input actions through the shared helpers.
it calls SceneCallback_Dispatch for its scene callbacks, so it is itself part of the event task chain.
live testing showed Ctrl and Shift do not reach this write (C6's negative result).
the fast-forward is a held action, not a key: the tick raises the state while the action stays down.

the trigger is `a2 == Input_ActionBit(0x1F)` only when g_ShopModeGate (0x1407D453C, the enhanced-edition flag) is 0; with the flag set the trigger is g_EventControl state (+8) == 3, which EventControl_PausedTick sets when the pause-overlay hold completes.

the gate is the same five-field test as EventSkip_IsAvailable: g_EventSkipEnabled (0x142E7FB3C) != 0, g_EventSkipVeto (0x142FF9E54) == 0, the armed dword 0x142FF9E50 != 0, the skip state (high dword of g_ScreenFade) == 0; then, when g_EventSkipOnce (0x142FF9EBC) is not 2, it writes skip state 1, fade mode 1, and turns g_EventSkipOnce 1 into 2.
in the enhanced edition the skip action alone never raises the state, which is why held keys did not reach the write; only the pause overlay's hold does.

notes: Name from C6, which identifies the function by this name. Evidence: C6 finding 1 (the only writer of 1), the body scan (19 calls). 2,103 bytes.

name: EventScript_TaskMain
purpose: The entry function of the event interpreter task: loads the current event, adjusts one global flag, and runs the interpreter.

behavior.text: calls EventScript_LoadCurrent first.
when the low dword of `xmmword_1437A62B0` is 0 it keeps the low dword of `qword_142E7FB1C` unless the high dword of `xmmword_142FF9E38` is 1, in which case it sets it to 1.
returns EventScript_Run().
it is started once as a task entry through SceneTask_Start.

notes: This is where an event begins to run as a task.
open_questions: What the two global flags select.

name: EventSequence_RecordTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x76.
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x76: takes a turn in the shared sequencer, then records two values per frame into a history until the task is stopped.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 54 in qword_140D40B38[256 * dword_140D40948].

calls sub_1402334FC(6, ...): it waits while dword_140D408B8 or dword_140D408BC is nonzero, sets dword_140D408B8 to 6, and waits until that value is cleared. It ends the task when word_140D408F8 equals 1.
the body does not read the operand bytes.

then tail-calls sub_1402CB7D4, which stores the current slot in dword_140809284, copies qword_140D409A0 into qword_140D40A38, calls SceneVar_Read(39), and calls sub_1402600BC twice to build two command records (the first with flag argument 6).
sub_1402CB7D4 writes constant values into a block of globals at 0x1437707AA to 0x143770808 and copies element 5 of each row into element 0 for a 12 by 32 table at unk_143770880.
it sets the slot's tag to 55 in qword_140D40B38 (the tag changes from 54 to 55 inside this task).

each frame it waits (SceneTask_WaitFrame), copies word_140809164 and byte_140809166 into the current half of the history buffers dword_1437707AA and dword_1437707AE (the half is chosen by the frame counter's parity), and breaks out when the qword at task block field 19 of the current slot equals 54 or the skip condition holds (the high dword of `qword_142FF9E08` nonzero and the high dword of `qword_142FF9E00` equal to 3).
the outer loop body runs once; after the inner loop it waits one more frame and ends through SceneTask_Terminate.
the history looks like a per-frame log of two values, but its reader is not in this entry.

notes: The opcode record for 0x76 (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: Who reads the history buffers and what word_140809164 and byte_140809166 hold; what field 19 of the task block is and who writes the value 54 there (the body writes 54 to the tag array, a different array); what sub_1402600BC's command records are used for.

name: EventSequencer_TakeTurn
callers: EventPanel_ShowTask (tag 12, call at 0x140233E86); EventSequence_RecordTask (tag 6, call at 0x14023357A); EventScript_Run (tag 13 in the 0x91 handler at 0x14023DA7C; tag 14 at 0x14023C177 in a path not identified here); EventUnitBlock_RunTask (tag 13 at 0x140235DD0, the 0x82 path); and routines sub_140233954, sub_14023397C, sub_1402339A8, sub_140233A28, sub_140233B24, sub_140233DA0, sub_1402357C4 and sub_1402C7EA8 (tags read from their call sites).
purpose: Waits for the shared sequencer to be free, claims it by writing the caller's tag, waits until it is released, and ends the caller when the flag word at word_140D408F8 is 1.

behavior.text: while dword_140D408B8 or dword_140D408BC is non-zero, calls SceneTask_WaitFrame.
writes the argument (the tag) to dword_140D408B8. This is the claim.

while dword_140D408B8 is non-zero, calls SceneTask_WaitFrame. Nothing in this routine writes it back to zero; other code releases it. sub_140234360 clears it with a value taken from a callback result, and sub_140243A60 and BattleLoad_StepFresh also write it (not traced here).
when word_140D408F8 is 1 after the release, calls SceneTask_Terminate, which ends the calling task. Otherwise it returns.
the return value is whatever the last wait left in the result register; no value is set on purpose.

notes: The tag is the number written to dword_140D408B8; the routine does not test the claim again after the first wait. Tag 12 is the 0x7D panel, tag 6 the 0x76 record task and tag 13 the 0x91 handler.
open_questions: Which code clears dword_140D408B8 and dword_140D408BC for each tag, and what the release value is; what sets the flag word at 0x140D408F8 (SceneTasks_Init and others write it).

name: EventSkip_IsAvailable
purpose: Says whether the running event script may be skipped now. The event pause overlay asks it when it opens (to show or hide the Skip hint) and on every paused frame (to accept the hold).

behavior.text: returns true at once when EventSkip_IsViewerEvent returns true (call at 0x140239838).

otherwise returns true only when all of these hold: g_EventSkipEnabled (0x142E7FB3C) is non-zero (0x140239847); the low dword of g_EventSkipVeto (0x142FF9E54) is 0 (0x14023984F); the high dword of g_EventSkipFlags (0x142FF9E50, 'armed') is non-zero (0x140239857); the high dword of g_ScreenFade (0x142FF9E0C, the skip state) is 0 (0x14023985F); g_EventSkipOnce (0x142FF9EBC) is not 2 (0x140239867).
it only reads globals: no input, no UI object, no write. The result is a pure function of state that exists while the script runs, so it can be evaluated from memory at any time.
EventScript_SkipTick applies the same five-field test before it raises the skip state (at 0x140239D02..0x140239D26, addresses inside EventScript_SkipTick, not this function).
g_EventSkipEnabled is always 1 (its only writer, VideoState_InitDefaults, stores 1), so in practice the test is armed != 0, veto == 0, skip state == 0 and skip-once != 2.

notes: The low dword of 0x142FF9E4C is not part of this test; it is the event-viewer flag (see g_EventSkipFlags). The dword at 0x142FF9E50 is.

name: EventSkip_IsViewerEvent
purpose: The second way an event becomes skippable: event variable 508 set (an event started from a viewer path), with the event number outside 410..425 and a blocking flag clear.

behavior.text: returns true when SceneVar_Read(508) is non-zero, SceneVar_Read(39) - 410 is above 15 (unsigned), and dword_141849E10 is 0; otherwise false.

the two writers of event variable 508 = 1 found here, EventViewer_EntryPage and sub_1402D28C8, also write event variable 39 (the event number), set both dwords of g_EventSkipFlags to 1 and set dword_141849E10 to (EventChain_Find(event) != -1).

sub_1402D28C8 is reached from a menu handler (sub_140169404) that starts an event by number and keeps a return value in dword_142FF9F4C, which SceneTransition_CheckTables later writes back to variable 39: an event replay / viewer path. In normal story play variable 508 is expected to be 0, so this branch is false.

notes: Event variable 508 is a flag bit: store + 556, bit 28 (I: the layout of the event-variable store).
open_questions: ? Whether any event opcode also writes variable 508 (only direct EventVar_Write callers were checked).

name: EventSlot_LoadTrack
callers: Music_StartSceneTracks, Scene_StartMusic, sub_1401D7DDC, sub_1401D9174, sub_1402C538C, sub_1402D50E4, sub_1402F2500, sub_14033FE00, sub_140345FE4 (also reached through the text-command slot pointer)
purpose: Loads a music track number into an event music slot when that slot is free.

behavior.text: returns 0 and changes nothing when qword_1418623F8[slot] is already set.
otherwise dword_142E7FB08[slot] = track, qword_1418623F8[slot] = the address of the shared record unk_14185A2E0, qword_1418623C0[slot] = 0, and it returns the slot.

notes: Slot count: the arrays are indexed 1 and 2 by every caller read; EventSlots_ResetAll clears both.
open_questions: ? what the shared record unk_14185A2E0 holds.

name: EventSlot_SetParam
purpose: Stores an event parameter record: -996, 100 * level / 127 and b into xmmword_140D3A910, and level into dword_1418623B8, when qword_1418623A8 is set.

behavior.text: when qword_1418623A8 is set it stores -996, 100 * level / 127 and b into xmmword_140D3A910 and level into dword_1418623B8.
part of the event's sound and parameter slots; EventControl_PausedTick calls it with 0 on a skip unless the EventId skip_no_reset byte is set (the test is in the caller).

open_questions: ? what the three stored values drive.

name: EventSlots_ResetAll
purpose: Resets the event's parameter slots and empties the event sound entry list.

behavior.text: calls sub_1402B1ED0 (resets xmmword_140D3A900 from xmmword_140723AE0 and clears qword_1418623A8, dword_1418623A0 and qword_1418623B0).
calls sub_1402B1E74(1) and sub_1402B1E74(2): clear slot n (qword_1418623C0[n], qword_1418623F8[n], dword_142E7FB08[n]; dword_142E7FB24 = -1 when it was n - 1).
calls sub_1401D9784 on the list at qword_143CD9DD8 + 1384, which calls EventSoundEntry_SetStateById for every entry of the list and empties it.
EventControl_PausedTick runs it on a skip unless the EventId skip_no_reset byte is set (the test is in the caller).

name: EventSoundEntry_Append
callers: EventScript_Run, at 0x14023E014 (opcode 0xA6, with the id read from operand bytes 1 to 4). Also sub_1401D964C (at 0x1401D975F, the cache branch of EventMusic_LoadTrack), sub_1400F4BCC (at 0x1400F4C3E), sub_1401BF8C4 (at 0x1401BF8F5), sub_1401C811C (at 0x1401C822C), and one data reference at 0x143D35BC0.
purpose: The body of opcode 0xA6: looks the id up in data table 280 and then, through a value in that row, in data table 279; when both rows are valid it creates a 56-byte sound resource that carries the id and appends it to the entry list of the sound object.

behavior.text: the table 280 handle is kept in qword_143CDA578. When that is null it is looked up once with sub_1403D325C(qword_143CD9CD0, 280). When neither can be obtained the routine does nothing.

row280 = sub_1403D3AE8(table 280, id). The routine goes on only when row280 is present and either its first qword is negative (then the static block unk_1406F5ED0 is used as its data) or its data pointer, from `sub_1403D2FD8`, is not null.

key279 = the dword at the data pointer of row280 plus 8. The table 279 handle is kept in qword_143CDA580 and is looked up the same way with id 279. row279 = sub_1403D3AE8(table 279, key279), with the same validity test.
the path pointer is the data pointer of row279 plus the dword at that data pointer plus 8. The second start value is the dword at the data pointer of row280 plus 12.

allocates 56 bytes with `sub_140011750` (heap at qword_140C696D0 + 32, alignment 8) and sets: the qword at +8 to 0, the qword at +16 to 0, the dword at +24 to 0, the dword at +28 to 0, the vtable to GameSoundResource_140713440, the dword at +32 to the id, the dwords at +44 and +48 to -1.0, and the word at +37 to 1.

calls `sub_1401D5EB0(resource, path pointer, 0, second start value)`. That helper sets the dword at +24 to 0 and the dword at +28 to the second start value, sets the byte at +36 to 0, and sets the handle at +8 through `sub_140091124` on the service qword_143CD9B88.

if the entry list's count is at its maximum it raises the length error 'list too long'. Otherwise it allocates a 24-byte node through the vtable of the allocator at obj + 272, sets node +16 to the resource, increments the count at obj + 288, and links the node at the tail of the list whose sentinel is obj + 280.
when either row is missing, nothing is allocated and the list is not changed.
the return value is whatever the last call left in rax; the caller does not use it.
the resource is the sound entry that later moves through states 0 to 4 in `sub_1401D5FA4` (not traced beyond its first branches).

notes: The list appended to here is the same list that `EventSoundEntry_SetStateById` (opcode 0xA7) scans and that EventMusic_LoadTrack also appends to.
open_questions: What `sub_140091124` and `sub_1401D5FA4` do in full. What the row fields mean: the key at table 280 +8, the second start value at +12, and the path offset at table 279 +8. What the static block unk_1406F5ED0 holds.

name: EventSoundEntry_SetStateById
callers: EventScript_Run, at 0x14023DFEF (opcode 0xA7, with the id read from operand bytes 1 to 4). Also sub_1400F4C54 (at 0x1400F4CC2), sub_1401BDB90 (at 0x1401BDBF2), sub_1401BF8C4 (at 0x1401BF8E7), sub_1401C01E4 (at 0x1401C0270), sub_1401C87A4 (at 0x1401C87D7), sub_1401D7F4C (at 0x1401D804D), sub_1401D9784 (at 0x1401D97B5), and data references at 0x143D35BCC.
callees: `sub_14009B550` (only for matches that hold a handle while the manager exists)
purpose: The body of opcode 0xA7: for every entry in the sound object's entry list whose id equals the operand, stops its resource if one is held, and sets the entry's state byte to 4.

behavior.text: walks the circular list whose sentinel is at obj + 280, from the sentinel's next node until it returns to the sentinel, following the qword at each node +0.
the resource of each node is the qword at node +16. It is a match when the dword at resource +32 equals the id; the comparison is a 32-bit compare.

for a match whose resource qword +16 is non-null, when the sound manager qword_143CD9B60 is also non-null, it calls `sub_14009B550(manager, resource + 16)` first and reloads the manager global afterwards.
for every match it sets the byte at resource +36 to 4.
there is no early exit; every entry is visited. Nothing changes when no entry matches.
the return value is whatever the last call left in rax; the caller does not use it.
state 4 is later acted on by `sub_1401D5FA4`, which releases the entry through `sub_1401D5F34` when byte +37 is non-zero (not traced here).

notes: Opcode 0xA7 and this routine match the record for 0xA7: the state byte is set to 4 for every matching entry.
open_questions: What `sub_14009B550` returns and does to the handle. Where byte +36 value 4 leads in `sub_1401D5FA4` for entries whose byte +37 is zero.

name: EventSoundGroup_Play
purpose: Plays the four sound effects of one event sound group.

behavior.text: calls sub_1402B20C0 first, then builds four ids from row (group - 1) of the sound group table (0x140681D00), each plus 0xE10000.
plays each id minus one through the novel sound player Sound_PlayNovelSe.

the argument is widened with a sign extension (movsxd) and there is no bound: the row address is table + 4 x group and each voice is the byte at -4 + voice from it, so group 0 reads the four bytes before the table and a group above 56 reads what follows it.

called with byte 9 of a class 44 command (EventCmd_SelectIndexedSet), with the command state's group word (sub_1402F109C, never above 255), and twice by EventCmd_ServiceRequests with the value of event variable 93 (a 32-bit cell).

notes: Read in full.
open_questions: ?: which stock scripts write event variable 93.

name: EventSprite_LoadTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x58
callees: GameData_ReadSectors, SceneTask_WaitFrame, SceneTask_Terminate, `sub_1402F3888` (allocate), `sub_1402F3A04` (free), the file helpers `sub_1403D2004`, `sub_1403D21F0`, `sub_1403D2358`, `sub_1403D21C8`
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x58: loads the sprite data for an event character into memory for one of two display sides, then ends.

behavior.text: reads two values from its task block: a side number (0 or 1) and a sprite id, which the interpreter stored there before the task ran.
allocates a 30,720-byte buffer and reads 15 sectors of data kind 44 for that sprite id with GameData_ReadSectors (start sector = 15 * sprite id).
for the sprite ids 35, 61, 96, 112 and 135 it also reads a texture file named `fftpack/spr/evtchr/evtchr_<id>.tex` into the buffer at offset 2432 (28,288 bytes).
when the global scale value `dword_142C81554` is at least 2.0 and `DWORD2(xmmword_142E7FC80)` is non-zero, it records the sprite id and a derived value for the chosen side in one of two global pairs.
stores the side in `dword_140D40818` and the buffer in `qword_140D40820`, waits one frame, frees the buffer and ends through SceneTask_Terminate.
the evtchr textures are the enhanced portraits or full-body art for those five characters.

notes: The opcode record for 0x58 (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What the two global pairs control and what the 15-sector data of kind 44 contains.

name: EventState_MoveTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x19
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x19: moves up to seven state-block values toward the operand targets over the operand step count, then writes the final values and ends.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 4 in `qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`, where index is `dword_140D40948`.

reads eight signed 16-bit words from the operand bytes at the task block pointer: words 0 to 6 are targets for state-block indices 26 to 32 (through the table `word_1406726B0`), and word 7 is the step count.
a target of 10000 leaves that value unchanged.
reads the global `dword_142FEC520`: bits 0-1 select a curve mode (1 uses one formula, other non-zero values another), bits 2-3 select a second mode, and bits 4-7 give a weight from 0 to 15.
when `dword_142FF8280` is non-zero it clears it, reads scene variable 30, and writes back that value or the value plus 4096, whichever is nearer to target word 4 (an angle unwrap).
reads the current values of the seven state entries; the first three are converted to 1/256 units by clearing their low 12 bits and dividing by 4.

for each step and each of the seven values it skips a value whose target is 10000, and skips the first three values too when `word_140D4090C` is non-zero; it also leaves a value alone when it is within 1536 units (6 in whole units) of its target for the first three, or within 96 units for the others.

otherwise it computes the new value by linear interpolation (`current + (target - current) * step / steps`, through `sub_140380310`) for mode 0, and by the curve formulas of the other modes, which use the weight and the step count.

each step clears bit 0 of state entry 32, then waits one frame with SceneTask_WaitFrame. The loop stops early when the high dword of `qword_142FF9E08` is non-zero and the high dword of `qword_142FF9E00` equals 3, which is the skip test the interpreter uses.

at the end, when `word_140D4090C` is zero, targets 0 to 2 are written to state indices 26 to 28 shifted left by 10; targets 3 to 6 are written to indices 29 to 32 unshifted; then bit 0 of index 32 is cleared, one frame is waited, and the task ends through SceneTask_Terminate.
the first three state values carry 10 fractional bits and the other four are whole values, which matches the shifts above.

`sub_140380310` and `sub_140380208` are signed (a * b) / c helpers, inferred from their 64-bit product and division loops; `sub_140380310` sets `dword_140D4093C` on some negative results (not fully traced).

notes: The opcode record for 0x19 (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What the seven state indices are in scene terms (camera, actor or screen), which curve each mode bit selects, and the exact formulas of the two curve modes.

name: EventStateTrack_RunTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x1D
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x1D: turns the 0x19 instructions of the block up to the next 0x1E into seven piecewise tracks, one per state value, and plays them frame by frame until the last track ends or the skip test fires.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 4 in `qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`, the same tag value as the 0x19 task.
allocates a 1148-byte block with `sub_1402202C8` and zeroes it with memset. The block holds seven tracks of 41 dwords (164 bytes each), one per state value.
walks the instruction stream from its operand pointer to the first 0x1E byte, counting the 0x19 instructions; the segment count is that count plus one, stored at dword 32 of each track.
sets `dword_142FEC53C` to the 4096-unit window base that contains the current angle (state index 30), searching windows from -16384 up to 12288.
segment 0 starts from the current state: each track's dword 1 is set to the current value, divided by 1024 for the first three values.

then it runs the block's instructions in order and records one segment per 0x19. For each of the seven values the target is the operand word, or for 10000 the running last-target value (divided by 1024 for the first three). Each segment stores a frame stamp equal to the previous stamp plus the 0x19 step count (operand word 7), and the target.
for the angle (index 4) the window base `dword_142FEC53C` is updated from the target.

opcode 0x1F is handled by `sub_1402404CC`: it resolves two unit ids; when either is missing it overwrites the opcode byte of the following 0x19 with 0xC0, which disables that instruction in the script bytes; otherwise it writes the next 0x19's three position targets from the two units' positions.
opcode 0x73 is handled by `sub_140240438`: the next 0x19's seven targets become its own seven operand words added to the running values, with 10000 kept as is.

opcode 0x38 is handled by `sub_14024075C`: it computes a frame count from the square root of a sum of squared differences, divided by its own signed 16-bit operand, and writes it to the following 0x19's frame count (operand bytes 15 and 16).
other opcodes in the block are skipped by their length with EventScript_InstructionLength.
each frame it evaluates the seven tracks with `sub_140235180` (indices 0 to 2 only when `word_140D4090C` is zero) and writes the results to the state entries 26 to 32.

when the skip test fires, it sets the track 3 done word (dword 163, which is the last dword of track 3) to 1 and ends after that update; when that word is already 1 it ends; otherwise it clears bit 0 of state entry 32 and waits one frame with SceneTask_WaitFrame.

`sub_140235180` returns the current value of one track in state units. Each call advances a frame counter; when the current segment is used up it moves to the next, and when it passes the last segment it sets the track done word (dword 40 of the track). Track 3's done word is the end condition of this task.
the task ends by freeing its block with `sub_1402203AC` and calling SceneTask_Terminate.

each segment uses three frame stamps and three values (at 4k, 4k+4, 4k+8 and 4k+1, 4k+5, 4k+9), so the tracks are piecewise quadratic through a middle value; this layout was read from `sub_140235180` and not fully traced.

notes: The opcode record for 0x1D (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: The exact field layout of a track segment and the curve used by `sub_140235180`, the angle values that `sub_1402404CC` writes when its mode byte is zero (two helpers not traced), and the meaning of `word_140D4090C`.

name: EventSubquestPanel_Run
callers: EventScript_Run, case 0xAC (call site 0x14023E1A4). No other code callers were found.
purpose: Shows a sub-quest UI panel that holds the opcode 0xAC operand, blocks until one of the input keys 0x15, 0x1A or 0x1B is active, then hides and releases the panel.

behavior.text: the argument is the 4-byte operand that EventScript_Run reads at instruction offset 1 before the call. The routine stores it in the new panel object at +80.

first it calls sub_1400EB5F4 with (show flag 0, a4 -1). That routine acts only when the virtual slot +16 of the object at [[qword_143CD9DA8+16]+112] returns nonzero, and then calls sub_14013C740 with flag 0, which calls sub_1401D1EAC on the panel at that object's +64 (close). So an older panel is closed before the new one is made.

allocates an 88-byte object (sub_140011750 with size 88), runs the base constructor sub_1401D1970 (base vtable, zeroes +16 to +40), then sets the vtable to the UIAddonFFTOSubquest table at 0x140710CF8 and zeroes +48, +56, +64, +72 and the dword at +80.

registers the object with sub_1401D16C4 on the manager at the pointer stored at [qword_143CD9DA8+16]+424. That routine stores the manager at +16, appends the object to the manager's list at +8, and gives it an id at +32 from the counter at qword_143CD9DA8+128 (the counter is set to 1 when it is -1) and inserts it into the map at the global's +48.

sets the object's +80 to the operand, then calls sub_1401D1A00 with 33. That looks up row 33 of table 24 with UITable_GetRow and, when the row exists, calls sub_1401D1A3C with the row's name-offset string (the internals of sub_1401D1A3C were not read).
stores the object at +64 of the manager (the manager is the object at +424 of the [qword_143CD9DA8+16] object).
sets the high dword of qword_142FF9E00 to 1 and calls sub_1401DB4E4 on the interface object at qword_143CD9FD0. Then it sets word +34 to 257, word +49 to 257 and byte +51 to 1 on that same object.

state 1 (the manager's state word at +72): if the panel at +64 has a GUI node at +48, it builds the key 'Show' with UIName_Key, finds that state with GUINode_FindState, and reads the state's running byte at +105. The state moves to 2 when there is no panel, no node, no Show state, or the running byte is 0. Otherwise it stays in state 1 and waits one frame with SceneTask_WaitFrame.

state 2: waits one frame at a time. When sub_1400FC598 reports the key 0x1A, 0x15 or 0x1B (each checked with the device argument 0), it checks the manager's virtual slot +16. If that is nonzero and the panel at +64 is set, it removes the panel with sub_1401D183C and clears +64. The state then becomes 3.

state 3: builds the key 'Hide' and finds the state on the panel's node. While that state's running byte is nonzero it waits a frame. When the byte is zero, or the node or state is missing, it sets the state to 0, waits one frame, then clears +49 and +51 and sets +34 to 256 on the interface object at qword_143CD9FD0, and returns.
the loop runs the whole time. The routine returns only after state 3 ends, so the interpreter is blocked for the full Show, input and Hide sequence.

sub_1400FC598 with device 0 returns nonzero when sub_1400F0D00 finds a nonzero state byte in the key's 48-byte record (the bytes checked are at record offsets 1362 and 1378). The meaning of the key codes 0x15, 0x1A and 0x1B was not confirmed.

notes: The panel's sub-routines are the second level: sub_1401D1A3C (addon setup), sub_1401D183C (removal, which calls the object's slot +40 when the flags at +44 and +45 are zero) and sub_1401D1F7C (a state-dispatch helper) were only partly read, so they have no sheets here.
open_questions: What sets the manager's state word at +72 to 1 before the loop (the loop exits at once when it is 0). What sub_1401D1A3C builds from row 33 of table 24. The virtual slot +40 of the panel class and what it does. The meaning of the key codes 0x15, 0x1A and 0x1B.

name: EventSubScript_RunTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x2A
callees: SceneVar_Write, SceneTask_WaitFrame, SceneTask_Terminate, SceneTask_Start, EventScript_InstructionLength, EventRef_ResolveSlot, `sub_1402355E0`, `sub_140240B8C`, `sub_140242A08`, `sub_1402356B0`, `sub_14023577C`, `sub_14023565C`, `sub_140241DF8`, `sub_140240F34`, `sub_140240D5C`, `sub_140240144`, `sub_140242140`, `sub_140240C9C`, `sub_1402F7C20`, SceneObject_FindBySlot, `sub_140269074`, `sub_140260AEC`, SceneUnit_SetFlag156, ScenePreview_ClaimForUnit, EventUnitMove_Task, EventObject_MoveTask
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x2A: runs the instructions after 0x2A up to 0x2B as a parallel script, dispatching each opcode to unit, scene-variable and wait helpers, and ends when the block ends or the skip test fires.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 8 in `qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`.

walks the instructions from its operand pointer until opcode 0x2B, or until the skip test (the high dword of `qword_142FF9E08` non-zero and the high dword of `qword_142FF9E00` equal to 3) fires; the next instruction is found with EventScript_InstructionLength.
opcode 0x21 sets `dword_140782CAC` to its operand word when there is no skip and the current value is not 166 or the operand is -1.
opcode 0x43 writes scene variable 83 as 1 when its operand byte is 9, or as 0 when it is 10; other values do nothing.
opcode 0x72 waits one frame, then sets `word_140D408E4` to 1.
opcode 0x28 sets `qword_140D40940` to `sub_1402355E0` and calls it on its operand; in a task slot other than 0 it clears two entries of the task pointer table first.

unit opcodes resolve their unit id through EventRef_ResolveSlot, and do nothing when it returns 2000. Opcode 0x79 stores its operand word at instruction byte 3 into `xmmword_142FEC620` at the unit's index. Opcode 0x29 calls `sub_14023577C`, which waits frames until the unit's byte at record offset 168 is zero. Opcode 0x68 calls `sub_14023565C`, which sets the unit byte at record offset 341 to 2 when the operand byte is 1, otherwise to 0. Opcode 0x97 calls `sub_140269074` on the unit record when it exists. Opcode 0x71 calls `sub_140260AEC`. Opcode 0x46 calls SceneUnit_SetFlag156 and, when `dword_1418112B8` is 2, also appends an entry to the table at `dword_1418112C0`. Opcode 0x44 calls ScenePreview_ClaimForUnit. Opcode 0x12 resolves the id only. Opcode 0x32 calls `sub_1402F7C20` with the unit index and the operand bytes at instruction offsets 3, 7, 4, 5 and 6.
opcode 0xF1 waits the number of frames given by its two operand bytes as a 16-bit value, one SceneTask_WaitFrame per frame.

opcode 0x7E calls `sub_140242A08`, which waits until `SceneVar_Read` of the operand variable is at least the operand value; it ends early when `word_141874530` or `word_142FEC554` is set, or when `dword_142E7FB3C` and the high dword of `qword_142FF9E08` are both set.
opcode 0x5F calls `sub_140240B8C`, 0x2D calls `sub_140240F34`, 0x53 calls `sub_140240D5C` with flag 1, 0x8C calls `sub_140240C9C`, and 0x11 calls `sub_140241DF8`, each with the operand pointer.
opcode 0x6F calls `sub_140240144`, which waits frames while a task with tag 11 for that unit is still running.
opcode 0x64 calls `sub_140242140` with its signed byte operand; opcode 0x65 calls it with -1, which waits frames.

opcode 0x3B (or 0x6E) searches the slots after this one, up to 16, for one whose qword 18 is zero, starts EventUnitMove_Task (for 0x3B) or EventObject_MoveTask (for 0x6E) in it with SceneTask_Start, and stores the operand pointer in `unk_140D40AA0` at that slot, tag 11 in `qword_140D40B38` at that slot, and the resolved unit id in `unk_140D40B40` at that slot. When no slot is free it calls SceneTask_Terminate and uses slot 0 (not traced further).
the task ends through SceneTask_Terminate when the block or the skip test ends its loop.
this is the same kind of interpreter as the main script loop, restricted to the opcodes listed here; the other opcodes in the block are skipped.

notes: The opcode record for 0x2A (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: Names for EventRef_ResolveSlot (unit id lookup) and SceneObject_FindBySlot (unit record lookup), the meaning of `dword_140782CAC` and of the table at `dword_1418112C0`, what the free-slot fallback to SceneTask_Terminate ends, and the helpers `sub_140240B8C`, `sub_140240F34`, `sub_140240D5C`, `sub_140241DF8` and `sub_1402F7C20`, which were not traced.

name: EventTable226_FindRecord
proto: uint64_t *EventTable226_FindRecord(uint64_t *out, uint32_t key, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
purpose: Looks up one record of table 226 by key and stores the record pointer in the output slot.

behavior.text: sets the output slot *out to 0 first.

uses the cached table pointer qword_143CDA820. When that is zero it gets table 226 from the root qword_143CD9CD0 with sub_1403D325C (root, 226) and caches it. If the table is still missing, nothing else happens.
when the table exists, it stores in *out the result of sub_1403D3AE8 (table, key, arg3, arg4). That is the generic row fetch, and the two extra arguments are passed through.
returns the output pointer.
EventScript_Run sets only the key (edx) before the call (the third operand from opcode 0xC4). The register values for arg3 and arg4 were not set in the disassembly, so their values are unresolved.

open_questions: What arg3 and arg4 hold at the 0xC4 call site, and what sub_1403D3AE8 does with them when the table is in its mode 1 or other modes.

name: EventTask_Start
callers: About 70 callers, including EventCmd_StartMessage and several of the task procedures.
purpose: Starts a task in the first task table: resets the slot's block, marks it runnable and records its entry function. The twin of SceneTask_Start.

behavior.text: sets `dword_140811624` to 1 (SceneTask_Start sets it to 0), then fills the slot's 2048-byte block in `off_14078D5D8`: the entry function at +136, the runnable flag at +144 set to 1, and the fields at +24, +112 to +128, +152 and +160 to +208 zeroed.

writes the entry function to the thread record's target field (+8) in the 288-byte record table at `unk_143791D70`, and sets the flags at +272, +280 and +284 to 1 (the second-table starter leaves +284 alone).
about 70 callers across the event, world-map and battle code.

notes: See SceneTask_Start for the second table; the two differ in the table written, the global flag value and the extra thread flag.
open_questions: What `dword_140811624` and the flag at +284 control.

name: EventTask_Terminate
callers: About 80 callers, mostly event and script-VM handlers.
purpose: Ends the current event task. It is also the VM's error trap: a divide by zero or an out-of-range variable id calls it.

behavior.text: clears the qwords at +144 and +152 of the current task's block, marking it no longer runnable.
advances the current-task index to the next block whose +144 qword is non-zero, up to 16, wrapping to 0.
calls EventPad_UpdateRepeat, restores the original index, then calls EventThread_ReturnToEntry, which does not return to the caller's code path.
called from about 80 places, including EventVar_Alu (divide by zero) and EventVar_ResolveSlot (id 1024 or more).
the effect is that the task that hit the error stops and its thread restarts from its saved entry point.

notes: Named for its observable effect; the task block fields are only partly decoded.
open_questions: Whether a task can be restarted later, and what clears the task table entry for a new task.

name: EventTask_WaitFrame
callers: About 70 callers across the event, world-map and battle code.
purpose: The event system's wait-one-frame primitive: moves on to the next runnable task, refreshes the held-button repeat state, then yields. About 70 routines call it to wait.

behavior.text: increments the current-task index `dword_14184B22C`, then scans forward through the task blocks (2048 bytes each, base `off_14078D5D8`) for the next one whose qword at +144 is non-zero, up to index 17, wrapping to 0.
calls EventPad_UpdateRepeat, then returns EventThread_Yield(0).
used in wait loops such as `sub_1402E9980`, which spins on this call until a request flag clears.
the non-zero qword at +144 marks a task as runnable.

notes: EventTask_Terminate uses the same scan with a bound of 16.
open_questions: The layout of the 2048-byte task block beyond the fields at +144 and +152.

name: EventTasks_Init
purpose: Initialises the first task group: points its task table, variable store and event buffer at their storage.

behavior.text: picks a per-language table from the language-info field at +8 (`unk_1408DE240` for 0, `unk_1408E0DA0` for 3, `unk_1408E2350` for 2 and `unk_1408DF7F0` otherwise) and stores it in `qword_14184B230`.
sets the first task table `off_14078D5D8` to `unk_14184B3C0`, the event buffer pointer `qword_141853BC0` to `unk_140D3CD50`, and the event variable store `off_14078DCE8` to `unk_140D40060`.
also sets `qword_141853BD0` and `qword_14184B220` to fixed blocks and clears `word_14184B288` and `word_14184B360`.
the per-language table is the phase-record bank selected for the game language.

notes:
SceneTasks_Init points the second task group at the same event buffer and variable store, which is why both groups see the same variables.

- V: 0x1402EA368 is a label inside this function (a branch target, not an entry; an earlier sheet named it `EventScene_SetBuffers`). What that path does:
  - V: it stores the fixed pointer 0x140D3CD50 in the global at 0x141853BC0; that address is the event-script file buffer.
  - V: it stores the fixed pointer 0x140D40060 in the global at 0x14078DCE8, the pointer the event work block is reached through.
  - V: it writes the 16-bit argument to the words at 0x14184B288 and 0x14184B360.
  - V: the event id arrives in r8w (the third integer argument), not rcx or rdx.
  - V: the body is 45 bytes with two pointer stores, two word stores and no call or branch.
  - V: it has no direct caller in the image; the scene setup reaches it through a stored pointer or an inlined copy.
  - I: the two buffers are the script image and the event work area, because the first is the buffer the script loader fills and the second is the pointer the event tasks read.
  - I: the two words are the current event id and its mirror, because the same id is written to both.
  - ?: what the second buffer at 0x140D40060 holds; its size and owner are not established.
open_questions: What the language values 0 to 3 stand for.

name: EventText_FindMessage
purpose: Finds an event message in memory from its packed 16-bit reference and returns a pointer to the start of its text.

behavior.text: the top 5 bits of the reference (`ref >> 11`) pick a text bank from a 32-entry table of bank pointers at `qword_14184A8A0`.
bank 14 is fetched through `sub_140332B48` (with the context argument); a reference whose top bits are 0xB000 (bank 22) first calls `sub_1402BACCC(9)` and then uses the pointer in `qword_14375F938`.

the low 11 bits are the message index within the bank: the routine walks the bank byte by byte and counts bytes whose value, ignoring the lowest bit, is 0xFE (so 0xFE and 0xFF), stopping when the count equals the index.
returns the position after that many terminators, which is the first byte of the requested message.
0xFE and 0xFF are the end-of-message markers; the two special banks are loaded or built on demand.

notes: Pairs with EventText_NextChar: this finds where a message starts, that routine steps through it.
open_questions: What `sub_140332B48` and `sub_1402BACCC` load for banks 14 and 22.

name: EventText_NextChar
purpose: Advances through an event message byte stream by one position, following the stream's back-reference codes.

behavior.text: returns null when `pos` is null; otherwise moves one byte forward.
`*runLeft` counts the bytes left in a back-reference run; when it reaches 0 the position is restored from `*returnTo`, which is then set to -1.

when the byte at the new position has the high nibble 0xF and a low nibble below 4 (codes F0 to F3) it is a back-reference: `*returnTo` is set to the position three bytes on, `*runLeft` to `(b1 >> 5) + 8 * (b0 & 3) + 4`, and the position moves backwards by `b2 + 254 * (b1 & 0xF)`.
this is an LZ-style compression of the message text: a short reference copies an earlier run of text.

notes: Only the position bookkeeping is here; the character codes themselves are handled by the caller.
open_questions: The meaning of the control bytes above 0xF3 and how the text length is bounded.

name: EventThread_ReturnToEntry
purpose: Restarts the calling event task thread from its saved entry context.

behavior.text: finds the calling thread in the 17-entry thread table (`qword_143CD9E98`).
for any entry above 0 it clears a dword at +272 and a qword at +8 of the task's 288-byte record at `unk_143791D70` and long-jumps to that record's saved jump buffer with code 1.
if the thread is not in the table, or is entry 0 (the scheduler), it returns without jumping.

notes: Together with EventThread_Yield this is how a task is stopped and restarted without destroying its thread.

name: EventThread_Yield
callers: About 31 callers, including EventTask_WaitFrame and many world-map, battle and event routines.
purpose: Hands control from the calling event task back to the scheduler and sleeps until that task is resumed. Each event task runs on its own OS thread, and this is the baton hand-off.

behavior.text: finds the calling thread in a 17-entry thread table (`qword_143CD9E98`, 96 bytes per entry, thread id at +24); index -1 if it is not listed.
stores `(mode != 1) - 2` in `dword_1408115F4` (so -2 for mode 1, otherwise -1), signals the scheduler's event handle (table +1640), then blocks forever on the thread's own event handle (entry +48).

once resumed it clears `dword_142FF9DE8` and `dword_142FF9DD8`, calls the optional hook `qword_14114B738`, and records its own index in `dword_140D40948` and in the current-task index `dword_14184B22C`.

it then checks the task's 288-byte record in the table at `unk_143791D70`: when the pending-target field (+0) is non-null and differs from the field at +8 it long-jumps through the task's saved jump buffer with code 1; when the flag at +280 is set and both fields are non-null it long-jumps with code 2.
SceneTask_Start writes the entry function into the record (+8) and sets the flags at +272 and +280, which is how a freshly started task is steered to its entry point through the code-2 jump.
code 1 restarts a task whose recorded target differs from its requested entry; code 2 starts a newly created task.

notes: The scheduler side is the main loop thread (entry 0 of the thread table); tasks are entries 1-16.
open_questions: Which scheduler routine wakes the next task.

name: EventUnitBlock_RunTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x49
callees: SceneVar_Read, SceneTask_WaitFrame, SceneTask_Terminate, EventScript_InstructionLength, `sub_1402334FC`, `sub_1402FB7C8`, `sub_140300D74`, `sub_140300768`, ScenePreview_FindEntry, ScenePreview_SlotOfIndex, `sub_140241128`, ScenePreview_ShowEntry, ScenePreview_ClaimForUnit, `sub_14027294C`
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x49: runs the instructions after 0x49 up to 0x4A once, handling the unit opcodes 0x45 and 0x82 and skipping the rest, then ends.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 14 in `qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`.
starts at its operand pointer (the instruction after 0x49) and walks the instructions by length with EventScript_InstructionLength until it reaches opcode 0x4A.
runs once with no frame wait of its own; the only waits are inside the handlers below.
opcode 0x82: when `SceneVar_Read(508)` is zero it sets `word_140D408F4` to 2, calls `sub_1402334FC(13)`, waits one frame, then calls `sub_1402FB7C8`, `sub_140300D74` and `sub_140300768`.

opcode 0x45: reads a 16-bit unit id from instruction bytes 1 and 2 and a flag byte from byte 3. It resolves the id with ScenePreview_FindEntry; when that result is -2 or negative it searches the 21-entry preview unit table (512-byte entries from `g_BattleUnitTable`) for the record and ends the task if it is not there. Otherwise it calls ScenePreview_SlotOfIndex, then ScenePreview_ShowEntry or ScenePreview_ClaimForUnit (depending on the flag byte) and `sub_140241128`, and may start `sub_14027294C` in a task slot as opcode 0x28 does. It then waits frames while `word_140D407D0` is non-zero.
`sub_1402334FC` waits while `dword_140D408B8` or `dword_140D408BC` is set, and calls SceneTask_Terminate when `word_140D408F8` is 1.
the task ends through SceneTask_Terminate after the block.
the flag byte of opcode 0x45 selects between two outcomes whose full logic was not traced.

notes: The opcode record for 0x49 (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: The full logic of opcode 0x45 and its flag byte, what the preview unit table and ScenePreview_FindEntry return, and the meaning of `word_140D407D0` and `word_140D408F4`.

name: EventUnitMove_Task
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x3B; also started by EventSubScript_RunTask (EventSubScript_RunTask) for opcode 0x3B inside its block
callees: EventObject_MoveWorker (the shared worker), EventRef_ResolveSlot, SceneObject_FindBySlot, `sub_140273908`, `sub_140272F04`, `sub_140273838`, `sub_140380310`, SceneTask_WaitFrame, SceneTask_Terminate
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x3B: moves a unit's three-value vector from its current value to three operand targets over the operand step count, then ends. It shares its worker with the 0x6E variant.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with the value 11 in `qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`, then calls EventObject_MoveWorker with flag 0 on its operand pointer and ends through SceneTask_Terminate.
the 0x6E variant (EventObject_MoveTask, a separate function) calls the same worker with flag 1.
the worker resolves the unit id from operand bytes 0 and 1 with EventRef_ResolveSlot; when it does not resolve it does nothing. Otherwise it stores the unit index in `unk_140D40B40` for this slot.
reads the unit's three-value vector from the unit record at offset 108 (three 16-bit values) as the start values.
reads the three targets from operand bytes 2 to 7, the mode byte from byte 8, the weight byte from byte 9, and the step count as a 16-bit value from bytes 10 and 11.
with flag 1 it replaces the step count: the square root of the summed squared differences (each difference times 16) divided by the operand step count.
scales the start values and targets by 256 (8.8 fixed point).

for each step from 1 to steps minus 1 it waits one frame, calls `sub_140273908` on the unit, and computes each component by the mode byte: mode 0 is linear (start + (target - start) * step / steps); modes 1 to 3 use the weight and other curve formulas; any other mode leaves that component unchanged.
it applies each step's change to the unit with `sub_140272F04`, first the negated previous offset and then the new value, and then calls `sub_140273838`.
it ends early when the unit record is gone (SceneObject_FindBySlot returns 0) during the steps.
at the end it applies the final targets the same way, clears the byte at unit record offset 139, waits one frame if the step count was 1, and ends through SceneTask_Terminate.

notes: The opcode record for 0x3B (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What the unit vector at record offset 108 is in scene terms (position or rotation), what the weight means in curve modes 1 to 3, and what `sub_140273908` and `sub_140273838` do.

name: EventUnitObject_ApplyId
proto: void EventUnitObject_ApplyId(void *obj, uint32_t id, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
purpose: Looks up a 4-byte id in table 87 and applies the matching text to the UI sub-object of the object at [[qword_143CD9DA8+16]+104], closing its panel first.

behavior.text: the object is [[qword_143CD9DA8+16]+104] as passed by EventScript_Run. The id is the dword read at instruction offset 1.
does nothing unless the object's +80 pointer (the sub-object) is non-null.
uses the cached table pointer qword_143CDA440. When it is zero it gets table 87 from the root qword_143CD9CD0 with sub_1403D325C (root, 87) and caches it.
when id is nonzero, it fetches the row with sub_1403D3AE8 (table 87, id, arg3, arg4). arg3 and arg4 come from EventScript_Run locals and were not resolved.
when the row exists, and the sub-object's +24 pointer is non-null with byte +74 nonzero and its +48 non-null, it calls sub_1401D1EAC on the sub-object (close the panel) first.
reads the row's 16-bit type code at data +8. Type 115 and type 113 are handled. Other codes do nothing.

type 115: reads the dword at data +12 and looks it up in table 86 (cached in qword_143CDA460, root key 86). When that row exists, it calls sub_14013AE64 on the sub-object with the string at (the row's data + its dword at +8) + 8.

type 113: reads the dword at data +12 and looks it up in table 85 (cached in qword_143CDA318, root key 85) to get row A. String A is row A's data + its dword at +12 + 12. It then reads the dword at row A's +8 and looks it up in table 85 to get row B. String B is row B's data + its dword at +12 + 12, or the default string Str1 when row B is missing. When row A exists, it calls sub_14013AEE0 on the sub-object with string A and string B.

the bodies of sub_14013AE64 and sub_14013AEE0 were only partly read. sub_14013AE64 sets byte +144 of the sub-object's +56 to 1 when the sub-object's +48 is non-null. The text effect of both is not confirmed.

notes: The two table-85 and table-86 lookups use the same row-field conventions as table 87, and the text offsets sit at different fields (+8 and +12) for the two type codes.
open_questions: What sub_14013AE64 and sub_14013AEE0 do with the strings (the text setter used). What arg3 and arg4 are at the 0xE7 call site. Which codes the 115 and 113 type words stand for (the code shows only the numbers).

name: EventUnitStatus_ApplyTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0x92.
callees: EventRef_ResolveSlot, ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot, EventUnitStatus_RunMembers, EventUnitStatus_SetBit, EventUnitStatus_RefreshNode, sub_140272964, sub_14021F414, SceneTask_WaitFrame, SceneTask_Terminate
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0x92: resolves a unit id, applies a mode-dependent update to the unit's preview row and status bits, runs the unit-end callback, waits the given frames, then ends.

behavior.text: tags its slot with 67 in qword_140D40B38 at the slot's index.
reads the operand through the pointer at +0 of its block: bytes 0 and 1 form the unit id (unsigned 16-bit), byte 2 is the mode, and bytes 3 and 4 form a signed 16-bit frame count.

resolves the id with EventRef_ResolveSlot, then takes the preview index of the slot with ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot; when the slot is 2000 or the index is -1 the index is 2000. The task ends with SceneTask_Terminate only when the second resolve of the id returns 2000.
calls EventUnitStatus_RunMembers with the id and 0 before the mode branch.

when the index is 0 to 20, the row is unk_141853D10 plus 512 times the index. When the index is above 20 (including 2000), the code uses the small values 48, 97 and 99 as row addresses, which are invalid (the decompile shows this; not confirmed by a run).
the state is 0 when bit 5 of the row byte at +0x31 is set; otherwise it is 2 minus bit 0 of the row byte at +0x33.

modes 1, 2 and 3 are switched on first. Mode 1: EventUnitStatus_SetBit with bits 5 (flag 0), 16 (flag 0) and 6 (flag 1); the per-unit byte at qword_142FF8268 plus the index plus 945 is set to 2; then the callback EventUnitStatus_RefreshNode runs with the slot.
mode 2: EventUnitStatus_SetBit with bit 31 (flag 1); the per-unit byte is set to 3; EventUnitStatus_RefreshNode runs with the slot; then sub_14021F414 runs with the slot and 22.
mode 3: EventUnitStatus_SetBit with bit 8 (flag 1); the per-unit byte is set to 4; EventUnitStatus_RefreshNode runs with the slot.

mode 4 and above: sets the word at +0 of the row to 0, calls EventUnitStatus_SetBit with bit 5 and flag 1, sets dword_140782CAC to 65 unless it is 166, and runs EventUnitStatus_RefreshNode with the slot.

modes 0 and other values (no switch case) use the state: state 2 runs sub_140272964 with the slot; state 1 does nothing; state 0 sets the per-unit byte to 1, calls EventUnitStatus_SetBit with bit 5 (flag 0) and bit 16 (flag 1), runs EventUnitStatus_RefreshNode with the slot, and sets dword_140782CAC to 65 unless it is 166.
a callback run here is stored in qword_140D40940; for task slot 0 it runs at once, for other slots the qwords at +96 and +104 of block 0 are cleared first.
after the branch, when the frame count is 1 or more, waits that many frames with SceneTask_WaitFrame; then ends with SceneTask_Terminate.

notes: The opcode record for 0x92 (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What sub_14021F414 and sub_140272964 do; what the per-unit byte at qword_142FF8268 plus 945 drives; what the row bits 5, 16, 6, 8 and 31 mean; the invalid row addresses for indexes above 20.

name: EventUnitStatus_DispatchActiveIcons
purpose: For one preview unit of an event scene, sends the status icon updater a message for every status the unit currently has.

behavior.text: points the scene callback slot (g_TextCommandSlot) at BattleUnit_SetStatusVisual, the status icon updater.
reads the effective set (unit +97) of the preview unit at slot (the 21-row table at 0x141853CE0) and loops over the ids 0..39 (a fixed bound of 40).
for each id whose bit is set it calls SceneCallback_Dispatch with kind 3, argument id + 1, the given mode, the slot and 0.
a slot above 20 makes the set pointer the bare offset 97 (a null-based read); the one caller (EventScript_Run) is expected to pass a valid slot.

notes: Name is ours. The unit row is reached through the address 0x141853D41 (the unit table at 0x141853CE0 plus 0x61), so the table address itself is not an operand. The mode is passed through to the icon updater (the status icon update takes on / off).
open_questions: ? the event opcode that calls it and the meaning of its mode values.

name: EventUnitStatus_RefreshNode
callers: EventUnitBlock_RunTask (call at 0x140235EA4); EventScript_Run (call at 0x14023C629); sub_14024138C (call at 0x140241697); EventUnitStatus_RunMembers (call at 0x1402417CD); EventUnitStatus_ApplyTask (calls at 0x1402419F6, 0x140241A65 and 0x140241B29). It is also stored as the callback at 0x140235E91, 0x14023C615, 0x14023C83B, 0x14023CAAF, 0x140241673, 0x1402417B8, 0x1402419DF, 0x140241A4F and 0x140241B16.
purpose: The unit-end callback installed by the 0x92 status paths: finds the unit node for a slot and passes it to sub_1401FAF54, which refreshes that unit's flag words and state.

behavior.text: calls SceneObject_FindBySlot with the slot and passes the node (or null) to sub_1401FAF54 with a tail jump. sub_1401FAF54 does nothing when the node is null.
sub_1401FAF54 sets the dword at node +348 to the dword at +356 OR-ed with the dword at +348 cleared of the bits in the dword at +364; the dword at +352 is set the same way from +360 and +368.
calls sub_140268F68 on the node. Then sets bit 0 of the word at node +24 when bit 0x10 of the byte at +352 is set, and clears it otherwise.

sets the byte at +880 to 1 when dword_142FF9F24 is zero and either the dword at +348 AND 0x1FFFC2C4 is not zero or the byte at +8 equals dword_140CF873C; otherwise 0. When +880 is 1 the word at +884 is set to 0.

calls sub_14026947C with the node, 0 and a flag that is 1 when dword_140CDB824 is zero; then sub_14026A048, sub_140269BBC and sub_140269DC4 with the node, sub_14026A1DC with the node and 0, and sub_1402694E4 (none of these traced).
then clears the qword at +356 and the qword at +364, and sets the byte at +864 to 0.

notes: When the callback is called through the task-slot path, the slot is passed as the argument; the direct calls pass the same slot.
open_questions: What the flag words at node +348 and +352 and the masks 0x1FFFC2C4 and 0x40 mean; what sub_140268F68, sub_14026947C, sub_14026A048, sub_140269BBC, sub_140269DC4, sub_14026A1DC and sub_1402694E4 do.

name: EventUnitStatus_RunMembers
callers: EventUnitStatus_ApplyTask (call at 0x140241949); EventScript_Run (calls at 0x14023A9EA and 0x14023EC94, opcodes not identified here).
callees: SceneGroup_ResolveId, SceneUnit_TestGroupMember, ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot, ScenePreview_FindEntry, `sub_14024138C`, `sub_140241128`, EventUnitStatus_RefreshNode, `sub_140273270`, SceneTask_WaitFrame
purpose: For each unit the reference selects, refreshes its per-unit block from its preview row and runs the unit-end callback for it, then waits 0, 40 or 80 frames; when flag is zero it finishes with the group-end callback sub_140273270.

behavior.text: sets qword_142FF8268 to qword_14184A9B0 plus 2040, the per-unit block base. Returns at once when word_140D408E8 is not zero.
calls SceneGroup_ResolveId on ref. When that returns 0 (no unit) the routine does nothing more.
clears the word at +1008 of the per-unit block.

loops over keys 0 to 20 with SceneUnit_TestGroupMember. For each member the slot is the resolved id; ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot gives its preview index, and when that index is not -1 the byte at +401 of the row for that index is passed to ScenePreview_FindEntry. For an index above 20 the code reads address 401 (not confirmed).

when the status from ScenePreview_FindEntry is 0 or more: if flag is not zero, calls sub_14024138C with the index and the slot. If flag is zero and sub_140241128 with the index returns non-zero, sets the callback to EventUnitStatus_RefreshNode (EventUnitStatus_RefreshNode) and calls it with the slot (directly for task slot 0, or after clearing the qwords at +96 and +104 of block 0 otherwise).
stops the key loop after the first member when the group mode is 0 (one unit).
when the word at +1008 is not zero, waits 40 frames with SceneTask_WaitFrame. When bit 0 of the low byte of +1008 is set, waits 40 more frames.

when flag is zero, sets the callback to sub_140273270 and calls it with 0 (same slot rule). That routine walks the unit list from qword_140D3A410 and calls SceneUnit_SetFlag156 with the key byte of each node whose byte at +0x160 has bit 0x40.
returns the value its last call left; nothing is set on purpose.

notes: For the 0x92 task the reference is a single unit, so the group loop runs once with mode 0 and the callback runs once.
open_questions: What bits 0 and 1 of the word at +1008 mean and which flag bytes of the per-unit block set them (sub_140241128 sets them; its bytes are not named); what sub_14024138C does; why bit 0 adds a second 40-frame wait; what the 0x9x callers pass as flag.

name: EventUnitStatus_SaveAndHide
purpose: For an event scene, saves the status state of a unit into the event unit store and clears the statuses the scene must not show.

behavior.text: returns 0 at once when the store marks the slot as done (store byte +924 + slot); otherwise copies +0x57, +0x1EF and +0x61 (five bytes each; the applied set is addressed as an offset from the store, 5 * (99 - slot)), the 16 countdown bytes, the charge counter +0x18D, the KO counter +0x07, the HP word +0x30 and +5 into the store (qword_142FF8268).

the pending remove +0x1E0 becomes +0x61 & a five-byte mask: byte_1406720EC when SceneVar 509 is 0, else byte_1406720B8 for some units (+0x12, the marker, the job) and byte_1406720F4 for the others; the same bytes go into two store areas; two flag bits of the store word +1008 follow.

when the remove holds Charmed (byte 4 bit 0x20) +5 takes +0x1EE; then sub_14030CFB8 removes the pending set from +0x61 and +0x57 (not +0x1EF), through the scene callback slot when dword_140D40948 is set; marks the slot done and returns 1.
sub_14024138C is the restore: it writes +0x57, +0x1EF, +0x61 and the countdowns back from the store.

notes: Name is ours. The removal here works on +0x61 and +0x57 and never on +0x1EF; the restore puts +0x61 back whole.
open_questions: ? what the three masks hold per scene kind.

name: EventUnitStatus_SetBit
proto: int64_t EventUnitStatus_SetBit(int64_t ref, int bit, int flag)
callers: EventUnitStatus_ApplyTask (eight call sites, 0x1402419BB to 0x140241B0B). A data reference at 0x143D384B8 was not traced.
callees: EventRef_ResolveSlot, ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot, SceneCallback_Dispatch (sub_14030C87C is set as the callback and not called here)
purpose: For one unit reference, clears two 5-byte bitmaps in the unit's preview row, sets one bit in one of them, and sends mode 2 of the scene callback dispatch for that row.

behavior.text: resolves ref with EventRef_ResolveSlot, passing the bit number as the flag argument (that routine does not use it). Returns with no change when the result is 2000.
takes ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot of the slot. Returns with no change when the index is -1 or 2000.

for an index from 0 to 20 the row is g_BattleUnitTable plus 512 times the index. For an index from 21 to 255 the row pointer is set to null, and the stores below then go through that null pointer (not confirmed by a run).
clears the five bytes at row +475 to +479 and the five bytes at row +480 to +484.

sets bit number bit in a bitmap: byte (bit divided by 8) of the first bitmap at row +475 when flag is not zero, or of the second bitmap at row +480 when flag is zero. The bit value is 1 shifted by (bit modulo 8).
sets the callback qword_140D40940 to sub_14030C87C and returns the result of SceneCallback_Dispatch with mode 2, the index, argument 1 and two zeros.

notes: The bitmaps are read by the mode 2 callback sub_14030C87C, which was not traced.
open_questions: What the two 5-byte bitmaps at row +475 and +480 mean and what the callback does with them; what the null row pointer does for indexes 21 to 255 (the code writes through it).

name: EventVar_Alu
proto: uint32_t EventVar_Alu(int op, int dst, int src)
callees: EventVar_ResolveSlot, EventVar_Read (for the write lock), EventTask_Terminate (error trap)
purpose: The event variable arithmetic unit: applies one operation to the destination variable using either a literal or another variable as the operand, and stores the result back into the packed store.

behavior.text: op parity chooses the operand. Even ops use `src` as a literal; odd ops read variable `src`. Variable 33 is a random source: a 16-bit linear congruential generator, `seed = seed * 25173 + 13849`, returned as an unsigned 16-bit value.
op meaning by range: up to 177 add; 178-179 subtract; 180-181 multiply; 182-183 divide; 184-185 modulo; 186-187 AND; 188-189 OR; 190 clears the destination (no operand).
a divide by zero calls the error trap EventTask_Terminate; so does any variable id of 1024 or more.

the current value of `dst` is read through EventVar_ResolveSlot, which also tells the width: dword, single bit or nibble. Bit and nibble variables are extracted before the arithmetic and merged back after it, masked to 1 or 15.
a re-entrancy flag, `byte_142FEC547`, skips the write checks when set.

write lock: a destination of 960 or above is stored only if its current value is below 12. In every case the store then happens only when variable 508 (0x1FC) reads 0, or the destination is in 0-43, 112-143 or 508-511, or is one of a fixed set within 48-102.
after a dword store, the low dword of `xmmword_14078D9C0` is refreshed; when the destination was variable 25 it takes the new value.
the lock mode is a protection that freezes most story variables, for example during a replay or a preview.

notes: The operation numbers 176-190 are the event system's own arithmetic opcodes (0xB0-0xBE in event scripts); the two accessors above use only 176, 177 and 190. The event interpreter uses the second-group twin, SceneVar_Alu, directly. The caller-saved scratch is variable 0.

name: EventVar_Read
callers: About 86 callers, e.g. the world-map event chooser `sub_1402D3120`, `sub_14033EC0C` and many battle and event routines.
purpose: Reads one event variable by index. The event system keeps story flags and counters in one packed variable space; this is the shared read accessor, called from about 86 places across the battle, world-map and event code.

behavior.text: saves variable 0 (the first dword of the variable store `off_14078DCE8`), because variable 0 is used as the scratch cell for the read.
for index 34 it first recomputes that variable from variables 35 and 36: `(var35 & 7) << 12` plus bit 0 of var36 shifted to bit 15, stored back with EventVar_Write.
runs two ALU steps through EventVar_Alu: op 190 clears variable 0, then op 177 adds the variable `index` into variable 0, so variable 0 now holds the value.
returns the value of variable 0, then restores variable 0 to its saved value, so the read leaves no trace.
index 34 behaves as a derived status word (an unnamed packed field built from variables 35 and 36).

notes: Variable ids are 0-1023 and map to three storage classes, documented on EventVar_ResolveSlot: full dwords (0-127), single bits (128-863) and 4-bit nibbles (864-1023). The old research called the read accessor `read_eventflag`; this function matches that role, but not the old address.
open_questions: What variable 34 and the 0x1FC lock variable mean to the game.

name: EventVar_ResolveSlot
purpose: Maps an event variable index to the address of the dword in the store that holds it.

behavior.text: indices 0-127 are whole dwords at `store + 4 * index`.
indices 128-863 are single bits: dword `(index - 128) / 32` of a region at `store + 512`; the bit is `index & 31`.
indices 864-1023 are 4-bit nibbles: dword `(index - 864) / 8` of a region at `store + 604`; the nibble is `index & 7`.
an index of 1024 or more calls the error trap EventTask_Terminate and returns null.
the store pointer is `off_14078DCE8`; the three regions total 604 + 80 = 684 bytes.

notes: Only the address is returned; EventVar_Alu works out the bit or nibble shift and mask from the index itself.

name: EventVar_Write
callers: About 47 callers across the battle, world-map and event code.
purpose: Writes one event variable by index. The shared write accessor for the packed variable space, called from about 47 places.
