behavior.text: a negative value is reduced to its low byte (`(uint8_t)value`); a non-negative value is used as is.
variable 44 is capped at 99,999,999 before the write.
saves variable 0, then runs EventVar_Alu twice: op 190 clears the target variable, then op 176 adds the literal value, which stores it. Variable 0 is then restored.
because variable 0 is the scratch cell and is restored at the end, writing index 0 has no lasting effect.

variable 44 is the party's gil (live 2026-11-04: it read 3,200 while the owner had 3,200 gil; `EventVar_Write(44, 99999)` made the shop show 99,999 and the purchases were paid from it). The variables are dwords at the pointer `*0x14078DCE8` (variable n at +4n).

notes: The store itself is subject to the write lock inside EventVar_Alu: while variable 508 is non-zero only a whitelist of variables can change.
open_questions: Which shop function writes variable 44 on a purchase (not needed for the meaning, which is confirmed live).

name: EventViewer_BuildList
purpose: Builds the list of replayable story events: for each of 78 positions, one event variable decides whether the entry is listed.

behavior.text: walks positions 0..77; positions 14, 16, 28, 33, 47, 61..66, 75, 76 and 77 read event variable 427 + n (n counts the special ones), every other position reads 444 + k (k counts the plain ones: 64 of them, variables 444..507).

an entry is listed when its variable is nonzero and EventViewer_IsHidden is false; the list item is a 16-bit text reference: 0xE800 + k for a plain entry, 0xE840 + n for a special one (bank 29 message index 0..63 and 64..77).

stores the item in the shared list array (0x140D498F0, 128 words) and a zero in the parallel array (0x140D497D0), with a range check at a byte offset of 0x100; then sets up the list widget (sub_140379F3C(10, n), sub_140379DF0) and pushes the page kind 29.
each store comes before its range check (the byte offset is compared with 0x100 after the write); the loop lists at most 78 entries, so the check never fires in this builder.

after the loop the count goes to the page record (dword at 0x140D8D8F0 + 0x5C x depth, the depth at 0x140D8DBA0) and to the widget, which shows at most 8 rows at once (the count capped at 8 for the visible window).

notes: The special positions are a chain of compares with constants; the table of event numbers has 78 words in the order plain 0..63 then special 64..77. The references 0xE800 and 0xE840 are results of the 16-bit subtraction of 0x19BC (6588) and 0x196B (6507) from the variable number, not constants in the code.

name: EventViewer_EntryPage
callees: EventVar_Read, Input_TestAction, EventVar_Write, EventChain_Find, sub_1402CD714, sub_1401D80A8, sub_14033FDAC, sub_14037A3F0, EventViewer_BuildList, sub_14037A168
purpose: The page of one replayable story event (page kind 30): shows the entry's text and, on the confirm, replays the event; on cancel it rebuilds the list.

behavior.text: dispatches on the page state at +0xC: state 1 counts frames at +0x10, state 2 (after 20 frames) sets a text reference of 0x8800 plus the entry index (+0) and opens it with sub_14037A168, state 3 returns to the list when the window is done.

on the confirm input (Input_TestAction with 0x10 / 0x1E) it writes event variable 508 = 1, then event variable 39 = the word of tbl_EventViewerList at the entry index (a zero-extended 16-bit read, twice), stores (EventChain_Find(event) != -1) in g_EventViewerChained, sets a flag bit and starts the scene change (sub_1402CD714(7, 0)).
row 67 of the table holds 0xFFFF: the confirm then writes 65535 to variable 39 and the chain lookup misses (seen in an emulation of the page's code on the pristine image).
on cancel it clears the page's highlight bits and calls EventViewer_BuildList to show the list again.
the reference 0x8800 + index is a message of text bank 17 by the same reference format (5-bit bank, 11-bit index) as the list's bank 29.

notes: The entry index comes from EventViewer_OpenEntry (the message index of the list item). 0x8800 is built by an `add` of the index; 65535 is the table word of row 67, not a constant in the code.
open_questions: Which scene the start with variable 39 = 65535 would load (no retail script sets variable 430, so the row is never listed in the retail game).

name: EventViewer_IsHidden
purpose: Says whether an unlock variable of the story event list is hidden: such entries are never listed.

behavior.text: true for variables 427, 428, 429, 431, 432, 434, 435, 436, 437, 438 and 439; false for all others (so of the 14 special entries only 430, 433 and 440 can be listed).

open_questions: Why these entries exist but are never listed.

name: EventViewer_ListInput
callers: the page dispatcher sub_140246078 (table at 0x140681400, kind 29)
purpose: Input handler of the story event list (page kind 29): confirms an entry, cancels, or scrolls.

behavior.text: on the confirm it takes the list item at the cursor (a signed 16-bit cursor), masks it with 0x7FF and opens the entry's page (EventViewer_OpenEntry); on cancel it clears the state and returns to the tavern top.

name: EventViewer_OpenEntry
purpose: Opens the page of one story event list entry: stores the entry index and sets the entry's text.

behavior.text: pushes page kind 30 with the entry index as its argument and sets the page text id to the index + 59392 (0xE800, bank 29).

name: EventViewer_StartReplay
purpose: Starts the replay of an event from the Chronicle.

behavior.text: EventVar_Write(508, 1), EventVar_Write(39, event), EventChain_Find(event) into g_EventViewerChained; sets the skip flags.
copies the user situation bytes 97..99 to 177..179; sets bit 0 of g_UserSituation +16 (the bank bit: replays use the second counter bank); dword_141D32EE4 = event.

open_questions: ? what the user situation bytes 97..99 / 177..179 are.

name: EventVoice_PlayTask
callers: Started as a task entry by EventScript_Run for opcode 0xC2; EventScript_Run starts it only when `dword_1407D453C` is 1
purpose: The task started by event opcode 0xC2 when the enhanced flag is set: starts a table entry for its id, keeps it in the list while it is present, and stops it when the object or the skip test says so.

behavior.text: tags its task slot with 72 (0x48) in `qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`.
reads the dword at +8 of its task block as the entry id (`ebx`); the opcode handler stores the operand there.
`sub_1401E8A9C(qword_143CD9DD0)` returns the dword at object+96, or 0 when `qword_140C69690` is set and its byte at +55 is 1, or is 2 while object+96 is 2.
when that value is 0, or the dword at object+88 is 0, and the list pointer p (`qword_143CD9DB8 + 40`) and p+32 are both non-null, it calls `sub_1401DA210(p, id)` to start the entry.

`sub_1401DA210` finds row `id` with `sub_1403D4534` in the table at p+24. When that row has a non-empty string at its offset and the id is not yet in the tree at p+56, it inserts the entry with `sub_1401DAB54`, creates an object through `sub_140091124` stored at entry+48, and sets the entry's byte at +64 to 1.

loop: while p and p+32 are set and `sub_1401DA4B8(p, id)` returns true (the id is present in the tree at p+56), each pass tests the object again: if sub_1401E8A9C is non-zero and object+88 is non-zero, or the skip test holds (dword +4 of `qword_142FF9E08` non-zero and dword +4 of `qword_142FF9E00` equal to 3), it calls `sub_1401DA410(p, id)` when p+32 is set and ends.
otherwise it calls SceneTask_WaitFrame and repeats the loop.

`sub_1401DA410(p, id)` finds the entry; if its +64 byte is 1 it sets it to 2, releases its +56 object through `sub_14009B550` when `qword_143CD9B60` and the field are set, calls `sub_1401D9EE8` on the field at +40, and removes the entry with `sub_1401DAAB4`.
ends through SceneTask_Terminate.

notes: The opcode record for 0xC2 (data/opcodes.jsonl) points here through `starts_task`.
open_questions: What the table at `qword_143CD9DB8 + 40` holds and what its entries are (the PanzerVoice vtable name in the IDB suggests voice lines, which is not confirmed), what `qword_143CD9B60` and `sub_140091124` create, and what the object at `qword_143CD9DD0` is.

name: FieldSchema_LoadFromNode

purpose: The load half of the field-schema walker: for each descriptor of a schema it looks a node up by name and decodes it into the record.

name: FieldSchema_Run
proto: void FieldSchema_Run(SchemaCtx *ctx, Node *node, uint8_t *record, const FieldDesc *fields, uint32_t count)
callers: About 54 schema functions, one per saved record (see SaveFile_Serialize, SaveWorld_Serialize, SaveUnit_Serialize and SaveJobNew_Serialize).
callees: Seven scalar helpers (`sub_1400B09B0`, `sub_1400B0A90`, `sub_1400B0B70`, `sub_1400B0C50`, `sub_1400B0D30`, `sub_1400B0E10`, `sub_1400B0EFC`), the node builders `sub_1405A483C`, `sub_1405A4690`, `sub_1405A6014`, the logger `sub_140026BD4`
purpose: The generic walker behind the game's save and config records: it takes a table of field descriptors and turns one in-memory record into a tree of named value nodes (or, for the other direction, fills a record from such a tree). About 54 schema functions call it, one per record type.

behavior.text: `ctx+8` selects the direction. 0 builds the tree from the record (this routine); 1 hands over to `sub_1400B059C` for the reverse; any other value returns at once.
a null node, record, field table or a zero count logs error 0x96090001 and stops.

each descriptor is 88 bytes: a name pointer at +0, a type code at +8, the field's offset in the record at +12, an element size (16-bit) at +16 and an element count (16-bit) at +18, plus callback slots at +24/+32 and a lookup callback at +56/+64.
for every descriptor it creates a child node named after the descriptor, fills it by type, then appends it to the parent.

types 1-5 read a scalar from the record and store it in a child named `v`: 1 is an unsigned byte, 2 a signed byte, 3 a signed 16-bit value, 4 a 32-bit value, 5 a 64-bit value. A count above 1 repeats this as `var` children.

type 0 calls the descriptor's own callback with the record address at the field's offset, so a field can be a nested record; with a count above 1 it builds that many `var` children, advancing by the element size.

type 6 and 7 write a value-only child without reading the record; type 8 passes the record's own bytes as the node value; type 9 maps the stored value through a lookup table (pairs of text and value) returned by the descriptor's callback.
errors: 0x96090000 node creation failed, 0x96090005 empty lookup table or no match and no default, 0x96090006 unknown type code. All are reported through the logger `sub_140026BD4`.
the element named `v` suggests an XML-like or JSON-like tree; type 6 and 7 are probably flag or constant nodes.

notes:
This is the engine's reflection layer for save data: adding a field to a record means adding a descriptor to its schema function.

- Correction: the load direction (`ctx+8 == 1`) calls FieldSchema_LoadFromNode per descriptor; an absent node is skipped (error recorded, field untouched) and the return value is discarded. J9: the manual save `fftsave.bin` does not use this tree (it is a flat memory image).
open_questions: What tree format the nodes produce and where the tree is written; what types 6 and 7 write.

name: Formula_02_WeaponCastsSpell
purpose: Weapon attack that can cast a spell: the whole weapon attack, and on the 19 percent status roll the weapon's inflict byte becomes the ability resolved next instead of a status.

behavior.text: sub_140306C90 first (the physical evade gate); a miss ends the handler.
then Formula_PhysAttackFull, the whole stock weapon attack (weapon stat, bonus, modifiers, critical, damage, element affinity).

when that returns 0 (the hit stands and Formula_StatusChance19's 19 percent roll succeeded) it does not apply the status: it writes the inflict byte (g_FormulaBlock +0x0D, the weapon record's byte +7) to the request word at 0x1407B0768 and 1 to the word after it; Battle_ResolveAction takes the next ability id from that word when the flag word is non-zero (see g_FormulaBlock), so the weapon's byte names a follow-up ability.

it copies the byte at 0x1407B0761 to 0x1407B0792, and when the flag byte at 0x1407B0790 (g_FormulaBlock +0x20) has its sign bit set it clears the byte and ANDs result word +18 with 0xBFFF (bit 0x4000, the knockback request), as Formula_ZeroResult does.
so a weapon with formula 2 casts the ability its inflict byte names on about one hit in five; the stock users are rods, a flail, a bow, a spear and a sword.

calculation:
```text
Hit: physical evade (sub_140306C90)
Damage: as formula 1 (weapon type A and B, + weapon bonus, modifiers, critical, A x B, element)
On the 19 % roll: follow-up ability = weapon record byte +7
```
notes: Read whole in IDA 2026-11-18 (current build).

```text
A = WP + weapon bonus (g_FormulaBlock +0x17)
B = WP
Damage = A x B after Formula_PhysMods and Formula_CritRoll
(no evade roll in this handler; status from inflict row 0)
```

name: Formula_04_MagicGun
callees: Battle_Rand15, AbilityAction_GetRecord, Mem_CopyChecked, Formula_ElemBoostWeapon, Formula_CasterMagMods, Formula_TargetPassiveMag, Formula_TargetStatusMag, Formula_Zodiac, Formula_DamageAB, Formula_SceneVarElemMod, Formula_EarthFloatAndAffinity, Formula_FaithScale, Formula_FinalizeAbsorb
purpose: Magic gun: picks one of three spells of the weapon's element by a random roll and deals its damage as (WP + bonus) x the spell's Y through the magic chain.

behavior.text: the roll is Battle_Rand15 scaled to 0..99; under 10 picks the third ability of the set, 10..39 the second, 40 and above the first.
the set comes from the weapon element byte 0x1407B07AE: the sign bit (tested with jns) gives 16..18, bit 0x40 gives 20..22, anything else 24..26.
the chosen id is written to g_FormulaBlock +8 and to caster +0x1A2, and its 20-byte action record (AbilityAction_GetRecord) is copied over the block's ability record copy with Mem_CopyChecked.
B = the copied record's Y (the byte at 0x1407B079E, block +0x2E); A = the weapon power byte 0x1407B07AC plus the weapon bonus (the low byte of the word at 0x1407B0787, block +0x17).

then Formula_ElemBoostWeapon, Formula_CasterMagMods, Formula_TargetPassiveMag, Formula_TargetStatusMag, Formula_Zodiac, Formula_DamageAB, Formula_SceneVarElemMod and Formula_EarthFloatAndAffinity; when the hit flag still stands, Formula_FaithScale and Formula_FinalizeAbsorb.
abilities 16..18, 20..22 and 24..26 are the three-tier fire, lightning and ice spells; the stock users are three guns, one per element.

calculation:
```text
roll 0..99: < 10 -> third tier, < 40 -> second tier, else first tier
element byte bit 0x80 -> abilities 16 / 17 / 18; bit 0x40 -> 20 / 21 / 22; otherwise 24 / 25 / 26
A = WP + weapon bonus, B = the chosen spell's Y
Damage = A x B with element boost, caster and target magic modifiers, zodiac, weather, faith
```

name: Formula_56_StatusOnlyApplication
purpose: Status-only application: the shared status engine used by many formulas; no damage component.

behavior.text: Current-build decompilation confirms the chain and arithmetic shown above.

Typical abilities: Salve, Petrify, Shadowbind, Bad Breath, Grand Cross (22 total).

reads the inflict record copy (g_FormulaBlock +0x40, flag byte then five status bytes) and writes the add set R+29..33 and the remove set R+34..38 (Status_FilterPendingSets' names for them); it is the status step of 16 handlers directly.

flag bit 0x20 first divides R+44 by 4; flag bit 0x80 (or bit 0x40 / 0x20 while g_BattleSimulating is non-zero) copies the five status bytes into R+29..33; bit 0x40 picks one listed status at random (Battle_Rand15); bit 0x20 drops each listed status when Rng_Percent(100, 24) is true (kept on a 24 percent roll; a preview at level 2 drops all) and adds the rest; bit 0x10 copies the five bytes into the remove set R+34..38 instead (V for the offsets; the sheet text above calls it a secondary add table).
at the end, when any status bit is set and Status_FilterPendingSets(0) is non-zero: R+39 |= 0x08, and R+18 |= 0x40 only when R+30 has bit 0x40; otherwise R+0 = 0, R+2 = 7, R+44 = 0 (no effect).
the damage formulas reach it through Formula_StatusTailKeepHit, which restores R+0, R+2 and R+44 afterwards.

calculation:
```text
status engine with 4 modes:
 bit 0x80: add statuses directly from ability data
 bit 0x40: random status from target's current statuses
 bit 0x20: remove matching statuses (faith roll)
 bit 0x10: add from secondary status table
No damage component — status only
```

purpose: HP restore item: heals 10 x the item's amount byte (an Undead target takes it as damage). No hit roll.

it ends with a tail call to Formula_HealSwap, which turns the amount into an HP heal, or leaves it as damage when the target is Undead.
no hit roll in the body.
the stock users are the three HP potions; the amount byte is stored in tens (an amount of 3 heals 30).

calculation:
```text

then Formula_HealSwap (heal; Undead: damage)
```

name: Formula_75_ItemRevive
callers: Formula dispatcher (`Formula_106_ReDispatchChainFormula`); reached as slot 75 of the formula registry through Battle_ResolveAction
purpose: Revive item: on a target being revived, heals a random 1 to the item's amount byte; on an Undead target, damage equal to its current HP.

behavior.text: it calls Formula_RevivePrecheck first and returns without writing anything when that returns 0 (no status pending and the target is not Undead).
when the target (g_BattleActingUnit) has bit `0x10` at +0x61 (Undead) it copies the target's current HP (+0x30) into the result's HP word (+6) and skips the item value.

otherwise it rebuilds the item id from the chemist slot byte at `0x1407B077E` by adding `0xF0`, calls Item_GetChemistRecord, reads the row's byte +1 (the amount), multiplies a Battle_Rand15 value by it, shifts the product down by fifteen bits and adds one: a random 1..amount.
it ends by calling Formula_HealSwap: a heal on a living target, damage on an Undead one.
so the item revives with a random HP from 1 to its amount (not scaled by ten, unlike formulas 72 and 73), and destroys an Undead target outright.
the stock user is the one revive item.

calculation:
```text
Formula_RevivePrecheck must pass (a status is pending, or the target is Undead)
Undead target: amount = target current HP (damage, through Formula_HealSwap)
otherwise:     amount = 1 + random(0 .. amount byte - 1)   (chemist record byte +1)
then Formula_HealSwap
```

name: Formula_EvadeRoll
purpose: The shared evade step of the physical and magic gates: scales the shown hit percent by the four evade bytes and rolls each of them.

behavior.text: runs only when the ability word (g_FormulaBlock +8) is 0 or bit 0x02 of the ability record copy's flag byte (0x1407B079A, record +6) is set; otherwise it returns at once.

the baseline is the byte at g_FormulaBlock +7 and the four evade bytes sit at 0x1407B0781..0x1407B0784 (block +0x11..+0x14), set by the gate that called. When any evade byte is >= the baseline it stores R+0 = 0 and R+44 = 0 (a sure evade, nothing rolled by chance).
otherwise R+44 = R+44 * (the product of the four percentages 100 * (baseline - evade) / baseline, divided by 10^6) / 100, so the preview percent falls by each evade.
then it calls Formula_EvadeByteRoll for the four bytes in order with reasons 1, 2, 3, 4 and stops at the first roll that fails the hit (the helper stores R+0 = 0 and R+2 = reason).
the four bytes are class / accessory / shield / shield evade (the two gates fill them from different record bytes); the names come from the gates' reads, not from a label.

notes: Block B03 (2026-11-12): 441 bytes, read whole. Contract for a data formula: needs the baseline byte, the four evade bytes and R+44; writes R+0, R+2 and R+44. Crosscheck: the evade bytes 0x1407B0781..0x1407B0784 (block +0x11..+0x14) are read as the dword at 0x1407B0781 and its byte parts, RIP-relative operands.

name: GameTasks_RunFrameSteps

purpose: Runs the game's task threads for one displayed frame: the whole per-frame step is repeated GlobalWork_GetSpeedMultiplier times, which is how fast-forward speeds the game up.

behavior.text: reads the multiplier once, then loops step = 0 .. multiplier - 1; each step stores the step number in GlobalWork +92, resets the per-frame draw lists, calls CharaRenderer_Update and resumes the task threads in order until one reports the end of the frame.

when the multiplier is above 1 it sets three 'do not draw' bytes (in the sprite renderer and two of its sub-objects) to 1 on every step but the last and to 0 on the last, so only the last step of a frame is drawn.
after the loop GlobalWork +92 is 0.

every task that waits by frames (event scripts, battle animation, walking, effects, message timers) therefore advances 3 or 5 times per displayed frame; nothing is skipped, the steps are simply run more often.

notes: EventControl_Update runs only while GlobalWork +92 is 0, so the event overlay and the hold logic tick once per displayed frame, on the first step.

name: GaussianKernel_Build
callers: UIBlur_BlurPassOrCopy, UIBlur_BlurPassSingle, UIBlur_DrawPass, UIBlur_DrawTexturedPass, UIBlur_Pass, UIBlur_TapCount, sub_1403ACEBC (V: 7 xrefs)
purpose: Builds the normalised one-sided 64-entry Gaussian weight table for the UI blur and returns the tap count.

behavior.text: returns 0 if |sigma| <= 1.1920929e-7 (FLT_EPSILON).
w[i] = expf(i*i * (-0.5/sigma^2)) for i in 0..63 into a 336-byte stack buffer; sum = w[0] + 2*sum(w[1..63]) (centre once, mirror taps twice). Returns 0 if |sum| <= FLT_EPSILON.

tap count: scan i from 0 while cutoff <= w[i]/sum; first i with cutoff > w[i]/sum is the returned count (taps = i, i.e. weights >= cutoff are kept; if none drops below, count stays 0 (v6 = 0) after 64 iterations).

second normalising sum s2 = sum over i < the scan stop of w[i]*(1 if i==0 else 2); returns 0 if |s2| <= FLT_EPSILON. Then all 64 floats (16 x __m128 divides) are divided by s2 and stored to out64 (so the table is normalised over the kept taps only, not the full 64).
x and y of the blur use the same table; UIBlur_DrawPass uploads it as 2 x 128 bytes into cGaussianBlurPS.

notes: Edge case worth knowing: if every weight stays >= cutoff the returned tap count is 0 (the V reading of the code: v6 only assigned on break), while the normalised table is still written. A zero count is treated by callers (UIBlur_Pass) as 'no blur: copy'.

callers: vtable slot +48 of 16 component classes (GUICore_SetCursorTarget and sub_1403D6F70 call virtual +48 on the old cursor target)
purpose: Component virtual +48: the GUI cursor target moved away; plays CursorOut unless the component keeps its cursor look while focused, and posts event 13.

behavior.text: (focusWidget, focusNode) = GUICore_GetFocus(g_GUICore). When there is no focus, or the focused node is not this component, or byte comp+569 is 0: GUINode_PlayCursorOutState(comp). So a focused component with +569 set keeps its CursorOver look.
always posts event {13} to the owners (comp+584, source comp).

name: GUIComponent_Disable

purpose: Mirror of GUIComponent_Enable: clears +554, plays the Disable state (Enable stopped) and posts event 11.

behavior.text: same recursion over the widget's reference nodes with GUIComponent_Disable(child, 1).
when comp+554 != 0: comp+554 = 0; StopState(comp, 'Enable' +4632); FindState(comp, 'Disable' +4648) +104 = 1, PlayState; event {11}.

name: GUIComponent_Enable
callers: about 22 UI addon methods (sub_1400EA5B8, sub_1401027D8, sub_14012C8AC, sub_14012FC6C, sub_14013F634, sub_14014129C, sub_140153CA0, ...)
purpose: Marks a component enabled (+554 = 1) and plays its Enable state (Disable stopped); optionally enables the components its reference nodes point at.

behavior.text: when recurse != 0: for every node of the widget's node vector (widget = comp+496; vector +160..+168) with kind (node+52) 12 and owner id (node+48) equal to this component's id (comp+8): the referenced component is found with GUIWidget_FindComponentCached(widget, node+208, node+224, node+304) and GUIComponent_Enable(child, 1) runs on it.

an already enabled component does nothing in the second part (the recursion still runs).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140408EBC). Byte +554 is the flag GUICore_UpdateFrame tests before delivering press / click (V); the separate +416 byte of other sheets is 'loaded'. The widget's node vector holds the reference nodes (kind 12) of nested components.

name: GUIComponent_GetFlag556
callers: 16 vtables (0x140721F48, 0x140721FC0, ..., entries of the UIAddon component classes)
purpose: Trivial virtual accessor: returns byte c+556.
