name: GUIComponent_Init
purpose: Initializes a component from its definition; copies the component object id (+8) into the layer node (+0x140).

behavior.text: contains a store at 0x1404089E3 that copies the dword at +8 of the object (loaded into a register a few instructions earlier) into the dword at +0x140 of the same object - the write that gave the component root its object id (caught by hardware watch).

notes: Object ids are unique runtime ids: stock tree components got ids 4754..4934 (step 10), the extra got 4964. They are NOT sprite part ids.

name: GUIComponent_LoadDef
callees: GUIComponent_LoadProps, sub_1403F5910, sub_1403F0654, sub_140402EDC, sub_140409684, sub_1403D8870, UIAnim_PlayStateTracks
purpose: Builds a runtime component from its UIB component record (0x40 bytes): property block, node tree, states.

behavior.text: GUIComponent_LoadProps(ld, rec, w, comp) first.

nodes: rec[5] entries of the node table at rec + rec[4]; entry k = int at table + 4k, the node at table + entry; each is built by sub_1403F5910 (-> GUINode_LoadTree) and linked into comp+272 in order.

states: rec[7] records of 0x60 bytes at rec + rec[6]; a record of type 3 (timeline, +8) gets a state object found by its name (sub_140409684): frame count (+36) -> state+88, loop byte (+40) -> state+108, its names, then UIAnim_PlayStateTracks.
every offset is a signed int added to the record's address, so a record may point backward.

notes: The name is ours. The state records hold the arrow states Lock / Unlock / LockOnCursor / UnlockOnCursor that JobTree_SetArrowState plays; two components may share one state table (they target their layer by name).
open_questions: What the record's last pointer (+36, an 8-byte block) holds (?).

name: GUIComponent_LoadProps
proto: char GUIComponent_LoadProps(__int64 a1, int *file, __int64 a3, GUIComponent *comp)
purpose: Reads a component's property block from the UIB file into the runtime component: the enable byte and values of every effect group (colour transform, offsets, single float, drop shadow, glow, opacity, clip, mask).

behavior.text: the property block v5 = the component record in the file plus the dword stored at record+12 (file + file[3]). Every 'props' offset below is a byte offset into that block; every 'comp' offset is a runtime offset in the component.

colour transform group (enable comp+60): comp+28 / +32 / +36 <- props dwords 7 / 8 / 9 divided by 100.0, comp+40 <- 1.0f, comp+44 / +48 / +52 <- props bytes 21 / 22 / 23 divided by 255.0, comp+56 <- 0.
offsets group (enable comp+88): comp+64..+84 <- props dwords 11..16 (six floats copied raw). Single-float group (enable comp+96): comp+92 <- props dword 18.

drop-shadow group (enable comp+120 <- props byte 76): comp+100 <- props float 20 (offset 80, blur radius), comp+104 <- props dword 21 (offset 84, strength), comp+108 <- props dword 22 (offset 88, offset x), comp+112 <- props dword 23 (offset 92, offset y), comp+116 <- colour: word at props 96 and byte at props 98 in the low three bytes, the top (alpha) byte forced to 0xFF.

glow group (enable comp+172 <- props byte 100): comp+156 <- props dword 27 (offset 108), comp+160 <- props dword 28 (offset 112), comp+164 <- colour: word at props 116 and byte at props 118, alpha byte forced to 0xFF (only bytes 116..118 are read), comp+168 <- mode from props dword 26 (offset 104): 0 -> 0, 1 -> 1, 2 -> 2, any other value leaves comp+168 unchanged.

comp+186 (enable <- props byte 176) group: comp+184 <- props byte 180, comp+185 <- props byte 184, comp+176 <- props float 47 (offset 188) * 0.01, comp+180 <- props dword 48 (offset 192). Opacity-like group: comp+192 (enable <- props byte 196), comp+188 <- props dword 50 (offset 200).

behavior.basis: (file data, ffto_job_tree.uib, UnitSelect component props at file 0x844)
behavior.text: byte 100 = 1 is the only effect enable set; dword 27 = 6.0, dword 28 = 0.8, colour bytes = (255, 239, 179).

the drop-shadow group is the one the later stages forward as the +177 layer group (ComponentEffects_Collect: comp+120 -> context +136; GUILayer_BuildRecord: -> record+153 = layer+177); the glow group is forwarded as +178 (context +156 -> record+154 = layer+178). The field meanings (radius, strength, offset, colour) are read from the consumers, not from names in the file.

notes: Both colours (shadow comp+116, glow comp+164) are read as three bytes with the alpha byte forced to 0xFF. Copy sibling: sub_1403DF454 (proposed name GUIComponentProps_Copy) copies the same fields from one component to another.
open_questions: ? which shipped UIB components set the shadow enable (props byte 76) and with which values; only the Job Tree UnitSelect glow was read from file data. ? the clip margins comp+196..+211 are copied from a local filled earlier in the function and were not traced. ? what modes 1 and 2 of comp+168 do (the glow consumer takes mode 3 for the Job Tree).

name: GUIComponent_OnClick
callers: vtable slot +72 (GUICore_UpdateFrame calls it as virtual +72)
purpose: Component virtual +72: a completed click; plays the Click state and posts event 16.

behavior.text: state = GUINode_FindState(comp, key +4760 = 'Click'); when it exists +104 = 1 and PlayState; event {16} to the owners.
GUICore_UpdateFrame calls it when comp+554 (enabled) is set, no re-target happened this frame and the release edge byte (a1+1902 or a1+1904, chosen by the press mode a1+2064) is set.
JobTree_OnEvent case 0x10 (= 16) sets addon+12242, so a click on a panel marks it held; the addon base handler plays the click sound (a1+612) on event 16.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040A444); 11 of the component vtables hold this entry (16 hold the Down / Up / cursor-leave entries), the rest override it.

name: GUIComponent_OnDown
purpose: Component virtual +56: the confirm button / mouse button went down on the component; sets the pressed flag, plays the Down state and posts event 14.

behavior.text: comp+555 = 1; GUINode_StopState(comp, key +4728 = 'Up'); state = FindState(comp, key +4744 = 'Down'), +104 = 1, PlayState; event {14} to the owners.

GUICore_UpdateFrame calls virtual +56 on the pressed component (v29) when its +554 (enabled) is set (and, when +570 is set, only if it is the cursor target); otherwise it calls virtual +80 (the disabled-click response, not read).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040A324); Down / Up / Click is the naming of the three state keys. Event 14 was listed only as '14..17' in the owner event notes.
open_questions: ? exactly which raw input (mouse left, confirm key) drives the press edge (GUICore_UpdateFrame reads cursor-state bytes +1903 / +1905).

name: GUIComponent_OnFocusGained
purpose: Component virtual +96: plays the component's FocusIn state (if the UIB has one; UnitJob has none, so nothing plays there) and posts event 19 to its owners.

behavior.text: only when comp +416 (enabled) is set; stops the FocusOut state (UI name key at qword_143CDA2A0+4680; V: static name list at 0x1406F6100 index 6), plays the FocusIn state (+4664, index 5), then GUIOwners_PostEvent with the event template {19}.

notes: JobTree_OnEvent case 0x13 -> JobTree_OnCursorEnter; this is where that event originates.

name: GUIComponent_OnFocusLost
purpose: Component virtual +104: plays FocusOut and posts event 20 (JobTree_OnCursorLeave).

behavior.text: stops FocusIn (+4664), plays FocusOut (+4680), GUIOwners_PostEvent {20}. (The CursorOver / CursorOut states at +4696 / +4712 are played by the cursor enter / leave virtuals and by GUINode_SetCursorOverState; V: the UnitJob UIB has no FocusIn / FocusOut state, its hover look is CursorOver.)

name: GUIComponent_OnUp
callers: vtable slot +64 (GUICore_UpdateFrame calls it as virtual +64)
purpose: Component virtual +64: the press ended; clears the pressed flag, plays the Up state and posts event 15.

behavior.text: comp+555 = 0; StopState(comp, key +4744 = 'Down'); FindState(comp, key +4728 = 'Up'), +104 = 1, PlayState; event {15} to the owners.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040A3B4). Inverse of GUIComponent_OnDown.

name: GUIComponent_ResetEffects
purpose: Resets a component to defaults: clears the effect enable bytes and frees its child list.

behavior.text: zeroes blend (+16), the enable bytes +60, +88, +96, +120, +172, +186, +192, +216, +244, +265 and word +268; sets +20 to 1.0f (opacity), +520 = 1920 and +524 = 1080 (design size).

name: GUIComponent_SetAllocatedSize
callers: GUIComponent_UpdateNodeTree, sub_14012F138, sub_1402A4DB4, sub_14040BBF0 and two vtable entries
purpose: Stores the size taken from a reference node (ref+64 / +68) as the component's allocated size comp+528 / +532, swapped for the rotated layout mode, and resizes the component root when it asks for it.

behavior.text: (w, h) = ints at ref+64 / ref+68. When comp+536 = 7 and comp+664 = 0 the pair is swapped (w <-> h); otherwise unchanged.
when comp+540 = 2: GUINode_SetSize(comp+272, w, h) (sub_1403EF6B4). Always comp+528 = w, comp+532 = h.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F2EF8). 13862 hits per 4 s. This is the 'allocated rectangle' that the text board and the alignment code (GUITextBoardComponent_Update) read.
open_questions: ? Meaning of comp+536 = 7 (I: a rotated/portrait layout kind) and comp+540 = 2 (I: 'fit root to reference').

name: GUIComponent_StopAllStates
purpose: Stops every state of a component.

behavior.text: for each state pointer of the vector comp+616 .. +624: GUINode_StopState(comp, state), with the state's own first name key (the key stored at state+0) as the key argument.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040996C). GUINode_StopState also stops the children of state links, so the Hand's scrubbed Loop is stopped with the main component's Loop.

name: GUIComponent_TickTree
purpose: Runs GUIComponent_UpdateNodeTree on the component's root node (comp+272) when the component is active, else clears the visible flags once.

behavior.text: when force != 0 or comp+559 != 0 or (comp+416 (loaded) != 0 and (comp+192 = 0 or comp+188 (opacity) > 0.0)): comp+562 = 1 and GUIComponent_UpdateNodeTree(comp, comp+272, force). Otherwise, if comp+562 was set, it is cleared and GUINode_ClearVisibleSubtree(comp, comp+272) runs once.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140409284). Not in the task list (called by sub_14040A1C8); documented because it fixes what comp+272 and comp+562 are.

name: GUIComponent_Update
purpose: Base per-frame update of a component: advance the state timers, apply the state animations, then update the node tree.

behavior.text: sub_1404099F4(comp, time) (advance / stop the active states), GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims(comp), GUIComponent_TickTree(comp, force).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040A1C8). Not in the task list.

name: GUIComponent_UpdateNodeTree
proto: char GUIComponent_UpdateNodeTree(GUIComponent *comp, __int64 unused, GUINode *node, char force)
callers: GUIComponent_TickTree (sub_140409284), itself, a handful of screen code paths (sub_1400F56D8, sub_14012D25C, ...)
callees: GUINode_ClearVisibleSubtree, GUINode_IsAncestorDirty, GUINode_ResolvePins_Fraction, GUINode_ResolvePins_Offset, GUIWidget_FindComponentCached, sub_1403F1234, sub_1403F2BD4, sub_1403F2EF8, sub_1403EF6B4, component virtual +32
purpose: Recursive layout / update walk over a component's node tree (started at comp+272 by sub_140409284): re-sorts layers by sort order, queues or runs the text relayout for dirty text nodes, and calls the update method of every nested component (kinds 9 and 12).

behavior.text: when force = 0 and comp+559 = 0 and (node+144 = 0 or node+108 <= 0.0 or (node+96 = 0 and the alpha byte node+103 of its own colour = 0)), the node and its whole subtree are skipped after GUINode_ClearVisibleSubtree (visible bytes +204 cleared). So a node with opacity <= 0, disabled, or an own colour of alpha 0 (with no colour id) is neither updated nor drawn, and neither are its children.
otherwise sub_1403EF860 resolves the node's pin layout when node+140 is set (+141 = 0 -> GUINode_ResolvePins_Fraction, 1 -> GUINode_ResolvePins_Offset), then switch on kind (node+52):

kind 1 (layer): when the re-sort flag node+216 is set, the child list (head node+208, next +32, previous +40) is insertion-sorted ascending by the children's sort order (+92) (stable: a later sibling moves ahead of an earlier one only when strictly smaller), flag cleared; then every child is processed recursively with the same force flag.

kind 3 (text): when an ancestor is dirty (GUINode_IsAncestorDirty) or node+316 (text dirty) is set: if the widget's flag (comp+496 -> +84) is set the node is appended as a 16-byte record {0, node} to the widget's vector at +304 (deferred relayout), otherwise sub_1403F1234 (resolve text id +248, copy string, GUITextNode_Layout) runs at once.

kind 9 (component reference with a 'mask' name at +248): component = GUIWidget_FindComponentCached(widget, node+248, node+264, node+288); none = return. The component's allocated size is set from the node's size (node+64/+68): comp+528 = width, comp+532 = height, swapped when comp+536 = 7 and comp+664 = 0; when comp+540 = 2 the component root is also resized to that size (sub_1403EF6B4(comp+272, ..)). Then the component's virtual method +32 is called (comp, time slot, changed = force or comp+559).

kind 12 (component reference, name at +208): same lookup (node+208, +224, +304); node+303 set -> sub_1403F2BD4(node, comp, 0); then sub_1403F2EF8(node, comp) (copy the reference's overrides onto the component) and the same virtual +32 call. Other kinds do nothing.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1404092EC). The cull in the first block is the only place found so far where an own colour alpha of 0 removes a subtree; it matters for the Job Tree because the TextMask rectangle and similar nodes are authored with colour data.
open_questions: The semantics of the +559 flag (force-visible?) and of the deferred relayout queue; what sub_1403F2EF8 copies.

name: GUIComponentCustom_Create
purpose: Allocates a 648-byte GUIComponentCustom from the UI pool (pages of 64), constructs it, links it into the owner's child list and registers it by id.

behavior.text: pool bookkeeping at qword_143CDA280+808.
sets vftable_faith::UISystem::GUIComponentCustom (0x140722490).

notes: Instances are named 'Unit#N' (N = creation order) for the tree's UnitJob references.

name: GUIComponentCustom_CursorEnter
purpose: Cursor-enter handler of a custom component (vtable slot +40): plays the CursorOver state and tells the node's owners.

behavior.text: when the node is not the focus or its byte +574 is 0 it calls GUINode_PlayCursorOverState; then GUIOwners_PostEvent(node+584, node, {event 0x1407232F0}) posts the cursor-enter event to the owners (the job tree addon).

name: GUIComponentGauge_Step
purpose: While the gauge value is animating (+688), eases three displayed fractions toward the target fraction using float tracks of the Increase / Decrease states, drives the GaugeBar / GaugeInc / GaugeDec states from them and posts the current value (event 37).

behavior.text: runs only when g+688 != 0. settled = true; the three ease values (bar, inc, dec) default to 1.0. State 'Decrease' (+4872): when it exists and its +104 is set, the float track of its '#GaugeBar' (+5192) channel group gives the bar ease and the one of '#GaugeDec' (+5224) the dec ease (sub_14040E350 samples track index 4 of the group at the state's frame +80); settled = (state+105 == 0). State 'Increase' (+4856): same with '#GaugeBar' (overrides the bar ease) and '#GaugeInc' (+5208) for the inc ease; settled = false when state+105 is set.

target = (float)(g+648 - g+656) / (float)(g+660 - g+656) (g+648 value, +656 min, +660 max). When settled: g+668 = g+676 = target and g+688 = 0 (animation finished). Otherwise g+668 = clamp((target - g+664) * barEase + g+664, 0, 1), g+676 = clamp((target - g+672) * incEase + g+672, 0, 1) and the third fraction clamp((target - g+680) * decEase + g+680, 0, 1).

g+684 = the third fraction (target when settled); sub_14040E1B8(g, ...) then puts the GaugeBar (+4888), GaugeInc (+4904) and GaugeDec (+4920) states on the frames that match the fractions (each is enabled, hold +109 = 1, frame = clamp((1 - fraction) * state+88, 0, last), read from sub_14040E1B8 for the first; its float arguments come from registers the decompile hides).
event {37, value} with value = (int)((float)(g+660 - g+656) * g+668 + (float)g+656) is posted to the owners.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040DEC4). Data flow read from the decompile; the fraction pairs are (+664 -> +668, bar track), (+672 -> +676, inc track), (+680 -> +684, dec track). Calling +676 / +684 the increase / decrease ghosts is I from the state names. Not Job Tree related.
open_questions: ? what writes the base values +664 / +672 / +680 and sets +688 (the set-value function, not read). ? sub_14040E1B8's three float arguments.

name: GUIComponentGauge_Update
purpose: Gauge component per-frame update (vtable slot 4): advances the states, runs the value animation step, applies tracks, updates the tree.

behavior.text: GUINode_UpdateStates(g, dt), GUIComponentGauge_Step(g), GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims(g), GUIComponent_TickTree(g, force).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040DE78). Kind 12 component (HP / MP style bars).

name: GUIComponentList_FindSlotNode
callers: GUIComponentList_GetSlotComponent, GUIComponentList_LayoutSlots and sub_140153CA0, sub_14028D44C, sub_14040C37C
purpose: Finds the layer node of slot number `slot`: the part named 'ListItem' for slot 0 and 'ListItem#n' for slot n.

behavior.text: key = sub_1403D8E5C(list, tmp, "ListItem", slot): when slot != 0 the name is Str_Format("%s#%d", "ListItem", slot), else plain 'ListItem'; then UIName_Key; node = GUINode_FindPartByName(list+272, key); the key's interned id is released.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040C1DC). The UIB of a list authors one node per slot: ListItem, ListItem#1, ListItem#2 ...

name: GUIComponentList_GetHScroll
callers: GUIComponentList_SetScrollX (0x14040C8B0), GUIComponentList_UpdateScrollBars and 11 list-user addon methods
purpose: Same as GUIComponentList_GetVScroll for the horizontal bar (key +5064 = 'HScroll').

behavior.text: identical to GUIComponentList_GetVScroll apart from the name key (+5064).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040C0EC).

name: GUIComponentList_GetItemComponent
callers: about 90 call sites in the UI addons (the most used list accessor)
purpose: The component currently showing item `item`, or null when that item is not in the shown window.

behavior.text: slot = GUIComponentList_ItemToSlot(list, item); slot < 0 returns 0; otherwise GUIComponentList_GetSlotComponent(list, slot).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040C270).

name: GUIComponentList_GetSlotComponent
callers: GUIComponentList_GetItemComponent and about 14 list-user addon methods (sub_1400F58A4, sub_1400F5974, sub_1400F6700, ...)
purpose: The component (a ListItem) behind a slot node: the slot node must be a reference node (kind 12).

behavior.text: node = GUIComponentList_FindSlotNode(list, slot); when node != 0 and node+52 == 12 returns GUIWidget_FindComponentCached(list+496, node+208, node+224, node+304), else 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040C228).

name: GUIComponentList_GetVScroll
callers: GUIComponentList_SetScrollY (0x14040C92C), GUIComponentList_UpdateScrollBars, and 13 list-user addon methods (sub_1400F56D8, sub_140112748, sub_140153874, sub_14028C5C4, ...)
purpose: Returns the list's vertical scroll bar component (the 'VScroll' child reference node), or null.

behavior.text: part = GUINode_FindPartByName(list+272, key +5048 = 'VScroll'); it must be a reference node (kind +52 == 12); component = GUIWidget_FindComponentCached(list+496, part+208, part+224, part+304); the component must have kind (+536) 8 (ScrollBar), else null.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040C080). 'List' is I: the function reads fields of a kind-9 style component (item count +648, columns +652); the ctor of kind 9 is the one that class has, the users were not each verified.

name: GUIComponentList_IsItemVisible
callers: sub_14028E720, sub_14028E850, sub_14028F320 (list cursor movement code)
purpose: True when the item's cell lies inside the list's viewport with at most half a cell cut off at each edge.

behavior.text: C = list+652 (columns), cell w = list+688, cell h = list+692, scroll x = list+676, scroll y = list+680, viewport w = list+696, h = list+700. x = (item % C) * w - scrollX; y = (item / C) * h - scrollY.
returns -w/2 <= x && x + w/2 <= viewportW && -h/2 <= y && y + h/2 <= viewportH (integer halves, C truncating division).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040C2FC). 'At least half visible' decides whether the cursor can sit on an item without scrolling.

name: GUIComponentList_ItemToSlot
purpose: Maps an item index to the recycled slot (a 'ListItem#n' node) that currently shows it, or -1 when the item is outside the window of shown items.

behavior.text: columns C = list+652, first shown item F = list+668, slot grid = list+660 (columns) x list+664 (rows). col = item % C; row = item / C; firstCol = F % C; firstRow = F / C.
returns -1 when col < firstCol, col >= firstCol + slotCols, row < firstRow or row >= firstRow + slotRows; otherwise (col % slotCols) + slotCols * (row % slotRows).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040C158). The same modulo mapping is used when the slots are placed (GUIComponentList_LayoutSlots), so a scrolled list reuses the slot nodes round-robin.

name: GUIComponentList_LayoutSlots
callees: GUIComponentList_FindSlotNode, GUINode_SetPosition, GUIWidget_FindComponentCached, GUICore_IsFocusTarget, GUICore_SetFocusComponent, GUICore_IsCursorTarget, GUICore_SetCursorTarget, GUINode_StopState, GUINode_PlayStateAtFrame, GUIOwners_PostEvent
purpose: Places the recycled slot nodes of a list for the current scroll offset, re-binds slots that now show a different item (resetting their visuals and clearing focus / cursor on them) and posts event 31.

behavior.text: C = list+652 columns, cell w = +688, cell h = +692, scroll x +676, scroll y +680, origin x +704, origin y +708, node size +336 / +340 (the clip test below), slot grid +660 columns x +664 rows, item count +648. firstCol = -((+704 - +676) / w), firstRow = -((+708 - +680) / h) (C truncating division). list+668 (first shown item) = C * firstRow + firstCol; the old value is kept for the rebind test.

for each row r = firstRow .. firstRow + slotRows - 1 and column c = 0..slotCols-1: item = firstCol + c + C * r; slot = ((c + firstCol) % slotCols) + slotCols * (r % slotRows); node = GUIComponentList_FindSlotNode(list, slot). A missing node is skipped.

cell position x = (item % C) * w - scrollX; y = (item / C) * h - scrollY; the node's visible byte (node+144) = item < count && -w < x + origin x < +336 && -h < y + origin y < +340; GUINode_SetPosition(node, x, y).

when the node is a reference node whose component has kind 10 (ListItem), the list's first shown item changed (+668 != previous) and the component's item index (+648) differs from `item`: if the component is the GUI focus target (GUICore_IsFocusTarget) the focus is cleared (GUICore_SetFocusComponent(core, 0, 0)); if it is the cursor target, GUICore_SetCursorTarget(core, 0, 0); component+652 = 0; states are reset with StopState + PlayStateAtFrame(-1, last frame): Active (+4936) -> Deactive (+4952), CursorOver (+4696) -> CursorOut (+4712), FocusIn (+4664) -> FocusOut (+4680); component+648 = item; when item < count event {30, item} is posted to the list's owners (list+584).
at the end list+685 = 0 and event {31} is posted.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040CB60). Takeaway for hover / focus on a list: slots are recycled; when the scroll moves a slot to a new item, its focus, cursor and Active / CursorOver / FocusIn states are forced back to the idle pose in the same frame. A model of hover that keys on a slot node (not on the item) will see the highlight jump.

name: GUIComponentList_SetItemCount
purpose: Sets the number of list items; when it changed, invalidates the bound slots and marks both the scroll bars and the layout dirty.

behavior.text: when list+648 != count: list+672 = -1; list+648 = count; sub_14040C604(list) (not read); word list+684 = 0x0101, i.e. +684 (scroll bars dirty) = 1 and +685 (layout dirty) = 1. Equal count does nothing.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040CA1C). list+672 = -1 is the 'nothing bound / no cursor item' marker (I; not read elsewhere here).
open_questions: ? what sub_14040C604 does (a re-layout or slot reset). ? role of +672.

name: GUIComponentList_SetScrollX
proto: void GUIComponentList_SetScrollX(GUIComponentList *list, int x, char snap, char clamp)
purpose: Sets the list's horizontal scroll offset, through the horizontal bar when there is one, and marks the layout dirty.

behavior.text: bar = GUIComponentList_GetHScroll(list); when it exists ScrollBar_SetPosition(bar, x, snap, clamp) and x = (int)roundf(bar+672) (the bar's current smooth position, so the value is clamped / eased by the bar).
list+676 = x; list+685 = 1 (layout dirty).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040C8B0). list+676 is the scroll offset the slot layout reads (x position = column * cell width - list+676).

name: GUIComponentList_SetScrollY
proto: void GUIComponentList_SetScrollY(GUIComponentList *list, int y, char snap, char clamp)
purpose: Vertical twin of GUIComponentList_SetScrollX: via the 'VScroll' bar, stores list+680 and sets the layout-dirty byte +685.

behavior.text: bar = GUIComponentList_GetVScroll(list); when present ScrollBar_SetPosition(bar, y, snap, clamp), y = (int)roundf(bar+672); list+680 = y; list+685 = 1.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040C92C). This is the call the job-change / ability list code makes when it scrolls a list (see ScrollBar_SetPosition's notes).

name: GUIComponentList_UpdateScrollBars
purpose: Gives the horizontal and vertical scroll bars their ranges from the item count and cell size, shows a bar only when the content is larger than the viewport, and clears the dirty byte +684.

behavior.text: C = list+652 (columns), n = list+648 (items), cell w = +688, cell h = +692. W = w * min(n, C); H = h * ((C + n - 1) / C) (integer, ceil(n / C) rows).

horizontal bar (GUIComponentList_GetHScroll): bar+681 = 1 (move pending), bar+652 (lower) = 0, bar+656 (upper) = max(W, 1), bar+660 (viewport) = max(list+696, 1), bar+416 = (W > list+696) (visible flag).
vertical bar: the same with H, list+700 and the bar returned by GUIComponentList_GetVScroll: bar+681 = 1, +652 = 0, +656 = max(H, 1), +660 = max(list+700, 1), +416 = (H > list+700).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040CA50). Writes the bar's +652 / +656 / +660 directly (V), which is what ScrollBar_SetPosition's sheet calls 'the wrong layout for this class' for raw writes from the outside: this function is the class's own way of doing it. bar+416 here toggles the bar's visibility (the same byte other sheets call 'loaded / enabled').
open_questions: ? whether bar+416 is really the visible flag for a ScrollBar (it is the byte GUIComponent_TickTree reads).

name: GUIComponentProps_Copy
purpose: Copies a component's 254-byte render-property block (the effect enable bytes and values: blend, colour transform, offsets, drop shadow, glow, clip and the two mask names) from one component to another. The pointers are component + 16.

behavior.text: the block offsets below are relative to component+16 (add 16 for the runtime component offset used by GUIComponent_LoadProps and ComponentEffects_Collect). It copies: +0 (blend type, comp+16), +4 qword (comp+20..+27, blend 17 parameters), +12..+27 and +28..+43 (comp+28..+59: colour multiply and add), +44 (comp+60 enable), +48 / +56 / +64 qwords (comp+64..+87: the six offset floats), +72 (comp+88 enable), +76 and +80 (comp+92 float, comp+96 enable).

drop-shadow group: +84 (comp+100, blur radius), +88 (comp+104, strength), +92 qword (comp+108 / +112, offset), +100 (comp+116, colour), +104 byte (comp+120, enable). Then +108..+139 eight dwords (comp+124..+155, the blend 14..16 parameters).

glow group: +140..+155 four dwords (comp+156..+171: strength, radius, colour, mode), +156 byte (comp+172, enable). Then +160 / +164 dwords (comp+176 / +180), bytes +168 / +169 / +170 (comp+184 / +185 / +186, the +186 group flags and enable), +172 dword (comp+188) and +176 byte (comp+192, enable).

clip: +180 sixteen bytes and +196 dword (comp+196..+211, +212 margins), +200 byte (comp+216, enable). Mask: UIName_Assign for the name at +208 (comp+224) and +232 (comp+248), dword +224 (comp+240), bytes +228 (comp+244 enable), +248, +249, +252 and +253 (comp+264, +265, +268, +269).
padding bytes between the fields are not copied; the function returns the last byte copied (+253).

its only caller sub_140408C4C calls GUIComponent_ResetEffects first, then sub_1403DF454(a1 + 16, a2 + 16), then copies the node data at +272 (sub_1403EF54C), the name at +504, the flags +520..+572 and the child list, and ends by stopping / playing the +554-selected state names (GUINode_StopState / GUINode_PlayStateAtFrame). I: it is the component clone / assign routine.

notes: Proposed name: GUIComponentProps_Copy (the in-memory twin of GUIComponent_LoadProps, which fills the same fields from the UIB file). The scan hit on fields +100 / +104 / +116 / +120 is this function's copy of the drop-shadow group (block +84 / +88 / +100 / +104 plus 16). sub_140408C4C has three callers: sub_1403F9DC4, sub_14040BFB0, sub_14040E7F0.
open_questions: ? which component operations call the three callers of sub_140408C4C (clone for list items, template instantiation?). ? the role of +4 qword (comp+20) for blend types other than 17.

name: GUIComponentRef_Draw
purpose: Draws a component reference node: finds the component, builds a draw context from its property block, opens an offscreen layer when the component has effects, draws its children, then composites the layer.

behavior.text: component = sub_1403F9938(ctx+488, ref+208, ref+224, ref+304); skipped when it is absent, when component+416 is 0, or when component+192 is set and the opacity float component+188 is <= 0.

ComponentDrawContext_Build copies the parent context (0x258 bytes) and multiplies matrix, opacity, colour and sort order; sub_1403E8FA4 decides whether an offscreen layer is needed (any effect group enabled) and opens it; sub_1403E9A2C draws the component children; sub_1403E9298 closes and composites the layer when one was opened.

the call is ComponentLayer_Begin(r, child context, 0) (no force); after the children, when a layer was opened, the parent's layer id (a2+548) is incremented when non-zero and GUILayer_Select(r, parent context) runs: the parent's later draws go to a NEW layer record built from the parent's context (an existing one is reused only when its id and settings match), so a child layer is bracketed by two records of the parent and keeps its place in the order. When no layer was opened the parent's offscreen flag ctx+554 is taken from the child's.

behavior.basis: (live 2026-10-30, 26 slots of a Job Tree frame)
behavior.text: the sequence of layer slots is reproduced exactly by this rule: a component that opens a layer takes the next slot, and the parent continues in the slot after it with the PARENT context (the continuation record carries the parent's inherited effect groups; the child context is a copy of the parent's, so effect groups inherited from ancestors stay set in nested contexts); a slot without any draw is reused, so only components with draws after them produce a continuation slot. See the behavior JobTreeLayerList.

notes: The Job Tree hover ring is the component UnitSelect drawn through this path.
open_questions: Layer composite shader selection (sub_1403E6728 / sub_1403E73A0) not yet decoded (?).

name: GUIComponentRef_DrawChildren
purpose: Draws the node tree of the component a reference node points at, or (when the layer mask path is active) just clears the current layer record's draw counter.

behavior.text: when byte r+606628 != 0 or byte ctx+184 = 0 -> GUINode_DrawChildren(r, ctx, (ctx+496)->+272) (the component's root node).
otherwise dword at r + 592 * (int r+606588) + 303508 = 0: field +28 of the current 592-byte layer record is zeroed and nothing is drawn.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403E9A2C). 6401 hits per 4 s. ctx+496 is the component, +184 is a draw-enable byte, r+606588 is the current layer index (see GUILayer_SetCurrent).
open_questions: ? Meaning of r+606628 and of record field +28 (I: command count; the branch drops what the layer collected).

name: GUIComponentScrollBar_StepKnob
callees: GUINode_FindState, sub_140400344 (track group by name), UIAnim_SampleFloatTrack, GUINode_FindPartByName, GUINode_IsAncestorDirty, GUINode_ResolvePinsDispatch, GUINode_SetPosition, GUINode_SetSize, GUIWidget_FindComponentCached, GUIComponent_SetAllocatedSize, GUIOwners_PostEvent
purpose: While the bar has a pending move (+681), eases the shown position toward the target using the ScrollUp / ScrollDown state tracks, then sizes and places the Knob part inside the Base part and posts event 27.

behavior.text: runs only when bar+681 != 0. ease = 1.0 and settled = 1. For the state 'ScrollUp' (+4968) and then 'ScrollDown' (+4984): when the state exists and its running byte (+105) is set, the float track at index 4 of the state's '#ScrollBar' (+5176) channel group (found by name with sub_140400344) is sampled at the state's current frame (+80) into ease and settled = 0.
shown = (float)(target bar+648 - start bar+676) * ease + start (bar+676). So with no running scroll state the knob jumps to the target at once; with one it follows the authored ease track.

parts 'Base' (+5096) and 'Knob' (+5112) are looked up with GUINode_FindPartByName(bar+272, ...). With both present: when bar+664 and +668 are both 0 the knob's authored size qword (knob+64) is stored there; the Base's pins are resolved when dirty (GUINode_IsAncestorDirty / GUINode_ResolvePinsDispatch).

range = max(upper bar+656 - lower bar+652 - viewport bar+660, 0); frac = range > 0 ? clamp((shown - lower) / range, 0, 1) : 0. Vertical (bar+680 == 0): knob length L = base.h when range <= 0, else max(authored knob height (+668), base.h * viewport / max(upper - lower, viewport)) with C integer division; knob size = (knob.w, L), knob position = (knob.x, base.y + roundf((base.h - L) * frac)). Horizontal (bar+680 != 0): the same on the x axis with base.w and the authored width (+664) as the minimum length, size = (L, knob.h), position = (base.x + roundf((base.w - L) * frac), knob.y). The knob is set with GUINode_SetPosition and GUINode_SetSize; a reference-node knob (kind 12) also gets GUIComponent_SetAllocatedSize.
when settled and bar+681 still set, bar+681 = 0. bar+672 = shown. Event {27} is posted to the owners.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040BBF0). Companion to ScrollBar_SetPosition (position +648, lower +652, upper +656, viewport +660, smooth +672 / +676). The ease value comes from game data: a float track inside the ScrollUp / ScrollDown state, so the scroll speed of every list is authored, not coded. The orientation byte at +680 and the exact use of +676 as the start of the move are read from this function only.
open_questions: ? who sets +676 (the start value of an eased move) and +680 (orientation). ? the track's authoring (curve / length).

name: GUIComponentScrollBar_Update
purpose: Scroll bar per-frame update (vtable slot 4): advances the states, applies their tracks, repositions the knob and then updates the node tree.

behavior.text: GUINode_UpdateStates(bar, dt), GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims(bar), GUIComponentScrollBar_StepKnob(bar), GUIComponent_TickTree(bar, force).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040BBA4). Compare GUIComponent_Update (base: UpdateStates, ApplyStateAnims, TickTree) and the Gauge version GUIComponentGauge_Update (the step is before ApplyStateAnims there).

name: GUICore_BeginFrame
purpose: Start of a UI frame in the GUI core: stores the frame times and the frame counters, advances the random state, refreshes the viewport transform and dispatches the queued events.

behavior.text: ++core+2092; core+2136 = the application's object at g_Application+1168; core+2100 = dt; core+2104 = dt2; core+2096 += (int64)(dt * 1000.0) (a millisecond clock, truncated per frame).
four dwords at core+2076 .. +2088 are rotated and mixed every frame.
that is a xorshift-style random generator.

when the layer transform scale core+2108 is not 1.0 the transform is reset and recomputed (GUILayerXform_Recompute) and the viewport flag core+2117 is set; with that flag set the viewport fields are refilled and an event of type 4 (carrying the size) is queued with sub_1403D69A8; an event of type 3 is queued every frame.
then the four event queues at core+88 (stride 32 bytes, 68-byte events) are drained in order into GUICore_DispatchEvent.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D6234). core+2100 is the dt that GUICore_TickWidget gives to widgets with selector 0 and that GUICursorHand_Update reads for its hold timer; core+2104 is the one for selector 1.

name: GUICore_CommitFrame
purpose: Per-frame UI commit: resets the renderer, runs every widget's draw, then expands each layer's bounds for its effects.

behavior.text: sub_1403E6160 resets the renderer (512 layer records reinitialised by sub_1403E73A0); widgets are drawn through vtable +88 / +96; two cursor-sized draws (sub_1403E5258); sub_1403E90A8 closes the last layer; then GUILayer_ExpandBounds for every layer 0..(r+606584).

widget order: the widget vector (core+24 .. +32) is walked from the LAST entry to the first (the vector is sorted by descending priority word w+62, so the lowest priority is drawn first and the highest ends on top); a widget is drawn when (w+74 or w+75) is non-zero and w+79 is zero, through GUICore_DrawWidget; otherwise only its vtable +96 hook runs. A widget whose root has no draw leaves no slot (the layer opened for it is reused).

after the widgets, for each of the two layer transforms (core+216 + 144 j) with the int at +128 equal to 1 GUICore_DrawOutsideBars runs and the draw counter is incremented even when the screen has no letterbox bars (live 16:9: transform 0 has the flag, the call adds no quad): the draws land in the slot after the last widget layer, which therefore gets counted (the last slot of the live frame, no quad, never used or packed).

name: GUICore_Ctor
purpose: Constructs the GUI core: widget lists, the UI renderer, the focus key strings, the screen size and the per-frame worker slots.

behavior.text: sets the two vftables; the widget list is a vector at +16 / +24 (sorted by the word at widget+62 each frame); four small vectors at +88 and two 144-byte entries at +216 (sub_1403F89B8) are initialised.

allocates the 606720-byte UI renderer object (sub_1403E5B84) and stores it at core+208 (the same object whose 592-byte layer records start at renderer + 303504); sets the design screen size 1920 x 1080 at +512 / +516 and +520 / +524.

the focus key strings at +1968 / +1984 / +2000 (and the other string slots up to +2048) start as the shared empty string; ten 264-byte slots start at +2144; an event handle (CreateEventA) is stored at +4784 and the frame callback sub_1403D7E9C is registered with the language info.

notes: g_GUICore + 208 is the UI renderer used throughout the glow / layer notes.

name: GUICore_DispatchEvent
purpose: Hands one raw UI event to each registered handler (core+56..+64, vtable slot 1) until one consumes it, then to the core's own message handler (core+8).

behavior.text: sets core+2116 while dispatching.

name: GUICore_DrawOutsideBars
proto: __int64 GUICore_DrawOutsideBars(UIRenderer *r, const float m[6], const int rect[4], const uint32 screen[2], unsigned int color, unsigned int sortKey)
callers: GUICore_CommitFrame (twice, for the two cursor-sized / border layers whose record flag +132 is 1)
purpose: Fills the part of the screen outside a transformed rectangle (the letterbox / pillarbox bars around the UI area) with a flat colour.

behavior.text: the rect corners (rect[0], rect[1]) and (rect[2], rect[3]) are pushed through m (x' = m0*x + m2*y + m4, y' = m1*x + m3*y + m5) giving X1, Y1, X2, Y2; screen = {W, H} unsigned ints (r+184).
when the rectangle lies completely outside the screen (X2 <= 0 or X1 >= W or Y2 <= 0 or Y1 >= H) the whole screen (0, 0, W, H) is filled through sub_1403DFE34 with the identity matrix.

otherwise up to four flat quads (4 vertices each, colour = the dword, z = 0, queued with UIRender_QueueImageDraw): left bar if 0 < X1 < W (x 0..X1, y Y1..Y2), right bar if 0 < X2 < W (X2..W, Y1..Y2), top bar if 0 < Y1 < H (full width, y 0..Y1), bottom bar if 0 < Y2 < H (full width, Y2..H); the bounds are extended with sub_1403DF670 for (0,0) and (the far corner).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403E5258). colour comes from sub_1403D9570(g_ColorTable, 1), i.e. colour table entry 1. The rect argument in CommitFrame is {0, 0, layer.w, layer.h} (I).
open_questions: ? The bars use the plain bar corners without the half-pixel rule; bar overlap at the corners is not handled (not needed while the rect is inside the screen).

name: GUICore_DrawWidget
callers: GUICore_CommitFrame (widgets with +74 or +75 set and +79 clear, called with layer = core + 216 + 144 * int16 w+60)
callees: sub_1403DFE34, sub_1403F9D6C, sub_1403F8A20, ComponentLayer_Begin, GUINode_DrawChildren, sub_1403E9218, GUILayer_ResetRecord
purpose: Draws one widget: bumps the sort group when the widget's draw order word changes, fills the widget background, then builds the root draw context from the layer transform and draws the widget's main component tree.

behavior.text: a = int16 w+62; when r+606616 != a: ++r+606600 and r+606616 = a. (r+606600 << 8 is the high part of every sort key, see GUINode_DrawChildren.)

when the high byte of the dword w+64 is non-zero (background alpha) a flat quad (sub_1403DFE34) covering (0, 0, layer+24, layer+28) in the identity matrix (xmmword_140906D60 = 1,0,0,1) with colour w+64 and the sort key r+606596 is queued; ++r+606592.
main component = sub_1403F9D6C(w) (first entry of the vector w+104..+112 with +536 == 1). It is drawn only when it exists, comp+416 (enabled) != 0 and (comp+192 == 0 or the float comp+188 > 0).

behavior.basis: (root draw context, 0x258 bytes on the stack, zero-filled except)
behavior.text: ctx+488 = w, ctx+496 = comp, ctx+504..+527 = the layer's matrix (layer+48..+71; recomputed first by sub_1403F8A20 when layer+128 is set), ctx+528 / +532 = layer+120 / +124 (the layer scale), ctx+536 = 0 (opacity add), ctx+540 = -1 (white), ctx+544 = 0 (order), ctx+548 = comp+552 << 16 (layer id), ctx+552 = 0 (depth), ctx+4 = 1.0f, ctx+132 / +148 / +476 = -1.

opened = ComponentLayer_Begin(r, ctx, 0); when r+606628 != 0 or the layer flag the call set is clear, GUINode_DrawChildren(r, ctx, comp + 272) draws the component's root layer node; otherwise the field at r + 592*r[606588] + 303508 is zeroed instead. When a layer was opened: sub_1403E9218(r, -1) and GUILayer_ResetRecord(r, r[606588]) close it.

ComponentLayer_Begin is called at depth 0 with the root context, where the force rule applies: widget byte +83 is 1 for all 51 widgets, so the widget root always opens a layer (feature byte r+606621 = 1).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403E97A8). This is where a screen's draw starts: the root context has identity opacity (add 0), white colour and the window-to-UI matrix; every colour / opacity / order on the Job Tree page accumulates from here down through GUINode_DrawChildren and the component contexts.
open_questions: ? The meaning of ctx+4 = 1.0f and of the three -1 fields; what r+606628 is.

name: GUICore_FindWidgetByKey
purpose: Finds the top-level widget that a key (name string + hash) names, walking the widget list; returns 0 when none matches. The focus key at core+1968 goes through it to give the focused widget.

behavior.text: iterates the widget pointer vector core+24 .. core+32.
when the widget's dword at +24 is non-zero and the key's dword at +8 is non-zero, a widget matches when the two dwords are equal (the hash of the .uib name).
otherwise it compares the widget's C string at +16 with the key's string pointer at +0 byte by byte, and matches on equality.
returns the first match, so a duplicate name resolves to the earlier widget in the list.

notes: The key at g_GUICore+1968 (string at +0, hash at +8) names the focused screen without calling game code; the screen name is the string at widget+16.
open_questions: Not yet read on the live game: whether the string at widget+16 is the full .uib path (?).

name: GUICore_FocusNode
purpose: Moves the GUI focus (and with it the finger cursor) onto a node, or clears the focus when the node is null. The job tree calls it with a panel node for every cursor move.

behavior.text: with a node: the owning widget is node+496; when sub_1403D6E8C(core, widget, node) reports the node is already the focus it returns that result, otherwise it clears the focus (sub_1403D6A64(core, 0, 0)) when sub_1403D6BFC(core, widget, node) is 0, calls GUICore_SetFocusComponent(core, widget, node) and finishes with sub_1403D6A64(core, widget, node).

with a null node: clears the focus (sub_1403D6A64(core, 0, 0)), then, when a focus exists (sub_1403D6E28), empties the three key strings at core+1968 / +1984 / +2000, calls the old focus node's virtual +104 (focus lost) and sets core byte +2128 = 1.

notes: The finger cursor widget follows the focused node; its placement is a widget transform, not a node position (live read: the Hand layer position did not change while the cursor moved). The code that converts the focus node into that transform was not located.

name: GUICore_GetFocus
purpose: Resolves the focus key triple (core+1968) to the live widget and node; returns 0 when nothing is focused.

behavior.text: widget = GUICore_FindWidgetByKey(core, core+1968); node = sub_1403F9938(widget, core+2000, core+1984, 0); both are written to the out parameters. The returned node is the panel's reference node for the job tree (live: Mystic = kind 12, pos (1220,485), size 64x80).

notes: Live read: widget = the ffto_job_tree.uib widget, node screen rect (1220, 517, 1284, 597), so the hand target is (left, centre y) = (1220, 557).

name: GUICore_IsCursorTarget
purpose: Same comparison as GUICore_IsFocusTarget against the cursor-target triple at core+1920 / +1936 / +1952.

name: GUICore_IsFocusTarget
purpose: Tests whether (widget, node) is the current GUI focus: compares the three keys (widget+16, node+504, node+280) with the focus triple at core+1968 / +1984 / +2000.

behavior.text: each key is compared by its cached hash when both hashes are non-zero (widget+24 vs core+1976, node+512 vs core+1992, node+288 vs core+2008), otherwise by string; any mismatch returns 0.

name: GUICore_OnInputState
purpose: The UI core's input listener: turns the frame's input state into queued UI events and then pumps the queue through GUICore_DispatchEvent.

behavior.text: copies the 0x548-byte state to core+528; stores the pointer x/y in core+1880/+1884 (the hit test reads them) and the wheel/buttons in +1896..+1911.

raw event ids queued by sub_1403D69A8 (68-byte records): 7 pointer state (x, y, buttons), 8 pointer moved, 9 wheel, 10..21 per-button pressed (&1) / released (&4) / held (&2) groups, 22..25 key queue, 26 pad axes; then event 1 (the frame tick) and a drain loop over the queue.
GUIMessageHandler_Dispatch maps these ids to GUICore virtuals; event 1 reaches GUICore_UpdateFrame, which does the hover hit test.

open_questions: Which raw id is the left button press (10..13 are four buttons) is not tied to a device (?).

name: GUICore_SetCursorTarget
purpose: Makes a node the GUI cursor target: stores its key triple in the core's cursor slot and sends it the cursor-enter virtual call (the old target gets the cursor-leave call).

behavior.text: the current target comes from sub_1403D6B98; when it already is (widget, node) the call returns 1. Otherwise the three key strings at core+1920 / +1936 / +1952 are cleared and the old node's virtual +48 (cursor leave) runs.

with a widget and a node whose byte +416 is set: when the node has an owner at node+576 the owner becomes the target; the keys (widget+16, node+504, node+280) are stored with sub_1403D87F4 and the node's virtual +40 (cursor enter, GUIComponentCustom_CursorEnter) runs; returns 1, else 0.

notes: The cursor target and the focus (core+1968 triple, GUICore_SetFocusComponent) are separate key triples.

name: GUICore_SetFocusComponent
purpose: Moves focus to a component node: the old focus node gets virtual +104 (focus lost, event 20), the new one virtual +96 (focus gained, event 19); stores the new key triple at core+1968.

behavior.text: returns 1 without change when the node already has focus.

name: GUICore_TickWidget
purpose: Gives one widget its frame time and calls its tick (vtable slot 7, GUIWidget_Tick).

behavior.text: nothing happens unless the widget is active (w+74) or pending (w+75).

block = (~(word w+88)) AND core+2132 (the low 16 bits). When block != 0 the widget is still ticked, with dt = 0 (its clocks stand still). Otherwise dt = core+2100 when w+48 == 0, dt = core+2104 when w+48 == 1, and for any other value of w+48 the widget is not ticked at all.

for a widget made by an addon, w+48 and the bits of w+88 come from the addon's row of the addon table (UITable 24): w+48 = byte 31 != 0, bit i of w+88 = byte 12 + i != 0 for i = 0..11 (sub_1401D1C6C).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D7670). A set bit in core+2132 that the widget's own mask lacks freezes the widget (for instance behind a modal screen).
open_questions: ? The table row of the finger cursor: whether its widget uses selector 0 or 1 and which block bits it is exempt from (it bobs while the Job Tree is open, so it is exempt from whatever the Job Tree sets).

name: GUICore_UpdateFrame
purpose: Per-frame UI update (raw event 1): finds the node under the mouse pointer and moves hover/focus onto it.

behavior.text: walks the widget list (core+16..+24; widgets are skipped when +74 = 0 or +79 != 0); for the first enabled widget with +77 (pointer-enabled) it maps the pointer (+1872/+1876 of this sub-object, = core+1880/+1884) through the widget's layer transform (GUILayerXform_MapPointFloat on core+208+144*layer) and runs GUIWidget_HitTestPoint with the filter 'Collision nodes only'.

the first hit's node (hit list entry +8) becomes the pointer target; when the pointer moved or a button changed (+1888/+1892/+1902) GUICore_SetFocusComponent/sub_1403D6A64 move focus to it and sub_1403D6F70 updates the hover record (+2064).

focus uses the key triple at +1968/+1984/+2000 (widget id, component name, node name); pointer hover is the triple at +1920..; the node's virtual +96 plays its CursorOver state and posts event 19, the previous focus gets +104 / event 20 (GUIComponent_OnFocusGained/Lost).

keeps the last pointed node by name, as three UI name keys at core +2016 (widget), +2032 and +2048 (the component's +504 and +280 keys; `UIName_Assign`, 0x1403D750A..). Each frame it finds the widget with `GUICore_FindWidgetByKey` (the live widget list core +24..+32, by name id or string) and the component with `GUIWidget_FindComponentCached(widget, +2048, +2032, no cache)` (the widget's map +128 / +136, then its vector +104) and calls that component's vtable +72 / +64 (cursor out); when the pointed node changes it resets the keys with `UIName_SetKey(key, Str)` (`Str` 0x1406F9FA0, the empty string).

the component the pointed-node lookup returned held the vtable of a `UIResourceHandle` (vtable 0x140721BF0, slot 8 its deleting destructor; a data address from the dump, not used by this function's own code), reached by the call through vtable +0x40 (return 0x1403D7638): a component pointer to freed memory reused by a resource handle of a screen opened since. I: the pointed-node names still named a node of a screen freed earlier; the minidump holds no heap, so which widget is not read. I (2026-11-18): the same signature (StringHandle_Release <- UIResourceHandle_Delete, return 0x1403D7638) as the row freed inside its decide event below, so likely the same cause.

on a mouse release over the pointed component it calls that component's vtable +0x48 (0x1403D75F3), resets the three keys (`UIName_SetKey(this + 0x7D8 / 0x7E8 / 0x7F8, Str)`, 0x1403D75FB..0x1403D762A; `this` = core + 8, as this function is the GUICore vtable at object +8, so these are core +2016 / +2032 / +2048) and then calls the SAME component pointer's vtable +0x40 (0x1403D7635, return 0x1403D7638); the pointer is not looked up again between the two calls.

behavior.basis: (seen live 2026-11-18, reproduced with one mouse click, two dumps)
behavior.text: a screen whose decide handler for a click on a list row rebuilt the list's rows at once (the list's row count set again, its rows shown again, inside the event) crashed in StringHandle_Release <- sub_140095E5C <- UIResourceHandle_Delete, called through vtable +0x40 at 0x1403D7635: the clicked row's component was freed inside the event and its memory reused. The same decide from the keyboard did not crash, and rebuilding the rows in the screen's next per-frame update instead of inside the event did not crash (click and keyboard). I: the decide event is raised inside the +0x48 call.

open_questions: Pad (stick) focus movement shares this function and is not documented (?).

name: GUICore_UpdateWidgets
purpose: Per-frame widget update (the second GUICore update function; see GUICore_UpdateFrame for the other): orders the widgets, wires the ten frame worker slots when a task object exists and updates every widget.

behavior.text: insertion-sorts the widget list (core+16 .. +24) so the widget with the larger word at +62 comes first.

when core+2128 holds an object, waits until the worker counter at +4788 is 0, resets the event (+4776), sets the counters (widget count at +4784, 10 at +4788), clears each widget's +600 field, then registers ten callbacks (sub_1403D79C4 and sub_1403D7A5C wrapped by sub_14009006C) on the object's virtual +48 for the 264-byte slots from core+2136.

for each widget, when there is no task object or the widget's +84 byte is 0, calls sub_1403D7670 and decrements the worker counter, signalling the event when it reaches 0; with no task object it then refreshes the component nodes that have their +562 / +559 flags (sub_1403F08C0).

notes: Only the structure was read; the callbacks and the task object at core+2128 are not documented.
open_questions: What the object at core+2128 is (a job system?) (?).

name: GUICursor_UpdateIndex
purpose: Chooses the cursor index the UI wants (g_GUICore + 1904) and shows or hides the OS cursor.

behavior.text: the wanted index starts from a field of the input state (+16); when that is 0 it is 3 if the top actor's byte +575 is set (the actor comes from sub_1403D7008 = the actor table entry for g_GUICore+2064) and 1 otherwise. The index is stored in g_GUICore+1904 when it changed, or 0 (the system arrow) when the pointer is not in use.
the cursor is shown (bit 0 of the cursor object's +148) when the UI is not in pad mode and the mouse flags allow it, and hidden otherwise; a change calls Cursor_Apply.
GUICore_OnInputState copies g_GUICore+1904 into the cursor object (+144, range -1..16) and calls Cursor_Apply when it differs.

notes:
The name is ours.

- V (2026-11-02): the byte +575 is a component flag, set to 1 by the screen builders that wire a component's `Collision00` hit area (13 write sites in 12 functions, each a one-byte write of 1 next to the hit-area lookup: `sub_140116914`, `sub_140118438`, `sub_140127174`, `sub_14013C804`, `sub_14015F730`, `sub_14017BF70`, the SaveLoad and BGMMode addons' `vfunc_4`, `sub_14018E6CC`, `sub_140293FD0`, `sub_1402AECA0`, `sub_1402AFEA0`; `sub_14042867C` also stores 0x20 at +575 of a different kind of object, not a flag). `sub_14018E6CC` is the Settings screen's tab-bar builder: it loops over `TabButton%02d` and flags every tab button. The Settings rows, switches and picklists are built elsewhere and not flagged.
- V: the component under the pointer is the actor `GUICore_UpdateFrame` hands to `sub_1403D6F70` (stored as the key at g_GUICore+2064; byte +416 must be set for it to count, +576 redirects to a parent; hover enter / leave are vfuncs 5 and 6). `sub_1403D7008` turns that key back into the actor, so over a flagged component the index is 3 and elsewhere 1.
- V (live, 2026-11-02, Settings > Gameplay, polling g_GUICore+1904 and the hovered-actor key at +2064 while the owner moved over the tab bar): over an unselected tab the index is 3 with a key of 6826, 6828 or 6830 (three different tab actors, 2 apart); off the tabs the key is 0 and the index 1. The selected tab never gave 3 (owner's observation: only unselected tabs react). Rows were not polled in this run.
- V (live, pointer x read from g_GUICore+1880 next to the index while the owner swept across a tab divider): between two unselected tabs the index drops back to 1 (hovered key 0) for about 4 layout px, x = 958..961 around the boundary at 960 (strip x 810 = 3 tabs of 270); x = 957 is the left tab (key 6828) and x = 962 the right one (6826). So the tab hit areas stop short of the 4 px divider (`TabSepalete`) on both sides; the gap is the divider's own width.
- V (pixels, the two quill captures of the index 1 and index 3 states): index 3 is the same quill turned about 11 degrees counter-clockwise (art axis 24.2 to 35.0 degrees above horizontal) and about 32 % lighter (luma 129 to 170; mean opaque colour (169,128,27) to (204,169,85)), same 128 px size and hotspot (61, 63). This is the "tilts left and lightens over a tab" look. The launcher mock uses it over its tabs.
open_questions: Whether the Job Tree flags any component (read g_GUICore+1904 live while hovering a unit panel; no Job Tree builder is among the 14 writers, so index 1 is expected). The other flagged screens (the writers above) have not been named one by one.

name: GUICursorHand_GetTargetPoint
purpose: The hand's rest position for the focused component (left edge + hand+80, vertical centre + hand+84), or the screen centre (960, 540) when nothing is focused.

behavior.text: the same rule as GUICursorHand_Update's second branch.

name: GUICursorHand_StepToward
proto: void GUICursorHand_StepToward(GUICursorHand *hand, int x, int y, char instant)
purpose: One step of the hand's travel: pos = roundf(pos + (target - pos) * k), per axis, written to the hand node.

behavior.text: k = hand+440 when hand+444 is set, else g_UIDataModule+24 = 0.4; skipped (the hand jumps to the target) when instant is set or hand+445 is 1 (first placement).
the integer position is stored in hand+432/+436; hand node +149 = 1 marks it moved.
called once per UI frame (60 per second: the main loop sleeps to 1/60 s), so the hand covers 40% of the remaining distance every 16.7 ms; rounding stalls it within 1 px of the target.

this step has no time term (it is per UI frame), while the glove's bob runs on the UI frame time; both results are integers, written to different nodes: this one to the cursor reference node, the bob to the IconHand node inside the Hand component. They meet only in the float node matrices, which add integers exactly: nothing rounds their sum.

notes: The studio reproduces the glove origin in its viewer code.

name: GUICursorHand_Update
purpose: Per-frame update of the pointing-hand cursor: finds the focused component, computes where the hand belongs and moves it there.

behavior.text: first counts down the hold timer hand+76 (ms, dt from core+2100) and does nothing while it is > 0.

target = the focused node's 'CursorAnchor' part rect if the component has one (x = rect.left + hand+80 - handWidth/2, y = (rect.top+rect.bottom)/2 + hand+84), otherwise, for a type-12 focus node with +144 set, x = rect.left + hand+80, y = rect centre + hand+84 (rect from GUIWidget_GetNodeScreenRect).
with a target the hand node (hand+56) is moved by GUICursorHand_StepToward's rule; without one the hand node is hidden and the next placement is instant (+444 = 0, +440 = default k, +445 = 1).

the placement happens only when the focused component's byte +568 is set and the target differs from the last placed position (+432 / +436); the step is computed from that last position every frame, so a stalled hand recomputes the same value.
while hand+132 (static mode, UIAgentCursor_SetStatic) is set the node is only made visible and is not placed. The agent's update thunk calls this function only when the cursor widget is active.
hand+80 / +84 are loaded from the cursor request being applied (UIAgentCursor_PopRequest) and cleared when the cursor is hidden.
this function neither starts nor stops any animation state: the glove's bob (flow CursorGloveFrame) is independent of arriving, leaving or retargeting.

the hand object a1 = 0x15DA3015000 in that session had hand+80 = hand+84 = 0; *(a1+64) is the cursor widget's reference node holder: +56 = the node (kind 12, size 100x100, pos = the last placement), +432 / +436 = the last placed (x, y), +440 = k (0.4), +444 / +445 = the flags. The job tree's focus node is the panel reference node (kind 12, pos = panel origin, size 64x80); its screen rect from GUIWidget_GetNodeScreenRect is (left, top + 32, left + 64, top + 112) (the 32 is the JobTree layer's y), so the target for Mystic (1220, 485) is (1220, 557). The rounded smoothing step stops 1 px short of the target when the remaining distance is 1 (|d| * 0.4 < 0.5): live pos (1219, 556).

notes: The Job Tree UIB has no CursorAnchor part, so its hand uses the second rule.
open_questions: Who sets the hold timer hand+76 is not traced, nor which request supplies hand+80 / +84 for the Job Tree (the stack's pusher was not found) (?).

name: GuideBar_Layout
purpose: Rebuilds the guide bar: hides and resets all 8 slots, then lays out the visible rows of table 33 in two passes (left-aligned, then right-aligned).

behavior.text: for the 8 slot nodes at g+280 (stride 272): if present set +144 = 0 (hidden) and GUINode_UpdateColourAndMatrix(node, 1); slot field +32 = -1 (no row).
n = sub_1403DBC20(33, g+2224) rows. Pass 1: x cursor j = g+2232; for row i < n while used < 8: if GuideBar_LayoutRow(g, &j, used, i, 0) succeeded then used++ (rows whose flag byte +37 is 0).
pass 2: j = 1920 - g+2232 (right edge of a 1920-wide screen); the same for rows with flag +37 == 1 (a5 = 1).
returns the last call's result.

notes: The 1920 constant is V. Left group grows right from the left margin g+2232; right group is placed from the right margin leftwards (GuideBar_LayoutRow subtracts the width).

name: GuideBar_LayoutRow
proto: char GuideBar_LayoutRow(ButtonGuide *g, int *x, int slot, unsigned int row, char rightPass)
callees: GUINode_ApplyStateAtFrame, GUINode_SetPosition, GUINode_SetSize, GUINode_UpdateColourAndMatrix, GUINode_UpdateSubtree, GUITextNode_SetString, GUIWidget_FindComponentCached, UIName_Key, sub_14013DD70, sub_14028BE4C, sub_1403DBDF4, sub_1403F1234, sub_1403D8D1C
purpose: Configures one guide slot for table 33 row `row`: sets the text, the up to four button icons (keyboard / pad variants), places the slot at x and starts its on-animation.

behavior.text: row = sub_1403DBDF4(33, g+2224, row); skipped (returns 0) when the row's bit is clear in g+2228, the row's text id (+12) is 0 or its placement byte (+37) != rightPass.

text: from the override map g+2288 (std::map keyed by row, string at node+32) when present else the row's text id into the text node at slot+240 (GUITextNode_SetString / dirty byte +316); the node is resized (GUINode_SetSize with text width, 432 - 424) and the slot width v47 is computed.

icons: row dwords +4 / +16 (pad) or +28 / +32 (when UI config byte 13696 == 1) pick the primary / secondary button ids; when the pad icon ids are 19 / 20 it sets four ids {0x24, 0x22, 0x23, 0x21} (the four direction buttons: a 4-button group); each is passed to sub_14028BE4C (set the icon of the button part).
'Hide2ndButton / Show2ndButton', '3rdButton', '4thButton' states are applied (GUINode_ApplyStateAtFrame, frame -1) on the slot's widget according to the button count v39 = dword slot+164.

sets the slot node's x with GUINode_SetPosition (x -= width on the right pass, += width on the left pass; extra buttons add g+2244 each), +144 = 1 visible, updates matrix / subtree, stores slot+264 = row, calls sub_14013DD70(g, row, placement) to fade it in. Returns 1.

notes: The 'four direction buttons' reading of the 19 / 20 group is I (ids 0x21..0x24 are the actions the direction helpers test). Column names of table 33 (UIButtonGuide, 2026-11-19): +4 guide_icon, +0xC title_text, +0x10 guide_icon_2, +0x1C key_texture, +0x20 key_texture_2, +0x25 right_aligned (the placement byte); +8 / +0x14 are the actions ui_key_assign / ui_key_assign_2.
