name: GUIFontRenderer_UploadPalette
purpose: Finds or appends an entry for a font palette block and writes it to the GPU structured buffer SDFPalette (192 bytes per entry) read by shader/SDFFont.tec.

behavior.text: palette +0..63 = a 4x4 matrix (sub_1403C043C); +64/+68/+72 = row floats at +4/+12/+20 (layer widths: UIFontSet.Unknown8 / UnknownC / Unknown10); +80/+84 = row +0x2C/+0x30 times a constant; +88/+92 = row +0x20/+0x24 (UIFontSet.Unknown18 / Unknown1C: the shadow layer's edge and width); +96/+100 = in-memory row +52/+56 (decimal; = UIFontSet.Unknown28 / Unknown2C, 0.1 and 1.0 in every row; live-checked 2026-10-27: every cached palette entry holds 0.1 and 1.0); +128/+144/+160/+112 = colours at row +8/+16/+28/+40 as floats (zeroed when the matching width is <= 0); +176 = (0, 0, 0, row +0x18).

the 80-byte in-memory row is filled by GUIFontTable_Load from the nxd record: +0 ui_font_type, +4 Unknown8, +12 UnknownC, +20 Unknown10, +24 Unknown14, +32 Unknown18, +36 Unknown1C, +44 Unknown20, +48 Unknown24, +60 Unknown30, +64 Unknown34, colours +8/+16/+28/+40 = Unknown54/58/5C/60, type bytes +68 ui_font_type_2, +72/+73/+74 ui_font_type_3/7/8.

behavior.basis: (decompile; the T values checked against the live palette cache)
behavior.text: the row's +60 (UIFontSet.Unknown30, 1.1) multiplies the threshold for runs flagged bold (GUITextNode_Draw: palette +64 = flag ? row+60 * row+4 : row+4), and +64 (UIFontSet.Unknown34, 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.5) is copied to the renderer's +9524 and used by SDFFontRenderer_EmitGlyph as the italic shear of the glyph quad, not as edge softness. [104] is never written here (stays 0, so the outline layer's cap is 0).

notes: docs/reference/fonts.md 'SDF text shader' lists the shader maths.

name: GUIFontSet_FontTypeForLanguage
purpose: Picks the UIFontType id of a font-set row for the current game language.

behavior.text: language code = *(int*)(qword_143CD9B10 + 8). Codes 1, 2, 3 (English, French, German) and a missing language object return row byte +68 = ui_font_type_2; code 4 (Simplified Chinese) returns +72 = ui_font_type_3; 5 (Traditional Chinese) +73 = ui_font_type_4; 6 (Korean) +74 = ui_font_type_5; every other code (0 = Japanese) returns the dword at +0 = ui_font_type.
the language codes are the index into the exe's name table japanese(0) english(1) french(2) german(3) schinese(4) tchinese(5) (strings at 0x1406FA8B8).
font set 60 (the hover name plate) = ui_font_type 7 (BO-ShinMGo, Japanese), ui_font_type_2 5 (Zilvertype Pro Bold); font sets 51 and 98 (level badge, chips) = type 6 (Jura SemiBold) in every column.

notes: The studio's label extractor reproduces this selection (English).

name: GUIFontSlotGroup_Destroy
purpose: Destructor: releases all slot references, frees both vectors, and drops the name key.

behavior.text: GUIFontSlotGroup_ReleaseAll(group) first.
vector B (begin +56): if non-null, freed via allocator (*(group+48)) vtable +24 with size (cap +72 - begin) & ~3; begin/end/cap = 0.
vector A (begin +24): likewise via allocator at +16 with size (cap +40 - begin) & ~0xF; zeroed.
if dword +8 != 0, UIName_ReleaseKey(g_UINameTable, key).
callers sub_1403E6038 (0x1403E6158), GUIFactory_FreeSlotGroup (0x1403FED59).

notes: Mirror of GUIFontSlotGroup_Init; does not free the object itself.

name: GUIFontSlotGroup_Init
purpose: Constructor of a per-widget group that owns slot references: sets two empty vectors, a name key and a trailing slot record.

behavior.text: +0 = global `Str` (vtable-ish / empty-string pointer), +8 dword = 0 (name key; released by Destroy via UIName_ReleaseKey).
vector A: allocator at +16 (= qword_143CDAA80[+32] or 0), begin +24, end +32, cap +40 all 0 (Destroy frees with a size masked to 16-byte multiples, so 16-byte elements).
vector B: allocator at +48, begin +56, end +64, cap +72 all 0 (4-byte elements: size masked to 4).

sub_1403DC1E8(group + 96) initialises an embedded member; then +80 qword, +88 word and +90 byte are stored from an uninitialised register (decompiler artefact, I: they are zeroed by the caller convention).
callers sub_1403E5B84 (0x1403E5BFE), GUIWidget_NewSlotGroup (0x1403FBAA4).

notes: Destroy sheet gives the element sizes. The +80..+90 stores should be re-read in the disassembly before being trusted.
open_questions: ? what the embedded object at +96 is. ? values stored at +80/+88/+90 (r9 / r10 leak in the decompile).

name: GUIFontSlotGroup_OnPartTableLoaded
callers: GUIFontSlotGroup_Poll (when g+84 != 0 and its slot is loaded)
callees: sub_1403DA594, sub_1403DA918, sub_1403DA30C, allocator vtable +16 / +24 (g+16), GUIOwners_PostEvent
purpose: Called by GUIFontSlotGroup_Poll once the group's part-table slot (g+84, the .utexpt file) is loaded: copies the table's part rectangles into the group's vector, requests the texture the table names and posts event 42.

behavior.text: record = sub_1403DA594(g_GUIFontSlots, g+84). Only when the dword at record+80 is exactly 1 (else g+88 = g+89 = 1 and g+90 = 1: done, nothing loaded).

blob = *(record+56). blob+0 = offset of the texture path string (relative to blob), blob+4 = offset of the entry array, blob+8 = entry count n. The part vector (g+24..+40) is cleared (end = begin) and grown to n * 16 bytes when needed.

for each of the n entries (20 bytes each, array at blob + blob[1]): the four dwords at entry +4..+19 (skipping the first dword) are appended as one 16-byte vector element. So part i of the group = the four ints of the .utexpt record i (the rectangle).

slot = sub_1403DA918(g_GUIFontSlots, blob + blob[0], ...) (request the texture by path, returns a slot id with type byte 2 and a 1-based index); the previous texture slot id g+80 is released with sub_1403DA30C when non-zero; g+80 = the returned slot id; g+89 = 1; when the returned id is 0 g+88 = 1 (nothing to wait for).
event {42, 0, 0, 0} with ev+16 = *g is posted to the owners at g+96.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F40AC). This is the place where the atlas rectangles of a .utexpt (e.g. ui_job_tree_uitx.utexpt) enter the runtime: the vector built here is what UIImage part lookups index (part index = part - 1 per the UIB notes; the whole-texture rectangle then overwrites element 0 in GUIFontSlotGroup_OnTextureLoaded, which is I). Entry layout of the file (+0 dword not copied, +4..+19 four ints) is V from the copy loop; which of the four is x / y / w / h is not read here.
open_questions: ? the meaning of the skipped first dword of each 20-byte entry. ? x / y / w / h order of the four ints (the studio reads them as [x, y, w, h] from the file).

name: GUIFontSlotGroup_OnTextureLoaded
callers: GUIFontSlotGroup_Poll (when g+80 != 0, g+88 == 0 and sub_1403DA3EC says the slot is loaded)
callees: sub_1403DA594, GUIFontSlots_GetSlot, UIPartRef_GetTextureSize, sub_14006635C, sub_1403F43C8, GUIOwners_PostEvent
purpose: Called by GUIFontSlotGroup_Poll once the group's texture slot (g+80) is loaded: stores the whole-texture rectangle as the first entry of the group's part vector, marks the group loaded and posts event 41 to its owners.

behavior.text: record = sub_1403DA594(g_GUIFontSlots, g+80) (the slot record of the id at g+80, null when the slot's count is 0). Everything below happens only when the dword at record+80 (read with an atomic add of 0) is exactly 1; otherwise g+88 = 1 and g+90 = 1 and nothing else (the group is marked loaded / finished without data).

size = UIPartRef_GetTextureSize(GUIFontSlots_GetSlot(g_GUIFontSlots, g+80)); a 16-byte entry {0, 0, width, height} (qword 0, then the two size dwords) is written over the first element of the part vector (g+24 begin, g+32 end, g+40 cap) when it is non-empty, else it is pushed back (grown with sub_14006635C when full).

g+88 = 1; when the dependant dword list (g+56 / g+64) is not empty sub_1403F43C8(g) runs; then event {41, 0, 0, 0} with ev+16 = *g (the group's name string pointer) is posted: GUIOwners_PostEvent(g+96, 0, ev).

the dword at record+80 is the texture object's reference count, so 'exactly 1' reads as 'only the slot table itself still holds it', i.e. the load finished; the else branch is the failed / shared case. Not tested live.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F3FAC);  the only caller found is the poll. Group layout read here (V): +0 name key {char *, id}, +16 allocator, +24..+40 part rectangle vector (16-byte entries), +48 allocator, +56..+72 dependant slot-id vector (dwords), +80 texture slot id, +84 part-table slot id, +88 loaded flag, +89 part table is a type-3 slot, +90 finished flag, +96 four owner widget ids. Entry 0 being the whole texture is I (it is overwritten only when the part table was filled first).
open_questions: ? what sub_1403F43C8 does (dependant groups kick-off). ? the exact meaning of record+80 == 1. ? the order of the two loaders in practice (part table first, then texture, is what the poll code implies).

name: GUIFontSlotGroup_Poll
purpose: Per-frame poll of one texture / font group: once its slots are loaded it runs the finishing steps and returns whether the group is complete.

behavior.text: slot id g+84 (type byte 3 with g+89 set looks in the type-3 vector of g_GUIFontSlots, +112 / +120 stride 16, loaded when byte +12 and +13 are set; otherwise sub_1403DA3EC) loaded -> sub_1403F40AC(g) (copies the group's entries from the slot, grows the vector at g+24, not read further).
slot id g+80 loaded and g+88 = 0 -> sub_1403F3FAC(g): reads the texture size (sub_1403DCA04), pushes {0, size} to the entry vector at g+24, g+88 = 1, posts event xmmword_140723480.

when g+90 (all dependants done) is set returns g+88. Otherwise the dword list g+56..+64 is walked: every id must be loaded; if all are, g+90 = 1; the return value is g+88 (0 when a dependant is missing).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F3EA4). 37761 hits per 4 s because it is polled for every group every frame. It also fills the per-group size entry that UIImage_ResolvePart / UIImage_DrawTiled read (texture size), but only once.

name: GUIFontSlotGroup_ReleaseAll
purpose: Releases every slot id the group holds (+80, +84 and every dword of the vector at +56) with GUIFontSlots_Release and resets the state.

behavior.text: slot id +80: GUIFontSlots_Release(g_GUIFontSlots, id), then +80 = 0; slot id +84: same, +84 = 0; for each dword of the vector +56..+64: Release then the dword = 0.
then word +88 = 0, byte +90 = 0 and +32 = +24 (the 16-byte vector is emptied, its end pointer reset to begin; elements are not individually released here).
returns the old +24.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F3DFC). GuiImage_SetIconById calls it before setting a new icon, so changing a Job Tree icon releases the old image slot first.
open_questions: ? what slot +80 holds versus +84 (+84 is the image slot id set by GUIFontSlotGroup_SetImageByName).

name: GUIFontSlotGroup_SetImageByName
purpose: Acquires the kind-3 image slot for name and stores it as the group's image slot; on failure sets the failed flags.

behavior.text: id = GUIFontSlots_AcquireImage(g_GUIFontSlots, name, a3). id != 0: +84 = id, byte +89 = 0; when the element at +8 is empty (id dword +8 == 0) UIName_SetKey(g, name); returns 1.
id == 0: word +88 = 0x0101 (bytes +88 and +89 both 1, the 'failed' flags) and returns the (zero) result.
any previous slot id at +84 is not released here (the caller released via GUIFontSlotGroup_ReleaseAll).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F3DAC).
open_questions: ? the meaning of the two flag bytes +88 / +89 (loaded / failed?).

name: GUIFontSlots_AcquireImage
proto: unsigned int GUIFontSlots_AcquireImage(GUIFontSlots *slots, const char *name, int a3)
callees: sub_1403DBB00, sub_1403DB390, sub_1403DA4C0, sub_140037CA4, sub_140091124, GUISlotVec16_Insert (sub_1403EE77C)
purpose: Gets a kind-3 (image) slot for a name: reuses an existing one (refcount +1) or requests the resource and appends a new record.

behavior.text: when slots+424 != 0 the name is first translated through sub_1403DBB00 (table 125, key 2000, column dword at slots+424); a failed translation keeps the original name.

sub_1403DB390 finds an existing record: found = sub_1403DA4C0 refcount +1 and the id returned. Otherwise a 32-byte local {resource ptr from sub_140091124(qword_143CD9B88, name, hash, 0, ..), refcount 1, +12 u16 flag 0} is inserted into the vector at slots+104 (GUISlotVec16_Insert, 16 bytes copied) and (index + 1) | 0x3000000 is returned.
the hash comes from sub_140037CA4(buf, name) (its first dword).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DB280). sub_1403DB6B8 maps a numeric icon key to a slot: keys 50..71 and 1100..1265 go to sub_1403DB420 / sub_1403DB5B4, other keys resolve a name with sub_1403DB140 and call this.
open_questions: ? the kind-3 record layout beyond +0 / +8 / +12 (written by the loader).

name: GUIFontSlots_AcquireTexturePart
callees: sub_1403DB0EC, sub_1403DBB00, sub_1403DAB60, sub_1403DA4C0, sub_140037C84 / sub_140037C04 (hash), sub_140091124, sub_140011750 (alloc), GUISlotVec32_Insert (sub_1403EE918)
purpose: Gets a kind-2 slot (texture part) for a path: reuses an existing record with the same name (refcount +1), otherwise requests the resource, appends a new 32-byte record with refcount 1 and returns its id.

behavior.text: first sub_1403DB0EC(slots, buf, a3, path) copies the path (256 bytes) into a local buffer, rewriting '_2k_' to '_4k_' when present, and returns whether the path had _2k_ or _4k_ (flag v7). When slots+424 != 0 the buffer is then translated through sub_1403DBB00 (table 125, key 2001, column index = the dword at slots+424).

sub_1403DAB60(slots, buf) scans the kind-2 vector for a record with refcount != 0 whose name string (the resource object's +24, or the empty string) equals buf; when found sub_1403DA4C0 increments its refcount and the function returns the existing id (the value in r11 after the call, not a Hex-Rays variable).

otherwise a name hash is computed (a rolling hash with the xor constant 0x50C5D1F over the lower-cased path, '\\' mapped to '/', seed 0x811C9DC5 = -2128831035 for an empty path), the resource is requested with sub_140091124(qword_143CD9B88, buf, hash, 0, out), a 40-byte auxiliary object is allocated through the allocator at qword_143CDAA80 + 8 (zeroed, byte +35 = the 2k/4k flag) and a 32-byte record {+0 resource ptr, +16 aux ptr, +24 u16 refcount = 1, +26 = 0, +28 loaded = 0} is inserted with GUISlotVec32_Insert at slots+72.
returns (index + 1) | 0x2000000 for a new record.

notes: Slot id layout (V, from the decode in GUIFontSlots_Release / _GetResource): id = (index + 1) | (kind << 24); kind 0 = plain slot vector (16-byte records at slots+16, refcount u16 at rec+8, loaded byte rec+12), kind 1 = vector at slots+48 (16-byte records, refcount rec+8), kind 2 = texture-part vector at slots+80 (32-byte records, refcount rec+24, loaded byte rec+28), kind 3 = image vector at slots+112 (16-byte records, refcount rec+8). The resource pointer is the first qword of the record. The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DA918). The call from GUITextNode_PlaceIcon passes the icon slot's name path from the slot record (+56).
open_questions: ? what sub_140091124 does (resource handle create or find; it returns a pointer whose +24 is the name). ? the hash function body (sub_140037C04). ? the meaning of the 2001 / 2000 translation rows of table 125 (language / platform path override?).

name: GUIFontSlots_FindImageByName
purpose: Linear search of the image records for one whose name equals name; returns an image id (1-based index | 0x03000000) or 0.

behavior.text: image vector: begin slots+112, end slots+120, 16-byte entries (count = (end-begin)>>4); empty returns 0.
an entry is considered only if its word at +8 != 0 and its qword at +0 (object pointer) != 0.
name pointer = the qword at obj + 24 if non-zero, else the global empty string `Str`; compared byte by byte (case-sensitive strcmp) with name.
on match returns (index + 1) | 0x3000000; no match returns 0.
callers sub_1403DA654 (0x1403DA727), GUIFontSlots_AcquireImage (0x1403DB2E5).

notes: Sibling of GUIFontSlots_FindPartByName (kind 3 images vs parts).
open_questions: ? what the word at entry+8 means (used as an 'in use' flag; I).

name: GUIFontSlots_FindPartByName
purpose: Linear search of the kind-2 (texture part) records for a live record whose resource name equals name; returns its id or 0.

behavior.text: iterates the 32-byte records at slots+80 / +88. A record counts when u16 rec+24 != 0 and the qword rec+0 is non-null; its name is the C string at *(rec+0)+24, or the shared empty string Str when that pointer is 0.
byte-wise strcmp with name; the first equal record returns (index + 1) | 0x2000000. No match returns 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DAB60). Case-sensitive compare.

name: GUIFontSlots_GetResource
callers: GUITextNode_PlaceIcon, GUITextNode_Draw, GUIWidget_AllResourcesLoaded, sub_1403F3C3C, sub_1403F3FAC, sub_1403F40AC, sub_1403F43C8, sub_1403FC440, sub_1400F4F20
purpose: Returns the resource pointer (first qword of the record) of a live slot, or 0 when the id is bad or the refcount is 0.

behavior.text: same id decode as GUIFontSlots_Release. kind 0: returns *(qword *)rec when u16 rec+8 != 0, else 0. kinds 1 and 3: same with the 16-byte records; kind 2: 32-byte records, refcount at rec+24.
bad index or unknown kind returns 0; a refcount of 0 returns 0 (so a released slot reads as empty even though the record is kept).
pure read; the caller in GUITextNode_PlaceIcon uses the result to test the record's own refcount (+80 of the pointed-to object) for exactly 1 before replacing the icon texture handle.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DA594). Different from GUIFontSlots_GetSlot (0x1403DB240), which is the lookup that GUITextNode_Draw uses by key; not compared here.

name: GUIFontSlots_GetSlot
purpose: Resolves a texture slot id to its record pointer: ids carry type 0x02 in the top byte and a 1-based index in the low 24 bits.

behavior.text: idx = (id & 0xFFFFFF) - 1; requires (id & 0xFF000000) == 0x02000000.
bounds: idx < (slots[+88] - slots[+80]) >> 5 (32-byte entries; vector begin +80, end +88).
result = the qword at +16 of entry idx (entries are 32 bytes, array begin pointer at slots+80), i.e. the record pointer at entry+16; otherwise returns 0.
callers sub_1403E3134, sub_1403E9344, GUIFontSlots_GetTextureRect, UIImage_ResolvePart, GUIFontSlotGroup_OnTextureLoaded.
id 0 gives idx = -1 which fails the type check, so 0 is the null id.

notes: Type bytes seen in this chunk: 0x02 textures here, 0x03 images (GUIFontSlots_FindImageByName).
open_questions: none beyond the record field meanings (see GUITextureSlot_Init).

name: GUIFontSlots_GetTextureRect
purpose: Writes the full-texture rectangle {0, 0, width, height} of a slot's texture into out; leaves out unchanged when the slot does not exist.

behavior.text: slot = GUIFontSlots_GetSlot(g_GUIFontSlots, slotId); non-null: UIPartRef_GetTextureSize(slot, &size) then out = {dword 0 = 0, dword 4 = 0, qword 8 = size (width, height)}.
returns the slot pointer / out. Hex-Rays loses the out pointer (it shows as a register); the disassembly stores through the hidden return-value pointer.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403E9590). The prototype is partly I because of the lost out pointer.
open_questions: ? whether out is the first argument (rcx) as assumed; verify in the disassembly before relying on the name.

name: GUIFontSlots_IsLoaded
purpose: True when the slot exists, has a non-zero refcount and its loaded byte is set (the texture / image behind it finished loading).

behavior.text: same id decode as GUIFontSlots_Release. For kind 0 / 1 / 3 the test is (u16 rec+8 != 0) and (byte rec+12 != 0); for kind 2 it is (u16 rec+24 != 0) and (byte rec+28 != 0).
returns 1 when both hold, else 0. An out-of-range id or unknown kind returns 0 (the local result is initialised to 1 but only returned on the success path).
pure read, no side effects.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DA3EC). Who sets the loaded byte (+12 / +28) was not traced.
open_questions: ? the writer of the loaded byte (probably the resource-load completion callback).

name: GUIFontSlots_Release
callers: GUIFontSlotGroup_ReleaseAll (3 sites), GUITextNode_Layout (end of layout, per icon reference), sub_1403DCF00, sub_1403F3BFC, sub_1403F40AC, sub_1403F43C8, sub_1403FCFEC, sub_1400F4EC4
purpose: Drops one reference from a slot of the GUI slot registry (g_GUIFontSlots): decrements the record's u16 refcount, never below 0, and never frees anything.

behavior.text: index = (slotId & 0xFFFFFF) - 1, kind = slotId & 0xFF000000. kind 0 reads the vector at slots+16 / +24 (16-byte records, refcount at rec+8), kind 0x1000000 the vector at +48 / +56 (refcount rec+8), kind 0x2000000 the vector at +80 / +88 (32-byte records, refcount rec+24), kind 0x3000000 the vector at +112 / +120 (refcount rec+8).

the index is bounds-checked against the vector size; an out-of-range id or an unknown kind returns without effect. If the refcount is non-zero it is decremented by 1 (a u16 store); at 0 nothing happens (saturating).

no destructor, texture release or list removal runs here; the resource stays in the record with refcount 0. The slot is reused later by the insert helpers (they take the first record whose first qword is 0, see GUISlotVec16_Insert), so a refcount-0 record is only 'free' for lookups (they skip refcount 0 records).

notes: Slot id layout (V, from the decode in GUIFontSlots_Release / _GetResource): id = (index + 1) | (kind << 24); kind 0 = plain slot vector (16-byte records at slots+16, refcount u16 at rec+8, loaded byte rec+12), kind 1 = vector at slots+48 (16-byte records, refcount rec+8), kind 2 = texture-part vector at slots+80 (32-byte records, refcount rec+24, loaded byte rec+28), kind 3 = image vector at slots+112 (16-byte records, refcount rec+8). The resource pointer is the first qword of the record. The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DA30C). The sibling that increments is sub_1403DA4C0 (same decode, +1, returns the old count).
open_questions: ? who finally frees the resource of a refcount-0 record (not traced; sub_1403D8D1C does the same for element records and frees there).

name: GUIFontTable_GetSetRow
purpose: Returns a pointer to the 80-byte UIFontSet row for a font-set key; out of range falls back to row 0, creating a default row if the table is empty.

behavior.text: count = (table[3] - table[2]) / 80; if key < count the result is table[2] + 80*key.

otherwise, if the vector is empty (table[2] == table[3]) it builds a UIFontSetRow_Default on the stack and appends it (same grow-or-copy 80-byte append as Load, via sub_1403EEECC when end == table[4]).
out-of-range returns table[2], i.e. row 0.
callers GUITextNode_Layout (0x1403DD0C3) and GUITextNode_Draw (0x1403EA229): the key is the text node's font set field (+300 per the Copy sheet; I).

notes: Draw and Layout both read per-set parameters (threshold, widths, colours; see UIFontSetRow_Default) from the returned row.
open_questions: ? which row fields Layout vs Draw consume (not read here).

name: GUIFontTable_Load
purpose: Rebuilds the in-memory UIFontSet row vector from UI table id 21: each 80-byte row starts from UIFontSetRow_Default and is then overwritten field by field from the source record.

behavior.text: table[3] = table[2] (end = begin: the vector is emptied first). Vector members: begin table[2], end table[3], cap table[4] (the `a1+1` base is passed to the grow helper sub_1403EEECC).
count = sub_1403DBBBC(21); for i in 0..count-1, src = UITable_GetRow(21, i); dst row is built on the stack (80 bytes) with UIFontSetRow_Default first.

field copy (src offset -> dst offset): +4 -> +0, +8 -> +4, +12 -> +12... precisely: src dwords 1,2,3 -> dst +0, +4, +12; src +84..+87 (4 bytes) -> dst +8; src dword 4 -> dst +20, dword 5 -> +24; dword 22 -> +16(low of 2nd qword group), 23 -> +20 region, 24 -> +24 region as decompiled (stack-temporary layout, see raw decompile); src +56, +72, +76, +80 bytes -> dst bytes at +68..+74 area.
if end == cap it calls the grow helper sub_1403EEECC(table+1, end, &tmp); else copies five 16-byte blocks to *end and adds 80 to table[3].
callers: sub_1403D5934 (0x1403D5A25) and a data ref 0x143D41560.

the column to field mapping above is only approximate: the decompiler merged the stack temporary into overlapping xmm stores. Treat exact offsets as ? until the per-row layout is read from disassembly.

notes: Row size 80 is confirmed by both Load (add 80) and GetSetRow (/80 and *80). The UIFontSet table id is 21 (V: literal 21 in both calls).
open_questions: ? exact per-column mapping (see behaviour 3). ? what the source row size is (largest src offset read is +87).

name: GuiImage_SetIconById
proto: void GuiImage_SetIconById(GuiImage *img, int iconKey, void *parent, char keepFlag)
purpose: Binds an icon image, chosen by its Icon table key, to a UI image object; used by many screens that show job, command or ability icons.

behavior.text: a non-null parent replaces the image's stored parent node (+24); with no parent stored it skips the name step.
otherwise it writes the image's name key (string at +56, through UIName_Key) into the parent node's name field (+232).
if iconKey differs from the cached key at +128 it (re)creates the image node at +40 from the layer at +16 and the node name at +96.
for iconKey > 0 it builds the path with Icon_FormatPath(iconKey, buf, 0, 256), i.e. the plain icon path, not the texture-part form, and binds it to the node.
on success it sets the changed flag at +132, caches the key at +128, then copies the Icon row's dword at +12 (the sheet's `UnknownC`) into the parent node at +248.
when keepFlag is 0 it clears the parent node's byte at +144.
has more than a dozen callers in the UI layer.

notes: The Icon table is registry id 118.
open_questions: What the Icon row dword at +12 controls on the node.

name: GUIInput_IsPointerOverLayer
purpose: Tells whether the mouse pointer is over a widget and hits a target tagged with the given id.

behavior.text: returns 0 unless the UI core's pointer-enabled byte (g_GUICore+1909) is set.
maps the pointer (g_GUICore +1880/+1884) through the layer transform of the widget's layer (w+60) with GUILayerXform_MapPointFloat, then hit-tests with GUIWidget_HitTestPoint.
returns 1 when one of the hits has byte +143 equal to `layerId`.
name and the meaning of byte +143 (layer or group id) are inferred; the function guards wheel scrolling of text/list gadgets.

notes: The stock wheel handler requires the pointer over its gadget through this check.

name: GUIInputQueue_Pop
callers: GUICore_OnInputState, sub_1403D6098 and two vtable entries
purpose: Pops the oldest 68-byte input record of queue `port` (vector at q + 32 * port) into out; false when empty.

behavior.text: v = q + 32 * port; begin = v+8, end = v+16; begin = end -> 0. Otherwise out = the 68 bytes at begin (4 x 16 + 4), memmove the rest down by 68 and end -= 68; returns 1.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DC32C). 120 hits per 4 s. A FIFO implemented as erase-front (O(n)); order is strictly first in, first out.
open_questions: ? Layout of the 68-byte record (I: button / stick state).

name: GUILayer_ApplyEffects
proto: __int64 GUILayer_ApplyEffects(UILayer *layer, unsigned char targetType, __int64 a3, __int64 a4, __int64 a5, __m128i *rect, __m128i *clampRect)
callees: GUILayer_EffectPass0, sub_1403B5170, sub_1403AEE0C, sub_1403B53C8, UIBlur_Run, GUILayer_CopyToTarget, GUILayer_BlurShadowPass, GUILayer_BlitFinal, GUILayer_GlowPass, UILayer_GetTarget
purpose: Runs the enabled effect passes of one finished layer in a fixed order, ping-ponging between two scratch render targets, then draws the layer's own pixels and finally the +178 effect group.

behavior.text: order: +489 (GUILayer_EffectPass0), +320 (sub_1403B5170), +484 (sub_1403AEE0C), +486 (sub_1403B53C8), the +176 group (blur with radius +180, UIBlur_Run mode flag 1), the +177 group (GUILayer_CopyToTarget + GUILayer_BlurShadowPass, skipped when +486), the plain layer blit (GUILayer_BlitFinal) and last the +178 group (GUILayer_GlowPass, skipped when +486). Source and destination target indices (26 / 27, 29 replacing 26) swap after every pass.

the swap bookkeeping: v7 = the render-target index holding the layer's pixels so far (starts 26), v11 = the next destination (starts 27). +489 (and +492 == 0 or (int)layer+36 >= 0): GUILayer_EffectPass0(layer, state, target, 27, 26), then v7 = 27, v11 = 29. +320: sub_1403B5170(layer, state, rect, target, v11, v7), then v7 and v11 exchange and a v11 equal to 26 becomes 29. +484: only when layer+80 == 0 is sub_1403AEE0C called (with v11, v7, and the flag +492 == 0); the exchange happens either way. +486: sub_1403B53C8(layer, state, target, v11, v7), then the exchange. +176: UIBlur_Run(layer, target, type, 30, 1, radius +180, rect, clamp, v11, v7, 28, -1), then the exchange. After an exchange the index 26 is replaced by 29 (for +320 only on the new v11; for +484, +486 and +176 on both v7 and v11), so 26 is never reused as a destination.

+177 and not +486: GUILayer_CopyToTarget(layer, state, rect, target, junk, v7) copies the current scratch RT into the shadow scratch, then GUILayer_BlurShadowPass(layer, state, targetType, rect, clamp, target); there is no exchange after them (the layer's pixels stay in RT v7). The fourth argument of both is target = UILayer_GetTarget(layer).

then the sort key is set to 0x6AC07600 and GUILayer_BlitFinal(layer, state, target, the rectangle at layer+240, junk, v7) draws RT v7 onto the target; last, when +178 is set and +486 is clear, GUILayer_GlowPass(layer, state, targetType, rect, clamp, target, v11, junk, junk, v7).

flag bytes: layer+176 / +177 / +178 = BuildRecord record+152 / +153 / +154 (layer+k = record+(k-24); the layer array base is r + 303480 + 592 * index), i.e. +176 = the single float group (comp+96 -> ctx+112, radius layer+180), +177 = the drop-shadow group (comp+120 -> ctx+136: strength +184, radius +188, offset +192 / +196, colour +456..+464), +178 = the glow group (comp+172 -> ctx+156: strength +200, radius +204, colour +468.., mode +480).

behavior.basis: (live read of the running Job Tree, 2026-10-29: layer bytes and census/trace hits)
behavior.text: the Job Tree uses the +177 group: its title layer has +177 = 1, +176 = 0, +178 = 0; GUILayer_BlurShadowPass and GUILayer_CopyToTarget are hit for that layer while sub_1403B5170, sub_1403AEE0C, sub_1403B53C8 and GUILayer_GlowPass are not (see also GUILayer_EffectPass0, which records the same layer's flags).

notes: The +178 group is the component glow (flag +178, strength +200, radius +204, colour +468.., mode +480) by the constant 24 offset to the BuildRecord page. Of the +176 / +177 groups the Job Tree uses +177, the drop shadow (live read above).
open_questions: ? what the +489 / +320 / +484 / +486 groups draw (their passes were not decompiled here). ? where layer+36 / +492 (the source-layer reference of the +489 pass) are set.

name: GUILayer_BlitFinal
proto: __int64 GUILayer_BlitFinal(UILayer *layer, __m128i *cmd, __int64 target, __m128i *rect, int a5, int dstTex)
purpose: Draws the layer's own pixels onto its parent with the layer blend mode (the pass after the +176 / +177 effects).

behavior.text: copies the rectangle into the command, sets selector digit 0 from layer+32 and digit 1 from whether any of the three offset vectors at +120..+140 is non-zero, binds the texture slots +64 / +66 (and +320's texture when enabled), blend type = layer+8 << 6, and queues a 96-byte command.

destination = the entry at g_Renderer + 800 x (byte target + 86) + 23736 (row slot 2, the frame target), stored at state+96 with its +40 member at state+144; the source texture of both texture slots is RT[a6] (g_Renderer + 40 x a6 + 20832, +40 member) with a6 = the index GUILayer_ApplyEffects passes (26, RT 26 the layer content, for a layer with no pass that moved it).

the blend word stored after the program apply is 2013397009 = 0x78020011 (enabled, source ONE, destination ZERO, add, alpha the same, write mask 0xF, decoded with the BlendDesc_FromWords field layout). The program's pixel shader writes no render-target output but the UAV u0 (the frame target), so the compositing arithmetic is in the shader: see the program LayerBlit and the behavior LayerBlitOverFrameTarget.

the quad is vertex slot (layer+8) << 6 of the layer quad buffer (stride 16): the layer's integer screen rectangle (rect - atlas offset), uv = position / target size; the shader adds the atlas offset to the uv, so it reads texel (pixel + atlas offset) of RT 26.
the sort key in force when the command is submitted is the caller's (GUILayer_ApplyEffects sets 0x6AC07600, pass 59), so the blits of an atlas page run after all the draws of the page.

name: GUILayer_BlurEffect
proto: void GUILayer_BlurEffect(UILayer *layer, __int64 a2, __int64 a3, __int64 a4, float *renderSize)
purpose: Whole-layer blur (the effect with radius at layer+500): copies the layer region, blurs it with UIBlur_Run and blits the result.

behavior.text: runs only when |layer+500| > 0; copies the layer rectangle (+208..+220) into target 27 (sub_1403AC620 / sub_1403ABEDC), builds the normalised clamp rectangle with half-pixel insets, calls UIBlur_Run(radius = |+500|, ..., 59, ...), then sub_1403B5664 and GUILayer_BlitFinal.

notes: Not the component glow (that is GUILayer_GlowPass).

name: GUILayer_BlurShadowPass
proto: char GUILayer_BlurShadowPass(UILayer *layer, __int64 stateCtx, unsigned char targetType, int *rect, __m128i *clamp, RenderTarget *target)
purpose: Second step of the +177 (drop shadow) effect group: blurs the silhouette in RT 3 by the radius at layer+188, then draws it onto the layer's target with selector #10 program 1, which darkens the target by the shadow strength and tint and adds the shadow alpha.

behavior.text: sets the sort key at state+8 = ((layer+12 & 0x1FF | ((layer+16 & 0x3F | targetType << 18) << 15) | 0x6AC02000) << 10) (targetType 1 treated as 0), runs UIBlur_Run(layer, target, targetType, 16, 1, radius = float layer+188, rect, clamp, 3, 3, 28, -1), then re-sets the key with the constant 0x6AC07600.

in the UIBlur_Run call 16 is the base of the sub-ordinal added into the sort key ((a4 + k) & 0x3F terms), 3 / 3 are the output and source render-target indices (RT 3 in place, as GUILayer_GlowPass passes output and source), 28 is the scratch index.
shifts the clamp rectangle in state+80..92 by minus the integer parts of layer+224 / +228 ((int) truncation toward zero) so it is in screen instead of atlas coordinates.

destination = the entry at 800 * (byte target+86) + g_Renderer + 23736, stored at state+96 with its +40 member at state+144 (the render target the draw writes to: the layer's parent target, the same one GUILayer_BlitFinal draws into afterwards); the fourth argument is the render target object from UILayer_GetTarget, not a layer.

source = RT 3 (g_Renderer + 20952, its +40 member) bound as the texture at state + 8 * (short layer+64) + 1608; the technique's default sampler words are copied as in GUILayer_CopyToTarget; the draw uses selector #10 (*(*(g_Renderer+37936) + 80)) with ShaderSelector_Apply(selector, state, 1): program index 1; no permutation digit is set in this function.

vertex buffers: state+136 = the manager object's element [1060], state+200 = the +40 member of element [1062], stride 16 (state+208) and byte offset (layer+8) << 6 (state+212): this layer's 64-byte quad; state+124 = (& 0xFFC06FFF) | 0x6000, state+6016 = 0; a 96-byte command from sub_140069A38(state, 4, 96) with +8 = 4, packed and submitted.

the only writes to the context's sampler words (+5704 + 4 * slot) in this function are the technique's own default words: the loop over the slot id list at technique+160 and the word list at technique+168 (count at technique+108), each stored & 0x7FFFFFFF, before ShaderSelector_Apply. It never writes slot 14 (g_Sampler) or slot 15.

the selector #10 technique lists slots 13 (ccc_lln_sampler) and 16 (ccc_lln_sampler_tMaskBuffer), both with the word 0x26A = clamp on all axes, min / mag linear, mip point. Slot names: see NameSlotTable_Lookup.
pixel shader 035E50 samples its source (T0) through g_Sampler, slot 14, which this pass does not set.

the word at context + 0x1680 (= +5704 + 4 * 14, slot 14) is 0 on all four Job Tree shadow passes, i.e. the default sampler word (0 at runtime, Sampler_DescFromWord): point filter, WRAP, MinLOD = MaxLOD = 0.

slot 14 still holds the default word because the shadow commands are packed during GUILayer_Composite (UIRender_SubmitFrame), after RenderContext_ResetFrame wrote the default into every sampler slot at the start of the frame and before UICommandRing_Flush replays the UI draws (UIRender_ApplyDrawState writes g_Sampler per UI draw, UICommandRing_Flush writes the default to slots 14 and 15). Basis: the call order in UIRender_SubmitFrame and the live trace above; the order against RenderContext_ResetFrame was not re-read here.
with shadow offsets 1.6 and 1.333 the blurred alpha lands 2 px and 1 px away from the layer pixels.
consequence: the blurred alpha is point-sampled (not bilinear), so the texel read for output pixel x is floor(x + 0.5 - offset). Basis: the slot 14 word above and the two captures.

the quad: element [1062] (byte offset 8496) of the UIRenderer object at g_Renderer + 37936 (the object UIRender_SubmitFrame is a virtual method of) is a buffer object that UIRender_SubmitFrame maps, storing the mapped pointer as element [1065] (offset 8520); GUILayer_FillQuadBuffers fills element [1065], at record 4 * (layer+8), with the layer rectangle moved by minus the atlas offset (position = rect - atlas offset, uv = that position / the target size g_Renderer+6568 / +6572). The vertex shader adds the shadow offset to the position, so the shadow is drawn over (rect - atlas offset) + offset.
nothing outside (rect - atlas offset) + offset can be darkened by this pass, because no pixel outside that moved quad is rasterised. Basis: the quad geometry above.

the vertex shader 035438 passes the uv through and adds cb12.zw (the shadow offset in pixels, layer+192 / +196) to the quad position before the pixel-to-clip matrix (rows 4-7). The pixel shader 035E50 samples A = alpha of T0 at uv + cb34.zw (atlas offset in UV) and computes s = saturate(cb13.x * A) (cb13.x = layer+184, the shadow strength); with the distance mask off (cb20.x = 0) it rewrites the UAV target: rgb = rgb * ((1 - s) + cb31.rgb * A), a = s + a * (1 - s), cb31.rgb = the shadow colour (layer+456..+464). With a black colour this is a plain black 'over' composite of strength s under the layer.

behavior.basis: (live read of the running game's selector, 2026-10-29, same walk)
behavior.text: selector #10 program 1 = vertex shader 035438 + pixel shader 035E50.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: GUILayer_BlurShadowPass). The +177 group is the component drop shadow (flag +177, strength +184, radius +188, offset +192 / +196, colour +456..+464); layer+k = BuildRecord record+(k-24). Pixel exact: the atlas -> screen offset is truncated to integers. Direction: the per-target entry at 800 * byte + 23736 is the destination (the render target) and RT 3 the sampled source.
open_questions: ? the blend / raster words of program entry 1 (not read; the pixel shader writes the target through a typed UAV, so the fixed-function blend is probably unused). ? the exact UIBlur_Run argument meanings (a4 = 16, a5 = 1).

name: GUILayer_BoundsAdd32
proto: int GUILayer_BoundsAdd32(UIRenderer *r, int a, int b)
purpose: Saturating signed 32-bit addition (a + b clamped to INT_MIN .. INT_MAX).

behavior.text: a >= 0 and b >= 0: when 0x7FFFFFFF - a < b returns 0x7FFFFFFF else a + b. a < 0 and b < 0: when (int)(0x80000000 - b) > a returns 0x80000000 else a + b. Mixed signs: a + b.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403E9560). 1044 hits per 4 s. The first argument (renderer) is unused. A simulator can use plain int addition unless coordinates reach about 2^31.

name: GUILayer_BoundsToRect
purpose: Converts the double-precision draw bounds accumulated in the renderer (r+152..+176) into the integer rectangle {left, top, right, bottom} of the draws since the last flush.

behavior.text: left = (int)clamp(r+152), top = (int)clamp(r+160), right = (int)clamp(r[+168] + 1.0 - DBL_MIN), bottom = (int)clamp(r[+176] + 1.0 - DBL_MIN); clamp = [-2147483648, 2147483647]; the casts are truncating (cvttsd2si). The - DBL_MIN is below double resolution, so right = trunc(maxX + 1) and bottom = trunc(maxY + 1).
for non-negative coordinates this is floor(min) for the left / top edge and floor(max) + 1 for the right / bottom edge (an exact integer maximum still grows by one pixel).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DF8D8). The four doubles are filled by UIRender_AccumulateQuadBounds (sub_1403DF71C): +152 min x, +160 min y, +168 max x, +176 max y over the four transformed corners of every quad.

name: GUILayer_BuildRecord
purpose: Fills one 592-byte offscreen-layer record from a component draw context: size, blend, colour transform and every enabled effect.

behavior.text: layer records live at r + 303504 + 592 * index (512 slots); +0/+2 = target size (r+184, r+188); +8 = blend type; +154 (byte) = glow enabled (ctx flag +156 AND the renderer feature byte r+606623); +176 (float) = glow strength = ctx+144; +180 (float) = glow radius = min(ctx scale x, y) * ctx+140; +444/+448/+452 = glow colour bytes / 255 (ctx+148..150); +456 = glow mode (ctx+152: 0 -> 3, 1 -> 1, 2 -> 2, any other value -> 3).

the layer object that GUILayer_ApplyEffects and its passes receive is the record minus 24 bytes: for every slot GUIRenderer_ResetFrame initialises the index dword at r + 303492 + 592 * i (= layer+12 with layer = r + 303480 + 592 * i) and the target pointer at r + 304064 + 592 * i (= layer+584, the field UILayer_GetTarget reads), so layer+k = record+(k-24): record+152 / +153 / +154 = layer+176 / +177 / +178 and record+432..+440 = layer+456..+464. The ctx scale x / y used below are the floats at ctx+528 / +532 (the code indexes them as int elements 132 / 133); 'min scale' = the smaller of the two.

drop-shadow group (ctx flag +136 AND the renderer feature byte r+606624): record+153 = 1 (layer+177), record+160 = the raw dword ctx+120 (strength, layer+184), record+164 = fabs(min scale * float ctx+116) (blur radius, layer+188), record+168 / +172 = ctx+124 * scale x / ctx+128 * scale y (offset in pixels, layer+192 / +196), record+432 / +436 / +440 = bytes ctx+132 / +133 / +134 divided by 255 (colour rgb, layer+456..+464). With the flag clear, only record+153 = 0 is written.

other effect groups copied the same way, with their gates: colour transform ctx flag +76: record+64 / +80 <- the multiply / add blocks ctx+44 / ctx+60 (defaults 1,1,1,1 and 0 when clear); offsets group ctx flag +104 (no feature byte): three float pairs ctx+80.. each scaled by scale x / y into record+96 / +104 / +112 (layer+120 / +128 / +136); single float group ctx flag +112 AND r+606622: record+152 = 1 (layer+176), record+156 = min scale * ctx+108 (layer+180, the blur radius GUILayer_ApplyEffects passes to UIBlur_Run); ctx+178 group with r+606627: record+462 = 1 (layer+486) and the data block at record+480..+531 (three 16-byte blocks and a dword); ctx flag +184: record+4 = 1 and record+476 = min scale * ctx+180 (layer+500); clip ctx+296: four edge entries at record+232.. ; ctx+409: record+465 = 1, record+466 = ctx+408; ctx+412 with ctx+554 and r+606626: record+460 = 1, record+461 = ctx+413.
ctx+384 with a non-empty part reference at ctx+336: texture and rectangle data from UIPartRef_GetTextureSize / UIPartRef_GetResource go to record+296 (flag) .. record+431.

at the end 488 bytes of the context (ctx+0..+487) are copied to r + 512 * index + 41336, ctx+548 (layer id field) to r + 512 * index + 41840 and a byte 'any effect or blend active' to r + 512 * index + 41844; the function returns ctx+548.

notes: Live check (read-only, UI renderer = [[g_GUICore]+208]): the Job Tree ring layer reads glow 1 / strength 0.8 / radius 4.0 (= 6.0 * 2/3) / colour (1.0, 0.937, 0.702) / mode 3, target 1280x720; three other layers read strength 0.5, radius 2.667 (= 4.0 * 2/3), white, mode 3. Feature-byte gates (V): single float r+606622, glow r+606623, shadow r+606624, ctx+412 group r+606626, ctx+178 group r+606627; the colour transform, the ctx+104 offsets group and the ctx+184 group are not gated.
open_questions: Meaning of the modes 1/2/3 in the compositor (?). ? what the renderer feature bytes r+606622..r+606627 mean and where they are set. ? the exact role of the ctx+178 group (record+462 = layer+486) and of the data block it fills (record+480..+531).

name: GUILayer_Compatible
purpose: Tests whether a draw context can share an existing layer: the blend type, colour transform, every effect group and their values must be equal (within 1.2e-7).

behavior.text: compares blend type (+0) and, for types 14..16 or 17, their parameters, then each enabled group (+76 colour transform, +104, +112, +136, +156 glow, +178, +184) by flag and floats; any clip rectangle (+296), +384 or +409 flag makes the layers incompatible; +412 / +413 must match.

notes: Two components with the same glow settings can share one layer; different settings never do.

name: GUILayer_Composite
proto: char GUILayer_Composite(UILayer *layer, char first, __int64 a3, __int64 a4)
callers: UIRender_SubmitFrame (once per used layer, the first call with flag 1)
callees: UILayer_FillConstants, GUILayer_FillQuadBuffers, LayerBinds_Replay, RenderCommand_Allocate, RenderCommand_Submit, GUILayer_CopyOffsetRegion, GUILayer_ApplyEffects, GUILayer_BlurEffect
purpose: Packs the commands of one finished offscreen layer for the frame: the clears of its atlas page, the effect passes and the blit of the layer onto its parent target. Called once per used layer by UIRender_SubmitFrame.

behavior.text: runs only when the layer's used byte +76 is set. Sets +491 = 1 unless the layer has +78, +487, +488 or a non-zero kind (+28), or the device byte at (*(g_RenderDevice + 88)) + 156 is 0; fills the layer's constants (UILayer_FillConstants) and, when that succeeded and the cull byte +79 is clear, the layer's quads (GUILayer_FillQuadBuffers).

builds the clamp rectangle {(x + 0.5) / W, (y + 0.5) / H, (x + w - 0.5) / W, (y + h - 0.5) / H} from the float rectangle +208..+220 and the int rectangle {(int)x, (int)y, (int)(x + w), (int)(y + h)} (the packed atlas rectangle) and passes them to the effect passes.

sort keys (the same layout in every use: (order & 0x1FF | ((page & 0x3F | target type << 18) << 15) | pass constant) << 10; a target type of 1 is written as 0): clear 0x6AC00200 (pass 1), copy 0x6AC00E00 (pass 7), final 0x6AC07E00 (pass 63) is left in the state at the end.

clears: when the layer's atlas page (+16) differs from the last cleared page (dword_140906B5C, reset to -1 each frame by UIRender_PrepareLayers) it queues, for the layer's target type table (g_Renderer + 512 x type + 24224), clear commands (RenderCommand_Allocate type 0, 32 bytes: the +40 member of the slot's target in the second qword, 16 zero bytes of colour after it) for slots 26, 27, 28 and 29 (offsets 24432 .. 24456); a 24-byte type-1 command for g_Renderer + 20632 when +492 and +484 are set. A drop-shadow layer (+177, +486 clear) also clears slot 3 (24248) once per page (dword_140906B60) and a masked layer (+487) slot 30 (24464) (dword_140906B64).

effects (when the byte +179 is set): the sort key becomes 0x6AC00E00; kind (+28) 1 runs GUILayer_BlurEffect (the whole-layer blur) and kind 0 runs GUILayer_CopyOffsetRegion (masked layers) or, when that returns 0, GUILayer_ApplyEffects, which draws the layer's effects and the layer blit (GUILayer_BlitFinal) and the glow pass.
the layer's own draws are not queued here: UICommand_ExecuteBatches replays them (sort key pass 2, constant 0x6AC00400) into RT 26.

notes: Earlier versions of this sheet listed only the head. The glow strength / gain / mode 3 combine is in GUILayer_GlowPass and its shader (decoded elsewhere). The clears fire once per atlas page, before any draw of the page (pass order), so the layer content target is empty (0, 0, 0, 0) where no draw lands.
open_questions: ? the type-1 command's target (g_Renderer + 20632) and when +484 / +492 are both set.

name: GUILayer_CopyOffsetRegion
purpose: Used when layer byte +487 is set: copies the layer's rectangle from target slot 30 into render target 26 (the first scratch), standing in for the effect ping-pong start.

behavior.text: returns 0 at once when layer+487 is 0. Otherwise sets the sort key state+8 = ((layer+12 & 0x1FF | ((layer+16 & 0x3F | tt << 18) << 15) | 0x6AC00E00) << 10) with tt = 0 when targetType == 1 (the key is set again after the copy).

rectangles are cast to int with truncation: dst = ((int)x, (int)y, (int)(x + w), (int)(y + h)) from floats +208 / +212 / +216 / +220; src = x' = (+232 - +224) + x, y' = (+236 - +228) + y, then ((int)x', (int)y', (int)(x' + w), (int)(y' + h)). (+224 / +228 = the atlas offset, +232 / +236 = the second atlas offset, both written by GUILayer_PackAtlasRect.)
calls UIBlur_CopyTarget(blurObj = *(g_Renderer+37928), layer target, srcSlot 30, dstRT 26, filter index 2, srcRect = the shifted rectangle, flag = the destination rectangle). Returns 1.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403B6028). The caller treats it as the replacement for GUILayer_ApplyEffects when +487 is set (see GUILayer_Composite). Rounding: truncation toward zero of float rectangle edges; the right edge is (int)(x + w), not (int)x + (int)w. Filter index 2 (UIBlur_CopyTarget digit 1) is not decoded.
open_questions: What slot 30 holds; meaning of filter index 2.

name: GUILayer_CopyToTarget
proto: char GUILayer_CopyToTarget(UILayer *layer, __int64 stateCtx, __int128 *rect, RenderTarget *target, int a5, int srcRT)
purpose: First step of the +177 (drop shadow) effect group: draws the layer's current scratch render target RT[srcRT] into slot 3 of the layer target's slot table with selector #10, program 0, clipped to a rectangle (a silhouette copy of the layer's alpha, see the shader note).

behavior.text: the fourth argument is not a layer: GUILayer_ApplyEffects passes UILayer_GetTarget(layer), the layer's render target object; its byte +86 selects the per-target slot table (g_Renderer + 512 * byte + 24224, 8-byte slots) used below.

destination = the table entry g_Renderer + 512 * (byte target+86) + 24248 (slot 3). It is stored at state+96 and its +40 member at state+144 (the render-target binding of the draw); when that member's type (+8) is 1 or 2 the low 3 bits of its +16 go to state+124 bits 9..11.

source texture = RT[srcRT] = the object at g_Renderer + 40 * srcRT + 20832 (its +40 member, 0 when the pointer is null), bound as the texture at state + 8 * (short layer+64) + 1608. srcRT is GUILayer_ApplyEffects' current scratch index (the one holding the layer's pixels so far).

the selector is the one at index 10 of the UI manager's selector array (*(*(g_Renderer+37936) + 80)); the technique's default sampler words (count +108, ids +160, values +168 of the technique) are copied to state + 5704 + 4 * id (top bit cleared); then ShaderSelector_Apply(selector, state, 0): program index 0 of the selected permutation.

no vertex buffers are bound (state+136 and +200 and the stride fields +208 / +212 are zeroed); state+112 |= 0x10 with its high bits cleared (clip enable) and the 16-byte int rectangle is copied to state+80; state+124 = (& 0xFFC06FFF) | 0x6000; state+6016 = 0; a 96-byte command is allocated with sub_140069A38(state, 4, 96), its +8 = 4 and +12 = 0, packed with RenderState_PackCommand and submitted with sub_140069980.

pixel shader 0349C0 samples T0 at the uv clamped to at most cb37.zw and writes (0, 0, 0, texture alpha), i.e. a black silhouette of the source alpha; its likely vertex partner 034080 builds an oversized triangle from SV_VertexID, so it needs no vertex buffer (consistent with the zeroed slots above).

behavior.basis: (live read of the running game's selector, 2026-10-29: *(*(*(g_Renderer+37936)
behavior.text: +80)+48/+56/+64/+40) program entries, program table, index list and shader objects): selector #10 program 0 = vertex shader 034080 + pixel shader 0349C0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: GUILayer_CopyToTarget). Direction: state+96 / state+144 hold the render target the draw writes to (GUILayer_BlitFinal and sub_1403CB8BC use the same fields for the real target), and the texture bound at state+1608 + 8 * slot is the one sampled; so RT[srcRT] is the source and the slot-3 entry is the destination. I: GUILayer_Composite queues a type-0 32-byte command on the slot-3 texture once per layer id when the layer has +177 set and +486 clear (it looks like a clear before this copy). I: the slot table entries point at the same render-target objects as the RT array (GUILayer_EffectPass0 writes slot 27 and the next pass reads RT 27; the blur after this step works on RT 3).
open_questions: ? what a5 is (unused). ? whether slot 3 of the target slot table is the same object as RT[3] (g_Renderer + 20952), which the blur pass uses. ? the pipeline state words of program entry 0 (blend, raster, samplers) were not read. ? which constant buffer program 0 sees: the vertex shader declares a 720-byte buffer (reads cb11.xy as a uv scale) and none is bound in this function.

name: GUILayer_EffectPass0
proto: __int64 GUILayer_EffectPass0(GUILayer *layer, RenderCtx *rc, void *target, int outSlot, int inSlot)
callers: GUILayer_ApplyEffects (only; called first with outSlot 27, inSlot 26 when layer+489 is set and (layer+492 = 0 or layer+36 >= 0); argument 3 is the target object from UILayer_GetTarget)
purpose: First layer-effect pass of GUILayer_ApplyEffects (run when the layer's props flag +489 is set): sets up one render command that binds two layer textures and a shader selector and queues a 96-byte command.

behavior.text: reads the shader selector from the renderer global (qword_143CDA098+37936, then +96) and the render target it WRITES from the per-target table at global+24224 indexed by (byte target+86 << 6) + outSlot (27 in the only call); stores it at rc+96 and its +40 member at rc+144; rc+124 bits 9..11 take the low 3 bits of that member's +16 when its type (+8) is 1 or 2.
copies the selector's constant list (count at +108, index array +160, value array +168) into rc+5704+4*index with the top bit cleared, then calls ShaderSelector_Apply(selector, rc).

binds the two textures it SAMPLES into rc+1608 at the slots given by layer+64 and layer+66 (global+20832+40*inSlot = RT 26, +40 member; and global+22032 = RT 30, the mask buffer, an R8 target (live: GPU resource 47, R8_UNORM 1280x720), +40 member); sets rc+136, rc+200, rc+208 = 16, rc+212 = layer+8 << 6, rc+120 = 0x77FD0010 and flag bits in rc+124 (0x6000), rc+6016 = 0.
allocates a command with sub_140069A38(rc, 4, 96), sets its +8 = 4 and +12 = 0, packs it with RenderState_PackCommand and submits it with sub_140069980 when the pack returns nonzero.

exactly ONE layer goes through this pass per frame (layer object 0x294523B2AE8 that run, the title's TextMask layer); the same layer also runs GUILayer_CopyToTarget, GUILayer_BlurShadowPass, UIBlur_Run (from the shadow pass) and GUILayer_BlitFinal, but not the glow pass. Its effect bytes: +176 = 0 (blur off), +177 = 1 (shadow blur ON), +178 = 0 (glow off), +179 = 1, +484 = 3, +489 = 1 (this pass), +492 = 1; floats +180 = 1.0, +184 = 1.0, +188 = 2.0 (the shadow blur radius), +196 = 2.6667, +200 = 0.3, +204 = 1.0, +208 = 2.0.

behavior.basis: (shader: shader/UIRender.tec split into its blobs, the DXIL disassembled with dxc -dumpbin)
behavior.text: the 2-texture mask pixel shaders of UIRender.tec (for example the blob at file offset 0x3D41C) read tTexture0 and the mask texture at the same uv, take the MASK TEXTURE'S ALPHA (optionally 1 - alpha, selected by a cbuffer word at cUIRender register 15 .z) and output tTexture0.rgba * mask for all four channels: result = gradientLayer.rgba * textLayer.a. The mask uses alpha only, not luminance. (I: which of the 2-texture blobs this pass selects (selector index 3) was not matched to a blob.)
changing the mask alpha (alpha^0.8, ^1.5, ^2, smoothstep) makes the title error worse (2.7 / 4.3 / 6.7 / 2.4 against 1.105), so the layer alpha is the straight text coverage, as the studio models it.

notes: The name is ours. ApplyEffects swaps the slot numbers (26/27, then 29) after this pass, so the slots look like ping-pong layer textures (I). I: this is the mask pass: the Job Tree title (TextMask) is the one component here with a Mask node, its mask component (TextBoard01, the text) is drawn into a separate layer first (ComponentLayer_DrawMaskComponent) and this pass binds two layer textures; the studio models it as the gradient rect times the text coverage, which matches the retail capture to a mean error of 0.65 (header region).
open_questions: Which UIRender.tec blob selector 3 picks; the meaning of the 0x77FD0010 word and of the 96-byte type-4 command; what +489 means in the props file (it enables this mask pass).

name: GUILayer_ExpandBounds
callers: GUICore_CommitFrame (once per slot 0..count - 1, after GUILayer_Flush), sub_1403D64F4
purpose: The last step that fixes a layer's float rectangle (layer+208..+220): the union of the quad bounds drawn into the slot (the dirty rectangle) grown by the blur reach of the slot's effects and by 16 pixels, clamped to the target. The layer-order part rotates the order values of layers that share a layer id.

behavior.text: input = the slot's dirty rectangle, four ints at r + 512 * i + 41824 (x0, y0, x1, y1), filled by GUILayer_Flush from the quad bounds and cleared every frame by GUIRenderer_ResetFrame. When it is empty (x0 >= x1 or y0 >= y1) the rectangle of the layer is not written (it keeps the default (0, 0, W, H) of GUILayer_ResetRecord; such a slot has no command and is never used).

radius R = 0, then max with: the float layer+500 when the layer kind dword layer+28 is 1 (whole-layer blur group); layer+188 when the drop-shadow byte layer+177 is set; layer+204 when the glow byte layer+178 is set; layer+180 when the single-float byte layer+176 is set (layer = r + 303480 + 592 * i, the record minus 24 bytes). The three radii in the record are the pixel values GUILayer_BuildRecord wrote (UIB radius x min scale); a group whose flag is clear is ignored even when its stale radius value is large.

R <= 0 adds nothing. Otherwise the pad P (pixels, added to every edge with saturation, GUILayer_BoundsAdd32) is f * UIBlur_TapCount(R / f, 1 / 255) with f = 1 for R <= 3.2, 2 for <= 6.4, 4 for <= 12.8, 8 for <= 25.6, 16 for <= 51.2 and 32 above (the sigma argument is R, R x 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625, 0.03125). With a float32 model of GaussianKernel_Build: R 0.667 -> 3, 0.8 -> 3, 1.0 -> 4, 2.0 -> 6, 2.667 -> 8, 4.0 -> 12, 6.0 -> 16, 6.667 -> 20, 10 -> 28.

when the byte layer+486 (the +178 context group) is set each padded edge e is replaced by round((e - W x sx) x k + e) (x edges: W = r+184, sx = float layer+504, y edges: H = r+188, sy = float layer+508), k = float layer+520 + 1, and then clamped so that it is never inside the original dirty rectangle (not exercised by the Job Tree: read in the code only).

then every edge grows by 16 pixels (saturating), and each edge is clamped into [0, W] (x) and [0, H] (y) with W = r+184, H = r+188; the result is stored as floats (x0, y0, x1 - x0, y1 - y0) at layer+208..+220. A rectangle entirely off the target collapses to a zero width or height (live: layers with x0 = x1 = 0).

behavior.basis: (live 2026-10-30, 26 + 40 layers of two Job Tree frames)
behavior.text: the integer rectangle that GUILayer_PackAtlasRect later derives from the float rectangle ((int)x, (int)y, (int)(x + w), (int)(y + h), layer+240..+252) equals the rule above applied to the dirty rectangle for every used layer (dirty (620, 475, 625, 485), radius 0.667 single float -> pad 3 + 16 -> (601, 456, 644, 504); dirty (834, 395, 935, 409), glow radius 2.667 -> pad 8 + 16 -> (810, 371, 959, 433); a shadow radius 2.0 -> pad 6).

layer ids: when the slot's layer id (r + 512 * i + 41840) is non-zero, the newest record whose id has the same high word and a larger low word is searched; if it is a later slot j > i, the order dwords (layer+12) of the slots i..j are rotated so that slot j takes the order of slot i and the slots i..j-1 move up by one (higher ids keep their place after compositing). The Job Tree frames have no layer id (all ids 0).

notes: Glow radius 4.0 falls in the (<= 6.4) class: f = 2, pad 12. The atlas margin of GUILayer_PackAtlasRect looks at radii above 3.2 of +500, +180 and +188 and not at the glow radius +204 (as read in that function; the two functions use different subsets). The rule is the one a software renderer needs to reproduce layer rectangles: see the behavior JobTreeLayerList.
open_questions: The blur pass itself (shader and weights) is not decoded (?). The +486 scaling branch was not exercised (?).

name: GUILayer_FillQuadBuffers
purpose: Writes the layer's rectangle as quads into the eight per-layer vertex buffers of the UI renderer, slot index layer+8 (4 vertices per layer).

behavior.text: W, H = (float) u32 at g_Renderer + 6568 / + 6572; (x, y, w, h) = floats layer +208 / +212 / +216 / +220 (no rounding here).
buffer [1064] (vertices 16 bytes, record index 4 * layer+8): corners TL, TR, BL, BR of the rectangle as (px, py, px / W, py / H). Buffer [1066] gets the same quad.
buffer [1065]: the same quad moved by (-layer+224, -layer+228) (the atlas offset): (x - dx, y - dy, ... / W, / H).

buffer [1059]: only positions (8 bytes), the rectangle expanded by 2.0 on every side. Buffer [1072]: 6-vertex x 16-byte records (position + uv, two triangles) of the plain rectangle. Buffer [1069]: 4 x (x, y, 0|1, 1) records (position with clip-style z / w constants 0 / 1.0).
buffer [1074]: the fixed full-surface quad (0,0) (W,0) (0,H) (W,H) with uv 0..1 in the same record; buffer [1075] (once, into a mapped constant): the u16 render size as floats and fixed unit corners.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403B12CC). Pixel-exact note: the vertices carry the layer rectangle as unrounded floats and the uv is simply px / size (no half-pixel offset); any snapping happens earlier, in GUILayer_PackAtlasRect, which overwrites +208..+220 with integer atlas coordinates for packed layers.
open_questions: Which shader reads which of the buffers.

name: GUILayer_Flush
callers: GUILayer_SetCurrent (sub_1403E9218, hence every layer switch), GUICore_CommitFrame
purpose: Closes the layer being built: merges the draws recorded so far into the layer's dirty rectangle and advances the layer count.

behavior.text: when r+606592 (the draw counter: +1 per emitted draw, see the node draw functions) > 0 it calls GUILayer_BoundsToRect (sub_1403DF8D8) for the integer rectangle of the quads accumulated since the last flush, resets the double bounds r+152..+176 to their sentinels, and merges the rectangle into the current slot's dirty rectangle at r + 512 * current + 41824 (four ints x0, y0, x1, y1): only when the new rectangle is non-empty (x0 < x1 and y0 < y1); when the slot's rectangle is empty it is replaced, otherwise it becomes the union (min of x0 / y0, max of x1 / y1). Then the counter is cleared and, when the current slot index r+606588 equals the slot count r+606584, the count is incremented.

so a slot is consumed (the next layer opens at the next index) by any draw, also one without a quad (a text node counts before it emits glyphs, the letterbox bars of GUICore_CommitFrame count when they are empty): the live Job Tree frame ends with such an empty slot (count 27, last dirty rectangle (0, 0, 0, 0)); a layer that received no draw at all leaves the count alone and its slot is reused by the next layer.
the dirty rectangle of every used slot grown by the effect pad and 16 pixels (GUILayer_ExpandBounds) reproduced the integer layer rectangle of all 26 used layers of a Job Tree frame.

name: GUILayer_GlowPass
proto: __int64 GUILayer_GlowPass(UILayer *layer, __m128i *cmd, unsigned char targetType, int *rect, __m128i *clamp, __int64 target, int srcTex, int a8, int a9, int dstTex)
purpose: Glow composite: blurs the layer by the glow radius and draws the result with the glow shader permutation selected by the mode field.

behavior.text: UIBlur_Run(layer, target, targetType, 44, 1, radius = layer+204, ..., a7 = blurred output, a10 = source, scratch 28); then selects the shader technique v12[11] of the UI selector, sets its permutation digit 0 from layer+480 (the mode: 3 for the Job Tree), binds the texture of the layer's slot +64 to the list entry srcTex and slot +66 to dstTex, takes the draw rectangle from layer+240 and queues a 96-byte command.

strength (+200), colour (+468..+476) and the other group values reach the shader through the constant buffer filled by UILayer_FillConstants (sub_1403B08AC): strength to constant offset 212, colour to 512..520.

notes: Shader (V): live read of the technique-11 selector gives programs for the digit-0 permutations 0..3 = pixel shader ids 53..56 (ids: 9 vertex shaders, then pixel shaders, in .tec file order), i.e. the 3rd to 6th pixel shader variants of the layer-effect family; the Job Tree glow (mode 3) is the 4th: add.rgb = 2 * strength * colour * A.rgb * (B.a * (1 - A.a) + (1 - B.a)), add.a = max(B.a, A.a), added to the UAV target (unorm) after textureLoad. Roles (V from the calls): T0 / A = slot +64 = the blurred output, T1 / B = slot +66 = the sharp source (UIBlur_Run reads a10 and writes a9). The target is the same object GUILayer_BlitFinal drew the layer into just before, so the add lands on top of the layer the layer content is premultiplied (V): the plain-image shader writes rgb * a and the default UI draw state blends ONE / INV_SRC_ALPHA (word 0x79420a11, see UIRender_ApplyDrawState), and the blur is linear.

name: GUILayer_PackAtlasRect
purpose: Decides where a layer's pixels live in the layer atlas pages, allocates the integer rectangle there and rewrites the layer rectangle (+208..+220) and its offsets (+224..+236) to the packed position.

behavior.text: layer +240..+252 (int rect) = ((int)x, (int)y, (int)(x + w), (int)(y + h)) from floats +208 / +212 / +216 / +220 (truncation toward zero, right / bottom edges truncated after the float sum); +224 / +228 = 0, +232 = 0, +492 = 0, +16 = +20 = -1 (page ids).
only when layer byte +79 (culled) is 0. Atlas allocators are at UIRenderer+8616 (primary) and +8632 (secondary).

fallback (no pack): when byte +179 is 0, dword +28 > 1, or bytes +78 / +486 / +488 are set, the allocation is for the whole target (rect 0,0,targetW,targetH from u16 +20 / +22) with margin 2 (which the allocator clamps to 0 for a full-page rectangle); +492 stays 0 and +208.. are unchanged. The result rectangle is discarded; only the primary page index (+16) is kept. A full-page rectangle always fails both fit tests, so every fallback layer takes a new page, and the next layer after it takes another new page (the cursor is left at the end of the row and page).

packed path: margin = 2, or 32 when |float +500| > 3.2 or float +180 > 3.2 or float +188 > 3.2 (a blur is present). When byte +487: the secondary atlas gets the rect first, giving the packed rect P2 (the page index +20 = its page), and the primary allocation is repeated. The primary result P replaces the layer rectangle: +208 / +212 = (float)P.x0 / P.y0, +216 / +220 = (float)(P.x1 - P.x0) / (P.y1 - P.y0); +224 / +228 = P.x0 - (float)orig.x0, P.y0 - (float)orig.y0 with orig the int rect (+240 / +244, truncated, not the float rect); +232 / +236 = P2 - orig (ints, as floats) when +487 (otherwise +232 / +236 = +224 / +228); +492 = 1; +16 = the primary page index (+20 = the secondary page index only for +487). V: when byte +487 and the secondary page index changed, the primary shelf is moved to a new page first (row height 0, page + 1, cursor (0, 0)); the primary allocation always uses the int rect, the same margin and the original (x0, y0) as alignment key. V (live 2026-10-30): P and the page index +16 were reproduced for 63 layers of a running frame (no +487 layer among them: the secondary path is read in the code only).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403B6A78). KEY for pixel-exact work: a layer's rectangle is not its design rectangle after this runs. It is truncated to integers, grown by the margin (2 px, 32 px with blur) inside the atlas, and the rectangle floats are then overwritten with integer atlas positions; the difference to the screen position is kept in +224 / +228 (and +232 / +236). A layer's content therefore lands on the screen at integer positions (floor toward zero of the unrounded float rect). The packed rectangle P is the content rectangle itself: the margin lies around it, so the content origin in the atlas is P.x0 / P.y0 and the atlas pixel of screen pixel (sx, sy) is (sx + P.x0 - x0, sy + P.y0 - y0) with (x0, y0) = the int rect origin.
open_questions: Who writes the float rect first (the UI layout / animation step); what +500 / +180 / +188 are exactly (blur radii of the effect groups).

name: GUILayer_ResetRecord
purpose: Resets one layer record to its defaults (full target size, identity colour transform, every effect group off).

behavior.text: +0 / +2 = target size (r+184 / r+188), blend type 0, colour multiplier (1,1,1,1), add (0,0,0,0), flag words +153/+154/... cleared, rectangle (0, 0, w, h), opacity 1.0f at +552; all effect pointers and group flags zero.

the dword at record+152 (layer+176) is set to 0x01000000: the three effect flags +176 / +177 / +178 become 0 and the byte layer+179 becomes 1; layer+179 is the 'composited' byte (GUILayer_Composite and GUILayer_PackAtlasRect only act on layers where it is set), cleared only by GUINode_DrawKind10. The dword at layer+486 (flags +486..+489) is zeroed and the kind dword layer+28 is set to 0.

name: GUILayer_Select
purpose: Finds an existing offscreen layer compatible with the context (same layer id and equal effect settings) or builds a new record, and makes it the current layer.

behavior.text: searches layer records from the newest (index r+606584 - 1) down for one whose id (ctx+548) matches and for which GUILayer_Compatible (sub_1403E7ADC) holds; the result index (or -1) goes to sub_1403E9218 (makes it current, sets the per-thread draw target) and then GUILayer_BuildRecord (while the current layer index is below 510) or sub_1403E73A0 (reset the slot).

notes: Layer records: 592 bytes at r + 303504 + 592 * i (512 slots, 510 usable).

name: GUILayer_SetCurrent
callers: GUILayer_Select, GUICore_DrawWidget, ComponentLayer_DrawMaskComponent and a vtable entry
purpose: Flushes the batch and makes layer record `index` current; out-of-range indices select the next free slot (capped at 510). Returns 1 when the current layer changed.

behavior.text: GUILayer_Flush(r) first. When index < 0 or index >= count (dword r+606584): index = min(count, 510). Equal to the current (dword r+606588) -> return 0.
otherwise r+606588 = index; (*(qword_143CDA098 + 37936) + 208) = &r[+303480 + 592 * index] (the UI renderer's current layer record pointer); dword r+606604 = -1; return 1.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403E9218). 2091 hits per 4 s. Layer records are 592 bytes (148 dwords) from r+303480, count r+606584, current r+606588; r+606604 = -1 invalidates a cached value.

name: GUILayer_UpdateActiveFlag
callers: GUINineGridNode_Draw, GUIRectNode_Draw, GUITextNode_Draw, UIImageNode_Draw, GUINode_DrawKind10, sub_1403EBFA0, sub_1403EC794, sub_1403ECA88 and a vtable entry
purpose: Sets the context's 'draws into an offscreen layer' byte (ctx+554) from a request and, when it changed, re-selects the layer.

behavior.text: want is forced to 0 unless r+606626 != 0, ctx+412 != 0 and ctx+553 = 0. When ctx+554 != want: ctx+554 = want and the return value is GUILayer_Select(r, ctx); otherwise returns 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403E6440). 6051 hits per 4 s. Every draw node calls it first, so most calls are a no-op compare.
open_questions: ? Meaning of ctx+412 (I: node has layer effects) and ctx+553 (I: forced flat / no layer).

name: GUILayerXform_MapPointFloat
purpose: Same transform as GUILayerXform_MapPointInt without rounding; used by GUICore_UpdateFrame to bring the pointer into UI coordinates before the hit test.

behavior.text: same matrix layout as the int variant.

name: GUILayerXform_MapPointInt
purpose: Maps an integer point through the layer's 2x3 matrix (x' = x*m0 + y*m2 + m4, y' = x*m1 + y*m3 + m5) and rounds back to integers (roundf).

behavior.text: the matrix is recomputed first when t+128 is set; core+216+144*layer holds the window-to-UI transforms.

name: GUILayerXform_Recompute
callers: GUILayerXform_MapPointFloat, GUILayerXform_MapPointInt, sub_1403F8D2C, GUICore_DrawWidget, GUICore_CommitFrame, sub_1403D6234, sub_14015AB34, sub_140175F58
purpose: Recomputes a GUI layer transform (one of the window-to-UI layers at GUICore + 216 + 144 * index): a letterbox fit of the UI size into the viewport, as a forward matrix, an inverse matrix and the scale. The return value is unused.

behavior.text: inputs: +0 / +4 ints = the UI (design) size w / h; +8 / +12 floats = layer scale multipliers; +16 / +20 ints = an extra offset added to the viewport centre; +24 / +28 ints = the viewport width W / height H; +32 / +36 / +40 / +44 ints = the viewport rectangle (left, top, right, bottom). GUICore's per-frame update fills them: +24 / +28 = right - left, bottom - top and +32.. = the rectangle.

fit scale f = W / w when w * H >= h * W, else H / h (the smaller of the two ratios, integer cross-multiplied); sx = (+8) * f, sy = (+12) * f; the viewport centre cx = (+16) + (left + right) / 2 and cy = (+20) + (top + bottom) / 2 (integer halves).

outputs (floats): +48..+68 = the viewport-local forward matrix [sx, 0, 0, sy, tx, ty] with tx = cx - (w / 2) * sx - left and ty = cy - (h / 2) * sy - top; +72..+92 = the inverse [1/sx, 0, 0, 1/sy, w/2 - cx/sx, h/2 - cy/sy] of the window-absolute transform; +96..+116 = the window-absolute forward matrix [sx, 0, 0, sy, cx - (w/2) * sx, cy - (h/2) * sy]; +120 / +124 = sx / sy; the dirty byte +128 is cleared. The zero entries are computed as products with 0.0.

consumers: GUILayerXform_MapPointInt / GUILayerXform_MapPointFloat map a window point to UI coordinates with the +72 inverse; sub_1403F8D2C maps a UI point to window pixels with the +96 matrix; GUICore_DrawWidget copies +48..+71 and +120 / +124 into the root draw context (ctx+504 and ctx+528 / +532); sub_14015AB34 and sub_140175F58 read the lengths of the +72..+84 rows (1 / scale); GUICore_CommitFrame recomputes a dirty transform before drawing the outside bars (only for transforms whose +132 dword is 1); sub_1403D6234 refills the viewport fields.

the callers either test the dirty byte +128 first (MapPoint*, sub_1403F8D2C, GUICore_DrawWidget, GUICore_CommitFrame, sub_14015AB34, sub_140175F58) or, like sub_1403D6234, set it to 1 and call directly.

notes: Proposed name: GUILayerXform_Recompute. Worked check: UI size 1920 x 1080 in a 1280 x 720 viewport at (0, 0): f = 2/3, tx = 640 - 960 * 2/3 = 0, sx = sy = 0.6667. The scan that listed this function as writing component fields +100 / +104 / +116 / +120 is a coincidence of offsets: here they are the layer transform's own floats (+100 = 0.0 zero term, +104 = 0.0, +116 = ty0, +120 = sx), not component properties.
open_questions: ? what +16 / +20 are (set outside this function; their values were not read). ? why the inverse (+72..+92) is built from the window-absolute matrix while the viewport-local matrix (+48) is the one drawn with. ? what +132 (set to 1 by sub_1403D6234, read by GUICore_CommitFrame to draw the outside bars) is exactly.

name: GUIList_SetCount
proto: void GUIList_SetCount(void *list, int count, int column, char rebuild)
callers: sub_14012EF90, sub_1401AAC74, sub_1401AAD50, sub_1401AEEF0, sub_1401AFC20, sub_1401AFDE4, sub_1402A62E4, ShopList_BuildEntries
callees: GUICore_FocusNode, sub_14028D7BC, sub_14028D870, sub_14040C7D8, UIName_Key, GUINode_StopState, UIName_ReleaseKey, GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState, GUIComponentList_GetSlotComponent, sub_1400F6068, sub_1402A89C0
purpose: Sizes and refreshes a list gadget: it stores the row count and column, rebinds the name key of the list node, and toggles the empty-list label.

behavior.text: the first argument is the list object; its +0x510 pointer must be non-zero or the function returns at once.
it clears the selected-row word at +0x541 and calls GUICore_FocusNode before any rebuild.
when the rebuild flag is zero it calls the list virtual method at +0x40, stores the count and jumps to the refresh.
when the rebuild flag is set it uses the existing node, releases the old name key and binds a new one through UIName_Key.
the strings ShowNoItem and HideNoItem are the two states of the empty-list label the function toggles.
the row count and column are stored in the list object and the node state is replayed with GUINode_PlayState.
the eight callers are the shop, item and menu list builders, so this is the common list sizer.
the column argument is the number of cells per row, because the same value is written to the gadget layout field.
what sub_1402A89C0 changes after the count; it runs only on the rebuild path.

notes: Whole function read (573 bytes). The two label strings are the only string operands in the body.

name: GUINineGridNode_Draw
