name: GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels
proto: void GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels(AnimChannelSet *a, float t, GUINode *node, char absolute)
callees: sub_1404080C4, sub_140407C18, UIAnim_SampleFloatTrack, sub_140408218, sub_140408328, sub_140407DF8, sub_140407D40, sub_140407D9C, GUINode_SetPosition, sub_1403EF6B4, sub_1403EF738, sub_1403F4604, sub_1403F1BB8, sub_1403F1C24, sub_1403F1C90
purpose: Samples every keyframe track of one animation channel set at time t and stores the results into the node's transform / colour / opacity / per-kind fields.

behavior.text: returns at once when node+150 != 0. Track pointers are a[6]..a[31]; a null track is skipped; a track that returns 0 (no key at or before t, or the key's interpolation id is 0) leaves the field unchanged.

a[6] position (int pair, sub_1404080C4) -> GUINode_SetPosition; a[7] size (int pair) -> sub_1403EF6B4; a[8] scale (float pair, sub_140407C18) -> sub_1403EF738; a[9] rotation float -> node+88 (dirty +149 when it changes by > 1.19e-7); a[10] sort order int -> node+92 (and sets parent+216 re-sort flag); a[11] colour -> node+100; a[12] colour percent -> node+104; a[13] opacity float -> node+108; a[14] bool track -> node+144 (visible).

behavior.basis: (combination with the current value when absolute = 0; with absolute != 0 the sampled value replaces it)
behavior.text: position += (node+56, node+60); size += (node+64, node+68); scale *= (node+80, node+84); rotation += node+88; sort order += node+92; colour: each byte c = sampled * node+100 byte / 255 (integer truncating, alpha too); colour percent: clamp(sampled * node+104 / 100, 0, 255) per channel, alpha likewise; opacity *= node+108; visible = sampled && node+144.

kind 2 (image) a[15] -> node+248, a[16] -> node+252 (ints; sets the part / frame); kind 3 (text) a[17] colour -> node+280; kind 4 a[15] -> +224; kind 5 a[15] -> word +312; kind 6 four colour tracks (indices 15..18, via sub_140407DF8) -> the four colour dwords node+208..+220 (colour multiply /255); kind 7 a[15] int -> +224, a[22]/a[23] floats -> +228 / +232, a[24]/a[25] colours -> +236 / +240; kind 8 a[26..28] floats -> +260 / +264 / +268 (+260 sets +279 dirty), a[29]/a[30] colours -> +240 / +244, a[31] float -> +284 (multiply; sets +279), and per element tracks 65.. (4 tracks per element of the 552-byte vector at node+216: two int pairs added to the element's +0/+4, +8/+12 and +16/+20, and a float multiplied into +24); kind 9 a[15] -> +232.

absolute = the state's byte +111 (GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims passes S+111). GUIComponent_LoadDef and UIAnim_PlayStateTracks set it to 1 for every UIB timeline state, so file states always replace the node's fields and nothing accumulates; the combining formulas above apply only to states created another way (? none found).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140400840). Colour tracks are interpolated per byte by sub_1404022A8 (float lerp, clamp 0..255, truncating (int)), position / size tracks by UIAnim_SampleInt2Track, so animated node positions are integers.
open_questions: Whether any state is created with absolute = 0 (file states are not); what kinds 4 / 5 / 6 / 7 are; the meaning of bool track a[14] timing (sub_1403F4604 handles hold length and curve < 1.0 steps).

name: GUINode_ApplyStateAtFrame
callers: UIAddon code (Launcher / Title / Job tree screens: 11+ call sites), GUIAddon_OnStateEvent-style link handlers
callees: GUINode_FindState, GUINode_FindPartByName, GUINode_FindDescendant, sub_1404007FC, sub_1404015C0, sub_140400840
purpose: Evaluates all property tracks of a named state at one frame and writes the results into the nodes, recursing into the nested state links.

behavior.text: state = GUINode_FindState(comp, key); none -> nothing. frame < 0 -> frame = state+88 (the last frame); f = (float)frame.

for each track group of the state (pointer vector state+144..+152): when sub_1404007FC(group) says the group is named with the component's own key (qword_143CDA2A0+5144, compared by interned id or string), sub_1404015C0(group, f, comp, state+111) applies the component-level properties; otherwise node = GUINode_FindPartByName(comp+272, group name) and sub_140400840(group, f, node, state+111) applies the node properties.

for every entry of the state's list (state+176.., 64 bytes) with type 5 (nested state link): child = GUINode_FindDescendant(comp, entry+16), childState = GUINode_FindState(child, entry+32) and the function recurses with frame' = (int)fmaxf(((f - (float)entry+8) * (float)childState+88) / (float)(entry+12 - entry+8), 0.0) in single precision. The child frame is NOT clamped to its length here (GUIAddon_OnStateEvent clamps).
returns at once when `GUINode_FindState` finds no state of that name: a name the file does not have changes nothing (the title's `Menu%d` with a count the file has no state for).

`GUIComponent_UpdateNodeTree` skips a node with enabled byte +144 = 0 together with its subtree, and `GUINode_ClearVisibleSubtree` follows a Reference into its component, so +144 = 0 on a Reference hides the referenced component; a state changes +144 only through a bool track (`GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels` a[14]).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140409A98). sub_140400840 (3.4 KB) maps the track slots of a group onto node fields (V, read in part): slot 6 position -> GUINode_SetPosition(node+56/+60), 7 size (+64/+68), 8 scale (KeyTrackVec2_Eval -> node+80/+84), 9 rotation (float, +88, radians), 10 order (int +92), 11 colour (+100), 12 colour percent bytes (+104..+106), 13 opacity (+108), 14 visibility (KeyTrackBool_Eval -> +144), then kind specific ones (kind 2 image: +248 / +252 ints, kind 3 text colour +280). With state+111 (a4) == 0 the value is combined with the node's CURRENT field (position, size, rotation, order: added; scale, opacity: multiplied; colours: per channel x / 255), with a4 != 0 it replaces it. A pixel-exact simulator must apply the tracks in this order.
open_questions: ? Whether a4 == 0 (relative) accumulates when evaluated every tick: the node field is overwritten, so relative tracks need a base reset; not traced. ? Slots above 14 and kinds 4..10 in sub_140400840.

name: GUINode_BuildFromFile
purpose: Copies a UIB file node into its runtime GUINode (position, size, pivot, colours, then the type-specific block).

behavior.text: file node +8/+12 origin -> GUINode_SetPosition (runtime +56/+60); +0x44/+0x48 size; +0x1C/+0x20 pivot (runtime +72/+76); +0x50 byte flag.

type 3 (Text): data block = src + *(int*)(src+0x4C) (= +0xB0 in the file): block+64 dword text id -> runtime +248; block+72 int16 size -> +304; block+80 int16 -> +306; block+84 int16 -> +308; block+76/+77/+78 bytes -> +311/+312/+313; src+0x70 (dword index 28) font-set key -> runtime +300. (Colours and alignment are set in other parts of the same function: not mapped here.)
font-set keys in ffto_job_tree.uib: TextBoardJobName Title 60, TextLv/TextLvNum 51; TextBoardJobLv Title/TextLv 98.

runtime +224 = the part index (texture reference +8), +228 / +232 / +236 / +240 = the four border ints at data block +0x68 (left, top, right, bottom, layout px), +244 = the fill type from block +0x78 (copied as 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 into +244; 2 and 3 are drawn with UIImage_DrawTiled, 3 with mirrored odd cells), +248 = the byte at block +0x7C. Job tree values: chip BG (10, 8, 10, 8), badge NineGrid00 (10, 10, 10, 10), name plate NineGrid02 (24, 0, 20, 0), all fill type 0.

the data block (header +0x4C = its offset) holds the fill RGBA at +8, the outline at +0xC, the opacity (float) at +0x10, the visible flag at +0x20 and the four corner colours (TL, TR, BL, BR) at +0x40..+0x4C; the loader copies the four corner dwords (block dwords 16..19) to runtime +208 / +212 / +216 / +220 and the node colour (fill with alpha x opacity) lands at +196. The same +0x20 byte is the visible flag of a Reference (header +0xC0); runtime +204 mirrors it (live: BGBlur's Rect00 and the Tab / MainTab rects with flag 0 read visible 0 and colour 0).

runtime node layout: +24 parent, +32 next sibling, +48 object id, +52 kind (1 layer, 3 text, 4 ninegrid, 12 component reference), +56/+60 position (int32), +64/+68 size (int32), +72/+76 pivot (int32), +80/+84 scale (float), first child +208; a component object embeds its own geometry node at +272 (its children start at +480). Live TextBoardJobLv root: pos (0,-2) size 40x24 pivot (20,12) although the file says 40x20; its Title text node is 14x24 (file 14x20): sizes and the root are re-fitted after the build (the code that does it was not located; the font line height gives the same 24).

behavior.text: 7 -> 7 (ellipse), 8 -> 8 (bezier), 9 -> 13 (collision), 10 (the default branch) -> 12 (component reference), 11 -> 10, 13 -> 9 (Mask); each branch returns when the node's runtime kind (+52) is not the one it expects.

V: the node's own name key is stored at +216, a second name key from the string at header +0xA0 at +248 (live and file: 'TextBoard01' for TextMask/MaskNode00), and +264 / +288 are refreshed from the key's table row; when the data block's count (block +0x44) is positive the first entry's name replaces +216 and its int goes to +232. The kind 9 node itself has no draw in GUINode_DrawChildren (the dispatch ignores it), so it is a name binding: MainTab_BindNodes finds the Title text node of the component this name selects.

name: GUINode_BuildLocalMatrix
purpose: Builds a node's local 2x3 matrix from scale (+80/+84), pivot (+72/+76), rotation (+88) and position (+56/+60).

behavior.text: S = [sx 0 0 sy | tx = sx * (float)(-pivotX), ty = sy * (float)(-pivotY)] with sx = node+80, sy = node+84, pivotX = int node+72, pivotY = int node+76 (scale about the pivot, the pivot is moved to the origin first).
sub_1403D83FC rotates all three row pairs by angle node+88: (m0,m1) -> (m0*cos - m1*sin, m0*sin + m1*cos), the same for (m2,m3) and for (tx,ty), with sinf / cosf of the raw float (radians).
then tx += (float)(pivotX + posX), ty += (float)(pivotY + posY) with posX = int node+56, posY = int node+60 (the integer sums are formed first).

result in the engine's row-vector layout [m0 m1 m2 m3 tx ty]: x' = m0*x + m2*y + tx, y' = m1*x + m3*y + ty. So a node point v (node-local, origin = top-left of the node box) maps to R(rot) * S * (v - pivot) + pivot + position, and the pivot is the point of the box that stays at position + pivot when the node is scaled or rotated.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F0270). The pivot default set by the size setter (sub_1403EF6B4 when node+142 = 0) is size / 2 in integer division, so an unscaled node is simply translated by its position (pivot terms cancel). For the Job Tree text nodes this is the matrix GUITextNode_Draw multiplies glyph pen positions with.

name: GUINode_ClearVisibleSubtree
purpose: Sets the visible byte (+204) to 0 for a node and everything below it, following layer children and nested components.

behavior.text: loop on node: node+204 = 0; kind 1 recurses into every child (+208 / +32); kind 9 (name +248) and kind 12 (name +208) find the referenced component (GUIWidget_FindComponentCached) and continue with that component's root (comp+272); kind 9 sets the component's +562 = 1 first, kind 12 returns unless the component's +562 is set and then clears it. Other kinds stop after clearing their own flag.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1404095B8). The renderer skips nodes with +204 = 0, so this is the 'hide' for culled subtrees.
open_questions: Why kind 9 sets +562 and kind 12 clears it (looks like the mask component is kept alive so it can still be drawn into its layer).

name: GUINode_DrawChildren

name: GUINode_DrawKind10

purpose: Draw hook for runtime node kind 10 (file type 11): resolves the node's two names, opens a component layer for the referenced component and queues an 80-byte draw record.

the component named by the key at node+224 is looked up in the widget's component map (sub_1403F96CC, widget +136). When it is found, loaded (component +416) and visible (+192 = 0 or opacity +188 > 0), a draw context is built (ComponentDrawContext_Build) and ComponentLayer_Begin(r, ctx, 1) opens a layer; the layer's texture size is read from the layer record.

purpose: Draw hook for runtime node kind 5: draws a string of characters (digits, a space, other characters) from one image part, each with its own advance; the draw counter makes it consume a layer slot.

the string is the std::string at n+272 (the pointer is n+272 itself when the capacity n+296 is below 16, else the heap pointer stored there); per character the advance is the int16 n+314 for '0'..'9', n+318 for a space and n+316 for any other character; a non-positive value falls back to the part width divided by 1 (2 when the part byte +35 is set); the sum of the advances is the string width used to place the quads.

purpose: Finds a named state (animation/visibility group) of a node in its state vector.

notes: The set-state idiom: FindState(node,key); state+104 = 1; GUINode_PlayState(state).

name: GUINode_IsAncestorDirty
purpose: True when the node or any ancestor has its dirty byte (+149) set.

behavior.text: node+149 != 0, or (parent node+24 != 0 and the same test recursively on the parent).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403EF834). Thunk-sized; listed because it gates text relayout.

name: GUINode_LoadTree
callees: GUINode_BuildFromFile, sub_1403F5910, sub_1403F0654, sub_1403F4BA8, sub_1403FA344, sub_1403D87F4, sub_1403DC750
purpose: Builds one node from its file record and, for a Layer, its children; a Reference node gets its component by name from the file's component array.

behavior.text: GUINode_BuildFromFile(ld, fileNode, node) first.
Layer (type 1): children from the table at fileNode + int(+0x90), int(+0x94) entries (offsets relative to the table), each built by sub_1403F5910 and linked in order.

Reference (type 10), when ld+32 is set: the file header is ld+8, the component array header + int(header+4) with int(header+8) records of 64 bytes; each record's name (record + int(record+0)) is compared byte by byte with the node's component name (fileNode + int(+0x70)); the FIRST match is instantiated (sub_1403F4BA8 -> GUIComponent_LoadDef), registered (sub_1403FA344) and its name key copied to node+208.
type 13 (Mask) is resolved after it the same way (not read further).

notes: The name is ours. The lookup is a linear search over every record of the file; names must be unique, the first match wins.

name: GUINode_NameEqualsKnownKey
purpose: Tests a name key against one global key (string at qword_143CDA2A0+5144, interned id at +5152): id compare when both ids are non-zero, byte-wise string compare otherwise.

behavior.text: the key at qword_143CDA2A0+5144 is the C string "#Component" (the runtime name of an embedded component root).
when k+8 != 0 and dword (qword_143CDA2A0 + 5152) != 0: returns k+8 == that id. Otherwise byte-wise C string compare of *k with the string pointer at +5144; returns equal.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1404007FC). 590 hits per 4 s. I: the key is a reserved state name (the state that is applied specially in ApplyStateAtFrame); the text was not read because it is filled at run time.

name: GUINode_NewState

behavior.text: GUINodeState_Alloc(qword_143CDA280 + 8) allocates the object; UIName_Assign(state, key); state+112 = 1.
the first free of the four owner id slots at state+120 .. +132 receives comp+8 (the component's own id), so the component is the owner that receives the state's events.
the state pointer is appended to the vector comp+616 .. +624 (end of storage +632).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1404096D4). The base component class routes event type 40 of its states to GUIAddon_OnStateEvent (vtable slot 2), which is how state links and jump targets work.

name: GUINode_PlayCursorOutState
callers: GUIComponent_CursorLeave, GUIComponent_OnFocusLost-family paths (GUIComponent_OnFocusLost itself plays FocusOut / CursorOut inline)
purpose: Stops the CursorOver state, starts the CursorOut state and clears the cursor-over flag +574 (mirror of GUINode_PlayCursorOverState).

behavior.text: GUINode_StopState(node, key +4696 = 'CursorOver'); state = GUINode_FindState(node, key +4712 = 'CursorOut'); when it exists +104 = 1 and GUINode_PlayState; node+574 = 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040A0E4). The key names are V from the static list (see the file docstring). Careful: the focus pair GUIComponent_OnFocusGained / OnFocusLost use the keys +4664 / +4680, which the same list names 'FocusIn' / 'FocusOut', not CursorOver / CursorOut as their sheets say; the CursorOver / CursorOut pair is only played by the cursor enter / leave virtuals.

name: GUINode_PlayCursorOverState
purpose: Stops the node's CursorOut state, starts its CursorOver state and sets the cursor-over flag (+574).

behavior.text: GUINode_StopState(node, key at qword_143CDA2A0+4712), GUINode_FindState(node, key at +4696) then +104 = 1 and GUINode_PlayState; byte node+574 = 1.

notes: The state keys are the element keys 'CursorOver' (+4696) and 'CursorOut' (+4712) (names read in the live state traces).

name: GUINode_PlayShowHide
proto: int *GUINode_PlayShowHide(GUINode *node, char show, unsigned char instant, const char *showName, const char *hideName)
callers: about 70 sites (EquipDetail_Refresh, JobTree_SetPanelRecord, WorldMapScreen_BindNodes and many panels)
callees: UIName_Key, GUINode_StopState, sub_140409824, sub_14002620C, memset, sub_1403D8D1C
purpose: Plays a node's Show or Hide animation (default state names 'Show' and 'Hide'): stops the opposite one and starts the wanted one, optionally jumping to its end frame.

behavior.text: node == 0 does nothing. Copies showName (default 'Show') and hideName (default 'Hide') into two 260-byte local buffers (memset 0x104; sub_14002620C copy, max 259).

the state stopped first is: show == 0 -> the Show buffer, show != 0 -> the Hide buffer. The state then played (UIName_Key + sub_140409824(node, key, (instant ^ 1) - 1)) is: show == 0 -> the Hide buffer, show != 0 -> the Show buffer (as decompiled: v11 = a2 ? Hide-buffer : Show-buffer is stopped, v12 = a2 ? Show-buffer : Hide-buffer is played).

sub_140409824(node, key, frame): find state, +104 = 1, GUINode_PlayState, then frame < 0 -> the state's own value at +88 (its length), else min(frame, +88); that value is stored as float at +80 and +84, and /60.0 at +76; +106 = 1. (x ^ 1) - 1 is 0 for instant = 1 and -1 for instant = 0; so instant = 1 passes frame 0 and instant = 0 passes -1 (the state's own value). Which of these is 'jump to end' versus 'play from start' depends on what the +80 / +84 / +76 fields mean (I: current frame / duration), not decoded.
both element keys are released.

notes: JobTree_SetPanelRecord uses it for each job panel's Show / Hide. The 'instant' parameter jumps the animation to its end frame (frame = state length), i.e. it makes the panel appear / disappear with no visible fade.
open_questions: ? the exact start-frame rule for sub_140409824 when a3 >= 0 (min with the state length at +88; read from the decompile, not the disassembly).

name: GUINode_PlayState
callers: JobTree_Set*State, JobTree_SetPanelRecord, GUINode_PlayStateAtFrame, GUINode_PlayStateAtFrameEx, GUIAddon_OnStateEvent, UIAddonFingerCursor_PlayLoop, the finger cursor pose functions
purpose: Starts a state: resets its time, sets the running flags (+105/+106) and the 60 fps frame time.

behavior.text: byte +107 (paused) is read and cleared. When it was set, nothing else happens: a paused state keeps its clock and only the pause is lifted.

otherwise time +76 = 0, frame +80 = 0, previous frame +84 = 0, +105 = 1 (running), +106 = 1 (dirty / restarted), +110 = 0 (hold). When the loop range start +92 is below its end +96, the frame is then set to (float)+92 and the time to +92 / 60.0 (the state starts inside its range).
it does not touch +104 (enabled), +108 (loop) or +72 (rate): callers set +104 = 1 first, and UIAddonFingerCursor_PlayLoop sets +108 = 1.
nothing is applied to the nodes here.
the first application happens in the next component update, after GUINodeState_Advance has moved the frame by one tick, so the first applied frame is about 1 (one tick of 60 fps frames), not 0.
sets the state's +105 / +106 to 1 (running), time 0 (or the start frame / 60 when +92 < +96).

notes: State fields: struct GUINodeState.

name: GUINode_PlayStateAtFrame
callers: about 170 call sites: every addon that snaps a state (e.g. GUIWidget_Show / Hide, GUIComponent list slot reset in GUIComponentList_LayoutSlots, JobTree-range addons sub_1401D3550 ...)
purpose: Starts the named state and jumps it to a given frame (a negative frame = its last frame).

behavior.text: state = GUINode_FindState(node, key); none = return. state+104 = 1; GUINode_PlayState(state).
f = frame < 0 ? state+88 (frame count) : min(frame, state+88); f = max(f, 0). Then state+84 = state+80 = (float)f, state+76 = (float)f / 60.0 and state+106 = 1 (dirty).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140409824). Because GUINode_PlayState leaves the frame alone when the state is paused (+107) this can also scrub a paused state. Calling it with frame -1 right after a StopState is the idiom for 'jump to the end pose of this state' (the resting look).

name: GUINode_PlayStateAtFrameEx
proto: char GUINode_PlayStateAtFrameEx(GUINode *node, NameKey *key, int frame, char flags)
purpose: GUINode_PlayStateAtFrame plus a flag byte that also sets the state's pause / hold / loop / keep-alive bytes.

behavior.text: same start as GUINode_PlayStateAtFrame (+104 = 1, PlayState, frame clamp, +84 = +80 = f, +76 = f / 60.0, +106 = 1).

bit0: when state+105 (running) is set and state+107 (paused) is clear, state+107 = 1. bit1: +110 = 1 (hold). bit2: +108 = 1 (loop); else bit3: +108 = 0. bit4: +109 = 1 (keep alive); else bit5: +109 = 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140409898). Flag byte meanings follow the GUINodeState_Advance field notes (+107 paused, +108 loop, +109 keep, +110 hold); the 'bit0 -> +107' rule only applies when the state is running.
open_questions: ? which flag combinations the callers pass. ? +109 meaning (read from GUINode_UpdateStates: the state is not stopped when it is past its end while +109 is set).

name: GUINode_PropagateField48
purpose: Recursively assigns `value` to child->+48 for the node's children (linked via +32), descending when child kind (+52) == 1.

behavior.text: used when a node is attached to a parent (sub_1403F0654): the child inherits the parent's +48.
this is why every 'Unit' gadget +0x30 equals its component root's object id.

notes: Do not treat +0x30 as sprite part data.

name: GUINode_ResolvePins_Fraction
purpose: Resolves a node's edge pins against its parent size when the pins are stored as fractions of the parent (left/top/right/bottom flags in node+140).

behavior.text: node+56/+60 = left/top, +64/+68 = width/height, +72/+76 = pivot (initialised to size/2 by the constructor sub_1403EF3B4 unless +142).

cached pin floats at +116..+136 start as FLT_MAX; the first call derives them as position / parent size; flags: 1 = left, 2 = top, 4 = right, 8 = bottom (5 / 10 = both opposite pins: the node stretches).
the file's `+0xD4` edge flags (bits 0x1, 0x100, 0x10000, 0x1000000) are the same L, T, R, B bits.

notes: Explains why line parts keep their offsets to the component edge when a Reference node is drawn larger than its component (docs/reference/arrows.md).
open_questions: Which node classes use this variant and which use GUINode_ResolvePins_Offset is not traced (?).

name: GUINode_ResolvePins_Offset
purpose: Resolves edge pins stored as pixel offsets from the parent edges (same flag bits as GUINode_ResolvePins_Fraction).

behavior.text: right/bottom pins are parent size minus the stored offset; both pins on one axis scale the node's size by the stored ratio (+132/+136).

name: GUINode_ResolvePinsDispatch
purpose: Chooses how a node's edge pins are resolved against its parent: pins as fractions (node+141 = 0) or as pixel offsets (node+141 = 1).

behavior.text: node+140 = 0 -> nothing. Otherwise node+141 = 0 -> GUINode_ResolvePins_Fraction(n); node+141 = 1 -> GUINode_ResolvePins_Offset(n); any other value does nothing.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403EF860). 30769 hits per 4 s: the single hottest helper on the Job Tree page (it runs for every node whose size or pins changed).
open_questions: ? What +141 values above 1 would mean (none dispatched).

name: GUINode_SetCursorOverState
callees: GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState, GUINode_StopState, UIName_Key, sub_140409898, sub_1403D8D1C
purpose: Plays the node's cursor animation states: on the cursor node CursorOver, on every other node CursorOut, honouring the Check / Uncheck pair of toggle nodes.

behavior.text: returns when node == 0 or (opts[3] == 0 and node+554 == 0) (node+554 is the 'enabled for pointer / cursor' flag).

reads state 'CursorOver' (GUINode_FindState by UIName_Key); v = state byte +105 (already playing / finished flag, same field tested elsewhere as 'is playing'). If v == 0: when opts[1] == 0 stops 'Check' and 'Uncheck'; stops 'CursorOut'; then sub_140409898(node, 'CursorOver', 0, flags) where flags = 4 if opts[0] != 0 else 8. Nothing is done when CursorOver is already active.

reads 'CursorOver' state byte +105. If it is NOT set: checks 'Check' state (+105) and opts[1] == 0: if the node is checked and opts[1] == 0 it stops Check, CursorOver, CursorOut and plays 'Uncheck' (state +104 = 1, GUINode_PlayState) and exits; otherwise if 'CursorOut' is already set it returns; otherwise if 'Uncheck' is set and opts[1] == 0 it returns. Then (reached also when CursorOver was set) when opts[1] == 0 stops 'Check' and 'Uncheck'; stops 'CursorOver'; plays 'CursorOut' (state +104 = 1, GUINode_PlayState).
every UIName_Key result is released with sub_1403D8D1C(qword_143CDA2A0, key) when its refcount word is non-zero.

sub_140409898(node, key, frames, flags) = find state, set +104 = 1, GUINode_PlayState, then set state+88-based start frame (a3 < 0 uses the state's own length at +88), +76 = frame / 60.0, +106 = 1, and from flags: &1 -> +107, &2 -> +110, &4 -> +108 = 1, &8 -> +108 = 0, &0x10 -> +109 = 1, &0x20 -> +109 = 0. So flag 4 / 8 sets a 'cursor sound-on / off' byte at state+108 (V byte, I meaning).

notes: This is the generic hover / cursor highlight used by every list: GUI animation states named CursorOver, CursorOut, Check, Uncheck are authored in the node's state list; a node without them is silently ignored (FindState returns null). opts[0] chooses the +108 byte value 1 / 0 at CursorOver start.
open_questions: ? meaning of state bytes +105 / +107 / +108 / +109 / +110 (names guessed only from use: +104 start request, +105 playing, +106 started). ? what opts[3] is (it is the 'force' byte; no caller reads showed it set besides the Active / Deactive switcher).

name: GUINode_SetPivot
proto: void GUINode_SetPivot(GUINode *n, int x, int y)
purpose: Sets the node pivot (+72 / +76), marks the node dirty and invalidates the resolved pivot pins.

behavior.text: no change when equal. Otherwise +72 = x, +76 = y, +149 = 1; when u8 +140 != 0 the floats +132 and +136 are set to 0x7F7FFFFF (unresolved).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403EF704). 1131 hits per 4 s. Unlike GUINode_SetSize it does not touch byte +142; I: the file loader sets the explicit-pivot flag itself.

name: GUINode_SetPosition
proto: void GUINode_SetPosition(GUINode *node, int x, int y)
purpose: Sets a node's integer position; the track sampler, the finger cursor's glide and the smooth-scroll animation all use it.

behavior.text: the arguments are integers (the earlier prototype with floats was wrong): when x or y differs from the stored pair, both are written to node+56 / +60 and the dirty byte +149 is set; when the low two bits of node+140 (the pin layout flags) are set, the cached pin result at +116 / +120 is reset to FLT_MAX.
so every animated or glided node position is an integer; fractions never reach the matrices through the position.

notes: V (live): called on the Job Tree widget's root node (no parent) it moves every panel, arrow, label, the floor and the title together.

name: GUINode_SetScale
proto: void GUINode_SetScale(GUINode *node, float sx, float sy)
callers: GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels (scale track), about 12 screen routines (sub_1400FD238, sub_140106C54, sub_140127544, sub_1401389C4, sub_14013ABCC, sub_140157580, sub_140159E1C, sub_14015CF00, sub_140161F80 and more)
purpose: Sets a node's scale pair (+80 / +84, floats); the node is marked dirty when either value changed by more than 1.19e-7.

behavior.text: when |node+80 - sx| or |node+84 - sy| exceeds 1.1920929e-7 both are stored and the dirty byte node+149 is set; nothing else is touched.

a dirty node rebuilds its matrix in GUINode_UpdateColourAndMatrix and GUINode_UpdateSubtree dirties every child, so the scale reaches the whole subtree on the next UI pass (the scale acts about the node's pivot, GUINode_BuildLocalMatrix).
callers outside the animation sampler exist in about a dozen screen routines (cross references of the function), so game code scales nodes directly as well as through authored scale tracks.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403EF738). A zoom of the Job Tree would be this call on the tree root node (pivot 960, 540); the matrices below it follow (GUINode_UpdateColourAndMatrix multiplies each child by the parent's matrix and accumulates the scale at +184 / +188).

name: GUINode_SetSize
proto: void GUINode_SetSize(GUINode *n, int w, int h)
callers: 34 functions incl. GUIComponent_UpdateNodeTree, GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels, GUITextBoardComponent_Update, GUIComponent_SetAllocatedSize, GUINode_BuildFromFile, GUIComponent_Ctor, GUIComponent_LoadProps
purpose: Sets node size (+64 / +68), marks the node dirty, invalidates resolved pins and, unless the node has an explicit pivot, re-centres the pivot at size / 2.

behavior.text: no change when (w, h) equals the stored size. Otherwise +64 = w, +68 = h, +149 (dirty) = 1.
when (u8 +140 & 0xC) != 0 the cached right/bottom pin floats +124 and +128 are set to 0x7F7FFFFF (FLT_MAX, 'unresolved'), so GUINode_ResolvePins_* recompute them.
when u8 +142 = 0 (pivot not explicit): pivot +72 = w / 2, +76 = h / 2 (C int division, truncation toward zero).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403EF6B4). 13717 hits per 4 s. FLT_MAX (0x7F7FFFFF = 2139095039) is the 'pin not resolved yet' sentinel; GUINode_ResolvePins_Fraction tests |x - 3.4028235e38| <= 1.19e-7 to recognise it. Note the even-rounding of text boards happens in the caller, not here.
open_questions: ? What +142 is called in the editor (I: 'custom pivot').

name: GUINode_StopState
purpose: Stops a named state (+104 = 0, clears timers and flags) and recursively stops the nested states of kind 5.

behavior.text: FindState, then zero +76/+80/+84/+104..+110; for each 64-byte entry in the state's child list (+176..+184) of type 5, look the child node up and stop it.

name: GUINode_UpdateColourAndMatrix
callers: GUINode_UpdateSubtree (sub_1403F08C0) for every child and for the node itself; a dozen screen code paths call it directly (GuideBar_Layout, sub_14015CB04, sub_1401F36A0, sub_1402AD0DC, sub_1402EE84C, sub_1403F2FDC)
purpose: Per-node update that every node of every kind goes through each frame: resolves the node colour, multiplies it (and the opacity) with the parent's, derives the visible flag (+204) and, when the node is dirty, rebuilds the node's 2x3 matrix at +160 and the accumulated scale / rotation / sort order at +184..+200.

behavior.text: id = node+96. When bit 30 (0x40000000) is set the colour is looked up by name through sub_1403D9570(palette object qword_143CDAA60, id & 0xBFFFFFFF) (a std::map by name hash, falling back to a linear search of UITable 20 rows by name; -1 on a miss). When id is nonzero without bit 30 it indexes the palette's dword vector (palette+40; out of range = sub_1403D9570(palette, 0)). When id = 0 the node's own colour dword node+100 (RGBA bytes) is used. Call the result C.

with a parent P = node+24: node+196 = C.r * P.r / 255, +197 = P.g * C.g / 255, +198 = P.b * C.b / 255 (unsigned integer divide each, so (a*b)/255 truncates), and node+199 (alpha) = (int)((float)(P.a * C.a / 255) * node+108), where node+108 is the node's own opacity float; the (int) is a truncating float-to-int and only the low byte is stored. P.a (parent+199) already contains the parent's opacity, so opacity multiplies down the tree through the alpha byte, not through a separate float. Without a parent: +196/+197/+198 = C.r/g/b, +199 = (int)((float)C.a * node+108).
node+204 = node+144 (enabled) != 0 && node+153 != 0 && alpha (+199) != 0 && (no parent || parent+204 != 0).

when any of the bytes node+104 / +105 / +106 is not 100, each of R, G, B is replaced by clamp(c * pct / 100, 0, 255) using the colour computed above (integer divide by 100, clamp to 255 then to >= 0). Alpha is not touched. The percent bytes default to 100, so for ordinary nodes this block is skipped.

behavior.basis: (matrix, only when force != 0 or (visible and node+149 dirty)
behavior.text: ; then +149 is cleared): local matrix = GUINode_BuildLocalMatrix (sub_1403F0270) into node+160; with a parent it becomes Matrix2x3_Multiply(node+160, node+160, parent+160) (local applied first, then the parent's world matrix). Then the accumulators: +184 = parent+184 * node+80, +188 = parent+188 * node+84 (accumulated scale x / y), +192 = parent+192 + node+88 (accumulated rotation), +200 = parent+200 + node+92 (accumulated sort order). Without a parent +184/+188/+192/+200 are copies of node+80/+84/+88/+92.
node+205 = node+151; the word at node+150 (two flag bytes, +150 and +151) is cleared. (+150 makes GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels skip the node.)
nothing here snaps or rounds the matrix: translation is the float sum of integer position and pivot (see GUINode_BuildLocalMatrix); the only integer steps are the colour byte divides above.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403EFF08). Field map used here (node = runtime GUINode): +24 parent, +52 kind, +56/+60 position (int), +64/+68 size (int), +72/+76 pivot (int), +80/+84 scale (float), +88 rotation (float, radians), +92 sort order (int), +96 colour id, +100 own colour RGBA, +104..+106 colour percent, +108 opacity (float), +144 enabled, +149 dirty, +153 flag, +160 matrix (6 floats), +184..+200 accumulators, +196..+199 final RGBA, +204 visible, +208 first child, +32 next sibling, +40 previous sibling.
open_questions: What node+153 and +151 / +205 mean; what the palette (UITable 20) colours are; whether (int) of an alpha above 255 can occur (opacity > 1 would wrap the byte).

name: GUINode_UpdateStates
purpose: Advances every enabled state (timeline) of a component node by dt, or stops it when it is no longer valid.

behavior.text: runs only when the byte at (comp+496)+80 is 0; for each state in the vector comp+616..+624 with state+104 != 0: when !GUINodeState_IsPastEnd(state) (sub_140400118) or state+109 or state+107 is set, GUINodeState_Advance(state, dt); otherwise (past its end and neither flag set) GUINode_StopState (V: re-read 2026-10-28 against the decompile; the earlier wording had the polarity inverted).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1404099F4). Listed as the caller of GUINodeState_Advance; the accept rule of sub_140400118 was not read.

name: GUINode_UpdateSubtree
callers: component / screen update code (sub_1400F56D8, GuideBar_LayoutRow, sub_1401AA85B, sub_1401F36A0, ... about 12 callers), itself
callees: GUINode_UpdateColourAndMatrix, sub_1403EF834 (any ancestor dirty), sub_1403F1FAC, sub_1403F2208
purpose: Recursive per-frame colour / matrix pass over a node and its children (siblings via +32), run before the component tree pass; also rebuilds the text-board nodes (kind 8) that changed.

behavior.text: dirty = node+149; GUINode_UpdateColourAndMatrix(node, force). For each child (first child node+208, next +32): when dirty, child+149 = 1 (a dirty parent dirties every child, so a moved parent re-derives every child matrix).

child kind 1 recurses; kind 8 runs GUINode_UpdateColourAndMatrix and, when the child is visible and (an ancestor chain is dirty (sub_1403EF834) or +279 is set or (+280 = 1 and +284 > 0.0 and +296 > 0.0)), clears +279 and runs sub_1403F1FAC then sub_1403F2208 (kind 8 geometry rebuild, not read); kind 14 calls its virtual method +8; every other kind just runs GUINode_UpdateColourAndMatrix.

kind 8 is the kind that carries glyph-array style content (its fields +216..+224 are a vector of 552-byte elements, see GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels); kind 3 (text) is not rebuilt here, it is rebuilt in GUIComponent_UpdateNodeTree.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F08C0). Kind 12 / 9 (component references) are not special-cased here: they take the generic branch, their inner trees are updated by their own component.
open_questions: What kind 8 is (the +279 flag, +280 mode, +284 / +296 floats); what sub_1403F1FAC / sub_1403F2208 build.

name: GUINodeState_Advance
purpose: The clock of a UIB state (timeline): advances its time and 60 fps frame, applies jump markers and looping, and posts the keyframe-event (40), loop (38) and finished (39) events to the state's owners.

behavior.text: nothing happens unless dt > 0. Saved: f0 = s+84 (frame at the previous tick), fr = s+80 (frame), dirty = s+106 (then cleared to 0).

advances only when running (s+105) and not paused (s+107 == 0) and s+110 == 0: [lo, hi) = (s+92, s+96) when s+92 < s+96, else (0, s+88 = frame count); s+76 (time) += dt * s+72 (rate); fr = s+76 * 60.0; s+80 = fr.

jump markers: for every entry of the state's list (s+176..+184, 64 bytes each) with type (+0) == 1: when (float)entry+12 > f0 and fr >= (float)entry+12: hit = 1, s+80 = (float)entry+8 and s+76 = entry+8 / 60.0 (a goto: playing past frame entry+12 jumps to entry+8).
end: the test uses the current s+80; when >= (float)hi: if s+108 (loop) is set: hit = 1, s+80 = lo, s+76 = lo / 60.0; else s+80 = hi, finished = 1, s+105 = 0 (stopped on the last frame).
s+84 = the frame after these rules (also when not advancing, then it equals s+80).

for every entry with type != 1, event 0x28 (40) with ev+16 = s and ev+24 = the entry index is posted to the owners (s+120, node 0) when entry+8 != entry+12 (a span entry: EVERY tick, so it can drive a continuous link), or when |f0 - fr| > 1.19e-7 and (float)entry+8 > f0 + (dirty ? -1.19e-7 : 0) and fr >= (float)entry+8 (a point entry fires the tick the frame passes it; on the first tick after a (re)start frame 0 fires). Here fr is the frame after the advance but BEFORE marker jumps and looping.
after the entries: hit -> event 0x26 (38) {state, -1}; finished -> event 0x27 (39) {state, -1}.

the arithmetic is single precision: time = (dt * rate) + time and frame = time * 60.0. A jump or a loop sets the frame to the target integer and the time to target / 60.0, so the overshoot past the end frame is dropped: a cycle lasts the whole number of ticks needed to reach the end frame (40 ticks of exactly 1/60 s for a 40-frame state, 40.0 reached at the 40th tick).

a state that is paused by a link (+107) is not advanced: only its dirty byte is cleared and +84 = +80; its frame is written by GUIAddon_OnStateEvent. With dt <= 0 nothing at all happens, not even the dirty clear.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403FFDF8). State layout (V): +72 rate, +76 time s, +80 frame, +84 previous frame, +88 frame count, +92 / +96 loop range, +104 enabled, +105 running, +106 dirty / restarted, +107 paused (scrub-driven by a parent link), +108 loop, +110 hold. The tracks are NOT evaluated here: GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims runs right after GUINode_UpdateStates in GUIComponent_Update and samples every active state at the float frame +80 (V; the key search inside the samplers truncates it, the interval position does not). GUINode_ApplyStateAtFrame (sub_140409A98) is the one-shot variant for a given integer frame. State fields: struct GUINodeState.

name: GUINodeState_Alloc
purpose: Takes a 208-byte state object from the state pool and gives it its default values.

behavior.text: the pool is a vector of 13312-byte blocks (64 objects of 208 bytes) with a 64-bit use mask per block; a new block is allocated when all are in use; the object is the first free bit.

defaults: the four name keys (+0, +16, +32, +48) empty; +64 = 0; +68 = -1; +72 = 1.0 (rate); +76 = +80 = +84 = 0; +88 = +92 = +96 = 0; +104 = 1 (enabled); +105 .. +111 = 0; +112 = 0 (set to 1 by GUINode_NewState); +200 = 0; the vectors at +144 and +176 are empty.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140405098). Field meanings: struct GUINodeState.

name: GUINodeState_IsPastEnd
purpose: Rule used by GUINode_UpdateStates to decide whether a running state is to be advanced: false when restarted, true when held, otherwise frame >= end frame.

behavior.text: byte s+106 (dirty / restarted) != 0 -> false. Byte s+110 (hold) != 0 -> true.
end = (s+92 >= s+96) ? (float)(int s+88) (frame count) : (float)(int s+96) (loop end); result = (float s+80 (current frame)) >= end.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140400118; earlier sheets call it the 'accept rule'). 338 hits per 4 s. The comparison is single-precision float >= on an int converted to float. Caution: the polarity (true = frame reached the end) conflicts with GUINode_UpdateStates' wording 'accepts it ... Advance'; see open question.
open_questions: ? Whether UpdateStates advances on true or on false (re-read the branch polarity in GUINode_UpdateStates before building the simulator's state loop).

name: GUIOwnerMap_Find
purpose: Looks an int key up in a std::map<int, T*> (red-black tree head at m+16) and returns the stored pointer or null.

behavior.text: lower_bound walk from head->parent (+8): node key is the int at node+32, left = +0, right = +16, sentinel flag = byte +25; value = node+40. Returns 0 when not found (lower bound is the head or its key > the wanted one).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DC1A8). 3184 hits per 4 s. A plain MSVC std::map find; no arithmetic.
open_questions: ? What the key is in GUIOwners_PostEvent (I: owner / event id).

name: GUIOwners_PostEvent
proto: int GUIOwners_PostEvent(unsigned int ownerIds[4], GUINode *node, UIEvent *ev)
purpose: Delivers a component event to every owner registered on the node: each non-zero id (node +584..+596) is resolved in the actor table and its vtable slot 2, OnEvent(owner, node, ev), is called.

behavior.text: this is the dispatcher that reaches JobTree_OnEvent (vtable slot 2 of the tree addon); the job tree registers itself on every panel node in JobTree_RefreshAddon (writes the addon id into the node's owner array).

notes: Event ids posted (templates at xmmword_1407232F0..): 12/13 select/deselect, 14..17, 18 (job tree panel tag), 19 component focus gained (CursorOver state), 20 focus lost (CursorOut), 21..27 scroll/drag, 31..36 list items, 38..41, 43/44 widget load/unload.

name: GUIQuad_EmitGouraud
proto: __int64 GUIQuad_EmitGouraud(UIRenderer *r, const float m[6], const int rect[4], const uint8 colors[16], unsigned int sortKey, char flags)
purpose: Emits one coloured quad (the Rect node's draw): the rectangle pushed through a 2x3 matrix, four corner colours, drawn as four triangles around a centre vertex; optionally also an outline command.

behavior.text: rect = {x0, y0, x1, y1}; each corner is (X, Y) = (m0*x + m2*y + m4, m1*x + m3*y + m5) in float: c0 = (x0,y0), c1 = (x1,y0), c2 = (x0,y1), c3 = (x1,y1) (rect[2] is the right edge, rect[3] the bottom edge).

colors = 4 RGBA dwords in the order c0, c1, c2, c3. The centre vertex has the position ((c0 + c1 + c2 + c3 computed as ((c0+c1)+c2)+c3) * 0.25) and the per-channel colour (sum of the four bytes) >> 2 (integer, truncating; alpha included).

a type-12 command with 12 vertices of 24 bytes (x, y, 0, RGBA at +12, zeros) allocated by UIRender_AppendCommand(r+37936 object, 12, sortKey, r+48): triangles (c0,c2,centre), (c2,c3,centre), (c3,c1,centre), (c1,c0,centre). So the colour varies linearly toward the centre, NOT as a bilinear gradient across a two-triangle quad.
after the vertices UIRender_AccumulateQuadBounds(r, the four corner positions) updates the draw bounds.
when (flags & 2) a second command (sub_1403B830C, type 8) with 8 vertices is built from the four corner positions and the corner colours with alpha halved (alpha >> 1; R, G, B unchanged).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403E00AC). Pixel-exact rule for a simulator: the interior of a Rect node with four different corner colours is a four-triangle fan with an integer-averaged centre colour; a single colour (all corners equal) is flat.
open_questions: ? Exact layout of the outline command (which vertex pairs) and the difference to sub_1403E0824 (the +224 variant).

name: GUIRectNode_Draw
purpose: Draws a Rect node (runtime kind 6): one quad with a colour per corner.

behavior.text: skipped when node+204 (visible) is 0 or node+145 (hidden) is set; otherwise sub_1403E6440(r, ctx, 1) selects the plain-colour pipeline state and the node's matrix (node+160) is multiplied with the context matrix (ctx+504).

the node colour (node+196, the fill with alpha x opacity) is multiplied per channel with the context colour (ctx+540), and each of the four corner colours (node+208 / +212 / +216 / +220) with that product, /255 each; the quad is node+64 x node+68 in size and goes to sub_1403E00AC (or sub_1403E0824 when node byte +224 is set) with the four vertex colours; node byte +225 adds the outline flag.

notes: The studio's chrome renderer (game_chrome.js) follows this: corner colour x fill colour (alpha x opacity), Gouraud across the quad, premultiplied-over blending, GPU pixel-centre coverage.
open_questions: The difference between sub_1403E00AC and sub_1403E0824 (the node's +224 flag) (?).

name: GUIRenderer_ResetFrame
purpose: Per-frame reset of the GUI renderer: default draw states, clip bounds sentinels, the quad UV transform and all 512 layer records.

behavior.text: UIDrawState_Copy(r, &unk_1408FF878) and UIDrawState_Copy(r+48, ...) install the default draw states in two slots; r+4 &= 0xFFFFFFF0, r+24 &= ~0x200, r+72 &= mask (I: clears blend / flag bits of those states).

r+96 = 0, byte r+136 = 0 (recording flag, read by UIRender_AppendCommand / QueueImageDraw bit 0). Bounds sentinels: r+152 and r+160 = 0x41DFFFFFFFC00000 (as a double = +2147483647.0) and r+168 and r+176 = 0xC1E0000000000000 (double -2147483648.0): an inverted min / max rectangle initialised to extremes (I).

for layer index 0..0x1FF (512): layer record (592 bytes each, base r+303492 + 592*i): +0 = index, +572 = v10 = *(qword*)(R + 8*? + 6560) (R = qword_143CDA098: a default render target pointer, array at R+6560; r+...); GUILayer_ResetRecord(r, i) is called for each; V (disassembly, 2026-10-30): per slot the dirty rectangle (16 bytes at r + 512 * i + 41824), the layer id dword (r + 512 * i + 41840) and the flag byte after it (+41844) are zeroed, which is what GUILayer_Flush / GUILayer_ExpandBounds use.

tail: r+606604 = -1, r+606584 / +606592 = 0, r+606600 = 0, r+606608 = 0, r+606616 = 0x7FFFFFFF, and the deferred-draw vector end r+606704 = begin r+606696 (clears the list GUIRenderer_RunDeferredDraws walks). *(*(R+37936)+208) = r + 303480 (current layer record pointer = the layer header just before the first record).

notes: The decompile lost several register assignments (r in rdx/r10 etc.), so offsets above are exact but the grouping of the sentinel bounds (which pair is min vs max, float vs double) is I.
