name: GUIRenderer_RunDeferredDraws
callees: virtual slot +104 of each record's object
purpose: After the frame's UI commands are recorded, calls each deferred draw callback registered in the renderer.

behavior.text: the list is a vector of 80-byte records between *(r+606696) (begin) and *(r+606704) (end); count = (end - begin) / 80 (the 0x6666666666666667 multiply is the divide by 5 of the 16-byte units).

for each record rec: layerNo = *(u32*)(r + 303492 + 592 * *(int*)(rec+76)) (the first dword of that layer's 592-byte record, the layer index/number written by GUIRenderer_ResetFrame); arg6 = layerNo - 1 if layerNo != 0 else 0.
calls rec->obj->vtable[+104]( obj = *rec, rec+16 (qword), rec+8 (qword), rec+32 (pointer to 24 bytes), *(u32*)(rec+56), arg6, rec+24 (qword), rec+60 (pointer) ) for each.
no clearing happens here; the list is cleared by GUIRenderer_ResetFrame (r+606704 = r+606696).

notes: Record layout I-ish from the use: +0 object, +8 / +16 / +24 qword args, +32 inline block, +56 dword, +60 inline block, +76 layer record index.
open_questions: ? who pushes the records (find the writer of r+606696..) and which objects use slot +104.

name: GUISlotVec16_Insert
proto: unsigned int GUISlotVec16_Insert(__int64 unused, GUISlotVec *vec, const __m128i *rec)
purpose: Inserts a 16-byte record into a std::vector-like container (allocator, begin, end, cap): reuses the first record whose first qword is 0, otherwise appends (growing by 1.5x).

behavior.text: vec = {+0 allocator object, +8 begin, +16 end, +24 cap}. Scans records 0..n-1 for a first qword of 0; the first hit is overwritten with *rec and its index returned.

otherwise, with end == cap the buffer grows: new capacity = cap + cap/2 (at least n + 1, clamped to 0xFFFFFFFF elements; > 0xFFFFFFFF throws via std::vector::_Xlen), allocated through allocator vtable +16, the old elements copied (and the tail shifted when inserting mid-vector, which never happens here), the old buffer freed through vtable +24; the new record is stored at index n. Without growth *end = *rec and end += 16.
returns the new size - 1 (the index of the appended record). The caller adds 1 and the kind bits to make a slot id.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403EE77C). The first-qword-0 free-record rule is what lets slot ids stay stable after a record's resource is released and cleared.

name: GUISlotVec32_Insert
proto: unsigned int GUISlotVec32_Insert(__int64 unused, GUISlotVec *vec, const __m128i rec[2])
purpose: The 32-byte-record twin of GUISlotVec16_Insert (used for the kind-2 texture-part vector).

behavior.text: same algorithm: first record with first qword 0 is overwritten (32 bytes copied), else append with 1.5x growth through the vec allocator (+16 allocate, +24 free), returning the index.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403EE918).

name: GUISwitch_SetOff
purpose: Sets a switch node off: plays its state and posts event 22 (constant at 0x140723390).

behavior.text: mirror of GUISwitch_SetOn.

name: GUISwitch_SetOn
purpose: Sets a switch node on: plays its state and posts event 21.

behavior.text: a switch node has kind 4 at +536 and its on flag at +648; the event goes to the add-on ids in its listener slots +584 (4 slots); the event constants are at 0x140723380.

name: GUIText_DecodeUtf8
purpose: Decodes one UTF-8 sequence (up to the old 6-byte form) into a code point and returns the pointer after it; the text layout's character reader.

behavior.text: lead < 0x80: 1 byte. lead < 0xE0 (including the stray continuation range 0x80..0xBF) is treated as a 2-byte lead (cp = (lead & 0x1F) << 6 | (b1 & 0x3F)). 0xE0..0xEF: 3 bytes; 0xF0..0xF7: 4; 0xF8..0xFB: 5; 0xFC..0xFD: 6 bytes; 0xFE / 0xFF: stores the lead byte itself and advances 1.
no validation of continuation bytes and no overlong / surrogate check (each continuation is masked with 0x3F).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D8510). The layout state pointers (+8 current, +16 next) are advanced with a separate decoder sub_1400796D0 in GUITextNode_HandleTag / PlaceGlyph; whether the two decoders differ was not compared.

name: GUIText_Expand
purpose: Runs the text formatter (qword_143CD9C00) over text with the argument vector (264-byte records) into out; returns 1 on success.

behavior.text: clears out (sub_140025C74). When qword_143CD9C00 = 0 returns 1 (out left empty). Otherwise r = sub_14007D060(formatter, out, text, args.begin = args+8, count = (args+16 - args+8) / 264); r >= 0 returns 1; r < 0 logs the error (sub_140026BD4) and returns 0.

sub_14007D060 packs up to 32 of the 264-byte argument records into 16-byte {value, type} cells (type at record+256: 1 and 2 = int, 3 = byte, 4 = pointer to the record, 0 = none) and calls sub_14007D160.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F0B10). 1276 hits per 4 s. With the formatter missing the node would be set to the empty string (the bool is 1 but out is empty); I: the formatter is always present at run time. sub_14007D160 (placeholder substitution) was not read.
open_questions: ? Placeholder syntax and the int type codes 1 vs 2 (sub_14007D160).

name: GUITextBoard_CacheAuthoredBox
callers: GUITextBoardComponent_Update (and one apparent mis-named region at 0x14040E3EA)
purpose: Once per component, snapshots the text node's authored rectangle and the component's authored size, the baseline GUITextBoardComponent_Update uses when it refits the board around the text.

behavior.text: runs only if byte comp+684 != 0 (the 'not yet cached' flag) and GUITextBoard_FindTextNode(comp) returns non-null.
with n = text node dwords: comp+648 = n[14] (x, node +56); comp+652 = n[15] (y, +60); comp+656 = n[16] + n[14] (right = w + x, node +64); comp+660 = n[15] + n[17] (bottom = y + h, node +68).
comp+664 = comp+336 (dword); comp+668 = comp+340 (dword): the component's authored width / height (I: +336/+340 are size).
comp+684 = 0 afterwards, so it is cached once.
callers GUITextBoardComponent_Update (0x14040E40E) and one more reference at 0x14040E3EA inside an exception-thunk-named region.

notes: Rect order is left, top, right, bottom in comp+648..+660 (I from the arithmetic).
open_questions: ? confirm that node +56..+68 are x, y, w, h (inferred from the sums).

name: GUITextBoard_FindTextNode
callers: GUITextBoardComponent_Update, UIAddonFFTOBattleMain4_vfunc_4 and about 18 addon functions
purpose: Returns the text node (kind 3) of a text-board component: the part found by name key qword_143CDA2A0+5000 under comp+272, or null.

behavior.text: the name key at qword_143CDA2A0+5000 is the C string "Title" (the text node every text board component names), so this returns the component's node called Title when its kind is 3.
node = GUINode_FindPartByName(comp+272, qword_143CDA2A0 + 5000); returns node only when node != 0 and node+52 = 3, else 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040AAC0). 5632 hits per 4 s.
open_questions: ? The name string at qword_143CDA2A0+5000 (set at runtime; not read).

name: GUITextBoardComponent_Update
callees: sub_14040E59C, sub_14040AAC0, sub_1403F1234, sub_1403EF6B4, GUINode_SetPosition, GUIComponent_Update
purpose: Update override of a text-board component class: fits the board's text node (kind 3 part named by qword_143CDA2A0+5000) to the text's extent, sizes the component to text plus margins (rounded up to even), and aligns the board inside the rectangle it was given, then runs the base update.

behavior.text: sub_14040E59C(comp) caches once (comp+684 flag) the text node's authored box: +648 = node x (+56), +652 = y (+60), +656 = x + w, +660 = y + h, +664 / +668 = the component's authored width / height (+336 / +340). The text node T is sub_14040AAC0 = GUINode_FindPartByName(comp+272, name) with kind 3 required; none = skip to the base update.
when comp+672 (a text id) is nonzero and differs from T+248, T+248 = it and T+316 (text dirty) = 1; when T+316 is set the text is re-laid-out at once (sub_1403F1234).

textW = T+432 - T+424, textH = T+436 - T+428 (the text's measured extent, int); w = max(textW, authored box width +656 - +648), h = max(textH, +660 - +652). Text node size = ((w + 1) & ~1, (h + 1) & ~1) via sub_1403EF6B4. Component root (comp+272) size = ((w + left + (authW - boxRight) + 1) & ~1, (h + top + (authH - boxBottom) + 1) & ~1) with left = +648, top = +652, boxRight = +656, boxBottom = +660, authW/authH = +664/+668. So every size is the content size plus the authored margins, rounded UP to an even integer.

behavior.basis: (alignment inside the allocated rectangle comp+528 x comp+532, which GUIComponent_UpdateNodeTree sets from the reference node's size)
behavior.text: horizontal mode comp+676: 0 or other = 0, 1 or 3 = (comp+528 - compW) / 2 (C integer division, truncation toward zero), 2 = comp+528 - compW; vertical comp+680 likewise with comp+532 and compH. The component root's position is set to that (GUINode_SetPosition(comp+272, x, y)).
finally tail-calls GUIComponent_Update(comp, time, force).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040E3F0). 8036 hits per 4 s. This is where a Job Tree text board's text node gets its size and the board its alignment offset; text pen y still follows GUITextNode_Layout / GUITextNode_Draw inside that node size (H = node+68 here is the even-rounded content height, so for a vertical-bottom node the 'H - size' term uses this rounded H, not the file H).
open_questions: Which text id / name the +5000 global is (likely 'Title', not read); whether the Job Tree digit boxes are instances of this class (the 8036 count suggests the text boards of the tab / row labels).

name: GUITextLayout_IconsReady
callers: GUITextNode_Layout, GUITextNode_UpdateLayout (sub_1403F1234, for nodes whose mode dword +416 is 3)
purpose: True when every inline-icon texture requested by the layout is loaded; caches the answer in layout+100 / +101.

behavior.text: byte layout+100 == 0 returns byte +101 (the cached 'ready' flag). Otherwise each 16-byte entry of the icon reference vector (+72 / +80, built by GUITextNode_PlaceIcon: dword +4 slot, dword +12 second slot) is tested with GUIFontSlots_IsLoaded on g_GUIFontSlots: entry+4 always, entry+12 only when non-zero; the first not-loaded returns 0.
when all are loaded (or the vector is empty) word +100 = 0x0100 (pending = 0, ready = 1) and +101 is returned.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DCE74). Called with node+320 = the layout. A layout containing icons is not re-laid-out until its icons are loaded (see GUITextNode_UpdateLayout).
open_questions: ? who sets +100 = 1 (probably GUITextNode_Layout when it records an icon).

name: GUITextNode_AlignVertical
purpose: Ends the layout of a text node: flushes the pending line and shifts every line's y by the vertical alignment offset of the node box (node+256), then computes the text bounds.

behavior.text: layout and st as in GUITextNode_FinishLine. Locals: H = (float)(int32 node+68), n = number of line records ((layout+48 - layout+40) / 24), content = last line.y + last line.height (line record +4 and +12 of the last record).
if there are no lines yet or st+64 (pending glyphs) is non-zero it first calls GUITextNode_FinishLine.

behavior.basis: (offset o by node+256, only when n > 0)
behavior.text: 0 top = 0; 1 middle = (H - content) * 0.5; 2 bottom = H - content; 3 distribute: step s = (H - content) / (n - 1) when n > 1, o = 0, and a single line gets (H - content) * 0.5; any other value = 0.
line i (i = 0..n-1) gets y += o + i * s (s is 0 except for mode 3).

then returns sub_1403DEE64(layout, st), which stores the text bounds at layout+104..116 (left = int(floor(min x) + 0.5), top = int(floor(min y) + 0.5), right = int(ceil(max x) + 0.5), bottom = int(ceil(max y) + 0.5), all ints; zeroed when empty or right <= left or bottom <= top; the extent uses each glyph's line.x + rec.x, line.y + rec.y and size * rec.f as the height).

notes: The name is ours (the IDB has sub_1403DE4D0). The offset is negative when the text is taller than the box (size 23 in H 20: bottom -3, middle -1.5), as in the live read of the Job Tree digit node. sub_1403DEE64 is not yet named in the IDB (proposed GUITextNode_ComputeBounds).
open_questions: ? who reads the bounds at layout+104..116 was not traced (sub_1403DCE74, called by GUITextNode_Layout after layout, is probably the consumer). ? the bounds formula was read from the decompile only, not checked live.

name: GUITextNode_ComputeBounds
purpose: Computes the integer bounding box of the laid-out text (all glyphs and line extents) and stores it at layout+104..116.

behavior.text: when the glyph vector (+8 / +16) and the line vector (+40 / +48) are both empty, layout+104, +108, +112, +116 are set to 0.

size = (float)(int16 node+304) with node = *st. Start xmin = ymin = +2^31, xmax = ymax = -2^31 (floats). For every glyph record (36 bytes): gx = line[rec+24].x + rec.x, gy = line[rec+24].y + rec.y (line records are 24 bytes: +0 x, +4 y); xmin = min(xmin, gx); ymin = min(ymin, gy); xmax = max(xmax, gx + rec.width (+8)); ymax = max(ymax, size * rec.f (+12) + gy). The glyph height is the node's size times the glyph multiplier, not a font metric.

for every line record, xmin = min(xmin, line.x (+0)) and xmax = max(xmax, line.x + line.width (+8)). So a right- / centre-aligned or justified line widens the box to the line extent even when its glyphs are narrower, and a left-aligned line (x = 0) forces xmin <= 0.

layout+104 = (int)(floor(xmin) + 0.5), +108 = (int)(floor(ymin) + 0.5), +112 = (int)(ceil(xmax) + 0.5), +116 = (int)(ceil(ymax) + 0.5); each value is first clamped to 2147483647. The conversion is a C truncation toward zero, so for non-negative values it is floor / ceil and for a negative value the +0.5 makes the result one larger (floor(-2.3) + 0.5 = -2.5 gives -2).
if left >= right or top >= bottom (checked after truncation) all four are set to 0.
the return value is not meaningful as a result (the last int stored, or a stale pointer in the empty case); the only caller returns it and GUITextNode_Layout ignores it.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DEE64). Layout+104..116 are read after layout by sub_1403DCE74 (GUITextNode_Layout's follow-up, not traced). The bounds include icon records too (they are ordinary glyph records, width size * f).
open_questions: ? the consumer of the bounds (sub_1403DCE74 and the draw path). ? whether the float or double path is used for the +0.5 (the values involved are exact in both for |v| < 2^24).

name: GUITextNode_Copy
purpose: Copies a text node's configuration fields from src into dst and marks dst dirty.

behavior.text: sub_1403EF54C(dst, src) copies the base node first.
if dst+208 != src+208 it runs sub_140025C74(dst+208) (re-init of the string member at +208; the string content itself is not copied here).
dword copies +248, +252, +256, +260, +264, +268, +272, +276, +280, +284, +288, +292 (text id, flags, colours); +296 is forced to 0 on dst (not copied).
+300 dword, +304 word, +306 word, +308 word, bytes +310..+315 copied; dst+316 = 1 at the end (needs relayout).
callers sub_140136A7C (0x140136AE0) and sub_1403FAD88 (0x1403FAF10).

notes: Does not duplicate the laid-out glyph vectors (+320..); the node relayouts because +316 = 1.
open_questions: ? whether sub_140025C74 clears or re-inits the string (called without src content).

name: GUITextNode_Draw
callees: GUIFontTable_GetSetRow, sub_1403EE35C, GUIFontRenderer_UploadPalette, sub_1403A94C8, UITable_GetRow, SDFFontRenderer_EmitGlyph
purpose: Draws one text node: builds the shader palette from the node's UIFontSet row and colours, then emits glyph quads (and the shadow pass) through SDFFontRenderer.

behavior.text: row = GUIFontTable_GetSetRow(node+300); the 80-byte row is copied into the palette block and its four colour slots (+8, +16, +28, +40) are blended with the node's colours (node +264..+292) by sub_1403EE35C and the draw alpha.
the block goes to GUIFontRenderer_UploadPalette (sub_1403EDEA4); each glyph is emitted by sub_1403A94C8 with the scale set by GUITextNode_SetRenderScale.

behavior.basis: (TEXT PLACEMENT, decoded 2026-10-28; Draw does NOT lay anything out, it only reads what GUITextNode_Layout stored)
behavior.text: the node holds a glyph vector at +328 (36-byte records: +0 x, +4 y, +8 width, +12 size multiplier f, +20 char, +24 line index) and a line vector at +360 (24-byte records: +0 x, +4 y, +8 width, +12 height, +16 x-squeeze, +20 flag). Per glyph Draw computes the pen y as line.y + rec.y + (UIFontType row +8 / 64) * size * rec.f, then the pen x as line.x + rec.x (lines 429-492 of the pseudocode: v77 = line+4 + rec+4, v78 = rec+0 + line+0, v92 = (row27[+8] * 1/64) * (size * rec.f) + v77), and maps (x, y) through the node matrix (node+160 times the draw state +504). SDFFontRenderer_EmitGlyph then places the quad at pen + (glyph.x0, glyph.y0) * size/64 (y0 is relative to the baseline), so the pen y IS the baseline.

behavior.basis: (live read of the Job Tree digit node, 2026-10-28, ReadProcessMemory only)
behavior.text: the node is W 18 x H 20, size 23, node+252/+256/+260 = 4 / 2 / 1; its line record is (x 0.0, y -3.0, width 13.80, height 23.0, squeeze 1.0, flag 0) and its single glyph '8' (56) is (x 0, y 0, width 13.80, f 1.0). So line.y = H - size = 20 - 23 = -3 exactly as the rule below predicts.

inside the node (origin = top-left of the node box, layout px) a line's y starts at the running cursor (node-local 0 for the first line; each finished line adds size + int16 node+308, where size = int16 node+304 and NOT the font's line height); the line record height is size. After all lines are built sub_1403DE4D0 adds an offset to every line.y with content = last.y + last.height and H = int32 node+68: node+256 = 0 top: +0; 1 middle: +(H - content) / 2; 2 bottom: +(H - content); 3 distribute: +(H - content) / (nLines - 1) * i, and a single line gets (H - content) / 2. The offset is negative when the text is taller than the box (size 23 in H 20 gives -3 for bottom, -1.5 for middle). Baseline in node-local y = verticalOffset + (UIFontType.Unknown8 / 64) * size  (for one line, f = 1).

the 'row +8' read by Draw (line 484-489) and sub_1403DDED8 is the in-memory row of nxd table 27 (UIFontType) as a raw record [unknown00 +0][path string offset +4][Unknown8 +8][UnknownC +12][Unknown10 +16][Unknown14 +20] (live: rows are 24 bytes, e.g. Jura = 0, 0x2xx, 56.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0). So the factor is Unknown8 / 64 = 56/64 = 0.875 for Jura SemiBold (type 6), 50/64 for Zilvertype (5), 55/64 for Bunyan (0), the nominal 'size' number and NOT the .fnt ascent (Jura ascent 62, descent 14, line height 76). The row offsets GUITextNode_Layout uses (+12 / +16 / +20 as the f multiplier, the alternate f and the 'size multiplier') are therefore UnknownC / Unknown10 / Unknown14 (1.0, 1.0, 0.0), one dword later than that page labels them; f = UnknownC = 1.0 for every row, and UnknownC * ... never changes the baseline (the f terms cancel: Layout adds K*size*(1 - f), Draw adds K*size*f).

line.x = 0 for node+252 = 0 (left) and for 4 (auto: becomes left unless the soft-wrap flag st+88 set by GUITextNode_WrapLine (sub_1403DE608) is on, in which case it is justified; without it, right only if layout+122, which is always 0), (W - lineWidth) / 2 for 1 (centre), W - lineWidth for 2 (right), 3 = distribute (extra space / (glyphs - 1) between glyphs); lineWidth = max(rec.x + rec.width) of the line, W = int32 node+64. Glyph rec.x = pen cursor + kerning; the pen advances by advance * (size / 64) * f (the .fnt advance in metric units), so rec.width = advance * size/64. Overflow node+260 = 2 (shrink): when lineWidth > W every glyph x and width is multiplied by W / lineWidth (stored as line+16 and applied again by Draw to the glyph scale x), lineWidth becomes W; = 3 sets the line flag only (not traced); 0 / 1 do nothing here.

text block dwords: +64 text id, +68 string offset, +72 int16 size (-> +304), +76/+77/+78 bold / italic / (+313 flag), +80 int16 -> +306, +84 int16 -> +308 (line spacing), +88 -> node+256 vertical, +92 -> node+252 horizontal, +96 -> node+260 overflow. So the quoted metrics list [1073, 70422, 1, 0, 0, 2, 4, 1] (text id, string offset, bold byte, +306, +308, VERTICAL 2, HORIZONTAL 4, OVERFLOW 1; the size 23 sits in the dword between) means: vertical = bottom, horizontal = auto (left), overflow 1. TextLv [1072, 70118, 1, 0, 0, 2, 4, 2] = bottom, auto/left, overflow 2 (shrink to fit).

behavior.basis: (test cases, layout px from the node top, font Jura SemiBold, H 20 for both boxes)
behavior.text: TextLv size 20: line.y = 20 - 20 = 0, baseline = 0 + 0.875 * 20 = 17.5. TextLvNum size 23: line.y = 20 - 23 = -3 (live), baseline = -3 + 0.875 * 23 = 17.125. The studio's baseline-middle shortcut (centre at origin.y + size / 2, baseline 24/64 * size below it) is origin.y + 0.875 * size = 17.5 / 20.125, so it agrees for the prefix (offset 0 because size = H) and puts the digit 3.0 layout px too low, i.e. 2.0 screen px at scale 2/3.

the function returns without drawing unless, in order, byte node+0xCC is non-zero, byte node+0x91 is zero, the string size qword at node+0xE8 is non-zero and sub_1403DBA94(font table, font set) returns true; r15 = node for the whole body (so r15 still names the node at SDFFontRenderer_EmitGlyph entry), r14 = ctx and rbx = st. Draw is therefore called for nodes it skips; 'Draw was called' is not evidence of drawing.

the node-local origin of (x, y) is the node's top-left corner (the node matrix at node+160 carries position and pivot; not decoded). Draw's right-edge fade (line 433-442: alpha falls off when a glyph's x passes W - size/2, for lines whose flag byte is set) was read but not exercised, so it is ? for these nodes.

notes: Placement formula (node-local layout px, one line): baseline_y = voff + Unknown8/64 * size with voff = 0, (H - size) / 2 or (H - size) for node+256 = 0, 1 or 2, H = node+68, size = int16 node+304; left_x = 0 (node+252 = 0 or 4), (W - w) / 2 (1), W - w (2). Measured by the owner: the retail digit sits about 1.25 screen px above the studio's baseline-middle; the rule gives 3.0 layout px = 2.0 screen px at scale 2/3 (live line.y = -3.0 confirms the 3.0), so either the retail estimate is low or the node scale is not exactly 2/3: not resolved. The font's own ascent / descent / line height are not used by placement at all (only the glyph quad offsets y0 / x0 from the .fnt are).
open_questions: Where the node matrix (node+160) gets its translation (position minus pivot, scale +80/+84) is not traced. Overflow mode 3 and the line flag byte (line+20) are not traced.

name: GUITextNode_FinishLine
callers: sub_1403DD3A0 (6 call sites: line-break tag handling), GUITextNode_AlignVertical, sub_1403DE608 (soft wrap)
callees: UITable_GetRow, sub_1403A942C (italic shear width), allocator vtable +16 / +24 for growing the line vector
purpose: Closes the current text line: measures it, applies the overflow rule and the horizontal alignment to the line's glyph records, adjusts each glyph's y for the font baseline term, appends the 24-byte line record and advances the y cursor.

behavior.text: layout (a1) holds the glyph vector (+8 begin, +16 end, +24 capacity; 36-byte records) and the line vector (+40 begin, +48 end, +56 capacity; 24-byte records), the allocator at +32, and the language flags set by GUITextNode_Layout (+122 always 0, +123 = Japanese / Simplified / Traditional Chinese). st (a2) is the layout state built on GUITextNode_Layout's stack: +0 node, +32 UIFontType id, +36 pen x, +40 line y cursor, +64 number of glyphs of the current line (they are the LAST st+64 records of the glyph vector), +85 horizontal alignment (node+252, 4 replaced by 0 for Korean), +88 soft-wrap flag (set to 1 only by sub_1403DE608, cleared here). Locals: size = (float)(int16 node+304), W = (float)(int32 node+64), K = UIFontType row (UITable_GetRow(27, st+32)) +8 (Unknown8) * 0.015625 (0 when the row is missing).

lineWidth = max over the line's glyphs of (rec.x + rec.width). When the renderer's shear (renderer+9524) is > 0 and the last glyph's italic byte (+29) is set, lineWidth = max + S * last.f, with S = sub_1403A942C = (font +232 * renderer+9500) * (shear * 96 * 0.5) (0 when renderer+189 is 0). I: S is the extra width the sheared top of an italic glyph needs.

when lineWidth > W, value 2 (shrink): squeeze = W / lineWidth, lineWidth = W, and every glyph of the line gets x = x * squeeze and width = width * squeeze; value 3: only the line flag (+20) is set to 1; other values do nothing here (value 0 wraps earlier, in GUITextNode_PlaceGlyph).

a = 4 (auto) with the soft-wrap flag set goes to the justify path; a = 4 without it becomes 2 (right) if layout+122 else 0 (left); 0 = left (x offset 0); 1 = centre, x offset (W - lineWidth) / 2; 2 = right, W - lineWidth; 3 = distribute: spacing d = (W - lineWidth) / (nGlyphs - 1) added between glyphs, a single glyph is centred; any other value = left. The justify path (a = 4 + soft wrap) is distribute when layout+123 is set (CJK), otherwise space justify: spaces = number of glyphs with char 32, per-space extra e = (W - lineWidth) / spaces, no spaces = centred. Distribute and justify set lineWidth = W.

behavior.basis: (per glyph i of the line, in order)
behavior.text: rec.x += (spaces before i) * e + i * d; rec.y += K * size - (size * rec.f) * K (so the later pen y of GUITextNode_Draw, which adds K * size * f, comes out at K * size for every f); a soft hyphen (char 173) becomes 32 unless it is the last glyph of the line, where it becomes 45 (hyphen-minus).

+0 x offset (the alignment value above, 0 for left), +4 y = st+40 (the cursor before this line), +8 width = lineWidth (W when shrunk, distributed or justified), +12 height = size, +16 x-squeeze (1.0 unless shrunk), +20 byte flag (overflow 3 and lineWidth > W), +21 byte = st+88 (soft wrap).
st+36 = 0, st+64 = 0, st+88 = 0, st+40 = size + (int16 node+308) + st+40. So the line pitch is the node's size plus the node's int16 +308 (UIB line spacing), not the font's line height.

notes: The name is ours (the IDB has sub_1403DDED8). The older text in GUITextNode_Draw said the horizontal 'auto' (4) becomes left 'unless the line ended on a forced break': the decompile says the flag is the soft-wrap flag set by sub_1403DE608, and then the line is justified (spaces for Latin, between glyphs for CJK); an unwrapped / last line is left aligned. Verified against live data for the single-line Job Tree nodes only.
open_questions: ? what sets st+88 other than sub_1403DE608 (no other writer was found in sub_1403DD3A0 or GUITextNode_PlaceGlyph). ? st+89 / st+90 meanings (read by GUITextNode_PlaceGlyph). ? the effect of the line flag (+20) and soft-wrap byte (+21) in GUITextNode_Draw (not read there per the earlier decode). ? multi-line behaviour was not checked against live memory (only a single-line node was read live).

name: GUITextNode_HandleTag
purpose: Executes one in-string control code of a text node (newline, alignment, colour push / pop, size, spacing, icon, soft-hyphen suppression); returns 1 when it was a known code, 0 otherwise.

behavior.text: the code is the dword at st+60. 10 (line feed): GUITextNode_FinishLine. 0xE000 / 0xE001: ++ / -- of byte st+86; 0xE002 / 0xE003: ++ / -- of byte st+87 (nesting counters; their effect in PlaceGlyph, probably bold / italic, was not re-read here: I).

0xE004 sets 0, 0xE006 sets 1, 0xE008 sets 2, 0xE00A sets 4; each first calls GUITextNode_FinishLine when the current line has glyphs (st+64 != 0). The odd codes 0xE005, 0xE007, 0xE009, 0xE00B finish the line and restore st+85 = the node's default alignment (byte node+252).

behavior.basis: (colour, st+84 = stack depth, st+68.. = stack bytes)
behavior.text: 0xE00C reads one parameter code point (plane-15 low 16 bits, else 0, sign-extended in the int): a negative value pops (--st+84), otherwise pushes the byte at st[68 + depth] and ++st+84. 0xE00D pops. 0xE00E sets byte st+89 = 1 and 0xE00F sets it to 0 (the flag copied to byte +32 of every glyph record, see PlaceIcon). 0xE010 sets byte st+90 = 1 (soft-hyphen suppress, read by WrapLine).

0xE100 reads a parameter, v = the node font set row (UITable_GetRow(27, st+32)) float +16 when byte g_GUIFontTable+40 is set else +12 (1.0 if no row), and sets st+52 (glyph multiplier f) = param * v / 256. 0xE101 reads two parameters: first * 0.0625 is stored in st+44 and added to the pen st+36, the second * 0.0625 (factor from a register, I) is stored in st+48. 0xE102: one parameter * 0.0625 into st+44 and added to st+36. 0xE103: one parameter * 0.0625 into st+48. 0xE104: one parameter -> GUITextNode_PlaceIcon(layout, st, iconKey).

a parameter is the code point that follows the tag in the string, taken only when (cp & 0xF0000) == 0xF0000 and then its low 16 bits, else 0. The string pointers st+8 (previous) and st+16 (next) are advanced by the decoder sub_1400796D0.
unknown codes return 0 (the caller then treats the code as a printable glyph).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DD3A0). Corrects the sheets GUITextNode_PlaceIcon / WrapLine only by adding the full code map: the icon tag is 0xE104 (V here). The mapping of 0xE004.. to alignment names (left / centre / right ...) is I: values 0, 1, 2, 4 are the node alignment enum, which GUITextNode_FinishLine uses.
open_questions: ? the glyph-level effect of st+86 / +87 (PlaceGlyph not re-read). ? the multiplier constant for 0xE101's second parameter. ? exact meaning of st+44 (probably the left margin of the current line).

name: GUITextNode_Init
purpose: Constructor defaults of a text node: base init with type 3, vtable, empty containers and default colours / flags.

behavior.text: sub_1403EF3B4(node, 3) (base node init, type 3); vtable at +0 = GUITextNode vftable 0x140721DA0.

three allocator pointer fields at +208, +320, +352, +384 each = qword_143CDAA80[+32] (allocator) or 0, followed by zeroed triples (+216.., +328.., +360.., +392..): empty std-vector / string members. +240 = 15 (small-string capacity), +232 = 0.
+416 dword = 0, +420 word = 256 (two bytes 0 and 1), +444 byte = 0, +448 = 0, +424..+440 zeroed; then sub_140025C74(node+208) (string init).
+304 = 32 (qword write: word +304 = 32, +306/+308 = 0), +312 = 0, +316 byte = 1 (dirty flag; GUITextNode_Copy also sets it to 1).
+300 (font set) is zeroed by the +296 qword store; +304 = 32 would be the size.

notes: Defaults here are the node's own; the font-set row defaults are separate (UIFontSetRow_Default). Offsets +248..+316 match those copied by GUITextNode_Copy.
open_questions: ? names of +264/+268/+272/+276 (alignment / flags, defaults 2,1,1,1). ? what the +320..+410 vectors hold (glyph / line lists, I).

name: GUITextNode_Layout
callees: GUIFontTable_GetSetRow, GUIFontSet_FontTypeForLanguage, sub_1403DBD60, GUITextNode_SetRenderScale, sub_1403DD3A0, sub_1403DD780, sub_1403DE4D0
purpose: Lays out one text node: resolves its font from the node's UIFontSet id and the game language, sets the glyph scale, then walks the string (colour/size tags) placing glyphs.

behavior.text: reads the UIFontSet key from node+300 and fetches the 80-byte row with GUIFontTable_GetSetRow (the singleton at qword_143CDAA48).
the UIFontType id comes from GUIFontSet_FontTypeForLanguage(row); if it is >= 18 or the font slot table qword_143CDA288[16*id+145] is 0 the node is not drawn.

per-type floats come from the UIFontType table via UITable_GetRow(27, typeId): +12 (UnknownC; +16 = Unknown10 instead when qword_143CDAA48+40 is set) is stored in the layout state as the per-glyph multiplier f, +20 (Unknown14) is the size multiplier. The nominal size Unknown8 (+8) is not read here (GUITextNode_FinishLine reads it for the baseline term).

size * UIFontType.Unknown14 + int16 node+306 is NOT the glyph size; it is the per-glyph x spacing stored at st+56 and added to each glyph's x from the second glyph on (the second term is 0 unless the node's data block sets it; forced to 0 for node+315 and a non-Japanese language). The glyph size is int16 node+304 (render scale = size / 64). Live: the Job Tree title and the chip prefix show no extra spacing.

calls GUITextNode_SetRenderScale, then loops sub_1403D8510 / sub_1403DD3A0 (tag handling; 0xE104 places an inline icon via GUITextNode_PlaceIcon) / GUITextNode_PlaceGlyph over the string, then GUITextNode_AlignVertical; it also resets the glyph / line vectors and the bounds, sets the language flags layout+120..124 (Korean maps alignment 4 to 0), moves out and finally releases the icon reference vector at layout+64, and writes layout+96 (1 or 3, 2 when the font is unusable).

notes: Text node runtime layout (V from sub_1403F0E24, sub_1403F5A80): +248 text id (UI-en key), +300 UIFontSet key, +304 int16 size, +306/+308 int16 extras, +310..+315 flags. See docs/reference/labels.md and fonts.md.
open_questions: The SDF shader (SDFFontRenderer) that applies the UIFontSet threshold/outline parameters is not decompiled (?).

name: GUITextNode_PlaceGlyph
callers: GUITextNode_Layout (one call per character not consumed by sub_1403DD3A0)
callees: sub_1400798F8 (UTF-8 encode), sub_1403A9A9C (glyph advance), sub_1403BF9D4 (UTF-8 decode), sub_1403A9114 (kerning pair), sub_1403A942C (shear width), sub_1401CBD68 (vector grow), sub_1403DE608 (word wrap)
purpose: Places one character of the string into the node's glyph vector: looks up its advance, applies fixed-width centring, italic and kerning adjustments, appends a 36-byte glyph record and advances the pen; wraps the line when the overflow mode is 0 and the glyph does not fit.

behavior.text: layout (a1): glyph vector at +8 / +16 / +24 (begin / end / capacity, 36-byte records), line vector at +40 / +48 (24-byte), language flags +120..+124 (+123 = ja / zh). st (a2): +0 node, +36 pen x, +40 line y, +48 y shift (added to rec.y), +52 f (glyph multiplier: UIFontType UnknownC, or Unknown10), +56 x extra (see below), +60 the character (UTF-32 code), +64 glyphs already in this line, +67.. colour index stack indexed by byte +84, +86 bold counter, +87 italic counter, +89 a byte copied to rec+32, +90 soft-hyphen-suppress byte. Locals: W = (float)(int32 node+64), size = (float)(int16 node+304), R = the renderer (qword_143CDA098 + 37944).

lookup char = 32 for U+00A0, 45 for U+2011 and U+00AD (173), else the char; it is encoded as UTF-8 and sub_1403A9A9C returns (R+9500 * glyph +16, R+9504 * glyph +20) = scaled (advance, y-advance), the first is used: adv. If adv is ~0 (missing glyph) the char is replaced by U+25A0 (non-Japanese language) or U+3013 (Japanese), written back to st+60, and the lookup is repeated. If st+90 is set and the char is 173, adv = 0 and the x extra = 0.

width = f * adv. If node+313 is set and not (node+315 set with a non-Japanese language): cell = f * size (size * 0.5 when the char is <= 0xFF), x offset = (cell - f * adv) * 0.5 and width = cell - x offset, so the glyph is centred in a fixed cell. I: node+313 is therefore a fixed-pitch (monospace) text flag; GUINode_BuildFromFile copies it from text block byte +78.

behavior.basis: (x offset when the line already has a glyph)
behavior.text: prev = last record of the glyph vector (the one before it when that record is a soft hyphen). x offset += st+56 (x extra: GUITextNode_Layout stores size * UIFontType.Unknown14 + int16 node+306 there, so it is a per-glyph spacing term). Italic transition (R+189 set): if shear R+9524 < 0 and prev is not italic (+29) and this glyph is italic: x offset -= S * f; if shear > 0 and prev is italic and this glyph is not: x offset += S * prev.f; S = sub_1403A942C (see GUITextNode_FinishLine). Kerning (only when not in fixed-width mode, or node+315 with a non-Japanese language, and R+189 set): the pair (prev char, this char) is looked up by sub_1403A9114 (binary search in the font's kerning table at font+216/+224 plus a second table at font+200); x offset += f * R+9500 * kern.x and the y offset = f * R+9500 * kern.y (zero otherwise).

+0 x = x offset + st+36 (pen), +4 y = y offset + st+48, +8 width, +12 f, +16 dword 0, +20 u16 char, +22 u16 ordinal of the glyph in the node, +24 u16 index of the line it belongs to (current line count), +26 byte colour index (st[67 + st+84], 0 when st+84 = 0), +27 0, +28 bold (st+86 != 0), +29 italic (st+87 != 0), +30 u16 0, +32 byte st+89. The vector grows through sub_1401CBD68 when full.
unless the char is 173, st+36 += x offset + width; st+64 += 1.

when node+260 (overflow) is 0 and rec.x + width > W it returns sub_1403DE608(layout, st), the word wrap, which moves the glyphs after the last break opportunity to a new line (sets st+88 = 1 and calls GUITextNode_FinishLine for the finished part). Other overflow modes are handled in GUITextNode_FinishLine.

notes: The name is ours (the IDB has sub_1403DD780). Hex-Rays lost the register for the st+56 and size locals in places; they were taken from the disassembly (movss xmm5 = [st+38h], xmm3 = int16 node+130h). The earlier text 'rec.width = advance * size/64' is consistent: R+9500 is size / 64 (GUITextNode_SetRenderScale).
open_questions: ? the exact meaning of st+89 / st+90 and of the colour index stack (+67..) was not traced (tag handler sub_1403DD3A0). ? whether the fallback glyph branch also updates the 'previous char' used for the soft-hyphen test (the decompile keeps the old copy). ? the second kerning table (font+200, sub_1403BA2D4) and the y-advance (R+9504 * glyph +20) were not decoded. ? the italic-transition rules were read as written; the intent (compensating the shear overhang) is I.

name: GUITextNode_PlaceIcon
proto: void GUITextNode_PlaceIcon(GUITextLayout *layout, GUITextLayoutState *st, unsigned int iconKey)
callees: UITable_GetRow, sub_1403DB6B8, SDFFontRenderer-side shear helper sub_1403A942C (SDFFont_ItalicShearWidth), sub_1401CBD68 (glyph vector grow), sub_1403DA594, sub_1403DA918, sub_14006635C (reference vector grow), GUITextNode_WrapLine
purpose: Places an inline icon (an Icon table image) in the text flow as a glyph record of width size * f with char 0, requests its texture slot, and wraps the line when it does not fit.

behavior.text: iconKey (a3) = the low 16 bits (sign-extended) of the code point that follows the tag, taken only when the code point is in plane 15 (code point & 0xF0000 == 0xF0000), else 0. The call is made from sub_1403DD3A0 (the in-string tag handler) for tag code 0xE104 (the branch of the 0xE100..0xE104 group where the decompile subtracts 0xE100 three times and compares the result to 1). Nothing happens when iconKey is 0 or UITable_GetRow(118, iconKey) (the Icon table, see Icon_FormatPath) returns null.

xe = st+56 (x extra, per-glyph spacing), W = (float)(int32 node+64), w = (float)(int16 node+304) * st+52 (f) = icon width, slot = sub_1403DB6B8(g_GUIFontSlots, iconKey) (texture slot id of the icon: keys 50..71 and 1100..1265 go through the two range helpers sub_1403DB420 / sub_1403DB5B4, other keys through a name lookup sub_1403DB140 / sub_1403DB280).

off = 0; if st+64 != 0 (not the first glyph of the line) off = xe, and when the renderer shear (R+9524, R = qword_143CDA098 + 37944) > 0 and the last glyph record's italic byte (+29) is set, off += S * last.f with S = SDFFont_ItalicShearWidth. x = off + st+36 (pen).

+0 x, +4 y = st+48, +8 width = w, +12 f = st+52, +16 dword slot id, +20 u16 char = 0 (this is what marks an icon record; GUITextNode_WrapLine never breaks next to one), +22 u16 ordinal = glyph count before the append, +24 u16 line index = current line count, +26 byte colour index (st[67 + st+84], 0 when st+84 = 0), +27..+31 = 0 (so bold and italic are off), +32 byte st+89.

a 16-byte entry is appended to the second vector at layout+64 (allocator +64, begin +72, end +80, cap +88): dword +0 iconKey, dword +4 slot, dword +8 = Icon row dword +12 (UnknownC), dword +12 = 0. If the slot record (sub_1403DA594(slots, slot)) exists and its refcount (+80) is exactly 1, entry +4 is replaced by the handle returned by sub_1403DA918 (a texture slot acquire / load request using the slot's path at +56). GUITextNode_Layout moves this vector out at the start of each layout and releases entry +4 and +12 (sub_1403DA30C) when it ends.
when node+260 = 0 and x + w > W it calls GUITextNode_WrapLine(layout, st).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DDC38). The icon's height is not stored; the bounds code (GUITextNode_ComputeBounds) uses size * f for every record. Not exercised by plain upright text.
open_questions: ? the exact tag byte sequence for 0xE104 in the UI strings and which Icon rows are used inline (the key range / the Icon table's row dword +12). ? how GUITextNode_Draw renders a char-0 record (reads +16 slot?). ? the semantics of sub_1403DB6B8 / sub_1403DA594 / sub_1403DA918 were only skimmed (slot lookup, refcount check, load request). ? the tag number 0xE104 was derived from the decompiled subtraction chain, not checked against a string.

name: GUITextNode_SetRenderScale
purpose: Sets the text renderer's per-node state: glyph scale = (int16 size) / 64 and the font slot of the resolved UIFontType.

behavior.text: scale = (float)(int16)node[304] * 0.015625 (= size/64), written as both x and y scale at renderer+9500/+9504.
font slot = signed byte at qword_143CDA288[16*(typeId+9)]; the slot is only set when it is >= 0.

with the font metric unit of 0.75 atlas px (docs/reference/fonts.md) one text size unit is 1/48 of the size in atlas px: output px per atlas px = size * (reference scale) * (screen scale) / 48 for every font. The studio's fontScale() uses exactly this.

when the node's byte +311 is non-zero the layout state's counter at +86 is incremented, and when +312 is non-zero the counter at +87; GUITextNode_Layout's glyph builder (sub_1403DD780) stores those counters as the glyph entry's bold (+86 != 0) and italic (+87 != 0) flags (glyph record bytes +28 / +29, read by GUITextNode_Draw to pick palette +64 = row +60 * row +4 for bold). The loader copies the text block's byte +76 to +311 and byte +77 to +312 (GUINode_BuildFromFile), so the flags are node data: every visible Job Tree text node has byte +76 = 1 (the arrow icon text 0). Live: all glyph records of the title, name plate and chip texts have +28 = 1.

notes: The earlier studio rule (divide by each font's ascent) was a fit; it was 5 % off for Zilvertype.

name: GUITextNode_SetString

purpose: Sets a text node's string; marks the layout dirty only when it differs. Always stamps the change time.

Family: sub_1403F106C (SetTextById) -> sub_1403F109C (SetTextExpanded) -> sub_1403F0B10 (format expander) -> SetString; sub_1403F1004 (printf form) -> SetString. name: GUITextNode_SetTextExpanded

purpose: Expands placeholders in text using args into a temporary std::string, then sets the result on the node; uses the raw text if expansion reports nothing.

if GUIText_Expand(&alloc, text, args) != 0, the string to set is the temp (heap pointer v8[0] when capacity >= 16, else inline v8); otherwise the original text pointer is used.
result = GUITextNode_SetString(node, str).
afterwards if capacity >= 16 the heap buffer is freed through allocator vtable slot +24 with size capacity + 1.

notes: This is where in-text macros (names, numbers) are resolved before the string reaches the layout. Chip text goes through this when set by id.

calls GUITextNode_SetTextExpanded(node, text, &args).
if args.begin != 0 afterwards, frees it through allocator vtable slot +24 with size 264 * ((cap - begin) / 264): the args vector has 264-byte elements.

name: GUITextNode_UpdateLayout

when the node mode dword +416 is 3 (text with inline icons) GUITextLayout_IconsReady(node+320) must also be true.

if the text id dword node+248 != 0, UIText_Get(id) fetches the string and GUITextNode_SetTextExpandedTemp(node, str) re-expands it (so a language change or a changed text id refreshes the string every update).

if GUINode_IsAncestorDirty(node), node+296 = *(g_GUICore + 2096) (the frame counter used by the draw path); then GUITextNode_Layout(node+320, node); a result of 1 clears byte node+316 (the layout dirty flag).

name: GUITextNode_WrapLine
callers: GUITextNode_PlaceGlyph (tail call, when node+260 = 0 and rec.x + width > W), GUITextNode_PlaceIcon (same test for an inline icon)
callees: sub_1400796D0 (UTF-8 decode of next), GUITextNode_FinishLine, allocator vtable +16 / +24
purpose: Word wrap: when the glyph just placed does not fit the node width, finds the last line-break opportunity in the current line, finishes the line before it (soft-wrap flag set) and starts a new line with the glyphs after it.

behavior.text: layout and st as in GUITextNode_FinishLine. Locals: n = st+64 (glyphs of the current line; they are the last n 36-byte records of the glyph vector at layout+8 / +16), next = the character decoded from the string at st+16 (the character AFTER the one just placed; only the French / German rules use it; the Hex-Rays text shows it as 0, the disassembly loads it from the decoder's output slot), j = number of trailing glyphs to move (starts at 1).

left = glyph record [count - 1 - j], right = record [count - j]; right starts as the last (overflowing) glyph. The scan stops with j when a break is allowed between left and right, otherwise j += 1 and left becomes the new right. It always stops (no break) when left.char (+20) is 0 or right.char is 0 (an inline icon record, see GUITextNode_PlaceIcon).

behavior.basis: (rules when layout+123 = 0, i.e. not Japanese / Chinese)
behavior.text: break when left is '-' (45) or an en dash (8211). If layout+121 (French and German only): also break when left is an em dash (8212) or a soft hyphen (173); and when right is a space: no language object = break; French (language 2) = no break when next is one of ! ? ; : % >> (U+00BB, U+226B, U+300B) or when left is one of << (U+00AB, U+226A, U+300A), otherwise break; German (language 3) = no break when next is '.', otherwise break; right not a space = keep scanning. If layout+121 is 0 (English and the rest): break when left is 8212 or 173, or right is a space (32). A no-break space (160) is not 32, so it never breaks here.

behavior.basis: (rules when layout+123 = 1, Japanese / Simplified / Traditional Chinese)
behavior.text: no break when right is in the 78-entry list at 0x1406FDFD0 (closing brackets and quotes, ! ?, : ;, full stops, commas, small kana, the long vowel mark, ellipsis) or left is in the 20-entry opening-bracket list at 0x1406FE070; no break between two equal characters of the list at 0x1406FE0A0 (em dash, two-dot leader, ellipsis); no break when either character is 160. Any other pair is a break (so CJK text breaks between any two glyphs).
j = 0 when n is 1, else j = 1, i.e. a single over-long word is split by moving only the last glyph to the new line. A single glyph in the line is never moved (the line is closed with it).

the last j glyph records are popped off the glyph vector into a temporary vector (reversed order) and st+64 -= j. If the first moved glyph (the one that was popped last) is a space (char 32) it is dropped from the temporary vector, so a wrapped line does not start with a space.
st+88 = 1 then GUITextNode_FinishLine(layout, st), which aligns / justifies the remaining glyphs, appends the line record (+21 = 1) and advances the y cursor (it also clears st+88, st+36 and st+64).

the moved records are appended back in text order with x = x - x of the first kept moved glyph (so the line starts at x 0) and +24 (line index) = the current line count; st+64 = number of re-added glyphs; st+36 (pen) = last.x + last.width. When st+90 is 0 and the last re-added glyph is a soft hyphen (173) and there are at least 2 glyphs, the pen is the previous glyph's x + width instead (the soft hyphen does not advance).
the temporary vector is allocated and freed through the allocator at qword_143CDAA80 + 32 (vtable +16 allocate, +24 free); the glyph vector grows through the layout allocator the same way.
the wrap is checked once per placed glyph by the caller; after one wrap the rebased line can still be wider than W only for a single glyph, which is then closed alone by the next wrap call.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DE608). Wrap only runs for overflow mode node+260 = 0; with modes 2 (shrink) or 3 it never runs. For a single-line text that fits (every glyph rec.x + width <= W) it is never entered.
open_questions: ? whether st+90 (soft-hyphen-suppress) is ever set outside the tag handler (not traced). ? the exact semantics of the French lists were read from the decompile (the Hex-Rays nesting of the inner `break` statements was resolved by hand and should be re-checked on a live French string). ? the CJK lists were dumped as code points only, not named one by one.

name: GUITextureSlot_Init
proto: char GUITextureSlot_Init(__int64 slots, unsigned int index)
purpose: Initialises one texture slot record from its source texture object, with two paths depending on a field of the texture.

v5 = the dword at tex + 76. If v5 != 0: rec[0..2] qwords = 0, rec+24 = v5, rec+28 = 0, rec+32 word = 0, rec+34 byte = 0 (placeholder / pending state carrying v5).
else: atomic increment of the dword at tex+12 (reference count), rec[0] = tex, rec+8, +16, +24 = 0, rec+32 word = 0, rec+34 = byte(tex+120) & 1 (flag bit).
both paths finish with rec+38 = 0 and rec+36 word = 0.
callers sub_1403D9EE0 (0x1403DA0F1) and sub_1403DACD4 (0x1403DAEC5).

notes: Slot-array layout matches GUIFontSlots_GetSlot (base +80, stride 32, record pointer at +16).
open_questions: ? meaning of tex+76 (non-zero looks like an error / pending code; I), tex+120 bit 0, and rec+24/28/32/34/36/38 flags.

name: GUIWidget_EnsureSlotGroup
proto: char GUIWidget_EnsureSlotGroup(GUIWidget *w, const char *name, char addRef)
callers: JobTreePanel_SetTextKey and about 34 UI addon methods (sub_14010824C, sub_140108828, sub_140109134, ... each with one texture / part name), sub_1403DC7BC, sub_1403DC8D0, UIAddonFFTOTitlePlaymode_vfunc_14
callees: UIName_Key, GUIWidget_FindResourceByName, Str_Format, sub_1403D8D1C, sub_1403DA4C0, GUIWidget_NewSlotGroup, sub_1403F3DAC
purpose: Makes sure the widget owns a texture slot group called `name` (a UI texture atlas) and starts loading its '<name without the first 17 characters>.utexpt' part table when it is new; with addRef set an existing group gets one more reference on its part-table slot.

path = Str_Format(buf[256], "%s.utexpt", name + 17): the first 17 characters of the name are skipped (what they are is not shown here).
when addRef != 0 sub_1403DA4C0(g_GUIFontSlots, group+84) adds one reference to the group's part-table slot; returns 1.

group = GUIWidget_NewSlotGroup(w, name); when it is null returns 0; otherwise sub_1403F3DAC(group, path) requests the part-table file (sets group+84 to the new slot id, group+89 = 0 and names the group when still unnamed; a failed request sets +88 = +89 = 1) and returns 1.

name: GUIWidget_FindComponentById
callers: GUIWidget_GetNodeScreenRect, sub_1402977C8, sub_140297990, sub_1403FAD88, sub_14040AEE8, sub_14040B128, sub_14040D298, sub_14040D48C, sub_14040DB1C (10 total)
purpose: Round-robin search of the widget's component vector for the component whose id (dword comp+8) equals the key's id (dword key+48); remembers where it found it.

behavior.text: n = vector count (w+104..+112); empty -> 0. For k = 0..n-1: idx = (u32 w+280 + k) mod n; comp = vec[idx]; when comp+8 = key+48: w+280 = idx and return comp. None -> 0 (cursor unchanged).

name: GUIWidget_FindComponentByName
callers: sub_1401BC92C (a dozen call sites), GUINode_DrawKind10 and others
purpose: Finds a component of the widget by its name key (component+280 name pointer, +288 hash): first in the widget's std::map at +136, then by a round-robin scan of the component vector at +104..+112; a vector hit is put into the map.

behavior.text: returns 0 when the name string is empty (first char 0).

map pass: the tree at w+136 is ordered by an unsigned int at node+32; the range of nodes whose key equals name+8 (the hash) is walked in order; a candidate (node+40) matches when its +512 is 0 and its name key equals `name` (hash compare when both nonzero, else string compare). The first match is returned.

vector pass (no map hit): components are the 8-byte pointers w[104..112); the scan starts at index w+280 (a cached cursor) and wraps modulo the count; the first element with +512 = 0 and an equal name key is taken, the cursor is set to its index, and 0 is returned when none matches.

after a vector hit it finds the element in the map by pointer (in-order walk), calls sub_140098898 on that position and then sub_140098A58 with (hash = comp+288, comp), i.e. it re-inserts the component into the map under its hash; the component is returned.

notes: The name is ours. Components whose +512 is nonzero are skipped; +512 is the hash of a second key (sub_1403F9938 matches it against its second name), so this function finds components whose second key is empty (I). The map acts as a lazily filled cache of the vector (I).
open_questions: What sub_140098898 does (erase or hint) was not read; the meaning of the component keys at +280 and +504 (name and source?) was not determined.

name: GUIWidget_FindComponentCached
callers: GUIComponentRef_Draw (ctx+488, ref+208, ref+224, ref+304), sub_140118438, sub_14013D064, GuideBar_LayoutRow, sub_140149148, sub_14014970C, sub_1401BED40, sub_1401BEF44, sub_1401BF48C, sub_1401BFB04
purpose: Finds a component by two name keys (+280 and +504) with a caller-owned cache cell: if the cell still holds a component whose two keys match it is returned at once, otherwise the same map and vector search as GUIWidget_FindComponentByName runs and the cell is refilled.

fast path: when cache != 0 and *cache != 0 and the cached component's +504/+512 equals name2 and its +280/+288 equals name, that component is returned.

when found and cache != 0: *cache = component; cache[1] = component+600; component+600 = cache (the cell is pushed onto an intrusive list headed at component+600).

notes: The name is ours. For a component reference node the arguments are node+208 (first key), node+224 (second key) and node+304 (the cache cell, a {component, next} record).
