behavior.text: nodes with +144 = 0 or +204 = 0 are skipped when query +49 is set; the node's matrix (+160, 2x3 affine) is multiplied into the frame (Matrix2x3_Multiply).

point mode 0: the frame matrix is inverted (Matrix2x3_Invert), the point is transformed into the node's local space and tested with GUICollisionNode_ContainsPoint; hits are appended as 32-byte entries (frame, node, local x/y).
with query +53 = 0 the walk returns as soon as one hit exists, so the FIRST Collision node in tree order wins.

notes: Rectangle mode 1 (query +52 = 1) instead overlaps the node's rounded rectangle (GUINode_ComputeRectInMatrix) with a point/box; not used by hover.

name: GUIWidget_HitTestComponent
purpose: Descends into a component reference node (kind 12, e.g. one UnitJob panel) by looking up its component's own node tree and testing that under the reference node's transform.

behavior.text: requires query +52 != 0; a component whose scale mode (+540) is 1 is rescaled by size ratio (node +64 over the component's +336).

name: GUIWidget_HitTestPoint
purpose: Hit-tests one point against a widget's node tree and appends the hits to q.

behavior.text: builds the query record (identity matrix at +24, point at +56/+60, mode at +52 = 0 meaning 'inverse-transform the point into each node'), finds the root layer node of the widget (first node with kind 1) and runs GUIWidget_HitTestSubtree.

notes: Query flags set by GUICore_UpdateFrame: type filter array (query +32..+47) = 1 for every node kind except 13 (Collision), so ONLY Collision nodes can be hit; +53 = 0 stops at the first hit; +49/+52/+54 = 1.

name: GUIWidget_HitTestSubtree
purpose: Runs the hit test over a node's children (GUIWidget_HitTestChildren) under the accumulated transform.

behavior.text: when the root has a transform (node +216) the node's matrix (+432) is combined with the query frame first.

name: GUIWidget_NewSlotGroup
purpose: Allocates a texture slot group from the global group pool, names it (default 'None'), registers the widget as one of its owners and appends it to the widget's group vector.

behavior.text: pool = qword_143CDA280 (the global factory): page vector at +176..+184 (16-byte {page pointer, 64-bit occupancy mask}), cursor dword +200, live count dword +204. A page is 7168 bytes = 64 groups of 112 bytes (sub_140011750(7168, allocator, 16)).

when the live count equals pages * 64 a new page is allocated and appended (cursor = its index); otherwise the pages are scanned starting at the cursor and going backwards (index = (n + cursor - i) mod n) for a page whose mask word is not -1; none = return 0 (0xFFFFFFFF index).

the lowest clear bit of that page's mask is set, the live count is incremented and the group at page + 112 * bit is constructed with sub_1403F3CAC (name {Str, 0}, two allocator-backed empty vectors at +24 and +56, ids +80 = 0, flags +88 / +89 / +90 = 0). A null construct result returns 0.
the name is set with sub_1403D8870(group, name ? name : "None") (interns it in the global name table).
the widget's object id (w+8) is stored in the first free slot of the four-dword owner array at group+96..+108 unless it is already present (an existing equal id stops the search).
the group pointer is appended to the widget's group vector (w+224..+232, capacity +240; sub_140031D7C grows it) and returned.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403FB960). The widget vector at +224 is the one GUIWidget_FindResourceByName searches and GUIWidget_ReleaseSlotGroup / sub_1403F9188 free. Calling the global at qword_143CDA280 'the factory' follows the vtable name GUIFactory next to the widget vtable (I).
open_questions: ? a 0xFFFFFFFF page index (all pages full but count != pages * 64) is treated as failure; whether that case can occur was not examined.

name: GUIWidget_OnEvent
purpose: Widget's own event handler (vtable slot 2 of the GUIWidget vtable at 0x140721E10): maps the widget load / unload events onto two virtual methods.

behavior.text: ev type (dword ev+0) 43: calls virtual +144 of the widget with ev+16; type 44: virtual +152 with ev+16; any other type does nothing (result is stale).
the addon base handler sub_1400F4D38 calls this first and then plays the hover (event 12) / click (event 16) sounds, so every UI addon passes its events through here.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403FC3B4). Event numbers 43 / 44 are the 'widget load / unload' of GUIOwners_PostEvent's notes. Naming of the two virtuals (OnLoaded / OnUnloaded) is not established.
open_questions: ? what virtual +144 / +152 do for the Job Tree widget (not traced).

name: GUIWidget_PostReadyEvent
purpose: Vtable entry: posts the event record xmmword_140723260 to the widget's owners (w+288) and returns whether the reply field was set.

behavior.text: ev = 16-byte constant xmmword_140723260; GUIOwners_PostEvent(w+288, w, &ev); returns ev dword[3] != 0 (owners write the reply there).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403FC0FC). 868 hits per 4 s. I: a query event ('is the widget busy / ready'); the constant's event id was not read.

name: GUIWidget_ReleaseSlotGroup
purpose: Removes a slot group from the widget's group vector and returns it to the pool.

behavior.text: scans w+224..+232 (8-byte pointers) for g; on a hit the tail is moved down with memmove, w+232 -= 8 and GUIFactory_FreeSlotGroup(qword_143CDA280, g) is called; no hit does nothing (the returned value is then stale).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403FBB20). Mirror of GUIWidget_NewSlotGroup. Whole-widget teardown (sub_1403F9188) frees the same vector element by element without going through this.
open_questions: ? the two callers were not read (texture unload paths).

name: GUIWidget_Show
callers: sub_1400EB0A4, sub_1400EB228, sub_14013EB34, sub_140181980, sub_1401881A8, sub_140196E0C, sub_1401D1E30, sub_140207AA0 (UI addon open paths)
purpose: Marks a widget shown and plays the Show state of its root component (Hide state stopped); posts owner event 5.

behavior.text: flags bit0 = instant (skip to the last frame), bit1 = force. When byte w+74 is 0 or bit1 is set: word w+74 = 1 (w+74 = 1, w+75 = 0); root = GUIWidget_FindFirstKind1Component2(w); when it exists GUINode_StopState(root, Hide key +4616) and sub_140409824(root, Show key +4600, frame) with frame = (bit0 == 0) - 1, i.e. 0 for an animated show, -1 (last frame) for an instant one; then event {5} is posted with GUIOwners_PostEvent(w+288, w, ev).
when w+74 is already 1 and bit1 is clear and bit0 is set: only the Show state of the root is snapped to its last frame (sub_140409824(root, Show, -1)); no event, no flag change.
when w+74 is already 1 and bit0 is clear nothing happens.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F930C). The Show / Hide states are authored in the UIB on the root component. 'a1' is a widget, not a component: it reads the root through the widget's component vector (w+104..+112, kind 1 = Root).
open_questions: ? the exact contract of w+75 and who reads w+74 (hit testing / draw?). ? the meaning of the flag combination values the callers use.

name: GUIWidget_Tick
purpose: Per-frame update of one widget: rebuilds the node lists when flagged, delivers the pending-ready event, ticks the main component, and posts the update event 4 to the widget's owners.

behavior.text: w+81 != 0 -> sub_1403FC5A0(w) (rebuilds the widget's lookup vectors; clears +81 itself).

w+75 != 0 (pending): comp = sub_1403F9DA0(w) (main component); when it is missing, or its state with the key at qword_143CDA2A0+4616 is missing or not running (state+105 == 0), event {7} is posted (GUIOwners_PostEvent(w+288, w, ev)); when the owner left ev+12 == 0, w+75 = 0.
main component comp = sub_1403F9D6C(w): when present, its virtual +32 is called (comp, dt, 0). I: dt is the incoming float argument, passed straight on (xmm6 in the disassembly).
w+72 (byte countdown) is decremented when non-zero; event {4} is posted to w+288; w+68 = g_GUICore+2096 (the frame counter).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403FC14C). Event 4 reaches JobTree_OnEvent (the 'held flag copy' in the addon's event handler). The key +4616 is one of the interned state names of qword_143CDA2A0 (next to +4664 CursorOver and +4680 CursorOut); its text was not read here.
open_questions: ? Text of the state key +4616 and the meaning of event 7 (I: 'widget ready / opened'; owners may veto it by setting ev+12).

name: GUIWidget_UpdateComponentsJob
callers: vtable entry (0x143D42100) and sub_14012B088, sub_14012B108, sub_1403D7A68
purpose: Work-stealing worker: updates the node tree of the widget's components in chunks of 16, so several threads can share one widget's component vector.

behavior.text: n = (w+112 - w+104) / 8 (component vector at w+104..+112, pointers). While the shared counter w+600 < n: base = InterlockedExchangeAdd(w+600, 16); for i = base .. base+15 while i < n: comp = vec[i]; when comp+562 != 0 or comp+559 != 0, GUINode_UpdateSubtree(comp+272, comp+559 != 0).
so +562 is the component's 'tree needs update' flag, +559 the 'force' flag (passed as the force argument).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F94EC). 15533 hits per 4 s. Each component is visited exactly once, in index order per chunk; the result of the per-node update does not depend on the thread, so a single-threaded simulator may just run it for i = 0..n-1.
open_questions: ? Who resets w+600 each frame (not in this function).

name: HdGroup_BuildPiece
proto: int64_t HdGroup_BuildPiece(HdSheetGroup *group, int index, uint32_t *palette, int hash, int x, int y, int w, int h, uint32_t *out, int pitch, int bpp)
purpose: Builds one texture of a sheet group: a rectangle of the group's sheet pixels, expanded through a converted palette into 32-bit texels.

behavior.text: the source is the group's buffer pointer (+2696); the texture is the group's record `index` (144 bytes each from +2704).
bpp 4: from byte y * (pitch / 2) + x / 2, w / 2 bytes a row, low nibble first, each nibble an index into `palette`; bpp 8: from byte y * pitch + x, w bytes a row, each byte an index.

the texels go to `out`; a texture that exists with the same width and height is updated in place (sub_1403D0BF8), else it is given the buffer as a new 32-bit source (TextureObj_SetSource, TextureObj_Commit) and the group's texture count (+21136) goes up for a new one.
then stores the hash, in-use 1, the age 60 and x, y, w, h in the record and returns the record's texture id (dword +48).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D0F8C). Structure: HdSheetGroup. Any other bpp value writes no texels and still makes the texture.

name: HdLayer_BindSheetTexture
proto: char HdLayer_BindSheetTexture(int *a1, unsigned a2, unsigned a3, __int64 a4, unsigned a5, unsigned a6, char a7)
purpose: Binds a sprite sheet texture id of the battle HD layer to the g2d entry that the sheet slot table holds.

behavior.text: for ids 123 to 266 the entry is dword_142E7FEBC[(id - 123) / 16], for 267 to 282 dword_142E7FEE0[(id - 267) / 16], for 283 to 298 dword_142E7FEE4, and fixed slots hold the other ids; the entry is stored in the draw record at +64.
the first three ids use the face table at 0x140714EA0 (limit 0xCD) instead.

the full map: 59..74 slot 16, 75..90 slot 17, 91..106 slot 18, 107..122 slot 19, 123..266 slots 20..28 (pools 0..8), 267..282 slot 29 (pool 9), 283..298 slot 30, 299..346 slots 31..33 (sub_1400D29F0, effect pages), 347..362 slot 34, 363..378 slot 35; the HD layer's texture tables end at 378 (HdLayer_BuildTextures).

binds the HD texture ids of the pool sheets (123 + 16 p + frame) to the g2d entry `dword_142E7FEBC[p]` (= g_HdSheetEntryBySlot[20 + p]); HdLayer_BuildTextures loads an entry that differs from the slot's loaded one with PackFile_ReadEntry(g2d pack `qword_140D3AD58`, entry).

notes:
The slot dwords are the ones SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry and sub_140260CF0 fill; there are 9 unit slots plus the shared slot 17.

The face table at 0x140714EA0 (206 g2d entry numbers) has four readers, each comparing the slot value unsigned with 0xCD first: sub_14041AE44 (0x14041B34E), sub_14041CAAC (0x14041CC09), this function (0x14041DA3F) and sub_14041DAA4 (0x14041DB82) (V, xrefs). Corrected 2026-11-08: this sheet named only one.
open_questions: ? the role of the 152-byte draw record.

name: HdLayer_BuildTextures
callees: HdGroup_BuildPiece, Pixels_ExpandToRgba, Rgb555ToRgba8888, PackFile_ReadEntry, TextureObj_SetSource, TextureObj_Commit, TextureObj_Reset, Mem_Alloc, sub_1403D2450, sub_1403D25A4, sub_1403D090C, sub_1403D0BF8, sub_1403D11DC, sub_140415BF4, sub_140415CFC, sub_140418F20, sub_14041DBCC, sub_14041DF24, sub_14041DF84, sub_14041DFB4, sub_14041E05C, sub_14041E3D8, sub_14041EA74, sub_1400C7734, sub_1400C92C8, sub_1400CB45C, sub_1400D575C, sub_1400D578C
purpose: The battle HD layer's texture pass: for every draw record of the frame it finds or builds the texture of its sheet piece and palette, and writes the texture id into the record.

behavior.text: walks the draw records (152 bytes each) of the list at +936 of the object at qword_140D3AD60; a record's texture slot is its dword +44 minus 2048, its sheet entry the dword +64, its palette id the word +68 and its piece number the dword +72.
the palette colours are read from the emulated video memory at g_SaveYoxPage + 32 * (id & 0x3F) + 2048 * (id >> 6).

slots 0..2, 7 and 8..58 are single textures: the cache keys are the entry (dword_143CC96C0[slot]) and the palette id (word_143CC9CB0[slot]); on a miss the entry is read, 16 colours go through Rgb555ToRgba8888 and the 4-bit pixels through Pixels_ExpandToRgba (512 x 512 for slot 7, 96 x 96 in 128 x 128 for 8..58, 96 x 64 or 64 x 96 otherwise); slots 5 and 6 hand the entry's bytes to sub_1403D090C with no palette.

slots 59 and up belong to the 20 sheet groups (g_HdSheetGroups, 21144 bytes each), 16 slots per group: 59.. group 0, 75.. group 1, 91.. group 2, 107.. group 3, 123..266 groups 4 to 12, 267.. group 13, 283.. group 14, 299..346 groups 15 to 17, 347.. group 18, 363.. group 19.
a group whose entry number (+2692) differs from the record's frees its 128 textures and reads the new entry into its buffer (+2696, 0x80000 bytes, allocated once).

a group texture is looked up by the hash of the palette colours (sub_14041DBCC, FNV-1a over 2 bytes per colour) and, for a piece, the piece's four rectangle values; on a miss a free texture is taken and HdGroup_BuildPiece builds it.
groups 15 to 17 hash and convert 256 colours and build with 8-bit pixels (pitch 512 or 256 by a per-group flag); every other group 16 colours and 4-bit pixels with pitch 512.

at its start it clears the per-frame tables, releases the single textures of the slots 3..7 no record names, and ages the group textures: a texture used in the last pass gets the age 60, an unused one counts down and is freed at 0, or at once while its group holds more than 64 textures (sub_1403D11DC).
records with a slot below 2048 (+44 up to 0x116) take another path through sub_14041DFB4, sub_14041EA74 and the character renderer's tables, not read here.

the slot tables hold exactly 379 slots (0..378; the release loop stops at 379, a record past slot 0x17A takes the other path) and lie back to back: dword_143CC96C0[379] is followed at once by word_143CC9CB0, the texture objects are 379 x 112 bytes from 0x142E9BDA0 with other data right after, and the 20 groups end where qword_142F0D7C0 begins (the ageing loop's end address).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140415D30). Read: the slot and group paths of the texture pass (the parts that turn sheet pixels and palette colours into textures); the path of records below slot 2048 only in outline. For the entries 602 and 425 it replaces the 16 colours in the video memory by the constants at 0x140722AD0 before it converts them. Which unit uses which group is set where the draw primitives are made (sub_140260CF0): sheet page 4 / 5 -> groups 0 / 1, pages 20..28 -> groups 4..12, page 0x11 -> group 13, with the slot inside the group from sub_14041E448(group, palette id) (HdSheetGroup_ClaimClutEntry).
open_questions: ? the path of the records below slot 2048; ? what the groups 2, 3, 14 to 19 hold in play (their entries are fixed numbers or set elsewhere).

name: HdLayer_ResolveQuadTexture
proto: int HdLayer_ResolveQuadTexture(int *layer, uint16_t *quad, unsigned colour, float w, float h, int *piece)
purpose: For a battle HD draw quad, turns its draw id (quad +64) into the HD layer's texture slot and finds or adds the quad's sheet piece in the matching sheet group; then writes the quad's vertices.

behavior.text: with enhanced graphics (g_GraphicsLevel >= 2) and the HD mode dword set, draw id ranges map to HD slot = id - 9992 and a sheet group: 10051..10066 group 0, 10067..10082 group 1, 10083..10098 group 2, 10099..10114 group 3, 10115..10258 group 4 + (id - 10115) / 16 (the nine unit sheets of pools 0..8), 10259..10274 group 13 (pool 9), 10275..10290 group 14, 10339..10354 group 18, 10355..10370 group 19; with refined effect textures on, 10291..10338 groups 15..17.
ids 10000..10050 are a third kind (fixed rectangles), 11111 one special page, 11112..11879 the three face slots (face number through g_FaceG2dEntryByFace, limit 0xCD).
the piece is looked up with HdSheetGroup_FindOrAddPiece(group, rectangle); its index is returned through the last argument.
the highest HD slot any range reaches is 378 (id 10370).

notes: Behavior: HdLayerUnitSheetsAreTenFixedGroups.

name: HdSheetGroup_ClaimClutEntry
purpose: Returns the index (0..15) of the palette entry a battle HD sheet group keeps for a draw quad's CLUT word, claiming a free one when the word is new.

behavior.text: the group is g_HdSheetGroups + 21144 x group; its 16 palette entries are 8-byte pairs at +2564 (the CLUT word, then a used flag).
returns the index of the entry holding the word and sets its used flag; else takes the first entry whose word is -1, stores the word and sets the flag; returns 0 when all 16 hold other words.

callers and the groups they pass: sub_140260CF0 (0 and 1 for sheet words 4 and 5, 18 and 19 for their alternates, 2 for word 9, 3 for word 11, word - 16 = 4..12 for words 20..28, 13 for word 17, 14 for word 30), EffectNxd_SelectPageTexture, sub_140311CB0 and sub_14031DA24 (14), sub_1403953D8.

notes: Behavior: HdLayerUnitSheetsAreTenFixedGroups.

name: HdSheetGroup_FindOrAddPiece
purpose: Finds a sheet piece (a 4-dword rectangle) among the 128 piece entries of an HD sheet group, or stores it in the first free entry; returns the entry index (0 when the group is full).

behavior.text: entries are 20 bytes from group +4: the 4 rectangle dwords and a used dword; a match sets the used dword and returns its index; else the first entry whose used dword is 0 takes the rectangle.

name: Icon_FormatPath
proto: char Icon_FormatPath(unsigned int iconKey, char *out, char wantUiUri, int cap)
purpose: Formats 'ui/ffto/icon/<path>' (or the same path with a texture-parts URI prefix) from Icon row iconKey (table 118, cache qword_143CDA328).

behavior.text: callers pass template rows: 11 = ability/textureparts/a_%03d_uitx (sub_1400FBFF8), 15 = job/textureparts/j_%03d_uitx (JobTreePanel_SetJobIcon), 16 = job_comm/textureparts/jc_%03d_uitx (sub_1400FBF30), 17 = attribute/at_%02d.

notes: Also known as IconTable_FormatPath (earlier sheet name). The template is then filled with the icon / index value by the caller's Str_Format.

name: IconBase_FormatPath
proto: void IconBase_FormatPath(int number, char *out, int size)
purpose: Builds the path of a numbered 'base' picture.

behavior.text: Icon_FormatPath(21, tmp, texture-parts form, 260), then Str_Format(out, size, tmp, number): the 'base_%02d' picture path for the number.
used for the Gossip picture and the Town picture columns (the latter through sub_140158CB0).

name: IconImage_AcquireById
purpose: Loads the image of an icon id.

behavior.text: maps icon ids 50..71 (pad icons) and 1100..1265 to other image sets first (sub_1403DB420, sub_1403DB5B4); other ids take the path of IconPath_FromIconId and load it with GUIFontSlots_AcquireImage.

notes: Name is ours.

name: IconPath_FromIconId
purpose: Builds the file path of an icon from its Icon id, using the IconGroup table to decide on the 4k texture variant.

behavior.text: walks the IconGroup rows from index 1 and keeps the last row whose first_icon (+4) is not above the icon id; a first_icon of 0 ends the list.
takes the Icon row's path (+8) and formats 'ui/ffto/icon/<path>'; when the kept group's select_4k byte (+9) is non-zero the path goes through UITexturePath_Select4k ('_2k_' becomes '_4k_').
an empty path gives an empty string.
54 of 75 IconGroup rows have select_4k set; no stock Icon path contains '_2k_', so the rewrite changes nothing in the shipped data.

notes: Name is ours. Row +0 of IconGroup and Icon, and IconGroup +8 / +0xA / +0xB, are never read.

name: IdRemap_Lookup
callers: EventChannel_StepTask, sub_140210AF0, sub_14024A6E8, sub_1402B20E4, SoundCue_Play, sub_140346648
purpose: Remaps an id above 0xA7 through the 406-row table `g_IdRemapPairs` (7 pairs of two dwords per row, 56 bytes); returns the replacement, or the id itself when it is not in the table.

behavior.text: ids <= 0xA7 are returned unchanged.
otherwise walks 406 rows x 7 pairs (table 0x140718C50, end 0x14071E520); on a match with the first dword of a pair returns the second dword; if that is -1 the result is -1.
no match returns the id.

the loop stops when the row pointer reaches the address loaded at 0x1402BA9FD (the end of the table); the table start is loaded at 0x1402BA9D0 and the match path reads the pair through that same start register.
sound cues go through it from SoundCue_Play: the Potion's effect cue 0x730000 becomes 0x137 (played) and 0x730001 becomes -1 (nothing).

notes: J8 note: 406 x 56 bytes. I: the ids are sound cue ids (every caller of SoundCue_Play passes a cue); the other callers' ids are not checked here.
open_questions: ? whether the callers other than SoundCue_Play (EventChannel_StepTask, sub_140210AF0, sub_14024A6E8, sub_1402B20E4, sub_140346648) pass sound ids too.

name: ImageDissolve_Step
purpose: One step of a dissolve that reveals an image through scattered pixels.

behavior.text: step 0 clears the target buffer to 0xFF and the 16 line counters; steps 1..49 copy, for each of 16 line groups, 32 pixels at the offsets of the next row of the dissolve table (0x1407BE720) per group and advance that group's counter (up to 32 rows); the buffer is uploaded after each group.
returns 1 when every group finished and 0 otherwise; a step above 49 ends the effect.

name: Input_IsActionHeld
callers: 36 call sites, among them BattleControl_FrameUpdate, WorldMap_UpdateFastForward, EventControl_RunningTick, sub_1400F02BC, sub_1400EFB50
purpose: True while any of the three bindings of an action row (one pad button, two keys) is held down.

behavior.text: returns 1 when the byte +12 of the row's pad binding, or of either key binding (16 bytes apart), is non-zero; the row is rows + 1352 + 48 * action.
rows is the input module + 8 (callers pass g_InputModule + 8), so the row is at the module + 1360 + 48 * action.

notes: Its two siblings read other bytes of the same bindings: Input_IsActionMapped byte +10 (pressed this frame) and sub_1400F0D98 byte +14 (repeat).

name: Input_IsCtrlHeld
callers: `sub_140021A90` (text-edit key handler, four sites), a vtable at `0x143D26AB8`
purpose: Returns true when Ctrl is held **and** Shift is not, no Windows key is down, and a pad state bit is clear. Used by the text-edit box for Ctrl+A/C/V/X.

behavior.text: `GetKeyState(91)` or `GetKeyState(92)` (left/right Windows key) down -> 0.
returns 0 when bit 0x20000000 of the dword reached through the context's pointer at +16 (three levels of indirection) is set (a pad/UI state that suppresses text shortcuts).
otherwise 1.

notes: This is **not** the gameplay Ctrl fast-forward path: its callers are the name-entry editor (`sub_140021A90`), and gameplay reads Ctrl from the action state built by `Input_TranslateMessage`. The sibling `0x140021F9C` is the same test for Shift, `0x14002200C` for no modifier.
open_questions: ? the meaning of the 0x20000000 bit in the ctx object.

name: Input_IsShiftHeld
callers: `sub_140021A90` (text-edit key handler, four sites), a vtable at `0x143D26AC4`
purpose: Returns true when Shift is held and Ctrl is not, no Windows key is down, and the ctx pad bit is clear.

behavior.text: Windows keys 91/92 down -> 0; ctx bit 0x20000000 set -> 0; otherwise 1.

notes: Text-editor modifier test only, like `Input_IsCtrlHeld`. The gameplay effect of Shift was not found in code (see `docs/reference/battle-ui-state.md` section 2.3).

name: Input_ListenerBroadcast
purpose: Delivers the frame's merged input state to the UI core: merges the input object's state into `state`, calls GUICore_OnInputState, then copies the 0x548-byte state back.

behavior.text: body: `sub_1400F17D4(g_Input, state); GUICore_OnInputState(g_GUICore, state); memmove(state, g_Input + 8, 0x548)`.
the only call to GUICore_OnInputState is at 0x1400E3AFE; the wheel notches arrive at state+8.
one code reference from sub_1400E28D0 and two data references (listener table).

name: Input_PauseFor
purpose: Makes the input module ignore input for a time.

behavior.text: the confirm close pauses it for 0.1 s after a choice.

name: Input_PollCursor
purpose: Reads the mouse: drains the mouse device's relative axes (wheel +24, deltas +28/+32) and stores the client-space cursor position.

behavior.text: GetCursorPos then ScreenToClient(window) into in+16 (x) and in+20 (y), whole window pixels; wheel in notches of 120 into in+24.

notes: The 48-byte state Input_Update fills is broadcast to the UI listeners; the UI core copies x/y into g_GUICore+1880/+1884.

name: Input_TestAction
proto: char sub_1400FC598(int mask, int selector, unsigned actionId, char mode)
purpose: The event system's "is this action down" test against the current merged button mask.

behavior.text: returns 0 immediately while the PauseManager's current pause row says input is locked: the byte at offset 0x17 of the pause manager (`qword_143CD9E60`) gives the stack depth, which indexes the id stack starting at offset 0x14, and a control value of 2 means paused.
mode 1: returns `(mask & sub_1400FC4E0(selector)) != 0`.
selector 0: returns `sub_1400F0D00(qword_143CD9EE8 + 8, actionId)` (a pure table query, no current state).
otherwise, when `mask != 0`, returns `(mask & sub_1400F6C8C(actionId)) != 0`.
when `mask == 0`, tests two bytes at `qword_143CD9EE8 + 0x56A + 48*actionId` (16 bytes apart) and returns 1 if either is non-zero.

notes: `mask` is the dword pointed to by `off_1407DCB48` (0x140D407E0) or `off_1407DD348` (0x140D407E4). `sub_1400F6C8C` maps an action id to a 16-bit button bit through the runtime binding table; with identity defaults Ctrl (17) is 0x04 and Shift (16) is 0x20 (I).
open_questions: ? the exact default binding rows; ? who writes 0x140D407E0/E4.

name: Input_TranslateMessage
proto: __int64 sub_14001EC2C(Input *in, __int64 unused, UINT msg, WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam)
purpose: Turns game-window messages into the input object's action queue: keyboard press/release, characters, focus changes and keyboard-layout refresh.

behavior.text: WM_KEYDOWN (0x100) and WM_SYSKEYDOWN (0x104) call `sub_14001EF64(in, wParam)` (the press path); WM_KEYUP (0x101) and WM_SYSKEYUP (0x105) call `sub_14001F040` (the release path).
WM_CHAR (0x102) and WM_SYSCHAR (0x106) queue a type-3 record whose payload is the character; keys >= 0x80 are dropped.

WM_ACTIVATE (0x006) with a zero low word clears every action (loop 0..0xA0 via `sub_14001F040`); with a non-zero low word it calls the input object's vtable +56 (device reset). Mode 2 (`wParam` high word) resyncs three keys taken from `unk_1406FA248` with GetAsyncKeyState.
WM_ENTERMENULOOP/WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE (0x211/0x231) clear every action; WM_MOUSEACTIVATE (0x1A) calls `sub_14001EE74`; WM_NCACTIVATE (0x51) falls through to the layout refresh.
after the keyboard cases it calls `sub_14001F0A4`, which reads `GetKeyboardLayoutNameA` and stores the layout id at in+1832.
the virtual-key -> action id map is `byte_14065CE00`; Ctrl (0x11) -> 17, Shift (0x10) -> 16, Space (0x20) -> 32, Esc (0x1B) -> 27.

notes: The function is reached for every window message via the subclass proc `sub_14001EBD0`. It is not the main WndProc; `Input_WindowSubclassProc` handles the mouse messages on the same window.
open_questions: ? what the three key codes in `unk_1406FA248` are (read live, or dump the data); ? why the focus-loss path uses 0x51.

name: Input_UpdateActionRow
callers: sub_1400EFB50 (all 256 rows each frame, row 57 first)
purpose: Per-frame refresh of one action row: reads the pad button and the two keys bound to the action and writes their value, pressed, released, held and repeat bytes.

behavior.text: the row is live only when UIKeyAssign (UI table 25) has a row for the action and the input module's context mask (dword +13720) has the row's context bit: 1 by default, 2 when the table row's byte +42 is set, plus 4 when byte +43 is set. Otherwise the pad binding's state bytes are zeroed.

pad binding (first 16 bytes): sub_1400F02BC reads the bound button (binding dword at +0) and returns its value, a 'pressed' flag taken from the pad's newly-pressed mask and a 'held' flag from its down mask; the row stores value at +8 and +9, pressed at +10, held at +12 and +13, released at +11 (the previous value was non-zero and it is no longer held) and the repeat flag at +14; the press time (the UI clock in ms) goes to +4 when the value rises from 0.

binding flag 0x10000 (bit 16, read with a bit test, so the constant itself is not in the body) turns the binding into a long press: pressed / held are reported only after 1000 ms down; flag 0x20000 (bit 17, same) into a short press reported on release within 1000 ms.
the two key bindings (at +16 and +32) are read by sub_1400F06AC and stored the same way (value +8 / +9, pressed +10, released +11, held +12, repeat +14).

on the two key bindings flag bit 19 (0x80000, tested as a bit number at 0x1400F01E6) is the long press: while the key is down, held and pressed stay 0 until the UI clock (GUICore +0x830) minus the press time reaches 1000 ms; then held is 1 and pressed is set for the frame in which the 1000 ms mark is crossed. The modifier flags of a key binding (bits 18 Shift, 16 Ctrl and 17 Alt, tested as bit numbers) are applied by sub_1400F06AC, not here.

the context mask of the row is 2 when UIKeyAssign context_2 (+0x2A) is set plus 4 when context_4 (+0x2B) is set, 1 when both are 0; the module's mask (+13720) is written only by its initialiser (InputModule_Init, a value holding contexts 1, 4 and 16), so context 2 is never live and context 4 is.

pad button ids in sub_1400F02BC: 9..12 the four d-pad bits, 13..16 bits 4..7, 17 bit 8, 18 bit 11, 21 bit 10, 22 bit 13, 23 bit 15, 24 bit 14 of the pad mask, 19 / 20 the two triggers, 1..8 stick directions; id 30 is bit 4 reported only while action 89 is held; id 45 a two-button chord.

the pad mask is built by sub_140020350 from the XInput buttons: bits 0..3 d-pad, bit 4 Y, 5 A, 6 X, 7 B, 8 LB, 11 RB, 10 left stick, 13 right stick, 14 Back, 15 Start, 9 / 12 the triggers past a threshold. So button id 18 is RB, 13 is Y, 15 is X.

notes: Key codes below 160 index a per-key state array (Windows virtual-key numbers: 17 Ctrl, 16 Shift, 53 the 5 key); 160..164 are the five mouse buttons (164 = the fifth).
open_questions: Answered 2026-11-19: the pad column is chosen by the layout argument of InputRows_ApplyPadLayout, which InputRows_Rebuild sets from a byte of g_CharaRenderMgr (+13493 != 0): only layouts 0 (UIKeyAssign +4) and 1 (+8) are selected, +0xC is never used. ? what that g_CharaRenderMgr byte is.

name: Input_WindowSubclassProc
proto: LRESULT Input_WindowSubclassProc(HWND hWnd, UINT msg, WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam, UINT_PTR id, DWORD_PTR input)
callers: sub_14001F174, sub_14001F298 (installed as the subclass callback)
purpose: Window subclass procedure of the game window: turns mouse, keyboard and focus messages into flags and counters on the input object (`input` is the reference data).

behavior.text: WM_MOUSEWHEEL (0x20A) adds the signed high word of wParam to the input object's wheel counter at +92; Input_PollCursor later divides it by 120.

message 0x209 (middle double-click) ORs bit 2 into the words at +40 and +48, and 0x20D (X-button up) ORs 8 or 16 by the button in the high word; message 6 (WM_ACTIVATE) with a zero low word falls into a path that calls sub_14001CEF4 on the input object.
every case ends in DefSubclassProc.
installed as a subclass callback from sub_14001F174 / sub_14001F298 (code references to its address); the SetWindowSubclass call itself was not read.

notes: See Input_PollCursor for what consumes the wheel counter.

name: InputGlyph_AppendId
purpose: Appends one glyph to a text buffer: the glyph escape code followed by the id with the high marker.

behavior.text: appends glyph code 0xE104 followed by (id | 0xF0000) (through sub_1400798F8).

notes: Name is ours.

name: InputGlyph_AppendPadButton
proto: void InputGlyph_AppendPadButton(void *text, uint32 binding, int alternate)
purpose: Writes the glyph text of an action's button into a text buffer: pad glyphs or keyboard modifier and key glyphs.

behavior.text: pad mode (input module +13696 == 0): reads the UIPadDefine row of the pad button (the low 16 bits of the binding, taken with a zero-extending load): glyph (+4), or glyph_alt (+0xC) when the alternate flag is set and +0xC is non-zero; then, when glyph_2 (+8) is non-zero, a separator (sub_1400F3940) and glyph_2 follow.

keyboard mode (+13696 == 1): the modifier glyphs for binding bits 18, 16 and 17 (flags 0x40000 Shift, 0x10000 Ctrl, 0x20000 Alt; tested as bit numbers, the masks are not in the body), then the key's glyph when UI table 35 has a row for it.
the glyph text is written by InputGlyph_AppendId (sub_1400F3998), which owns the glyph escape code and the id marker.

notes: Name is ours. Row +0 of UIPadDefine is never read.

name: InputGlyph_AppendSeparator
purpose: Appends the separator between two glyphs of a button chord.

behavior.text: appends a plus sign (character 43) between two glyphs.

notes: Name is ours.

name: InputKey_ReadBinding
purpose: Reads the state of one keyboard or mouse binding of an action row, honouring its modifier flags.

behavior.text: key codes of 160 and above are mouse buttons (160..164).
key codes 16, 17 and 18 (Shift, Ctrl, Alt) read the key states at input module +640, +644 and +648 directly.
any other key code reads the key state at +576 + 4 * key.

the modifier flags of the binding gate every key except 16..18: bit 18 (0x40000, Shift), bit 16 (0x10000, Ctrl) and bit 17 (0x20000, Alt) are tested as bit numbers (the masks are not in the body) and the key counts only while the matching modifier key's state (+640, +644, +648) has bit 0 set.

notes: Name is ours. The long-press flag 0x80000 is not handled here: Input_UpdateActionRow tests it after this function returns.

name: InputModule_Init
purpose: Initialises the UI input module, among other fields its context mask.

behavior.text: writes the context mask at input module +13720 = 0x15 (contexts 1, 4 and 16); nothing else in the image writes it.
with UIKeyAssign context_2 and context_4 (read by Input_UpdateActionRow, not here) a row's mask is 2 / 4 (1 when both are 0): context 2 is never active, context 4 is.

notes: Name is ours; only the context mask was read closely.

name: InputRows_ApplyKeyBindings
purpose: Builds the two keyboard bindings of every action row from the key-assignment table: key code plus modifier and long-press flags.

behavior.text: for each UIKeyAssign row 1..255 key binding 1 (input module +1360 + 48 * row + 16) = row key (+0x10) OR flags: 0x100000 when byte +0x2D is set, 0x10000 for key_ctrl (+0x24), 0x20000 for key_alt (+0x25), 0x40000 for key_shift (+0x23), 0x80000 for key_long_press (+0x26).
key binding 2 (+32) = row key_2 (+0x14) with the same flags from +0x2D, +0x28 (key_2_ctrl), +0x29 (key_2_alt), +0x27 (key_2_shift) and +0x2C (key_2_long_press).
the flags are read by InputKey_ReadBinding (modifiers 0x40000 Shift, 0x10000 Ctrl, 0x20000 Alt) and by Input_UpdateActionRow (0x80000 = long press).
no instruction in the image tests binding bit 0x100000 (set from UIKeyAssign +0x2D); its reader was not found.

notes: Name is ours. Rows 1..255 only: row 0 is never built.

name: InputRows_ApplyPadLayout
purpose: Copies one of the three pad-button columns of the key-assignment table into the pad binding of every action row.

behavior.text: stores the layout number (0..2) at input module +13724.

for each UIKeyAssign row 1..255 it clears the 16-byte pad binding at input module +1360 + 48 * row, then sets its first dword to the row's pad_layout_0 (+4), pad_layout_1 (+8) or pad_layout_2 (+0xC) column for layout 0, 1 or 2, with flag 0x10000 added when the matching pad_long_press_0 / _1 / _2 byte (+0x20 / +0x21 / +0x22) is set.
sets the input module's 'bindings changed' byte (+13672) to 1.

this answers the open question of Input_UpdateActionRow: the pad column is chosen by the layout argument; the only caller passes 0 or 1 (see InputRows_Rebuild), so layout 2 is read here but never selected.

notes: Name is ours. Binding flag 0x10000 on a pad binding is the long press tested by Input_UpdateActionRow.
open_questions: ? what the layout argument stands for beyond the byte of g_CharaRenderMgr that InputRows_Rebuild passes (the Enhanced-mode set being layout 1 is I, from the fast-forward rows existing only there).

name: InputRows_Rebuild
purpose: Rebuilds the input module's action bindings after a change of the pad / keyboard glyph set or the button layout.

behavior.text: sets the pad layout number at input module +13724 from a flag byte of g_CharaRenderMgr (+13493 != 0), swaps the keyboard glyph set when the byte at +13725 changed, then calls InputRows_ApplyPadLayout with that layout, InputRows_ApplyKeyBindings and (unless input module +2608 is 14) sub_1400F2344.
sets the bytes at +13727 and +13730 to 1.
because the layout number is a truth value, only pad layouts 0 and 1 are ever selected; the layout 2 columns of UIKeyAssign (pad_layout_2 and pad_long_press_2) are dead in the stock code.

notes: Name is ours.
open_questions: ? what g_CharaRenderMgr +13493 is: no instruction writes it with that displacement (it is read here and by sub_1400EC678).

name: Inventory_AddCount
callers: 32 direct sites in 21 functions: Item_CountTotal, sub_1402875A4, sub_140288590, sub_1402888E8, Party_ReturnHandItems, Inventory_BuildEquipList, sub_14028916C, sub_1402D65D4, sub_1403331F8, sub_140333640, sub_140333884, sub_140334208, sub_140334A48, sub_1403358FC, sub_140336664, JobChange_FillUnitEntry, sub_14036B71C, sub_14036C874, sub_1403931F0, sub_1403934B0 and sub_140396D08
purpose: Adds a signed delta to the owned count of one item id and returns the new count, or zero when the id is outside the accepted range.

behavior.text: the id argument is masked to ten bits (0x3FF) before the range test, so only the low ten bits of the id reach the count array.
the range test accepts ids 1 through 260 and rejects 0 and everything above 260 ((id - 1) > 0x103).
count = byte_1411A7C00[id] + delta, clamped below at 0 rather than wrapping, stored as a byte and returned.
there is no upper clamp here; the callers cap at 99.
it is a leaf: it calls nothing and reads only the count array (one rip-relative operand) and its own arguments.
32 direct call sites in 21 functions, including the menu list builder, the shop handler and the equip-preview code, which makes it the single write point for counts in most of the item path.
the clamp-at-zero behaviour is what makes a negative delta safe for a sell or a use; the 99 cap is enforced by the callers, not here.
the 10-bit mask is not redundant with the bound: callers pass packed words such as the party hand word (bit 15 = slot present), and the mask strips those flag bits before the id is used.

notes: - V: leaf function; the whole body was read.

name: Inventory_AddWithOverflow
proto: int Inventory_AddWithOverflow(void *unused, uint16_t id, void *report, int delta)
purpose: Adds to an item's owned count with the game's 99 cap, sells the excess for gil, and appends a four-field record of the transaction to a caller-supplied vector.

behavior.text: the first argument register (rcx) is not read; the id is the 16-bit value in dx, sign-extended and compared against 260 (0x104) before anything else; above it the function returns 260 and changes nothing.
it adds the delta (the low byte of the fourth argument, r9) to the byte count of that id in the inventory array.
over = count + Item_CountEquippedByParty(id) - 99; when over > 0 the stored count becomes 99 - equipped and over * Item_SellPrice(id) is added to gil (event variable 44, sub_140284684).

the transaction record holds four 32-bit fields (a kind tag 1, the item id, the trimmed amount and the gil amount) and is appended to the vector passed in the third argument (r8): begin at +0x10, end at +0x18, 16 bytes per record.
a full vector goes through sub_14006635C instead of writing in place.
only one direct caller reaches it, and it calls the equipped-count helper, the sell-price helper and the gil-adding helper.
the four-field record looks like an audit/log entry for the UI, not state that the item path reads back.
the sign-extension of the id argument is a hazard for ids above 32767: the 16-bit compare is still safe but later 64-bit indexing uses the sign-extended value.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140101058). The prototype keeps the unused first pointer argument because the id arrives in dx and the report vector in r8; source-level three-argument forms that put the id first do not match the register use.

name: Inventory_BuildEquipList
proto: int Inventory_BuildEquipList(int16_t unit, int16_t sortWord, char group, uint16_t *out, int unused, uint8_t mode)
purpose:
Builds the candidate list of items a unit may take from one menu group, in id order, and then orders that list either by
a sort field or by the saved user order. It is the one producer of the shared menu list that the equipment and shop screens
display.

behavior.text: scans item ids from 1 up to 260 (the loop bound is 0x105) in ascending order.

drops an id whose count is zero; the count comes from the mode byte: mode 3 reads the inventory count alone through
  Inventory_AddCount with a zero delta, every other mode reads owned plus equipped through Item_CountTotal.

keeps an id only when its menu category matches the group argument. The hand group accepts two categories (0 and 1);
  groups 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 map to categories 2, 3, 4, 0, 1 and 5, so six further groups map to one category each.

asks the equip check whether the given unit may equip the id; the job comes from the unit record's word at +0x24 and
  the equip flags from byte 0x73 of the same record.

in mode 1 a refused item is kept and marked with bit 14 of its list word; the bit is set as bit 0xE, so the literal
  0x4000 does not appear as an immediate. In mode 2 and above the refused item is dropped, and mode 0 performs no equip
  check.

stops at 145 entries and writes the 0xFFFF terminator after the last one; the terminator is produced as an all-ones
  register and stored as a word, so the literal 0xFFFF is not in the immediate stream.

after the build the second word argument decides the order: zero keeps the id order as built, a value from 1 to 5
  filters the list through one of the saved order lists at 0x14067F498 (the index is derived from the group) and drops the
  entries the list does not name, and any other value sorts it with `sub_140285B10` using the argument's low four bits as
  the sorter group.

the fifth declared argument is never read by this function, and the call sites examined do not write it, so only five
  arguments carry data; the mode byte is the sixth stack argument.
the second word argument is stored at entry and read again after the build as the order selector.

the equipment screen and the item menu call it, which is why the same 145-entry cap and the same output array appear in
  both.
what the unused fifth argument was meant to carry.
in mode 1 a refused item gets bit 14 through the bit-set at 0x140288CAF and is stored with the id at 0x140288CB6; modes 2 and 3 drop the item instead, and mode 0 never tests it.

the Fitting list and the Status equipment list show no row for an item the unit cannot equip; the mark of mode 1 is not drawn as a greyed row there (behavior EquipListsDropRowsAUnitCannotEquip, flow ItemMenuListLifecycle).

notes:
Read end to end (466 bytes); the category mapping was cross-checked against the item category table. The post-build branch
was re-read from the bytes for this merge: the order selector is the second word argument, not the fifth.

name: Inventory_RebuildOrders
callees: sub_1402BB37C, UnitWork_BuildForSlot, ItemOrder_SyncGroup, sub_1402BE694, sub_1400F72F0, sub_1400F7334
purpose: Rebuilds the five item order lists and the derived menu state after a load or a party change: it picks the owning unit, syncs every group and refreshes the list globals.

behavior.text: it asks sub_1402BB37C for the current party slot and materialises that unit through UnitWork_BuildForSlot.
the result byte is stored at 0x140D407BB and the five order groups are synced by five calls to ItemOrder_SyncGroup with group 0..4.
sub_1402BE694 rebuilds the derived item lists, and sub_1400F72F0 and sub_1400F7334 refresh the two menu globals.
it clears the words at 0x142FEC52E and 0x142FEC532 and the bytes at 0x142FEC542 before the rebuild.
the group lists are the five item order lists; each is rewritten from the live inventory.
the five callers are the load, party-change and menu-entry paths.
the rebuild is needed because the order lists are saved as indices and must be filtered against the current inventory.
what sub_1402BB37C returns when no party member is valid; the caller still runs the sync.

notes: Whole function read (436 bytes). The five sync calls are the ItemOrder_SyncGroup call sites.

name: Inventory_ReturnItem
purpose:
Puts one item back into the party inventory: the refund step for a use that was cancelled or resolved away. It is the
counterpart of the item-consume path and leaves the same store it takes from.

behavior.text:
it refuses to act while the battle-context dword at `0x14186AF80` is nonzero; that dword is set to 2 around
  reaction and secondary actions, so those actions never refund.
it refuses item id 0 and id `0xFF`, which are the empty-slot values.

it refuses every item id at or above `0x105` (261); an item numbered above 260 cannot be
  returned by this path.
it refuses when the owning unit's team bits (record +0x1EE, mask `0x30`) are set, so enemy units get no refund.
it counts how many copies the party owns and has equipped, using Item_CountOwnedAndEquipped.

it writes the item id and a zero into the block reached through the render-manager global (g_CharaRenderMgr), at
  +0x3524 and +0x3528.

when the count is below 99 it increments the per-id byte count in the inventory array at `0x1411A7C00` and
  returns 0.

when the count is 99 or more it calls `sub_14030CF38` with the unit, a zero and the id instead of incrementing, and
  returns that call's value.

the count test is the 99-per-stack rule, and `sub_14030CF38` handles the overflow case, because the ordinary
  shop-add path uses the same threshold.

the pair at +0x3524 and +0x3528 is the UI's last-item record, because the same write appears in other inventory
  routines.
the result applier calls it twice because a result can be undone once per actor and once per target list.
what `sub_14030CF38` does with a full stack; it was not read for this sheet.

notes: - V: the whole function was read (it is short); the overflow helper was not.

name: Inventory_SellOverflow
purpose: Sells down every inventory count above 99 and adds the gil, which is the overflow rule the rest of the item path relies on.

behavior.text: one loop walks the inventory from id 1 while the id is below 261 (0x105), calling Item_CountTotal for each one; there is no second walk.
for a total of 100 or more it computes over = total - 99, adds over * Item_SellPrice(id) gil and writes the capped count back.

when the inventory byte itself is below over, the count is set to 0 and the item is unequipped from the party member whose byte +0x175 (373) is highest among those wearing it in the five hand words +84..+92; sub_140288590 does the removal (unit index, slot, 0).
returns whether anything was sold (the byte in al).
the index is range-checked against 0x105 before the write, with a call to __report_rangecheckfailure on the failure path.
because the loop bound and the array size are the same 261, this function is one of the places where growing the item space without moving the array would read past it.

notes:
- I: the 99 cap is a game rule carried in the code, not a width; it is separate from the 261 id bound.
- V: four helper calls plus the compiler's bounds trap; the earlier note of a second loop and eight helpers is not in the bytes.

name: Item_BuildAttributeLines
purpose: Appends the equipment attribute lines of an item to the detail panel: the five stat bonuses, the move and jump bonuses and the element list.

behavior.text: the item record is fetched by id and its attribute index byte +7 is read.
an index of 0x55 or above skips the attribute block and leaves the lines unchanged.
each valid index selects a 0x1A-byte row in the table at 0x14080FEA0.
the row bytes +3, +4, +2, +0 and +1 are emitted with the text ids 0x39D, 0x39E, 0x39F, 0x3A0 and 0x3A1 when they are non-zero.
sub_14029F4B4 formats one line per call into the caller buffer; the function does not write text itself.
the five calls are unconditional in order except for the zero test, so the panel always gets the same line order.
the five values are the HP, MP, speed, attack and magic bonuses in the order the item attribute record stores them.
what the row bytes past +4 hold; the element and status fields are not emitted here.

notes: Whole function read (184 bytes). The attribute table layout is the one the W1a item study lists.

name: Item_CanUnitEquip
proto: int Item_CanUnitEquip(unsigned short id, short job, void *equipFlags)
purpose:
Answers whether a unit's job may equip an item, combining the job's equip-category bits with a small set of item ids the
game special-cases.

behavior.text: The item id is masked to ten bits, and a zero id returns 1 (true) immediately, not false.
The job id is sign-extended from 16 bits and kept for the special-id test.
The function first asks the menu-category helper for the id; menu category 5 returns -1 (false).

The unmasked ids 262, 288, 293, 301 and 310 are reached as a chain of subtractions from 0x106, then 0x1A, 5, 8 and a
  compare with 9; each of them returns 1 only for jobs 161 and 164, and -1 for every other job.

The generic path reads the item record's byte at +5 (equip_category) as a bit index and reads one bit from the stream
  passed in the third argument through the bit reader; the bit set gives 1 and the bit clear gives -1.
The two outcomes are 1 and -1 (the failure value is produced as all-ones), not 0 and 1.

Six direct callers reach it over seven call sites, and it calls the category lookup, the record accessor and the bit
  reader.

The two job ids are almost certainly the two special jobs that may equip the reserved items, but the code does not
  name them.

The five special ids lie past the stock items (0..260) and are leftovers of a larger item list; Item_CanUnitEquipPreview
  applies the same test.

name: Item_CanUnitEquipPreview
proto: int Item_CanUnitEquipPreview(short job, unsigned short id)
purpose:
The preview-record twin of the equip check: it decides whether the job shown in an equip preview could equip the candidate
item.

behavior.text:
The item id arrives in the second argument here, unlike the live check where it is first; the job is the first
  argument.
It masks the id to ten bits, and a zero id returns 1 (true), the same value the live check returns for zero.
The menu-category helper is asked for the id; menu category 5 returns -1 (false).

It carries the same five special-cased ids as the live check, 262, 288, 293, 301 and 310, reached as the same chain
  of subtractions. For those ids it reads the job word at +0x24 of the preview unit record and returns 1 only for the two
  jobs 161 and 164; every other job gets -1.

The generic path looks up the preview unit record in qword_141D3B7A0 by the unit argument, builds the equip-flag
  stream at record +0x73, reads the item record's category byte at +5 and reads one bit through `sub_14039EA84`; the bit
  set gives 1 and the bit clear gives -1.
Two direct callers reach it; it calls the menu-category, record and bit-reader helpers rather than the live job row.

Sharing the special-case table with the live check is what keeps the preview and the real equip decision from
  disagreeing.

notes: - I: The special ids lie past the stock items (0..260); the same test is in Item_CanUnitEquip.

name: Item_CategoryFirstId
callers: the five sub-record accessors sub_1402B8C74, sub_1402B8CD4, sub_1402B8D3C, sub_1402B8DA0, sub_1402B8E04
purpose: Returns the first item id of the category (type) that contains the given id, so a caller can index a sub-record table from its start; 0 when the id is rejected.

behavior.text: index = Item_FindCategoryIndex(id); -1 returns 0.
otherwise `g_ItemCategoryFirstId[ g_ItemCategoryFirst[ g_ItemCategoryType[index] ] ]` (word, zero-extended).

notes:
Data names applied in the same pass: g_ItemCategoryFirstId (0x1406804E0, 14 x u16), g_ItemCategoryType (0x14067FB78, 14 x u32), g_ItemCategoryFirst (0x14067FB38, 10 x u32), g_ItemRecords (0x14080EA90, 256 x 12), g_ItemRecordsHigh (0x140680510, 5 x 12).
- Category lookup read:
  - V: category -1 returns 0.
  - V: otherwise kind = g_ItemCategoryType[category] (u32, 0..9), first category of the kind = g_ItemCategoryFirst[kind], result = g_ItemCategoryFirstId[that category].
  - V: stock kinds by category: 0 0 1 2 2 3 4 5 5 6 7 7 8 9; first category per kind: 0 2 3 5 6 7 9 10 12 13.
  - V: preserves r9 and r10 for its callers (only rax, rcx, rdx, r8 are written).

name: Item_CompareSortOrder

name: Item_CountEquippedByParty
purpose: Counts how many party units hold a given item id in their five equipment words.

behavior.text:
It masks the argument with 0x3FF (`v2 = a1 & 0x3FF` in the export) and walks `g_PartyCount` units and five
  words per unit.

The comparison is a raw word equality (`*v5 == v2`), not a masked compare. A word with bit 15 set does not
  equal the masked id, so a session-pending item is not counted as equipped.
It returns 0 when the argument masks to zero.

The function is used by the shop row count; during a session a pending purchase therefore reads as "not
  equipped" until the commit strips the bit.

notes: V: compares each raw party word with the masked argument (0x1402874D8); a bit-15 word is not counted as equipped.

name: Item_CountTotal

purpose: Returns everything the party owns of an item: the inventory count plus the number equipped by the party.

It passes the same masked id to Item_CountEquippedByParty and returns the sum.
It calls exactly two functions and has twelve direct callers, including the shop rows and the item menu.

name: Item_FindCategoryIndex
callers: Item_CategoryFirstId, six item sub-record accessors (sub_1402B8C74 .. Item_GetEquipPalette), Item_IsInCategory, sub_1403099B0 (9 call references)
purpose: Turns an item id into its category index: the number of leading entries of the 14-word first-id array (`g_ItemCategoryFirstId`) that are <= the id.

behavior.text: ids above 0xFD are rejected unless they are 0x100..0x104 (0xFE and 0xFF are rejected); a rejected id returns -1.
scans the word array from entry 1 (0x1406804E2) while id >= entry, counting; returns -1 if the scan runs off the end (0x1406804FC).
the index is then mapped by `g_ItemCategoryType` (index -> type 0..9) in the callers.

notes:
J8: the category map is hand-aligned with the item id ranges; each sub-record table starts exactly where the previous one ends, so a relocation moves them as one block.
- Reading of the code:
  - V: ids above 0xFD that are not 0x100..0x104 return -1 (so 0xFE and 0xFF never have a category).
  - V: otherwise counts the 13 category first-ids from entry 1 on (g_ItemCategoryFirstId + 2 .. + 28) while the id is at least the entry; reaching the end returns -1, so category 13 is unreachable.
  - V: stock first-ids give categories 0..12 = ids 0x00, 0x7A, 0x80, 0x90, 0xAC, 0xD0, 0xF0, 0x100, 0x102 (empty), 0x102 (empty), 0x102, 0x103, 0x104.
  - V: leaf; leaves rcx, r9, r10 untouched, which its callers rely on (Item_GetEquipPalette reuses cx, Item_IsInCategory keeps its category in r9).

name: Item_GetEquipPalette
purpose: Returns the palette-selector row of an item, chosen by the item's equipment category, or null when the item has no palette.

behavior.text: gets a category index for the id from Item_FindCategoryIndex.
a category index of -1 returns null.

a per-category selector dword (14 entries at 0x14067FB78) picks the table: values 0 and 1 use the table at
  0x140785CF0, values 5 and 6 use the table at 0x140672B54, any other value returns null.

the first table is indexed by the raw id and covers ids 0x00..0x8F, which is where 0x8F comes from in the earlier
  reading; the bound is not an immediate in this body.
the row is the table base plus twice the raw item id, so a row is two bytes.
for the second table the ids 0x100 and 0x101 land at 0x140672D54, which is 0x200 bytes past the base (twice 0x100).
reuses cx after Item_FindCategoryIndex, because that callee leaves rcx untouched.
only two direct call sites exist: ItemSprite_LoadPalettes and a second sprite routine.

byte 0 of the row holds two four-bit palette indices; ItemSprite_LoadPalettes loads the high nibble into palette slot 5
  and the low nibble into slot 6. Byte 1 has no reader found.

Item_FindCategoryIndex accepts ids 1 to 253 and 256 to 260; 0, 254, 255 and 261 and above return -1, so those ids
  have no palette selector.

the palette colours themselves live in a separate 512-byte table of 16 palettes at 0x140D35750 (that address is not
  referenced by this body; the sprite loader reads it), since the row only selects.

notes: - V: whole body read.

- ?: the extent and index base of the second table (0x140672B54).
- ?: the reader of byte 1 (sub_14026BC60 not studied).

name: Item_GetMenuField

behavior.text: the menu category comes from sub_1402890C0; a category of 0 with a non-zero id uses the weapon record byte +4.
category 1 uses the shield record byte +0 and categories 2 and 3 use the armour record byte +0.
every other category reads the item record byte +2.
when the category is 5 and Item_IsInCategory(id, 4) is false, 0x22 is added to the result.
the value is returned zero-extended in eax; no record or item bound is applied beyond the category lookup.
the two callers are the auto-equip picker and the item-list field selector, so the same byte serves both the list and the comparison.
the +0x22 offset in the accessory case shifts the byte into the range the accessory list expects, because the raw record byte is a small index.
whether a category 5 item in category 4 should also get the offset; the condition is only the category membership test.

notes: Whole function read (117 bytes). This is the field-2 accessor of the item order data.

name: Item_GetRecord
callers: 79 functions, 111 call sites (Unit_LoadEquipmentAndEvade, EquipDetail_Refresh, PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave, Unit_ApplyEquipment, sub_140277F10, ItemSprite_LoadPalettes, sub_1402C60E4, sub_140344B68 ...)
purpose: Returns the 12-byte record of an item.

behavior.text: ids below 0x100 return g_ItemRecords + 12 * id (256 records); ids 0x100 and above return a second base (the 5 high records, ids 256..260) + 12 * (id - 256).
no upper bound: an id above 260 returns an address past the high records (no caller check here).
leaf function; touches rax, rcx, rdx only. Callers keep live values in r8..r11 across the call (Unit_LoadEquipmentAndEvade keeps its unit pointer in r11).
the only code that addresses the record tables (census: one operand each).

record layout (data/tables/exe_item.fields.jsonl): +0 icon palette, +1 icon, +2 level, +3 slot bits (0x80 weapon, 0x40 shield, 0x20 head, 0x10 body, 0x08 accessory), +5 equipment category (bit index into the JobTable equip flags, V), +7 attribute record index, +8 price (u16), +10 shop progress.

no range check: an id below 0x100 indexes the first 12-byte table, every other id the second table by 12 times the id, so an id that still carries bit 15 reads a record far past the item block (behavior OutfitterPreviewReadsRecordPastItemBlockWithSessionFlag).

notes: - Proposed data names: g_ItemRecords (256 x 12), g_ItemRecordsHigh (5 x 12).
open_questions: - Bytes +4, +6, +9, +11 have no reader near any call site.

name: Item_IsInCategory
proto: int Item_IsInCategory(unsigned short id, int category)
purpose: Tests whether an item belongs to a given menu category, accepting the matching category or one exactly seven apart.

behavior.text: It resolves the item's category through Item_FindCategoryIndex and compares it with the requested category.
An exact match returns 1 immediately.

Otherwise it takes the absolute difference and returns -1 when that is exactly seven, and 0 for every other
  difference; the value is all-ones, not 1, so the test is non-zero rather than true.

It keeps the category in r9 across the Item_FindCategoryIndex call, which is safe because that callee leaves r9
  untouched.

It has nineteen direct callers over fifty-six call sites, which makes it one of the most reused item predicates in the
  game.
Categories c and c + 7 are the same kind in the low and the high id space (0 and 7 are the weapon kinds 0 and 5).

The seven-apart form is a table geometry fact, not a width; it survives an id-space change only if the category table
  keeps that layout.

name: Item_IsOwned
purpose: Answers whether the party owns an item, either in the inventory or equipped on one of the 54 units.

behavior.text: the first argument register is not read; the id is the 16-bit value in dx, sign-extended, and anything above 0x104 is rejected.
it looks up the Item-en row of the id (NXD table 45, 0x2D); when the row exists and its byte +44 (0x2C) is 0 the answer is false.
a missing table or row skips that veto and continues with the inventory check.
otherwise it reads byte_1411A7C00[id] and returns true when the byte is non-zero.

if the inventory is empty it walks the 54 unit records (g_UnitSaveData, 600 bytes apart) and their seven equipment words at +14 (0xE), comparing each word with the id; a record whose byte +1 is 0xFF is skipped.
the seven words are compared whether or not a slot is empty, with no per-slot marker byte.
it calls three helpers and has a single direct caller.
the sign-extension means ids above 32767 become negative before the 64-bit index, which is only safe while the 0x104 bound rejects them first.

notes:
V: the Item column at +0x2C is named unknown2c in the table row structure; the only caller is the scenario condition of type 81, which answers 'item owned' only for items whose byte is non-zero.

The name is ours (IDB: sub_140100F78). The veto at row byte +44 is the reading the bytes support: the byte at +0x2C is tested after the row lookup and a zero returns false; every stock Item-en row has 0 in the column at +0x2C, so the meaning of the veto is still open.
open_questions: What byte +44 of the Item-en row in memory is (the veto); why a stock row would veto every id.

name: Item_IsValidId
purpose: The stock validity test for an item id: one contiguous low range plus a five-id high range.

behavior.text: It accepts ids 1 through 253 and ids 256 through 260.
Ids 0, 254 and 255 are invalid, which is why 255 can be used as the empty-slot value everywhere else.
The test is two range comparisons on the 16-bit id and returns 1 or 0; it calls nothing.
The ranges are immediates: the id minus 1 is compared with 0xFC, and the id minus 0x100 with 4.
Twenty-one distinct callers use it over twenty-four call sites.

The five-id gap at 254 and 255 is deliberate, not an accident of the table, because the same gap appears in the
  category threshold table.

notes: - I: Because the test is a pure range check, making 254 or 255 assignable would silently break every 255-is-empty site.

name: Item_SellPrice

purpose: Returns the gil a shop pays for one unit of an item: half its record price, with a floor of one.

behavior.text: A zero id returns zero without touching the record table.
It masks the id to ten bits (0x3FF) and reads the price word at record +8.
It halves the price and raises a zero result to one, so a priced item never sells for nothing.
It calls the record accessor only and has five direct callers.

name: ItemIcon_Set
callers: sub_14022AFEC, sub_140266890, sub_1402F9F20, sub_140311CB0, sub_140315B10, sub_14033A37C, sub_1403932C8, sub_140399A64 (eight direct sites)
purpose: Fills the small draw state of one classic item icon from the item record's two icon bytes: a 16 by 16 tile in a shared sheet and a palette selector.

behavior.text: the item id is masked to nine bits (0x1FF) before the record lookup, so only the low 512 ids reach the record.
reads record byte +0 as the icon palette and record byte +1 as the tile index.

writes the tile origin as two bytes: state+0x14 = (tile + tile / 15) * 16, the column, and state+0x15 = (tile / 15 + 2) * 16, the row plus two header rows. The division by 15 is a multiply by 0x88888889 and a shift.
clamps the palette to 15 (cmova with 0xF).
writes a 16 by 16 size as the dword 0x00100010 at state+0x18.

builds one packed word at state+0x16 from the palette: a page part of 254 plus palette / 8 (clamped below 0x200, then shifted left 6), and a palette part of 40 plus palette modulo 8 (the base 640 divided by 16).- V: eight direct call sites.

the state is a 32-byte record (the highest field written here is +0x18); the icon builders advance a state pointer by that stride in their own bodies, not here.
the callers are unit and battle panels, a shop-row setter, a bulk icon builder and a sprite wrapper, judged from the code around each call.

the list branches walk an array at object +0x90..+0x98 with 48-byte elements and take the element at the row index.
the element's first field is a dword but is read as a 16-bit word; an entry below 261 (`0x1402C4458`) goes to `Item_GetRecord` and is returned as an item.
an entry at or above 261 is fetched through `UITable_GetRowByKey(0xEC, ...)` at element +24, so it is a UI row, not an item.
an item whose record is missing or whose record byte +0xA is below 0x14 also takes the table-row path.
the function returns the mapped index, or -1 when the id has no row.
the `0x105` test is a discriminator between two entry kinds, not an item-id bound; an item id and a table row share the dword.
the switch is on the panel that owns the list, because the six text ids are the six possession-list headings.

name: ItemOrder_FilterList
callers: sub_140286228, Inventory_BuildEquipList, sub_1403368C0, sub_140338250, ShopList_BuildEntries (five direct sites)
purpose: Reorders a 0xFFFF-terminated item list by a saved order list, dropping every entry the order list does not name. The list is filtered in place; the return value is the number of entries kept.

behavior.text: takes the saved order list in the first argument and the display list in the second; both are arrays of 16-bit words.
reads the order list until it meets the value 255 or any value of 261 or above (0x105); both end the scan.
for each order entry it walks the display list from the start and compares against the entry's low ten bits (0x3FF), so the flag bit carried by display entries is ignored for matching.
on a match it copies the display entry unchanged (flag bit included) into a stack buffer at rsp+0x20.
after the last order entry it writes the 65535 terminator into the buffer and copies the buffer back over the display list with memmove, two bytes per entry plus the terminator.
entries of the display list that no order entry names are lost.
there is no capacity check on the order list; the stack buffer covers the largest display list (256 words) plus a terminator.
the copy is followed by the compiler's stack-cookie check.
both the shop list builder and the equipment list builder call it, so the saved user order is the single ordering rule for those screens.
whether a display entry with the flag bit set is ever meant to sort differently from the same id without it.

the order id is compared unmasked with the list word masked by 0x3FF (constant at 0x140285E5E, mask at 0x140285E63); a match copies the whole list word to a stack buffer at 0x140285E7E, and the buffer is moved back with memmove at 0x140285EA8. Flags travel, and a flagged order id never matches.

behavior.text: takes the id in the first argument (ecx) and the list pointer in the second (rdx); it leaves the index where the removal started in eax, which the callers ignore.
walks the list until it meets 255 (0xFF) or a value of 261 or above, the same two end conditions every order-list reader uses; the 261 bound is formed as 0xFF + 6, not an immediate.
on the first entry equal to the id it copies the following entry over it, then repeats with the next pair, so the tail moves left by one and the terminator moves with it.
if the id is not present the list is left untouched.
it reads and writes only the caller's array; it uses no global and calls nothing.
because the three synchronisers call it for every owned id that is no longer held, the list shrinks without ever being rewritten from scratch.
none.

behavior.text: the argument is a group index from 0 to 4 and selects `off_14067F498[group]`, one of the five saved item order lists.
the scan runs over item ids 1 to 260 and keeps an id only when `Item_IsValidId` accepts it and `Item_MenuCategory` puts it in this group.

after the item list it calls `sub_140286070` for the equipment order list (groups below 4) and then tail-jumps `sub_140286160` for the obtain-order list.
the item ids are plain u16 words; no bit 14/15 flag is tested or stored here.
the front insertion is why a newly acquired item appears first in its menu; nothing sorts it afterwards unless the player asks for a sort.
whether the missing capacity check can be reached with stock data (the saved lists leave at most two spare words).
