name: Job_HasMonsterPair
purpose: True when the Job row's poach_item (+0x24) or poach_item_rare (+0x28) is nonzero: the job can be poached. The function name says 'monster pair'; that reading was wrong, the two values are the PoachItem ids a Poach on a unit of the job can give.

behavior.text: reads the Job row (table 46) and returns 1 when the dword at +0x24 or the dword at +0x28 is nonzero, else 0 (also 0 when the table or the row is missing).
Poach_GiveResult is the reader that uses the two values as PoachItem ids (see its sheet); nothing in this function treats them as sprites or portraits.

notes: M: in stock the values are nonzero only for the jobs that can be poached (monster jobs); the name Job_HasMonsterPair is the old reading and stays only because it is the name applied in the executable database.

name: Job_IdToIndex
purpose: Maps a job key to its tree/unlock index.

behavior.text: anything else -> 0.
the index, not the job id, selects the per-job arrays: unlock rows, job-level nibbles, JP arrays, learned-bit groups and GeneralJob rows. JobTable and the unit's job byte use the id.
also called by Job_LearnAbilityByMenu and the job-list helper sub_1402867BC.

notes:
The ids 160 and 161 are hard-coded here, as are the 0xA0 base-constant sites elsewhere.

Ids 94 and above (monsters) and ids below 74 (special characters) all return index 0, so they collide with Squire in any per-index array.

- Correction: 34 callers (another count found 37 sites in 33 functions).

name: Job_IsChemistType
purpose: True when the Job row of the unit's job byte (unit+3) has jobtype +24 == 31.

behavior.text: hard-coded jobtype 31 (Chemist).

notes: Engine hard-code that depends on the stock jobtype numbering.

name: Job_IsHiddenFromTree
callers: JobList_Build, Job_IsLockedForParty, PartyUnit_FillFromWork, sub_1401442FC, sub_140284F6C, sub_140289298, sub_14028A474, sub_14028ACD8, sub_1402867BC
purpose: Returns 1 when the Job row (table 46, row = job id) has a nonzero hidden_from_job_list byte at +60, else 0.

behavior.text: returns 0 when the registry or the Job table is missing, or the row cannot be fetched.
reads row byte +60 and returns whether it is nonzero.
the Job table object is cached in a global after the first lookup.

notes: Hidden jobs are skipped by the party-wide lock test and keep their stored unlock mask instead of a recomputed one.

name: Job_IsLockedForParty
purpose: Returns 1 if NO party member has the job unlocked, else 0.

behavior.text: if `byte_140D407BB` (party count) is 0, returns 1.

per party unit (skipping units where sub_1402CBED4(unit+36) is true): sets `qword_143C49BF8 = unit+120` (unlock bitfield) and `byte_142FF3CA7 = 1`, reads Job_IdToIndex(id) bits, then 1 bit via BitStream_ReadBits. Bit set -> returns 0.
falls through all units -> returns 1.
the bit field it tests is the mask at B+120 of each party record (PartyUnit_FillFromWork stores it there).

notes: The bitfield is the 24-bit mask Unit_BuildJobUnlockMask produces; index 20 -> mask bit 0x8.

name: Job_LearnAbilityByMenu
proto: void Job_LearnAbilityByMenu(int unusedArg, int16_t jobId, int16_t abilityId)
callees: Job_IdToIndex, Skillset_BuildAbilityList, GeneralJob exp getter (sub_1402CC008), sub_1402867BC, sub_140285744, sub_1402BD05C, sub_1400DF354
purpose: Marks an ability as learned in the current party member's record when the player buys it in the job menu, then refreshes the hidden Onion Knight level and posts the learning notification.

behavior.text: the first argument is not used; Unit_SpendJp passes the ability id there and then deducts the JP cost itself.
the skillset id comes from byte 0 of the JobTable row of `jobId` (0 for ids of 174 or more); the ability list is Skillset_BuildAbilityList(set, 47) when bit 0x40 of party byte +112 is set, else 31.

the ability's position in that list picks the learned bit: party record B byte +123 + 3 * Job_IdToIndex(jobId) + position / 8, bit 7 - (position mod 8). The position search has no bound, so the ability must be in the list.
afterwards it counts jobs 76..92 (74, 75 and 93 are skipped) for which sub_1402867BC with mode 3 reports no unlearned ability left; the count is halved and capped at 8.

that value becomes the level of job id 161 (index 21): the nibble in the level array at B+189 and the JP at B+248+2*index, taken from Job_GetJpForLevel(index, level) (I: the stock rule that the hidden class levels with mastered jobs).
then it writes the party record back to the save (sub_140285744), runs sub_1402BD05C, and sends an AbilityLearningByMenu notification (party index and job id).

notes: The current party member is the index in word_141811428. Learning from a menu always succeeds; the learn-chance roll is only in Unit_TryLearnAbility. Its JobTable row guard is the bound 0xAE loaded into a register, then compared.

name: Job_LevelFromTotalJp
proto: int Job_LevelFromTotalJp(unsigned int jobIndex, unsigned short totalJp)
purpose: Returns the job level (0..8) a total JP gives: how many of the 8 GeneralJob thresholds it reaches.

behavior.text: for level 1..8 counts the levels with totalJp >= Job_GetJpForLevel(jobIndex, level).
with no GeneralJob row (or no nxd registry) every threshold is 0 and the answer is 8.

level 1 needs job_level_jp[1], 100 JP in the stock curve [0,100,200,400,700,1100,1600,2200,3000] (rows 0..19): a total below 100 gives level 0. Stock never gets there: Unit_InitJobJp gives a new unit 100 + 0..99 JP in every job (slot 49: every stock job a unit may have held 100 or more).

name: Job_ReadLearnedBitsForBattle
purpose: Walks the skillset of a work record's current job and tests each slot's learned bit (3 bytes at C +162 + 3*index).

behavior.text: index from Job_IdToIndex(c +3); copies the 3 learned bytes to the stack, then for each slot tests bit (0x80 >> slot%8) of byte slot/8 and asks Skillset_GetAbility(c +18 skillset, slot).

notes: None.
open_questions: I: name from the reads; the output list is not traced.

name: JobAbilityList_Build
proto: int64_t JobAbilityList_Build(uint16_t unit, int16_t jobId, int tab, int16_t *out, int mode)
callers: JobTree_FillJobRecords, Job_LearnAbilityByMenu, sub_1400DC77C, sub_140286A78, sub_1402B9090, sub_1402B9598, sub_1402B9C20, sub_140366FE0
callees: Job_IdToIndex, Skillset_BuildAbilityList, Ability_GetJpCost, Job_IsHiddenFromTree, BitReader_ReadBits, sub_1402866E4
purpose: Builds the list of abilities shown for a job (skill-set abilities filtered by tab) for the job screen, learn menu and job-list availability tests.

behavior.text: with mode 1 and tab 0 it returns JobSecondaryList (sub_1402866E4) instead.

converts the job id with Job_IdToIndex, then scans g_JobTable (49-byte rows) for the row whose first byte matches; the skillset is that row's byte 0. A miss falls back to the unit's own job (unit+94).
gets the abilities with Skillset_BuildAbilityList and zeroes every id outside the tab's range (tab 0: 1..421, tab 1: 422..453, tab 2: 454..485, tab 3: 486..509).
8 callers, including JobTree_FillJobRecords and Job_LearnAbilityByMenu.

an entry carries the ability id plus one of three flags: 0x1000 is loaded at 0x140286A03 and ORed at 0x140286A2A; 0x4000 is loaded at 0x1402869ED and 0x140286A16 and ORed at 0x1402869F3; 0x6000 is loaded at 0x140286A25 and ORed at 0x140286A2A again. Mode 0 (tree/availability) writes 0x4000 or 0x6000, mode 2 (learn list) writes 0x4000 when the JP cost is above the unit's JP and 0x1000 otherwise, and mode 3 counts only.
the flag word is appended without a further mask, and the list terminator 0xFFFF is produced from an all-ones register rather than from an immediate.

notes:
The tab filter (0x1402868DC..0x1402868F8) zeroes every entry outside [cx, ax], so an ability id of 512 or more would be dropped from every tab; the list words carry state flags 0x1000 / 0x2000 / 0x4000 and their readers mask with 0x3FF, so ids stay below 1024. The same loop exists twice more (Skillset_BuildTabAbilityList, sub_140392620).

The skillset of a job lives in the executable job table (byte 0), not in an nxd table.

The row guard and the search for the first row holding the job's skillset share one register loaded with the bound 0xAE; a job id of 0xAE or more reads no row (a null read; seen as a crash in the Jobs screen at +0x6A).
open_questions: Tab boundary constants beyond tab 0 and 1 were read from the head of the function only.

name: JobChange_FillUnitEntry
proto: void JobChange_FillUnitEntry(void *entry, char slot, void *a3, char current)
callees: sub_1400C6178, sub_1400B1D24, sub_14028662C, sub_1400F72F0, Item_CountTotal, Inventory_AddCount, sub_140289FAC, sub_1400FBB7C, JobRecord_FillIconAndGenericFlag, sub_1400FB8E4
purpose: Fills one 704-byte unit entry of the job-change screen: unit name, job list state, the current JobRecord/icon and the five equipped ability ids.

behavior.text: stores the slot at entry+693; reads the viewed unit g_PartyUnits[word_141811428] and writes its name (party record unit+376+88*slot) via sub_1400C6178 / sub_1400B1D24.
sets entry+164 = 2, then walks the job ids returned by sub_14028662C(unitIndex, &list, 0); when sub_1400F72F0(id, unitJob) is true it sets entry+164 = 0 and adopts that id.

clears five 16-byte slots at entry+180 and five 88-byte slots at entry+332, then marks a slot 2 when the candidate job fails the Item_CountTotal / Inventory_AddCount / sub_140289FAC availability checks.

builds a unit snapshot (job row +189, levels +202, flags +112, job id +36), calls JobRecord_FillIconAndGenericFlag(entry+156, ...), copies five job ids to entry+172 (16-byte stride) and five ability records to entry+252 (88-byte stride, sub_1400FB8E4).
when `current` is set it renders the unit preview (sub_140103C50 / sub_1402C1628 / sub_1400ED124), otherwise clears it (sub_140115148).

notes: The caller hands the 704-byte entry to sub_140115CC8 / sub_140117BEC; only the writes above are verified.
open_questions: Full layout of the 704-byte entry and the meaning of the five slot state values.

name: JobChange_RunPreviewAnim

purpose: Runs the job-change preview: builds scratch sprite/palette buffers and drives the change-animation node for the chosen job.

behavior.text: on first use allocates three 480-byte buffers, runs the job-change action sub_1402888E8(54, jobId, 0) on a scratch unit (id 54) and reads the result with sub_140289548.
looks up animation nodes by name (UIName_Key + GUINode_FindState) and releases the keys with UIName_ReleaseKey.
only caller is JobScreen_UpdateState (0x368DC1).

name: JobChangeAddon_SetState
proto: void JobChangeAddon_SetState(JobListAddon *addon, int state, bool force)
callers: JobList_SelectEntry, sub_14012E620, sub_14012E640, sub_14012E82C, sub_140130DF0, sub_140131068, sub_1401312C8

purpose: Switches the job-change list addon (UIAddonFFTOUnitJobChange2) to a new mode and updates focus, tab bar, sprite requests and cursor for that mode.

7 callers, including JobList_SelectEntry (modes 6 and 3).

name: JobCommand_SameGroup
proto: bool JobCommand_SameGroup(unsigned int idA, unsigned int idB)
purpose: True when two job command ids are the same command: equal ids, or rows with the same group key.

behavior.text: equal ids are the same; otherwise both JobCommand rows (table 41) are fetched and the dword at +0x14 (column group) is compared; a missing row gives false.

name: JobCommandTable_GetRow
purpose: Returns the JobCommand-en row (table 41, cache qword_143CDA2E0).

behavior.text: row +4 icon (drawn only when 1..24, sub_1400FBF9C), +8 Name, +20 group number (sub_1400F7334 compares), +28 flag, +32 extra_text (sub_140129260).

notes: The command's ability list is not in this row (nor in any nxd table).

name: JobLearnList_ReadSelectedJp
purpose: The JP the Learn Abilities list shows: the selected party unit's JP in the job the Jobs screen has selected.

behavior.text: returns the u16 at g_PartyUnits[g_SelectedUnitIndex] + 202 + 2 * word_14375F088 (the party record's JP words).
word_14375F088 is written only by JobScreen_FillUnitRows: Job_IdToIndex of the selected row's job id (word_14375EFF8).
no code calls it; JobScreen_BuildLearnList (0x1402B9602) and JobScreen_RefreshLearnList (0x1402B9C99) take its address (lea), as the list's JP callback.

name: JobList_ApplyCellRecord
proto: void JobList_ApplyCellRecord(JobListAddon *addon, void **gadget, JobRecord *rec, char withSprite)
callees: CharaRender_RegisterSlot, GUINode_PlayShowHide, GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState, GUINode_StopState, sub_14013206C
purpose: Shows one job record in a job-change cell gadget: star, Active/Deactive/Black state, the unit sprite, the current-job mark and the job text.

behavior.text: gadget[0] (star node): plays ShowStar or HideStar by rec+140.
gadget[2] (unit node): stops all states, plays Active / Deactive / Black for record state (+132) 0 / 1 / 2.

with withSprite set, finds the part named `Unit` of gadget[2] and registers the record's render slot (+0x5C) to it through CharaRender_RegisterSlot; a slot outside 0..255 is refused there, so nothing is registered.
gadget[1] (text node): ShowCurrent/HideCurrent by rec+141, ShowJobText unless the state is 2, then hands gadget+32 and the record to sub_14013206C.

notes: One render slot has one node: two cells (or a cell and a tree panel) given the same slot take the sprite from each other; the job-change list gives cell i slot 61 + i.
open_questions: What sub_14013206C fills from the record (?).

name: JobList_Build
purpose: Builds the runtime job list `g_RuntimeJobList` (uint16[], length `g_RuntimeJobListLen`). Entry = job id | 0x2000 (locked/unreleased) | 0x4000 (current job). The job tree and the job-change list both consume this list by position.

behavior.text: dst[0] = the viewed unit's own job (flagged 0x4000 if current).
loop i = 1..21 (stock loop bound: the counter is compared against 0x16 at 0x1402865F1, looping while below): id = i + (i < 20 ? 74 : 140), i.e. 75..93 then 160, 161.
ids 91/92 (Dancer/Bard pair) are filtered by the unit's gender bit, so only one of the pair is listed.
availability uses Job_IsLockedForParty(id): result > 0 -> 0x2000, else unflagged. Hidden extras 160/161 pass in this build, so the stock builder emits both (observed live: [..., 93, 160, 161]).

`info` is not the party record: it carries the job marker (+2), a flags byte (+3: bit 0x20 combined with the hide-from-tree test, bits 0x40 and 0x80 filter jobs 91 and 92) and a byte (+4) that, when non-zero, reduces the list to the unit's own job. The hide-from-tree test is sub_1402CBED4: byte +60 of the Job text-table row is non-zero.
the bits come from a bit reader over the unit's 3-byte unlock mask (party record +120), most significant bit first, one bit per job index; the first bit (index 0) is read and discarded.

mode 2 marks the entry equal to the unit's own job 0x4000; a clear bit is skipped when no party unit has the job (Job_IsLockedForParty) and otherwise listed with 0x4000. Mode 3 lists every job and flags a clear bit 0x2000 when no party unit has it, else 0x4000. Other modes skip clear bits.

the list's first entry, the unit's own job, comes from the marker byte `info` +2 (JobList_BuildForPartyUnit passes party record +114, which PartyUnit_FillFromWork copies from save record +0): 128 or 129 (a generic man or woman) -> Squire 74; 130 (a monster) -> the current job (`info` +0); any other marker (Ramza, a story unit) is itself the job id.
the bit reader is fed the 3-byte mask at B+120 of the viewed unit (set by the caller sub_14028662C); one bit is discarded, then one bit is read per job index 1..21, most significant bit first.
mode 3 (jobs screen): bit set gives the plain job id; bit clear gives id | 0x2000 when Job_IsLockedForParty says no party member has it, otherwise id | 0x4000.
mode 2: bit clear skips the job when no party member has it, else adds 0x4000; the unit's own job is marked 0x4000 in this mode.
when Job_IsHiddenFromTree(unit job) is true and the unit flag 0x20 is set (or the caller's fourth info byte is nonzero), the list is only the unit's own job.

notes:
Stock hidden jobs 160 (Dark Knight gate) and 161 (Onion Knight) are normally kept out by story gating in Unit_BuildJobUnlockMask, not here.

So 0x4000 means different things by mode: the current job in mode 2, and 'known to the party but not unlocked for this unit' in mode 3.

Runtime check on a fresh unit with only the starting levels: the mask allowed the first four jobs and every other job carried the 0x2000 flag.
open_questions: Who normally keeps 160/161 out of the list in the stock game (story gate on a4 >= 20 path)?

name: JobList_BuildForPartyUnit
proto: int JobList_BuildForPartyUnit(uint8 partyIndex, uint16 *list, int mode)
callers: 7 (job tree, job change screen, sub_14028A7C0, sub_14028A8B0, sub_1402B90D4, Unit_CollectJobSkillsets, sub_1400DCFE4)
purpose: Builds the job list of one party unit: points the bit reader at its unlock mask and calls JobList_Build with its job, marker and flags.

behavior.text: the unit is g_PartyUnits[partyIndex]; the bit reader pointer becomes its record +120 (the unlock mask).
passes a 6-byte summary (job word +36, marker +114, flags +112, and whether +62 is positive) and returns JobList_Build's count.

name: JobList_IsSelectedEntryUnflagged
purpose: Tells whether the runtime-list entry under the list cursor lacks the 0x4000 flag (the 'current job' flag), when the list has two or more jobs.

behavior.text: `g_RuntimeJobListLen >= 2 ? (~g_RuntimeJobList[g_JobListSelectedEntry] & 0x4000) >> 14 : 0`.

g_JobListSelectedEntry (word_143C51880, int16) has six references: reads in this function (0x140367F0D, after the early return of a list shorter than 2) and JobScreen_UpdateState (0x140368CF5, 0x140368D2D); writes at 0x140368C45, 0x140368E74 and 0x140368FE4, all in JobScreen_UpdateState.
with a scrolled list the stored value must be the entry (index into g_RuntimeJobList); the stock game stores a cell index, which equals the entry only for lists of 19 or fewer.

notes: Global: g_JobListSelectedEntry at 0x143C51880, int16, cursor position the job screen last chose. A leaf function without unwind data; its `lea` of g_RuntimeJobList is at 0x140367F15. The function returns early (ret at 0x140367F0C) for a list shorter than 2; the 0x4000 test and the list read follow that return, so a scan that stops at the first ret does not see them; the other addresses in the second bullet are in JobScreen_UpdateState.

name: JobList_OnCursorChanged
proto: void JobList_OnCursorChanged(JobListAddon *addon, int64_t index, int64_t flag)
purpose: Cursor-change handler of the job-change list (UIAddonFFTOUnitJobChange2).

behavior.text: cursor index at addon+19016, mode at +19008; layout root node at *(addon+88). Called from 0x130FD1 and 0x1303A7.
the grid has 19 cells in rows of 6/7/6; cell gadgets are 256 bytes each at addon+11712 with the cell root node in slot 3 (+24). Records are stored by JobList_StoreCell at addon+0x2280+148*i.

name: JobList_RecomputeAvailability
purpose: Recomputes the party-wide job-availability flags from each unit's job levels and the runtime job bits.

behavior.text: walks 50 x 600-byte unit save records starting at unk_1411A7D12, skipping records whose byte-1 is 0xFF.
derives the unit's job id from byte-2 (128/129 -> 74, 130 -> byte 0, else the byte), looks up its Job row, and when the row id (+24) is 1..124 and byte_1411A7490[id+21] is set, clears that flag.

for records where sub_1402CBED4(byte0) == 0 and (uint8)(byte+5 + 80) > 0x2F, loops job indices i = 0..20 but breaks at i == 20; for each Job row (74+i) whose id is >= 125 or has the flag set, resets the bit reader to record+45 and reads i bits then one bit; a set bit clears flag[id+21] for id < 125.
the record pointer used here starts 2 bytes into the 600-byte save record, so the reader base +45 is save-record +47, the stored unlock mask: the same MSB-first bits JobList_Build uses.

notes:
The loop's `if (i == 20) break` means index 20 is never considered.

Per-job bits are addressed by job index (Job_IdToIndex), not job id.
open_questions: Whether the i == 20 skip is an off-by-one or deliberate (only 20 stock tree jobs).

name: JobList_SelectEntry
callees: UIPosFollow_SetTarget, UIPosFollow_Snap, JobChangeAddon_SetState, sub_140132D48, sub_140132D6C, sub_140132ED4, sub_1400F4BCC (sound)
purpose: Handler for screen message 128 (a tree panel was clicked): puts the job-change list cursor on cell `idx`, moves the highlight there and switches the list mode.

behavior.text: does nothing unless `idx <= 0x12` (19 cells); this guard is why a list longer than 19 needs the scroll window before the call.

stores `idx` at addon+19016 (cursor cell), re-targets the two position followers (UIPosFollow_SetTarget + UIPosFollow_Snap) at the selected cell's node, then runs two cell-refresh helpers (sub_140132ED4, sub_140132D6C).

if the mode byte at addon+19012 is 4 the state change goes to mode 2; otherwise the cell's record is read (148-byte records at addon+8904, dword at +60): non-zero -> JobChangeAddon_SetState(addon, 6, 0) and sound 25, zero -> JobChangeAddon_SetState(addon, 3, 0) and sound 14.
only caller is the screen message switch sub_140113F40, case 128, call site 0x14011468D.

notes: Prototype read from the decompile; the argument is a cell index, not a job id and not a runtime-list entry.
open_questions: What sub_140132ED4 / sub_140132D6C refresh (head only read).

name: JobList_StoreCell
purpose: Copies a 148-byte job record into cell `index` of the job-change list (addon+0x2280+148*index); `if (index >= 19) return` (cmp at 0x14012EC81).

behavior.text: 19 UI slots only; any index from 19 up returns without storing.

then applies the cell through JobList_ApplyCellRecord (the cell gadget, or the detail gadget at +16832 in the browsing states), which registers the record's render slot (+0x5C) to the cell's Unit node.
in modes <= 2 a record with showUse (+141) set moves the cursor (+19016) to this cell (to 0 in states 1..3).

notes: None recorded.

name: JobListScreen_GetCursorIndex
purpose: Returns the job-change list's current cursor index through the holder object that owns the list addon.

behavior.text: returns 0 when the holder's virtual slot 2 (+16) reports false or the addon pointer at holder+120 is null.
when the addon's mode (addon+19008) is 9 the value is the ability row at addon+3672, otherwise the cursor cell at addon+19016.
the only caller is JobScreen_UpdateState, which calls it at four sites (0x368DAA, 0x368E61, 0x368E9E, 0x368F8D) and uses the result to index g_RuntimeJobList.
the result is a cell and not an entry.

name: JobRecord_FillIconAndGenericFlag
purpose: Looks up the Job row, then the JobType table (id 0xC8) row, and stores an icon id (male/female) at out[0]; out[4] = 'not a generic job' flag.

behavior.text: flag = (id - 74) > 0x13 when useId, else key[1] != 74.

the icon is read from the JobType row (table 200) named by the Job row's job_type column (+0x18): the dword at +0x0C (column female_card_icon) when the byte key+8 is not negative (bit 7 clear), the dword at +0x08 (column male_card_icon) when bit 7 is set; no JobType row stores 0.
this is the only reader of the JobType table in the executable; its columns +0, +4 are read by nothing.
the icon id is the male JobType visual (row +8) when the sex byte at key+8 is negative, otherwise the female one (row +12); no row stores 0.

notes:
I: bit 7 of the key byte is the male bit, because the code takes the male_card_icon column when it is set; which sex the bit means was not read from a sex test.

Shapes and records for a job come from the same key: see JobRecord_FromJobId.

name: JobRecord_FromJobId
callers: JobTree_FillJobRecords, JobChange_FillUnitEntry and about a dozen other screens (`BattleUnit_BuildJobRecord`, `sub_14013297C`, `sub_14022F868`, `sub_1402B5AE8`, `sub_1402BA1FC`, `sub_1402C1310`, `sub_1402C185C`)
purpose: Builds the 148-byte job record used by the job tree and job-change screens from a job key and the unit's job arrays.

behavior.text: stores the key's job id at rec+72.
the Job row is taken from the key id (or the key's +36 field when the id is not positive) via JobTable_GetRow; rec+64 receives the row's dword at +44 (icon_part, the job icon number), 0 if no row.
rec+0..63 receives the display text: a formatted UI text 0x3FA with the job id and a flag (key +32 bit 0x40) for positive ids, or text 0x50 otherwise.
if the key carries a level array (+8) rec+68 gets the job's 4-bit level (high nibble for even job index, low nibble for odd).

if the key also carries a total-points array (+24), rec+84 is the points still needed for the next level (a threshold lookup for level+1 minus the stored total); level 8 or above, and job 161, give 0x20000000.
rec+76 and rec+80 are 16-bit values read from the key's arrays at +16 and +24 indexed by the job index.
the two arrays are most likely the unit's current and total job points.

the level is read through [array pointer + index / 2] with the pointer in the second address register (0x1400FBE09) and no bound check on the index (behavior JobArrayAccessesPutTheRecordPointerInTheIndexRegister).

notes: rec+64 is the value JobTreePanel_SetJobIcon later turns into the j_NNN icon path.

name: JobScreen_BuildAbilityTabList
proto: int JobScreen_BuildAbilityTabList(int tab, int job_id, int mode)
purpose: Builds the ability list of one tab for the party member the job screen has selected, then hands it to the job screen list builder.

purpose: Finds which job a secondary skillset belongs to for the selected party unit: the first (job, skillset) pair of the unit's secondary list whose skillset matches, else the unit's own job; then hands (job, skillset) on.

for each entry calls sub_140367AA0 and the page-list adders sub_14012EF90 / sub_14012F000 of the list addon.

purpose from the call pattern; only caller is JobScreen_UpdateState (0x368D4A, 0x368E85).

name: JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange
purpose:
Refreshes the job/equip screen after a change: it copies the selected party record into the 0x1407B27xx record,
the 0x141876E90 panel block and the 0x141876C80 tail record, then rebuilds the job list.

behavior.text:
It copies the selected unit record's first 0x30 bytes to `xmmword_1407B27C0`/`qword_1407B2758` and the
  record's +0x30..+0x6F to `xmmword_141876E90` with four 16-byte moves (0x1402BD15D, 0x1402BD168, 0x1402BD173,
  0x1402BD17E). The hand words at record +0x54..+0x5C therefore land at block +0x24..+0x2C.

It copies the record's +0x70 onward to the 0x141876C80 region with a 4x128-byte loop, so that block is the
  tail of the same record.

It also builds the 0x1407B27xx fields from a battle unit when the selected unit is in the battle table
  (the `sub_1402855F0`/`sub_140360700` branch); that branch overwrites the same block fields.

It calls `sub_1402C1310` with the record parts and the C80 block (0x1402BD5B0 passes the block to
  `sub_1402C19EC`), which renders the equip screen.

The block copy is raw: a bit-15 word in the unit record reaches block +0x24 and is passed to the renderers
  and the panel task unchanged.
It does not strip or mask any equipment word; the only masks are in the callees that read ids.
This is the writer that makes the panel block's hand words a copy of the live party record, not of the save.

it copies the selected party unit's block from +112 (unlock mask, learned bits, levels, the first JP words) into the preview record at 0x141876C10, which never receives +44; the header and preview panels are built from it.

notes: V: copies record +0x30..+0x6F to the panel block with four movaps (0x1402BD15D-0x1402BD17E), so the hand words at +0x54..+0x5C land at +0x24..+0x2C raw.
open_questions:
- ?: whether the battle-unit branch runs while the Outfitter is open; it would replace the block with a
  battle record's words.

name: JobScreen_RefreshLearnList

whether the refresh preserves the cursor row; the list gadget state is not read here.

name: JobScreen_ShowJobAbilities
purpose: Fills the job screen's detail panel for a job: the skillset header row and the four ability tabs of the current party unit.

behavior.text: the unit is g_PartyUnits[word_141811428]; when it is not in a special state (+62 <= 0) and the job is its own, the header shows its secondary skillset (+94), otherwise the job's JobTable row skillset (row guard: job < 0x40 + 0x6E, built in a register).

adds the header record (JobCommand row of the skillset, JobRecord_FromJobId) to the UI list, then for tabs 0..3 the rows of JobScreen_BuildJobTabRows (or sub_14028A770 for the own job) through sub_140367AA0.
called from JobScreen_UpdateState with the job of the selected tree / list entry (or -1).

name: JobScreen_UpdateState
callers: no direct call sites (reached through a function table)
callees: JobListScreen_GetCursorIndex, JobList_IsSelectedEntryUnflagged, JobScreen_OpenJobPage, JobChange_RunPreviewAnim, JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange, JobTree_FillJobRecords, Unit_SpendJp, PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave, UnitWork_BuildFromSaveIndex, Unit_BuildPreviewSpriteRecord, Unit_ResolvePreviewShape, sub_1402888E8
purpose: Per-frame state machine of the job screen (states 1400..1412): reads the job-change list cursor, picks the job from g_RuntimeJobList, shows its ability page, runs the job change and the preview animation.

behavior.text: reads and writes g_JobListSelectedEntry (6 references in total: three writes in this function, reads here and in JobList_IsSelectedEntryUnflagged).

calls JobListScreen_GetCursorIndex (4 sites), JobList_IsSelectedEntryUnflagged, JobScreen_OpenJobPage (0x140368D4A, 0x140368E85), JobChange_RunPreviewAnim (0x140368DC1), the job-change action sub_1402888E8, Unit_SpendJp, JobTree_FillJobRecords and JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange.

three inline copies of the cursor-to-entry read exist: the load of the dword at +0x4A48 of the object pointed to by the qword at +0x78 of the screen object, at 0x140368FDE (states 1401 and 1405), the mouse click copy at 0x140368C40 (state 1408, from a2[1]) and the write at 0x140368E74 (state 1404).
the name and the per-state meaning are inferred from the call pattern; the state numbers themselves are read from the code.
the preview shape of the selected Change Job entry is Unit_ResolvePreviewShape(unit, .., the entry's low byte), zero-extended into edx at 0x140368FAC.

notes: Earlier notes called it JobList_StateMachine; one name is kept. It reads g_RuntimeJobList six times as image base + list RVA + index * 2 (rsi holds the image base from a rip-relative lea): at 0x140368D06 and 0x140368D42 the index is g_JobListSelectedEntry, at 0x140368DB9, 0x140368E7D, 0x140368EC5 and 0x140368F9A it is the result of the cursor call just before (JobListScreen_GetCursorIndex, wrapped by the scroll runtime); the read at 0x140368F9A takes only the low byte.
open_questions: Full state table (only the cursor-reading states were read).

name: JobTable_GetNameText
proto: char JobTable_GetNameText(String *out, int language, unsigned int jobId, int variant)
purpose: Copies one of the four Job text slots (name +8, name_2 +0x0C, description +0x10, description_2 +0x14) into out, chosen by the kind (0 name, 1 help text) and the variant (0 or 1), falling back to the other variant when the chosen string is empty.

behavior.text: UITable_GetRowByKey(0x2E, jobId) gets the Job row; the second argument is the kind (0 = name slots, 1 = help slots; any other value returns 0) and the fourth the variant: kind 0 variant 0 = +8, variant 1 = +0x0C; kind 1 variant 0 = +0x10, variant 1 = +0x14.
when the chosen string is empty it tries the other variant of the same kind; returns 0 when both are empty or the row is missing, else 1 after copying the string into out.
the offsets are string offsets relative to row +8 (the string is at row + 8 + the stored value).

its caller TextTag_ExpandKeyIcon passes kind 0 for the 'jobname' tag and kind 1 for the 'jobhelp' tag, the key from the tag argument and the variant from the argument pair (see behavior JobNameAndHelpTextTags).

notes: Table 0x2E = 46 = Job-en (columns name, name_2, description, description_2). The offsets 8, 0x0C, 0x10 and 0x14 are reached as dword indexes 2..5 of the row pointer (the +0x14 slot is dword index 5), so no byte offset 0x14 appears in the body.

name: JobTable_GetRow
callers: JobList_RecomputeAvailability, JobRecord_FillIconAndGenericFlag, sub_1400F72F0, sub_1400FBB7C, sub_140117E1C, sub_14012F138, sub_14012FC6C
purpose: Returns the Job-en row for a job key (null if missing). Lazily caches table 46 in qword_143CDA2D8.

name: JobTree_Create
purpose: Factory that allocates a UIAddonFFTOUnitJobTree and runs JobTree_Ctor (call at 0x140113E28).

behavior.text: operator new(0x2FD8) at 0x140113E16 (the size is an immediate first argument): the whole addon is one fixed-size object.

name: JobTree_Ctor
purpose: Constructor for UIAddonFFTOUnitJobTree (RTTI). Sets vtables 0x140711618 and 0x140711718.

behavior.text: the destructor body is sub_140133574 (via wrapper sub_14013349C in vtable slot 0).
the in-process hardware watch arms an execute breakpoint here to catch construction.

notes: The addon base moves per run (ASLR), but panel-20 Unit gadget sat at addon - 0x19A3F60 in 5 runs.

name: JobTree_Dtor
purpose: Destructor body of UIAddonFFTOUnitJobTree (called through wrapper sub_14013349C, vtable slot 0).

behavior.text: restores the base vtables, destroys the 20 panel records (stride 456) in reverse, then runs the base destructor. The wrapper deletes with size 0x2FD8.

name: JobTree_FillJobRecords
purpose: Walks `g_RuntimeJobList` and, per list position, builds the 148-byte job record plus the sprite record, then hands them to the job-change list (sub_14012EC5C) and the tree (JobTree_SetPanelRecord).

behavior.text: stock loop bound is min(19, g_RuntimeJobListLen): the 19 is a 32-bit immediate loaded into edx at 0x1403686E9.
the stock list of a generic unit in mode 3 is 21 entries (74..93 without one of 91/92, then 160 and 161 flagged 0x2000), so positions 19 and 20 (the hidden extras) are never drawn by the stock bound.
the sprite record's render slot (record +0x5C) is set to 61 + list position; the tree panels use slots 80 + panel, so a list position of 19 or more names a tree panel's slot.
job id = word_143C51890[pos] & 0x3FF; calls sub_1400FBB7C (job row -> record), JobRecord_FillIconAndGenericFlag, sub_1402C1D40.

record state at +132 (assigned from the runtime job-list entry): 2 = LockUnreleased when entry bit 0x2000 is set, or when a story flag (sub_1400FF8A4(unit, 2010)) is set and the job id is 78..93; 1 = LockReleased when bit 0x4000 is set; otherwise 0 (unlocked; +137 is then set when sub_1402867BC(...) reports 0). The current job is not a state: rec+141 (showUse) = the unit's job == this job.

preview shape: for ids {160,161,164} or 74..93 uses an inline formula (`female + 2*job - 52` generic; 160 -> `female - 97` = 159/160; 161/164 -> `female - 95`), else Unit_ResolvePreviewShape. Special-case base constant is the immediate 0xA0 (160) loaded into a register at 0x14036898D.
calls sub_14012EC5C(listAddon, record, pos) and JobTree_SetPanelRecord(treeAddon, record, pos).
every shape branch of a cell joins at 0x140368A03, where dl is zero-extended into eax and stored as a dword into the record.

notes: The job-change list is the other consumer of the same list; it has 19 cells. The list is addressed through three rip-relative `lea` here (0x1403684B8 hands it to JobList_BuildForPartyUnit, 0x1403687A5 reads the entry, 0x14036885A tests the two flags).

name: JobTree_HandleInput
purpose: Per-frame pad input for the tree: confirm, back and 8-way cursor movement over the panel grid.

behavior.text: reached from sub_140115EA8 on event 1409 (focus) as a direct call with the focused input object; it is NOT addon vtable slot 26 (that slot is JobTree_ReleaseCharaSlots, slot 27 is JobTree_OnFocusChange).

confirm (Input_TestAction(0, 0, 26)) or the held flag addon+12241: sends message 128 with the selected index (index-1 when >= 18, because of the Bard/Dancer pair) and returns code 1400. Back (Input_TestAction(0, 0, 27)): sound 15, code 1400.

direction = two groups of four pad bytes at qword_143CD9EE8 + 13648..13651 and + 13652..13655, each ordered down, left, up, right; up wins over down and right over left, giving up 0, up-right 1, right 2, down-right 3, down 4, down-left 5, left 6, up-left 7, none -1; the first group is used unless it gives none.

neighbour lookup (columns cursor_<direction>, cursor_<direction>_2 and the _primary_only flags of the GeneralJob row, see behavior JobTreeCursorNeighbourTable): panel record +0x1A8 (addressed as addon + 496 + 456 x panel: the record starts at addon + 72) holds a navigation table, 8 directions x 2 candidates x (panel byte, flag byte) = 32 B; a candidate equal to the hidden gender slot (17 or 18 by addon+12240) is skipped; with the second group a candidate whose flag byte is set is skipped too.

the starting panel is addon+12232 (the panel under the cursor) when it is a panel; otherwise addon+12236 when it is below the panel count (at least 0), else the constant 20 at 0x140671F04. The chosen neighbour is focused with GUICore_FocusNode(addon + 72 + 456 * panel) when it is below the panel count.

notes: The panel record +0x1A8 is reached as the panel address (addon + 72 + 456 * panel) plus a computed offset, so the constant 0x1A8 does not appear in the body. The navigation table is copied into the panel record at refresh time from the GeneralJob row (JobTree_RefreshAddon loop tail).

name: JobTree_NodeStem
purpose: Tree index -> UIB node-name stem. The stem is the name of the job's panel node and the `A`/`B` parts of arrow names `Line<A><B>`.

behavior.text: id = index + 74; 74 Squire, 75 Chemist, 76 Knight, 77 Archer, 78 Monk, 79 White, 80 Black, 81 Time, 82 Summoner, 83 Thief, 84 Orator, 85 Mystic, 86 Geomancer, 87 Dragoon, 88 Samurai, 89 Ninja, 90 Arithmetician, 91 Bard, 92 Dancer, 93 Mime; anything else returns the default Str1.

notes: V: a leaf that writes only rax and edx; the caller at 0x140133A42 reads the arrow's level back from ecx after the call.

name: JobTree_OnCursorEnter
purpose: Cursor moved onto panel `jobIdx`: lights every arrow and label attached to it (its 6 requirement edges and its 6 dependent edges).

behavior.text: guard jobIdx <= cap (0x13 in the game's code). Loops 6 slots of the panel's requirement table (record+0x88, 24 B each) and 6 of its dependents table (record+0x118); the code walks one pointer, addon + 456 x panel + 228, and reads 20 bytes before it and 124 after it (the record starts at addon + 72).

met = required job's JobRecord.state == 0 (record+132) and edge level <= record+68 (the job's level). Each edge calls JobTree_SetArrowState(line, onCursor=1, met) and JobTree_SetLabelState(board, show=1, met).
the Bard/Dancer pair (indices 17/18) is special-cased with addon+12240 (gender flag): only the visible one of the pair is processed.
only 6 dependents are kept per job, so a job required by more than 6 others highlights only the first 6 of its outgoing arrows.

notes: Mirror image of JobTree_OnCursorLeave. V: JobTree_OnEvent calls it on event 19 for a panel node, after storing the panel at addon+12232. I: event 19 is every cursor arrival on a panel, the pad's focus (GUICore_FocusNode) and the mouse's hover (event 12 focuses the hovered panel node).

name: JobTree_OnCursorLeave
purpose: Cursor left panel `jobIdx`: puts its arrows and labels back to the resting (not on cursor) states.

behavior.text: same loop as JobTree_OnCursorEnter but passes onCursor=0 to JobTree_SetArrowState and show=0 to JobTree_SetLabelState (labels hide when the cursor leaves).

name: JobTree_OnEvent
purpose: UI event handler of the tree addon (vtable slot 2).

behavior.text: event 4 = copy the 'held' flag addon+12242 to addon+12241 and clear it; 0x10 = set addon+12242; 0xC on a panel node (node+544 == 18) = GUICore_FocusNode(node).
event 12 is the mouse arriving over a panel (the pad focuses through JobTree_HandleInput); the focus then arrives as event 19 like the pad's.
event 19 (cursor enter) on a panel node: addon+12232 = panel index (node+548); JobTree_OnCursorEnter(addon, index); then vtable slot 3 and sound id 17 (sub_1400F4BCC).
event 20 (cursor leave) on a panel node: JobTree_OnCursorLeave(addon, index).

notes: Panel nodes carry kind 18 at node+544 and the job index at node+548 (set in JobTree_RefreshAddon).

name: JobTree_OnFocusChange
proto: void JobTree_OnFocusChange(JobTreeAddon *addon, int newFocus, int oldFocus)
purpose: Focus change handler (vtable slot 27): when the tree gains the input focus (id 1409) it puts the cursor back on the remembered panel; when it loses it, it tells its parent.

behavior.text: second argument == 1409: sub_1401D1E30(addon, 0), then GUICore_FocusNode on the node of panel addon+12236 when that panel is within the cap (stock <= 0x13, the plan raises it).
third argument == 1409: sub_1401D1EAC(addon, 0) and message 127 to the parent (addon+16, its vtable +48).
the second argument is the focus gained and the third the focus lost (the first branch restores the cursor, the second reports to the parent).
1409 is the tree's input focus: sub_140115EA8 sends focus 1409 to JobTree_HandleInput and every other focus to the job list addon.

notes: addon+12236 is written by JobTree_SetPanelRecord: the panel of the unit's current job, so a reopened tree starts on it.

name: JobTree_RefreshAddon
callees: JobTree_NodeStem, GUINode_FindDescendant, sub_140409134, sub_1403DBC74, Str_Format, UIName_Key
purpose: UIAddonFFTOUnitJobTree vtable slot 4. Builds the tree: finds the 'JobTree' root, looks up one panel node per job BY NAME, finds each node's 'Unit' gadget and text children, and wires Line* connector nodes.

behavior.text: runs at BOOT (title screen), not when the tree opens (exec breakpoint fires about 5 s after launch).
stock panel loop bound is 20 (the immediate at 0x140133944).
node name = sub_140134980(table, i): job index -> stem ('Squire'..'Mime'); the index past the stock 20 falls to the default Str1.
stores node at addon+72+456*i, Unit gadget at +8, name gadget at +16, title at +24.
requirement lines come from GeneralJob rows (nxd table 189): node names 'Line%sLv%02d' / 'Line%s%s'; missing line nodes are null-checked.

the name format is chosen by the requirement's position code, not by which node exists: code 5 or 6 -> 'Line<required>Lv<level>' (one node shared by every requirement on that job at that level: the stock Squire / Chemist two-branch arrows), any other code -> 'Line<required><job>'. Codes 3, 5 and 6 all select the B label board.

second loop (jobs 0..n-1): for each job reads its GeneralJob row; per requirement j < min(6, count): required job, level and position code. Stores the arrow node at panel record +0x88+24*j (line), the label board at +0x90, required job at +0x98, level at +0x9C.

position code -> board name: 1 -> TextBoardJobLvL, 2 -> R, 3/5/6 -> B, 4 -> T. The board is looked up BY NAME on the REQUIRED job's panel node, so every requirement pointing at the same side of the same panel resolves to the same board (the last text written wins).

the board's 'LvMaster'/'LvNum' states are started and its 'Title' text receives the level number: the requirement's level, the i16 at row + [row+0x18] + j*2 (rdi = the GeneralJob row, r12 = j; 0x140133C5B).

sharing one board is how the stock tree labels arrows that leave one side at one level: Squire's B board shows one 'Lv. 2' for both Chemist and Knight; seen live 2026-11-12 (three Lv. 2 arrows under Squire, one label).

the boards are References to the 40 x 20 component TextBoardJobLv at scale 1.2, pivot = centre, in UnitJob's LayerRoot (origin (0, 8)): centres relative to the panel node L (-54, 90), R (116, 90), T (32, -38), B (32, 136), the disc centre being (31, 88). Every one of the 30 stock arrows leaves its side on the centre lane (L / R at y 87..90, B at x 26..36), so each board sits on its side's centre lane just outside the panel box.
the same pass records the reverse edge in the required job's dependents table (record +0x118, 6 entries x {line, board, child job, level}); more than 6 dependents are dropped.

the loop tail copies the job's 8-direction navigation pairs (cursor grid) from the GeneralJob row into the panel record at +0x1A8: per direction, candidate 0 takes the low byte of the dword at row +0x28 + 4 * direction and the flag byte at row +0x68 + direction, candidate 1 the low byte of the dword at row +0x48 + 4 * direction and the flag byte at row +0x70 + direction (columns cursor_<direction>, cursor_<direction>_2, cursor_<direction>_primary_only, cursor_<direction>_2_primary_only); record byte 4 * direction + 2 * candidate = panel index (0..19, 20 = none), the next byte = the flag. See behavior JobTreeCursorNeighbourTable.

notes: The panel record offsets (+0x88, +0x90, +0x98, +0x9C, +0x118, +0x1A8) are reached through a running pointer into the 456-byte record, so they appear only as sums in the body. Panel stride is 456 bytes; the addon is 0x2FD8 bytes in stock (allocated in JobTree_Create). Limits in this function: 6 requirements per job, 6 dependents per job, 4 label boards per panel (one per side).
open_questions: Requirement arrows are authored nodes: a job with no Line* node draws no arrow.

name: JobTree_ReleaseCharaSlots
purpose: Releases the unit-preview render slots used by the tree panels (CharaRender slot ids 80..98).

behavior.text: loop of 19: slot id 80+i; clears the 112-byte slot at CharaRenderMgr+14920+8960+112*i (sub_1400ED768) and releases it from the renderer (sub_1400CC52C).
the loop count is 19, not 20: the panel at index 19 (slot 99) is not released here, and the extra panels (slots 100+) are not either.

notes: None.
open_questions: Whether the unreleased slots leak or are reused.

name: JobTree_SetArrowState
proto: void JobTree_SetArrowState(JobTreeAddon *addon, GUINode *lineNode, char onCursor, uint8_t met)
purpose: Sets the look of one requirement arrow: activates exactly one of the named states Lock / Unlock / LockOnCursor / UnlockOnCursor on the line node.

behavior.text: state index = met + (onCursor ? 2 : 0); the other three states are stopped (GUINode_StopState). Null node: no-op.
'met' = the required job is learned (record state == 0) and its level >= the edge's required level (see JobTree_OnCursorEnter).
Lock = grey, Unlock = lit; the OnCursor pair is the highlighted variant drawn while the cursor is on either end of the arrow (green in game screenshots).

notes: Arrows are `Line<A><B>` nodes authored in ffto_job_tree.uib; the states live in the shared shape component (LineBottom, LineRightBottom, ...).

name: JobTree_SetLabelState
proto: void JobTree_SetLabelState(JobTreeAddon *addon, GUINode *labelBoard, char show, char met)
purpose: Sets one level-label board: activates exactly one of the named states Hide / ShowLock / ShowUnlock.

behavior.text: state = 0 (Hide) when !show; otherwise 1 (ShowLock) or 2 (ShowUnlock) by `met`. Others are stopped. Null board: no-op.
ShowLock is the red 'not yet' chip, ShowUnlock the green one (as seen: green 'Lv. 4' chips).

notes: Boards are the `TextBoardJobLv{L,R,T,B}` children of the panel template (component UnitJob); one board is shared by every requirement that lands on that side of that panel.

name: JobTree_SetPanelRecord
purpose: Stores a job record into the tree panel slot and sets the panel's Lock/Unlock/LvNum UI states.

behavior.text: slot = pos; if rec->jobId - 92 <= 1 (Dancer/Bard) slot++, because one of the pair is missing from the list. So Mime (93) at list position 18 lands on panel 19.
if slot > cap (stock 0x13) return. Copies the 148-byte record to addon+9192+148*slot; stores slot+80 at addon+9284+148*slot and registers a render slot via CharaRender_RegisterSlot.

fills the name board's texts through sub_14029B140 (JobTreePanel_FillTexts; name via JobTreePanel_SetJobIcon with locked = (rec.state == 2)), then plays LvNum for an unlocked record (state 0) and LvNone for any locked one (state 1 or 2), and Unlock / LockReleased / LockUnreleased by state (rec+132); ShowUse/HideUse by rec+141.
the Bard/Dancer branch swaps the 'Bard'/'Dancer' label.

notes: Panels are indexed by LIST POSITION (+1 shift), not by job key. This was the key to the scrambled-sprite bug.

name: JobTreePanel_FillTexts
purpose: Fills the texts of one tree panel's name board from its job record: the job icon (JobTreePanel_SetJobIcon) and the level texts.

behavior.text: when the record's level (rec+68) is <= 0 the Title text takes UI text 157 ('Lv. --') and the level-number text UI text 80 ('--'); otherwise the level values (rec+68 / +76 / +80) are written as text arguments.
each text node is marked dirty through sub_14028F754 after its text list changes.

notes: JobTree_SetPanelRecord plays LvNum for an unlocked record (state 0) and LvNone for any locked one (state 1 or 2) right after this call.
open_questions: Meaning of the three level arguments (rec+68/+76/+80) (?).

name: JobTreePanel_SetJobIcon
proto: __int64 JobTreePanel_SetJobIcon(int ctx, int a2, unsigned int jobNameKey, __int64 titleNode, __int64 rec, char locked)
purpose: Formats the job icon image path (j_NNN) of a tree panel from its job record; a LockUnreleased job gets the placeholder icon 24 instead.

behavior.text: formats the Icon table template (row 15) with the third argument, or with 24 when `locked` is set, and hands the resulting path to the setter (sub_14029BC00).
when `locked` is set and a Title node exists, the node's text id (+248) is forced to 1010 and its dirty byte (+316) set: UI text row 1010 is '???' in the English text table.

formats the Icon table's template (row 15) with the third argument, or with 24 when the locked flag is set, i.e. a job icon image path of the form j_%03d; the number is the job row's icon_part (record +64).

notes:
`locked` is rec.state == 2 (LockUnreleased) as passed by JobTree_SetPanelRecord. The studio reads the string from the extracted UI-en row 1010 (labels.json locked_tag).

Also known as JobTreePanel_SetNameText (earlier IDB name, renamed because this routine builds the job's icon image path j_NNN, not its name text). The locked placeholder is icon 24.

name: JobTreePanel_SetTextKey
proto: void JobTreePanel_SetTextKey(__int64 ctx, __int64 binding, const char *key, __int64 textNode, __int64 args)
purpose: Points a name-board text binding at a text key and clears the text node's fixed text id so the keyed text is used.

behavior.text: when a text node is given, its text id (+248) is cleared (dirty byte +316 set) and sub_1403F0F8C(node, args) applies the arguments.

when a binding is given, the key string stored at binding+232 is compared with `key`; if it differs and the context's owner resolves the key (sub_1403FBE3C), the binding is re-keyed with UIName_Key + sub_1403D87F4.

notes: JobTreePanel_SetJobIcon overrides the cleared id with 1010 afterwards for a locked job.

name: JournalDetail_Fill
purpose: Fills the Events detail panel.

behavior.text: title (+0x10) and text (+0x14); 'ShowPlace' / 'HidePlace' by place_name (+0x1C: the PlaceName table 85 row, string +0xC into the node at +880); 'Clear' (node at +896, bound in sub_14016A5EC) plays 'Enable' / 'Disable' by clear_mark (+0x25).

name: JournalList_Build
purpose: Builds the Chronicle Events list from the Journal rows that are met.

behavior.text: walks the rows by index; for each met user_situation (+0xC) pushes {key, row +8, kind, save byte at save block +6922 + i, byte at +7050 + i} (kind: 1 when movie (+0x24) is set, 2 when event_id (+0x18) is 0, else 0).
the list is insertion-sorted by entry +4 (= Journal sort_order, +8).

name: JournalList_DrawRow
purpose: Draws one row of the Events list.

behavior.text: 'TextName' = title (+0x10); the kind 0 / 1 / 2 plays 'Event' / 'Movie' / 'Battle'; quest_mark (+0x26) plays 'ShowQuest' / 'HideQuest'; sub_14016B31C is called with the entry's new mark (entry +9).

name: JournalList_RestoreCursor
purpose: Puts the list cursor back on the replayed entry.

behavior.text: back in the list, re-finds the entry by event_id (+0x18) / event_id_2 (+0x20) to restore the cursor.

name: JournalPanel_Tick
purpose: The replay panel's state steps.

behavior.text: state 1: pauses input, closes the list, sub_1400FB3B0(-2), hides the guide, sub_1402CD714(7), then state 2.
state 2, after the fade: EventViewer_StartReplay(panel +112, +126); dword_142FF9F4C = +116; +127 = 1; state 3.

name: JournalReplay_StartEvent
purpose: Starts the replay of the chosen Events entry (action 2).

behavior.text: panel +112 = event_id (+0x18), +116 = event_id_2 (+0x20), +120 = list cursor, +124 = 1 (start), +126 = 0; then plays UI sound 0x73.

name: JournalReplay_StartMovie
purpose: Starts the replay of a movie entry (action 3).

behavior.text: like JournalReplay_StartEvent but only for rows with movie (+0x24) set; panel +112 = +0x18, +116 = +0x20, +120 = list cursor, +124 = 1, +126 = 1; then UI sound 0x73.

name: JournalScreen_OnAction
callees: JournalReplay_StartEvent, JournalReplay_StartMovie, JournalList_RestoreCursor, UIGuide_Set, UIGuide_Show, sub_140169678, sub_1401163C4, sub_1400DF354
purpose: Handles the actions of the Events screen.

behavior.text: action 1: when the entry's new mark (entry +9 of the 12-byte list entries) is set it clears it and, for every word of the save block's list at +6666 (128 entries) equal to the entry key, clears the byte at +6922 + i and sets the byte at +7050 + i to 1.
action 2 calls JournalReplay_StartEvent; action 3 calls JournalReplay_StartMovie.

action 65537 (0x10001): when panel +112 is non-zero it calls sub_1401163C4(save block, 4, 1, 0) and sends a JournalNotification carrying panel +112; then JournalList_RestoreCursor and the guide 13002. Action 65538 calls sub_140169678 (both tested as the action number minus 3 minus 65534, so 0x10001 does not appear as a constant).

name: KeyTrack_FindKey
callers: KeyTrackVec2_Eval, KeyTrackBool_Eval and the other KeyTrack evaluators (sub_140407B14, sub_1404080C4, sub_140408218, sub_140408328)
purpose: Binary search in a keyframe track: returns the index of the last key whose frame (u16 at key+0) is <= frame, or -1 when every key is later.

behavior.text: the track is a small vector: count = int at t+72; keys 0..3 are stored inline at t + 16*i, keys 4.. in the heap array at *(t+64) + 16*(i-4). A key is 16 bytes: u16 frame (+0), u16 span (+2), u32 curve id (+4), 8 bytes of value (+8, +12).
lo = 0, hi = count, mid = count / 2; a key later than frame moves hi, otherwise lo; the result is the last mid that was <= frame (-1 when none).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14040222C). Callers pass the frame truncated to int (cvttss2si for the float evaluators).

name: KeyTrackBool_Eval
purpose: Evaluates the boolean (visibility) track of a UIB state at an integer frame; the result drives node byte +144.

behavior.text: key = KeyTrack_FindKey(t, frame); none -> return 0 (property untouched). Let span = u16 key+2, f = key.frame (u16 +0), v = (key+8 != 0).
span != 0: frame > f + span -> *out = 0, otherwise *out = v (a key with a span is a pulse of that many frames); return 1.

span == 0 and frame == f: *out = v. Span == 0 and the key's curve id (key+4) != 0: not the last key: s = (frame - f) / (next.frame - f) (int to float divide), e = UIAnim_Curve(curve, s), *out = (e < 1.0) ? v : next.v, so the value flips to the next key's value exactly when the eased curve reaches 1.0; last key: *out = v. Curve id 0 -> return 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F4604). In sub_140400840 the output is stored as node+144 = out (absolute mode, a4 != 0) or node+144 = out && node+144 (relative mode, a4 == 0): a relative visibility track can only hide.
open_questions: ? Which UIB property this track is called in the editor (only its node effect +144 was read).

name: KeyTrackVec2_Eval
proto: char KeyTrackVec2_Eval(KeyTrack *t, float frame, float out[2])
callers: sub_140400840 (GUINode_ApplyTracks, scale track a1[8]), sub_1404015C0 (component-level tracks, five call sites)
purpose: Evaluates a two-float keyframe track (the scale track of a UIB state) at a frame: finds the key, eases between it and the next key with UIAnim_Curve and writes the interpolated pair.

behavior.text: key index = KeyTrack_FindKey(t, (int)frame) (the frame is TRUNCATED for the search). Index < 0 returns 0 (no value: the caller leaves the property alone). The key's curve id (u32 at key+4) = 0 also returns 0.

when the key is not the last one: next = key + 1; s = (frame - (float)key.frame) / (float)(next.frame - key.frame) with the UNtruncated float frame; e = UIAnim_Curve(key.curve, s); out.x = (next.x - key.x) * e + key.x and out.y = (next.y - key.y) * e + key.y (single precision, this operation order).
when the key is the last one the output is that key's pair unchanged (the value holds after the last key); the function returns 1.
the easing of a segment is chosen by the curve id of the segment's FIRST key.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140407C18). sub_140407B14 (one float, rotation and opacity tracks) and the int / colour evaluators sub_1404080C4, sub_140408218, sub_140408328 follow the same key layout (not read here).
open_questions: ? The key's u16 at +2 is not read by this evaluator (KeyTrackBool_Eval uses it as a hold length).

name: Launcher_DrawControlsPage
callees: UIName_Key, GUINode_ApplyStateAtFrame, UIName_ReleaseKey, GUINode_StopState, GUINode_PlayStateAtFrame, GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState

notes: Name is ours. The hand-over to Launcher_FillControls (sub_1401BBB30) is a tail jump, not a call.

name: Launcher_DrawInfoPage
callees: UIName_Key, GUINode_ApplyStateAtFrame, GUINode_StopState, GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState, GUINode_FindGadgetPart, NxdEntry_GetRow, GUITextNode_SetTextExpandedTemp, UIGadgetFFTOVScrollText_Refit
purpose: Draws an information page of the launcher's guide.

behavior.text: plays the 'Info' state, puts the caption into the info text and shows the picture with GuiImage_SetIconById(+624, the row's icon (+4)).

notes: Name is ours.

name: Launcher_DrawPage
callees: NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys2, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_1401BB9D8, sub_1401BBDD0, sub_1401BB77C, sub_1402EE84C, sub_1401BBF80
purpose: Draws the current page of the launcher's guide pages.

behavior.text: reads the LauncherGuide row of the current set and page: controls_page (+0xC) non-zero draws Launcher_DrawControlsPage; else start_page (+0xD) non-zero draws Launcher_DrawStartPage; else Launcher_DrawInfoPage.

notes: Name is ours.

name: Launcher_DrawStartPage
callees: UIName_Key, GUINode_ApplyStateAtFrame, UIName_ReleaseKey, GUINode_FindPartByName, NxdEntry_GetRow, GUITextNode_SetTextExpandedTemp, UIGadgetFFTOVScrollText_Refit, GUINode_FindGadgetPart, GUICore_FocusNode
purpose: Draws the guide page that carries the Start button.

behavior.text: plays the 'Start' state on node +520, puts the caption (+8) into the scrolling text and refits it, sets the gadget parts 'ButtonStart' and 'Title' to UI text 2214 and focuses the node at +560.

notes: Name is ours.

name: Launcher_FillControls
callees: NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_1400F81CC, GUITextNode_SetTextById, GUITextNode_UpdateLayout
purpose: Fills the controls list of the launcher guide.

behavior.text: lists the control entries of table 278 (cache qword_143CDA570): column +0x18 for the Enhanced set, column +4 for the Classic set.
entries 4006..4018 get extra glyph lists.

notes: Name is ours.

name: LayerBinds_Push
purpose: Appends a (slot, resource) pair to the binder's per-layer (mode 1) or per-target (mode 2) vectors; the pairs are replayed into a render command by LayerBinds_Replay.

behavior.text: mode = byte b+135: 0 does nothing; 1 uses idx = u8 layer+86 and the vector pair at b+176+200*idx (u16 slots) / b+144+200*idx (qword resources); 2 uses idx = u8 layer+90 and the pair at b+376+200*idx / b+344+200*idx; other values return.

both vectors are std::vector: begin at +8, end at +16, capacity end at +24 of the 16-byte-offset header; a push with spare capacity stores the value and adds 2 (slots) or 8 (resources) to the end pointer, else it calls the grow helper (sub_1403C1868 for u16, sub_140031D7C for qwords).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403A83B0). Trivial helper; IDA shows it as variadic because the resource pointer is the 4th argument.

name: LayerBinds_RecordAllLayers
purpose: Walks every live render layer and records the per-layer shader-resource binds for those flagged as recordable.

behavior.text: renderer R = qword_143CDA098. n = *(u16*)(R+13734) (live layer count). Sets binder+135 = 1 at entry and 0 at exit (recording-mode flag).
for i in 0..n-1: slot = *(u16*)(R + 2*i + 7262) (order table), layer = *(qword*)(R + 8*slot + 88). Null layers skipped.

only layers with (*(u32*)(layer+80) & 0x10000000) (bit 28) are recorded: binder[200*(*(u8*)(layer+86)) + 136] = layer (a 200-byte per-group record whose first qword is the layer pointer; layer+86 is the layer group id), then LayerBinds_RecordLayer(binder, layer).
the loop also re-checks *(u16*)(R+13734) != 0 on every iteration.

notes: Companion of the per-layer path in RenderFrame_Record, which calls LayerBinds_RecordLayer directly.
open_questions: ? meaning of bit 28 of layer+80 (probably 'owns a constant buffer'). ? the 200-byte binder group record layout beyond +0.

name: LayerBinds_RecordLayer
purpose: Records two bind entries for one layer: the per-group constant buffer and, if the layer has a render target, that target's buffer.

behavior.text: target = *(qword*)(layer+40). First push: LayerBinds_Push(binder, layer, *(u16*)(binder+48), *(qword*)(binder + 8*(*(u8*)(layer+86)) + 8)), i.e. slot index binder+48 with the buffer pointer from the per-group array starting at binder+8, indexed by layer group id (layer+86).
if target != 0, second push: LayerBinds_Push(binder, layer, *(u16*)(binder+50), *(qword*)(target+3248)); the buffer comes from target+3248.
returns the result of the last push.
u16s at binder+48 and +50 are shader constant-buffer slot indices resolved at init (cf. UIRender_CreateBuffers storing slot ids as u16).

open_questions: ? what the second buffer at target+3248 holds (per-target size / texel constants?).

name: LayerBinds_Replay
purpose: Copies the recorded bind lists of a layer into a render command: resource pointers into cmd+328+8*slot, texture handles into cmd+1608+8*slot, and 31-bit constants into cmd+5704+4*slot.

behavior.text: r = 200 * u8 layer+90; three (value vector, slot vector) pairs at b+352+r / b+384+r (qwords), b+416+r / b+448+r (qwords, dereferenced), b+480+r / b+512+r (dwords); the count is the slot vector's byte span >> 1.

pair 1: cmd[328 + 8*slot] = resource pointer. Pair 2: cmd[1608 + 8*slot] = (resource ? *(resource + 40) : 0), the same slot field GUILayer_EffectPass0 writes at rc+1608 for textures. Pair 3: *(u32*)(cmd + 5704 + 4*slot) = value & 0x7FFFFFFF, the shader-selector constants of GUILayer_EffectPass0 (rc+5704, top bit cleared).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403A8468). Called once per draw command (per batch), so it is hot, but it only copies binds; it does not touch glyph positions. The same call is made by every layer draw (composite, effect passes), not only by SDF text.
open_questions: ? which of the 328 / 1608 / 5704 areas are constant buffers, textures and shader constants respectively beyond the equivalence with GUILayer_EffectPass0 (I).

name: LegacyMenu_BuildLocationList
purpose: Builds the legacy location menu's list of unlocked world map locations.

behavior.text: for locations 0..42 reads event variable 512 + n; every non-zero one is appended to the live location list (the table at 0x140789550) as 0x9000 + n (computed as n minus 0x7000 in a 16-bit word).
a parallel state word list gets 0 when event variable 615 + n is non-zero, otherwise 8, and 4 for the location equal to event variable 49 (the current one).
splits the count into a page of 7 and the overflow, and picks the cursor row so the current location is visible.

notes: Name is ours.

name: LegacyMenu_InitWorld
purpose: Initialises the legacy world menu: loads its text resource and picks the screen state block of the current text language.

behavior.text: initialises the event tasks, loads resource slot 4, copies it into a work buffer and clears event variable 510.

text language 0 selects the block at 0x14080CAB0, 3 the block at 0x14080D930, 2 the block at 0x14080E070 and every other value (1, default) the block at 0x14080D1F0; the choice becomes the active screen block.
builds a pointer list into the work buffer, then writes event variables 511 = 0, 52 = 1, 53 = 0 and 54 = 1.

notes: Name is ours.

name: LegacyMenu_LoadRowList
purpose: Loads the row id list of the legacy menu named by the screen block into the live row array and starts the menu command screen.

behavior.text: the menu id is the signed word at +872 of the active screen block; the row count comes from LegacyMenuRowCounts and the list from LegacyMenuRowListPointers.
each row byte is turned into a text id by subtracting a fixed base and stored in the live row array; at most 7 rows are shown on a page (the first word is the count shown, the second the overflow).
ends by calling the command screen builder BattleCommand_BuildScreen.

notes: Name is ours; the existing name of the callee comes from an earlier pass.

name: LegacyMenu_PickLocation
purpose: Confirms the highlighted location of the legacy location menu.

behavior.text: reads the location id from the live list at the cursor index (+608 of the screen block) or, with a pending selection object, from that object.

when the entry is selectable, writes the id to event variable 51, sets bit 14 of a shared flag word (a bit-test-and-set, value 0x4000), clears the next two task slots and, when no pending selection object exists, sets the menu result code to 1; otherwise the result code becomes 5.
ends the calling task.

notes: Name is ours.

name: LegacyMenu_StoreRow
purpose: Stores the row chosen in the current legacy menu into the acting unit's row memory, for the menus that remember it.

behavior.text: looks for the current menu id among the first 12 records of the menu row result table (0x1407DCFF0) and copies the node's row byte (+80) into the unit's 17-byte memory (0x1407DD1E0).

name: LegacyMenuTasks_Run
callers: started by the legacy menu start as a scene task
purpose: Task body of the legacy menu panes: keeps three pane tasks in step with the menu state.

behavior.text: picks a row of LegacyMenuTaskSetups by the menu state word (values above 3 use row 0).
for each of the three panes compares the row's expected owner id with the live pane owner and sets one of two flag patterns in the pane's task slot depending on the match.
never returns: it loops forever as a task and yields between passes.

notes: Name is ours.

name: LegacyOptions_DrawTask
callees: EventTask_Start (starts LegacyOptions_RowTask), EventTask_WaitFrame, Input_TestAction, VramPage_CopyRect, sub_140242AFC, sub_1402E2C54
purpose: Task that draws the legacy options window and handles its cursor.

behavior.text: lays out one row per option with the choice texts (message id = text base of the option + the live choice) and the cursor cells.
copies the key repeat preset row (6 bytes chosen by option bits 9..11) into the live repeat settings.

name: LegacyOptions_Open
callees: EventTask_Start (starts the draw task LegacyOptions_DrawTask), EventTask_Terminate, EventTask_WaitFrame, sub_140364408, sub_1403664E4
purpose: Opens the legacy options screen: unpacks the option word into the 12 live choices.

behavior.text: the option word 0x140782A24 holds the choices (3-bit fields for the first five, 2-bit fields for the rest); each is stored in the live choices array (0x1408FA460).
sets a flag when every live choice equals its default (0x1408FA420) and starts the draw task.

name: LegacyOptions_RowTask
purpose: Task that edits one option row of the legacy options screen and packs the choices back.

behavior.text: left / right changes the option's choice within its choice count; the selection starts from the defaults when asked.
repacks the 12 choices into the option word and refreshes the live key repeat settings.

name: LegacyTask12_Build
callees: GradientWindow_ColourFromPaletteA, GradientWindow_ColourFromPaletteB, NumberFields_Draw, SceneTask_WaitFrame, sub_140242AFC, sub_140220450
purpose: Scene task 12: builds the plates and number fields of a battle-side panel from per-language cell lists.

behavior.text: mode 12 reads the command block 0x140901300, any other mode 0x1409014E0; the cell block of the text language (0x140900EC0 language 0, 0x1409011F0 language 3, 0x1409010E0 language 2, 0x140900FD0 otherwise) supplies 17 six-word cells.
colours its gradient windows with GradientWindow_ColourFromPaletteA / B, draws number fields with NumberFields_Draw and waits frames with SceneTask_WaitFrame.
the name 'task 12' is the task id this function tests (12) before choosing its command block.

name: ListScroll_HandleStick
callees: GUIComponentList_GetVScroll, GUIComponentList_GetHScroll, GUIInput_IsPointerOverLayer, ListScroll_Step, sub_14028E850, sub_14028D44C
purpose: Mouse wheel or right stick scrolls a component list by whole rows, independent of the cursor.

behavior.text: acts only when the list component (h+24) is enabled (its +554), h+120 is set, sub_14028D44C(h) is 0 and the int at h+104 is negative.
wheel (in+8 != 0), when h+126 is clear or the pointer is over the list layer 9: a vertical bar present -> ListScroll_Step, else a horizontal bar -> sub_14028E850; returns 1.

otherwise, when h+122 is set: right stick vertical byte in+1227 != 0 with a vertical bar -> ListScroll_Step; right stick horizontal byte in+1226 != 0 with a horizontal bar -> sub_14028E850; returns 1 when either ran, else 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14028E5D0). The Job Tree has no VScroll bar and no reader of the input state's bytes +1224 .. +1227 (a scan of every instruction with those displacements, 2026-11-10: no JobTree_* function among them), so the right stick does nothing there today.
open_questions: ? the flags at h+120 / +122 / +126 are named from use only; ? the callers (an addon update).

name: ListScroll_Step
purpose: Scrolls a component list vertically by rows x row height, then re-homes the focus when the focused item left the view.

behavior.text: scroll y = list+680 - list+692 (row height) x (rows * -1), through GUIComponentList_SetScrollY(list, y, snap 1, clamp 1).

when the cursor widget is active: if the focused item (h+96, when not negative) is not visible, the first visible usable item (scrolling down: scanned from the first shown item) or the last visible usable one (scrolling up) is focused with sub_14028D8F4(h, item, item, 0); when none is usable the focus is cleared (GUICore_FocusNode(0)). g_GUICore+2112 is set to 3 at the end.
so a stick scroll never moves the focus while the focused item stays visible, and pulls it to the nearest visible item when it does not.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14028E720). The float argument is the step in rows (sign = direction), passed in xmm1. This is the game's own pattern for stick scrolling with a focused item.
open_questions: ? where the float comes from (value and scale).

name: LookPool_ClaimForSprite
purpose: Finds or claims the look pool record for a sprite number and returns its index, or 0xFFFF when all 15 records are in use.

behavior.text: walks the 15 records of 0x32D6 bytes at 0x140D005A0 and returns the index of the first one whose byte +1 equals the argument, after storing the low byte of the argument into its byte +0.
when none matches it takes the first record whose byte +0 is zero, stores the low byte of the argument in +0 and +1 and returns its index.
returns 0xFFFF when no record is free.
first the record whose byte +1 equals the sprite (sets +0 to it), else the first record whose +0 is 0 (sets +0 and +1 to the sprite); 0xFFFF when all 15 are claimed.

notes: Structure: LookPoolRecord. Both stores and the comparison are single bytes. The name is ours (IDB: sub_140268FF4).
open_questions: ? the purpose of the second caller sub_14026A048.

name: LookPool_ResetForBattleLoad
purpose: Clears the scene-unit in-use flags and the look pool claims before a battle load, and resets the load state machine.

behavior.text: unless the global at 0x142FF9E2C is 1, sets the in-use dword of each of the 16 scene-unit records and the first byte of each of the 15 look pool records to 0.
clears the list head qword_140D3A410 and the state words at 0x140CE3240 (pass, step, entry index, buffer).

only byte +0 (the claim) of a pool record is cleared here; byte +1 (the sprite the record holds) and the record's data stay, so CharaPalette_ReloadForShape's pass 2 still finds the record by +1 and skips reading that sprite's classic file. The battle setup sub_140210AF0 clears byte +1 of all 15 records itself, before a resume restore (flow BattleResumeRestoresTheLooks).
clears the scene list head always, and the scene-unit in-use flags and the pool claim bytes +0 only when the load mode (0x142FF9E2C) is not 1: a resumed battle keeps the restored pool records.

notes: Structures: SceneUnitSlot, LookPoolRecord. The name is ours (IDB: sub_14026F5CC).

name: LookQueue_Add
proto: void LookQueue_Add(char a, char b, char c, int16_t d, int16_t sprite, int16_t palette, int16_t slotRequest, void *unit, int flag)
purpose: Appends one entry to the 16-entry look load queue that CharaPalette_ReloadForShape later turns into scene units.

behavior.text: writes the nine arguments into the entry at the current count (entry n is at 0x141856720 + 8 + 32 * n; the count is the dword at 0x141856720).
the sprite argument is stored as a 16-bit word at entry +6; a signed value of 170 (0xAA) or more is replaced by 1 right after (the compare at 0x140304207).
the count is increased only while it is below 16, so the 17th call overwrites entry 16 and the count stays 16.

behavior.basis: (unicorn, pristine exe, empty queue; the values are arguments fed in, not constants of the code)
behavior.text: the stored word for the sprite argument 0, 1, 169 is itself; 170, 200, 254, 255, 256 and 0x7FFF become 1; 0x8000 and 0xFFFF stay (the compare is signed).

behavior.basis: (unicorn, Unit_ResolvePreviewShape for every marker x job)
behavior.text: 10,320 of the 65,536 pairs give a shape of 170 or more (Unit_ResolvePreviewShape's markers above 0x82 with jobs from 130, its markers 0x80 / 0x81 with jobs below 43; no generic job 74..93), so the clamp is reachable by stock data.

notes:
Structure: LookQueueEntry. The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403041A4). The clamp at 0x140304207 is a ceiling: the queue feeds the battle's byte-wide stores.

The function is a leaf: at the point after the clamp's store (0x140304222) the sprite argument is at rsp+0x28 and the unit pointer at rsp+0x40, r10 = &g_LookQueueCount and rcx the entry index.
open_questions: ? whether any caller can queue more than 16 entries.

name: LoreDictionary_BuildList
proto: void LoreDictionary_BuildList(int category, void *out, int unused, int mode)
callers: sub_1401703C0 (list refresh: mode = glossary +3488 + 4 * tab, category = dword_14070E768[tab]), sub_1401705E0 and sub_1401E4B24 (mode 1, all)
purpose: Builds the glossary list of one category.

purpose: Returns the second key of the glossary row shown for an entry and page.
