name: MainTab_BindNodes
callers: JobTree_RefreshAddon and sixteen other screen builders
purpose: Finds the header (MainTab/Tab) nodes of a screen and keeps them in the controller: the tab, the TextMask mask node, the title text node and the other tab title boards.

behavior.text: ctl[2] = descendant 'Tab' of 'MainTab' under the screen root; ctl[3] = the 'MaskNode00' (kind 9) found through 'TextMask' inside the tab; ctl[4] = the 'Title' part (kind 3, a text node) of the mask node's embedded component (the TextBoard01 component: one Title text node 60 x 120, plus a TextBoard02 reference at x 96).
ctl[5..7] = the 'Title' text nodes of the chained boards 'TextBoard02' .. 'TextBoard04' (each board references the next at x 96); ctl[8] = the 'MainTab' node.

notes: JobTree_RefreshAddon calls it with the 'JobTree' node, then MainTab_SelectTab(ctl, 1), then writes text id 3885 into ctl[4] (+248; the byte +316 = 1 marks it dirty). UI-en row 3885 is 'Job Tree'. Live read (2026-10-28): the Title node is kind 3, size (60,120), pivot (30,60), text id +248 = 0xF2D = 3885.
open_questions: How the kind 9 mask node draws the TextBoard01 text through the TextMask/Rect00 gradient: GUINode_DrawChildren has no draw for kind 9, so the masking happens elsewhere.

name: MainTab_SelectTab
callers: JobTree_RefreshAddon (index 1) and the other screen builders
purpose: Plays the header state that belongs to tab `index` and stops the other three.

behavior.text: the four states are 'Hide02', 'Hide03', 'Hide04', 'Show04' for index 1..4; the selected one gets +104 = 1 and GUINode_PlayState, the others GUINode_StopState.

notes: The Job Tree plays 'Hide02' (only its own title board shows).
open_questions: What the states change on the boards (not read from the file yet).

name: Map_LoadBattleData
purpose: Loads the per-map data of a battle map: its Move-Find row, its draw-index lists and its 4096-byte map block.

behavior.text: copies the map's 24-byte Move-Find row (0x140783840) into the live copy (0x140D8DC90).
clears the 3000-byte block buffer (0x14114A4F0) and takes the block's file sector from the language-0 or other-language per-map table (0x1407B6F30 / 0x1407B7130); a sector of 0 returns null.
calls MapDrawLists_Load unless a flag is set, records the map id and reads 4096 bytes from the sector.

name: MapAnim_Load
proto: int MapAnim_Load(void *animSet, unsigned mapId, int source)
purpose: Reads the map's anim file when the RefinedBgAnim rows ask for one.

behavior.text: returns 1 without a read when the anim set is already loaded or MapAnim_ReadRows answers 0; no row answers 1, so the file is requested.

the path is the map id in three digits inside the anims folder; a missing file or a failed read returns 1 quietly; the header's tag and its dword at +8 must equal the map id (seen in the stock files), else the buffer is freed.
on success sets the table pointers (32-byte header, then the 1,040-byte block) and runs two precompute steps.

name: MapAnim_ReadRows
purpose: Copies the RefinedBgAnim rows of a map into the anim set's per-entry table; returns 0 when any row's kind is 0.

behavior.text: no table or no row of the map: returns 1 (anim wanted); otherwise for each row of the map's set stores kind (+4) and the byte at +8; a row whose kind is 0 returns 0 at once (no anim file).
map 5's only row has kind 0 and the pack holds no anim file for map 5; the other maps with a mesh and a non-zero kind have one.

name: MapBlock_ApplyLayerCommand
callees: MapRow_SelectVariation, MapRenderer_ApplyMapRow, MapMesh_Load, MapRenderer_ReuseLoadedMesh, MapTextures_Reset, MapTextures_LoadSystemSlots, MapTextures_LoadMapSlots, MapAnim_Load
purpose: Applies one layer's records of the loaded map block to the draw tables and, for layer 0 in the enhanced graphics mode, starts the map mesh, texture and anim loads.

behavior.text: reads the map block's u16 token stream and fills one 0xA8-byte layer record; writes 0x79 to the word after the battle tile table.
copies the layer's tile and polygon records from the block into the global draw tables; this part does not read any renderer data table.

reads scene variables 39 (the story event number), 48 (map state), 36 (night) and 35 (weather level) and calls MapRow_SelectVariation with the map id on every call (any layer); the chosen index and kind code are stored in the global work record at +116 and +120 (MapBlock_RunCommand reads the index from there).

for layer 0 with the graphics-mode flag non-zero: MapRenderer_ApplyMapRow, a second read of the Map row's chosen variation element, then MapMesh_Load (given scene variables 48 and 34, the index and the kind) when the mesh set's loaded-id field is -1, else MapRenderer_ReuseLoadedMesh.
from the chosen element, its floats at +0x30 and +0x34 are stored into the battle control block at +689068 and +689072, and (value * 12 - 36) * 4096 as integers at +689084 and +689088.
no code reading those four battle control fields was found (the constructor clears them; BattleControl_FrameUpdate works near +689100 only).

a mesh load that returns 0 is followed by MapTextures_Reset, the id fields of the texture set, MapTextures_LoadSystemSlots, MapTextures_LoadMapSlots and MapAnim_Load; any other result skips all of them (the result is tested right after the call).
ids 15 and 33 skip the texture steps as well; id 53 sets one extra node bit; ids 6, 62 and 92 adjust single stock tile records.

open_questions: ?: the meaning of the block's record fields beyond the ones copied; who reads the four battle control fields written from the element's +0x30 and +0x34.

name: MapBlock_RunCommand
proto: char MapBlock_RunCommand(unsigned char opcode, unsigned char *record)
callers: sub_1402514E0, sub_1402516BC (the map load task, which first reads the block with Map_LoadBattleData)
purpose: Runs one command record of the loaded map block (layers, camera, palettes, lights) and dispatches the layer commands to MapBlock_ApplyLayerCommand.

behavior.text: it is the map setup task: its scene-task-26 branch calls the tile-table builder with the level's map record, and the nine 0xA8-byte layer records (slots 0 and 2..8; slot 1 is a runtime index) are the ones the battle snapshot captures.
opcodes 0x24..0x2B call MapBlock_ApplyLayerCommand for layers 1..8; the base layer's command calls it with layer 0.
with the graphics-mode flag at 0, the base layer's command also starts the classic texture load keyed by the loaded map id.
a palette command compares the current map id with 26 and 127 and takes fixed values for those two.

command 50 (0x32, reached by the running subtraction 44, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2 of the compare chain, so no immediate 0x32 appears; the chain after 44 sends 46..48 to the sub-command loop, 50 to the light block and 51 to sub_1402F7594): the light block. It reads nine 16-bit light colour values from record +0 (each clamped to 0x2000), three light vectors from record +18 (a dword and a word each), hands them to sub_140249F58, and passes the ambient colour bytes of record +36, +37 and +38 to sub_14024A068 (map id 26 takes the fixed ambient values 48 / 34 / 36 and id 127 takes 128 / 128 / 128 instead).

the same block then reads the chosen variation element of the map's Map row (index from the global work record +116, taken only when below the element count) and lets its six int16 members at +0x38..+0x42 override the two background colour triples: bytes 0..2 and 4..6 of qword_14114A4E8 take the member's value, or, when the member is above 255, the byte of the command record at +39..+41 and +42..+44. The result is copied to qword_142FF9DA8, qword_142FF86A8 and qword_142FF8498 (see MapBackgroundColourPairOverride).
other writers of the pair exist (sub_1402F52D8 and ClutManager_Update); sub_14024A6E8 puts it into the vertex colours.

open_questions: ?: the command list and operand meanings (the light block's layout is read; the other commands are not).

name: MapDrawLists_Load
purpose: Fills the two map draw-index bitsets from the per-map index lists of the current battle map.

behavior.text: clears both bitsets, finds the map's record by linear search over 50 records of the map draw-index table (0x140672780) and sets one bit per listed index (lists end with 0xFFFF).
a map without a record leaves both bitsets empty.

open_questions: ?: what the two map draw passes do with a marked record.

name: MapMesh_ApplyPolygonRows
purpose: Rebuilds the per-polygon override arrays from the RefinedBgMeshPolygon rows of the loaded map whenever the battle state value or the loaded map changed.

behavior.text: runs from CharaRenderer_Update only while the mesh set holds a map id; the state value is the battle state's value in states 52, 58 and 59, else -1.

clears the override arrays, takes the whole row set of the map, and for each row follows its condition id into RefinedBgMeshPolygonCond; a row whose condition does not apply, or whose condition row is absent, writes nothing; an applying row writes its 16-bit value into the array chosen by its kind code at its index of its layer.

open_questions: ?: what each kind code's array does to the drawing.

name: MapMesh_FindNodeRows
proto: unsigned MapMesh_FindNodeRows(NodeRowSpan *out, unsigned mapId, unsigned variation)
purpose: Finds the RefinedBgMeshNode rows of one map and variation: a pointer to the first row and the row count (0, 0 when there are none).

behavior.text: reads the table by id 153 (cached); needs a triple-keyed table; searches the file's set index for the map, then the child set for the variation, then the first row through the three keys.

name: MapMesh_InitNodeFlags
purpose: Sets the 32 node slots of the mesh set to their start flags from the node rows, marks the nodes the mesh references, and applies the per-map stock offsets.

behavior.text: every slot starts with two flag bits set and no invisibility values; slot k takes the k-th node row (by position): start-visible bit from +20, two flag bits from +23 and +24, and the two 16-bit values of the RefinedBgMeshNodeInvisType row named by +16.
every node index below 32 found in the mesh's per-layer index arrays is marked used; a used node with no row gets the visible bit set.
the last loop stores MapMesh_StockNodeOffset's answer per node.

name: MapMesh_Load
proto: int MapMesh_Load(void *meshSet, unsigned mapId, int sceneVar48, int sceneVar34, int variation, int kind)
purpose: Reads the map's mesh file into the mesh set and sets up its node rows; 0 = built, 1 = nothing built.

behavior.text: ids 15 and 33 return 1 at once. The path is the map id in three digits inside the meshes folder (lower-cased); the open, the size and the read go through the resource manager and each failure returns 1 with no message.

a size over 7,534,452 bytes returns 1; the 48-byte header must carry the format tag and, at +8, the requested map id, else the buffer is freed and 1 is returned (seen in the instructions and in the headers of three stock files); +12 is the layer count (1 in those files).
per layer the tile-index, height and polygon arrays are copied in; for stock maps up to id 116 MapMesh_StockNodeOffset shifts node positions.

stores the map id in the mesh set, reads the node rows with MapMesh_FindNodeRows (variation key when the kind code is 0, else 0; a second try with key 0), then MapMesh_InitNodeFlags and the node ordering; returns 0.

open_questions: ?: what the texture manager does when a requested texture file is missing.

name: MapMesh_Reset
purpose: Clears the mesh set: node arrays, layer data and counts.

behavior.text: clears the large arrays, refills the per-layer index blocks with 0xFF, sets the layer count and node state to 0; the loaded-id field is set to its none value by the caller.

name: MapMesh_StockNodeOffset
proto: int MapMesh_StockNodeOffset(int mapId, int node, float *x, float *y, float *z)
purpose: A hard-coded list of position offsets for single nodes of nine stock maps; 0 for every other map and node.

behavior.text: ids above 116 return 0 at once (the stock renderer tables end at 116); for the listed maps and nodes it returns a kind number and fills the three offsets.

name: MapRenderer_ApplyMapRow
proto: void MapRenderer_ApplyMapRow(void *renderer, unsigned mapId, int variation, int kind)
purpose: Tears down a mesh set that belongs to another map or variation, then applies the chosen variation of the map's Map row to the renderer's post-effect settings.

behavior.text: when the mesh set holds an id and it differs from the requested one, or the kind code is non-zero, or the texture set was built for another variation: the mesh and texture sets are reset (MapTextures_Reset, MapMesh_Reset) and the loaded-id field set to -1.
the Map row of the id is read with the generic row lookup; a missing row ends the function with nothing applied.

the variation element at index `variation` (row + variations offset + 72 * index) feeds MapRenderer_ApplyVariationEffects with its post-effect keys at +0x14 (glare), +0x18 (LUT), +0x1C (depth LUT) and +0x28 (depth of field); those four offsets are read in the callee as dword indices 5, 6, 7 and 10, so they do not appear in this body.

the element's byte +0x45 is stored as a dword into the mesh set at +6070656; byte +0x46 into the renderer sub-object at +1097 (lut_row_offset); +0x47 == 0 into the renderer byte +147905 (with +147904 set to 1).
element +0x2C non-zero: EffectNxd_DepthBiasFloat (DepthBias row, key = the member) replaces the renderer's depth bias at +147840.

element float +0x20 is stored in dword_1407DC6DC; the effect scale limits are max(1.0, dword_1407DC6E0, +0x20, dword_1407DC6E4) times dword_142E7FAF8, stored times 4096 in dword_1407DC4F8 and times 2048 in dword_1407DC6C8 (the same formula as EffectNxd_LoadRow).

open_questions: ?: what the two derived scale globals and the +0x45 / +0x47 flags drive in the drawn picture.

name: MapRenderer_ApplyVariationEffects
purpose: Loads the four post-effect rows that a Map variation element names (glare, colour lookup, depth lookup, depth of field) into the renderer sub-object.

behavior.text: the first argument is the sub-object that MapRenderer_ApplyMapRow passes (renderer + 148512), the second the 72-byte variation element.
stores element +0x28 (post_effect_dof) at sub +4320, +0x14 (post_effect_glare) at +4324, +0x18 (post_effect_lut) at +4332 and +0x1C (post_effect_depth_lut) at +4328, and clears byte +4295.

calls sub_1400D1AB8 with the depth-of-field key (it loads a PostEffectDOF row, table 227, through sub_1400D1F54), EventCharaSprite_SetTable256Entry with the glare key (PostEffectGlare, table 256), sub_1400D24CC with the colour lookup key (PostEffectLUT, table 285) and sub_1400CE9FC with the depth lookup key (PostEffectDepthLUT, table 284).

after the LUT and depth LUT loads it copies the freshly loaded lookup values over the sub-object's current-value copies (the LUT block at +4232 from +4256 / +4264, the depth LUT block at +4128 from +4192 / +4208) and sets one word of each block to -1.0 (+4272 and +4228).
the copy and the -1.0 words make the new rows take effect at once, without a fade (the words look like a no-fade-running marker).

notes: Each key is the row key of its table; the value 0 is a valid key (the rows are looked up by key like any other).
open_questions: ? the contents of the four row types as used by the picture (only their loads were read).

name: MapRenderer_ReuseLoadedMesh
purpose: Re-runs the node setup of an already loaded mesh set (a second battle on the same map).

behavior.text: with the mesh set's id at none it re-initialises the nodes; for id 64 it also sets one flag bit on three nodes; then it reapplies the anim set's table when the anim is loaded.

name: MapResource_Read
purpose: Reads one resource file of the current battle map, using the per-map file list when the request carries the marker id.

behavior.text: does nothing when the request's flag byte (+13) is 0.

when the request's sector field holds the marker value, the sector and size come from pair n of the current map's file list (0x140685050 for language 0, 0x140685450 otherwise); otherwise the request's own sector and size are used.
reads only when the size is not 0 and a destination is given.

name: MapRow_SelectVariation
proto: void MapRow_SelectVariation(int *variation, int *kind, int mapId, int sceneVar35, int sceneVar36, int sceneVar48, int sceneVar39)
purpose: Chooses which variation struct of a map's Map row applies now, and a kind code, from four scene variables.

behavior.text: both outputs start at 0; no Map row, or a map id of 0 or less, returns with them at 0.

the variation structs (72 bytes) are tried from the last to the first (index 0 is the fallback); a struct matches when its selector fields equal the scene values or hold the wildcard (2, 5, -1), its fixed field is 0 and, when it names a condition row, the condition accepts the scene value; one more field may name a user situation that must hold.

the arguments after the map id are the weather level (scene variable 35), the night flag (variable 36), the map state (variable 48) and the story event number (variable 39), as MapBlock_ApplyLayerCommand reads them.

story branch (g_BattleModeFlag is not 1): the elements are tried from the count minus 1 down to 1; element 0 is never tested and is the result when none matches (index 0, kind 0). An element is accepted when +0x10 is 0, +0 is 2 or the night flag, +4 is 5 or the weather level, +8 is -1 or the map state, and either +0xC is 0 or the MapVariationEvent row of that key exists and its event (+8) or one of its more_events equals the event number (a missing row rejects the element), and either +0x24 is 0 or UserSituation_IsMet accepts it.

random-battle branch (g_BattleModeFlag is 1): the kind wanted is 1 / 2 / 3 by day and 4 / 5 / 6 at night (night flag non-zero), for weather level 0 or 5 and above / 1..2 / 3..4; the last element (count minus 1 down to 1) whose +0x10 equals the wanted kind is chosen (index 0 when none), and the wanted kind is returned as the kind code either way. None of the other selectors is tested in this branch.
the table MapVariationEvent is fetched here and nowhere else; MapVariationRandomBattle is never fetched.

open_questions: ?: what the loaders do with the kind code (which texture and lighting set they pick).

name: MapTextures_LoadMapSlots
purpose: Requests the map's colour and lighting textures from the RefinedBgTexture rows, deduplicating equal names.

behavior.text: the whole row read is conditional on the set's map id being 127 or less (unsigned compare of the id field with 0x7F) and the texture-source field being 0; otherwise the slot count is 0 and nothing is requested.

slot count = children of the map's set; for each slot two variant codes (MapTextures_SlotVariantCode), then 201 frame indices; each name from MapTextures_NameOfFrame becomes a path of the map id in three digits and the name; a name seen earlier in the same frame column reuses its handle.

name: MapTextures_LoadSystemSlots
purpose: Requests the 8 system textures of the map: names from RefinedBgSystemTexture, default colour table when there is none.

behavior.text: for slot 0..7 reads leaf n of the child (map id, 0) of table 141; the name comes from the array chosen by the kind code or the variation; the path is the map id in three digits as a folder plus the name and .tga.
no row, an empty array or an empty first character uses the stock default colour table file; there is no bound on the map id here.

open_questions: ?: the texture manager's answer to a missing file.

name: MapTextures_NameOfFrame
proto: const char *MapTextures_NameOfFrame(void *textureSet, int slot, int frame, int source)
purpose: Builds the file name of one frame of one slot of the map's textures; null when there is none.

behavior.text: slot must be below 21; frame 0 and 1 are the colour and lighting names (type 0 and 1), frame 2 type 2, frames 3..101 further colour frames, 102 up further lighting frames; a source other than 0 gives null.

the table row (map id, slot, type) is read; the name comes from the primary array at the variation index or, when a kind code is set, from the second array at the kind index; a frame above 0 replaces the name's trailing 0 with the frame number; the name must end in .tga after the copy.

name: MapTextures_Reset
purpose: Releases every map and system texture of the texture set and sets its id fields to none.

behavior.text: for 21 slots x 201 frames releases the texture handle unless it is a shared copy; releases the 8 system handles; the map id, texture-source and variation fields become -1 or 0.

name: MapTextures_SlotVariantCode
proto: int MapTextures_SlotVariantCode(void *textureSet, int slot, int type)
purpose: Returns the per-variation integer of a texture row minus one (0 when the entry is 0 or the row is absent).

behavior.text: reads the row (map id, slot, type) and the integer array at the variation or kind index; only when the texture-source field is 0.

name: MapTitle_SetFromMapId
purpose: Writes the title text of a map into the window's map-title label from the map id's Map row.

behavior.text: fetches the Map row (table 60, cache qword_143CD9FA0) of the id.
takes the text of the PlaceName key in row +0x8 (place_name) through PlaceName_GetText and the row byte +0x1C (title_ja_state) and hands both to MapTitleLabel_SetText.
the Map row's place_name_2 and place_name_3 are not read here (the save list reads them).

open_questions: ? which screen's window it fills (only the caller sub_1401EF0D8 was noted).

name: MapTitleLabel_SetText
proto: char MapTitleLabel_SetText(void *window, unsigned textId, __int64 arg3, const char *text, char jaState)
callees: GUINode_FindDescendant, GUINode_FindPartByName, GUIWidget_FindComponentCached, GUITextNode_SetString, GUITextNode_SetTextById, GUINode_StopState, GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState
purpose: Fills the 'Text' and 'Text00' nodes of the 'TextMapGrade' label of a window and plays its 'En' or 'Ja' state.

behavior.text: acts only when the window's node tree exists: finds the node 'TextMapGrade', its part 'MaskNode00' (a node of kind 9), the component it names, and in it the text parts 'Text' and 'Text00' (kind 3).
each text part gets the passed string when it is non-null, else the text of the id (GUITextNode_SetTextById).

state choice: when the language record is missing, or its language id (record +8) is not 0, 4, 5 or 6, or the flag argument is 0, the 'Ja' state is stopped and 'En' is played; otherwise 'En' is stopped and 'Ja' played.
the state found is marked (byte +104 set to 1) and played.

notes: With the Map row's title_ja_state at 0 (the ten closing-title rows, M) the label plays 'En' in every language; with 1 (the other 119 rows) it plays 'Ja' for the language ids 0, 4, 5 and 6.
open_questions: ? which language names the ids 0, 4, 5 and 6 stand for, and what the two states look like.

name: Matrix2x3_Invert
purpose: Inverts a 2x3 affine matrix (1/det with det = m0*m3 - m1*m2).

behavior.text: no check for det = 0.

name: Matrix2x3_Multiply
proto: float *Matrix2x3_Multiply(float out[6], const float a[6], const float b[6])
callers: UI hit test and render paths
purpose: Concatenates two 2x3 affine matrices (a applied first, then b); the UI's node and layer transforms use this layout [m0 m1 m2 m3 tx ty].

behavior.text: out0 = b0*a0 + b2*a1, out1 = a0*b1 + a1*b3, out2 = b0*a2 + b2*a3, out3 = a2*b1 + a3*b3, out4 = a4*b0 + a5*b2 + b4, out5 = a4*b1 + a5*b3 + b5.

name: Matrix2x3_Rotate
proto: float *Matrix2x3_Rotate(float out[6], const float m[6], float angle)
purpose: Rotates a 2x3 matrix by angle radians (single-precision sinf / cosf), applied AFTER m.

behavior.text: s = sinf(a), c = cosf(a); out0 = m0*c - m1*s; out1 = m0*s + m1*c; out2 = m2*c - m3*s; out3 = m2*s + m3*c; out4 = m4*c - m5*s; out5 = m4*s + m5*c (in this operand order; all inputs read before any output is written, so out may alias m).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D83FC). With the point convention x' = m0*x + m2*y + m4, y' = m1*x + m3*y + m5 this rotates points by +angle in the usual maths sense, i.e. clockwise on the y-down screen.

name: Mem_Alloc
callers: hundreds of call sites (every engine allocation), among them NxdTable_CreateHandle and NxdTable_BindRows
purpose: The engine's allocation entry: asks the heap object for `size` bytes with at least 8-byte alignment.

behavior.text: size 0 returns the constant 32 (no allocation).
alignment = max(align, 8); calls heap->vtable[6] (offset 48)(heap, size, alignment, &zero).

notes: A buffer allocated with it from the handle's own heap is found by the engine's later Mem_Free of that buffer.

name: Mem_CopyChecked
proto: void Mem_CopyChecked(void *dst, size_t dstSize, const void *src, size_t count)
callers: 127 call sites in 51 functions, among them sub_140281488, BattleAction_BuildReaction, BattleAction_ReleaseCharged, Battle_ExecuteSecondaryAction, BTurn_PreviewAction, Battle_ResolveAction, EventScript_LoadIntoBuffer, sub_1400C7F54 (IDA code references)
purpose: The game's checked copy: copies the smaller of the destination size and the count, and reports a destination too small or a null pointer; every copy of the 20-byte action block (unit +0x1A0) and of the formula block's record copies goes through it.

behavior.text: n = min(count, dstSize); with n zero nothing is copied. With a null destination it stores errno 22 and calls _invalid_parameter_noinfo.

with both pointers set it calls memmove(dst, src, n); with a null source it clears the destination (memset to dstSize), stores errno 22 and calls _invalid_parameter_noinfo. The errno 34 (range) branch tests dstSize >= n, which min() always satisfies, so it cannot run (I: the compiler kept the C runtime's own code).
when dstSize is smaller than count it calls sub_140026BD4 (a report helper, arguments: a string, dstSize, a constant, 2) after the copy.
127 call sites in 51 functions (IDA code references, 2026-11-12): the event script loader, the file command readers, the unit record copies and the battle action code.

the battle action block at unit +0x1A0 (0x14 bytes: +1 command byte, +2 ability id u16) is never copied by a move instruction: every copy of it (the request queue, the reaction and charge saves, the secondary action, the preview, the AI current action) calls this function with size 0x14 (the size, the block offsets +0x24 and unit offset +0x1A0 are the callers' arguments, never operands of this body). Battle_ResolveAction also uses it for the 0x14-byte ability record copy at g_FormulaBlock +0x24, the 8-byte weapon record at +0x38 and the 6-byte inflict record at +0x40.

notes: Read 2026-11-12. 175 bytes, read whole. The name is the C runtime's (the shape and the two errno values, 22 invalid argument and 34 range, are Mem_CopyChecked's); the extra truncation to the smaller size is the C runtime's own behaviour here.
open_questions: ? what sub_140026BD4 does with its arguments (not read).

name: Mem_Free
callers: hundreds of call sites; ResourceHandle_FreeData frees a handle's file buffer with (p, 0, null)
purpose: The engine's free entry: finds the heap that owns a pointer (or uses the one given) and returns the block to it.

behavior.text: the constant 32 (a zero-size allocation) is ignored.
with a heap given whose flag 0x2000 (dword index 92) is clear, or that claims the pointer through its slot 13, that heap frees it; else sub_140011620(p) finds the owner.
calls owner->vtable[9] (offset 72)(owner, p, size).

name: MemFile_Read
proto: __int64 MemFile_Read(MemFile *f, void *dst, unsigned int offset, unsigned int len)
callers: EventScript_LoadFile, GameData_ReadSectors, EventSprite_LoadTask, EventMapTitle_LoadTexture, sub_1403D2450 and about 20 more
purpose: Copies len bytes at offset from an in-memory file buffer (clamped to its size); returns 0 on success, 1 when the file has no buffer.

behavior.text: obj = *(qword *)(f + 24); 0 returns 1. buf = *(obj + 56), size = *(obj + 64). When offset + len > size then len = size - offset. memmove(dst, buf + offset, len); returns 0.
no check that offset <= size (a larger offset makes len wrap; I: callers are trusted).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D2358). Medium confidence on the 'file' reading; the +24 object may be a streaming buffer object.

name: MessageWindow_OpenMode0
purpose: Opens the legacy unit info message window for the acting unit with level and experience (mode 0).

behavior.text: refreshes the preview buffers (sub_1402DE564), sets a window flag word to 2 (3072 when a flag in the status page word is set) and clears two scene words.
calls the panel window builder with the actor window record, mode 0, the ten-row number table 0x1408E5050 and the actor preview buffer 0x14078DE10.

notes: Read in full.

name: MessageWindow_OpenMode1
purpose: Opens the legacy unit info message window for the acting unit with the hit chance, after a preview of the action (mode 1).

behavior.text: finds the actor and target units (preview unit table, 512 bytes per unit), runs the damage and result calculation sub_140305264 and, when the action is not a plain secondary action, starts it (task function Battle_ExecuteSecondaryAction).
waits two frames, refreshes the preview buffers, clamps the predicted hit points and MP against each unit's maxima and stores them in the window widgets.
finally calls the panel window builder with mode 1, the eight-row number table 0x1408E52D0 and the actor preview buffer.

notes: Read in full; the preview arithmetic is only summarised.
open_questions: ?: what the two stored widget words are.

name: MessageWindow_OpenMode2
purpose: Opens the legacy unit info message window for the target unit with the hit chance (mode 2).

behavior.text: starts task slot 12 (sub_1402BA718) when that slot does not carry tag 19, waits two frames, refreshes the preview buffers and clamps the predicted values against the action result block, writing them into the window widgets.
calls the panel window builder with mode 2, the eight-row number table 0x1408E53D0 and the target preview buffer 0x14078DE70.

notes: Read in full; the clamp arithmetic is only summarised.

name: MessageWindow_OpenMode3
purpose: Opens the legacy unit info message window for the target unit with level and experience (mode 3).

behavior.text: refreshes the preview buffers, sets the same window flag word as mode 0 and calls the panel window builder with mode 3, the ten-row number table 0x1408E5190 and the target preview buffer 0x14078DE70.

notes: Read in full.

name: ModelSkeleton_BuildBoneLinks
purpose: Builds the list of bone links of a loaded model by matching its bone names against the 33 bone name pairs.

behavior.text: the bone count comes from the model's skeleton resource (or its override object at +1168); the list at +1184 is reset to empty and a 35-entry scratch array of 12-byte records (two bone indices, a flag byte) is cleared to all ones (the decompilation shows -1 for each 16-bit field; 0xFFFF as unsigned).

for every bone name of the model, compares it with both names of each of the 33 pairs of BoneLinkPairs; a match stores the bone index in the first or second half of the pair's scratch record and the flag byte, which is set when the bone name contains 'spine'.
when the model's file name contains 'c1001' or 'c1002', the flag byte of two of the scratch records is set as well.
every scratch record with both bone indices found is appended to the model's link list (12 bytes per entry, grown through the model's allocator).

notes: Name is ours. The link list is stored on the model object; its use is not decoded.

name: MoveFind_ApplyTrap
purpose: Applies the trap of a unit's tile to the unit as an action result.

behavior.text: makes the unit the acting unit, resets its action result block (+446) and switches on the trap kind reported by MoveFind_ProbeTile.
kind 0 sets a result flag and a value of 256.
kind 0 is Degenerator (a level loss), by elimination.
kind 1 inflicts status 39 Doom; kind 2 inflicts status 35 Sleep; kind 3 deals damage equal to max HP / 5.
kinds 1, 2 and 3 are Death Trap, Sleeping Gas and Steel Needle (matched by effect).
kinds 4, 5 and 6 also exist here and set one status bit each, but the Move-Find flags only produce kinds 0..3.
those bits are statuses 16 Oil, 24 Poison and 3 Undead, by the status byte order.
a status kind first asks Status_FilterPendingSets; when it refuses, the result becomes a miss.

open_questions: ?: the exact meaning of kind 0's value; whether anything else can start kinds 4..6.

name: MoveFind_ProbeTile
proto: MoveFindResult *MoveFind_ProbeTile(int x, int y, int layer)
purpose: Reports what a battle tile hides: another unit, a Move-Find item not yet taken and a trap kind.

behavior.text: bit 4 of the result: a unit stands on the tile (its slot kept beside the result).
matches the tile against the four hidden tiles of the live Move-Find row (x high nibble, y low nibble, layer bit 7 of the flags).

bit 1: the hidden tile has an item (flag 0x20 clear) whose taken bit is still clear; the taken bits are indexed by scene variable 51 (two maps per byte, four bits per map); the common and rare item ids are copied into the result.
bit 2: the hidden tile has a trap (flag 0x10 clear); flags 0x01 / 0x02 / 0x04 / 0x08 give trap kind 0 / 1 / 2 / 3.
it is the only reader of the loaded Move-Find row (g_MoveFindWorkingRow) and tests exactly the bits 0x80, 0x20, 0x10 and 0x0F of each tile's flag byte; bit 0x40 is read by nothing.

name: MoveFind_TakeItem
purpose: Gives a unit the Move-Find item of its tile: rolls common against rare by Brave and marks the tile taken.

behavior.text: the rare item (+4 of the hidden tile) is taken with a chance of (100 - Brave) percent, the common one (+2) otherwise.
the chance gains 25 points (capped at 100) when a mode global is set, the unit's support bit (+158 bit 0) is set and Job_IsChemistType accepts the unit.
sets the tile's taken bit (scene variable 51 selects the map's four bits).

open_questions: ?: which support ability the +158 bit is.

name: Movie_Start
callees: sub_14027A2B0, sub_1401D6F9C, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_140026D3C, sub_1401D7608, sub_1400EBA64, sub_1400EB90C, sub_1400EBB44, sub_1400EBC38, UIAgent_DetachAddon
purpose: Starts the playback of a movie from its MovieData row: picks the file, the sound banks, the subtitle window and the controller flags.

behavior.text: reads the MovieData row of the movie id (table 65, the only reader of the table).

path = classic_path (+0x18) when non-empty; the language track (+0x20) is then not used and the classic subtitle style is set. Otherwise path (+8), plus the localized_path (+0x20) as a second track when the language is not language 0.
sound_bank (+0x1C) is passed to MovieSound_LoadBank for slots 20, 21 and 22 (bgm, voice, se); a negative value loads nothing.
the link at +0x10 (table id as a 16-bit value, key at +0x14): 192 opens the classic subtitles window (UIClassicSubtitles key), 209 the subtitles window with a half-size flag.
sets the controller flags: 0x20 from pausable (+0x24), 0x10 from skippable (+0x25), 0x08 from skip_on_press (+0x26).
the listeners called at the end get the listener and the movie id only.

notes: Name is ours (it is the name the database carries). The controller flags live at MovieController +24 (GameUIManager +0xE0); Boot_UpdateVideo passes GameUIManager +200 to Movie_Start.
open_questions: ? which screen plays the movies that end on one press.

name: MovieControl_IdleHint
purpose: While a movie plays unpaused, shows the 'Pause' button hint for about 5 seconds after any input.

behavior.text: when sub_1400F12C0 reports input it stores the time at +16 and shows the hint; while +24 is set the hint stays until 5 s (timestamp units / 300000) have passed.
when the shown state changes it calls sub_1400EB65C(9102, -1) on show and sub_1400EB5F4 with the new state, and stores it at +24.
UIButtonGuide row 9102 is one entry, 'Pause' (text 2645, action 95).

name: MovieControl_PausedTick
callees: sub_1400EB7EC, sub_1400F144C, sub_1400F1510, Input_TestAction, sub_14027A2B0, sub_1401D6F9C, sub_1400F4BCC, sub_1400F0E98
purpose: Paused frame of the movie overlay: a completed hold with byte +25 set takes the skip (state 3); the pause or back action resumes.

behavior.text: when byte +25 is non-zero and Input_TestAction(action 0x5D) fires, it closes the overlay, sets +8 = 3, calls sub_1401D6F9C(qword_143CD9DD8, 7, 0) and sub_1400F4BCC(0xBA).
otherwise, on action 0x5F or 0x1B (and the hold not in progress), sets +8 = 0 and calls sub_1401D6F9C(qword_143CD9DD8, 7, 0).

name: MovieControl_TryOpenPause
callees: Input_TestAction, sub_1400F144C, sub_14027A2B0, sub_1400EB65C, sub_1400EB5F4, sub_1401D1E30, sub_1401D6F9C
purpose: Opens the movie pause overlay on the pause action, with or without the Skip hint by MovieControl +25.

behavior.text: returns 0 unless Input_TestAction(action 0x5F) is true.
sets +8 = 2, arms the hold action 0x5D, and passes 502 with mask -1 when byte +25 is set, -3 when not, to sub_1400EB65C.
clears qword_143CD9DD0 + 88 and calls sub_1401D6F9C(qword_143CD9DD8, 7, 1).

notes: Same button guide (502) as the event overlay.

name: MovieController_UpdateSkip
callees: MovieControl_PausedTick, MovieControl_TryOpenPause, MovieControl_IdleHint, sub_14027A2B0, sub_1404BA570, sub_1400EBABC, sub_1400D8B9C, sub_14009D68C
purpose: Per-frame movie pause / skip handling of the GameUI MovieController (a virtual of its second vtable): publishes whether the playing movie can be skipped and runs the MovieControl state machine.

behavior.text: receives the controller pointer + 8; the movie flags are at +16 of that (controller +24) and the result bits at +20 (controller +28).
when flags bit 0x8 is clear and result bit 0 is clear and g_MovieControl (0x143CDA078) is set, it writes MovieControl +25 = (flags & 0x10) != 0 every frame.

only when flags bit 0x20 is set, and g_ShopModeGate (enhanced flag) is non-zero, it steps MovieControl state +8: 0 -> 1; 1 -> MovieControl_TryOpenPause (or MovieControl_IdleHint when that returns 0, when the player at qword_143CD9C28 has +16 == 3, or when a UI dialog node byte +74/+75 is set); 2 -> MovieControl_PausedTick.
when flags bit 0x10 is set, it copies (MovieControl +8 == 3) into result bit 0 (the skip is taken).

notes: Movie_Start sets the flags from the MovieData (NXD 65) row: byte +36 -> 0x20, +37 -> 0x10, +38 -> 0x8. The controller is at *(qword_143CD9DC8) + 0xC8 (Boot_UpdateVideo passes that address to Movie_Start).

name: MovieSound_LoadBank
proto: void MovieSound_LoadBank(void *sound, int slot, int number)
purpose: Loads one sound bank of a movie.

behavior.text: returns at once when the number is negative.
slot 20 / 21 / 22 formats 'sound/movie/movie%04d/movie%04d_bgm.sab' / '_voice.sab' / '_se.sab' with the number and loads that bank.

notes: Name is ours.

name: MsgWindow_BuildFrame
callers: SceneMsgTask_Run and eleven other message tasks
purpose: Sets up the frame primitives of a message window and its decoration cells by window kind and language.

behavior.text: window kinds 0..4 place one cell from a per-language table of five (0x1407B27E8..0x1407B28A8).
kinds 5..9 place four cells from the per-language decoration tables (0x1407B2AD0 language 0, 0x1407B29E0 default, 0x1407B28F0 language 2, 0x1407B2BC0 language 3), starting at (kind - 5) x 4.

notes: Read: the cell selection.

name: Music_StartSceneTracks
purpose: Starts a scene's music: resets the event slots, loads the two tracks into music slots 1 and 2, then starts slot 1.

behavior.text: first calls EventSlots_ResetAll.

for each non-zero track it points the text-command slot pointer at EventSlot_LoadTrack and dispatches a scene callback of kind 2 with (track, slot 1 or 2); EventSlot_LoadTrack stores the track number in dword_142E7FB08[slot].

when track 1 is non-zero it points the slot pointer at MusicSlot_FetchRecord and dispatches a scene callback of kind 3 with (1, 127): music slot 1 starts at volume 127 from the music slot record of the track. Track 2 is only loaded, never started here.
the two arguments come from the scenario setup record bytes +5 and +6 (the caller Scene_StartMusic reads them from the scene words it holds), or from the saved pair in qword_140816CD0 on a resume.

notes: Return value: the last callback result, or the reset result when both tracks are 0.
open_questions: ? what the kind 2 and kind 3 scene callbacks do beyond reaching the two handlers named above.

name: MusicSlot_FetchRecord
callers: EventCmd_ActivateSlotParam and about 18 more event and menu functions
purpose: Activates an event sound slot: loads its sound id and the three record dwords into the music state.

behavior.text: clears the music state (resets it from a default block); a slot of 0 returns 0.
stores slot - 1 as the active slot, loads the sound id of the slot into the music state and copies the three dwords of the sound's record (MusicSlotRecords, stride 12) into words 1..3.
when the slot has an object, remembers it as the current slot object and returns it.

notes: Name is ours.
open_questions: ?: what the two record numbers do in the music loader.

name: NameSlotTable_Lookup
callers: UIRender_CreateBuffers, UIRender_LoadShaders, SDFFontRenderer_CreateResources, FrequentUtilRenderer_CreateResources, CEGL2_SHADER_vfunc_1, CEGL2_SHADER_vfunc_6, CEGL2_SHADER_vfunc_7, sub_1400423E0, sub_1400424DC, sub_140042788, sub_140042874, sub_140042A24, sub_140042B38, sub_140042C68, sub_140042D54, sub_14009C1F8, sub_1400CCCA8, sub_1400CEB4C, sub_1403A33F0, sub_1403A7AD8, sub_1403A7B3C, sub_1403AE954, sub_1403B7C34, sub_1403C55E4, sub_1403CAFD0, sub_1403CC5D4, sub_1403E5B84
callees: EnterCriticalSection, LeaveCriticalSection, strcmp, sub_140025C74 (string assign), std::_Tree_val::_Insert_node
purpose: Turns a shader resource name (constant buffer, texture or sampler) into a small dense slot id, adding the name to the table the first time it is seen.

behavior.text: takes the critical section at table+32 on entry and leaves it on every path (a 40-byte CRITICAL_SECTION occupying +32..+71; the entry array pointer follows at +72).

hashes the NUL-terminated name with a 32-bit FNV hash: start 0x811C9DC5 and, for every byte, hash = (hash * 0x01000193) XOR byte. This multiplies before the xor, which is the FNV-1 order (FNV-1a xors first). The length is found by scanning for the terminator.

the index is an MSVC red-black tree (std::map layout): head node pointer at table+16, node count at table+24, the head's parent link is the root. Node layout (40 bytes, allocated through the allocator object at table+8, virtual slot +16): left link +0, parent +8, right link +16, colour byte +24, nil byte +25, key = the 32-bit hash at +28, slot id (16 bits) at +32.
the search finds the run of nodes whose key equals the hash (the usual lower-bound and upper-bound walks) and visits the run in order, so different names that share a hash get separate nodes.

for each node of the run the candidate name is read from the entry array: entry = (qword at table+72) + 40 * slot. An entry is a 40-byte allocator-aware string object: allocator pointer at +0, inline 16-byte buffer or heap pointer at +8, length at +24, capacity at +32 (the characters are inline when the capacity is below 16). The name is compared with strcmp; on a match the slot id of that node is returned.

when no node matches: slot = the 16-bit count at table+80. When the dword capacity at table+84 is greater than the slot, the name is copied into entry[slot] (sub_140025C74, the string assign), a node {hash, slot} is allocated and linked at the position found by descending from the root (hash >= key goes right, otherwise left; the tree size is checked against 0xFFFFFFFF first), std::_Tree_val::_Insert_node links and rebalances it, the count is incremented and the new slot is returned.
when the table is full (capacity not greater than the count) nothing is inserted and 0xFFFF (-1 as a 16-bit value) is returned.

slot ids are dense and handed out in order of first use (0, 1, 2, ...); the count is never decremented here, so an id never changes. The same name always gives the same id, so every shader module that mentions g_Sampler shares one slot.

there are three tables in the device globals qword_140C696A8: constant buffers at +5056, textures at +5064, samplers at +5072 (the callers load the table pointer from these fields just before the call). UIRender_CreateBuffers resolves cUIRenderRemap, cUIRender and cSDF from the first, tTexture0 from the second, g_Sampler and g_Sampler_tMaskBuffer from the third. 171 call sites were scanned: 168 load the table pointer from one of the three fields right before the call (the other three, in sub_1403A33F0, were not matched).

the slot id is the index into the render context binding arrays: constant-buffer handles at context+328 + 8 * slot, texture handles at +1608 + 8 * slot, sampler words at +5704 + 4 * slot (RenderContext_ResetFrame clears 160, 512 and 64 entries of these arrays).

behavior.basis: (live read 2026-10-30, the sampler table at qword_140C696A8 + 5072, 31 entries)
behavior.text: 0..11 s_none1..s_none12, 12 ccc_ppn_sampler, 13 ccc_lln_sampler, 14 g_Sampler, 15 g_Sampler_tMaskBuffer, 16 ccc_lln_sampler_tMaskBuffer, 17 www_lln_sampler, 18 cwc_lln_sampler, 19 PointSampler, 20 LinearSampler, 21 LinearSampler_esgeTex, 22 LinearSampler_areaTex, 23 LinearSampler_searchTex, 24 LinearSampler_blendTex, 25 www_lll_sampler, 26 www_ppn_sampler, 27..30 sSampler0..sSampler3.

the names follow a code: three address letters (c clamp, w wrap) and three filter letters (l linear, p point, n none; min, mag, mip). For ccc_lln that matches the word 0x26A that the Job Tree technique holds for slots 13 and 16 (clamp on all axes, min / mag linear, mip point; see GUILayer_BlurShadowPass and Sampler_DescFromWord). Basis: the names and that decoded word.
the first twelve entries (s_none1..s_none12) look like placeholder names for unused sampler indices. Basis: the names only.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140089280 until applied). The sampler slot ids index the +5704 words of every render context: slot 14 (g_Sampler) is the one UIRender_ApplyDrawState writes with the UI draw's sampler word and the one the Job Tree shadow pixel shader reads (GUILayer_BlurShadowPass); slot 15 (g_Sampler_tMaskBuffer) is written with the same word. The 31 sampler names were read live from the running game and were not re-read here.
open_questions: ? the capacity stored at table+84 for each of the three tables (the context arrays hold 160 / 512 / 64 entries, probably the same limit, I). ? the contents of the constant-buffer and texture tables (only the sampler table was read live). ? where the entry strings' allocator pointers (entry+0) are set (not in this function).

name: Novel_GetPageText

the only reader of the five Novel tables; row +0 is never read.

name: NovelReader_Open
purpose: Opens the book reader on a book (vtable slot at 0x143D36220).

loads the sound bank 'sound/common/novel.sab' once into the audio object at +1232 and calls sub_1401E2774(+16, 2).

name: NovelReader_SendReadThrough

the achievement class AchievementOtherNovel matches this notification (see AchievementOtherNovel_Match).

name: NovelReader_ShowPage

name: NumberFields_Draw
proto: void NumberFields_Draw(void *buffer, const NumberField *fields, short *pos, int count)
callers: Battle_UnitStatusFillAlt, StatsPanel_Build and seven other panel builders
purpose: Draws a list of number fields (32-byte records) into a staging buffer.
