name: NxdEntries_Search2
proto: NxdEntry *NxdEntries_Search2(NxdEntry *entries, uint64 lo, uint64 hi, uint64 keys)
purpose: Binary search of bound 16-byte entries by (key1, key2), packed as key1 | key2 << 32.

behavior.text: an entry of kind below 2 compares as keys (0, 0); otherwise its pointer's first two dwords are (key1, key2).
order: key1 unsigned first, then key2 unsigned; an equal qword returns the entry, an empty range null.

notes: So the file's flat entry table must be sorted by (key1, key2) for every key to be found.

name: NxdEntries_Search3
proto: NxdEntry *NxdEntries_Search3(NxdEntry *entries, uint64 lo, uint64 hi, const unsigned int keys[3])
purpose: Binary search of bound 16-byte entries by (key1, key2, key3), recursive on the half that can hold the keys.

behavior.text: an entry of kind below 3 is skipped upward; otherwise the three dwords at its pointer are compared with the keys in order (unsigned); all three equal returns the entry.

name: NxdEntry_CopyKeys
proto: bool NxdEntry_CopyKeys(NxdEntry *entry, unsigned int *out, uint64 n)
callers: sub_1400DA5D8, sub_1400DAD58, sub_1400DB384, sub_1400F94DC, sub_14015E0FC (the position of an entry inside its set)
purpose: Copies the first n keys of the row an entry points to (the record's leading dwords); false when the entry's kind has fewer than n keys.

behavior.text: kind = qword 0 without bit 63; kind below n returns false; else out[i] = pointer dword i for i < n (none when out is null or n is 0), true.

name: NxdEntry_GetRow
purpose: Returns the row data an entry points to: the entry's pointer plus the offset its kind names.

behavior.text: kind = entry qword 0 without bit 63; 0 returns null.
kind 1: pointer + dword at pointer +4; kind 2: + dword at +8; other kinds: + dword at +16.

name: NxdHandle_GetHeap
purpose: Slot 14 of the nxd handle vtables: the heap the handle's file buffer is allocated from.

behavior.text: byte +160 = 0 (every nxd and root.nxl handle): sub_14001A29C(qword_140C696D0).
else the heap at qword_140C696D8 + 8, or qword_140C69708 when that is null.
ResourceHandle_ReadData passes it to the reader that fills +56.

name: NxdHandle_OnLoaded
callers: ResourceHandle_LoadNow and the resource system's asynchronous load path (vtable slot 8)
purpose: Slot 8 of the NexResourceHandle and NxlResourceHandle vtables: when the file has been read, calls the handle's load callback with its context and the handle.

behavior.text: returns 0 when the context at +104 is null; else calls the invoker at +96 with (context +104, &callback +112, &h), which calls callback(context, h).
for an nxd table the callback is NxdTable_BindRows(table, h); for root.nxl it is NxdRegistry_LoadRootNxl(registry, h).
ResourceHandle_LoadNow calls it (vtable +64) once the read has reached state 3.
returns 0 when the context (+104) is null, else makes an indirect call to the invoker at handle +96 with (context, &callback at +112, &handle); the invoker is Callback_InvokeWithHandle.

open_questions: ? the thread the asynchronous path calls it on (I: a resource loader thread).

name: NxdHandle_OnReady
purpose: Slot 13 of the nxd handle vtables: calls the second callback pair (+128 invoker, +136 context, +144 function) after the load finished.

behavior.text: returns 0 when the context at +136 is null; else invoker(+136, &+144, &h).
for an nxd table the function is NxdTable_OnReady.

name: NxdRegistry_CreateRootHandle
purpose: The resource-handle factory for root.nxl: a 168-byte NxlResourceHandle (vtable 0x140721580) whose load callback is NxdRegistry_LoadRootNxl.

behavior.text: allocates 168 bytes from the registry's heap (+8), ResourceHandle_Init, flags 0x2000, byte +160 = 0, vtable NxlResourceHandle.
callback pairs: +112 NxdRegistry_LoadRootNxl, +144 sub_1403D3858, both with the registry as context.

notes: Its vtable shares NxdHandle_OnLoaded (slot 8) with the nxd tables' handles.
open_questions: ? what sub_1403D3858 does after the root list loaded.

name: NxdRegistry_Find
callers: UITable_GetRow, UITable_GetRowByKey, Job_IsHiddenFromTree, AbilityAction_BuildWorkingCopy, OverrideEntry_LoadBattleEntries, Party_EggUpkeep, and every other by-id table reader (cached into a per-table global after the first lookup)
purpose: Returns the table object registered under a table id, or null when the id is unknown.

behavior.text: hashes the 4 bytes of the id with the 64-bit FNV-1a hash (offset basis and prime of the standard algorithm) and masks the result with the registry's bucket mask (+112).
each bucket holds a first/last node pair in the bucket array (+88); the bucket is walked until a node whose id (+16) equals the argument is found or the last node is passed.
a node is {+0 next, +8 prev, +16 id, +24 table object}; the table object is returned. A miss returns 0 (the registry's end sentinel at +64 is never returned).
does not trigger loading; callers check the table state (+12) and use the row accessors themselves.

notes: Ids seen at call sites: 19 ui, 39 Ability, 41 JobCommand, 45 Item, 46 Job, 96 OverrideEntryData, 189 GeneralJob, 247 OverrideAbilityActionData, 310 Egg.

name: NxdRegistry_LoadRootNxl
callees: Str_Format, sub_140011750 (allocator), sub_140037CA4, sub_140091124 (file open), sub_1400E1ADC (hash insert)
purpose: Builds the table registry from the root.nxl list: one table object per listed table, keyed by table id, each pointing at its .nxd file. Every nxd table in the game (jobs, abilities, UI, scripted entries) is reachable through the registry this fills.

behavior.text: skips the first 3 bytes of the file (byte-order mark), then walks CR/LF separated lines; any line whose first character is '#' is skipped, which drops the `#NXLT,1` header line.
counts the remaining lines, then allocates one zeroed array of 80-byte table objects (count stored in the registry at +40, array at +32); returns an error code if the allocation fails.

per line, splits on commas: field 1 is the table name, field 2 is the table id (parsed as a number). Only these two fields are read here; the row-count and kind columns are not consumed by this function.
builds the data file name as `<directory>/<name>.nxd`, where the directory comes from the source file info, and asks the file manager to open it with a load callback pair.
fills each table object: +0 owner, +8 id, +12 state = 1 (not yet loaded), +48 file object; then inserts (id -> object) into the registry's hash map.
returns 0 on success.
the table object's row array (+16), row count (+40) and data pointer (+56) are filled later when the file finishes loading, not here.

notes: Table object layout used by the readers: +8 id, +12 state (2 or 3 = usable), +16 row array, +40 row count, +48 file object, +56 nxd data. A live walk of the registry found 246 entries whose ids and row counts match the lines of root.nxl. Localized tables share the id of their base name.

name: NxdSet3_FindChild
callers: NxdTable_GetEntryByKeysIndex3, NxdTable_GetLeafCount3, sub_1400D5934 and the five set-scanning readers
purpose: Finds the child record of a key2 inside one triple-keyed set: binary search over the set's 20-byte children (offset +4 relative to the set record, count +8).

behavior.text: child i at set + int(set +4) + 20 * i, key2 at +0, compared unsigned; middle first, then NxdSet3_SearchChild.
returns the child or null.

notes: A child holds its leaves at +12 (offset relative to the child) / +16 (count); retail children also store the leaf offset at +4 with count 0 at +8.

name: NxdSet3_SearchChild
proto: NxdChild3 *NxdSet3_SearchChild(NxdSet3 *set, uint64 lo, uint64 hi, unsigned int key2)
purpose: The halving loop of NxdSet3_FindChild over a set's children.

behavior.text: as NxdSets_Search3, the records at set + int(set +4).

name: NxdSets_Find2
callers: NxdTable_GetEntryCount, NxdTable_GetEntryByKeyIndex, NxdTable_GetSetEntries, and five readers that scan a set's array themselves (sub_1400DA5D8, sub_1400DAD58, sub_1400DB384, sub_1400F94DC, sub_14015E0FC)
purpose: Finds the set of a key1 in a double-keyed file: binary search over the 12-byte set records the index header at file +32 points to.

behavior.text: sets = (int offset relative to itself, int count); record i at sets + offset + 12 * i; key1 at record +0, compared unsigned.
tests the middle record first, then continues in NxdSets_Search2 on the half that can hold the key; returns the record or null (count 0 or not found).

notes: The callers pass *(table +0x30 handle)->data + 32, so they read the loaded buffer, not the table object.

name: NxdSets_Find3
callers: NxdTable_GetEntryCount, NxdTable_GetEntryByKeyIndex, NxdTable_GetEntryByKeysIndex3, NxdTable_GetLeafCount3, sub_1400D5934 and the five set-scanning readers
purpose: Finds the set of a key1 in a triple-keyed file: the same search over 20-byte set records.

behavior.text: as NxdSets_Find2 with a 20-byte stride; the continuation is NxdSets_Search3.
NxdTable_GetEntryCount also uses it for any table mode other than 1 and 2.

name: NxdSets_Search2
proto: NxdSet2 *NxdSets_Search2(NxdSetTable *sets, uint64 lo, uint64 hi, unsigned int key1)
purpose: The halving loop of NxdSets_Find2 over [lo, hi) of the 12-byte set records.

behavior.text: mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; equal key returns the record; key >= record key continues above mid, else below; an empty range returns null.

name: NxdSets_Search3
proto: NxdSet3 *NxdSets_Search3(NxdSetTable *sets, uint64 lo, uint64 hi, unsigned int key1)
purpose: The halving loop of NxdSets_Find3 over 20-byte set records.

behavior.text: as NxdSets_Search2 with a 20-byte stride.

name: NxdTable_BinarySearchRow
proto: __int64 NxdTable_BinarySearchRow(__int64 entries, unsigned __int64 lo, unsigned __int64 hi, unsigned int id)
purpose: Binary search over an array of 16-byte entries sorted by the first dword of the row each entry points to; returns the entry address or 0.

behavior.text: entry i = entries + 16 * i. An entry is treated as empty when (qword[0] & 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) == 0 and compared as key 0; otherwise the key is the dword at the pointer stored at entry+8. Equal key returns the entry address.
standard half-open halving: mid = lo + ((hi - lo) >> 1); key <= id moves lo to mid + 1, key > id moves hi to mid. Returns 0 when the range is empty.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D4278). Returns the entry, not the row pointer; the caller uses the result as is.
open_questions: ? the high bit of qword[0] (masked out) is probably a flag (deleted / extended entry).

name: NxdTable_BindRows
callers: through a function pointer set by sub_1403D3E64
purpose: Binds a loaded nxd file to its table object: reads the header's layout, row count and the contiguous-keys flag, and builds the 16-byte entry array (kind, row pointer).

behavior.text: header byte 9 = 1 or 2 (single key): mode (+56) = header byte 8, row count (+40) = header dword +36; a non-zero header byte 10 sets +65 (rows by position) and +68 = header dword +12 (the first key).
byte 9 = 3 or 4: count from dword +48; 5 or 6: count from dword +44; other values return error 0x96130006.
mode 1: entry i = (1, rows + 8 * i) with rows at header dword +32; +72 = the last row's key; without the flag the caches at +24 and +32 are freed.
mode 2: entry i = (2, header + dword +44 + 12 * i); other modes: (mode, header + dword +40 + 20 * i).
grows the entry array when the new count is larger.

can run again on a bound table: it reads the header of the handle's buffer (+56), sets the row count (+40) and kind (+56); only when the new count is larger than the old one it frees the entry array (+16, `sub_14041FB00(p, 16)`) and allocates another (`Mem_Alloc(16 * n, table heap +0, 8)`), else it rewrites the entries in place (kind, pointer into the new buffer); for a table without the contiguous-keys flag (header +10 = 0) it frees the lookup arrays +24 / +32 (built again on use).

an item name table bound again on the game thread at the title screen (same keys, a changed file) showed the new name in the Outfitter Buy list and the Inventory list on the next screen, with no crash, also after four rebinds in one session; the weapon power in the Outfitter's detail panel is read from the weapon record when drawn and followed a changed record on the next visit.

notes: Retail files set byte 10 only when the keys are contiguous from the first key (all 188 single-key files checked). A table with a gap must clear it.

name: NxdTable_CreateHandle
callers: NxdRegistry_LoadRootNxl (as the factory of the file-open call)
purpose: The resource-handle factory NxdRegistry_LoadRootNxl passes for every nxd file: creates the 168-byte NexResourceHandle whose callbacks bind the loaded file to the table object.

behavior.text: allocates 168 bytes with Mem_Alloc from the registry's heap (table +0), runs ResourceHandle_Init, sets flags 0x2008 in +92 and byte +160 = 0, and sets the vtable 0x140721600 (NexResourceHandle).
stores two callback pairs, each (invoker sub_1400674E8, context = the table object) followed by (function, 0): +96/+104 with NxdTable_BindRows at +112, and +128/+136 with NxdTable_OnReady at +144.
returns null when the allocation fails.

notes: Slot 8 of this handle's vtable is NxdHandle_OnLoaded; +112 holds NxdTable_BindRows.

name: NxdTable_GetEntryByIndex
callers: NxdTable_GetRowById (the contiguous-keys path), UITable_GetRow and about 45 other readers
purpose: Returns the entry at a row position; null when the position is not below the row count.

behavior.text: mode 1: null when index >= count (+40), else entries (+16) + 16 * index.

mode 2: the index-th SET of the buffer's set table (index below the set count, file +36); a set with a positive count gives its first array record's keys; returns NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys2 of them (the set's first row).

other modes: the index-th triple set, descends to the first child while a record's +8 count is positive, needs a leaf count above 0, and returns NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys2 of the first leaf's (key1, key2) (that child's first leaf).

notes: Item-en with key 300 after 0..260 and the flag kept: key 300 asked position 300 of 262 rows (live read).

name: NxdTable_GetEntryByKeyIndex
proto: NxdEntry *NxdTable_GetEntryByKeyIndex(NxdTable *table, unsigned int key1, int index)
callers: NxdTable_GetRowById (mode 2, index 0), UITable_GetRowByIndex, CharClut_ApplyToPalette, CharaAnim_ReadStep, UIAddonFFTOLauncher_ShowPage and five more
purpose: The index-th row of the set key1 (double keyed), or the first leaf of the index-th child of the set (triple keyed), reached through the file's set index and then the bound entries.

behavior.text: mode 2: set = NxdSets_Find2(file +32, key1); index must be below the set's count (+8); the array record at set + int(set +4) + 12 * index gives (key1, key2); returns NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys2(table, key1, key2).

other modes: set = NxdSets_Find3; index below the child count; walks from that child to its first descendant while a record's +8 count is positive (retail children have 0), needs a leaf count (+16) above 0, and returns NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys2(table, leaf key1, leaf key2) (that is the first leaf of child (key1, key2)).
returns null when a set, index or leaf is missing.

notes: So NxdTable_GetRowById(table, id) of a double-keyed table returns the FIRST row of set id (of a triple-keyed one: the first leaf of child (id, 0), through NxdTable_GetEntryByKeysIndex3). The array record's own row offset (+8) is not read here: the row comes from the bound entries.

name: NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys2
proto: NxdEntry *NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys2(NxdTable *table, unsigned int key1, unsigned int key2)
callers: NxdTable_GetEntryByIndex, NxdTable_GetEntryByKeyIndex, NxdTable_GetSetEntries, OverrideEntry_LoadBattleEntries, EventNode_SetFromTable224 and about 25 more readers
purpose: The row entry of (key1, key2): for a double-keyed table the binary search over the bound entries; for a triple-keyed table the first leaf of child (key1, key2).

behavior.text: mode (table +0x38) 0 or 1 returns null.
mode 2: NxdEntries_Search2(entries +0x10, 0, count +0x28, key1 | key2 << 32): the 16-byte entries bound from the file's flat entry table, sorted by (key1, key2).
other modes: NxdTable_GetEntryByKeysIndex3(table, key1, key2, 0).

notes: UITable_GetRowByKeys wraps it with the registry lookup by table id. A key pair that is not a row returns null.

name: NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys3
proto: NxdEntry *NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys3(NxdTable *table, unsigned int key1, unsigned int key2, unsigned int key3)
callers: NxdTable_GetEntryByKeysIndex3, sub_1400CAA54, sub_1400CACDC, sub_1400D5934, sub_1402FB7C8, sub_140343AF8
purpose: The row entry of (key1, key2, key3) in a triple-keyed table: the binary search over the bound entries.

behavior.text: mode below 3 returns null; else NxdEntries_Search3(entries +0x10, 0, count +0x28, {key1, key2, key3}).

name: NxdTable_GetEntryByKeysIndex3
proto: NxdEntry *NxdTable_GetEntryByKeysIndex3(NxdTable *table, unsigned int key1, unsigned int key2, int index)
callers: NxdTable_GetRowById (mode 3, keys (id, 0), index 0), NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys2 (mode 3, index 0), sub_1400CA47C
purpose: The index-th leaf of child (key1, key2) of a triple-keyed table, through the set index and then the bound entries.

behavior.text: mode below 3 returns null; set = NxdSets_Find3(file +32, key1); child = NxdSet3_FindChild(set, key2); the leaf at child + int(child +12) + 20 * index gives (key1, key2, key3); returns NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys3.
the index is not checked against the leaf count (+16) here.

open_questions: ? whether every caller keeps the index below the leaf count.

name: NxdTable_GetEntryCount
callers: UITable_GetRowCount, UITable_GetRowByIndex, CharClut_ApplyToPalette, sub_1400C795C and about twenty more
purpose: For a double / triple keyed table: the record count of the set key1 (double: its rows; triple: its children), or 0.

behavior.text: mode = *(qword *)(table+56) - 1; mode 0 (value 1) or value 0 returns 0. set table = *(qword *)(*(qword *)(table+48) + 56) + 32 (the loaded buffer's index header). Mode 1 (double keyed) uses NxdSets_Find2 (12-byte sets), other modes NxdSets_Find3 (20-byte sets).
found set: returns the int at set+8 (its count); not found: 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D3A34). The index layouts are the format NxdMultiKeyIndex (V against all 58 multi-key retail files).

name: NxdTable_GetLeafCount3
proto: int NxdTable_GetLeafCount3(NxdTable *table, unsigned int key1, unsigned int key2)
purpose: The number of leaves (key3 rows) of child (key1, key2) of a triple-keyed table, or 0.

behavior.text: mode below 3 returns 0; NxdSets_Find3 then NxdSet3_FindChild; returns the child's +16 count.

name: NxdTable_GetRowById
callers: JobTable_GetRow, AbilityTable_GetRow, ItemTable_GetRow, JobCommandTable_GetRow, Icon_FormatPath, UITable_GetRowByKey, JobTree_FillJobRecords, GuiImage_SetIconById and ~250 more
purpose: The generic row lookup of a loaded Nxd table by id: used by JobTable_GetRow, AbilityTable_GetRow, ItemTable_GetRow, JobCommandTable_GetRow, Icon_FormatPath and over 250 other readers.

behavior.text: mode = *(qword *)(table+56); 0 returns 0. Mode 1: when byte +65 is set and id is in [dword +68, dword +72] the row comes from sub_1403D3BE4; when +65 is clear and the dense cache pointer +24 is 0 the binary search sub_1403D4278(*(table+16), 0, *(table+40), id) runs; with a cache, id in [+68, +72] indexes the cache (*(qword *)(cache + 8 * (id - dword +68))), else 0.
mode 2 calls NxdTable_GetEntryByKeyIndex(table, id, 0) (the first row of set id), any other mode NxdTable_GetEntryByKeysIndex3(table, id, 0, 0) (the first leaf of child (id, 0)).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D3AE8). The mode is the file's header byte 8: 1 single, 2 double, 3 triple keyed (formats NxdSingleKeyHeader, NxdMultiKeyIndex).
open_questions: ? what +65 (range-dense flag) is exactly and who builds the dense cache at +24.

name: NxdTable_GetSetEntries
callers: 22 readers (sub_1400C9DCC, sub_1400CB870, sub_1401004B4, sub_14015E0FC, sub_14016BC30 and others)
purpose: The rows of one set of a double-keyed table as a span of bound entries: (entry of the set's first record, record count).

behavior.text: only mode 2; set = NxdSets_Find2(file +32, key1); out = (NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys2(table, first record's key1, key2), set count); else (null, 0).

its callers walk the span as consecutive 16-byte entries (for example sub_14015E0FC steps entry + 16 * i), so the rows of one set must be consecutive in the bound entries: the file's arrays, concatenated in set order, must equal its flat entry table.

notes: The X6 row overlay rebuilds the index so this stays true after new keys (its tests walk every set of the result).

name: NxdTable_OnReady
purpose: Marks a table usable after its file loaded: state +12 = 2 when the load status (+80 of the handle) is 1, else 3.

behavior.text: writes table +12 = (status != 1) + 2 and returns 0.

notes: NxdRegistry_LoadRootNxl leaves every table at state 1 (not loaded); readers accept 2 or 3.
open_questions: ? what status values other than 1 mean for a usable table (state 3).

name: Opening_LoadMessageSprites
purpose: Loads the opening message textures and selects the language's sprite list for the opening text.

behavior.text: reads two message texture files into the video buffer one after the other, waiting for the upload each time.
selects one of four 12-pointer sprite list sets by the text language (0x1407BEF20 language 0, 0x1407BEFE0 language 3, 0x1407BEF80 language 2, 0x1407BF040 default) and starts the opening text task.

name: OverrideEntry_FillUnitEntry
purpose: Copies one OverrideEntryData row into a 40-byte unit entry of a scripted battle: the fields whose row value is not the 'keep' marker overwrite the entry, and the flag bytes build a bit set.

behavior.text: does nothing unless the unit, flags and row pointers are set; when row byte +0x8D (141) is non-zero it only clears unit byte 0 (no field is copied, *flags is left as it was).
reads the row at +0x08, +0x10..+0x48 (dwords), +0x7C..+0x8A (words), +0x8C..+0x99 (bytes); the largest offset read is +0x99.
the dword +0x10 (column job), when not 0, is stored as one byte into unit +10 (load 0x1401EA6D0, store 0x1401EA6D4): a job id above 255 keeps only its low byte (300 becomes job 44).

the 40-byte unit entry is a spawn record: OverrideEntry_LoadBattleEntries fills the battle's entry block in place, and Battle_PlaceEntryUnits builds battle unit i from entry i through Unit_BuildFromRecord, whose UnitWork_InitFromSpawnRecord copies +10 into C +3 (2026-11-09).
a dword +0x44 that is not 0 is a key of nxd table 218 whose row byte +8 goes to unit +32.

bytes +0x8E..+0x97 and +0x99 set bits 0..10 of *flags; Battle_PlaceEntryUnits stores that flag set at battle unit +504, and bit 2 (the byte at +0x90, column flag_2) is the one BattleObjective_ShowsTarget tests.

the row fields land in the spawn entry as follows: level (+0x7C) -> entry +3, brave (+0x82) -> +6, faith (+0x84) -> +7, from_guest_record (+0x98) -> bit 3 of entry +1 (build the unit from the guest save record 50..53 with the same marker), head / body / accessory / right_hand / left_hand (+0x2C, +0x30, +0x34, +0x38, +0x3C) -> entry +18..+22 as one byte each, presence (+0x48) -> bits 0xC0 of entry +24.

each item dword is stored as one byte, so a pre-placed unit cannot start with an item id above 255 (the same one-byte limit as the job); 0xFF in the entry means an empty slot and 0xFE a default pick (markers compared by the consumer UnitWork_ApplyStartingEquipment, not by this function).
the name key (+0x0C, column chara_name) is not copied here; Unit_ApplySpawnRecord and UnitWork_SetNameKey read it from the row directly.

notes: The OverrideEntryData rows are 156 bytes apart in the retail file; the last column, Unknown9C (+0x9C), is therefore the next row's first byte, which this reader never reads. X6 locks that column on stock rows.
open_questions: ? the meaning of the copied fields not listed above.

name: OverrideEntry_LoadBattleEntries
proto: void OverrideEntry_LoadBattleEntries(unsigned int key, uint8_t *entries, int *extra, const char **rows)
callees: sub_1403D325C, sub_1403D3B5C (row by two keys), sub_1403D2FD8, OverrideEntry_FillUnitEntry
purpose: Fetches the 16 pre-placed unit entries of one scripted battle from OverrideEntryData (nxd table 96) and converts each row into a 40-byte unit entry.

behavior.text: looks up nxd table 96 (cached in a global after the first lookup).
for index 0..15 asks the table for the row with the pair (key, index); the lookup is by two keys, not by row position.
when a row exists, stores its pointer in the caller's row array and calls sub_1401EA638 to fill the 40-byte entry for that index; absent rows leave the entry untouched.
advances the output entry pointer by 40 bytes and the second output by 4 bytes per index.

its caller Battle_BuildEntryUnits passes the battle's entry block itself (Battle_GetEntryBlock), so the rows overwrite the loaded entries in place, and hands the row array on to Battle_PlaceEntryUnits, which gives row i to Unit_BuildFromRecord as its fifth argument for battle unit i.

notes: The table holds 516 rows in the shipped data, which is 16 slots for each scripted battle. Battle_BuildEntryUnits tests the dword at 0x1407D453C.
open_questions: Whether the script runner calls this path as well; only Battle_BuildEntryUnits appears as a direct caller.

name: Pack_MountList
purpose: Mounts the game's twelve stock data packs, by leaf name, through the one-pack mount call.

behavior.text: builds twelve leaf names, 0000.pac through 0011.pac, and calls the single-pack mount for each.
stops at the first negative result and returns that result; returns zero when all twelve mount.
has one direct call site, in the startup function that also sets up the data directory.
the twelve packs are the game's base data set; the numbering matches the retail pack folder.

notes:
- V: whole body read (220 bytes).
- V: the name is the research name; the database label is the plain sub_ form.
open_questions: - ?: what the manager's negative result means at startup beyond a failed mount.

name: Pack_MountOne
callers: Pack_MountList, one further site in sub_140092A04's neighbourhood
callees: sub_140037CA4 (name hash), sub_140093108 (registry tree), Resource_AcquireHandle (reader open)
purpose: Finds or creates the registry entry for one pack leaf name and opens the pack behind it.

behavior.text: hashes the leaf name, then uses the hash's low nine bits as a bucket index in the manager's pack table.
looks the name up in a per-bucket tree; equal hashes are resolved by a byte-wise name comparison.
takes the leaf name only, not a directory path.
an already-present entry is returned as-is under the manager lock; the pack is not reopened.
a failed open reports error code 0x96080010; the tail also holds a "list too long" message for a full list.
the same bucket mask and tree serve the file registry, so both pack names and file names share 512 buckets.
two direct call sites.

notes: - V: head and main body read; the tail after the open was not read.
open_questions: - ?: the exact lifetime of the old handle when a name is mounted twice.

name: PackedBlock766_Load
callers: sub_140247E8C, EventCmd_SetRecordOffset, sub_14033EC0C, sub_140344B68, sub_14036FD50, sub_140371CAC, sub_140374484
purpose: Starts loading one block of packed data file 766 into the shared block buffer.

behavior.text: does nothing when the block is already the current one.

waits for any read in progress, then takes start = table[index] and length = table[index + 1] - table[index] from the sector table at 0x140684CD0 and starts the read (length in 2048-byte sectors) into the block buffer.

notes: Read in full (one small function).

name: PackedBlock767_Load
purpose: Starts loading one block of packed data file 767 into its block buffer.

behavior.text: does nothing when the block is already the current one; sets the buffer pointer first.
waits for any read in progress, then (for indexes below 114) takes start = table[index] and length = table[index + 1] - table[index] sectors from the table at 0x1408FA200 and starts the read.

notes: Read in full (one small function).

name: PackEntry_Inflate
purpose: Reads one pack entry: a 16-byte header, then either stored bytes or a zlib stream.

behavior.text: header +4 bit 1 set = zlib (inflate 1.2.11) of the data after the 16-byte header into out in chunks; otherwise memmove of header +8 bytes from entry + 16. Returns the byte count (or -1).

name: PackFile_EntryPtr
purpose: Returns the in-memory address of a loaded pack entry: from one of the 8 cached entry slots when index is cached, else base + (offset[index] - offset[first loaded]).

behavior.text: cache check over 8 slot ids at pack+456; chunk table at pack+16 (16 bytes per entry: offset at +0).

name: PackFile_ReadEntry
purpose: Copies (and, when needed, inflates) one entry of an index-addressed pack into a caller buffer.

behavior.text: PackEntry_Inflate(state with window 0x8000, out, PackFile_EntryPtr(index)).
the pack handle of all three callers is the g2d.dat reader `qword_140D3AD58` (see sub_1403D2450); the result is the inflated length, -1 makes the callers load the entry again once.

= PackEntry_Inflate(state, out, PackFile_EntryPtr(pack, n), size) with no test of n against the pack's entry count; PackEntry_Inflate's first access to the entry (the address is inside that callee, not in this body) is a test of the entry's flag byte +4 (0x1403D1EF0, stored or zlib). An entry number past the pack faults there (seen live 2026-11-13).

notes: The unit renderer's sheet index (dword_1407151F0[shape] + which) is passed here; these are the entry numbers of g2d.dat (V 2026-11-10: the handle is the g2d.dat reader).

name: Pad_Poll
purpose: Polls pad number pad+608 with XInputGetState and fills one output block: sticks, triggers, buttons.

behavior.text: XInputGetState(pad+608, state); a non-zero result returns 0 and nothing is written.

Pad_ReadSticks writes out[0..3]; out[4] = left trigger / 255 * 100 and out[5] = right trigger / 255 * 100 (truncated, 0 .. 100); sub_140020350 merges the button bits into the dwords at out +8 / +12 / +16 (bit numbers: Input_UpdateActionRow). Returns 1.
the trigger bytes are the input state's bytes +1228 / +1229 (sub_1400F0BC8, the 'any input' test, reads +1224 .. +1229 together).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1400200F8).

name: Pad_ReadSticks
purpose: Turns the two thumb sticks of one XInput state into four signed bytes in -100 .. 100.

behavior.text: each stick axis is a signed 16-bit value divided by 32767 (negative values by 32768); the pair goes through sub_14001C080 with the stick's threshold (pad+592 for the left stick, pad+596 for the right), then out[i] = truncate(value * 100).
output order out[0] = left stick X, out[1] = left stick Y, out[2] = right stick X, out[3] = right stick Y.
these four bytes become the input state's bytes +1224 .. +1227 (UI code reads those offsets in the same order; +1227 is the right stick's vertical axis in the list scroller).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1400201F4).
open_questions: ? what sub_14001C080 does exactly (radial or per-axis dead zone, rescale) and the values of the two thresholds; ? how the output block is copied into the input state at +1224.

name: Palette_ConvertToRgba
proto: int Palette_ConvertToRgba(int kind, const short *src, unsigned int *dst)
purpose: Converts a 16- or 256-colour palette of 15-bit words into 32-bit colours with alpha.

behavior.text: the count comes from the palette format table (0x140672C38) by kind.
word 0 becomes fully clear, 0x8000 opaque black; other words take their colour from a 32768-entry lookup.

with semi-transparency on, words with the top bit take the alpha of the current blend mode (blend mode alpha table, 0x1407143E8), the others a fixed alpha; the return value says whether any opaque colour was seen.

name: PanelScreen_InitVram
purpose: Uploads the palette and strips of the second panel screen to VRAM.

behavior.text: the same upload sequence as EquipScreen_InitVram with the other palette block (0x1408F9370): the staging block at x 256, the 64 x 4 word palette at (256, 250) and two small strips.
then clears an eight-word state block and one dword; there is no inventory snapshot or order list work.

notes: IDA carried a wrong library name for this function.

name: Party_AnyItemBelow99
purpose:
Answers whether any item held by the party has reached a high count. It works on a private copy of the inventory counts,
adds the items the party members have equipped, and reports the first id whose total reaches one hundred.

behavior.text: takes no arguments.

copies the 261-byte live inventory count array into a 272-byte stack buffer with fixed 16-byte moves plus a dword and
  a byte.

walks the party unit pointer table at 0x141800F50 for the party count byte; for each member it reads one word at +0x54
  masked to ten bits plus five unmasked words at the start of the record, and increments the copied count for every word
  the validity check accepts (that check also keeps the index inside the 261-entry range).
then scans the copied counts from id 0 to 260 and returns 1 as soon as one of them is 100 (0x64) or more.
returns 0 when the whole scan finds no such count.
the buffer is larger than the copied array (272 bytes for 261), and only the copied range is scanned.

the comparison is an unsigned above-or-equal against 0x64, so the answer is "some count reached one hundred", not
  "some count is below ninety-nine"; the name reads the test backwards.
the routine is a "some stack is full" gate rather than a per-item query.
which menu or battle decision consumes the answer; the caller was not read.

name: Party_CountMasteredJobs
purpose: Counts the generic jobs whose every ability is learned and returns half of that count, capped at 7.

behavior.text: walks the job ids 74..93 except 74, 75 and 93; for each, the 24-entry ability list of its JobTable row's skillset (Skillset_BuildAbilityList, mask 15) and the learned bits at learnedBits + 3 x Job_IdToIndex(job).
a job counts when no listed ability has its learned bit clear; the result is count / 2, at most 7.
the JobTable row guard (id >= 0xAE -> no row) never fires: the loop stays below 0x5E.

notes: The job id bound stays 0xAE, so only the jobs the game ships are counted here.

name: Party_CountUnitsAtLevel
proto: bool Party_CountUnitsAtLevel(int level, void *unused, char skip_battle)
purpose: True when at least 5 party units have reached a level.

behavior.text: unless the third argument is set, counts the units of records 16..20 (slot byte not 0xFF) whose level (+0x29) is at least the given level and marks their roster indices; then counts the roster units (54 records) not marked whose level byte (+29) is at least the level; returns count >= 5.

name: Party_EggUpkeep
callees: EventVar_Read, sub_14027528C, sub_140278B24, sub_140279328, sub_1402CD168, sub_1403D325C, sub_1403D3AE8
purpose: Per-step upkeep of monster eggs over the 54 save slots: counts down existing eggs and hatches them, and may also create a new egg from a monster that carries an Egg key. The name (I) covers the hatch part only; the function does both.

behavior.text: seeds a random generator state from event variables and a fixed constant, then loops save slots 0..0x35, skipping empty ones (slot id byte A+1 = 0xFF).

for a unit with the egg flag (A+4 bit 2), decrements the low nibble of A+5; when it reaches zero the flags are set to 0x20, event variables 46 and 47 are read, a value is written into the word at A+5, and an egg-hatched notification object is posted.
for other units, reads the Job row (table 46) of the unit's job (A+2); a nonzero dword at row +52 marks the unit as an egg parent candidate and its slot index is added to a candidate list.
with at least one candidate, one random byte decides a stage: below 6 gives stage 3, below 16 gives stage 2, below 32 gives stage 1, otherwise nothing happens.
a random candidate's job row +52 is the key into the Egg table (id 310); Egg row +8 / +12 / +16 (job / job_2 / job_3) gives the new monster's job id for stage 1 / 2 / 3.
a free save slot is found with sub_14027528C; the new unit gets the job id at A+2, the egg flag (A+4 bit 2), and a random value 0..3 at A+288.
Egg row +20 acts as a modulus: n = random % value + 1 (minimum 2); the egg timer stored at A+5 is 17 * n (reset to 1 when above 0x16D).

notes: Also known as Party_HatchEggMonster (earlier proposal; renamed because the function creates eggs as well as hatching them).
open_questions: Exact meaning of the value written to A+5 on hatch (built from event variables 46 and 47).

name: Party_GetSlotState
callers: sub_140288788, Party_GetSlotStateSpecial, sub_1402C20F0, sub_140332DB0, sub_140333974, sub_1403343E4, sub_1403358FC
purpose: Returns the availability state of one party slot: usable, absent, blocked or a special job, as a small signed code.

behavior.text: a slot of 0x38 or above, or a negative slot, returns -1.
the party unit pointer is g_PartyUnits[slot]; a non-zero byte at +0x167 returns -2.
a non-zero word at +0x3E, or Job_IsHiddenFromTree on the job word at +0x24, returns -3.
party unit +0x70 bit 2 returns -4.
a job of 0x5D (93) returns -6 instead of 1.
the normal usable result is 1.
the four negative codes and the two positive values are the whole return set; there is no other branch.
the codes are the party/errand list states: -1 bad slot, -2 absent, -3 blocked, -4 in use, -6 special job.
which screen maps which code to which label; the consumer switches were not read.

notes: Whole function read (134 bytes).

name: Party_GetSlotStateSpecial
purpose: Wrapper around the party slot check that replaces the usable result with the special-job code for jobs 161 and 164.

behavior.text: a slot of 0x38 or above, or a negative slot, returns -1 without calling the inner check.
it calls Party_GetSlotState and passes every result other than 1 straight through.
for a usable slot it reads the job word at +0x24 and returns -6 when the job is 0xA1 or 0xA4 (the second reached as 0xA1+3).
every other usable slot keeps the value 1.
the function does not write anything; it is a pure filter over the inner result.
0xA1 and 0xA4 are the two jobs whose party records cannot be used in the normal unit list, which is why the caller needs a distinct code.
whether the caller treats -6 as hidden or as unusable; the four call sites were not compared.

notes: Whole function read (76 bytes).

name: Party_GetUnitJobId
purpose: Returns the job id of a party member, normalising the generic-unit marker values.

behavior.text: unit = g_PartyUnits[partyIndex] (int16 index); marker = unit+114.
marker 128 or 129 -> 74 (generic male/female base job).
marker 130 -> the int16 at unit+36 (the unit's actual job id).
any other marker -> returned unchanged.

notes: The same normalisation is inlined in JobChange_FillUnitEntry. Markers 128/129/130 are the generic-unit variants.
open_questions: What marker 130 means exactly (a generic unit whose job id is stored at +36).

name: Party_ReturnHandItems
purpose:
Returns a party unit's equipment to the inventory and clears its slots, with special handling for the two-handed
and dual-wield cases.

behavior.text:
It masks the left-hand word with 0x3FF only inside the category helpers; the word passed to
  `Inventory_AddCount` is the raw party word (0x140288A24 body), and that callee masks internally.

It walks five slots and calls `sub_140288788` on each raw word; a refusal or a "not needed" result clears
  the slot and adds the raw word to the inventory.
Slot 0x36 (the dummy unit) is skipped for the inventory add but still cleared.

It moves a one-handed second hand into the primary slot and clears the second; it also clears the
  two-handed/double-grip fields for the special jobs.

Because `Inventory_AddCount` masks with 0x3FF, a bit-15 word is returned as its id; the flag does not
  corrupt the inventory, but the unit word is cleared as a whole.

notes: V: passes the raw party word to Item_IsInCategory and Inventory_AddCount; both mask with 0x3FF internally, so a flagged word's id is preserved here.
open_questions: - ?: whether the dummy unit 0x36 is the only one that drops items instead of returning them.

name: PartyUnit_BuildJobRecord
purpose: Returns the classic-graphics face value of a save unit record: it finds the record's portrait code the way sub_14032AB3C does (marker, job byte, job row), from its own copy of the code words, and turns the code into the value PartyUnit_GetFaceRecord builds the classic face record from.

behavior.text: saveIndex below 0x36 selects g_UnitSaveData + 600 * index; a larger index leaves the record pointer null and the marker read goes through it (a fault; the one caller passes a record index).

the look index: a marker below 0x80 is the index itself; 0x80 gives 2 * job - 52 and 0x81 (tested by subtracting 0x80, then 1) 2 * job - 51 (Mime, job 93, two less); 0xA2 and 0xA3 give index 0; every other marker of 0x80 and up takes byte +46 of the job row of the job byte.
on every path of a marker 0x80 and up (except Mime with 0x80) job 91 gives index 130 and job 92 index 131.
an index below 0xD3 reads the code word of g_PortraitCodeA; otherwise, and for marker 0, the code is 0.
markers 0x80 and 0x81 with job 160 give code 104 (105 for 0x81), with job 161 or 164 code 106 + (marker & 1); these tests read the job byte from the record again.

the value: code 24 returns 122; a code below 63 is the value (one less for a marker of 0x80 and up); codes 63 to 82 read a signed byte table at 0x14067FAC9 (its entries 63 to 82 hold 62 to 81 in another order), codes of 83 and up and markers 0xA2 / 0xA3 its entry 63 (marker 0x82 skips the job and 0xA2 / 0xA3 tests).
a value of 62 or more returns 3 * value - 124 + job row byte +47 (0 when no job row was read: markers below 0x80, 0x80, 0x81, 0xA2, 0xA3).
writes nothing; the result is in eax.

notes: Whole function read (2026-11-08). Rewritten from the 2026-10-27 reference sheet, which read the 0xA0..0xA4 tests as markers (they test the job byte) and the job 91 test as a table choice (it sets the index). The look index part is the same code as sub_14032AB3C, EventMessage_Scripted, sub_140300768 and sub_140300D74, each against its own copy of the code words (behaviour LookSumSeesTheBaseJob). The name is historical: the function returns a face value, not a record.
open_questions: ? what the value 3 * v - 124 + job row byte +47 selects in the classic face record (atlas cell ((code >> 2) + 224) << 6).

name: PartyUnit_FaceIndexForJob
purpose: Maps a job id to the face (portrait) record index of a generic unit.

behavior.text: Mime (0x5D) gets a fixed index; ids below 0xA0 give 2*job - 124; 0xA2 / 0xA3 give 88 / 89; other ids 2*job - 236.

name: PartyUnit_FillFromWork
purpose:
Builds the 640-byte party record B from a work record (the save row image) and the save row. The equipment words
at record B +0x54..+0x5C come from work +0x0E..+0x1A and are zeroed when the full 16-bit word is not a valid id.

behavior.text:
It writes record B +0x54 from work +0x14 or +0x16, +0x56 from work +0x18 or +0x1A, and +0x58/+0x5A/+0x5C
  from work +0x0E/+0x10/+0x12 (0x140284C19..0x140284C51). The choice within each hand pair is made by the
  equip-category check at 0x140284BFF..0x140284C13.

It then walks the five output words at 0x140284C55 and calls `sub_1402B8EBC` on each. That callee accepts
  only 1..0xFD and 0x100..0x104; any other full word (including a bit-14 or bit-15 word) makes the caller write
  zero (0x140284C62).
The save words are copied raw from the work record; the validity check is the only sanitizer.

Earlier in the function it builds the non-equipment fields from the work and save records; that part was
  not traced in detail.

This is where a flagged save word is dropped: it cannot survive the record-B rebuild, because the full
  word fails the id-range test and is replaced by zero.

notes: V: copies the work record's equipment words to record B +0x54..+0x5C (0x140284C19-0x140284C51) and zeroes each word whose full 16-bit value fails sub_1402B8EBC (0x140284C59-0x140284C62).
open_questions: - ?: the exact write order and the non-equipment fields; only the hand block and the sanitizer were read.

name: PartyUnit_FillFromWorkRecord
purpose: Builds a party record B from a work record C alone (the per-job arrays come from C).

behavior.text: copies the unlock mask byte-swapped (C +159..161 -> B +120..122), learned bits, levels, JP and total JP in 16-byte blocks.
fixes JP and total JP of the current job to at least the value it already had (two compares per word).

name: PartyUnit_GetFaceRecord
callees: sub_1402B5644 (a JobTable byte 46/47 reader, see the W0 correction), sub_1402897B4
purpose: Selects the face / portrait record of a party unit and writes it to the output: 12 bytes copied from `g_PartyFaceRecords` plus a rebuilt face-variant word.

behavior.text: job word (+36) 72, 144, 145, 150, 151, 153..154 select fixed record indexes (76, 82, 79, 81); marker byte (+114) 0x82, 0xA2, 0xA3 select others (61 + the byte at +358, 88, 89); markers below 0x4A index `g_PartyFaceIndex[marker]`; markers 0x4A and above call sub_1402897B4(job, flag, out).
the record is `g_PartyFaceRecords + 12 * index`: a qword and a dword are copied to the output; for indexes other than 88/89 the word at out+8 is rebuilt from the result of sub_1402B5644.
the job ids it handles are written in the code (hard-coded).

notes: Data names applied: g_PartyFaceRecords (0x14080C660, 12-byte records), g_PartyFaceIndex (0x14067F840, 80 bytes, marker -> record).
open_questions: What exactly the face-variant word at out+8 encodes (I: portrait page and cell).

name: PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment
purpose:
Rebuilds the selected unit's work record from its save row and refreshes the three screen records: the 0x1407B27xx
party record, the 0x141876E90 panel block and the per-unit stat block. The live equipment words are copied into
the panel block raw.

behavior.text:
It builds a work record from the unit's save index (`UnitWork_BuildFromSaveIndex`) and fills seven equipment
  words at work +0x1BA..+0x1C6 with 0xFF before copying items.

It masks the five live words with 0x3FF (0x1402BD9B9..0x1402BDA32) and sorts the two hand items by the
  record's equip category (19 goes to the shield slots); it then replaces 0, 0xFF and values at or above 0x105
  with 0xFF.

It calls `PartyUnit_FillFromWork` to build the 64-byte record B (0x1402BDA97), then copies record B's
  +0x30..+0x3F to `xmmword_141876E90` (0x1402BDB20), and the live five words to a 32-byte stack value which is
  stored at `ymmword_141876EB0` (0x1402BDB42), i.e. the hand words land at block +0x24 (0x141876EB4).

The live-word copy at 0x1402BDABB/0x1402BDAB7 is raw: the words are read as a qword and a word and are
  not masked before they are stored in the block, so a bit-15 word reaches the panel block.

It computes the two-handed word with `sub_140284998` (0x1402BDACB) and stores it as the low word of
  `xmmword_141876EA0` (0x1402BDB37); the rest of that 16-byte value is not written in this function.

It calls `sub_140287398(&xmmword_141876E90, unit+0x54)` (0x1402BDB57) to add the five items' stats to the
  block; that callee masks each id with 0x3FF and writes only the stat words.
It sets eight refresh flags (`dword_14078CFAC`, `dword_141848B24`, ...) and ends through the stack cookie.

The earlier "seven equipment words" description of the work record is right, but the panel block is not
  the work record: it is a 64-byte copy of the party record slice, and its hand words are the raw live words.

notes: V: the panel block writer. The five live words are copied raw (movsd 0x1402BDABB, word 0x1402BDAB7) and stored at block +0x24 (movaps 0x1402BDB42); the ids used for the work-list are masked with 0x3FF (0x1402BD9B9-0x1402BDA32).

name: PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave
purpose:
Writes one party unit's record back into its 600-byte save row. The five equipment words go to the save raw,
without a mask or flag test.

behavior.text:
It builds a work record from the save index (`UnitWork_BuildFromSaveIndex`) and fills the non-equipment
  fields from the party record.

It writes the two hand words at record +0x54 and +0x56 to save +0x16/+0x14 and +0x1A/+0x18; the category
  19 (shield) item goes to the second word of each pair, the other item to the first (0x140285829..0x140285884).
It writes +0x58, +0x5A and +0x5C to save +0x0E, +0x10 and +0x12 (0x140285890..0x1402858BF).

The stores are whole-word copies: no 0x3FF mask and no bit-15 test. Before each pair it writes 0x00FF00FF
  to the two-word slot, so an empty half stays 0xFF.

It calls `Item_GetRecord` with the raw word at 0x140285845 and 0x140285872. That accessor indexes the item
  table with the full 16-bit value, so a bit-15 word would read far past the table.

The job: the save record is `g_UnitSaveData + 0x258 * (signed word at party +0x2C)`, and its job byte at +2 is
  the low byte of the party record's job word (a byte load from party +0x24 and a byte store to save +2, 0x1402857D3..0x1402857DB). A job
  change edits that party word (a u16 in `PartyUnit_FillFromWork`'s store at 0x140284AF1), so this store is where a changed
  job reaches the save record. Observed live 2026-11-04 (a data watch on the combat-set job byte saw this function copy
  the whole record); the three combat-set job bytes at party +462 / +550 / +638 are copied here and never read as a job.
It ends with `PartyUnit_FillFromWork` to rebuild the party record from the save row.

The commit handler strips the flags before this function runs; every other caller relies on the session
  having ended cleanly.

notes: V: stores the five party words raw at save +0x0E..+0x1A (0x140285829-0x1402858BF) and calls Item_GetRecord with the unmasked word at 0x140285845/0x140285872; a bit-15 word would index past the item table.
open_questions: - ?: whether any caller can run with a bit-15 word still in the unit.

name: PauseManager_Pop
purpose: Pops the top pause id and restores the previous pause (or unpauses).

behavior.text: id = byte at `pm+20+depth`; clears that byte; depth--; `sub_1400B47B4(pm, id)` applies the id's "off" controls.
if a new top exists, `sub_1400B4968(pm, newTop)` applies its "on" controls; otherwise sets the word at `g_CharaRenderer+153012` to 0.
returns the depth after the pop.

notes: `sub_1400B47B4` also looks up the row and calls `sub_1401D6F9C(qword_143CD9DD8, row[+8], 0, ...)` when row dword +8 is non-zero, which is what removes the pause UI state.

name: PauseManager_Push
purpose: Pushes a pause id onto the PauseManager's small stack (max depth 3), applying the previous top's "off" controls and the new top's "on" controls.

behavior.text: depth = byte at pm+23; `depth+1 >= 3` returns without pushing.
depth != 0: re-applies the current top (`sub_1400B47B4(pm, topId)`); depth == 0: sets the word at `g_CharaRenderer+153012` to 1.
increments the depth, stores the id at `pm+20+depth`, then calls `sub_1400B4968(pm, id)`.

notes: `sub_1400B4968` reads NXD table 282 row `id` and writes the row's 8 control bytes at `+16..+23` through `sub_1400B4894`, plus the row dword `+8` through `sub_1401D6F9C(qword_143CD9DD8, value, 1)`. The top id gates input (see `Input_TestAction`).
open_questions: ? the meaning of `g_CharaRenderer+153012`; ? the NXD 282 row contents.

name: PauseManager_Tick
callers: `sub_1400B57FC` and the update functions of ~15 other managers
purpose: Ticks the pause overlay: when a pause is on the stack, loads its duration from NXD table 282 into the remaining-time float.

behavior.text: depth `pm+23` == 0 -> return.
id = byte at `pm+20+depth`; 0 -> return.
row = NXD table 282 row `id`; missing row or zero dword at row+4 -> `sub_1400B4760(pm)` (pop).
otherwise `*(float*)(pm+16) = (float)row[+4] / 1000.0` (milliseconds -> seconds).

notes: Called at the top of every manager update, so a paused game still ticks the overlay but skips the manager work (the managers return early); `sub_1400B57FC` is the clearest example.
open_questions: ? whether a row with duration 0 means "wait for input" rather than "no pause".

name: Pixels_ExpandToRgba
proto: uint64_t Pixels_ExpandToRgba(uint32_t *out, int64_t unused, uint8_t *src, uint32_t *palette, int w, int h, unsigned bpp, int outPitch)
purpose: Expands a block of 4-, 8-, 16- or 32-bit pixels into 32-bit texels.

behavior.text: bpp 4: two texels per byte, low nibble first, through the palette; with outPitch -1 the rows follow each other, else the output skips outPitch - w texels after each row.
bpp 8: one texel per byte through the palette, rows following each other.
bpp 16 (only with outPitch -1): each 5-5-5 word becomes a texel with each channel times 8 and the top byte all ones (the constant 0xFFFF8000 is shifted up with the blue channel).
bpp 32: a plain copy of 4 * w * h bytes.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14041DDB0).

name: PlaceName_GetText
purpose: Returns the text of a PlaceName row (table 85) by its key, or the empty string.

behavior.text: uses the cached table pointer qword_143CDA318; when it is zero the table is fetched from the registry by id 85, and a missing registry or table returns the empty string.
key 0 returns the empty string; a missing row returns it too.
otherwise returns the string at row + 12 + (the dword at row + 12): the text offset stored at row +12 is counted from row +12.
the Map row's three name members (place_name, place_name_2, place_name_3) are keys of this table; the title, the save list and the map-name nodes read them through this function.

notes: Keys that name no row (for example 10100 on five Map rows, M) give the empty text, not an error.

name: Poach_GiveResult
purpose: Gives the result of a Poach action: an item, or gil when the stock is full, and sends the poach notification.

behavior.text: runs only when not simulating and action block +18 bit 0x20 is set.

picks the poach id from the acting unit's Job row (table 46) by Rng_Percent(256, 31), which is true when 256 * rand15 / 0x8000 >= 31 (225 of 256 draws): true -> Job +0x24 (column poach_item), false -> Job +0x28 (column poach_item_rare, about 12 %). The id is a PoachItem row (table 236).
when the id is above 96 or its held count is below 99 it adds the item (sub_1400D6FB0); otherwise it gives PoachItem row +0x28 / 2 gil (sub_140284684, sub_1400EC5F4) and flags the gil message.
then it sends BattleActionPoachNotification.

notes: The constant 0x8000 in the roll rule belongs to the callee Rng_Percent (256 * rand15 / 0x8000 >= 31).

name: PoachersDen_AddStock
proto: int PoachersDen_AddStock(unsigned short id, int delta)
purpose:
Adds a signed delta to the Poachers' Den stock count of one item id and returns the resulting count, clamped to the byte
range the store uses; the shop list builder calls it with a zero delta, so in the shop path it is a stock query.

behavior.text: the id argument is masked with 0x3FF before use, so only the low ten bits reach the store.
an id at or above 261 (0x105) is rejected and the function returns 0 without touching the store.

the count is one byte per id in the array at 0x1411A7700; the address is loaded by the rip-relative lea at
  0x14028757F, in the continuation the early return falls through to, which lies past the end of the unwind range the
  cross-check scans.
the function reads that byte, adds the delta and keeps the result in a 32-bit register.
a negative result is replaced by 0, and a result above 255 is clamped to 255.
the clamped byte is written back and returned in the low 32 bits of the return value.
the function reads and writes only the den stock array; it has no other state and calls nothing.
its only direct caller is Shop_BuildItemList, which passes a delta of zero, so the shop path only reads the count.

the 0..255 clamp mirrors the one-byte count arrays used elsewhere for items, and the wrap to zero on a negative total
  makes the store behave like a saturating counter.
the code path that actually adds stock (poaching) is not a direct call from any function in the image.

notes:
- V: the array is 261 bytes at 0x1411A7700; the item badge block starts 272 bytes after the array base, so only 11 unused
  bytes separate the two stores.
open_questions:
- ?: which routine or script adds den stock during play, given that the only direct caller always passes zero.
- ?: whether the add path enforces the same 261-id bound that this function enforces.

name: PoachList_Build
purpose: Builds the poacher shop's list: one 48-byte entry for each poach id (1..96) with a non-zero held count.

behavior.text: for poach ids 1..96 with a non-zero count (unk_1411A7A1B), builds a 48-byte entry (see PoachListEntry): +0 item id (PoachItem +0x2C), +4 equipped count, +8 index, +16 total held, +24 poach id, +28 count, +32 PoachItem +0x24 (price), +36 PoachItem +0x28 (sell price), +40 new flag (unk_1411A7B3F).

notes: The list is sorted by sub_1401CAFE0 (sort_name strings of the PoachItem rows); the other poach list sorters are sub_1401CAB50 and sub_1401CAC8C, the row label is built by sub_1402A6710.

name: PoachRow_SetMonsterIcon
purpose: Sets the monster icon of a poacher list row.

behavior.text: IconMonster plays 'Rare' or 'Normal' by PoachItem +0x34 (column rare); its Icon part frame is PoachItem +0x30 (column icon).

name: PoachSell_FillRow
purpose: Fills one row of the poacher sell list.

behavior.text: runs sub_1402A4230, ShopItemList_SetPrice(entry +36), plays 'ShowPoacherSell' and sets the new marker from entry +40.

name: PoachSell_ShowTotal
purpose: Shows the sale total of the poacher sell screen.

behavior.text: shows amount x the value at window +2808 (the sell price of the chosen row: PoachItem row +0x28, read by the code that fills the window, not in this body) as the row price.

name: PoachTable_GetRowById
purpose: Returns the PoachItem-en row for a poach type through the shared NXD table interface.

behavior.text: the resource object is at 0x143CDA880 and the table interface at 0x143CD9CD0.
the table is opened once, cached, and the row is looked up by the id.
the entry is advanced by eight bytes plus its own header offset before it is returned.
a failed open or a missing row returns null.
the only caller is the event message builder, which needs the poach name for a message.
the table id is 0xEC (PoachItem-en) for this accessor.
whether the +8 advance is the payload start of every row or specific to this table.

notes: Whole function read (135 bytes).

name: PoachTip_Fill
purpose: Fills the poach help tip.

behavior.text: sets the text from sub_1402B8B00 (the PoachItem name) and an icon path (PoachItem +0x34 != 0) + 503.

name: PortraitCode_FillCell
proto: uint8_t PortraitCode_FillCell(void *rec, int code, int *outSlot, int *outColour)
callers: sub_14032AB3C, EventMessage_Scripted, sub_1402C4550, sub_1402D7954, sub_1402D9490, sub_1402DF374, sub_14032D31C, sub_140376040
purpose: Turns a portrait code into the classic portrait atlas cell of a draw record and its colour, and returns the code's low byte.

behavior.text: when outSlot is not null it is set to -1.
the colour is ((code >> 10) & 3) + 8, written to *outColour: bits 10 and 11 of the code choose one of four colours.

the cell comes from the code's low byte b: column (b % 40) & 7 (32 pixels wide, byte +20 and +36), row (b % 40) >> 3 (48 pixels high, +21 / +29 and +37 / +45), page b / 40 + 26 (word +30, low 4 bits, with bit 0x10 set).

the word +22 packs a CLUT row in its bits 6 and up (350 + code for codes 104 to 111, the fixed portraits; 506 + (b - 63) % 6 for low bytes 63 to 82; else 496 + ((b % 40) >> 2); each wrapped with & 0x1FF from 512 up) and a column in its low 6 bits.
returns (uint8_t)code; bits 8 and above (and the colour bits 10, 11) never reach the return value.

notes: So on every path through this function a portrait code is a byte plus two colour bits: at most 256 distinct faces can come out of a code. The name is ours (IDB: sub_1402E16A8).

name: PostTarget_DrawFitted
proto: __int64 sub_1403CB9C4(PostTargetDesc *desc, float width, float height, int filterMode, char stretch)
callees: sub_14003E120, sub_14003E228, sub_1403C043C, sub_1403CC204, ShaderSelector_SetDigit, ShaderSelector_Apply, sub_140069A38, RenderState_PackCommand, sub_140069980
purpose: Draws one textured quad from a render-target descriptor (136-byte entries at unk_142C819D0) into the current UI render target, fitted into the 16:9 area of the window, with the layer-composite selector #9 in permutation digit 0 = 18.

behavior.text: the current render target = the object at g_Renderer + 8 * (byte g_Renderer+13754) + 6560 (0 when the byte is 0xFF); its u16 width / height at +20 / +22 give W / H.

maps the descriptor's constant buffer (desc+56) and fills the cUIRender layout like UILayer_FillConstants: rows 0-3 and 4-7 = the two pixel-to-clip matrices (scale 2/W, -2/H; atlas offset 0), +128 = 0, +136 = the float at desc+112, +144 (row 9) = (1, 1, 1, 1), +548 (34.y) = 18, +552 = (0, 0), +568 / +572 (35.zw) = 2.6 / 2.6, and zeros for the other rows UILayer_FillConstants writes (rows 36 and 37 are not written). The buffer is committed and bound at constant-buffer slot short(desc+40).

the destination rectangle comes from sub_1403CC204(&rect, (int)width, (int)height, stretch): with the display size read from the object pointed to by (qword_140C696A8 + 88) (dwords +40 / +44) it takes the 16:9 box that fits the display (pillarbox or letterbox, centred), scales the source by box height / height, and the width is box width when stretch != 0, else width * that scale; rect = (left, top, right, bottom) in display pixels.

maps the vertex buffer (desc+72) and writes four 16-byte vertices (x, y, u, v): (left, top, 0, 0), (right, top, width / desc+116, 0), (left, bottom, 0, height / desc+120), (right, bottom, width / desc+116, height / desc+120): the top-left width x height part of the descriptor's source texture is stretched to the rectangle (desc+116 / +120 = the source texture size).
selector = the UI manager's selector #9 (+72); skipped when it is null. ShaderSelector_SetDigit(sel, 0, 18), SetDigit(sel, 1, 0); default sampler words copied; ShaderSelector_Apply(sel, state, 0).

sampler word = dword_141D8BC7C with bits 0x3C0 cleared when filterMode == 0, bits 0x3C0 set to 0x240 when filterMode == 1, unchanged otherwise (top bit cleared); stored at state + 5704 + 4 * slot for the sampler slots short(desc+42) and short(desc+44).
texture = the object at g_TextureTable + 8 * dword(desc+16) + 8 (+40 member, 0 when null), bound as texture slots short(desc+46) and short(desc+48) (state + 1608 + 8 * slot).

state: +136 = desc+64, +200 = the +40 member of the object at desc+72, +208 = 16 (stride), +6016 = 0, +128 = desc+80, +124 = (& 0xFFC06FFF) | 0x6000; clip enable: state+112 |= 0x10 with the rectangle copied to state+80; a 96-byte command is allocated with sub_140069A38(state, 5, 96) (the layer passes pass 4 there) and its header words are written +4 = 4, +8 = 0, +12 = 0 (the layer passes write +8 = 4, +12 = 0), packed and submitted; afterwards the 0x10 clip bit is cleared again. The draw writes the render target that sub_1403CB8BC installed (state+96 / +144 = the current UI target, previous state+96 saved at desc+0).

callers: CharaRenderer_PostFrame passes (descriptor unk_142C819D0 + 136 * v5, its second argument, the target height as float, the value at 0x142E7FC70 when dword_142E7FC68 != 0 else 0, a stretch flag that is 1 only when dword_142E7FC68 == 7 and dword_142E7FC6C == 0); sub_1402F3284 passes (unk_142C819D0, ..., (float)v6, the value at 0x142E7FC70, 0).

notes: Proposed name: PostTarget_DrawFitted. The two float arguments arrive in xmm1 / xmm2 (the IDB prototype shows the second argument as an unused integer a2 and only the third as a float). It is the final present-style quad of the unit-renderer post chain (CharaRenderer_PostFrame calls sub_1403CB8BC to set the target, then this). sub_1403CC204 (proposed UIRect_Fit16x9) is the rectangle helper. The scan that listed this function as referencing the layer record's shadow colour offset (303936) does not hold: the decompile and the disassembly contain no such displacement; that offset occurs only in GUILayer_BuildRecord.
open_questions: ? what digit-0 value 18 of selector #9 draws (which pixel shader / blend variant; UILayer_FillConstants feeds layer+32 to the same digit). ? what dword_141D8BC7C is and why bits 0x3C0 = 0x240 are set for filterMode 1 (probably a point / linear filter choice). ? the meaning of the value at 0x142E7FC70 / dword_142E7FC68. ? the descriptor fields +80, +112 and +116 / +120's producer.

name: PreviewUnit_BuildRecord
proto: __int64 PreviewUnit_BuildRecord(SpriteRecord *out, int partyIndex, int previewIndex, int a4, int a5, int slotArg, char applyAltRow)
callers: Unit_BuildPreviewSpriteRecord (when unk_142FF9F30 and qword_142FF9F34 are both 0, i.e. always in normal play), sub_140143EA8, sub_140147268, sub_140218F78, sub_1402D0108, sub_1402D3838, sub_1402ED078
purpose: Normal-play builder of a unit's sprite record: creates the preview unit, resolves its shape and palette, fills the record and applies the alternate row (table 0x112).

behavior.text: builds a 512-byte preview unit with sub_140275C70(previewIndex), calls Unit_ResolvePreviewShape (shape, palette); for a unit with flag 4 it takes the palette from the save data byte +288 (+0x120).

calls SpriteRecord_Fill(out, partyIndex, shape, palette, a4, 0, slotArg, flagWord) where flagWord = 0x40000000 when the unit's low nibble (byte +8 of the preview unit; the 'flag 4' test is bit 4 of byte +6) is <= 1, else 0x20000000, only for a unit with flag 4 and save data, otherwise 0; slotArg is the caller's 2 * slot + 4.
with applyAltRow, row 0x112 (by the unit's first byte) sets record +10 from sub_1401E39BC when its field +4 is non-zero.
the byte answer of Unit_ResolvePreviewShape is zero-extended into r11d at 0x1400FB1D4, copied to the work record's +399 (0x1400FB1D8) and handed to SpriteRecord_Fill as r8d (0x1400FB23F).

notes: Supersedes the impression that PreviewUnit_BuildSpriteRecord is the tree's builder: that one is only reached when the two debug globals are set.

name: PreviewUnit_BuildSpriteRecord
proto: int PreviewUnit_BuildSpriteRecord(void *out, int jobId, int previewIndex, int a4, int a5, int palette, char allowAltShape, char setPalette, char a9)
callers: Unit_BuildPreviewSpriteRecord, sub_14013C238, sub_14013FAB0, sub_140142884, sub_1401442FC, sub_14014A970, sub_1402C6514, sub_1402C72B8, sub_1402D0080
purpose: Builds a sprite record from preview-table entry `previewIndex` (<= 0x14), resolving shape/palette and applying the entry's flag-driven overrides.

behavior.text: initializes the record and returns it zeroed with job -1 when previewIndex > 0x14; otherwise writes jobId to +0.
PreviewUnit_ResolveShape(previewIndex, &shape, &palette); the shape goes to +4 and +16, the palette to +8.
with allowAltShape, entry+99 bit 4 selects shape -100 (0x9C) and bit 2 selects shape -99 (0x9D).
with setPalette, a row for entry+0 in table 0x112 (sub_1401E39BC) overrides the palette: +10 gets that byte and +20 = 0; otherwise +8 keeps the resolved palette.
+24 gets 2 when the palette argument is 4, else the argument; a8 -> +20 = sub_1400FAFB0(entry+97); +12 = 0; +28 = -1.

notes: This is the generic preview-sprite builder behind the job-change/unit-preview screens; the tree path reaches it through Unit_BuildPreviewSpriteRecord. Fields: +0 job id, +4/+16 shape, +8 palette, +10 alternate value, +12 flags (filled later by SpriteRecord_SetPaletteBits), +20 override flag, +24 palette id, +28 -1.
open_questions: Consumers of the +10 alternate value and the +20 override flag (CharaRender path) were not traced.

name: PreviewUnit_ResolveShape
purpose: Resolves shape/palette for entry `idx` (<= 0x14) of the 21-entry preview table g_BattleUnitTable (stride 512).

behavior.text: calls Unit_ResolvePreviewShape; stores shape at entry+399 and palette at +400; the palette may be overridden by a table lookup (sub_140260ABC).

notes: Bound check `idx <= 0x14` already admits index 20.
open_questions: Live table reads as zeros when the tree is open; is it only populated in battle/party contexts? Not investigated.

name: RangeOverlay_BuildRowMasks
purpose: Builds the 18 row words of the range overlay diamond for a given distance.

behavior.text: for the three distance modes 0, 1, 2 the distance comes from two unit fields or their sum; 16 and above clears the overlay.

for every row it takes the bit-run mask of the row's distance from the table (0x140693090), shifts it to the unit's column and stores the 18 resulting words; an optional pass removes bits outside the unit's lane.

notes: The table address is reached as an image-relative displacement, so the address does not appear as a plain operand.

name: Recruit_GenerateUnit
callers: sub_14027528C (one new recruit, called by GameState_ResetParty and Party_EggUpkeep), sub_1402EFBE0 (the starting roster loop)
purpose: Fills a fresh save record with a newly generated unit: identity marker, starting job, birth sign, Brave and Faith, stat accumulators, equipment and sprite palette.

behavior.text: `kind` 0 = male generic (marker 0x80, job 74, flag byte +4 = 0x80), 1 = female generic (marker 0x81, flag 0x40), 3 = marker 0x82 with flag 0x20, job 74; any other value becomes 2 = a story unit (marker 1, job 1, flag 0x80).
the starting job is always 74 (Squire) for kinds 0, 1 and 3; it is written before the stats and is not read by the roll.
level byte +29 is 1 (the word at +28 is set to 256); Brave +30 and Faith +31 are each 40 + (31 * rand15 >> 15), so 40 to 70; kind 2 sets both to 70.
birth sign byte +5 is 1 + (365 * rand15 >> 15), then the zodiac sign byte +6 comes from sub_140279328.
Unit_RollStartingStats(accumulators at +32, +35, +38, +41, +44; kind) rolls HP, MP, SP, PA, MA; the row is the kind, so the roll depends on gender and not on the job.

the equipment words at +14..+27 are seven 16-bit words copied from bytes 5..11 of the kind's 12-byte start row: kinds 0 and 1 = 157, 186, 255, 19, 255, 255, 255; kind 2 = 157, 186, 208, 19, 255, 255, 255; kind 3 = all 255 (255 means empty).

when the flag byte +4 has bit 6 or 7 set (kinds 0, 1 and 2), each of the 20 generic jobs gets the same random 100..199 as current JP (word at +128 + 2i) and total JP (word at +174 + 2i), and the level byte +116 + i/2 is set to 0x11 (level 1 for both nibbles); the Bard slot (i = 17) is skipped for flag 0x40 and the Dancer slot (i = 18) for flag 0x80, and the bytes +124 / +125 are then set to 0x10 / 0x01, so a female unit has no Bard level and a male unit no Dancer level.
the dword at +560 is a name id: a base of 256 (male), 512 (female) or 768 (kind 3), 0 for the story kind, plus a random 0..255, redrawn until no live save record with the same marker holds it.
returns the result of sub_140279508 on the record.

notes: sub_1402EFBE0 draws the kind of each roster unit from one random bit (0 or 1) and forces the other kind once a counter reaches 8 (I: at most 8 of either gender; which counter is which was not traced). The displayed level-1 stats of a male or female Squire follow from the roll and the Squire row (M = 100, 75, 100, 90, 80): male HP 30 or 31, MP 10 or 11, SP 6, PA 4, MA 3; female HP 28 or 29, MP 11, SP 6, PA 3, MA 4 (computed from the formula in Unit_ComputeStats, not read from a running game).
open_questions: ? the item names of ids 157, 186, 208 and 19 were not looked up.

name: RenderCommand_Allocate
callers: 117 call sites: every layer pass and UI draw (GUILayer_Composite, GUILayer_BlitFinal, GUILayer_BlurShadowPass, UIRender_SubmitFrame, UIRender_DrawLetterbox, RenderContext_ResetFrame, ...)
purpose: Allocates one command of the given size from the context's current 8 KB command block, writes its type, and returns the pointer.

behavior.text: size is rounded up to a multiple of 8; used = the dword at rc+52 and the block is the pointer at rc+24. When used + size <= 0x2000 the command is carved from the current block; otherwise a new block is taken from the device pool (g_RenderDevice + 5120 + the dword at +5148, advanced by 0x2000) after the pool counter at +5144 is advanced by 0x2000 and compared with the limit at +5108.
when the pool limit is exceeded the counter is rolled back, the byte at g_RenderDevice + 5106 is set to 1 and the function returns null (the frame's commands are dropped).
on success rc+52 = the new used size and the first dword of the command = type; the function returns the pointer (null when the block pointer was null).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140069A38). The command types seen at its call sites: 0 (clear target, 32 bytes), 1 (24 bytes, a second clear kind), 4 (96 bytes: a draw with the packed state), 5 (96 bytes: the fitted post draw and the letterbox), 19 (16 bytes: resource state transition).
open_questions: ? the meaning of type 1 and of the type 19 flag word (2 / 1).

name: RenderCommand_ClearTarget
callers: the render-thread command dispatcher (table at 0x1406FD168, not a direct call)
callees: sub_14005BA74 (flush barriers), sub_140060A1C (bind target), sub_140050BC0 (close barriers), ID3D12GraphicsCommandList::ClearRenderTargetView
purpose: Render-thread executor of the command type 0 that GUILayer_Composite and RenderContext_ResetFrame queue: clears one render target to the colour stored in the command.

behavior.text: command layout as built by GUILayer_Composite: dword +0 = type 0 (written by RenderCommand_Allocate), qword +8 = the target view object (the +40 member of the render target object), 16 bytes at +16 = the clear colour (four floats). GUILayer_Composite writes the 16 bytes as zero, so a layer target and its scratch targets are cleared to (0, 0, 0, 0).

the function flushes pending resource barriers (sub_14005BA74: the command list's vtable slot +208, ResourceBarrier), binds the target (sub_140060A1C with the thread's binding state at rt+896; sub_140050BC0 closes the pending barrier list) and calls the command list's vtable slot +384 with (list, the render-target descriptor handle of the view at view + 56 + 8 x (dword_140C69D24 & 1), the colour pointer cmd + 16, 0, 0).

vtable slot +384 is ID3D12GraphicsCommandList::ClearRenderTargetView (index 48 of the interface, five arguments including the two rectangle arguments 0 / 0), so the whole target is cleared. Basis: the argument list and the slot arithmetic; the interface order was taken from the D3D12 header, not from the game.
the descriptor handle is selected by the low bit of a frame counter, so each target has two descriptors used on alternate frames. Basis: the address arithmetic (+ 8 x (counter & 1)).

name: RenderCommand_Submit

purpose: Appends a finished command to the context's list as a {sort key, command pointer} pair; the list is later executed in key order (the sort itself was not read here).

behavior.text: the pair is written at the list write pointer rc+40: the first qword is the context's current sort key (rc+8) at this moment, the second the command pointer; the pointer then advances by 16 and the remaining-entries counter rc+56 is decremented.

when the counter reaches zero a new 1 KB group is taken from the device pool (g_RenderDevice + 5120 + 5108 - (the dword at +5152 + 1024)); the pool counter at +5144 is advanced by 0xC00 and +5152 by 0x400, and a failure sets g_RenderDevice + 5106 and returns null; the previous group's last link is set to the new group, the group count rc+60 is incremented and the counter is reloaded with 63.

the sort key stored is therefore the value the caller put in rc+8 before this call, not the one it sets afterwards; the layer passes set rc+8 before packing each command (GUILayer_Composite, GUILayer_BlurShadowPass, GUILayer_BlitFinal's caller).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140069980). These render-context lists are not the lists UIContext_SortCommands sorts (those hold the UI draw records of UIRender_AppendCommand); the sort and execution of the {key, command} lists belong to the render device's frame submission, which was not read here.

these are the command-memory pool counters. Basis: sub_140069A38 adds 0x2000 per 8 KB command block to +5144 and +5148, sub_140069980 adds 0xC00 to +5144 and 0x400 to +5152 per 1 KB list group, and both set dev+5106 and give up when the pool at dev+5120 (limit dev+5108) is exhausted; sub_140088280 (called later in App_RunFrame) switches dev+5120 between the two halves of the pool, dev+5112 and dev+5112 + dev+5108.

then it loops over the dev+5088 (dword count) contexts of the array at dev+4984, stride 6032, and rewrites every context as listed in the next bullets (all offsets are inside the context). UIRender_GetThreadContext divides a context address by 6032 to find its index.

+24 / +52 are the current 8 KB command block and the bytes used in it (0x2000 = full, so the next command allocation takes a fresh block); +32 / +40 are the head and the write pointer of the list of {sort key, command pointer} entries that sub_140069980 keeps in 1 KB groups; +56 is the entry count left before the next group and +60 the group count. Basis: the code of sub_140069A38 and sub_140069980.
+80..+95 (four dwords) = 0, 0, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0x7FFFFFFF (an IDB constant) and +96 (qword) = 0.

+80 is the clip rectangle (x0, y0, x1, y1), reset to unbounded; +96 / +144 hold the render target object and its handle. Basis: GUILayer_CopyToTarget and GUILayer_BlurShadowPass copy a rectangle to +80, set the clip-enable bit 0x10 in +112 and store the target at +96 / +144.

After the reset bits 0..4 are 0xF, bits 5..12 and bit 32 are unchanged and every other bit comes from the constant. Basis: UIRender_ApplyDrawState, BlendDesc_FromWords and GUILayer_BlurShadowPass.
bindings: +128, +136, +144 (qwords), +152..+199 (48 bytes) and eight 16-byte slots from +200 up to +327 are zeroed (the loop writes the qword at +200 + 16 * k and the qword at +208 + 16 * k).

when the flag byte has bit 0x08 it sets the queue count (task +469) to 0 and, unless block +29 has bit 0x20, walks the five bytes of the added set (block +29..+33) and the removed set (block +34..+38) bit by bit (status id = 8 * byte + bit, bit 0x80 first): a bit of the first set queues byte_140672CC0[id], a bit of the second set queues byte_140672CC0[id] | 0x80 (the second is skipped when unit +475 bit 0x40 or unit +476 bit 0x01 is set and block +34 has bit 0x20). the queue is task +476 (bytes); the walk stops adding at 0x1B entries.

then the status queue: while the count task +469 is non-zero it decrements it, takes the entry task +476[count] (so the queue is shown from its last entry), stores entry & 0x7F as the BattleSignal id and kind 96, or 112 when bit 0x80 is set.
