name: RootSignature_CreateWithSampler
proto: __int64 __fastcall RootSignature_CreateWithSampler(__int64 unused1, RootSigRecord *out, int shaderVisibility, int numRootConstants, __int64 unused5, int numUavs, unsigned int samplerWord)
callees: Sampler_DescFromWord, D3D12SerializeRootSignature, sub_140084744 (device error report), sub_140026BD4 (error log helper, returns its third argument)
purpose: Builds one Direct3D 12 root signature (optional root constants, one SRV descriptor table, optional UAV descriptor table, at most one static sampler decoded from a sampler word), serialises and creates it on the device, and stores the interface pointer and a 64-bit hash of the serialised blob.

behavior.text: arguments in order: the first (rcx) and the fifth (the first stack slot) are never read. out (rdx) is a 16-byte record, [0] = the ID3D12RootSignature pointer and [8] = the blob hash; a null out gives the error result without doing anything. shaderVisibility (r8) goes into the ShaderVisibility field of every root parameter and into the static sampler. numRootConstants (r9), numUavs (the sixth argument) and samplerWord (the seventh; read as a dword, the decompile types it as 16 bits) are described below.
the root signature flags are 0x1D: allow input assembler input layout, deny hull, deny domain and deny geometry shader root access (vertex and pixel access are not denied).

the parameters, in this order: (1) only when numRootConstants != 0: 32-bit root constants, ShaderRegister 0 (b0), RegisterSpace 0, Num32BitValues = numRootConstants; (2) always: a descriptor table with one range, type SRV, 1 descriptor, base register 0 (t0), space 0, offset 0; (3) only when numUavs != 0: a descriptor table with one range, type UAV, numUavs descriptors from register 0 (u0), space 0, offset 0. The parameter count is therefore 1 to 3, with the SRV table at index 0 or 1.

static sampler: unless (samplerWord & 0x3C0) == 0x380 (bits 6..9 equal to 0xE) the one sampler is Sampler_DescFromWord(&desc, &samplerWord, ..., shaderVisibility), which decodes filter, address modes, LOD and comparison from the word and stores the visibility at +48 of the description; its ShaderRegister and RegisterSpace (+40 / +44) are 0, so it is s0, space 0. With the 0x380 pattern the root signature has no static sampler (NumStaticSamplers 0).

it calls D3D12SerializeRootSignature with the version-1 description, then creates the object through the device at (qword_140C696A8 + 3504) with vtable slot +128 (CreateRootSignature: node mask 0, the blob pointer and size, the root signature interface id, the result pointer).

on success out[0] = the new interface pointer and out[8] = a 64-bit hash of the serialised blob bytes (start 0xCBF29CE484222325 and, for every byte, hash = (hash * 0x100000001B3) XOR byte: the FNV-1 order with the 64-bit constants); both blobs are released and 0 is returned.

on a null out, a failed serialise or a failed CreateRootSignature it releases both blobs and returns 0x96100001 (the value sub_140026BD4 returns after logging); the serialise and create failures also report the HRESULT through sub_140084744 first. Every caller tests the sign of the result.

the seven call sites (out slot offset in the owner object; shaderVisibility, numRootConstants, numUavs, samplerWord): sub_140042018 +0x88: 0 (all), 8, 1, 0x26A; +0x98: 0, 4, 1, 0x2A; +0xC8: 0, 0, 2, 0x3AA; +0xD8: 0, 48, 1, 0x3AA. sub_14004318C +0x78: 5 (pixel), 4, 0, 0x3AA. sub_1400435C4 +0xA8: 5, 4, 0, 0x2A. sub_14004386C +0xB8: 0, 4, 4, 0x3AA.
the 0x3AA words select no static sampler; 0x26A is clamp on all axes with min / mag linear and mip point; 0x2A is clamp on all axes with point filtering.

the records filled by the four sub_140042018 calls are passed to sub_140039E24 right after each call; it reads record[8] and uses it in a lookup key (the hash plus 31 times a dword read through the shader object) in a cache guarded by an SRW lock, creating the cached object with sub_1400511BC on a miss.

that cached object is a compute pipeline state and the hash identifies the root signature in its cache key. Basis: the call order and the shape of sub_140039E24; the shaders behind these signatures were not read.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140042E64 until applied). The parameters are laid out as the 32-byte D3D12_ROOT_PARAMETER (type, then the union at +8 and +16, visibility at +24), the ranges as the 20-byte D3D12_DESCRIPTOR_RANGE, the static sampler as the 52-byte D3D12_STATIC_SAMPLER_DESC.
open_questions: ? what the pipelines behind the +0x88 / +0x98 / +0xC8 / +0xD8 signatures compute (sub_140042018 and its shaders were not read). ? what sub_14004318C, sub_1400435C4 and sub_14004386C build with their signatures (two pixel-visibility signatures with 4 root constants, one with and one without a point sampler, and a 4-UAV signature). ? the first and fifth arguments (unused).

name: Sampler_DescFromWord
proto: D3D12_STATIC_SAMPLER_DESC *Sampler_DescFromWord(D3D12_STATIC_SAMPLER_DESC *out, unsigned *word, __int64 a3, __int64 a4, int shaderVisibility)
purpose: Decodes a 32-bit packed sampler word (the words kept in the draw state at +5704 + 4 * slot) into a D3D12 static sampler description.

behavior.text: filter: if bits 6..9 are all set the filter is anisotropic (0x55); otherwise bit 6 = MIN linear (0x10), bit 9 = MAG linear (0x04), bit 8 = MIP linear (0x01); bit 27 adds the comparison flag (0x80). Bit 7 is only read for the anisotropic test.
address modes: AddressU = (word & 3) + 1, AddressV = ((word >> 2) & 3) + 1, AddressW = ((word >> 4) & 3) + 1 (1 wrap, 2 mirror, 3 clamp, 4 border, 5 mirror once).

MipLODBias = (signed 10-bit field word bits 10..19) * 0.03125 (the shift pair (word << 12) >> 22); MaxAnisotropy = {1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16}[(word >> 24) & 7]; ComparisonFunc = ((word >> 28) & 7) + 1; MinLOD = (word >> 20) & 0xF; MaxLOD = FLT_MAX when bit 7 or bit 8 is set (mips enabled), otherwise MinLOD; BorderColor = 0 (transparent black); the 52-byte description is completed with ShaderRegister = 0 and RegisterSpace = 0 (+40 / +44) and ShaderVisibility = a5 (+48).

the default word dword_141D8BC7C holds 0xFFFFFFFF in the database. That value decodes as anisotropic with the comparison flag, BORDER addressing on all axes and MinLOD 15 (the contexts store it masked with 0x7FFFFFFF, which drops bit 31). It is not the runtime value.

the default word is 0 at runtime. It decodes as point filtering, WRAP addressing on all axes, MinLOD = MaxLOD = 0, with MaxAnisotropy 1 and ComparisonFunc NEVER (unused: the comparison filter flag is clear). Every slot a fresh context or a reset context stores from the default (RenderContext_ResetFrame for all 64 slots, sub_14003A048) therefore holds 0.

all 15 references to dword_141D8BC7C are reads (sub_14003A048, RenderContext_ResetFrame, sub_1400CEB4C, sub_1400CF9BC, UICommandRing_Flush, UIRender_ApplyDrawState, sub_1403CB56C, PostTarget_DrawFitted, CharaRender_SubmitQuads). No direct xref writes it; the code that changes it from the IDB value to 0 was not found statically.

behavior.basis: (live read 2026-10-30; names on the NameSlotTable_Lookup sheet)
behavior.text: the slot index of a word in the +5704 array is the id from the sampler name table: 12 ccc_ppn_sampler, 13 ccc_lln_sampler, 14 g_Sampler, 15 g_Sampler_tMaskBuffer, 16 ccc_lln_sampler_tMaskBuffer, up to 30 sSampler3 (31 entries, the full list is on that sheet). The UI draw word goes to slots 14 and 15 (UIRender_ApplyDrawState); the technique defaults for the Job Tree shadow are slots 13 and 16 (GUILayer_BlurShadowPass).

behavior.basis: (live read 2026-10-28, ShaderSelector_Apply entry with r8 = 2 = the SDF font renderer's call, 300 records on the Job Tree: slots 0..7 of state+5704 all 0x26A)
behavior.text: the SDF text atlas sampler is min / mag linear, mip point, CLAMP on U / V / W, MinLOD = MaxLOD = 0, i.e. plain bilinear with clamping. The generic UI draw word (UIRender_ApplyDrawState a2+4, 368 of 400 records) is 0x2C0: min / mag linear, mip point, WRAP, MinLOD 0, MaxLOD FLT_MAX; the rest are 0 (point, wrap). The UI .tex headers carry one mip, so the mip fields do not matter on this screen.

the chara atlas slot clears bits 6..9 (point filtering, MinLOD = MaxLOD = 15) and the three LUT slots have bits 6 and 9 set with 7 and 8 clear (0x240 pattern): min / mag linear, mip POINT, MinLOD = MaxLOD = 15 (i.e. the last mip that exists), BORDER addressing. So the LUT is sampled bilinearly (as render_chara models), and the atlas with a point filter.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140068D54). Bits 6..9 equal to 0xE (a7 & 0x3C0 == 0x380 in the caller) select 'no static sampler' (the shader samples through a descriptor-table sampler instead).
open_questions: ? the code that makes dword_141D8BC7C 0 at runtime (all 15 references read it, none writes it). Which bit pattern selects the descriptor-table path in the caller (0x380), and whether any UI slot uses it; whether the LUT texture really has a single mip (MinLOD 15 would force a 1 x 1 level otherwise).

callees: memset, sub_140245A88, sub_140245C84, sub_14037ABBC, sub_140245D44, sub_14039D828, EventThread_Yield, CardSlot_IsValid, sub_14021849C, SceneTask_Start, sub_1402F7F4C, sub_1402D3918, Status_BuildFlagMasks, sub_14033FB84, sub_14031EF70, sub_140273D78, sub_1402B2004, sub_14025F7C0, sub_1402B1CD0, sub_140283E24, sub_1402B2124, sub_140283F64, sub_1401D6F9C, sub_1400EC678, sub_1400ECC5C, sub_14013EA54, sub_14013EE4C, sub_14037ADB8, sub_140257354, EventVar_Write, sub_1402F41D0, GameData_ReadSectors, sub_14033D6B0, sub_140246078, sub_140210AF0, sub_1402B20C0, SceneVar_Write, sub_1402BA744, sub_14024599C, sub_1402D38EC, sub_1402BAB04, sub_1400E43B4, sub_1401DDEC4, sub_1401E2D64, sub_1401E3744, sub_14039DCE8
purpose: The boot-time save clear: it fills the save cache and the auto slot with the empty pattern, resets the save manager and the auto-slot header, and starts the reload state machine.

behavior.text: the slot cache at 0x142C8B970 is filled with 0xFF over 0x1EA488 bytes, and the 0x9CE4-byte auto-slot image at 0x142E75DF8 with 0xFF as well (the fill byte is edx = -1).

the clear-and-reload state machine is started with sub_140245C84 and the auto-slot header is imported with sub_14021849C.
the single caller is the boot sequence, so this runs before any slot is read.
the 0x1EA488 cache size is the flat image of the 50 manual slots, which is why the whole image is cleared at once.
whether a card-present boot with an absent file takes the same clear path; the condition was not decoded.

name: Save_ResumeCheckpoint
purpose: After a slot load, decides whether the auto-slot checkpoint is a plain world-map one: only then it copies the checkpoint into the save work block and unpacks it to the live records. For every other case (including a battle resume) it only raises a flag.

behavior.text: calls sub_14021849C(arg, 0) (the classic auto-slot header import); when that returns false the function sets dword_142E7FF68 = 1 and returns (it does not return silently).

otherwise reads the payload part count: qword_143CD9EE0 is a pointer to the auto-slot object; the pointer at +0x3D5188 (4,018,568) of it points at an object whose dword at +12 is read (I: the payload part count, as the earlier sheet named it), clamped to 2. A null object or null header counts as 2.
when the part count is not 0, the function only sets dword_142E7FF68 = 1 and returns: SaveWork_UnpackToLive does not run.
when the part count is 0: calls sub_140257354, points Src at g_SaveWorkCurrent, copies 0x9CE4 bytes from g_SaveCheckpointCopy to it with memmove and tail-jumps to SaveWork_UnpackToLive(0).

a battle autosave has payload parts (a battle snapshot), so a battle resumed from it takes the flag-only path and its live unit records come from the battle snapshot (Battle_RestoreSceneVars), not from SaveWork_UnpackToLive; a world-map autosave has part count 0 and unpacks. Seen live 2026-11-09: a hook on SaveWork_UnpackToLive logged nothing during a cold battle resume, while a world-map autosave load logged. See the behaviour ResumedBattleRestoresUnitRecordsWithoutUnpack.
the two callers are the title-screen load state and a load-confirmation path.
what dword_142E7FF68 = 1 triggers for the battle path (its readers were not traced).

notes: Whole function read (decompiled in IDA, 2026-11-09), rewritten: the earlier sheet said the function returns when the header import fails and that a "check byte at 0x143CD9EE0" must be set (it is a pointer), and that memcpy is used (it is memmove).

name: SaveWork_CopyErrandState
purpose: Copies the party-wide status masks, the errand arrays and the active errand slot records between a save work block and the live globals, in the direction the second argument selects.

behavior.text: the older index entry points at three int3 padding bytes; the body starts at 0x14027966C, which is the target of every call.
the first argument is the base of the save work block and the second is the direction: 1 copies work to live, 0 copies live to work.
the work block is read at fixed offsets (+0x114, +0x22C and later sub-blocks), each sub-block copied as a run of 16-byte units with a tail.
the live side is the contiguous state region that begins at the party-wide status masks 0x1411A6A70; this body moves the errand part that follows the masks and never touches the masks themselves.
the direction test is repeated in front of every sub-block, so the same routine serves the capture and the restore path.
it returns without a value and calls no helper; it is a pure byte mover.
the sub-blocks correspond to the errand and status state named in the save-layout records; the exact length of each was not counted here.
where the work block itself is allocated and whether it is cleared before a capture; this body only moves bytes.

notes: The older index entry is padding; the real body starts three bytes later at 0x14027966C. Direction and offsets read from the body; the block lengths belong to the save-format records.

name: Scenario_CheckBattleRecord
purpose: Finds the scenario setup record of the current event and lets the battle set-up continue only for a battle record.

behavior.text: linear search of up to 887 records (24 bytes) of the scenario setup table (0x1408ECAB0) by the 16-bit event number; 0 ends the search.
a record whose byte +0x14 is not 0x80, or no record, sets the battle state to 59.
otherwise links two entries for the current slot into a list and advances a counter; at 30 the state is set to 59 too.

notes: Read: the search and the state checks; the list entries are not identified.
open_questions: ?: what battle state 59 is; what the linked entries are.

name: ScenarioSetup_ApplyRecord
callers: sub_14020E578 (the scene entry; it turns refresh state 2 into 3 before the call, so every scene start rebuilds), sub_1402357C4, EventUnitBlock_RunTask (one event instruction)
callees: SceneVar_Read, SceneVar_Write, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdTable_GetEntryCount, NxdTable_GetLeafCount3, NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys3, NxdEntry_GetRow, SaveWork_UnpackToLive_Repair, EventChain_Find, sub_140257384, sub_140326080
purpose: At a scene start, applies the scenario setup record of the scene's event to the scene variables and rebuilds the per-event word table; in the mid-event refresh it only re-reads two scene bytes through the event's link.

behavior.text: when the refresh state word (0x140D408F4) is 2 (set by one event instruction in EventUnitBlock_RunTask and by sub_1402357C4, each while scene variable 508 is 0, right before they call this function), it clears the scene bytes 0x140C6AD7A / 0x140C6AD76, reads g_BattleMapWords[var 39], and when the word is non-zero searches the records for the event number (w & 0xFF) + ((w >> 2) & 0x300) and copies that record's bytes +13 / +14 into them; nothing else is done (the table is not rebuilt).

otherwise: clears scene variables 112..143, sets 509, moves var 39 on to the next event when variable 100 asks for it (with fixed jumps 90 -> 116, 298 -> 328, 740 / 742 -> 678), then rebuilds the words: for every record up to the first whose event number is 0 (bound 887, an immediate loaded into a register that also bounds the next search) it stores byte +18 + (byte +19 << 10), OR byte +20 << 8, at words[the record's event number].
after the loop it writes words 401..404 and 400 as constants (400 and 404 depend on scene variable 510).
then it searches the records for the scene's event (var 39, or the resume copy when the resume flag is 1); no record: variables 48 and 39 are set to 0 and it returns.

with a record it reads the fields into scene variables: map byte +2 -> 51 (event 93 keeps 51), +3 nibbles -> 48 / 35, +4 -> 36, +7 or +15 -> 50, +9 / +11 -> 53 / 54 and their count -> 52, +17 -> 511, the two scene bytes +13 / +14, and collects the scene's characters from the EnhancedBattleEvent rows of the key at +22 (it returns before writing variable 51 when that key has no row, has 16 or more entries, or the list reaches 512 words).
event numbers are read sign-extended from 16 bits in every search.

byte +3 low nibble is the weather level (scene variable 35, 0..4) and the high nibble the map state (variable 48, 0..15); byte +4 is the night flag (variable 36). What they select: see the behaviours ScenarioWeatherLevelAndNightFlag and ScenarioMapStateIsOnlyAMapVariationSelector.

bytes +5 and +6 are stored sign-extended in the scene words 0x140D407C4 / 0x140D407C8, the music tracks of music slots 1 and 2 (0 = none); Scene_StartMusic reads them and starts them through Music_StartSceneTracks.

byte +13 is a portrait code (stored at 0x140C6AD7A) and byte +14 the event unit number that shows it (0x140C6AD76); the turn panel small-face code (sub_14022AA88) gives a unit whose +401 equals the second byte the first byte as face code, and the portrait cache builder sub_140300768 takes the code of its entry 54 from it.
byte +15 replaces +7 as the unit entry number while scene variable 508 is set and dword_142FF9F4C is 0; the event viewer entry page (sub_1402D28C8) writes variable 508 = 1 for a replay.

byte +17 is copied to variable 511 only when the area at +9 is non-zero: with 511 set the deployment grid pre-fills its first free cell with party member 0 and the commence check (DeploymentGrid_CommenceCheck) refuses a formation without member 0.
byte +21 is read by neither ScenarioSetup_ApplyRecord nor Scenario_CheckBattleRecord, and no other code refers to the record block (whole-image operand census).

each word of the character list collected from the EnhancedBattleEvent rows is the row's 16-bit condition opcode (column condition, row +4); a row whose value is 0 is skipped, any other value is appended to the word list at 0x140D3F550 as the trigger-condition opcode.

notes: Read: the whole decompilation and the three loops in the disassembly; the character list collected from EnhancedBattleEvent only as far as its bounds. An older sheet under the address name described this function as the filler of a save snapshot block; that was wrong.
open_questions: ?: what the flag bits 8, 9 and 12..15 of the word mean to the battle functions that test them.

name: Scene_StartMusic
callees: NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, SceneVar_Read, SceneCallback_Dispatch, Music_StartSceneTracks, sub_1402B1E74, sub_1402CD758, sub_140226C2C, sub_14024A528, sub_140257440
purpose: At a scene start, keeps the running music when the scene's track is the one already playing, otherwise starts the scene's tracks.

behavior.text: runs only when word_140D407CC is non-zero and scene variable 39 is not in 410..425.

when the previous pair (words 0x140D4091C / 0x140D408FC) is empty and a resume capture is active (DWORD2(xmmword_142FF9E24) == 1), both tracks come from qword_140816CD0 into the scene words 0x140D407C4 / 0x140D407C8.

otherwise it calls Music_StartSceneTracks(track1, track2).
afterwards the previous pair is set to the new pair, sub_14024A528(99, ...) runs, and sub_140226C2C runs unless dword_143807790 is 3.
on a skip with a non-playing scene it forces track 12 when the EventId row (variable 39) has +0x1C == 2 and dword_142E8A134 is 0; the meaning of that EventId field is not decoded.

open_questions: ? the exact role of the previous-pair words (0x140D4091C / 0x140D408FC) and of word_140D40900.

name: SceneCallback_Dispatch

Two of the callers, sub_14033D4C0 and the routine named NaptrDnsRecordConvert_1 in the IDB, are outside the event code.

purpose: Calls the callback in the global function pointer `qword_140D40940` for modes 0 to 6. The caller sets that pointer first; the mode decides what the callback receives.

behavior.text: if `dword_140D40948` (the current task index) is not zero, it writes zero to the qwords at +96 and +104 of block 0 of the task table `off_140783088`, whatever the index is.
mode 0 calls qword_140D40940 with the mode (0) as its argument.
modes 1 to 6 call it with `arg`, and its return value is returned.
any other mode returns 0 without calling anything.
the callback pointer is not tested for null. Callers in the visible code use modes 1, 2, 3 and 4. EventScript_Run uses mode 1 three times and mode 3 once.
some callers pass more arguments than the two declared here; the extra values are ignored.
