open_questions: Who sets qword_140D40940 for the event system and what each mode does in the callback; why modes 5 and 6 have no callers in the code read; what the two words at block 0 +96 and +104 are used for.

name: SceneColourPair_WriteVertexColours
purpose: Writes the scene's two-colour pair (qword_14114A4E8) into the colour entries of four vertices of a render block, a two-colour vertical gradient.

behavior.text: first links three render blocks of the object at qword_140DE2BC8 (at +1769608, +1769472 and +1769576) into the list at +6128 of the object at +1769640 and tags each with word_14114A4E4.

writes the pair to four consecutive vertex colour entries of the block at qword_140DE2BC8 + 1769484: bytes 0..2 of the pair (colour 1) into the entries at +1769484 and +1769492, bytes 4..6 (colour 2) into the entries at +1769500 and +1769508, each value as (byte * 128) / 255.
then calls sub_14027483C with the render block and the light tables.
that the two colours are the top and bottom of the background gradient rests on the colour 1 / colour 2 order of the four entries; the vertex layout was not read.

notes: The pair is set by MapBlock_RunCommand's light block (with the Map variation element's background_color members overriding it) and moved by sub_1402F52D8 and ClutManager_Update (fades).
open_questions: ? what the other writes of the function (the long tail after the vertex colours) do.

name: SceneGroup_ResolveId
callers: EventScript_Run (opcode 0x81 through the call at 0x14023D716, and opcode 0x80 through the call at 0x14023D79C); SceneGroup_SetFlag04 (opcodes 0x6C and 0x6D); sub_140241CB0 (opcode 0x83 body); sub_140240D5C, sub_140240F34, sub_1402416C8, sub_140241DF8, sub_140241EC4 and sub_140241FF0 (helper bodies that are called from EventScript_Run).
purpose: Reads an operand id and decides whether it names one unit or a group: ids 1 to 255 are resolved to a unit id, and ids 0 and 256 and up select a group mode for SceneUnit_TestGroupMember.

behavior.text: if *id is 0 it writes 1 to *groupMode, leaves *id unchanged and returns 1.

if *id is 256 or more it writes *id - 254 to *groupMode (so ids 256, 257, 258 and 259 give modes 2, 3, 4 and 5), leaves *id unchanged and returns 1. Larger ids give larger modes, which the group test treats as no match.

for ids 1 to 255 it calls EventRef_ResolveSlot with the id, stores the result in *id as a 16-bit value and writes 0 to *groupMode. It returns 0 when the result is 2000 (0x7D0, no unit) and 1 otherwise.
how ids 1 to 255 map to slots (including the special ids 100 to 105) is described in EventRef_ResolveSlot.

notes: The id values 0 and 256 and up are group selectors; the operand itself never names a group by byte, only through this 16-bit range.
open_questions: What the 16 records scanned for id 104 and the unit data behind ids 105 and above hold; see EventRef_ResolveSlot.

name: SceneGroup_SetFlag04
callers: EventScript_Run at 0x14023D1B5 and 0x14023D298 (opcodes 0x6D and 0x6C, set = 1 and set = 0 in the pseudocode, per the opcode records).
purpose: The shared body of opcodes 0x6C and 0x6D: sets or clears bit 0x04 of byte +143 of each unit selected by the operand.

behavior.text: copies selector into a local word and calls SceneGroup_ResolveId on it; if that returns 0 the function does nothing more.
loops over keys 0 to 20. For each key, SceneUnit_TestGroupMember returns nonzero when the key is in the group; the key is then in the local word.

for each member, it finds the unit node with SceneObject_FindBySlot. When set is nonzero it sets bit 0x04 of the byte at node+0x8F (143). When set is zero it clears that bit. A missing node is skipped.
the loop stops after the first member when the group mode is 0 (a single unit).
the return value is whatever the last call left in rax; no value is set on purpose.

notes: This is the flag-04 companion of the 0x81 path, which sets bit 0x02 at the same offset +143.
open_questions: What bit 0x04 at +143 controls in the game.

name: SceneMsgTask_Run
callers: the scene task scheduler (the entry is reached through the scene task table; there is no direct call site, and the dispatcher was not read)
callees: sub_1400FC85C, sub_1400EF9EC, sub_1400E5F78, sub_1400EEC18, sub_1401EC01C, sub_140243330, SceneTask_WaitFrame, SceneTask_Terminate and other scene and UI helpers (39 direct calls in all)
purpose: Scene task that reads the current scene's message word and dispatches a message descriptor built from it.

behavior.text: reads the current scene task record, selected by dword_140D40948 in the table at off_140783088 (entry index shifted left 8, a 256-byte stride).
takes the 16-bit message word at record +28 (0x1C); group = word >> 11 selects qword_140D40990[group] (32 entries), index = word & 0x7FF.
sub_1400FC85C(group object, &class, &kind) yields the descriptor's class and kind.
passes the descriptor to sub_1400EF9EC and sub_1400E5F78, and posts the word to the text command at sub_140243330.
some scene codes are handled before the message dispatch (codes 0x1F and 0x2B are compared), and one branch resolves index 0x1C5 through the battle message object.
the traced descriptor {0, 2, 10, 0x5062} is group 10, index 98 of an event-script message (0x5062 = 10 << 11 | 98).
whether the banner call traced during an ability cast came from this task is not established.
the function returns no value and runs as a task, not as a callee.
the message word is an event-script message reference, not an ability or item id; the traced descriptor with group 10 and index 98 is consistent with that.
its role in battle is inferred; the scene task table and the message group table are read, but the task's place in the battle banner path was not proven.
which scene table entry selects this task and what the pre-dispatch scene codes mean.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140231D7C). It is a void(void) scene task, 0x6B8 bytes (about 1.7 KB). Read for the group and kind decode, as part of the item text research; the task scheduler that reaches it was not read.
open_questions: Whether it produces any battle banner descriptor (the traced ability-cast banner call is not attributed to it); what sub_1400EF9EC and sub_1400E5F78 do with the descriptor; what the group objects at qword_140D40990 are; the task-table slot that runs it; the meaning of the 0x1C5 special case.

name: SceneObject_FindBySlot
callers: About 121 routines with 207 call sites, including EventScript_Run (more than ten sites), EventRef_ResolveSlot (the ref 105 path), EventMessage_Task (2) and many scene and world-map routines.
purpose: Finds the object list node for a slot number. It returns the node or null, and it is the most widely called lookup in the scene code.

behavior.text: walks a singly linked list from the head in `qword_140D3A410`. The next pointer is the qword at node +0, and the list ends at null.

a node's key is the low byte of the qword at node +8. The test compares that byte with the argument as a 16-bit value, so only slots 0 to 255 can match; negative values and values above 255 never match.
returns the first matching node pointer, or null when the list ends. It reads no other field and writes nothing.
a node is one object record of the scene object list, and the slot is the object's id byte.

notes: The slot passed here is the same slot number that EventRef_ResolveSlot returns. Only node +0, +8 and +328 are read by the functions in this group.
open_questions: The rest of the node layout, what creates and removes nodes, and why the key is compared as one byte.

name: SceneObject_FindByUnitIndex
purpose: Walks the scene object list and returns the object whose battle unit record has the given unit index, or null.

behavior.text: the list head is `qword_140D3A410` (next pointer at +0); the object's battle unit record pointer is at +0x148 and its unit index at record +444.

name: SceneObject_SnapFieldBands
purpose: Walks the linked list at qword_140D3A410 and sets a 16-bit field of each entry from that entry's low 12 bits of another field; EventScript_Run calls it at the start of the 0xE3 transition path.

behavior.text: starts at qword_140D3A410 and follows the first qword of each entry as the next pointer until it reaches null.
for each entry it reads a 16-bit field at an offset inside the entry that the decompile expresses through the entry's third sub-record (exact byte offset not resolved) and keeps its low 12 bits.
when those bits are 512 to 1535 it writes 1024 to the second 16-bit field of the entry; when they are 1536 to 2559 it writes 2048; when they are 2560 to 3583 it writes 3072.
otherwise, including values below 512 and from 3584 up, it writes 0 to that field.
returns the end of the list (null).

notes: The same list is walked by the mode 255 branch of EventScript_SetupScene.
open_questions: What the two fields of each list entry are; what the value written represents; the exact byte offsets, which the decompile shows only as field-unit offsets.

name: SceneObjects_StepStates
callers: CharaPalette_ReloadForShape, sub_140207880, sub_14020BCF0, sub_14020CC50, sub_14020DC78, sub_14020E174, sub_140210AF0
callees: sub_14026CAA4, sub_140266180, sub_140266288, sub_1402F7C20, SceneUnit_SetFlag156, SceneUnit_Release
purpose: Per-update pass over the drawn units: runs three per-unit helpers and, for a unit whose two state bits read 'gone', takes it off the field and releases its drawing.

behavior.text: for each node of g_SceneObjectList: sub_14026CAA4; sub_140266180 unless a byte at +27 of its third block is 45 or 49 (masked compare); sub_140266288 when a flag byte is set.

state bits (byte +60 of its eighth block, bits 4..5): value 1 -> becomes 2 and starts a screen-tint step (sub_1402F7C20(4, 4, slot, -31, -31, -31)); value 2 -> unless the unit is the one dword_140CF873C names (SceneUnit_SetFlag156 for it), sets both bits, writes 0xFF to its battle record's slot byte and 0x80 to its on-field byte (when the slot byte was not already 0xFF), and calls SceneUnit_Release.
the state value 2 is a unit vanishing from the field (the step that frees its drawing slot and, when unshared, its look).

open_questions: ? which game events set the state to 1 or 2 (KO, crystal, chest, leaving).

name: ScenePad_UpdateRepeat
purpose: Updates the held-button repeat for the second task table. The twin of EventPad_UpdateRepeat.

behavior.text: acts only when `word_140D408E8` is 2 and the current index `dword_140D40948` is non-zero.

when the current task's flag qword (`qword_140D40B38[256 * index]`) is 1, it reloads the repeat cell `off_1407DCB48` from `dword_142FEC518`, and, while the button group id 0x1D in the mask `off_1407DD348` is held, counts frames in `dword_142FF8278`.
when the count reaches the threshold (the byte at 0x1407829FF divided by `dword_140782D14`) it writes the repeat mask into the cell and resets the count; otherwise it resets the count.
this is the same auto-repeat idea as EventPad_UpdateRepeat, applied while a scene task owns the input.

notes: Button ids are not decoded.

name: ScenePlacement_WriteGroup
purpose: Writes a 7-byte placement record for each unit of a unit or group that passes the group test against the 21 keys, each record headed from a cell position given by the operands. Opcode 0x69 calls it.

behavior.text: `operands` points at the operand bytes after the opcode. Operands 1 and 2 are the 16-bit unit or group reference (operand 1 is the low byte). Operand 3 is a cell x value and operand 4 a cell y value, each one byte. Operand 5 is not read. Operand 6 goes into record byte 1, operand 7 indexes the byte table at 0x1406720B0 (its value goes into record byte 2), and operand 8 is the scale.
it resolves the reference with SceneGroup_ResolveId and returns, writing nothing, when that returns 0. Nothing in the routine tests the resolved slot against 0 to 20.
it walks the same 21 keys at 0x1406720C0, in the same order as ScenePlacement_WritePair, calling SceneUnit_TestGroupMember with the reference for each key. A failed test goes on to the next key.
on a pass, the unit whose slot is in the reference after the test gets a record. The routine copies that unit's words with SceneUnit_CopyField4C (out[0] = node +0x4C, out[2] = node +0x50).

heading: Y = 28 times operand 4, plus 14, minus the unit's +0x50 word; X = 28 times operand 3, plus 14, minus the unit's +0x4C word; both as signed 16-bit values. H = 3072 minus the truncated value of atan2(Y, X) times 4096 divided by 2 pi.

the record is 7 bytes at table unk_142FEC580 plus 7 times the unit slot. Byte 0 = bits 8 to 11 of H. Byte 1 = operand 6. Byte 2 = the byte at 0x1406720B0 indexed by operand 7. Bytes 3 and 4 = 0 and 1 (the 16-bit value 256). Byte 5 is not written. Byte 6 = the count times operand 8, divided by 4 rounded down, where the count is 1 for the first record of the call and rises by one after each write.
after each write, if the group mode output of the test is zero, the walk stops. A failed test does not stop it.
the record offset is 7 times the slot number with no bound test, so a slot of 21 or more is written at an offset past the 21 rows.
the routine writes only the table rows; it changes no object fields.

notes: Unlike ScenePlacement_WritePair it writes no first-unit record and makes no difference check, and its heading comes from the cell position instead of a second unit.
open_questions: Whether a single-unit reference can resolve to a slot of 21 or more and reach the record write; what operand 5 is for (not read here); what the cell scale 28 and the offset 14 are in the game.

name: ScenePlacement_WritePair
callers: EventScript_Run (one call at 0x14023BD4E: opcode 0x2C enters just before it and clears the flag register, so it passes flag 0; opcode 0x53 jumps in after that clear and passes the flag 1 that the interpreter sets at the start of each instruction); EventSubScript_RunTask (call at 0x140235BDB for opcode 0x53, passing 1).
callees: SceneGroup_ResolveId, EventRef_ResolveSlot, SceneUnit_TestGroupMember, SceneUnit_CopyField4C (called twice per match), atan2f (C library)
purpose: Writes 7-byte placement records for a pair of units: the second unit for each valid, different unit that passes the group test, and the first unit too when flag is 0, with headings computed from the two units' position words. Opcode 0x2C calls it with flag 0 and opcode 0x53 with flag 1.

behavior.text: `operands` points at the operand bytes after the opcode. The first unit reference is the 16-bit value at operands 1 and 2 (operand 1 is the low byte). The second reference is the 16-bit value at operands 3 and 4. Operand 5 goes into record byte 1, operand 6 indexes the byte table at 0x1406720B0 (its value goes into record byte 2), and operand 7 is the scale.

it resolves the second reference with SceneGroup_ResolveId and returns at once, writing nothing, when that returns 0. It then resolves the first reference with EventRef_ResolveSlot and returns unless the result is 0 to 20 (an unsigned 16-bit compare).

it walks the 21 16-bit keys at 0x1406720C0 in this order: 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 3, 7, 11, 15. For each key it calls SceneUnit_TestGroupMember with the second reference; a failed test goes on to the next key.

when the test passes and the slot now held in the second reference differs from the first unit's slot, it copies the position words of both units with SceneUnit_CopyField4C. If that slot is 0 to 20, it writes the records described below. After that, whatever the slot was, the walk stops when the group mode output of the test is zero.
a passing key whose slot equals the first unit's slot is skipped, and it does not stop the walk.

CopyField4C writes out[0] (the unit's word at node +0x4C) and out[2] (the word at node +0x50). Y is the second unit's +0x50 word minus the first unit's +0x50 word, and X is the second unit's +0x4C word minus the first unit's +0x4C word, both as signed 16-bit values. The heading H is 3072 minus the truncated value of atan2(Y, X) times 4096 divided by 2 pi.

each record is 7 bytes at table unk_142FEC580 plus 7 times the unit slot. The first unit's record (written only when flag is 0) uses H; the second unit's record uses H minus 2048, which is the opposite heading.

byte 0 = bits 8 to 11 of the heading value used for that record. Byte 1 = operand 5. Byte 2 = the byte at 0x1406720B0 indexed by operand 6. Bytes 3 and 4 = 0 and 1 (the 16-bit value 256). Byte 5 is not written. Byte 6 = operand 7 divided by 4, rounded down, for the first unit's record. For the second unit's record, byte 6 = the count times operand 7, divided by 4 rounded down, where the count is 1 for the first write of the call and rises by one after each second-unit write.
the first unit's record is written before the second unit's, and both sit in the same branch (second slot 0 to 20 and different from the first).
the routine changes no object fields; its only writes are the 7-byte table rows.

notes: The first unit's record exists only for flag 0, so a caller that passes another flag gets the second unit's record alone.
open_questions: What the three position words at node +0x4C, +0x4E and +0x50 mean in the game; what the 21 keys and the byte table at 0x1406720B0 describe; what the game reads from the 7-byte records (heading, table value, scale).

name: ScenePresetOverrides_Apply
purpose: Copies the sprite palette and pose entries named by the current scene's preset list into the live sprite tables.

behavior.text: the list is chosen by the scene id (22, 27, 30, 47 and 50 each have one, a default list otherwise); each list is null terminated.
per record: a variant 0..2 selects one of three groups of the 144-byte job-sprite row, then two copies write the sprite tables for the record's unit slot and set a terminator.

open_questions: ?: what the scenes' presets are in the game.

name: ScenePreview_ClaimForUnit
callers: EventScript_Run (opcode 0x45 path, at the calls near 0x14023B208 to 0x14023CA9F); sub_1402029DC, EventSubScript_RunTask, EventUnitBlock_RunTask and sub_140269DC4 (helpers).
purpose: For one unit: sets its state words at +0x0E and +0x1F8 to 1 and claims its preview entry. Used by opcode 0x45 on the unit side.

behavior.text: calls SceneObject_FindBySlot(key). If there is no unit node it returns 0.
sets the words at node+0x0E and node+0x1F8 to 1.
reads the node's sub-record pointer at +0x148. When it is nonzero, it reads the byte at sub-record +0x1BC (the preview index) and calls sub_1402718CC with that index.
returns 1 when the node exists.

BattleUnit_RevealOnField(index) puts the battle unit record on the field when it is off it (detail on its sheet); so this turns a unit that is already drawn but not placed (an entry built with presence 0xC0) into a unit on the field.

notes: The brief calls this the release side of opcode 0x45; in the code it claims the entry (writes the slot into the owner byte), and the release is not in this function. Cross-check note: 0xC0 is an entry presence value (Battle_PlaceEntryUnits), not a constant of this body.
open_questions: What word_14114B0B4 and byte_140D405A2 hold. The release path: one EventScript_Run case (at 0x14023BFA0) writes 0xFF to the record slot byte and a register value to +0x1B5; which opcode owns it is not confirmed.

name: ScenePreview_FindEntry
callers: 17 routines (26 call sites): EventScript_Run (3), EventRef_ResolveSlot (4), sub_1402DE204 (4), sub_1402C60E4 (2), and about 11 others including sub_1400CB870, sub_140226CA0, sub_140227458, EventUnitBlock_RunTask, sub_140239144, sub_140239294, sub_140240B8C, sub_1402416C8 and sub_14033BE88.
purpose: Finds a preview-unit record by a one-byte key and reports how it was found through the status pointer. The table is 21 records of 512 bytes at g_BattleUnitTable.

behavior.text: the table is 21 records of 512 bytes, starting at `g_BattleUnitTable` (0x141853CE0) and ending at 0x1418566E0. The key is compared with byte +401 of each record; the flag bytes read are +1, +97, +98 and +437.

pass 1, records 0 to 20 in order: a record matches when byte +1 is not 0xFF and byte +401 equals the key. The status is the record index (0 to 20), or -3 when bit 0x40 of byte +97 or bit 0x01 of byte +98 is set. The record pointer is returned in both cases.

pass 2, only when pass 1 finds nothing: a record matches when byte +1 is 0xFF, byte +401 equals the key and byte +437 is not 0xFF. Byte +437 = 0 gives status -2, 0x80 gives -3 and 2 gives -6; each returns that record. Other values are skipped.
when nothing matches it returns null and sets status -3.
the key is a char parameter, so only its low 8 bits are compared. The function writes nothing else and calls nothing.

notes: sub_140272538 reads the same records by byte +0 (its unit id), so each record carries a unit id at +0 and a second id at +401.
open_questions: What bytes +1, +97, +98, +401 and +437 represent, and what the status codes -2, -3 and -6 mean to the callers.

name: ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot
callers: 21 routines (30 call sites): EventScript_Run (10), EventRef_ResolveSlot, EventMessage_Task, sub_140221C00, sub_140222740, sub_140214284, sub_1402356B0, sub_140240A78, sub_1402416C8, EventUnitStatus_ApplyTask, sub_140241BD0, sub_140241CB0, sub_1402D9490, sub_1402D9F4C, sub_1402DE204 and sub_1402DE418, among others.
purpose: Returns the preview index of the object in a slot: byte +444 of the object's preview data, or -1 when the slot has no object or no preview data.

behavior.text: calls SceneObject_FindBySlot(slot). When the node exists and the pointer at node +328 is not null, it returns the byte at that pointer +444, a value from 0 to 255.
otherwise it returns 0xFFFFFFFF, which is -1 as a signed 32-bit value. EventRef_ResolveSlot and EventScript_Run test for that value.
callers use the result as a record index into g_BattleUnitTable (512 bytes per record), for example `g_BattleUnitTable + 512 * result` in EventRef_ResolveSlot.
the preview index is the record number in g_BattleUnitTable for the object.

notes: Its inverse is ScenePreview_SlotOfIndex.
open_questions: What the object's preview data at node +328 is, and what byte +444 holds beyond its use as a record index.

name: ScenePreview_ShowEntry
purpose: Shows the preview-table entry for a slot: clears the preview globals, claims the entry and queues a draw entry built from the record's fields. Used by opcode 0x45.

behavior.text: clears dword_141856720, the qword at xmmword_140CE3240, the dword at +8 of that global and qword_140CE3250.
when slot is 0 to 20 it uses the record g_PreviewUnitTable + slot*512; otherwise the record pointer is null.
calls BattleUnit_RevealOnField(slot): the preview table is the battle unit table, so a parked entry record (slot byte 0xFF, on-field byte 0) is put on the field.

calls sub_1403041A4 with the record's byte +79, byte +80, byte +81 bit 7, byte +81 low nibble, the word from +399 (0x18F) as the fifth argument, the word from +400 (0x190) as the sixth, 255 as the seventh, the record pointer as the eighth and flag as the ninth.
returns 1.

notes: sub_1403041A4 appends an 8-dword entry to the list at dword_141856720 (the count is its first dword, the limit is 16). A fifth argument of 170 or more sets the high word of that entry's second field to 1.
open_questions: What consumes the queued entries, what the record bytes +79, +80 and +81 mean, and what the flag argument selects.

name: ScenePreview_SlotOfIndex
callers: 13 routines (14 call sites): EventScript_Run (2), EventRef_ResolveSlot, sub_1400CB870, sub_14021F538, sub_14022AA88, sub_140233588, sub_1402346D0, EventUnitBlock_RunTask, sub_140239144, sub_140239294, sub_140240B8C, sub_1402DE204 and sub_140360048.
purpose: The reverse of ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot: finds the object whose preview index is the given value and returns its slot number.

behavior.text: walks the object list from `qword_140D3A410`, following the next pointer at node +0.
for each node whose pointer at node +328 is not null, it compares byte +444 of that pointer with the argument. The first match gives the slot, which is the low byte of the node key at +8.
returns 0xFFFFFFFF (-1 as a signed 32-bit value) when no node matches.
EventRef_ResolveSlot passes a record index of 0 to 20, or 21 when no record matched. The value is in ECX at the call; the decompiler does not show it as an argument.
the result is the slot of the object that uses the given preview record.

notes: Pairs with ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot. The decompiled signature shows no argument at the call site in EventRef_ResolveSlot; the value is the loop counter.
open_questions: Whether more than one object can share a preview index; the function returns the first one found in list order.

name: SceneState_Reset
purpose: Resets the shared scene state before a legacy scene and installs its menu node arrays.

behavior.text: clears a long list of scene words, resets the face display state, the dialogue face slots and the event skip words.

when the chara render manager exists stores pointers to seven nodes (stride 88) from slot 126, from 0x1408F2C10 (language 0) or 0x1408F2E80, then from 0x1408F30F0 two nodes, then seven nodes from slot 133 (0x1408FA5F0 or 0x1408FA890) and two from 0x1408FAB30.

notes: Read to the end of the node installation (1671 bytes).
open_questions: ?: the cleared words one by one.

name: SceneTask_FindFree
callers: 6 routines (31 call sites): EventScript_Run (23), sub_1402C72B8 (3), sub_1402C6514 (2), sub_1402C7DAC, sub_1402CB9E8 and sub_14038FE58.
callees: SceneTask_Terminate (only when no slot is free; it takes no argument, so the value left in the register is not used)
purpose: Finds a free slot in the second task table for a task that the caller is about to start with SceneTask_Start. EventScript_Run passes 16, which asks for any free slot from 1 to 16.

behavior.text: reads the high dword of `qword_142FF9EC0` as a 32-bit mask `m`; bit n of `m` marks slot n as taken.
when the argument is 16 or more, or its bit in `m` is set, it searches slots 1 to 16 from the start for one whose bit is clear and whose runnable qword (block +144 in `off_140783088`) is zero.
if that search fails, it searches again from slot 1 for a slot whose runnable qword is zero; this second search does not check the mask.
if the second search fails, it calls SceneTask_Terminate, which ends the current task, and returns 0.
when the argument is below 16 and its bit is clear, it returns the argument at once, without checking its runnable qword.
the bit test uses only the low 8 bits of the argument. Task blocks are 2048 bytes apart in `off_140783088`, so the runnable qword of slot n is at byte offset 2048 * n + 144.
EventScript_Run passes 16 at 22 of its 23 calls. The other call passes a value from ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot.

notes: The function does not start a task. It is called before SceneTask_Start, and SceneTask_Start is not one of its callers. I: the returned slot is the one the caller then starts.
open_questions: What sets the high dword of qword_142FF9EC0 and what its bits mean; what the callers do when it returns 0, since only EventScript_Run's calls were read.

name: SceneTask_FindTag
callers: 10 routines (19 call sites): EventScript_Run (7), sub_1403015A4 (3), sub_140227558 (2), sub_140228778, sub_14022A19C, sub_140234468, EventScript_LoadCurrent, sub_1402F8684, sub_140338A28 and sub_1403980AC.
purpose: Finds a running task in the second table by its tag. The event script uses it to wait while a task of a given kind is still running.

behavior.text: checks slots 1 to 16 in order and returns the first slot that matches.
skips slot `dword_140D40948` (the current task), any slot whose runnable qword at block +144 of `off_140783088` is zero, and any slot whose tag differs.
the tag of slot n is the qword at `qword_140D40B38 + 2048 * n` (the same as `qword_140D40B38[256 * n]`). It is compared with the whole argument as a 64-bit value.
returns the slot number 1 to 16, or 0 when no task matches.
EventColor_Task writes tag 6 and EventCamera_MoveTask writes tag 7 into this tag table, which is the table read here.

notes: The tag table `qword_140D40B38` is separate from the task table `off_140783088`, but both use 2048-byte blocks indexed by slot. EventScript_Run's calls use tags 8, 13, 14, 55 and 61.
open_questions: Which task kinds carry tags 8, 13, 14, 55 and 61.

name: SceneTask_Start
callers: About 46 callers, including the event dispatcher `sub_14023A868`.
purpose: Starts a task in the second task table: resets the slot's block, marks it runnable and records its entry function so its thread begins there.

behavior.text: clears `dword_140811624`, then fills the slot's 2048-byte block in the table at `off_140783088`: the entry function goes to +136, the runnable flag at +144 is set to 1, and the fields at +24, +112 to +128, +152 and +160 to +208 are zeroed.
writes the entry function to the thread record's target field (+8) in the 288-byte record table at `unk_143791D70`, and sets the flags at +272 and +280 to 1.
about 46 callers across the event, world-map and battle code; nine of them pass `EventMessage_Task` as the entry.
the runnable flag at +144 is the same one SceneTask_WaitFrame and EventTask_WaitFrame scan for.

notes: There are two task tables with the same block layout and a shared thread table: `off_14078D5D8` (index `dword_14184B22C`) used by EventTask_WaitFrame, and `off_140783088` (index `dword_140D40948`) used here and by SceneTask_WaitFrame. EventThread_Yield sets both indices.
open_questions: What distinguishes a task in the first table from one in the second.

name: SceneTask_Terminate
callers: About 130 callers, including EventMessage_Task, EventScript_FindInstruction, SceneVar_Alu and many task bodies.
purpose: Ends the current task in the second task table; the error trap and the normal exit for scene and event-script tasks. The twin of EventTask_Terminate, with about 130 callers.

behavior.text: clears the qwords at +144 and +152 of the current task's block in `off_140783088`, marking it no longer runnable.
advances the current index `dword_140D40948` to the next block whose +144 qword is non-zero, up to 16, wrapping to 0.
calls ScenePad_UpdateRepeat, restores the original index and calls EventThread_ReturnToEntry.
called by SceneVar_Alu and SceneVar_ResolveSlot as their error trap, and by about 130 task bodies as their ending.

notes: Same structure as EventTask_Terminate but on the second task table.

name: SceneTask_WaitFrame
purpose: The wait-one-frame primitive for the second task table; over 100 routines call it to wait. It is the twin of EventTask_WaitFrame.

behavior.text: runs only when `byte_140D408EE` is 0, `byte_142FEC54F` is 0, or the current index `dword_140D40948` is non-zero.
increments the index and scans the second table's blocks for the next one whose qword at +144 is non-zero, up to 16, wrapping to 0.
calls ScenePad_UpdateRepeat, then EventThread_Yield(0).

notes: Same structure as EventTask_WaitFrame, but on `off_140783088` and `dword_140D40948`.

name: SceneTasks_Init
purpose: Initialises the second task group: clears its task table and points its table, variable store and event buffer at their storage.

behavior.text: sets the second task table `off_140783088` to `unk_140D40AA0`, the event buffer pointer `qword_140D40A90` to `unk_140D3CD50` and the variable store `off_1407830D8` to `unk_140D40060`, which is the same store the first group uses.
clears the whole task table (0x8800 bytes, 17 blocks of 2048), sets the current index `dword_140D40948` to 0 and marks block 0 runnable (the flag at +144).

picks a per-language table from the language-info field and stores it in `qword_140D40950`, copies two blocks of default scene records, and initialises a 63-entry record array whose flag is set only for entries 24, 25 and 58.
called once from `sub_14020E578`.

notes: Together with EventTasks_Init this shows the two task groups share one event buffer and one variable store.

name: SceneTransition_CheckTables
proto: int64_t SceneTransition_CheckTables(int64_t a1, int64_t a2, int64_t a3, int a4)
purpose: Runs a transition check over the scene group tables and, in one case, writes scene variable 39; the value it returns is not used by its caller in EventScript_Run.

behavior.text: when the low dword of qword_142FF9E4C is non-zero and dword_142FF9F4C is non-zero, it writes dword_142FF9F4C to scene variable 39 with SceneVar_Write and returns 1.
otherwise it writes 0 to the byte at qword_143CD9DD0 plus 108.

it then goes through entries 0 to 15 of the table word_140D40040. It stops at the first entry after entry 0 whose value is 0; for each entry it walks the word table word_140D3F550 (indexed by entry value divided by 2), calling sub_140239294 on each record and advancing by the record length from byte_140672140, until the call returns something other than 1.
when a call returns 2 the function returns 1 at once.
when no call returns 2 the function returns 0.
in EventScript_Run the call is part of a comma expression: EventScript_Run sets dword_1407DC494 to 255, calls this function and ignores its result, then tests the result of EventScript_LoadCurrent.

notes: Its return value is not read by EventScript_Run; only its side effects matter there.
open_questions: What sub_140239294 returns; what the tables word_140D40040, word_140D3F550 and byte_140672140 contain; what qword_143CD9DD0 plus 108 is.

name: SceneUnit_AddPosition
purpose: Adds a three-word delta to the position words of the unit node for a slot.

behavior.text: finds the unit node for the slot with SceneObject_FindBySlot; when there is none it returns 0.
adds the delta words 0, 1 and 2 (16-bit) to the node words at +108, +110 and +112 respectively.
returns 1.

notes: The delta pointer is in the second argument register.

name: SceneUnit_ApplyFlagRow
callers: EventScript_Run (opcode 0x8C case; call at 0x14023DC01); EventSubScript_RunTask (call at 0x140235C27).
purpose: Sets or clears a flag on one unit, writes its 7-byte row when the slot is 0 to 20, and calls two scene helpers with the slot and operand values. Opcode 0x8C calls it.

behavior.text: `operands` points at the operand bytes after the opcode. Operands 1 and 2 are the 16-bit reference (operand 1 is the low byte), resolved with EventRef_ResolveSlot. If the result has bit 15 set (negative as a 16-bit value), the routine returns that result at once and does nothing else.
otherwise it looks up the 16-bit slot with SceneObject_FindBySlot. A slot of 2000 finds no object, because the key is compared as a 16-bit value against a byte.

operand 5 is the high byte of the signed 16-bit value at operands 4 and 5. If it is zero and the object exists, bit 0x01 of the object's byte +143 is cleared. If it is nonzero and the object exists, bit 0x01 of byte +143 is set and the word at +24 is set to 0.
if the slot is 0 to 20 (unsigned 16-bit compare), it writes the 7-byte row at unk_142FEC580 plus 7 times the slot: byte 0 = operand 3, byte 4 = 0 and byte 6 = 0. Bytes 1, 2, 3 and 5 are not written.

for any slot that is not negative, including 2000, it calls sub_14021F538 with the slot and operand 3 as a byte, and then returns the value of sub_14021F414 called with the slot and the signed 16-bit value of operands 4 and 5.

sub_14021F538 (helper): if event variable 509 is zero and ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot(slot) is 0 or more, it reads byte +436 of preview record number index (for index 21 or more it reads the absolute address 0x1B4). When that byte is nonzero it calls sub_140272B14 with ScenePreview_SlotOfIndex(byte AND 0x1F). It always ends by calling sub_140272B14 with the slot and the value.

sub_140272B14 (level 2): if the object exists, it stores the value times 256 as a word at +0x7C, calls sub_140268E04 with the count max(2, the unsigned word at +0x1FC divided by 2) and the object, and returns the slot. Without an object it returns -1.

sub_14021F414 (helper): it calls sub_140272A04 (slot, value) and returns, when event variable 509 is nonzero, when event variable 111 is zero, when ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot is negative, when the value is 500 or more (unsigned), and when sub_140249088(4, ...) returns under 2 and byte +436 of the record has no bits 0xC0. Otherwise it sets the global callback qword_140D40940 to sub_1402729EC when byte +436 has bits 0xC0, or to sub_140272964 otherwise, and calls it with the slot. When dword_140D40948 is nonzero it first zeroes the qwords at +96 and +104 of block 0 of off_140783088 and calls through the global pointer.

sub_140272A04 (level 2): if the object exists, and when the global dword_140782A94 is 439 and the object's byte +10 is 0x45, it calls sub_1402735F0(slot, 1, 2) for value 600, and for value 2 it calls sub_14026947C(object, 0, 1) and zeroes dword_142E7FB18[slot + 420] when that dword is at least 100. In every case with an object it then sets the word at +16 to value + 1.
sub_140249088 (level 2): for selector 4 it returns bits 5 to 7 of byte 3 of 8-byte record number (a2 + a3 times the byte at 0x140C6AD6A + (a4 << 8)) in table byte_140D8DCB0.
sub_140268E04, sub_1402729EC, sub_140272964, sub_1402735F0 and sub_14026947C were read only as far as their first lines; the fields they write beyond those lines are not described here.

notes: A reference that resolves to 2000 still reaches both helpers, which then find no object, so only the row write and the flag write depend on the slot being found.
open_questions: The meaning of object byte +143 bit 0x01, word +24 and the 7-byte row; which index values ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot can return, since 21 or more makes both helpers read the absolute addresses 0x4F to 0x51 and 0x1B4; what the game does with the value sent through the callbacks.

name: SceneUnit_ApplyModeAndAction
callees: SceneGroup_ResolveId, SceneUnit_TestGroupMember, SceneObject_FindBySlot, sub_14021F414, sub_140235804 (frame-wait loop)
purpose: Applies a mode byte to the flag byte of each unit that an id names, then passes an action code to the state helper, and waits for frames when the code is 83, 84 or 85.

behavior.text: reads the id as the 16-bit value at operand bytes 1 and 2 and resolves it with SceneGroup_ResolveId; when that returns 0 nothing else happens.

for keys 0 to 20 in order it calls SceneUnit_TestGroupMember with the id; each key that is a member is processed. When the group mode written by SceneGroup_ResolveId is 0 (a single unit), the loop stops after the first processed member.

mode byte at operand 5. Mode 0 finds the unit node with SceneObject_FindBySlot and clears bit 0 of the byte at node +143. Mode 1 sets bit 0 of the byte at node +143 and writes zero to the 16-bit word at node +24. Other values change neither.
the action code is the 16-bit value at operand bytes 3 and 4.
calls sub_14021F414 with the unit slot and the action code.

when the action code is 83, 84 or 85 it calls sub_140235804 before the next member, which waits frames: it calls SceneTask_WaitFrame in a loop until sub_1402737D0 returns 0 (the value of dword_140CDB824), and it returns early through sub_14031A7E0 when the high dword of qword_142FF9E08 is non-zero and the high dword of qword_142FF9E00 is 3.
the function does not wait for any other action code. It ends after the loop; the instruction then continues.

notes: In the common path of sub_14021F414 (sub_140272A04) the action code is stored plus one in the 16-bit word at node +16 of the unit; the preview path can dispatch through the callback pointer instead.
open_questions: What the flag bit at node +143 and the word at node +24 mean to the game; the rest of sub_14021F414 (the preview-table branch) and sub_1402729EC / sub_140272964 were not traced.

name: SceneUnit_ApplyStatusTint
proto: void SceneUnit_ApplyStatusTint(SceneUnitSlot *unit, int ambient, int64_t now)
purpose: Gives a scene unit its colours: a status tint chosen from the unit's flag dword, or the plain row with the ambient light when no tint flag is set.

behavior.text: does nothing when the unit's byte +300 has any of the bits 0x30.
reads the flag dword +348; when none of the bits 0x60C26020 is set it calls SceneUnit_RunPlacement(unit, ambient, now).
flag 0x20: mode 6 with offsets 0, 0, 0 (grey).
flag 0x20000: mode 6 with offsets 3, -1, 8.
flag 0x4000: mode 4 with offsets 8, 0, 0.
flag 0x400000: mode 5 with offsets 0, 8, 0.
flag 0x20000000: mode 4 with offsets 0, 0, 8.
flag 0x800000: mode 5 with offsets -4, -4, -4; flag 0x2000: mode 5 with offsets -8, -8, -8.
flag 0x40000000, unless the sprite byte (+10) is 0x8B or 0x8C: mode 5 with offsets 4, 0, 5.

the flags are tested in that order and the first one set wins; each case calls SceneUnit_TintOwnRow with the unit's slot byte (+8) as the slot. Apart from the group mask 0x60C26020 and 0x20, the code tests the flags by bit number (17, 14, 22, 29, 23, 13, 30), so their masks 0x20000, 0x4000, 0x400000, 0x20000000, 0x800000, 0x2000 and 0x40000000 are not in it as numbers; the sprite test adds 0x75 to the byte and compares with 1, which is 0x8B or 0x8C.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140269330). The flag 0x40000000 with sprite 0x8B or 0x8C falls through to SceneUnit_RunPlacement.
open_questions: ? which status each flag bit stands for in play (not seen live).

name: SceneUnit_ApplyStatusVisuals
purpose: Applies a scene unit's status visual set / clear masks and redraws the pose.

behavior.text: (mask 0x100 is tested as bit 8) +0x15C = +0x164 | +0x15C & ~+0x16C and +0x160 = +0x168 | +0x160 & ~+0x170; clears the masks; redraws the pose (sub_14026947C, sub_14026A048 for the chicken / frog sprite 146, SceneUnit_SyncSpriteFromPool for the effect sprites 155..158).
+0x15C bits 0x1FFFC2C4 make it set +0x370 (a pose flag); +0x160 bits 0..3 select the effect sprites 155..158 and bits 7 / 8 a pending transform (0x100 = sprite 146).
SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry zeroes the status visual words +0x15C..+0x170 (0x14026EEF9..0x14026EF1C, addresses in the caller) and ends with this function.

name: SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry
proto: SceneUnitSlot *SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry(char a, char b, char c, int16_t d, uint16_t sprite, int16_t palette, int16_t slotRequest, void *unit, int flag, void *file)
callees: LookPool_ClaimForSprite, sub_14027032C, sub_14026E838, sub_14026947C, SceneUnit_BuildPalette, SceneUnit_SetFlag12C, ItemSprite_LoadPalettes, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow
purpose: Builds the scene unit of one look queue entry: takes a scene-unit slot, claims the look pool record of the sprite, picks the palette row, loads the pool's palette and frames, sets the HD sheet slot and links the unit into the scene-object list; returns the scene unit or null.

behavior.text: the arguments are the queue entry's fields (CharaPalette_ReloadForShape, pass 2) plus the classic file buffer.

when the load mode dword at 0x142FF9E2C is 1 (the resume path) the scene-unit slot comes from g_UnitSceneSlotIndex[unit +444] and, after LookPool_ClaimForSprite, the pool index is replaced by g_UnitLookPoolIndex[unit +444]; a null unit or an index above 20 returns null.

otherwise a slot request below 16 takes that slot (null when an in-use slot already carries that number or the slot is in use), else the first free one of the 16; the pool index from LookPool_ClaimForSprite(sprite) is stored into g_UnitLookPoolIndex[unit +444] and the slot into g_UnitSceneSlotIndex (another unit's entry naming the same slot becomes -1).
writes the sprite's low byte to scene unit +0xA and the pool index to +9; a pool index of 0xFFFF frees the slot and returns null (the unit is not drawn).

palette source: sprites 159..162 and 96..133 (the generic looks, tested as sprite - 0x60 <= 0x25) take unit byte +4 (the queue's palette word when there is no unit) with a limit of 5; every other sprite looks up its CharShape row (NXD 174, key = the sprite word): a non-zero colour override id at +12 gives sub_1401E3A10's answer with a limit of 16, else the queue palette with a limit of 5; scene unit +0xB = the value when below the limit, else 0.
sprites 69 and 73 rewrite one byte of every battle unit (the loop walks 0x141853ECD, g_PreviewUnitTable + 493, in steps of 512): 1 -> 7 for 69, 7 -> 8 for 73.

calls sub_14026E838 (palette, pool face value, frames) and sets the HD sheet slot word +0x14 = pool + 20 (17 from pool 9 up); with enhanced graphics and the HD mode dword set it copies hd_entry_by_shape[sprite] into g_HdSheetEntryBySlot[20 + pool] (pools 0..8) or dword_142E7FEE0 (pool 9) when it is not -1; pools 10..14 get no HD entry.

so pools 9..14 all carry sheet word 17, and sub_140260CF0 draws word 17 from group 13 (pool 9's sheet, entry dword_142E7FEE0) whenever that entry is set: a unit of pools 10..14 is cut from pool 9's HD sheet at its own frame rectangles (the scrambled pieces seen live with 11 or more looks).
the scene unit's CLUT word +0x16 is 0x78C0 | (slot & 0x3F) and its palette row is marked dirty with sub_1402F7594(.., bank 4, row = slot), a bank of 16 rows.

stores the unit pointer at scene unit +0x148, links the scene unit at the head of qword_140D3A410 (except on the resume path when the slot was already in use) and loads the held item's palettes (ItemSprite_LoadPalettes).
writes the scene unit's sprite byte +0xA from its sprite argument (bpl, 0x14026EDA0) and the pool index +9.

in load mode 1 (resume) it calls LookPool_ClaimForSprite(sprite) but takes the pool index from g_UnitLookPoolIndex[unit +444] (0x14026ED8D), not from the claim; the scene slot comes from g_UnitSceneSlotIndex[unit +444] (0x14026ECB5; none -> no build), the in-use flag is tested (0x14026ECFB) and the record is not linked again when it was in use (the `!v87` test before `*v13 = qword_140D3A410`). In mode 0 it takes the scene slot named by its slot argument (refused when a slot with that id is in use) and links it.
the queue entry layout: bytes +0 / +1 / +2 = x, y, layer, word +4 facing, +6 sprite, +8 palette, +0xA slot, qword +0x10 unit, dword +0x18 flag; the loader passes them in that order.

notes: Whole function read in the decompile (2026-11-08), written from scratch; it replaces the 2026-10-27 head-only sheet (whose purpose line called it a palette helper and the slot table a shape table). The HD entry bounds are at 0x14026F006 / 0x14026F02D and the attribute read is at 0x14026F452. The name stays the address.
open_questions: ? what sub_14027032C and sub_14026947C build; ? the meaning of the unit byte +493 rewrite for sprites 69 and 73.

name: SceneUnit_BuildPalette
callers: EventScript_Run, at 0x14023DFC7 (opcode 0xA8, with the unit from `SceneObject_FindBySlot`). Also SceneUnit_RunPlacement (at 0x14026921F), SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry (at 0x14026EFC0), sub_1402735F0 (at 0x140273677), and one data reference at 0x143D39058.
callees: `sub_1403D325C`, `sub_1403D3AE8`, `sub_1403D2FD8`, `sub_1402F7594` (level 2: `sub_1402F74D8` splits each 15-bit word into five-bit fields and a flag bit in a 7-byte-stride table)
purpose: The body of opcode 0xA8: when the unit exists, builds 16 packed 15-bit words from the table 302 row selected by the unit's byte +343 and passes them to `sub_1402F7594` with the index 3.

behavior.text: returns at once when the unit pointer is null.
the key is the unit's byte at +343. Opcode 0xA8 writes that byte before calling this routine (see the record for 0xA8).
the table 302 handle is kept in qword_143CDA868. When it is null it is looked up once with sub_1403D325C(qword_143CD9CD0, 302). When neither can be obtained, nothing is written.

row = sub_1403D3AE8(table 302, key). The routine goes on only when the row is present and either its first qword is negative (then the static block unk_1406F5ED0 is used as its data) or its data pointer is not null.

for 16 steps, i = 2, 5, 8, ... 47: it reads three bytes at the data pointer plus the dword at data +8 plus i - 2, plus i - 1 and plus i. The first byte becomes bits 0 to 4 of the word (from its bits 3 to 7), the second becomes bits 5 to 9 (from its bits 3 to 7) and the third becomes bits 10 to 14 (from its bits 3 to 7).
bit 15 of the first word is clear; bit 15 is set on every later word of the 16.
the 16 words are stored in a 32-byte stack buffer, and then `sub_1402F7594(buffer, 3, 15)` is called. The fourth argument of that call is not set in the visible code.
returns nothing. When the row is missing nothing is written.

notes: The record for 0xA8 calls the effect a packed value; the code builds 16 words into a 32-byte buffer.
open_questions: What the table 302 rows hold beyond the three bytes per step. What the block with index 3 is, what the fourth argument of `sub_1402F7594` is, and what bit 15 means. Why the calls to `sub_1402F7594` take index 3 and 15.

name: SceneUnit_BuildPoint
purpose: Builds the three-word world point (x, height, z) of a unit from its live record.

behavior.text: finds the scene node for the preview index with `sub_140260ABC`; missing -> 0.
out[0] (world x) is 28 times the tile-x byte at offset 79 of the node's unit record, plus 14 (tile x centre).
out[2] (world z) is 28 times the tile-y byte at offset 80 of the node's unit record, plus 14 (tile y centre).
height = `sub_140262B20(record, &point)`; when `(node+300 & 3) == 1` it adds a unit height term minus 10.
returns 1.

notes: Confirms that unit tile coordinates are bytes +79/+80 and that the grid pitch is 28 world units with a 14-unit centre offset. The Legate's live read (Ramza 6,8 -> 6,7) matches this rule.
open_questions: ? the exact height expression (the decompiler loses one register); ? the meaning of node+300 bits.

name: SceneUnit_CallbackSend19
callers: EventScript_Run (opcode 0x98, through the global callback qword_140D40940; the reference is at 0x14023DD25).
callees: SceneObject_FindBySlot (unit lookup), sub_1401FAE5C (builds and sends the record), sub_140310B64 (not read)
purpose: The callback that opcode 0x98 installs in the global qword_140D40940: for one unit key it sends the value 0x13 to the unit's sub-record and returns whether the unit exists.

behavior.text: calls SceneObject_FindBySlot(key) to get the unit node. If there is none, it returns 0.
if there is a node, it calls sub_1401FAE5C(node, 0x13) and returns 1.

sub_1401FAE5C builds a 232-byte local record with the node's key byte (node+8) and a fixed word pattern, then calls sub_140310B64 with the value 0x13 and the sub-record's byte +4, but only when the node's pointer at +0x148 is nonzero; otherwise it returns 0.
the function is stored in a global callback pointer, not called by a fixed name, so the key is the only argument it receives.

notes: Installed with mode 1 by the opcode 0x98 record (opcode records, data/opcodes.jsonl). The pseudocode line that stores it sits under a label the search read as case 0xC4, which is not what the record says.
open_questions: What sub_140310B64 does with the value 0x13. The meaning of mode 1 is not seen in this function.

name: SceneUnit_CopyField4C
callers: sub_140240D5C (opcode 0x53 body, at 0x140240E16 and 0x140240E21); sub_140241FF0 (opcode 0x69 body, at 0x140242073); a data reference at 0x143D37E64.
purpose: Copies three 16-bit words from a unit node into a caller buffer, used by the opcode 0x53 and 0x69 bodies.

behavior.text: calls SceneObject_FindBySlot(key) to get the unit node. If there is none, it returns without writing anything.
if there is a node, it copies the word at node+0x4C to out[0], the word at node+0x4E to out[1] and the word at node+0x50 to out[2].
it returns nothing; the return register holds a leftover value that the callers do not use.

notes: The function is a plain copy; its name says what it reads, not what the caller does with it.
open_questions: What the three words at node+0x4C are in the game. The callers' use of them is only read from the opcode records.

name: SceneUnit_EntryById
purpose: Returns a scene unit entry of the selector scenes (564 bytes each at 0x1408E6CB0) by its id, or null.

behavior.text: id 0 to 15 and a scene id word (0x141848BB0) of 21, 43, 44 or 51 give 0x1408E6CB0 + 564 * id; anything else null.
sub_1402C1628 does not test the null: an id above 15 in those scenes faults there.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1402EFF34).
open_questions: ? the screens of scene ids 21, 43, 44 and 51.

name: SceneUnit_FillSpriteRecord
purpose: Builds a work record from the selector-scene unit entry named by the object's byte +180 and fills the object's sprite record (+188) with its preview shape.

behavior.text: SceneUnit_EntryById(obj byte +180); null returns false.
sets dword_1437414A0 = 1 and UnitWork_BuildFromSave(work, entry, entry byte +1); a non-zero result returns false.
Unit_ResolvePreviewShape(work, &palette, work job byte +3); the byte answer is widened into r8d at 0x1402C259A.
SpriteRecord_Fill(obj + 188, id, shape, palette, 0, .., slot 6 when the id equals dword_141848B14 else 4, 0); returns true.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1402C2520).

name: SceneUnit_LoadExtraPage
proto: int SceneUnit_LoadExtraPage(uint8_t *sceneUnit, int page, int slot)
purpose: Gives a scene unit one of the two extra sprite pages for its second-sheet frames (special poses such as a punch) and points that page's HD sheet slot at the unit's second sheet entry.

behavior.text: with graphics level 2.0 or more and the dword at 0x142E7FC88 non-zero: when the scene unit's sprite byte (+0xA) has an HD entry e (the HD entry table, not -1), slot 11 + page (0x142E7FE98) = 0 and slot 16 + page (0x142E7FEAC) and the dword at 0x142E7FEF4 + 4 * page = e + 1, the second sheet of the pair.
otherwise (classic graphics) it copies the unit's classic frames into the page with VramPage_CopyRect.
then the page owner (0x140CE3260 + 0x7CE8 * page) = scene unit byte +8 | 0x80, and the page's in-use words are set.
caller sub_14026CAA4 (per frame) looks for a page whose owner's low 5 bits are the unit's; with none it takes a free page (owner 255).
a resumed battle restores slot 16 from the save (g_HdSheetEntryBySlot 13..28 come from the payload), so it names the second sheet of the unit that last used page 0 while every page owner reads 255.
the sprite byte decides the second sheet: a scene unit whose byte read 0 left slot 16 as it was (another unit's entry), and the HD layer drew that unit's second-sheet pieces in its colours.

notes: Slot 16 + page is read by the battle sprite draw (sub_140260CF0, the page-4 path) as the entry of the extra page; a draw that finds it -1 sets it lazily from the drawn object's sprite byte.
open_questions: ? what the dword at 0x142E7FC88 stands for (a video mode: 2 picks the copy branch too).

name: SceneUnit_MeasureRange
proto: int64_t SceneUnit_MeasureRange(int16_t sourceIndex, int16_t *point, int32_t targetIndex)
callers: EventScript_Run, at 0x14023D995 (opcode 0x87, which sets qword_140D40940 to this routine just before the dispatch). One data reference at 0x143D3D870 (a function-pointer table entry, not traced).
callees: `sub_1402736D0` (speed value), `sub_140272BD0` (unit point), `sub_140249000` (grid cell lookup), `sub_1402746E8` (scaled square root). Level 2, not traced past its use here: `sub_140260ABC`, `sub_140262AF4`, `sub_140262B20`, `sub_140262808`.
purpose: The callback that opcode 0x87 installs in the global qword_140D40940: it measures a scaled distance from a source unit to a target unit, or to a fixed three-word point when no target unit has a preview index, and returns that value.

behavior.text: from opcode 0x87 it is called through SceneCallback_Dispatch mode 3, which passes the second unit's preview index as the first argument, the address of word_142FEF848 as the second and the first unit's preview index (or -1) as the third. The dispatcher's extra arguments reach the callback in registers; the decompiler shows only the first.
the source is the unit whose preview index is `sourceIndex`. A unit is found by preview index with `sub_140260ABC`, which returns the scene node whose sub-record byte +444 equals the index.

source height adjustment: v6 = (2 times the speed of the source) divided by 3 (integer division). The speed comes from `sub_1402736D0`, which returns byte_140673303 at offset 4 times byte +10 of the unit node, or 0 when the node's byte +352 has bits 0x09 set or its byte +348 has bit 0x04 set. The source's height word at word_14186D77A is set to that word minus v6.

the source point is written by `sub_140272BD0` into the three words at word_14186D778 (x, height, z): x is 28 times sub-record byte +79 plus 14, z is 28 times byte +80 plus 14, and the height comes from `sub_140262B20`.

when targetIndex is -1: the target x is 28 times point[0] plus 14, the target z is 28 times point[2] plus 14, and the target height is -12 times the unsigned byte at offset 2 of the grid cell that `sub_140249000` returns for (point[0], point[2], point[1]). The target words are at word_14186D780 (x), word_14186D782 (height) and word_14186D784 (z).

when targetIndex is not -1: the target point is the unit's point from `sub_140272BD0` (same layout, into word_14186D780 to word_14186D784). Its height is lowered by v5, which is (3 times the target unit's speed) divided by 4 (integer division).

D is the sum of the squares of the x, height and z differences between the target and the adjusted source; the height difference uses the adjusted source height. The result is the integer square root of D divided by 8, computed by `sub_1402746E8` as a floating-point square root scaled by 4096 and then shifted back down; a value of 0 or less gives 0.
the result is stored in dword_14186D770 and returned as an unsigned 32-bit value, zero-extended.
the opcode 0x87 body does not read the returned value.
the value is a range measure between the two units. Its use by any other caller is not read.

notes: The 0x87 record names its operands as unit slots; the values passed to this routine are preview indexes from ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot, and the target is the first operand's unit (or the point when that unit has no preview index). The result is stored in the global dword_14186D770.
open_questions: What fills the three words at word_142FEF848 (used as the point when the first unit has no preview index). What byte_140673303, unit byte +10, and the grid cell byte at offset 2 mean. The meaning of the height offsets 2/3 and 3/4 and of the sub-record height from sub_140262B20.

name: SceneUnit_Oscillate120
purpose: Runs a 120-frame sequence on one unit: a callback, a helper call, two SceneUnit_ResetAndQueue4 calls with +31 and then -31, waits of 10, 50 and 60 frames, and a final clear of two bytes of the unit's preview record. Opcode 0x94 calls it.

behavior.text: `ref` is the sign-extended 16-bit operand 1 passed as 32 bits. It is resolved with EventRef_ResolveSlot. If the result is exactly 2000, the routine returns with nothing done.
it sets dword_140782CAC to 166 when it already is 166, and to 106 otherwise.

it sets the global callback qword_140D40940 to SceneUnit_CallbackSend19. When dword_140D40948 is nonzero it first zeroes the qwords at +96 and +104 of block 0 of off_140783088 and calls through the global pointer; otherwise it calls SceneUnit_CallbackSend19 directly. Both pass the slot.
index = ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot(slot), kept as a sign-extended value.
it calls sub_14021F414 with the slot and the value 27.
waits 10 frames (SceneTask_WaitFrame ten times), then calls SceneUnit_ResetAndQueue4(slot, 2, 31, 31, 31).
waits 50 frames, then calls SceneUnit_ResetAndQueue4(slot, 2, -31, -31, -31).
waits 60 frames.

writes 0xFF to byte +1 and 0 to byte +437 of preview record `index`, at g_BattleUnitTable plus 512 times index. No test is made on index, so index -1 or a value of 21 or more writes outside the 21 records.
the waits total 120 frames (10 + 50 + 60); the callback and the helper call come before the first wait.

notes: The name is an inference from the alternating +31 and -31 values; what the sequence looks like in the game is not read.
open_questions: What the action code 4 queued by SceneUnit_ResetAndQueue4 does with the +31 and -31 values; what the callback does with the value 27 and the slot; whether the final clear can see index -1 or 21 or more, which would write outside the table.

name: SceneUnit_Release
callers: EventScript_Run (the case that takes a unit off: slot byte 0xFF), sub_1401F0948, sub_1401F22D0, sub_1401F3128 (deployment: a unit taken back off its cell), SceneUnits_ReleaseAll, SceneObjects_StepStates
purpose: Frees a drawn unit's scene unit (drawing slot) and, when no other drawn unit uses the same look pool record, frees that record too.

behavior.text: clears the in-use dword of scene unit [unit+8] (0x140D30030 + 1352 x index).

walks g_SceneObjectList for another node with the same pool index (byte +9) whose scene unit is still in use; when none is found it clears the pool record's first byte (g_LookPool + 13014 x pool), freeing it; then unlinks the node.

notes: Behavior: SixteenSceneUnitsComeOnlyFromTheLookQueue.

name: SceneUnit_ReleasePartner
callers: SceneUnit_ResetFields (SceneUnit_ResetFields) and the callers listed in the decompiler (sub_1401FDD7C, sub_1401FE59C, sub_14020B6DC, sub_140268F68, sub_140272D70 and others).
purpose: When the unit node's low status bits equal 1, clears the unit's and its partner's status fields and calls the release routine for both.

behavior.text: tests the low two bits of the byte at node +300; it does nothing unless they equal 1.
reads the partner slot from the byte at node +320 and finds the partner node with SceneObject_FindBySlot.
clears bit 1 of the dword at node +348, clears the low two bits of the byte at +300, sets the byte at +298 to 0 and the byte at +320 to 0.
calls sub_1401FAF54 on the node found by the node's own slot byte at +8.

when the partner node exists, clears the low two bits of the partner's byte at +300, sets the partner's byte at +320 to 0, and calls sub_1401FAF54 on the partner node found by the partner's slot byte at +8.

notes: This is a partner-link release; the names of the two status fields are not decoded.
open_questions: What sub_1401FAF54 does; the meaning of the status bits.

name: SceneUnit_ResetAndQueue4
proto: int64_t SceneUnit_ResetAndQueue4(int16_t key, int32_t arg2, int16_t arg3, int16_t arg4, int16_t arg5)
callers: EventScript_Run at 0x14023DE52 (inside a loop over 21 slots that compares byte +401 of each preview entry with the operand, with arguments slot, 2, -31, -31, 0; matches opcode 0x99 per the record); EventScript_Run at 0x14023C2E0 (same argument pattern, opcode not confirmed); sub_140240A78 (opcode 0x94 helper, at 0x140240B24 with +31 and at 0x140240B4C with -31); sub_14020435C and sub_14026A048 (other helpers).
callees: SceneObject_FindBySlot (unit lookup), sub_140260AEC (move to front), sub_1402F7C20 (queued action, not read in full)
purpose: Resets a unit's state bytes and words and queues an action (code 4) with the given values through sub_1402F7C20. Used by the opcode 0x94 and 0x99 paths.

behavior.text: calls SceneObject_FindBySlot(key) to get the unit node. If there is none, it returns 0 and does nothing else.
calls sub_140260AEC(key), which moves the node to the front of the unit list at qword_140D3A410 and returns 1 when it finds the node.
clears bit 0x20 and sets bit 0x10 of the byte at node+0x12C.
clears bit 0x40 and sets bits 0x21 of the word at node+0x18.
sets the byte at node+0x318 to 1.

calls sub_1402F7C20(4, arg2, key, arg3, arg4, arg5). The value 4 is passed by value. sub_1402F7C20 applies the action to slot key when key is below 16, and to all 16 slots (indices 0 to 15) when key is 16 or more.
sets the dword at node+0x80 to 0, the word at node+0x12 to 0xFFFF and the byte at node+0x156 to 0.
returns 0.

notes: The arguments arg3 and arg4 are the +31 and -31 values that opcode 0x94 passes through sub_140240A78.
open_questions: What arg2, arg3, arg4 and arg5 mean inside sub_1402F7C20 (not traced), and what the flags at node+0x12C, +0x18 and +0x318 control.

name: SceneUnit_ResetFields
proto: int64_t SceneUnit_ResetFields(int16_t slot, uint8_t mode_bits, uint8_t op4)
purpose: Resets the state fields of one unit node and calls the partner release routine on it.

behavior.text: finds the unit node for the slot with SceneObject_FindBySlot; when there is none it returns 0.
sets the byte at node +168 to 1, the word at +294 to 0, and the byte at +293 to 0.

sets the byte at +169 to: bits 0 and 1 from the low two bits of the r8 argument (operand 3 minus 1), bits 5 to 7 from bit 0 of the node byte at +138 (bit 5), and the low two bits of the op4 argument (bits 6 and 7).
sets the dword at +68 and the dword at +72 to 0x2000, sets the dword at +164 to 0.
calls SceneUnit_ReleasePartner on the node and returns 1.

notes: The arguments come from registers: the slot in cx, the operand 3 minus 1 in r8 and the operand 4 byte in edx; the decompiler does not show the last two.
open_questions: Meaning of the byte at +169 and of the fields set to 0x2000.

name: SceneUnit_RunPlacement
proto: int64_t SceneUnit_RunPlacement(uint8_t *node, int32_t offset_sel, int32_t flag)
callers: EventScript_Run (opcode 0x97 path, see findings), EventSubScript_RunTask (EventSubScript_RunTask), sub_1401009E8, sub_140269330, sub_14026A1DC.
callees: SceneVar_Read, sub_1402F7594, sub_1402F78A4, SceneUnit_BuildPalette, SceneUnit_SetFlag12C (not read)
purpose: Runs the placement setup for one scene object record, using the record's bytes 8 to 11 to choose a table entry and a position table.

behavior.text: reads the record bytes +8 (slot), +9 (table index), +10 (selector) and +11 (sub-index).
chooses a table pointer from unk_140D005A0 at 13014 bytes per entry indexed by byte +9, choosing one of two sub-regions by testing the byte at entry offset +1 against a set of values.
calls sub_1402F7594 with a buffer, the count 10 and the slot byte.
the second argument selects a base offset: 0 gives 0, 1 gives -4, 2 gives -8, 3 gives -12; other values give 0.
reads SceneVar 35 and 36 (both are tested against the bits of dword_140D3A830 first) and selects offsets for three values from the results.

when the selector byte +10 is 0x9B, 0x9C, 0x9D or 0x9E it uses base offsets 320, 0, 160 or 512 plus 32 times byte +11, and calls sub_1402F78A4 with these, the slot, and the third argument as the last value.
for any other selector it calls SceneUnit_BuildPalette and SceneUnit_SetFlag12C on the node, then calls sub_1402F78A4 with another base.
the function does not wait.

notes: This pass decoded only the structure of the routine; the meaning of the table entries and the arguments of sub_1402F78A4 are not established.
open_questions: What the two sub-regions and the 13014-byte entries hold; what sub_1402F78A4 does with its base offsets.

name: SceneUnit_SetFlag12C
callers: EventScript_Run, at 0x14023DF84 (opcode 0xA9, with the unit from `SceneObject_FindBySlot`). Also SceneUnit_RunPlacement (at 0x140269227), SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry (at 0x14026EFC8), sub_1402735F0 (at 0x140273693), and data references at 0x143D39058 and 0x143D39064.
purpose: The body of opcode 0xA9: clears bit 0x40 of the unit's byte +0x12C (300) and sets it again to bit 0 of byte +8 of the table 305 row selected by the unit's byte +345, when that row exists.

behavior.text: returns at once when the unit pointer is null.
clears bit 0x40 of the unit's byte at +300 (0x12C) in every case where the unit exists.
the table 305 handle is kept in qword_143CDA860. When it is null it is looked up once with sub_1403D325C(qword_143CD9CD0, 305). When neither can be obtained, the bit stays clear.

row = sub_1403D3AE8(table 305, the unit's byte +345). The routine goes on only when the row is present and either its first qword is negative (then unk_1406F5ED0 is used as its data) or its data pointer is not null.
bit 0 of the byte at data +8 becomes bit 6 of the unit's byte +300; the other bits of that byte are kept.
when no row is found the bit stays clear. Returns nothing.

notes: The byte at +345 is written by opcode 0xA9 before this call. The bit is the same byte that the flag at +0x12C holds in the unit record.
open_questions: What the table 305 rows hold and what the bit 0x40 of the unit byte at +300 controls in the game.

name: SceneUnit_SetFlag156
callers: EventScript_Run (opcode 0x46, at the calls near 0x14023B313 to 0x14023C9F5); sub_140210AF0, EventSubScript_RunTask, sub_14026E194 and sub_140273270 (helpers).
purpose: Marks a unit's flag byte at +0x156 as set (0 during event 54) and clears two of its state words. The body of opcode 0x46 on one unit.

behavior.text: calls SceneObject_FindBySlot(key). If there is no unit node it returns 0.
sets the byte at node+0x156 to 1.
reads the current event number dword_140782A94; when it equals 54 (0x36) the byte is set to 0 instead.
clears the word at node+0x0E and the word at node+0x1F8.
returns 1 when the node exists.

notes: The byte at +0x156 is the one the opcode record for 0x46 describes as set to 1, with an exception for event 54.
open_questions: What the byte at +0x156 and the two words at +0x0E and +0x1F8 are read for elsewhere.

name: SceneUnit_SyncSpriteFromPool
callees: SceneUnit_RunPlacement, sub_140268E80, sub_140268EB0, sub_14026947C, sub_140269BBC, sub_14026AE1C
purpose: Keeps a scene unit's sprite byte in step with its look pool record, and switches to the four effect sprites 155 to 158 when the unit's effect flags ask for them.

behavior.text: when none of the low four bits of the unit's flag dword (+352) is set, reads the byte at +1 of the pool record named by unit +9 and, when it differs from unit +0xA, copies it there and rebuilds the unit's frame data (sub_14026947C, sub_140269BBC, sub_14026AE1C).

when one of the flags is set it picks 155 (bit 0), 156 (bit 1), 157 (bit 2) or 158 (bit 3) as the sprite and, when it differs from the current byte, replaces the unit's frame sources and runs SceneUnit_RunPlacement.

called from sub_1401FAF54 (SceneUnit_ApplyStatusVisuals); sets the scene unit's sprite byte back to its pool record's +1 when no effect sprite (155..158) is shown, taking the saved frame tables (+0x230 / +0x238; +0x238 is reached through the pair copy).

notes: Structure: SceneUnitSlot. The name is ours (IDB: sub_14026A1DC). The four effect sprites are the ones CharaRender_BuildAtlasTexture answers with HD entry 160.
open_questions: ? what the flag bits mean in play.

name: SceneUnit_TestGroupMember
callers: EventScript_Run (opcode 0x80 through the call at 0x14023D735 and opcode 0x81 through the call at 0x14023D7BB, both as the loop test); SceneGroup_SetFlag04 (opcodes 0x6C and 0x6D); the helper bodies listed under SceneGroup_ResolveId.
callees: SceneObject_FindBySlot (unit lookup), ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot (preview index of a unit)
purpose: Tests whether unit key 'key' (0 to 20 in the callers' loops) is a member of the group selected by *groupMode. Used in a loop over 21 keys by the callers of SceneGroup_ResolveId.

behavior.text: if *groupMode is 0 it returns 1 at once, without writing *id. That case is a single unit whose id was already resolved, so the caller's loop runs once.
for any other mode it first writes key to *id, then calls SceneObject_FindBySlot(key) to find the unit node. Without a node it returns 0 for every mode.

with a node, it calls ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot(key) to get the preview index: the byte at node+0x148 then +0x1BC, or -1 when there is no such record. An index of 0 to 20 selects the entry g_BattleUnitTable + index*512; otherwise there is no entry.
mode 1 (from id 0) returns 1 for every key that has a unit node.
mode 2 returns 1 when the preview index is -1. Otherwise it returns 1 only when the entry's byte +5 has bits 0x30 clear.

mode 3 returns 1 when the preview index is -1. Otherwise it returns 1 only when none of the five bytes +97 to +101 of the entry is nonzero (each mask byte at 0x1411A6A98 to 0x1411A6A9C reads as 0xFF) and the entry's byte +5 has bits 0x30 clear.
mode 4 returns 1 only when the preview index is 0 to 20 and the entry's byte +5 has bits 0x30 set.
mode 5 returns 1 only when the preview index is 0 to 20, the entry's byte +5 has bits 0x30 set, and none of the bytes +97 to +101 is nonzero, with bit 0x10 of byte +97 ignored.
modes 6 and above return 0 for every key.

notes: The mode values are the ones SceneGroup_ResolveId writes. Mode 0 means a single unit; modes 1 to 5 are the group kinds read from the code.
open_questions: What the mask bytes at 0x1411A6A98 to 0x1411A6A9C mean in the game (they all read 0xFF in the file), and what bytes +97 to +101 and +5 of the preview entry describe. The meaning of each group kind (modes 2 to 5) is read from the tests only.

name: SceneUnit_TintOwnRow
proto: int64_t SceneUnit_TintOwnRow(SceneUnitSlot *unit, int mode, int64_t unused, unsigned slot, int unused2, int16_t dr, int16_t dg, int16_t db, int now)
purpose: Picks the 16-colour row a scene unit is drawn with and passes it to UnitClut_TintRow with the caller's mode and offsets.

behavior.text: the row is 32 bytes at 32 * the unit's palette byte (+11) inside the palette of the unit's look pool record: 0x140D03676 + 13014 * the pool byte (+9).
for the sprite bytes 155, 156, 157 and 158 (+10) the row comes from the block at 0x140D354B0 instead, at 320, 0, 160 and 512 bytes plus 32 * the palette byte.
ends in a jump to UnitClut_TintRow with the mode in the first argument and the row in the second; the other arguments pass through.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_14026929C). The call of UnitClut_TintRow is a tail jump. Structures: SceneUnitSlot, LookPoolRecord.

name: SceneUnit_UpdateNearFlag
purpose: Sets or clears one flag byte of a unit node by comparing two values from sub_140262808, only when the global mode dword_140782A94 equals 386.

behavior.text: does nothing unless dword_140782A94 equals 386.
finds the unit node for the slot with SceneObject_FindBySlot.

builds three 16-bit sums from words of three node fields and a comparison value v2 (the sum of three words at +74, +90 and +106); calls sub_140262808 with a pointer to the three sums and the flag 0, and again with the flag 1.

sets the byte at node +138 to 1 when the flag-1 result is non-zero, is at least v2, and either the flag-0 result is below v2 or the distance from v2 to the flag-1 result is below the distance from v2 to the flag-0 result; otherwise it sets it to 0.
the three sums are taken from the words at node +76, +92 and +108 and at +80, +96 and +112; the field offsets were derived from the struct layout of the list node.

notes: Not called by opcode 0x70 (the earlier sheet listed it as a callee); the caller is EventObject_MoveWorker.
open_questions: What sub_140262808 returns; the meaning of byte +138.

name: SceneUnit_ZeroPosAndReset
purpose: Zeroes the three position words of the unit named by its operands and then calls the unit reset routine on it, with one preview-table byte set to 6 for the duration of that call.

behavior.text: resolves the id at operand bytes 1 and 2 with EventRef_ResolveSlot, using the low byte of the id as the flag. When the result is 2000 it does nothing.
reads the three 16-bit words at unit node +108, +110 and +112 and stores their negated values in a three-word buffer.
calls SceneUnit_AddPosition with the slot and the buffer. That routine adds the three buffer words to the unit words at +108, +110 and +112 (16-bit wrap), so the position words become zero.

calls ScenePreview_IndexOfSlot for the slot. When the index is 0 to 20 it saves the byte at unk_141853D23 plus 512 times the index, sets that byte to 6, and restores it after the next call. When the index is above 20 (including -1) the byte pointer is the address 67, which the code reads and writes.

calls SceneUnit_ResetFields with the slot in the cx register (not set by the visible code after the preview lookup), operand 3 minus 1 in the r8 register and operand 4 in the edx register. It returns the result of SceneUnit_ResetFields, which is 1 when a unit node exists and 0 otherwise.
the function does not wait.
when the slot resolves but no unit node exists, the code reads the node's words through a zero pointer; no null test is made before the first read.

notes: The preview byte is at unk_141853D23 with 512-byte records; it is a per-unit byte of the preview table, meaning not decoded.
open_questions: Whether the cx value passed to SceneUnit_ResetFields is the unit slot; what the preview byte set to 6 means; what happens for a slot with no node.

name: SceneUnits_ReleaseAll
purpose: Releases every drawn unit (SceneUnit_Release on each node of g_SceneObjectList) after clearing 32 pending dwords and their 8 linked bytes.

behavior.text: calls sub_140254A70; for the 32 dwords from 0x142FF8F00 that are not 0 clears the linked byte (index - 1 below 8) and the dword; clears byte_142FEC52A; then SceneUnit_Release on every scene object.

name: SceneUnits_SaveRestore
purpose: Copies the scene units, the scene list, the CLUT image and the CLUT manager to or from the battle capture.

behavior.text: with restore = 1 it copies the 16 scene-unit records back (0x140D30030, 0x5480 bytes), recomputes their frame and sequence table pointers (+0x220 / +0x228 and the saved copies +0x230 / +0x238) from each record's sprite byte, rebuilds the scene list `qword_140D3A410` from the in-use flags, links each battle unit through g_UnitSceneSlotIndex (scene +0x148 = unit) and restores g_ClutImage (0x1C00 bytes) and g_ClutManager (0x86DC bytes).

name: SceneVar_Alu
proto: uint32_t SceneVar_Alu(int op, int dst, int src, int64_t extra, char flag)
purpose: The second task group's event variable arithmetic unit. The event interpreter calls it directly to carry out the variable opcodes 0xB0 to 0xBE.

behavior.text: the same arithmetic as EventVar_Alu: even operations use `src` as a literal, odd ones read a variable, variable 33 is the 16-bit random source (`seed * 25173 + 13849`), and operations 176 to 190 are add, subtract, multiply, divide, modulo, AND, OR and clear.
the same write-lock rules and constants (960, 508 and the 0xC test), using SceneVar_Read for the lock check and SceneVar_ResolveSlot to find the storage.
errors (divide by zero, variable id of 1024 or more) call SceneTask_Terminate instead of EventTask_Terminate.
takes two extra arguments compared with the first-group copy.
called by SceneVar_Read, SceneVar_Write and directly by EventScript_Run.

notes: The operation numbers 176 to 190 are the event opcodes 0xB0 to 0xBE, so the interpreter can pass the opcode straight through.
open_questions: What the two extra arguments do.

name: SceneVar_Read
callers: About 250 call sites, including EventScript_Run (15), EventScript_LoadCurrent and many scene and battle routines.
purpose: Reads one event variable by index through the second task group's copy of the variable system. The event interpreter and most scene code use this copy; it is by far the most used accessor.

behavior.text: identical in logic to EventVar_Read, but it works on the store pointer `off_1407830D8` and runs its two steps through SceneVar_Alu.

both pointers (`off_14078DCE8` for the first group and `off_1407830D8` for this one) are set by the task-group init routines to the same storage, `unk_140D40060`, so both copies see the same variables.
about 250 call sites.

notes: See EventVar_Read for the variable layout and the index 34 rule.

name: SceneVar_ResolveSlot
purpose: Maps an event variable index to the address of its dword in the second task group's variable store.

behavior.text: the same mapping as EventVar_ResolveSlot (dwords 0-127, bits 128-863, nibbles 864-1023) on the store pointer `off_1407830D8`.
an index of 1024 or more calls SceneTask_Terminate and returns null.

notes: See EventVar_ResolveSlot.

name: SceneVar_Write
proto: void SceneVar_Write(int index, int value, char flag, int extra)
callers: About 110 call sites, including EventScript_Run (14) and EventMessage_Task.
purpose: Writes one event variable by index through the second task group's copy of the variable system.
