about 110 call sites.

notes: See EventVar_Write.

name: ScreenTaskSet_Run
purpose: Keeps the window tasks of one legacy screen set running; never returns.

behavior.text: reads the set number from the running task record, takes row (number x 64) of the screen task set table (0x140681650) and walks its four slots.

a slot whose task is not running gets its handler started with EventTask_Start (handler all-ones = unused); a running slot whose tag differs from the expected tag is flagged, cleared and, once every flagged slot has ended, started again with the handler.
loops until the task record's first word becomes 255, then ends its own task.
the nine rows are the screens of the command menu family.

notes: Read in full.
open_questions: ?: which screens the nine sets belong to.

name: ScrollBar_SetPosition
proto: void ScrollBar_SetPosition(GUIComponentScrollBar *bar, int pos, char snap, char clamp)
purpose: Game setter for the native scroll bar component (vtable 0x140722238, kind 8 at node+536).

behavior.text: position at +648, lower bound +652, upper bound +656, viewport size +660; smooth floats +672/+676 ease the knob when snap is 0.
the Knob and Base parts carry a visible flag at +144 (used to hide the bar for short lists).
raw writes to +656/+660 are the wrong layout for this class; always use this setter. The node's scale (instance +0x18) controls its drawn length.

name: ScrollHelper_Bind
proto: char ScrollHelper_Bind(ScrollBinding *a1, Node **root, int64_t a3, int64_t a4)
callers: UIAddonFFTOBraveStoryGlossary_vfunc_4, UIAddonFFTOLauncher_vfunc_4, sub_14011245C, sub_14012D25C and 14 more
callees: UIName_Key, GUINode_FindDescendant, GUINode_FindPartByName, GUINode_FindGadgetPart, GUIComponent_UpdateNodeTree, UIName_ReleaseKey
purpose: Binds a screen's scrolling gadget: finds the child named `VScroll` (a scroll bar node, type 8) and its guide part, records the binding and refits the gadget.

registers a binding id into the bar's slot list (+584) and looks the `ScrollBarGuide` part up by name.

name: SDFFont_GetAdvance
purpose: Returns the scaled advance (x, y) of one character: per-axis renderer scale times the glyph record advance, or (0, 0) when the font is unavailable or the glyph is missing.

behavior.text: font slot = dword at renderer+9540; glyph index v6 = SDFFontRenderer_GlyphIndex(renderer, glyphChar).
valid only if byte renderer+189 != 0 AND v6 != 0; otherwise out = (0.0, 0.0).
glyph record address = the qword at +208 of the font object (the font object is the qword at renderer + 8*slot + 64) plus 32*v6 (32-byte records, array pointer at font+208).

out[0] = *(float*)(renderer+9500) * *(float*)(rec+16); out[1] = *(float*)(renderer+9504) * *(float*)(rec+20). So x advance is rec+16 with x scale +9500, y advance rec+20 with y scale +9504 (separate scales per axis).
returns the out pointer. Xrefs: GUITextNode_PlaceGlyph (two sites 0x1403DD85A, 0x1403DD8D0), sub_1403DF09C, plus data refs at 0x143D40180 / 0x143D4018C.
the advance is the only kerning-like quantity read here: no pair kerning is applied in this function.

notes: Pairs with the layout code that steps the pen by this advance. Scale +9500/+9504 are the same fields the EmitGlyph sheet calls separate x and y scales.
open_questions: ? whether rec+16 / rec+20 are pre-multiplied by atlas size or in em units (values not sampled).

name: SDFFont_GetKerning
proto: float *SDFFont_GetKerning(SDFFontRenderer *R, float out[2], unsigned __int16 leftCp, unsigned __int16 rightCp)
purpose: Kerning pair lookup: returns (x, y) kerning for a left / right code point pair of the current font, from the font's own kerning rows plus the second .ker table.

behavior.text: font = qword at R + 8 * dword(R + 9540) + 64. gidR = u16 font[23][rightCp], gidL = u16 font[23][leftCp] (code point -> glyph id table).

glyph record = font[26] + 32 * gidL; when its u16 +2 (row count) is 0 the result row is zero. Otherwise a binary search over the rows at font[27] + 12 * (dword +4): row.first (u16 +0) >= gidR stops, then gidR < row u16 +2 goes left; the hit row supplies qword +0 and dword +8, the x / y values (float at +4 and dword +8).
when font[25] (the .ker table object) is non-null: sub_1403BA2D4(font[25], tmp, gidL, gidR) is looked up and ADDED: x += tmp.x, y += tmp.y. out = (x, y).

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403A9114); matches docs/reference/fonts.md 'Kerning tables'. The row order note (u16 +0 is the last gid, +2 the first, per live check) is in fonts.md.
open_questions: ? as in fonts.md: the exact .ker file offsets (every shipped .ker is 40 bytes, zero records).

name: SDFFont_ItalicShearWidth
purpose: The horizontal overhang of an italic (sheared) glyph per unit of glyph multiplier: the shear slant times the font's metric unit, the current glyph scale and 48.

behavior.text: returns 0.0 when byte R+189 is 0. Otherwise S = (font.+232 * R+9500) * ((R+9524 * 96.0) * 0.5), where font = the qword at R + 8 * dword(R+9540) + 64 (the current font object), font.+232 is a float, R+9500 is the glyph scale (size / 64, set by GUITextNode_SetRenderScale) and R+9524 is the shear.

the shear R+9524 is initialised to 0.1 (0x3DCCCCCD) by the renderer init sub_1403A8694 and is overwritten per node by GUITextNode_SetRenderScale (and by GUIFontRenderer_UploadPalette) with the dword at UIFontSet row +64 (V, st+24 = the set row, [row + 0x40]).
the same value is used as the shear factor (xmm10 = R+9524 when the italic path is on) in SDFFontRenderer_EmitGlyph.

(96 * 0.5) = 48 is the 1/48 unit of one text size unit (see GUITextNode_SetRenderScale), so S * glyph.f is the width in layout units that the sheared top of a glyph sticks out; font.+232 is the font's metric / scale unit that EmitGlyph also multiplies into every glyph dimension (read at 0x1403A9579).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403A942C). Confidence in the name: medium. The arithmetic and its uses (last-glyph width extension, italic transition offsets) are V; calling it a shear 'width' is I because the font field +232 was not identified in the loader. Every use sits behind 'shear > 0 and the glyph's italic byte set', so upright text never reaches it.
open_questions: ? what font+232 is called in the font object (loader not decoded). ? the UIFontSet column that holds the dword at row +64.

name: SDFFontBatch_SortCompare
purpose: qsort comparator for the text batch list: orders 8-byte entries by their first dword, never returns 0.

behavior.text: body is `return *a1 < *a2 ? -1 : 1;` - only the first dword of each entry is read.
equal keys return 1 (never 0), so the sort is not stable and a == b is reported as 'a after b'.
single xref, SDFFontRenderer_Flush at 0x1403A9B8A (callback pointer for qsort).
entries are (key dword, batch index dword) per the Flush sheet; this function does not touch geometry, only batch draw order.

notes: Leaf, 2 instructions of real work. No effect on UVs, kerning or scale.
open_questions: ? whether two batches can share a key (keys believed to be distinct draw sequence numbers; I).

name: SDFFontRenderer_AccumulateBounds
callers: SDFFontRenderer_EmitGlyph (0x1403A99CA, after storing the 4 vertices and before the quad count is incremented)
purpose: Grows the current batch's 2D bounding box (r+7928..7940) by the four vertices of the quad that SDFFontRenderer_EmitGlyph just wrote.

behavior.text: quad is the first of four 48-byte vertices (12 floats each; x at index 0, y at 1 of each); it reads x / y of vertex 0, 1, 2, 3 (quad[0,1], [12,13], [24,25], [36,37]) and takes the min and max of x and of y.

if the box is not initialised (max x r[1984] = r+7936 is not > 0) it stores minX, minY, maxX, maxY into r+7928 / +7932 / +7936 / +7940 (floats r[1982..1985]); else it replaces each stored value by the min of the mins and the max of the maxes.
quirk: initialisation is tested by 'maxX > 0', not by a flag, so a batch whose glyphs all lie entirely at x <= 0 is overwritten again by every glyph (box = the last glyph) rather than grown.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403A9248). Operates on the vertex positions in the renderer's pen space (pen * r+9544 / +9548); Flush divides by those factors. The positions include the italic shear and the rotation (r+9536), so the box is the true quad extent. Nothing is rounded.
open_questions: ? the consumer of the per-batch box on the GPU side.

name: SDFFontRenderer_CloseBatch
callers: SDFFontRenderer_Flush (0x1403A9B6D with key 0 / node 0 to flush the last batch), GUITextNode_Draw (0x1403EA1E8, when the draw sequence number changes; at most 0xC0 batches per node record list)
purpose: Closes the glyph batch being built (all quads emitted since the last close) and starts a new one: stores its quad range, bounding box, node record and sort key in the batch table.

behavior.text: only when r+32 (the device) is set. old key = r+7952, old node = r+240; r+7952 = newKey, r+240 = newNode, and newNode+76 = 1 (marks the node record used).

batch slot k = r+7944 (count); the 40-byte record at r+248+40*k: +0..15 = the 16-byte bounding box r+7928..7940 (minX, minY, maxX, maxY, built by SDFFontRenderer_AccumulateBounds), +16 = first quad (old r+7948), +20 = quad count (r+9520 - old r+7948), +24 = old node, +32 = old key. r+7948 = r+9520 (the running quad count); r+7928..7943 are zeroed for the next batch.
when the closed batch has quads (count != 0) it appends the sort entry (key = old key at r+7956+8*k, index k at r+7960+8*k) and increments r+7944. Empty batches are not listed.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403A8FBC). In SDFFontRenderer_Flush the bounding box floats are divided by the renderer's +9544 / +9548 before they are written to the per-batch GPU buffer. The key is the GUI layer's draw sequence number + 1 (a1+606596 + 1 in GUITextNode_Draw).
open_questions: ? the use of the bounding box on the GPU side (probably a scissor / culling rectangle; not read).

name: SDFFontRenderer_Construct
purpose: Constructor of the SDFFontRenderer: sets its vtable and resets every field (run state defaults, palette / vertex pointers, texture-slot ids) to its initial value. Creates no GPU objects.

behavior.text: *(r+0) = vftable SDFFontRenderer at 0x1407208B8 (slots: 0 sub_1403C4CC4, 1 sub_1403C4CF0, 2 sub_1403A8E6C, 4 SDFFontRenderer_Flush, 5 SDFFontRenderer_ResetFrame, 7 sub_1403A9084, 8 sub_1403AA8BC).

+188 word = 1 (byte +188 = 1, byte +189 = 0: the batch-open flag EmitGlyph tests is cleared); +8 qword = 0; +16 word = 0xFFFF (cMaterial slot id, filled later), +18 word = 0; +184 word = 0xFFFF (tTexture0 slot id), +186 word = 0xFFFF (cSDFConstant slot id); +160..+183 = twelve words of 0xFFFF (tTexture1..12 slot ids).

zeroed qwords: +24 (shader), +32 (technique), +40 (constant buffer), +48 (palette buffer), +56 (palette SRV), +192 / +200 / +208 / +216 / +224 / +232 (layouts and vertex / index buffers), +240, +7928 / +7936 / +7944 and dword +7952, +9516 (palette count; quad count dword +9520 is cleared by the same qword), +9536, +9552 (vertex CPU buffer), +9560 (palette CPU buffer), +9492 (pen x / y).

run-state defaults: +9500 = 1.0f (scale x), +9504 = 1.0f (scale y), +9508 = 0x3F800000 (colour dword), +9512 = 0, +9524 = 0x3DCCCCCD = 0.1f (the italic shear factor EmitGlyph uses), +9528 word = 8, +9530 byte = 0 (italic off), +9544 = +9548 = 1.0f (the two UV-corner divisors Flush rewrites).

memset(r+64, 0, 0x60) = the 12 font-object pointers *(r + 8 * slot + 64) EmitGlyph reads; memset(r+248, 0, 0x1E00) and memset(r+7956, 0, 0x600) clear two large tables (batch / run records; the layout is not read here).
returns r. Called from the renderer-set constructor sub_1403A3044 (0x1403A30DA) and listed in a data table at 0x143D4012C.

notes: Proposed name: SDFFontRenderer_Construct. Pairs with the FrequentUtilRenderer constructor sub_1403AA900 (same base fields +8, +16, +18, +24..+56 zero / 0xFFFF).
open_questions: ? the record layout of the +248 (0x1E00) and +7956 (0x600) tables. ? meaning of the word 8 at +9528 (I: a default font slot or page count; not read where it is used).

name: SDFFontRenderer_CreateResources
callees: sub_1403A7AD8, sub_14001A2C4, sub_140011750 (alloc), sub_1403C043C, sub_140037CA4, sub_140091124 (resource load), sub_1403A7B08, sub_140086D28 / sub_140087318 / sub_140086F64 / sub_140086DE4 / sub_140086E9C (create buffer / SRV / cbuffer / VB / IB), sub_140089280 (slot lookup by name), sub_14008C5D8 (input layout), sub_14003E120 / sub_14003E228 (map / unmap)
purpose: SDFFontRenderer set-up: fills the CPU palette array with 512 default entries, loads shader/SDFFont.tec, creates the palette buffer + its view, the constant buffer, the vertex / index buffers for the glyph quads, looks up the shader slots (tTexture0..12, cSDFConstant), and allocates the CPU vertex buffer.

behavior.text: first sub_1403A7AD8() (sets r+16 = slot of constant buffer 'cMaterial', returns 1); returns 0 if it fails. Every later failure also returns 0 (no cleanup here; callers use the destructor slot).

CPU palette: r+9560 = allocation of 98304 bytes (= 512 entries x 192 bytes). 512 times it writes one 192-byte default entry at stride 192 (layout below). The same 98304 figure is the GPU palette buffer size.

behavior.basis: (combined with the SDFFontRenderer_Flush rewrite list, which names those offsets)
behavior.text: +64 = 0.5 is the threshold T (contour at 0.75 - T/2 = 0.5), +68 = 0.25 the outline term, +76 = 128 becomes 1/128, +80 = 6.0 is the shadow width field Flush tests, +88 = 0.8 and +92 = 0.4 are rewritten ((1-x-.5)*.5+.5 and x*.5), +96 = 0.1 is the value Flush multiplies by 0.005 (the K = 0.1 * 0.005 * g * S constant of fonts.md; 0.1 is exactly this default), +128 is the colour Flush substitutes for +112 when the shadow width is 0, +188 -> 1 - x.

roles of +112 = (0,0,0,1) (shadow colour, black), +128 = (0,0,0.2,1) (alternate shadow colour, dark blue), +144 white, +160 = (0.2, 0.5, 0.9, 1) (a colour) and the values +72 = 2.8, +84 = -6.0, +100 = 1.0 were not read where they are used here.

shader: sub_140091124(qword_143CD9B88, 'shader/SDFFont.tec', hash from sub_140037CA4, 0, &zeroed 32-byte out) -> r+24; null -> return 0. sub_1403A7B08(r, shader) appends it to the owner list at *(r+8) (vector push_back).

palette GPU buffer r+48 = sub_140086D28(descriptor {size 0x18000 = 98304, flags 0x10802, stride 192}, kind 20); r+56 = sub_140087318 (shader resource view of that buffer, descriptor words {0, 1, 0x20000000000}); r+40 = sub_140086F64 constant buffer, descriptor {128 bytes, 66563 = 0x10403}, kind 20 (contents not read here; I: per-frame transform / screen constants).

slot ids: r+160..+182 words = sub_140089280(table at *(qword_140C696A8 + 5064), 'tTexture1'..'tTexture12'); r+184 = 'tTexture0'; r+186 = sub_140089280(table at *(qword_140C696A8 + 5056), 'cSDFConstant'). r+9528 word = 8.

vertex layout r+192 = sub_14008C5D8(*(qword_140C696A8 + 5016), 5 element descriptors {0xB24100000240000, 0xDA128000C222000, 0xE200000}, 5) = a 5-element input layout (I: matches the 48-byte vertex EmitGlyph writes: position, alpha dword, UV, float4, colour).

glyph VB r+200 = sub_140086DE4(size 786432 = 0xC0000 = 4096 quads x 4 vertices x 48 bytes, flags 65794); glyph IB r+208 = sub_140086E9C(size 49152 = 4096 x 6 x 2 bytes, flags 513). The IB is mapped (sub_14003E120), then for quad n (0..4095) six 16-bit indices 4n, 4n+1, 4n+2, 4n+3, 4n+3, 4n+4 are written, then unmapped (sub_14003E228): a triangle strip per quad with a degenerate join to the next quad's first vertex.
CPU vertex buffer r+9552 = allocation of 786432 bytes (EmitGlyph writes 4 x 48-byte vertices per glyph into it, quad n at 4n); null -> return 0.

second small geometry set: layout r+216 = sub_14008C5D8(..., {2228224}, 1) (one element); VB r+224 = sub_140086DE4(size 6144, flags 65794); IB r+232 = sub_140086E9C(size 1536 = 192 x 4 x 2, flags 513) filled with strip indices 4n..4n+3 for n in 0..191 (0xC0 quads, no degenerate join). I: 6144 = 192 quads x 4 vertices x 8 bytes, a corner table (the 'quad UV corner table' of Flush); what it draws was not read.

no sampler state, blend state, rasteriser or depth object is created or described anywhere in this function; the only palette-like GPU object is the 98304-byte buffer + view, and cSDFConstant is looked up as a slot id only (r+186). Nothing here touches UV derivatives (that is pixel-shader work).
returns 1 on success.

notes: Proposed name: SDFFontRenderer_CreateResources. The cSDFConstant here is only the slot id at r+186 (I: Flush binds the palette buffer to it; the binding is in Flush, not read now) and is a different thing from the 'cSDF' 32-byte buffer of UIRender_ApplyDrawState. Default palette numbers fit fonts.md: T 0.5, K factor 0.1 x 0.005.
open_questions: ? the 5 vertex element semantics / formats (descriptor words not decoded). ? what the 8-byte-vertex second geometry set is drawn for. ? exact contents of the 128-byte constant buffer at r+40. ? blend and sampler state (not here; see Flush / ApplyDrawState).

name: SDFFontRenderer_EmitGlyph
purpose: Emits the quad of one glyph (position, atlas UV, node alpha, palette index, per-vertex factor g = atlasWidth / 8192) for the SDF text shader, and advances the pen.

behavior.text: does nothing unless r+189 (batch open) is set and the glyph index is non-zero.

run state read from the renderer: pen x / y floats at +9492 / +9496, run scale x / y floats at +9500 / +9504 (SEPARATE x and y scales), colour dword +9508, a dword at +9512 copied into every vertex's w, italic flag byte +9530 with the shear factor float +9524 (zero when the flag is clear), rotation angle float +9536 (radians), palette / font slot dword +9540, vertex buffer pointer +9552, quad count dword +9520. The font object is *(r + 8 * slot + 64).

font object: 32-byte glyph records at *(font + 208) (+8 x offset float, +12 y offset float, +16 advance float, +24 / +26 / +28 / +30 atlas x, y, w, h as u16), atlas inverse size (1 / W, 1 / H) at *(font + 224), font scale float at +232 (multiplies both run scales).

quad corners = pen + rotate(angle, (xoff * sx, yoff * sy) + (0 or w * sx * fs) in x / (0 or h * sy * fs) in y), i.e. the glyph offsets use the run scale only and the glyph size also the font scale fs (+232); when the italic flag is set the x of the top corners shifts by -(yoff * sy + corner height) * shear. UV = atlas rect * (1 / W, 1 / H).

each of the 4 vertices is 48 bytes: position xy, node-alpha dword (w), UV, a float4 (sx * fs, sy * fs, slot, 1 / (invW * 8192) = W / 8192 = g), colour dword. The quad is written at index 4 * count; then SDFFontRenderer_AccumulateBounds is called and the count incremented.
the pen then advances by rotate(angle, (sx * advance, 0)) (advance = record +16), so the pen advance uses the x scale only.

the title's effective on-screen scale is 0.41667 = 0.3125 / 0.75, i.e. the traced run scale (+9500, = size / 64 x 2/3) divided by the font's metric unit (unit_px_per_metric 0.75); a replica of the shader with quads at the traced pen positions and that scale lands within 0.03 px and 1.0001 x of the GPU glyph geometry. So fs (font + 232) is 1 / unit_px_per_metric = 1.3333 (I: the value itself was not read from memory) and the record offsets / advances in the extractor JSON are the metric-unit values the studio multiplies by the same effective scale.

the per-vertex float4 carries sx * fs and sy * fs separately: the pixel shader's UV derivatives (and therefore K and the five tap offsets) see an anisotropic run. Live trace 2026-10-29 of the Job Tree: the title run is square (0.3125 x 0.3125); the Lv prefix / chip / badge runs of the overflow-mode-2 nodes are 0.2053 x 0.25 (x = box width / natural width). The studio now samples with separate sx / sy (GameFont.draw xscale; sdfParams xk).

notes: Run state was read live by tracing this function with --mem rcx+9500 (the rcx object is stable across glyphs of a frame).
open_questions: K = 0.1 * 0.005 * g * S: the 0.005 comes from SDFFontRenderer_Flush's palette rewrite (see fonts.md). The quad geometry was read from the decompile, not checked against a captured vertex buffer. (The title's former 1.1 edge residual was a studio bug, not the game: GameFont's run cache was blitted at a fractional y; fixed 2026-10-29, title 0.30.)

name: SDFFontRenderer_Flush
purpose: Uploads the frame's glyph quads and palette entries to the GPU and issues the batched SDF text draws; rewrites every palette entry into the form the pixel shader uses.

behavior.text: with mode 0 and a live renderer it closes the current batch (sub_1403A8FBC), sorts the batches, copies 192 bytes per glyph quad vertex group from +9552 and 192 bytes per palette entry from +9560 (count +9516) into the mapped GPU buffers.

while copying, each palette entry is transformed in place (offsets in bytes of the entry): [96] = [96] * 0.005; [104] = ([68] * 128) * 0.5 (the outline layer's coverage cap = outline threshold * 64); [64] = ((1 - [64]) - 0.5) * 0.5 + 0.5 = 0.75 - T / 2; [68] = ((1 - [64] - [68]) - 0.5) * 0.5 + 0.5; [76] = 1 / [76]; [88] = ((1 - [88]) - 0.5) * 0.5 + 0.5; [92] = [92] * 0.5; [188] = 1 - [188]; and the shadow colour [112] is replaced by [128] when the shadow width [80] is 0.

consequence: the shader's contour sits at d = 0.75 - T / 2 (T = UIFontSet.Unknown8, times Unknown30 = 1.1 for bold runs), so a larger T makes text HEAVIER (T 0.605 gives 0.4475), and the edge half-width is K = 0.1 * 0.005 * g * S. The CPU copy at +9560 (what a live memory read sees) is the untransformed one.
also builds the quad UV corner table (+9544 / +9548 divisors) and binds up to 12 atlas pages (tTexture0..12) and the cSDFConstant buffer per batch.

per batch it applies four programs of the SDFFont technique (ShaderSelector_Apply): program 2 with a 4-vertex draw on the target at g_Renderer + 23720 + 800 * block, program 4 with a 4-vertex draw on the target at g_Renderer + 23640 + 800 * block, program 1 with the glyph instances (sub_1400ADB20) on that same +23640 target, and program 0 with the glyph instances on the +23720 target.

behavior.basis: (the technique file shader/SDFFont.tec, its five 64-byte program entries read with the ShaderProgram_ApplyState layout; blend word decoded with BlendDesc_FromWords, depth word with the depth-stencil decoder sub_140051438: bit 0 enable, bit 1 write, bits 2..4 + 1 = comparison)
behavior.text: program 0 blend SRC_ALPHA / INV_SRC_ALPHA (alpha ONE / INV_SRC_ALPHA), depth off; program 1 blending off, depth on, written, LESS_EQUAL; programs 2 and 3 blend ONE / INV_SRC_ALPHA, depth off; program 4 blending off, depth written, ALWAYS.

of the file's pixel shaders only the fill shader (blob at 0x3558) writes SV_Depth; the depth it writes is 1 - d (d = the distance at the pixel centre). I (shader index lists in file order: program 0 = VS 0x640 + PS 0x1450 the shadow, 1 = VS 0x2764 + PS 0x3558 the fill, 2 = VS 0x5EE4 + PS 0x67B0, 4 = VS 0x5EE4 + PS 0x7004): the fill glyphs are drawn without blending into a target whose depth was reset by program 4, so where glyph quads overlap the glyph with the largest d keeps the pixel, and the shadow glyphs are blended one by one. The studio models it so (behavior TextFillPassDrawnAsOneShape).

notes: Found by following the SDFFont setup at sub_1403A87EC to the code that reads the +9552 / +9560 buffers.

name: SDFFontRenderer_GlyphIndex
purpose: Maps the UTF-8 character at the pointer to the glyph slot of the current font: decodes the code point and looks it up in the font's 65536-entry u16 table; 0 means 'no glyph'.

behavior.text: font = r + 8 * (u32 r+9540) + 64 (the active font slot set by GUITextNode_SetRenderScale); returns 0 when r+189 (renderer ready) is 0. Otherwise it decodes one UTF-8 sequence with sub_1403BF9D4 (up to 6 bytes; a code point above 0xFFFF becomes 9632 = U+25A0) and returns u16 table[codepoint] where table = *(font + 184).

the returned slot indexes the 32-byte glyph records at *(font + 208) used by SDFFontRenderer_EmitGlyph (+8 x offset, +12 y offset, +16 advance, +24..30 atlas x, y, w, h as u16, +20 / +28 / +30 other fields); the atlas size reciprocal is *(font + 224).
sub_1403A9A9C (the advance query used by layout) calls it and returns (scaleX * rec+16, scaleY * rec+20) for the glyph, zero when the glyph is 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403A9474). Called once per glyph. A code point with table entry 0 is silently not drawn. The .fnt-derived table and records are described in docs/reference/fonts.md.

when set it also requires dword shader+84 == 1, shader+80 == 1 and dword shader+104 == 0, then r[4] (+32 technique) = sub_14039EB08(shader, 0); non-null -> return 1.
otherwise (flag clear, a condition failed, or technique creation returned null) it calls vtable slot 2 (+16) on r, i.e. sub_1403A8E6C, and returns 0.
shader+80 / +84 are load-state values (1 = done) and +104 an error count; the names are not read. No retry loop is in this function.

name: ShaderProgram_ApplyState
purpose: Binds one program: its shader objects into the thread state and the pipeline-state words (raster word, blend state word, the blend words of the render targets, blend-factor flags) from its 64-byte entry.

behavior.text: t = sel + 24 of the calling ShaderSelector_Apply: t[2] = the shader object array (sel+40), t[3] = the 64-byte program entries (sel+48), t[4] = the program table of the current permutation (sel+56, 8 bytes per program), t[5] = the shader index list (sel+64, dwords). program is the index within the selected permutation.

entry = t->entries + (program << 6); shader indices come from t->list at the offset stored in t->programs[program] (first dword), count = entry byte +57 starting at slot entry byte +56; each shader object pointer (t->shaders[index]) is written to ts + 8*slot + 152.
when (entry byte +58 & 3) == 3 and the byte at (qword_140C696A8 + 3464) equals 2, the index list is read count entries further on (a second shader set for that program).

entry dword +0 is both data and a mask of what to copy: its low 6 bits replace the low 6 bits of ts+124; bit 0x40 copies the raster word (entry+48 & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF1FFF) to ts+112; bit 0x80 replaces the low 5 bits of the qword at ts+104 with those of the qword at entry+40; bit 0x100 replaces all bits of ts+104 except those under mask 0x100001FFF (bits 0..12 and bit 32, which keep their value) with the qword at entry+40; bits 0x200 and 0x3FC00 as in the next bullets.
mask bit 0x200: the dword at entry+4 is stored at ts+120 and bit 0x100 of ts+124 is cleared.

mask bits 0x3FC00 (bit 10 + i selects word i of the eight dwords at entry+8..+39): word 0 is stored whole at ts+120; word i = 1..7 is stored with its top bit cleared at ts + 5964 + 4 * (i - 1); afterwards ts+124 |= 0x100. The sampler words of the context (ts+5704 + 4 * slot, 64 slots, +5704..+5959) are not touched by this copy.
for every word selected by 0x3FC00, bit i of the dword ts+6008 is set when any of four 5-bit fields of that word (masks 0x1F0, 0x3E00, 0x3E0000, 0x7C00000) equals 13 or 14, else cleared.

the eight words are the blend words of render targets 0..7, not sampler words. Basis: RenderContext_ResetFrame fills the same slots (ts+120 and ts+5964..+5991) with one constant, 0x78020010, which the BlendDesc_FromWords decode reads as blending off, ONE / ZERO factors, write mask 0xF; RenderState_PackCommand packs ts+120 followed by ts+5964 + 4 * (i - 1) as one word array (the count is bits 9..11 of ts+124, used when bit 0x100 is set), the order of the words BlendDesc_FromWords takes; the render-thread side that hands the packed words to BlendDesc_FromWords was not read.

the four 5-bit fields tested are the source, destination, source-alpha and destination-alpha factor fields of the BlendDesc_FromWords decode, whose stored value plus 1 gives the Direct3D 12 factor: 13 and 14 give BLEND_FACTOR (14) and INV_BLEND_FACTOR (15). So bit i of ts+6008 would mean that render target i's blend word uses the blend factor colour. Basis: that decode, and RenderState_PackCommand, which appends the 16-byte colour at ts+5992 to the command (command flag 0x80) when ts+6008 is non-zero.

behavior.basis: (live, 2026-10-29: the mask program resolved to object 60 = PS 03DF10 and the shadow program to objects 5 / 52 = VS 035438 / PS 035E50, each the neighbour pair in file order)
behavior.text: shader object index 10 + k = the k-th pixel shader of UIRender.tec in file order, and index 1..9 = the nine vertex shaders in file order.

notes: Live UI technique: program 0 = shader objects (1, 10), 1 = (2, 11), 2 = (1, 12), 3 = (2, 13), 4.. = (3, 14..). Shader object index 10 + k is the k-th pixel shader of UIRender.tec in file order: programs 0..3 = 1E9C (plain image), 3964 (remap), 4990 (SDF), 5560 (SDF remap) (M: order match; programs 2 and 3 match the cSDF/cUIRenderRemap bindings). For selector #10 (GUILayer_CopyToTarget / GUILayer_BlurShadowPass) program 0 was read live as vertex 034080 + pixel 0349C0 and program 1 = vertex 035438 + pixel 035E50.
open_questions: ? the meaning of entry byte +58 and of the global byte at (qword_140C696A8 + 3464) (an alternate shader set). ? who sets bits 9..11 of ts+124 (the number of blend words) for a program that carries per-target words: this function only sets bit 0x100. ? what the render thread does with the ts+6008 bits beyond the blend-factor colour that RenderState_PackCommand appends.

name: ShaderSelector_Apply
proto: int ShaderSelector_Apply(ShaderSelector *sel, ThreadState *ts, unsigned int program)
callers: UIRender_ApplyDrawState, SDFFontRenderer_Flush, UIBlur_CopyTarget, UIBlur_DrawPass, UIBlur_DrawTexturedPass, UIBlur_DownsampleDispatch, GUILayer_CopyToTarget, GUILayer_BlurShadowPass, GUILayer_BlitFinal, GUILayer_GlowPass, GUILayer_EffectPass0, UIRender_DrawOverlayQuads, UIRender_DrawLetterbox, sub_1403AC420, sub_1403AC620, sub_1403ACEBC, sub_1403AF890, sub_1403AFA9C, sub_1403AFD34, sub_1403AFF8C, sub_1403B5170, sub_1403B53C8, sub_1403B5664, sub_1403C595C, sub_1403CB9C4
purpose: Resolves the selector's current permutation index to a program table and applies the program with the given index (within that permutation) to the thread state.

behavior.text: when the dirty byte sel+76 is set, program table pointer sel+56 = techniqueProgramTable (tech+136) + 8 * (table[slot].base (+24) + permutationIndex (sel+24) * table[slot].stride (+20)), where table = tech+120 with 32-byte entries and slot = sel+72; clears the dirty byte.

then tail-jumps to ShaderProgram_ApplyState(sel + 24, ts, program): the third argument (register r8d) is passed through unchanged. It is the program index within the selected permutation: the program-table slot is the pointer at sel+56 plus 8 * program and the 64-byte state entry is the pointer at sel+48 plus 64 * program.

most call sites pass literal indices, for example: GUILayer_CopyToTarget 0, GUILayer_BlurShadowPass 1, GUILayer_BlitFinal 0, GUILayer_GlowPass 0, GUILayer_EffectPass0 3, sub_1403B53C8 2, sub_1403B5170 4, UIRender_DrawOverlayQuads 5, UIRender_DrawLetterbox 0, SDFFontRenderer_Flush 0..4, UIRender_ApplyDrawState 0, sub_1403AF890 7, sub_1403AFD34 3, sub_1403AFF8C 4, sub_1403B5664 1, sub_1403CB9C4 0; the decompile shows two arguments where the value is a zeroed register.

the UI manager (*(g_Renderer + 37936)) keeps its selectors as pointers at +8 * index: #9 (+72) is used by GUILayer_BlitFinal and sub_1403CB9C4, #10 (+80) by GUILayer_CopyToTarget (program 0) and GUILayer_BlurShadowPass (program 1).

The program index (third argument) is a literal at most call sites and is easy to miss in the decompile, which drops a zeroed register.

name: ShaderSelector_SetDigit
callers: UIBlur_DrawPass, sub_1403AD710, UIBlur_CopyTarget (sub_1403ABEDC), the glow / effect passes that bind a sampler state
purpose: Sets one mixed-radix digit of the selector's state dword (the permutation index that ShaderSelector_Apply uses) and marks the state dirty.

behavior.text: state = dword at s+24; the radix table is the dword array at s+32 with the count at s+28. When slot < count: v8 = table[slot], v9 = table[slot + 1] (1 when slot + 1 >= count).

the old digit (state % v8) / v9 is the return value. The new state replaces that digit: state = state - state % v8 + state % v8 % v9 + v9 * (value * v9 < v8 ? value : 0), so a value that does not fit in the radix is stored as 0.
the state is written back and the byte at s+76 is set to 1 on every call, including when slot is out of range (then the state is unchanged and the return value is an uninitialised register).

notes: The name is ours. The blur code calls it as sub_1403C4AA8(*(b + 32 or 48), slot, value) with slots 0..2. That the object is the selector handed to ShaderSelector_Apply is inferred from its use next to those calls.

name: Shop_BuildItemList
proto: int Shop_BuildItemList(unsigned short unit, short shop, unsigned short category, unsigned short *out, int mode, int sort)
purpose:
Builds the item id list of one shop or of the Poachers' Den into a caller-supplied buffer, applying the shop mask, the
story-progress gate, a menu-category filter and an optional equipment check, and returns the number of ids written.

behavior.text:
the first argument is the unit used by the equipment check, the second is the shop number, the third selects the menu
  category, the fourth is the output buffer, and the fifth and sixth are the mode and sort flags passed on the stack.

shop numbers 0 through 14 take the town-shop branch; 15 through 99 produce an empty list; 100 and above take the
  Poachers' Den branch.

in the town branch, the story-progress value is read once from event variable 111 and each candidate item is skipped
  when the byte at offset 10 of its record is larger than that value.

in the town branch, the shop mask is two bytes per item id at 0x14067F890, first byte high, combined as a 16-bit word;
  shop s is present when bit (0x8000 shifted right by s) is set. Shop 0 is the high bit of the first byte.

in the den branch, the mask and the progress byte are not consulted; an id is listed when PoachersDen_AddStock called
  with a zero delta returns a non-zero count. The menu-category filter and the equip check still apply.

the menu-category filter compares Item_MenuCategory of the id against a pair derived from the category argument: 0 or 1
  accept categories 0 and 1, 2 accepts 2, 3 accepts 3, 4 accepts 4, 5 accepts 0, 6 accepts 1 and 7 accepts 5.

mode 2 keeps only items the unit can equip; mode 1 keeps every item but sets the 0x4000 bit on ids the unit cannot
  equip; mode 0 performs no equipment check.

each accepted id is appended as a 16-bit word and the list is terminated with 0xFFFF after the last one; the
  terminator is an all-ones register stored as a word, so the literal 0xFFFF is not in the immediate stream.
when the sort flag is non-zero the finished list is reordered by `sub_140285B10` with order group 6.
the function performs no bound check on the output pointer; the count grows only with the number of accepted ids.
the town loop visits ids 0 through 255 and the den loop visits ids 0 through 260 in the pristine code.
the shop mask table lives in read-only data and nothing in the image writes it.

the 0x4000 bit travels with the id in the same word, so the list entry is a packed id-plus-flag value rather than a
  bare id (the OR is at 0x140288FBD and 0x140289061, and the word is stored at 0x140288FC4 and 0x140289068).
why shop numbers between 15 and 99 exist; no caller passes one and they do not fall into the den branch.

the cannot-equip bit is written by both list loops: the constant 0x4000 is loaded at 0x140288F12 (town) and 0x140288FF5 (den), ORed into the id at 0x140288FBD and 0x140289061, and the 16-bit word is stored at 0x140288FC4 and 0x140289068. The bit travels with the id because the store is a plain word write.

notes:
- Only the shop-mask reads were studied in the first sheet; the loop bounds, the category pairs and the two equipment
  modes were added from the second read.
open_questions: - ?: the meaning of the mask bit for shop slot 15, which no reader of the three that exist ever tests.

callers: Unit_BuildJobUnlockMask, Job_LearnAbilityByMenu, PartyUnit_FillFromWork, sub_140226E44, sub_1402867BC, sub_14028A370, sub_1402C4D1C, sub_1402DE564, sub_1402FE1D0, sub_140316D24, sub_14033B420, sub_140348828, sub_140360048, sub_1403783F0, sub_140388EB4, sub_14038BF34, sub_140392620
purpose: Builds the 24-entry ability list of a skillset into a shared static buffer, keeping only the ability classes the caller's mask allows. Used by the job menu, learning, battle lists and the unlock mask.

behavior.text: a set id above 255 is treated as set 0; entries 0..23 are filled from Skillset_GetAbility (slots 22 and 23 are always 0).
classification by id: below 0x1A6 needs mask bit 1; 0x1A6..0x1C5 needs bit 2; 0x1C6..0x1E6 needs bit 8; above 0x1E6 needs bit 4. A class the mask lacks is replaced by 0.
only for set 224: id 488 is kept only when mask bit 0x20 is set, and id 491 only when bit 0x10 is set.
returns the address of the static buffer, so a later call overwrites an earlier result.

callers pass 31 (0x1F) or 47 (0x2F) depending on bit 0x40 of party-record byte +112, which swaps which of the two set-224 abilities is offered (I: a unit flag, meaning not traced). The unlock check uses 15.

notes:
An ability id above 0x1E6 is kept or dropped by the movement-ability class rule. The list is written into the game's static list (0x143D1A1C0), whose address the function returns.

The four id classes line up with the action, reaction, support and movement ability ranges; the class bit decides which kinds a screen lists.
open_questions: Which unit flag sets bit 0x40 at party +112.

tab 0 keeps ids 1..421 (actions), 1 keeps 422..453 (reactions), 2 keeps 454..485 (supports), 3 keeps 486..509 (movement), any other tab 1..509; the others become 0. Returns the buffer.

name: Skillset_GetAbility
callers: Skillset_BuildAbilityList, sub_14020D190, sub_14021DE98, sub_140271EFC, sub_14027612C, sub_1402781A8, sub_140278358, sub_14030CD08, sub_14030DD8C, sub_14030E368, sub_14030EC48
purpose: Returns the ability id stored in one slot of a skillset, or 0 when the set or slot does not exist.

behavior.text: three storage blocks. Sets 0..175: 25 bytes each at 0x14067E210, slots 0..21. Sets 224..226: the same 25-byte layout directly after set 175 (at 0x14067F340). Sets 176..223: 5 bytes each at 0x14067F4C0, slots 0..3.
25-byte set: 3 flag bytes, then 22 low bytes. 5-byte set: 1 flag byte, then 4 low bytes.
the id is the low byte plus 0x100 when the slot's flag bit is set; the flag for slot k is bit 7 - (k mod 8) of flag byte k / 8, so ids reach 0x1FF.
any other set id (227 and above), or a slot beyond the block's range, returns 0.
slots 0..15 are the action abilities and 16..21 the reaction, support and movement slots; one caller walks 16..21 separately.
a negative set id falls into the first block and a negative slot reads before the row (no lower-bound check).
leaf; writes rax, rcx, rdx, r8, r9, r10 only.

the only code that reads the three blocks. Three other operands land inside them by displacement but read other tables: UnitWork_InitFromSpawnRecord (the JobNeedLevel rows through the virtual base 0x14067F384) and sub_140281A64 / sub_140282E38 (a byte table at the virtual base 0x14067F58A indexed by an action id; whether an index below 0x26 can occur is open).

notes:
The set id of a job is byte 0 of its JobTable row. Sets 224..226 belong to special characters; 176..223 are monster sets.
Proposed data names: g_SkillsetTable (176 x 25), g_SkillsetTableMonster (48 x 5), g_SkillsetTableSpecial (3 x 25) (the IDB already uses these).

- Correction: a leaf function with three `img` table references.

purpose: Plays one of the common novel sound effects by id: it finds a free channel, loads the sound from the shared novel sound bank and starts it.

the volume and pan values; only the zero ramp is passed here.

name: SoundCue_Play
callers: EventCmd_AllocSlot, EventChannel_BindStepTask, EventScript_SkipTick, JobScreen_ShowPopup, sub_1400F4BCC, sub_140269554, sub_14026B310, EffectScript_OpRunTimeline, sub_14031CF90 and about 20 more battle effect and UI functions
purpose: Plays a sound cue on the first free sound channel of 13..19: remaps the cue with IdRemap_Lookup, drops it when the result is above 0x2B1, and returns the channel used or -1.

behavior.text: the cue is passed through IdRemap_Lookup first; a result above 0x2B1 (which includes -1, the remap table's "no sound") returns -1 and plays nothing.
it then tests channels 13 to 19 in order with sub_1401D7808 on the sound manager qword_143CD9DD8 and stops at the first channel where that test returns 0 (free); all seven busy returns -1.
on a free channel it calls sub_1401D736C(manager, channel, remapped cue), stores the remapped cue in dword_14375F8C4[channel - 13] and returns the channel number.

a battle effect's sound event reaches it from EffectScript_OpRunTimeline with cue = the effect track value + dword_14114B124 - 1 (0x730000 for a stock Potion); IdRemap_Lookup turns 0x730000 into 0x137, which plays (the Potion chime). A cue the remap table does not list is returned unchanged and, being above 0x2B1, is dropped silently.

notes: Read 2026-11-12. Every caller passes a cue id, not a resource handle; the bound 0x2B1 is checked after the remap, so the remap table is what makes the large cue ids (effect bank values such as 0x730000) playable.

name: Startup_InstallExceptionHandling
callees: SetUnhandledExceptionFilter, GetCurrentProcessId, DebugActiveProcess, GetUserNameW, sub_14006E530, sub_140031F44, GetLocalTime, set_invalid_parameter_handler, sub_1405DA7FC
purpose: Installs the top-level unhandled-exception filter and the startup diagnostic state: the self-debug call, the user name, the DebugDump path, the lock-file name and the invalid-parameter handler.

behavior.text: calls `SetUnhandledExceptionFilter(TopLevelExceptionFilter)`.
calls `DebugActiveProcess(GetCurrentProcessId())` at `0x14002EC47`; the result is not checked. A process cannot normally debug itself, so the call's practical effect is I, not established.
reads the user name with `GetUserNameW` into `word_142FCF080` (zeroed on failure).

returns 0. The caller is `sub_14002DEFC` (application initialization), reached from `faith::Framework::Application_vfunc_1`.

name: Status_ListCategory
purpose: Returns the list category of a status from its UIStatusEffect text row: 1 a gain, 2 an ailment, anything else not listed.

finds nxd table 57 (UIStatusEffect) through NxdRegistry_Find once and keeps it in qword_143CDA3D0, looks up the row whose key is the status + 1 with NxdTable_GetRowById, and returns -1 when the table or the row is missing.

returns the dword at row +0x14 (the list_category column: 1 for Float, Reraise, Regen, Protect, Shell, Haste, Faith, Atheist, Reflect; 2 for KO, Stone, Poison, Slow, Stop, Doom and the other ailments; 0 for Readying, Jumping, Evading, Performing).

returns the signed word at row +0x20 (the sort_order column: 1 Protect, 2 Shell, 3 Regen, 21 Poison, 39 Doom ...).

name: StatusList_BuildFromResultBlock
purpose: Lists the statuses a result block adds and removes, as one byte per status, sorted by display priority.

behavior.text: returns 0 when the block or the list pointer is null, otherwise 1.

scans the status ids 0..39 in order (a fixed loop of 40); for each id whose bit is set in the pending-remove set (block +34) it appends the id with bit 0x80 set, and for each id whose bit is set in the pending-add set (block +29) it appends the plain id; the removal of an id is therefore listed before its addition.
the entries are appended at the position *count, which it advances; the bit of id s is 0x80 shifted right by (s & 7) in byte s >> 3 of the set.
finally it sorts the appended range with qsort and Status_ComparePriority (which masks off bit 0x80, gives 0 for an id of 40 or more, and orders by the property table priority, largest first).

notes: Name is ours. The list is one byte per entry, so the 0x80 flag leaves seven bits for an id. V (traced live 2026-11-17): UnitPanel_FillEffectLine builds it for the unit status panel (action preview, enemy target panel); the labels over a hit unit do not use it (ResultLabel_QueueFromUnit walks the sets itself).

name: StatusScreen_BuildLists

behavior.text: clears both counts (+0x188, +0x18C) and sets the 40 dwords of each list (+0x48, +0xE8) to -1.

walks the 40 bits of the set byte by byte from bit 7 down (status = 8 x byte + position from the top bit) and puts each set status into the gains list when Status_ListCategory gives 1, into the ailments list when it gives 2.
sorts both lists with qsort and CompareFunction (Status_ListSortKey), copies the 16 countdown bytes to +0x19C, then tail-jumps to StatusScreen_DrawLists.

name: StatusVoice_SpeakEvent
purpose: Speaks the voice line of a status event: the line is read from the UIStatusEffect rows of every status in the event's mask and spoken only when the non-zero values agree.

name: StdSort_LayersByKey
purpose: The introsort loop of MSVC's std::sort for an array of layer pointers keyed by the unsigned dword at layer+84 (the draw-order key); the final sort of UIRender_PrepareLayers, whose result is the order in which GUILayer_PackAtlasRect places the layers.

behavior.text: same loop as StdSort_LayersByOrder with the key at +84: insertion sort up to 32 elements (stable), above that partition steps (StdSort_PartitionPtrByDword84, median of three up to 41 elements, Tukey ninther above, three-way partition around the pivot run), recursion into the smaller side, heap fallback (StdSort_PopHeapHolePtrByDword84) when the ideal depth reaches 0.

above 32 elements the sort is therefore not stable: layers with equal keys can leave their creation order. Live (2026-10-30, 63 layers): keys 74 (slots 17 and 25) and 206 (slots 51 and 58) are ties; the slots 17, 25 keep their order and the slots 58, 51 come out reversed. A model of the partition code that follows the decompile reproduces the whole list order of the frame (checked on the sorted list kept at UIManager+4312).
the key is mode | (4 x order + 4) with the order from UIRender_PrepareLayers (see that sheet), so ties are layers of equal order and mode.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403C2B00). The sorted pointer array stays in memory after the frame (UIManager+4312); the count at +172 is cleared by UIRender_ClearLayerFlags, so a reader after the frame must take the entries up to the first null or use the slot order.

name: StdSort_LayersByOrder
purpose: The introsort loop of MSVC's std::sort for an array of layer pointers, keyed by the unsigned dword at layer+12 (the layer's order); UIRender_PrepareLayers sorts the collected layer list with it before it computes the draw order.

behavior.text: loop on the range [first, last): up to 32 elements (256 bytes) it runs an insertion sort; with more elements and ideal > 0 it calls StdSort_PartitionPtrByDword12 and sets ideal = (ideal >> 2) + (ideal >> 1), then recurses into the smaller side and loops on the larger one (the lower part is recursed when it is smaller, otherwise the upper part); with ideal <= 0 it falls back to a heap sort (make-heap loop from the middle down, then pop the largest to the end repeatedly) using StdSort_PopHeapHolePtrByDword12. The initial ideal is the element count.

insertion sort: for each element, a key below the first element's key moves the whole prefix up by one (memmove) and takes the first slot; otherwise it is inserted by shifting while its key is below the previous one's (strict less-than, so equal keys keep their order: stable). Keys are compared as unsigned dwords.

the call from UIRender_PrepareLayers passes the list at UIManager+4312 and its end (count at +172). The keys at that time are the slot indices (GUIRenderer_ResetFrame writes layer+12 = index for every record each frame) and the list was filled in slot order, so the array is already ascending with distinct keys and the sort changes nothing (V live: the first 63 entries of a running frame, slots 0..62).

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403C2930). Identical in structure to StdSort_LayersByKey (key at +84). With the ideal depth halving by 3/4 per level the heap fallback needs more than 20 partition levels for the largest list (512 layers) and is not expected to run.

name: StdSort_PartitionPtrByDword12
callers: StdSort_LayersByOrder (the introsort loop), which UIRender_PrepareLayers calls
purpose: Introsort partition step on an array of object pointers keyed by the dword at object+12: median-of-three (or Tukey ninther for more than 41 elements) pivot choice and three-way partition; returns the equal range [lo, hi) in pair.

behavior.text: size <= 41 elements: median of first / middle / last; larger: median of medians of three groups spaced n >> 3 apart (n = the element count; the first group starts at the first element, the last ends at the last). Keys are the unsigned dwords at *ptr + 12.

then expands the pivot run left and right over equal keys and partitions the rest into < pivot, == pivot, > pivot, stable only up to the usual std::sort swaps; returns pair[0] = end of the lower part, pair[1] = start of the upper part.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403C37EC). This is MSVC's _Partition_by_median_guess_unchecked specialised for the key at +12 (the layer sort key). Same code as StdSort_PartitionPtrByDword84 with a different key offset.
open_questions: The list is the UI layer list of UIRender_PrepareLayers (key +12 = the layer's order, initially its slot index; V).

name: StdSort_PartitionPtrByDword84
purpose: Same partition step as StdSort_PartitionPtrByDword12 with the key at object+84.

behavior.text: identical structure (median-of-three / ninther, three-way partition, returns the equal range in pair); the key is the unsigned dword at *ptr + 84 instead of +12.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403C3AC8).
open_questions: The list is the UI layer list of UIRender_PrepareLayers (key +84 = the draw-order key; V).

name: StdSort_PopHeapHolePtrByDword12
purpose: MSVC's heap 'pop with hole' step for the layer pointer array, key = dword at layer+12: moves the hole at index hole down to a leaf along the larger child, then sifts the value up from there.

behavior.text: while the hole has two children below count it takes the child with the larger key (the right child when its key is not below the left's) and moves it up; a lone left child at the end is taken the same way; then the value is sifted up from the final hole while the parent's key is below the value's key, and stored.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403C3EF4). Only reached by the heap-sort fallback of the introsort (ideal depth exhausted).

name: StdSort_PopHeapHolePtrByDword84
purpose: The same heap step as StdSort_PopHeapHolePtrByDword12 with the key at layer+84.

behavior.text: identical code with the key offset 84 instead of 12.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403C3FA0).

name: Str_Format
proto: int Str_Format(char *buf, size_t size, const char *fmt, ...)
purpose: snprintf-style formatter (thin wrapper around sub_140026084). Builds arrow and label node names.

behavior.text: 'Line%sLv%02d' / 'Line%s%s' for arrows; the four fixed names 'TextBoardJobLvB/T/R/L' are written with it at 0x140133B09.

name: StringHandle_Release
purpose: Frees a {allocator, pointer} string-like member.

behavior.text: named from its use in the crash below.

an access violation reading 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF at its first load through rcx (rcx = 0x3F80000000000000), reached from sub_140095E5C <- UIResourceHandle_Delete (0x1403D99C0) <- GUICore_UpdateFrame <- GUICore_DispatchEvent <- App_RunFrame; the object's vtable was the ResourceHandle vtable 0x1406FF618 left by its destructor (I: the caller addresses and values come from the dump, not from this body).

name: sub_140025D74
proto: uint32_t sub_140025D74(uint32_t seed, const void *data, size_t len)
purpose: Computes the CRC-32 checksum the save format stores in every entry header: the manual-slot payload, the resume entries and the settings block are all sealed with it.

behavior.text: it is the platform CRC-32: reflected polynomial 0xEDB88320 (baked into the table data, not an immediate), a slicing-by-4 table of four 0x400-byte planes based at 0x14065D6E0 (read at +0, +0x400, +0x800 and +0xC00), and a caller-supplied seed (zero at every site read).
it takes a seed, a buffer and a byte length and returns the 32-bit result; it is a leaf with no global state of its own.

the four call sites are the entry attach check (`sub_140033DA4`), the resume-entry writer (`sub_1400C3140`, which stores the result at object `+12`), the settings writer (`sub_1400C3814`) and the manual-slot flush (`SaveSlots_StoreToFile`).
the checksum covers the payload only; the 16-byte entry header that carries it is excluded, which is why the writer computes it before the header is built.
because the same routine seals every container, a replacement writer must reproduce it exactly or the game's attach check rejects the entry before any of its fields are looked at.

notes: The polynomial and table base come from the save-container research; the body itself reads four 0x400-byte table planes, so it is the slicing-by-4 form.

name: sub_14002620C
proto: char *sub_14002620C(char *dst, size_t dstCapacity, const char *src, size_t srcLimit)
callers: 160 direct sites, including `sub_1403DB0EC`, `sub_1400ED328`, `sub_140028874` and the save container's path helpers
purpose: A bounded string copy: it moves a source string into a caller buffer, stopping at either the destination capacity or an explicit source limit, and terminates the result.

behavior.text: the argument order as used is destination, destination capacity, source, source limit; the UI passes `(buffer, 256, path, 255)`, so the copy is capped one byte below the 256-byte buffer.
it is the single copy primitive behind the texture and part path builders, the save container's entry-name handling and dozens of UI addon methods (160 direct call sites counted in the code).

the bounded form is used everywhere a path or a name is assembled into a fixed buffer: the 0x104-byte item picture buffers, the 0x100-byte UI path buffers and the 264-byte block copied into a UI part (the 0x100 and 0x104 are caller buffer sizes, not operands here).
it stops at the source limit or at the terminator, whichever comes first, and always writes a terminator, so a truncated result is still a valid string.
whether a source exactly at the limit is truncated silently or reported to the caller was not read; no caller tests a return value.

notes: Named only in prose: the function's shape (bounded copy) is proven by its call sites and by the path builders that use it, but it is a generic helper with no game meaning, so it keeps its address name.

name: sub_14002BA44
callers: the application initialiser (2 references in that routine)
callees: the folder and pack helpers, the save-file name builder
purpose: Builds and probes the console save thumbnail path, `system/savedata/ICON0.PNG`, and mounts or opens the save folder that would hold it.

behavior.text: the literal path it builds is the console thumbnail location (`system/savedata/ICON0.PNG`), not a PC save file.
it is reached twice from the application initialiser and from nowhere else in the executable.
on this build nothing ever writes that path and neither of the owner's save sets contains it, so the whole routine is inert on PC.
it is a leftover of the console save UI: the thumbnail is what a console front end shows for a save, and the PC build keeps the code but not the feature.
what the routine does when the path exists (mount, open for read, or only remember it) was not traced, because there is no file to observe.

notes: Counted with the legacy/console group in the save research (four functions, all inert on PC). Sheet written from the path string, the two references and the absence of the file.

name: sub_140033CBC
purpose: Asks the save-file object for one named container entry: it builds a request that carries both the requesting object and the entry name, and queues it so the delivery path can fill the requester's buffer and size later.

behavior.text: the request is a 0x120-byte record; it carries the requester object and a copy of the name, and is pushed on the file object's request list.
the entry is not read here. Delivery happens later and writes the buffer pointer and the size into the requester at `+624` and `+632` (the offsets the resume writer uses) plus the CRC at `+12`.
five call sites: the settings boot path, the manual-slot loader (for `fftsave.bin`), the resume name fan-out, the battle-resume part of a slot load, and the title's Continue probe.
a request while the file object reports busy returns an error instead of queueing, so a second request in the same frame is dropped rather than nested.

the attach member that fills the requester is the same one the writer checks (`+624`/`+632`), so a request whose name is absent simply leaves the requester untouched; the game then sees an empty or damaged slot.
whether a duplicate request for the same name is coalesced was not read.

notes: The read seam of the save system: every resume entry and the manual slot pass through it. The attach member is read indirectly (through the delivery path), not in this function.

name: sub_140033DA4
proto: int sub_140033DA4(SaveData *obj, const void *payload, size_t size)
purpose: The attach check: compares the CRC word the entry header carries with the checksum of the payload that was just inflated, and refuses the entry when they differ.

behavior.text: it compares the stored CRC at object `+12` with the CRC-32 of the payload bytes, header excluded.
on a mismatch it returns an error and the caller leaves the object's buffer as it was, so a damaged entry is never copied into the slot image.
it is called once per attach from the three handlers: the manual-slot handler, the settings handler and one further handler in the same family.
the check is on the payload, not on the container: the PNG chunk's own integrity is libpng's business and the header fields other than the CRC are trusted.
because the check runs before any field is interpreted, a replacement writer that changes the payload without updating the header word is rejected exactly like a corrupted file.

notes: The size check that pairs with this one lives in `sub_1400C2ED8` and applies only to version 14 (the manual slot); this routine is version-agnostic.

name: sub_140033DF0
proto: int sub_140033DF0(SaveData *obj, const void *entry, size_t entrySize)
purpose: The generic entry dispatcher: takes one inflated container entry, copies its 16-byte header into the file object, and hands the payload, size and version to the object's own handler.

behavior.text: it copies the 16-byte entry header into the file object and then dispatches the payload, the payload size, the version word and a "checked" flag to the handler selected by the object's vtable.

the handler is the file object's own (its vtable's first slot); the header's version word is passed to it as an argument, not used to choose it, so the object that asked for the entry decides which routine runs.
it is called once per entry record from the per-record dispatch loop, so a container with several entries runs it several times in one load.
the name of the entry is copied aside before the dispatch, so the handler does not need to see the container layout.
this is the seam where a second named entry would be delivered; the loader only dispatches names that were requested, so an entry nobody asked for never reaches here.

notes: Read as the entry point of the load chain `sub_140032F8C` -> this -> per-object handler -> `sub_1400C2ED8`.

name: sub_1400348F8
purpose: The boot "has any save" probe: asks whether the manual, the autosave and the system containers exist and remembers the answers on the manager so the title knows whether to offer a load or a continue.

behavior.text: it sets two flag bytes at manager `+0x258` and `+0x259` from the results of the probes.
it is called once, from the application initialiser, before the title screen exists.
the probes are the container existence test and the legacy numbered-file scan, so the flags also answer "is there an old-style save set".
the two flags are "a save file is present" and "a resume point is present"; the title's Continue entry is what reads them (the read side was not traced in this pass).
which feature reads each flag individually; only the write side was proven.

notes: I: the title shows its load entry from this probe's answer.

name: sub_140034C64
proto: int sub_140034C64(SaveFileObject *obj, int kind, const char *area)
purpose: Kicks the container write state machine for one area name: it hands the file object the area whose queued entries should be packed and written.

behavior.text: the arguments as used are the file object, a request kind (4 for the manual slot, 6 for the autosave) and the area name (`ENHANCED`, `CLASSIC`, `AUTOENHANCED`, `SYSTEM`).
it only starts the machine; the entries themselves were queued earlier with `SaveFile_QueueEntry`, so a kick with nothing queued has nothing to write.
five direct sites cover the four writers: the settings block, the manual-slot flush, the per-frame resume flush, a battle save and the world-map save.
the request object carries a busy flag (the same one the entry requests test), so a second kick inside one frame is dropped rather than queued.
the area name is a key into the request object, not a path: the same call serves `enhanced.png` and `autoenhanced.png` with no change.

notes: Paired with `sub_140034CF0` (the read kick).

name: sub_140034CF0
proto: int sub_140034CF0(SaveFileObject *obj, int kind, const char *area)
purpose: Kicks the container read state machine for one area name, which makes the pending entry requests for that area get looked up, inflated and delivered.

behavior.text: the shape mirrors the write kick: file object, request kind (5 for the manual slot, 7 for the autosave) and the area name.
it runs after the requests were queued with `sub_140033CBC`, and only the names queued in that pass are delivered.
six direct sites: the settings boot probe, the manual-slot loader, the resume fan-out, the battle-resume part of a slot load and the title probe.
it shares the request object's busy flag with the write kick, so a pending write has to finish before a read starts.
the machine is the same one the writer uses, in the opposite direction.

notes: Paired with `sub_140034C64`.

name: sub_140034D7C
callers: none found — it is installed in the manager's vtable
purpose: The container writer: a multi-state machine that re-reads the existing PNG, adopts every entry it did not queue itself, rebuilds the `UMIF` header and entry table, deflates each entry and writes the picture back.

behavior.text: it is the manager's vtable slot 15 and is never called directly, which is why a direct-call scan finds no callers.
state 4 opens the old `%s.png`, walks its entry table (magic compared at `0x1400352E4`) and appends a record for every name that is not already in its queue, inflating the adopted entry first.
state 5 sums the entry sizes, writes the container header (a 16-byte header plus 32 bytes per entry, magic `UMIF`, version 1, entry count) and calls the PNG writer.
the container body is then scrambled and deflated with the 32 KB preset dictionary, and the PNG chunk is written into the picture.
it creates the save folder before writing (the mkdir helper is called from this routine as well as from the folder builder).
adoption is what makes a named entry the game did not queue survive its save, and what makes the writer's output larger than the number of entries it queued.
the exact state numbers are from the research table; the machine was not re-walked state by state for this sheet.

notes: The largest routine of the container group (about 0xB2F bytes) and the only one that writes a file.

name: sub_140035A28
proto: int sub_140035A28(SaveDataManager *manager, const void *chunk, size_t size)
purpose: Walks the `UMIF` entry table of a freshly read container: validates the header, descrambles the entry names and keeps one record per entry for the lookup that follows.

behavior.text: it checks the container header (magic `UMIF`, version, entry count) before touching the entries.
the entry records are 32-byte descriptors: name length, data length, name offset, uncompressed length and data offset.
it descrambles the names only; it does not inflate payloads here, which is why an entry nobody requests is never inflated on load.
the resulting records are what the name search (`sub_140036064`) later walks.
because the walk keeps every entry, an entry with an unknown name is retained in the container model and simply never requested; it is not rejected.
whether a malformed descriptor is skipped or aborts the whole walk was not read.

notes: Read as the reader half of the container: this routine builds the entry list, `sub_140036064` searches it, `sub_140033DF0` dispatches a hit.

name: sub_140036064
purpose: Finds one entry in the container's entry list by name, inflates it and returns its record; it is the name lookup the loader uses for `fftsave.bin`, `settings.sav` and every resume entry.

behavior.text: it compares the requested name against the descrambled names the entry walk produced, and returns only on an exact match.
the payload of the matching entry is inflated here, with the container's preset dictionary, before the record is handed back.
no match means no inflation and an empty result; the caller then sees a requester with no buffer and treats the slot as empty.
it is called once per requested name from the reader state machine, not once per entry in the file.
the exact-match rule is what makes an unknown extra entry harmless on read and useful on write: the loader never asks for it, the writer carries it forward.
whether a name longer than the 32-byte descriptor field can match was not tested.

notes: The read-side counterpart of the writer's adoption loop; together they decide what a second named entry means.

name: sub_1400366B0
purpose: Answers whether the container file for one area name exists, formatting the path against the save root selected by its second argument.

behavior.text: the path is built from the area name and the literal `%s%s.png` against the root returned by the root selector, then handed to the file-existence helper.

the second argument selects the root: index 0 is the Steam-id subfolder at +0x430, index 1 the parent folder at +0x530; the argument is doubled and incremented before the selector call, and the two offsets are in the selector's body, not this one.
a 0x100-byte stack buffer holds the formatted path, so a name longer than the buffer would be truncated by the formatter.
fourteen direct sites: the boot probe, the mount machine, the title and load-screen checks and the settings reads.
it is a pure probe: it does not open, read or create anything, so a false answer means the caller skips its file step entirely.
whether the second root is a fallback tried after the first fails, or a separate question, is decided by each caller; the routine itself answers for the root it is given.

name: sub_140036724
purpose: The legacy per-slot probe: scans numbered container names `0001.png` through `0050.png` in one save root and reports whether any of them exists.

behavior.text: the loop runs a counter from 1 to 0x32 (50) and formats each name with the `%s%04d.png` template before testing it.
it returns as soon as one name exists, so the answer is "any", not "which".
it is reached from the boot "has any save" probe and from the manager's vtable slot 20; no writer for those numbered files exists in this build.
neither of the owner's save sets contains a numbered PNG, so on a normal install the scan always answers false.
the numbered set is the legacy per-slot layout of an earlier build or platform; the modern build keeps the probe for the first-run decision only.
what slot 20 does with the answer beyond the boot flags was not traced.

notes: The scan cost is 50 formatted paths and 50 existence tests on every call; the boot probe calls it once.

name: sub_1400367F4
callers: none found — installed in the manager's vtable
purpose: The mount machine: a six-state routine that creates the save folder, then probes, opens and if necessary deletes the containers the game knows about (`AUTOENHANCED`, the numbered set `0001` to `0005`, and `SYSTEM`).

behavior.text: state 0 creates the save folder through the mkdir helper, on the primary root.
the following states walk the known area names in order: the autosave container, the numbered names 1 to 5 and the system container.
for each area it asks the existence probe, opens what is there and can delete an area file through the delete routine.
it is a vtable slot, never called directly, so no caller list exists in the code.
none of the numbered containers exists in the owner's save sets, so on a normal install only the autosave and system steps do anything.
this machine is what makes a save folder appear on a first run even before any save is written.
what the numbered 0001..0005 containers are for; no manual-slot path reads them.

name: sub_140036AE0
purpose: Opens one area container for reading: it checks the parent-folder candidate exists, then prefers the Steam-id subfolder copy and falls back to the parent folder when only that one exists.

behavior.text: it formats the %s%s.png path against the root at +0x430 and against the root at +0x530 (both are inline manager offsets here, not selector calls); it checks the +0x530 candidate first, then prefers +0x430 and falls back to +0x530 when only that one exists.
the existence probe asks for the same two roots one at a time, so "exists" and "open" agree about where a file is.
a 0x100-byte buffer holds each formatted candidate path.
the file is opened read-only; the routine returns a handle or a failure for the caller to interpret.
the two-root order is what makes a save written under one Steam account still findable after the account id changes.
which error paths fall through to the second root and which return at once.

notes: The read counterpart of the delete and exists calls; it is the only op that looks in both roots.

name: sub_140036BD4
purpose: Deletes the container file of one area: it formats the `%s%s.png` name and removes it through the file layer.

behavior.text: the name formatting and root selection follow the exists and open routines, so the same area name and root give the same path.
it has exactly one caller, the mount machine, which uses it when an area file is present but not usable.
it removes only the container file; slots inside a container are not files, so a slot delete is a rewrite of the whole container, not this call.
a missing file is not an error path here; the mount machine only calls it for a file it has just seen.
this is the repair path of the mount, not a user action, which is why the menu's delete never reaches it.
whether a failure is reported to the user or only logged was not traced.

name: sub_140036D8C
purpose: Writes the finished container into a PNG: it creates the picture, adds the private chunk that holds the container body, and saves it under the formatted `%s.png` name.

behavior.text: the PNG library is libpng 1.6.17, created by the reader/writer pair in this group; this routine is the write half.
the container body goes into a private chunk named `ffTo`; the picture itself is the same 776x436 logo in every file, so there is no per-save thumbnail.
the chunk length is a 32-bit field, so the whole container body must fit in 4 GB (a limit never approached: the largest observed file is a few MB).
it is called from the container writer after the header and the entry table are built and the entries are deflated.
the picture is a fixed asset and not derived from the save, which is why all three containers look identical in an image viewer.
the chunk-splitting behaviour for a body above the chunk limit was not read.

notes: The only routine in this group that touches the picture format itself; everything above it is the container.

name: sub_14006B144
purpose: Builds the save folder path once at startup: Documents, the game folder, the profile part and the Steam account id, then creates it.

behavior.text: it starts from the shell's Documents folder, appends a `My Games` segment and the game's folder name (a demo variant is used when a flag byte is set).
it normalises the separators to forward slashes and lowercases the whole string, so every later path comparison is case-insensitive.
it appends the profile part and then `Steam/<account id>/`, the id taken from a call on the Steam user object.
the finished path is stored at manager `+0x430`; the same routine creates the folder through the mkdir helper.
it is called once, from the application's folder setup (`sub_14006AD04`).
the lowercasing is why every literal in the container code is spelled in lower case even though the display names are not.
what the profile part contains when no Steam user is signed in.

notes: The path itself is not reproduced on this page: only its shape and the order of the segments were read.

name: sub_14006BA2C
purpose: Returns one of the two save-root strings held on the manager, selected by index: the primary root or the fallback root without the Steam id.

behavior.text: it is a nine-way switch: index 1 returns the string at +0x430 and index 3 the string at +0x530; the other seven indices return further manager fields, and any other index a fixed string.

sub_1400366B0 passes index 1 or 3 (it doubles its boolean and adds 1); the switch cases sit past the first ret, at 0x14006BA60..0x14006BA9D, so a scan that stops at that ret sees only the default case.
the three callers are the exists, the open and the legacy numbered-file probes, all of which format a path against the returned root.
it does not build or copy anything, so the caller shares the manager's buffer and must not write into it.
the second root exists so that a save written before the account id was known can still be found.
whether the second root is populated at startup or only when the Steam id is unavailable.

notes: Not present in the exception directory: a leaf with no unwind data, which is why address scans that rely on that table miss it.

name: sub_14006BAA8
purpose: Reads a file through the engine's virtual file system: it resolves the path, opens the stream, copies the bytes into the caller's buffer and closes it.

behavior.text: it is the generic read routine of the file layer, used by the save code, the pack code and several loaders (13 direct sites counted in the code).
the path is resolved against the mount table first, so a file inside a mounted pack is served without touching the disk.
the buffer and the expected length come from the caller; the routine reports how many bytes were read and whether the read succeeded.
the legacy flat-image save loader reaches it for the numbered per-slot files, which is the only save path that uses it.
because the save containers live outside any pack, the disk branch is the one the save code exercises.
the behaviour on a partial read (short file) was not traced.

notes: Area chosen as resource: it is the file layer, not the save container itself.

name: sub_14006C6F4
purpose: A typed read wrapper over the virtual file system: opens a named file, optionally seeks to an offset, reads a fixed block and closes it.

behavior.text: it delegates the actual transfer to the virtual read routine, so it inherits the pack-first resolution.
the callers are the legacy save loader and three asset loaders, all of which read one known file into one buffer.
the offset and length are the caller's; the routine does not parse what it reads.
the legacy save loader uses it to fetch a numbered flat image, the fallback path that only runs when the legacy flag is set.
it is the "read exactly this file at this offset" convenience layer, which is why six unrelated loaders share it.
whether a failed open is reported as a short read or as a distinct error.

notes: Written from the caller list and the delegation to the read routine; the argument order was not decoded.

name: sub_14006E5DC
purpose: Resolves the user's Documents folder through the shell and returns it as the base for the save path.

behavior.text: it is called once, by the save folder builder, before the `My Games` segment is appended.
it asks the shell for the known folder rather than reading an environment variable, so a redirected Documents folder is honoured.
the returned string is used as a base only; the routine does not append the game folder itself.
a failure returns an empty or null base and the folder builder then produces a relative path (the caller does not branch on failure).
the shell call is what makes the save folder follow the user's profile, and why two Windows accounts see different saves.
the exact shell interface used and its failure value.

notes: The path helper the brief names; only its role and its one caller were read.

name: sub_140073918
purpose: Creates a directory: the engine's mkdir, used for the save folder, the pack cache and the log folder.

behavior.text: it takes one path and creates it, returning a status; it does not create intermediate directories on its own.
eleven call sites, all of them folder setup: the save folder builder, the boot mount machine, the container writer and several asset caches.
it is called before the first save is written, so a player who never saves still gets the save folder.
the recursive case is handled by the callers, which build the path one segment at a time or know the parent exists.
the status is ignored at most sites, because a folder that already exists is not an error.
whether an existing directory returns success or a distinct "already there" code.

notes: A generic filesystem helper; it keeps its address name because it has no game meaning.

name: sub_140093108
purpose: Looks a file name up in the mounted-pack registry's hash tree, inserting a new node when the name is not there yet.

behavior.text: the registry is an array of 512 buckets selected by the low nine bits of a 32-bit hash of the name.
a node holds the hash at `+0x20` and the name at `+0x18`; equal hashes are resolved by a byte-wise name comparison.
it is the tree operation of the registry: find, and insert when absent, in one call.
five call sites: the pack mount list, the single-pack mount and three lookups in the file layer.
the bucket mask is the same for the pack registry and the file registry, so both hold 512 buckets of names.
because the name is stored lower-cased by the mount code, the comparison is effectively case-insensitive.
what the node's other fields are; only the hash, the name and the bucket link were read.

notes: Leaf of about 0x123 bytes; it is the whole registry data structure in one routine.

name: sub_1400B5E24
purpose: Applies a changed option block and asks for the settings container to be written.

behavior.text: it is the config update path: the new values are collected by the caller and handed on, and the settings writer is called at the end.
the settings writer copies a 240-byte block into the save object, computes its CRC and queues `settings.sav` with version 0, then kicks the `SYSTEM` container write.
one direct caller, the option-change handler; the launcher's mode flags go through a different caller of the same writer.
the write happens immediately on the change, not at quit, so a settings change survives a crash.
the block is a whole snapshot, not a delta: every field is rewritten, which is why an older build's missing field comes back as a default.
which option change reaches this path and which one only updates memory until the next write.
