notes: Part of the settings pair (writer `sub_1400C3814`, reader `sub_1400C5F8C`); this sheet covers the trigger, not the schema.

name: sub_1400C2ED8
proto: int sub_1400C2ED8(GameSaveData *obj, const void *payload, size_t size, int version, int checked)
purpose: The manual-slot handler: for a version-14 `fftsave.bin` entry it verifies the CRC and the exact payload size, then copies the whole 50-slot image into the save object.

behavior.text: the CRC of the payload is verified through the attach check before anything is copied.
for version 14 the size must be exactly `0x1EA488` (2,008,200 bytes = 50 slots of 40,164); any other size zeroes the buffer and returns an error.
the exact-size rule applies only to the manual slot: the settings entry (version 0) and the resume entries (version 17) are not size-checked here.
on success it copies the payload as one opaque block into the object at `+624`, so all 50 slots become plain bytes in one move.
it is reached only through the object's vtable, from the generic entry dispatcher.
this single rule is why a manual slot can never be widened in place: a larger payload is rejected before any field is read.

notes:
- V: the version-and-size gate sits at `0x1400C2F4B`, 115 bytes into this function: it compares the entry version with 14, then the payload size with `0x1EA488`.
- V: on a mismatch it zeroes the object's image and returns an error, so every slot in the file reads as empty rather than partially loaded.
- V: the same gate is skipped for the settings (version 0) and resume (version 17) handlers, which is why those entries accept variable sizes.
- I: accepting a larger manual slot needs this comparison and the writer's size changed, not the container.
- There is no separate function at `0x1400C2F4B`; it is a branch inside this one.

name: sub_1400C30BC
proto: void sub_1400C30BC(ResumeGroup *group, const void *buf, size_t len)
purpose: Stores a freshly built payload into one resume group: it frees the group's previous buffer, allocates the new size, copies the bytes and marks the group ready.

behavior.text: it frees the old buffer at group `+0x270` with the engine's allocator, then allocates the new size from the same allocator and copies the payload in.
it writes the new length to `+0x278` and sets the ready byte at `+0x281`, which is what the flush later tests.
the allocator is the one held on the file object (`qword_140C696D0 + 0x10`); allocating from a different heap would corrupt the next free.
two call sites: the producer that captures a snapshot and the per-name map insert.
the ready byte is cleared by the flush after the payload is queued, so a group is written at most once per capture.
whether a zero length is allowed (the copy would then be a no-op with a valid buffer).

notes: The only writer of a group's payload pointer; a replacement reader/writer pair has to keep the allocator contract.

name: sub_1400C3140
purpose: Turns one ready buffer into a named container entry: it seals the buffer with a CRC, queues it under the given name with version 17 and marks the object clean.

behavior.text: it only acts when both the buffer pointer at `+624` and the length at `+632` are set; otherwise it returns without queueing.
it stores the CRC-32 of the buffer at `+12` and then queues the entry with version 17 and the buffer length.
after queueing it clears the dirty byte at `+641`, so the same buffer is not queued twice.
three sites: the flush's per-record queue, the map insert's fallback and the manual battle save's `resume_enmaNN_world.sav`.
version 17 is the resume version; the manual slot uses 14 and the settings block 0.
the guard on both pointer and length is why an empty group produces no entry at all rather than an empty one.
whether the queue keeps the buffer or copies it; the allocator note in `sub_1400C30BC` implies the queue takes a copy.

notes: The write seam of the resume system; every resume entry, including a manual slot's battle entry, passes through it.

name: sub_1400C3B84
purpose: The per-frame resume flush: it turns every dirty resume group into named entries, rotates the three-point ring and kicks the autosave container write.

behavior.text: group 1 (world) dirty writes the single `resume_enwm_main.sav` entry.
group 3 (battle) dirty writes the four `resume_enbtl_*` entries (world, attack, fturn, main) in that order.
group 0 (main) dirty writes the four `resume_enNN_*` entries at the next ring index and advances the three-point ring.
after the groups it calls the named-entry queue walk, then one write kick for the `AUTOENHANCED` area if anything was queued, and stamps the manager.
it runs once per frame from the main update, so a capture made during a frame is on disk by the end of that frame.
the order (groups 1, 2, 3, then 0) is what makes `main` the last entry written, which the reader relies on to know the newest part.
what the boot argument changes; the one call site is the boot update and passes a value that was not decoded.

notes: The fan-out is V in the research table; the argument semantics are not.

name: sub_1400C3DBC
purpose: Walks the resume name-to-record map and queues every dirty record as a container entry, erasing each record as it goes.

behavior.text: the map is the per-group dedupe map: a record is keyed by entry name and holds the buffer and its dirty state.
each dirty record is handed to the entry writer, which seals it and queues it under its name.
the record is erased after queueing, so the map only holds entries that still have to be written.
it returns whether anything was queued, which the world-save caller uses to decide whether to kick a write at all.
two call sites: the per-frame flush and the world-map save.
erasing on queue is why a name can be recaptured later without a duplicate entry in the same container.
what the three helper calls do; only the map walk and the queue were read.

notes: The "queue everything that is ready" half of the resume writer; `sub_1400C4198` is the "prepare one record" half.

name: sub_1400C3ED8
proto: void sub_1400C3ED8(SaveDataManager *manager, ResumeGroup *group, const char *name, int point, bool flag)
purpose: Packs one resume record under a given name: it ensures a map record exists for the name, copies the group's buffer into it, clears the group's ready byte and queues the entry.

behavior.text: the name is the entry name already formatted by the caller; this routine does not build names.
it stores the group's payload through the group store, which frees the old record buffer and copies the new one.
after the copy it clears the group's ready byte, so the same capture is not packed twice.
when the file object is absent it falls back to queueing the entry directly through the entry writer.
one call site, the name fan-out of the flush.
the map insert plus the store is the dedupe: two captures for one name keep the newer bytes and one queued entry.
what the fourth and fifth arguments select (point and flag) beyond being passed through.

notes: Written from the writer table and the call list; the internals of the map insert were not decoded line by line.

name: sub_1400C4198
proto: void sub_1400C4198(SaveDataManager *manager, ResumeGroup *group, int part, int point, bool flag)
purpose: Prepares and queues one named resume entry: formats the entry name from a part and a point, then hands the group to the packer.

behavior.text: the name is produced by the name builder from the part index (main, world, attack, fturn) and the point index.
it is called eight times by the flush, once per group-and-point combination the ring writes.
it does not touch the payload itself; the group's buffer is read by the packer.
the flag argument is passed straight through to the packer, so a caller can force the direct queue path.
eight calls in one flush explain why the autosave container holds up to twelve resume entries after a full rotation.
what the part index maps to beyond the four names the builder knows.

notes: The join between the name table and the payload groups; both halves are separate sheets.

name: sub_1400C4214
proto: void sub_1400C4214(SaveDataManager *manager, int point, bool allParts)
purpose: Requests one resume point from the autosave container: the main part always, and optionally the world, attack and fturn parts, then kicks the read.

behavior.text: it always requests the main part of the point.
with the all-parts flag it requests the world, attack and fturn parts for points 2 to 4, or the world and attack plus the main part for point 1.
the per-entry requests are made by the name routine, six of them at most in one call.
it ends with one read kick for the `AUTOENHANCED` area, which is what makes the delivery path run.
four callers and six sites: the boot ring builder, the load-screen setup, the load confirmation and the title.
the "point 1 has no fturn part" exception matches the fan-out, which writes four parts for a battle point and three for a world point.
what a point index above 4 would request; no caller passes one.

notes: The read fan-out that mirrors the flush; both are driven by the same point numbering.

name: sub_1400C42E0
proto: void sub_1400C42E0(SaveData *target, ResumeGroup *group, int part, int point)
purpose: Requests one named resume entry from the autosave container: it formats the name for a part and a point and queues the request on the group object.

behavior.text: the name comes from the shared name builder, so read and write agree on every spelling.
the request is queued through the generic entry request routine on the group object passed in.
six sites, all inside the read fan-out.
it does not kick the read; the fan-out does that once after all six requests.
queueing all requests before one kick is what lets the container be opened once for a whole point.
whether a missing entry leaves the group's previous buffer in place.

notes: The read twin of the packer `sub_1400C3ED8`.

name: sub_1400C4360
proto: void sub_1400C4360(char *out, int part, int point)
purpose: Builds a resume entry name from a part index and a point index: `resume_enNN_<part>.sav`, `resume_enwm_main.sav` or `resume_enbtl_<part>.sav`.

behavior.text: point 2 to 4 produce `resume_en%02d_%s.sav` with the part name appended.
point 0 produces the single world-map name `resume_enwm_main.sav`, which has no index.
point 1 produces `resume_enbtl_%s.sav`, the battle-copy name with no index either.
the part names come from a four-entry table (main, world, attack, fturn) based at `0x140671E70`.
the output buffer is the caller's; the longest name fits well inside the container's 32-byte name field.
the asymmetric numbering is what makes the autosave set look irregular in a file listing: three point patterns and one fixed pair.

notes: The single source of the resume spellings.

name: sub_1400C43D8
purpose: Returns the payload buffer and length of one part of the current resume point, so the Continue path can read the header without a copy.

behavior.text: the out pointer is read from one of four fixed manager offsets (0x3D5190 for the default part, one per part for 2, 3 and 4), and the qword returned comes from the field 8 bytes before the chosen offset (0x3D5188 for the default); the parts are 0x288 apart but each offset is a separate immediate, not a stride multiply.
it returns pointers into the manager's own storage; it does not copy and the caller must not free them.
it is called once, by the Continue header import.
it is not present in the exception directory, so tooling that enumerates functions from that table does not see it.
because the returned buffer is the group's live buffer, a later capture into the same group would invalidate what the caller just read.
what the caller does when the part has never been captured (a null buffer).

notes: A leaf accessor; the "not in the exception table" detail is why address scans can miss it.

name: sub_1400C4690
purpose: The resume-order state machine: it walks the three-point ring at boot, requests each point's parts and keeps the newest three points in order.

behavior.text: the state lives at manager `+0x3D5938` and is read from `+0x38`; state 0 clears the index and timestamp arrays.
state 1 requests the next point (`count + 2`) through the read fan-out when fewer than three points are held, then moves to state 2.
state 2 validates the delivered payload (magic `FFTI`, the 0x7A word, a kind below 2) and, when it passes, stores the payload's timestamp word into the ring and increments the count.
state 3 sorts the ring through the order-rebuild helper and writes the new order back.
it is called once, from the title setup, and is therefore the only place the ring is populated at startup.
the ring is a three-slot MRU list: the count, the next index and the timestamps are all that the title needs to offer the newest Continue.
which scene event creates a new point; the ring proves three rotating points, not when each is captured.

notes: Read in full (the state machine and all four states). The title setup passes a manager pointer and no other argument.

name: sub_1400C480C
purpose: The world-map save step: it flushes any ready resume record and, only when something was queued, kicks the autosave container write.

behavior.text: it delegates the queueing to the map walk and uses its answer to decide whether to write at all.
when something was queued it kicks the `AUTOENHANCED` write (kind 6) and stamps the manager.
it is cheap when nothing is dirty: one map walk and no file work.
two call sites, both on the world map: the screen's own update and the boot update.
the `resume_enwm_main.sav` name itself is produced by the group-1 branch of the per-frame flush, not here.
calling it every update is what makes a world-map position reach the disk without an explicit save.
which world-map action marks group 1 dirty in the first place.

notes: The world-map trigger of the autosave, as distinct from the per-frame flush that also covers it.

name: sub_1400C6008
purpose: Fills a 50-slot save image with the empty-slot pattern, so a missing or rejected file reads as 50 empty slots instead of stale bytes.

behavior.text: it writes the empty pattern over the whole `0x1EA488`-byte image; a slot with no valid magic then fails the slot-validity test and is not listed.
it is the first thing the manual-slot loader does, before any entry is requested.
it is also called from the image setup at `sub_1400C33A8`, so the buffer is never left uninitialised.
the pattern is the same one the delete and boot-clear paths use for a slot, so an empty slot from this routine and a deleted slot are indistinguishable.
this is why a corrupt container degrades to "no save data" rather than to an error dialog: the slots simply fail the magic test.
whether the pattern is all `0xFF` or a per-field pattern; the brief describes an empty-slot pattern rather than a plain fill.

notes: The reset that pairs with the loader.

name: sub_1400D6FB0
proto: void sub_1400D6FB0(int unused, int type, int delta)
purpose: Adjusts the count of one poach type, clamps it, and keeps the two ordered poach lists in step when a type enters or leaves the collection.

behavior.text: the type is the second argument; a type above 96 reads as zero and the function returns without writing anything.
the current count is the byte at 0x1411A7A1A plus the type index, one of 97 entries based at 0x1411A7810 + 522 (reached as base + 0x20A).
the new total is clamped to 99, and if the delta drives it below zero it becomes zero.
the clamped value is written back to the count array whether or not the total changed.
the function compares whether the type was empty before and is non-empty after; only when that state changes does it touch the two ordered lists.
on a change it walks the 97-byte order list at 0x1411A7810 + 619 and the 97-byte sort list at + 716, removing the type from its old position and inserting it at the new one through sub_1400D710C.
the scan of each list stops at 96 entries and shifts the remaining bytes down by one when an entry is removed.

the order list is the player-visible sequence of collected poach types and the sort list is the user reordering of the same sequence, because both hold the same type values and are maintained together.
the 99 cap matches the inventory count cap, which suggests both are the same game rule applied to two stores.
what the callers pass in the first argument; the function itself never reads it.

notes:
- V: the count, order and sort arrays are 97 bytes each, indexed by poach type 0 through 96; index 0 is unused by the naming.
- V: this function does not touch the item id space; the poach type values are a separate byte namespace.
open_questions: - ?: whether a poach type can ever be removed from the collection, which is the only case that rewrites the two lists.

name: sub_1400DC4C8
proto: bool sub_1400DC4C8(void *unitSource, bool (*accept)(void *), bool (*each)(void *, void *), int want)
callers: 18 sites in the targeting-predicate family of the battle code (all in the `0x1400DC..`-`0x1400DD..` range)
callees: the source object's kind accessor (vtable), the caller's callbacks
purpose: One of the battle targeting predicates: it decides whether a unit (or its target list) qualifies, and in this variant it accepts only a Mime and then walks the unit's stored target list through the caller's callback.

behavior.text: it rejects a null object or a null predicate, and requires the source object's kind accessor to answer 9 (a battle-unit record).
the unit index at object `+8` must be 21 or below, which is the bound of the preview-unit table (512 bytes per entry).
a flag bit 0x08 in the record's word at `+0x1EE` must be set; when the mode byte on the stack is zero the record's job byte at `+3` must also be 0x5D (Mime).

the caller's predicate is then run on the record, and if it passes the list at object `+0x0C` (count) and `+0x10` (indices) is walked, calling the second callback for each entry until the requested count is reached.
the Mime test is the reason this variant exists: the action it guards can only be aimed at, or performed by, a unit in that job.
what the flag bit at `+0x1EE` means, and which action uses this exact variant (18 callers share the shape).

notes: Read in full. The sibling `sub_1400DDC70` is the same shape with the opposite job test.

name: sub_1400DDC70
callers: none found as a direct call (reached through the predicate table)
purpose: The complement of the Mime predicate: it accepts a battle unit that is not a Mime and carries a particular marker, then walks the target list looking for an entry that is flagged.

behavior.text: it requires the same record shape as the Mime predicate: kind 9, index 21 or below, and the flag bit 0x08 set at `+0x1EE`.
it rejects the record when its job byte at `+3` is 0x5D (Mime), the opposite of the sibling routine.
it further requires the byte at `+0x1A1` to be 0x15 (21).
the list at `+0x0C` and `+0x10` is then walked and each entry's record is accepted only when its own byte at `+0x1BE` is non-zero.
the pair of tests (a status-like byte at `+0x1A1` and a list-entry flag at `+0x1BE`) suggests a "has already been acted on" check, but the meaning of both bytes is unproven.
which action uses this variant; no direct call was found, so it is installed as a predicate pointer.

notes: Read in full. Kept with its address name: the behaviour is clear, the game purpose is not.

name: sub_1400E615C
purpose: A guarded variant of the item-row text setter: it forwards an item id and four caller values to the item-row builder, but only when three UI subsystems are alive and the caller's kind is the one it serves.

behavior.text: it tests three UI sub-objects through their kind accessors and returns without doing anything if any of them is not up.
it then accepts only kind 3: a kind of 1 returns, and every other value returns as well.
it takes the UI object at one of those sub-objects (`+0x48`), and forwards the item id with five values from the caller's frame to the item-row text builder (`sub_140153CA0`).
the three guards and the single accepted kind make this the "battle banner" spelling of the item row, as opposed to the menu spelling that calls the builder directly.
what the four extra arguments are; the item row builder reads them as text-slot parameters, but they were not decoded.

notes: Head only: the guards, the kind test and the forwarded arguments were read; the callee's use of the extra values was not.

name: sub_1400ED328
proto: void sub_1400ED328(int a1, int a2, int a3, int a4, int a5)
purpose: Publishes a built list to the UI: it checks that the UI list module is open and hands the list parameters to the module's list setter with a "publish" flag.

behavior.text: it resolves the UI module through its global, asks the module whether it is open, and returns when it is not.
it then takes the module's list object and forwards four caller values plus a stack byte of 1 to `sub_140128E1C`.
the constant 1 on the stack is the publish/visible flag, so the call both fills and shows the list.
two call sites: the equip-screen list builder and the job-screen list builder, both right after they filled the menu list.
"publish" is the moment the list becomes visible; a builder that skips it leaves the previous list on screen.
what the four parameters mean to the setter (start index, count, selection, mode).

notes: Read in full. A thin adapter between a list builder and the UI module.

name: sub_1400ED3E8
purpose: Returns the equip screen's current slot selector: the byte at the UI object's `+0xF1C`, or 0 when the UI module is not up.

behavior.text: it asks the UI module whether it is open and returns 0 when it is not, so a caller never reads a stale object.
the value it returns is the byte at `+0xF1C` of the module's equip object, the field the equip screen keeps the selected slot in.
eleven call sites, all in the equip, sort and item-menu code.
it is a pure read: nothing is written and no argument is taken.
the 0 returned when the module is down is indistinguishable from "slot 0", which is safe because no caller runs while the screen is closed.
the meaning of the slot numbering (which value is the right hand, which the head).

notes: Read in full. The pair `sub_1400ED4BC` returns a different field of the same object.

name: sub_1400ED4BC
purpose: Returns the item screen's current list mode: the dword at the UI object's `+0x12EC`, or 0 when the module is not up.

behavior.text: it is the dword twin of the equip-slot getter: same module check, same fallback of 0, field `+0x12EC`.
two call sites, both in the item screen's list and sort handlers.
the value is used as a mode selector by those callers, not as a count or an index.
it takes no argument and writes nothing.
the field is the page or tab the item list is showing; the item research uses it to tell the equip screen from the item menu.
the exact set of mode values and their page names.

notes: Read in full. Its role as a screen discriminator is inferred from the two callers.

name: sub_1400EEC18
purpose: The handler for a scene message word: it resolves the 5-bit class and 11-bit index of the word and dispatches to the text setter of that class.

behavior.text: the index it decodes is the low 11 bits (0x7FF) of the dword at +0xC of the object loaded from the scene-message global; the 5-bit class half is not in this head.
the class selects one of a table of handlers; this routine is the generic entry, and each class lands on a different text or number setter.
the eight callees are the per-class setters: plain text, formatted number, icon-bearing text and the item and ability name variants.
two call sites, both in the scene task code that consumes the message word.
this is how a scene script shows a message without knowing which text table the word refers to.
the exact class-to-setter mapping; only the range and the callee set were read.

notes: Head only: the decode and the dispatch table are read, the per-class argument marshalling is not.

name: sub_1400F4BCC
callers: about 290 sites, among them JobTree_OnEvent, JobTree_HandleInput, sub_140130DF0, sub_140131068, sub_140131688, sub_140131734, sub_1400F4D38, sub_14012E82C
purpose: Plays a UI sound cue: looks key soundKey up in UI table 0x45 and starts the sound the row names, dispatching on the row's type word.

behavior.text: row = UITable_GetRowByKey(0x45, soundKey); returns the (null) row when missing and does nothing.

switch on the u16 at row+8: 0x66 -> SoundCue_Play(row[3] - 1); 0x15E -> EventSoundEntry_Append(qword_143CD9DD8, row[3]); 0x17E -> sub_1401D964C(qword_143CD9DD8 + 1384, row[3]); 0x180 -> sub_1401D80A8(qword_143CD9DD8, 10, row[3] + 1); any other type value does nothing. row[3] is the dword at row+12 (the sound / entry id).
a1 is ignored (callers pass a leftover register). The function has about 290 callers: every screen's confirm / cancel / cursor-move cue goes through it.
Job Tree / job-list uses: ids 14 (0xE, confirm-like), 15 (0xF, cancel), 17 (0x11, cursor enter in JobTree_OnEvent), 0xE6 (230, refused action).

notes: Proposed name UISound_Play (medium confidence; kept as sub_ because the table 0x45 columns and the four handler types are not decoded). Counterpart that stops / sets state is sub_1400F4C54.
open_questions: ? what the four type words 0x66 / 0x15E / 0x17E / 0x180 name (sound effect banks?). ? table 0x45 column layout. ? the meaning of ids 14 / 15 / 17 / 230 (judged from use only).

name: sub_1400F4C54
purpose: The stop / state counterpart of sub_1400F4BCC: same table 0x45 lookup, but calls the stop-type function of each of the four handlers.

behavior.text: row = UITable_GetRowByKey(0x45, soundKey); null = nothing.

switch on u16 at row+8: 0x66 -> sub_1402B20E4(row[3]); 0x15E -> EventSoundEntry_SetStateById(qword_143CD9DD8, row[3]); 0x17E -> sub_1401D7F4C(qword_143CD9DD8, row[3]); 0x180 -> sub_1401D80EC(qword_143CD9DD8, 10, row[3] + 1).
a1 ignored. Called by sub_14028F804 (gauge out: stops the sound whose key is at +24).

notes: Proposed name UISound_Stop (not applied). Pairs with sub_1400F4BCC (the 0x180 case uses the same +1 offset in both).
open_questions: ? exact effect (stop vs set-state) of each of the four callees; they were not decompiled.

name: sub_1400F4D38
purpose: Event handler (slot 2) of the UIDerivedWidget vtable at 0x140704578: forwards the event to the base handler, then plays the widget's own press / release cue when the event is type 12 or 16 and the owner is in the right state.

behavior.text: first calls sub_1403FC3B4(widget, owner, event): events 43 and 44 are forwarded to widget vtable +144 / +152 with event+16.

event type 12 (the same id JobTree_OnEvent treats as click): result = 0; if byte widget+616 != 0 it is cleared and the function returns (one-shot suppress); else when widget+74 (active), owner+416, owner+554 and owner+557 are all non-zero and the dword at widget+608 is non-zero, plays sound sub_1400F4BCC(_, widget+608).
event type 16: same condition but plays the dword at widget+612 (no suppress flag).
no direct callers; it is referenced from the vtable data (0x140704588, slot 2).

notes: Event 12 and 16 are press and release in JobTree_OnEvent terms (12 focuses the node, 16 sets the 'pressed' byte); that reading of 16 is I. owner+554 / +557 are the node flags also tested by sub_1400F5C78 (+554) and sub_1400F5674 (+557).
open_questions: ? what owner+416 / +557 mean (416 is also written by sub_1400F6148). ? which widgets use this vtable.

name: sub_1400F5674
purpose: Focuses a GUI node (GUICore_FocusNode) with its byte +557 temporarily cleared while any 'character render' slot is active, so the focus switch does not trigger the node's 557 behaviour.

behavior.text: node == 0: returns GUICore_FocusNode(0) (clears focus).

saves b = node+557. Scans the dword array at g_CharaRenderMgr + 13624 (the loop as decompiled is a first-element test: it exits on the first non-zero element, or after the first iteration when the first is zero); when it finds a non-zero dword it sets node+557 = 0. Then GUICore_FocusNode(node) and node+557 = b (restored).
the scan loop is a decompiler artefact of a short loop; the net effect is 'if some chara-render slot flag is set, focus without the 557 flag'.

notes: Used by the node-list focus helpers sub_1400F5B0C / sub_1400F5BCC to focus the cursor item.
open_questions: ? meaning of node+557 and of g_CharaRenderMgr+13624 (array of dwords; length not read). ? the exact trip count of the scan (disassembly not read).

name: sub_1400F5B0C
proto: char sub_1400F5B0C(__int64 focusOwner, GUINode **nodes, int count, int cursor, char flagA, char flagB)
purpose: Moves the cursor on a list of GUI nodes: optionally focuses nodes[cursor], then updates every node's CursorOver / CursorOut animation (sub_1400F5C78) with 'is cursor' = (index == cursor).

behavior.text: valid = nodes != 0 && count > cursor && cursor >= 0. If focusOwner == 0 and valid: result 0 (no focus change). If focusOwner != 0 and valid: result 1. If not valid and focusOwner == 0 it first calls GUICore_FocusNode(0). (Invalid with focusOwner != 0 returns the unset result.)

when nodes != 0: if result != 0, sub_1400F5674(nodes[cursor]) focuses the cursor node. Then for i in 0..count-1, for every non-null node, builds a 4-byte option struct {+0 flagA, +1 flagB, +2 u16 = 0} and calls sub_1400F5C78(node, &opts, i == cursor).
returns the last result (focus result or the void call's leftover).

notes: Proposed name GUINodeList_SetCursor. This is the call JobList_OnCursorChanged uses to move the visible highlight (flagA = opts[0] -> 'CursorOver' play flags 4 vs 8 in sub_1400F5C78; flagB = opts[1] 'keep checked').
open_questions: ? the return value is not consistently defined (the decompile leaves it unset for the invalid + focusOwner != 0 case). ? what callers pass for flagA / flagB in JobList_OnCursorChanged (only the signature was read).

name: sub_1400F5BCC
proto: char sub_1400F5BCC(__int64 focusOwner, GUINode **nodes, int count, int cursor, _BYTE *opts)
callers: sub_1402A9944 (the Active / Deactive tab switcher; it builds opts {x, x, 1} on the stack)
purpose: Same as sub_1400F5B0C but takes the option struct as a pointer instead of two flags.

behavior.text: identical focus logic to sub_1400F5B0C (valid = nodes && count > cursor && cursor >= 0; focus nodes[cursor] with sub_1400F5674 when focusOwner != 0 and valid; GUICore_FocusNode(0) when invalid and focusOwner == 0).
loops i over 0..count-1 and calls sub_1400F5C78(node, opts, i == cursor) for every non-null node with the caller's opts (no copy).

notes: Proposed name GUINodeList_SetCursorEx.

name: sub_1400F6148
proto: void sub_1400F6148(GUINode *node, int dir, element *keyA, element *keyB, unsigned char noLoop)
callers: about 65 sites (arrow / toggle animations on many screens; not Job Tree specific)
callees: GUINode_FindState, GUINode_StopState, sub_1403D87F4, sub_1403D8A24, sub_1403D8D1C, sub_140409898, sub_14040996C
purpose: Three-way (-1 / 0 / 1) animation switch for a node with two named states (default A = qword_143CDA2A0+5240 / +4600 pair, B = +5256 / +4616 pair): plays one, stops the other, and sets node+416 accordingly.

behavior.text: node == 0 returns. Resolves stateA / stateB: key given (keyA / keyB != 0) = the caller's element copied through sub_1403D8A24; otherwise the default key (+5240 / +5256 from qword_143CDA2A0 if the node has that state, else the fallback +4600 / +4616).

dir == -1: stateA.+109 = 0 and GUINode_StopState(A); then if stateB exists and its +109 is 0, plays B with sub_140409898(node, B, (noLoop ^ 1) - 1, 16) (frames = -1 when noLoop is 0, 0 when 1; flag 16 sets state+109 = 1). If stateB is missing node+416 = 0.
dir == 0: stateB.+109 = 0 and GUINode_StopState(B); if stateA missing: node+416 = 1; else if stateA.+109 == 0: node+416 = 1 and plays A the same way.
dir == 1: clears +109 of both states and calls sub_14040996C(node) (stops every state in the node's active list at +616..+624); node+416 = 1.
any other dir: clears +109 of both, stops all states, node+416 = 0.
releases both element keys at the end (sub_1403D8D1C).

notes: Looks like a scroll-arrow / blink helper: dir selects which of two looping states plays. node+416 is a bool 'animating'. The +109 byte is a 'queued by this helper' guard.
open_questions: ? which UI names +4600 / +4616 / +5240 / +5256 are (qword_143CDA2A0 is the interned UI-name table; names not looked up). ? semantics of the guard byte +109.

name: sub_1400F69BC
proto: char sub_1400F69BC(__int64 outStr, unsigned int actionId, __int64 ctx, int *outIconKey, __int64 outBuf, unsigned int slot)
purpose: Looks up the button icon / name string for a control action id: the icon a key / pad rebinding table gives for (actionId, slot), else the default one from UI table 25.

behavior.text: *outIconKey = 0. When the config byte g (qword_143CD9EE8 + 13696) == 1 (pad mode): key = sub_1400F6B5C(u16 at qword_143CD9EE8 + 16 * (slot + 86 + 3 * actionId)) (the bound button's icon id); if key != 0, writes the icon text with sub_1403DC8D0(outStr, key, outBuf, 0).
if no key: slot 1 returns 0; slot 0 reads UITable_GetRow(25, actionId): when the row's dword at +16 is non-zero, uses icon 165 (a default / 'unbound' mark) via sub_1403DC8D0.
otherwise (mode != pad or nothing found): id = sub_1400F6A80(actionId); if id != 0 returns sub_1403DC7BC(outStr, id, outBuf, 0) else 0.

notes: Used by the button-guide bar (GuideBar_LayoutRow -> sub_14028BE4C) to turn an action id into the icon string shown in the guide. The 3 * actionId stride is the per-action binding record (3 u16 slots of 16 bytes?).
open_questions: ? what sub_1400F6A80 and sub_1403DC7BC / sub_1403DC8D0 return exactly (string formatters). ? what config byte +13696 == 1 means (pad vs keyboard assumed).

name: sub_1400F6B5C
purpose: Resolves a button id through an Nxd table (qword_143CDA2C0, found by NxdRegistry_Find index 35) and returns one of four glyph ids according to the player's pad layout (byte at qword_143CD9EE8 + 13726).

behavior.text: table = cached qword_143CDA2C0, else NxdRegistry_Find(g_NxdRegistry, 35) (null = return 0). row = sub_1403D3AE8(table, key, ...) (null = 0); a row whose first qword is >= 0 must also yield sub_1403D2FD8(row) non-null, else 0 (a negative first qword uses the static default at 0x1406F5ED0).
switch on byte [qword_143CD9EE8 + 13726]: 2 -> dword at +16 of the record, 3 -> +20, 4 -> +24, default (0 / 1 / other) -> +12.

notes: Selects one of four per-controller-type icon ids (default = Xbox-like column 12; 2 / 3 / 4 = alternative layouts, plausibly PlayStation / Switch / Steam). The mapping to concrete controller types is I.
open_questions: ? which controller type each value 2 / 3 / 4 is. ? what Nxd table index 35 is called.

name: sub_1400F6D58
proto: __int64 sub_1400F6D58(unsigned int cur, unsigned int min, int max, unsigned int keys, int repeat)
purpose: Steps a cursor value by one with wrap-around when the 'vertical' direction pair is pressed (actions 35 / 36, masks 0x8000 / 0x2000), via sub_1400F6FA0.

behavior.text: calls sub_1400F6FA0(&delta, &wrap = 1, keys, repeat). If it reports no press (delta 0) returns cur.
n = cur + delta. wrap flag set: returns n; but n > max returns min, and n < min returns max (wraps). wrap flag clear: clamps to [min, max] (result = n bounded by max, then not below min).

notes: Used in the job-list panel input handlers for moving the cell cursor inside a column (min / max from the column table at panel+72). Which physical direction masks 0x8000 / 0x2000 are (up/down vs left/right) is not determined; the sibling sub_1400F6DD4 uses 0x1000 / 0x4000.

name: sub_1400F6DD4
proto: __int64 sub_1400F6DD4(unsigned int cur, unsigned int min, int max, unsigned int keys, unsigned int repeat, char wrapSeed)
purpose: Same as sub_1400F6D58 but for the other direction pair (actions 33 / 34, masks 0x1000 / 0x4000) via sub_1400F704C.

behavior.text: delta / wrap from sub_1400F704C; no press returns cur; else n = cur + delta and wrap / clamp exactly as in sub_1400F6D58 (the a6 argument is overwritten with 1 before the call).

notes: In sub_140130DF0 it moves between column groups (index 0..2); sub_1400F6D58 moves inside a group.

name: sub_1400F6FA0
proto: char sub_1400F6FA0(int *delta, char *wrapOut, unsigned int keys, int repeat)
purpose: Reads the second direction pair (actions 35 = -1 and 36 = +1, masks 0x8000 and 0x2000): reports a step and whether it may wrap.

behavior.text: if sub_1400FC29C() (an analog stick held in both opposite directions, see that sheet) returns 1 the result is 0 (no step).
if sub_1400FC6D8(keys, 0x8000, 35) then *delta = -1; else if sub_1400FC6D8(keys, 0x2000, 36) then *delta = +1; else returns 0.
on a step: repeat < 0 -> *wrapOut = 1; else *wrapOut = sub_1400FC598(repeat, mask, action) (is the repeat flavour of that key held: pressed => wrap allowed); returns 1.

notes: repeat is the repeat-fired key mask; repeat < 0 means 'always allow wrap'. Pad direction mapping of the masks not determined.
open_questions: ? exact meaning of the third argument of sub_1400FC598 (action id vs bit) in this use.

name: sub_1400F704C
proto: char sub_1400F704C(int *delta, char *wrapOut, unsigned int keys, int repeat)
purpose: First direction pair: actions 33 = -1 (mask 0x1000 = 4096) and 34 = +1 (mask 0x4000), same protocol as sub_1400F6FA0.

behavior.text: identical to sub_1400F6FA0 with masks 4096 / 0x4000 and actions 33 / 34 and the same repeat / wrap logic; sub_1400FC29C() == 1 blocks it.

notes: See sub_1400F6FA0.

name: sub_1400F7378
proto: char *sub_1400F7378(__int64 ctx, GUIPanel *panel, unsigned int tableKey, unsigned int rowKey)
callees: UITable_GetRowByKeys, sub_1400F681C, sub_1400F69BC, GUINode_FindPartByName, UIName_Key, sub_1403D87F4, sub_1403D8D1C
purpose: Fills one button-guide entry of a panel: from row (tableKey, rowKey) of UI table 33 sets the IconButton part's label key and the Title text id.

behavior.text: row = UITable_GetRowByKeys(33, tableKey, rowKey); null = return null.

if row dword +4 != 0: v = sub_1400F681C(ctx, row[1], row byte +36, buf); if row dword +8 != 0: v = sub_1400F69BC(ctx, row[2], ..., &key, buf, 0). When v != 0, finds part 'IconButton' (GUINode_FindPartByName(panel+272, ..)) of kind 2 and writes the icon string key at part+232 (sub_1403D87F4).

finds part 'Title' of kind 3 (text node) and sets its text id (dword +248) to row dword +12, setting the dirty byte +316 when it changed. If the part is missing the writes go to null + 248 (as decompiled; a missing Title part would crash, so every button-guide node has one).
returns row dword +12 (the title text id).

notes: UI table 33 is the button-guide table (the same table GuideBar_LayoutRow reads for the 8-slot guide bar). Part kinds 2 / 3 = icon button / text.
open_questions: ? sub_1400F681C (key / icon builder for a given source). ? the table 33 column names.

name: sub_1400FA7AC
proto: void sub_1400FA7AC(void *state, int itemId, uint8_t slot)
purpose: Adds an equipped item's attribute record and added-effect statuses to a unit's status state.

behavior.text: the item's attribute index (record +7) selects a 26-byte attribute record when below 0x55, else none.

weapon slots (slot below 5) take the weapon sub-record's added-effect index (+7); slot 5 and above take the chemist sub-record's (+2); the 6-byte added-effect record's flag byte 0x80 ORs its 5 status bytes into state +9.., 0x10 into state +14...
it also ORs the weapon element (+6) and the attribute record's bytes into the state.

notes: - Only the table reads were studied.

name: sub_1400FA94C
purpose: Fills an effect description (out) from a usable item's or an action's added-effect record.

behavior.text: for an item it reads the chemist sub-record's added-effect index (+2), for an action the action record's byte 11; the record's flag byte selects a copy of the 5 status bytes to out +9.. (0x80 / 0x20) or out +14.. (0x10).

notes: - Only the table reads were studied.

name: sub_1400FABC4
proto: __int64 sub_1400FABC4(char dirMask, char *geom, int *cursor, int repeatMask)
purpose: Two-pane grid cursor navigation (5 columns per row): moves a (pane, index) cursor with up / down / left / right and pane switch, and returns the flat index across both panes.

behavior.text: cursor[0] = pane (0 or 1; > 1 returns -1), cursor[1] = index in pane. geom = { int count0, int count1, bool valid0, bool valid1, bool noEmptySkip, ... }: pane counts are used only when geom[8 + pane] != 0, else 0.

dirMask bit 1 = move up a row (index - 5), bit 2 = down a row, bit 4 = left, bit 8 = right, bit 0x10 = previous (index - 1 with pane roll over), bit 0x20 = next. repeatMask < 0 or the matching bit means the key was repeat-fired (wrap allowed, flag v = 1); a non-repeat press stops at pane edges (does not wrap, returns the old pane).

single-axis moves use sub_1400F52C8(index, dx, dy, 0, last, 5, wrap) = move in a 5-wide grid with row / column wrap; moving beyond the last row switches pane (the other pane is entered at the same column, clamped to its length) and empty panes are skipped (up to two tries).
after the move, if the index >= count of the pane: an empty pane with a2[10] clear re-runs itself with dirMask 1 and flag byte 2 set (recursion), else clamps to count - 1.
result = sum of counts of the panes before cursor[0] + cursor[1] when valid, else -1.

notes: Not a Job Tree function (item-list style two-pane cursor with 5-wide pages); included because it was live on the screen chunk. The 5-wide row stride is V (constant 5 passed to sub_1400F52C8).
open_questions: ? which screens call it live (callers sub_1402C0DB8 / sub_1402C1244 / sub_14036CC50 not named). ? exact geom layout beyond count0 / count1 / flags at +8 / +9 / +10.

name: sub_1400FB93C
purpose: Fills a caller structure with an item's record and its category sub-record: the numbers the equip detail panel prints.

behavior.text: it takes the item id, fetches the 12-byte item record, then branches on the item's category to fetch the matching sub-record (weapon, armour, accessory or consumable).
the four sub-record accessors it can call correspond to the four record kinds; the routine copies the numeric fields into the caller's structure rather than exposing the pointers.
two call sites: the equip detail refresh and one further UI filler.
it carries no width site: the id is passed through unchanged, with no mask or limit applied in this routine.
the flattening is why the panel can print power, evade, element and price without knowing the category.
the caller structure's field order; only the four accessors and the copy direction were read.

notes: Purpose inferred from the callers and from the four sub-record accessors; the individual field copies were not listed.

name: sub_1400FB9F0
purpose: Classifies an item into the equipment slot group it belongs to, and writes the id and the group into a two-dword structure.

behavior.text: it stores the id at `[out]` and the group at `[out+8]`.
an item of category 1 (the second weapon range) takes group 5 without reading the record.

otherwise the record's slot-flag byte at +3 decides: bit 0x80 (a sign test, not an immediate) or 0x40 gives group 1, bits 0x30 give group 2, bit 0x08 gives group 4, and anything else falls through to group 5.
a record with the high bit of the flag byte set is also group 1.
the groups are the equipment slots the battle and menu code uses: hand, head/body, accessory, and an "other" bucket.
which group number corresponds to which named slot; only the numbers were read.

notes: Read in full. The category test is the same one the item command uses to tell the two weapon ranges apart.

name: sub_1400FC29C
purpose: Detects an 'opposite directions held at once' state on the pad / keyboard direction set: returns true when two opposite inputs of any axis are down together, which makes direction stepping ignore input.

behavior.text: reads the analog stick bytes at qword_140C69680 + 2608 / + 2609 (signed); a magnitude above 0x32 (50) counts as pressed in the sign's direction (v0..v3 booleans).

v7 = the input source byte; when it is 2 (an input source that reports no digital keys) the digital tests are skipped, otherwise sub_1400F0D4C(qword_143CD9EE8 + 8, action) is tested for actions 0xA4 / 0xA5, 0xA6 / 0xA7, 0x21 / 0x22, 0x23 / 0x24, 0x2A / 0x29.
for each opposite pair (A4+A5, A6+A7, 21+22, 23+24, 2A+29) the function returns true when both members are down (digital or analog).
otherwise false.

notes: Prevents stepping when e.g. Left and Right are both held; the five pairs are actions 33/34, 35/36, 41/42 and the stick action 164..167.
open_questions: ? which of the pairs are up / down vs left / right. ? sub_1400F0D4C (digital action test) not decompiled.

name: sub_1400FC6D8
proto: char sub_1400FC6D8(int mode, int mask, unsigned int action)
purpose: 'Was this action pressed this frame' test for the direction helpers: checks the action's pressed / repeat flags, with an optional key-mask test.

behavior.text: returns 0 when the input source byte is 2. mask == 0: returns 1 when sub_1400F0D00(input+8, action) or sub_1400F0D98(input+8, action) says the action's pressed (+1362 / +1378 stride 16) or repeat flags (+1366 / +1382) are set.
mask != 0: when mode != 0 and (sub_1400F6C8C(action) & mask) != 0 returns 1; else returns 1 when any of the first two press bytes at input + 48 * action + 1386 or 1390 (stride 16) is set.

notes: sub_1400F6C8C maps an action id to its pad mask (action 9 -> 4096, 10 -> 0x4000, 11 -> 0x8000, 12 -> 0x2000, 17 -> 4, 18 -> 8, 19 -> 1, 20 -> 2, 21 -> 512, 22 -> 1024, 23 -> 2048, 24 -> 256 ... as decompiled; the action ids are rows of a +1360 u16 type column). The caller's 'mode' is passed through from keys.
open_questions: ? the exact field names of the input record (stride 48 per action). ? meaning of mode.

name: sub_1400FC85C
callers: BattleMsg_ResolveEntry, EventMessage_Task, EventMessage_Scripted, sub_14022CBE4, SceneMsgTask_Run, sub_140232434, sub_14023286C, sub_1402E38E4, sub_1402E8384, sub_1402E8A38, sub_1402E8E54
purpose: Identifies which text pack and which text kind a string-pool pointer belongs to. The scene message and battle message code use it to turn a raw pool pointer back into a class and a kind before choosing a handler.

behavior.text: both output dwords are set to -1 before anything else; a null input returns 0 with those values.
the function walks a table of 45 qword pack pointers with a stride of 8 bytes.
for pack classes 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 the pack pointer itself is compared with the input; a match reports kind 0.
for the other classes the input is compared with all 32 group bases of that pack, each computed as the pack base plus a fixed header plus the dword offset stored for that group.
a match writes the class index and the kind index and returns 1; the walk stops after class 44 and returns 0.
the function calls nothing; it only reads the pack tables.
the class is one localized text pack (45 of them) and the kind is the 5-bit text-id kind, so the pair (class, kind) is the full namespace of one text id in that pack.
what each of the 45 packs is; the class numbers 0 to 7 being treated as single-group packs is unexplained.

notes:
- V: read in full (about 166 bytes) for the scene message path.
- V: 11 direct call sites, mostly message tasks and scene screens.
open_questions:
- ?: the mapping from class numbers to the 45 pack files.
- ?: why classes 0 to 7 have no 32-group table.

name: sub_1400FCE48
purpose: Checks that no 'busy' gate is active: returns 1 when the global gate variables at 0x142FF9F24..0x142FF9F50 are all clear (or the alternative gate function says OK).

behavior.text: if dword_142FF9F24 != 0: returns the result of sub_1402082FC() (0 when that is false). Otherwise returns 0 when any of qword_142FF9F30, the dword at 0x142FF9F34, the pair (0x142FF9F34/38) vs dword_142FF9F44, or dword_142FF9F50 is non-zero; else 1.

notes: Used by the job-list panel to decide whether the job action (class change confirm) is allowed right now: false selects the refusal sound / message 204 or 200 in sub_140131068.
open_questions: ? what the gate variables are (some save / event busy flags). ? sub_1402082FC.

name: sub_1400FE810
purpose: Appends one 16-byte element to a segmented container whose control block sits at a fixed global plus 0xF8. When the current segment is full it allocates the next 0x3800-byte block and links it into the block list.

behavior.text: the control block is reachable from a global pointer plus 0xF8; the element begin and end pointers are at +8 and +0x10 and a block count is at +0x24.
the capacity used for the full test compares a dword at +0x24 with the current element count shifted left by 6; the two are not a plain element count, so the unit of that comparison is unclear.

when the container is full, the function asks the game allocator at 0x140011750 for a 0x3800-byte block, using the heap pointer held by a global object when that object exists and a null heap otherwise.
the new block pointer is stored in the block list and the element is appended; the element's second qword is cleared.
an allocation failure returns 0 without appending.
the element is 16 bytes because the append advances the end pointer by 16 and writes a qword pair, and 0x3800 bytes is the segment size.
what the +0x24 comparison counts and what the element type is.

notes:
- V: found in the text-id research as a non-text use of the constant 0x3800.
- V: only the prologue and the growth branch were read; the rest of the function is unknown.
- V: the twin function sub_140405DF4 does the same for a control block at another global offset.
open_questions:
- ?: what the container holds.
- ?: whether the 64-unit capacity expression is a count of 64-byte groups or a different unit.

name: sub_140107914
proto: void sub_140107914(BattleMainWindow *w, unsigned int kind, unsigned int phase)
callees: AbilityTable_GetRow, GUINode_StopState, GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState, GUINode_PlayStateAtFrame, UIName_Key, sub_1400F4BCC, sub_1400F5828, sub_1400F6148, sub_14010745C, sub_1402607C0, sub_1403D8770
purpose: Plays the show / hide states of the battle command list cursor for one cursor event of the battle main window.

the same state is also chosen when the character render manager's flag byte (+13501) is set while the battle control's flag at +693392 is clear.
the two states are 'ShowUnknown' and 'HideUnknown' (the research reading of the key strings); the test marks abilities whose details are not shown to the player yet.

name: sub_14010824C
callers: `sub_1400E6740` (one site; also installed as an addon method)
purpose: The Land ability help panel's content method: it reads the Land row's ability id and icon and fills the panel's text and icon slots.

behavior.text: it reads the Land table row's ability id at `+4` and its icon index at `+16`.
it resolves the ability row through the ability table and the icon through the icon table, then sets the panel's name and help text.
it is one of the family of UI addon methods that take a resource name and a part and fill a widget group.

name: sub_140109134
callees: sub_1400F8474, sub_1400F84F4, sub_1400F8674, sub_1400FC0D8, FormatArgs_Push, sub_1402B889C, sub_14028F754 and other UI helpers
purpose: Refreshes a battle-side panel object from a packed text id or from the panel's own selection fields. It fills the icon, the name and the help text of the panel's cells, choosing the source by the text kind.

behavior.text: the function takes the panel object in the first argument and reads two of its fields (+0xE5A4 and +0x102AC), clearing the second.
it looks up named gadget parts of the panel by string and checks the part kind before using them.
a text kind of 0x3800 selects the item path: an Item-en row through the inlined accessor and a large icon path through ItemIcon_FormatLargePath.
a text kind of 0x7000 selects the ability path through AbilityTable_GetRow.
a text kind of 0xB000 takes a third branch that does not use the Item-en or ability tables.

window byte +66256 is a random-icon flag, cleared first: an ability action (kind 0x7000) copies the Ability row byte +0x42 (column random_icon); a weapon attack (kind 0xB000) sets it when either of the two hand item ids kept at window +66252 has the Item row byte +0x2D (column random_icon).
when the flag is set, after the damage number is drawn the node at window +248 (IconRandom) plays 'Show' and 'Hide' is stopped.

it is a panel refresh driven by the currently selected id, not a per-row list builder.

the chosen string is written through the text-node setter at 0x1403F0F8C and a dirty byte is set on the node.

name: sub_140130DF0
proto: char sub_140130DF0(JobPanel *p, int *out, int keys, int repeat)
callees: JobList_OnCursorChanged, sub_1400F4BCC, sub_1400F6D58, sub_1400F6DD4, sub_1400FC598, sub_14012FC6C, sub_140131688, sub_140131734, sub_140132D48, sub_140132D6C, sub_140152494
purpose: Input handler of the job-list panel for mode 2 (the main cell grid): confirm / cancel / detail buttons and cursor movement across the 19 cells.

behavior.basis: (confirm, action 26 or p+8528 / p+8824 click flag set)
behavior.text: if sub-mode p+19012 == 4 posts command 18 to the addon owner (sub_140152494(owner+152)); else when cell = p+19016 <= 0x12 calls sub_14012FC6C(p, cellState != 0 ? 6 : 3, 0) where cellState = dword [p + 148 * cell + 8964], and plays sound 14.
sub_140131734 (action 0x8E: detail / refuse), sub_140131688 (action 0x7E), sub_140132D48 (palette gate) can consume the event and return; action 143 (0x8F) suppresses movement.

cur = p+19016; column table at p+72 (3 ints, upper bounds, 19 as the last): group g = first index with cur < bound; v17 = sub_1400F6D58(cur, groupLow, groupHigh - 1, keys, repeat) moves inside the group; if unchanged sub_1400F6DD4(g, 0, 2, ...) switches group: new cell = clamp(cur +/- width of a group) into the new group's range (width at p+76, sign by direction). A forced cell p+8520 >= 0 (pointer hover) overrides the result when it differs from the current cell.
when the cell changed: p+19016 = cell, JobList_OnCursorChanged(p, cell, 0), out[1] = cell, out[2] = 1, sub_140132D6C(p) (refresh every cell's palette / state).
out[0] = 1409 / 1410 / 1100 are the event ids returned to the addon (1409 appears when the cursor is not moved; 1410 is set when the detail action returns).

notes: The job-list panel has up to 19 cells, 148 bytes each from p + 8832 (state dwords at +8964, +8904 (job id compare with 93), +8972..8974 byte flags), cursor at +19016, mode at +19008, sub-mode +19012. The 'rows of three groups' reading (p+72) is I.

purpose: Gives the input focus to one of the two option nodes of a choice window: the node the message window task calls "the cursor line" while a story choice waits.

behavior.text: first calls virtual slot +16 of the agent (a readiness test); nothing else happens when it returns false.
reads the window object pointer at agent +64 and does nothing when it is null.

`sub_14013AAC8(window, variant, size)` returns the address of one of six sub-blocks of the window object: variant 1 selects the blocks at +656 / +808 / +960, any other variant the blocks at +128 / +280 / +432, and size 0 / 1 / 2 picks the first, second or third of its triple (any other size value gives the first).
only option values 0 and 1 are acted on (the test is unsigned below 2); a larger value leaves the function without a focus change.

the option node is the pointer stored in the chosen sub-block at +136 + 8 * option, or at +120 + 8 * option when the language record exists and its field at +8 is 0 (a language-dependent layout of the two nodes); with no language record the +136 layout is used.
clears byte +132 of the cursor agent (`*(*(qword_143CD9DA8 + 16) + 8)`) when it is set, calls GUICore_FocusNode(option node), then clears byte +557 of that node.
returns the focus call's result; the other branches return the readiness result or the sub-block address.

EventMessage_Task and EventMessage_Scripted call it every frame of the choice loop with the cursor as the option value (the action ids and the choice code belong to the callers, see StoryChoiceBalloon), then call sub_140136654. The same pair is called from sub_140136DB8, whose own body (not this one) tests up / down / confirm actions on a list window, so I: that function is the window class's own list-choice handler and this function is its focus step.
seen live 2026-11-09 at the Mandalia Plain opening: the focused widget during the choice is the event window and the option nodes are two (cursor 0 and 1), matching the unsigned-below-2 test.
what the +557 byte of an option node means (it is cleared right after the focus call).

then looks at the cursor agent (`*(*(qword_143CD9DA8 + 16) + 8)`): it shows the cursor when that agent has no addon at +64, or the addon has no object at +24, or a byte at +74 of that object equals the value left in register r8 (I: zero, since the caller-side setup of the readiness test cleared r8; not confirmed live).

called right after sub_1401365AC in every frame of the story choice loop (see StoryChoiceBalloon), so the cursor is re-requested each frame while the choice waits.

name: sub_140153CA0
proto: char sub_140153CA0(__int64 a1, unsigned int a2, int a3, __int64 a4, int a5, __int64 a6, int a7)
callees: sub_1400FC14C, ItemTable_GetName, AbilityTable_GetRow, Ability_GetAuxRecord, sub_1400F8474, sub_140153B8C, sub_140275A78, GUI helpers
purpose: Binds one item or ability to a UI cell: it sets the cell's icon path and name from a 16-bit text id, reads the inventory count for an item, and records the cell state.

behavior.text: the fifth argument is the 16-bit text id; the kind is `a5 & 0xF800` and the value is `a5 & 0x7FF` (`0x140153EF5`).

kind 0x3800 is the item case: it formats the small item icon path with `ItemIcon_FormatSmallPath`, resolves the name with `ItemTable_GetName(a5 & 0x7FF)`, and for a value below 0x105 writes the inventory count from `g_InventoryCounts` (`0x14015415B`).
kind 0x7000 is the ability case: it formats the ability icon path, resolves the row with `AbilityTable_GetRow`, and reads the ability's auxiliary record for the level text.
the two-kind split is why the same 11-bit value serves an item id and an ability id; the field is a text-id value, not an item word.
the kind is stored in the cell node at +0xF8; a dirty byte at +0x13C is set; the cell state dword at +0x60 is set to one of four constants (0x67, 0x68, 0x69, 0x6A).
the function returns no value and has one direct caller.
this is the renderer that consumes the 16-bit cell words the item and ability lists build.
the producer of the fifth argument; the meaning of the two cell-state constants.

- V: read for the 0x3800/0x7000 dispatch, the 0x7FF value mask and the 0x105 count bound; the node plumbing is not classified.

name: sub_1401560D0

purpose: Fills the four command radio buttons of a command screen: each button gets the icon and the title of the skillset named by its text token (name token 0xB000 | set), so it is the one place a skillset's name is read straight from the JobCommand-en table.

behavior.text: finds RadioButton01..04 (as parts of the widget's node and as descendants) and, for each button whose token dword (at widget + 0xA4 + 8 * i) is non-zero, sets the button's flag byte (+144) and takes set = token - 0xB000 as an int with no mask (the marker 0xFE is only a value the subtraction can give, not an operand).

name: sub_14020435C

purpose: Runs the first pending tile event of the flag word dword_142FCE878 (set when a unit has stopped on a tile): crystal or chest pickup, map item, trap and the other terrain events. Only the crystal / chest branch (flag value 1) matters for learning.

behavior.text: it always starts by dispatching battle message 12 with the acting unit's slot (BattleMsg_Dispatch(12, 0, slot, 0, 0, 0)) and sets g_BattleState = 21 (the pickup state, whose per-frame function is sub_14020BFD4).

the flag word is tested in the order 1, 2, 4, 8, 0x10, 0x200, 0x400 (the last two are bit tests that the compiled code does not show as immediates; they read the decompiled `& 0x200` / `& 0x400`), else a fall-through that ends the state (g_BattleState = 49 when sub_140202930 is non-zero, else sub_140203FDC) and returns 0; every other branch returns 1.

flag 1 (a crystal or chest unit on the stopped unit's tile, see sub_140271AC0): the roll is run with the picker's record (g_PreviewUnitTable + 512 x the slot byte at record +444 of the first scene object, found by sub_1402607C0) as its argument, through g_TextCommandSlot (this function first sets that slot to Unit_RollAbilityLearning itself); the result pointer is stored in qword_140D40810.

any other result word (2, 3 or -1): message 27 is requested; when record +494 has a 0x30 bit, or its bit 0x08 is clear, the unit is restored at once with sub_1402722D8(unit, 2) (HP and MP to full) and the action result is applied; otherwise BattleMsg_Dispatch(12, slot, slot, 0, 1, 0) opens the crystal choice window (sub_140324658 case 2) and the outcome comes back later through sub_140237FA4 and sub_14020BFD4.
the branch ends by resetting the crystal's scene unit (SceneUnit_ResetAndQueue4(slot, 4, 31, 0, 0)) and returns 1.

the 0x30 bits of record +494 mark a unit the game controls itself (no choice window), so only a player-controlled unit gets the learn / restore choice; what sets bit 0x08 of that byte was not traced (?).

flag 4 is the map-item branch (sub_140271CA8 gives the item, the discovery notification is sent), flag 8 the trap branch (sub_14030C39C), flag 2 a terrain branch (sub_14030C5A0, Battle_ActorResultLevels); the meaning of 0x10, 0x200 and 0x400 was not decoded here.
the function makes no team test on the unit.

name: sub_140220EA0
proto: uint16_t sub_140220EA0(TextMeasure *out, const uint8_t *proportional, const uint8_t *text)
callees: `sub_14022138C` (reads the operand bytes of a code), `sub_14022627C` (digit count of a number), `sub_140220E10` (tag helper), `sub_140331E60` (width of one glyph)
purpose: The message measuring pass: walks a message's byte string (with its argument codes and back-references) without drawing and reports the width of every line, the widest line and the number of lines. EventMessage_Task runs it before it builds and draws the window.

behavior.text: the third argument is the text pointer; the second points at a flag byte: zero means a fixed width of 1 per printable byte, non-zero means proportional text (each glyph width comes from `sub_140331E60`, and the fixed widths below are 6 or 10 by the language record's field at +8).

the first argument is the output record: a pointer to an array of per-line widths (dwords) at +0 with its capacity as a word at +8, a pointer to the widest-line word at +16, a pointer to the line-count word at +24, and a running widest-line word at +32 that it raises.
the argument vector read by the number and name codes is the message argument block at 0x140783210 (a dword per argument); the function advances through it once per consumed argument.

a byte below 0xD0 is a printable character: its width (fixed or glyph width) is added to the current line; a byte whose high nibble is 0xD (0xD0 up to the top of that nibble) also sets a page prefix that the next byte combines with to pick the glyph; bytes of 0xD0 and above that are not handled by a case add no width. the story choice codes (the two bytes just above 0xFA) are not literals in this body and fall into that last group, so they add no width.
code 0xFA adds one fixed width to the current line.

codes 0xE4 and 0xE6 are number codes: they add the printed width of an argument (digit count times the fixed width) to the line; 0xE8 stores an operand used as a digit-count override by the next number code; 0xEE sets the current column from its operand.

the codes found by the range tests `b - 0xE2 <= 1`, `b - 0xF5 <= 1` and `b == 0xEC` (so 0xE2 and its successor, 0xF5 and its successor, and 0xEC; the successors are not literals) are skipped with their operand through `sub_14022138C` without adding width.

before the other tests the tag helper `sub_140220E10` is asked whether the byte plus the current argument stands for a replacement string; when it does, the walk continues in a static replacement string (address 0x14067213C) and then returns to the byte after the code.

a back-reference is a byte whose high nibble is 0xF and low nibble is below 4 (`(b & 0xF0) == 0xF0 and (b & 0xF) < 4`); the next two bytes give a distance, the walk continues that many bytes earlier in the text and returns afterwards. The limit 3 comes from the test, it is not a literal.

code 0xF8 ends the current line: its width is stored in the per-line array (while the line index is below the capacity), the widest-line values are raised, the line index goes up and the column restarts at 0.

a byte above 0xFD (the two top values, reached by the unsigned compare) ends the text unless a back-reference return is pending, in which case the walk resumes at the return point. The compare is `> 0xFD` in the code, so the top value is not an immediate in the body.

when a line ended right after code 0xFA its trailing 0xFA width is taken off before the longest-width test; at the very end one fixed width is added to the widest value when the last line was the widest.
on return writes the widest line width to the word behind the pointer at +16 and the line count to the word behind the pointer at +24, and returns the line count.
at the start it also copies a dword from 0x140723A50 to 0x142FF3CC0 and 16 bytes from 0x1411A7DEC to 0x142FF3CB0 (side effect: two static copies; what they feed is not read here).
the argument-block read at 0x1402210A1 is one consumer of this walk (besides the number codes).

notes: Whole function read (decompiled in IDA, 2026-11-09), rewritten from scratch: the earlier Behavior section described the number formatting only. 1,041 bytes.

reads the unit's held-item pointer at +0x148 and calls a pose/shape helper.
when the helper's result is below 2, takes the item branch.

on the item branch it calls ItemSprite_LoadPalettes with the item id taken from the held record at +0x1C2 and the flag set to

eleven direct calls (sub_140204CDC three times), plus the stack-cookie check.

the callers are battle and unit-render paths, because they pass unit objects and the flag controls whether the palette is

the meaning of the 26 and 52 pose values.

name: sub_14026C2E8
purpose: Loads or refreshes the high-definition sprite entry for one render slot.

behavior.text: it reads the high-definition sprite entry by shape, one of the four readers the live census hit.
it compares a record byte with 0xAA, the marker T1 records for this function.
it calls the sprite and texture helpers and reads the renderer's slot state.
the 0xAA value marks an entry that has no HD sprite, so the slot falls back to the base sheet.
a slot load that runs when a unit's job or equipment changes its sprite.
which slot it fills and when the load is retriggered.

name: sub_14026E838
purpose: Battle side of the palette load: copies the classic file's palette into the unit's look pool record, applies the CharShape colour override keyed by the unit's sprite byte, and uploads the palette and frames for the slot.

behavior.text: stores the unit's sprite byte (+0xA) at g_LookPoolFaceValue[pool index (+9)], once in each branch (0x14026E88B and 0x14026E9BB, each after its own byte load of +0xA); the readers take the value as the pool's battle face.

copies the first 0x200 bytes of the file into pool record + 0x30D6 (the lea of 0x140D03676 = pool base 0x140D005A0 + 0x30D6) with the opaque bit 0x80 on every odd byte except byte 1 of each 32 (as CharaPalette_LoadClassic).
calls CharShape_ApplyClut with cl = the sprite byte (a byte load of +0xA at 0x14026E8F3); the copy loop's byte mask of the index with 0x1F (0x14026E8D0) leaves ch = 1 when the loop ends.
slots below 9 upload through sub_140260718, others copy 0x8000 / 0x1000 bytes into fixed buffers; then 12500 bytes of frame data move into the pool record.
at the call cx = 0x100 | sprite for every sprite byte 0..255.

in load mode 1 the classic VRAM frame uploads of pools 0..8 (sub_140260718 under `mode != 1`) are skipped; the palette copy into the record (+0x30D6, 512 bytes, then CharShape_ApplyClut), the face value and the record data copy (+2, 12,500 bytes from file +0x9000) run in every mode (the record offsets are computed from the pool base, so +0x30D6 is not an immediate here).

notes: Only the palette part was read in full. V (2026-11-08): the pool index (a2) chooses fixed per-pool resources: pools 0..8 go through sub_140260718 at positions derived from the index (((a2 + 4) << 6) and (((a2 >> 3) + 13) << 6)); pools 9..14 copy 32 KB to 0x1437ADF4C + ((a2 - 7) << 15) (buffers 2..7, ending at 0x1437EDF4C; the pointer goes to g_PoolFrameBuffers[a2 - 7]) and 4 KB to 0x1437B5F4C + 4096 * (a2 & 7). A sixteenth record (pool 15) would write its 32 KB from 0x1437EDF4C (word_1437EDF4C and dword_1437EDF50, globals of EventScript_SkipTick and Battle_SaveCapture) and its pointer over dword_1411A37C8. The face store writes g_LookPoolFaceValue[a2] for every pool 0..14, so pools 10..14 store past the 10 dwords the setup clears (0x1437A5A08..0x1437A5A18).

name: sub_14027032C
purpose: Looks up the sprite shape's LUT parameter record for a scene unit and stores it, with two CharShape bytes, in the scene object's block +960..+979.

behavior.text: builds a small request (byte 0 = scene object dword +348 bit 2, byte 1 = whether the object's byte +300 low two bits equal 1, byte 2 = a value derived from the tile data at the object's position, read through sub_140249000) and calls CharaRender_LookupLutParams with the shape key (the object's word +28, from its byte +10).

stores the result's float at +960, dwords at +968 / +972 and words at +976 / +978 (the LUT parameter record), the byte the lookup returns at +3 of its output into object byte +964 (the CharShape depth_sort_height_offset column) and the byte it returns at +20 into object byte +966 (the CharShape unknown_2e column).
only recomputes when the shape key, the flag dword or the layer value changed from the cached ones at +28 / +32 / +30; a shape key beyond the CharShape row count falls back to row 0.
when the renderer has no LUT block (the global renderer's field at +148128 is 0) the record keeps its defaults and both bytes are 0.

notes: Name is ours. Byte +964 is read by UnitSprite_DepthSort; no code reads byte +966 (a dead store: the CharShape column behind it has no effect).
open_questions: ? what the two other tests on the object (+300 low bits, +352 mask 0x240) select in the layer value.

name: sub_140271AC0
callees: Battle_IsTileOccupied, Battle_ResultReset, Status_FilterPendingSets, Battle_StatusResolve, Job_IsChemistType, sub_140271D80, sub_140271C50
purpose: Builds the flag word (dword_142FCE878) of tile events that apply to a unit that has just stopped, for sub_14020435C to work through.

behavior.text: bit 1 is set when Battle_IsTileOccupied(unit +79, +80, +81 >> 7, 65) is not negative: flag 65 (0x41) matches only units whose +0x61 bit 0x40 (status Crystal) or +0x62 bit 0x01 (status Chest) is set (the byte tests are inside Battle_IsTileOccupied, not in this body), so bit 1 means a crystal or a chest is on the unit's tile. No team or job test is made.
bit 0x400 (set by a bit-or the compiled code does not show as an immediate) is added when a pending status set on the unit is non-empty (Status_FilterPendingSets), after resolving it.

bit 4 is added when the tile record (sub_140271D80) has its bit 0 set and the unit has +158 bit 0 (or is a Chemist-type job while g_ShopModeGate is set); else bit 8 when the tile record has its bit 1.
bit 0x10 is added when sub_140271C50 is true. The remaining bits (2 and 0x20..0x200) come from the unit's +156 / +157 flag bytes.
bit 4 is the map item and bit 8 the trap, from the branch each takes in sub_14020435C.

notes: Read in full on 2026-11-10 (static).

name: sub_140271EFC
purpose: Rolls which abilities a unit learns from the unit on the tile it names; fills the result block at dword_1411A6AB0 and returns its address.

behavior.text: the other unit is Battle_IsTileOccupied(a1 +79, a1 +80, a1 +81 >> 7, 65); above 20 (no unit) the result word is -1. Otherwise that unit is battle record `slot` of g_PreviewUnitTable (512 bytes each) and the slot goes to byte_1411A6B0A.

clears 19 bytes from unk_1411A6B4E and 19 qwords 64 bytes apart from unk_1411A6B61; when the other unit's +98 bit 0 is set the result word is 4 and word_1411A6B0C = sub_1402723EC(that unit), and nothing is rolled.
the result word is 2; nothing is rolled when either unit has bit 0x20 of +6 set.

walks the job indices 0..18 (the loop bound 19 is compared at 0x140272294) with the job id 74 + index; index 0 runs only when both units have the same character byte (+0) and then uses that byte as the job when it is below 0x80 or 0xA2 / 0xA3; any other index runs only when bit (0x800000 >> index) of a1's unlock mask (+159..161) is set, index 17 not with a1 +6 bit 6, index 18 not with a1 +6 bit 7.

the skillset is byte 0 of the job's JobTable row (the image-relative read at 0x14027213C); slots 0..23 are candidates when the other unit has the slot's learned bit (+162 + 3 x index) and a1 has not; skillset 224 drops ability 488 unless a1 +6 bit 6 and ability 491 unless a1 +6 bit 7.

the roll is `Rng_Percent(100, byte_140787F82[8 * ability])` (the ability's learn percent); a zero return marks the slot in the job's three roll bytes (stored at result +24 + 3 x index) and, for abilities up to 0x1FF (the compare at 0x1402721E0), sets bit (ability & 7) of result +94 + ability / 8 and of result +177 + 64 x index + ability / 8.
bit 0 of the result word is set when any slot was marked.
the job byte +3 of either unit is never read: every row id is 74..92 or a character byte, and the indices stop at 18; the result block holds 19 job entries.
Rng_Percent(100, p) returning 0 is the success case here (the code treats `!Rng_Percent` as learned).

notes:
The walk, the 19 three-byte roll entries and the 19 64-byte bit sets of the result block are sized for the 19 stock jobs.

Static reading (2026-11-10): the picker (a1) is the unit that has just stopped on the crystal; a1 +79..81 is its own tile (sub_14020435C passes the record of the first scene object's unit). The other unit is the Crystal or Chest unit on that tile (Battle_IsTileOccupied flag 65 matches status Crystal at +0x61 bit 0x40 and Chest at +0x62 bit 0x01). The result block is read by sub_14020435C (word and +92), sub_1402722D8 (the +24 roll bytes, applied to the picker's +162.. bits) and sub_140323D1C (the +94 set, the +158 job ids and the +177 per-job sets, for the window's list); no other code reads it. Layout and readers: see struct CrystalRollResult.

- V: the result block's byte +158 + i is the job id written at 0x140272136 for every index the walk entered; only 8 of each entry's 64 bytes at +177 + 64 x i are cleared at the start (the clear writes one qword per entry), so bits for abilities 64 and above in an entry can survive from an earlier roll; the 512-bit set at +94 is cleared whole.
- V: the walk has no team test; a1 is not checked to be a player unit here.
- V: the unlock mask read at a1 +159..+161 is 24 bits wide (indices 0..23) but only 0..18 are walked.
open_questions: - ? what bit 0x20 of +6 means (either unit having it turns the roll off).

name: sub_1402722D8
purpose: Applies the outcome of a crystal or chest pickup to the picking unit's record: a chest item goes to the inventory, a crystal restores HP and MP, or the rolled abilities are learned.

behavior.text: it resets the unit's action result block (record +446) and then acts on the bits of `flags`.
bit 4 (chest): Inventory_ReturnItem(unit, word_1411A6B0C), the item id the roll chose (result block +92).

bit 2 (crystal restore): the result block's HP and MP deltas are max minus current (record +0x32 - +0x30, +0x36 - +0x34), the result block's type bytes (+0 = 1, +2 = 0, +39 = 0x50) are set and a UI sound cue (id 0xE9) is started.

bit 1 (crystal learn): for 19 jobs x 3 bytes it ORs the roll's learned-slot bytes (the result block at +24, 0x1411A6AC8) into the unit's learned bits at record +162 (the job's three bytes at +162 + 3 x index), then sends an AbilityLearningBySuccession notification with the unit slot (record +444) and the byte at +2.
it returns 0, or the Inventory_ReturnItem result for a chest.
the loop bound is 19 and nothing else is written: no JP, no level, and nothing outside the unit's record, so a stock job's learned bits live only in the battle record until a later write-back.
where the battle record's learned bits are copied to the save at the end of a battle.

notes: Corrects the earlier sheet, which called this a succession refund: the chest item return is only its bit-4 branch. Read in full on 2026-11-10 (static).

name: sub_1402723EC
purpose: Chooses the item a chest unit gives to the unit that steps on it.

behavior.text: returns 255 at once while g_BattleSimulating is non-zero.
it reads the seven u16 values at the dead unit's record +26..+39 and counts those that Item_IsValidId accepts.

with at least one valid id it picks one of them with the game's xorshift generator (state xmmword_1408E5FC8), the index being (random 15 bits, masked with 0x7FFF, x count) / 0x8000, the divisor reached as the shift by 15.
with none it builds a random id near 240..253 from the same generator (the range is read from the immediates 240, 245 and the 13-wide scaling; the exact set was not enumerated).

the seven words are the dead unit's equipment slots, since the span +26..+39 covers the right and left hand offsets used elsewhere (+0x20, +0x24; those offsets are not in this body); so a chest gives back one piece of what the unit wore.

notes: Read in full on 2026-11-10 (static).

name: sub_140274DB0
purpose: Builds ten 5-byte status masks (one bit per status 0..39) from the flag bytes of the status property table.

walks the 40 entries of the status property table (the address 0x140788FE5, entry 0 byte 5, is loaded at 0x140274DCA; step 16).
byte 4 bits 0, 1, 2 and 7 set status bit k in masks 0, 1, 2 and 3 (mask m at +5*m); byte 5 bit 7 and bits 0..4 set masks 4..9.
then writes three constants (word +0x32 = 0x8560, byte +0x34 = 14, byte +0x36 = 32).
the masks group statuses by property (for example which statuses are removed at battle end); the meaning of each bit is ?.

name: sub_140275EF4
proto: ? (job row, unit index, equipment words, output work record)
purpose: Builds a unit's working stats from its job row and its equipment words, one of the two paths that turn equipped items into stats.

behavior.text: It sign-extends the unit index from the second argument and keeps the fourth argument as a pointer to the output work record.

The job row is read through the first argument and supplies the base stats before the equipment contributions are added.

name: sub_1402760E8
purpose: The end of a unit build: loads the unit's equipment, applies the equipment attributes and the move and jump bonuses, then sets the name key.

behavior.text: calls Unit_LoadEquipmentAndEvade, then Unit_ApplyEquipment(work, 1, row), then Unit_ApplyMoveJumpBonuses(work, 0), then returns UnitWork_SetNameKey(work, row).

the second argument is the OverrideEntryData row of the unit's entry (null when the unit has none); it is passed on to Unit_ApplyEquipment, whose Unit_ComputeStats pass adds the row's speed_bonus word to the final Speed byte (work +58), and to UnitWork_SetNameKey (chara_name column).
