name: sub_140278CF0
proto: int sub_140278CF0(uint8_t *unit, int status, int clear)
purpose: Sets or clears the countdown of a timed status on a unit record.

behavior.text: status 2 sets unit +7 to 0xFF when (unit +5 & 4) or (unit +6 & 9), else to 3.

statuses 24..39 only (the range check at 0x140278D10 subtracts 0x18 from the status and skips results above 0x0F, unsigned): with `clear` it zeroes unit +78 + status; otherwise it copies status entry byte 3 into unit +102 + (status - 24) (the address 0x140788FE3, entry 0 byte 3, is loaded at 0x140278D46 and indexed as that address + 16*status).
status 39 uses slot 15 and returns -1 when unit +117 is already non-zero.
returns 0 otherwise.

name: sub_140278FEC

name: sub_140279110
callers: none direct; passed as the CompareFunction of a sort by sub_1402791FC (0x14027928A) and sub_1402792B0 (0x140279306)
purpose: Sort comparator: orders two status ids by byte 2 of their status property entries.

behavior.text: takes the low 7 bits of *a and *b; returns 0 when either is >= 40.

reads entry byte 2 of both (the table base 0x140788FE0 is loaded at 0x140279125 and the byte is read at base + 16*id + 2); returns 1 when a's byte is smaller, -1 when larger, 0 when equal (descending order).
byte 2 is a display / processing priority.

notes: None recorded.

name: sub_140279150
purpose: Returns a code for the highest-priority status present in two 5-byte status sets of a unit state.

behavior.text: loops over the 40 statuses (the address 0x140788FE5, entry 0 byte 5, is loaded at 0x14027915E; step 16); bit k of the sets at +34 and +29 selects status k.
keeps the status whose entry byte 2 is the largest; the result is 129 + k (set at +34) or 1 + k (set at +29), plus 128 when entry byte 5 has bit 3 set.
the code selects a status icon or message.

name: sub_14027F270
purpose: Computes the reachable-tile highlight for a unit, extending the base movement/jump by the best Jump-command abilities in its skillset.

behavior.text: gets the unit's ability list via sub_14030E368 (v39 = ids) and for every id with `(id - 394) <= 11` reads kind3: byte 0 (byte_140789260[2*(id-394)]) and byte 1 doubled (byte_140789261[...]); each is kept as a maximum over the list (initial 8 / 16 when the unit byte +0x...E3 == 93, else 1 / 2).
the range check at 0x14027F3A9 subtracts 0x18A from the id and skips results above 0x0B (unsigned); the byte reads follow at 0x14027F3B1.
the maxima feed sub_14027EBF8 and a 256-entry tile pass that sets or clears flag 0x40 on tile records at 0x140D8DCB0 + 8*i + 5; returns the number of marked tiles.

notes: Kind3 is horizontal (byte 0) and vertical (byte 1) jump values for ids 0x18A..0x195 (I: names from the verified table description).

name: sub_14027F974
callees: AbilityAction_GetRecord, BattleRange_FlagTargetTiles, BattleRange_MarkWeaponReach, BattleRange_SpreadDiamond, sub_14027EA18, sub_14027F684, sub_14002630C
purpose: Marks the tiles of an action's area (the range marks) for a request; ability 220 gets four extra directional marks.

behavior.text: copies the 20-byte request; its word at +2 is the ability id and the action row is fetched with AbilityAction_GetRecord.
when the ability id is exactly 220, after the common marking it calls sub_14027F684 four times with the arguments 2, 0, 6 and 4: its own area in four directions.

the rest marks the weapon reach, the diamond spread and flags target tiles through the BattleRange helpers (the callee list); the same row under any other ability number gets none of the four directional marks (the test is on the exact id).

name: sub_140280170
purpose: Builds the weapon part of a battle action: which item is in the acting unit's hands, what damage it does, and which animation it uses.

behavior.text: It reads the acting unit's hand words and passes each one to the weapon accessor only when it is not 255 and is below 261.
The accepted weapon id is stored in the action record's weapon field.
The weapon record then supplies the attack value and the animation selector used by the rest of the action build.
It calls eight helpers and has a single direct caller.
This is the point where an equipped weapon becomes the action's weapon, so an item the weapon accessor cannot see becomes an unarmed attack.

name: sub_140280850
purpose: Marks the units that satisfy the two Arithmeticks mask abilities of an action; returns the number marked, -1 when invalid.

behavior.text: requires the action's two ability words in 414..421; kind5 bytes are read via the virtual base: v3 = g_AbilityKind5_vbase[word1], v4 = g_AbilityKind5_vbase[word2] (0x1402808CC, 0x1402808E4).
accepts only when `(v3 & 0xF0) != 0`, `(v4 & 0x0F) != 0`, `(v3 & 0x0F) == 0` and `(v4 & 0xF0) == 0` (tests `& 0xF0` at 0x1402808CC and `& 0x0F` at 0x1402808E4).

for each of 21 units a value v8 (chosen by v3 bits 0x40 / 0x20 from two unit bytes, otherwise a derived byte, or the +33 byte when v3 is negative) is tested against v4: bit 8 = membership in table byte_14067E1D0 (54 entries), bit 4 = multiple of 5, bit 2 = (v8 & 3) == 0, bit 1 = multiple of 3.
matching units set flag 0x80 on their tile record byte 5 at 0x140D8DCB0 + 8*tile and are counted.

notes: The high nibble of kind5 picks the unit value (CT / Brave / Faith style in the classic game: I), the low nibble the divisor test.

name: sub_140281488
purpose: Validates a candidate action per command type and, when a3 asks for it, consumes the item or MP; returns -1 invalid, else a small result code (0..3).

behavior.text: copies the 20-byte action to a local; returns -1 when the actor byte >= 0x15 or the actor/target unit slot is 0xFF.
command type 1 (Items) requires Item_GetRecord(item)[5] == 34, rewrites the action id to item + 128 and decrements the stock byte_1411A7C00[item] when a3 & 1.

command type 2 (Throw) loops id from 382 comparing the kind2 byte (`[id + r9 + 7901458]`, 7901458 = 0x789112 = kind2 vbase) with Item_GetRecord(item)[5], until id reaches 394 (-1 if none), at 0x140281638; writes the id to a2+2 and decrements stock.
command type 10 (charge) returns -1 when `(id - 406) > 7`, else v26 = g_AbilityKind4_vbase[2*id], at 0x1402818A4; sets v5[441] when a3 & 1.
types 0/3/6/7 go through the common path: ids > 0x16F return -1, else AbilityAction_GetRecord(id)[12] & 0x7F is the cost (halved or zeroed by status flags in unit byte +155), stored at unit +397.
its Charge test is at 0x140281882 and its Arithmeticks test at 0x1402815CF.

name: sub_140281A64
purpose: Collects target units for a preview action by action id (440, 444, 446 special-cased).

behavior.text: reads a byte table at the virtual base 0x14067F58A indexed by the signed action id word_14186AFF0 / the unit's action word (bit 0x04 / 0x08 / 0x30 tests).
the index domain is not established: an index below 0x26 would land in the monster skillset rows (0x14067F4C0..0x14067F5B0).

notes: - Only the table read was studied.

name: sub_1402828E4
purpose: Returns a small action-mode code for a unit from its command flags and its current ability, special-casing ability 367 and job 93.

behavior.text: the unit command byte at +0x1A1 is looked up in the command table at 0x14067E010 and the result is kept in a register.
it clears a global byte, calls sub_14030DD1C on the unit and inspects unit +0x63 bit 2 and unit +0x65 bit 4.
bit 2 of +0x63 with an ability of 0, 0x16F or 0x1D gives one path; otherwise the ability record is fetched.
an ability id of 0x16F (367) is compared directly; this equality is separate from the 368 boundary compare.
a job byte of 0x5D (93) changes the result through the job check that follows.
the returned codes are small values 1, 5, 6, 7 and 8, plus a negative value for an invalid unit.
when the state word at 0x14186AF9C is zero it calls sub_140279370 with 0xFF before the main switch.
the codes select an action prompt or cursor mode, because the callers are the preview and commit paths.
the meaning of each code; only the values are read, not the consumer switch.

the unit is the argument; the command byte is +0x1A1 and the ability word the signed word at +0x1A2; the answer is, in order: a unit with mask 0x04 at +0x65 or a non-zero sub_14030DD1C answer returns that answer + 6 (7 for the +0x65 case); a Toad unit (+0x63 mask 0x02) returns 5 unless the ability is 0, 367 or 29 (a command kind of 10 returns 5 whatever the ability); an ability above 0x16F skips everything below and returns 0.
for an ability up to 0x16F with command kind 0 or 6: the action row's flag byte +5 mask 0x20 together with the unit's +0x62 mask 0x08 returns 2.

for command kind 0 only, and a unit whose job byte is not 93: the MP cost is action-row byte +13, halved when unit +0x99 has bit 7; it is stored in the byte at 0x1407B078E; a unit MP (+0x34) below the cost returns 3; otherwise the cost is subtracted unless the simulate mode (g_BattleSimulating) is 2; then it returns 0.

so an ability id above 0x16F is never checked and never pays MP; see AbilityAboveStockBoundaryHasNoMpCheckOrCost. The preview twin is sub_14030B1A0 (it stores the cost without paying). The 367 equality is at 0x140282960.
the id bound is a 16-bit compare of the ability id with ax = 0x16F, then a jump past the MP block when above (ax also serves the Toad test's 367 just before).

notes: Whole function read (277 bytes). The 367 comparison is the special case the ability-width study lists.

name: sub_14028531C
callers: not in the exported set; a battle-unit builder
purpose:
Copies the selected party unit's five equipment words into a battle unit record and mirrors the two hand words
into the save row, all raw.

behavior.text:
It finds the battle-table row for the selected unit's save index (0x1402853A0..0x1402853B4), clears the
  two hand pairs to 0x00FF00FF (0x1402853B9, 0x1402853E6) and reads the party words at +0x54 and +0x56.

Each non-zero word is passed raw to `Item_GetRecord` (0x1402853CA, 0x1402853F7); the category byte +5
  decides whether it goes to the second or first word of the pair (0x1402853D5/0x1402853DC).

The words +0x58, +0x5A and +0x5C are copied raw to battle +0x1A, +0x1C and +0x1E
  (0x140285415..0x140285444).

It copies the battle hand pair back to the save row (0x14028546D..0x14028547D) and calls
  `sub_140287398` on the unit's +0x54 for the stat bytes.

There is no 0x3FF mask and no bit-15 test: a flagged party word would reach the battle unit and the save
  row as a full 16-bit word, and the `Item_GetRecord` call would index past the table.
This is a battle-start copy; the party words are assumed committed by the time it runs.

notes: V: copies the five party words raw to the battle unit fields +0x1A..+0x26 and to the save record (0x1402853B4-0x140285444); Item_GetRecord is called with the raw word.
open_questions: - ?: the caller and whether a battle can start while the Outfitter's flag on the party words is still set.

name: sub_1402855F0
callers: not in the exported set; a battle/party record builder
purpose:
Fills a 72-byte local record from the selected party unit's words, including the five equipment words copied
raw into +0x1A..+0x1E and +0x20..+0x26.

behavior.text:
It reads +0x54 and +0x56 and passes each raw word to `Item_GetRecord` (0x14028564D, 0x14028567E); the
  category decides the slot pair.
It copies +0x58, +0x5A and +0x5C raw to +0x1A, +0x1C and +0x1E (0x140285699..0x1402856D0).
It calls `sub_140287398` on the unit's hand pointer to fill the stat bytes at +0x44..+0x47.
No mask and no flag test; a bit-15 word would be copied and looked up raw.
This is the party-record variant of the battle copy; it is used when the unit has no battle-table row.

notes: V: the same raw copy into a 72-byte local record (0x140285637-0x1402856D0); no mask and no flag test.
open_questions: - ?: the caller and whether it runs at battle start.

name: sub_140285A6C
purpose: Writes every party unit's record back to its save row.

behavior.text: It loops `g_PartyCount` units (0..count-1) and calls `PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave` for each (0x140285A7F).

It is called by the commit handler after `sub_1402D65D4` has stripped the session bits, so the save rows
  receive clean words on that path.

It is also called by the equip-now path `sub_140288590` and the return path `Party_ReturnHandItems`, which
  write committed (masked) ids.

This is the save write of the equip session; a caller that runs before the strip would write a flagged
  word and `PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave` would index the item table with it.

notes:
- V: It does not mask or test any word; the sanitizing is the caller's job.
- V: The loop is over the party count, not the 54 save rows.
open_questions: - ?: whether any caller other than the commit handler can run with a bit-15 word.

name: sub_140285B10
purpose:
Sorts a 0xFFFF-terminated item list in place by one of eight preset field orders. Before sorting it removes ids the validity
check rejects, so an invalid id never takes part in a comparison.

behavior.text: the second argument is the list; the first is a field selector, masked to four bits.
the selector indexes a table of eight byte lists; each byte names one record field the comparator should use, in order.

the first pass compacts the list: every id the validity check rejects is overwritten by the next entry, so the list
  shrinks.

the second pass is an insertion sort over adjacent pairs; two entries are swapped when the comparator reports the left
  one as not smaller.
the end condition of this function is the 0xFFFF terminator only (compared as the word -1, formed by an OR with -1); it does not use the 255/261 rule of the saved lists.
it reads item records and counts only through the comparator and key helpers; it writes nothing but the list.
this is the sort the player picks in the menu, as opposed to the saved user order maintained by the synchronisers.
the meaning of each of the eight preset field orders was not established beyond the field keys themselves.

compaction shifts whole words and the sort swaps whole words at 0x140285BF6 and 0x140285BFA; the validity test masks with 0x3FF (constant at 0x140285B4A, mask at 0x140285B4F), so flags travel but do not affect the order.

name: sub_140285F2C
purpose:
Copies the shared display list into the saved order list of one menu group, so that the order the player left the menu list
in becomes the stored order.

behavior.text: takes one group index and looks the list pointer up in a table of five pointers, without a range check.
reads the shared display list from its first word and copies entry after entry into the group list.

it stops at the 0xFFFF terminator of the display list (compared with the word -1) and then writes the value 255 into the group
  list as its end marker.

there is no capacity check; the group list is the smaller array (21 to 141 words) and the display list can hold up to
  256 words.
it touches no other global and calls nothing.

the single caller is the item-menu handler that rebuilds all five group lists after a sort, which fits "confirm the
  displayed order as the saved order".

whether a display list longer than the group list has ever been observed; the stock group sizes leave at most two spare
  words.

the whole 16-bit word is copied from the shared display list to the saved order list off_14067F498[group] (load at 0x140285F2C, store at 0x140285F57), with no mask; a flagged entry would be copied with its flag.

name: sub_140286070
purpose: The equipment-order twin of the item synchroniser: it applies the owned/not-owned rule to the equipment order list of one group. Groups at or above four return immediately, because only four equipment lists exist.

behavior.text: returns immediately when the group argument is 4 or more.
selects one of four equipment list pointers from `off_14067FA90` (8-byte entries).
scans item ids 1 to 260 and keeps only the ids `Item_IsValidId` accepts and `Item_MenuCategory` assigns to the group.
the list walk tests each word against 0xFF and 0x105; the upper constant is the form 0xFF+6 built by the lea at `0x1402860AB`, not a literal.
an owned id that is absent is inserted at index zero with a right shift of the tail; an id that is not owned is removed.
the end conditions are the word 0xFF and any word at or above 0x105.
it writes only the selected list; the sort order is never touched.
it is called from the item syncer and from the snapshot syncer, so both paths keep the equipment order current.
none.

notes: - V: whole body read. The four equipment lists are the saved `equip_user_sort_*` fields.

name: sub_140286160
callers: none direct (reached by tail jumps from ItemOrder_SyncGroup and sub_14039684C)
purpose: Applies the owned/not-owned rule to the obtain-order list, the single list that records the order in which items were first acquired. It takes no argument and always works on that one list.

behavior.text: takes no arguments and reads no group; the target list is `word_141874726`, and the same routine also reads the buffer at `word_141874540 + 243`.
scans item ids 1 to 260 and keeps the ids `Item_IsValidId` accepts (no category test).
the list walk tests each word against 0xFF and 0x105; the upper constant is the form 0xFF+6 built by the lea at `0x140286185`, not a literal.
an owned id that is absent is inserted at index zero; an id that is not owned is removed.
the end conditions are the word 0xFF and any word at or above 0x105.
it has no direct call site; both synchronisers jump to it after their own work.
the obtain order is the "order acquired" sort the menu offers as its special sort mode.
whether anything else consumes the list besides that sort and the save copies.

notes: - V: whole body read. The list is the last of the five saved order lists but is addressed directly, not through the pointer table.

name: sub_140286228
proto: int sub_140286228(int field, uint16_t *list, int order)
purpose:
Sorts the shared display list by one chosen field, or rebuilds it in obtain order. It is the sort the sort menu and the
shop list use, as distinct from the eight-preset sorter.

behavior.text: the first argument is the field selector; the third is an id used as a tie-break input by the comparator.

field selector 8 is special: the list is first filtered through the obtain-order list, then the given id is inserted at
  the front when it is positive. This is the "obtained order" view.

every other selector runs an insertion sort with the comparator over three fields: the equality of the tie-break id,
  the chosen field, and the id itself.
an id the validity check rejects is compacted out before the sort, as in the preset sorter.
the scan that finds the insertion point stops after 145 entries, the same cap the list builder uses.
the list must be 0xFFFF-terminated; this function does not use the 255/261 rule.
it returns the resulting count.

because the third argument is the id the player acted on, the sort keeps that id at the front after the chosen field
  has been applied.
none.

compaction shifts whole words at 0x140286273, the insert writes the row word unmasked at 0x140286339, and the sort swaps whole words at 0x1402863AA and 0x1402863AE; the row compare masks the list side with 0x3FF (constant at 0x14028625A, mask at 0x14028625F).

name: sub_14028668C
purpose: Builds the job list of a unit given as a work record (C), not a party index: it points the bit reader at the work record's unlock mask and calls JobList_Build in mode 1, so the result holds only the jobs the unit has unlocked.

behavior.text: sets the job-list flag byte to 1 and the bit reader to C + 159 (the unlock mask of the work record) before the call.
builds JobList_Build's four info bytes from the record: the job word is the byte at C+3 widened to 16 bits, then C+0, C+6 and a flag (byte C+0x12 + 0x50 <= 0x2F).
the list goes to the caller's buffer and JobList_Build's count is returned; g_RuntimeJobList is not written.
JobList_Build is called directly from here (JobList_BuildForPartyUnit is a separate entry).

notes: Whole function read (decompilation and disassembly).

name: sub_140286A78
proto: void sub_140286A78(unsigned short unit, int mode)
purpose: Collects the abilities of a party unit's current job into the list buffer used by the job screen, marking each entry that is available to the unit.

behavior.text: the unit index is the first argument and selects the unit record from the party table g_PartyUnits; the unit's job id comes from the 16-bit field at record offset 0x24.

it calls Party_GetUnitJobId for the unit, then calls JobAbilityList_Build 19 times (the unit's own job, then jobs 75..93), accumulating the entries into a 200-word stack array; one call can append up to 24 entries.
after building, it sorts the accumulated words in place with an adjacent-comparison sort.

it then writes the sorted abilities into the shared list buffer at 0x141811470, one 16-bit word per entry, adding 0x4000 to the id when sub_140289F4C returns non-zero and writing the bare id when it returns zero.
the loop stops at the 0xFFFF terminator (compared against -1 held in a register) or at the end of the accumulated list, whichever comes first.
the 0x4000 bit means "known or available", by analogy with the same bit on the shop list where it means "cannot equip" and with the fact that the other branch writes the plain id.
the buffer at 0x141811470 is a general UI list buffer reused by several screens, not a shop-only array, because this job-screen function writes ability ids into it.

sub_140289F4C returns 1 for the small hand-written set of job-specific abilities in 0x1D6..0x1DE: job 15 accepts 0x1D6, 0x1D9, 0x1DD and 0x1DE, and jobs 75, 78, 84 and 89 accept one id each (0x1DA, 0x1D8, 0x1D9, 0x1DD).
why the stock game marks those innate abilities with 0x4000 in this list; the screen's consumer is not in the exported set.

an entry is marked with 0x4000 when sub_140289F4C reports non-zero: the constant is loaded at 0x140286B7C, ORed at 0x140286B81, and dropped again at 0x140286B89 when the test was zero. The marked word is written to the shared display list.

the insertion sort compares signed 16-bit words (compare at 0x140286B23, signed branch at 0x140286B27), so a 0x4000-marked entry sorts above every plain id; the de-duplication compares raw words at 0x140286B5E and 0x140286B6A, so a marked and an unmarked copy of one id are both kept.

notes: - V: this is the only job-screen function in this set that writes the shared list buffer rather than reading it.
open_questions:
- ?: the exact meaning of the 0x4000 mark on this screen.
- ?: whether the 19-slot limit corresponds to a fixed ability-slot count or to the row count of the panel.

name: sub_140286C8C
purpose: Fills an item descriptor from the record table and the sub-record that matches the item's category.

behavior.text: It zeroes two words of the output structure before filling it.
The id argument is masked to ten bits and passed to the item record accessor.
The record's kind byte then selects the weapon, shield, armor, accessory or consumable sub-record, and that sub-record supplies the rest of the descriptor.
It calls six helpers and has two direct callers.
The ten-bit mask is the category-table width, not the record width; both lookups would accept a wider id.

name: sub_140287118
proto: __int16 __fastcall sub_140287118(_WORD *block, __int64 record, __int16 job, __int16 mode, __int64 unit_words, __int64 candidates, __int64 extra)
purpose:
The stat calculator behind `sub_140287354`: it masks the five unit and candidate words and computes the
attack/defence differences into the block.

behavior.text:
When `unit_words` is set it fills two five-word arrays with the unit words and the candidate words, each
  masked with 0x3FF (0x140287176/0x140287196).

It calls `sub_140286FEC` twice to build stat rows for the job/mode and the extra argument, then
  `sub_140286E7C` to write the difference into the block.
It returns the difference of two stat words and stores them at record +14 and +20.
A flagged word is masked before it reaches the stat row; no flag is tested.
This is the only place the block's +0x06/+0x12/+0x1C stat groups are written from a candidate/unit pair.

notes: - V: The two five-word arrays are stack copies; the function never writes the caller's hand words.
open_questions: - ?: the meaning of the job and mode arguments and the extra pointer.

name: sub_14028728C
purpose:
Computes the equip block's stat deltas from the unit's live words and the candidate array, comparing each pair
masked to ten bits.

behavior.text: It clears the block's first 0x24 bytes (0x1402872C1..0x1402872D7) and then loops five times.

It reads the unit word and the candidate word, masks both with 0x3FF (0x1402872EE/0x1402872F6), calls
  `sub_140286DDC` with the pair (0x1402872FA) and accumulates the difference into the block with
  `sub_140286E7C` (0x14028730E).

It accumulates two words at 0x1407B27D4 and 0x1407B27CE (0x140287323/0x14028732A), which are the record's
  attack/defence mirrors.
It never writes the candidate or hand words; the outputs are the stat fields only.

Because both sides are masked, a bit-15 unit word and a plain candidate compare by id, which is what
  makes the preview show the change rather than the flag.

notes:
- V: The block pointer is `g_EquipSet`; the candidate pointer is `g_EquipCandidates` (0x141876C64) and the
  unit pointer is unit +0x54.
- V: The five-word loop includes the accessory slot, even though the Outfitter only edits four.
open_questions: - ?: whether the two accumulated words are the same attack/defence pair the record renderer reads.

name: sub_140287354
proto: __int64 __fastcall sub_140287354(__int64 block, __int64 record, __int64 unit_words, __int64 candidates, __int16 job)
purpose:
Clears the equip block and recomputes it from the record, the unit words and the candidate words through
`sub_140287118`.

behavior.text: It clears the block's first qword and the words at +0x08..+0x0C, +0x12 and +0x1C (0x14028737B..0x140287389).

It passes the block, the record, the unit word pointer, the candidate pointer, the job word and the
  selected unit to `sub_140287118` (0x14028738D).
It does not read the hand words itself; the callee masks them with 0x3FF.
This is the one-line wrapper used by every equip screen refresh to keep the stat block in sync.

notes: - V: The block address is `g_EquipSet` at 0x141876C40; the candidate address is 0x141876C64.
open_questions: - ?: whether the cleared +0x08..+0x0C range is a separate stat group from the one sub_140287118 writes.

name: sub_140287398
purpose:
Sums the stat contributions of five equipment words into the 0x141876E90 block (or a caller block) using only
their masked ids.

behavior.text:
It loops five times, reads each word, masks it with 0x3FF (a 0x3FF mask at 0x1402873F6), and calls
  `sub_140286C8C` for the item's stat row.

It accumulates the returned stat words into block +0x06, +0x08, +0x0A, +0x0C, +0x16, +0x18, +0x20 and
  +0x22 (0x140287408..0x14028747D). It does not touch block +0x24 (the hand words).
The block is cleared at +0x06, +0x16 and +0x20 before the loop (0x1402873B4..0x1402873C0).
This is the stat half of the panel refresh; the hand half is the raw copy done by the caller.

notes: - V: A flagged word contributes its masked id's stats, not a different item.
open_questions:
- ?: whether the stat block's +0x00..+0x04 and +0x0E/+0x10 words are written elsewhere; this function only
  writes the listed offsets.

name: sub_1402875A4
proto: char __fastcall sub_1402875A4(unsigned __int16 unit, unsigned __int16 *out, __int64 unused3, __int64 unused4)
purpose:
The alternate candidate filler: it builds the five equip candidates from the equipment inventory list (mode 3,
no bit-14 marks), sorts each category's stack list and copies the chosen ids into the output.

behavior.text:
It reads the selected unit's two hand words and flag byte +0x16E, decides which hand is the primary from
  the item category, and calls `Inventory_BuildEquipList` with mode 3 (0x14028775E) for each of the five
  category bytes.

Mode 3 of the builder never sets bit 14; this path therefore produces plain ids, unlike the shop builder
  with mode 1.

It merges the category lists through the same stack sorter and `sub_14028B180` comparator; when two hands
  hold the same category it prefers the one with the higher menu field.

At the end it may swap the first two output words (a two-word swap
  at 0x140287D64/0x140287D68/0x140287D6B) when the primary hand is one-handed and the pair fails its weapon
  check.

It does not set bit 15 anywhere; the output is a plain candidate list, and the caller (`sub_140333FE0`)
  passes it to `sub_140287354` for the stat block.

This is the equip screen's own picker, while `sub_140287D9C` is the Outfitter/shop picker; the two use the
  same output shape but different mark conventions.

notes:
- V: The swap moves whole words, so any flag a caller had put in the output would travel with the swap.
- V: The sheet's earlier "five words" is right for the buffer, but this filler writes the five from its own
  category lists, not from the unit's +0x5C.
open_questions: - ?: which of the five categories maps to which output slot; the category byte order is read from a table.

name: sub_140287D9C
purpose:
Builds the Outfitter's candidate list for the selected unit and shop: five category lists are merged, ordered,
and the first four output words are marked with bit 15 when they differ from the live and override words.

behavior.text:
The pointer arguments are not read; the unit is `g_SelectedUnitIndex` (0x141811428) and the shop is
  `g_SelectedShopIndex` (0x141811684).

For each of the five category bytes 5, 6, 2, 3 and 4 it calls `Shop_BuildItemList` with mode 2 and the
  sort flag set, writing into a 152-word stack list.

It merges the lists into the caller's output, capping at 146 entries and stopping on 0xFFFF. The merge is
  an insertion sort whose adjacent comparisons go through `sub_14028B180`; the comparison group per position
  comes from the byte table reached through the pointer at 0x14067FAE8.

The sort swaps two stack words at 0x140288256/0x14028825B (load, store, store): the candidate list is
  reordered in place, flags and all.

It then walks the output and, for each of the first four words, compares the signed candidate word with
  the unit's raw word (0x140288525/0x14028852C) and the override word (0x140288537/0x140288540). A candidate
  that matches neither is OR-ed with 0x8000 (the constant 0xFFFF8000 is loaded at 0x140288544, OR-ed at
  0x140288549 and stored at 0x14028854C).

The mark loop runs four times: 0x140288471 sets the count to 4 (a loop count of 4), not five. The fifth
  output word is not written by this function; the session functions copy it from the unit's +0x5C.

A unit word that already has bit 15 does not equal the signed candidate, so the mark is re-applied on a
  pending word; the "changed" test is therefore against the raw word, not its masked id.

The stack list entries are masked with 0x3FF before they are sorted (0x1402882A0/0x1402882B3); the mark
  is the only flag added.

notes:
- V: The function writes a 5-word-capable output but only four marks. The earlier sheet's "five output words"
  was one too many; the fifth is the caller's copy of unit +0x5C.
- V: It never reads or writes the shared menu list; the bit-14 "cannot equip" marks of the shop list are not
  copied here because mode 2 filters those entries out.
open_questions:
- ?: whether the caller relies on the fifth word being pre-filled; both call sites do fill it before the call.
- ?: the exact comparison-group table layout at the pointer 0x14067FAE8.

name: sub_140288590
purpose:
Equips one item into a party slot: it validates the id, returns the old item to the inventory and writes the
masked id into the slot; for a one-handed weapon it may swap the two hand words.

behavior.text:
It masks the id with 0x3FF (the 0x3FF constant at 0x1402885B4, a 0x3FF mask at 0x1402885BD) and calls
  `sub_140288788` (0x1402885CB) to validate.

On a valid result it adds the old slot word to the inventory with `Inventory_AddCount` (0x14028861B) and,
  for a hand slot, adds the other hand word too (0x140288647) before clearing it (0x14028864C).
It writes the masked id to the slot (0x140288656); this is a plain id, never a flag.

For a hand slot with a two-handed weapon (`sub_140284998` at 0x140288674 returns non-zero) it swaps the two
  hand words (0x140288699/0x14028869E), so the primary hand keeps the two-handed item.
It calls `sub_140285A6C` to save every unit unless the unit index is 0x36 (the dummy).

This is the "equip now" path of the equip screen; it never sets bit 15, so a word written here is a
  committed word.

notes:
- V: The mask is applied before both the validate and the store; a flagged input word loses its flag here.
- V: The swap moves whole words; because the stored word is masked, no flag travels through it.
open_questions: - ?: whether the caller can pass a word with bit 15 here; the Outfitter uses `sub_1402D7280` for that case.

name: sub_140288788
purpose:
Validates whether a unit can equip an id in a slot and whether the other hand's weapon conflicts with it;
returns 1 for a legal pick, 0 for a legal-but-not-needed pick, and a negative value for a refusal.

behavior.text:
It rejects a non-existent unit through `Party_GetSlotState` and otherwise masks the id with 0x3FF
  (`a3 & 0x3FF` in the export) before `Item_CanUnitEquip`.

A zero id returns 1. A non-zero id goes through the equip check with the unit's job/level data
  (+36 and +115).

For a hand slot it inspects the other hand's word, masks it with 0x3FF, and applies the two-handed /
  dual-wield rules through `Item_GetWeaponRecord` bytes +1 (bits 1, 4 and 8).
It never reads or writes bit 15 of the incoming word: the mask removes it before any item lookup.

The function is the gate that keeps a flagged word from reaching `Item_CanUnitEquip`; the flag is removed
  by the mask, not by a test.

notes:
- V: The caller `sub_1402D7280` passes the candidate word with its bit 15 possibly set; this function sees only
  the low ten bits.
- V: The return value 1 is the "write the id" signal used by `sub_140288590` and `sub_1402D64CC`.
open_questions: - ?: the exact weapon-record bits (1, 4, 8) and the class of item each selects.

name: sub_1402888E8
proto: int sub_1402888E8(unsigned short unit, unsigned short job, int reequip)
purpose: Sets a party unit's job, returns the old equipment to the inventory and, when asked, equips the best available set for the new job.

behavior.text: the unit index selects the record in g_PartyUnits; the new job id is written to the 16-bit field at record offset 0x24.
when the job changes, the byte at record offset 0x177 is set to 0xFF.
that byte caches a job-dependent value, because it is invalidated exactly when the job id changes and is read again after the re-equip.

when the job id is not 0x5D and the unit is not the special index 0x36, the routine returns each of the five equipment words at record offsets 0x54 through 0x5C to the inventory with a +1 count, then zeroes the words (the loop starts at 0x54, steps by 2 and stops at 0x5E, so the fifth word is 0x5C).
it then rebuilds the unit with sub_140285A6C and sub_140288A24.

when the third argument is non-zero, it calls sub_1402875A4 to pick a new five-piece set, adds each chosen id to the inventory with +1, writes the chosen id into the equipment word and then removes one from the inventory.
the function always returns 1.
the add-then-remove pair around each chosen piece is a way to keep the inventory count consistent when the same id is both returned and re-equipped.
the special cases (job 0x5D, unit 0x36) are units whose equipment is not player-controlled, resting on the fact that they skip both the unequip and the re-equip.

notes:
- V: the five equipment words are returned to the inventory before the replacement set is chosen, so the picker can choose the same items again.
- V: the callers are the job-change preview and the job screen's apply step.
open_questions:
- ?: what the byte at record offset 0x177 caches.
- ?: why unit 0x36 is excluded; the index is outside the normal party range but its role was not traced.

name: sub_1402890C0
callers: Shop_BuildItemList, Inventory_BuildEquipList, ItemOrder_SyncGroup, sub_140286070, Item_CanUnitEquip and others
purpose: The menu group of an item from its category.

behavior.text: a chain of Item_IsInCategory(id & 0x3FF, c) for c = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (each also matches c + 7, the high categories): category 0 gives 0, 1 gives 5, 2 gives 1, 3 gives 2, 4 gives 3.
category 5 gives 4 and anything else 5 (the decompiler shows `v - (test != 0)` with v not resolved).

notes: - Proposed name: Item_MenuCategory.

name: sub_14028916C
proto: int sub_14028916C(unsigned short unit, int slot, unsigned short ability, int rearm)
callees: sub_140289320, sub_140285A6C, sub_140288A24, sub_1402875A4, Inventory_AddCount, sub_14031EEA8
purpose: Writes one word into a party unit's ability slots (primary skillset, secondary skillset, reaction, support, movement) and re-derives the unit's state, used by the Status screen's ability lists and the combat sets when the player changes one slot. (Corrected 2026-11-10: this sheet first called these words equipment slots; the equipment words are at +0x54.)

behavior.text: the unit index selects the record in g_PartyUnits and the slot selects one of the five 16-bit ability words at record offsets 0x5E onward (slot 1 = secondary +0x60, 2 = reaction +0x62, 3 = support +0x64, 4 = movement +0x66).
the word is stored exactly as the caller passes it; the callers strip the ability list's flag bits (0x800, 0x1000, 0x4000) first (sub_140333338's `& 0x3FF`).
when the record's byte at offset 0x177 is not 0xFF and the slot word differs from the id being stored, the byte is reset to 0xFF, which invalidates the cached value the byte holds.
the new word is stored in the slot unconditionally (no range or validity test).
the function then calls sub_140285A6C and sub_140288A24 to rebuild the unit's derived state.

depending on its fourth argument (set by the callers for supports that affect what the hands may hold, sub_14036771C), it calls sub_1402875A4 to pick a five-piece equipment set, moves each chosen id from the inventory into the unit with an inventory -1, and returns the previous item through Inventory_AddCount.
sub_140289320 and sub_14031EEA8 run on the paths where the set is rebuilt, and the function returns an integer status.
this is the single-slot counterpart of the job-change re-equip, because it writes one slot first and then asks the same picker to fill the rest.
the meaning of the status value and of the flag that selects the rebuild path.

notes:
- I: the slot words it writes are copied to the save row (+8..+13 for R/S/M) by PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave and back by PartyUnit_FillFromWork.

name: sub_14028A474
proto: __int64 __fastcall sub_14028A474(__int64 a1, __int16 a2, __int16 a3, __int64 a4, __int64 a5, int a6)
purpose: Builds a list of the first 24 ability slots of a party unit's job, tagging each id with display bits, in 9 modes selected by a6.

behavior.text: for each slot reads a learned flag (BitReader_ReadBits(1) or forced 1) and the id a1[2*i]; id 0 is skipped.
modes 0, 2 and 6 test the aux flags3 sign `byte_140787F83[8*id] >= 0` (0x14028A5F7, 0x14028A652, 0x14028A668); in mode 0 a clear sign sets token bit 0x4000, a set sign (not learned) gives 0x6000.
the sources of Ability_GetAuxRecord are used in mode 8 only: entries whose category is not 6..8 are kept.
modes 2 / 6 compare the unit's JP (word at +2*job+202) with Ability_GetJpCost and set 0x4000 when the JP is too low; modes 4 / 5 / 7 set 0x1000 for learned entries.
outputs 8-byte records at a5 (job in word 0, tagged id in word 1), terminated with 0xFFFF0000 except modes 3 and 8; returns the count.

the ability word of an 8-byte row gets 0x1000 (loaded at 0x14028A61B and 0x14028A62E, ORed at 0x14028A620 and 0x14028A633) or 0x6000 (ORed at 0x14028A678). No separate 0x4000 or 0x2000 immediate exists in this function: the 0x4000 half always arrives together with 0x2000 in the 0x6000 case.

notes: I: token bits 0x4000 (greyed), 0x2000 combined with 0x4000 (flags3-negative, not learned), 0x1000 (learned); flags3 bit 7 reads as a 'not learnable through JP' marker.

name: sub_14028A8B0
proto: int sub_14028A8B0(__int64 a1, int a2, uint64_t *list, int mode, char sort)
callees: JobList_BuildForPartyUnit, JobScreen_BuildJobTabRows, NxdEntry_GetRow, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, Party_GetUnitJobId, sub_140289F4C
purpose: Builds the ability list of a job-screen ability page for the selected party unit: the rows of the unit's own job plus the jobs 75..92, optionally sorted by a name-row order key.

behavior.text: it calls JobScreen_BuildJobTabRows for the unit's job id and then for job ids 75..92 (the loop runs 18 times, id = index + 74 for index 1..18); the ids of other jobs are never tried.

for modes 2, 4 and 6 (the test (mode - 2) & ~6 == 0 with mode 8 excluded) a job from the loop is built only when JobList_BuildForPartyUnit lists it for the unit; other modes build all 18. (Corrected 2026-11-11: this line first said modes 2, 3 and 9.)
every row's ability word (the word at row +2) is tested with sub_140289F4C(job word at party +36, word & 0x3FF), a ten-bit ability id.

when the sort flag is set, a bubble sort orders the rows by the sort_order column of the Ability row (table 39, int32 at row +0x34); 999999 when the row is missing or the value is 0; ties by ability id.
the rows are 8 bytes; the finished list copies one row per distinct run of the ability word at +2 and ends with a row whose +2 word is 0xFFFF; the function returns the count.

notes: 927 bytes read (read 2026-11-10). The value 0xFFFF is the list terminator the function writes (built from a register, not an immediate). The order key is the Ability column sort_order (+0x34), used only here.
open_questions: ? the meaning of the mode values for the callers.

name: sub_14028B180
proto: int sub_14028B180(int field, uint16_t id_a, uint16_t id_b, int order)
callers: sub_140285B10 (twice), sub_140286228, sub_1402875A4 (four calls), sub_140287D9C (four calls), sub_140396FEC (twice)
purpose:
Compares two item ids by one named record field and returns a signed ordering value. It is the single comparison used by
every item sort in the game.

behavior.text: masks both ids to ten bits before doing anything else.
obtains one key per id from the key helper, passing the field and the extra order argument through.
for most fields the result is the second key minus the first.

for three fields (the type, the id itself and the name-table key) the sign is inverted, so those fields sort the other
  way round.
field 2 has an extra rule: ids in one particular category are ranked before the others, independent of their keys.
field 9 compares the item names as byte strings, fetched from the item name table; equal strings compare equal.
it returns zero only when the chosen field cannot distinguish the two ids.
the inversion of three fields is deliberate and gives those fields the opposite order to the rest.
the exact intent of the field-2 category exception.

name: sub_14028B354
proto: int sub_14028B354(int id, int field, int order)
callees: Item_GetRecord, Item_GetWeaponRecord, Item_GetShieldRecord, Item_GetAccessoryRecord, Item_CountTotal, sub_140285A98, Item_IsInCategory, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow
purpose: Produces the numeric sort key of one item for one field. The comparator calls it twice per comparison, once per id.

behavior.text: field 0 returns the equip type byte of the item record, with one type value remapped to a larger number.
field 1 returns the price word of the item record.
field 2 returns a sub-record byte chosen by the item's menu category.

field 3 returns a byte of the equipment sub-record: the weapon record's fifth byte for weapons, the shield or accessory
  record's first byte otherwise, and zero when the id fits neither.
field 4 returns the shield or accessory record's second byte and zero for weapons.
field 5 returns the owned-plus-equipped count of the id.
field 10 returns the id itself.
field 11 returns one when the extra order argument equals the id and zero otherwise.

field 12 returns the dword at row +0x28 of the item's name-table row (column sort_order), and a large constant when the row is missing; none of the eight field lists at 0x14067FAB0 (read in the caller sub_14028B180, not in this body) contains field 12.
fields 6, 7, 8 and 9 have no case and return zero; field 9 is handled inside the comparator instead.
the pair of equipment bytes (fields 3 and 4) is what the equip screen sorts by when it orders gear within a category.
which screen sorts by field 12 (no field list names it).

name: sub_14028B510
purpose: Marks the items sold in any open shop.

behavior.text: walks item ids 0..; an item whose record +10 is not above event variable 111 is checked against every shop (sub_1401DF5B4 says which shops are open) with the same mask test.
the mask is two bytes per item at 0x14067F890 + 2 * id (high byte first).

name: sub_14029554C
purpose: Pure this-adjusting thunk: forwards (a1 + 16, a2, a3) to sub_1402AB5B0, the gadget event dispatcher. Stored in the vtables of UIGadgetFFTOVScrollText, UIGadgetFFTOUnitEquipSetDetailShop and UIGadgetFFTOUnitEquipSetDetail at slot 2 (the second base's copy).

behavior.text: the whole body is `return sub_1402AB5B0(a1 + 16, a2, a3)`.

, read for context): switches on the dword at event+0. 0x1B calls gadget virtual +64 (gadget, node, event, 0); 0x1C and 0x1E look up the child node with id event[1] (sub_14040C270) and, when its kind (+536) is 10, call virtual +32 / +56 (gadget, child, id); 0x20 and 0x21 call virtual +40 / +48 (gadget, node, node+648). Any other code does nothing.

the event codes are the GUIOwners_PostEvent codes (19 = cursor over, 20 = cursor out are posted by GUIComponent_OnFocusGained / OnFocusLost); 0x1C / 0x1E / 0x20 / 0x21 were not matched to a producer here.

name: sub_14029643C
purpose: Fills one row of a multi-column item list, choosing the row filler by a kind argument.

behavior.text: takes a context, a row source object, a row record, a row index and a kind on the stack.
kind 1 selects a per-row entry at the row record plus 0x140 plus 0x58 times the index.

for that entry it calls one of two fillers depending on a byte in the entry, then optionally writes a value into a node from a
  looked-up row.
kind 0, the other branch, calls ItemCell_SetItem with the row's item id, which sets the small picture and the name.
any other kind returns without filling.
three direct call sites, all in one list-refresh function.
the list is a shop or inventory list with several columns, because the filler is chosen per column kind.

name: sub_14029BCD4
proto: unsigned __int8 sub_14029BCD4(__int64 unused, IconSlot *slot, unsigned int *iconRec, char skipStates)

callees: UIName_Key, GUINode_StopState, sub_140409824 (play state at frame), sub_1403D8D1C (release key), GuiImage_SetIconById
purpose: Shows or hides one icon image slot and sets its icon by id: plays the node's Show / Hide state and, when the icon is shown, calls GuiImage_SetIconById.

behavior.text: slot (a2): qword +0 = the slot's GUI node (nothing happens when it is 0), +8 = embedded GuiImage object, +32 = pointer to a second slot-like record, +136 = dword (previous icon id), +144 = byte 'shown'. iconRec (a3): dword +0 = icon id, byte +4 = 'hide' flag. a4 = skipStates.
new shown = (iconRec.id > 0 and iconRec[4] == 0); the old byte is kept in v6 and slot+144 = new shown.

stops the OPPOSITE state (shown -> 'Hide', else 'Show' via UIName_Key + GUINode_StopState, key released with sub_1403D8D1C) and then plays the wanted one with sub_140409824(node, key, -1), i.e. at its last frame (instant, see sub_140409824 note in sub_1402A91E4).

GuiImage_SetIconById(slot+8, iconRec.id, 0, 1). If the slot was hidden before and is shown now and slot+32 is non-null, byte (slot+32)+144 = (slot+136 == iconRec.id) - i.e. the paired record is marked 'same icon as before' only on a hidden -> shown edge.
the return value is the last call's result and is meaningless to callers.

notes: Name kept as sub_ (the role of the slot class is not known). The job detail window feeds it the job icon record (icon id dword at record +92, hide byte at +96).

name: sub_1402A291C

name: sub_1402A3470
purpose: Clears both list pages of a double-buffered list gadget: calls sub_14028D7BC(list, 0) twice and swaps the two page pointers at a1+56 / a1+64 after each call.

behavior.text: loop of two iterations: sub_14028D7BC(a1 + 32, 0); then if both qwords a1+56 and a1+64 are non-null they are exchanged. Two exchanges restore the original assignment, so the net effect is that BOTH list nodes are cleared and the pointers end where they started.

, read for context): list node = *(list + 24) = a1 + 56. Sets list +96 = -1, node+416 = (count > 0), sub_14040CA1C(node, count) (stores count at node+648, resets +672, rebuilds, sets +684/+685 = 1), and for count == 0 with list+104 >= 0 also resets the cursor (list+104 = -1, sub_14028F320), then refreshes the node (sub_14040C8B0 / sub_14040C92C / sub_14040CA50 / sub_14040CB60) and sub_14028F404, sub_14028DCA4.

name: sub_1402A6710
callees: GUINode_FindPartByName, GUITextNode_SetTextExpandedTemp, Item_GetRecord, Item_MenuCategory, SceneVar_Read, ShopItemList_FillRow, and 17 more
purpose: Refreshes one possession or shop panel row: it resolves the entry in the third argument either as an item id or as a UI table row and fills the row's icon, name and grey-out state.

behavior.text: it builds a 512-byte work area and then processes the entry at a3.
the first dword of the entry (`*(int *)a3`) is compared with 261 at `0x1402A69CE`; below it the entry is an item id, at or above it a UI table 0xEC row.
the item branch calls `Item_GetRecord(*(unsigned __int16 *)a3)` and uses record byte +0xA (>= 0x14) for the grey-out state; the 4-byte entry is read as a word by the record accessor.
the item id and the table row share the dword; the comparison is a discriminator, not a width bound on a packed word.
the row fill then calls `ShopItemList_FillRow` and sets the "GrayOutPossession" state from the count and the scene variable 44.
the dword is written by the shop list builder; the accessor reads only its low word.
the function is shared by the shop and possession panels, which is why the entry can be either kind.
which producer writes an entry at or above 261.

the row label is text line 2098, or 2099 when the item record's byte +10 (for an item id below 261) is 0x14 or more or the PoachItem row byte +0x36 (column notice_mark) is non-zero; the PoachItem row is the one of the entry dword +24; it calls PoachRow_SetMonsterIcon for the icon.
