purpose: Returns the 3-byte usable-item sub-record (I: formula, amount, status record index into the 6-byte table at 0x14080FBA0), or null when the item is not of this kind.

behavior.text: calls Item_CategoryFirstId(id) and computes index = id - that first id (16-bit); then calls Item_FindCategoryIndex(id) again; -1 returns 0.

kind = g_ItemCategoryType[category]; kinds 4 and 9 select the tables 0x14080FB70 (ids 0xF0..0xFF; 0xFE and 0xFF are never reached) and 0x14067277C (kind 9 is unreachable); element size 3, index = id - first id of the kind; any other kind returns null.
relies on the callees leaving r9 and r10 untouched (it keeps the id in r9 and the index in r10 across both calls); the stock callees only touch rax, rcx, rdx and r8.

notes: - Proposed name: Item_GetChemistRecord. The two tables of each accessor are separate arrays (the high one serves the ids above 0xFF).

name: sub_1402BAB78
proto: void sub_1402BAB78(int64_t a1, int64_t a2, int64_t a3)
purpose: Applies the pending music request: starts the requested track, stops the current one, and runs the pending fade.

behavior.text: the request state is 16 bytes at 0x140D3A900 (sound id, then the three dwords of the music slot record); a request of -999 stops the channel; -998 and -997 clear the state; -1 means none.
for another id it calls EventMusic_LoadTrack(sound object, channel 8, id - 1), copies the id and the three record dwords to the current-track block at 0x140D3A8E0 and clears the request.
when the current track id is 99 and the channel is no longer busy the channel is stopped (the compare at 0x1402BAB8C).
nothing reads the three record dwords after this copy (census of 0x140D3A8E0..0x140D3A91F, 39 operands).

notes: The track file is named from the id, not looked up. 0x140D3A91F in the last bullet is the end of the censused range, not an address this function uses.
open_questions: What the record dwords were for (a data offset in the original game: value_a is always 1024 x n - 64).

name: sub_1402BBBCC
proto: char __fastcall sub_1402BBBCC(__int64 a1, __int64 a2, __int64 a3, __int64 a4)
callers: not in the exported set; the equip screen's confirm handler
purpose:
The equip screen's confirm/refresh path. On the confirm message it toggles the unit's locked byte, saves the
unit, then copies record +0x30..+0x6F into the panel block and renders.

behavior.text: On message 1008 it reads and toggles the unit's +0x174 byte and calls `PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave` (0x1402BBEE7).

It then copies the record's first 0x30 bytes to the 0x1407B27xx fields, record +0x30..+0x6F to
  `xmmword_141876E90` (0x1402BBF68..0x1402BBF90), and record +0x70 onward to the 0x141876C80 region.

The block copy is raw; the hand words at record +0x54..+0x5C land at block +0x24..+0x2C and reach the
  renderers and the panel task with their flags.
It calls `sub_1402C17F4`/`sub_1402C19EC` on the block to render the equip screen.

Because the save write happens before the block copy, a flagged word would reach both the save and the
  panel; the only guard is the earlier commit strip.
the same copy into the preview record at 0x141876C10 from the selected party unit (g_PartyUnits[g_SelectedUnitIndex] + 112).

notes: V: on the confirm message it calls PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave (0x1402BBEE7) before copying record +0x30..+0x6F to the panel block; a flagged word would reach both the save and the block.
open_questions: - ?: the exact message ids around 1008 and whether the save write can be interrupted before the strip.

name: sub_1402C0554
proto: void sub_1402C0554(int slot, int16_t *row_out, int16_t *scroll_out, uint16_t *list)
callers: JobScreen_FillUnitRows, JobScreen_BuildLearnList, JobScreen_RefreshLearnList, sub_140333974, sub_140366FE0, sub_14036A9D8
purpose: Restores a list's cursor when the list is built again: it reads the list's saved entry (row, scroll, word) from the table at word_143760800 and puts the cursor back on the row that holds the saved word.

behavior.text: the saved entry is three words at word_143760800 + 6 * slot: the row, the scroll position and the word that row held; the row goes to the first output and the scroll to the second.
it counts the 0xFFFF terminators in the list's rows before the saved row; when the word at the saved row equals the saved word and no terminator came before it, the saved row and scroll stay.

otherwise it scans the list from row 0 to the first 0xFFFF and stops at the first word that, masked with 0x3FF, equals the saved word: that row is the result. With no match both outputs are 0 (the top of the list).
the saved word and the word at the saved row are read sign-extended (movsx); the scanned words are read zero-extended.

notes:
- V: the slots seen: 9 = the Change Job list (JobScreen_FillUnitRows); 10 + the tab = the Learn Abilities list; sub_140366FE0 uses 4 + its tab byte; the shop list uses g_ShopOrderGroup; sub_140333974 uses its own slot from its caller.
- V: the savers store the word masked: JobScreen_FillUnitRows, JobScreen_BuildLearnList, JobScreen_RefreshLearnList, sub_140333974 and sub_140366FE0 each store list word & mask into the entry's third word.
- sub_14033DDFC is the same code for the unit-pointer screens, with its own table.
open_questions: - ?: which slot numbers the remaining screens use (the table holds at least 14 entries).

name: sub_1402C1628
proto: int64 sub_1402C1628(uint8_t *out, const uint8_t *header, const int16_t *middle, const uint8_t *block, int sceneUnit)
purpose: Fills a unit's stat summary from a party record handed over in the same three copied parts as sub_1402C185C.

behavior.text: out +0 = sub_1402C17F4(header, middle, block); out +8 from the header (sub_14036099C or sub_1402C064C by a scene flag); out +4 from nxd table 274's row for the block's byte +2 (the record's +114, the marker); the stat words from the middle part; out +80 = the dword at save record +560 of the slot at header + 10 (dword_1411A7F40, 600-byte stride), or the scene unit's +560 in four scenes; out +92 = the header's job word.
the save-record read by header + 10 is the second proof that the header's +10 is the save slot (+44).
callers: sub_1402C19EC, sub_140333FE0, sub_140336444, JobChange_FillUnitEntry, sub_14036C320 (several pass party record 54's copies).

the 5th argument (on the stack) is a scene unit id: in scenes 21, 43, 44 and 51 out +80 is read from SceneUnit_EntryById(id) + 560 with no null test, so an id above 15 faults (access violation at 0x1402C178B; one caller is the Warriors' Guild candidate page). A negative id takes the save-record path.
sub_1402C19EC passes the dword at its object's +180 (read with +176 through sub_1400ECEE4).

open_questions: ? whether sub_1402C17F4 reads per-job entries from the block.

name: sub_1402C185C
proto: int64 sub_1402C185C(uint8_t *out, const uint8_t *header, const int16_t *middle, const uint8_t *block)
purpose: Builds a unit's detail panel (job line, icon, equipment, ability names) from a party record handed over in three copied parts.

behavior.text: the record arrives in parts: `header` = the party record's +34..+47 (its +2 is the job word +36, its +10 the save slot +44), `middle` = from +48, `block` = from +112 (unlock mask, learned bits, levels, JP). Every writer of the header buffer qword_1407B2758 fills it from +0x22, +0x2A and +0x2E (sub_1402BBBCC, JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange, PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment); sub_1403783F0 writes a header of its own.

the job line goes through JobRecord_FromJobId with a key whose pointers are block + 77 (levels), + 90 (JP) and + 136 (total JP), the job word from the header; then the icon and generic flag (JobRecord_FillIconAndGenericFlag; markers 0x80 / 0x81 use job 74, 0x82 the header's job), five equipment words from the middle part, five ability names (sub_1400FB8E4), and sub_1402C17F4(header, middle, block).
callers: sub_1402C19EC (passes its own three parts on), sub_140333FE0 (the preview record at 0x141876C10 with the header buffer), sub_14036BBFC (the Fitting screen: stack copies of party record 54).
a stack copy of the block belongs to no record.

notes: Found by a census re-check (sub_14036BBFC's copy) and confirmed live.

name: sub_1402C20F0
proto: int __fastcall sub_1402C20F0(__int64 panel, __int16 unit, int case_id)
callers: not in the exported set; an equip change controller
purpose:
Applies an item id to the first slot that does not already hold it and updates the equip block and the stat
readout.

behavior.text:
Case 1 finds the slot by raw word equality (`*(u16*)(unit+2*slot+0x54) != id`, 0x1402C20F0 case 1); when
  the item is already equipped it marks the panel byte and returns.

Otherwise it copies the unit to the scratch record (`sub_140289894`), picks a slot with `sub_140288D68`,
  applies the id through `sub_140288590` (masked), then copies the scratch hand words to `g_EquipCandidates`:
  four with a qword move (0x1402C241F) and the fifth with a word (0x1402C242C).

It calls `sub_140287354` with `g_EquipSet` and the candidates, then reads the block's stat words at
  +0x06/+0x12/+0x1C and +0x58/+0x62 for the panel cells.
The raw compare at the first step means a bit-15 word is not seen as the same id.
This is the equip screen's "change one item" path; it writes a committed id, not a flag.

notes: V: finds the slot by raw word comparison (0x1402C20F0 case 1), applies the id through sub_140288590 (masked), then copies the scratch hand words to the candidate array (0x1402C241F-0x1402C242C).
open_questions: - ?: whether the raw compare is intended to treat a pending purchase as "not equipped".

name: sub_1402C4D1C
purpose: One of the battle unit panel builders: it fills the panel rows for a unit's equipment from the unit's item slots.

behavior.text: It walks the unit's equipment slots and masks each id to nine bits before the item record lookup.
A slot word equal to 255 is treated as empty and draws no row.
The record's category byte decides which icon and which sub-record the row uses.
It calls seven helpers, including the record and weapon accessors, and has one direct caller.
The nine-bit mask is the panel convention shared with the other four panel builders; the record accessor itself accepts a full 16-bit id.

name: sub_1402C53F0
callers: EventMode_DispatchTask (as a task, no direct call)
purpose: Run as a task by EventMode_DispatchTask; the part read picks the top unit of the placed party for a result page.

behavior.text: picks, among records 16..20 with a slot byte other than 0xFF, the one with the highest score in the battle controller's per-record score array (from +693460) and passes its record index and display name to sub_1400EB048.
text id 2698 when scene variable 39 is 325, else 2655.

notes: Only the top-unit part was read.

name: sub_1402C60E4
purpose: Reconciles a unit's equipment words with the inventory: every equipped item is counted, duplicates beyond the cap are sold, and the unit's slots are cleared afterwards.

behavior.text: It walks the 54 party units and the five hand words of each one.
A word equal to 255 is skipped as empty; anything else is tested against the 261 bound before use.
For an accepted id it asks the owned-and-equipped counter whether the party already has 100 or more, and sells the excess through the record price when it does.
Otherwise it increments the inventory count of that id by one.
After each unit it writes 255 into a per-unit byte slot in a 600-byte-stride array and calls a helper that finishes the unit's equipment pass.
It carries four separate 255 sentinel loads and one 255 byte store, because each pass over the slots re-establishes the empty value.

for each of the 54 roster records in use it searches battle records 0..20 (not only the placed range 16..20) for one whose +2 is the roster index, whose +0x1B5 is not 0xFF and whose +401 is not 0, and works on the pair (ScenePreview_FindEntry of +401); see the behaviour PartyResultsAreFoundBySaveIndexInAllRecords.
The per-unit byte slot is some kind of equipment-changed or equipped-count marker, but the field it belongs to was not pinned.

notes: - I: Read the equipment loop and the sale branch; the per-unit tail call was not identified.
open_questions: - ?: What does the 600-byte-stride byte slot at the end of each unit pass hold?

name: sub_1402C6514
callees: Resource_GetSlotObject, SceneVar_Read, SceneTask_Terminate, sub_1402C59C4, sub_1401DB4E4, SceneTask_FindFree, SceneTask_Start, sub_1402C52F0, sub_1401D1F28, UIName_Key, GUINode_FindDescendant, UIName_ReleaseKey, sub_1400F71E8, sub_1402B20C0, sub_1400EB5F4, sub_1400F4BCC, sub_140103C50, sub_1402CBCA0, sub_140291490, PreviewUnit_BuildSpriteRecord, CharaRender_RegisterSlot, sub_1400EB0A4, sub_1400EB174, GUINode_FindState, SceneTask_WaitFrame, sub_1400D6DAC, Input_TestAction, sub_1401FA5F0, sub_140214134, memcpy, sub_1401EDD50, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_1401EC278, sub_1403D4534, Str_Format, sub_1402C3570, sub_1401E8B7C, sub_14021E7FC, GUIWidget_FindFirstKind1Component2, GUINode_PlayState, sub_1401DB508, sub_1402F7F4C, sub_14041FAE0
purpose: One of the scene-task bodies event opcode 0x78 starts (mode 5): it places the units of the scene, shows their speech balloons and unit markers, and runs until the task is stopped.

behavior.text: the event opcode 0x78 dispatcher starts this body for mode 5, in the same way it starts the other mode bodies.
it obtains the scene resource slot through Resource_GetSlotObject and reads the scene variables it needs with SceneVar_Read.
unit preview sprites are built with PreviewUnit_BuildSpriteRecord and registered with CharaRender_RegisterSlot.
the UI node states it drives are named Show, Hide, ShowBalloon, ShowUnit and HideUnit; the strings are the node state names the widget looks up.
the message text id is written into the shared text slot and the balloon is played through the UI state machine.
it creates the scene task with SceneTask_Start, waits each frame with SceneTask_WaitFrame and ends with SceneTask_Terminate.
the function has no direct caller; the mode dispatcher reaches it as a task entry.
the body is a dialogue/balloon scene task, because the nodes it drives are the balloon and unit markers and it copies the shared text slot.
which event opcode argument selects mode 5; the dispatcher owns that switch.

notes: Whole function read (3376 bytes). The node-state names are string operands in the body; the mode number is the one the event dispatcher documents.

name: sub_1402C72B8
callees: Resource_GetSlotObject, sub_1402C5D68, SceneTask_Terminate, SceneTask_WaitFrame, sub_1401DB4E4, SceneTask_FindFree, SceneTask_Start, sub_1402C52F0, sub_1401D1F28, UIName_Key, GUINode_FindDescendant, UIName_ReleaseKey, sub_1400F71E8, sub_1402B20C0, sub_1400F4BCC, sub_140103C50, sub_1402CBCA0, sub_140291490, PreviewUnit_BuildSpriteRecord, CharaRender_RegisterSlot, sub_1400EB228, sub_1400EB2F8, sub_140142EDC, sub_1402C7244, sub_1401FA5F0, sub_140214134, memcpy, sub_1401EDD50, NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_1401EC278, sub_1403D4534, Str_Format, sub_1402C3570, sub_1401E8B7C, sub_14021E7FC, GUIWidget_FindFirstKind1Component2, GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState, sub_1400EB5F4, sub_1402F7F4C, sub_14041FAE0
purpose: One of the scene-task bodies event opcode 0x78 starts (mode 6): a unit-display scene that also drives the desertion marker, built on the same balloon and unit-marker task skeleton as mode 5.

behavior.text: the event opcode 0x78 dispatcher starts this body for mode 6, in the same way it starts the other mode bodies.
it shares the scene setup with the mode 5 body: resource slot, scene variables, preview sprite records and CharaRender slots.
the node states it drives include Show, Hide, ShowBalloon, ShowUnit, HideUnit and ShowDesertion.
the extra desertion state is the only node name that does not appear in the mode 5 body.
it waits with SceneTask_WaitFrame and ends with SceneTask_Terminate, like the other mode bodies.
it has no direct caller; the mode dispatcher reaches it as a task entry.
the desertion marker makes this the scene body used when a unit leaves the party or the battle, which is why the skeleton is shared with the balloon task.
what sub_1402C5D68 and sub_1402C7244 prepare before the nodes are played; neither was decoded.

notes: Whole function read (2802 bytes). The ShowDesertion state name is the distinguishing string.

name: sub_1402C8010
purpose: Sells the equipment a unit owns beyond the 99-per-item cap, the equip-side twin of the inventory overflow pass.

behavior.text: The unit index argument is accepted only up to 20, which matches the 21 battle unit records rather than the 54 party units.
It walks the unit's five equipment slots and skips a slot holding 255.
An id above the 261 bound is skipped as well.
For a valid id it asks the owned-and-equipped counter for the total; at 100 or more it resolves the record and sells the excess.
It calls four helpers and has two direct callers.
The 21-unit limit and the battle record layout say this runs on the battle copy, not the roster copy.

name: sub_1402C80D8
purpose: Counts the copies of an item a unit has equipped, used by the equip screens to show whether another copy is available.

behavior.text: It walks the unit's equipment words and masks each one to nine bits for the record lookup.
A word equal to 255 is skipped; three separate sentinel loads re-establish that value across the loops.
The count it returns is the number of matching slots, not a boolean.
It calls fourteen helpers and has one direct caller.
The walk covers the roster record's seven equipment words, while the battle record exposes only five hand slots.

name: sub_1402C9F78
purpose: Takes a snapshot of the inventory counts that the battle code reads while the item menu is open.

behavior.text: It clears a global dword, calls a helper on a global buffer and then walks the inventory.
Each item id is masked to nine bits before the record lookup that decides whether the id is listed.
The buffer it fills is the inventory snapshot the battle code reads, because the only other writer of that buffer is the equip-snapshot function.
It calls five helpers and has one direct caller.
The snapshot exists so that the battle item list does not change while the player is browsing it.

name: sub_1402CCEE0
callees: EventVar_Read, EventVar_Write, sub_140340FD0, Party_EggUpkeep, sub_14015B578, sub_14041EF2C
purpose: Checks the errand state on a world tick: it reads the active errand slots and their delay bytes, ages the eggs, and posts the result message when an errand is due.

behavior.text: it reads and writes the errand delay array at 0x1411A7140 (96 bytes, one per errand) and the active slot records g_ErrandActive (the body holds rbx = 0x1411A71A2, the base+2, and indexes -2/+1/+3 from it).

one calendar day: event variables 46 / 47 (month, day) advance; each active slot without flag 0x04 gets now_day + 1 and, at max_day (or with flag 0x02), flag 0x04 and sub_140340FD0(its town) for a dispatch that was not called off; the low 6 bits of every g_ErrandDelay byte count down (min(d, 32) - 1).
the 64 day counters at 0x1411A7220 (index 0 for the date in event variables 95 / 96, the others for the dates of byte_1407B8130) count up to 99 on their date; they are not errand finish days.
Party_EggUpkeep is called as part of the same tick, so the egg counters age with the errands.
the message is posted through sub_14015B578, which builds a parameterised text message; sub_1402CD168 is reached from there.
EventVar_Read and EventVar_Write carry the current day and the story progress the errand rules use.
the function returns without a value and does not start a task.
this is the world-map errand tick, because the only caller is the world update and the state it touches is the errand delay/active block.
whether an errand whose delay has not elapsed is skipped or only logged; the branch count was not decoded.

notes: Whole function read (648 bytes).

name: sub_1402CD168
callers: sub_14015B578, sub_1401C6720, sub_1401C6C4C, SaveWork_PackFromLive, Party_EggUpkeep, Errand_IsAvailable, SaveHeader_FillBattleFields, sub_140343110, sub_140371CAC, sub_140374484, sub_140378FA4, sub_140379180
purpose: Posts a parameterised UI message from a kind and a value, after checking both against the small pair table the message system accepts.

behavior.text: the first argument points at the kind dword and the second at the value dword.
the kind must be 1 through 12 and the value 1 through 30; anything outside returns without posting.
the pair is looked up in the byte table at 0x140681010, which maps a kind to its accepted value range.
the kind is converted through a table walk and the value is compared with the selected range.
sub_1401D80A8 receives the resolved pair as a UI message.
the routine is used by the save header, the errand results and several scene screens, so it is the common message poster.
the 12 by 30 pair space is a message-kind registry rather than free text, because the value is range-checked per kind.
what each kind means; the table entries were not named.

notes: Whole function read (267 bytes). The two bounds and the pair table are the whole validation.

name: sub_1402CEEE8
purpose: The checkpoint writer: it builds a fresh work copy of the party, stores it in the checkpoint copy, and then overwrites the checkpoint copy's unit area and many other fields with the live state, so the checkpoint holds the live records and not what the pack produced.

behavior.text: takes no argument. Points the save work pointer (Src) at g_SaveWorkCurrent (0x142C81C80), fills the 0x9CE4 bytes (40,164, one slot record) with the byte -1 (all bits set), calls UnitWork_BuildForSlot(0) and SaveWork_PackFromParty(0).
copies the 0x9CE4-byte work copy to g_SaveCheckpointCopy (0x142E80450) with one memmove.

calls `sub_1402CD788` with section pointers inside the checkpoint block (0x142E898B0 and further addresses up to 0x142E8A12C) to store the world / campaign half; I: that is what the name of its restore twin sub_1402CD9D8 (called by sub_1402CF768) suggests.

then copies many live fields into the checkpoint block by fixed offsets: scalar and 16-byte copies from the live area around 0x1411A7030..0x1411A7270 and 0x1411A7560 (two rounds of 128 bytes plus 24) to 0x142E80608..0x142E8095D.

copies 0x7E90 bytes (54 unit records of 600) from g_UnitSaveData (0x1411A7D10) to 0x142E80968 with a memmove. 0x142E80968 - 0x142E80450 = 0x518, which is the unit area offset inside a slot record (arithmetic of the two addresses; the pack code writes the units at work copy + 1304, the same number, in SaveWork_PackFromLive), so this write lands exactly on the unit area of the checkpoint's slot record.

copies the inventory counts (261 bytes from g_InventoryCounts) to 0x142E887F8 and the Poachers' Den stock (261 bytes from g_PoachersDenStock) to 0x142E888FD, 128 bytes from 0x1411A7680 to 0x142E88A02, 1,024 bytes (eight rounds of 128) from the event variable store behind off_1407830D8 to 0x142E88A84, a run of scalar and block copies from a run of globals in the 0x1407B2xxx range to 0x142E88E84..0x142E890CC, and the item-new flags (g_ItemNewFlags, 0x1411A7810) to 0x142E894BE.

consequence for any hook on the pack step: whatever a hook on SaveWork_PackFromLive or SaveWork_PackFromParty changed in the unit area of the work copy (job bytes, spare bytes) is in the checkpoint copy only until the live-record memmove of this function overwrites it; the checkpoint copy then holds the live records. See the behaviour CheckpointCopyHoldsTheLiveUnitRecords.

the one caller sub_1402B8690 calls it when event variable 508 reads 0 and the byte at +100 of g_GlobalWork is 0, and then sets the low dword of a state word (in the caller, not in this function) to 3; sub_1402B8690 has thirteen callers in the event and scene code (sub_140246078 and others). I: so the checkpoint is captured from scene-change and event paths, not on a save-menu action; the trigger of each caller was not read.
what the group copies from that 0x1407B2xxx range are (names of those globals were not studied).

notes: Whole function read (decompiled in IDA, 2026-11-09), rewritten from scratch: the earlier sheet described item order lists of 282, 60, 76, 68, 42 and 1010 bytes and a callee `sub_140284F6C`, which this body does not contain. The restore twin is sub_1402CF768, which copies the checkpoint's unit area back to g_UnitSaveData.
open_questions: ? which caller of sub_1402B8690 fires the capture in a battle; ? the scalar groups from that 0x1407B2xxx range.

name: sub_1402CF768
purpose:
The reverse of the slot-record builder: it takes the work copy and writes its sections back into live state, including the
ten item order lists.

behavior.text: passes an incoming register through to its first helper together with the value 1, so it does take at least one argument.
then calls one routine with five section pointers taken from globals.
that routine restores the world/campaign half of the record, resting on its name and the section pointers.

writes the five item order lists back into their live arrays one at a time, and the whole equipment block in one move,
  in the opposite direction from the builder.
the six copies have the same sizes as on the save side: 282, 60, 76, 68, 42 and 1010 bytes.
the live arrays it writes are the same ones the manual save unpacker writes, so both restore paths agree.
the three callers are load-related paths (their names are not informative), which fits a restore.
the prototype; only the first argument is forwarded in the head.
which of the three callers corresponds to the title-screen load and which to an in-game reload.

name: sub_1402D57C0
callers: none direct; called through the screen table pointer at 0x140680A70
purpose:
The Outfitter entry handler: it prepares and calls the menu function at 0x1402BE7E8, then runs the per-frame
dispatcher.

behavior.text:
It sets up a small stack message (two dword -1, a byte 0, the input word and the menu word) and calls
  `sub_1402BE7E8` with it (0x1402D5809).
It tail-calls `sub_1402D6F10` (0x1402D5812), which dispatches on the current menu id.
The first call arms the screen; the second runs the frame. No equipment word is read or written here.

notes: - V: The function is reached only through the screen table; there is no direct call in the census.

name: sub_1402D5818
callers: none direct; called through the screen table pointer at 0x140680A78
purpose: A second Outfitter entry handler; it only clears the entry byte once and runs the per-frame dispatcher.

behavior.text: On the first call it clears `byte_143CDA8C4` and sets `byte_14184A646` (0x1402D5821/0x1402D5828).
It tail-calls `sub_1402D6F10` (0x1402D582F).
This is the "return to the screen without rebuilding the task" entry; it does not touch equipment.

notes: - V: No direct caller; the table at 0x140680A78 is its only entry.
open_questions: - ?: which screen state selects this entry instead of sub_1402D57C0.

name: sub_1402D58EC
callers: none direct; called through the screen table pointer at 0x140680A88
purpose:
The Outfitter slot-list handler: it tracks the selected slot, shows its help id, and on confirm either undoes
a pending bit-15 purchase or opens the equip-change preview for the slot.

behavior.text:
It reads the selected slot word at unit +0x54 + 2*slot, masks it with 0x3FF for the help token
  (a 0x3FF mask at 0x1402D59E6) and stores 0x6800 + id in `g_HelpIdSlot`.

On the confirm input it tests the word against 0x8000 (a comparison with 0x8000 at 0x1402D5A6C): a word below it
  sets UI state 5 and does nothing; a word at or above it is treated as a pending purchase.

For the pending word it subtracts its masked price from `dword_143D1AC68`, calls `sub_1402D64CC` to
  restore the override (0x1402D5A90), calls `PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment` (0x1402D5A95) and sets UI state 7.

When the selected slot changes it re-reads the word, tests it against 0x8000 again (a comparison with 0x8000 at
  0x1402D5ACD), and either closes the preview (below 0x8000) or opens it by calling `sub_140286DDC` with
  `g_EquipSet` (0x1402D5B00), the unit's record copy and the override word (0x1402D5AF7).

It updates the help panel (`sub_140328F0C`) and the cursor word at 0x143CDA8C2; it ends with the price
  delta helper `sub_1402D5854` when `byte_140D408E3` is set.

The two 0x8000 tests are the same session flag at two moments: the first is the confirm/undo action, the
  second is the preview switch when the cursor moves.

notes: V: the slot navigation/undo handler. Two unsigned 0x8000 tests (0x1402D5A6C, 0x1402D5ACD); confirming a bit-15 word removes its price and restores the override.
open_questions: - ?: the exact UI states 5 and 7 (the byte names are the stock constants; their screen meaning was not read).

name: sub_1402D5B50
callers: none direct; called through the screen table pointer at 0x140680AA0
purpose: The Outfitter's per-frame update entry: it clears a one-shot byte and calls the dispatcher.

behavior.text: On the first call it clears `byte_143D1AC6F` and sets `byte_14184A64C` (0x1402D5B60/0x1402D5B66).
It tail-calls `sub_1402D6F10` (0x1402D5B6B).
This is the update wrapper used while the screen is open; it writes no equipment word.

notes: - V: No direct caller in the census.
open_questions: - ?: the difference between this entry and sub_1402D5818.

name: sub_1402D5B6C
purpose:
The Outfitter cancel/restore: for every party unit and every one of its five equipment words, it puts the
override word back when the live word is flagged or when an override exists, then clears the override.

behavior.text:
It walks `g_PartyCount` units and five words per unit (unit +0x54..+0x5C) and the parallel
  `g_UnitEquipOverride` entry at 0x14184A680.

The replacement condition is `unit_word >= 0x4000` or `override_word != 0`; the constant 0x4000 is loaded
  at 0x1402D5B9E and compared at 0x1402D5BA6. So a word with bit 14 or bit 15 set is always replaced, even
  when the override is zero.

The replacement copies the whole 16-bit override word (a zero-extending read of the override word at 0x1402D5BB2, store at
  0x1402D5BB5), then clears the override (a store that clears the override at 0x1402D5BBA).

The function makes the session disappear: a pending word is dropped and the original word (or empty) is
  restored. It is the cancel counterpart of the commit strip.

notes:
- V: It does not mask with 0x3FF: the restore is a whole-word copy, so a bit-14 override survives if one was
  stored.
- V: It is called from the cancel branches of `sub_1402D6914` and `sub_1402D6E14`; the two call sites are the
  only direct calls.
open_questions: - ?: whether a bit-14 word can be in a unit slot when this runs; no stock writer sets one there.

name: sub_1402D5CC4
callers: none direct; called through the screen table pointer at 0x140680A80
purpose:
Opens the Outfitter's equipment-change state: it backs up the selected unit's four editable hand words, builds
the five candidate words from the shop list, refreshes the panel block, and on the leave message applies the
candidates to the unit and charges their prices.

behavior.text:
On the first pass it saves the four words at unit +0x54..+0x5A to an 8-byte stack slot with
  `sub_1402D7584(&v26,0,0)` (0x1402D5D75), builds the candidates with `sub_140287D9C` (0x1402D5D84), stores
  the fifth candidate `word_141876C6C` from unit +0x5C (0x1402D5DA3), writes the saved four words back
  (0x1402D5DAF) and calls `sub_14028728C` to compute the stat block (0x1402D5DBE).

It writes the two-handed word at 0x141876C50 with `sub_140284998` (0x1402D5DE0) and sets the screen
  flags `byte_143CDA8BB`, `byte_140782B8F` and `dword_14184A9B8`.

On the leave message (the wait returns 0) it walks four slots. The candidate is loaded signed
  (a signed load at 0x1402D5ED3); a zero candidate or one with bit 15 set (a bit-15 test of the candidate at 0x1402D5EEB)
  goes through `sub_1402D6464` on the current unit word and adds the candidate's masked price to
  `dword_143D1AC68`.

For a plain candidate it tests the current unit word's bit 15 with a zero test and a nonzero branch
  (0x1402D5EFA/0x1402D5EFD): bit 15 set means the old price is subtracted and the override cleared; bit 15
  clear means the override is cleared only when it equals the candidate.

It stores the candidate word at unit +0x54..+0x5A (0x1402D5F69), so a bit-15 candidate becomes the unit
  word, then calls `PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment` (0x1402D5F88) and closes the screen state.

It tests only bit 15 (`0xFFFF8000`), not bit 14; a bit-14 candidate would be stored. No stock builder
  produces one on this path.

The two `sub_1402D7584` calls are a no-op pair: the first copies the words to the stack and substitutes
  overrides, the second restores the untouched stack copy.

notes: V: the candidate apply/leave path. The four candidate words come from g_EquipSet +0x24; only bit 15 is tested (0x1402D5EEB); a word at or above 0x4000 in the unit is treated as flagged.
open_questions:
- ?: why the first `sub_1402D7584` substitution is immediately undone; no lasting unit change was found.
- ?: whether the bit-14 candidate case is reachable.

name: sub_1402D5FE4
callers: none direct; called through the screen table pointer at 0x140680A90
purpose:
The Outfitter/shop sell-or-confirm handler for the selected slot. It refuses a pending (bit-15) word, prices
the slot on the confirm branch, and clears the slot when the sell is accepted.

behavior.text:
It reads the slot word at unit +0x54 + 2*slot and tests it as signed (a zero test at 0x1402D6129, a negative branch
  at 0x1402D612E). A bit-15 word is negative and takes the state-5 branch instead of the sell branch.

On the confirm branch it prices the slot with `Item_SellPrice` and stores the price in
  `xmmword_14078D9C0`.

On the accepted sell path (the menu word 4 is zero) it clears the selected slot word at 0x1402D625A,
  refunds the stored price with `sub_140284684`, calls `PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment` and sets UI state -105.
The help token is built with a 0x3FF mask (0x1402D60F3) from the same word.

The signed test is the flag test: because bit 15 makes the word negative, a pending purchase cannot be
  sold until it is committed or undone.

notes: V: the sell/confirm handler. A signed test (0x1402D6129 js) refuses a bit-15 word; the empty path clears the word at 0x1402D625A and reloads the panel.
open_questions: - ?: the two menu words (`WORD4`/`WORD5` of xmmword_141811430) and their screen labels.

name: sub_1402D62EC
callers: none direct; called through the screen table pointer at 0x140680A98
purpose:
Leaves the Outfitter to the equip screen: it starts the equip task, resets the task slots and switches the
menu state.

behavior.text:
On the first call it starts task 2 with `sub_14032D31C`, saves the flag bytes, calls `sub_1402BDF34` to
  reset the task slots, and sets the menu state word to 4.

It then calls `sub_1402C4880(4)` and, when the menu id is 4, `sub_14036C49C`; when it is 5,
  `sub_14036C648`.

If the menu id is non-zero it stores it and switches to state 11; otherwise it switches to state 6 and
  posts the "return" message.
It does not call `sub_1402D65D4` or `sub_1402D5B6C`: no flag is stripped or restored here.
This is a screen transition, not the session commit; the flags stay in memory for the next screen.

notes:
- V: Because no flag is cleared here, a transition through this handler leaves any bit-15 words in the unit
  records; the next commit/cancel message still has to clear them.
open_questions: - ?: whether every route out of the Outfitter reaches this handler or the commit/cancel messages first.

name: sub_1402D6464
purpose:
Clears one party equipment slot and either refunds a pending purchase or preserves the original word in the
per-unit override array.

behavior.text: It reads the selected unit's word at +0x54 + 2*slot and tests it against zero (0x1402D648C).

A word at or above 0x8000 (a comparison with 0x8000 at 0x1402D6490 and an unsigned branch at 0x1402D6496) is a session-pending
  word: it is masked with 0x3FF (0x1402D64AA), priced, and the price is subtracted from `dword_143D1AC68`
  (0x1402D64BB). No override is stored.

A word below 0x8000 is stored whole in `g_UnitEquipOverride` at 0x14184A680 (0x1402D649F), so bit 14 can
  be preserved there.
It then clears the unit word at 0x1402D64C1.

The two branches are "undo a pending purchase" and "remember the original item"; the second is what the
  cancel path restores.

the pending word is reduced to an id by AND 0x3FF (mask loaded at 0x1402D64AA) before the price lookup; a mask that keeps bit 15 prices the record past the item block (behavior OutfitterPreviewReadsRecordPastItemBlockWithSessionFlag).

notes: V: a word at or above 0x8000 is refunded and cleared; a word below it is stored raw in the override array, so bit 14 can be preserved there.
open_questions: - ?: what the first argument is for; the body never reads it.

name: sub_1402D64CC
purpose: Puts the override word back into a cleared slot, or clears the slot's override when the slot is not restored.

behavior.text:
It clears the unit word first (0x1402D6515) and reads the override word for the selected unit and slot
  from `g_UnitEquipOverride` (0x1402D651A).

For slot 2 or above it writes the whole override word back (0x1402D65A7) and clears the override
  (0x1402D65AC), with no flag test.

For slots 0 and 1, when both hand words are zero it restores both from the override array
  (0x1402D654F loop) and clears the first two override words as one dword (0x1402D656A).

Otherwise, when the override is non-zero, it calls `sub_140288788` for the override id (0x1402D6581);
  only a return of 1 writes the override back (0x1402D6593) and clears it.
The whole-word copy means a bit-14 override is restored unchanged; the routine never masks the id.

notes: V: restores the override word to the slot or clears the override; no flag test, the whole 16-bit override word is copied, so bit 14 travels.
open_questions:
- ?: whether the override array can hold a bit-14 word in a stock session; the store path in
  `sub_1402D6464` copies any word below 0x8000.

name: sub_1402D65D4
purpose:
The Outfitter commit strip: it removes the session bits from every party equipment word, returns each stored
original to the inventory, and clears the override array.

behavior.text:
It walks `g_PartyCount` units and five words per unit (unit +0x54..+0x5C) with the parallel override
  entry at 0x14184A680.

It compares each unit word with 0x4000 (the 0x4000 constant at 0x1402D6617, a comparison with 0x4000 at 0x1402D6621,
  an unsigned branch at 0x1402D6624). A word below 0x4000 is left untouched.

A word at or above 0x4000 has its low ten bits extracted with a 0x3FF mask (0x1402D6632) and the
  override compared with them (0x1402D6634); the unit word is then masked with 0x3FF (a 0x3FF mask of the unit word at
  0x1402D6641), which clears both flag bits.

It returns the override word to the inventory with `Inventory_AddCount(override,1)` (0x1402D6650) and
  clears the override (0x1402D6655), for every slot.

Because the mask is 0x3FF, a word with bit 14 set is stripped the same way as a bit-15 word; bits 10..13
  would also be cleared, but no stock writer sets them.

the strip mask is loaded at 0x1402D6609; the commit decides whether a word carries a session flag by comparing it with 0x4000 (0x1402D6621), which a plain id of 16,384 or more also passes (behavior OutfitterPreviewReadsRecordPastItemBlockWithSessionFlag).

notes: V: the commit strip. Every party word at or above 0x4000 is masked with 0x3FF and its override is returned to the inventory; words below 0x4000 are untouched. Called once, from sub_1402D6E14.
open_questions:
- ?: whether the override count can be non-zero for a unit whose word is below 0x4000; the routine returns it
  to the inventory anyway.

name: sub_1402D67C8
purpose:
The equip screen's message handler for the leave messages 0, 6 and 7: it closes the screen, refreshes the job
screen when the unit changed, and zeroes the session price accumulator.

behavior.text: Message 6 calls `sub_1402C4880(6)`; message 0 posts message 63490 and closes.

Message 7, when the selected unit differs from `word_141811420`, calls `JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange` and
  then copies the selected unit record into a stack record with `sub_1402C33D0`.
At the end of the message-7 branch it sets `dword_143D1AC68 = 0`, so the session price is dropped.
It does not call `sub_1402D65D4` or `sub_1402D5B6C`; the strip/cancel is in the other handler.

Message 7 is "leave the equip screen", and the price accumulator belongs to the Outfitter's equip session, so it
  is cleared here when the equip screen closes.

notes: - V: The handler is reached from the dispatcher on menu id 6.
open_questions:
- ?: whether message 7 can run while a bit-15 word is still in a unit; if so, the price is dropped without a
  strip.

name: sub_1402D6914
purpose:
The Outfitter/shop message handler. It covers the cancel message, the leave message, the shop-order message,
the "equip this pick" message and the "apply the candidate list" message.

behavior.text:
The switch is on the message dword. Message 6 calls `sub_1402D5B6C` (the cancel restore); message 0xC
  handles the overflow check; message 0x25 sets `g_ShopOrderGroup` and calls `sub_1402D7640`.

Message 0x45 reads the selected slot word (0x1402D6C30), clears bit 15 with a bit-15 clear (0x1402D6C35),
  and calls `sub_1402D7280` with the cleared word (0x1402D6C47). This is the re-buy/confirm path.

Message 0x46 copies the unit's five words to a stack record with `sub_1402D7584` (0x1402D69A3), sets the
  fifth candidate from unit +0x5C (0x1402D69F9), builds the candidates with `sub_140287D9C` (0x1402D6A18) and
  recomputes the two-handed word (0x1402D6A34).

In the same message it walks four candidates loaded signed (a signed load at 0x1402D6A55). A zero candidate or
  one with bit 15 set (a bit-15 test (the 0xFFFF8000 constant) at 0x1402D6A74) is removed from the slot with `sub_1402D6464`
  and its price added to `dword_143D1AC68`; a plain candidate either clears a matching override or subtracts
  the old pending price.

It stores the candidate word at unit +0x54..+0x5A (0x1402D6AC0), so bit 15 is written when the candidate
  carries it, then calls `PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment` and the stat/candidate refreshers.
It tests only bit 15 in the candidate and unit comparisons, not bit 14.

Message 0x45 is "buy/confirm the pick" and 0x46 is "apply the list and leave"; both are part of the same
  session that only the commit/cancel messages end.

notes: V: the shop/equip message handler. Case 0x45 clears bit 15 with btr (0x1402D6C35) before re-buying; case 0x46 applies four candidates and charges their prices.
open_questions:
- ?: whether message 0x46 can run without a following commit/cancel message.
- ?: the meaning of the 0x25 shop-order branch's 1515/1518 calls.

name: sub_1402D6E14
purpose:
The Outfitter's commit/cancel message handler. Message 0x3D commits: it flushes the session price, strips the
flags from all units, saves them and refreshes the job screen. Messages 0 and 6 cancel.

behavior.text:
Message 0x3D posts message 0xF811 (0x1402D6E47), then flushes `dword_143D1AC68` to gil by calling
  `sub_140284684` with its negation (0x1402D6E54) and zeroes the accumulator (0x1402D6E5B).

It then calls `sub_1402D65D4` (0x1402D6E61) to strip the session bits and return the overrides, calls
  `sub_140285A6C` (0x1402D6E66) to write every party unit to the save, and ends with a tail jump to
  `JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange` (0x1402D6E9C).

Messages 0 and 6 call `sub_1402D5B6C` (0x1402D6F03) to restore the override words; message 0 posts
  0xF802 and message 6 posts 0xFFFFFFFF.
Message 7 only posts the close message.

The order is deliberate: the price is charged first, then the flags are stripped, then the cleared words
  are written to the save. A save taken between the flush and the strip would not contain a flag.

notes:
- V: This is the only call site of `sub_1402D65D4`. The cancel site is one of the two call sites of
  `sub_1402D5B6C`.
open_questions: - ?: whether a save can interrupt the handler between the flush and the strip.

name: sub_1402D6F10
purpose:
The per-frame dispatcher of the Outfitter/equip screens: it builds a small message from the input state and
calls one of the three screen handlers by menu id.

behavior.text:
It reads `word_141848BB0` (0x1402D6F23) and builds a message with dword -1, byte 0, the input dword and
  the input word (0x1402D6F45 and 0x1402D6F50).

Menu id 6 calls `sub_1402D67C8` (0x1402D6F9E); menu id 7 calls `sub_1402D6914` (0x1402D6F92); menu id 12
  calls `sub_1402D6E14` (0x1402D6F86).
Every other id falls through without a handler.

The three handlers are the equip screen, the shop screen and the commit/cancel screen; the dispatcher is
  the single place that decides which one runs.

notes: - V: The message it passes is the same shape the handlers read as `a1`.
open_questions:
- ?: which menu id is the Outfitter slot screen and which is the shop; the two ids 6 and 7 are swapped between
  the two screens in the reading of the entry table.

name: sub_1402D6FB8
purpose:
Builds the five (id, price) preview pairs for the equip panel from the live unit words and the override array,
then posts the preview record.

behavior.text:
It clears a 5-pair (8 bytes each) stack array, then walks five slots of the selected unit
  (`g_PartyUnits[g_SelectedUnitIndex]`) against the override array at 0x14184A680.

The word is loaded zero-extended and its bit 15 is extracted with a shift right by 15 (0x1402D704C); a set bit
  yields the masked id (0x1402D7056), a clear bit yields -1 (0x1402D7060).

It also compares the raw unit word with the signed override word (a signed read of the override word at 0x1402D7060): when
  they differ, the pair is zeroed (0x1402D706F); this is how a slot whose value equals the override is marked
  unchanged.
For a set bit 15 it prices the masked id with `Item_GetRecord(..., +8)` (0x1402D7087-0x1402D7094).

It calls `sub_140284998` with the five candidate words and the unit's flag byte +0x16E (0x1402D70BE)
  and stores the two-handed result as a byte in the posted record.

The preview distinguishes "pending purchase" (bit 15) from "unchanged" (equal to the override); a plain
  changed word is shown without a price.

the id of a flagged slot is the hand word AND 0x3FF (mask loaded at 0x1402D7027), which strips the session flag; a mask that keeps bit 15 makes the id 32,768 plus the id and `Item_GetRecord` then reads a record 32,768 rows past the item block (behavior OutfitterPreviewReadsRecordPastItemBlockWithSessionFlag).

notes: V: builds five (id, price) pairs for the preview. Bit 15 is taken with shr 0xF (0x1402D704C); the override is compared as a signed word, so a bit-14 override reads as negative.
open_questions: - ?: which screen reads the posted record.

name: sub_1402D7280
purpose:
Applies one shop/Outfitter pick to a party unit slot: it refuses a "cannot equip" candidate, removes the old
slot, records the new price, and writes the chosen item id with the session-pending bit 15.

behavior.text:
It rejects a candidate with bit 14 set with a bit-14 test (0x1402D72A0) and jumps to the UI state 5 path
  without touching the unit.
It calls `sub_140288788` to validate the id against the unit; a negative result leaves the state at 5.

It reads the current unit word and tests it as signed: a zero test and a negative branch (the export shows the equivalent
  `v7 >= 0` test) decides whether the slot already holds a bit-15 word.

It removes the old word with `sub_1402D6464`, and when the old word was the same masked id it restores
  the override with `sub_1402D64CC` and sets UI state 7 (the "undo purchase" branch).

Otherwise it adds the new item's price to `dword_143D1AC68` and writes `id | 0x8000` to the unit word
  (the constant is loaded at 0x1402D732C, OR-ed at 0x1402D733A, stored at 0x1402D7345), then sets UI state 10.

When the slot is 1 (the second hand) and the unit's new hand pair is one-handed, it repeats the same
  operation with slot 0 (0x1402D743C), so a one-handed weapon fills the other hand too.
It ends in `sub_1402D6FB8` to refresh the preview pairs.

The bit-14 rejection is a list-mark check, not a width check: bit 14 is the shop list's "cannot equip"
  mark and the unit word must not receive it.

notes: V: the bit-15 setter. It rejects a candidate with bit 14 (0x1402D72A0), adds the price and writes id | 0x8000 (0x1402D733A). It is called from sub_1402D6914 and the shop message handler sub_14036BE10.
open_questions:
- ?: whether the "same masked id" compare is intended to toggle a pending purchase off; the branch restores
  the override instead of clearing the slot.

name: sub_1402D746C
purpose:
Applies an id to a slot, then mirrors the selected unit's four hand words and the fifth word from the scratch
record into the candidate array and refreshes the stat block.

behavior.text:
It calls `sub_1402D7584(&v8,1,1)` (0x1402D749B) to snapshot all five unit words with overrides
  substituted for empty and pending slots.

When the id is non-negative it calls `sub_140288590(0x36,slot,id)` (0x1402D74B7); a return other than 1
  triggers a second call with the unit's current word if it differs from the scratch record (0x1402D74DA).

It copies `qword_141801100 + 0x54` to `g_EquipCandidates` with a qword move (0x1402D7501/0x1402D7506) and the
  word at +0x5C to 0x141876C6C (0x1402D750E/0x1402D7513). The copy is raw, so a bit-15 word travels.

It calls `sub_140287354` to rebuild the stat block (0x1402D753A) and `sub_14036C320` to refresh the
  two-handed/detail state.

It writes the snapshot back to the unit's five words after the refresh, so the override substitution is
  undone.

This is the shop's "equip from the list" path: the scratch record is the source of truth for the displayed
  candidates, while the unit keeps its original words until the commit.

notes: V: copies four hand words with movsd (0x1402D7501) and the fifth with the word at 0x1402D750E from the scratch record to g_EquipCandidates; a flagged source word is copied as is.
open_questions: - ?: why the second `sub_140288590` call re-applies the unit's own word when it differs from the scratch copy.

name: sub_1402D7584
proto: void *__fastcall sub_1402D7584(void *out, unsigned __int8 extra, char substitute_zero)
purpose:
Copies the selected unit's equipment words to a caller buffer and substitutes the override word for any word
that is session-pending (or, with the third argument, empty).

behavior.text:
It copies `2*extra + 8` bytes from unit +0x54 with `memmove` (0x1402D75CA), so `extra=0` copies four
  words and `extra=1` copies all five.

It then walks `extra + 4` words. A word compared with zero and found negative (a signed comparison of the unit word with zero at
  0x1402D75E1 and a signed branch at 0x1402D75E6) is replaced by the override word (0x1402D7614).

With `substitute_zero != 0` it also replaces a zero word when the override is non-zero (0x1402D7606 and
  0x1402D7612).
The override source is `g_UnitEquipOverride` at 0x14184A680, indexed five words per selected unit.

The buffer is a backup snapshot before a temporary edit; the caller restores it afterwards, so the
  substitution is a preview, not a lasting change.

notes: V: memmove of 2*a2+8 bytes from unit +0x54 to the caller buffer, then replaces a negative (bit-15) word with the override word (0x1402D75E1); with a3 set it also replaces a zero word.
open_questions: - ?: whether any caller keeps the substituted buffer instead of restoring the original.

name: sub_1402D7640
purpose:
Rebuilds the shop's displayed item list into the shared menu list and then syncs the candidate array from the
selected unit's scratch record.

behavior.text:
It reads the shop cursor/order byte and the shop order group, calls `Shop_BuildItemList` with the selected
  unit and shop and writes the list into `g_MenuList` (0x141811470), then binds the rows with
  `ShopList_BuildEntries`.

It calls `sub_140289894` to copy the selected unit into the scratch record (0x141801100), then
  `sub_1402D746C` to copy the four + one hand words from the scratch record into `g_EquipCandidates`.

The list builder is called with mode `(v6)+1`; the mode controls whether an unequippable item is marked
  with bit 14. The call sites in this function use the value from `sub_140336788`, so a marked list is possible
  here.

This is the shop's list refresh; it is the bridge between the shop list (bit 14 marks) and the equip
  candidates (bit 15 marks).
the list is built with Shop_BuildItemList at 0x1402D76D0 using mode (v6 + 1), so mode 1 can set bit 14 on a refused item and mode 2 drops it; the list is then ordered in place at 0x1402D76E1.

notes: - V: The candidate copy is raw; a hand word that already carries bit 15 reaches the candidate array.
open_questions:
- ?: whether the bit-14 mode is 1 or 2 on this path in a stock shop; the flag argument is computed from the

The context flag at +6 & 0x20 skips the hand reads entirely.
Otherwise it resolves the item ids at +0x1E, +0x20, +0x22 and +0x26 through Item_GetRecord and the per-slot accessors, and copies weapon and armour bytes into 0x1407B0781 and 0x1407B0782.

name: sub_140305A48
purpose: Scales the working attack by a percentage tied to the equipped item category and stores the result as a 1/100 fraction.

behavior.text: It reads the item id at 0x1407B077A, resolves it with Item_GetRecord and takes the category byte at record+5.
The command byte at +0x3E and the level byte at +0x2B are read from the context at 0x14186AF78 (the body also reads +0x3F, +0x40 and +0x2D there).
It writes the command value to 0x1407B0770 and command*level/100 to 0x1407B0772, using the divide-by-100 reciprocal multiply.
A zero result is raised to 1 before it is stored.
Six call sites in four functions, all physical formulas: NormalAttack three times, WotL distance-scaled, Dancer, and sub_140306EF0.

this is the weapon-stat setup of the formula blocks (proposed name Formula_WeaponPA). Its output is the pair A (g_FormulaBlock +0) and B (+2), not a fraction: type 0 (bare hands) gives A = the caster's PA (+0x3E) and B = max(1, PA * Brave (+0x2B) / 100); every other weapon type gives B = the weapon power byte 0x1407B07AC and an A that depends on the type (PA, (PA + Speed) / 2, PA * Brave / 100, a random share of PA, or other mixes).
the older bullets above call the two inputs 'command value' and 'level byte'; they are PA and Brave.

it loads caster +0x3E (PA) into r9, +0x3F (MA) into r11 and +0x2B (Brave) into ebx; by the item record's category byte (+5): 0 (bare hands) A = PA and B = max(1, PA x Brave / 100); every other category B = the weapon power byte 0x1407B07AC and A = PA for 3, 7, 11, 15 (swords, rods, crossbows, spears); (PA + Speed (+0x40)) / 2 for 1, 2, 12, 32 (knives, ninja blades, bows, thrown stars); max(1, PA x Brave / 100) for 4, 5 (knight swords, katanas); MA for 8, 16 (staves, poles); 1 + a random value below PA (Battle_Rand15) for 6, 9, 17 (axes, flails, bags); (PA + MA) / 2 for 13, 14, 18 (harps, books, cloths); max(1, PA x (100 - Faith (+0x2D)) / 100) for 35; A is left as it was for any other category (guns, 10, use formula 3).

notes: I: the categories that take the multiplier path are those tested by the switch at 0x140305AB3..0x140305B03.

name: sub_140305C18

purpose: Applies the three multiplicative modifiers that follow the attack scale: a 4/3 step, a 3/2 step and a final halving.

behavior.text: It tests three independent flags on the context: +0x99 & 0x10, +0x9A & 0x20 and +0x9B & 1.
The first flag multiplies the working value by 4/3 (shift left by two, then divide by three).
The second flag, only when the item category at record+5 is zero, multiplies the value by 3/2.
The third flag multiplies by 3/2 again and stores the halved result at 0x1407B0770.
Eight callers, six of them formulas (StealEXP, Monk averaged, Pummel, Purification, Chakra, Revive, Rush).

correction to the bullets above: the third step multiplies A by 3/2 (4/3 for +0x99 bit 0x10, 3/2 for +0x9A bit 0x20 when the item category is 0, 3/2 for +0x9B bit 0x01); there is no halving. Formula_PhysMods repeats the same steps inline.

notes: I: the three flags read as support abilities that raise physical damage; their names are not in the bytes.

name: sub_1403064D8
purpose: The shared stat-sap effect: picks which stat byte the formula writes by the ability being resolved.

ids 143 and 197 write the result byte +20 of the action block, 144 and 198 write +22, 145 and 199 write +23: the value is the byte at 0x1407B079D (the copied action row's byte +9) & 0x7F; the block's flag byte +39 gets bit 0x01.

notes: Read 2026-11-10: the case labels are 143..145 and 197..199. 130 bytes, read whole. Behaviour: FormulaHandlersChooseTheirEffectByAbilityId.

name: sub_1403067D0
purpose: Post-dispatch step for the physical formulas (id below 7): it filters the pending status set, checks the defender's state and flags the result.

behavior.text: It returns at once unless the context byte at +0x27 is negative.
It builds a two-word request (unit id from +6, then 0xFFFF - the all-ones word is produced by ORing eax with -1, not an immediate) and calls sub_140309FB8 on it.
It reads the defender's HP word at +0x30 and adds the pending amount at +8 before the checks.
It refuses to continue when the defender has +6 & 0xC0, +0x61 & 0x20, a negative byte at +0x62, or +0x64 & 1.
It calls Job_HasMonsterPair and Status_FilterPendingSets, then sub_1403052DC; on success it sets result bit 0x40 and phase 9.
One caller: Battle_ResolveAction, which reaches it only for formula ids below 7.
it acts only on an HP damage result (R+39 bit 0x80) and works from HP left = the target's HP (+0x30) + R+8 - the clamped R+6 (sub_140309FB8).

with the caster's +0x9A bit 0x40 set and the target not player-flagged (+5 bit 4 clear), a target that would die (HP left below 1, or R+29 bit 0x20) and has a monster pair (Job_HasMonsterPair) gets R+18 |= 0x20 and the byte at 0x1407B07B8 = 6, clearing the knockback and the queued request first.

with the caster's +0x9A bit 0x80 set and the HP left at or below max HP (+0x32) / 5, it sets R+30 bit 0x40, and when Status_FilterPendingSets(0) keeps something it sets R+18 |= 0x40, R+39 |= 8 and the byte at 0x1407B07B8 = 9.

notes: I: the flags it tests look like the 'already resolved / dead / petrified' guards of a physical hit.

name: sub_140306C90

purpose: Second half of the physical attack setup: it applies the attacker's state modifiers after the hands are read and returns whether the action may continue.

behavior.text: It calls sub_1403055F0 first, so the hand values are always refreshed before the modifiers.
Attacker +0x99 & 1 zeroes the dword at 0x1407B0781 (the four hand bytes).
Attacker +0x62 & 0x30 halves the working byte at 0x1407B077F, and +0x63 & 0x10 zeroes the dword at 0x1407B0781.
It calls sub_140305700 and sub_14030573C, then for weapon categories 11 and 12 reads scene variables 35 and 36 and scales the byte at 0x1407B077F by three quarters when variable 36 is 1.
It returns true only when the byte it finally tests is zero.
Twenty-three callers, nearly all physical formulas.

this is the physical gate of the formula blocks (proposed name Formula_PhysGate): after the evade bytes are prepared it calls Formula_EvadeRoll and returns 1 when R+0 is 0 (the hit failed), else 0; 23 formula functions call it directly.
for item category 11 or 12 (record +5 of the item word at g_FormulaBlock +0x0A) it scales the baseline byte by 3/4 when SceneVar 36 is 1 and by 3/4 again when SceneVar 35 is 3 or 4.

notes: V: the scene variables are read through sub_1402332D8, the same accessor the battle code uses elsewhere.

name: sub_140306D70

purpose: Magic-side counterpart of the physical setup: it seeds the magic working bytes from the caster's hands and accessory.

behavior.text: It writes 100 to 0x1407B077F and zeroes the dword at 0x1407B0781 at the top.

Caster +6 & 0x20 skips the hand reads; otherwise it copies byte +1 of the records for the item ids at +0x1E, +0x22 and +0x26 into 0x1407B0781, 0x1407B0782 and 0x1407B0783 (the per-slot accessor is chosen by the item's flag bits 8 and 0x40).
It applies the same +0x63 & 0x10 zeroing of the dword at 0x1407B0781 as the physical setup.
It calls sub_140305700, sub_14030573C and sub_14030588C, then returns (byte == 0) like its physical twin.
Twenty-two callers, all magic formulas (Black Magick, Gravity, Faith status, Death, the drains, Iaido, Geomancy and others).

this is the magic gate of the formula blocks (proposed name Formula_MagicGate): the baseline byte is set to 100, only the accessory and the two shield evade bytes are filled (the dword at 0x1407B0781 is zeroed first, so the fourth evade byte stays 0), then Formula_EvadeRoll runs; it returns 1 when R+0 is 0, else 0.
the accessory is read when item record byte +3 has bit 0x08, a shield when its record byte +3 has bit 0x40; 23 formula functions call it directly.

notes: I: the pair sub_140306C90 / sub_140306D70 is the physical and magical split of one setup step; the field offsets differ by the record each hand type reads.

name: sub_1403095E4
purpose: Executes a reaction ability: builds the result record the reaction causes from the reaction id in the word at 0x14186AFF0, or refuses an id it does not handle.

behavior.text: first, an id of 440 loads the unit pointer 0x14186AF78 from the unit table at the index in dword 0x14186AFF4.
the gate table at 0x14067F730 is indexed by id - 422 (32 entries, ids 422..453); an entry whose low two bits are 1 returns 0 at once: the ids 435, 436, 437, 440, 441, 442 and 453.

otherwise both result records are reset and a switch on the id fills the action block: the cases are 422..434 and the single ids 438, 439, 444 and 446; each case writes one or two bytes or words of the block (which ones depends on the id; 422, 423, 424 write +22, +23, +20, 425..428 set status groups and then test Status_FilterPendingSets).
any other id (435..437, 440..443, 445, 447 and above) clears the block's byte +39 and returns -1: the reaction is dropped. The default is at 0x140309795.
a handled id stores its kind flag in the block's byte +39, calls sub_14030A11C and returns 1 (with bit 0x01 of +39 added when the block's word +18 is non-zero).
the only caller is Battle_ResolveAction, which runs it first when the battle-state gate 0x14186AF9C is non-zero; a non-zero answer there ends the resolve (Action_SetWeaponItem, return 0).

notes: 742 bytes (2026-11-10). The compare chain has the cases 444 and 446 and no case for 435..437 and 440..443 (the case list above is from the compare chain). Only 'which block byte is written' was read per case; the names of the reactions are not given here (ids only). Behaviour: AfterDamageReactionChain.
open_questions: ? what the cases 444 and 446 are; why the gate table holds 42 and 45 at index 12 and 18.

name: sub_1403099B0
callees: sub_14002630C, Item_FindCategoryIndex, sub_1402B8C74, sub_1402B8E04, Item_IsInCategory, AbilityAction_GetRecord, sub_1403067D0, sub_140309540, sub_1403095E4, Action_SetWeaponItem, sub_14030A11C, sub_14030A410, sub_14030AFEC, __security_check_cookie
purpose: Resolves one battle action: copies the 20-byte action, sets up per-command data, dispatches the formula and runs the post steps.

behavior.text: copies the 20-byte action a1 and sets up pointers into g_BattleUnitTable for the actor (action byte 0) and target a2.
reads the aux flags4 dword for the ability id; `& 3` and `& 0x1000000` are stored at unit-state byte +26 (bytes read at 0x140309C5E, 0x140309C6C).
for command type 10 clamps `if ((unsigned)(id - 406) > 7) id = 406` then reads kind4 byte 1 (byte_140788F55[2*id]) into word_1407B0787, at 0x140309EC3.
for ids < 368 copies the 20-byte AbilityAction_GetRecord(id) into the action block; command type 1 uses the item record (sub_1402B8E04).

the u8 formula id v23 (forced to 1 when outside 1..0x6A) is dispatched through the formula registry by an indirect call at 0x140309F53 (the handler is g_FormulaHandlers[v23]: an 8-byte-entry table at image offset 0x682BC8, indexed by v23).
after the call: `v23 < 7` calls sub_1403067D0 (0x140309F5B); `v23 >= 7` with `v23 == 100` clears word +0x12 of the action (0x140309F68); then sub_14030A11C(1).

notes:
Returns 1 early when the formula-target byte is 0 after setup, 0 on handled paths.
- Inline item category read:
  - V (head only): calls Item_FindCategoryIndex on the action's item and reads g_ItemCategoryType of the result INLINE (not through an accessor).
  - I: kinds 0 and 5 (the weapon kinds) keep the item id for the action; other kinds clear it.
  - V: then copies the 8-byte weapon sub-record (sub_1402B8C74) and its byte 7 into the action record.
  - V: this inline read is the one code reference to the category tables outside the item functions.

name: sub_14030A11C
proto: int sub_14030A11C(char runHook, int64_t a2, int64_t a3, int64_t a4)
callers: Battle_ResolveAction (0x140309F78), sub_1403095E4, sub_1403062F0, sub_1403063B8 (IDA code references)
purpose: Finishes the result block of one resolved action: either drops the whole result when the acting unit's own state forbids it, or runs the per-formula post hook, clamps the numbers to 999 and decides whether a follow-up result is needed.

behavior.text: tests three status bits of the acting unit (g_BattleActingUnit; the dword's flags are tested as bytes +0, +1 and +3 of 0x14186B028 and the later masks sit in registers): +0x61 bit 0x20 (KO; it counts only when bit 0x20 of dword 0x14186B028 is clear or the unit also has +0x61 bit 0x10), +0x62 bit 0x80 (with bit 0x8000 of the dword clear) and +0x64 bit 0x01 (with bit 0x1000000 clear); when one holds it removes the unit's slot byte (unit +0x1BC) from the 16-byte list at 0x14186B030, resets both result records with Battle_ResultReset (g_BattleActionBlock and qword_14186AF60), clears the flag bits it set and leaves byte +2 of the block at 8.

otherwise, when runHook is non-zero and the gate g_ShopModeGate is non-zero, it hands the block's words +6 and +10 to sub_140309FB8 and writes them back, then runs the per-formula hook: row = g_PostBattleCalc + 8 + 32 * (formula - 1) for a formula byte (g_FormulaBlock +0x18) below 107; when the row's argument qword (+8) is non-zero it calls the row's function (+0) with that argument and a pointer to a copy of the row's second half (the row's +0x10 and +0x18 qwords).

then it clamps the block's words +6, +8, +10 and +12 (signed) to 999; when the HP word (+6) reaches the acting unit's current HP (+0x30) it also clears the g_FormulaBlock flag byte (+0x20, bit 0x80) with block word +18 bit 0x4000 and the dword at 0x1407B0768 with word +18 bit 0x200; and, when the block's byte +39 and byte 0 are non-zero outside the battle-state gate, a per-side word of qword_14186B020 is set and bit 0x08 of byte 0x1407B0799 is set, it sets byte +2 = 10 and word +18 = 0x8000 and calls sub_14030A43C.
the hook rows exist for 12 formula ids only; formula ids above 106 skip the hook by the bound (no overflow).

notes: Source: read 2026-11-12. 753 bytes, read whole. The name keeps the address: the roles of the flag words and of the follow-up result (sub_14030A43C) were not read in full. The hook table: struct PostBattleCalc, global g_PostBattleCalc, built by sub_1401F92A8.

name: sub_14030AFEC
purpose:
A post-resolution reaction helper: after an action resolves it can queue one of a small set of reaction abilities
for the acting unit, under a set of command, unit-flag and item-category conditions.

behavior.text: it returns immediately when the battle state dword at `0x14186AF9C` is nonzero.
it returns when the byte at battle context +0x18 is 7 or `0x6A`.
it returns when the 16-bit word at context − 8 is set while the word at context − 6 is zero.
it loads the acting unit from `0x14186AF68` and the action block from `0x14186AF70`.

when the unit's byte at +0x65 has bit 2, the word at context − 8 is zero, the byte at context +6 is not `0x15`
  and the byte at context +0x29 has bit `0x80`, it writes ability `0x1B8` at action +0x10, copies the word at
  context +8 into action +0x28, clears action +0x2C and action +0, and sets action +2 to 9.
it returns when action +0x10 is already set or when the state dword is nonzero.

it calls sub_140278FA8 with the unit and the constant 4, then sub_14030DD1C; a nonzero result from either ends
  the function.

when the unit's byte at +0x97 has bit 4 and the byte at context +0x2A has bit `0x10`, it writes 100 minus the
  unit's byte at +0x2B into action +0x2C, then calls sub_140278E68 with 100 and that same unit byte.
the same branch then stores ability `0x1C3` at action +0x10 and sets action +2 to `0x0B`.

when +0x97 has bit 2 instead, the function requires the byte at context +0x27 to have bit `0x20` and the item id
  at context +0xA to name an item whose equip-category byte is `0x0B` or `0x0C`.
that second branch does the same CT arithmetic, then stores ability `0x1C4` and sets action +2 to 4.
both branches refuse to run while the dword at `0x14186AF80` is nonzero, and check it again after the call.

the two abilities are reactions, because they lie in the reaction range of the ability id space and the block
  fields written are the ones an action queue uses.

100 minus the unit byte is a CT spend, because 100 is the CT scale and the value is written into the action
  block the queue reads.
which reaction each of the two branches represents.
what the byte at context +0x18 and the word pair before the context mean.

notes:
- V: the context offsets +0x18, +0x27 and +0x2A are absolute RIP operands of the block based at 0x1407B0770 (0x1407B0788, 0x1407B0797 and 0x1407B079A); base+offset is folded into each displacement, so the literal offsets do not appear as operands.
- V: the whole function was read; the three helper calls were not.

name: sub_14030B1A0
purpose: The preview twin of sub_1402828E4: works out the MP cost of the action under the cursor and the same refusal codes, without paying.

behavior.text: clears the MP cost byte (byte 0x1407B078E); the command kind is looked up in g_CommandKind at the formula block's command byte (0x1407B0776); the ability is the word at 0x1407B0778; the unit is the pointer at 0x14186AF78.

the same chain as sub_1402828E4: a unit with the +0x65 mask-0x04 status or a non-zero sub_14030DD1C answer returns that answer + 6; a Toad unit (+0x63 mask 0x02) returns 5 unless the ability is 0, 367 or 29 (a command kind of 10 returns 5 whatever the ability).

an ability above 0x16F skips the rest, so it gets no cost and no refusal here; for a kind-0 or kind-6 command with a stock id the action row's flag +5 mask 0x20 together with the unit's +0x62 mask 0x08 returns 2.

for command kind 0 and a unit whose job byte is not 93 the cost is action-row byte +13, halved when unit +0x99 has bit 7; it is stored in byte 0x1407B078E only (no MP is taken, no 'not enough MP' answer).
the single-id tests against 367 and 29 sit at 0x14030B202 and 0x14030B208.

notes: 216 bytes, read whole (read 2026-11-10).
open_questions: ? the meaning of the return values 2 and 5 for the caller (only the values were read).

name: sub_14030B278
purpose:
Checks whether the unit can answer with an automatic item: it picks one of the two item words the unit carries,
tests that the item is a usable weapon-slot item, and queues the fixed ability `0x1BF` when the test passes.

behavior.text: it loads the unit pointer from `0x14186AF68` and reads the unit's byte at +0x97.
when bit `0x40` of that byte is set it calls sub_14030DD1C and remembers whether the call returned 0.

it returns false when the unit's byte at +6 has bit `0x20` set, which is the monster marker used elsewhere in
  the battle code.
it returns false unless the remembered check passed, so the `0x40` bit and a zero return are both required.

it then reads the byte at battle context +0x18 and returns false unless that byte equals one of a fixed set of
  values in the `0x26`..`0x65` range.
it reads the two 16-bit item words at unit +0x20 and +0x24.

for each word it calls Item_GetRecord and requires the record's slot-flags byte at +3 to be signed-negative,
  which is the weapon-slot bit.

the first item word is accepted only when the byte at context +0x12 is nonzero; the second only when the byte
  at context +0x13 is nonzero.
on success it stores ability `0x1BF` at action +0x10 and returns true.
otherwise it returns false and leaves the action block untouched.

this is an automatic item reaction, because it spends an item the unit carries at fixed record offsets and
  queues a reaction-range ability rather than an action the player chose.
what the fixed value set and the two context bytes mean.
whether the two item words are the unit's equipped item slots or a reaction-specific pair.

notes:
- V: the context offsets +0x12, +0x13 and +0x18 are absolute RIP operands of the block based at 0x1407B0770 (0x1407B0782, 0x1407B0783 and 0x1407B0788); base+offset is folded into each displacement.
- V: the whole function was read; sub_14030DD1C was not.

name: sub_14030B4F0
proto: ? (returns a byte; builds a request in a 0x450-byte frame)

purpose: Reaction and auto-item path: it picks an item or weapon reaction, builds the action for it and applies it without consuming the item.

It also uses sub_14030AF88, sub_14030B1A0 and sub_14030B37C to test and then spend the item.
Two callers: sub_140228990 and sub_1402DF58C.

name: sub_14030BE18
purpose: The Brave roll that decides whether a reaction fires; on success it stores the reaction id and the amount the reaction acts on in the action block.

behavior.text: runs only when the action block's flag byte +39 has bit 7 set (the result may be reacted to).

in a simulation (g_BattleSimulating non-zero) it passes without a roll; otherwise it rolls Rng_Percent(100, unit byte +0x2B) on the unit at g_BattleActingUnit and passes on the roll's failure value as the code is written (the helper's polarity was not read; I: the Brave percent roll).
on a pass it copies the block's word +6 (the HP result) to word +40 and stores the reaction id at word +16.
