name: sub_14030BE68
purpose: The second reaction helper: the same Brave roll as sub_14030BE18, only for a unit with status bit 0x01 at +0x63, and it stores the reaction id without copying the HP result.

behavior.text: requires the unit at g_BattleActingUnit to have mask 0x01 set at byte +0x63 (status 23, Critical; I).
then the same two tests as sub_14030BE18 (flag +39 bit 7; no roll in a simulation, else Rng_Percent on unit byte +0x2B) and stores the reaction id at action block word +16.

notes: 74 bytes, read whole (2026-11-10). Behaviour: AfterDamageReactionChain.

name: sub_14030BF04
purpose: Handles a break or destroy effect on a piece of equipment: it finds the item, checks whether it can break, and removes it from the slot.

behavior.text: It reads an equipment word and accepts it only when it is below 261.
The item record's breakable flag decides whether the effect applies; an unbreakable item is left alone.
A broken item is removed from the slot and returned through the inventory-return path.
It calls three helpers and has one direct caller.
The bound is the stock 261 rather than the packed hand word's ten bits, so this path reads a plain id.

name: sub_14030CAA8
proto: char __fastcall sub_14030CAA8(unsigned int a1, unsigned int a2)
purpose: Applies a unit's pending status bits (bitset at unit-state +29..+33) to its status state, subject to immunity and conflict checks.

behavior.text: sets the current preview unit a1 (g_BattleUnitTable + 512*a1, 512-byte records) and loops v7 over 0..39 status bits (`v7 < 40`).

reads the status property table (0x140788FE0, 40 x 16 bytes) through compiler-folded operands: byte_140788DFC = 0x140788FEB + 16*v7 + i (bytes 11..15) at 0x14030CB31, ANDed with the unit's 5 bytes at +495; a hit skips the status.
otherwise copies 5 bytes from aDefghijklmnopq = 0x140788FE6 + 16*v7 + j (bytes 6..10) into the unit-state byte array at +34 (0x14030CB7B).
then calls sub_1403052DC(a2), sub_14030CA00(a1), sets the bit in the unit's +495 mask and calls sub_140278CF0(unit, v7, 0); a non-zero result skips the rest.
special cases after that: status 19 clears byte +46; statuses 9 and 34 copy bits 0x30 of byte +5 from a second record (status 9 also clears some +494 bits and a word pair).

notes:
The displacements byte_140788DFC and aDefghijklmnopq lie numerically inside the aux table (0x140787F80..0x140788F80) but address the status property table at 0x140788FE0; the names are IDA auto-names, not real objects.

Both folded operands (0x14030CB31, 0x14030CB7B) address the status property table with folded offsets.
open_questions: ? meaning of status property bytes 6..10 (copied) and 11..15 (mask), and of the notify code passed to sub_1401FB064.

name: sub_14030CD08
purpose: Finds a unit that learns the current ability from the action, rolling the learn chance; returns the unit index or -1.

behavior.text: returns -1 when dword_14186AFF8 != 0, no current ability (word_14186AF5C == 0), or the ability's aux flags3 & 0x20 is clear (`*((_BYTE*)&g_AbilityAuxTable + 8*id + 3) & 0x20`, 0x14030CD40).
scans units (512-byte records) other than a1 whose state byte has bit 2 set, sets that byte to 4 and requires sub_140278FA8(unit, 4) == 0.

for that unit's job walks 24 skillset slots; when Skillset_GetAbility equals the ability and the slot's bit is clear it rolls `Rng_Percent(100, *((_BYTE*)&g_AbilityAuxTable + 8*id + 2))` (learn_percent, 0x14030CE28); a zero return stores the ability in *a2 and returns the unit index.
a unit counts only when its per-unit byte at +0x1BB has bit 1 set (I: the unit was hit by the action); a unit whose skillset id is 26 is skipped when the ability is 154.
the learned bits are three bytes per job, read through the job index (Job_IdToIndex); slots 0..23 are scanned.
the function only names the unit and the ability; applying the learning is the caller's job.

notes: I: flags3 bit 5 (0x20) marks abilities that can be learned this way.
open_questions: ? what unit byte +6 bit 0x20 (tested together with the hit byte) and the hit byte's value 4 stand for.

name: sub_14030CF38
proto: int sub_14030CF38(void *item, int amount, unsigned short extraItem)
purpose: Adds an item's sale value to the gil total: a quarter of the item price, added to scene variable 44 and clamped.

behavior.text: It does nothing when the no-consume dword at 0x14186AF80 is set, or when the item record's +5 byte has bits 0x30.
When the caller passes a second item id it resolves that record and adds a quarter of its price (price >> 2) to the amount.
It reads scene variable 44 through SceneVar_Read, adds the amount, clamps the sum to 99,999,999 and writes it back with SceneVar_Write.
While the sale runs it also stores the amount at +0x3528 of the object at 0x143CD9DC0.
Two callers: Battle_ApplyActionResult and Inventory_ReturnItem.

notes: V: the cap 0x5F5E0FF is the same 99,999,999 limit the gil display uses.

name: sub_14030CFB8
purpose: Clears every pending status on a unit and refreshes the status icons.

behavior.text: It takes the unit pointer, stores the pending-status block at unit+0x1BE into 0x14186AF70, and ANDs five bytes at +0x1E0 (addressed in the body as (unit+0x1BE)+0x22) with the live status bytes.
It walks 40 status slots, testing bit 0x80 >> (i & 7) of the pending block.
For a set bit it calls sub_140278CF0(unit, index, 0) to clear the status and sub_1401FB064(index + 1, 0, unit id) to refresh the icon.
The unit id comes from +0x1BC and is passed to the icon refresh.
One caller, sub_140241128.

notes: I: this is the clear path of the status tick; the countdown reset is done by Unit_SetStatusCountdown elsewhere in the same tick.

name: sub_14030D1CC
callees: AbilityAction_GetRecord, sub_14002630C, sub_140278FA8, sub_14027FE20, sub_140281488, sub_14030D3F0
purpose: Builds and submits an item request for a reaction, temporarily marking the item as not consumed.

behavior.text: It returns at once when the no-consume dword at 0x14186AF80 is set, when sub_140278FA8(4) is non-zero, when the unit's +5 byte bits 0x30 differ from the stored flag, or when the unit id equals the stored actor.
It sets 0x14186AF80 to 2 around the call and restores it afterwards (site 0x14030D379).
It resolves the ability action record and the item, then calls sub_140281488 to turn the request into a unit action block.
It also calls sub_14030D3F0, the item damage and effect entry used by reactions.
One caller, Battle_TurnEngine.

notes:
V: the frame is 0x70 bytes and keeps a stack cookie, so it is compiled as a normal function rather than a leaf.
It rewrites byte 0 of +0x61 as `+0x57 | (+0x1EF & 0xF2)` (charge states cleared, under g_BattleSimulating = 2).

name: sub_14030DD8C
proto: char *__fastcall sub_14030DD8C(unsigned int a1, unsigned __int8 a2, _WORD *a3, __int64 a4, unsigned __int8 *a5, int a6, __int64 a7, __int64 a8)
purpose: Builds a unit's usable ability list for skillset a2 (ids plus cost, value, flag and availability arrays); sibling of sub_14030E368.

behavior.text: loops 16 skillset slots with Skillset_GetAbility(a2, slot); ids 1..0x16F take data from AbilityAction_GetRecord (byte 12 & 0x7F cost, byte 13 value halved when unit flag +153 is negative, byte 5 bits).

ids 406..413 take the kind4 byte 0 as cost: the byte is read from byte_140789280 at offset id*2 - 0x32C (0x32C = 2*406), after a range check that subtracts 0x196 from the id and skips results above 7 (unsigned), at 0x14030DF77.
the cost is halved or zeroed by unit status flags in byte +155 (bits 8 / 4) unless record byte 5 & 4; availability comes from sub_14030E2F0(unit, cost, ctx, 0).
writes ids to a3 (0xFFFF terminated), cost to a5 and parallel arrays a4, a7, a8; returns the count.

at 0x14030DEA9 it reads the ability's action record (AbilityAction_GetRecord, then byte +6); an id with no action record (a Charge ability) faulted the scene task at 0x14030DEC4 and the game froze (behaviour AFaultInAGameTaskFreezesTheGame).

name: sub_14030E010
purpose: Builds the battle command list for a unit: it reads the two command-set bytes, maps each command to its kind and lets the per-kind builder fill the list.

behavior.text: It resolves the unit through sub_14030DB88 and returns -1 when that fails.
It reads the command-set bytes at unit+0x12 and +0x13 and rejects a pair whose command kinds do not fit together.
Each command id is mapped to a kind through g_CommandKind (0x14067E010) and masked with 0x0F.
It writes a leading byte to the output and calls sub_14030E174(unit, kind, ...) to append that kind's entries.
Two callers, sub_1402371F8 and sub_1402EB174, the two battle menus.

the output list is a byte array (rdx): g_BattleCommandBytes (0x140D40838, from sub_1402371F8, which stores 0 there first) or g_BattleCommandBytesB (0x14184B2C0, from BattleCommand_BuildUnitList, call at 0x1402EB1A6); these addresses and the call site belong to the callers, the body only receives the pointer; the caller's pointer travels in rdx and r8 inside, so the prototype in the open database shows only the unit index.

list shape: byte 0 = 1; then the primary set (+0x12) unless it is 0 or 0x18; then the secondary set (+0x13) unless 0; then 2 when bit 0x40 and 3 when bit 0x20 of the unit's byte +0x9B is set (both only when +0x63 bit 0x02, Toad, is clear); then the terminator 0xFF. A unit whose +0x65 has bit 0x04, or whose +0x1B4 has bit 0x40 with dword_14185670C zero, gets the list 0xFF alone.

a unit with a monster set (0xB0..0xDF, tested as byte + 0x50 <= 0x2F, in +0x12 or +0x13) is answered early: the list is the primary set alone (0xFF after it), g_BattleCommandKinds[0] = g_CommandKind[set], byte_14184A9A0[0] = 0, and the function returns 1; every other path returns 0 (or -1 when the unit lookup fails).
afterwards, for up to 6 entries until the 0xFF, it writes g_BattleCommandKinds[i] = g_CommandKind[byte] & 0xF and byte_14184A9A0[i] = (sub_14030E174(unit, ...) == 0).

notes: V: the output pointer is advanced in place, so the list is built as a byte stream rather than an array of descriptors.

name: sub_14030E174
proto: int sub_14030E174(int unitIndex, unsigned char kind, int mode)
callees: Unit_ListArithmeticksAbilities, Unit_ListItemCommandItems, Unit_ListThrowableItems, sub_14030E368, sub_14030EA38, sub_14030EB44, and 2 more
purpose: Per-kind list builder: it dispatches on the menu selector to the item list, the throw list, the Arithmeticks list and four more per-command builders.

behavior.text: The selector is compared through a chain of subtractions, giving cases 0..15.
Selector 1 calls Unit_ListItemCommandItems (0x14030E297) and selector 2 calls Unit_ListThrowableItems (0x14030E28A).
Other selectors call Unit_ListArithmeticksAbilities, sub_14030E368, sub_14030EA38, sub_14030EB44, sub_14030EEF0 and sub_14030EFE4.

The unit argument is turned into a 512-byte record index (shift left by nine) and bit 1 of the record's byte +3 is tested at 0x141853D43 + index*512; when it is set, selectors other than 0, 5, 6 and 8 return 0 early.
One caller: sub_14030E010.

notes: V: the frame is 0x1A0 bytes with a stack cookie; the case that returns 0 early is the one whose command is not usable by the unit.

name: sub_14030E368
proto: char *__fastcall sub_14030E368(unsigned int a1, unsigned __int8 a2, _WORD *a3, __int64 a4, unsigned __int8 *a5, __int64 a6, __int64 a7, __int64 a8)
callers: sub_14023678C, sub_14027F270, sub_1402EA58C, sub_14030E174, Unit_ListItemCommandItems, Unit_ListThrowableItems, sub_14030E94C, sub_14030EA38, sub_14030EB44, sub_14030EEF0, sub_14030EFE4
callees: Skillset_GetAbility, Job_IdToIndex, AbilityAction_GetRecord, sub_14030DB88, sub_14030E2F0, sub_14030FFC4, __security_check_cookie
purpose: Builds the list of ability ids (with cost and availability arrays) a unit has for command/skillset a2; the shared worker of the per-command list functions.

behavior.text: a2 selects the skillset: 5..0x17 map by index (a2 - 5), 0xE0 via Job_IdToIndex(160), else it must equal the unit's byte +18 or +402; the available-slot mask comes from the unit's bytes +162..+164 (3 per job index).
loops 16 slots (`v20 < 16`) with Skillset_GetAbility(a2, slot); ids 1..0x16F take cost data from AbilityAction_GetRecord like sub_14030DD8C.

ids 406..413: the byte read from byte_140789280 at offset id*2 - 0x32C, after a range check that subtracts 0x196 from the id and skips results above 7 (unsigned), yields the kind4 byte 0 as cost, at 0x14030E5D9.
outputs a3 ids (0xFFFF terminated), a5 cost bytes and side arrays a4, a7, a8; returns the count.

the learned-slot mask for the skillset a2 is chosen so: a skillset 5..0x17 uses job index a2 - 5; 0xE0 uses Job_IdToIndex(160); a skillset equal to the unit's byte +18 or +402 (primary or secondary) uses index 0; for any other skillset, and for any monster unit (byte +6 mask 0x20), and when the index found is -1, the mask is set to all 24 bits, so every slot counts as learned (it is not the Squire bits).
its Charge test is at 0x14030E5D3.
the learned-bit group is chosen at the join 0x14030E55A; for a skillset id above 226 that is the unit's primary or secondary skillset the game's group 0 applies (an Archer's Squire bits were seen).

notes: Same body as sub_14030DD8C apart from the skillset resolution prologue.

name: sub_14030E94C
proto: __int64 __fastcall sub_14030E94C(unsigned int a1, __int64 a2, _WORD *a3, unsigned __int8 a4)
purpose: For a unit whose command is 21 (Arithmeticks), lists its ability ids whose kind5 mask intersects a4, 0xFFFF terminated.

behavior.text: requires command byte 21 and gets the ability ids via sub_14030E368(.., 21, ..).

for each id with `(id - 414) <= 7` keeps it when `a4 & byte_140784688[id - 414]` is non-zero (the kind5 real start 0x140784688 is loaded and the byte at that start + (id - 0x19E) is tested against a4 after the range check, at 0x14030EA09).
kept ids are appended to a3, terminated with -1; returns the count.

notes: None.

name: sub_14030EC48
proto: ? (writes text cells; takes a unit index and a selector byte)
purpose: Builds the usable list for a battle command: it checks the command kind and writes one text cell per entry for the menu.

behavior.text: It resolves the unit with sub_14030DB88 and gives up when that fails.

It looks the selector up in g_CommandKind (0x14067E010) and compares the kind with 6; for any other kind it writes 0xFFFF (the all-ones word, produced by ORing eax with -1) into the first cell and returns.
For kind 6 with unit flag +0x63 bit 2 set it writes the synthetic text id 0x16F and calls sub_1402BB060.
The cells it writes hold the item table id (or 0xFFFF, the same all-ones word) and ids that come from sub_140275860.
Two callers, the two battle menu builders sub_14023678C and sub_1402EA58C.

notes: V: the usable-list builder has two callers; id 0x16F is a synthetic text id, not an item id.

name: sub_14030FCDC
purpose: Finds the position of a unit's status in the 40-entry status display list and returns it, or one of the negative codes for the missing cases.

behavior.text: It returns -1 when the unit's second byte is 0xFF.
It calls the can-act predicate sub_14030FE18 first and returns -3 when that says the unit cannot act.
It sets the UI core dword at +0x347C to 1 and builds the list with sub_14030FFC4.
It scans up to 40 entries, comparing (entry & 0x1F) with the unit's status id from +0x1BC; a match returns the index and no match returns -2.
Three callers: PartyUnit_FillFromWorkRecord, sub_140226CA0 and sub_14039625C.

notes: V: the -1 / -3 / -2 are its return codes; the 40-entry bound is the 0x28 loop limit read here.

name: sub_14030FE18
purpose: Answers whether a unit can take its turn: a short predicate over four status flags and the display-list gate.

behavior.text: It returns 1 when the unit's second byte is 0xFF.
While the UI core dword at +0x347C is not zero it returns 1 for +0x61 & 0x40, and for +5 & 4 together with +0x61 & 0x20.
Otherwise it returns 1 for +0x61 & 0x60.
It also returns 1 for +0x62 & 0x81 and for +0x1B4 & 0x40, and 0 when none of the tests fire.
Two callers: sub_14030FCDC and sub_14030FFC4.

notes:
V: the three tests are +0x61 & 0x60, +0x62 & 0x81 and +0x1B4 & 0x40; the two extra branches are gated by the UI core flag.

V: the .pdata entry for this function ends at 0x14030FE46, so the +0x61 / +0x62 / +0x1B4 tests that follow it (up to the ret at 0x14030FE5D) are outside the recorded body; the bytes there are still part of this function.

name: sub_140311CB0
callees: ItemIcon_Set, and element/position helpers not read
purpose: Builds one icon-bearing UI element: it sets the classic item tile from the id, then positions and scales the element.

behavior.text: takes a context, an item id in the second argument, a source object and a short value in the fourth register.
calls ItemIcon_Set with the id into a stack icon state.
then reads several globals and converts integer positions to floats for the element's placement.
one direct caller, sub_140315B10.

the element is drawn as a quad from the state set by ItemIcon_Set, because the state is written immediately before the
  placement maths.
the meaning of the short argument and of the four globals read after the icon call.

notes: - V: head (about 0x100 bytes of read extent, not an operand) and the icon call were read; the rest of the 0x631-byte body (the .pdata size of the function) was not.
open_questions: - ?: the full element layout and the caller's four arguments.

name: sub_140315B10
callers: none found (reached through a UI table)
purpose:
Builds the elements of an item or effect panel: for ordinary items it sets the classic icon, and for one special category it
allocates and fills a block of effect entries.

behavior.text: has no direct callers; it is reached through a UI dispatch table.
reads a global mode and branches on it.
reads the item id from a dword at record +0x28 and looks the record up.
when record byte +5 is not 0x20 it sets the classic item icon from that id.

when the byte is 0x20 it allocates a 0xA00-byte block and fills 0x50-byte entries in two nested loops (the inner loop runs
  sixteen times; the outer count was not read), storing the block on the record.
the filled entries carry a constant byte, the item id and a per-entry value.
0x64D-byte body (the .pdata size, not an operand).
the 0x20 category is a special item kind with its own effect list, because the code takes a completely different branch for it.
the panel the elements belong to and the meaning of the mode branch.

notes: - V: both id sites and the special-category branch were read; the remaining maths was not.
open_questions: - ?: the record type and the dispatch slot that calls this function.

name: sub_1403166C0
purpose: Resets the shared text-cell buffer and rebuilds the action-name row of every unit in the preview table.

behavior.text: It points 0x141871698 at the static buffer 0x1418716A0, the 82-cell text buffer.
It clears the per-slot flags and writes two fixed packed words (0x84A700C8 and 0x84A9016F) into the block.
It copies the bytes at 0x140C6AD6A and 0x140C6AD6B into the block's state bytes at 0x1418724E2 and 0x1418724E3.
It loops over the unit slots, skips the empty ones (marker 0xFF) and calls sub_1403167E4 for each occupied slot.
It ends by setting the byte at 0x141873063 to 1.
Three callers: sub_14020DAEC, BattleLoad_StepFresh and sub_14030476C.

notes: V: 68 instructions; the row loop is driven by a slot byte compared against 0xFF, not by a constant count.

name: sub_1403167E4
purpose: Rebuilds one unit's action row in the shared text buffer: it collects the unit's candidate actions and writes their packed words.

behavior.text: The unit index scales by 512 into the preview table at 0x141853CE0; an empty slot (byte +1 = 0xFF) returns at once.
It rejects units whose command count byte at +0x1998 is 0x10 or more.
It calls sub_140316B04 to fill the candidate slots, then writes 0xFF00 into the row header at +9.
Each entry is built through AbilityAction_GetRecord and Action_BuildCurrentAction, the same packed action word the AI and the preview use.
Six callers, among them sub_1403166C0, sub_1401FB064, sub_14020A7F0 and sub_14020AD64.

notes: V: 205 instructions; the row is addressed by the unit index shifted left by four inside the 0x1418716A0 block.

name: sub_140316B04
purpose: Seeds a unit's candidate action slots for its current command before the action row is written.

behavior.text: It reads the unit's command byte at +0x12 (absolute 0x141853CF2 + index*512, record base 0x141853CE0) and branches on the item/throw command range 0xB0..0xDF (the upper bound is tested by comparing al with 0xE0 and branching below, not as a 0xDF immediate).
It marks the candidate record (0x88 bytes per slot) with 1 and stamps the unit index into the high bits of a word.
It sets the slot flags (bit 1 of +2, bit 0 of +3) and writes 0x80 into byte +1.
It calls sub_140316C90 and sub_140316D24, the latter adding up to 16 skillset slots per command.
One caller: sub_1403167E4.

the row of the AI command table (g_AiCommandTable, 16 rows x 34 entries x 4 bytes) is byte_141873038[unit slot]; the function writes entry 0 (command byte 1, word = slot << 10) for a unit whose primary set is outside 0xB0..0xDF (compared against 0xB0 and 0xE0), fills the row header at byte_141872E20 (8 bytes: byte +2 |= 2, byte +3 |= 1, byte +1 = 0x80, the rest cleared) and, when unit byte +0x06 bit 0x20 is clear, calls sub_140316C90 for the unit's two hand words (+0x20 and +0x24) and sets header bits from the result.

it then calls sub_140316D24 for the primary set (+0x12) and, when the primary byte (+0x12) is outside the monster range (the 8-bit test add 0x50, cmp 0x2F at 0x140316C16), for the secondary set, and ends the row with an entry of word (slot << 10) + 367 and bytes +2 / +3 = 0xA9 / 0x84 (one word store of 0x84A9) and, when fewer than 34 entries are used, the terminator 0xFF in byte +2 of the next entry. It returns the entry count + 1.

the two set bytes are loaded at 0x140316BF1 and 0x140316C1E (displacement 0x1853CF2 / 3 from the table base 0x141853CE0 = unit +0x12 / +0x13, so the offsets are not separate operands; the hand words +0x20 / +0x24 are addressed the same way).

notes: V: the slots have a 0x88-byte stride and are walked in a 16-slot loop; this page confirms their flag bytes.

name: sub_140316C90
purpose: A thin weapon-record lookup for a unit: it filters the empty and out-of-range ids and returns the weapon sub-record.

behavior.text: An id of 255 returns no record.
An id at or above 261 returns no record.
Otherwise it calls the weapon record accessor and returns its result.
It calls one helper and has one direct caller.
The two filters are what make it safe to call with a raw equipment word.

name: sub_140316D24
proto: __int64 __fastcall sub_140316D24(int a1, int a2, int a3)
purpose: Adds a unit's candidate action slots for command a2 (one entry per usable ability, or a fixed set for Throw / Items / Jump) to the AI slot table at word_141872598.

behavior.text: the command type (byte_14067E010[a2]) 2 adds fixed slots (ids 122.. and 125.. groups of 3) plus one more; type 3 adds one slot; other types loop 16 slots of Skillset_BuildAbilityList(a2, 1).
aux flags4 sign test at 0x140316F1D (the byte at 0x140787F87 + 8*id, i.e. byte 3 of the flags4 dword, is compared with 0): only ids whose flags4 top bit (byte 3 negative) is set are added.
for ids < 0x170 it also needs AbilityAction_GetRecord(id): byte 13 (halved by a unit flag) <= a unit word and record byte 6 bit 8 or 4 matching unit status bits.
ids >= 0x170 go straight to the sub_1403170CC(unit, command, slot) availability check; entries store id | (unit << 10) in the slot and the command at byte 2.

arguments are the unit slot (a1), the command (skillset) byte (a2, an int the caller loaded from the unit's +0x12 or +0x13; the offsets are the caller's) and the number of entries already in the row (a3); the result is the new entry count. The row is byte_141873038[unit] x 34 entries of 4 bytes in g_AiCommandTable (struct AiCommandEntry): word id | slot << 10, byte +2 the command, byte +3 flags.

command kinds (g_CommandKind[a2]): 2 adds up to six fixed entries (ids 122..124 when sub_1403170CC(unit, a2, 0) passes, 125..127 for 1; command byte a2) and one more entry when any of 12 further checks passes; 3 adds one entry (word = slot << 10, byte +2 = a2); 10 returns at once when the item record named by the row header's item word (word_141872E24, header +4) has type byte 10; 9 adds one jump entry (byte +2 = 18, word = slot << 10) when no list ability below 0x18F was added; every kind loops the 16 slots of the set's list (Skillset_BuildAbilityList(a2, 1)).

for a monster set (a2 - 176 <= 0x2F) the entry's flag byte +3 gets bit 0x08 for the fourth list slot and loses it for the others; the stores of the command byte are at 0x140316DE0, 0x140316E35, 0x140316E78, 0x140316E9F, 0x140316FFF (variable) and 0x1403170AB (constant 0x12, the jump entry).
a2 arrives as an int with the byte's value.

notes: I: flags4 bit 31 reads as an 'AI may use' flag.

name: sub_1403170CC
proto: int sub_1403170CC(int unitIndex, int abilityId, int slot)
purpose: Answers whether a unit may use one ability id: it checks the unit's availability flag and then the learned bit for that id.

behavior.text: The unit index scales by 512 into the table at 0x141853CE0; a set bit 0x20 at +6 makes the id unavailable and the function returns 1.
Ids 5..0x17 are accepted without a learned-bit test (the body tests `(id-5) <= 0x12`, so 0x17 is the inclusive upper bound, not an immediate).
Id 0xE0 is mapped through Job_IdToIndex on the unit's job byte at +3 before the test.

Otherwise the id must equal the unit's command byte at +0x12 or +0x192; then the learned bit is read from the array at +0x36 (byte id >> 3, bit id & 7), and the function returns 0 for set and 1 for clear.
Eleven call sites in four functions, all AI candidate or scoring code.

notes: V: the function tests the learned bit; the two command-byte comparisons and the 0xE0 mapping are part of that same test, not extra gating.

name: sub_14031EF70
purpose:
Initialises the item order state at the start of a game: it terminates the five saved item order lists, clears the whole
equipment order block, terminates its five lists, and re-creates the sort-field lists the menu sorters read.

behavior.text:
takes no arguments and is called twice from the main loop, both times in the world-init branch after the same preceding
  calls.
writes the value 255 into the first word of each of the five item order lists.

builds a zeroed 1010-byte template on the stack and copies it over the five-list equipment block, which clears all five
  lists at once.
then writes 255 into the first word of each of the five equipment lists.
re-creates six of the eight sort-field byte lists (the two remaining ones are static in the image and are not touched).
also writes a twelve-byte table of small values ending in 255 at a fixed address.
it does not touch the shared display list and does not fill any list with ids; that is the synchronisers' job.

because it clears the equipment block, any in-memory order state before this call is lost; the save load must run after
  it.
what the twelve-byte table is for; nothing in the order-list code reads it.

name: sub_140323D1C
callees: SceneTask_Start, SceneTask_Terminate, SceneTask_WaitFrame, sub_1402F7F4C, sub_1402F7E90, sub_1401FA648, BattleMsg_SetKind1, Item_CountOwnedAndEquipped, Item_GetRecord
purpose: Runs the crystal / chest window: lists the abilities the roll chose, asks the player to learn them or restore HP and MP (or announces a chest item) and stores the answer in dword_140D40958.

behavior.text: it reads the roll's result block through qword_140D40810 (set by sub_14020435C).

it builds the ability list from the result block's 512-bit set at +94: for each set bit (ability id) it stores the id plus 0x7000 (built as the byte index plus 0xE00, shifted left by 3, plus the bit number, so 0x7000 is not an immediate) in word_141873B30 (512 entries) and, from the 19 per-job sets at +177 + 64 x i, the first index i whose set has the bit, then stores that job's id byte (result +158 + i) in word_1437ACE40.
the list count is the number of set bits; the first page shows at most 8 entries.
result word 4 (chest): the item at result +92 is announced (text 4122, or 4123 when 99 are already held) and dword_140D40958 = 4.
result word 3: a menu (sub_14022CBE4) offers the learn list or the restore confirm; choosing the list and confirming sets dword_140D40958 = 1, confirming the restore sets 2, backing out leaves 0.
result word 2: only the restore confirm is shown, and it loops until confirmed (dword_140D40958 = 2).
a result word of 0 shows text 6204 and no choice; Unit_RollAbilityLearning never returns 0, so this was not seen reachable.
nothing is applied here: sub_140237FA4 turns dword_140D40958 into the choice word that sub_14020BFD4 acts on.
what the job word list is drawn as (icon or name) in sub_140321DB8.

notes: Corrects the earlier sheet (an item panel): this is the crystal window. Read in full on 2026-11-10 (static), except the drawing helpers.

name: sub_140324658
callees: sub_140323D1C, SceneTask_Start, SceneTask_Terminate, SceneTask_WaitFrame, Battle_TimelineBuildStrings, sub_140325E98
purpose: Opens one of three battle panels for a message-script command: mode 0 a panel through sub_140324970, mode 1 a 19-row list panel (sub_140321DB8), mode 2 the crystal / chest window.

behavior.text: mode 2 returns the result of sub_140323D1C.
it clears four task slots for modes other than 1 and 2 before starting.

sub_1402339A8 (mode 2) is a message-script command handler; the crystal flow reaches it through BattleMsg_Dispatch(12, ..., show = 1) from sub_14020435C, the command being the one sub_140237FA4 treats as id 105.
the link from BattleMsg_Dispatch to these three command handlers was not traced.

notes: Read in full on 2026-11-10 (static).

name: sub_140327004
purpose:
Moves the ten item order lists between a work record and the live arrays, in either direction. The record keeps the lists
contiguously after a small header, so one call can save or load all of them.

behavior.text: the first argument is the record; the second selects the direction.

direction zero copies the live lists into the record; a non-zero direction copies the record's lists into the live
  arrays.

the record holds the lists from offset 50 onwards in this order: five item order lists of 141, 30, 38, 34 and 21
  words, then the equipment block of 141, 30, 38, 34 and 262 words.
the copies are twelve inlined fixed-size moves, six per direction, with the sizes 282, 60, 76, 68, 42 and 1010 bytes.
besides the lists it copies a number of other record fields in the same direction.
it writes only the record or the live arrays, never both in one call.
the two callers are the pair that stores and restores a world-state copy, so this is their order-list half.
which game record the callers pass; one passes a static buffer, the other a variable.

name: sub_14032AB3C
proto: int sub_14032AB3C(unsigned saveIndex, void *rec, __int64 unused, int *outColour)
purpose: Finds the portrait code of a save unit record (by its marker byte, job byte and job row) and fills a portrait draw record with it; returns the code's low byte, or -1 when the code carries bit 8 or 9.

behavior.text: saveIndex below 0x36 selects g_UnitSaveData + 600 * index; a larger index leaves the record pointer null and the function reads its marker byte through it (a fault: no caller passes one).

the look index: a marker below 0x80 is the index itself; 0x80 (man) gives 2 * job - 52 and 0x81 (woman) 2 * job - 51 (Mime, job 93, two less); 0x82 takes byte +46 of the job row of the job byte; 0xA2 / 0xA3 take the byte at record +2 as job with index 0; job 91 gives index 130 and job 92 index 131 on the 0x82 path.
an index below 0xD3 reads the code word of its own copy of the portrait codes (word_140683A70); otherwise the code stays 0.

marker 0x82 ORs job row byte +47 << 10 into the code (the colour bits); a zero marker gives code 0; markers 0x80 / 0x81 with job 160 give code 104 (105 for odd markers), jobs 161 and 164 give 106 + (marker & 1); 0xA2 gives 108 and 0xA3 109.
a code with bit 8 or 9 set is refused (returns -1, nothing filled); otherwise PortraitCode_FillCell(rec, code, null, outColour) runs and its byte is returned.

notes: Rewritten 2026-11-08: the earlier sheet called this a text id builder for a script message; the code builds a portrait, not text. The bit 8 / 9 test is why a portrait code on this path is a byte: the code table could hold any 16-bit word, the function refuses every word above 0xFF except the colour bits.
open_questions: ? where the 0x82 marker's own sprite rows (job row +46) come from in play (special characters).

name: sub_14032ACE0
proto: int sub_14032ACE0(int64_t *pos, int *mode, unsigned *indexA, unsigned *indexB, char *pal, void *recs, int side, char *a8, int *outColour)
purpose: Builds the portrait draw records for one or two save units in a layout chosen by *mode, and returns the first unit's portrait code byte (sub_14032AB3C) or -1.

behavior.text: first sets the position words of four 136-byte draw records at recs (from qword_1408F3298).
*mode 0: returns sub_14032AB3C(*indexA, recs, .., outColour) and nothing else (the path Unit_GetSpriteSetId uses).
*mode 1: the same for *indexB, then *mode += 1.

*mode 2 and 3: two records (indexB, then indexA at recs + 136) with their positions copied into the palette words of pal; *mode 4 to 9: four records with per-mode offsets from the byte tables at 0x1406839D8 and 0x1406838E4 (mode 4 also sets bit 15 of 32 palette words first); *mode 10 or more returns -1. Then *mode += dword_14078D578.

notes: Only the mode 0 path was followed into its callee in full; the multi-record layouts were read for their structure.
open_questions: ? the screens that use modes 2 to 9 (sub_14032B1A4 is an event-script face window, I).

name: sub_14032B1A4
callers: none direct; a battle result/unit panel task
purpose:
A battle/result panel that copies the 0x141876E90 block into the 0x14078DDD0 render area and draws the unit's
equipment summary.

behavior.text:
It copies `xmmword_141876E90`/`xmmword_141876EA0`/`ymmword_141876EB0` to 0x14078DDD0/0x14078DDE0/
  0x14078DDF0 with four 16-byte moves (0x14032BFEF, 0x14032BFE0, 0x14032C004, 0x14032C019). The block's hand words
  at +0x24 travel with the copy.

It reads the record's +4 word and forms a cell value with a sign shift right by 15 (0x14032BFF6) and a mask by 0xBFE plus
  2. That is bit 15 of the **record's +4 field**, not of a hand word.
It draws six equipment rows from the record/block and uses `sub_1402EC3C8`/`sub_1402EC9D0` for each.
It does not test bits 14..15 of any hand word; the only bit-15 test is the record +4 field above.
The copy is the reason the block's flags reach the render area; the panel itself uses only the ids.

notes:
- V: The copied block is 64 bytes; the destination 0x14078DDD0 is a separate render staging area.
- V: The earlier census row for this function's bit-15 test was a false positive for the equip flags: the
  field is record +4, not +0x54.
open_questions: - ?: what record +4 is and why its top bit selects the cell value 2 vs 0xC00.

name: sub_14032EDB8
proto: _QWORD *sub_14032EDB8(void)` (event task; the task id selects the carrier)
callers: none direct; started as task 9 by `sub_1402BDC6C` and as task 10 by `sub_1402BDBC0`
purpose:
The flag-aware equip panel task. One function serves two screens: task 9 draws the five Outfitter candidate
words and task 10 draws the five hand words of the equip-screen copy at 0x141876E90.

behavior.text:
It reads the current task id from `dword_14184B22C` and branches on 10. Task 10 uses `xmmword_141876EA0`
  (0x141876EA0) and the five words at 0x141876EB4 (0x141876EB4); every other task uses `word_141876C50`
  (0x141876C50), the five candidate words `g_EquipCandidates` (0x141876C64) and `unk_141876C4E` (0x141876C4E).

The first branch also selects a different text bank (the 0x1437F8330/0x1437F6670 pair for task 10, the
  0x1437F9050/0x1437F74D0 pair otherwise), so the carrier and the font are chosen by the same task id.

The hand loop walks five words of the chosen carrier. For each, it masks the id with 0x1FF
  (0x14032F160), skips 0xFF and any value at or above 0x105, and calls the item text/icon path for the rest.

Before the id is used, the same word's bits 14..15 are extracted with a shift right by 12 (0x14032F178) and
  a mask of 0xC (0x14032F17D) and stored in `dword_14184B228` (0x14032F189) for the text draw. The word is
  not masked to ten bits first: the two flag bits are part of the same 16-bit carrier word.

The second loop draws five icons from the same carrier pointer and passes the whole word to
  `sub_1402E1604`; that callee masks again, so a flagged word is drawn by its low nine bits.

The function copies a 1,840-byte text block with `memmove` and clears two 0xD20-byte blocks with
  `memset`; it waits one frame per iteration and ends through `EventTask_Terminate`.

The bit-14 half of the two-bit value is not produced by the Outfitter: the candidate builder marks only
  bit 15. On the task-9 path the value is therefore 0 or 2, not the "cannot equip" mark of the shop list.
what the stored two-bit value selects in the text draw.

notes: V: task 9 uses g_EquipCandidates (0x141876C64) and word_141876C50 (0x141876C50); task 10 uses 0x141876E90..+0x2C. The hand walk is five words; bits 14..15 are extracted with shr 0xC and and 0xC (0x14032F178-0x14032F17D), the id is masked with 0x1FF (0x14032F160).
open_questions:
- ?: what the two-bit value selects in the text draw.
- ?: whether any stock task-10 carrier ever holds bit 14.

name: sub_14032F410
callers: none direct; started as task 10 by `sub_1402BDE0C`
purpose:
A two-row equip panel variant: it reads five display words at carrier +0x2E, not the five hand words, and draws

behavior.text:
Task 10 takes the carrier 0x141876E90 and the words at 0x141876EBE/0x141876EC2 (0x14032F495/0x14032F482);

name: sub_14032F9F8
callers: none direct; started as task 9 by `sub_1402BDEC0`
purpose:
The equip detail panel: it reads the five hand words at 0x141876EB4 and a second five-word array at
0x141876EBE, and draws both rows without extracting the top two bits.

behavior.text:
It reads the header words at 0x141876E9E and 0x141876EA0 (0x14032FB70, 0x14032FB93) to choose the text

The first icon loop walks five words at 0x141876EB4 (0x14032FF05) and masks each id with 0x1FF; it calls

name: sub_140332B48
callers: EventText_FindMessage, sub_140226208, sub_1402F8684, sub_14032A8A0, sub_14032ACE0, and 7 more
purpose: Returns the string pool that belongs to a text kind; the kind selects a pool, which is prepared and then returned by pointer.

Each case calls sub_1402BACCC with a fixed pool index (9, 12, 16, 22 and others) and then loads a global pointer.

Twelve callers, including EventText_FindMessage, sub_140226208 and the two scene tasks.

name: sub_140332C54
purpose: A shop row helper: it returns the party's total holding of the item shown in a shop list row, with a flag bit for whether it can be equipped.

behavior.text: It reads the 16-bit entry of the global shop list at the row index, masks it to ten bits as the item id, and asks the item total for that id.
It then tests bit 14 of the entry and, when set, marks the result with a high bit before returning.
The bit-14 flag is the list's cannot-equip marker, so the return value is a count plus a flag rather than a plain number.
It calls two helpers and has no direct caller.
Returning the flag inside the count means the caller must mask before using the number.
the id is masked with 0x3FF at 0x140332C70; bit 14 is tested at 0x140332C78 and, when set, bit 30 is set in the result at 0x140332C7F. The return is count | 0x40000000 for a greyed row.

name: sub_140332C8C
purpose: The equipped-count twin of the shop row helper: it returns how many copies of the row's item the party has equipped, with the same flag bit.

behavior.text: It masks the list entry to ten bits for the item id and asks the equipped-by-party count.
It tests bit 14 of the entry with a 0x4000 mask and sets a high bit on the result when the flag is present.
It calls one helper and has no direct caller.
The two helpers differ only in which count they ask for, so the shop row can show both totals.
the id is masked at 0x140332CA8, bit 14 is selected by the 0x4000 constant at 0x140332CB0 and the AND at 0x140332CB5, and bit 30 is set at 0x140332CBA.

name: sub_140332CD0
purpose: Fills the shop row's category text from the item in the global shop list.

behavior.text: It reads the shop list entry at the row index and masks it to ten bits.
The item record's category byte then indexes the shop's category text table, and two bytes of that row are written to the row's text globals.
It also writes a fixed 0xC000C value to a row state field, which looks like two packed text attributes.
It calls one helper and has no direct caller.
The category byte is the same one the equip checks use, so the shop's category text and the menu category agree.
the id is masked at 0x140332CEC before the item record lookup at 0x140332CEF; the entry's flag bits are discarded.

name: sub_140332D48
purpose: Draws the item icon for a shop list row.

behavior.text: It reads the shop list entry, sign-extends it from 16 bits and masks it to ten bits.
The masked id is passed to the item icon wrapper, which resolves the record and sets the icon tile and palette.
The resulting tile and palette bytes are copied into the row's icon globals.
It calls two helpers and has no direct caller.
The sign-extension is harmless because the ten-bit mask follows it, but it shows the entry is read as a signed word first.
the id is masked at 0x140332D5F before the help lookup; the flag bits are discarded.

name: sub_1403331F8
proto: void sub_1403331F8(unsigned char slot, int item, unsigned char flag)
purpose: Changes one equipment slot of the unit shown in the status panel, including the two-hand and shield-slot cases, and refreshes the panel afterwards.

behavior.text: the slot is the first argument, the item id the second, and a flag the third; the unit is the selected unit from the 16-bit global at 0x141811428, read through the party table.
it reads the unit's current word for the slot from the five-word array at record offset 0x54.
slot 1 has a special case: when the unit's word at record offset 0x40 is non-zero and the slot word is zero, the value used is taken from the record offset 0x54 word instead.
when the incoming item id is zero the function follows an unequip path, otherwise it follows the equip path.
both paths end with a call to Inventory_AddCount for the item that leaves or enters the inventory, then sub_140288590 and JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange.
sub_1400ED3E8 and sub_140336664 run on the paths where the slot change has an effect.
the zero-item case is an unequip because the function must return the old piece to the inventory, which matches the Inventory_AddCount call on that branch.
the slot-1 special case is the shield slot, because the code substitutes a second hand word when the shield word is empty.
the meaning of the third argument; it selects between two paths but its game meaning was not read.

the list entry is compared as a whole 16-bit word at 0x1403332DC and sign-extended at 0x1403332E2 before the id compares; nothing masks the flag bits, so a flagged entry can never equal a plain item id.

notes: - V: head and both branches were read; the exact inventory arithmetic at the tail was not followed instruction by instruction.
open_questions:

- ?: what sub_140336664 validates after the change.

name: sub_140333338
proto: int sub_140333338(unsigned char slot, unsigned int word, char learned_only_off, char refresh)
purpose: Equips one ability list word into an ability slot of the selected party unit (the Status screen's ability lists and the combat sets): it checks the word's list flags, strips them, and hands the plain id to sub_14028916C.

behavior.text: the unit is g_SelectedUnitIndex; the slot's current word is read from the party record at +0x5E + 2 * slot.
a zero word is accepted only when the slot already holds something (an unequip); otherwise the function sets byte_140D407BE to 5 and returns 0.
a word with bit 14 (0x4000) set is refused the same way; when the third argument is 0 the word must carry bit 12 (0x1000), else refused; a word with bit 11 (0x800) returns 0 at once.

the word is masked with 0x3FF and passed to sub_14028916C(unit, slot, id, 0); on success it calls JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange when the fourth argument is set, then sub_1403369F8(word, previous word).
sub_1403333F0 (a combat set) ORs bit 12 into the stored set word itself before calling it.

notes: - I: bit 12 marks a learned entry, bit 11 an entry already equipped or innate, bit 14 a greyed entry; the flags live in bits 10..15 of the list word, so ability ids above 1023 do not fit in the word.
open_questions: - ?: the meaning of byte_140D407BE's value 5 (a refusal sound or message code).

name: sub_140333974
purpose: A shop list gadget handler: it edits the shop's displayed list and emits the message token for the item it acts on.

behavior.text: It reads and writes entries of the global shop list, masking each entry to ten bits whenever it needs the item id.
Before editing it checks that the row index is inside the current list length.
One branch builds a 0x6800 message token from the entry's id, which is how the shop names the item in its message line.
The entry's other bits are preserved when an id is written back, so the list's flag bits survive an edit.
It calls twelve helpers and has one direct caller.
The edit-in-place pattern and the preserved flag bits are the shop list's own convention, shared with the row helpers.

the sell action tests bit 14 with the 0x4000 constant at 0x140333C58 and the test at 0x140333C5D; a flagged entry is refused through the error byte at 0x140333C62. The help token masks the word at 0x140333C14.

notes: - I: Read the list read/write and the token branch; the gadget's selection state machine was not traced.

name: sub_140333FE0
callers: not in the exported set; an equip screen refresh
purpose:
Refreshes the equip preview: it zeroes or fills the five candidate words, rebuilds the stat block, and compares
each unit hand word with the block to mark changed rows.

behavior.text:
When `a1` is set it clears five words starting at `g_EquipCandidates` (0x14033401E), including the fifth
  at 0x141876C6C; otherwise it fills them with `sub_1402875A4`.

It calls `sub_140287354` with `g_EquipSet`, the record, the unit's +0x54 and the candidates, then computes
  the two-handed word with `sub_140284998`.

It reads the block's +0x10 word (`xmmword_141876EA0`, 0x1403340E2) and compares each of the five unit words
  with the record's block entry; a mismatch or a zero entry sets the changed byte in the 5-row structure.

The comparison uses the raw unit word (`*v11 != ...`), so a bit-15 word counts as changed even when its id
  equals the candidate.
It does not write a flag; the candidate fill and the two-handed word are the only writes.
The block's +0x10 word is the two-handed value in this path, not a record field.

notes: V: zeroes five candidate words at 0x14033401E when a1 is set, otherwise fills them via sub_1402875A4; compares each unit hand word with the block and the two-handed word.

name: sub_1403343E4
purpose: Refreshes an item detail or help panel for the selected record and builds the help text id that the panel shows.

behavior.text: the selected index is a 16-bit global; the function compares it with the previously shown index and, on a change, calls the record and panel setters before reading the new record.
the record pointer comes from a global pointer table at 0x141800F50 indexed by the selection; its +0x54 and +0x5C fields are copied into UI state.

name: sub_1403348A0
purpose: Item-menu command handler: it reacts to the current menu command read from the UI core, opens the shop or the list, and advances the menu state.

behavior.text: It reads the dwords at UI core +0x3488 and +0x348C and returns 1 when they are equal.

name: sub_140334A48
callees: sub_1401AA494, sub_1400B458C, sub_1401AC284, sub_14028A138, memset, sub_1402AE264, sub_140288590, Inventory_AddCount, Item_CountTotal, ItemOrder_SyncGroup, sub_140338060, ShopEntry_InitFromList, sub_1401AB0C0
purpose: Refreshes the shop's equip-detail panel: it builds the shop row entries for the selected unit, synchronises the item order group and updates the counts shown beside each row.

the exact set of rows it walks; only the call sites and the three list-buffer reads were traced.

purpose: Draws a shop row's text: it resolves the row's item id and passes it, with the row's text context, to the draw call.

name: sub_1403358FC
callees: sub_1403368C0, sub_140336B88, sub_140336444, sub_140335604, sub_1400ED3E8, sub_1400ED4BC, Inventory_AddCount, PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave, Item_CountEquippedByParty, Unit_SpendJp, GUICore_FocusNode, Input_TestAction, and others
purpose:

name: sub_140336444

purpose:

name: sub_140336664
proto: void sub_140336664(void *entry, int index, uint8_t kind)
purpose:
Fills one row of the equipment list from the shared display list at a given index: the item, its price and count, and three
boolean flags the row gadget shows.

behavior.text: takes the output row pointer, the list index and a kind byte.
initialises the row from the display list entry at the index.
reads bit 14 of that entry and stores it as the row's "cannot equip" flag.

compares the row's item id with up to five equipped words of the selected unit record and stores the result as the

when the item's count check fails, it asks the inventory helper and a shop-entry helper for a fallback, and stores the
  result as a third flag.
ends by calling the UI routine that pushes the row to its gadget.

purpose: Runs one coded UI action for a menu screen: it sets a state flag, chooses a case from the code and calls the screen helper for that case.

behavior.text: the function takes three arguments; the first is the action code and the other two are values used by the cases.

it calls sub_1402CD758 with argument 0, then switches on the code minus 0x1B.

the cases are 0x1B, 0x1C, 0x1D, 0x2C, 0x2D and 0x2E (the body subtracts 0x1B then walks 1, 1, 0xE, 1, 1, so only 0x1B appears as an immediate); each calls a different screen helper (page change, list rebuild, close).
the 0x2E case reads a list count, computes a record address with a 0x5C-byte stride and calls the record handler.
the function returns no value.
it belongs to the same menu family as the item list screens, because the callers are the same screen tasks.
which screen sends the codes and what each code means.

notes:
- V: read the head and the switch, as part of the item text research.
- V: the 0x3800 constant here is the reason the function appears in the text-id site scan, but it is a state bit.
open_questions:
- ?: the code meanings.
- ?: the owner of the state dword.

purpose:

name: sub_14039684C
callers: the routine at 0x14033DE68 (five calls, groups 0 to 4; its symbol label is unrelated)
purpose: A second synchroniser for the saved item order lists. It applies the same owned/not-owned rule as `ItemOrder_SyncGroup`, but takes membership from `g_InventorySnapshot` instead of the live count, and reaches the lists through the alias table `off_140689C38`.

behavior.text: takes a group index from 0 to 4 and selects `off_140689C38[group]`, a pointer table to the five saved order lists.

the loop index runs 1 to 260 (`0x14039694D`); the entry word is compared with 0xFF and with 0x105, where the upper constant is the form 0xFF+6 built by the lea at `0x14039687E` from the 0xFF sentinel.
membership is the byte `g_InventorySnapshot[id]` (`0x1403968B8`); a zero byte means not owned, and the `& 0x3FF` on the index is redundant because the loop index is below 261.
`Item_MenuCategory(id)` selects the group: category zero maps to group zero, otherwise category - 1.
an owned id that is absent is inserted at index zero and the tail is shifted right; an id that is not owned is removed by shifting the rest left.
the list end is the word 0xFF or any word at or above 0x105; the insertion path stops at 146 entries.
afterwards it calls `sub_140286070(group)` for the equipment order list and tail-jumps `sub_140286160` for the obtain-order list.
this is the path used when the live inventory is not the authority, for example after a battle or a snapshot rebuild.
which game moment the calling routine belongs to; its symbol name is wrong and its own callers were not traced.

notes:
- V: whole body read. The order-list pointer table is the alias table.
- V: the stock order lists terminate at the word 0x00FF, not 0xFFFF.

name: sub_140396984
purpose: Fills the attribute part of an equip preview: which stats an item would add and which of them the unit already has.

behavior.text: It zeroes two words of the output record and keeps the item id in a 16-bit register.
The id is masked to ten bits for the record lookup and again for each sub-record lookup.
The record's kind byte selects the weapon, shield, armor or accessory sub-record, and that sub-record supplies the attribute and inflict bytes.
Each attribute index is compared with the unit's current attribute values so the preview can show the delta.
It calls five helpers and has five direct callers.
The preview uses the same sub-record selection as the live stat functions, so the two views cannot drift as long as both read the same tables.

name: sub_140396D08
purpose: Validates an equip preview against the unit's current equipment: it compares the candidate item with the item already in the slot and with the job's equip rules.

behavior.text: It reads the unit's hand word for the slot, masks it to ten bits and compares it with the candidate.
A candidate identical to the current item is accepted without further checks.
Otherwise it asks the preview equip check whether the job may equip the candidate, and the category check whether the candidate is a valid item.
It also tests a per-slot byte at +0x177 of the unit state, which marks a slot that is locked or already changed.
It calls six helpers and has three direct callers.
The locked-slot byte is what prevents two preview changes from being applied to the same slot in one pass.

name: sub_140396FEC
proto: __int64 __fastcall sub_140396FEC(__int64 a1, __int64 a2, __int64 a3, __int64 a4, __int64 a5, char a6)
purpose: Builds the item screen's 256-word list `word_141D32F00` for one category: it walks the item-id space, keeps the owned ids of the category, marks preview-unequippable entries with bit 14, terminates the list, and optionally applies the saved order list.

behavior.text: the loop index runs 1 to 260 (`0x14039711F`); an id is considered only when `g_InventorySnapshot[id & 0x3FF]` is non-zero (`0x14039702F`).
`Item_MenuCategory(id)` selects the category; the branch compares it with the requested group, including the special mappings 0..7 used by the screen.
when `a6` is non-zero it calls `Item_CanUnitEquipPreview(0, id, 2)`; for `a6 == 1` an unequippable id is written with bit 14 set, for `a6 == 2` it is dropped.
each accepted id is written as a word to `word_141D32F00`; the list stops at 145 entries (`v10 >= 145`) and is terminated with the word 0xFFFF, written as -1.
when the requested order is one of the saved groups, it calls `sub_140396748(group)` to apply that order list.
otherwise it walks the built list, drops ids `Item_IsValidId` rejects, and sorts the remainder with the comparator table `qword_1406931C0`.
the 0x3FF on `g_InventorySnapshot[id & 0x3FF]` is redundant because the loop index is below 261; the `0x3FF` on `v17[v19] & 0x3FF` drops bits 14/15 of a list entry.
the list is the item screen's display buffer, not a saved list; it is rebuilt each time the screen opens.
the meaning of the `a6` modes at the call sites; the comparator table's exact ordering.

notes: - V: read for the list build, the 145 cap, the terminator, the order-list call and the sort; the tail of the sort is not classified.

name: sub_140399A64

purpose:
The battle-side flag-aware equip panel. It draws the five hand words of the battle copy at 0x141D3B880, a
64-byte copy of a battle record's +0x30..+0x6F region.

behavior.text:
It takes its carrier from `xmmword_141D3B890` (0x141D3B890) and its five hand words from

Bits 14..15 are extracted with a shift right by 12 (0x140399E24) and a mask of 0xC (0x140399E29) and stored in

name: sub_14039DA58
purpose: Advances the calendar held in event variables 0x67 (year), 0x2E (month) and 0x2F (day) by a number of days and updates the 64 date-keyed bytes and records beside it.

behavior.text: It divides the day count in ecx by 365 (`imul` by 0xB38CF9B1, `sar 8`) and adds the quotient to event variable 0x67, the year.

It converts the current month and day (event variables 0x2E and 0x2F) to a day-of-year with the 12 month lengths at 0x140680FF8 (the last 12 bytes of the 0x140680F00 table), adds the remaining days and carries a full year into 0x67.
It walks the same 12 month lengths to split the result back into month and day, which it writes to event variables 0x2E and 0x2F.

For the 64 slots it adds the year delta to the bytes at 0x1411A7220 and clamps them to 0x63; slot 0 takes its month bounds from event variables 0x5F and 0x60, the others from the byte pairs at 0x1407B8130.
It walks the 64 records of 9-byte stride at 0x1411A71A2, tests the flag byte at -2 against bits 2 and 4, advances the byte at +0 and calls sub_140340FD0 with the word at +2 when the flags allow it.
It updates the 64 bytes at 0x1411A7140 with a 0x3F mask derived from the elapsed day count.
It does not read the instruction-length table or return an instruction address; the earlier text-cursor reading was wrong.
One caller, sub_14033EEDC.

notes: V: T2's live census never saw this reader run (readers_missed); it reads the 0x140D407B2 state byte, so it is part of the event-task family.

name: sub_1403D2450
proto: __int64 sub_1403D2450(__int64 a1, unsigned int first, int last, int forceNew)
purpose: Loads the byte range of chunks [first, last) of a chunked file into one of 8 cached buffers (or a single scratch buffer) and returns 0 on success.

behavior.text: a table of 16-byte chunk records at *(a1 + 16): size = rec[last].offset + rec[last].size - rec[first].offset (the three dwords at 16 * last - 16, -12 and 4 * first * 4); a 4-chunk step is used for the index (v13 = 4 * first).

no slot (-1): sub_1403D25A4 drops the scratch buffer, a new buffer of that size is allocated with sub_140011750 into qword +24 / +32; with a slot: sub_1403D26C4(a1, slot, size, first) allocates it (qword +328 + 8 * slot and +392 + 8 * slot, dword +456 + 4 * slot = first).
dword +316 = first; the data is read with MemFile_Read(*(a1), buf, rec[first].offset, size) when the memory source qword +304 is 0, else memmove from +304 + offset. Returns 1 on allocation failure.

its three callers pass the g2d.dat reader `qword_140D3AD58` (a 488-byte reader opened on system/ffto/g2d.dat by sub_1401E7C58): the chunked file is g2d.dat, 'YOX' header with the table offset at +8 and the entry count (2450) at +12, rows of (u32 offset, u32 stored size, u32 type 6, u32 0). Every caller loads one entry n as [n, n + 1), reads it with PackFile_ReadEntry and drops the scratch buffer with sub_1403D25A4.
