purpose: Answers whether rumour `id` may be listed in the tavern of `town`.

behavior.text: false when the Gossip row of the id is missing and the town test below fails; the row is read with UITable_GetRowByKey(181, id).
false when the row's condition (+36, a UserSituation id) is nonzero and UserSituation_IsMet says no.

true when the row's flag (+44, column always_listed) is nonzero: the rumour is then listed in every tavern, without the town mask and without its unlock variable 721 + id; only the +36 condition above still applies.
otherwise, when town >= 0, false unless bit (0x4000 >> town) of g_RumourTownMasks[id] is set; then true only when event variable 721 + id reads nonzero.

notes: The town mask table holds 64 entries; the unlock variable of id n is 721 + n (721..784 for ids 0..63).

name: TavernRumourPage_Show
purpose: Shows a rumour's text and picture.

behavior.text: the text goes through sub_14019EF74(title, text); 'ShowImage' / 'Default' by (counter (+4) and counter_value (+8) both non-zero).

the picture is the Icon row 21 pattern ('base/textureparts/base_%02d_uitx') filled with picture (+0x28); panel +1044 = 1 + shown; panel +1048 = 1.0f while the situation counter of +4 is still below +8.

name: TavernRumours_BuildList
callers: the tavern screen's task (through the task table)
purpose: Builds the tavern's Rumors list: walks rumour ids 0..63, keeps the ones the current town may show, and pushes each into the list widget with its new marker.

behavior.text: the loop runs over ids 0..63 (an unsigned compare of the counter with 64) and calls TavernRumour_IsAvailable(id, current town) for each id; the current town is the dword at 0x140D493E8.
for an available id it stores the word id - 14336 into the shared list of the tavern pages (g_ErrandBoardList) at the next position, with a range check of the byte offset, and 0 into g_PageListFlags.

it pushes a 16-byte entry into the list widget's vector (the widget at [[[0x143CD9DA8]+16]+328]+112, vector at +992): the id as a dword at +0, the Gossip row's fields +4 and +8 at +4 and +8, the new marker at +12, 1 at +13.

the new marker is the first byte of the id's pair in g_RumourNewFlags, read only when the low byte of the id, taken as a signed byte, is 0..63 (the test looks at the low byte, not the whole id); otherwise the marker is the value held in the low byte of rbp.
when the Gossip row's field +4 is nonzero, byte +13 of the entry is set to whether the progress value of that situation is below the row's field +8 (a quest rumour not yet taken).
the list showed The Corpse Brigade, King Ondoria III and The Fifty Years' War with their blue new markers, and the markers cleared as the cursor passed over each entry.

notes: The text, title and icon of an entry come from the nxd Gossip row whose key is the id (table 181), read by the widget when it draws.
open_questions: ? what sub_14019DCD4(widget, 2) does to the list (sort or redraw).

name: TexHeader_TableSize
proto: unsigned __int64 TexHeader_TableSize(const unsigned char *hdr, const unsigned char *hdr8)
purpose: Size of the sub-image table of a TEX file header: returns (low dword = bytes of the table after the 40-byte header start, high dword = 40), or 0 for a header that is not version 4.

behavior.text: returns 0 when hdr[4] != 4 (version). flags = hdr[5]. size = 32 * hdr8[0] (hdr8 = hdr + 8; hdr8[0] = number of 32-byte entries N).

when flags bit 0x01 is set and (hdr8[12] & 0xF) == 3: size += 16 * u16(hdr8 + 2). When bit 0x01 is clear and bit 0x10 is set and (hdr8[12] & 0xF) != 0: size += 24 * u16(hdr8 + 2). High dword of the return = 40 (the header start offset of the table).

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BA9B0). The TEX header layout (I, from this and the loader): +0 'TEX ' (0x20584554), +4 version 4, +5 flags, +6 byte (copied as an argument to the image create call), +8.. a first 32-byte entry whose first byte is the entry count.
open_questions: ? the semantics of the flag bits 0x01 / 0x10 and of the 16 / 24-byte extension records (I: per-array-slice or per-mip records).

name: TexHeader_ValidateCopy
proto: __int64 TexHeader_ValidateCopy(void *dst, unsigned int n, const unsigned char *hdr, const unsigned char *hdr8, const void *src, unsigned int srcSize)
purpose: Checks that a TEX header table fits and copies it: returns 0 on success, 2 for a wrong version, 3 for an entry count of 0 or above 255, 4 when the table is larger than the data available.

behavior.text: need = 32 * n; when hdr[5] bit 0x01: if (hdr8[12] & 0xF) == 3 need += 16 * u16(hdr8 + 2); else if hdr[5] bit 0x10 and (hdr8[12] & 0xF) != 0: need += 24 * u16(hdr8 + 2) (same rule as TexHeader_TableSize).
hdr[4] != 4 returns 2; (n - 1) > 254 returns 3; need <= srcSize: memmove(dst, src, need or 32 * n) when dst != src (the shorter size when neither flag bit 0x11 is set), return 0; else returns 4.

the Hex-Rays text shows only three arguments at the call sites (dst, src, size); the disassembly passes dst in rcx, n = first byte of the entry in edx, hdr in r8, hdr + 8 in r9, src and the size on the stack.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BAA14).

name: TextKind25_LoadPool
purpose: Loads the text pool that serves text kind 25 (base 0xC800): it sizes the buffer from the current pool count, allocates it, and reads one of five sectors into it.

behavior.text: the current pool selector is the dword at 0x141856930; a zero selector returns without loading.
a selector of 0x200 or more allocates 0xC800 bytes and reads sector 0x37C.

a selector below 0x80 reads 0x14000 bytes from sector 0xE0; 0x80..0xFF uses 0xE1, 0x100..0x17F uses 0xE2 and 0x180..0x1FF uses 0xE3 (the ranges are written as the compare bounds 0x100, 0x180 and 0x200).
the buffer pointer is stored at 0x141856938 and the allocation is checked for null before the read.
GameData_ReadSectors performs the actual read; the function returns without a value.
the three callers are the text decoder, the NXD loader and the second event text path, so the pool is shared.
the five sectors are size variants of the same text pool, selected by the pool count rather than by language.
what the selector at 0x141856930 counts; this body only compares it with the four thresholds.

notes: Whole function read (210 bytes). The address is one of the two producers of kind 25 text.

name: TextTag_CountedNounArticle
purpose: Counted-noun text tag builder that first adds an article or form string from a per-language table.

behavior.text: resolves the tag row with UIText_ResolveCategoryRow and picks the record string by the count: 0 plain (+16), 1 singular (+0), 2 or more plural (+8); then replaces '[n]' with the count.

before that it adds an article string from a per-language table (sub_1400F3F10(language, row)) chosen by the tag record byte +24: row 3 * byte for a count of 1 (singular article), row 3 * byte + 1 for a count of 2 or more; a non-zero byte +27 skips the article. A count of 0 uses no article.

notes: Name is ours. The record bytes +24..+27 are filled by UIText_ResolveCategoryRow from C_Mes_Id_Sample bytes +0x10..+0x13 and the matching bytes of Ability (columns noun_class, noun_number_form, noun_class_2, noun_prefix_flag), Item and PoachItem. In the stock data every Ability row holds 0, 1, 0, 0 in those four columns (M).
open_questions: ? which builder serves which language (the builder is chosen by the caller TextTag_ExpandKeyIcon from the language and the tag).

name: TextTag_CountedNounForms
callees: UIText_ResolveCategoryRow, strstr, sub_1400F40D8, sub_1400769EC, sub_1400F3E2C, Str_Format
purpose: Counted-noun text tag builder that adds a form string chosen by two record bytes.

behavior.text: same count rule as TextTag_CountedNounArticle (0 plain, 1 singular, 2 or more plural, '[n]' replaced by the count).

record byte +26 is the initial form index (replaced by 3 for a count of 2 or more); a non-zero byte +27, or a string containing the marker [t], skips the extra word that is otherwise put before the string (not for a count of 0); the form strings come from sub_1400F40D8(language, index) (UI table 0xE5, 14 per-language form strings per row).

after the string is written the markers [t], [p], [pa], [a] and [n] are replaced (the count for [n]; [t], [pa] and [a] by form strings of the same table, [p] by an empty string when the string has no [p]).

notes: Name is ours. The UI table id 0xE5 is read inside the callee sub_1400F40D8, not in this body.

name: TextTag_CountedNounIndexed
purpose: Counted-noun text tag builder that indexes a per-language form table with three record bytes.

behavior.text: same count rule as TextTag_CountedNounArticle.

block = 4 * (record +24 + 2 * record +26) of sub_1400F4430(language, index): a non-zero record byte +27 adds form 0 of the block before the string (singular or plural by the count); otherwise record byte +25 chooses the form: 0 adds form 3 and uses the singular string, 1 adds form 1 for a count of 1 and form 2 for a larger count, 2 adds form 2 and uses the plural string. A count of 0 adds nothing.

notes: Name is ours.

name: TextTag_CountedNounPlain
purpose: Counted-noun text tag builder with no article or form string.

behavior.text: resolves the tag row and picks the string by the count (count 0 = record pointer +16, 1 = +0, 2 or more = +8), then replaces '[n]' with the count.
reads none of the four record bytes.

notes: Name is ours.

name: TextTag_ExpandKeyIcon
proto: void TextTag_ExpandKeyIcon(void *text, const char *tag, const char *argument, ...)
callees: UITable_GetRow, UITable_GetRowByKey, sub_1400F39EC, sub_1400F3998, sub_1400F3F94, sub_1400F4200, sub_1400F4558, sub_1400F4718, UIText_ResolveCategoryRow, JobTable_GetNameText
purpose: Expands the in-text tags of the UI text engine; the 'keyicon' tag inserts the button glyph of a named input action. The same function dispatches the counted-noun tags.

behavior.text: for the tag 'keyicon' it loops UIKeyAssign rows 1..255 and compares the tag argument with the row's name string (+0x18); on a match it writes the glyph of that action with InputGlyph_AppendPadButton (action 57 asks for the alternate glyph).
other tags call UIText_ResolveCategoryRow and the four counted-noun builders (sub_1400F3F94, sub_1400F4200, sub_1400F4558, sub_1400F4718).
the tags 'jobname' and 'jobhelp' (compared as packed constants) take one argument pair {key, variant} and call JobTable_GetNameText with kind 0 (name) or 1 (help).

notes: Name is ours; only the keyicon branch was read closely.
open_questions: ? the other tags this function handles.

name: TextureLoadInfo_Alloc
purpose: Allocates and zero-initialises the 280-byte streaming state record of a texture load (the header copy, the image pointer array and the id array).

behavior.text: sub_140011750(280, heap, 8) with the heap from sub_14001A2EC(qword_140C696D0), retried once with sub_14001A2C4; null on failure.

fields: +8..+39 zero (first header entry), +208 = 0, +216 = &+208 (image pointer array: self-pointing means 'one inline slot'), +224 = &+40 (header buffer: inline at +40), +232 = 0 (u16 id array), +240 = 0 (descriptor array), +248 = 0, +252 = 168 (header buffer capacity), +256 / +264 / +272 = 0 (bytes read / current image / current mip / slice counters used by TextureResourceHandle_StreamStep), +276 = 0, +278 = 0xFFFF (single image id).

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BAABC); field meanings from the users.
open_questions: ? what +252 = 168 sizes (the buffer from +40 to +208 is 168 bytes).

name: TextureLoadInfo_Free
purpose: Releases a TextureLoadInfo: releases its images, returns its ids to the id allocator, frees the arrays and the record, and clears *pp.

behavior.text: images: for i < byte info+8 (the entry count): sub_14003ABD0(info+216 [i]) (release) and the slot set to 0; then the image array is freed (sub_140011804) unless it is the inline slot at +208.

the header buffer (+224) is freed unless it is the inline +40. The u16 id array (+232, count u16 +276): each id != 0xFFFF is returned with sub_140088674(qword_140C696A8, id) and reset; the array freed. The single id u16 +278 likewise. The descriptor array +240 is freed. Finally the record itself and *pp = 0.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BAB84).
open_questions: ? sub_140088674 / qword_140C696A8 (an id allocator for GPU image handles; see TextureResourceHandle_RegisterImages for the other side).

name: TextureObj_Commit
callers: CharaRender_BuildAtlasTexture, sub_1400CAF20, sub_1400CEB4C, sub_1403CA874, sub_1403D0F8C, sub_140415828, sub_140415D30, sub_14041E05C
callees: sub_1403D0BF8, TextureTable_Create32, TextureObj_Reset, sub_140011804, sub_1403C5F08, sub_14041FB00
purpose: Turns the pending source pixels into a GPU texture (or updates the existing one), then frees the source buffer and the loader object.

behavior.text: +76 != 0: sub_1403D0BF8(t, *(+24), 0, 0, +36, +40) updates the existing texture in place; the rest is skipped.

otherwise +64 = 0; bpp +52 == 8: texture index = 0 (no GPU creation); bpp == 32: index = TextureTable_Create32(g_TextureTable, 32, w, h, pixels); any other depth: TextureObj_Reset and return 0xFFFFFFFF. Stores +48 = index, floats +68 = w, +72 = h.

then frees the source buffer: when qword +24 is non-null, if dword +32 != 0 sub_140011804(ptr, 0, 0) frees it, +32 = 0; +24 = 0. If qword +16 (a 304-byte loader object) is non-null it is cleared, destroyed with sub_1403C5F08 and freed with sub_14041FB00(ptr, 304).
returns 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D0B10). Only 32-bit RGBA textures are created; 8-bit sources (palette indexed) get index 0 here (handled elsewhere: ?).
open_questions: ? what an index 0 texture means for 8-bit sources; ? sub_1403D0BF8.

name: TextureObj_Reset
callers: CharaRender_DrawFrame, sub_1400CAE10, sub_1400CE1AC, sub_1400CF1D4, sub_1401E7440, sub_1403CAB00, sub_1403D090C, TextureObj_SetSource, TextureObj_Commit, sub_1403D0E10, sub_1403D11DC, sub_140415D30, sub_1404175DC, sub_14060FD44..FDAC
purpose: Resets a texture wrapper: frees pending source buffer and loader object, releases its entry in the global texture table and restores the default state.

behavior.text: frees qword +24 (flag +32) and the 304-byte object at +16 exactly as TextureObj_Commit does.
clears qword +52 (bpp and +56 width), dword +60, dword +76, qword +36 (+36 and +40).
when dword +48 != 0: entry = g_TextureTable[+8 * index + 8]; non-null: sub_14003ABD0(entry) (release the GPU texture) and the slot is zeroed; +48 = 0.

sets floats +84 and +88 to 1.0 and fills the 4 groups of bytes at +96..+111 with 0xFF (word at +96 + 4k, byte at +98 + 4k, byte at +99 + 4k): a default tint / UV-rect state. Returns 4 or 0 (Hex-Rays loop counter).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D0C6C).
open_questions: ? the meaning of the 0xFF block at +96..111 (four RGBA bytes?).

name: TextureObj_SetSource
proto: __int64 TextureObj_SetSource(TextureObj *t, void *pixels, int w, int h, int bpp, int a6, int a7, char a8)
purpose: Gives a texture wrapper new source pixel data (pointer, size, bit depth): when the existing GPU texture has the same size and depth it is marked for update-in-place, otherwise it is reset.

behavior.text: when dword t+48 (texture table index) != 0 and dword +56 == w, +60 == h, +52 == bpp: dword +76 = 1 (reuse flag). Otherwise sub_1403D0C6C (TextureObj_Reset).
stores +36 = a6, +40 = a7, byte +80 = a8, +56 = w, +60 = h, +52 = bpp, +44 = bpp, qword +24 = pixels. Returns 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D0A80). Used by the character atlas builder, so this class is not UI specific; it ran on the Job Tree because the chara portraits / icons share it. Field meanings of +36 / +40 / +80 are ?.

name: TextureResourceHandle_BuildDescriptors
purpose: For a TEX file whose entries carry per-slice records: builds the array of 96-byte upload descriptors (one for the inline payload and one per record) and hands it to the handle's consumer callback (state 1005 = finish).

behavior.text: info = qword h+112; images = info+216, header = info+224. size/offset = TexHeader_TableSize when info[4] == 4, else 0; extra = (low + high) total and n = u16 info+10 entries.

allocates 96 * (n + (inline extra != 0)) bytes (heap via sub_14001A2EC / A2C4), zeroes them and stores at info+240. When the inline extra is non-zero, record 0 = {+8 = size, +16 / +20 / +32 = extra, +24 = &images + (info+248 - extra), +64 = 0, +72 = 0, +80 = 0}.

when (info[20] & 0xF) == 3 and n != 0: for each 16-byte file record (at header + 32 * N + 8): record i: +72 = (a / 4 != b), +8 = dword (rec - 8), +16 = dword(rec - 4) >> 2, +20 = dword rec, +32 = byte(rec + 4) & 0x7F, and by the low 2 bits of dword(rec - 4): 1 -> +64 = 3, +80 = the image object, +24 = the image's inner pointer (or its image view when the global byte 142C81C7A is 0 and the kind is 1 or 4); 0 -> sub_14006D730(record, image, count).

state h+84 = 1005; h+92 &= ~0x100; h+56 = 0; calls the consumer at h+48 (vtable +56)(consumer, records, count); returns 0x96080017 (no consumer) otherwise. When the header is version != 4 it frees the info and returns 0x96120005.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BAFE4); medium confidence on the name: the record meaning (96-byte upload descriptors) is I from how the array is passed to the consumer.
open_questions: ? the consumer behind h+48 (vtable +48 = read request, +56 = descriptors ready) and the record fields at +8 / +16 / +20 / +24 / +32 / +64 / +72 / +80.

name: TextureResourceHandle_Create
purpose: Allocates and constructs a faith::Graphics::TextureResourceHandle (144 bytes).

behavior.text: sub_140011750(144, heap, 8); null -> 0. CustomResourceHandle_Ctor, then vtable = vftable_faith::Graphics::TextureResourceHandle_1407203C8, +112 = 0, dword +128 = -1, flags +92 |= 0x104038, u16 +122 = -1, u16 +136 = -1, u16 +120 = 0, dword +124 = 0.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BAD34). +112 = the load info / image array, +120 u16 = (count << 3) | 3 flag bits, +124 = payload size, +136 u16 = single image id.

name: TextureResourceHandle_CreateImage
purpose: Creates the GPU image for one 32-byte TEX header entry by its type (low 2 bits of dword 0): 0 -> sub_1400873D8, 1 -> sub_14008757C, 2 -> sub_1400876A8, 3 -> sub_140087834, each building a faith::Graphics::Texture plus ShaderResourceView.

behavior.text: dword 0 = e. Common: v4 = byte (info+6) (the flag byte passed on as the usage argument), depth / array fields from the entry words (u16 +8, +10, +12, +14), dword +4, and a 'srgb-like' byte = ((e >> 3) & 1) * 2 or 4.
type 0 -> sub_1400873D8: view dimension 2 (or 3 when the array count u16 > 1) written as the byte before creation; i.e. D3D11_SRV_DIMENSION values TEXTURE1D (2) / TEXTURE1DARRAY (3) - I.

type 1 -> sub_14008757C (view 4 / 5 = TEXTURE2D / 2DARRAY, I). When info+20 has bit 0x10 set it first creates with a flag byte 4 (a second texture), returns that result when non-zero, then creates the normal one.
type 2 -> sub_1400876A8 (view 8 = TEXTURE3D, I). Type 3 -> sub_140087834 (view 9 / 10 = TEXTURECUBE / CUBEARRAY, I). Any other value returns 0.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BBC64). The dimension mapping to 1D / 2D / 3D / cube rests on the numeric view-type bytes in the four create functions (2/3, 4/5, 8, 9/10) matching the D3D11 SRV enum, hence I.
open_questions: ? the field meaning of the 32-byte entry beyond type (low 2 bits), the format bits at (dword >> 3) and the sizes (u16 +4 .. +14).

name: TextureResourceHandle_Dtor
purpose: Scalar deleting destructor (vtable slot 0): resets the vtable to the Custom handle, runs the base destructor and frees the 144 bytes when bit 0 of flags is set.

behavior.text: *h = CustomResourceHandle vtable; sub_140095E5C() (base dtor); when (flags & 1) sub_14041FB00(h, 144) (free with size); returns h.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BAE44).

name: TextureResourceHandle_FinishLoad
purpose: Last step of the TEX load (state 1005): moves the finished images from the load info into the handle and marks the handle ready.

behavior.text: info = qword h+112. u16 h+120 = (h+120 & 7) | (8 * byte info+8) (image count in the upper 13 bits); dword h+124 = info+248.

when info+216 (image array) == &info+208 (one inline slot): h+112 = *(info+208) (the image pointer itself) and u16 h+136 = u16 info+278 (its id), info+278 = -1. Otherwise h+112 = the array and, per image, the u16 ids of info+232 are re-matched by their dword keys against the array after the pointers and copied into the id area that follows the pointer array (the source ids are set to 0xFFFF).
info+216 = 0 (the array now belongs to the handle), TextureLoadInfo_Free(&info), state dword h+84 = 5, return sub_140096190(h) (base 'mark loaded').

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BAE84). The id re-matching loop was read from the decompile; its exact record layout is ?.
open_questions: ? the key dword compared at (v10 + 4 * i) (a key per image, I: the sub-image index or a hash).

name: TextureResourceHandle_RegisterImages
purpose: Slot 21 of TextureResourceHandle: when the handle's status dword (+80) is 1 (loaded), registers each of its images in the global image table under an id (allocating a fresh id when the stored one is 0xFFFF).

behavior.text: does nothing unless the atomic dword h+80 == 1. Always returns 0.
single image (count 1 and h+124 == 0): id = u16 h+136, allocated with sub_140088604(qword_140C696A8) when 0xFFFF and stored back; sub_1400886A8(qword_140C696A8, id, image h+112).
several images: same per image with the id array after the pointer array (h+112 + (h+120 & 0xFFF8)) and the image pointer (h+112)[i].

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BBB78). Counterpart of the id release in TextureResourceHandle_Unload.
open_questions: ? what the table at qword_140C696A8 is read by (the draw path resolves texture ids through it, I).

name: TextureResourceHandle_StreamStep
callees: TextureLoadInfo_Alloc, TextureLoadInfo_Free, TexHeader_TableSize, TexHeader_ValidateCopy, TextureResourceHandle_CreateImage, TextureResourceHandle_BuildDescriptors, TextureResourceHandle_FinishLoad, sub_14003E638, sub_14003E674, sub_14003E6D0, sub_14003E5D8, sub_14003E6A8, sub_14003E604, sub_14003E7C4, sub_140069C28, consumer callback h+48
purpose: Slot 17 of TextureResourceHandle: the incremental TEX file loader. Each call consumes the bytes the previous read produced and requests the next read: header, header table, then the pixel data of every image, mip and slice, until the images are complete.

behavior.text: state = atomic dword h+84. States: 1000 allocate the TextureLoadInfo (TextureLoadInfo_Alloc, failure 0x96120001), state = 1001, request min(h+64, info+252) bytes of header into the info header buffer (info+224); h+92 |= 0x100; h+56 = the buffer; the read request is the consumer callback at h+48 (vtable +48); no consumer returns 0x96080017.

1001 (first chunk): requires >= 8 bytes with dword 0x20584554 ('TEX '), byte +4 == 4, byte +5 bit 0x01, >= 0x28 bytes and a non-zero entry count at +8 (else TextureLoadInfo_Free and 0x96120002). Copies the 8-byte magic block to info+0 and the first 32-byte entry to info+8. When the count > 1 or info+12 / +16 are non-zero it sizes the payload (info+248 = info+12 + info+16 + ((2N + 7) & 0x3F8) + 8N), allocates the image array (info+216, 8N bytes, filled with the 0xFFFF id area) and, when info+16 != 0, records the payload tail in h+96 / h+104. Then uses TexHeader_TableSize to find how much more header there is; when the first chunk already holds it, validates with TexHeader_ValidateCopy, otherwise allocates a larger header buffer (info+252), copies what it has, sets state 1002 and requests the rest.

1002 (rest of the header, or after 1001 completes): TexHeader_ValidateCopy again (a non-zero result gives 0x96120002); h+120 bits 0 / 1 / 2 = (dword header >> 2 / >> 4 / >> 5) & 1; h+128 = header dword +24; then for each of the N entries calls TextureResourceHandle_CreateImage (failure 0x96120005, info freed); finally, when (info[20] & 0xF) != 0 it calls TextureResourceHandle_BuildDescriptors, else (when the table has an inline payload) goes to state 1004 with info+256 = the first entry's size and requests it, else straight to the pixel-data setup.

1004 / pixel data setup: sub-resource buffer = sub_14003E6D0(image, mip + slice * mips); null frees the info and returns 0x96120006. Size = ((w >> mip) * (h >> mip) * bytes-per-pixel (sub_140069C28), 4x4 block compressed formats use (w + 3) >> 2) rounded up to 8; state = 1003, the read is requested with h+56 = the buffer; info+256 += size.

1003 (one image slice's data arrived): uploads it (sub_14003E7C4 with the slice index = mip + slice * mipCount), then advances the counters in order: info+268 (mip) up to the mip count (sub_14003E638), info+272 (slice) up to the slice count (sub_14003E674), info+264 (image) up to the entry count; between images info+256 = the next entry's size; when everything is done calls TextureResourceHandle_FinishLoad. Otherwise continues at the pixel data setup.
1005 calls TextureResourceHandle_FinishLoad; any other state returns 0.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BB25C). Read from the decompile only: the file layout is this loader's, the registers lost in Hex-Rays (the image width, height and format of the size computation: sub_14003E5D8 / E6A8 / E604) were not recovered, hence the exact size formula is I. Error codes: 0x96120001 out of memory, 0x96120002 bad header, 0x96120005 image create failed, 0x96120006 sub-resource missing, 0x96080017 no consumer.
open_questions: ? the file format fields beyond those listed (+6 byte passed on, the dword at header +24 stored in h+128, flags bits). ? the consumer interface at h+48. ? the sub_14003Exxx image accessors by name.

name: TextureResourceHandle_Unload
purpose: Slot 19 of TextureResourceHandle: releases the GPU images of the handle (count in the upper 13 bits of h+120) and their ids, then clears the count.

behavior.text: n = u16 h+120 >> 3. n == 0: TextureLoadInfo_Free-style cleanup via sub_1403BAB84(h+112). n == 1 with h+124 == 0 (a single image): releases the image (sub_14003ABD0, h+112 = 0) and either (flag 0x20000 of h+92 set) creates a fresh TextureLoadInfo that remembers the id (+276 = 1, +278 = h+136) or returns the id to the allocator (sub_140088674(qword_140C696A8, h+136), h+136 = 0xFFFF).

otherwise (several images or a payload): releases each image pointer (sub_14003ABD0); with flag 0x20000 a TextureLoadInfo keeps the ids (+276 = n, +232 = the old array, h+112 = info), without it the ids are returned and the array freed through the allocator vtable +72.
at the end u16 h+120 &= 7 (count cleared) and h+124 = 0.

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1403BB9CC). The 0x20000 flag keeps the ids for a later reload (I).

name: TextureTable_Create32
proto: unsigned int TextureTable_Create32(TextureTable *tbl, int bpp, int w, unsigned int h, const void *pixels)
purpose: Creates a w x h 32-bit texture, copies the pixel rows into it and registers it in the global texture table; returns the table index (1..0x7FF) or 0.

behavior.text: finds the first free index i (i = 1.. while tbl[16 + 8 * (i - 1)] != 0; fails when i reaches 0x800). Only bpp == 32 is accepted (else 0).

descriptor {u16 w, u16 h, dword 0x10001, dword 660560, qword 1, dword 0x80000801 (-2147481599)} is passed to sub_14008757C(1, desc, 8) to create the texture; null returns 0. The texture's first mapped surface is obtained with sub_14003E6D0 (the descriptor slot at +0x38 comes back as the row pitch, I), each row (4 * w bytes) is copied with memmove, then sub_14003E7C4 unmaps.
tbl[8 * i + 8] = the texture; returns i.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403D1528). The slot walk starts at table+16, the store is at table + 8 * i + 8, so index 1 maps to table+16.
open_questions: ? the descriptor constants (format / usage flags) were not decoded.

name: Time_GetTimestamp
callers: App_RunFrame, App_ProcessMessages and 70+ UI/render/input call sites (see the IDB xrefs).
callees: Indirect clock-provider vtable calls (+8, +16); no direct game calls.
purpose: Returns a monotonic timestamp in 1/300000-second units. The value is derived from a clock provider's counter and frequency; callers divide by 300000.0 to get seconds.

behavior.text: reads the clock provider at `qword_143CD9BC8`; when it and its `+8` object are non-null, calls the object's vtable slot +8 and uses the result as the counter; otherwise the counter is 0.
calls the same object's vtable slot +16 for the divisor; when the object is missing the divisor is 1.
computes `300000 * counter / divisor`; a large period constant (`0x1BF647612F36`) is used to split the counter and keep the result monotonic across a wrap.
`App_RunFrame` divides the return value by 300000.0 to obtain seconds and uses the same value for the 1/60 s frame limiter and the second frame cap.
the vtable slot +8 returns the counter and slot +16 returns the frequency; the object is a platform clock provider.
the large period constant corrects for a counter wrap, not for a unit conversion.

notes: This is the project name for the timestamp source; the game's clock object is not otherwise documented.
open_questions: The concrete clock implementation behind `qword_143CD9BC8` and the exact wrap period.

name: TimImage_Parse
callers: EventCmd_SetRecordOffset, sub_140344B68 (two sites), sub_140371F68, sub_14037270C, sub_140372990, sub_14037472C
purpose: Reads the header of a legacy-container image (pixel mode, optional palette block, pixel block) into a small descriptor.

behavior.text: the argument points past the 4-byte magic: its first dword holds the pixel mode in bits 0..2 and a palette-present flag in bit 3.

with a palette: the palette block length is the next dword; its VRAM rectangle (x, y, width, height) is read from +8..+14 and its colour data pointer is +16; the pixel block starts after the palette block (rectangle at +4..+10 of that block, data pointer +12).
without a palette: the pixel block rectangle is read from +8..+14 and its data pointer is +16, the palette fields are zeroed.
writes mode, the pixel rectangle, the pixel data pointer, the palette rectangle and the palette data pointer into the descriptor; returns the palette height.

notes: Read in full (one small function).
open_questions: ?: whether the container is used for anything other than UI images.

name: TitleMenu_AddEntry
purpose: Appends one row to the title menu: sets the row's label by kind and stores the kind.

behavior.text: appends at index `count` (+216): sets the row's text node text id (+248, dirty byte +316) by kind, stores the kind byte, count + 1.
does not check the count against 6.

text ids (UI table, nxd id 19): kind 0 gives 2215 New Game, 1 gives 2226 New Game +, 2 gives 2223 Continue, 3 gives 2218 Load Game, 4 gives 2224 Music Player, 5 gives 2217 Select Version; any other kind gives text id 0. The strings were read in the stock English UI table.

writes the text id to `*(a1 + 24 * (count + 3) + 8)` (when non-null) and the kind to `a1 + 24 * (count + 3) + 16`. With six rows taken, row index 6 would put its text node at +224 (the last input tick), its button node at +216 (the count) and its kind byte at +232 (inside the 240 bytes, past the last field).

notes: Registry: TitleMenuEntryKinds.

name: TitleMenu_Build
purpose: Fills the title menu's rows according to the save state and the cleared flag, plays the matching layout state and shows the menu with the cursor on the row the agent asks for.

behavior.text: count = 0. The flag 'a save exists' is true when the save manager reports a save or an `AUTOENHANCED` file exists; 'game cleared' is the byte at `g_SaveManager`+888.

adds kind 0 (New Game) always, kind 1 (New Game +) if the game is cleared, kind 2 (Continue) if a save exists, kind 3 (Load Game) always, kind 4 (Music Player) if cleared, kind 5 (Select Version) always, each through `TitleMenu_AddEntry`.
the six calls of `TitleMenu_AddEntry` are at 0x1401C3555 (kind 0), 0x1401C3564 (1), 0x1401C3573 (2), 0x1401C357D (3), 0x1401C358C (4) and 0x1401C3596 (5, the last).
then plays the layout state `Menu<count>` (`Str_Format("Menu%d")`, `GUINode_ApplyStateAtFrame` on the TitleEnhanced node), arms the idle timeout (+230 = 1, +224 = now) and shows the add-on.
puts the cursor back by the agent's byte +90 (1 selects kind 0, 2 selects kind 1, 3 selects kind 3, 5 selects kind 4, through `TitleMenu_SelectKind`) and shows the hand cursor.

the menu has 3 to 6 rows: 4 for a game that is not cleared and has a save (New Game, Continue, Load Game, Select Version), 6 for a cleared game with a save. The add-on holds six rows and the layout file has the states Menu3 to Menu6 only.

the add-on fields at +216 and above (count +216, current row +220, last input tick +224, flags +228 / +229 / +230) are read or written at 32 instructions in the title code: TitleMenu_Build (6), TitleMenu_AddEntry (2), TitleMenu_FocusCurrent (6), TitleMenu_SelectKind (2), TitleMenu_IdleTimeout (3), TitleMenu_StampInput (1), 0x1401C410C (1), UIAddonFFTOTitle_OnEvent (2), UITitleMenu_BindNodes (1), UIAddonFFTOTitle_Create (6), TitleMenu_MoveCursor (2, through the +48 part at its +168 / +172); none reads or writes +231..+239; 0x1401C410C is another function of the title code that touches these fields, not a callee of Build.

the AddEntry calls are at 0x1401C3555 (New Game), 0x1401C3564 (New Game +), 0x1401C3573 (Continue), 0x1401C357D (Load Game), 0x1401C358C (Music Player), 0x1401C3596 (Select Version); `[g_SaveManager]` +888 is read by a byte load of +0x378 at 0x1401C3539.

it does not reset the current row (+220); it focuses it through slot 18 before showing the add-on, arms the idle timeout, ends the UI fade state (UIState_EndTransition) and shows the hand cursor; it is the title agent's way back to its menu (from its sink on event 65537 and after the other title screens) and ends with the guide bar hidden.

notes: This name replaces an earlier one (`sub_1401C34B4`, a sheet that described it as a save list builder); the save probe it makes (`sub_1400366B0`) only decides whether Continue is offered. 'Game cleared' is an inference from what the byte gates (New Game +, Music Player).
open_questions: ? how the byte at `g_SaveManager`+888 gets set (only its readers were read).

name: TopLevelExceptionFilter
purpose: The unhandled-exception filter installed by Startup_InstallExceptionHandling. It shows the localized 'an error has occurred, the application will close' dialog and returns 1, so the process terminates.

builds a six-entry message table with English, French and German variants, then selects an entry from `g_LanguageInfo+8` (language code 0..5; fallback 1).
when `qword_143CD9B40` is non-null, calls `sub_14007EB7C` with the selected message.
leaves the critical section, decrements the counter and returns 1 (EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER), which ends the process.
no direct caller; it is installed as a callback with SetUnhandledExceptionFilter.

name: TurnList_Build
proto: int __fastcall TurnList_Build(uint8_t *list, int mode, int fillCurrent)
purpose:
Builds the 40-entry turn-order forecast: simulates each unit's CT until it reaches 100, inserts entries sorted by
time, and adds the entries of pending (charging) actions.

behavior.text: clears 40 entries to `0xFFFFFFFF`.
unless `mode == 2` or `fillCurrent == 1`, inserts the unit currently marked active (`+0x1B8 != 0`) at time 0.

for each of the 21 records (`g_BattleUnitTable`, stride 512): skips units for which `sub_14030FE18` returns
  true (dead/removed/statuses); reads the unit's `+0x64`/`+0x65` status bits and its `+0x6C`/`+0x71` modifier
  bytes to raise the effective speed, and skips units flagged `+0x61 & 2`.

the time simulation: `ct = unit[0x41]`, `speed = max(unit[0x40], 1)`; while `ct < 100` add speed (halved by
  Slow via `+0x64 & 4`, x1.5 by Haste via `+0x64 & 8`), incrementing a tick counter; after the tick, `ct %= 100`
  and the entry time is `(tick << 8) - ct + 100`. Up to 40 entries and 255 ticks per unit.

a pending action (`+0x18D != 0`) adds an entry with `0x40`, its ability low byte and the charge time from
  `AbilityAction_GetRecord(ability)[12] & 0x7F`, at `tick + charge`; the ability id's bit 8 goes to flag `0x80`.

mode 3 (`a3 == 1`) is the AI prediction: it sets `g_BattleSimulating = 2` around the call (saved/restored by the
  callers `BTurn_PreviewAction` and `Battle_AITurnRun`); mode 0 is the normal timeline.
the tail is filled with copies of the last entry so all 40 slots are valid.
returns `-1` when nothing was inserted, else 0.

notes:
The IDB/exported name is `TurnList_Build` (kept: `symbols/functions.json` and the `TurnList_InsertEntry` sheet already
use it; renaming to a `BTurn_*` name would break those references). The low 5 bits of entry byte 0 are the unit slot; 31 (0x1F) ends the list.
open_questions: The exact tie-break of equal times (the insertion is a stable "first time above" shift, so equal times append after).

name: TurnList_InsertEntry
proto: bool TurnList_InsertEntry(int unit, int isAction, uint16 time, uint8 *list)
purpose: Inserts one 4-byte entry into a 40-entry turn-order list, sorted by its time key; a pending-action entry also carries the unit's ability (9 bits).

behavior.text: entry = byte 0 flags, byte 1 ability low byte, word +2 time; the list is kept ascending by time: the first entry whose time is above `time` and every entry after it move down one (the 40th drops); returns 0 when no entry was above `time` (list full).

byte 0 = unit (bits 0..4; 31 marks the end of the list); isAction adds 0x40; then, when the unit's command byte (unit work record +0x1A1) is 18, 0x20 and no ability; otherwise byte 1 = low byte of the unit's ability word (+0x1A2) and 0x80 when that word is above 0xFF.
so 9 bits of the ability survive: 512 is stored as (0x80, 0) and read back as 256 (Vengeance).

notes: The only writer of the ability byte of a turn-order entry (V: xrefs of g_TurnList and of the local lists of TurnList_Build's callers).

name: TurnPanel_FillUnitEntry
proto: bool TurnPanel_FillUnitEntry(int64 panel, int index, ... (19 arguments), _BYTE *set /* arg 16 */, _BYTE *countdowns /* arg 17 */, ...)
callers: sub_1400E5910 (from TurnPanel_SetUnitPanel with the unit record +0x61 and +0x66), sub_140106C54
purpose: Fills one entry (448 bytes at panel + 448 x index) of a battle turn panel: the unit's numbers, name and its status byte list.

behavior.text: the entry keeps a copy of the set (+38712) and of the 16 countdown bytes (+38717); its status byte list at +0x95C8 (count +0x95C4) is cleared, then the set is listed with StatusList_BuildFromSet and every status whose Status_ListCategory is 1 or 2, except 23, is kept as one byte.
the list is then compared with the one drawn last (+0x24C0 further on, count +0xBA84): a different count or byte marks the entry for redraw.
sub_14010C624 draws the bytes as icons (Icon row 0x16 with the byte), no names.

notes: Name is ours. Read for its status list only (the other fields are copied from the arguments). The status set is the stack argument at rsp+0x128 (a point after the list loop and before the compare is 0x14010C533).
open_questions: ? the meaning of the other 17 arguments.

name: TurnPanel_SetTag
proto: void TurnPanel_SetTag(int tag, int listIndex, int unit, uint8 entryFlags, unsigned int entryAbility)
purpose: Fills one tag of the turn-order panel from a list entry: the unit's portrait data and, for a pending action, the ability name.

behavior.text: the name: when entryFlags has 0x40 and not 0x20, ability = entryAbility + (entryFlags & 0x80 ? 256 : 0); ids 394..405 get no name; otherwise AbilityTable_GetRow(ability) gives the text (formatted into byte_143CDA780).
the rest comes from the unit's work record (shape through sub_14022AA88, HP / MP words +48 / +50, status bytes +494, +504) and goes to sub_1400E5814.

notes:
One of two readers of the entry's ability (the other: TurnPanel_SetUnitPanel). A census of this decode (the byte plus 256 chosen by the flag) over the whole exe finds three; the third, in TurnList_Build, only tests the result for != 0.

2026-11-08: the portrait face is an inline copy of SpriteId_ToShape (the code bound at 0x14021569D, the table read at 0x1402156A5, the cap register r8d = 0xCD set at 0x14021568B and compared at 0x140215786). For an unset code (-1) the value capped is the per-pool value from sub_14022AA88, not a table answer. Its list for codes above 0x9F differs from SpriteId_ToShape's at code 205 (no face here; run under unicorn). The bound is 0x9F and the cap 0xCD.

name: TurnPanel_SetUnitPanel
proto: char TurnPanel_SetUnitPanel(int a1, int a2, int unit, uint8 entryFlags, unsigned int entryAbility)
purpose: Fills the unit panel shown for a turn-order entry, with the pending ability's name when the entry is an action.

behavior.text: the same name decode as TurnPanel_SetTag (0x40 and not 0x20: entryAbility + (0x80 ? 256 : 0), then AbilityTable_GetRow), into unk_143CDA7C0.

unit > 20 returns through sub_140214F54; when the unit's record from sub_140260ABC is the acting one, the panel mode (dword_140C6B1CC) is 25 and no name was set, the name comes from that record's word +0x17A instead (AbilityTable_GetRow, or JobCommand row 18 for 394..405; the word is read as a full u16).

notes:
TurnPanel_ShowUnitAction passes the flags and ability byte of the unit's own pending-action entry in g_TurnList.

The portrait face is an inline copy of SpriteId_ToShape (the code bound at 0x1402150B4, the table read at 0x1402150BC, the cap register r8d = 0xCD set at 0x1402150A2 and compared at 0x14021519D). For an unset code (-1) the value capped is the per-pool value from sub_14022AA88. Its list for codes above 0x9F differs from SpriteId_ToShape's at code 205 (unicorn).

name: UI_FrameUpdate
callees: UIAgentCursor_Show, UIAddonFingerCursor_FreezePose, GUICore_BeginFrame, GUICursor_UpdateIndex, sub_1401D1148, sub_1403D6098
purpose: Per-frame update of the UI: sets the UI frame time, runs a pending cursor restart, updates the agents (the hand's glide) and hands the frame time to the GUI core.

behavior.text: when ui+13488 != 0: ui+13480 = dt * g_UIDataModule+28 (the UI time scale), ui+13484 = a second time value computed from sub_1401E8AC4 (not traced).
g_UIDataModule+28 is 1.0 in the table the module is created with.
it never changes (no other writer was found).
after housekeeping loops (not read) sub_1401D1148(addon manager qword_143CD9DA8) runs the addon load / show / hide bookkeeping.

agent = element 1 of the manager's agent vector (UIAgentCursor). When agent+128 == 2: UIAgentCursor_Show(agent) (which now takes the PlayLoop branch) and, when agent+132 != 0, UIAddonFingerCursor_FreezePose(agent+64). Then agent+128 = 0.
virtual +8 of every agent is called (for the cursor agent: GUICursorHand_Update through a thunk that first requires an active cursor widget); then agent+128 = 1.
sub_1403D6098(g_GUICore), then GUICore_BeginFrame(g_GUICore, ui+13480, ui+13484) stores the frame times the widgets read.

sub_1400B3770 and sub_1400B57FC compute dt as (float)((double)ticks * scale / 300000.0) from an object whose +8 holds the tick count and +32 a double scale; sub_140246078 passes a float it computed earlier (not read); the title scene start passes 0.
that object is the application's frame timer (app+1160 in App_RunFrame): App_RunFrame forms the identical expression from the same two fields.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1400E3B20). The database calls the first argument g_CharaRenderMgr at the call sites; its +13480 .. +13489 fields are the UI frame state, so the name is probably wrong (I).
open_questions: ? The frame timer's maximum step (timer+16) that clamps dt; the second time value at ui+13484.

name: UI_GetHelpSlotState
purpose: Decides whether the shared help-description slot is visible and returns a masked UI state word for the caller.

the two callers are the shop open path and the sell-list builder.
the help slot is the shared item-description id, so this function is the gate that hides the help panel when the slot is empty.
what each of the three mode bytes suppresses; only the zero test is read.

name: UIAddonFingerCursor_FreezePose
callers: UI_FrameUpdate (when agent+132 is set), UIAgentCursor_SetStatic, UIAddonFingerCursor_SetPose
purpose: Plays the main component's Loop state to its last frame and then stops every state of that component (the bob ends).

behavior.text: comp = GUIWidget_FindFirstKind1Component2(addon+24); GUINode_PlayStateAtFrame(comp, Loop, -1) (frame = the state's frame count), then GUIComponent_StopAllStates(comp).

the stop clears every enable byte (+104), so no later state application runs for these states; the nodes keep whatever the last application wrote. Whether that is the Loop's last-frame pose was not checked.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1401D3550).

name: UIAddonFingerCursor_PlayDefault
purpose: Plays the Default pose state on the Hand component (vtable slot 6 of the addon).

behavior.text: with addon+48 present: state Default of addon+48: +104 = 1, GUINode_PlayState. g_GUICore+1908 = 1 in every case.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1401D34B4). Default is a one-frame state of the Hand: IconHand position and rotation 0 (V, UIB data). I: the bob state writes only the position, so the unrotated glove comes from this state having played once.

name: UIAddonFingerCursor_PlayLoop
purpose: (Re)starts the idle bob of the finger cursor: shows the cursor widget and plays the Loop state of its main component from frame 0 with looping switched on.

behavior.text: sub_1401D1E30(addon, 0) first (GUIWidget_Show of the widget at addon+24).

comp = GUIWidget_FindFirstKind1Component2(addon+24), the widget's main component (the file's Widget component, which owns the Loop state with the link to the Hand's Loop); with none the function ends here.
state Loop of comp: byte +108 (loop) = 1 (set by this code; the file stores 0), +104 = 1, GUINode_PlayState: time, frame and previous frame = 0, running and dirty flags set.

GUINode_PlayState only clears the pause flag when the state is paused, so a paused Loop would not restart; nothing in the code read sets +107 on the main component's Loop (the Hand's Loop is the one that is paused, by the link).

the main component of ffto_finger_cursor.uib is Widget: 1920 x 1080, one Reference node CursorRef (to component Hand of ffto_common_cursor.uib), states HomePosition, Show, Hide and Loop; Loop is 40 frames with one state-link track (frames 0 to 40) to state Loop of CursorRef.

name: UIAddonFingerCursor_ResetGlide

then state Default of addon+48 is played (+104 = 1, GUINode_PlayState) and UIAddonFingerCursor_PlayLoop(addon) restarts the bob from frame 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1401D3694).

name: UIAgentCursor_PopRequest
purpose: Takes the last cursor request off the agent's request stack and applies it: mode, rest offset, static flag, show or hide.

otherwise the last entry is removed and applied: agent+72 = entry int +0 (mode), agent+80 / +84 = entry ints +4 / +8 (the offsets GUICursorHand_Update adds to the focused node's rect), agent+132 = entry byte +13 (static flag). Mode 1 or 2 calls UIAgentCursor_Show; any other mode sets agent+72 = 0, hides and clears the offsets.
when the entry's byte +12 is set, UIAgentCursor_Show is called once more unless the cursor widget is already active.

name: UIAgentCursor_Show
callers: UI_FrameUpdate, UIAgentCursor_PopRequest and about 30 other code paths (sub_1400FB3B0, sub_140119688, sub_140134B54, sub_140136654, Boot_Update, ...)
purpose: Asks the finger cursor to appear and to restart its Loop animation. In the agent's normal state the restart is deferred to the start of the next UI frame.

behavior.text: when agent+128 is 1 the call only sets agent+128 to 2 (a pending show); nothing else happens yet.
otherwise (agent+128 is 0 or 2) and when the agent has its addon (agent+64) it calls UIAddonFingerCursor_PlayLoop(agent+64) at once.

UI_FrameUpdate calls this function again at the start of a frame when agent+128 is 2, which takes the second branch. A show request therefore ends in a PlayLoop at the start of the next frame (a request made while one is already pending also plays the Loop at once), and the bob restarts from frame 0 each time.

the Job Tree code does not restart the bob itself; a call through a helper was not ruled out.
