name: UIAnim_ApplyComponentTrack
purpose: Applies a state track aimed at the component itself (target kind 4002, property tags >= 5031) as an animated component-effect property.

behavior.text: tags 5031 to 5034 (cases 0 to 3) do not animate a property; they append an entry to the state's entry list (sub_140400448; 64-byte entries, fields at +0 type, +4 track id, +8 start frame = track +12, +12 end frame = start + track duration (+16), +48 / +52 a value). 5031: type 1 = a jump marker (GUINodeState_Advance: playing past the end frame jumps to the start frame; the Hand's Loop carries one from 0 to 40). 5032 / 5033 / 5034: types 2 / 3 / 4 with the id at value block +80 (5034 also value +84 x 256 at entry +52), the entries GUIAddon_OnStateEvent turns into trigger calls.

switch on tag - 5031; value = 32 bits at track value block +84 (some x 0.01), curve from UIAnim_InterpToCurve(+80); queued with sub_1403F8708 on the component effect object (qword_143CDA2A0 + 5144) with a property id: tag 5050 -> 38 and 5051 -> 39 (decoded as the glow radius and strength: the Line states set 0 / 0 for Lock and Unlock, 4.0 / 0.5 for the *OnCursor states), 5052 -> 40 (x 0.01), 5053 -> 41; other tags use other offsets (5176.. = other targets).

notes: Property 38 / 39 = glow radius / strength is inferred from the values (0 / 0 idle, 4.0 / 0.5 on cursor) and the live layer records (radius 2.667 = 4.0 * 2/3, strength 0.5) (V/I).

name: UIAnim_ApplyTrack
proto: __int64 UIAnim_ApplyTrack(__int64 a1, int *track, __int64 state, __int64 node, __int64 part)
purpose: Converts one state track aimed at a node (target kind 4001, property tags 5001..5030) into a queued property animation on that node.

behavior.text: switch on tag - 5001; cases read the value block (track+28 offset) at +116/+120 (two ints), +84 (floats) or +4 bytes (colours), the curve from UIAnim_InterpToCurve(+48) and queue the animation with sub_1403F8708 under an internal property type (tags 5002 -> 3, 5003 -> 4, ...).
tags above 5030 are not handled here (default returns); they go through UIAnim_ApplyComponentTrack.

tag 5002 (case 1): the value pair is the two ints at value block +116 / +120, the interpolation id at +48 (curve = UIAnim_InterpToCurve), the key frame is the track's start frame (+12), key type 3 (node position); UIAnim_StoreKey stores it as key {frame, curve, pair}. So a position track with several keys becomes one key track whose key k holds the pair of file key k and the curve that shapes the interval from k to k + 1.

tags 5028 / 5029 / 5030 (cases 27 / 28 / 29) append state-entry records instead (sub_140400448): type 5 (state link) / 6 (state reset) / 7 (part trigger) with start frame = track +12, end frame = start + duration, name 1 = the target node's name, and for 5 and 6 name 2 = the string at value block +48 + the int stored there (the child state's name); for 7 an int at value +48. Data: the finger cursor's Widget component Loop state has one 5028 track, target CursorRef, frames 0 to 40, child state Loop.

notes: The UIB timeline tag table documents the tag -> value kind mapping read from the same switch.
open_questions: Only the switch head was read, not every case (?).

name: UIAnim_Curve
callers: KeyTrackBool_Eval, UIAnim_SampleFloatTrack, KeyTrackVec2_Eval, UIAnim_SampleInt2Track, UIAnim_SampleIntTrack, UIAnim_SampleColorTrack
purpose: Easing curve evaluator for keyframes: maps the position t within a key interval (0 to 1) to the blend factor of that interval. Curve ids are those of the registry UIAnimCurves.

behavior.text: the id arrives in the first integer register and t in the second float register (the decompiler shows the second parameter as an integer); every curve is evaluated in single precision (sinf, cosf, powf, sqrtf, float literals), and t is not clamped except where a case tests it. The callers pass t = (frame - key frame) / (next key frame - key frame).

ids 1 to 21: 1 step, 2 linear, 3 smoothstep t*t*(3 - 2t), 4 t*t, 5 t*(2 - t), 6 in-out quad, 7 t^3, 8 1 + (t - 1)^3, 9 in-out cubic, 10 t^4, 11 1 - (1 - t)^4, 12 in-out quart, 13 t^5, 14 1 - (1 - t)^5, 15 in-out quint, 16 2^(10t - 10), 17 1 - 2^(-10t), 18 in-out expo, 19 1 - cos(t * pi / 2), 20 sin(t * pi / 2), 21 (1 - cos(t * pi)) / 2.

ids 22 to 39: 22 1 - sqrt(1 - t*t), 23 sqrt(1 - (t - 1)^2), 24 circular in-out (sub_140402BB8), 25 back in, 26 back out, 27 back in-out, 28 elastic in, 29 elastic out, 30 elastic in-out (sub_140402C14), 31 bounce in, 32 bounce out, 33 bounce in-out (sub_140402CA0), 34 to 39 cubic Bezier easings solved for t (sub_140402D38). Any other id, and id 0, gives the step: 0 below t = 1, else 1. The full formulas are in the registry UIAnimCurves.
pi is the single-precision constant 3.1415927; curve 20 = sinf((t * pi) * 0.5) and curve 19 = 1 - cosf((t * pi) * 0.5), in that operand order.
the evaluator never rounds; the sampling functions that call it do (UIAnim_SampleInt2Track truncates to an integer).

notes: Owner-visible effects: UnitJob CursorOver (curve 5), Hand Loop (20 then 19). Callers earlier recorded as UIAnim_ApplyTrack were wrong: that function only stores curve ids, it never evaluates.

name: UiAnim_DrawFrame
purpose: Advances one widget animation by a frame and draws the sprite pieces of the frame set the current step names.

behavior.text: the animation state holds a sequence index (+4); the sequence list table (0x140693A50) gives a list whose first dword is the step count and whose later dwords carry a frame set id in the low 16 bits and the step duration in the high 16 bits.

the step counter (+16) increases each draw (unless a global pause bit, bit 27 of the world state dword, is set and the widget's own flag 0x800 is clear); when it reaches the step's duration the step number (+12) advances (wrapping to 0 at the end of the list) and the counter restarts; a duration of 0xFFFF holds the step for ever.
the frame set pointer comes from the language's frame set table: language 0 uses 0x1406935E0, language 2 uses 0x140693E60, language 3 uses 0x1406942D0, every other language 0x140694740.

for each piece (count from the frame set's first dword) the code turns the two piece dwords into one textured quad with the widget's screen offset; the frame sets for ids 41 and 42 use two extra offset lists (at 0x14071E9A0 and 0x14071E9A8) when they have four pieces.
this is the draw step of the animated cursor and icon widgets.

notes: Read: the whole function except the exact bit layout of the piece dwords.
open_questions: ?: the meaning of the piece dword bits; the two extra offset lists.

name: UIAnim_InterpToCurve
purpose: Maps a UIB keyframe interpolation id to the easing curve id used by UIAnim_Curve: n -> n + 1 for 0 to 35, anything else -> 2 (linear).

behavior.text: n -> n + 1 for n = 0 .. 35 (0 -> 1, 1 -> 2, 2 -> 3, ..., 35 -> 36); there are no other exceptions; any other value (negative or above 35) -> 2.
the Hand's Loop keys carry file ids 19, 18 and 1, so curves 20 (sin), 19 (1 - cos) and 2 (linear).

name: UIAnim_LerpColor
proto: uint8_t *UIAnim_LerpColor(uint8_t out[4], uint32_t c0, uint32_t c1, float t)
purpose: Per-channel linear blend of two packed RGBA colours with truncation and clamping to 0..255.

behavior.text: for each byte i = 0..3 of the two dwords: v = (float)(c1[i] - c0[i]) * t + (float)c0[i]; out[i] = (int)clamp(v, 0, 255) (compare >= 255.0 then take 255.0; compare <= 0.0 then 0.0; the final (int) is a truncation toward zero).
returns the out pointer. The four channels are treated alike (alpha is byte 3 of the dword).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1404022A8). Gives the byte-exact rule for colour keyframes: float math on the byte difference, then truncate (not round).

name: UIAnim_PlayStateTracks
callers: GUIComponent_LoadDef (the only code caller; an earlier note named GUINode_PlayState, which does not call it)
purpose: Converts the tracks of one UIB state record (a timeline) into the runtime state object when a component is built: frame count, loop byte, absolute flag, key tracks and entries.

behavior.text: state record +0 type (3 = timeline), +4/+8 tracks offset/count, +20/+24 target table, +28 frame count, +32 loop byte; a track's target entry 4001 names a node part.

for a type 3 record: state+88 = frame count, state+108 = the loop byte, state+111 = 1 (absolute: the sampled values replace the node's fields, they are not combined with them); state+104 = 0 when the loader's byte +33 is set.
each track (32 bytes): target entry kind 4001 -> UIAnim_ApplyTrack with the node part found by name; kind 4002 -> UIAnim_ApplyComponentTrack.

notes: Format documented in docs/reference/animations.md; the studio's timeline decoder reads it. It runs at load time, not when a state is played.

name: UIAnim_SampleColorTrack
callers: GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels, GUIComponent_ApplyAnimChannels, sub_140407DF8 (the four-colour kind-6 tracks)
purpose: Samples a packed-RGBA colour keyframe track at a frame: the key before t blends to the next with its easing curve through UIAnim_LerpColor.

behavior.text: i = KeyTrack_FindKey(trk, (int)t); i < 0 or curve id of the key = 0 returns 0.

for i < last: s = (t - (float)key.frame) / (float)(next.frame - key.frame); e = UIAnim_Curve(key.curve, s); out = UIAnim_LerpColor(key.colour, next.colour, e) (colour = the dword at key+8, read byte by byte). For the last key out = key.colour. Returns 1.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140408328). Colours are sampled per byte, so an animated alpha is interpolated and truncated like the RGB channels.

name: UIAnim_SampleFloatTrack
callers: GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels (rotation, opacity, floats), GUIComponent code (about 8 callers)
purpose: Samples a float keyframe track at time t with the easing curve of the key before t.

behavior.text: key record = 16 bytes: u16 time (+0), u16 (+2), u32 curve id (+4), float value (+8), value2 (+12). The first 4 keys are stored inline at trk+0..+63, further keys in the vector at trk+64 (index - 4); count at trk+72.

i = sub_14040222C(trk, (int)t): a binary search for the last key whose time <= (int)t (t truncated to an integer frame for the search); -1 (no key yet) or a key whose curve id (+4) is 0 returns 0 (the channel is not applied).

for i < last: u = (t - key[i].time) / (float)(key[i+1].time - key[i].time) (float t, not truncated); out = UIAnim_Curve(curve id of key[i], u) * (key[i+1].value - key[i].value) + key[i].value. For i = last, out = key[last].value (hold).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140407B14). The easing curve belongs to the key at the left of the interval.

name: UIAnim_SampleInt2Track
proto: char UIAnim_SampleInt2Track(KeyTrack *trk, float t, int out[2])
purpose: Same as UIAnim_SampleFloatTrack for a track of integer pairs (position and size).

behavior.text: key search and u as in UIAnim_SampleFloatTrack; for i < last each component = (int)((float)(next - cur) * curve(u) + (float)cur) (integer difference converted to float, truncating conversion toward zero, so a fractional position is dropped toward 0, not floored); i = last returns the key's pair unchanged.

behavior.basis: (disassembly; the decompiler hides the interval position)
behavior.text: the frame searched is (int)t; u = (t - (float)key.frame) / (float)(next.frame - key.frame) in single precision with the float t; curve = UIAnim_Curve(key.curve, u); x = truncate(fl(fl((float)(next.x - key.x) * curve) + (float)key.x)), y likewise. The product, the sum and u are each rounded to single precision.

returns 0 (the field is left alone) when no key is at or before the frame, or when the key's curve id is 0. The caller stores the pair with GUINode_SetPosition, so a position track yields integer positions.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1404080C4). sub_140408218 is the single-int sibling used for sort order and per-kind ints; sub_140408328 interpolates colours per byte.

name: UIAnim_SampleIntTrack
callers: GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels (its integer tracks: sort order and the per-kind int fields)
purpose: Samples an integer keyframe track at a (float) frame with the easing curve of the key before it.

behavior.text: i = KeyTrack_FindKey(trk, (int)t); i < 0 or the key's curve id (key+4) = 0 returns 0 (value left alone).

for i < last: s = (t - (float)key.frame) / (float)(next.frame - key.frame); e = UIAnim_Curve(key.curve, s); out = (int)(e * (float)(next.value - key.value) + (float)key.value), a C truncation of the float result; the int difference is taken in integers before the float conversion. For the last key out = key.value. Returns 1.
key layout is the one of UIAnim_SampleFloatTrack: 16 bytes, +0 u16 frame, +4 u32 curve, +8 int value; keys 0..3 inline, the rest at *(trk+64) - 4 entries; count at trk+72.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140408218). Same structure as KeyTrackVec2_Eval and UIAnim_SampleFloatTrack, with a truncating integer result.
open_questions: ? which node fields use the int track (see GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels).

name: UIAnim_StoreKey
proto: __int64 UIAnim_StoreKey(UIAnimLoader *ld, int *track, GUINodeState *state, element *target, int propType, unsigned frame, short word, void *value, int curveId)
purpose: Stores one keyframe of a UIB state track into the state's runtime key track for a target and property type.

behavior.text: the key track is found (or made) with sub_1404003F4(state, target, propType); sub_1404020E4(keytrack, frame) returns the key slot for that frame (nothing is stored when it is negative).
the slot gets: value (8 bytes) at key+8, word at key+2, curve id at key+4. The key's frame (u16 at +0) is set by sub_1404020E4.
the function ends with a call of the loader object's virtual +40 with (ld, track, state, target name, propType); what it does was not read.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403F8708). Property type 3 is the integer position pair (tag 5002); the key layout is that of struct KeyTrack.
open_questions: ? sub_1404020E4 (ordered insert) and the loader callback were not read.

name: UIBlur_BlurPassOrCopy
proto: char UIBlur_BlurPassOrCopy(UIBlurRenderer *b, __int64 layer, int srcRT, int dstRT, int slot, float sigma, float tail, __m128i *clamp, __m128i *rect, unsigned flags)
purpose: One Gaussian blur pass toward dstRT; when the kernel has 1 tap or less it degenerates to a plain copy.

behavior.text: returns 0 at once when b+308 (enabled) is 0.
taps = GaussianKernel_Build(sigma, tail, weights). When taps <= 1: if srcRT != dstRT it calls UIBlur_CopyTarget(b, layer, srcRT, dstRT, ..., filter 0, clamp, 0) and returns 0.

otherwise copies the rect, looks up the layer slot texture at g_Renderer + 8 * (slot + (layer byte +86 << 6)) + 24224 and the render target at g_Renderer + 40 * dstRT + 20832, and calls UIBlur_DrawPass(b, g_Renderer, RT object, slot texture, ..., sigma, tail, clamp, rect, &taps, weights, flags); its result is the return value.

notes: The name is ours. Same argument list as UIBlur_Pass (0x1403ACAB8) but the pass is a single UIBlur_DrawPass instead of sub_1403ACEBC. UIBlur_Run calls it as (ctx, layer, 32, 32, 37, radius * 0.5, 0.004, rect, rect, a12).
open_questions: Whether this is the horizontal or the vertical pass (there is no direction argument here); what the slot argument (37) selects in the layer slot table; the return value is 0 on the copy path and whatever UIBlur_DrawPass returns otherwise.

name: UIBlur_BlurPassSingle
proto: void UIBlur_BlurPassSingle(UIBlurRenderer *b, __int64 layer, int slotA, __int64 unused, int rtB, float sigma, float tail, __m128i *clamp, int a9, unsigned flags)
purpose: Variant of UIBlur_BlurPassOrCopy that always draws: builds the Gaussian kernel and hands one textured pass to sub_1403AD710.

behavior.text: does nothing when b+308 (enabled) is 0.

taps = GaussianKernel_Build(sigma, tail, weights); looks up the slot texture g_Renderer + 8 * (slotA + (layer byte +86 << 6)) + 24224 and the render target g_Renderer + 40 * rtB + 20832, and calls sub_1403AD710(b, slot texture, 5 * rtB, slotA + (layer byte +86 << 6), RT object, sigma, tail, clamp, ..., &taps, ..., flags).
there is no copy fallback and no return value; the tap count is passed on even when it is 1 or less.
ShaderSelector_SetDigit slot 1 = (clamp == null), slot 0 = flags (0 when -1), slot 2 = taps - 2 clamped to 7; then it applies the shader and queues the draw.

notes: The name is ours.
open_questions: Whether this is the horizontal or the vertical blur (no direction argument; the hypothesis is unverified); the meaning of the 5 * rtB argument; some arguments (rect, weights) are not clearly recovered in the decompile.

name: UIBlur_CopyTarget
proto: void UIBlur_CopyTarget(UIBlurRenderer *b, __int64 layer, int srcSlot, int dstRT, int unused, int filterIdx, __m128i *srcRect, __int64 flag)
callees: ShaderSelector_SetDigit, ShaderSelector_Apply, sub_14003E120, sub_14003E228, sub_14003E5D8, sub_14003E604, sub_14003F794, sub_140069A38, RenderState_PackCommand, sub_140069980
purpose: Draws a layer slot texture into a render target with a chosen filter index; the copy used between blur stages.

behavior.text: returns when b+308 (enabled) is 0. dstRT 64 selects the layer's own target (g_Renderer + 40 * layer byte +86 + 23392); other values index g_Renderer + 40 * dstRT + 20832. The source texture is the slot g_Renderer + 8 * (srcSlot + (layer byte +86 << 6)) + 24224.

binds the source (render state +96 / +144, its format bits into state+124 bits 9..11), then ShaderSelector_SetDigit(b+32, 0, 1) and, for filterIdx 0, 1 or 2, ShaderSelector_SetDigit(b+32, 1, filterIdx); any other filterIdx leaves slot 1 unchanged.

srcRect and flag are optional. With srcRect the rectangle is scaled by the texture size into state +80 (state flag +112 bit 4 set); with neither, the constant xmmword_140723990 is written as the full-surface coordinates; the flag with srcRect also fills two more per-texel-size constants.

finishes by binding the destination texture (state +1608 + 8 * index), resetting the state words (+124 mask, 0x6000) and queueing a draw command (sub_140069A38 size 96, header 3, RenderState_PackCommand, sub_140069980).

notes: The name is ours. The filter index is only a selector digit (slot 1); which sampler or shader variant each of 0 / 1 / 2 is was not traced. The decompile loses the arguments of some inlined helpers (texture size lookups).
open_questions: What the filter values 0, 1, 2 mean; the 5th argument (unused in the decompile); what the sub_14003E5D8 / sub_14003E604 results are (texture width / height ?); the layout of the 96-byte command.

name: UIBlur_DownsampleDispatch
proto: void UIBlur_DownsampleDispatch(__int64 obj, __int64 stateCtx, __int64 layer, int rtIndex, int *rect, int levels, __m128i *clamp)
purpose: Queues the tiled downsample of a rectangle by 2^levels (compute-style dispatch over 64-pixel tiles); the work done by UIBlur_DownsampleRegion.

behavior.text: only when levels > 0. Binds RT[rtIndex] (g_Renderer + 40 * rtIndex + 20832, handle +40) at state + 8 * (short obj+18) + 1608 (the output) and the object's constant buffer (obj+8) at state + 8 * (short obj+16) + 328.

tile arithmetic (integers): tx0 = rect.x0 >> 6, ty0 = rect.y0 >> 6, tilesX = ((rect.x1 - 1) >> 6) - tx0 + 1, tilesY likewise; constant record: [0] = levels, [4] = tilesX * tilesY, [8] = tx0, [12] = ty0, [16] = (1 / renderW, 1 / renderH) (floats; both 1.0 when the render size is <= 1.19e-7), [32..47] = clamp rectangle copy, [48..63] = (x0 >> levels, y0 >> levels, x1 >> levels, y1 >> levels) (arithmetic shifts, i.e. floor).

source texture = slot 3 table entry of the layer (800 * layer byte +86 + g_Renderer + 24184, handle +40), sampler constants of the selected program copied to state + 5704 + 4 * id (& 0x7FFFFFFF), ShaderSelector_Apply(selector at +128 of the UI renderer table, state, 0), then sub_1403C49B0(state, tilesX, tilesY, 1) (the dispatch) and obj+28 = 1.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403B01F0). Pixel snapping: the downsampled rectangle is floor(rect / 2^levels) with right / bottom floored too, so odd sizes lose a pixel at the far edge; the tile grid is 64 px aligned.
open_questions: Exact semantics of sub_1403C49B0 (dispatch vs draw).

name: UIBlur_DownsampleRegion
proto: __int64 UIBlur_DownsampleRegion(__int64 unused, __int64 stateCtx, __int64 layer, int srcRT, int *rect, int targetId, __m128i *clamp)
purpose: Wrapper for the half-size path of UIBlur_Run: converts the target id into a level count, runs sub_1403B01F0 on the downsample object and returns the level count used.

behavior.text: obj = *(*(g_Renderer + 37936) + 8608); levels = min(targetId - 31, *(int *)(obj + 24)). With targetId = 32 that is 1.
copies the 16-byte clamp rectangle to the stack and calls sub_1403B01F0(obj, stateCtx, layer, srcRT, rect, levels, &clamp); returns levels.

binds RT[srcRT] (g_Renderer + 20832 + 40 * srcRT, texture at +40) as an input, queues a constant record (levels, tile count, tile origin = rect >> 6, 1 / size read at g_Renderer+37936 -> +6568, the clamp rectangle, rect >> levels), applies a shader through ShaderSelector_Apply, calls sub_1403C49B0(state, tilesX, tilesY, 1) with the rect counted in 64 px tiles, and sets obj+28 = 1.
the effect is a copy that downsamples the rect by 2^levels; the destination is the layer's own slot (800 * layer byte +86 + g_Renderer + 24184), not chosen by the id argument.

notes: The name is ours (from the call context and the >> levels arithmetic; not verified live). The first argument is unused.
open_questions: What sub_1403C49B0 does (a draw or a dispatch over a tile grid); whether the destination really is render target 32 (only the level count is derived from the id here); what obj+24 (maximum level) holds.

name: UIBlur_DrawPass
proto: char __fastcall UIBlur_DrawPass(__int64 blur, __int64 layer, __int64 srcTex, __int64 dstTarget, int a5, float sigma, float cutoff, __m128i *rect, __m128i *colour, int *tapsIn, _OWORD *kernelIn, int mode)
callees: GaussianKernel_Build, sub_14003E120 (map), sub_14003E228 (unmap), sub_14003E604, sub_14003E5D8, ShaderSelector_SetDigit, ShaderSelector_Apply, sub_140069A38 (alloc cmd), RenderState_PackCommand, sub_140069980 (submit)
purpose: Draws one direction of the separable Gaussian blur: uploads the cGaussianBlurPS constants (sigma, cutoff, tap count and the 64 weights), selects the shader permutation by tap count and records a draw command.

behavior.text: returns 0 if *(u8*)(blur+308) == 0. mode = a12, where -1 is treated as 0. ts = thread state *(TLS+56) (the per-thread draw state, cf. UIRender_FlushBatch).
tap count: from *tapsIn if a10 given (kernel from a11), else GaussianKernel_Build(sigma, cutoff, local 256 bytes) and uses that.

constant buffer: map = sub_14003E120(*(blur+56), 2) (map, type 2). Writes sigma at +0, cutoff at +4, taps at +8 (dword), and copies the 64 weights (16 x 16 bytes = 256 bytes) starting at +16. Then unmap sub_14003E228(*(blur+56)). Buffer id stored at blur+56 (created with 0x400 flags in UIRender_LoadShaders path of the shared blur: see CreateBuffers cSDF-style 32-byte layout; ? the blur constant buffer size).

shader selector (blur+48) digits: digit 1 = (rect == null) (1 when no rect/scissor), digit 0 = mode, digit 2 = taps-2 clamped to 7 when (taps-2) > 6 as unsigned (so taps 2..8 select permutations 0..6 and any bigger count, 9 or more, selects 7).

state setup on ts: ts+96 (v17[6]) = dstTarget, ts+144 (v17[9]) = *(dstTarget+40); format-type field of that object (+8 == 1 or 2) takes its dword at +16 and puts (v & 7) into bits 9..11 of ts+124; per-slot values from the shader's table at *(shader+160) (u16 slot ids) and *(shader+168) (dwords) are written masked & 0x7FFFFFFF into ts + 16*356 + 8 + 4*slot (resource slots).

after ShaderSelector_Apply: source texture *(srcTex+40) stored at ts+1600 + 8*(*(s16*)(blur+252)+1) (texture slot); if rect != null: ts+112 flags |= 0x10 (& 0xFFFF1FFF), ts+80 = *rect (16 bytes). ts+124 &= 0xFFC06FFF | 0x6000 (draw-call type bits set to 6 in the 0x6000 field, i.e. same field UIRender_FlushBatch sets to 2 / 5). Constant buffer bound at ts+320 + 8*(*(s16*)(blur+292)+1) = *(blur+56).
allocates a 96-byte command with sub_140069A38(ts, 4, 96); sets *(cmd+8) = 3, packs state with RenderState_PackCommand(cmd+16) and submits with sub_140069980. Returns 1.

colour a9 is copied to ts+272 (v17[17]) and ts+60-ish word 3 gets sub_14003E5D8 result added: v27->m128i_i32[3] (ts+12) = result of sub_14003E5D8 + v26 (? two sub-results added; not resolvable from the decompile, registers lost).

notes: The constant layout uploaded to the GPU is: float sigma, float cutoff, int taps, pad dword, then 64 floats at +16 (total >= 272 bytes: 16 + 256). Gaussian weights are therefore NOT computed in the shader; the shader loops over `taps` entries.
open_questions: ? the unsplit decompile of sub_14003E604 / 5D8 arguments (ts+12 write uses lost registers). ? size of the blur cbuffer (struct above is 272 bytes with 16-byte header; confirm in cGaussianBlurPS). ? ts offsets are given from v17[n] = n*16 byte indexing: v17[6] = +96, v17[9] = +144, v17[7] = +112, v17[5] = +80, v17[17] = +272.

name: UIBlur_DrawTexturedPass
proto: void UIBlur_DrawTexturedPass(UIBlurRenderer *b, __int64 slotTex, __int64 a3, __int64 a4, __int64 rtObj, int sigma, int tail, __m128i *clamp, int a9, int *taps, int a11, unsigned flags)
purpose: Queues one Gaussian blur draw of a layer slot texture into a render target, selecting the shader permutation from the tap count.

behavior.text: does nothing when b+308 (enabled) is 0. flags -1 is treated as 0.
selector digits on the selector at b+48: digit 1 = (clamp == null), digit 0 = flags, digit 2 = min(taps - 2, 7) (taps = *taps, or GaussianKernel_Build when taps == null).

state+96 = slotTex, +144 = its +40 handle; texture format bits (dword +16 of the handle when kind +8 is 1 or 2, & 7) into state+124 bits 9..11; the sampler constants of the selected program (program +160 ids / +168 words, each & 0x7FFFFFFF) are copied to state + 5704 + 4 * id; then ShaderSelector_Apply(selector, state, 1).

binds rtObj's handle (+40) at state +8 * (short b+252) + 800; when clamp is given the 16 bytes are copied into state+80 and the flag +112 |= 0x10 (clamp rectangle active); +124 is reset to (& 0xFFC06FFF) | 0x6000; the constant buffer b+56 is bound at slot (short b+292); queues a 96-byte command of header type 3.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403AD710). The clamp is passed to the pass as a rectangle in state+80, not as a sampler address mode; its units were not traced here. The sampler filter is not set in this function: the sampler words come from the selected program entry.
open_questions: What the program's sampler words encode (point / linear); units of the clamp rectangle (pixels of the source texture, presumably).

name: UIBlur_Pass
proto: void __fastcall UIBlur_Pass(__int64 blur, __int64 layer, int srcTarget, int dstTarget, int tmpTarget, float sigma, float cutoff, __m128i *rect, __m128i *colour, unsigned int mode)
purpose: One blur step between two render targets: builds the kernel and runs the separable blur through sub_1403ACEBC, or plain-copies the target when the kernel is a single tap.

behavior.text: does nothing unless *(u8*)(blur+308) != 0 (blur enabled).
taps = GaussianKernel_Build(a6, a7, buf[32 qwords = 256 bytes]); stored in v20[0].

taps > 1: target pointers come from the renderer array R = qword_143CDA098: src = *(R + 8*((layer+86 << 6) + a3) + 24224), tmp = *(R + 8*((layer+86 << 6) + a5) + 24224) (64 entries per layer group, 8 bytes each), plus dst = *(R + 40*a4 + 20832) and tmp2 = *(R + 40*a5 + 20832) (40-byte records). Then calls sub_1403ACEBC(blur, src, dst, tmp, tmp2, sigma, cutoff, rect, &copy_of_colour(a9), &taps, kernel, mode) with a 16-byte local copy of *a9.
taps <= 1 and a3 != a4: UIBlur_CopyTarget(blur, layer, a3, a4, ..., 0, rect, 0) (a plain copy src -> dst, no blur). taps <= 1 and a3 == a4: nothing.
sigma and cutoff are passed as float bit patterns in int args a6 / a7 (decompile types them int; they are forwarded to GaussianKernel_Build as floats).

notes: The TLS touches in the decompile are only the thread-state init guard around UIBlur_CopyTarget.
open_questions: ? which of a8 (rect) / a9 (colour) is which: a9 is copied 16 bytes and handed on, a8 is passed through; their roles are decided in UIBlur_DrawPass (a9 -> command state +272 (index 17), a8 -> state +80 (index 5)). ? what mode a10 is (see UIBlur_DrawPass: first shader digit, -1 treated as 0).

name: UIBlur_Run
proto: void UIBlur_Run(__int64 blur, __int64 shaderCtx, unsigned char a3, int a4, char a5, float radius, int *a7, __m128i *rect, int a9, int a10, int a11, int a12)
purpose: Runs the layer blur for one effect radius: chooses a downscale level from the radius and runs separable Gaussian passes through the render-target chain.

behavior.text: radius > 51.2 -> 1/32 size with sigma = radius / 32; the thresholds 25.6 / 12.8 / 6.4 / 3.2 select 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2 and full size (sigma = radius / factor, i.e. radius in full-resolution pixels); each level calls UIBlur_Pass (kernel from GaussianKernel_Build with tail threshold 998277249 = ~0.004) horizontally and vertically.
the rectangle is padded by 32 pixels before downscaling.

notes: Only the head and the first level were read.
open_questions: Where strength, colour and mode 3 enter the final composite (sub_1403B59D4 chain) (?).

name: UIBlur_TapCount
purpose: Returns the tap count of the Gaussian kernel for (sigma, tail) and throws the weights away.

behavior.text: builds a 256-byte weight table on the stack with GaussianKernel_Build(sigma, tail, buf) and returns its result unchanged.
used to size a blur (how many pixels it reaches) without running it; its only caller is GUILayer_ExpandBounds.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403ACA7C).

name: UIColor_CombineSlot
proto: unsigned *UIColor_CombineSlot(unsigned *out, unsigned drawColour, unsigned nodeColour, unsigned rowColour, int mode)
callers: GUITextNode_Draw (8 call sites: 4 palette layers x 2 paths)
purpose: Colour combiner used by GUITextNode_Draw for each of the four font palette layers: picks or multiplies the draw colour, the node's per-layer colour and the UIFontSet row colour according to a mode.

behavior.text: mode 0: out.r = drawColour.r * nodeColour.r / 255, out.g likewise, out.b likewise (unsigned, truncating), out.a = nodeColour.a (the draw colour's alpha is not used here); the row colour is ignored.
mode 1: out = rowColour (the UIFontSet row colour as is).
mode 2: out.rgb = drawColour * nodeColour * rowColour / 65025 (0xFE01, one divide for the triple product, truncating), out.a = nodeColour.a * rowColour.a / 255.
other modes: out = 0xFFFFFFFF. Returns out.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403EE35C). In GUITextNode_Draw: drawColour = node colour (+196) times the context colour (per byte / 255), nodeColour = node+280 / +284 / +288 / +292 (the four layer colours), rowColour = UIFontSet row +8 / +16 / +28 / +40, mode = node+264 / +268 / +272 / +276. So the glyph fill colour is only the product drawColour * layer colour in mode 0; which mode the Job Tree nodes use is not read (the mode bytes come from the UIB text block).
open_questions: The mode values of the Job Tree text nodes (live read of node+264..+276); what the draw alpha does to the palette afterwards.

name: UICommand_Append
proto: __int64 UICommand_Append(UIContext *ctx, int type, unsigned vertexCount, UInt64 *key, UIDrawState *state)
purpose: Appends one 64-byte command record (type dword, then the draw state at +8) to the per-thread command block and reserves its vertex range.

behavior.text: command blocks are 2 KB (0x800) taken from the manager 2 MB buffer at manager+176; records are 64 bytes; vertices are 24 bytes from the pool at manager+184.
the record also stores the vertex count (+56) and first-vertex index (+60), and (key, record) is pushed to the sort list.

notes: Layout confirmed by reading the live buffer (records start with 34 = 0x22).

name: UICommand_ExecuteBatches
purpose: Walks the frame sorted command list and draws it in batches, flushing a batch whenever the pipeline/state key changes.

behavior.text: a batch breaks when the type nibble (&0xF0), the layer id, state words +8/+12 (&0x7FFFFFFF), the 0x1FF field, or any of the floats at +36/+40/+44 (0.5/0.2/1.0 defaults) differ from the previous command, or the vertex range is not contiguous; then UIRender_FlushBatch is called for the finished range.
also selects the render-target dependent bits (scissor rectangle from the context at +208..+220) when the layer id changes.

each command carries a layer index; a layer that is culled (+79) or has no constants (+572 clear) is skipped. When the layer changes the function sets the sort key ((order & 0x1FF | ((page & 0x3F | target type << 18) << 15) | 0x6AC00400) << 10, pass 2), the draw target = the entry at g_Renderer + 800 x (byte target + 86) + 23720 (row slot 0, RT 26's resource: the layer content target), the target's format bits into state+124 bits 9..11, the scissor rectangle state+80 = {(int)x, (int)y, (int)(x + w), (int)(y + h)} of the layer's packed float rectangle (+208..+220, atlas coordinates), and binds the layer's constant buffer (layer+40) at the cUIRender slot (UI ring +66).
the blend word is not set here: UIRender_FlushBatch -> UIRender_ApplyDrawState sets state+120 = the draw state's first dword (0x79420a11 in the default state: ONE / INV_SRC_ALPHA).

open_questions: Only the head of the function was read; the index building at its end is not documented (?).

name: UICommand_MergeSortRange
proto: _UNKNOWN **__fastcall UICommand_MergeSortRange(int unused, __int64 dst, __int64 src, int lo, int hi)
purpose: Recursive stable merge sort over 16-byte records [lo, hi] keyed by the first qword (unsigned), ping-ponging between two buffers, with insertion sort for short ranges.

behavior.text: if hi - lo >= 7: mid = (lo + hi) >> 1; recursively sorts both halves with the buffer arguments swapped (a3, a2), then merges them from src into dst. Merge takes the right element only if left.key > right.key (strict), so equal keys keep order (stable). Leftover tail is memmove'd (16 * remaining bytes).
if hi - lo < 7 (7 or fewer elements): copies src[lo] to dst[lo] and insertion-sorts dst in place using the same strict > comparison on the first qword.
record = 16 bytes; key = first qword, unsigned compare. Argument a1 is unused.
key is the UI command sort key (layer / depth | order) and the second qword the command index or pointer; UIContext_SortCommands calls it.

notes: The classic JDK-style mergesort with insertion cutoff 7.
open_questions: ? what the 64-bit key encodes (see UICommand_Append / UIContext_SortCommands).

name: UICommandRing_Flush
purpose: Uploads the collected command stream into the ring's constant buffer, sets the base pipeline state and executes the batches.

behavior.text: maps ring+16 (sub_14003E120, kind 2) and memmoves ring+168 bytes from ring+184 into it; sets thread-state +208 = ring+212, +200 = the buffer handle (+40), +216 = the handle of qword_143CDAA00+8.

draw state words: +124 = (& 0xFFFFFFC3) | 3, +128 = ring+32, +136 = ring+8, +120 = dword_1407C28E4 (0x20010794 20a41 as a qword: low dword 0x79420a41, i.e. the default UI blend word 0x79420a11 with a different low byte), +104 = low 5 bits 0xC then the 0x100001FFF-masked qword_1407C28F0 (0 after the mask), +112 = qword_1407C28F8 (0x27) & ~0xE000.

samplers: before the batches are executed it writes the default sampler word (dword_141D8BC7C & 0x7FFFFFFF) to the g_Sampler slot (the short at UIRender object ring+70, state + 5704 + 4 * slot) and to the g_Sampler_tMaskBuffer slot (ring+74). The value is 0x7FFFFFFF with the IDB image of the global and 0 at runtime (live read 2026-10-30, see Sampler_DescFromWord); the slot ids are 14 and 15 in the live sampler name table (NameSlotTable_Lookup).

other bindings: a buffer handle at state + 8 * (short ring+64) + 328 (ring+64 is the cUIRenderRemap slot id from UIRender_CreateBuffers, so +328 is the constant-buffer handle table; an earlier version of this sheet called it textures) and the texture handle of ring+40 at state + 8 * (short ring+72) + 1608 (ring+72 = tTexture0).
calls the ring callback (ring+112)(ring+120, ring+128, &state), then UICommand_ExecuteBatches(ring); resets ring+208 to 0 and unmaps.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403ADF04). The sampler constants 0x7FFFFFFF here are for the command-stream buffer, not for layer textures.
open_questions: What the callback at ring+112 does.

name: UICommandRing_Reset
purpose: Resets the per-frame UI command ring: clears the write counters and re-initialises the 32 UIContext slots (80 bytes each).

behavior.text: zeroes the interlocked counters ring+156 / +160 / +164 / +168 (the last gets ring+148, the capacity, when ring+24 is 0), sets ring+184 = ring+24 (current write base).
for each of 32 slots at (ring+200) + 80 * i: +16 = 0, +24 = 0, +32 = ring+184, +56 = slot+48, +64 = 2048, +68 = 1024, +72 = 1 (block size 2048 bytes, 1024 entries..., first block count 1).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403ADE60). The meaning of 2048 / 1024 / 1 inside a slot is inferred from how UIContext_SortCommands reads the same slot (+76 = block count, +48 = first block).

name: UIContext_SortCommands
purpose: Collects the 16-byte command records of one UIContext slot into a contiguous region of the command ring and stable-sorts them by the 64-bit key in the first qword.

behavior.text: *outCount = 0 and returns 0 when ctx+76 (block count) is 0. Reserves 2 * blocks * 1024 bytes from the ring with an interlocked add on (ring+164) and fails (returns 0) when it does not fit.
copies each 1024-byte block (a chain: next pointer at block +1008) with 16-byte moves, then duplicates the region once and computes count = bytes / 16 - ctx+72.

sorts the records by unsigned 64-bit key (record +0): insertion sort for <= 7 entries, otherwise merge sort via UICommand_MergeSortRange on the two halves and a manual merge. Equal keys keep their order (stable).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403AE508). The key is the value the draw helpers store at state+8 (see UIRender_SubmitFrame notes for its bit layout).

name: UIDraw_QuadFromTexelRect
proto: __int64 UIDraw_QuadFromTexelRect(UIRenderer *r, float xform[6], int rect[4], GUIFontSlot *part, int texelRect[4], unsigned tintRGBA, unsigned layer)
purpose: Thunk-like helper for plain quads: converts a texel rectangle of a texture part into UVs and draws one quad with UIDraw_QuadTransformed.

behavior.text: (w, h) = sub_1403DCA04(part) = the texture size read from the part's texture record as u16 at +136 / +138 (1, 1 when there is no texture).

u0 = (float)texelRect[0] / (float)w, v0 = (float)texelRect[1] / h, u1 = (float)texelRect[2] / w, v1 = (float)texelRect[3] / h (so texelRect is x0, y0, x1, y1 in texels, plain division with no half-texel offset); passes the UV list [u0 v0, u1 v0, u0 v1, u1 v1] to UIDraw_QuadTransformed.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403E0AC0). 8555 hits per 4 s. The nine-grid draw emits each of its up to 9 cells through this function, so each cell's UV is exactly texel / texture size with no inset.
open_questions: Whether texelRect[2..3] are exclusive end coordinates (the arithmetic is the same either way).

name: UIDraw_QuadTransformed
proto: __int64 UIDraw_QuadTransformed(UIRenderer *r, float xform[6], int rect[4], GUIFontSlot *part, float uv[8], unsigned tintRGBA, unsigned layer)
callers: UIDraw_QuadFromTexelRect (sole code caller; UIImage_DrawTiled has its own vertex emitter)
purpose: Emits one image quad: the rectangle rect = (x0, y0, x1, y1) mapped through the 2x3 matrix, with given UVs and one colour, as 4 vertices of 24 bytes.

behavior.text: returns without drawing when x0 == x1 or y0 == y1 (empty rectangle). Otherwise UIDraw_SetStateFromSlot(r, .., part) and UIRender_QueueImageDraw(renderer global +37936, 4 vertices, ..) reserve the vertices.

X = m0*x + m2*y + tx, Y = m1*x + m3*y + ty for the corners in the order (x0,y0), (x0,y1), (x1,y1), (x1,y0), where the sums are formed as (m0*x + m2*y) + tx with the integer rect values converted to float first.

+0 X, +4 Y, +8 z = 0.0, +12..+15 the colour bytes of tintRGBA exactly as passed (no multiply here), +16 u, +20 v. UVs by vertex: (uv[0], uv[1]) at (x0,y0), (uv[4], uv[5]) at (x0,y1), (uv[6], uv[7]) at (x1,y1), (uv[2], uv[3]) at (x1,y0), so uv[] = [u0 v0, u1 v0, u0 v1, u1 v1] as UIDraw_QuadFromTexelRect builds it.
the four transformed points are then passed to UIRender_AccumulateQuadBounds.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403E0B80). 8555 hits per 4 s (the same count as UIDraw_QuadFromTexelRect: every plain quad goes through both). The caller passes the node matrix (node+160 combined with the draw state matrix) as xform, so the on-screen position of an image / nine-grid cell is the matrix of GUINode_BuildLocalMatrix times the parent chain, applied to the integer rectangle, with no pixel snapping; any snapping would have to happen in the vertex shader or the camera matrix.
open_questions: The vertex colour semantics beyond 'tintRGBA bytes copied' (premultiplication, which byte order) belong to the shader.

name: UIDraw_SetStateFromSlot
purpose: Fills the draw-state flag word from a texture slot record: texture pointer, blend/permutation bits and the SDF flag.

behavior.text: state+16 = the slot texture (sub_1403DCA6C); state+24 low nibble = 6 when slot byte 36 is set else 2; bits 0x70: 0x50 when byte 37 is 0 else 0; state+4 bits 0x2C0 when byte 38 is 0; bit 0x800 = slot byte 34 (the texture SDF flag, texture+120 bit 0); bit 0x1000 = slot byte 33.
with no usable slot the texture pointer is cleared.

notes: The ring state word reads 0x52 live (low nibble 2, 0x50, no 0x800).

name: UIDrawState_Copy
purpose: Copies the 48-byte draw state with the masks the command format keeps.

behavior.text: dst[0] = src[0] & 0x7FFFFFFF; dst[1] = src[1] & 0x7FFFFFFF; +8 masked 0xFFFFFFFEFFFFE000; +16 texture; +24 flags (all bits); +28/+32/+36 floats; +40 qword.

name: UIFontSetRow_Default
purpose: Fills an 80-byte UIFontSet row with engine defaults and returns the row pointer.

behavior.text: colours (ARGB dwords): +8 = 0xFFFFFFFF, +16 = 0xFF000040 (-16777024 as signed), +28 = 0xFFDCDCDC, +40 = 0xFF202020; +0 = 0.
+72 word = 0, +74 byte = 0. The word/byte stores at +9/+17/+29/+41 (0xFFFF) and +11/+19/+31/+43 (0xFF) re-write bytes of the colour dwords with 0xFF (redundant with the dwords).
the field names (threshold, outline widths, colours) come from the earlier sheet; this page confirms the numeric values only.
callers GUIFontTable_Load, GUIFontTable_GetSetRow, sub_1403E5B84.

notes: Values are exact from the decompile; the semantic of each float (width, softness, outline) is not resolved in this function.

name: UIGadget_GetOwnerWidget
purpose: Returns the owning widget of the gadget's owner node: node = *(g + 8); returns node + 496 (0 when there is no node).

behavior.text: v1 = qword (a1 + 8); returns 0 when null, else the qword at (v1 + 496).
node+496 is the owning widget of a GUI node (GUICore_FocusNode reads it that way).

notes: Name proposed (IDB: sub_1402A7A84); the same trivial getter is shared by the three job detail window classes.

name: UIGadgetFFTOJobDetailWindow_SetJob
callers: sub_140132B34 (record copy; called from JobList_StoreCell twice, sub_14012FC6C twice, sub_1401312C8)
callees: GUITextNode_SetTextById, JobTreePanel_FillTexts, sub_14029BCD4, UIName_Key, GUINode_StopState, GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState, sub_1400F638C, Str_Format, AbilityTable_GetRow, GUITextNode_SetString, vtable +64

behavior.text: rec is a 148-byte-style record built by sub_140132B34 from the job list addon record at addon+8832+148*cursor (+19016): copies +0..63 and +64..87, qword +92 (the icon record: dword id, byte hide), byte +100 = addon+19032, byte +101 = source +141 (the 'showUse' byte, see JobTree_FillJobRecords), byte +102 = source +140, byte +103 = (addon byte +19012 is 1, 2 or 3). for the four text bindings at w+80, +184, +288, +392 (104 bytes each: +16 node, +32 string, +64 argument vector, +96 text id) the string is emptied, the argument vector reset (end = begin), the text id = 80 ('--' per JobTreePanel_FillTexts) and, when the node exists, GUITextNode_SetTextById(node, 80, args). The binding pointer array at w+664 / +672 / +680 is zeroed. Skips the state code and goes on to FillTexts.

text ids are set to 3882 (binding 0, w+176), 1021 (binding 1, w+280) and 1023 (binding 3, w+488); binding 2 (w+384) gets 1022 when rec+68 (level) < 8, otherwise its string is emptied, its id is 80 and the text is set to '--' (and its pointer slot is 0). The binding pointers w+664 = binding 0, +672 = binding 3, +680 = binding 1, +688 = binding 2 (or 0).
then JobTreePanel_FillTexts(w+24, w+648, rec, 0) fills the level texts from the record, and sub_14029BCD4(w+496, rec+92, 0) sets the job icon.

stops 'Hide' / 'Show' and plays 'Show' when rec+101 != 0 else 'Hide' (state +104 = 1, GUINode_PlayState). Node w+64: plays 'ShowNext' (found by FindState). Node w+72: sub_1400F638C(node, rec+102, 0, 0, 0) = show / hide that node (Show / Hide states, animated).

behavior.text: the job id rec+72 (>= 0xAE is replaced by a dummy pointer) indexes g_JobTable (0x140785E30, 49-byte rows): the pointer used is row + 1 = the four u16 innate ability ids (the JobTable layout). For j = 0..3: stops state 'Sp<j>' on node w+32; when the id != 0: sets the ability name string into the name node at w+704+16*k (k = count of non-zero ids so far, AbilityTable_GetRow(id): string at row + *(int)(row+8) + 8; the node's text-id dword +248 is cleared and its dirty byte +316 set first) and plays 'Good' or 'Bad' on the node at w+696+16*k (the ability row's dword +0x30, column drawback: a value of 2 plays 'Bad', any other value plays 'Good': the code stops the state that is not wanted and plays the other); k += 1. Empty ids are skipped, so the shown abilities are packed.

after the loop plays state 'Sp<k>' on node w+32 (k = number of shown innate abilities, 0..4), then calls virtual +64 of the window (a1, rec) (UIGadgetFFTOJobDetailWindowWithButton slot 8 = sub_1402A7C38 passes the job id and a flag as text arguments).

notes:

This is what the hover shows beside the job list: job name / level texts, the job icon, and the job's four INNATE ability names (JobTable row + 1) with a Good / Bad frame. purpose: Slot 8 of the 'with button' job detail window (called from UIGadgetFFTOJobDetailWindow_SetJob through virtual +64): resets the text argument list at w+1168, pushes the job id and a flag, refreshes the text and refits the scroll area.

name: UIGadgetFFTORadioButtonMenu_Ctor
purpose: Constructs the 304-byte radio-button menu gadget used by the battle command page (Move / Abilities / Wait / Status) and by other UIB screens.

behavior.text: sets vtable `vftable_ffto::Game::UI::UIGadgetFFTORadioButtonMenu_140716730`, `+16` (entry count) = 0, `+24..` (entry node pointers) left as allocated.
`+280` (selected index) = -1 (`0x1402AD5F8`), `+284` (hover index) = -1 (`0x1402AD5FE`).

The Legate's live read confirmed `+1120` as the visible command row (0 Move, 1 Abilities, 2 Wait, 3 Status).

name: UIGadgetFFTORadioButtonMenu_Event
purpose: Maintains the radio menu's selected/hover index from the UI event stream. This is the writer of the command row's live selection.

behavior.text: event `msg[0] == 0x0C` or `0x10`: clears `+280` (`0x1402AD881` for 0x0C, `0x1402AD8D1` for 0x10), finds `sender` in the entry-pointer array at `+24` (count at `+16`), and stores its index at `+280` (`0x1402AD8BA`). event `0x0D`: clears `+280` (`0x1402AD8C7`) and returns.

name: UIGadgetFFTOVScrollText_ApplyScroll
purpose: Applies the scroll offset: moves the text node (g+40) to y = -scroll and re-centres the marker node (g+160) on the 'ScrollMark' part of the owner.

GUINode_SetPosition(text node g+40, its x (+56), y).

part = GUINode_FindPartByName(ownerNode + 272, key at qword_143CDA2A0 + 0x13F8). When the marker node (g+160) and the part exist: SetPosition(marker, its x, marker.h (+68) + part.y (+60) + part.h (+68) / 2 - marker.h / 2) with C integer halving. (Hex-Rays showed v6 as an unset register; the disassembly loads it from g+0xA0.)

name: UIGadgetFFTOVScrollText_HandleScrollInput
callers: about 20 window update methods (the glossary, equipment windows, job windows ...): sub_140112748, sub_14012E82C, sub_140131068, sub_140168A18 ... sub_140295D2C, sub_14037085C
purpose: Mouse wheel / stick scrolling of a scroll-text gadget: moves the scroll bar by 20 units per wheel notch or by the stick axis; returns 1 when it scrolled.

name: UIImage_DrawTiled
proto: float UIImage_DrawTiled(UIRenderer *r, float *xform, int *rect, GUIFontSlot *part, int *uv, int tintRGBA, char mirror, unsigned layer)

name: UIRender_AppendCommand

purpose: Appends a type-32 command to the calling thread's UIContext, tagged with the current layer; also marks the layer used.

behavior.text: returns 0 unless (*(u8*)(renderer + 136) & 1) (the frame is recording UI commands; GUIRenderer_ResetFrame zeroes +136).

name: UIRender_ApplyDrawState
purpose: Programs the graphics pipeline from a draw state: shader permutation, blend/raster bits, texture, samplers and the cSDF constant buffer.

behavior.text: shader permutation index = 4 * ((flags & 0xF) + 8 * ((flags >> 4) & 7)) (stored at thread state +228 when it changes); the ring flags 0x52 give 168.
binds the texture at state+16 (texture+40 handle) and its sampler constant (state+4 & 0x7FFFFFFF); state+0 goes to thread state +120; blend words from state+8 (mask 0x100001FFF).

when the draw has a texture (draw+0x10 != 0) it binds the texture handle (texture+40) at the tTexture0 slot (UIRender object +72, context + 1608 + 8 * slot) and writes the draw's sampler word (draw+4 & 0x7FFFFFFF) to the g_Sampler slot (UIRender +70, context + 5704 + 4 * slot) and to the g_Sampler_tMaskBuffer slot (+74).

when the draw has no texture it binds the default texture instead (the object at UIRender +0x28, its +40 handle, or 0 when that object is null) and writes the default sampler word (dword_141D8BC7C & 0x7FFFFFFF) to both slots.

the sampler word of a textured UI draw is 0x2C0 (min / mag linear, mip point, WRAP; see Sampler_DescFromWord); the default word is 0 at runtime (point, wrap). The slot ids are 14 (g_Sampler) and 15 (g_Sampler_tMaskBuffer) in the live sampler name table (NameSlotTable_Lookup).
only when flag bit 0x800 is set the cSDF buffer (r+48) is written: {1, state+28, state+32 * 0.005, state+36, state+40 (float2)}; otherwise a zeroed 32-byte buffer (r+56) is bound.

the draw state's FIRST word (state+0) is the render-target blend word, stored straight into the thread state at +120; sub_140051284 (BlendDesc_FromWords) later unpacks every blend word into a Direct3D 12 render-target blend description: enable = bit 0, blend op = ((w >> 1) & 7) + 1, colour source / destination factor = ((w >> 4) & 0x1F) + 1 / ((w >> 9) & 0x1F) + 1, alpha op = ((w >> 14) & 7) + 1, alpha source / destination factor = ((w >> 17) & 0x1F) + 1 / ((w >> 22) & 0x1F) + 1, write mask = (w >> 27) & 0xF (each factor field is the D3D12_BLEND value minus 1: 0 ZERO, 1 ONE, 4 SRC_ALPHA, 5 INV_SRC_ALPHA, 13 / 14 BLEND_FACTOR / INV_BLEND_FACTOR).

behavior.basis: (live read of the default draw state at 0x1408FF878, copied by GUIRenderer_ResetFrame at the start of every frame)
behavior.text: word0 = 0x79420a11 = enabled, ADD, source ONE, destination INV_SRC_ALPHA, alpha ONE / INV_SRC_ALPHA, mask RGBA, i.e. premultiplied-over blending. state+4 is the sampler word (UIDraw_SetStateFromSlot's 0x2C0 mask acts on it), not a blend word.

notes: cSDF is read by two SDF image pixel shaders (shader_4990 and shader_5560). No live texture has the flag set.

name: UIRender_CreateBuffers

purpose: Allocates the UI renderer's command and vertex buffers and its 32 UIContext objects, and looks up the cUIRender / cUIRenderRemap / cSDF constant buffers and the g_Sampler / tTexture0 slots.

behavior.text: params[0..2] = v4 (command buffer bytes), v6 (vertex buffer bytes), v8 (index/extra buffer bytes); LoadShaders passes {0x200000, 0x600000 (6291456), 0x100000} (V from its v46 array). Copies params +16..+79 (4 x 16 bytes) to r+80..+143. r+144 / +148 / +152 = the three sizes; r+212 = 24.
r+176 = allocation of v4 bytes (align 8) from heap qword_140C696D0 (command memory); null -> returns 0.

allocates 2568 bytes = 8-byte count (32) + 32 UIContext objects of 80 bytes each (vftable faith::Graphics::UIRender::UIContext, zeroed fields); stored at r+200 (pointer past the count). Each context gets +8 = r (owner) and +40 (dword) = 24.
shaderModule (a3) null -> frees r+8 if set and returns 0. Otherwise refcount +1 (dword at +12 atomic add), r+8 = module (previous released).

buffer creation via sub_140086DE4 / 86E9C / 86F64 with {size, flags, kind} descriptors: r+16 = descriptor {size = v6, 65794 (0x10102)} 20 bytes (vertex buffer); r+24 = v6-byte CPU heap block; r+32 = {size = v8, 66050 (0x10202), 1} (index buffer); r+48 = {32, 66563 (0x10403)} and r+56 = {32, 1028 (0x404)} constant buffers. The 32-byte cbuffer at r+56 is mapped (type 2), zeroed (two 16-byte stores) and unmapped.

r+40 = *(qword_140C696A8 + 5312) (a shared object, refcount +1). Slot lookups by name (sub_140089280): cUIRenderRemap -> r+64, cUIRender -> r+66, cSDF -> r+68 (all constant-buffer table at +5056 of the device object), g_Sampler -> r+70 and g_Sampler_tMaskBuffer -> r+74 (sampler table +5072), tTexture0 -> r+72 (texture table +5064). Returns 1.

notes: This is the only place the SDF pass's cbuffer name 'cSDF' and samplers 'g_Sampler' / 'g_Sampler_tMaskBuffer' are bound to slot ids; the text pipeline (SDFFontRenderer_Flush, UIRender_ApplyDrawState) uses these u16s. There is ONE sampler named g_Sampler (not per-pass); the mask buffer has its own.
open_questions: ? meaning of the kind words 65794 / 66050 / 66563 / 1028 (flag bits: usage / bind). ? what the shared object at device+5312 is. ? 'a2' unused.

name: UIRender_DrawLetterbox
callees: UILayer_GetTarget, ShaderSelector_Apply, sub_1403A8468, sub_14003E120, sub_14003E228, sub_140069A38, RenderState_PackCommand, sub_140069980
purpose: When the output surface is a different size than the UI target, fills the border regions (letterbox / pillarbox bars) with selector program 0.

behavior.text: base = the renderer's current target; (baseW, baseH) = its u16 +20 / +22, (outW, outH) = dwords +40 / +44 of the frame target object (*(qword_140C696A8 + 88)). Does nothing when they are equal.

bars: dx = (outW - baseW) * 0.5, dy = (outH - baseH) * 0.5 (floats, not rounded; a non-positive half difference becomes the full size); the two rectangles are (0, 0)-(dx, dy-or-H) and (outW - dx, outH - dy)-(outW, outH) converted to clip space (x * 2 / W - 1, 1 - y * 2 / H) into the 2-quad buffer ui[1055]; the draw uses the full output rect (0, 0, outW, outH) as the clamp in state+80 and queues a command of header type 5 with the key (targetByte << 43) | 0x1AB60000000.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403B93BC; the letterbox role is inferred from the arithmetic: bars of half the size difference). The bars use fractional half differences, so an odd size difference puts the content boundary on a half pixel.
open_questions: Where the base target is scaled to the output (not in this function); the fill colour.

name: UIRender_DrawOverlayQuads
callees: UILayer_GetTarget, sub_1403A8468, ShaderSelector_Apply, sub_14003E120, sub_14003E228, sub_140069A38, RenderState_PackCommand, sub_140069980
purpose: Draws up to three textured rectangles registered at ui+8672 (48-byte records) over the base target with selector program 5.

behavior.text: runs when any of the three records at ui+8672 + 48 * i has a texture. The target size is the u16 +20 / +22 of the base target (UILayer_GetTarget of layer 0, or the current one); sort key state+8 = (targetByte << 43) | 0x1AB00080000.

per record: texture at record+0, pixel rect ints (x0 = +8, y0 = +12, x1 = +16, y1 = +20), uv floats at +24 / +28 / +32 / +36. Positions are written to the vertex buffer ui+8424 in clip space with x = px * (2 / W) - 1 and y = 1 - py * (2 / H); no half-pixel offset and no rounding. The command copies a clamp rect from record+8 (4 ints) into state+80, uses stride 16 and a 64-byte buffer offset per quad and queues command type 4.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403B8F20; purpose I: overlay / cursor-like quads, unverified). The pixel-to-clip mapping is useful as a reference for how integer pixel rectangles become vertices.
open_questions: What the three records contain at runtime.

name: UIRender_FlushBatch
proto: unsigned int __fastcall UIRender_FlushBatch(__int64 r, int kind, unsigned int first, unsigned int count, int a5, __int64 drawState)
purpose: Issues one batched draw: sets the draw-call type bits of the thread state for the command kind, applies the draw state and submits the range.

behavior.text: ts = *(TLS-state + 56); the dword at ts+124 is rewritten with its low 12 bits and top 10 bits kept (& 0xFFC00FFF) and bits 12..21 (the 0x3FF000 field) set to: kind 16 -> 0x2000, kind 32 -> 0x5000. Any other kind returns 56 and draws nothing.

if count (a3 in the decompile naming = a3 != 0): UIRender_ApplyDrawState(r, drawState) then sub_1400ADB20(ts, a3, a4) (the draw / submit of the range) and returns its result. If a3 == 0 only the state bits are updated.

kind 16 = the plain geometry command, kind 32 = the layer command that UIRender_AppendCommand emits (type 32); 0x2000 / 0x5000 select a primitive / draw type value (2 vs 5) in the same bit field UIBlur_DrawPass sets to 6.
a5 is unused.

notes: Parameter naming: first / count are I from the call (a3, a4).
open_questions: ? decode of the 0x3FF000 field (values 2, 5, 6). ? whether kind 34 (image) is flushed elsewhere (it is not accepted here).

name: UIRender_GetThreadContext
purpose: Returns the UIContext slot (80 bytes) belonging to the calling thread, chosen by the thread state's position in the thread-state array.

behavior.text: ts = *(TLS-state + 56) (the thread's render thread state, lazily initialised by _dyn_tls_on_demand_init).
index = (ts - *(qword_140C696A8 + 4984)) / 6032 (array of 6032-byte thread states).
returns *(*(renderer + 8408) + 200) + 80 * index. The UIContext array (80 bytes each, 32 of them) is the one built by UIRender_CreateBuffers at r+200.
the +8408 object is the UIRender Renderer, +200 its UIContext array: a per-thread command list so UI draws can be recorded from up to 32 threads without locking.

name: UIRender_LoadShaders
callees: sub_1403A7AD8, sub_140091124 (load .tec), sub_1403A7B08, UIRender_CreateBuffers, UICommandRing_Reset, sub_14008C5D8, sub_140086DE4, sub_140086F64, sub_140089280, sub_1403B7E2C, sub_1403B7F64, sub_1403AE954, sub_1403B7888 (cleanup)
purpose: Loads the five UI shader containers and creates the UI renderer, its command ring, the SMAA / down-sampling helpers and their constant buffers.

Then loads, via sub_140091124(qword_143CD9B88, name, hash, 0, opts), each container and stores it at ui+offset: 'shader/UIRender.tec' -> +24, 'shader/SMAA.tec' -> +32, 'shader/RadialBlur.tec' -> +40, 'shader/BahamutEffect.tec' -> +48, 'shader/DownSampling.tec' -> +56; each followed by sub_1403A7B08(ui, container). Any failure goes to cleanup sub_1403B7888 and returns 0.

creates (once, qword_143CDAA00) a 24-byte Graphics::UIRender::Utility object; creates two buffers for it: sub_140086DE4 desc {224, 257, ...} (vertex-ish) and sub_140086F64 {96, 1025} (constant buffer); object+8 / +16 hold them. On failure both are released.

creates the UI Renderer object: 216 bytes, vftable faith::Graphics::UIRender::Renderer, slot ids at +64..+74 init to 0xFFFF, stored at ui+8408. Calls UIRender_CreateBuffers(renderer, ?, shaderModule v20, {0x200000, 0x600000, 0x100000}); failure -> free renderer, cleanup, return 0. Then UICommandRing_Reset(*(ui+8408)). v20 comes from sub_14008C5D8(*(qword_140C696A8+5016), {0x0230000 / 0x0344 0C0 words...}, 4) (a shader / module lookup from an 8-byte+8-byte descriptor).

sub_1403B7E2C(ui, *(u16*)(R+6568), *(u16*)(R+6572), 484176) and sub_1403B7F64(ui) (resolution-dependent setup; R = qword_143CDA098, 6568 / 6572 = screen width / height (I)). Creates a 96-byte object at ui+8600 with slot ids at +56..+70 = 0xFFFF and a float2 (width, height) at +80, byte +88 = 0; then sub_1403AE954.

creates a 32-byte Graphics::DownSampling object at ui+8608: name 'spdLinearSamplerConstants' -> +16 (u16 slot), a 64-byte buffer desc {64, 66563} created at +8, 'tTexture1' -> +18 if the buffer was created.
the renderer ui: 'tTexture0' slot -> ui+148, 'cConstant0' -> ui+150; creates {80, 66563} cbuffer -> ui+8416 and {192, 65794} buffer -> ui+8424. Returns 1.

notes: Command memory sizes are 2 MiB commands, 6 MiB vertices, 1 MiB indices (V from v46). The renderer's cSDF / g_Sampler slots are resolved in UIRender_CreateBuffers, not here.
open_questions: ? contents of the 8408 / 8600 / 8608 objects beyond the offsets listed. ? purpose of constant 484176 (0x76350). ? what the descriptor passed to sub_14008C5D8 selects.

name: UIRender_PrepareLayers
purpose: Per-frame layer setup: collects the used layers, finds overlaps, assigns draw order and atlas pages, then packs every layer's rectangle.

behavior.text: resets both atlas allocators (UIRenderer+8616 / +8632 = cursor (0, 0), row height 0, page 0; the cursor value is qword_143D12018, 0 at runtime), clears dword_140906B58..68 = -1, and collects the layers of the 512 entries (+216) whose byte +76 is set into the list at +4312 (count +172).

walking the list from the back: layer+20 = 0; when +489 is set the nearest lower layer with +487 is found, its +8 copied to this +36 and, when the two rectangles do not overlap (float compares on +208 / +212 / +216 / +220, strict), byte +79 (culled) is set. The list is sorted (sub_1403C2930).

for every layer with +487, +179 set, +28 != 2, +78 / +486 / +488 clear: the int rect (truncation) is allocated in a temporary atlas with margin 2 or 32 (|+500|, +180, +188 > 3.2); when the temporary page changes (the breaking layer is not counted on the new page: the cursor is reset to (0, 0) after it), +20 of this layer and of every later layer in the list is set to this layer's +12 (its order at that moment), not to a page number; the temporary pass only exists for these +487 layers. Further passes compute the draw order +12 as 1 + the order of the nearest overlapping lower layer, and the key +84 = mode | (4 * (+12) + 4) with mode = 1 when +28 == 0 and +177 or +178 is set, else 2 when +28 == 0, else 0; sorted again (sub_1403C2B00); +12 is renumbered densely by key change.
finally calls UILayer_GetTarget and GUILayer_PackAtlasRect for each layer in order.

the order +12 starts as the layer's index (GUIRenderer_ResetFrame). Walking from the top of the list down, a layer whose float rectangle (+208..+220) overlaps (strictly) the nearest lower layer gets +12 = (+20, the page base) + that layer's current +12 + 1; a layer with no overlapping lower layer keeps its index (0 when +487). A further pass sets +12 = lower + 1 only where the nearest overlapping lower layer is a masked layer (+487 with +179, kind != 2 and +78, +486, +488 clear). The sort key +84 = mode | (4 x +12 + 4) with mode 1 for a kind 0 layer with +177 or +178, 2 for another kind 0 layer, 0 otherwise; the list is sorted by it (StdSort_LayersByKey, sub_1403C2B00: an MSVC std::sort introsort, a stable insertion sort up to 32 elements, partition based and not stable above) and +12 renumbered densely by key change, starting at 1 (equal keys share a number). The pack order of GUILayer_PackAtlasRect is this final list order. V (live 2026-10-30, 63 layers): keys, list order (including a tie broken against the slot order) and every packed position were reproduced; the first sort (by +12, whose values are the slot indices, already ascending) changes nothing. A layer that overlaps a lower layer q gets the order idx(q) + 1 (idx = the slot index), at most its own index, so it can be packed before layers created between q and itself.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403B85B0). Only the loops' arithmetic is V; the intent of each pass (layer order, page assignment, overlap) is I. Overlap tests are strict float compares of the unrounded rectangles.
open_questions: Why overlap decides +12 (I: layers that overlap are blended in order, so the later one must not be ordered before the earlier one). The +487 flag is written by ComponentLayer_DrawMaskComponent (V, 2026-10-30: the mask component of a component whose property block has a mask is drawn into a fresh record and the flag is set when it produced draws; live in a Job Tree frame).

name: UIRender_QueueImageDraw
proto: __int64 __fastcall UIRender_QueueImageDraw(__int64 renderer, unsigned int layer, int a3, __int64 drawState)

additionally *(u8*)(L+78) = (*(u32*)(drawState + 24) & 0x1000) != 0 (drawState dword +24 bit 12 copied into the layer's byte +78; ClearLayerFlags clears words +78..79).

name: UIRender_ResolveBase
callees: UILayer_GetTarget, sub_1403B7E2C, sub_1403A8468, sub_140087AB4, sub_1403AC420, sub_14003ABD0
purpose: Copies the base (bottom) layer surface to the frame target once per frame, with the base-layer sort key.

behavior.text: needs a thread state, the blur object g_Renderer+37928 and layer pointer ui+216; base target = UILayer_GetTarget(layer 0), or the current target when that is 0. Skipped when byte ui+141 is negative (already done). When the stored size qword ui+8664 differs from (W, H) = g_Renderer + 6568 / 6572 it calls sub_1403B7E2C to resize first.

sort key state+8: when DWORD2(xmmword_142E80230) == 0 it is (targetByte << 43) | 0x1AB00080000 (targetByte 1 -> 0), otherwise ((lastLayer+12 & 0x1FF) | ((lastLayer+16 & 0x3F | targetByte << 18) << 15) | 0x6AC01C00) << 10.

builds a rect (0, 0, W, H), creates a view with sub_140087AB4 (from ui+8648 or null) and calls sub_1403AC420(blurObj, view, destination) where destination is the render target of the base target's byte, or the frame target (*(qword_140C696A8+88) +128) when the flag is 0; then ui+141 = -1 and releases the view.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403B8BF4; role I: a copy of the base target, not verified live). The copy rectangle is the whole render size without scaling.
open_questions: What sub_1403AC420 / sub_140087AB4 do exactly (copy region vs resolve).

name: UIRender_SubmitFrame
callers: none direct (probably a virtual call of the UI renderer)
callees: UIRender_ResolveBase, UIRender_DrawOverlayQuads, GUILayer_Composite, UIContext_SortCommands, UICommandRing_Flush, UICommandRing_Reset, UIRender_DrawLetterbox, sub_14003F7C0, sub_14003E120
purpose: End-of-frame UI submission: composites every prepared layer, sorts the commands of all 32 contexts, merges them into one stream and executes it.

behavior.text: runs only when a2 == 0. Calls UIRender_ResolveBase and UIRender_DrawOverlayQuads, then for the layers whose page changes (layer+16) with +492, +179 and +79 == 0 and +28 != 2 emits one clear-style command (type 19) per atlas texture of the page (sort key ((page & 0x3F | targetByte << 18) << 25) | 0x1AB01D80000, flag word 2 when the renderer option bit is set).

maps 7 command buffers (ui+8464..8584) and calls GUILayer_Composite for each of the active layers (first call with flag 1, cleared once a layer has +76 set), then repeats the per-page loop with key 0x1AB01DFFC00 and flag word 1.

sorts the 32 contexts with UIContext_SortCommands and k-way merges them by key into one region at the end of the ring (ring+192, count ring+208), then UICommandRing_Flush, UICommandRing_Reset and UIRender_DrawLetterbox.

the call order in the function is UIRender_ResolveBase, UIRender_DrawOverlayQuads, GUILayer_Composite once per layer (the layer effect passes, among them the +177 shadow, are packed into the contexts' command lists inside it), UIContext_SortCommands, UICommandRing_Flush, UICommandRing_Reset, UIRender_DrawLetterbox.

the effect commands are therefore recorded before UICommandRing_Flush replays the UI draws, so the sampler state they are packed with is whatever the context holds at that moment (the default words from RenderContext_ResetFrame for slot 14; see GUILayer_BlurShadowPass). Basis: the call order above and the live trace on that sheet.

sort key layout (shifts and masks read from the helpers, all keys are 64-bit): bits 10..18 = layer order (+12), bits 19..24 = the pass constant (const >> 9 & 0x3F: 7 copy 0x6AC00E00, 14 base 0x6AC01C00, 16 / 59 the +177 blur 0x6AC02000 / 0x6AC07600), bits 25..30 = atlas page (+16), bit 43 and up = render target byte. Commands therefore execute grouped per target, then per atlas page, then per pass, then by layer order.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403B9844). The key layout and the command type meanings (19, 4, 5) are inferred; the loops themselves were read in full. This is the function the Job Tree frame goes through every frame.
open_questions: Exact semantics of the type-19 commands (barrier / discard of the page textures, I); the second loop's key 0x1AB01DFFC00.

name: UiScript_Run
proto: void UiScript_Run(const unsigned char *script, int firstRow, int flag)
callers: JobScreen_FillUnitRows, JobScreen_BuildLearnList, JobScreen_RefreshLearnList, sub_1402C4980, sub_1402D5854, sub_1402EED3C and others
purpose: Runs one UI script: the byte-coded layout and behaviour program of a list or panel screen.

behavior.text: stores the flag in a state dword, calls the state reset sub_140329E1C, clears the script cursor words and the pending-line flag, and takes the first row from the second argument unless the flag is non-zero.

loops until the next opcode byte is 0x21: it calls the handler for that opcode from the 29-entry handler table (0x1406838F0, opcodes 0..28) with the record pointer, and the handler returns the pointer to the next record.

record shape: opcode byte, total length byte, operands (opcode 22 is a single byte); conditional opcodes (the handler at 0x140327954) run the following records only while a row callback accepts the current row and skip them by their length otherwise.

notes: The handler table is addressed relative to the image base, and the conditional handler 0x140327954 is reached through that table, so neither address appears in this body. Read: the interpreter loop and two handlers (conditional and the one-byte opcode 22); the other opcodes are not decoded.
open_questions: ?: the operands and effect of each opcode.

name: UIState_EndTransition
purpose: Ends the UI fade state given (fade +24 = 0).

behavior.text: used by TitleMenu_Build after the menu is shown.

name: UITable_GetRow
purpose: Returns the in-memory row of an nxd table by table id and row index (null when the table or row is missing).

behavior.text: tables live under qword_143CD9CD0; id 27 is used for the UIFontType rows by GUITextNode_Layout (V, GUITextNode_Layout / GUITextNode_FinishLine: the row dwords are Unknown8 (+8, the baseline term), UnknownC (+12, the per-glyph multiplier), Unknown10 (+16, its alternative when GUIFontTable+40 is set) and Unknown14 (+20, the size multiplier)).
the registry it searches through NxdRegistry_Find is the table list built from root.nxl by NxdRegistry_LoadRootNxl; the table state must be 2 or 3 (loaded) or the call returns null.

notes:
sub_1403DBC74 is the keyed variant used by the job tree (table 0xBD = job-need rows).

Registry details (hash map, table object layout, 246 tables) are on the NxdRegistry_LoadRootNxl and NxdRegistry_Find pages.

name: UITable_GetRowByIndex
proto: char *UITable_GetRowByIndex(int tableId, unsigned int key, unsigned int index)
callers: sub_1403DBB00, sub_1402EE994, sub_1402A876C, UIAddonFFTOSaveLoad_vfunc_12, sub_14013CA80 and about ten more
purpose: Returns the index-th sub-row of a key in a multi-row UI table, or null.

behavior.text: same registry / type / state checks as UITable_GetRowCount; additionally index must be < sub_1403D3A34(table, key) (the count).

the row comes from sub_1403D3C98(table, key, index); a null result returns null; a row whose first qword is negative returns the constant block unk_1406F5ED0 (a default / deleted-row placeholder); otherwise sub_1403D2FD8(row) converts the row to its data pointer.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DBDF4).

name: UITable_GetRowByKey
proto: void *UITable_GetRowByKey(unsigned int tableId, unsigned int key)
callers: JobRecord_FillIconAndGenericFlag, JobTree_RefreshAddon, JobTree_FillJobRecords, PreviewUnit_BuildSpriteRecord, and most other NXD consumers
purpose: Returns the row of an NXD table by table id and row key, or null when the table or row is missing.

behavior.text: the table manager qword_143CD9CD0 must be loaded; table = sub_1403D325C(manager, tableId).
the table state at table+12 must be 2 or 3, and sub_1403D3A10(table) must not report a problem.
row = sub_1403D3AE8(table, key); a missing row returns null and a negative key at row+0 returns the default row unk_1406F5ED0.
otherwise returns sub_1403D2FD8(row), the row data pointer.

notes: Key-based companion of UITable_GetRow (index-based). Table ids seen: 46 Job, 189 GeneralJob, 41 JobCommand, 0xC8 JobType, 0x112 unit-flag table.
open_questions: Meaning of the table state values 2/3 and of the default row.

name: UITable_GetRowByKeys
proto: char *UITable_GetRowByKeys(int tableId, unsigned int key1, unsigned int key2)
callers: EquipDetail_Refresh, GuideWindow_ShowPage, sub_1400F7378, sub_1400F74F4, sub_14011C940, sub_140125F38 and about fifteen more game-data readers
purpose: The row of (key1, key2) of a double-keyed table (for a triple-keyed table: the first leaf of child (key1, key2)), looked up by table id; its data pointer, or null.

behavior.text: same registry, type (2 or 3) and state checks as UITable_GetRowCount. The entry is NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys2(table, key1, key2) (a binary search of the bound entries by the key pair); null returns null; first qword negative returns unk_1406F5ED0; else NxdEntry_GetRow(entry).
unlike UITable_GetRowByIndex there is no count check: key2 is a key, not a position.
GuideWindow_ShowPage reads GuidePage-en (table 188) with (guide, page) through it.

notes: X6 (2026-10-30) decoded the callee and named it (IDB: sub_1403DBCE4).

name: UITable_GetRowCount
callers: sub_1403DBB00 (table 125), sub_1402EE84C, sub_1402A5E38, sub_1402A62E4, sub_1402A876C and about ten more game-data readers
purpose: Number of sub-rows of a key in a multi-row UI table (the count field of the key's entry), or 0 when the table or key does not exist.

behavior.text: needs g_NxdRegistry != 0; NxdRegistry_Find(registry, tableId) must return a table whose type dword at +12 is 2 or 3; sub_1403D3A10 must return 0 (it is 'not in a locked / loading state': the status dword at (table+48)+80 is not 2 or 3); then the result is sub_1403D3A34(table, key).
any failed step returns 0.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DBC20). Paired with UITable_GetRowByIndex (row by key and position) and UITable_GetRowByKeys (row by two keys). Table 125 is the language / path override table used by the slot registry. Type 2 / 3 are the double / triple keyed files (format NxdMultiKeyIndex, V against all 58 retail files); the count is the set's record count (double: the rows of key; triple: its children).

name: UIText_Get
callers: 27 xrefs; named: GUITextNode_SetTextById, GUITextNode_UpdateLayout, JobList_StoreCell, JobRecord_FromJobId, JobTreePanel_FillTexts, Options_ApplyBlock
purpose: Returns the UI text string for an id from UI table 19, or a shared empty string when the row is missing.

behavior.text: row = UITable_GetRow(19, id) (table 19 = UI text).
found: returns row + *(int*)(row+4) + 4 (string stored at a dword offset in the row, relative to row+4 + offset; ie. offset base is row+4).
missing: returns the global empty string Str.

about 27 callers (JobTreePanel_FillTexts, GUITextNode_SetTextById, GUITextNode_UpdateLayout, JobList_StoreCell, JobRecord_FromJobId, Options_ApplyBlock and many sub_ UI screens). One xref is listed as DxgkInitialize, which is an IDA mislabel of a neighbouring address (I).

notes: Note the row-relative offset: the field is a dword at row+4, added to row+4 (V from the expression &Row[*((int*)Row+1)+4]; this reads as row + off + 4 where off = dword at row+4, i.e. the offset is relative to row+4 only if the stored value excludes the dword itself).
open_questions: ? whether the offset is relative to row+4 or to row. ? the compression / encoding of the text itself (decode path is the caller's).

name: UIText_ResolveCategoryRow
proto: char __fastcall UIText_ResolveCategoryRow(__int64 out, const char *category, unsigned int key)
purpose: Resolves the category name and key of a <category=key> text tag to a table row and fills a 28-byte result record with three string pointers and four flag bytes.

behavior.text: category is compared with sub_140079090(a2, name, len incl NUL) (string compare, 0 = equal) in this order: 'Item' (len 5) -> UITable_GetRowByKey(0x2D, key); 'PoachItem' (10) -> table 0xEC; 'C_MES_ID_SAMPLE' (16) -> table 0xAC; 'Ability' (8) -> table 0x27; 'CharaSlot' (10) -> no table, array qword_143CDA350; 'JobCommand' (11) -> table 0x29. Anything else, or a missing row, returns 0 (the local v6 = 0).
result record out: +0, +8, +16 are three string pointers, +24, +25, +26, +27 are four bytes copied from the row (see per-category lines). Returns 1 on success.

Item (0x2D): base = row+4; out[+24..+27] = row bytes 24..27; out+0 = base + base[1] (dword), out+8 = base + base[2], out+16 = base + base[0] unless the byte there is 0, in which case it falls back to out+0's offset (base[1]). PoachItem (0xEC) is the same with base = row+8 and the four bytes from row bytes 28..31.

C_MES_ID_SAMPLE (0xAC): p = row+4; out+0 = row+4+row[+8] unless that string is empty (first byte 0), then out+0 = p + *(int*)p; out+8 = row+4+row[+12]; out+16 = p + *(int*)p; bytes +24..+27 = row bytes 16..19.

Ability (0x27): out+0 = out+16 = row + row[2] + 8 (dword index 2); out+8 = row + row[4] + 8; bytes out+24 = row byte 22 (Ability column noun_class), +25 = 23 (noun_number_form), +26 = 24 (noun_class_2), +27 = 25 (noun_prefix_flag); the pointer at out+8 is the Ability plural column (+0x10), out+0 and out+16 the name (+8).

CharaSlot: row = qword_143CDA350 + 4*(9*key + 12) (36-byte stride, key*9 dwords); all three pointers = that address; out+24 = row byte 32, out+26 = row byte 33, out+25 = 1, out+27 = 0. JobCommand (0x29): pointers = row + row[2] + 8; dword at out+24 is set to 256 (so +25 = 1, others 0).
the three string pointers are (singular name, plural name, name used for a count of 0); the four bytes are the noun grammar bytes of the counted-noun builders. I (other categories): the same roles.

notes: The IDA comment already names the categories; this sheet adds the row layouts. Tables 0x2D / 0xEC / 0xAC / 0x27 / 0x29 are keyed UI tables (V from the calls).
open_questions: ? what the four bytes mean for each category other than Ability (for Ability they are the language specific noun grammar bytes read by the four counted-noun builders, see behavior CountedNounTagRecord). ? layout of the CharaSlot array (36-byte stride, base qword_143CDA350).

name: UITexturePath_FromRow
proto: bool UITexturePath_FromRow(unsigned row, char *out, int size)
purpose: Builds a UITextureParts path (that scheme followed by the row's text) from one row of UI table 0x8F.

behavior.text: UITable_GetRowByKey(0x8F, row); a missing row returns false and leaves out unchanged.
otherwise Str_Format(out, size, format, text): the UITextureParts scheme and the text at the row's offset in its dword +4.
