name: UITexturePath_Select4k
proto: bool UITexturePath_Select4k(GUIFontSlots *slots, char *out, __int64 a3, const char *path)
purpose: Copies a texture path into out (255 characters at most) and, when the path contains '_2k_', changes it to '_4k_'; returns true when the path contains _2k_ or _4k_.

behavior.text: sub_14002620C(out, 256, path, 255) copies the string; strstr(out, '_2k_') found: byte [1] of the match is overwritten with '4' (52) and true is returned; otherwise returns strstr(out, '_4k_') != 0.
unconditional - there is no resolution option read here, so every _2k_ path is promoted to _4k_ (the build only ships the high-resolution parts).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403DB0EC). The caller keeps the returned flag in byte +35 of the 40-byte auxiliary record.
open_questions: ? what byte +35 of that auxiliary record is used for (probably a 'scale by 2' flag for 4k parts).

name: UITitle_OnMenuAction
purpose: Carries out the row the player chose on the title menu.

behavior.text: kind 0 goes to `UITitle_OpenPlayMode`; kind 1 to `UITitle_StartNewGamePlus`; kind 2 to `UITitle_StartContinue`; kind 3 to `UITitle_StartLoadGame`.
kind 4 (Music Player) fades out and sets agent state 0x501; kind 5 (Select Version) fades out and sets agent state 0x601. Any other kind does nothing.

notes: Registry: TitleMenuEntryKinds.

name: UITitle_OpenPlayMode
purpose: Kind 0 (New Game): starts UI state 19 and agent state 2, after which the agent hides the menu and shows the play mode screen.

behavior.text: the menu action for kind 0 jumps here; the agent in state 2 then runs `UITitle_ShowPlayMode`.

notes: This name replaces an earlier, misleading one (`UITitle_Reopen`).

name: UITitle_ShowMenu
purpose: Creates the title agent's three add-ons and builds the menu.

behavior.text: creates the menu add-on (0x1401CB9B4), the play mode add-on (0x1401CBA60) and a third add-on (0x1401CA6C4, row 256 `ffto_saving.uib`), stored at agent +64, +72, +80.
calls `TitleMenu_Build`.

name: UITitle_ShowPlayMode
purpose: Hides the title menu add-on and shows the play mode add-on.

behavior.text: hides with `sub_1401D1EAC(addon, 1)` and shows with `sub_1401D1E30(addon, 0)` (the add-on hide and show calls).

name: UITitle_StartNewGamePlus
purpose: Kind 1 (text 2226, New Game +): fades out and sets agent state 0x201, only when no save request is pending.

behavior.text: the menu action for kind 1 jumps here.

name: UITitleMenu_BindNodes
purpose: The title menu add-on's node binding (vtable slot 4): finds the TitleEnhanced and Menu nodes and the six MenuButton nodes, and tags them for the event handler.

behavior.text: finds the node `TitleEnhanced`, then `TitleEnhanced/Menu`, then `MenuButton01` to `MenuButton06` (format `MenuButton%02d`, a loop of 6).

each button found gets node +544 = 121 (the tag `UIAddonFFTOTitle_OnEvent` tests), +548 = its index, +557 = 0, the add-on's id in its listener list (+584, 4 slots), and its `Title` text part is stored in the add-on's row.

the buttons are kind 3 nodes (+536); `+220 = -1` at the end. The kind byte of row i is read at +88 + 24 * i by UIAddonFFTOTitle_OnEvent (event 16, the decide on a node tagged 121, index = node +548), by TitleMenu_FocusCurrent and by TitleMenu_SelectKind.

notes: This name replaces an earlier one (`UnDecorator::getZName`) that was a wrong library match in the database.

name: Unit_ApplyEquipment
purpose: Adds the armor and attribute contributions of a unit's equipped items to the unit's stats.

behavior.text: It clears the output field at +0x3C and walks the unit's equipment words from the slot index passed in the second argument.
Each word is tested against 255 and against the 261 bound before it is used.
For a valid word the item record and then the armor sub-record are read, and the armor's attribute byte is applied to the stat block.
It calls three helpers and has three direct callers.
The 255 test and the 261 bound are both present because the word can hold either an empty marker or a stock id.

it first zeroes +0x3B..+0x3D (a word at +0x3C and a byte at +0x3B) and calls Unit_ComputeStats(unit, mode + 1); for each equipped item it adds the attribute record's three stat bytes (bonus PA, MA, Speed) into +0x3B..+0x3D (capped at 255), Move +3 / Jump +4 into +0x42 (cap 253) / +0x43 (cap 7), ORs its 15 status bytes into +0x57.. (innate a, innate b, effective) and its 5 bytes into +0x76.

the seven equipment words are the 7 u16s from +0x1A (0xFF = empty); an item's attribute record is the 26-byte row g_ItemAttributeRecords + 26 x (item record +7) when that byte is below 0x55, and its 15 status bytes go +5..+9 -> +0x57 (always), +10..+14 -> +0x5C (immune), +15..+19 -> +0x61 (current).

its last loop (a pointer from +0x3E, with -3 and -6 from it) makes the totals: +0x3E = min(+0x38 + +0x3B, 99) (PA), +0x3F = min(+0x39 + +0x3C, 99) (MA), +0x40 = min(+0x3A + +0x3D, 50) (Speed, the CT gain Battle_TurnEngine adds); HP / MP are clamped to their maxima.

notes: Name is ours. The offsets +0x38..+0x3F, +0x5C and +0x61 are reached through loops (a pointer walked with a count, and the pointer -3 / -6 of the totals loop), not as constants in the code.

name: Unit_ApplyLevelGrowth
callers: sub_140289900 (hatching a monster from an egg, I)
purpose: Raises a save record's level by a number of levels, growing the five 24-bit stat accumulators at each step from the job row's growth C values.

behavior.text: `save` is the UnitSaveData record (A): job id at +2, level at +29 (0x1D), accumulators at +32, +35, +38, +41, +44 (HP, MP, SP, PA, MA).
the new level is min(level + levels, 99); one growth step runs per level actually gained.

one step: for each stat, accumulator += accumulator / (level + C), then the 24-bit value is clamped; the level byte is incremented after all five stats. C is the even byte of the stat's pair at job row +14+2i, and a C of 0 counts as 1.
the row is chosen by the job id at +2, with one substitution: job 161 uses row 164 when the low nibble at +126 (the level of job index 21) is 8 or more.
returns the final level (the capped target when no level was gained).
the row-164 substitution is a second growth profile for the hidden job 161 once it reaches level 8.

notes: Only the M byte of each pair is ignored here; it is used later by Unit_ComputeStats. The step matches the per-level loop that Unit_ComputeStats replays for generated units.
open_questions: What row 164 holds in the stock build and whether any other caller reaches this routine.

name: Unit_ApplySpawnRecord
purpose: Applies a 40-byte spawn entry to a unit work record before the job and stat build: copies the side and presence byte, picks the save-record path for party and guest units, and sets level, birthday, Brave and Faith with their random rules.

behavior.text: work +4 = entry +23; work +5 and work +494 = entry +24 (the whole byte is copied; the side bits 0x30 and presence bits 0xC0 are read from it by other functions).

entry +1 bit 3 set: UnitWork_BuildFromGuestOrPartyRecord builds the unit from a guest save record; if that fails and event variable 508 is 0 the function returns -1 (Unit_BuildFromRecord then returns -1: no unit). With variable 508 set it falls through to the entry path.

without bit 3, an entry whose marker (entry +0) is 1..3 and whose entry +4 is 0 updates the first party save record whose marker is 0..3 (the marker, the job byte for the reset jobs, the three special ability bits of the old and the new job's skillsets through Skillset_GetAbility 151 / 153 / 154 and sub_1401E8C9C), then builds from it with UnitWork_BuildFromGuestOrPartyRecord.
copies 7 bytes of g_CurrentSpawnEntry (entry +33..+39) to work +407..+413.
marker 0x80 / 0x81 / 0x82 force work +6 bits 0xE0 to 0x80 / 0x40 / 0x20 (values reached by shifts of the marker, not as immediates), keeping the low 5 bits of entry +1.
work +6 = entry +1 (adjusted), work +0 = entry +0, work +2 = 0xFF (no save record).

level (work +41) from entry +3: 0 or 0xFE (tested as (value + 2) & 0xFD == 0) = random from H - H/8 to H, where H is the highest save-record level capped at 99 (the byte at 0x140D405AB, set by Battle_PlaceEntryUnits); 100..253 = value - 100 + H; the result is clamped to 1..99.
birthday from entry +4 (month 1..12) and +5 (day 1..31), otherwise a random day of 365; sub_140279328 turns it into the zodiac nibble of work word +8; job 0x97 (entry +10) forces zodiac 0xC.
Brave: work +43 and +42 = entry +6, a value above 100 replaced by 45 + Rng(30). Faith: work +45 and +44 = entry +7, same rule.
work +40 = entry +28 (above 99 = Rng(100)); work dword +508 = entry +2 (the name byte, replaced later by UnitWork_SetNameKey when the OverrideEntryData row names a key).

open_questions: ? what the special-ability bit copy of the party-record path is for (the three skillset abilities 151 / 153 / 154 were not identified).

name: Unit_AwardJobJp
proto: int Unit_AwardJobJp(int battleUnit, int jp, char team, unsigned int jobIndex)
callers: sub_14030C7C4 (the acting unit's award, index from Job_IdToIndex)
purpose: Adds JP to one job of a battle unit: current JP and total JP (both capped at 9999), recomputes the job's level from the total and rebuilds the unit's unlock mask. The battle JP award goes through it.

behavior.text: the unit is record `battleUnit` of the 21 battle work records (512 bytes each); returns -1 when the slot is empty (+1 = 0xFF), when flags at +97 (0x60) or +98 (bit 0) or +6 (0x20) are set, or when the team bits at +494 differ from `team`.
job index 17 is refused while flag +6 bit 6 is set, job index 18 while +6 bit 7 is set.
JP at +240 + 2*jobIndex and total JP at +286 + 2*jobIndex get `jp` added, each capped at 9999.
the level nibble at +228 + jobIndex/2 (low nibble for odd indices) becomes the number of levels 1..8 whose job_level_jp (GeneralJob row = jobIndex) the new total reaches (`sub_140278D5C`).
then `Unit_BuildJobUnlockMask(+228, +6, +162, +500)` and the 24-bit result is stored big-endian at +159..161.
returns 0 after an award.

name: Unit_BuildAbilityBits
callers: UnitWork_BuildFromSave, Unit_BuildFromRecord, Unit_ReloadFromJobRow, Unit_ReloadFromJobRowEx, sub_140275EF4 (IDA code references)
purpose: Rebuilds a battle unit's passive-ability bit map from its innate ability words and its equipped reaction, support and movement ability.

behavior.text: clears unit +0x94 (8 bytes), +0x9C (one word) and +0x9E (one byte): the whole 11-byte map.
calls Unit_SetAbilityBit for the four innate words at +0x0A, +0x0C, +0x0E, +0x10, then for the equipped reaction (+0x14), support (+0x16) and movement (+0x18) words, seven calls in that order.

Unit_SetAbilityBit stores a reaction-range id (below 454) in +0x14, and the equipped reaction word is read only after the four innate calls, so an innate reaction-range id has already replaced the equipped reaction word when that word is read.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140276DF4, renamed 2026-11-10); read 2026-11-10. 104 bytes, read whole. The five callers are the unit build and reload paths.

name: Unit_BuildFromRecord
proto: int Unit_BuildFromRecord(uint8_t *work, uint8_t *spawn, int arg3, int mode, const uint8_t *overrideRow)
callers: Battle_PlaceEntryUnits (battle slot i from entry i), sub_1402841D0 (new-game save records from the entry block, a stack work record), Battle_RebuildUnitInPlace (mode 130, no spawn record)
callees: Unit_ApplySpawnRecord, UnitWork_InitFromSpawnRecord, Unit_InitAbilitiesFromJob, Unit_ComputeStats, UnitWork_ApplyStartingEquipment, sub_140276DF4, sub_1402757B0, sub_1401EA910, sub_14027788C, sub_1402760E8, sub_14002630C
purpose: Builds a unit work record from a spawn record: applies the record, sets up job state, abilities and growth, computes the stats and the starting equipment.

behavior.text: unless mode is 130 it first clears several work fields (+65, +396, +436, +440, +443, +492, +500) and calls Unit_ApplySpawnRecord; a non-zero result returns -1.

then (for mode 130, or by the record's own flags) UnitWork_InitFromSpawnRecord, Unit_InitAbilitiesFromJob and sub_140276DF4 run, five stat pointers (+123, +126, +129, +132, +135) go to sub_1402757B0, and 10 bytes of the job row from row offset 14 (growth pairs) are copied to +138 (job 0xA1 uses row 164 when the low nibble of +238 is 8 or more).
Unit_ComputeStats runs with work+2 temporarily 0xFE (when it was 0xFF); the starting equipment is applied when mode is not 130 and work+2 is above 19.
for a unit of team 0..3 the first save record with that team (byte 0 below 4, byte +1 not 0xFF) supplies bits of the word at work+8 (its +5 and +6 bytes).

the fifth argument (kept in rbp from 0x140275CBF) is passed to UnitWork_InitFromSpawnRecord as its third: the entry's OverrideEntryData row from Battle_PlaceEntryUnits, null from sub_1402841D0 and Battle_RebuildUnitInPlace (2026-11-09).
UnitWork_ApplyStartingEquipment is called with (work, entry) at the end (rcx is set before the leaf sub_14027788C, which does not write it); the gate is mode not 130 and work +2 above 0x13.

notes: The row offset for the growth copy is computed at 0x140275DDF; r8 holds the offset (before the table base is added) at 0x140275DEA.
open_questions: What the last block (the save record lookup and the +8 word) is for (? by name only).

name: Unit_BuildInnateStatuses
callers: sub_140278C1C, sub_14028531C, PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment, sub_14030BF04, sub_14033E4C4, sub_14039651C
callees: sub_140276DF4, sub_140277C58, Unit_LoadEquipmentAndEvade, Unit_ApplyEquipment, sub_14027788C, Unit_ReinitStatusCountdowns, BattleUnit_SetStatusVisual
purpose: Builds the three innate status groups of a unit from its job row, its equipment attributes and its permanent extra set, restores the battle-applied set, and refreshes the status display.

behavior.text: the fourth innate source at unit +0x198 is ORed into the group at +0x61 before the job row is copied, matching the fourth group reported in the status model.
the job row is selected from the unit job byte at +3 (with the Mime special case at 0xA1), and its three five-byte status sets are copied over the groups at +0x57, +0x5C and +0x61.
the battle-applied set at +0x1EF is saved on the stack before the copy and restored afterwards.
the equipment attribute apply (Unit_ApplyEquipment) then ORs the status bytes of the equipped items into the same groups.
it calls Unit_LoadEquipmentAndEvade and sub_14027788C to rebuild the ability/RSM side, and sub_140276DF4 for the stat block.
Unit_ReinitStatusCountdowns runs at the end for the two reload variants, and BattleUnit_SetStatusVisual refreshes the status icon/flag owner.
the second argument selects the reload path; the six callers include the job-change, equipment-change and save-reload paths.
the fourth group at +0x198 has no identified producer, so the extra innate statuses are only as complete as whatever fills that field.
whether an equipment status in group 3 survives the first battle refresh; the order of the copy and the restore here does not settle it.

it saves +0x1EF before the rebuild and writes that copy back afterwards (never +0x61 into +0x1EF), and it rewrites Move +0x42 and Jump +0x43 from the job row (+24, +25 & 0x7F) before the equipment bonuses; the PA / MA / Speed bases +0x38..+0x3A are kept (Unit_ComputeStats runs with mode 1 through its callee Unit_ApplyEquipment) and only the totals +0x3E..+0x40 are rebuilt (in that callee).

notes: Whole function read (612 bytes). The order of the group writes was checked; the source of +0x198 remains open.

name: Unit_BuildJobUnlockMask
proto: uint32_t Unit_BuildJobUnlockMask(int64_t *levels, char flags, int64_t statePtr, int storyStage)
purpose: Builds the 24-bit job-unlock mask for a unit. Bit (0x400000 >> r) is job index r+1: index 20 (our job) = bit 0x8, index 21 = bit 0x4.

behavior.text: `levels` is the unit's nibble-packed job levels (two jobs per byte).
loops over rows of g_JobNeedLevelRows (12 bytes/row, nibble-packed required levels). A row is satisfied when each required nibble <= the unit's level; satisfied -> the row's mask bit is set.
stock loop count is 19 (rows 0..18 = Chemist..Mime). The plan raises it to 21 so rows 19 and 20 (indices 20 and 21) are evaluated.

tail - if storyStage >= 20, a second check for the two hidden jobs (ids at unk_14071EA38) walks 24 entries from sub_140275980; if an entry is unmet, or storyStage < 20, execution reaches the instruction at 0x140348806 that ANDs the mask register with 0xFFFFFFF7, which CLEARS mask bit 0x8.
the story table's exact meaning (what the 24 entries are).

rows of g_JobNeedLevelRows (0x14067F390) hold 24 nibbles, high nibble first; nibble n is the level required in job index n. A row's bit is set only when ALL ten compared bytes (20 nibbles) are at or below the unit's levels, so a bit set means every prerequisite is met.
`flags` 0x20 skips the row loop (mask 0); flag 0x40 pads the local level copy and clears mask bit 0x40; flag 0x80 pads it and clears mask bit 0x20.

for story stage 20 and above, bit 0x8 also needs every listed ability to be learned in both jobs whose ids are stored at 0x14071EA38 (76 and 80 in stock, two u32 values): the learned bits of each job (3 bytes per job index, read with the bit reader) are checked against Skillset_BuildAbilityList(set, 15).
PartyUnit_FillFromWork stores the result at party-record +120..+122 (high byte first), which is where JobList_Build reads it.
the work-record builder also keeps the mask in the save record at +47..+49, so it is recomputed on every entry to the jobs screen and needs no saved unlock bit.
a set bit means all prerequisites of that job's row are met (every required level nibble is satisfied); a clear bit means at least one is not.

callers store the three mask bytes (high byte first) at A+47..49 in the save record (UnitWork_BuildFromSave) and at B+120..122 in the party record (PartyUnit_FillFromWork); the job list and Job_IsLockedForParty read the B+120 copy.

notes:
Row r <-> job index r+1. The earlier session zeroed row 20 (index 21: Onion Knight, Squire 6 + Chemist 6) by mistake; the correct row for index 20 is row 19.

Stock rows verified against the classic requirements: Mime needs Squire 8, Chemist 8, Knight 3, Archer 3, Monk 4 and so on. Rows 19 and 20 exist in the stock data (index 20: Geomancer, Dragoon, Samurai and Ninja at 8; index 21: Squire 6 and Chemist 6) but are only read after the 19 -> 21 row-count change. The executable rows, not the GeneralJob table, decide what the jobs list offers; GeneralJob is read only by the tree panel and the exp getter.

The mask is recomputed on every work/party record build, so the save needs no manual unlock bits. The job list is decided by these executable rows, not by the GeneralJob nxd table.
open_questions: Who stores the returned mask into the unit (unit+120), and which events re-run this?

name: Unit_BuildPreviewSpriteRecord
proto: int Unit_BuildPreviewSpriteRecord(SpriteRecord *out, int partyIndex, unsigned char slot, char a4, char a5, char a6, char a7)
purpose: Builds the sprite record for a party unit's preview. In normal play it just forwards to PreviewUnit_BuildRecord with slotArg = 2 * slot + 4.

behavior.text: clears the record (job -1); when both debug globals unk_142FF9F30 and qword_142FF9F34 are zero it returns PreviewUnit_BuildRecord(out, partyIndex, unit preview index (unit +44), 0, ..., 2 * slot + 4, a4).
otherwise (debug path) a6 selects overrides from the preview entry flags (4, 52 or 72 as the slot argument) and it tail-calls PreviewUnit_BuildSpriteRecord.

name: Unit_BuildRsmAbilityList
proto: uint16 Unit_BuildRsmAbilityList(UnitWork *c, uint16 request, char kinds, void *spawn)
purpose: Answers a reaction / support / movement request of a spawn record: a fixed id is returned as is, a 'random' request (>= 0x1FE) picks one of the learned RSM abilities of the unit.

behavior.text: request < 0x1FE: returned unchanged. Units flagged 0x20 at +6 get 0.

walks the jobs 74..93 (list index 0..19; index 0 = the spawn job or the unit's marker job): the 3rd learned byte of each job (C +164 + 3 x index) selects slots 16..21 of the job's skillset; abilities 422..453 (reaction), 454..485 (support), >= 486 (movement) are collected by the kind bits.
then picks one with the battle random generator.
the compare of the request word with the bound 0x1FE and its jump are at 0x140278392; the first range test is at 0x1402784DB (the request mask is r9b, reloaded every slot).

notes: Only generic jobs are walked; this concerns generated units only (a player's unit equips through the job menus).

name: Unit_ChangeBattleStat
proto: int Unit_ChangeBattleStat(char change, uint8_t *stat, uint8_t cap, uint8_t min)
purpose: Applies one stat change of an action result to a unit stat byte, clamped, and keeps the stat total in step.

behavior.text: change bit 7 set = an increase by the low 7 bits, clear = a decrease; with cap 0xFF and an amount of 127 the amount becomes 255.
the new value is clamped to min..cap; it returns 0 when the value does not change, else writes it and returns 1.
when min is 1 it also writes stat[6] = min(value + stat[3], cap): for the base stats +0x38..+0x3A (the pointer the caller passes) this is the total +0x3E..+0x40 = base + equipment bonus +0x3B..+0x3D.

the caller passes the change and the byte: Battle_ApplyActionResult calls it for result block +0x14 on +0x3A (Speed, cap 50, min 1), +0x15 on +0x41 (CT, cap 255, min 0), +0x16 on +0x38 (PA, cap 99, min 1), +0x17 on +0x39 (MA, cap 99, min 1), +0x18 on +0x2B (Brave, cap 100) and +0x19 on +0x2D (Faith, cap 100, min 0) (offsets of the caller, not of this function).

notes: Name is ours. Whole function read.

name: Unit_CheckSpawnTile
purpose: Answers whether battle record n may stand on its tile: 0 = yes, -1 = no.

behavior.text: reads the record's tile (+0x4F, +0x50, the layer bit 7 of +0x51; the body reaches these and +0x9D / +0x9E as the absolute addresses of record 0's fields plus 512 times the record); no when it is outside the map size, when the map cell's flags or height bits refuse the unit (its +0x9D / +0x9E movement bits are tested), when the terrain kind is 18 or 28, or when a lower record whose slot byte is not 0xFF stands on the same tile and layer.

notes: Named from its result; the meaning of each map flag was not read.

name: Unit_CollectJobSkillsetPairs
purpose: Lists (job, skillset) pairs of the jobs a party unit can take as its secondary skill: 8-byte entries, 0xFFFF in the second word ends the list.

behavior.text: the job list is JobList_BuildForPartyUnit(partyIndex, list, 1); skips the unit's own job (B +36), 93, 161 and 164.
each entry gets the job id and its JobTable row's skillset (row guard: job < 0xAE stock); returns the count.

the job list is a 24-word stack buffer (rsp+0x28); the terminator is the qword at out[count] whose low dword is 0xFFFF0000 (the high dword is an uninitialised stack word); words 2 and 3 of an entry are not written.

name: Unit_CollectJobSkillsets
purpose: Builds the secondary-skillset choice list of a party unit: the skillset byte of every job the unit can take, except its own job and three excluded ids, terminated by 0xFFFF. Returns the count.

behavior.text: reads the unit's job word at party record +36, then fills a 24-word list with JobList_BuildForPartyUnit(unit, list, 1).

for each listed job id except the unit's own job, 93, 161 and 164, writes the byte at g_JobTable + 49*id (the skillset byte, row +0) to the output; ids >= 174 (0xAE) use a null row pointer and read address 0 (a null-page read, same finding as J7).
writes 0xFFFF after the last entry and returns the number written.
of the JobTable fields it reads only the skillset byte (+0).

notes:
J5c/J5e: the list holds skillset ids (224 for job 160); the command NAME later comes from JobCommand key = skillset id. The function is one of the 15 JobTable bound-readers (its bound is a compare against 0xAE).

The bound 0xAE is loaded into a register and compared from there.

The job list is a 24-word stack buffer (rsp+0x20). The ability screen's Secondary list in g_MenuList is built by this function, called from sub_140366FE0 through JobAbilityList_Build.
open_questions: What reads ids 93, 161, 164 specially (Mime-like and hidden jobs, I).

name: Unit_ComputeStats
purpose: Turns a work record's five 24-bit stat accumulators and the job row's growth pairs into the unit's displayed HP, MP, Speed, PA and MA. Called whenever a work record is built or refreshed.

behavior.text: `work` is the work record (C). The accumulators are 3 bytes each at +123, +126, +129, +132, +135 (order HP, MP, SP, PA, MA); the growth pair for stat i is the C byte at +138+2i and the M byte at +139+2i, copied there from the job row by UnitWork_ApplyJobRow.

each stat is ((accumulator * M) / divisor) >> 14, at least 1. The divisor is 100 for every stat, except that HP and MP use 10 and a cap of 65535 (instead of 999) when bit 2 of work+6 is set (I: the egg/monster flag).
caps: HP and MP 999, SP 50, PA and MA 99. The accumulator itself is clamped to 24 bits and written back.

destinations: HP max +50 and MP max +54 always; current HP +48 and current MP +52 only when `flags` is 0. SP goes to +58, PA to +56, MA to +57, all three skipped when `flags` bit 0 is set.
  - V: the store instructions are `0x140277082` (current HP), `0x140277078` (max HP), `0x140277058` (current MP), `0x14027704E` (max MP), `0x140277011` (SP), `0x140277048` (PA), `0x14027703E` (MA).
when bit 1 of work+155 is set, HP is multiplied by 6/5 after the cap (I: a status or equipment effect).
SP also gets the signed word at extra+128 added when `extra` is non-null and `flags` bit 0 is clear.

when `flags` is 0 and the slot id at work+2 is 0xFE, the accumulators are first re-grown from level 2 up to the level at work+41, using raw += raw / (C - 1 + n) for n = 2..level. A C of 0 counts as 1.
the 0xFE branch rebuilds a generated unit's stats from level 1 values; other units keep the accumulators they already carry.

notes:
Stat accumulators are 24-bit fixed point: the >> 14 means a stock accumulator near 16384 * 100 / M gives the raw stat. The record offsets here are the work-record (C) layout; the same five accumulators sit at +32..+46 of the save record (A), which Unit_ApplyLevelGrowth edits.

C1 (2026-10-30): the work record C is the **live** battle unit record: `g_BattleUnitTable` (`0x141853CE0`) is an
array of 21 C records (stride 512), not a copy. `UnitWork_BuildFromSaveIndex` calls this function with `flags = 0`,
so a roster build sets current HP/MP equal to max; after that `Battle_ApplyActionResult` (`0x14030A488`) is the only
writer of current HP/MP (`0x14030A62F`, `0x14030A638`). See `docs/reference/battle-units.md` for the field table and
the three independent readers per field.
open_questions: Meaning of the extra argument's word at +128 (a caller-supplied SP bonus?), and the exact source of the work+155 bit.

name: Unit_GetFaceIndex
purpose: Maps a unit job and its variant byte to the face index the portrait and unit panel draw.

behavior.text: the job word is unit +0x24; jobs 0x5E through 0x8D (the bound is job-0x5E at most 0x2F) are looked up as a dword at 0x140715378 + job*4 and the table value is returned.
job 0x48 returns 0x4C; 0x90 returns 0x4E; 0x91 returns 0x51; 0x96 returns 0x4E; 0x97 returns 0x4F; 0x99 and 0x9A return 0x51 (the later ids are reached by chained subs from 0x48 and 0x90).
the remaining jobs read the variant byte at unit +0x72.
a variant of 0x82 returns unit +0x166 plus 0x3D; variant 0xA2 (0x82+0x20) returns 0x58 and 0xA3 (+1) returns 0x59.
a variant below 0x4A is looked up in the byte table at 0x14067F840; a variant of 0x4A or above tail-jumps to PartyUnit_FaceIndexForJob with the job and unit +0x70 bit 0x40 as arguments.
the return value is a small face index; the function writes nothing.
the table and the fixed values cover the generic jobs, while the special jobs (Mime, monsters, story characters) get hand-written indices.
the meaning of the 0x4A threshold and of the 0x14067F840 table; the table contents were not decoded.

notes:
Whole function read (204 bytes, no unwind entry). The T2 live census lists it as a face-index reader that its scenarios did not reach.

V (2026-11-08): the read at 0x1402896D3 is `dword_140715378[word +0x24]` behind the guard word - 0x5E <= 0x2F, so it reads the 48 dwords at 0x1407154F0 (one per monster job 94..141), the table right after the HD sheet entry table. 0x140715378 is a virtual base 392 bytes inside the HD table.

name: Unit_GetReachHeight
purpose: The height (in half-steps) the weapon reach rules measure from: the unit's own tile without its water depth, raised when the unit is mounted or floating, with the depth added back for some movement flags.

behavior.text: tile = the record at x + (layer << 8) + width * y (x +0x4F, y +0x50, layer = +0x51 bit 7); h = (b3 & 0x1F) + 2 * b2 (8-bit); depth = 2 * (b3 >> 5).
when unit +0x1B4 has bit 7, h += 2 and the flags below are read from the unit record at slot (+0x1B4 & 0x1F) instead.
when flags byte +0x9E has bit 0x08, or +0x63 has bit 0x40 (status 17, Float), h += 2 and the unit counts as raised.
when depth is not 0: raised or +0x9E bit 7 -> h += depth; else +0x9E bit 6 -> h += depth - 2; else nothing.
+0x1B4 bit 7 = riding (the low bits name the mount) and +0x9E holds movement-ability flags (bit 3 a float-like ability, bits 7 / 6 water movement); the readers here do not name them.

notes: Unlike the target height (BattleRange_MarkTileInBand), the unit's own height leaves the water depth out unless a flag adds it.
open_questions: ? Which movement abilities set +0x9E bits 3, 6 and 7.

name: Unit_GetSpriteSetId
proto: int Unit_GetSpriteSetId(int mode, unsigned id, int *outBits)
callers: sub_1401F3F70, sub_1402C08C0, sub_1402C1310, sub_1402C1EA8, sub_14036F5D0, sub_140370414 (errand result scene)
callees: SpriteId_ToShape, SceneUnit_EntryById, sub_14032ACE0, sub_140214134, sub_1401E39BC, UITable_GetRowByKey
purpose: Resolves a unit's sprite number for the event and scene code. In scenes of a few types it reads the generic-job selector table and converts its value to a sprite shape; otherwise it takes a generated or saved path.

behavior.text: mode 0 returns whatever sub_140214134(id, outBits) gives; modes other than 0 and 1 return -1.

mode 1 uses the selector path only when the scene id word at 0x141848BB0 is 21, 43, 44 or 51. Then the unit entry is looked up by SceneUnit_EntryById: entries are 564 bytes at 0x1408E6CB0, id 0..15, only valid in those scenes (else the call returns 0).

selector index = (0x60, or 0x61 when bit 7 of entry byte +4 is clear) + 2 * (entry byte +2 - 74); entry byte +2 is the job id. If the index is below 0xD3, the 16-bit value at word_1406807C0[index] is read, else 0.

the value goes through SpriteId_ToShape (a 160-entry u32 table at 0x1407146D0 for values up to 0x9F, a few fixed ids above) and is rejected (-1) when it exceeds 0xCD; the result is returned and `outBits` receives ((value >> 10) & 3) + 8.

for generic jobs 74..91 the selector value, mapped through SpriteId_ToShape, gives the same shape number as the battle-sprite rule for all 36 job-sex pairs; for jobs 92 and 93 the two numberings differ (selector gives 132..135, the battle rule 130..133).

in other scenes the id comes from sub_14032ACE0 and the save record (the table with key 0x112 is queried with the record's marker byte), is passed through SpriteId_ToShape when the global mode word allows, and is capped at 0xCD; it returns -1 when a float setting is below 2.0.
the selector value is the second numbering of the same sprites (the event-character sprite number); the earlier note that it is a portrait index is not supported.

on the save-record branch the code comes from sub_14032ACE0 -> sub_14032AB3C -> PortraitCode_FillCell and is a byte (or the record index when no code is set); the function writes it unmapped to dword_142E7FCAC[0] and dword_142FF9EDC before any face mapping.

with the mode word & ~2 = 0 no code gives -1 at the cap 0x1402C0816: 146 codes map to faces up to 204 and the 110 unmapped codes return as themselves (50 of them 206..255); in modes 1 and 5 the codes 206..255 give -1.

a face number 9056 / 9057 returned for a unit whose look byte is 56 / 57 makes the roster and the Status screen draw the texture `wldface_9056_08` / `wldface_9057_08`: the face number is formatted into the texture name unchanged at four digits.

notes:
Conflict between earlier readings: one pass called the selector value a shape id (via the table at 0x1407146D0), another called it the event-character sprite number; the code path supports both statements (the value is converted by SpriteId_ToShape). The selector is indexed by a shape-style number (96..133 for the 20 generic jobs), not by job id.

The selector words are one of six identical copies of one 211-word table (the words are portrait codes; five other readers use the other copies). The two face-number caps differ: on the scene path (0x1402C0816) the cap also clips the raw id when the mode word skips SpriteId_ToShape, on the generic path (0x1402C086C) it clips only SpriteId_ToShape's answer and an unmapped code is returned uncapped.
open_questions: Which scenes use the 21/43/44/51 path in play, and how the non-scene branch picks its id.

name: Unit_GetVoicePatternId
callers: sub_1400F8930, sub_1400F8D6C, sub_1401D7874, sub_1401E37D4, sub_1401EDB88 and others
callees: NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, NxdTable_GetEntryCount, NxdTable_GetEntryByKeys2, UserSituation_IsMet
purpose: Returns the voice pattern id of a unit: from its job row, else by a rule over the CharaName rows.

behavior.text: the Job row's voice_pattern column (+0x1C, Job table 46) when non-zero is returned as the unit's voice pattern id; otherwise a rule over CharaName rows (checked with UserSituation_IsMet).

notes: Name is ours; read as the source of the pattern id only.

name: Unit_HasStatusGroup
purpose: Tests whether a unit carries any status of one of the ten party-wide status groups by ANDing its five status bytes against that group's five-byte mask.

behavior.text: the second argument indexes the ten 5-byte masks at 0x1411A6A70; the mask stride is five bytes.
the unit status bytes at +0x61, +0x62, +0x63, +0x64 and +0x65 are tested one at a time against the matching mask byte (the pointer is incremented from +0x61, so only +0x61 is an immediate).
it returns 1 as soon as one byte shares a bit, and 0 after all five bytes.
a group index outside 0..9 is not bounded by this body; the address arithmetic simply reads whatever follows the mask table.
the masks are built once by Status_BuildFlagMasks; this function only reads them.
group 3 is the Crystal/Stone/Chest/Stop/Sleep set used by the turn-start status check, and group 4 is the "can learn" test.
the meaning of the remaining eight groups; the mask bytes are data and were not decoded here.

notes: Head and whole body read (0x7C bytes, no unwind entry); the 17 call sites were counted from the image.

name: Unit_InitAbilitiesFromJob
callees: Mem_Free and others in the part not read
purpose: Sets a unit work record's skillset and innate ability words from its job row (head read: the skillset choice and the innate copy).

behavior.text: the job is work[3]; job 0xA1 uses row 164 when the low nibble of work+238 is 8 or more. With no spawn record it clears +20 and returns.
the skillset byte at +18 is the spawn record's byte at +29 when that byte is 1 to 254, else the job row's byte 0 (row = JobTable + 49 * job).

the job id is stored in a stack slot (rsp+0x48) and the four innate ability words at +10 are built from row bytes 1..8 of the row of that stored job, after the (not read here) middle part that handles the unit's team bits and the learned-ability bytes at +162..+227.

for a unit built from a spawn record, the OverrideEntryData row (third argument) is read: its array at +0x4C (granted_abilities: offset dword +0x4C, count +0x50, i32 elements, low 16 bits used), its array at +0x54 (withheld_abilities: offset +0x54, count +0x58) and its byte +0x9A (free_abilities). List 1 is the spawn record's reaction / support / movement words (below 0x1FE) plus the granted array, list 2 the withheld array.
both lists and the byte +0x9A are passed to Unit_QueueJobAbilitiesToLearn for each pair of generic jobs (see the behaviour EntryAbilityListsOfPreplacedUnits).

for a human unit (c + 6 & 0xC0) built from a spawn record, its loop over the level bytes c + 228..237 gives job indices 0..19 their starting JP (Unit_InitJobJp) and queues their abilities (Unit_QueueJobAbilitiesToLearn).
the spawn record's three R / S / M words join the learn queue only below 0x1FE (dx, shared by the three compares at 0x1402772E2, 0x1402772F3, 0x140277307).

notes: Only the head and the final innate copy were read. At 0x140277234 the job is in rcx on the path that reads the row's skillset, which is also what the stack slot is filled from; the stack slot (rsp+0x48) is read at 0x1402774AE.
open_questions: The middle part (team bits 0xC0 handling, the learned-ability bytes) was not studied.

name: Unit_InitBattleStatusState
purpose: Sets up the status state of a unit that has just been built into the battle: the applied set, the countdowns and the KO counter.

behavior.text: sets +0x40 to 1 when it is 0; with reset it clears the word +0x194 and the byte +0x196.
derives the applied set from the effective one: +0x1EF = +0x61 & ~+0x57 (five bytes; a loop from the +0x61 base: +398 and -10 from it).
zeroes the 16 countdown bytes +0x66..+0x75 (one 16-byte store at +0x66) and sets the KO counter +0x07 to 0xFF when +5 bit 2 or +6 bits 0x09 are set, else 3; then calls Unit_ReinitStatusCountdowns.

notes: Name is ours. Whole function read; a leaf without unwind data. The only place the game derives +0x1EF from +0x61; each caller builds the record (from the save, a spawn record or the roster) right before.

name: Unit_InitJobJp
proto: void Unit_InitJobJp(UnitWork *c, uint8_t flags, unsigned int jobIndex, int level)
purpose: A new unit's starting JP in one job: the GeneralJob curve's value at the job's level plus a random part.

behavior.text: JP (c + 240 + 2 * index) and total JP (c + 286 + 2 * index) both get base + rand * step >> 15, where base = Job_GetJpForLevel(index, level) (100 at level 0), step = the distance to the next level's value when it is below 100, else 100 (the same at level 8); rand = 15 bits of the game's xorshift128 (xmmword_1408E5FC8).
index 18 with flags bit 7, or index 17 with flags bit 6 (the gender-locked jobs), get 0.
with the stock curve every human unit's jobs start at level 1 with 100..199 JP; slot 49's save: every stock job a unit may have holds 100 or more total JP.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1402770BC).

name: Unit_ListItemCommandItems
proto: int Unit_ListItemCommandItems(int unit_slot, uint8_t command, uint8_t *out)
purpose:
Builds the item list for the Item command: it takes the usable ability list of the command's skill set and rewrites
each of the fourteen item abilities into the item id the command offers.

behavior.text: the first argument is a battle unit slot and the second a command id; the third is the caller's output buffer.
it returns 0 when the unit slot has no live unit, and 0 when the command id is not 6.
for command 6 it calls `sub_14030E368` to build the usable ability list for that command and gets a count back.

it walks the returned 16-bit ability words and accepts only ids 368 through 381 (the test subtracts 0x170 and rejects
  results above 0x0D); everything else is skipped.

each accepted ability is translated to an item id by the fourteen-row byte table at `0x140785E18`, indexed by
  the ability id minus 368.
the table read at 0x14030E722 is the single call site of that table in the image.
each result is written into the output buffer as one byte, and the list is terminated with `0xFF`.
it returns `0x100 + count`, not a bare count; the zero case is the failure value.
it performs no inventory check; an item with a zero count is still listed by this function.

the `0x100` in the return value is a list-type tag the menu uses to tell an item list from an ability list,
  because the sibling list builders return small counts.

the fourteen rows cover ids 240..253, so a consumable numbered 254, 255 or above can never appear here even when
  the rest of its data is valid.
whether any caller bounds-checks the count against the output buffer size.

notes:
- V: the whole function was read, and the single call site of the table in the image was confirmed.
- I: kind1 gives the item id per Item-command ability (ids 0x170..0x17D).

name: Unit_ListThrowableItems
proto: int Unit_ListThrowableItems(int unit_slot, uint8_t command, uint8_t *out)
purpose:
Builds the candidate list for the Throw command: the item ids in the unit's inventory that the game considers
throwable, ordered for the menu.

behavior.text: the arguments are a battle unit slot, a command id and the caller's output buffer.
it returns 0 when the unit slot has no live unit, and 0 when the command id is not 20.

it calls `sub_14030E368` to build the command's usable ability list, then converts the throw abilities 382..393
  into the twelve equip-category bytes of the table at `0x140789290`; the table read is at 0x14030E886.
it then scans item ids from 0 to 255 inclusive; an item numbered 256 or above is never examined.
an item is kept only when its record's equip-category byte at +5 is one of those twelve values.
an item is kept only when its record's slot-flags byte at +3 is signed-negative, which is the weapon-slot bit.
an item is kept only when its weapon record's flag byte at +1 has bit 2 set.

the stock test is skipped when the owning unit's team bits (record +0x1EE, mask `0x30`) are set: the set case jumps
  straight to the append, so an enemy unit lists a throwable even with a zero count, and only a unit with the bits clear
  needs a non-zero inventory count at `0x1411A7C00`.
it writes each kept id as one byte and terminates the list with `0xFF` at the position the count points to.
it returns the count as an 8-bit value, so a list of 256 entries would report zero.
before returning it sorts the list with the standard sort routine `sub_1405DB690`, element size one.

the comparator it passes (0x14030E774, handed to qsort, not called here) reads the two item ids, asks 0x1400F8674 for
  each one's row and orders them by the 32-bit field at row +0x28, ascending; both addresses belong to the comparator, not
  to this body.

the twelve categories are the throwable weapon classes, because each maps one-to-one onto a Throw ability and
  items 122..127 are the six throwing weapons.

weapon flag bit 2 is the stock "can be thrown" marker, because the six throwing weapons set it and no other
  weapon in the stock table does.

the comparator is sub_14030E774 (Item_CompareSortOrder): it returns -1 / 0 / 1 from the Item row dword +0x28 (column sort_order; read in the comparator, not in this body), smaller first; sub_14030EEF0 uses it as well.
sort_order is an order key, not a price: lists sorted by it place the smaller value first.

notes:
- V: the whole function was read, and the comparator and the sort routine were read at their heads to identify them.
- I: kind2 maps each Throw ability
  (ids 0x17E..0x189) to a thrown item type.

name: Unit_LoadEquipmentAndEvade
purpose: Fills the unit work record's weapon and evade bytes (+68..+78) from the job row and the equipped items.

behavior.text: clears +68..+78; +75 = JobTable byte 26 (class evade) of the unit's job (job 0xA1 uses row 164 when the job level nibble at +238 is 8 or more).
skipped when bit 0x20 of work+6 is set.
item at +30: when record +3 has bit 0x08, accessory sub-record bytes 0 / 1 go to +72 / +76.
items at +34 and +38: when record +3 has bit 0x40, shield sub-record bytes 0 / 1 go to +73 / +77 and +74 / +78.
items at +32 and +36: when record +3 has bit 0x80, weapon sub-record bytes 4 / 5 go to +68 / +70 and +69 / +71.
keeps the work pointer in r11 across every item call.
+30 accessory, +32 / +36 right / left hand, +34 / +38 shields; +68.. weapon power, +70.. weapon evade, +72..+74 physical and +76..+78 magic evade.

notes: - Only the item reads were studied.

name: Unit_MouseHitTest
callees: NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_1401F8618, sub_14027A46C, sub_1400D425C, cosf, sinf
purpose: Tests the mouse position against the hit areas of the units on the field.

behavior.text: loads the CharShape row's char_mouse_collision key (dword at +0x28) and looks up CharMouseCollision (table 334); the collision row's float +8 (times 0.5) and +0xC / +0x10 size the area tested around the unit's tile.

notes: Name is ours; only the collision lookup was read closely.

name: Unit_QueueJobAbilitiesToLearn
proto: int Unit_QueueJobAbilitiesToLearn(UnitWork *c, uint16 job, ..., uint16 *list, long count, uint16 *list2, long count2, char flag)
purpose: Marks the abilities of one job as learned in a work record when they appear in a given list (unit setup).

behavior.text: index = Job_IdToIndex(job). Job 74 (Squire) is always taken (a story unit's marker job replaces it); any other job must have its unlock bit set (C +159..161 as a 24-bit value tested against 0x800000 >> index).
jobs 91 / 92 are skipped when C +6 bit 6 / bit 7 are set.

the skillset is C +18 for the unit's own job, else the job's JobTable row byte 0; for each of the 24 slots whose ability is in the first list, Unit_TryLearnAbility(c, index, slot, ability, guaranteed, charge) runs; then every slot not in the second list.

'the unit's own job' is the compare of the queued job with the job byte C +3 (0x140278248..0x14027824F); the own-job pass also sets the guaranteed flag when the spawn record's skillset byte (+29) is 0.
its only caller, Unit_InitAbilitiesFromJob, queues the jobs 74..93 in pairs (i + 73, i + 74 for i = 1, 3, .. 19), between level fixes of the two jobs (sub_1402770BC).

the last argument (the row's free_abilities byte): pass 1 calls Unit_TryLearnAbility(c, index, slot, ability, 1, charge) with charge = 1 only when that byte is 0 and the job is not the unit's own job with the default skillset (spawn +29 = 0); with the byte set the abilities of list 1 are learned for no JP.
pass 2 goes over every slot whose ability is not in the second list and calls Unit_TryLearnAbility(c, index, slot, ability, own_default, !own_default).

open_questions: I: the meaning of the two lists (abilities to learn and abilities to keep) from the callers.

name: Unit_ReactionVoiceAllowed
purpose: Answers a yes / no question about a unit's reaction voice line by the rule row of its current ability.

behavior.text: gets the Ability row of the unit's current ability (unit word +322), reads row +0x38 (column ability_reaction_voice_type) as a key of AbilityReactionVoiceType (nxd 330, cache qword_143CDA2C8), copies that row's 11 dwords (+4..+0x2C) and switches on the dword picked by the third argument.

rule value 0 -> true; 1 -> false; 2 -> sub_14026A508(unit); 3 -> not sub_14026A508(unit); 4 -> a once-per-unit gate in byte_141873180 indexed by the unit (+8) or by the other unit (+8 of the second argument); other values -> true.
returns false when a row is missing.
the Ability column holds 0 on 486 rows, 2 on 21 rows and 3 on 5 rows; the rule table has rows 0..3.

open_questions: ? what sub_14026A508 tests and which reaction each of the 11 slots is.

name: Unit_ReinitStatusCountdowns
purpose: Re-initialises the countdown bytes of a unit after its innate status set has been rebuilt: it merges the saved innate status bytes into the effective set and starts a duration for every battle-applied status that has none.

behavior.text: unit +0x9E bit 3 sets bit 0x40 of unit +0x59 before anything else.

five bytes are processed in one loop: for i 0..4 the innate byte at +0x57+i is ORed with the saved byte at +0x1EF+i into the effective byte at +0x61+i, and the innate bit is cleared from the group byte at +0x5C+i; the loop walks one pointer over +0x5C with displacements -5, +0x193 and +5.
the battle-applied set starts at +0x1EF; the bit for status id s is in byte +0x1EF+(s>>3), so the ids below test the bytes at +0x1EF+3 and +0x1EF+4.
a status whose bit is set in the battle-applied set at +0x1EF and whose countdown byte at +0x66 is still zero gets a new duration through Unit_SetStatusCountdown(unit, id, 0).
the loop covers status ids 24 through 39 (0x28), one countdown byte each at unit +0x66 onward.
the function is the "second half" of the innate-status build: the first half writes the sets, this one repairs the countdowns that the rewrite disturbed.
whether a status already present with a non-zero countdown keeps it; the code only starts one when the countdown byte is zero.

notes:
Whole function read (134 bytes). Called from the innate builder and from its reload twin.
V: it starts countdowns only for +0x1EF bits, never from +0x61 (its loop runs from the +0x5C base: +0x57 is -5 and +0x61 is +5 from it).

name: Unit_ReloadFromJobRowEx
purpose: The same re-read of the job row as Unit_BuildInnateStatuses (0x140278688, the plain variant), reading the status bytes from a second copy at +495 (head read).

behavior.text: the row is JobTable + 49 * work[3]; job 0xA1 uses row 164 when the low nibble of work+238 is 8 or more.
the first copies are the same as Unit_BuildInnateStatuses's (+66, +67, +82, +87, +92, +96, +97, +101, +118 from the row).

notes: Only the row reads were studied. The row offset is in r8 after 0x140278954 (row stride 49). V: it rewrites Move +0x42 and Jump +0x43 from the job row (+24, +25 & 0x7F) as the plain variant does.
open_questions: Whether the Ex variant differs from the plain one in anything besides where it takes the saved status bytes (? tail not read).

name: Unit_ResolvePreviewShape
proto: unsigned char Unit_ResolvePreviewShape(unsigned char *unit, unsigned char *outPalette, unsigned char job)
callers: JobTree_FillJobRecords, PreviewUnit_BuildRecord, PreviewUnit_ResolveShape and about seven other unit-building functions
purpose: Returns the sprite shape id for a unit/job pair (and a palette byte for special units).

behavior.text: outPalette = 0 first; job 92 and 93 are mapped to 91 and 92 (Dancer/Mime share ids shifted down by one).

unit marker byte unit[0]: 128 (male) and 129 (female) generic job units return marker + 2 * (job + 38) (byte arithmetic): Squire (74) -> 96/97 ... Mime (93 -> 92) -> 132/133; jobs 160, 161 and 164 use marker + 31 / + 33.

marker 130 returns unit[399] with palette unit[400]; markers 165..169 return themselves (the constants -90..-87 are the bytes 166..169); markers 162 and 163 return 163 and 164; any other marker returns itself when it is <= 128, else job + 40.
the marker byte unit[0] is copied from byte +0 of the save record (A+0) when the work record is built.
for marker 130 the shape and palette come from unit+399 and unit+400, which UnitWork_ApplyJobRow fills from the executable job table row bytes 46 and 47 (byte 48 goes to unit+398).

notes:
Every tree job (Squire..Mime) maps to a shape in 96..133; all of them use CharShapeLUTParam row 2.

Row bytes 46 and 47 are zero for the generic jobs; they matter for monsters and special units.
open_questions: The branch for markers above 165 is only partly traced (?).

name: Unit_RollStartingStats
callees: none (the random generator step is inline)
purpose: Rolls the five 24-bit stat accumulators (HP, MP, Speed, PA, MA) of a new unit from a base value and a random span taken from the start row; the job is not an input.

behavior.text: `accumulators` is an array of five pointers (HP, MP, SP, PA, MA); `row` selects a row of the start tables (0..3 occur).

for each stat i: accumulator = (base[row][i] << 14) + ((rand15 * span[row][i]) >> 1), where rand15 is the low 15 bits of the next output of the global random generator; three bytes are stored, low byte first. So the raw value in whole units is uniform in [base, base + span).
base[row] is the first five bytes of the 12-byte row at 0x14067F7D0 + 12 * row; span[row] is the five bytes at 0x14067F800 + 5 * row.
one random draw is consumed per stat, five in all; the job row and the unit's flags are not read.

notes: The raw value is the stat before the job's multiplier: Unit_ComputeStats shows ((accumulator * M) / 100) >> 14 with M from the job row, and Unit_ApplyLevelGrowth grows the accumulator with the job's C at each level. Rows 0 and 1 are the male and female recruits (Recruit_GenerateUnit passes 0 and 1); Unit_BuildFromRecord picks 0 for a unit flagged special (+6 bit 7), 1 for flag 0x40 and 3 otherwise.
open_questions: ? what the callers of the party-reset and egg paths pass for rows 2 and 3 (row 3 is the spawn default for units that are neither flagged female nor special).

name: Unit_ScreenSpan
callees: NxdRegistry_Find, NxdTable_GetRowById, sub_140028B10, NxdEntry_GetRow, sub_140261F60, sub_1400D3460
purpose: Returns the screen x and the y of a unit's base and of its base plus its shape height.

behavior.text: reads the CharShape row's height (+0x2C) and projects the unit's base and base + height.

notes: Name is ours.

name: Unit_SetAbilityBit
purpose: Records one passive ability (a reaction, support or movement ability) in the battle unit's passive-ability bit map; a reaction-range id also becomes the unit's equipped reaction.

behavior.text: index = abilityId - 422 (0x1A6); an id outside index 0..87 (ids 422..509) changes nothing.
for an id below 454 (0x1C6) the word at unit +0x14 is set to the id (the equipped reaction); ids 454 and above leave +0x14 alone.
then bit (0x80 >> (index & 7)) of byte unit +0x94 + (index >> 3) is set, so +0x94..+0x9E hold 88 bits, one per passive id, most significant bit first.
the three id bands by the ability-type counts (32 reactions 422..453, 32 supports 454..485, 24 movement 486..509); the band split at 454 is the only one the code tests.
the function only sets bits; Unit_BuildAbilityBits clears the map first.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_140276E5C, renamed 2026-11-10); read 2026-11-10. 96 bytes, read whole. Struct fields: UnitWorkRecord +0x14, +0x94..+0x9E. Behaviour: PassiveAbilitiesAreAPerUnitBitMap.
open_questions: ? what sub_14030B4F0 does with the call (its reads of the bit map were not traced).

name: Unit_SetChargeStateBits
callers: sub_14020A7F0 (2), sub_14020AD64 (2), sub_140271C50, BattleAction_ApplyRequest, sub_140281488 (2), sub_1402828E4, Battle_AITurnRun
purpose: Sets which of the four action states Readying, Jumping, Evading, Performing (statuses 4..7) a unit is in, and the charge counter that goes with it.

behavior.text: state -1 is replaced by 8 when Performing (status 7, +0x61 byte 0 bit 0x01) is effective, else 0.

state 5 / 6 / 7 / 8 selects the bit 0x08 / 0x04 / 0x02 / 0x01 (status 4 Readying, 5 Jumping, 6 Evading, 7 Performing); state 8 also sets +0x1BD and the charge counter +0x18D from byte +12 & 0x7F of the action record of the word at +0x1A2 (AbilityAction_GetRecord); state 0 sets the charge counter to 0xFF.
byte 0 of the applied set +0x1EF keeps its high nibble, its low nibble becomes the selected bit only; byte 0 of the effective set +0x61 becomes byte 0 of +0x57 OR that byte.
for the statuses 4..7 whose effective bit changed it calls BattleUnit_SetStatusVisual(id + 1, 0 or 1, slot) (off when it was set before), unless g_BattleSimulating is set.

notes: Name is ours. Whole function read. It rewrites byte 0 of +0x61.
open_questions: ? what +0x1BD holds besides the charge time copy.

name: Unit_SpendJp
purpose: Subtracts the ability's JP cost from the unit's JP of the given job: *(u16 *)(g_PartyUnits[unit] + 2 * Job_IdToIndex(jobId) + 202) -= cost.

behavior.text: JP per job is a u16 array at unit +202 indexed by the Job_IdToIndex value (0..21).

name: Unit_TryLearnAbility
proto: char Unit_TryLearnAbility(uint8_t *work, int jobIndex, int slot, uint16_t abilityId, char force, char payJp)
callers: sub_1402781A8 (queues a job's abilities for learning, I)
purpose: Attempts to mark one ability of a job as learned in a work record, optionally charging JP and rolling the ability's learn chance. Returns 1 when the learned bit was set.

behavior.text: nothing happens (returns 0) when the ability id is 0, or when `force` is 0 and the learn roll fails.
the roll is Rng_Percent(100, learn_percent) == 0, where learn_percent is byte +2 of the ability's 8-byte aux record at 0x140787F80 + 8 * id.
with `payJp` 0 the bit is set at once and no JP is touched.
with `payJp` set, the cost is Ability_GetJpCost(id); if the unit's current JP for that job (u16 at work+240+2*jobIndex) covers it, the JP is deducted and the bit is set.
when JP is short and `force` is set, the Ability table row is looked up (table id 39, result unused here) and the bit is set anyway without charging JP; with `force` 0 it returns 0.
the learned bit is slot bit 7 - (slot mod 8) of byte slot / 8 in the job's 3-byte group at work+162+3*jobIndex.
the purpose of the row lookup in the forced-short-JP path (its result is never used in this function).

notes:
Its aux operand (lea at 0x1402780DD) reads learn_percent.

The work record is layout C: learned bits +162, current JP array +240. The party record B keeps the same data at +123 and +202.
open_questions: Whether the forced path is used by battle learning with a short-JP unit, and what the row lookup is for.

name: UnitClut_TintRow
proto: int16_t UnitClut_TintRow(int mode, uint16_t *row, int unused, unsigned slot, int unused2, int16_t dr, int16_t dg, int16_t db, int now)
purpose: The battle side's tint rule: turns one 16-colour palette row into a unit slot's colours in bank 3 of the palette manager.

behavior.text: loops over the 16 colours of the row; a colour word of zero gives red, green and blue 0 and skips the mode and the offsets.

mode 5 takes each channel halved to 4 bits (word bits 1..4, 6..9, 11..14); mode 6 puts (blue + 3 green + 2 red) / 6 in all three channels; mode 7 the same sum / 12; every other mode value (the callers pass 4 and 8) takes the channels as they are.
adds dr, dg, db to red, green, blue, limits each to 31, and puts a channel below 1 to 0.
when all three channels are 0 and the low 15 bits of the source word are not, blue becomes 1.
writes the word (bit 15 kept from the source) to word_140C6D770[16 * slot + i], the base row of bank 3, and sets the manager's first dirty dword.

with `now` non-zero it also writes the word to word_140C74170[16 * slot + i] (bank 3 of the final image) and, when the slot's byte at 0x140C6CFE0 + 9 * slot is 0, the four state bytes red, green, blue, bit 15 of the colour (7 bytes per colour from 0x140C6D070).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1402F7628). Structure: ClutBank. The same four modes and the same offset, limit and blue-1 lines are inline in CharaRender_BuildAtlasTexture for the menus.
open_questions: ? what the third and fifth arguments are for (not read by the body).

name: UnitClut_TintRowPlain
proto: int16_t UnitClut_TintRowPlain(uint16_t *row, int unused, unsigned slot, int unused2, int16_t dr, int16_t dg, int16_t db, int now)
purpose: Calls UnitClut_TintRow with mode 8 (the channels as they are plus the offsets) for a row and a slot.

behavior.text: one call: UnitClut_TintRow(8, row, slot, slot, _, dr, dg, db, now).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1402F78A4). SceneUnit_RunPlacement hands it the unit's own row and the ambient offsets it worked out.

name: UnitInfo_FillFromBattleUnit
callers: EventPreviewUnit_StageSlot, Battle_InitScene, sub_14013F71C, sub_14013FAB0, sub_1401F3F70, sub_140214404, sub_140214610, sub_140214828, sub_140217630, sub_1402C6514, sub_1402C72B8 (IDA code references; which one draws the deployment card was not traced)
purpose: Fills the unit information record a battle panel draws (the deployment carousel's unit card, an event's unit preview) from a battle unit record: its job line, face, level, HP / MP / CT, Brave and Faith.

behavior.text: sub_140360700(unit, frame) first copies the unit's display fields into a stack frame (the job is the frame's word 18, the level nibbles and the JP / total JP words are frame copies sized for the stock jobs).
out +196 is set to -1, then out +156 = sub_140214134(unit +444, out +196): the unit's battle face and colour.

the job line is JobRecord_FromJobId(out, key) with a key built on the stack: +0 and +36 the frame's job, +8 / +16 / +24 pointers into the frame's level and JP copies, +32 a flags byte; then sub_1400FBB40(out + 92, frame).

then out +160.. takes the frame's level, EXP, HP, MP, CT (100 at +176), Brave and Faith words, +184 / +185 flag bits of the unit's byte +6, +188 the unit's slot byte (+1), +200 the dword at unit +504, +204 a side value from byte +6 (0 when bit 7 is set, else 2 or 1 by bit 6).

behavior.basis: (live 2026-11-10, tracepoint on JobRecord_FromJobId with the return address)
behavior.text: the deployment carousel's card calls it through this function (return 0x1402CBD42); the key held 0x4A for Ramza (Squire).

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1402CBCA0). The key points at stock-sized frame copies of the level and JP words.
open_questions: ? the meaning of a3 / a4 (passed through to sub_140360700) and of out +200.

name: UnitList_Compare
proto: int UnitList_Compare(const uint8_t *a, const uint8_t *b, int keyKind, char favoriteFirst)
purpose: Compares two party units for the unit list sort by one key kind: the sign is negated for a row of table 44 whose byte +6 is 0.

behavior.text: with the last argument set, a unit whose record byte +112 has bit 2 sorts before one without it (both set: equal).
the keys of both units come from UnitList_SortKey; key kind 17 falls back to kind 14 when the two keys are equal and not 1.
the result is the difference (key of b - key of a), negated unless the table-44 row of the key kind has byte +6 non-zero; a missing table or row gives the negated difference (smaller key first).
bit 2 of the record byte +112 is the unit-list 'favourite' flag, because the unit list screen has a favourite toggle and this is the only per-unit bit the sort puts first.

notes: Name is ours (executable database: sub_14028ADF8). Table 44 is the sort-mode table; its byte +6 chooses ascending (0) or descending order.
open_questions: ? the sort-mode table's name and its other columns.

name: UnitList_SortKey
purpose: Returns the value a party unit list is sorted by for one sort mode (key kind 0..18), read from the unit's save record.

behavior.text: key kind 2 (the 'job' sort) reads the Job row (table 46) of the record's job word (+36): the sort_order column (+0x38) when it is not negative, else the job id itself.

key kinds 0 and 3 return the word at record +44, kind 1 the word at +0, kind 4 +38, 5 +40, 6 +12, 7 +16, 8 +18, 9 +22, 10 +24, 11 +28, 12 +30, 13 the byte at +373, 14 the byte at +371; any other kind below 15 returns 0.

kind 15 returns 5 when the record's word at +44 equals the party leader's id or an event-provided id; otherwise the result depends on the battle-mode globals and the word at +44 being below 0x32 (a 0 / 1 flag). Kind 16 returns the same kind of 0 / 1 flag for the word at +44 below 0x32. Kinds 17 and 18 return 0 or the byte at +372 plus 1.
the words at +44 and +36 are the unit's level and job (the +36 word is the job word other sheets read as party +36); the meaning of the other offsets was not named.

notes: Name is ours (executable database: sub_14028AEFC). Only key kind 2's use of the Job sort_order column was read to the end; the other kinds are listed by the record offset they return.
open_questions: ? the meaning of key kinds 15..18 and of the record bytes +371..+373.

name: UnitPage_Task
purpose: Task of the legacy unit page: builds the cells and the fifteen number fields of the unit page.

behavior.text: uses the 18-cell blocks at 0x1408EBF20 .. 0x1408EC1C0 (four languages) and the number field tables at 0x1408EC2A0 and 0x1408EC480 (two variants of fifteen rows, selected by the page mode).
the page shows movement, jump, speed, weapon power, defence and the four evade values.

notes: Only the table references were read (1439 bytes).
open_questions: ?: the page layout and update loop.

name: UnitPanel_FillEffectLine
purpose: Fills the effect line of the unit status panel (the panel beside the action preview and the AI's target panel) from the current target's result block: damage, recovery, a stat change, or the statuses the action would add or remove.

behavior.text: reads the result block at qword_142FF3CF8 (the current target); flag byte +39: bit 0x80 HP damage (+6), 0x40 HP recovery (+8), 0x20 MP damage (+10), 0x10 MP recovery (+12), then the word +14 and the byte +42 with bit 0x01.
with bit 0x08 it picks the top status (Status_PickHighestPriority), builds the status list (StatusList_BuildFromResultBlock into a 40-byte stack buffer) and hands it to UnitPanel_SetSignalList.
called while the action preview is up (a forecast pass) and on enemy turns (the target panel); not called when an action's result shows over the hit unit.

notes: Name is ours.
open_questions: ? the meaning of the word +14 and the byte +42 labels.

name: UnitPanel_FillJobLine
callers: sub_140291490 (the unit panel fill; skipped for job id 28), sub_140295558
purpose: Fills the job line of a unit panel from a 148-byte job record: the job icon, the job level, the JP and the JP to the next level.

behavior.text: sets the job icon from rec +64 (JobTreePanel_SetJobIcon).
the level node: when the level rec +68 is 0 or less it shows UI text 0x9D ("--"); otherwise the level as a number.
the JP node (rec +76) and the next node (rec +80): UI text 0x50 ("--") when the level is 0 or less or the value is negative; otherwise the number.
the fourth node (rec +84): also "--" when the level is 8 or more.
a monster unit (all job levels 0) shows "Lv. --" and "--" for JP and next.

notes: Name is ours. The record is the one JobRecord_FromJobId builds (BattleUnit_BuildJobRecord for the battle panels).
open_questions: ? the meaning of rec +80 versus rec +84 beyond "JP" and "next".

name: UnitPanel_SetSignalList
purpose: Turns a status list (ids, bit 0x80 = removed) into the panel's list of BattleSignal ids.

behavior.text: clears the count at panel +66216, then for each entry looks up UIStatusEffect (NXD table 57) row (id & 0x7F) + 1.
the two UIStatusEffect columns used are list_category (+0x14, must be non-zero) and battle_signal (+0x18, 59 means none); sub_140217A7C builds the same list for another panel with the same two tests.

an entry is kept when the row's field +20 is non-zero, its field +24 is not 59, and BattleSignal (table 214) has a row for field +24; it stores field +24 | (entry & 0x80) at panel +66176 + count and advances the count.

notes: Name is ours. The same UIStatusEffect fields (+20, +24) are what a status needs for its label over a hit unit.

name: UnitPanel_SetStatusBytes
callers: sub_1400E56A0 (from Battle_TimelineRefresh, Battle_UnitStatusFill, Battle_UnitStatusFillAlt, sub_1402DF374, all with the unit record +0x61)
purpose: Fills a battle unit panel's status byte list (the icons on the panel) from a five-byte status set.

behavior.text: which 0, 2, 3 use the list at panel +0x101A4 (count +0x101CC, a 16-byte copy of extra at +0x101D8); 1, 4, 5 and any other value the list at +0x10160 (count +0x10188, extra at +0x10194). Only 0x10160, 0x10194 and 0x101D8 are operands; the other offsets are built from them (lea rdi+28h, rax-0Ch, rax-34h).
clears the 40-byte list and its count, lists the set with StatusList_BuildFromSet and keeps each status whose Status_ListCategory is 1 or 2, one byte each.

notes: Name is ours. I: sub_14010A550 draws the list as icons (Icon row 0x16 with the byte), no names.
open_questions: ? which panel each which value is.

name: UnitSprite_DepthSort
purpose: Computes the depth value of a unit sprite for sorting.

behavior.text: for a scene object whose dword +0x15C has bit 4 set it adds the render object's byte +964 (the CharShape unknown_2d column, signed, copied there by sub_14027032C) to the unit's y before the depth value is computed.
the same flag makes BattleFormation_DrawUnits use the alternate height (CharShape height_2).

notes: Name is ours.
open_questions: ? what scene object flag +0x15C bit 4 marks.

name: UnitWork_ApplyJobRow
purpose: Copies a unit's JobTable row into its work record: skillset, innate abilities, equipment flags, growth pairs, Move/Jump, status groups, elemental groups and the three trailing bytes. Run after the save fields are copied in.

behavior.text: the row is JobTable + 49 * work[3] (job id); job 161 uses row 164 when the low nibble at work+238 (level of job index 21) is 8 or more.
row byte 0 (skillset id) goes to +18; bytes 1..8 (four u16 innate ability ids) to +10; bytes 9..13 (equipment bit field) to +82; bytes 14..23 (growth C/M pairs) to +138.

after the growth copy, sub_1401EA910 may add small amounts to the HP and SP pairs (+138, +139, +142, +143, each capped at 254) from the optional tweak tables in the second argument, indexed by a byte of a global record (I: a difficulty or new-game-plus setting).

byte 24 (Move) goes to +66; byte 25 bits 0..6 (Jump) to +67 and bit 7 sets or clears bit 0x40 of +81, the unit that blocks its allies in move ranges (see the behaviour UnitThatBlocksItsAlliesInMoveRanges).

bytes 27..31, 32..36 and 37..41 (three status bit fields) go to +87, +92 and +97; when bit 2 of work+5 and either of bits 0 and 3 of work+6 are set, the +92 group is OR-ed with two bit fields from a global record (I).
bytes 42..45 (four element bit fields) go to +118..+121, and +122 is cleared.

bytes 46, 47 and 48 are copied to +399, +400 and +398. For marker byte 130, Unit_ResolvePreviewShape returns work+399 as the sprite shape and work+400 as the palette byte, so row byte 46 is the shape id and 47 the palette for such units. Byte 48 lands in +398, which damage formulas for dragon-type units read (I: species or family).
separately, work+402 gets the skillset id of the row indexed by marker byte work[0] when that byte is below 0x4A (special characters), or is 162 or 163; otherwise 0.
the three trailing bytes are zero in the stock generic rows and in rows 160 and 161 read from the running game.

notes: Same copy pattern appears in two reload paths (sub_140278688, sub_1402788EC). Job 94 is the stock example of a non-zero byte 46. Status and element groups are zero in all stock generic rows, so their order is untested there.
open_questions: Whether byte 48 is a species id.

name: UnitWork_ApplyStartingEquipment
purpose: Seeds a unit work record with its starting equipment while the unit is built from a setup record: the five slot bytes of the setup record are resolved to item ids and the hand slots and the two-handed state are derived from them.

behavior.text: the first argument is the 512-byte unit work record and the second the setup record read by the spawn initialiser; the five bytes at setup +0x12..+0x16 are the starting ids for the five equipment slots.
when work +6 bit 0x20 is set the five bytes are copied straight to the work words at +0x1A, +0x1C, +0x1E, +0x20 and +0x24, with 0xFF written to +0x22 and +0x26.
otherwise each slot is walked in a fixed order; a byte of 0xFE means "pick a default" and is passed to UnitWork_PickStartingItem with the category base 0x80 and the slot index.
the first slot that yields an id other than 0xFE fills the right hand at +0x20; when the slot still returns 0xFE the left-hand path is tried instead.
Item_GetRecord is called on the chosen hand id and its slot-flags byte +3 bit 0x40 clears the left hand at +0x22.
Item_GetWeaponRecord is called on the right-hand id and its flags byte +1 bit 1 also clears the left hand; unit +0x9A bit 1 has the same effect.
the picked head, body and accessory ids land in the work words at +0x1A, +0x1C and +0x1E.
the 0xFE sentinel means "no forced item, use a level-appropriate default", because the picker only accepts records whose level is not above the unit level.
the routine runs during unit construction only; the saved equipment path (Unit_LoadEquipmentAndEvade) later overwrites the hands and evade values.
whether a setup record with a non-0xFE byte can name an item the unit cannot equip; this body does not test the equip flags for those ids.

notes: Whole function read (806 bytes, single caller). The five-byte setup field and the 0xFE sentinel are read from this body; the field has not been tied to a named column of the spawn record.

name: UnitWork_BuildForSlot
callers: sub_1400DCDBC, sub_1400DCF18, sub_1400DCFE4, sub_1401004B4, sub_14021A030, sub_140246014, sub_1402B803C, Inventory_RebuildOrders, sub_1402BC720, sub_1402C314C, sub_1402CEEE8, sub_1402EEE30, sub_1402FB4F8, sub_1403264A0, sub_140326EF8, sub_140332DB0, sub_1403666CC, sub_14036AC74, sub_14036B71C
callees: EventVar_Read, memset, UnitWork_BuildFromSaveIndex, memmove, PartyUnit_FillFromWork, Job_IsHiddenFromTree, Item_CanUnitEquip, sub_140360780, sub_140285C30, sub_14041FAE0
purpose: Builds a unit work record for a party slot from the save record, then applies the job row and the equipment so the caller can read derived stats without touching the live unit.

behavior.text: the first argument is a 16-bit slot and the second a kind; kinds 0x65 and 0x68 take a special path.

it copies a 0x200-byte record into a stack buffer, clearing it when the slot is outside the party, and fills it from the unit save table at 0x1411A7D10 with a stride of 0x258 (the base is image base + 0x11A7D10, the stride an imul).
PartyUnit_FillFromWork copies the party-side fields into the work buffer, and sub_140285C30 applies the job row to it.
Item_CanUnitEquip is consulted for the equipment words, and Job_IsHiddenFromTree for the job visibility.
the result is a complete work record: the job row stats, the equipment hands and the derived attack/evade values.
the routine is called from the save, shop, job screen, errand and battle paths, so it is the shared way to materialise a unit.
it returns no value; the caller supplies the buffer through the stack and reads it back.
the special kinds 0x65 and 0x68 are the Mime and one other job whose row cannot be applied normally, because the kind is compared with the job ids before the copy.
whether the routine writes a live unit record or only the caller buffer; the body keeps the work record on the stack.

notes: Whole function read (941 bytes). The callers and the save-table stride are the ones the party/unit studies list.

name: UnitWork_BuildFromGuestOrPartyRecord
purpose: Finds the save record a spawn entry names and builds the work record from it.

behavior.text: entry +1 bit 3 set: searches the save records 50..53 (the guest range of g_UnitSaveData) for a used record (+1 not 0xFF) whose byte +0 equals entry +0; otherwise sub_1402752E0(entry +0) picks the index.

returns -1 when no record is found; else calls UnitWork_BuildFromSaveIndex(work, index, dword_1437414A0), sets work +6 = (work +6 & 0xEE) | (entry +1 & 0x11), work +5 and work +494 = entry +24, and returns 0.

name: UnitWork_BuildFromSave
callers: sub_140275C70 (build by save index), sub_14028B7D0, SceneUnit_FillSpriteRecord
callees: sub_140278DA8, Unit_BuildJobUnlockMask, UnitWork_CopySaveFields, UnitWork_ApplyJobRow, sub_140276DF4, sub_140276EBC, sub_14027788C, sub_1402760E8
purpose: Builds the 512-byte unit work record C from a save unit record A. It first refreshes the unit's unlock mask inside the save record, then copies and completes the work record.

behavior.text: returns -1 when the save slot is empty (A+1 = 0xFF).
calls sub_140278DA8 on the second JP array (A+174) with the job levels (A+116) before anything else.
recomputes the job unlock mask with Unit_BuildJobUnlockMask(levels A+116, flags A+4, learned bits A+50, story stage A+289) and stores its three bytes at A+47 (high), A+48, A+49 (low).

clears a set of work fields (words/bytes around C+65, C+396, C+436..443, C+492, C+500), stores the third argument at C+2, then calls UnitWork_CopySaveFields, UnitWork_ApplyJobRow(work, 0) and four more fill helpers.
the value stored at C+2 is overwritten by UnitWork_CopySaveFields with A+1.
returns 0 on success.

notes: Side effect worth knowing: the save record's unlock mask is rewritten every time a work record is built, so a save needs no manual unlock bits.
open_questions: Roles of the four trailing helper calls.

name: UnitWork_CopySaveFields
purpose: Copies the fields of a save unit record A into the work record C. It defines the A -> C offset mapping.

behavior.text: single bytes: C+0 = A+0 (marker byte), C+2 = A+1 (slot id), C+3 = A+2 (job id), C+6 = A+4 (flags), C+19 = A+7, C+500 = A+289 (story stage).
C+4 = A+3 only when the slot id is 0x32 or higher, else 0; C+5 and C+494 are set to 11 when the marker is below 4, otherwise 8.
C+8 (word) gets a 9-bit value from A+5 / A+6 and a 4-bit value from the top nibble of A+6 in bits 12..15; words C+20, C+22, C+24 are built from byte pairs A+8..13; C+26 takes 14 bytes from A+14.
C+40 = A+28, C+41 = A+29, C+42 and C+43 = A+30, C+44 and C+45 = A+31; A+32..46 land at C+123..137 as a mix of words and bytes.
the 3-byte unlock mask A+47..49 goes to C+159..161.

block copies: A+50 (66 bytes, learned-ability bits) -> C+162; A+116 (12 bytes, job levels) -> C+228; A+128 (46 bytes, current JP) -> C+240; A+174 (46 bytes, second JP array) -> C+286; A+220 (64 bytes) -> C+332; dword A+560 -> C+508.
zeroes C+407 (dword), C+411 (word) and C+413.

notes: Offsets A+116 and C+228 are both the 24-nibble job level array; the mask, learned bits and JP arrays move by a constant per block, not uniformly.

name: UnitWork_FindJobBySkillset
purpose: The first job of a work record's job list whose JobTable row holds `skillset`; the record's own job (+3) when none does.

behavior.text: the list is sub_14028668C(c, list) (JobList_Build from the record's unlock bits at +159, mode 1).
row guard per entry: job < 0xAE (stock); returns the matching job id or c +3.

sub_14022F868 and BattleCommand_BuildScreen call it with the acting unit's record and the skillset byte of the battle command list being opened (a byte array indexed by the command kind 1..7; a 0 byte skips the call and keeps the record's job byte). The answer is the job id of the job record they build for that list (JobRecord_FromJobId), whose name heads the list: the job that owns the command, for the unit's own command and for a secondary one alike.
sub_140335140 calls it for a named command (its second argument not 1) of list kinds 5 and 6, for the job record of the command header.
asked for a skillset that no job of the unit's list holds, it answered the record's job byte (76), and the list was headed by that job's name.
its fallback is the unit's job byte +3 at 0x14028ACB5; 0x14028ACB9 is a branch target; the loop before it walks the unit's job list.

name: UnitWork_InitFromSpawnRecord
purpose: Builds a new unit's job state in its work record from a spawn record: job levels, unlock mask, job row and secondary skillset. It holds the stock rule that gives every generic job level 1 to a new unit.

behavior.text: clears the 12 level bytes (C +228..239).

when the spawn record is present, not flagged 0x20 at +1 and its job index (+8) is below 20: the job's level nibble becomes spawn +9 & 0xF; then for the 10 level bytes (indices 0..19) each byte is OR-ed with the JobNeedLevel row of the spawn job (virtual base 0x14067F384 + 12 x index; index 0 uses 0x11 / 0x01, built in a register by a select, not an immediate operand), and every nibble still 0 becomes 1. So every generic job (0..19) starts at level >= 1; indices 20..23 stay 0.
spawn +1 bit 6 clears the low nibble of byte 8 (index 17), bit 7 the high nibble of byte 9 (index 18).
then Unit_BuildJobUnlockMask(levels, flags, C +162, C +500) -> C +159..161 (big-endian), job = spawn +10, UnitWork_ApplyJobRow.
