spawn +29 (1..254) sets the skillset byte C +18; spawn +11 is the secondary skillset, 0xFE = the skillset of a random unlocked job (Unit_PickUnlockedJobAtRandom).
with no spawn record: job row 0, C +6 = 0x20, empty unlock mask.

the third argument is the OverrideEntryData row of the entry (Unit_BuildFromRecord's fifth argument, from Battle_PlaceEntryUnits; null from the other callers); it is only passed on to UnitWork_ApplyJobRow, whose UnitWork_AddEntryGrowthBonus reads the row's four bonus arrays.

notes: The job comes from one byte, spawn +10 (0x140276B04, stored into C +3 at 0x140276B07), so a spawn names a job id of one byte only (behaviour SpawnedUnitsCarryAOneByteJob).

name: UnitWork_PackJobLevels
purpose: Rebuilds the packed job-level nibbles of a save record from the unit total-JP array, two jobs per byte.

behavior.text: it reads ten 16-bit total-JP values from the first argument, one per job index 0..9.
Job_LevelFromTotalJp converts each value to a level, and the low nibble of the first level becomes the high nibble of the output byte.
the loop writes ten bytes, so 20 job levels are packed; the loop bound is 0x14 (20 values read as ten pairs).
the first argument advances four bytes per output byte, so the JP array is a sequence of 16-bit entries, not a byte array.
the second argument receives the packed bytes and is advanced one byte per iteration.
the packed form matches the save field described as 12 bytes of 24 nibbles; this routine writes the first ten of those bytes.
how the remaining two bytes (jobs 20..23) are produced; this function stops at ten output bytes.

notes: Whole function read (98 bytes). Used on load, where the levels are recomputed rather than trusted from the file.

name: UnitWork_PickStartingItem
proto: uint8_t UnitWork_PickStartingItem(void *work, uint8_t category, uint8_t slot, uint8_t flags)
purpose: Chooses one item id for a starting-equipment slot: it scans a category of the item table, keeps the ids the unit may use at its level, and returns one of them at random, or 0xFE when the category offers nothing.

behavior.text: the second argument is a category base id (0xD0, 0xAC, 0x90, 0x80 or 0x100 after the shift) and selects the id range to scan; the range end is derived from the base.
each candidate record is rejected when its slot-flags byte +3 has bit 2 set (the "skip in best-equipment" flag).
when the fourth argument is not 0xFF the record equip-category byte +5 must equal it.
the record level byte +2 must not exceed the unit level at work +0x29.
the unit equipment bits at work +0x52 are tested against the record equip-category byte +5, so an item the job cannot equip is skipped.
when the third argument is non-zero it is a mask tested against the flags of the weapon record byte +1.
accepted ids are collected on the stack and one is chosen with the global random state at 0x1408E5FC8; the function returns 0xFE when the list is empty.
the random pick is unweighted over the collected ids; the level test only filters, it does not bias the choice.
what the two 16-bit words written to the global random state represent; the same state is advanced on every call.

notes: Whole function read (415 bytes). Only called from the starting-equipment walk.

name: UnitWork_SetNameKey
callers: sub_1402760E8 (the end of Unit_BuildFromRecord, with the OverrideEntryData row)
purpose: Sets a unit's name key (work dword +508) and name string (work +332).

behavior.text: a unit without a save record (work +2 == 0xFF): when an OverrideEntryData row is given and its dword +0x0C (column chara_name) is non-zero, work +508 = that dword; otherwise, when the name key is still 0xFF, it draws a random generic name key (256 + Rng(256) for work +6 bit 7, 512.. for bit 6, 768.. otherwise) that no save record (+0x22C) and no battle unit (+508, same gender bits) already uses.
a unit with a save record: work +508 = save record dword +0x230 and work +332 = save record string +0xDC (64 bytes).
clears work +475..+484.
every non-zero value of the OverrideEntryData chara_name column is a key of the CharaName table.

name: UnitWork_StoreToSaveSlot
purpose: Writes a work record back into a save record: the unit's slot (a new slot for a recruit), job, flags, equipment and the per-job arrays. Returns the save slot or -1.

behavior.text: chooses the save slot (`sub_1402751D0`); a guest slot 50..53 can be freed first.
copies job (+3 -> A +2), marker, flags, the unlock mask (3 bytes), learned bits (66), levels (12), JP (46) and total JP (46) with a memcpy-style helper.
then sets total JP of job index 21 to Job_GetJpForLevel(21, mastered jobs + 1) and its level nibble (the Onion-Knight-like rule) and clears C +286.

notes: V: c +2 (the save index) is only read, never written, so after the call it still says where the unit came from.

name: UserSituation_IsMet
callers: BarTop_Setup and about 50 more (JobTree_FillJobRecords, Shop_GetUiRowId, sub_1401607D4, sub_140341094, ...)
purpose: Answers whether a UserSituation condition (nxd table 90, keyed by situation and entry) holds; the UI asks it to show or lock features.

behavior.text: 0 holds always; otherwise for each entry of the key (NxdTable_GetEntryCount / GetEntryByKeyIndex) it runs the checks k = 0..2 of the row in order through UserSituation_TestCheck: the kind at +8 + 4k, the ids at +24 + 8k and +60 + 8k, the values at +44 + 4k (fifth argument) and +80 + 4k (sixth argument); the values are passed only for kinds 3..11.

per check k, in order: kind 0 returns false; a TestCheck result that differs from the byte at +92 + k (column blocking_result) abandons this entry and moves on to the next one; when all three checks equal their bytes the function returns false.

after every entry was abandoned it returns true. So the byte at +0x5C + k is the result that blocks the situation, not a success value: an entry makes the situation unmet only when each of its checks returns exactly that byte.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_1400FF8A4). Situation 3220 (one entry: kind 6 on id 0, value 450, blocking_result 0) opens the tavern errand row.
open_questions: ? the meaning of the union type 121 in the row (the id is read alone).

name: UserSituation_SetValue
proto: void UserSituation_SetValue(SituationStore *store, unsigned int id, int value)
purpose: Sets one situation counter and tells the registered listeners.

behavior.text: writes the dword at +24 + 4 * id (or +104 + 4 * id when bit 0 of +16 is set), then calls the second virtual function of every listener on the list at qword_143CD9DE8 +24.

behavior.basis: (read in the caller EventScript_Run, not in this body)
behavior.text: event opcode 0xE9 calls it with an id and a value from the script; opcode 0xEA calls a twin (sub_1400FF6B8) that sets a flag byte (+72 / +152).

notes: Name is ours (was sub_1400FF660). Whole function read; the listener calls are indirect.

name: UserSituation_TestCheck
proto: bool UserSituation_TestCheck(void *unused, unsigned int type, unsigned int id, unsigned int id2, unsigned int value, unsigned int value2)
purpose: One check of a UserSituation row against the situation store (qword_143CD9DE0): a flag byte, a counter compare or a scene variable.

behavior.text: the store has two banks chosen by bit 0 of its byte +16: flags at +72 / +152 (one byte per id), counters at +24 / +104 (one dword per id).

type 1 / 2 = flag set / clear; 3 = counter == value; 4 <=; 5 <; 6 >=; 7 >; 8..11 = a range of counter id (8: >= value, 10: > value; 9: >= value, 11: > value) together with counter id2 (8, 10: <= value2; 9, 11: < value2); 12..15 = SceneVar_Read(id) equals the type (12..15); 16 = SceneVar_Read(id) is in 12..15.
kinds 3..11 are the ones that receive values; UserSituation_IsMet passes them only for those kinds.

notes: Name is ours (was sub_1400FFAF0). Whole function read.
open_questions: ? what selects the second bank (byte +16 bit 0).

name: Utf8_DecodeUnit
purpose: Decodes one UTF-8 sequence to a 16-bit code unit and returns the number of bytes used.

behavior.text: sequence length from the lead byte (< 0xC0 / 0xE0 / 0xF0 / 0xF8 / 0xFC limits give 1..6); the value = lead & mask followed by 6 bits per continuation byte.
values above 0xFFFF are replaced by 9632 (0x25A0, a black square); the low 16 bits are stored to *out.

notes: The name is ours (IDB: sub_1403BF9D4). No validation of continuation bytes; characters beyond the BMP become U+25A0.

name: Video_OnResize
proto: __int64 Video_OnResize(__int64 window, int width, int height)
purpose: Stores the new backbuffer size for the main window and refreshes the unit-image width factor.

behavior.text: only for the main window (qword_140C696A8 + 88); dword_140D3AD24 = width, dword_140D3AD4C = height; g_UnitImageAspectX = 1.1408199 when g_UnitImageAspectOn is non-zero, else 1.0; then sub_1403CA668 (viewport update).

name: Video_RefreshState
purpose: Re-applies the video state (mode flags, viewport, aspect factor) after a mode change.

behavior.text: sets the update flags of the main window object, recomputes g_UnitImageAspectX with the same rule as Video_OnResize, refreshes the viewport (sub_1403CA668) and resets several frame-state globals.

notes: Only the head of this function was read (?).

name: VideoState_InitDefaults
purpose: Initialises the video/render state globals to their defaults.

behavior.text: among many resets it sets g_UnitImageAspectOn (dword_142E7FCA0) = 1, so the unit image width factor 1.1408199 is active in normal play.

notes: The only store to g_UnitImageAspectOn found by cross-references is this one (value 1).

name: VramPage_CopyRect
callers: EffectFile_UploadTexture, sub_140210AF0 and about ten more
purpose: Copies a rectangle of 16-bit pixels into the 1024 by 512 video page (g_SaveYoxPage) and marks that area for upload.

behavior.text: rect holds x, y, width, height in halfwords; a y of 512 or more is reduced by masking with 0x1FF and an x of 1024 or more has 1024 subtracted.
the rectangle is clipped to the page (rows beyond 512 and columns beyond 1024 are dropped, a negative x skips source columns) and copied row by row with memmove at 2048 bytes per page row.
afterwards it calls sub_14025F998, sub_14025FF68 and sub_14026060C on the rectangle, which update the area bookkeeping of the page.

notes: Name is ours. The page is the same one HdLayer_BuildTextures reads when it builds the Enhanced battle layer textures.
open_questions: ? what the three bookkeeping calls do exactly.

name: WindowPattern_Build
proto: char *WindowPattern_Build(int width, int rows, const short *rect, int mode)
purpose: Builds the pixel pattern of a legacy window frame row by row and, in mode 2, uploads it to VRAM.

behavior.text: a width above 244 is taken as 255 pixels (a 16-bit word holds four pixels, so the row is rounded up to whole words); the buffer holds rows x width / 2 bytes (a fixed buffer in mode 2 when a display flag is 2, otherwise a scratch allocation).

each row picks a template base in the window pattern table (0x1407B8260, 64 words per template): modes 0 and 1 use template 64 x row for the first 8 rows, cycle through templates 8..23 for the middle rows and use templates 24..31 for the last 8 rows; modes 2 and 3 use base 54 + 64 x row for the first 16 rows, the same cycle for the middle rows and base 1078 + 64 x (0..15) for the last 16 rows.
writes the two end words of each row from the template (words 8 and 9) and fills the middle with WindowPattern_FillRow.
in mode 2 it copies the buffer to the VRAM rectangle, waits one frame and releases the buffer; it returns the buffer.

notes: Read: the row template selection and the buffer handling.
open_questions: ?: which template index is which window part.

name: WindowPattern_FillRow
proto: void WindowPattern_FillRow(int unused, unsigned short *dest, int words, int templateBase)
purpose: Fills one row of a window frame pattern from a six-word template.

behavior.text: writes template words 0 and 1 at the row start and words 6 and 7 at the row end, then repeats words 2, 3, 4 and 5 across the middle with a stride of four words (each word starting at its own offset).

notes: Read in full.
open_questions: ?: the pixel meaning of the words.

name: WindowRect_AnimateCurve
proto: int WindowRect_AnimateCurve(unsigned short *rect, short *primA, short *primB, int curve)
purpose: Opens or closes a window by moving two rectangles along one of the five animation step lists.

behavior.text: takes the rectangle (x, y and extents from the window record) and, when the second primitive is used, a second rectangle.

steps through the list chosen from the five-pointer table at 0x1406818C8 (values grow towards 4096, the list ends with 4096); each step waits (3 minus the speed setting) frames and calls the rectangle updater sub_140226880 for the first and, if used, the second primitive.
curve 4 also writes a grey level from (4096 minus the step) / 32 into the primitive colour bytes.
after the last step it waits one frame and draws the final rectangle.

notes: Read in full.
open_questions: ?: the meaning of the five curves.

name: WorldEncounter_Roll
proto: int WorldEncounter_Roll(int location, int arrivalRoad, bool fixedRoll)
purpose: Decides whether a random battle starts at a battleground and which formation it uses.

behavior.text: only locations 24..42 have rows; the row is the one of the three whose first byte is the road the party arrived on.
the story variable named in the row picks the first of four tiers whose limit it does not exceed; a tier with chance 0 gives no battle.
rolls 0..99 against the chance; a game option forces the roll to always or never pass.
picks one of the formations allowed by the tier's bit mask at random and stores it, the battle number 0x200 + row byte 1 and row byte 22.

open_questions: ?: the meaning of row byte 22; which option value forces which way.

name: WorldMap_ApplyProgressInfo
purpose: Applies the world-map progress rows that the story counters select to the world-map location values.

behavior.text: skipped while the low dword of g_EventSkipFlags is set.

for each GameProgress (nxd 92) counter index i: counter = g_UserSituation +24 + 4i; row = GameProgress (i, counter); then the WorldMapProgressInfo (nxd 123) row named by the GameProgress columns world_map_progress_info (+0x08) and world_map_progress_info_2 (+0x0C).
when that row's +0x1C (column user_situation) is 0 or UserSituation_IsMet holds, its +8 and +0xC (47 = none) are taken as location values (index 0 keeps +0xC as well).

open_questions: ? where the location values are stored for the map screens (I: the progress row's keys are kept at world-map screen +3308 / +3312 by WorldMapScreen_SetProgress and compared with location ids by sub_14036E5DC, which marks the location records with state 3 / 2).

name: WorldMap_InitLocations
callees: PackedBlock766_Load, EventVar_Read, EventVar_Write, sub_140340FD0, sub_140340B94, sub_1403413C4, sub_140341094, sub_1403426F8
purpose: Sets up the world-map screen: the sprite piece list, the location markers and the road markers.

behavior.text: converts 13 groups of 17 piece templates (0x1407BAC78, 24 bytes each) into the live sprite piece list.
for each of 48 locations (index 47 skipped) builds a 52-byte marker record from the location offset table (0x1406933A0, 8 bytes each); the first 43 become active markers.
reads event variables 556 + n for the 51 roads and event variables 84, 49, 46 and 47 for the screen state.
calls the packed block loader with a block index and several set-up helpers (a per-location helper in the marker loop and four more after it).

notes: Head only: the first half (piece, marker and road set-up); the rest of the function is not read.
open_questions: ?: the second half of the function.

name: WorldMap_UpdateFastForward
purpose: On the world map (mode 3) sets the fast-forward level to 1 while action 89 is held, else 0.

behavior.text: when GlobalWork_GetFastForwardMode returns 3, GlobalWork +88 = Input_IsActionHeld(action 89) (0 or 1).
action 90 is not read here, so the world map has no level 2.

mode 3 is written by sub_14033EC0C (the world map set-up); several world UI routines clear the level when they open a panel while the mode is 3 (sub_14014DC80, sub_140157864, sub_140157C30, sub_14015B7C4, sub_140247A4C, sub_1402CC2E0).

open_questions: ? Which world-map states its three callers cover.

name: WorldMapBaseScreen_Open
purpose: Opens a location's own world-map screen file.

behavior.text: loads wm_base_<'%02d' of Town base_number (+0x2C)>.uib (UIAddon 137) when Town base (+0x30) is set, else UIAddon row 141.
the name of this function is proposed from the file names it builds.

name: WorldMapLocationPanel_Fill
purpose: Fills the world-map location info panel from a location record.

behavior.text: skipped when Town locations_list (+0x24) is 1; sub_140158CB0 fills the name, description and picture into the node set at +1816 (or +1792 when Town has_shop (+0x31) is set).

with has_shop set: 'ShowProfit' / 'HideProfit' by UserSituation_IsMet(3220); 'ProfitDefault' / 'ProfitNone' by any of the record's dwords 0..2 above 0; then three counters through sub_1400FE9D0. Without it: text 1583 or 1584 by record byte +12.
then 'On' / 'Off' on 35 nodes (from +64) from the 35-byte category mask at record +16.

notes: The record is WorldMapLocationRecord, built by sub_14036E5DC.

name: WorldMapNode_PlayTexChange
purpose: Plays the texture-change state of a location's base node.

behavior.text: plays the state 'TexChange%02d' (Town base_number, +0x2C) on a node; location 21 uses 'TexChange14_34'.

name: WorldMapProgress_GetObjectiveCaption
purpose: Returns the world-map objective line for a progress row.

behavior.text: finds the index of the entry (set a2, key a3) in its set (NxdEntry_CopyKeys / NxdSets_Find2/3 paths), then walks backwards to the first row whose sets_objective byte (+0x29) is non-zero and returns its caption (+0x18).
a2 == 0 gives an empty string.

name: WorldMapRoute_Refresh
proto: void WorldMapRoute_Refresh(void *screen, const char *flag, int route)
purpose: Shows or hides one route on the world map and sets its grey state.

behavior.text: for a route id a3 up to 50 (Route table 97, +4 = the route's node name): plays 'Show_R_%s' or 'Hide_R_%s' by *a2.
then grey = (progress row user_situation (+0x1C) is 0 or met) and the route is in the progress row's routes list (+0x10); calls WorldMapRoute_SetGrey(screen, route, grey).

name: WorldMapRoute_SetGrey
proto: void WorldMapRoute_SetGrey(void *screen, int route, int grey)
purpose: Plays a route's grey or default colour state.

behavior.text: plays 'R_%s_Color_Grayout' when grey is non-zero, else 'R_%s_Color_Default' (and stops the other) on the route node at screen +512.

name: WorldMapRoute_StartGrow
purpose: Starts the grow animation of a route between two locations.

behavior.text: creates UIAddonFFTOWorldMapRouteGrowEffect from 'wm_route_<Route name (+4)>.uib' (UIAddon row 138).
the direction byte +209 is flipped when the request's byte +24 is 0 and the current WorldMapProgressInfo row has reverse_route (+0x28) set.
effect +188 / +192 = start / end location (Route town +8 / town_2 +0xC, swapped when flipped); +196 / +200 = Route +8 / +0xC.

name: WorldMapRouteGrow_OnState
callees: UITable_GetRowByKey, GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState, GUIComponent_StopAllStates, Str_Format, sub_1400F4BCC
purpose: Plays the state of the route-grow effect.

behavior.text: plays 'Show' / 'Hide' with the Route state_suffix (+0x10) appended when growing forward, or state_suffix_2 (+0x14) when reversed (effect +105); then plays UI sound 44 or 45.

name: WorldMapScreen_BindNodes
callees: GUINode_FindDescendant, GUINode_FindDescendant2, GUINode_FindPartByName, GUINode_FindGadgetPart, UITable_GetRowByKey, UIName_Key, Str_Format
purpose: Binds the world-map screen's nodes: the widget's root, MapAll with its Route and Bases groups, the 48 base/point nodes, and each base's TextBoardMapName title.

behavior.text: the root comes from sub_1403F9DA0(a+24); 'MapAll' is found under it and its part (size x 0.5 and x 0.25 are stored at +2440..+2452); 'Route' and 'Bases' are descendants of MapAll.

for i in 0..47 the UITable 0x34 row i names the base ('Base%s' when its byte +48 is set, else 'Point%s'); the node is bound at a+520+24*i, tagged (+544 = 31, +548 = i) and, when it is a base, set up with sub_140158E30; the 'Title' part of its 'TextBoardMapName' gadget gets the row's name text.

the UITable 0x34 is the Town table: the node name suffix is Town node_name (+0x18), 'Base' is chosen by the base byte (+0x30); each location's entry at a+520+24*i holds the node, its part, +16 = locations_list (+0x24) and +20 = the base byte.

notes: The name is ours; only the first half of the function (to the 'Days' group) was read. It uses the same TextBoardxx / 'Title' gadget lookup as the Job Tree's MainTab_BindNodes.

name: WorldMapScreen_ScrollToProgress
purpose: Computes the map scroll target of the current progress row.

behavior.text: when WorldMapProgressInfo map_x (+0x20) and map_y (+0x24) are both not -1 they are the scroll target; clamped and stored at screen +3324 / +3328.

name: WorldMapScreen_SetProgress
purpose: Stores the current story progress on the world-map screen and shows the objective line.

behavior.text: screen +3336 = a2[0]; the GameProgress (92) row (0, a2[1]) gives +8 / +0xC, stored at screen +3308 / +3312 (the keys of the current WorldMapProgressInfo row).
the node 'TextTodo' (+2104) gets WorldMapProgress_GetObjectiveCaption(...).

name: WorldMapScreen_SetRoute
proto: void WorldMapScreen_SetRoute(void *screen, int route, int flag)
purpose: Records the route being opened on the world-map screen.

behavior.text: screen +3284 = route, +3296 = flag, +3288 = Route town (+8) when the flag is set, else town_2 (+0xC).

name: WorldRoads_BuildMarkers
purpose: Builds the drawable marker points of every open road on the world map.

behavior.text: loops over the 48 entries of the road point list table (0x140684B50), from event variable 556: a road is drawn only when its event variable is set.

for each way point id in the road's list converts it to a screen position with sub_140274BC0 and marks whether it lies inside the visible area; every four points it emits one marker segment with sub_140340494.
does nothing when a world-map flag (bit 5 of the world state dword) is set.

notes: Read in full.
open_questions: ?: the visible area bounds used for the test.

name: WorldRoute_Search
purpose: Recursive shortest-route search over the open world-map roads; keeps the best road list.

behavior.text: walks the 51 roads of the road table (0x140684980); a road is usable when event variable 556 + road id is set and it is not already on the current path.
follows a road from either end (bit 8 of the stored entry = travelled from its second location to its first) and adds the road's length to the running cost.
a path that reaches the target with fewer roads, or as many roads and a lower cost, replaces the kept route (up to 16 roads).

name: WorldWeather_Update
purpose: Updates the world map weather level when the calendar advances.

behavior.text: reads scene variables 46 (month) and 47 (day) and 35 (the current weather level).
finds the calendar span by comparing (month, day) with the four boundary pairs of WeatherBySeason, maps the span to a row of ten adjustments and draws one with the random generator.
new level = level + adjustment, clamped to 0..4; stored in scene variable 35 unless a flag word says the map is busy, then a one in three random value is stored in scene variable 36.

notes: Name is ours; the variable meanings (weather) are inferred.
open_questions: ?: what scene variables 35 and 36 do on screen.

name: ZodiacStone_AnyMet
purpose: Tells whether any ZodiacStone row has its user_situation met.

behavior.text: walks every set and every row of the ZodiacStone table (the last row of each set first) and returns 1 at the first row whose user_situation (+8) passes UserSituation_IsMet, else 0.

name: ZodiacStone_AnyMetAndNew
purpose: Tells whether any ZodiacStone row is met and still carries its new mark.

behavior.text: the same walk as ZodiacStone_AnyMet; returns 1 at the first row whose user_situation is met and whose byte at save block +6608 + 4 * set + index is non-zero.
that byte is the row's 'new' mark (see SaveBlockUiMarks).

name: ZodiacStone_ClearNewMarks
purpose: Clears the new mark of every ZodiacStone row that is met.

behavior.text: the same walk; for every met row it clears the byte at save block +6608 + 4 * set + index.
the save block therefore holds a 4-byte-per-stone array of row marks at +6608 (see SaveBlockUiMarks).

name: ZodiacStone_FillDetail
purpose: Fills the stone's detail page (icons, name, description, Clear mark).

behavior.text: the icon +0x20 goes to the node at +64 without any condition; the name (+0x10) and the description (+0x18) fall back to row (n, 0) when empty; the icon +0x1C goes to the node at +568.
row +0x24 (clear_mark) drives the node at +56 ('Clear', bound in sub_14016DB90): 'Enable' when set, else 'Disable'. (A first reading took it for a gate on the icon; it is not.)

name: ZodiacStone_FillTip
purpose: Fills the stone's tip (icon, name, summary).

behavior.text: the icon node at +472 gets GuiImage_SetIconById(row +0x20 icon_2); the texts are the name (+0x10) and the summary (+0x14), taking the row (n, 0) when the chosen row's string is empty.

name: ZodiacStoneBoard_Setup
callees: MainTab_BindNodes, MainTab_SelectTab, sub_1402AAB0C, UserSituation_IsMet, Icon_FormatPath, sub_1400F4E74, GUINode_FindState, GUINode_PlayState, GUINode_StopState, GUITextNode_SetTextExpandedTemp
purpose: Sets up the Zodiac Stone board: for each of the 13 stones picks the row to show, plays the stone's state and sets its name.

behavior.text: binds the main tabs (tab 2 selected) and finds the node 'Arazlam'; the node 'Board' plays 'Loop'.

walks ZodiacStone: for each stone (first key) it stores in the board's dword array at +408 (dword index 102) the highest second key whose user_situation (+8) is met (-1 when none) and preloads that row's icon (+0x1C, Icon_FormatPath); it also preloads the icon of row (n, 0) for the 13 stones.

per stone the node 'Zst_%02d' (kind 3) gets node +548 = n + 100 and +557 = 0. No met row: 'HideStone', and 'Loop' is stopped there. Otherwise row +0xC (zodiac_stone_owner_timeline) decides: 0 plays 'ShowStone'; non-zero plays, when the value is not 1, the state named by string +8 of the ZodiacStoneOwnerTimeline row (table 238) with that id, then 'ShowUnacquired'.
the text node 'TextBoardName' (kind 13) gets the name (+0x10).

notes: The 'Show<owner>' state names come from the owner-timeline table, the 'Hide<owner>' names from its +0xC (reader not looked for).
open_questions: ? what the 'Loop' animation looks like; ? the reader of ZodiacStoneOwnerTimeline +0xC.
